Or: he is the peacemaker between God and men, appeasing the wrath of God and restoring men to the grace of God, by interceding and satisfying for their sins, and causing God to love men and men to love God, so that there is a constant and eternal peace and concord between God and men.

units.la: Differunt medius & mediator: illud est nomen naturæ, vel personæ, hoc officij, Christus vtrumque est. Medius, quia in eo est natura vtriusque partis, hoc est, diuina & humana. Mediator, quia nos reconciliat Deo: seu, quia est persona μεσίτης.
units.tr: A medius and a mediator differ: the former is a name of nature or person, the latter of office; Christ is both. He is medius because in him is the nature of both parties, that is, divine and human. He is Mediator because he reconciles us to God; or because he is the person μεσίτης [mesitēs].

units.la: II. An Mediatore nobis apud Deum opus sit.
units.tr: II. Whether we need a Mediator with God.

units.la: Mediator est nobis necessarius.
units.tr: A Mediator is necessary for us.

units.la: 1. Quia justitia Dei non admittit reconciliationem sine reditu in gratiam: Ergo requiritur internuncius. Nec sine deprecatione: Ergo & deprecator. Nec sine satisfactione: Ergo & satisfactor. Nec sine applicatione; oportet enim beneficium accipi: Ergo & applicator. Nec denique sine expurgatione peccati & instauratione imaginis Dei in nobis, vt delinamus offendere: Ergo & expurgator peccati & instaurator naturæ. Hæc autem ipsi non possumus præstare: placare Deum offensum, & nos ei acceptosfacere, &c. Alio igitur opus est Mediatore, qui ista possit, & nobis præstet.
units.tr: 1. Because the justice of God does not admit reconciliation without return to favour; therefore an intermediary is required. Nor is it possible without intercession; therefore also an intercessor. Nor without satisfaction; therefore also a satisfier. Nor without application, for the benefit must be received; therefore also an applier. Nor finally without the cleansing of sin and the restoration of the image of God in us, so that we cease to offend; therefore also a cleanser of sin and a restorer of nature. But we ourselves cannot perform these things: to appease God when offended, and to make ourselves acceptable to him, and so on. We therefore need another Mediator, who can do these things and perform them for us.

units.la: 2. Deus postulabat Mediatorem à parte, quæ offenderat. Deus enim, quatenus Deus, noluit à se accipere satisfactionem, sed voluit pro sua justitia, vt pars offendens eam præstaret, vel gratiam impetraret per Mediatorem, & eum ipsa daret, qui posset perfectè satisfacere, quique Deo gratissimus esset, ne repulsam pateretur, sed gratia sua, qua apud Deum valeret, nos Deo reconciliare posset, satisfaciendo, deprecando & intercedendo pro nobis. Hanc vero personam neque nos sustinere, neque ex nobis dare poteramus: quia omnes eramus filij iræ. Opus igitur erat aliquo tertio, scilicet Mediatore. Datus ergo esta Deo tertius, qui & homo esset, & Deo gratissimus.
units.tr: 2. God required a Mediator on the part of the party that had offended. For God, as God, was unwilling to receive satisfaction from himself, but in accordance with his justice willed that the offending party should make it, or obtain grace through a Mediator, and that he should give the one who could satisfy perfectly and who would be most acceptable to God, so that he would not suffer rejection, but by his grace, which had weight with God, could reconcile us to God, by satisfying, pleading and interceding for us. We could neither sustain this person nor provide him from among ourselves, since we were all children of wrath. There was therefore need of some third party, namely a Mediator. A third person was therefore given by God, who should be both man and most acceptable to God.

units.la: 3. Quos necesse est vel per se, vel per alium justitiæ Dei satisfacere, vt liberentur: per se autem non possunt: ij opus habent Mediatore. Nos oportet justitiæ Dei vel per nos, vel per alium satisfacere, vt liberemur: per nos autem non possumus. Ergo opus habemus Mediatore.
units.tr: 3. Those who must satisfy the justice of God, either by themselves or through another, in order to be freed, and who cannot do so by themselves, need a Mediator. We must satisfy the justice of God, either through ourselves or through another, in order to be freed; but we cannot through ourselves. Therefore we need a Mediator.

units.la: Obiect. Vbi vnus tantum est satisfaciendi modus, non est quærendus etiam alius. Lex modum satisfaciendi agnoscit tantantum vnum, videlicet per nos. Ergo non ponendus est etiam alius, nec dicendum, vel per nos, vel per alium. Resp. Conceditur totum de Lege. In ea enim tantum vnus satisfaciendi modus ponitur, & alius frustra quæritur. Interim Lex ita ponit modum vnum, vt non neget alterum. Dicit quidem, satisfacien-dum esse per nos. Sed nusquam dicit: tantum per nos. Nusquam igitur excludit modum satisfaciendi per alium. Etsi autem Deus hunc alterum modum in lege non expressit: tamen in suo arcano consilio eum posuit: & postea in Euangelio renelauit. Lex igitur eum modum non explicat: relinquit vero Euangelio patefaciendum. Inst. Ergo Euangelium pugnat cum Lege. Resp. Non pugnat. Nam quod Euangelium ponit, Lex non negat: quia Lex nullibi addit exclusiuam, quod tantum per nos oporteat fieri satisfactionem.
units.tr: Objection. Where there is only one way of satisfying, another is not to be sought as well. The Law acknowledges only one way of satisfying, namely through ourselves. Therefore another is not to be posited, nor should it be said, either through ourselves or through another. Answer. The whole is granted concerning the Law. For in it only one way of satisfying is set down, and another is sought in vain. Yet the Law sets down the one way in such a manner that it does not deny the other. It indeed says that satisfaction is to be made through ourselves. But nowhere does it say: only through ourselves. Nowhere, therefore, does it exclude the way of satisfying through another. Although God did not express this other way in the Law, nevertheless he had posited it in his hidden counsel, and afterwards revealed it in the Gospel. The Law therefore does not explain that way; it leaves it to be made known by the Gospel. Objection. Then the Gospel fights against the Law. Answer. It does not fight. For what the Gospel sets forth, the Law does not deny; because the Law nowhere adds an exclusive clause, that satisfaction must be made only through ourselves.

units.la: 4. Mediatore nobis opus esse apud Deum, ostendunt multa alia. 1. Pauores & cruciatus conscientiæ in nobis. 2. Pœnæ impiorum. 3. Sacrificia à Deo ordinata, quibus perfectum Christi sacrificium significabatur. 4 Sacrificia Ethnicorum & Papistarum, quibus volunt placare Deum, quia sentiunt, satisfactione apud Deum opus esse.
units.tr: 4. That we need a Mediator with God is shown by many other things. 1. The fears and torments of conscience within us. 2. The punishments of the wicked. 3. The sacrifices ordained by God, by which the perfect sacrifice of Christ was signified. 4. The sacrifices of the Gentiles and the Papists, by which they want to appease God, because they feel that satisfaction is needed before God.

units.la: III. Quod sit Mediatoris officium, & quæ beneficia.
units.tr: III. What the Mediator's office is, and what benefits it brings.

units.la: Oportet Mediatorem agere cum vtraque parte, offensa & offendente. Christus igitur Mediator agit cum vtraque parte.
units.tr: The Mediator must deal with both parties, the one offended and the one offending. Christ, then, as Mediator, deals with both parties.

units.la: Cum Deo offenso agit: 1. Intercedit apud Patrem, & culpam deprecatur pro nobis. 2. Offert se ad satisfactionem. 3. Ipsa præstat satisfactionem, moriendo pro nobis, & luendo pœnam sufficientem, tempore quidem finitam, sed dignitate & valore infinitam. 4. Spondet fore, vt nos eum non amplius offenda-mus. Namq; absque hac sponsione, nec apud homines quidem, nec dum apud Deum, locum inuenit intercessio. 5. Tandemque hanc sponsionem in nobis efficit, dato Spiritu sancto, & vita æterna.
units.tr: In dealing with God, who has been offended: (1) he intercedes with the Father and pleads for our fault; (2) he offers himself as satisfaction; (3) he himself makes the satisfaction, by dying for us and paying a penalty that is sufficient, finite in time but infinite in dignity and worth; (4) he pledges that we will no longer offend him. For without this pledge, intercession finds no place, neither among men nor yet with God. (5) And finally he brings about this pledge in us, by giving the Holy Spirit and eternal life.

units.la: Nobiscum vt cum parte offendente etiam agit. 1. Prodit in medium tanquam Legatus Patris, patefaciens hoc eius consilium, quod ipse se sistat Mediatorem, & quod Pater satisfactionem eius accipiat. 2. Præstat satisfactionem: præstitam nobis imputat, donat & applicat. 3. Dato Spiritu sancto efficit in nobis fidem, qua oblatum beneficium amplectamur, & non respuamus, quia non fit reconciliatio, nisi vtraque pars consentiat. Ipse efficit velle & perficere. 4 Efficit per eundem Spiritum, vt desinamus peccare, & inchoemus vitam nouam. 5. Seruat nos in reconciliatione, fide & obedientia noua, ac defendit aduer- sus diabolos & omnes hostes, etiam aduersus nos ipsos, ne de- ficiamus. 6. Deniq; suscitabit nos, & glorificabit, hoc est, per- ficiet inchoatam salutem, & dona, tum quae nos amisimus, tum quae ipse nobis est meritus.
units.tr: He also deals with us as the offending party. (1) He comes forward as the Father's envoy, making known this purpose of the Father, that he himself presents himself as Mediator and that the Father accepts his satisfaction. (2) He makes the satisfaction: he imputes what was done to us, grants it, and applies it. (3) By giving the Holy Spirit he creates in us the faith by which we embrace the offered benefit and do not reject it, since reconciliation does not take place unless both parties consent. He himself brings about both the willing and the doing. (4) Through the same Spirit he brings it about that we cease to sin and begin a new life. (5) He keeps us in reconciliation, in faith and new obedience, and defends us against the devils and all enemies, even against ourselves, so that we do not fail. (6) Lastly, he will raise us up and glorify us; that is, he will complete the salvation begun, and the gifts both those that we have lost and those that he himself has merited for us.

units.la: Haec omnia Christus Mediator agit, impetrat & perficit me- rito & efficacia: quia non solum suo sacrificio nobis meretur, sed etiam sui Spiritus virtute efficaciter confert sua beneficia, justitiam & vitam aeternam, juxta dicta: Ego pono animam meam pro ovibus. Ego do eis vitam aeternam. Sicut Pater habet vitam in se ipso, sic dedit & Filio habere: & sicut Pater vivificat, ita & Filius, quos vult, vivificat. Sine me nihil potestis facere.
units.tr: Christ the Mediator accomplishes, obtains and completes all these things by merit and by efficacy: for he not only merits them for us by his sacrifice, but also by the power of his Spirit he effectually confers his benefits, righteousness and eternal life, according to the sayings: I lay down my life for the sheep. I give them eternal life. As the Father has life in himself, so he has given the Son also to have life in himself; and as the Father quickens, so also the Son quickens whom he will. Apart from me you can do nothing.

units.la: In officio Mediatoris continentur beneficia. Nam officium Mediatori à Deo iniunctum, est dare beneficia Ecclesiae. Ea Paulus breuissimè complectitur, cum inquit: Ex ipso vos estis in Christo Iesu, qui factus est nobis sapientia à Deo, justitia, & sanctificatio & redemptio. Sapientia est nobis factus. 1. Quia est materia & subiectum nostrae sapientiae. Non decreueram quicquam scire inter vos, nisi Iesum Christum eumq; crucifixum. Praedicamus Christum crucifixum, Iudaeis offendiculum, Graecis stultitiam. Ipsis autem vocatis tum Iudaeis tum Graecis, Dei potentiam, & Dei sapientiam. 2. Quia est causa nostrae sapientiae, idque tripliciter: tum quia protulit eam ex sinu aeterni Patris: tum quia instituit & conseruat ministerium verbi: per quod nos docet de voluntate Patris, & de suo officio. 3. Quia est efficax in cordibus electorum, ut assentiantur doctrinae, & ad imaginem Dei renentur. Breuiter, est sapientiae nostrae subiectum, author & medium. Iustitia: id est, justificator. Ipse enim eam nobis donat merito & efficacia. Sanctificatio: id est, sanctificator, qui nos regenerat & sanctificat per Spiritum sanctum. Redemptio, id est, redemptor, quia liberat finaliter. Nam ἀπολύτρωσις non tantum pretium, sed etiam effectum pretij & complementum redemtionis significat.
units.tr: The benefits are contained in the office of the Mediator. For the office enjoined on the Mediator by God is to give benefits to the Church. Paul summarises these very briefly when he says: But of him are you in Christ Jesus, who was made to us wisdom from God, righteousness, sanctification and redemption. He was made wisdom to us: (1) because he is the matter and subject of our wisdom. For I determined to know nothing among you except Jesus Christ, and him crucified. We preach Christ crucified, to the Jews a stumbling block, to the Greeks foolishness; but to those who are called, both Jews and Greeks, the power of God and the wisdom of God. (2) Because he is the cause of our wisdom, and this in three ways: first, because he brought it forth from the bosom of the eternal Father; second, because he instituted and preserves the ministry of the Word, through which he teaches us about the Father's will and about his own office; third, because he is effective in the hearts of the elect, so that they assent to the doctrine and are renewed into the image of God. In short, he is the subject, author and means of our wisdom. Righteousness: that is, the justifier. For he himself bestows it on us by merit and by efficacy. Sanctification: that is, the sanctifier, who regenerates and sanctifies us through the Holy Spirit. Redemption: that is, the redeemer, because he delivers us finally. For apolytrōsis [ἀπολύτρωσις] signifies not only the price but also the effect of the price and the completion of the redemption.

units.la: IV. Qualis Mediator esse debeat?
units.tr: IV. What sort of Mediator ought he to be?

units.la: Haec quaestio optimè cohaeret cum superioribus. Quia enim constat I. Esse satisfaciendum. II. Per alium. III. Satisfactione Mediatoris, quae jam est descripta: Quaeritur IV. Qualis sit & esse debuerit? Respond. Mediator Dei & hominum est & esse debuit 1. Homo. 2. Homo verus ex nostro genere naturam habens, & perpetuò retinens. 3. Homo perfectè justus. 4. Verus Deus. Summa: Debuit esse persona θεάνθρωπος, utramque naturam, humanam & diuinam habens in vnitate personae: ut esset verè medius & mediator inter Deum & homines, tam persona, quàm officio. Nam propter officium tale, mediatorem talem esse oportuit. Sunt autem jam supra explicatæ ad qq.catechet. xv. xvi. xvii. vbi requirantur.
units.tr: This question fits very well with what has gone before. For it is established: (I) that satisfaction must be made; (II) that it must be made through another; (III) through the satisfaction of the Mediator, which has already been described. The question now is (IV) what sort of Mediator he is and ought to have been. The answer: the Mediator between God and men is, and ought to have been, (1) a man; (2) a true man, of our kind, having and constantly retaining our nature; (3) a man perfectly righteous; (4) true God. In summary: he ought to have been a person who is God-man [θεάνθρωπος], having both natures, human and divine, in the unity of one person, so that he might be truly in the middle and a mediator between God and men, both in person and in office. For on account of such an office, the Mediator had to be such a person. These matters have already been explained above, at the catechism questions 15, 16 and 17, where they may be consulted.

units.la: V. Quis sit iste Mediator ΘΕΑΝΘΡΩΠΟΣ?
units.tr: V. Who is this God-man [ΘΕΑΝΘΡΩΠΟΣ]?

units.la: Mediator hactenus descriptus est ipse filius Dei, Dominus noster Iesus Christus, quemadmodum supra ad quæst. catech. xviii. est demonstratum. Summa est, quod scriptura vni & soli Christo hæc tria simul tribuit.
units.tr: The Mediator described so far is the Son of God himself, our Lord Jesus Christ, as has been shown above at catechism question 18. The sum is that Scripture ascribes these three things together to Christ alone.

units.la: Primò: Quod sit Deus. Sermo erat Deus. Omnia per ipsum facta sunt. Deus proprio sanguine acquisiuit Ecclesiam. Qui declaratus est Filius Dei potenter secundum Spiritum sanctificationis. Quisquis credit in eum, non pudefiet. Tres sunt, qui testificantur in cælo: Pater, Sermo, & Spiritus sanctus: & hi tres unum sunt. His addenda sunt loca, quibus Christo tribuitur cultus diuinus, inuocatio, exauditio, & opera solius DEI propria: Item ea, quæ Christo attribuunt nomen Iehouæ. Ier.23,6. Zach.12,10. Mal.3,1. Item ea, quæ de Iehoua olim dicta ad Christum referuntur, vt Esa.6, 9. Iohannis 12. verf.40. &c.
units.tr: First: that he is God. The Word was God. All things were made through him. God obtained the Church with his own blood. He who was declared to be the Son of God with power, according to the Spirit of sanctification. Whoever believes in him shall not be put to shame. There are three who bear witness in heaven: the Father, the Word, and the Holy Spirit; and these three are one. To these must be added the passages in which divine worship is ascribed to Christ, invocation, answering of prayer, and works proper to God alone: likewise those which ascribe to Christ the name Jehovah, Jer. 23:6; Zech. 12:10; Mal. 3:1; likewise those which refer to Christ what was formerly said of Jehovah, such as Isa. 6:9; John 12:40, etc.

units.la: Secundò: Quod sit verus homo. Huc pertinent dicta, quæ Christum vocant hominem, filium hominis, filium Dauidis & Abrahami, fructum ventris Mariæ; Item, quæ dicunt, factum ex semine Dauidis secundum carnem, habere corpus carnis: venisse in carne particeps factus esse carnis & sanguinis. Item, quæ Christo tribuunt propria hominis, vt, crescere, edere, bibere, nescire, defatigari, quiescere, circumcidi, baptizari, contristari, lætari, &c.
units.tr: Second: that he is a true man. To this belong the sayings which call Christ man, son of man, son of David and of Abraham, fruit of the womb of Mary; likewise those which say that he was made from the seed of David according to the flesh, that he had a body of flesh, that he came in the flesh, was made a partaker of flesh and blood. Likewise those which ascribe to Christ the things proper to man, such as to grow, to eat, to drink, not to know, to grow weary, to rest, to be circumcised, to be baptized, to be sorrowful, to rejoice, etc.

units.la: Tertiò: Quod duæ naturæ in Christo vnam personam constituant. Huc pertinent dicta, quæ per communicationem idiomatum tribuuntur personæ Christi, quæ diuinæ vel humanæ naturæ sunt propria. Sermo ille est caro factus. Particeps factus est carnis & sanguinis. Deus proprio sanguine acquisiuit ecclesiam. Antequam Abraham fieret, ego sum. Ego vobiscum sum omnibus diebus usque ad consummationem seculi. Locutus est nobis per Filium, per quem & mundum fecit, &c. Iesus Christus venit in carnem. Christus Deus laudandus supra omnia secula. Si cognouissent, nequaquam Dominum gloriæ crucifixissent.
units.tr: Third: that the two natures constitute one person in Christ. To this belong the sayings which, by the communication of properties, are attributed to the person of Christ, though they are proper to the divine or the human nature. That Word was made flesh. He was made a partaker of flesh and blood. God obtained the Church with his own blood. Before Abraham was, I am. I am with you always, even to the end of the age. He has spoken to us by his Son, through whom also he made the world, etc. Jesus Christ came in the flesh. Christ God, to be praised above all things for ever. If they had known, they would never have crucified the Lord of glory.

units.la: II. An sint plures Mediatores?
units.tr: II. Whether there are several mediators?

units.la: Vnus tantum est mediator Dei & hominum. Ratio, quia solus Filius Dei est Mediator: & solus mediatoris officium præstare potest. Filius autem Dei naturalis est vnus. 1 Tim. 2, 5.
units.tr: There is only one mediator between God and men. The reason: only the Son of God is Mediator, and only he can perform the office of Mediator. Now the Son of God is one by nature. 1 Tim. 2, 5.

units.la: Vnus Deus, vnus etiam Mediacor Dei & hominum, homo Christus Iesus.
units.tr: There is one God, and also one Mediator between God and men, the man Christ Jesus.

units.la: Obiect. 1. Etiam Sancti pro nobis intercedunt: Ergo & illi sunt mediatores. Respond. Discrimen ingens est intercessionis Christi & sanctorum in mundo degentium, & precantium pro se & aliis, etiam pro persecutoribus & hostibus. Sancti enim nituntur Christi merito: Christus suo. Et hic solus se obtulit sponsorem & satisfactorem, pro nobis semetipsum sanctificans, hoc est, sistens judicio Dei: quod de sanctis dici nequit. Quod sancti etiam in coelo intercedant pro nobis, est commentum Platonicum Papistarum, Christi gloriæ derogans, & Scripturæ repugnans.
units.tr: Objection 1. The saints also intercede for us; therefore they too are mediators. Answer: There is a huge difference between the intercession of Christ and that of the saints who live in the world and pray for themselves and others, even for persecutors and enemies. For the saints rely on the merit of Christ, whereas Christ relies on his own. And he alone offered himself as surety and satisfaction, "sanctifying himself for us," that is, presenting himself to the judgment of God; this cannot be said of the saints. That the saints in heaven also intercede for us is a Platonic invention of the Papists, which detracts from the glory of Christ and contradicts Scripture.

units.la: Obiect.2. Vbi multa sunt media, ibi non est vnus Mediator. Sed multa sunt media salutis nostræ. Ergo non vnus est Mediator. Resp. Maior negatur. Non enim sunt idem, media & Mediator salutis.
units.tr: Objection 2. Where there are many means, there is not one Mediator. But there are many means of our salvation. Therefore there is not one Mediator. Answer: The major premise is denied. For the means of salvation and the Mediator of salvation are not the same thing.

units.la: DE FOEDERE DEI.
units.tr: ON THE COVENANT OF GOD.

units.la: Dictum est, quod Mediator sit persona reconcilians partes diffidentes, Deum & homines. Ista autem reconciliatio in scripturis dicitur fœdus, quod est correlatiunm Mediatoris: Omnis enim mediator est alicuius fœderis mediator, & duarum partium conciliator. Quare cum doctrina de Mediatore cohæret doctrina de fœdere Dei. De hoc præcipuæ quæstiones sunt: I. Quid sit. II. Possitne iniri sine Mediatore. III. Sitne vnum, an plura. IV. Quomodo vetus & nouum fœdus conveniant & differant.
units.tr: It has been said that the Mediator is the person who reconciles the parties at odds, God and men. This reconciliation is called a covenant in the Scriptures, and it is the correlate of the Mediator: every mediator is the mediator of some covenant and the conciliator of two parties. Therefore the doctrine of the Mediator is bound up with the doctrine of God's covenant. Four main questions arise about it: I. What it is. II. Whether it can be made without a Mediator. III. Whether there is one covenant or several. IV. How the old and new covenants agree and differ.

units.la: I. Quid sit fœdus Dei.
units.tr: I. What the covenant of God is.

units.la: Fœdus in genere est mutua pactio duarum partium, qua altera alteri se certis conditionibus obligat ad aliquid faciendum, vel accipiendum, adhibitis signis & symbolis externis ad solennem testificationem, confirmationis causa, ut promissio fiat inviolabilis. Hinc facile colligitur definitio fœderis Dei. Est enim mutua pactio inter Deum & homines, qua Deus confirmat hominibus, se futurum eis propitium, remissurum peccata, donaturum justitiam novam, Spiritum sanctum, & vitam æternam, per & propter Filium Mediatorem: Vicissim homines se obligant Deo ad fidem & pœnitentiam, hoc est, ad præstandam Deo veram obedientiam. Hæc pactio mutua Dei & hominum symbolis externis confirmatur, quæ vocatur tur sacramenta, hoc est, sacra signa testificantia de hac Dei erga nos voluntate, & nostra erga Deum gratitudine atque officiis.
units.tr: In general, a covenant is a mutual agreement between two parties, by which one binds itself to the other, under certain conditions, to do or to receive something. External signs and symbols are used for solemn witness and for confirmation, so that the promise may be made inviolable. From this we can readily draw the definition of God's covenant. It is a mutual agreement between God and men, in which God assures men that he will be gracious to them, will forgive their sins, will bestow on them new righteousness, the Holy Spirit and eternal life, through and for the sake of the Son, the Mediator. In turn, men bind themselves to God to faith and repentance, that is, to render to God true obedience. This mutual agreement of God and men is confirmed by external symbols, which are called sacraments, that is, sacred signs bearing witness to this will of God toward us and to our gratitude and duties toward God.

units.la: Testamentum proprie dicitur ultima voluntas testatoris, qua moriens disponit de rebus suis, quid de illis fieri velit post mortem.
units.tr: Properly speaking, a testament is the last will of a testator, by which a dying man disposes of his property, stating what he wishes to be done with it after his death.

units.la: In scriptura nomen foederis & testamenti ad denotandum hoc Dei foedus pro eodem sumuntur. Utrunque enim reconciliationem nostri cum Deo, seu mutuam illam pactionem inter Deum & homines designat.
units.tr: In Scripture the names covenant and testament are used interchangeably to denote this covenant of God. Both designate our reconciliation with God, or that mutual agreement between God and men.

units.la: Foedus autem vocatur haec pactio & reconciliatio, quia Deus nobis promittit certa bona, & a nobis vicissim pacisci tur obedientiam, adhibens etiam ceremonias solennes ad eius confirmationem.
units.tr: This agreement and reconciliation is called a covenant because God promises us certain good things, and in turn we pledge ourselves to obedience, and he also adds solemn ceremonies to confirm it.

units.la: Testamentum vocatur, quia interveniente mortis Christi testatoris facta est haec reconciliatio, ut esset rata: seu, quia Christus hanc reconciliationem morte sua acquisivit, eamque nobis reliquit, non secus ac patentes morientes defuncti bona sua liberis relinquunt. Haec ratio affertur in epistola ad Hebraeos: Itaque ob id novi foederis mediator est, ut morte intercedente vocati accipiant promissionem aeternae hereditatis. Nam ubi testamentum est, mors intercedat necesse est testatoris. Testamentum enim in mortuis ratum est: quemadmodum nondum valet, cum vivit testator. Habet enim testator jus mutandi, detrahendi, addendi, quoad vivit. Hebraea vox בריה tantum significat foedus, non testamentum. Interpretes tamen verterunt διαθήκη, quae vox Latinis utrumque significat: unde epistolam eam non Hebraice (ut quidam putant) sed Graece scriptam esse colligitur.
units.tr: It is called a testament because this reconciliation was made by the intervening death of Christ the testator, so that it might be ratified; or because Christ obtained this reconciliation by his death and left it to us, just as dying men leave their goods to their children by will. This reason is given in the Epistle to the Hebrews: And for this cause he is the mediator of the new testament, that by means of death, for the redemption of the transgressions that were under the first testament, they which are called might receive the promise of eternal inheritance. For where a testament is, there must also of necessity be the death of the testator. For a testament is of force after men are dead: otherwise it is of no strength at all while the testator liveth. A testator has the right to change, remove or add to his will as long as he lives. The Hebrew word berith [בְּרִית] signifies only covenant, not testament. The translators, however, rendered it diathēkē [διαθήκη], a Greek word which in Latin means both. From this it is gathered that this Epistle was written not in Hebrew (as some think) but in Greek.

units.la: Obiect. Testamentum est ratum morte testatoris. Sed Deus non potest mori. Ergo testamentum eius non est ratum: vel reconciliatio haec non potest dici testamentum. Resp. Negatur minor, quia Deus redemit ecclesiam proprio sanguine. Deus ergo est mortuus: sed in humana natura. Christus enim testator Deus & homo est: mortuus est igitur non divinitate, sed carne, teste Petro: Mortificatus carne.
units.tr: Objection. A testament is ratified by the death of the testator. But God cannot die. Therefore his testament is not ratified, or this reconciliation cannot be called a testament. Answer. The minor premise is denied, because God redeemed the Church with his own blood. God therefore died, but in human nature. For Christ the testator is God and man; he died therefore not in his divinity but in his flesh, as Peter witnesses: Put to death in the flesh.

units.la: II. Quomodo foedus inter Deum & hominem iniri possit?
units.tr: II. How can a covenant between God and man be entered into?

units.la: Hoc foedus non potuit fieri sine mediatore. Nos enim non poteramus satisfacere, nec redire in gratiam cum Deo, immo nec accipere beneficium reconciliationis ab alio partum. Deus vero propter justitiam & veritatem suam noluit nos absque satisfactione sufficiente admittere. Eramus hostes Dei: ideo reditus ad Deum nobis non patebat, nisi intercedente pro nobis Christo mediatore: quemadmodum hoc fusius declaratum est supra quaestione: Cur necessarius sit mediator. Non potuit igitur inter Deum & homines foedus iniri, & reconciliatio fieri, sine satisfactione & morte mediatoris & hominis.
units.tr: This covenant could not be made without a mediator. We could not make satisfaction, nor return into favour with God, nor even receive the benefit of reconciliation if it were procured by another. God, however, on account of his justice and truth, was unwilling to admit us without sufficient satisfaction. We were enemies of God, so a way back to God was open to us only if Christ the Mediator interceded for us, as has been explained more fully above under the question: Why a mediator is necessary. Therefore a covenant could not be entered into between God and men, nor reconciliation be made, without the satisfaction and death of the Mediator, who was both God and man.

units.la: III. Sitne unum, an plura.
units.tr: III. Whether there is one or several.

units.la: Foedus Dei est unum substantiâ, duplex circumstantiis: seu est unum, quoad conditiones principales, quas Deus nobis, & nos Deo stipulamur: & sunt duo, quoad conditiones minus principales, vel, ut alij loquuntur, quoad modum administrationis.
units.tr: The covenant of God is one in substance but twofold in circumstances. That is, it is one as to its principal conditions, which God stipulates with us and we with God; and it is two as to its less principal conditions, or, as others put it, as to the mode of administration.

units.la: Unum est substantiâ. I. Quia unus est Deus, unus mediator Dei & hominum Christus Iesus: unus modus reconciliationis: una fides: una salutis via ab initio omnium qui servantur, & servati sunt. Quaestio magna est, an aliter servati sin Patres veteris testamenti, quam nos: quae nisi recte explicetur, magnae tenebrae offunduntur Euangelio. De eo vero docent haec dicta: Iesus Christus heri & hodie idem est, & in saecula. Constituit eum caput Ecclesiae super omnia. Ex quo totum corpus coagmentatur congruenter, & Deum nemo vidit unquam; Filius, qui est in sinu Patris, revelavit nobis. Non est aliud nomen sub caelo, quod datum sit inter homines, per quod oporteat nos servari. Nemo novit Patrem nisi Filius: & cui Filius voluerit revelare. Nemo venit ad Patrem nisi per me. Ego sum via, veritas & vita. Ego, inquit, nempe solus sum via, per quam etiam Adam ad salutem pervenit. Multi reges & prophetae cupierunt videre diem quae vos videtis, & non viderunt. Abraham gestiit videre diem meum, & vidit, & gavisus est. Omnes ergo tam sub Lege, quam sub Euangelio salvandi fide respexerunt ad unicum mediatorem Christum, per quem solum Deo reconciliati sunt atque servati. Foedus proinde substantiâ est unum.
units.tr: It is one in substance. First, because there is one God, one Mediator between God and men, Christ Jesus; one way of reconciliation, one faith, one way of salvation from the beginning for all who are saved and have been saved. There is a great question whether the Fathers of the Old Testament were saved otherwise than we are, and unless this is rightly explained, great darkness is cast over the Gospel. On this point these sayings teach: Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, and today, and for ever. He gave him to be the head over all things to the Church. From whom the whole body fitly joined together. No man hath seen God at any time; the only begotten Son, who is in the bosom of the Father, he hath declared him. Neither is there salvation in any other: for there is none other name under heaven given among men, whereby we must be saved. No man knoweth the Father, save the Son, and he to whom the Son will reveal him. No man cometh unto the Father, but by me. I am the way, the truth, and the life. "I," he says, "am alone the way, by which Adam too attained salvation." Many prophets and kings desired to see those things which ye see, and have not seen them. Abraham rejoiced to see my day, and he saw it, and was glad. Therefore all, both under the Law and under the Gospel, looked in faith to the one Mediator Christ, through whom alone they were reconciled to God and saved. The covenant is therefore one in substance.

units.la: II. Unum duntaxat est, quia conditiones principales, quae substantia foederis dicuntur, eaedem sunt ante Christum & post Christum. Nam in utroque testamento, ante & post Christum exhibitum, Deus credentibus & poenitentiam agentibus promittit remissionem peccatorum, & homines se obligant ad credendum Deo, & ad poenitentiam agendam. Huic testimonium dant omnes Prophetae, &c.
units.tr: Second, it is one only, because the principal conditions, which are called the substance of the covenant, are the same before Christ and after Christ. For in both covenants, before and after Christ was revealed, God promises forgiveness of sins to those who believe and repent, and men bind themselves to believe God and to repent. To him give all the prophets witness, &c.

units.la: Duo autem dicuntur foedera, vetus & novum, quoad circumstantias & conditiones minus principales, quae fuerunt modus administrationis subserviens principalibus, ut eas harum admiculo fideles consequi possent. Quae autem sint illae, ex sequentibus patebit.
units.tr: But there are said to be two covenants, the old and the new, as to circumstances and less principal conditions, which were the mode of administration serving the principal ones, so that the faithful might attain those principal things by means of these. What these are will become clear from what follows.

units.la: IV. Qua-
units.tr: IV. Qua-

units.la: IV. Quomodo conveniant & discrepent vetus & novum foedus.
units.tr: IV. How the Old and New Covenants agree and differ.

units.la: Cùm foedus sit vnum, & tamen scriptura loquatur de eo, vt de duobus: in quibus igitur conveniant, & in quibus differant vetus & novum foedus, consideranda est.
units.tr: Since the covenant is one, and yet Scripture speaks of it as two, we must consider in what respects the Old and New Covenants agree and in what respects they differ.

units.la: Conveniunt 1. in autore, qui est Deus, & in mediatore, qui est Christus, in utroque idem. At Moses fuit mediator foederis. Resp. Typicus, adjunctus significato, qui etiam tunc erat, nunc autem est solus sine typico. Nam manifestatus est in carne; nec typis amplius est tectus.
units.tr: They agree (1) in the author, who is God, and in the mediator, who is Christ, the same in both. But Moses was the mediator of the covenant. Answer: he was a typical mediator, joined to what was signified, who was indeed then present, but now is the sole mediator without the type. For he has been manifested in the flesh, and is no longer hidden under types.

units.la: 2. In promissione gratia de remissione peccatorum, & vita aeterna gratis danda credentibus, per & propter Christum. Quae promissio veteri populo nobiscum communis fuit: etsi jam clarior fit & saepius repetita. Promisit enim Deus eandem gratiam omnibus credentibus in Mediatorem. In semine tuo benedicentur omnes gentes terrae: Semen mulieris conteret caput serpentis. Ergo Deus tuus & feminis tui. Et: Qui credit in Filium, habet vitam aeternam. Per gratiam Domini Iesu Christi credimus nos servari, quemadmodum & illi. Loquuntur autem non in specie de circumstantiis gratiae, sed in genere, de promissione gratiae.
units.tr: (2) In the promise of grace: the forgiveness of sins and eternal life, given freely to believers, through and on account of Christ. This promise was common to the ancient people together with us, although it is now clearer and repeated more often. For God promised the same grace to all who believe in the Mediator: In your seed shall all the nations of the earth be blessed; the seed of the woman shall bruise the head of the serpent. Therefore God is your God and of your descendants. And: Whoever believes in the Son has eternal life. We believe that we are saved by the grace of the Lord Jesus Christ, just as they were. But these passages speak not of the particular circumstances of grace, but in general, of the promise of grace.

units.la: 3. In conditione respectu nostri. In utroque enim requirit Deus ab hominibus fidem & obedientiam. Ambula coram me, & esto perfectus. Et: Resipiscite & credite Evangelio. Convenit igitur foedus novum cum vetere, quoad principales conditiones; tam ex parte Dei, quam ex parte nostra.
units.tr: (3) In the condition on our part. For in both God requires faith and obedience from men: Walk before me, and be perfect. And: Repent and believe the Gospel. The New Covenant therefore agrees with the Old in its principal conditions, both on God's side and on ours.

units.la: Differunt autem duo foedera. 1. Promissionibus corporalibus. Vetus enim habet promissiones speciales de certis quibusdam beneficiis corporalibus: de terra Chanaan ecclesiae danda, de fortuna cultus ceremonialis & politiae Mosaicae in illa terra conservanda usque ad tempus Messiae: de Messia nascituro ex illo populo, &c. Novum vero eiusmodi promissiones corporales speciales non habet, sed tantum in genere, quod Deus Ecclesiam, & aliqua eius hospitia sit servaturus usque ad finem, &c.
units.tr: The two covenants differ, however: (1) in their bodily promises. The Old has special promises of certain bodily benefits: of the land of Canaan to be given to the Church; of the preservation in that land of the ceremonial worship and the Mosaic polity until the time of the Messiah; of the Messiah to be born from that people, and so on. The New has no such special bodily promises, but only in general that God will preserve the Church, and some of its dwelling-places, until the end, and so on.

units.la: 2. Circumstantia promissionis gratiae. In veteri recipiebantur in gratiam credentes propter Messiam exhibendum, & sacrificium eius futurum: in novo propter Messiam exhibitum, & sacrificium eius jam praestitum.
units.tr: (2) In the circumstances of the promise of grace. Under the Old, believers were received into favour on account of the Messiah who was to be exhibited, and his sacrifice which was to come; under the New, on account of the Messiah already exhibited, and his sacrifice already made.

units.la: 3. Ritibus seu signis promissioni gratiae additis. In veteri erant sacramenta alia, eaqi varia & laboriosa, ut circumcisio, pascha, oblationes, sacrificia. In novo item sunt alia, eaque pauca & simplicia, ut baptismus & coena Domini.
units.tr: (3) In the rites or signs added to the promise of grace. Under the Old there were other sacraments, various and laborious, such as circumcision, the Passover, oblations and sacrifices. Under the New there are also others, but few and simple, such as baptism and the Lord's Supper.

units.la: 4. Claritate. Vetus habebat typos & umbras bonorum futurorum: omnia erant typica, ut sacerdotes, sacrificia, &c. Ideo omnia etiam obscuriora. In nouo habetur typorum implo-tio, eoque omnia sunt clariora, tam in sacramentis, quàm in doctri na.
units.tr: (4) In clarity. The Old had types and shadows of the good things to come: everything was typical, such as the priests, the sacrifices, and so on. Therefore everything was also more obscure. In the New there is no multiplicity of types, and so everything is clearer, both in the sacraments and in the doctrine.

units.la: 5. Donis. Olim angustior & parcior erat: nunc largior & vbe-rior est donorum Spiritus sancti effusio. Feriam fœdus nouum. Si ministerium condemnationis fuit gloriosum, &c. Effundam de Spiritu meo super omnem carnem, &c.
units.tr: (5) In gifts. Formerly the outpouring of the gifts of the Holy Spirit was narrower and more sparing; now it is more abundant and copious. I will make a new covenant. If the ministry of condemnation was glorious, etc. I will pour out my Spirit upon all flesh, etc.

units.la: 6. Duratione. Vetus erat temporarium vsque ad Messiam: nouum est æternum. Sempiternum fœdus feriam cum illis.
units.tr: (6) In duration. The Old was temporary until the Messiah; the New is eternal. I will make with them an everlasting covenant.

units.la: 7. Obligatione. Vetus populum obligabat ad totam legem mo-ralem, ceremonialem & forensem. Nouum nos obligat tantum ad legem moralem, & ad vsum sacramentorum Christi.
units.tr: (7) In obligation. The Old bound the people to the whole of the moral, ceremonial and judicial law. The New binds us only to the moral law and to the use of Christ's sacraments.

units.la: 8. Amplitudine. In veteri, Ecclesia erat inclusa in gente Judai-ca, ad quam alios accedere oportebat, qui seruari vellent. In no-uo ecclesia est sparsa per omnes gentes, & ad eam accessus patet omnibus credentibus, cuiuscunque sint nationis, conditionis, aut linguae.
units.tr: (8) In extent. Under the Old, the Church was enclosed within the Jewish nation, and others had to be admitted to it if they wished to be saved. Under the New, the Church is scattered among all nations, and access to it lies open to all believers, of whatever nation, condition or language.

units.la: Obseruatio. Vetus testamentum seu fœdus sæpe in scriptura synecdochicè sumitur pro lege, respectu eius partis, quæ præci-puè in eo tractatur. Nam in veteri fœdere Lex magis vsurpatur, & multæ erant eius partes: Euangelium verò erat obscurius. Contra nouum testamentum seu fœdus fere sumitur pro euan-gelio: quia in nouo magna pars legis est abrogata, & euangelium clarius patefactum.
units.tr: Observation. The phrase "Old Testament" or "Old Covenant" is often used in Scripture, by synecdoche, for the law, with respect to the part that is chiefly treated in it. For in the Old Covenant the Law is more prominent, and its parts were many, while the Gospel was more obscure. On the other hand, "New Testament" or "New Covenant" is used almost always for the Gospel, because in the New a great part of the law has been abrogated and the Gospel has been more clearly revealed.

units.la: QVÆSTIO XIX.
units.tr: QUESTION XIX.

units.la: Vnde id scis? RESPONSIO.
units.tr: How do you know this? ANSWER.

units.la: Ex Euangelio: quod Deus primum in paradiso patefecit, ac deinceps per patriarchas & prophetas profecit, ac deinceps per patriarchas & prophetas pro-pagauit: sacrificiis, reliquisque ceremoniis Legis adumbrauit: ad extremum verò per Filium suum vnige-nitum e compleuit.
units.tr: From the Gospel, which God first revealed in paradise, then advanced and spread through the patriarchs and prophets, foreshadowed by the sacrifices and the other ceremonies of the Law, and at last completed through his only-begotten Son.

units.la: EXPLICATIO.
units.tr: EXPLICATIO.

units.la: Hæc quæstio respondet tertiæ. Vnde agnoscis miseriam? Ex lege. Ita hic: Vnde agnoscis liberationem? Ex Euangelio. Cùm igitur de mediatore sit dictum: necessariò etiam dicendum est de doctrina, in qua nobis mediator ostenditur, describitur, & offertur. Ea doctrina est Euangelium. Deinde dicendum quoque de medio, quo mediatoris ac beneficiorum eius simus participes. Id medium est fides. 1. Quia mediator est subiectum euangelij. Docet enim, quis & qualis sit. 2. Quia eiusdem est author. Nam pars officij mediatoris est revelare euangelium; sicut dicitur: Vnigenitus ille Filius, qui est in sinu Patris, ipse revelavit nobis. 3. Quia Euangelium est pars fœderis: & nouum fœdus sæpè pro Euangelio sumitur.
units.tr: This question answers the third: "How do you recognize your misery? From the law." So here: "How do you recognize deliverance? From the Gospel." Since we have spoken of the Mediator, we must now necessarily speak of the doctrine in which the Mediator is shown to us, described, and offered. That doctrine is the Gospel. Next we must also speak of the means by which we become partakers of the Mediator and of his benefits. That means is faith. (1) Because the Mediator is the subject of the Gospel: for it teaches who and what he is. (2) Because he is also its author: for it is part of the office of the Mediator to reveal the Gospel, as it is said: "That only-begotten Son, who is in the bosom of the Father, he has revealed it to us." (3) Because the Gospel is a part of the covenant, and the new covenant is often taken for the Gospel.

units.la: DE EVANGELIO.
units.tr: ON THE GOSPEL.

units.la: Quæstiones præcipuæ sunt istæ. I. Quid sit. II. An noua doctrina. III. Quomodo differat à Lege. IV. Qui sint proprij effectus. V. Vnde constet eius certitudo.
units.tr: The principal questions are these. I. What the Gospel is. II. Whether it is a new teaching. III. How it differs from the Law. IV. What its proper effects are. V. How its certainty is known.

units.la: I. Quid sit Euangelium.
units.tr: I. What the Gospel is.

units.la: Ipsa vox Euangelium significat: 1. lætum nuncium: 2. sacrificium, quod offertur Deo pro læto nuncio: 3. præmium, quod datur læta nuncianti. Hic significat doctrinam seu nuncium lætum de Christo exhibito: vt; Euangelizo vobis gaudium magnum, quia vobis hodie natus est Christus.
units.tr: The word Gospel itself signifies: (1) a joyful message; (2) a sacrifice offered to God for a joyful message; (3) the reward given to the one who brings good news. Here it signifies the teaching, or joyful message, about Christ now made manifest, as in: "I bring you good news of great joy, for today Christ is born to you."

units.la: Differunt ἐπαγγελία & εὐαγγέλιον. ἐπαγγελία est promissio de Messia exhibendo: εὐαγγέλιον est nuncius de Messia exhibito. Quanquam discrimen hoc non est perpetuum; & potius est in vocibus, quàm in re ipsa. Notantur enim eadem beneficia Messiæ per vtrumque, vt patet ex dictis. Abraham vidit diem meum, & gauisus est. Nemo venit ad Patrem, nisi per me. Ego sum ostium, &c. Constituit eum caput super omnia, Iesus Christus heri & hodie, &c.
units.tr: Epangelia [ἐπαγγελία] and euangelion [εὐαγγέλιον] differ. Epangelia is the promise about the Messiah who is to be revealed; euangelion is the message about the Messiah already revealed. Yet this distinction is not constant, and it lies more in the words than in the thing itself, for the same benefits of the Messiah are signified by both, as is clear from what has been said: "Abraham saw my day, and was glad." "No one comes to the Father except through me." "I am the door," etc. "He gave him to be head over all things, Jesus Christ, the same yesterday and today," etc.

units.la: Est igitur Euangelium doctrina diuinitus per filium Dei mediatorem in paradiso statim post lapsum patefacta, & prolata è sinu æterni Patris: qua promittitur & annunciatur ex gratuita Dei misericordia omnibus credentibus in Filium Dei, & pœnitentiam agentibus liberatio à peccato, à morte, à maledictione, & ab ira Dei, hoc est, remissio peccatorum, salus & vita æterna, per & propter eundem Filium Dei mediatorem: & per quam Spiritus sanctus efficaciter operatur in cordibus fideliū, accendens fidem, pœnitentiam, & initium vitæ æternæ. Vel ex qq. catechet. 18. 19. & 20. hoc modo: Euangelium est doctrina, quam Deus primum in paradiso patefecit, & deinceps per Patriarchas & Prophetas propagauit; sacrificiis reliquisq; ceremoniis Legis adumbrauit: ad extremum vero per Filium suum vnigenitum compleuit: docens, quod Filius ille Dei Dominus noster Iesus Christus factus sit nobis sapientia, justitia, sanctificatio & redemtio, hoc est, perfectus mediator, satisfaciens pro peccatis generis humani, & justitiam ac vitam æternam restituens omnibus iis, qui vera fide ipsi inseruntur, eiusq; beneficia amplectuntur.
units.tr: The Gospel is therefore the doctrine, revealed by God through the Son of God as Mediator in Paradise immediately after the Fall, and brought forth from the bosom of the eternal Father. In it is promised and announced, from the free mercy of God, to all who believe in the Son of God and repent, deliverance from sin, from death, from the curse, and from the wrath of God; that is, forgiveness of sins, salvation and eternal life, through and for the sake of the same Son of God, the Mediator. By this the Holy Spirit works effectively in the hearts of the faithful, kindling faith, repentance, and the beginning of eternal life. Or, following the Catechism questions 18, 19 and 20, it may be put thus: the Gospel is the doctrine which God first revealed in Paradise, and afterwards propagated through the Patriarchs and Prophets, foreshadowed by the sacrifices and other ceremonies of the Law, and at last completed through his only-begotten Son; teaching that this Son of God, our Lord Jesus Christ, has been made to us wisdom, righteousness, sanctification and redemption; that is, the perfect Mediator, who satisfies for the sins of the human race and restores righteousness and eternal life to all those who are truly grafted into him by faith and embrace his benefits.

units.la: Hanc definitionem confirmant omnes Euangelij summæ, vt: Hæc est voluntas eius, qui misit me, vt qui videt Filium, & credit in eum, habeat vitam æternam: ego vero suscitabo eum in nouissimo die. Notum sit vobis, fratres, annunciari vobis remissionem peccatorum per iStium. Oportuit prædicari in eius nomine resipiscentiam ac remissionem peccatorum, apud omnes gentes. Lex per Mosen data est, gratia verò per Iesum Christum.
units.tr: All the chief summaries of the Gospel confirm this definition, for example: "This is the will of him who sent me, that everyone who sees the Son and believes in him may have eternal life; and I will raise him up at the last day." "Be it known to you, brethren, that through this man forgiveness of sins is announced to you." "Repentance and forgiveness of sins was to be preached in his name among all nations." "The Law was given through Moses, but grace came through Jesus Christ."

units.la: II. An Euangelium semper fuerit notum in Ecclesia, an verò sit doctrina noua.
units.tr: II. Whether the Gospel has always been known in the Church, or whether it is a new doctrine.

units.la: Euangelium alias significat doctrinam de promissione gratiæ & remissionis peccatorū gratis dandæ propter sacrificium Messiæ: alias doctrinam de Messia exhibito. Posteriore significatione Euangelium non semper fuit, sed cum nouo testamento cœpit: priore semper fuit in Ecclesia. Nam statim post lapsum hominis in paradiso est patefactum primis parentibus, ac deinde per Patriarchas ac Prophetas propagatum & declaratum, tandemq; à Christo ipso completum & illustratum.
units.tr: The Gospel sometimes signifies the doctrine of the promise of grace and of the forgiveness of sins, given freely on account of the sacrifice of the Messiah; at other times it signifies the doctrine of the Messiah already revealed. In the latter sense the Gospel did not always exist, but began with the New Testament. In the former sense it has always been in the Church. For immediately after the fall of man it was made known in Paradise to our first parents, then propagated and declared through the Patriarchs and Prophets, and at last completed and made clear by Christ himself.

units.la: Probatur. 1. Testimoniis Apostolorum. Vt Petri: Huic testimonium dant omnes Prophetæ, remissionem peccatorum accepturum per nomen eius quemuis, qui crediderit in eum. Item: De qua salute inquisierunt & seruati sunt Prophetæ. Et Pauli: Quod (Euangelium) ante promiserat per Prophetas in scripturis sanctis. Ipsius etiam Christi, dicentis: Si crederetis Mosi, crederetis mihi: de me enim ille scripsit.
units.tr: This is proved: (1) by the testimonies of the Apostles. Thus Peter: "To him all the Prophets bear witness, that everyone who believes in him will receive forgiveness of sins through his name." Likewise: "Concerning this salvation the Prophets inquired and searched." And Paul: "which he had promised beforehand through his Prophets in the holy Scriptures." Also Christ himself, saying: "If you believed Moses, you would believe me, for he wrote of me."

units.la: 2. Idem constat ex omnibus promissionibus & vaticiniis de Messia.
units.tr: (2) The same is established by all the promises and prophecies concerning the Messiah.

units.la: Hoc ideo diligenter notandum est: quia vult Deus nos scire, inde ab initio mundi vsque ad finem tantum vnam fuisse & esse doctrinam & viam salutis per Christum, sicut dicitur: Iesus Christus heri & hodie idem est, & in secula. Ego sum via, veritas & vita: vita: nemo venit ad Patrem, nisi per me. Moses de me scripsit. Quomodo, inquis, Moses scripsit de Christo? 1. Quia recitat promissiones de Messia: In semine tuo benedicentur omnes gentes terra. Suscitabit Deus Prophetam, &c. Orietur stella ex Iacob. Non auferetur sceptrum de Iuda, donec veniat Siloh. 2. Quia eadem restringit ad certam familiam, ex qua Messias erat nasciturus, & cui subinde magis ac magis renouata est, & declarata promissio de Messia. 3. Totum sacerdotium Leviticum, & totus cultus ceremonialis, sacrificia, oblationes, altare, templum, & quæ Moses descripsit, Christum spectabant: etiam regnum, & Reges erant typus Christi, & regni eius. Valde igitur multa scripsit Moses de Christo.
units.tr: This must be carefully noted, because God wills us to know that from the beginning of the world to its end there has been and is only one doctrine and one way of salvation through Christ, as it is said: "Jesus Christ is the same yesterday and today and forever." "I am the way, the truth and the life; no one comes to the Father except through me." Moses wrote of me. How, you may ask, did Moses write of Christ? (1) Because he recites the promises concerning the Messiah: "In your seed all the nations of the earth shall be blessed." "God will raise up a Prophet," etc. "A star shall rise out of Jacob." "The sceptre shall not depart from Judah, until Shiloh comes." (2) Because he restricts these promises to a certain family from which the Messiah was to be born, and to which the promise concerning the Messiah was afterwards renewed and declared more and more. (3) The whole Levitical priesthood, the whole ceremonial worship, the sacrifices, offerings, altar, temple, and all that Moses described, looked to Christ; even the kingdom and the kings were types of Christ and of his kingdom. Moses therefore wrote very much about Christ.

units.la: Obiect. 1. Paulus dicit, Euangelium fuisse promissum per Prophetas: & Petrus: Prophetas venturam in nos gratiam prædicasse. Non igitur Euangelium semper fuit. Resp. Conceditur de Euangelio secunda significatione accepto, hoc est, de doctrina impletæ promissionis gratiæ per Christum in carne exhibitum, & de doctrinæ huius claritate. Olim enim euangelium non erat: sed promittebatur per Prophetas: 1. quoad impletionem eorum, quæ in veteri testamento de Messia fuerant prædicta: 2. quoad clariorem cognitionem promissionis gratiæ: 3. quoad uberiorem donorum Spiritus sancti effusionem: hoc est, Euangelium olim non erat concio de Christo exhibito, mortuo, resuscitato, evecto ad dextram Patris, qualis nunc est: sed erat concio de Christo exhibendo, & hæc omnia præstituro. Nihilominus erat Euangelium, hoc est, lætus nuncius de beneficiis Messiæ venturi, sufficiens patribus ad salutem; sicut dicitur: Abraham vidit diem meum, & gavisus est. Huic testimonium dant omnes Prophetæ, &c. Finis Legis est Christus.
units.tr: Objection 1. Paul says that the Gospel was promised through the Prophets, and Peter: "The Prophets prophesied of the grace that would come to us." Therefore the Gospel has not always existed. Answer. This is granted of the Gospel taken in the second sense, that is, of the doctrine of the promise of grace fulfilled through Christ, manifested in the flesh, and of the clarity of this doctrine. For formerly the Gospel did not exist in the sense of a message: it was promised through the Prophets (1) as regards the fulfilment of those things which had been foretold concerning the Messiah in the Old Testament; (2) as regards a clearer knowledge of the promise of grace; (3) as regards a more abundant outpouring of the gifts of the Holy Spirit. That is, the Gospel formerly was not the preaching of Christ already given, dead, raised, and exalted to the right hand of the Father, as it now is; it was the preaching of Christ who was yet to be given and who would accomplish all these things. Nevertheless it was the Gospel, that is, a joyful message of the benefits of the coming Messiah, sufficient for the fathers to salvation; as it is said: "Abraham saw my day, and was glad." "To him all the Prophets bear witness," etc. "The end of the Law is Christ."

units.la: Obiect. 2. Idem Paulus ait, Euangelium à temporibus æternis fuisse tacitum, & aliis seculis non innotuisse filiis hominum. Resp. Est fallacia divisionis. Addit enim Apostolus, ut nunc, quod non est omittendum: quia indicat, etiam olim innotuisse, etsi minus clarè, & paucioribus, quàm nunc. Est etiam fallacia à dicto secundum quid. Non enim sequitur, simpliciter non innotuisse, vel tectum fuisse, eò quod nunc clarius & pluribus innotuit. Nam & patribus fuit notum, licet non tam notum, quàm nobis. Atqui hoc discrimen illud ἀποκέκρυμμένον & ἀποκάλυψιν prius expositum proprie pertinet.
units.tr: Objection 2. The same Paul says that the Gospel had been kept silent from eternal times and had not been made known to the sons of men in other ages. Answer. This is a fallacy of division. For the Apostle adds "as now," which must not be omitted, since it shows that it was made known in former times too, though less clearly and to fewer people than now. There is also a fallacy of the dictum spoken with qualification (secundum quid). For it does not follow that it was simply not known, or was hidden, merely because it is now more clearly and more widely known. For it was known to the fathers too, although not so well known as to us. But this distinction between apokekrymmenon [ἀποκέκρυμμένον], the hidden, and apokalypsin [ἀποκάλυψιν], the revelation, explained earlier, properly applies here.

units.la: Obiectio 3. Lex per Mosen data est, gratia & veritas per Iesum Christum. Ergo non semper fuit Euangelium. Resp. Gratia & veritas per Christum exstitit, nempe quoad impletionem typorum, & plenam exhibitionem, atque uberiorem applicationem eorum, corum, quæ in veteri testamento olim promissa erant. Sed hinc non sequitur, veteres prorsus fuisse destitutos gratia. Nam & ipsis gratia est facta per & propter Christum, manifestandum olim in carne, etsi languidius, quàm nobis. Quicquid enim gratiæ & veræ cognitionis Dei vnquam in hominibus fuit, id per Christum eis contigit, sicut dicitur: Vnigenitus ille Filius, qui est in sinu Patris, ipse reuelauit nobis. Nemo venit ad Patrem, nisi per me. Sine me nihil poteritis facere.
units.tr: Objection 3. "The Law was given through Moses, but grace and truth through Jesus Christ." Therefore the Gospel has not always existed. Answer. Grace and truth came through Christ, namely as regards the fulfilment of the types, the full manifestation, and the more abundant application of those things which had formerly been promised in the Old Testament. But it does not follow from this that the ancients were wholly destitute of grace. For grace was also given to them through and for the sake of Christ, who was to be manifested in the flesh in time, though more faintly than to us. For whatever grace and true knowledge of God has ever existed among men, it has come to them through Christ, as it is said: "The only-begotten Son, who is in the bosom of the Father, has himself revealed him to us." "No one comes to the Father except through me." "Without me you can do nothing."

units.la: Inst. At dicit: Per Mosen Lex: ergo non Euangelium. Resp. Per Mosen Lex, quia principale officium Mosis fuit promulgare Legem. Interim & Euangelium docuit: quia de Christo scripsit & docuit, licet obscurius, vt modò dictum est. Christi verò præcipuum munus erat, promulgare Euangelium, licet interim & Legem docerer, sed non principaliter, vt Moses. Moralem enim legem purgauit à corruptelis, ceremonias impleuit, & vnà cum forensi lege abrogauit.
units.tr: Inst. But he says: "The Law came through Moses"; therefore it is not the Gospel. Resp. The Law came through Moses because the principal office of Moses was to promulgate the Law. Yet he also taught the Gospel, since he wrote and taught about Christ, though more obscurely, as has just been said. But the chief office of Christ was to promulgate the Gospel, although he also taught the Law at times, though not principally, as Moses did. For he purified the moral law from its corruptions, fulfilled the ceremonies, and abrogated them together with the forensic law.

units.la: III. Quid Euangelium à Lege differat.
units.tr: III. How the Gospel differs from the Law.

units.la: Euangelium & Lex conueniunt eo, quod vtraque doctrina est à Deo, & quod in vtraque de natura, voluntate & operibus Dei agitur.
units.tr: The Gospel and the Law agree in that both teachings are from God, and that both deal with the nature, will and works of God.

units.la: Sed plurimum etiam inter se differunt.
units.tr: But they also differ greatly from one another.

units.la: 1. Patefactionibus, seu modo patefactionum. Lex impressa est mentibus hominum in creatione, eoque natura omnibus est nota, etsi nulla accedat patefactio alia: Gentes opus legis scriptum habent in cordibus. Euangelium non est natura notum, sed coelitus patefactum est soli Ecclesiæ per Christum Mediatorem. Nam illam legis mitigationem de satisfactione pro peccatis nostris per alium, de qua supra dictum est, nulla creatura videre vel sperare potuisset, si Filius Dei non reuelasset. Nemo nouit Patrem, nisi Filius, & cui Filius voluerit reuelare. Caro & sanguis non reuelauit tibi. Filius, qui est in sinu Patris, exposuit nobis.
units.tr: 1. By the manner of revelation. The Law has been impressed on the minds of men at creation, and so it is known to all by nature, even if no other revelation is added: The Gentiles have the work of the law written in their hearts. The Gospel is not known by nature, but has been revealed from heaven to the Church alone, through Christ the Mediator. For that mitigation of the law, the satisfaction for our sins by another, of which we have spoken above, no creature could have seen or hoped for, unless the Son of God had revealed it. No one knows the Father except the Son, and anyone to whom the Son wills to reveal him. Flesh and blood has not revealed this to you. The Son, who is in the bosom of the Father, has declared him to us.

units.la: 2. Ipso doctrinæ genere seu subiecto. Lex docet, quales nos esse, & quid præstare Deo debeamus; sed non confert vires id præstandi, nec ostendit rationem, qua tales euadere possimus. Euangelium verò docet, quomodo tales fiamus, quales nos esse lex præcipit. Offert enim promissionem gratiæ de Christi iustitia nobis per fidem imputata, non secus ac si nostra propria esset, docens, nos hac imputatione iustitiæ Christi esse iustos coram Deo. Lex dicit: Redde quod debes. Hoc fac, & vives. Euangelium: Tantum modo crede, &c. Crede in Dominum Iesum Christum, & seruaberis tu, ac domus tua.
units.tr: 2. By the very kind or subject of the teaching. The Law teaches what kind of people we are, and what we ought to render to God; but it does not supply the strength to do so, nor does it show the way by which we might become such people. The Gospel, however, teaches how we become such as the law commands us to be. For it offers the promise of grace, that the righteousness of Christ is imputed to us through faith, just as if it were our own, teaching that by this imputation of Christ's righteousness we are righteous before God. The Law says: Pay what you owe. Do this, and you will live. The Gospel says: Only believe, etc. Believe in the Lord Jesus Christ, and you and your household will be saved.

units.la: 3. Pro-
units.tr: 3. Pro-

units.la: Quæst. XIX.
units.tr: Question XIX.

units.la: 3. Promissionibus. Lex promittit vitam in se justis, seu cum conditione propriæ justitiæ & perfectæ obedientiæ à nobis præstitæ. Qui fecerit ea, viuet in eis. Si vis ingredi in vitam, serua mandata. Euangelium eandem promisit justificatis fide in Christum, seu cum conditione justitiæ alienæ, nempe Christi, per fidem nobis applicatæ.
units.tr: 3. By the promises. The Law promises life to those who are just in themselves, that is, on condition of one's own righteousness and perfect obedience rendered by us. He who does these things shall live by them. If you wish to enter into life, keep the commandments. The Gospel promises the same to those justified by faith in Christ, that is, on condition of the alien righteousness, namely that of Christ, applied to us through faith.

units.la: Nec propterea Euangelium & Lex inter se pugnant. Etsi enim lex vult mandata abs te præstari, si velis vitam ingredi: non tamen excludit à vita, si alius ea pro te præstet. Ponit quidem vnum satisfaciendi modum, nempe, per te: sed non excludit alterum, vt supra est dictum.
units.tr: Nor for this reason do the Gospel and the Law fight against each other. For although the law wills that the commandments be performed by you, if you wish to enter life, yet it does not exclude you from life if another performs them on your behalf. It indeed sets down one way of satisfying, namely through yourself, but it does not exclude the other, as was said above.

units.la: 4. Effectus. Lex sine Euangelio est litera occidens, & ministerium mortis. Quoniam ex Lege est agnitio peccati: &, Lex iram operatur: &, litera occidit. Per literam vero intelligitur prædicatio externa, & nuda notitia faciendorum. Euangelium est ministerium vitæ & spiritus, hoc est, habet coniunctam efficaciam spiritus, & viuificat: quoniam per illud, quasi per organum, Spiritus sanctus fidem & vitam operatur in electis. Euangelium est potentia Dei ad salutem, &c.
units.tr: 4. Effects. The Law without the Gospel is the letter that kills, and the ministry of death. For through the Law comes the knowledge of sin; and the Law works wrath; and the letter kills. By the letter is meant the external preaching and the bare knowledge of what must be done. The Gospel is the ministry of life and of the Spirit, that is, it has the power of the Spirit joined to it, and it gives life, because through it, as through an instrument, the Holy Spirit works faith and life in the elect. The Gospel is the power of God unto salvation, etc.

units.la: Ex tertio discrimine sic argumentantur Flacciani: Euangelij nulla est præceptio, sed legis. Prædicatio pœnitentiæ est præceptio. Ergo prædicatio pœnitentiæ non pertinet ad Euangelium, sed ad legem. Resp. Maior vniuersaliter sumpta est falsa. Hæc enim præceptio est propria Euangelij, Resipiscite & credite Euangelio, jubens nos à peccatis resipiscere, Euangelio credere, beneficia Christi fide amplecti, & gratitudinis ergo nouam obedientiam, seu justitiam, quam Lex requirit, inchoare.
units.tr: The Flacians argue from this third difference as follows: there is no precept in the Gospel, only in the Law. The preaching of repentance is a precept. Therefore the preaching of repentance belongs not to the Gospel but to the Law. Resp. The major premise, taken universally, is false. For this precept is proper to the Gospel: Repent and believe the Gospel, commanding us to turn from sins, to believe the Gospel, to embrace the benefits of Christ by faith, and, out of gratitude, to begin a new obedience, or righteousness, which the Law requires.

units.la: Instant. Etiam Lex jubet nos credere Deo. Resp. Lex jubet nos credere Deo in genere, hoc est, fidem adhibere omnibus promissionibus, præceptis & minis diuinis, idque cum comminatione pœnæ, nisi faciamus. Euangelium vero in specie nos jubet fide amplecti promissionem gratiæ, & deinde hortatur, intus & foris, per Spiritum sanctum, & per verbum, vt viuamus Euangelio digne, sed hortatur tantum in genere, non explicans per species, hoc vel illud facies, sed relinquit hoc Legi: sicut contra non dicit in genere, crede omnibus Dei promissionibus, relinquens hoc Legi: sed in specie dicitur: crede huic promissioni: confuge ad Christum, & remittentur tibi peccata: quod Lex non facit.
units.tr: Objection again. The Law also commands us to believe God. Resp. The Law commands us to believe God in general, that is, to give credence to all God's promises, precepts and threats, and this with the penalty threatened unless we do so. But the Gospel commands us, in particular, to embrace by faith the promise of grace, and then exhorts us, inwardly and outwardly, through the Holy Spirit and through the Word, to live worthily of the Gospel. Yet it exhorts only in general, not explaining in particular, you shall do this or that; this it leaves to the Law. Likewise, on the other hand, it does not say in general, believe all God's promises, leaving this to the Law; but in particular it is said: believe this promise; flee to Christ, and your sins will be forgiven you, which the Law does not do.

units.la: IV. Qui sint proprij effectus Euangelij.
units.tr: IV. What are the proper effects of the Gospel.

units.la: Proprij effectus Euangelij sunt:
units.tr: The proper effects of the Gospel are:

units.la: 1. Fides: quia fides ex auditu, auditus per verbum Dei, Euangelium gelium est ministerium Spiritus. Et potentia DEI ad salutem omni credenti.
units.tr: 1. Faith: because "faith comes by hearing, and hearing by the word of God" (Rom. 10.17); the Gospel is the ministry of the Spirit, and "the power of God unto salvation to everyone who believes" (Rom. 1.16).

units.la: 2. Per fidem tota conuersio, justificatio, regeneratio & salus.
units.tr: 2. Through faith comes the whole conversion, justification, regeneration and salvation.

units.la: V. Vnde constet certitudo Euangelij.
units.tr: V. Whence the certainty of the Gospel is established.

units.la: Euangelij certitudo & veritas constat. 1. Ex testimonio Spiritus sancti. 2. Ex vaticiniis Prophetarum. 3. Ex impletione eorundem vaticiniorum præstita in nouo testamento. 4. Ex miraculis, quibus est confirmata Euangelij doctrina. 5. Ex ipsius Euangelicæ doctrinæ testimoniis: quia ipsa sola monstrat viam effugiendi peccatum & mortem, & solidam consolationem ostendit afflictis conscientiis.
units.tr: The certainty and truth of the Gospel is established: 1. From the testimony of the Holy Spirit. 2. From the prophecies of the Prophets. 3. From the fulfilment of those same prophecies accomplished in the New Testament. 4. From the miracles by which the doctrine of the Gospel was confirmed. 5. From the testimonies of the Evangelical doctrine itself: because it alone shows the way of escaping sin and death, and offers solid consolation to afflicted consciences.

units.la: QVÆSTIO XX.
units.tr: QUESTION XX.

units.la: Num igitur omnibus hominibus, qui in Adamo perierant, per Christum salus redditur?
units.tr: Is salvation therefore restored through Christ to all men who perished in Adam?

units.la: RESPONSIO.
units.tr: ANSWER.

units.la: Non omnibus, verum iis tantum, qui vera fide ipsi inseruntur, eiusq; beneficia omnia ample&tuntur.
units.tr: Not to all, but only to those who are truly engrafted into him by true faith and embrace all his benefits.

units.la: EXPLICATIO.
units.tr: EXPLANATION.

units.la: Post explicatam doctrinam de modo liberationis per Christum, recte etiam quæritur, qui & quomodo liberationis fiant participes, omnesne, an tantum aliqui. Si enim nulli fierent participes, frustra facta esset. Quæstio igitur 20. est ad doctrinam de fide, sine qua neque mediator, neque prædicatio Euangelij vllis proderet. Simul occurritur securitati carnis, & calumniæ, quod Christus sit minister peccati.
units.tr: After explaining the doctrine of the manner of deliverance through Christ, it is rightly asked also who become partakers of this deliverance, and how: all men, or only some? For if no one became a partaker, the thing would have been done in vain. Question 20 therefore belongs to the doctrine of faith, without which neither the mediator nor the preaching of the Gospel would be of any use. At the same time it meets the security of the flesh and the calumny that Christ is a minister of sin.

units.la: Resp. 1. Non omnibus, qui in Adamo perierunt, per Christum salus redditur: 2. sed tantum iis, qui vera fide Christo inseruntur, eiusque beneficia ample&tuntur.
units.tr: The answer: (1) Not all who perished in Adam are restored to salvation through Christ; (2) but only those who are truly engrafted into Christ by true faith and embrace his benefits.

units.la: Prior pars nimis patet per experientiam, & ex scriptura. Qui non credit in Filium, non habebit vitam, sed ira Dei manet super eo. Non omnis, qui dicit mihi, Domine, Domine, introibit in regnum cœlorum. Nisi quis renatus fuerit desuper, non potest introire in regnum Dei. Causa, cur non omnes seruentur per Christum, non est insufficientia meriti & gratiæ Christi, (est enim Christus expiatio pro peccatis totius mundi, quantum ad dignitatem & sufficien- tiam λυτρου attinet) sed hominum infidelitas, quâ beneficia Christi in Euangelio oblata repudiant, eoque non Christi, sed suâ culpâ pereunt.
units.tr: The first part is plain enough both from experience and from Scripture: "He who does not believe in the Son shall not have life, but the wrath of God abides on him"; "Not everyone who says to me, Lord, Lord, shall enter the kingdom of heaven"; "Unless someone is born again from above, he cannot enter the kingdom of God." The reason why not all are saved through Christ is not any insufficiency of the merit and grace of Christ (for Christ is the propitiation for the sins of the whole world, as far as the dignity and sufficiency of the ransom [λύτρου] are concerned), but the unbelief of men, by which they reject the benefits of Christ offered in the Gospel, and so perish not through Christ's fault but through their own.

units.la: Altera pars etiam patet ex scriptura. Quotquot receperunt eum, eis dedit potestatem fieri filios Dei. Notitia sui seruus meus justus justificabit multos. Ratio autem, cur soli credentes seruentur, est: quia hi soli beneficia Christi amplectuntur: & quia in his solis Deus assequitur suum finem, cuius gratia filium suum in mortem tradidit. Soli enim credentes agnoscunt misericordiam & gratiam Dei, & pro hac ei gratias agunt.
units.tr: The second part is also plain from Scripture: "As many as received him, to them he gave power to become the sons of God." "By his knowledge my righteous servant shall justify many." The reason why only believers are saved is that they alone embrace the benefits of Christ, and because in them alone God attains his end, for the sake of which he gave up his Son to death. For only believers acknowledge the mercy and grace of God, and give thanks to him for it.

units.la: Summa igitur est. Licet mediatoris Christi satisfactio pro peccatis sit perfectissima, non omnes tamen per eam liberantur, sed soli illi, qui Euangelio credunt, & meritum Christi fide vera sibi applicant.
units.tr: The sum, therefore, is this. Although the satisfaction of the mediator Christ is most perfect for sins, yet not all are delivered by it, but only those who believe the Gospel and apply the merit of Christ to themselves by true faith.

units.la: Obiect. 1. Gratia exsuperat peccatum. Ergo si peccato Adami omnes perierunt, multo magis gratia Christi omnes debent seruari. Resp. ad antecedens. Gratia exsuperat delictum, quoad satisfactionem, non quoad applicationem. Quod ergo non omnes per gratiam Christi seruantur, incredulis est asscribendum, qui gratiam oblatam respuunt.
units.tr: Objection 1. Grace exceeds sin. Therefore, if all have perished through the sin of Adam, much more ought all to be saved by the grace of Christ. Answer to the antecedent. Grace exceeds the offence as regards satisfaction, not as regards application. That not all are saved by the grace of Christ is therefore to be ascribed to unbelievers, who reject the grace offered.

units.la: Obiect. 2. Praestita satisfactione sufficienti pro offensis omnes debent recipi in gratiam. Christus praestitit satisfactionem sufficientem pro omnibus offensis. Ergo omnes debent recipi in gratiam: aut si hoc non fit, Deus est injurius hominibus, vel Christi merito derogatur. Respondeo ad maiorem, quae vera est, nisi addita sit satisfactionis conditio, ut ij tantum per eam seruentur, qui eam fide sibi applicant. Est autem conditio expressa addita: Sic DEVS dilexit mundum, ut Filium suum daret, ut OMNIS QVI CREDIT in eum, non pereat, sed habeat vitam aeternam.
units.tr: Objection 2. When a sufficient satisfaction has been made for offences, all ought to be received into favour. Christ has made a sufficient satisfaction for all offences. Therefore all ought to be received into favour; or, if this does not happen, God is unjust to men, or the merit of Christ is diminished. I answer to the major premise, which is true, unless a condition of the satisfaction has been added, namely that only those are saved by it who apply it to themselves by faith. And indeed the condition is expressly added: "God so loved the world that he gave his Son, that whoever believes in him should not perish, but have eternal life."

units.la: Obiect. 3. Adam omnes damnationi subjecit. Christus aliquos duntaxat seruat. Ergo maior est vis peccati Adami ad condemnandum, quàm satisfactionis Christi ad seruandum. Resp. Negatur consequentia, quia vis, excellentia, & efficacia satisfactionis Christi non aestimatur multitudine aut numero hominum, qui per eã seruantur, sed ipsius beneficij magnitudine. Atqui maius est opus, unum vel alterum hominem liberare à morte aeterna, quàm omnes homines aeternae mortis reos facere per peccatum. Deinde, quo minus ad omnes penetret vis efficaciae beneficij Christi, sicut vis peccati Adami ad omnes penetrauit: culpa est in ipsis hominibus, qui non aequè sibi applicant meritum Christi per fidem, atque sibi applicant peccatum Adami per natunaturam & imitationem.
