Habuerunt alij hoc nomen: quia fuerunt servatores typici. At (inquis) parentes Josuæ quando infanti hoc nomen indebant, ne suspicari quidem potuerunt liberationem futuram per ipsum. Resp. Sed Deus sciuit, & voluntatem parentum direxit.
units.tr: Objection. 1. Many others also have had the name Jesus, such as Joshua the leader, Jesus the high priest, etc. Therefore nothing can be concluded from this name. Answer. Others had this name because they were typical saviours. But (you will say) the parents of Joshua, when they gave this name to the infant, could not even suspect the future deliverance through him. Answer. But God knew it, and directed the wishes of the parents.

units.la: Magnum verò est discrimen inter alios, & hunc Iesum. 1. Alij nomen fuerunt sortiti voluntate hominum, hic ab Angelo. 2. Alij fuerunt typi: hic est significatus & verus servator. 3. Per alios Deus beneficia tantum corporalia suo populo præstabat, hic non tantum à corporis, sed ab animæ malis culpæ & pœnæ liberat. 4. Alij tantum erant instrumenta & ministri, per quos dabat Deus illa beneficia corporalia: hic est author non modo corporalium, sed & spiritualium beneficiorum.
units.tr: The difference between the others and this Jesus is indeed great. 1. The others obtained their name by the will of men, this one from an angel. 2. The others were types; this one is the signified and true Saviour. 3. Through the others God bestowed only bodily benefits on his people; this one frees not only from bodily evils but from the evils of the soul, guilt and punishment. 4. The others were merely instruments and ministers through whom God gave those bodily benefits; this one is the author not only of bodily but also of spiritual benefits.

units.la: Ergo Filius appellatur Jesus κατ' ἐξοχὴν, tanquam verus seruator.
units.tr: Therefore the Son is called Jesus par excellence [κατ' ἐξοχὴν], as the true Saviour.

units.la: 1. Quia seruat nos ab vtroque malo, culpæ & pœnæ. A malo culpæ, teste angelo: Ipse seruabit populum suum a peccatis ipsius. A malo pœnæ: quia sublato peccato tollitur & pœna peccati, quæ est effectus peccati; Sublata enim causa tollitur effectus. Populus autem, quem Iesus seruat, sunt omnes & soli electi seu credentes. Horum tantum est saluator: quia in his tantum assequitur suum finem. Constituit enim Ecclesiam in hac vita colligere & seruare, sed ea conditione, vt ea beneficium illud accipiat, & sit ipsi grata.
units.tr: 1. Because he saves us from both evils, that of guilt and that of punishment. From the evil of guilt, as the angel testifies: He will save his people from their sins. From the evil of punishment: because when sin is taken away, the punishment of sin, which is the effect of sin, is also taken away; for when the cause is removed the effect is removed. The "people" whom Jesus saves, however, are all and only the elect, or believers. He is the Saviour of these alone, because only in them does he attain his end. For he has determined to gather and preserve the Church in this life, but on this condition, that it receives that benefit and is pleasing to him.

units.la: 2. Quia solus seruat. Solus enim est noster mediator, ideo & solus noster Seruator. Hoc declarant testimonia scripturæ. Non est aliud nomen sub cœlo, quod datum sit inter homines, per quod oporteat nos seruari. Qui non credit in Filium, iam condemnatus est, quia non credit in nomen vnigeniti Filij Dei. Vitam æternam dedit nobis Deus, & hæc vita æterna in Filio eius est. Vnus Deus, vnus et iam mediator, Dei & hominum, homo Christus Iesus. Ego, ego sum, qui deleo iniquitates tuas propter me. Tantum in me est salus: præter me non est seruator.
units.tr: 2. Because he alone saves. For he alone is our Mediator, and therefore he alone is our Saviour. The testimonies of Scripture declare this: There is no other name under heaven given among men by which we must be saved. He who does not believe in the Son is already condemned, because he does not believe in the name of the only begotten Son of God. God has given us eternal life, and this life is in his Son. There is one God, and one mediator between God and men, the man Christ Jesus. I, I am he who blots out your iniquities for my own sake. In me alone is salvation; beside me there is no saviour.

units.la: Obiect. Etiam Pater & Spiritus sanctus nos seruant. Ergo non solus Filius. Resp. 1. In modo est discrimen. Pater seruat per Filium tanquam fons salutis: Spiritus sanctus seruat tanquam immediatus effector regenerationis: Filius seruat suo merito, tanquam solus mediator, soluens pro nobis λύτρον, dans Spiritum sanctum, regenerans & suscitans ad vitam æternam. Efficacia igitur est communis tribus personis: modus autem est Filio proprius. 2. Solus opponitur omnibus creaturis. Excludit igitur omnes creaturas, non Patrem aut Spiritum sanctum. Sicut in dicto: Nemo novit, quæ sunt Dei, nisi Spiritus Dei. Alioqui & hinc sequeretur, Patrem & Filium seipsos non nosse.
units.tr: Objection. The Father and the Holy Spirit also save us. Therefore the Son is not the only one. Answer 1. There is a difference in the manner. The Father saves through the Son as the fountain of salvation; the Holy Spirit saves as the immediate effector of regeneration; the Son saves by his merit, as the sole Mediator, paying a ransom [λύτρον] for us, giving the Holy Spirit, regenerating and raising us to eternal life. The efficacy, therefore, is common to the three persons; the manner, however, is proper to the Son. 2. "Alone" is set against all creatures. It therefore excludes all creatures, not the Father or the Holy Spirit; as in the saying: No one knows the things of God except the Spirit of God. Otherwise it would follow from this too that the Father and the Son do not know themselves.

units.la: 3. Seruator est duobus modis, merito & efficacia. Merito seu satisfactione seruat nos: quia suâ obedientiâ, passione, morte & intercessione meritus est nobis remissionem peccatorum, reconciliationem cum Deo, Spiritum sanctum, salutem & vitam æternam. Ipse est propitiatio pro peccatis nostris, nec pro nostris solum, sed etiam pro totius mundi peccatis, hoc est, pro peccatis quorumlibet hominum, cuiuscunque sint ætatis, sexus, ordinis ac loci, in ipsum credentium. Sanguis Iesu Christi Filij Dei purgat nos ab omni peccato. Quem proposuit Deus, vt esset placamentum per fidem in sanguine ipsius, ad declarandam iustitiam suam per remissionem peccapeccatorum praecedentium. Per vnius obedientiam justi constituentur multi. Iehova conjecit in eum iniquitates omnium nostrum. Efficacia etiam nos seruat: quia non solum merendo impetrat remissionem peccatorum, justitiam & vitam amissam, sed etiam totum redemptionis beneficium Spiritus sui virtute per fidem nobis confert & applicat. Nam quae meritus est morte sua, nequaquam sibi retinet, sed nobis confert. Salutem enim & vitam aeternam (quam habebat) non sibi, sed nobis peperit, utpote noster Mediator. Ergo reuelat nobis voluntatem Patris, instituit & conseruat ministerium, per hoc dat Spiritum sanctum, & convertit homines, colligit ecclesiam, largitur etiam bona ad hanc vitam necessaria, defendit contra hostes, ecclesiam denique suam in nouissimo die excitabit ad vitam, & liberabit ab omnibus malis, abiectis hostibus in poenas. Ista facere est solius DEI veri omnipotentis. Breviter: Efficacia sua per verbum & Spiritum regenerat nos in hac vita, & seruat renatos, ne rursus deficiamus, & tandem suscitabit ad vitam aeternam. De reuelatione & regeneratione loquuntur haec dicta: Nemo novit quis sit Filius, nisi Pater, & quis sit Pater, nisi Filius, & cuicunque voluerit Filius detegere. Vnigenitus ille Filius, qui est in sinu Patris, ipse nobis exposuit. Ipse est, qui baptizat Spiritu sancto & igne. Ego mittam vobis Spiritum sanctum a Patre. Ascendens in altum, captiuam duxit captiuitatem, & dedit dona hominibus, alios pastores, alios doctores, &c. Apparuit Filius Dei, ut destruat opera diaboli. De conseruatione loquuntur haec testimonia: Ne conturbetur cor vestrum, creditis in Deum, & in me credite, &c. Vobiscum sum usque ad consummationem seculi. Non relinquam vos orphanos. Ego & Pater veniemus, & mansionem apud eum faciemus. De suscitatione: Ego suscitabo eum in nouissimo die. Oues meas nemo rapiet ex manu mea. Ego do eis vitam aeternam, nec peribunt in aeternum. Cum omnia sibi subiecerit, sistet ecclesiam gloriosam in conspectu Dei, quam colligit ab initio mundi ad finem usque venit. Ex his intelligitur, donationem Spiritus sancti, etiam esse partem nostrae salutis, & per mediatorem fieri debuisse. Nam Spiritus sanctus renouat corda, expurgato peccato, quo abolitus mors definit, ad quam destruendam Christus in mundum venit.
units.tr: 3. A saviour is so in two ways, by merit and by efficacy. He saves us by merit or satisfaction, because by his obedience, passion, death and intercession he has merited for us the remission of sins, reconciliation with God, the Holy Spirit, salvation and eternal life. He himself is the propitiation for our sins, and not for ours only, but also for the sins of the whole world, that is, for the sins of whatever men, of whatever age, sex, rank and place, who believe in him. The blood of Jesus Christ the Son of God cleanses us from all sin. Whom God has set forth to be a propitiation through faith in his blood, to declare his righteousness through the remission of sins previously committed. By the obedience of one shall many be made righteous. Jehovah has laid on him the iniquities of us all. He also saves us by efficacy, because he not only obtains by merit the remission of sins, righteousness and the life that was lost, but also by the power of his Spirit confers and applies to us through faith the whole benefit of redemption. For what he has merited by his death he by no means keeps for himself, but bestows on us. For he gained salvation and eternal life (which he possessed) not for himself, but for us, as our Mediator. Therefore he reveals to us the will of the Father, institutes and preserves the ministry, through this gives the Holy Spirit and converts men, gathers the Church, also bestows the goods necessary for this life, defends against enemies, and finally on the last day will raise his Church to life and free it from all evils, casting its enemies into punishment. To do these things belongs to the true omnipotent God alone. In short: by his efficacy, through the Word and the Spirit, he regenerates us in this life, preserves the regenerate lest they fall away again, and at last will raise them to eternal life. The following sayings speak of revelation and regeneration: No one knows who the Son is except the Father, and who the Father is except the Son, and anyone to whom the Son wills to reveal him. That only begotten Son, who is in the bosom of the Father, has himself made him known to us. He is the one who baptizes with the Holy Spirit and with fire. I will send you the Holy Spirit from the Father. Ascending on high, he led captivity captive, and gave gifts to men, some apostles, some teachers, etc. The Son of God appeared that he might destroy the works of the devil. The following testimonies speak of preservation: Let not your heart be troubled; you believe in God, believe also in me, etc. I am with you always, to the end of the age. I will not leave you orphans. I and the Father will come and make our home with him. Concerning raising up: I will raise him up on the last day. No one shall snatch my sheep out of my hand. I give them eternal life, and they shall never perish. When he has subjected all things to himself, he will present the glorious Church before the sight of God, which he has gathered from the beginning of the world to the end. From these things it is understood that the gift of the Holy Spirit is also part of our salvation, and that it had to be brought about through the Mediator. For the Holy Spirit renews hearts, sin having been purged away, by which death, which Christ came into the world to destroy, has been abolished.

units.la: 4. Plenè & perfectissimè seruat, hic incipiendo, demum verò perficiendo in nobis salutem: tum quia meritum eius est perfectissimum, idque duas ob causas: ut supra est explicatum. 1. Quia Deus est. Deus enim suo sanguine redemit Ecclesiam: unde & satisfactio ipsius antepeonitur omnium angelorum poenis & satisfactionibus. 2. Propter gravitatem supplicii quod sustinuit pronobis: tum quia salutem nobis perfectissimè confert. In ipso estis consummati, id est, habetis omnia, quae ad beatitudinem aeter-nam petinent, per & propter hunc Jesum estis filij Dei perfecti & beati. Quoniam in eo placuit Patri omnem plenitudinem inhabita- re. Sanguis Iesu Christi Filij Dei purgat nos ab omni peccato. Nulla est condemnatio iis, qui sunt in Christo Iesu. At iste propterea quod in aeter- num manet, perpetuum habet sacerdotium, unde & seruare prorsus potest eos, qui per ipsum accedunt ad Deum.
units.tr: He saves fully and most perfectly, beginning this work here and at last bringing salvation to completion in us. This is so, first, because his merit is most perfect, and it is so for two reasons, as explained above: (1) because he is God: "For God redeemed the Church with his own blood" [Acts 20:28]. For this reason his satisfaction is placed above the punishments and satisfactions of all the angels. (2) Because of the gravity of the punishment that he endured for us. Second, he confers salvation on us most perfectly: "In him you are complete" [Col. 2:10], that is, you have all things that pertain to eternal blessedness. Through and because of this Jesus you are perfect and blessed sons of God. "For in him it pleased the Father that all fullness should dwell" [Col. 1:19]. "The blood of Jesus Christ, the Son of God, cleanses us from all sin" [1 John 1:7]. "There is no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus" [Rom. 8:1]. But he, because he remains forever, has an everlasting priesthood, and therefore he is wholly able to save those who come to God through him [Heb. 7:24–25].

units.la: Hactenus dicta de nomine Jesu breuiter ad has quaestiones reuocantur. 1. Quis seruet? Filius Dei est noster Iesus, hoc est, salvator. 2. Quos? Populum suum, hoc est, omnes & solos electos sibi à Patre datos. 3. A quibus malis? Ab omnibus peccatis & peccatorum poenis. 3. Quomodo? Duobus modis, merito & efficacia, & utroque modo perfectissimè.
units.tr: These things said about the name of Jesus are briefly brought back to these questions. (1) Who saves? Our Jesus, the Son of God, that is, the Saviour. (2) Whom? His people, that is, all and only the elect given to him by the Father. (3) From what evils? From all sins and the punishments of sins. (4) How? In two ways, by merit and by efficacy, and in both ways most perfectly.

units.la: Jam ergo quid est Credo in Iesum? 1. Credo esse aliquem generis humani seruatorem. 2. Credo hanc personam Iesum natum ex Maria virgine, esse istum seruatorem, de quo Pater clamat de coelo: Hic est Filius meus dilectus, in quo acquiesco, hunc audite. Hunc Deus vult coli & celebrari. Qui non honorat Filium, non honorat Patrem, qui misit eum. 3. Credo hunc Iesum nos liberare à malis culpae & poenae, merito & efficacia: in hac vita inchoatione, in futura autem consummatione. 4. Credo hunc non aliorum solum electorum, sed meum quoque unicum & perfectum seruatorem esse, hic incipiendo, tandem verò perficiendo in me salutem.
units.tr: What, then, is "I believe in Jesus"? (1) I believe that he is someone who is the Saviour of the human race. (2) I believe that this person, Jesus, born of the Virgin Mary, is that Saviour of whom the Father cries from heaven: "This is my beloved Son, in whom I delight; hear him" [Matt. 3:17]. God wills that he be worshipped and honoured. "He who does not honour the Son does not honour the Father who sent him" [John 5:23]. (3) I believe that this Jesus frees us from the evils of guilt and punishment, by merit and by efficacy: a beginning of this in the present life, and its completion in the life to come. (4) I believe that he is the one and perfect Saviour not only of other elect, but also of me, beginning here and at last bringing salvation to completion in me.

units.la: QVAESTIO XXX. Creduntne igitur illi in unicum seruatorem Iesum, qui à sanctis, aut à se, aut aliunde felicitatem aut salutem quaerunt? RESPONSIO.
units.tr: QUESTION XXX. Do those believe in Jesus as the one Saviour who seek happiness or salvation from the saints, or from themselves, or from elsewhere? ANSWER.

units.la: Non. Etsi enim verbo quidem eo seruatore gloriantur: re ipsa tamen abnegant unicum seruatorem Iesum a. Necesse est enim, aut Iesum non esse perfectum seruatorem: aut qui eum seruatorem vera fide amplectuntur, eos omnia in ipso possidere, quae ad salutem requiruntur b.
units.tr: No. For although they indeed boast in the word "Saviour", in fact they deny Jesus to be the only Saviour [a]. For it must be either that Jesus is not the perfect Saviour, or that those who embrace him as Saviour with true faith possess in him all the things required for salvation [b].

units.la: EXPLICATIO.
units.tr: EXPLANATION.

units.la: Quæstio hæc posita est propter eos, qui quidem de nomine Jesu gloriantur, interim vero salutem, vel totam, vel ex parte quærunt alibi extra hunc Jesum in meritis sanctorum, indulgentiis Papæ, suis satisfactionibus, operibus, jejuniis, precibus, eleemosynis, &c. vt faciunt Pontificij, Jesuitæ, & similes hypocritæ. Quæritur ergo, an hi in vnicum seruatorem Jesum credant, necne? Resp. Non credunt, sed re ipsa eum abnegant, quicquid verbis glorientur. Summa responsionis hoc syllogismo explicatur, ducto à descriptione vnici & perfecti Seruatoris: Qui est perfectus & vnicus seruator, is neque cum aliis salutem confert, neque tantum eius partem. At Jesus est seruator solus & perfectus, vt probatum est quæstione præcedente. Ergo neque cum aliis salutem confert, neque tantum partem eius, sed totam solus perfectissimè. Et per consequens, qui salutem suam totam vel ex parte alibi quærunt, re ipsa negant eum solum esse perfectum seruatorem. Vel sic: Quærentes salutem alibi quam in Christo, apud sanctos, aut apud se, &c. non credunt in vnicum seruatorem Jesum. Pontificij & Jesuitæ, statuentes opera meritoria, illud faciunt. Ergo non credunt in vnicum seruatorem Jesum. Minor est in confesso: maior patet ex descriptione precedente perfecti seruatoris.
units.tr: This question is raised on account of those who indeed boast in the name of Jesus, yet meanwhile seek salvation, either wholly or in part, elsewhere than in this Jesus: in the merits of the saints, in the indulgences of the Pope, in their own satisfactions, works, fastings, prayers, almsgiving, and so on, as the Papists, the Jesuits, and similar hypocrites do. The question, then, is whether these men believe in Jesus as the one Saviour or not. Answer: they do not believe, but in fact deny him, whatever they may boast with their words. The substance of the answer is set out in this syllogism, drawn from the description of the one and perfect Saviour. He who is the perfect and only Saviour neither shares salvation with others nor provides only a part of it. But Jesus is the sole and perfect Saviour, as was proved in the preceding question. Therefore he neither shares salvation with others nor provides only a part of it, but alone and most perfectly provides the whole. And consequently, those who seek their salvation elsewhere, wholly or in part, in fact deny that he alone is the perfect Saviour. Or thus: those who seek salvation elsewhere than in Christ, among the saints, or in themselves, and so on, do not believe in Jesus as the one Saviour. The Papists and the Jesuits, holding that meritorious works are necessary, do this. Therefore they do not believe in Jesus as the one Saviour. The minor premise is admitted by all; the major is evident from the preceding description of the perfect Saviour.

units.la: Obiect. Deus vult, vt alij pro aliis orent. Ergo tribuere sanctis partem intercessionis non pugnat cum officio & gloria vnici seruatoris Jesu. Resp. Magnum est discrimen intercessionis Christi & sanctorum. Christus intercedit pro nobis apud Patrem vigore propriæ dignitatis & meriti: & propter seipsum exauditur, & quæ petit, impetrat. Sancti in hac vita pro se mutuo orant, non suâ, sed mediatoris dignitate & merito, & propterea bona, quæ petunt, sibi & aliis impetrant. Pontificij autem fingunt sanctos non in hac vita, sed in cœlo existentes, dignitate suorum meritorum aliis impetrare gloriam Dei, & certa bona. Manifestè igitur officio & gloriæ Jesu derogant, eumq; vnicum seruatorem esse negant.
units.tr: Objection: God wills that some pray for others. Therefore to attribute a share of intercession to the saints is not inconsistent with the office and glory of Jesus as the one Saviour. Answer: There is a great difference between the intercession of Christ and that of the saints. Christ intercedes for us before the Father by virtue of his own dignity and merit, and he is heard on his own account, and what he asks he obtains. The saints in this life pray for one another, not by their own dignity and merit but by the dignity and merit of the Mediator, and therefore they obtain for themselves and others the good things they ask. The Papists, however, imagine saints who are not in this life but are in heaven, obtaining for others by the dignity of their own merits the glory of God and certain good things. Clearly, then, they detract from the office and glory of Jesus, and deny that he is the one Saviour.

units.la: QVÆSTIO XXXI.
units.tr: QUESTION XXXI.

units.la: Quare appellatur Christus, hoc est, vnctus? RESPONSIO:
units.tr: Why is Christ called, that is, the Anointed? ANSWER:

units.la: Quod à Patre ordinatus, & Spiritu sancto vnctus sit * summus propheta & doctor, b qui nobis arcanum conconsilium & omnem voluntatem Patris, de redemptione nostri patefecit c: & summus Pontifex d, qui nos vnico sacrificio sui corporis redemit e, assidueque pro nobis apud Patrem intercedit f: & rex, qui nos suo verbo & Spiritu gubernat, & partam nobis salutem tuetur ac conseruat g.
units.tr: Because he was appointed by the Father and anointed with the Holy Spirit to be the highest prophet and teacher,ᵇ who revealed to us the hidden counsel and the whole will of the Father concerning our redemption;ᶜ and the highest priest,ᵈ who redeemed us by the one sacrifice of his body,ᵉ and constantly intercedes for us before the Father;ᶠ and the king, who governs us by his Word and Spirit and guards and preserves the salvation he has won for us.ᵍ

units.la: EXPLICATIO.
units.tr: EXPLANATION.

units.la: Jesvs est nomen proprium Mediatoris, CHRISTVS quasi cognomen. Ita enim est Jesus, vt etiam sit Christus, hoc est, promissus Seruator & Messias. Vtroq; officium eius designatur, sed nomine magis summatim, quàm expressè: cognomine clarius & expressius. Cognomen enim Christus notat tres certas officij partes, propheticam, sacerdotalem, & regiam. Nam Christus significat vnctum. Est ergo Jesus seruator, ita, vt sit Christus seu vnctus, hoc est, officium vncti habens. Hoc autem in tribus con- sistit: prophetia, sacerdotio & regno. Ratio, quod tria haec noten- tur nomine Christi, est: quia tria haec hominum genera olim vn- gi solebant, prophetae, sacerdotes & reges: qua vnctione signi- ficabatur tum ordinatio ad officium, tum etiam collatio dono- rum ad obeundas partes illas necessariorum. Sic igitur concludi- tur: Qui futurus erat propheta, sacerdos, & rex, & dicitur vn- ctus, is propter haec tria dicitur vnctus. Christus futurus erat haec tria, propheta, sacerdos, & rex, & dicitur vnctus. Ergo pro- pter haec tria dicitur vnctus seu Christus. Tres igitur hae officij mediatoris partes vno titulo Messiae, Christi, Vncti, μεσσιας μι- χῶς exprimuntur.
units.tr: Jesus is the proper name of the Mediator, and Christ is, as it were, a surname. For Jesus is so called that he is also Christ, that is, the promised Saviour and Messiah. Both offices are indicated, but the name indicates them more summarily than explicitly, while the surname does so more clearly and expressly. For the surname Christ denotes three definite parts of the office: the prophetic, the priestly and the kingly. For Christ means anointed. Jesus is therefore the Saviour in such a way that he is Christ, or anointed, that is, one who holds the office of the anointed. This office consists in three things: prophecy, priesthood and kingship. Reason: these three are signified by the name of Christ because in former times three classes of men were customarily anointed, prophets, priests and kings; by this anointing was signified both the appointment to the office and also the bestowal of the gifts necessary for discharging those duties. So it is concluded: He who was to be prophet, priest and king, and who is called anointed, is called anointed because of these three. Christ was to be these three, prophet, priest and king, and is called anointed. Therefore he is called anointed or Christ because of these three. These three parts of the Mediator's office are therefore expressed by the one title Messiah, Christ, the Anointed, Messias [μεσσίας].

units.la: Sed hic quaeritur: I. Quid sit Christi vnctio. II. Quod sit Christi propheticum munus. III. Quod sacerdotale. IV. Quod regium.
units.tr: But here the following questions arise: I. What is the anointing of Christ? II. What is the prophetic office of Christ? III. What is his priestly office? IV. What is his kingly office?

units.la: I. Quid sit vnctio Christi.
units.tr: I. What is the anointing of Christ?

units.la: Vnctio erat ceremonia, qua prophetae, sacerdotes & reges confirmabantur in suo officio, ad quod vngebantur oleo vnue singulari, siue vulgari adhibito. Et significabat vnctio: 1. Ordinatio tionem seu vocationem ad officium. 2. Promissionem donorum ad sustinendam impositi officij molem necessariorum, & eorundem collationem. Analogia signi & rei per eam significatæ hæc erat: quod sicut oleum membra arida pinguefacit, vegetat, reficit, confirmat, & homines ad exsequendum officium sudm promtos & alacres reddit: ita Spiritus sanctus nos natura ineptos ad boni aliquid agendum vegetat, recreat, idoneos reddit ad efficiendas res Deo gratas, & suppeditat vires administrandi officia à Deo nobis injuncta.
units.tr: Anointing was a ceremony by which prophets, priests and kings were confirmed in their office, for which they were anointed with a single, special oil, or with common oil. And the anointing signified: 1. The ordination or calling to the office. 2. The promise of the gifts necessary for bearing the burden of the office laid upon them, and their bestowal. The analogy between the sign and the thing signified by it was this: just as oil makes dry limbs supple, enlivens, refreshes and strengthens them, and makes men ready and eager to perform their duty, so the Holy Spirit enlivens us, who are by nature unfit to do any good, recreates us, makes us fit to carry out things pleasing to God, and supplies the strength to administer the offices enjoined on us by God.

units.la: Porrò qui vngebantur in veteri Testamento, typi erant Christi, vt dictum est, & vnctio eorum tantum erat vmbra, ideoque valde languida & imperfecta. Sed vnctio Christi perfecta est. In ipso enim habitat omnis plenitudo Deitatis corporaliter: & ipse solus omnia Spiritus dona habet numero & gradu. Summa. In veteri Testamento vncti alij dona accipiebant plura, alij pauciora, nulli omnia, nec omnes eodem gradu. Hic autem Christus vnus habet omnia. Licet igitur vnctio & illis & Christo competat: tamen Christo vere & perfectè.
units.tr: Moreover, those who were anointed in the Old Testament were types of Christ, as has been said, and their anointing was only a shadow, and therefore very faint and imperfect. But the anointing of Christ is perfect. For in him dwells all the fullness of the Godhead bodily, and he alone has all the gifts of the Spirit in number and degree. Summary. In the Old Testament, some of the anointed received more gifts, others fewer, none all, and not all in the same degree. But Christ alone has all things. Although anointing therefore belongs both to them and to Christ, yet it belongs to Christ truly and perfectly.

units.la: Obiect. Atqui nusquam legimus in sacra historia, Christum esse vnctum. Respond. Non quidem est vnctus ceremonialiter: vnctus est verò spiritualiter & realiter, hoc est, quod ad rem significatam attinet. Propterea vnxit te Deus, Deus tuus, oleo exultationis ultra consortes tuos. Spiritus Dei super me, ideo vnxit me. Hoc de Christo in utroque Testamento dicitur. Non debebat esse typicus rex, sacerdos, propheta, sed significatus & verus. Ideo non typicè, sed realiter debebat vngi. Nam oportebat esse analogiam inter officium & vnctionem, & per consequens, oportebat esse vnctionem non sacramentalem, sed spiritualem: non typicam, sed realem.
units.tr: Objection. Yet we never read in sacred history that Christ was anointed. Answer. He was indeed not anointed ceremonially; but he was anointed spiritually and really, that is, as far as the thing signified is concerned. Therefore God, your God, has anointed you with the oil of gladness above your fellows. The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he has anointed me. This is said of Christ in both Testaments. He ought not to have been a typical king, priest and prophet, but a signified and true one. Therefore he had to be anointed not typically but really. For there had to be an analogy between the office and the anointing, and consequently the anointing had to be not sacramental but spiritual, not typical but real.

units.la: Vnctus est igitur Christus 1. Quia ordinatus est ad officium Mediatoris diuinitus, voluntate Patris. A me ipso non veni, Pater me misit. Pater locutus est per Filium, quem constituit heredem omnium. 2. Quia natura ipsius humana donis Spiritus sancti est ornata sine mensura. Is quem misit Deus, verba Dei loquitur. Non enim huic admetitur Deus Spiritum. Hæ duæ partes vnctionis Christi inter se differunt hoc modo: quod donorum collatio humanam tantum naturam, ordinatio ad officium mediatoris, ad vtramque naturam pertinet.
units.tr: Christ was therefore anointed: 1. Because he was divinely appointed to the office of Mediator by the will of the Father. I did not come of myself; the Father sent me. God spoke through the Son, whom he appointed heir of all things. 2. Because his human nature was adorned without measure with the gifts of the Holy Spirit. He whom God has sent speaks the words of God, for God does not give the Spirit to him by measure. These two parts of the anointing of Christ differ from one another in this way: the bestowal of gifts pertains only to the human nature, while the appointment to the office of Mediator pertains to both natures.

units.la: Hinc patet responsio ad aliam Obiect. Deus non potest vngi. Christus est Deus. Ergo non potest vngi. Resp. Concedo totum: secundum quod Deus est, non potest vngi. 1. Quia diuinitati nihil justitiæ, sapientiæ, potentiæ potest accedere. 2. Quia Spiritus sanctus, cuius est vngere, proprius est Christi non minus quam Patris. Sicut igitur nemo tuum spiritum, qui est in te, tibi dare potest; quia quod habes, id tibi non datur: sic Deo, Spiritum sanctum, qui est in ipso, ex quo est, cuius est proprius, & à quo datur aliis, nemo potest dare.
units.tr: Hence the answer to another objection is clear. God cannot be anointed. Christ is God. Therefore he cannot be anointed. Answer. I grant the whole: insofar as he is God, he cannot be anointed. 1. Because nothing of justice, wisdom or power can be added to the divinity. 2. Because the Holy Spirit, whose office it is to anoint, belongs to Christ no less than to the Father as his own. Just as no one can give you your spirit, which is in you, because what you have is not given to you, so no one can give to God the Holy Spirit, who is in him, from whom he proceeds, whose own he is, and by whom he is given to others.

units.la: Instant. Si Christus non potuit vngi secundum diuinitatem: Ergo tantum secundum humanitatem est propheta, sacerdos, rex & mediator. Nam secundum quam naturam potuit vngi, secundum eam solam est mediator. Secundum solam humanitatem potuit vngi. Ergo secundum solam humanitatem est mediator. Minorem confirmat vnctionis definitio. Vngi est accipere dona: sed secundum naturam humanam Christus tantum accepit dona. Ergo, &c. Resp. Negatur minor: quia non est sufficiens definitio vnctionis. Vnctio enim non tantum est donorum acceptio, quæ competit soli humanitati, sed & ordinatio ad officium mediatoris, quæ conuenit etiam diuinitati. Etsi men non sequitur exclusio diuinitatis ab vnctione, quatenus est designatio ad officium. Negatiuè clarius fit solutio. Juxta quam naturam Christus non vngitur, secundum eam non est Mediator. Juxta deitatem non vngitur: Ergo, &c. Resp. Sunt quatuor termini. In maiore vnctio sumitur pro vtraque parte vnctionis, seu pro tota vnctione: in minore tantum pro altera vnctionis parte. Manet igitur, Christum esse vnctum secundum vtramque naturam, licet diuersimode, vt pater. Ergo etiam est propheta, sacerdos, rex, & mediator vtriusque naturæ respectu, id quod hæ duæ regulæ in verbo Dei fundatæ confirmant.
units.tr: Objection. If Christ could not be anointed according to his divinity, then he is prophet, priest, king and Mediator only according to his humanity. For according to whatever nature he could be anointed, according to that alone is he Mediator. He could be anointed only according to his humanity. Therefore he is Mediator only according to his humanity. The minor premise is confirmed by the definition of anointing. To be anointed is to receive gifts; but according to his human nature alone Christ received gifts. Therefore, etc. Answer. The minor is denied, because it is not a sufficient definition of anointing. For anointing is not only the receiving of gifts, which belongs to the humanity alone, but also the appointment to the office of Mediator, which belongs to the divinity too. Although it does not follow that the divinity is excluded from the anointing, insofar as it is the designation to the office. The solution is made clearer by a negative form. According to whatever nature Christ is not anointed, according to that he is not Mediator. He is not anointed according to his deity; therefore, etc. Answer. There are four terms. In the major premise, anointing is taken for both parts of the anointing, or for the whole anointing; in the minor, only for one part of it. It remains, therefore, that Christ is anointed according to both natures, though in different ways, as is clear. Therefore he is also prophet, priest, king and Mediator with respect to both natures, which the following two rules, founded in the Word of God, confirm.

units.la: 1. Proprietates alterius naturæ mediatoris tribuuntur toti personæ in concreto, secundum communicationem idiomatum, sed respectu eius naturæ, cuius sunt proprietæ: vt, Deus nascitur, patitur, moritur, nempe secundum humanitatem suam. Homo Christus est omnipotens, æternus, vbique, nempe secundum diuinitatem suam.
units.tr: 1. The properties of each nature of the Mediator are attributed to the whole person in the concrete, according to the communication of properties, but with respect to that nature of which they are properties: as God is born, suffers and dies, namely according to his humanity. The man Christ is almighty, eternal and everywhere, namely according to his divinity.

units.la: 2. Nomina verò officij mediatoris tribuuntur toti personæ, respectu vtriusque naturæ, seruatis tamen naturarum proprietatibus & actionum discriminibus: quia ad officium mediatoris peragendum requiritur & diuina & humana natura, & vtriusque actio, ita vt quælibet agat, quod suum est, cum alterius communione.
units.tr: 2. The names of the office of mediator, however, are attributed to the whole person with respect to both natures, yet with the properties of the natures and the distinctions of their actions preserved; because to carry out the office of mediator both the divine and the human nature are required, and the action of each, so that each nature performs what is its own in communion with the other.

units.la: Irenaus dicit nomine vnctionis comprehendi tres personas, vngentem Patrem, vnctum Filium, & vnctionem, qui est Spiritus.
units.tr: Irenaeus says that under the name of "anointing" three persons are comprehended: the Father who anoints, the Son who is anointed, and the anointing, which is the Spirit.

units.la: II. De munere Christi prophetico.
units.tr: II. On the prophetic office of Christ.

units.la: Superest, vt de munere triplici, seu de tribus partibus officij mediatoris, ad quod Christus est vnctus, breuiter dicatur. Hic verò tenendæ sunt definitiones prophetæ, sacerdotis & regis, quæ petuntur ex partibus officij, quibus illi fungebantur.
units.tr: It remains to say briefly something about the threefold office, or the three parts of the office of mediator, to which Christ was anointed. Here we must hold to the definitions of prophet, priest and king, which are drawn from the parts of the office that each of them performed.

units.la: Propheta à προφημι, quasi foras enuncio: nempe res futuras, in genere est persona à Deo vocata, vt annunciet & explicet hominibus voluntatem Dei de rebus siue præsentibus, siue futuris, quæ alioqui hominibus manerent occultæ, & quas homines per se non possent cognoscere. Est autem propheta vel minister, vel caput prophetarum, quod est vnus Christus. Ministeriales prophetæ alij sunt veteris, alij noui testamenti. Noui testamenti alij in specie, alij in genere dicti.
units.tr: Prophet, from [προφημι], as if I announce outwardly: in general, the one who foretells future things is a person called by God to announce and explain to men the will of God concerning things both present and future, things which would otherwise remain hidden from men and which men could not know by themselves. A prophet is either a minister or the chief of the prophets, which is Christ alone. Ministerial prophets are some of the Old Testament and others of the New. Of the New Testament, some are called prophets in the specific sense and others in the general sense.

units.la: Propheta veteris testamenti erat persona immediatè à Deo vocata & missa ad populum Dei, vt taxaret errores & vitia, cum comminatione pœnarum, & inuitatione hominum ad pœnitentiam, repurgaret doctrinam & cultum à corruptelis, declararet & illustraret promissionem de Messia, eiusque beneficiis & miraculo, & prædiceret futuros euentus, &c. habens donum miraculorum, aliaque testimonia diuina & certa, quod non erraret in doctrina, & simul aliquam partem negotiorum politicorum aliquando sustinens.
units.tr: A prophet of the Old Testament was a person called and sent immediately by God to the people of God, to rebuke errors and vices, with threats of punishments and with invitations of men to repentance; to purge doctrine and worship of corruptions; to declare and illustrate the promise about the Messiah, with his benefits and miracles; and to foretell future events, and so on. He had the gift of miracles and other divine and certain testimonies, so that he did not err in doctrine, and at the same time he sometimes took on some part of political affairs.

units.la: Propheta noui testamenti in specie erat persona immediatè vocata à Deo, & ornata dono prophetiæ ad præuidendum & prædicendum futura, quales erant Paulus, Petrus, Agabus, &c. In genere est, quisquis habet donum intelligendi, explicandi, & ad vsum Ecclesiæ & singulorum applicandi scripturas propheticas. Sic vsurpatur nomen prophetæ 1 Corinth. c.14. verf. 3.4. 5.29.
units.tr: A prophet of the New Testament in the specific sense was a person called immediately by God and endowed with the gift of prophecy, to foresee and foretell future things; such were Paul, Peter, Agabus, and others. In the general sense, anyone who has the gift of understanding and explaining the prophetic Scriptures and applying them to the use of the Church and of individuals is a prophet. The name of prophet is used in this way in 1 Corinthians 14:3, 4, 5, 29.

units.la: Propheta summus est Christus, persona immediatè ordinata à Deo, missa inde ab exordio Ecclesiæ in paradiso, ad patefaciendam voluntatem Dei erga genus humanum, ad instituendum ministerium verbi & sacramentorum, & ad tandem patefaciendum se in carne, doctrina & operibus diuinis, quod ipse sit æternus & consubstantialis Patris Filius, author Euangelicæ doctrinæ, dans per eam Spiritum sanctum, accendens fidem in cordibus, mittens Apostolos, & colligens sibi ex genere humano ecclesiam, à qua audiatur, inuocetur & colatur.
units.tr: The chief prophet is Christ, a person ordained immediately by God and sent from the beginning of the Church in paradise, to make known the will of God towards the human race, to institute the ministry of the Word and the sacraments, and finally to reveal himself in the flesh, by his doctrine and by his divine works; he is the eternal Son, consubstantial with the Father, the author of the evangelical doctrine, who through it gives the Holy Spirit, kindles faith in hearts, sends the apostles, and gathers for himself from the human race a Church, which hears him, calls upon him and worships him.

units.la: Munus ergo propheticum Christi est 1. Patefacere angelis & hominibus Deum, & eius voluntatem omnem, quæ non potuit nisi per Filium & singularem patefactionem cognosci. Filius, qui est in sinu Patris, ipse enarrauit nobis. Ego quæ audiui à Patre, hæc loquor. quor. Item legem promulgare & repurgare à corruptelis. 2. In- stituere & conseruare ministerium Euangelij, excitare & mittere prophetas, apostolos, doctores & alios ministros ecclesiæ, con-fere his donum prophetiæ, & instruere eos denis ad vocatio-nem necessariis. Ipse dedit alios prophetas, alios doctores, &c. Propter- ea dicit sapientia Dei: Mittam ad eos prophetas & apostolos, &c. Spi- ritum, cui non potuerunt contradicere, neque resistere omnes adver- santes. Spiritus Christi locutus est per prophetas. 3. Per ministerium esse efficacem in cordibus auditorum, intus docere, illuminare mentes, movere corda ad credendum, & obtemperandu Euan-gelio. Ipse vos baptizabit Spiritu sancto & igne. Tunc aperuit eorum mentem, ut intelligerent scripturas. Christus semetipsum tradidit pro ecclesia, ut eam sanctificaret mundatam lavacro aquæ per verbum. Illi egressi prædicarunt ubique, Domino unà operante, & sermonem con- firmante per signa subsequentia. Dominus adaperuit cor Lydiæ, ut attenderet ea, quæ dicebantur à Paulo. Dominus dabat testimonium sermoni gratiæ suæ, &c. Breviter. Partes officij prophetici Christi sunt tres. 1. Revelare voluntatem Patris. 2 Instituere ministerium. 3. Intus docere seu efficacem esse per ministerium. Hæc tria ab exordio ecclesiæ præstitit & usque ad finem mundi præstabit Christus, idque sua authoritate, potentia, & efficacia. Ideo vocatur λόγος, non tantum respectu Patris, à quo genitus est cogitatione intuente se, & cogitante imaginem sui non cua-nescentem, sed subsistentem ipsi Patri consubstantialem & co-æternam: verum etiam respectu nostri: quia est persona, quæ locuta est patribus, & protulit vivificum verbum seu Euange-lium ex sinu Patris.
units.tr: The prophetic office of Christ, therefore, is: 1. To make God known to angels and men, and all his will, which could not be known except through the Son and by a unique revelation. The Son, who is in the bosom of the Father, has made him known to us. What I have heard from the Father, that I speak. Likewise, to proclaim the law and purge it of corruptions. 2. To institute and preserve the ministry of the Gospel, to raise up and send prophets, apostles, teachers and other ministers of the Church, to bestow on them the gift of prophecy, and to instruct them in the gifts necessary for their calling. He himself gave some prophets, some teachers, and so on. Therefore the wisdom of God says: I will send to them prophets and apostles, and so on. The Spirit, whom all who oppose them could not resist or withstand. The Spirit of Christ spoke through the prophets. 3. To be effective through the ministry in the hearts of the hearers, to teach inwardly, to enlighten minds, and to move hearts to believe and to obey the Gospel. He himself will baptize you with the Holy Spirit and with fire. Then he opened their minds, that they might understand the Scriptures. Christ gave himself up for the Church, that he might sanctify it, cleansing it by the washing of water through the word. They went out and preached everywhere, the Lord working with them and confirming the word by the signs that followed. The Lord opened the heart of Lydia, that she attended to what was said by Paul. The Lord bore witness to the word of his grace, and so on. In brief: the parts of the prophetic office of Christ are three. 1. To reveal the will of the Father. 2. To institute the ministry. 3. To teach inwardly, or to be effective through the ministry. Christ has performed these three things from the beginning of the Church, and will perform them until the end of the world, and he does so by his own authority, power and efficacy. For this reason he is called the Word [λόγος], not only with respect to the Father, from whom he was begotten by the Father's mind looking upon itself and thinking of an image of itself that is not unaware of itself, but a subsistent Person consubstantial and coeternal with the Father; but also with respect to us, because he is the Person who spoke to the fathers and brought forth the life-giving Word, or the Gospel, from the bosom of the Father.

units.la: Hinc apparet discrimen inter Christum & alios prophetas, & cur Christus sit summus doctor & propheta, atque adeo pro- phetarum omnium princeps. 1. Christus Filius Dei Dominus omnium: alij prophetæ tantum homines & servi. 2. Christus immediate profert verbum è sinu Patris, prodit legatus & in-ternuncius a Patre missus ad homines: alij ab hoc mittuntur & ordinantur prophetæ, apostoli. 3. Christi prophetica sapientia est infinita, atque etiam secundum humanitatem omnibus do-nis antecellit alios. 4. Christus est author doctrinæ & ministe-rij: aliis revelatur prophetia ab hoc Propheta. Ideo dicitur Christi Spiritus in prophetis locutus. Nec tantum prophetis patefecit doctrinam, sed omnibus pijs: Explenitudine eius omnes accepimus, &c. 5. Christus per externum ministerium efficaciter hominibus Spiritus sancti virtute interne concionatur: alij sunt Christi organa & ὄργανα. 6. Christi doctrina clarior & ple- nior est, quam Mosis & omnium aliorum prophetarum. 7. Denique nique Christus à seipso, alij à Christo habent authoritatem: Christo loquenti credimus propter ipsum: aliis, quia Christus loquitur in ipsis.
units.tr: From this the difference between Christ and the other prophets appears, and why Christ is the chief teacher and prophet, and so the prince of all the prophets. 1. Christ is the Son of God, the Lord of all; the other prophets are only men and servants. 2. Christ immediately brings forth the word from the bosom of the Father; he comes forth as the ambassador and messenger sent by the Father to men. The other prophets and apostles are sent and ordained by him. 3. The prophetic wisdom of Christ is infinite, and even according to his humanity he surpasses the others in all gifts. 4. Christ is the author of the doctrine and of the ministry; prophecy is revealed to others by this Prophet. Therefore it is said that the Spirit of Christ spoke in the prophets. And he revealed the doctrine not only to the prophets but to all the godly: From his fullness we have all received, and so on. 5. Christ, through the external ministry, effectively preaches inwardly to men by the power of the Holy Spirit; the others are the instruments [organa] and ministers of Christ. 6. The doctrine of Christ is clearer and fuller than that of Moses and of all the other prophets. 7. Finally, Christ has authority from himself, while the others have it from Christ: we believe Christ speaking because of himself; we believe others because Christ speaks in them.

units.la: III. Quod sit munus Christi sacerdotale.
units.tr: III. That the priestly office of Christ is what it is.

units.la: Sacerdos in genere est persona à Deo ordinata, ad offerendum victimas & sacrificia, ad orandum, & alios docendum. Alius est typicus, alius significatus. Typicus est persona ordinata ad offerenda sacrificia typica, & ad orandum pro se & pro aliis, atqi ad docendū populum de voluntate, & de futuro Messia. Tales fuerunt omnes sacerdotes veteris testamenti. In his vnus erat summus, alij inferiores. Summus pontifex 1. Solus quotannis ingrediebatur in sanctuarium semel, & quidem cum sanguine & suffitu. 2. Maiorem habebat ornatum, quàm reliqui. 3. Præerat reliquis. 4. Offerebat & orabat pro se & pro populo. 5. Ordinatus erat ad petenda oracula, & responsa, quæ ad Arcam dabantur. Omnes reliqui erant inferiores sacerdotes, quorum officium erat sacrificare, docere doctrinam legis, & promissionem de Messia, intercedere pro se & pro aliis.
units.tr: A priest, in general, is a person ordained by God to offer victims and sacrifices, to pray, and to teach others. There is a typical priest and a signified priest. The typical priest is a person ordained to offer typical sacrifices, to pray for himself and for others, and to teach the people about God's will and about the Messiah to come. All the priests of the Old Testament were of this kind. Among them one was the high priest and the rest were lower priests. The high priest (1) alone entered the sanctuary once a year, and that with blood and incense; (2) had greater adornment than the others; (3) presided over the rest; (4) offered and prayed for himself and for the people; (5) was appointed to seek oracles and answers, which were given at the Ark. All the others were lower priests, whose office was to sacrifice, to teach the doctrine of the law and the promise of the Messiah, and to intercede for themselves and for others.

units.la: Obiect. Videntur igitur prophetæ & sacerdotes nihil differre, & utrique docebant. Resp. Etsi utrique docebant, tamen variè distinguebantur. Prophetæ excitabantur immediatè a Deo ex quavis tribu: sacerdotes ordinabantur mediatè ex sola tribu Leuitica. Prophetæ docebant extraordinariè: sacerdotes habebant ordinarium ministerium. Prophetæ accipiebant doctrinam immediatè à Deo: sacerdotes discebant eam ex lege. Prophetæ habebant testimonia diuina, quod non errarent: sacerdotes poterant errare in doctrina, & errabant sæpe discedentes à lege, & à prophetis reprehendebantur.
units.tr: Objection. Prophets and priests therefore seem to differ in nothing, since both taught. Answer. Although both taught, they were distinguished in various ways. Prophets were raised up immediately by God from any tribe; priests were appointed mediately from the tribe of Levi alone. Prophets taught extraordinarily; priests had an ordinary ministry. Prophets received their doctrine immediately from God; priests learned it from the law. Prophets had divine testimony that they did not err; priests could err in doctrine, and they often did, departing from the law, and were rebuked by the prophets.

units.la: Sacerdos significatus Christus est persona immediatè ordinata à Patre, & vncta Spiritu S. ad hoc officium, vt assumta natura humana patefaciat nobis arcanum consilium & voluntatem Dei erga nos, & seipsum offerat sacrificium propitiatorium pro nobis, & intercessione sua nobis applicans sacrificium suum, habens promissionem, quod omnium nomine, pro quibus intercedit, certò semper exaudiatur, iisque impetret remissionem peccatorum; deniq; per ministerium verbi & per Spiritum sanctum colligens, illuminans & sanctificans ecclesiam.
units.tr: The signified priest is Christ, a person ordained immediately by the Father and anointed by the Holy Spirit for this office: that, having assumed human nature, he might reveal to us the hidden counsel and will of God toward us, offer himself as a propitiatory sacrifice for us, and by his intercession apply his sacrifice to us, having the promise that, in the name of all for whom he intercedes, he will always certainly be heard and will obtain for them the forgiveness of sins; and finally, by the ministry of the Word and through the Holy Spirit, gather, enlighten and sanctify the Church.

units.la: Munus ergo sacerdotale Christi est 1. Docere nos, & quidem aliter, quàm alij sacerdotes, hoc est, non tantum in auribus per verbum, sed etiam in cordibus per Spiritum sanctum. 2. Offerre seipsum victimam pro mundi peccatis. 3. Orare, intercedere pro nobis perpetuò apud Patrem, vt propter hanc intercessionem & voluntatem, tatem, & propter perpetuum sacrificij sui vigorem, Pater nos recipiat in gratiam: & habere promissionem exauditionis & vnctionis in omnibus, quæ petit. 4. Applicare suum sacrificium his, pro quibus orat, hoc est, accipere in gratiam credentes, & efficere, vt Pater nos recipiat, & deniq; operari fidem in cordibus, qua nos accipiamus meritum eius, & per Spiritum sanctum nos regenerare ad nouam & æternam vitam.
units.tr: The priestly office of Christ, therefore, is (1) to teach us, and that in a way different from other priests, that is, not only in our ears through the Word, but also in our hearts through the Holy Spirit. (2) To offer himself as a victim for the sins of the world. (3) To pray and intercede for us perpetually before the Father, so that, by this intercession and this will, and by the perpetual efficacy of his sacrifice, the Father receives us into favour; and to have the promise of being heard and anointed in all that he asks. (4) To apply his sacrifice to those for whom he prays, that is, to receive believers into favour, to bring it about that the Father receives us, and finally to work faith in our hearts, by which we receive his merit, and through the Holy Spirit to regenerate us to a new and eternal life.

units.la: Ex his liquet, quid à Christo reliqui sacerdotes differant. 1. Illi tantum externa voce docent: Christus etiam interna Spiritus sancti efficacia. 2. Alij non intercedunt perpetuò, nec semper quos sacerdotes impetrant. 3. Nemini sua beneficia applicant. 4. Non se offerunt victimam pro peccatis aliorum. Hæc verò omnia sunt solius Christi.
units.tr: From these points it is clear how the other priests differ from Christ. (1) They teach only by an outward voice; Christ also teaches by the inward efficacy of the Holy Spirit. (2) Others do not intercede perpetually, nor do they always obtain what they seek for those for whom they pray. (3) None of them applies his benefits to others. (4) None of them offers himself as a victim for the sins of others. But all these things belong to Christ alone.

units.la: IV. Quod sit regium Christi munus.
units.tr: IV. That the kingly office of Christ is what it is.

units.la: Rex est persona ordinata à Deo, vt in populo aliquo imperet sola, secundum honestas leges, & habeat potestatem ac potentiam bonos ornandi præmiis, & malos puniendi, ac defendendi subditos aduersus hostes, non habens dominum superiorem. Rex regum Christus est persona immediatè ordinata à Deo, vt ecclesiam suam sanguine suo redemptam regat verbo & Spiritu, defendat contra hostes, & præmiis æternis afficiat, hostes verò in æternas pœnas abijciat. Vocaturq; nomen eius sermo Dei, habebat in vestimento & in femore suo nomen scriptum: Rex regum, & Dominus dominantium.
units.tr: A king is a person ordained by God to rule alone over some people, according to honourable laws, and to have the power and might to reward the good with prizes and to punish the wicked, and to defend his subjects against enemies, having no superior lord. Christ, the King of kings, is a person ordained immediately by God to rule his Church, redeemed by his own blood, by his Word and Spirit, to defend it against enemies, to reward it with eternal prizes, and to cast its enemies into eternal punishments. His name is called The Word of God; he had written on his garment and on his thigh a name: King of kings, and Lord of lords.

units.la: Officium ergo regium Christi est 1. Regere Ecclesiam Spiritu & verbo, hoc est, non tantum ostendere verbo, quid nobis sit faciendum, sed etiam efficere suo Spiritu, vt faciamus. 2. Tueri nos contra hostes externos, quod duplici ter facit: dum & ipse nos defendit sua omnipotentia, & nos ipsos armis, hoc est, Spiritu suo ad hostibus resistendum instruit. 3. Ornare ecclesiam donis & gloria, ac tandem liberare ab omnibus malis: hostes verò vincere & frænare potentia sua, tandemque plane debellatos in æternas pœnas detrudere.
units.tr: The kingly office of Christ, therefore, is (1) to rule the Church by his Spirit and Word; that is, not only to show us by the Word what we must do, but also to bring it about by his Spirit that we do it. (2) To defend us against external enemies, which he does in a twofold way: both by defending us himself with his almighty power, and by equipping us with arms, that is, with his Spirit, to resist our enemies. (3) To adorn the Church with gifts and glory, and at last to deliver it from all evils; and to conquer its enemies and restrain them by his power, and finally, when they are utterly defeated, to thrust them down into eternal punishments.

units.la: QVÆSTIO XXXII.
units.tr: QUESTION 32.

units.la: Cur verò tu Christianus appellaris a?
units.tr: Why then are you called a Christian?

units.la: RESPONSIO.
units.tr: ANSWER.

units.la: Quod per fidem membrum sum Jesu Christi b, & vnctionis ipsius particeps c, vt & nomen eius confiteat d, meque sistam ipsi viuam gratitudinis hostiam stiam c, & in hac vita contra peccatum & Sathanam libera & bona conscientia pugnem f, & postea æter-num cum CHRISTO regnum in omnes creaturas teneam g.
units.tr: Because through faith I am a member of Jesus Christ, and a partaker of his anointing, so that I confess his name, present myself to him as a living sacrifice of thanksgiving, fight in this life against sin and Satan with a free and good conscience, and afterwards reign eternally with Christ over all creatures.

units.la: EXPLICATIO.
units.tr: EXPLANATION.

units.la: Quæstione hac agitur de dignitate & xοιvωνία Christianorum cum capite suo Christo, & de eorum officiis. Christianorum nomen cœpit vsurpari tempore Apostolorum in ecclesia Antiochena. Prius fratres & discipuli appellabantur. Christianus enim est discipulus Christi, seu is, qui sectatur doctrinam & vitam Christi, seu is, qui habet communionem cum Christo, qui Christo insertus est. Suntautem Christiani duplices: alij apparentes tantum, alij veri. Apparentes tantum sunt, qui quidem baptizati sunt in cœtu vocatorum, & profitentur Christianam fidem, sed sine vera conuersione, hoc est, simulati, hypocritæ, & oretenus Christiani. De his dicitur: Multi vocati, pauci electi. Non omnis, qui dicit mihi, Domine, introibit in regnum cœlorum, &c. Veri sunt, qui non tantū sunt baptizati, & profitentur doctrinam Christi, sed etiam vera fide sunt prædisi, & eam fructibus pœnitentiæ declarant: seu, qui per fidem vere sunt membra Christi, & vocationis ipsius participes. Omnes veri Christiani etiam sunt apparentes, quia dicitur: Luceat lux vestra coram hominibus. Ostende mihi fidem tuam ex operibus tuis. Sed non contra omnes apparentes etiam sunt veri; quia multis dicetur: Nunquam novi vos. Hic de veris duntaxat Christianis agitur, non simulatis. Quæritur ergo, cur appellemur Christiani, hoc est, vocati? Causæ duæ sunt: quia per fidem sumus membra Christi, & quia sumus vnctionis Christi participes. hoc est, Christiani dicimur communicatione personæ, officij & dignitatis Christi.
units.tr: This question concerns the dignity and communion [κοινωνία] of Christians with their head Christ, and concerns their duties. The name "Christians" began to be used in the time of the Apostles, in the church at Antioch. Previously they were called brethren and disciples. For a Christian is a disciple of Christ, that is, one who follows the teaching and life of Christ, or one who has communion with Christ and is grafted into Christ. There are, however, two kinds of Christians: some only apparent, others true. Those are only apparent who indeed have been baptized into the company of the called and profess the Christian faith, but without true conversion, that is, who are feigned, hypocrites, and Christians in word only. Of these it is said: Many are called, but few are chosen. Not everyone who says to me, Lord, Lord, shall enter the kingdom of heaven, etc. The true are those who not only have been baptized and profess the teaching of Christ, but are also truly sanctified by a true faith and declare it by the fruits of repentance; or, who by faith are truly members of Christ and partakers of his calling. All true Christians are also apparent, since it is said: Let your light shine before men. Show me your faith by your works. But not conversely are all apparent Christians also true, since to many it will be said: I never knew you. Here we speak only of true Christians, not feigned ones. The question, then, is why we are called Christians, that is, named? There are two causes: because through faith we are members of Christ, and because we are partakers of the anointing of Christ. That is, we are called Christians by the communication of the person, office and dignity of Christ.

units.la: Fieri & esse membrum Christi. Est Christo inseri seu copulari, perinhabitantem in ipso & in nobis eundem Spiritum sanctum, & ornari ab eo tali iustitia & vita æterna, qualis in Christo est: & in hac vita, quia hæc iustitia est imperfecta, placere Deo propter iustitiam Christi fide nobis imputatam. De hac xοι-νωνία nostri cum Christo loquuntur dicta: Multi sumus vnum corpus in Christo. An ignoratis corpora vestra esse membra Christi? Qui adglutinatur Domino, unus spiritus est. Prorsus adolescamus in eum per omnia, qui est caput, nempe Christus, &c.
units.tr: To become and to be a member of Christ. It is to be grafted into or joined to Christ, by the same Holy Spirit dwelling in him and in us, and to be adorned by him with such righteousness and eternal life as is in Christ; and in this life, since this righteousness is imperfect, to be pleasing to God on account of the righteousness of Christ imputed to us by faith. Of this communion of ours with Christ the sayings speak: We, being many, are one body in Christ. Do you not know that your bodies are members of Christ? He who is joined to the Lord is one spirit. Let us grow up in every way into him who is the head, namely Christ, etc.

units.la: Ratio similitudinis membrorum & capitis in natura corporis humani optimè declaratur. Sicut enim membra habent unum caput, cum quo per nervos ipsa inter se cohærent, & ex quo in totum corpus vita & motus propagatur: & sicut in capite formantur spiritus vitales, proximum instrumentum sensus & motus: sicut item in capite sunt omnes sensus exteriores, quibus totum corpus & singula membra viuificantur, & ita ex solo capite vita in omnia membra propagatur, non autem ex uno membro in aliud, si tamen maneant copulata capiti & sibi invicem: sic Christus est vivum caput, ex quo uno in omnia membra spiritus ipsius spargitur, non autem ex uno membro in aliud, & à quo omnia membra vivificantur & reguntur, si tamen ei maneant copulata per spiritum in nobis & in ipso habitantem, idque per fidem, qua & nos membra Christi. Per fidem enim accipimus Spiritum, per quem fit ista unio. Membra autem copulata sunt inter se per dilectionem, quæ non potest abesse, si nos capiti coniuncti. Coniunctio enim capitis cum corpore, est causa connexionis membrorum inter se.
units.tr: The comparison of the members and the head is very well explained by the nature of the human body. For just as the members have one head, with which they cohere among themselves through the nerves, and from which life and motion are propagated into the whole body; and just as in the head the vital spirits are formed, the immediate instrument of sense and motion; likewise in the head are all the external senses, by which the whole body and each member are quickened; and thus life is propagated into all the members from the head alone, and not from one member into another, provided they remain joined to the head and to one another: so Christ is the living head, from which his Spirit is poured into all the members, not from one member into another, and by which all the members are quickened and governed, provided they remain joined to him through the Spirit dwelling in us and in him, and this through faith, by which we too are members of Christ. For through faith we receive the Spirit, through whom this union comes about. The members, moreover, are joined together by love, which cannot be absent if we are joined to the head. For the joining of the head with the body is the cause of the connection of the members among themselves.

units.la: Deinde; sicut in corpore humano varia sunt dona & officia membrorum, & una tantum vita movens omnia: sic in hoc Ecclesiæ corpore varia sunt dona & officia, & unus tantum Spiritus, cuius beneficio singula membra possunt obire suam functionem.
units.tr: Next: just as in the human body there are various gifts and offices of the members, and one life alone moves all things, so in this body of the Church there are various gifts and offices, and one Spirit only, by whose benefit each member can perform its own function.

units.la: Denique; sicut caput est in summo loco, ideoque dignius, & fons omnis vitæ: sic in Ecclesia Christus habet superiorem gradum, & in eo Spiritus est sine mensura, & fons omnium bonorum, in membris autem certæ sunt mensuræ donorum, quæ in illos ex uno capite CHRISTO deriuantur. Unde apparet, mentiri Pontificem Romanum, cum dicit, se esse caput Ecclesiæ.
units.tr: Finally: just as the head is in the highest place, and therefore more worthy, and the fountain of all life, so in the Church Christ has the higher rank, and in him the Spirit is without measure, and is the fountain of all good things; but in the members there are fixed measures of gifts, which are derived to them from the one head, Christ. Whence it appears that the Roman Pontiff lies when he says that he is the head of the Church.

units.la: Tripliciter autem Christus est caput. 1. Perfectione personæ: quia est Deus & homo, donis antecellens omnibus creaturis: etiam quoad naturam humanam. In ipso habitat omnis plenitudo deitatis corporaliter, & estis in eo completi. Ipse solus dat Spiritum sanctum: Hic est, qui baptizat Spiritu sancto. 2. Dignitate & ordine, gloria & maiestate, qua declarat se esse regem, dominum & hæredem omnium. Sicut enim Deus per ipsum creavit omnia: sic fecit eum hæredem omnium, & administratorem domus. 3. Officio: est redemptor & sanctificator ecclesiæ, præest omnibus membris, regit, gubernat, vivificat, alit & confirmat omnia membra. in ipso manentia, & cum reliquis membris coniuncta, sicut caput regit & viuificat totum corpus.
units.tr: Christ is head in three ways. 1. By the perfection of his person: because he is God and man, surpassing all creatures in gifts, even as to his human nature. In him dwells all the fullness of the Godhead bodily, and you are complete in him. He alone gives the Holy Spirit: he is the one who baptizes with the Holy Spirit. 2. By dignity and order, glory and majesty, by which he shows that he is King, Lord and heir of all. For just as God created all things through him, so he made him heir of all and steward of the house. 3. By office: he is the redeemer and sanctifier of the Church; he presides over all the members, rules, governs, quickens, nourishes and strengthens all the members abiding in him and joined with the rest, just as the head rules and quickens the whole body.

units.la: Tripliciter etiam nos sumus membra Christi. 1. Quia per fidem & Spiritum sanctum ipsi copulati sumus, atque etiam inter nos cohaeremus, sicut membra cohaerent cum capite & inter se. Membrorum enim coniunctio inter se non minus requiritur, quam coniunctio totius corporis cum capite. Nam si separes brachium a manu, illud & a capite separabis, proinde non amplius habebit vitam. Vt inhabitet Christus per fidem in cordibus vestris. 2. Quia Christo sic insiti ab eo viuificamur & regimur, & ex eo tanquam ex fonte omnia haurimus, ac nisi maneamus in ipso, non habemus vitam manentem in nobis, sicut nec membra avulsa a capite vitam in se retinent. Nisi quis in me manserit, eiectus extra statim vt palmes arescet. 3. Quia sicut in corpore variae sunt membrorum facultates & ministeria: sic varia sunt dona & officia membrorum Christi in ecclesia: & sicut omnes actiones partium corporis serviunt conservationi ipsius: sic omnia membra Christi, quidquid agant, debent referre ad conservationem corporis, quod est ecclesia. Quemadmodum in vno corpore membra multa habemus, membra vero omnia eandem non habent actionem: ita multa vnum corpus sumus in Christo. Vnicuique datur declaratio Spiritus ad vtilitatem.
units.tr: We too are members of Christ in three ways. 1. Because we are joined to him through faith and the Holy Spirit, and also cohere among ourselves, just as the members cohere with the head and with one another. For the joining of the members among themselves is required no less than the joining of the whole body with the head. For if you separate the arm from the hand, you will also separate it from the head, and so it will no longer have life. That Christ may dwell through faith in your hearts. 2. Because, grafted thus into Christ, we are quickened and ruled by him, and draw all things from him as from a fountain; and unless we remain in him, we do not have life abiding in us, just as members torn from the head do not retain life in themselves. Unless someone abide in me, he is cast out as a branch and immediately withers. 3. Because, as in the body there are various faculties and ministries of the members, so there are various gifts and offices of the members of Christ in the Church; and as all the actions of the parts of the body serve its preservation, so all the members of Christ, whatever they do, ought to refer to the preservation of the body, which is the Church. For as in one body we have many members, but all the members do not have the same function, so we, being many, are one body in Christ. To each is given the manifestation of the Spirit for the common good.

units.la: Quoniam nunc intelligimus, quid sit esse membrum Christi, & quomodo eius membra simus: etiam clarius apparebit, quid sit vocationis Christi participem esse. Vocatio significat collationem donorum: participatio vocationis significat communionem donorum & officij Christi: seu, vocatio est participatio omnium Christi beneficiorum, & consistit in participatione regni, sacerdotij & muneris prophetici Christi. Est igitur participem esse vocationis Christi 1 Esse participem Spiritus sancti & donorum eius. Nam Spiritus Christi in nobis non est otiosus, sed eadem in nobis operatur, quae in Christo, nisi quod Christus vnus habet plura dona, quam nos omnes, eaque gradu etiam perfectiora. 2. Christum nobis communicare suum munus propheticum, sacerdotale, & regium.
units.tr: Since we now understand what it is to be a member of Christ, and how we are his members, it will also appear more clearly what it is to be a partaker of the calling of Christ. Calling signifies the bestowal of gifts; partaking of the calling signifies communion in the gifts and office of Christ; or, the calling is the participation in all the benefits of Christ, and consists in the participation in the kingly, priestly and prophetic office of Christ. To be a partaker of the calling of Christ, therefore, is 1. to be a partaker of the Holy Spirit and his gifts. For the Spirit of Christ is not idle in us, but works in us the same things that are in Christ, except that Christ alone has more gifts than all of us, and these also more perfect in degree. 2. For Christ to communicate to us his prophetic, priestly and kingly office.

units.la: Dignitas prophetica in nobis est agnitio & confessio verae doctrinae de Deo ad salutem necessariae: seu, officium nostrum propheticum est 1. vere agnoscere Deum & eius voluntatem. 2. vere agnitum profiteri, fidelitate, audacia, & constantia confessionis. Quisquis confessus fuerit me coram hominibus, confitebor & ego eum coram Patre meo, qui est in coelis.
units.tr: The prophetic dignity in us is the recognition and confession of the true doctrine of God, which is necessary for salvation. In other words, our prophetic office is 1. to recognise truly God and his will; 2. to profess what has been truly recognised, with faithfulness, boldness and steadfastness in confession. Whoever confesses me before men, I will also confess before my Father who is in heaven.

units.la: Sacerdotale munus est, docere, orare, sacrificare. Nostrum igitur sacerdotium est 1. Etiam alios docere, hoc est, agnitionem veri
units.tr: The priestly office is to teach, to pray, and to sacrifice. Our priesthood, therefore, is 1. also to teach others, that is, to spread the knowledge of ## Question 32.

units.la: Quæst. XXXII.

veri Dei propagare ad alios. Et tu conversus confirma fratres tuos. 2. Deum recte agnitum invocare. 3. Præstare Deo gratitudinis officia, cultum, obedientiam internam & externam: seu, offerre sacrificia eucharistica Deo grata, & sacrificio Christi sanctifica-ta: videlicet 1. Nos ipsos, mortificando veterem hominem in nobis, & sistendo membra nostra arma justitiæ Deo. 2. Preces nostras. Offeramus Deo sacrificia laudis, hoc est, fructum labiorum confitentium nomen eius. 3. Eleemosynas nostras. Preces tuæ & eleemosynæ ascenderunt in memoriam coram Deo. 4. Confessionem Euangelij. Operans Euangelio Dei, ut oblatio gentium fiat accepta. 5. Crucem & calamitates à Deo immissas patienter tolerando. Si pro libamento offerar super hostia & sanctificatione fidei vestræ, gaudeo & gratulor omnibus vobis. Ego jam liber, & tempus resolutionis meæ adest.
units.tr: the true God to others. And you, when you have turned again, strengthen your brothers. 2. To call upon God as he is rightly known. 3. To render to God the duties of gratitude: worship, obedience inward and outward. In other words, to offer to God eucharistic sacrifices pleasing to him and sanctified by the sacrifice of Christ, namely: 1. ourselves, by mortifying the old man in us and presenting our members as weapons of righteousness to God; 2. our prayers. Let us offer to God the sacrifice of praise, that is, the fruit of lips confessing his name. 3. our alms. Your prayers and alms have ascended as a memorial before God. 4. the confession of the Gospel. Serving the Gospel of God, so that the offering of the Gentiles may become acceptable. 5. bearing patiently the cross and the calamities sent by God. If I am poured out as a drink offering upon the sacrifice and the service of your faith, I rejoice and congratulate you all. I am already free, and the time of my departure is at hand.

units.la: Porrò hoc officium sacerdotale nobis communicat Christus. 1. Efficiendo, ut hæc sacrificia ἀναφέρομεν Deo offeramus. 2. Efficiendo, ut Deo sint grata.
units.tr: Moreover, Christ communicates this priestly office to us: 1. by causing us to offer these sacrifices to God, up-lifted [ἀναφέρομεν]; 2. by causing them to be pleasing to God.

units.la: Differt igitur sacrificium Christi sicut à veterum sacerdotum sacrificio, sic & à nostro. 1. Christus obtulit ἁπαξ & ἐφάπαξ simul: nos offerimus ἐπαναληπτικῶς tantum. Veteres etiam sacerdotes obtulerunt ἐπαναληπτικῶς: quia hæc sunt totius Ecclesiæ inde ab initio usque ad finem. Quæ illi præterea obtulerunt, tantum fuerunt typica. At neque nos offerimus typica, quia tantum ἐπαναληπτικά, neque Christus. Non enim typicum, sed reale & significatum sacrificium obtulit, quippe non typicus, sed significatus sacerdos existens. 2. Christus obtulit sacrificium utrumque perfectum: nos imperfecta, & multis peccatis inquinata. 3. Christi sacrificium est meritorium per se, & valet coram Deo propter se ipsum, nostra nihil merentur, & valent propter sacrificium Christi.
units.tr: The sacrifice of Christ therefore differs from the sacrifice of the old priests, and also from ours. 1. Christ offered once for all [ἅπαξ] and at once [ἐφάπαξ]; we offer only repeatedly [ἐπαναληπτικῶς]. The old priests also offered repeatedly, because these sacrifices belonged to the whole Church from its beginning to its end. What they offered besides was only typical. But neither do we offer typical sacrifices, since ours are only repeated, nor did Christ. For he offered not a typical but a real and signified sacrifice, being not a typical but a signified priest. 2. Christ offered a sacrifice that was perfect in both respects; we offer imperfect sacrifices, stained by many sins. 3. The sacrifice of Christ is meritorious in itself and avails before God on account of itself; our works merit nothing, but avail on account of the sacrifice of Christ.

units.la: Regale nostrum officium est, 1. Per fidem pugnare, & vincere diabolum, mundum, carnem nostram, & omnes hostes. 2. Per eandem fidem tandem obtinere vitam & gloriam æternam. Possidete regnum paratum vobis à jactis fundamentis mundi. Regnum igitur nostrum est: 1. Quod domini sumus omnium creaturarum in Christo. Omnia vestra sunt. 2. Quod vincimus hostes per fidem in Christum. Qui victoriam dedit nobis. Victoria, qua vincimus mundum, est fides nostra.
units.tr: Our kingly office is 1. through faith to fight and overcome the devil, the world, our flesh and all enemies; 2. through the same faith at last to obtain eternal life and glory. Possess the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world. Our kingdom therefore is: 1. that we are lords of all creatures in Christ. All things are yours. 2. that we conquer our enemies through faith in Christ. Who has given us the victory. The victory by which we overcome the world is our faith.

units.la: Differt autem Christi regnum à nostro. 1. Christi regnum est hæreditarium. Ipse enim est naturalis Filius. Nostrum est jure adoptionis. Nos enim per & propter ipsum sumus filij adoptiui. Christus ut Filius domus suæ præest. Quem constituit hæredem omnium. 2. Ipse solus est rex omnium creaturarum, & inprimis ecclesiæ. Nos non sumus reges & domini angelorum & ecclesiæ, sed tantum reliquarum creaturarum: cœlum & terra atque adeo omnia serviunt nobis: gloria, maiestas, excellentia donorum non vulgaris nobis erit, sed maxima ex eo, quod condemnabimus hostes, hoc est, in condemnandis illis judicio Dei subscribemus: regnum, inquam, habebimus, non in ecclesiam, sed in omnes reliquas creaturas. Solus autem Christus & in ecclesiam universam, & in omnes creaturas pleno jure regno obtinet. Sedebitis super thronos duodecim, & judicabitis duodecim tribus Israel. An nescitis sanctos mundum judicaturos? 3. Ipse vicit hostes sua potentia: nos autem vincimus hostes in ipso & per ipsum, hoc est, ipsius gratia & auxilio. Confidite, ego vici mundum. 4. Ipse regit ecclesiam sceptro sui Spiritus & verbi, movens corda, & restituens in nobis imaginem amissam. Hoc est solius Christi. Nos non possumus dare Spiritum sanctum: sed tantum sumus ministri & administratores externæ vocis & rituum: sicut & Baptista dixit: Ego quidem baptizo vos aquâ: is verò, qui post me venit, baptizabit vos Spiritu sancto & igni. Quis igitur est Paulus? quis autem Apollos? ministri sunt, per quos credidistis, & ut cuique Dominus dedit.
units.tr: Christ's kingdom, however, differs from ours. 1. Christ's kingdom is hereditary, for he is the natural Son; ours is by right of adoption, for we are adopted sons through him and on account of him. Christ, as Son, presides over his own house; whom he appointed heir of all things. 2. He alone is king of all creatures, and especially of the Church. We are not kings and lords of the angels and of the Church, but only of the remaining creatures: heaven and earth, and indeed all things, serve us.
