Ego accepi a Domino, quod tradidi vobis. Baptizate eos in nomine Patris, & Filii, & Spiritus sancti. Revelans futura. Ego Iesus misi angelum meum, ut testificaretur vobis haec in ecclesiis. De meis accipiet, & annunciabit vobis. Colligens ecclesiam. Ego sum pastor ille bonus, & cognosco meas oves, & cognoscor a meis. Alias etiam oves habeo, quae non sunt ex ovili hoc: illas quoque oportet me adducere: vocem meam audient, & fiet unum ovile, & unus pastor. Illuminans mentes. Nemo novit Patrem, nisi Filius, & cui Filius voluerit revelare. Tunc aperuit mentes eorum, ut intelligerent scripturas. Regenerans
units.tr: 4. The same Scripture ascribes all the divine works equally to the Son and to the Father. First, the universal works: that he is creator. All things were made through him. He is the preserver and governor of all: He upholds all things by his powerful word. Then the special works pertaining to the salvation of the Church: that he sends prophets, apostles, and other ministers of the Church. As the Father sent me, so I also send you. And he gave some to be prophets, some apostles, some evangelists, some pastors and teachers. He equips ministers with the necessary gifts: I will give you a mouth and wisdom, which all your adversaries will not be able to contradict or resist. He reveals the doctrine: The only-begotten Son, who is in the bosom of the Father, he has declared him to us. He confirms the doctrine by miracles: They went out and preached everywhere, the Lord working with them and confirming the word by the signs that followed. He institutes the sacraments: I received from the Lord what I also delivered to you. Baptize them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. He reveals future things: I, Jesus, have sent my angel to testify these things to you in the churches. He will take of what is mine and declare it to you. He gathers the Church: I am the good shepherd, and I know my sheep, and I am known by mine. I have other sheep also, which are not of this fold; I must bring them too, and they will hear my voice, and there will be one flock and one shepherd. He enlightens minds: No one knows the Father except the Son, and anyone to whom the Son chooses to reveal him. Then he opened their minds, that they might understand the Scriptures. He regenerates

units.la: rans & sanctificans. Hic est, qui baptizat Spiritu sancto. Qui tradidit semetipsum pro nobis, ut redimeret nos ab omni iniquitate, & mundaret sibi ipsi populum, peculiarem, studiosum bonorum operum. Gubernans actiones & vitam impiorum. Sine me nihil potestis facere. Vivo autem jam non ego, sed vivit in me Christus. Quod consoletur in tentationibus. Venite ad me omnes, qui fatigati & onerati estis, & ego faciam ut requiescatis. &c. Pacem meam relinquo vobis, pacem meam do vobis. Quod confirmet & defendat adversus tentationes diaboli, & conservet conversos in fide usque ad finem.
units.tr: regenerating and sanctifying. He is the one who baptizes with the Holy Spirit. Who gave himself for us, that he might redeem us from all iniquity and cleanse for himself a people of his own, zealous for good works. Governing the actions and life of the wicked. Without me you can do nothing. Yet it is no longer I who live, but Christ lives in me. Because he comforts us in temptations. Come to me, all you who are weary and burdened, and I will give you rest. etc. My peace I leave with you; my peace I give to you. Because he strengthens and defends us against the temptations of the devil, and keeps those who have been converted in the faith to the end.

units.la: Confidite, ego vici mundum. Oves meae non peribunt in aeternum: & nemo rapiet eas ex manu mea. Quod exaudiat invocantes. Si quid petieritis in nomine meo, ego faciam. Ter rogavi Dominum, & respondit mihi: sufficit tibi gratia mea. Quod condonet peccata, justificet nos, & adoptet in filios Dei. Notitiâ sui servus meus justus justificabit multos. Ut sciatis, Filium hominis habere potestatem remittendi peccata in terra. Quotquot receperunt eum, dedit eis potestatem filios Dei fieri. Quod det vitam & salutem aeternam. Ego vitam aeternam do eis. Hic est verus Deus & vita aeterna. Quod judicet mundum. Ipse est, qui constitutus est à Deo judex vivorum & mortuorum. Eo quod Deus statuit diem, in quo judicaturus est orbem terrae in justitia per eum virum, per quem decreverat, &c. Haec opera divina Filio attributa à proprietatibus divinis eidem attributis differunt, ut effecta à causis.
units.tr: Take heart, I have overcome the world. My sheep will never perish, and no one will snatch them out of my hand. Because he hears those who call upon him. If you ask anything in my name, I will do it. Three times I asked the Lord, and he answered me: my grace is sufficient for you. Because he forgives sins, justifies us, and adopts us as children of God. By his knowledge, my righteous servant shall justify many. That you may know that the Son of Man has power on earth to forgive sins. As many as received him, to them he gave power to become children of God. Because he gives eternal life and salvation. I give them eternal life. This is the true God and eternal life. Because he judges the world. He is the one appointed by God to be judge of the living and the dead. Because God has fixed a day on which he will judge the world in righteousness through that man whom he has appointed, etc. These divine works ascribed to the Son differ from the divine properties ascribed to him as effects differ from their causes.

units.la: 5. Etiam honor aequalis & communis tribuitur Patri & Filio, quae aequalitas ex aequalitate essentiae & operum sequitur. Adoratur ab angelis, & ab ecclesia. Et adorent eum omnes sancti angeli eius. Et dixit ipse: Ut omnes honorent Filium, sicut honorant Patrem. Fiducia & spes in illo collocatur. Creditis in DEVM, & in me credite. Nominatur Deus absolute, ut patet. Hic est verus Deus & vita aeterna. Instituit sacramenta, quibus colitur. Obligamur baptismo in eius cultum, & obedientiam. Baptizantes eos in nomine Patris, & Filij, & Spiritus sancti. Sedet ad dexteram Dei, in throno Patris: aequali potentia regnat cum Patre. Celebratur aequali honore cum Patre ab Ecclesia triumphante: Sessori throni & agno benedictio, & honor, & gloria, & robur in secula seculorum. Denique est sponsus, maritus, caput, rex ecclesiae: ecclesia est ipsius domus, templum, cuius ipse architectus, &c.
units.tr: 5. Equal and common honour is also given to the Father and the Son, and this equality follows from the equality of essence and works. He is adored by the angels and by the Church. And let all his holy angels worship him. And he himself said: That all may honour the Son, just as they honour the Father. Trust and hope are placed in him. You believe in God, believe also in me. He is named God absolutely, as is clear. This is the true God and eternal life. He instituted sacraments by which he is worshipped. We are bound by baptism to his worship and obedience. Baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. He sits at the right hand of God, on the throne of the Father; he reigns with equal power together with the Father. He is celebrated with equal honour together with the Father by the Church triumphant: To him who sits on the throne and to the Lamb be blessing, and honour, and glory, and power, for ever and ever. Finally, he is the bridegroom, husband, head, and king of the Church; the Church is his house, his temple, of which he is the architect, etc.

units.la: Obiecti 1. Qui omnia habet ab alio, inferior est eo, à quo habet. Filius omnia habet à Patre. Ergo est Patre inferior. Resp. Maior vera est de eo, qui habet ex gratia donantis: posset enim non habere, ideoq; naturâ est inferior: falsa de eo, qui omnia habet generatione & naturâ, ut Filius Dei λόγος omnia habet à Patre. Pater dedit filio habere vitam in se ipso, sicut ipse vitam habet in se ipso. Omnia mea tua sunt, & tua mea sunt.
units.tr: Objection 1. He who has everything from another is inferior to him from whom he has it. The Son has everything from the Father. Therefore he is inferior to the Father. Answer. The major premise is true of one who has by the grace of the giver; for he could fail to have it, and therefore is inferior by nature. The minor is false of one who has everything by generation and by nature, as the Son of God, the Word [λόγος], has everything from the Father. The Father has given to the Son to have life in himself, just as he himself has life in himself. All that is mine is yours, and all that is yours is mine.

units.la: Obiect. 2. Qui alterius voluntate praeeunte agit, est eo inferior. Filius agit praeeunte voluntate Patris. Ergo est Patre inferior. Resp. Ordo agendi personarum non tollit aequalitatem. Sic enim se Deus patefecit verbo, quod Pater omnia agat per Filium & Spiritum: Filius a Patre per Spiritum, &c. Neque hic ordo est temporis, aut dignitatis, aut naturae, sed tantum ordinis. Ad maiorem igitur: qui agit alterius voluntate praeeunte, scilicet tempore vel natura. Filius autem ita agit, ut voluntas Patris non praeat, aut sit prior tempore, vel natura, sed tantum ordine.
units.tr: Objection 2. He who acts at the prior will of another is inferior to him. The Son acts at the prior will of the Father. Therefore he is inferior to the Father. Answer: The order of action of the persons does not take away equality. For God has so revealed himself in the word, that the Father does all things through the Son and the Spirit, the Son from the Father through the Spirit, etc. Nor is this order one of time, or of dignity, or of nature, but only of order. As for the major premise: one who acts at the prior will of another, namely in time or in nature. But the Son so acts that the will of the Father does not go before him, or is not prior in time or in nature, but only in order.

units.la: IV. Quod Filius sit Patri ὁμοούσιος, hoc est, consubstantialis.
units.tr: IV. That the Son is homoousios [ὁμοούσιος] with the Father, that is, consubstantial.

units.la: His positis vltro sequitur ὁμοουσία. Haeretici concedunt, Filium esse ὁμοιούσιον, similis essentiae cum Patre. Recte quidem, sed non satis. Duo homines sunt ὁμοιούσιοι, qui tamen non sunt ὅμοιοι, quia non sunt unus homo. Pater vero & Filius ita sunt ὁμοιούσιοι, ut etiam sint ὁμοούσιοι, hoc est, eiusdem essentiae, & unus Deus. Alius quidem est Pater, alius Filius: sed non alius Deus est Pater, alius Deus Filius, &c. Johannes dicit: Tres sunt, qui testificantur in coelo, non autem tres dij, qui testificantur. Dicimus itaque contra Arium, Christum non tantum esse ὁμοιούσιον, sed & ὁμοούσιον Patri, hoc est, habere eandem cum Patre essentiam diuinam.
units.tr: From these points, homoousia follows of its own accord. The heretics concede that the Son is homoiousios [ὁμοιούσιος], of like essence with the Father. Rightly, indeed, but not enough. Two men are homoiousioi [ὁμοιούσιοι], of like nature, and yet they are not alike [ὅμοιοι], because they are not one man. But the Father and the Son are so homoiousioi that they are also homoousioi [ὁμοούσιοι], that is, of the same essence, and one God. The Father is one person, the Son another; yet the Father is not one God and the Son another God, etc. John says: There are three who bear witness in heaven, but not three gods who bear witness. Therefore we say against Arius that Christ is not only homoiousios but also homoousios with the Father, that is, has the same divine essence as the Father.

units.la: 1. Quia Filius vocatur Jehoua, qui vnus tantum est essentia. Nec tantum nomen Jehouae ei tribuitur, sed & proprietates, quae soli Jehouae conueniunt. Hoc est nomen eius, quo vocabitur: Iehoua iustitia nostra. Deus exspectatus & seruator noster Iehoua. Hic expectatus Deus & seruator est Messias, qui eodem sensu desiderium gentium appellatur. Dicitur etiam Jehoua: Sic dicit Dominus exercituum: Propter gloriam misit me ad gentes: scietisque, quod Dominus exercituum misit me. Ad templum suum Iehoua veniet. Priusquam veniet dies ille Iehouae, magnus & tremendus.
units.tr: 1. Because the Son is called Jehovah, who is only one in essence. Nor is only the name Jehovah given to him, but also the properties that belong to Jehovah alone. This is his name by which he shall be called: Jehovah our righteousness. The God who was awaited, and our Saviour, Jehovah. This awaited God and Saviour is the Messiah, who in the same sense is called the desire of the nations. He is also called Jehovah: Thus says the Lord of hosts: For the sake of glory he has sent me to the nations; and you shall know that the Lord of hosts has sent me. Jehovah will come to his temple. Before that great and terrible day of Jehovah comes.

units.la: Huc pertinent loca, quibus Angelus Jehouae nominatur ipse Jehoua: item ea, quae in veteri testamento de Jehoua loquuntur, in nouo autem de Christo citantur. Ascendit in altum, captiuam duxit captiuitatem, & dedit dona hominibus. Tentatus in deserto est Jehoua. Idem est Christus. Et adorent eum omnes angeli eius. Tu Iehoua initio terram fundasti, & opera manuum tuarum sunt coeli. Ponam lapidem in Sion, lapidem preciosum, & lapidem offendiculi. Ego primus & nouissimus.
units.tr: To this belong the passages in which the Angel of Jehovah is named Jehovah himself; likewise those things which are said of Jehovah in the Old Testament and are cited of Christ in the New. He ascended on high, led captivity captive, and gave gifts to men. Jehovah was tempted in the wilderness. It is the same Christ. And let all his angels worship him. You, Jehovah, laid the foundation of the earth in the beginning, and the heavens are the works of your hands. Behold, I will lay in Zion a stone, a precious stone, and a stone of stumbling. I am the first and the last.
2. Because also (Rev. 21, 6).

units.la: 2. Quia dicitur verus Deus: verus autem Deus non nisi unus est. Hic est verus Deus & vita aeterna. Qui est Deus supra omnia Ὁ λογητός, benedictus in secula.
units.tr: 2. Because he is called the true God, and the true God is only one. This is the true God and eternal life. He who is God over all, Who is blessed [Ὁ λογητός], blessed for ever.

units.la: 3. Patris & Filij est unus & idem Spiritus, quem utrque spirat, per quem utrque agit. Ergo non essentia, sed tantum personis sunt distincti: alioqui singuli suum & diuersum spiritum spirarent.
units.tr: 3. The Father and the Son have one and the same Spirit, whom each breathes forth and through whom each acts. Therefore they are distinguished not by essence but only by persons; otherwise each would breathe forth his own and a different Spirit.

units.la: 4. Quia est proprius & unigenitus Filius Patris, habens essentiam sibi communicatam eandem & integram.
units.tr: 4. Because the Son is the proper and only-begotten Son of the Father, having the essence communicated to him, the same and whole.

units.la: His consideratis, facile est respondere ad sophismata haereticorum, praesertim si fontes eorum considerentur. Aut enim principiis falsis nituntur: Aut, quae rerum creatarum sunt propria, ad creatorem transferunt: Aut, quae de Christo secundum humanam naturam sunt dicta, ad ipsius diuinitatem trahunt: Aut Mediatoris officium cum natura vel persona confundunt: Aut ab iis, quae Patri tanquam Filij & Spiritus sancti & omnium diuinarum operationum fonti tribuuntur, Filium & Spiritum sanctum excludunt: Aut ea, quibus diuinitas in persona Patris a creaturis aut idolis discernitur, Filio & Spiritui sancto detrahunt: Aut denique phrasin scripturae corrumpunt.
units.tr: Having considered these points, it is easy to answer the sophisms of the heretics, especially if their sources are examined. Either they rest on false principles; or they transfer to the Creator what is proper to created things; or they draw to the divinity what has been said of Christ according to his human nature; or they confuse the office of the Mediator with his nature or person; or they exclude the Son and the Holy Spirit from those things which are attributed to the Father as the fount of all divine operations, including those of the Son and the Holy Spirit; or they take away from the Son and the Holy Spirit those marks by which the divinity in the person of the Father is distinguished from creatures or idols; or finally, they corrupt the phrasing of Scripture.

units.la: Regulae generales, ex quibus ad haec fundamenta haereticorum respondetur.
units.tr: General rules, by which these foundations of the heretics are answered.

units.la: 1. Cum ex falsis vel naturalibus principiis argumentantur: ut, si Deus genuit unum filium, etiam potest plures gignere, & filius potest alium filium gignere, &c. Resp. Per inficiationem, ex hac regula: De Deo est judicandum tantum ex verbo patefacto, non autem ex cerebro haereticorum. Sed Deus patefecit se talem, qui tantum unum filium genuerit, habeat, & habere velit, non plures, &c.
units.tr: 1. When they argue from false or merely natural principles, as: if God begot one Son, he could also beget several, and the Son could beget another son, etc. Answer. By denial, from this rule: Concerning God we must judge only from the revealed Word, and not from the brains of heretics. But God has revealed himself as one who has begotten, and wishes to have, only one Son, and not several, etc.

units.la: 2. Quia multa principia vera de rebus finitis sumunt. Exempli gratia. Tria non possunt esse unum. Gignens & generatum sunt unum essentia. Persona infinita non potest infinitam gignere. Essentia una non potest communis esse pluribus. Qui communicat totam essentiam suam alteri, non manet id, quod erat, &c. Ad haec respondendum est, non per simplicem inficiationem sed per distinctionem ex hac regula: Principia, quae vera sunt de natura finita, non sunt transferenda ad essentiam Dei infinitam: alioqui fiunt falsa.
units.tr: 2. Because they take many true principles from finite things. For example: three cannot be one; the begetter and the begotten are one in essence; an infinite person cannot beget an infinite person; one essence cannot be common to several; he who communicates his whole essence to another does not remain what he was, etc. To these we must reply, not by a bare denial but by a distinction, from this rule: Principles that are true of finite nature are not to be transferred to the infinite essence of God; otherwise they become false.

units.la: 3. Cum ex propriis naturae humanae argumentantur: ut, Christus est passus, mortuus, &c. quae non competunt Deo: respondendum est distinctione naturarum in Christo, ex hac regula gula : Qua sunt propria humanæ naturæ, non sunt transferenda ad diuinam.
units.tr: 3. When they argue from the properties of human nature, as: Christ suffered, died, etc., which do not belong to God, we must answer by the distinction of the natures in Christ, from this rule: What belongs to human nature is not to be transferred to the divine.

units.la: 4. Cùm ex proprietatibus officij argumentantur: vt; Deus non mittitur à Deo: respondendum est ex regula Cyrilli: Missio & obedientia non tollunt æqualitatem potentiæ aut essentiæ. Vel: Inæqualitas officiorum non tollit æqualitatem naturæ aut personarum. Ex hac regula etiam respondetur ad dictum : Pater maior est me. nempe quoad officium & naturam humanam: non autem quoad essentiam diuinam.
units.tr: 4. When they argue from the properties of an office, as: God is not sent by God, we must answer from the rule of Cyril: Mission and obedience do not take away the equality of power or essence. Or: Inequality of offices does not take away equality of nature or of persons. From this rule also we answer the saying: The Father is greater than I, namely with respect to office and human nature, but not with respect to the divine essence.

units.la: 5. Passim in scriptura tribuit Filius sua opera Patri tanquam fonti operum diuinorum: vt, Pater in me manens facit opera. Hinc concludunt: Ergo Filius non est Deus, aut est Deus inferior. Ad hæc respondendum est ex regula : Quæ tribuuntur Patri vt fonti, ea non remouentur à Filio, cui sunt communicata, vt habeat ea propria. Agit enim ὁμοίως cum Patre.
units.tr: 5. Throughout Scripture the Son attributes his works to the Father as the source of the divine works, as: The Father abiding in me does the works. From this they conclude: therefore the Son is not God, or is a lesser God. To these we must reply from the rule: What is attributed to the Father as the source is not removed from the Son, to whom it has been communicated, so that he may have it as his own. For he acts in like manner [ὁμοίως] with the Father.

units.la: 6. Sic cùm argumentantur ex dictis, quæ opponunt Patrem falsis numinibus, non facta mentione Filij, & concludunt, Filium non esse illum unum Deum: facilis est responsio ex regula: Cùm aliquid tribuitur alicui personæ diuinitatis, vt opponatur creaturis aut fictitiis numinibus, vt ab his discernatur: non excluduntur à diuinitate personæ aliæ, sed tantum ea, cum quibus fit collatio. Vel: Cùm remouentur à Deo, quæ sunt extra eum, non remouentur Filius & Spiritus sanctus. Vel: Cùm una persona diuina opponitur creaturis aut idolis, non sequitur, Filium aut Spiritum sanctum non esse eiusdem essentiæ cum persona, quæ opponitur creaturis & idolis. Vel : Cùm soli Patri oppositò creaturis & idolis tribuitur gloria & honor, non excluduntur reliquæ personæ diuinitatis, sed tantum illa, secundum quam fit antithesis : alioqui multa absurda sequerentur. Vel: Proprietates, operationes, honor diuinus, vni alicui personæ tribuuntur ita, vt non à reliquis personis deitatis, sed tantum à creaturis remoueantur. Vel : Oratio superlatiua aut exclusiua, de vna persona usurpata, non excludit alias diuinitatis personas, sed creaturas & fictitia numina, quibus verus Deus, siue in vna, siue in pluribus personis opponitur. Vt: Pater maior est omnibus: nempe creaturis, non Filio aut Spiritu sancto. Solus Pater nouit diem judicij, hoc est, nulla creatura. Hinc etiam respondetur ad dictum: Vt cognoscant, te solum esse verum DEVM. Non excluditur à vera Deitate Filius : sed idola, & falsa numina, quibus Pater verus Deus opponitur.
units.tr: 6. Likewise, when they argue from sayings which set the Father against false deities, without mention of the Son, and conclude that the Son is not that one God, the answer is easy, from the rule: When something is ascribed to one person of the Godhead in order to set it against creatures or fictitious deities, so as to distinguish it from them, the other persons of the Godhead are not excluded from deity, but only those with whom the comparison is made. Or: When things that are outside God are removed from God, the Son and the Holy Spirit are not removed. Or: When one divine person is set against creatures or idols, it does not follow that the Son or the Holy Spirit is not of the same essence as the person who is set against creatures and idols. Or: When glory and honour are ascribed to the Father alone, set against creatures and idols, the remaining persons of the Godhead are not excluded, but only that one with respect to whom the antithesis is made; otherwise many absurdities would follow. Or: Properties, operations and divine honour are ascribed to one particular person in such a way that they are removed not from the other persons of the Godhead, but only from creatures. Or: An exclusive or superlative expression, used of one person, does not exclude the other persons of the Godhead, but creatures and fictitious deities, to which the true God is opposed, whether in one person or in several persons. Thus: The Father is greater than all, namely than creatures, not than the Son or the Holy Spirit. Only the Father knows the day of judgment, that is, no creature does. Hence also we answer the saying: That they may know you, the only true God. The Son is not excluded from true Deity; rather idols and false deities are excluded, to which the Father as the true God is opposed.

units.la: Inst. Atqui valet: Maximilianus est Imperator. Ergo Rudolphus non est Imperator. Cur non etiam, Pater est Deus: ergo Filius non est Deus? Resp. Valet quidem in relatis propriis. Pater est Pater à se. Ergo Filius non est pater, nec à se: & de adjunctis singusingularibus: quale est, Imperatorem esse: sed non valet de essentia Deitatis, communi Patri & Filio: sicut nec de adjunctis communibus.
units.tr: Objection. But the inference holds: Maximilian is emperor; therefore Rudolf is not emperor. Why not also: the Father is God; therefore the Son is not God? Answer. The inference holds indeed in proper relative terms: the Father is Father of himself; therefore the Son is not Father, nor of himself; and in the singular accidents, such as being emperor. But it does not hold concerning the essence of the Godhead, which is common to Father and Son, just as it does not hold concerning common accidents.

units.la: 7. De phrasibus, quas corrumpunt, est judicandum ex circumstantia locorum, & ex aliorum dictorum collatione. Ut, Tradet regnum Deo & Patri, sic scilicet, ut & ipse illud retineat, sicut Pater regnum tradidit Filio, ut tamen idipsum non amiserit. Sic Filius non facit quicquam, nempe a se, seu non praeeunte voluntate Patris: facit tamen per se a Patre.
units.tr: 7. Concerning the phrases which they distort, we must judge from the circumstances of the passage and from the comparison of other sayings. For example, He will deliver the kingdom to God and the Father, understood in such a way that he himself also retains it, just as the Father delivered the kingdom to the Son, and yet the Father has not lost it in the same way. So too, The Son does nothing, namely of himself, or without the prior will of the Father; yet he does by himself what he does from the Father.

units.la: Regulae speciales contra haereticorum sophismata, & ad intelligendas scripturas necessariae.
units.tr: Special rules against the sophisms of the heretics, and necessary for understanding the Scriptures.

units.la: 1. Nihil obstat, quo minus, qui essentia sunt pares, officio sint impares.
units.tr: 1. Nothing prevents those who are equal in essence from being unequal in office.

units.la: 2. Quod Pater dedit Filio, ut perpetuo illud habeat, nunquam ab eo repetet. Quod vero ad certum tempus ei datum & commissum est, id cum deponere, vel depositisse necesse est.
units.tr: 2. What the Father has given to the Son so that he may hold it forever, he will never take back. But what has been given and entrusted to him for a certain time must necessarily be laid down or already have been laid down.

units.la: 3. A relativo ad absolutum non valet consequentia.
units.tr: 3. The inference from the relative to the absolute does not hold.

units.la: 4. Non sequitur: cuiuscunque persona est ab alio, eius etiam essentiam ab alio esse.
units.tr: 4. It does not follow that, if a person is from another, his essence is also from another.

units.la: 5. De persona in concreto dicitur, quod unius tantum naturae est: sed non nisi respectu sui naturae, cuius proprium est.
units.tr: 5. A person, taken concretely, is said to be of one nature only, but only with respect to that nature of which he is the proper possessor.

units.la: 6. Sapientia duplex est: alia creata in creaturis exsistens, quae est ordo rerum in natura sapienter institutus: alia increata in Deo subsistens, quae cum opponitur creatutis, est ipsa mens diuina, seu aeternum de hoc rerum ordine decretum Patris, Filii & Spiritus sancti. Cum vero haec sapientia in Deo subsistens, distinguitur a Deo, pro Filio Dei recte accipitur.
units.tr: 6. Wisdom is twofold. One kind exists in creatures: it is the order of things in nature, wisely instituted. The other subsists in God uncreated; when it is set against creatures, it is the divine mind itself, or the eternal decree of the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit concerning this order of things. But when this wisdom subsisting in God is distinguished from God, it is rightly taken to mean the Son of God.

units.la: 7. Quoties in scriptura una deitatis persona creaturis aut fictitiis numinibus opponitur, & ab his discernitur, aliae personae non excluduntur a deitate, sed tantum creaturae, cum quibus fit collatio veri Dei. Idem sentiendum est de orationibus exclusivis & superlativis.
units.tr: 7. Whenever in Scripture one person of the Godhead is set over against creatures or fictitious deities and distinguished from them, the other persons are not excluded from the Godhead, but only the creatures with which the true God is compared. The same must be understood of exclusive and superlative expressions.

units.la: 8. Deus absolute nominatus in scriptura, non nisi verus Deus intelligitur.
units.tr: 8. God named absolutely in Scripture is understood only as the true God.

units.la: 9. Quia ex Patre est Filius & Spiritus sanctus, & Pater agit per Filium & Spiritum sanctum, neq; humiliatus est, ut Filius, frequenter scriptura, praesertim Christo loquente, Patris nomine etiam Filium & Spiritum sanctum intelligit.
units.tr: 9. Because the Son and the Holy Spirit are from the Father, and the Father acts through the Son and the Holy Spirit, and is not humbled as the Son is, Scripture frequently, especially when Christ is speaking, understands the Son and the Holy Spirit under the name of the Father.

units.la: 10. Quando Deus absolute seu per se consideratur, vel creaturis opponitur, tres personae comprehenduntur. Cum autem Filio opponitur, persona deitatis prima, quae est Pater, intelligitur.
units.tr: 10. When God is considered absolutely, or in himself, or is set against creatures, all three persons are comprehended. But when he is set against the Son, the first person of the Godhead, who is the Father, is meant.

units.la: II.
units.tr: II.

units.la: 11. Distinguit persona personas, quando eas inter se opponit, aut confert, aut earum proprietates personales exprimit, quibus nomen DEI commune ad certam personam restringit. Omnes autem simul intelligit, cum verum DEUM creaturis aut fictitiis diis opponit, vel absolutè secundum suam naturam consideratur.
units.tr: 11. A person distinguishes persons when he sets them against one another, or compares them, or expresses their personal properties, by which he restricts the name of God, common to all, to a certain person. But he understands all of them together when he sets the true God against creatures or fictitious gods, or when he is considered absolutely according to his own nature.

units.la: 12. Solet Filius ad Patrem referre, quod cum ipso habet commune, non facta sui mentione, quando in persona Mediatoris loquitur.
units.tr: 12. The Son is accustomed to refer to the Father what he has in common with him, without mention of himself, when he speaks in the person of the Mediator.

units.la: 13. Filius dicitur videre, discere, audire & agere à Patre, naturæ quidem utriusque respectu: sed salvo naturarum discrimine. Mente enim ipsius humanæ voluntas Dei per revelationem ignoratur. Deitas ipsius per se perfectissimè voluntatem Patris novit, & intuetur ab æterno.
units.tr: 13. The Son is said to see, learn, hear and act from the Father, with respect to the nature of each; but with the difference of the natures preserved. For the human mind of the Son does not know the will of God through revelation. His deity knows the Father's will perfectly in itself and beholds it from eternity.

units.la: 14. Si operationes externæ trium personarum essent diversæ, facerent diversas essentias: quarum una agente, altera cessare posset.
units.tr: 14. If the external operations of the three persons were different, they would make different essences, one of which could act while the other ceased.

units.la: 15. Quando Deus dicitur pater Christi & fidelium: non sequitur, eadem ratione horum & illius patrem esse.
units.tr: 15. When God is called the Father of Christ and of believers, it does not follow that he is the Father of these in the same way as of him.

units.la: 16. Nunquam Pater sine Filio, nec Pater & Filius sine Spiritu suo fuerunt, quandoquidem nec augeri, nec minui, nec mutari deitas potest.
units.tr: 16. The Father was never without the Son, nor the Father and the Son without their Spirit, since the Godhead can be neither increased, nor diminished, nor changed.

units.la: Sophismata quaedam haereticorum contra æternam Filii deitatem breviter refutata.
units.tr: Some sophisms of the heretics against the eternal deity of the Son, briefly refuted.

units.la: 1. Unum essentia non sunt tres personae: seu, non habet tres personas. Jehova est una essentia. Ergo, &c. Resp. Maior vera est tantum de una essentia finita.
units.tr: 1. Three persons are not one essence; or, they do not have three persons. Jehovah is one essence. Therefore, etc. Answer: The major premise is true only of a single finite essence.

units.la: 2. Habens principium non est æternus. Filius habet principium. Ergo non est æternus ille Iehova, qui est pater. Resp. ad maiorem: Æternus non est, habens principium essentiæ & temporis: Filius autem dicitur habere principium non essentiæ, & temporis: sed solummodo personæ, & ordinis. Habet enim unam & æternam essentiam cum Patre, non temporali, sed æterna generatione. Egressus eius ab initio à diebus æternis. Glorifica me Pater apud temetipsum ea gloria, quam habui apud te, priusquam hic mundus exsisteret. Sicut Pater habet vitam in semetipso, sic dedit Filio habere vitam in semetipso.
units.tr: 2. He who has a beginning is not eternal. The Son has a beginning. Therefore that Jehovah who is the Father is not eternal. Answer to the major: He is not eternal who has a beginning of essence and of time. But the Son is said to have a beginning not of essence or of time, but only of person and of order. For he has one and the same eternal essence with the Father, by an eternal, not a temporal, generation. His going forth has been from the beginning, from the days of eternity. Glorify me, Father, with that glory which I had with you before the world was. As the Father has life in himself, so he has given to the Son to have life in himself.

units.la: Inst. Etiam qui personae seu originis principium habet, non est Iehova. Filius habet principium personae seu originis. Ergo. Resp. Maior universaliter est falsa. Scriptura enim docet verum, Filium esse Iehovam, & esse genitum, hoc est, habere originem personae à Patre.
units.tr: Objection: He who has a beginning of person or origin is not Jehovah. The Son has a beginning of person or origin. Therefore, etc. Answer: The major is universally false. For Scripture teaches that the Son is Jehovah, and that he is begotten, that is, that he has his origin of person from the Father.

units.la: 3. Vnitas nostra cum Deo est consensus. Vnitas Filij cum Patre talis est, qualis nostra. Vt sint vnum, sicut & nos vnum sumus. Ergo non essentiæ, sed consensus tantum est vnitas Filij cum Patre. Resp. Est plus in conclusione, quàm in præmissis: quia conclusio est vniuersalis, cùm minor sit particularis. Est enim præter consensum, alia etiam vnitas Filij cum Patre, nempe essentiæ: quia sunt vnus Deus. Ego & Pater vnum sumus. Ego in Patre, Pater in me. Qui videt me, videt Patrem. Qui est expressa imago substantiæ Patris.
units.tr: 3. Our unity with God is agreement. The unity of the Son with the Father is such as ours is. That they may be one, as we also are one. Therefore the unity of the Son with the Father is only one of agreement, not of essence. Answer: There is more in the conclusion than in the premises, because the conclusion is universal while the minor is particular. For besides agreement there is also another unity of the Son with the Father, namely of essence, because they are one God. I and the Father are one. I am in the Father, and the Father in me. He who sees me sees the Father. He is the express image of the Father's substance.

units.la: 4. In quo est tota deitas, præter eum non est alius, in quo sit tota Deitas. In Patre est tota Deitas. Ergo non etiam in Filio. Resp. Maior de deitate infinita est falsa. Tota enim essentia Deitatis infinita, quæ est in Patre, etiam est in Filio, & in Spiritu sancto. Axioma igitur est vnum ex eis, quæ vera sunt tantum de rebus finitis.
units.tr: 4. In whom is the whole Godhead, there is no other in whom the whole Godhead may be. In the Father is the whole Godhead. Therefore not also in the Son. Answer: The major, concerning infinite deity, is false. For the whole essence of the infinite Godhead, which is in the Father, is also in the Son and in the Holy Spirit. This axiom, then, is one of those which are true only of finite things.

units.la: 5. Essentia diuina non est genita. Filius est genitus. Ergo non est essentia diuina, quæ Pater. Respond. Ex puris particularibus nihil sequitur. Maior enim vniuersaliter exposita fit falsa. Quicunque est essentia diuina, non est genitus: ac si dicas: Homo non est genitus. Ergo filius non est homo. Maior vniuersaliter est falsa.
units.tr: 5. The divine essence is not begotten. The Son is begotten. Therefore the Son is not the divine essence which the Father is. Answer: Nothing follows from purely particular premises. For the major, when expressed universally, becomes false. Whoever is the divine essence is not begotten; it is as if you said: a man is not begotten; therefore the son is not a man. The major, universally taken, is false.

units.la: 6. Vbi sunt distinctæ operationes, ibi etiam essentiæ distinctæ sunt. Patris, Filij & Spiritus sancti operationes internæ sunt distinctæ. Ergo, &c. Resp. Maior est falsa. Externæ quidem operationes distinctas facerent essentias distinctas: internæ verò, vt sunt generatio Filij, & processio Spiritus sancti, adeo nullam essentiæ diuersitatem faciunt, vt vnitatem essentiæ quammaximè confirment: quia per eas ipsas fit, vt fit vna trium personarum essentia: cùm sint vnius eiusdemq; essentiæ Patris ineffabilis communicatio.
units.tr: 6. Where there are distinct operations, there the essences are also distinct. The internal operations of the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit are distinct. Therefore, etc. Answer: The major is false. External operations, indeed, would make distinct essences if they were distinct; but internal operations, such as the generation of the Son and the procession of the Holy Spirit, make no diversity of essence at all, but rather most strongly confirm the unity of essence, because by these very acts it comes about that the essence of the three persons is one, since they are the ineffable communication of one and the same essence of the Father.

units.la: 7. Christus secundum eam naturam est Filius Dei, secundum quam dicitur Filius Dei in scriptura. Sed filius dicitur tantum secundum humanam naturam. Ergo, &c. Resp. Minor est falsa, quia dicitur filius de cœlo, descendisse, in cœlo esse, cùm eâro esset in terra. Per Filium dicitur Pater omnia creasse. Hæc autem non dicuntur de Filio secundum humanam naturam.
units.tr: 7. Christ is the Son of God according to that nature according to which he is called the Son of God in Scripture. But he is called Son only according to his human nature. Therefore, etc. Answer: The minor is false, because he is said to have descended from heaven, to be in heaven when he was in fact on earth. Through the Son the Father is said to have created all things. These things, however, are not said of the Son according to his human nature.

units.la: 8. Filius habet caput, & est minor Patre. Ergo non est vna essentia cum Patre. Resp. Filius habet caput, & est minor Patre respectu naturæ humanæ, & respectu officij mediatoris. Hæc verò nihil adimunt eius deitati.
units.tr: 8. The Son has a head and is less than the Father. Therefore he is not one essence with the Father. Answer: The Son has a head and is less than the Father with respect to his human nature and with respect to the office of Mediator. But these things take nothing away from his deity.

units.la: 9. Essentia diuina est incarnata. Pater, Filius & Spiritus sanctus sunt essentia diuina. Ergo incarnati sunt Pater, Filius, & Spiritus sanctus. Resp. Ex puris particularibus nihil sequitur. Maior
units.tr: 9. The divine essence is incarnate. The Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit are the divine essence. Therefore the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit are incarnate. Answer: Nothing follows from purely particular premises. The major...

units.la: Quæst. XXXIII. DE DEITATE FILII.
units.tr: Question 33. On the Deity of the Son.

units.la: Maior non potest resolui vniuersaliter. Nam non quicquid est essentia diuina, est incarnatum, hoc est, non omnis persona in essentia diuina subsistens est incarnata: seu, non incarnata est essentia diuina in tribus personis, sed in vna tantum, nempe in persona Filij.
units.tr: The major premise cannot be resolved universally. For not whatever is the divine essence is incarnate; that is, not every person subsisting in the divine essence is incarnate. Or rather, the divine essence is not incarnate in all three persons, but in one only, namely in the person of the Son.

units.la: 10. Solus Pater est verus Deus. Vt cognoscant te solum esse verum Deum, &c. Ergo Filius non est verus Deus. Resp. 1. Exregula generali sexta. Fit oppositio non Patris, Filij & Spiritus sancti, sed Dei & idolorum atque creaturarum. Particula igitur μόνον solum non excludit a Deitate Filium & Spiritum sanctum, sed tantum ea, quibus Pater verus Deus opponitur. 2. Est fallacia diuisionis. Sequitur enim: & quem misisti Iesum Christum. Ergo in hoc etiam consistit vita æterna, vt Iesus Christus à Patre missus similiter cognoscatur esse verus Deus, sicut dicitur: Hic est verus Deus, & vita æterna. 3. Est etiam fallacia compositionis. Nam exclusiua μόνον non pertinet ad subiectum te, sed ad prædicatum verum Deum, quod articulus ostendit in Græco, ἵνα γινώσκωσι σὲ τὸν μόνον ἀληθινὸν θεόν. Sensus enim est: vt cognoscant te Patrem esse Deum illum, qui solus est verus Deus.
units.tr: 10. Only the Father is the true God: "that they may know thee, the only true God, etc." [ἵνα γινώσκωσι σὲ τὸν μόνον ἀληθινὸν θεόν]. Therefore the Son is not the true God. Answer: (1) From the sixth general rule. The opposition is not between the Father and the Son and Holy Spirit, but between God and idols and creatures. The particle "only" [μόνον] therefore does not exclude the Son and the Spirit from the Deity, but only those things to which the Father, as the true God, is opposed. (2) It is a fallacy of division. For it follows: "and Jesus Christ, whom thou hast sent." Therefore eternal life also consists in this, that Jesus Christ, sent by the Father, is likewise known to be the true God, just as it is said: "This is the true God, and eternal life." (3) It is also a fallacy of composition. For the exclusive "only" [μόνον] does not belong to the subject, "thee", but to the predicate, "true God", which the article shows in the Greek. The sense is: that they may know you, the Father, to be that God who alone is the true God.

units.la: 11. Christus discernit se à Patre dicente: Pater maior me est. Ergo non est ἴσος τῷ Patri. Resp. Discernit se à Patre. 1. Respectu naturæ humanæ. 2. Respectu officij Mediatoris. Pater igitur maior est Filio, non quoad essentiam, qua Patri Filius est æqualis, sed quoad officium & naturam humanam. Soluitur ex regula quarta generali.
units.tr: 11. Christ distinguishes himself from the Father when he says: "The Father is greater than I." Therefore he is not equal [ἴσος] to the Father. Answer: he distinguishes himself from the Father (1) with respect to his human nature, and (2) with respect to the office of Mediator. The Father is therefore greater than the Son, not in respect of essence, in which the Son is equal to the Father, but in respect of office and human nature. This is resolved by the fourth general rule.

units.la: 12. Mediator Dei & hominum non est ipse Deus. Filius est Mediator Dei & hominum. Ergo, &c. Resp. Maior est falsa: quia eadem ratione sequeretur, Mediatorem Dei & hominum, non esse hominem.
units.tr: 12. The Mediator between God and men is not God himself. The Son is the Mediator between God and men. Therefore, etc. Answer: the major premise is false, because by the same reasoning it would follow that the Mediator between God and men is not a man.

units.la: Inst. 1. Deus non est inferior Deo, hoc est, seipso. Mediator apud Deum est inferior Deo. Ergo non est Deus. Resp. Maior est vera de officio: de natura negatur, ex eadem regula quarta generali: Inæqualitas officij, non tollit æqualitatem naturæ vel personarum.
units.tr: Objection 1. God is not inferior to God, that is, to himself. The Mediator with God is inferior to God. Therefore he is not God. Answer: the major premise is true of the office, but it is denied of the nature, by the same fourth general rule. Inequality of office does not remove equality of nature or of persons.

units.la: Inst. 2. Filius est Mediator apud Iehouam, Filius non est Mediator apud ipsum. Ergo ipse non est Iehoua. Resp. Maior non est vniuersalis. Non enim quicunque est Iehoua, apud eum filius est Mediator. Est enim Mediator apud Patrem. Ex particularitate nihil sequitur.
units.tr: Objection 2. The Son is Mediator with Jehovah; the Son is not Mediator with himself. Therefore he himself is not Jehovah. Answer: the major premise is not universal. For not whoever is Jehovah has the Son as Mediator with him; the Son is Mediator with the Father. From a particular premise nothing follows.

units.la: Inst. 3. Ergo Filius & Spiritus sanctus non sunt vere placati, aut sunt placati une mediatore. Resp. Negatur consequentia: quia eadem est trium personarum voluntas. Placato Patre placatur & Filius & Spiritus sanctus. Inst. 4. Quem Filius placat, apud eum est Mediator. Placat autem non tantum Patrem, sed & seipsum. Ergo apud seipsum est Mediator: quod videtur absurdum.
units.tr: Objection 3. Therefore the Son and the Holy Spirit are not truly appeased, or they are appeased without a mediator. Answer: the inference is denied, because the will of the three persons is one and the same. When the Father is appeased, the Son and the Holy Spirit are appeased too. Objection 4. Whom the Son appeases, with him he is Mediator. But he appeases not only the Father but also himself. Therefore he is Mediator with himself, which seems absurd.

units.la: Resp. 1. ad Maiorem. Apud eum Filius est mediator proprie, quem ita placat sua satisfactione, ut ab eo consilium & voluntas placandi tanquam a fonte oriatur. Is vero est solus Pater. Itaque hoc modo Filius non est apud se mediator, sed apud solum Patrem. 2. Non est absurdum dicere, Filium etiam erga se esse mediatorem: seu suo ipsius merito placari: sicut Jehova dicit Es. 43. v. 25. Ego, ego sum, qui deleo prauaricationes tuas propter me ipsum. Hoc est, propter meum ipsius meritum. Neque enim absurdum est dicere, cum utrumque officium gerere, & Dei recipientis, & Mediatoris reconciliantis, diverso respectu: illud, quatenus Deus est, seu ratione naturae divinae: hoc est, quatenus mediator est, seu ratione officii, &c.
units.tr: Answer to the major premise of the first objection: the Son is properly Mediator with him whom he so appeases by his satisfaction that the will and purpose of appeasing arises from him as from its source. This is the Father alone. Thus in this sense the Son is not Mediator with himself, but only with the Father. (2) It is not absurd to say that the Son is also a mediator towards himself, that is, that he is appeased by his own merit, just as Jehovah says in Isaiah 43:25: "I, even I, am he that blotteth out thy transgressions for mine own sake." That is, for the sake of his own merit. Nor is it absurd to say that one and the same person bears both offices, that of God receiving and that of the Mediator reconciling, under different respects: the former insofar as he is God, that is, by reason of the divine nature; the latter insofar as he is Mediator, that is, by reason of the office, and so on.

units.la: Has obiectiones conferre licebit cum iis, quae sunt allatae supra ad locum de Trinitate personarum. Quibus enim strophis essentia divina & Trinitas oppugnatur, iisdem oppugnantur personae singulae: & quibus una oppugnatur persona, iisdem oppugnatur Dei essentia. Plures videantur volum. 1. Versini a pag. 115. usque ad pag. 125.
units.tr: These objections may be compared with those which were brought forward above under the head of the Trinity of persons. For whatever arguments are used to assail the divine essence and the Trinity, the same are used to assail the individual persons; and whatever arguments assail one person, the same assail the divine essence. More may be found in volume 1 of Versinus, from page 115 to page 125.

units.la: QVÆSTIO XXXIV.
units.tr: QUESTION 34.

units.la: Qua de causa appellas eum Dominum nostrum? RESPONSIO.
units.tr: Why do you call him our Lord? ANSWER.

units.la: Quia corpus & animam nostram a peccatis, non auro, argento, sed pretioso suo sanguine redemit, & ab omni potestate diaboli liberauit, atque ita nos sibi proprios vindicauit a.
units.tr: Because he redeemed our body and soul from sins, not with gold or silver but with his precious blood, freed us from all the power of the devil, and so claimed us as his own.

units.la: EXPLICATIO.
units.tr: EXPLANATION.

units.la: Hic duo sunt consideranda. I. Quo sensu Christus dicatur Dominus. II. Propter quas causas & quot modis sit noster Dominus.
units.tr: Two things are to be considered here. I. In what sense Christ is called Lord. II. For what reasons, and in how many ways, he is our Lord.

units.la: I. Quo sensu Christus dicatur Dominus.
units.tr: I. In what sense Christ is called Lord.

units.la: Dominus est, qui habet jus in rem, vel in personam. Christus, itaque est Dominus omnium, & noster. 1. Quia habet dominium in omnia, & in nos, hoc est, quia curat, custodit, & servat omnia, & nos maximè. 2. Quia omnia ei sunt subiecta, & nos ei sumus obligati ad seruiendum, corpore, & animo, vt per nos glorificetur.
units.tr: A lord is one who has a right over a thing or over a person. Christ, therefore, is the Lord of all things and of us. (1) Because he has dominion over all things and over us, that is, because he cares for, keeps and preserves all things, and us most of all. (2) Because all things are subject to him, and we are bound to serve him with body and soul, so that he may be glorified through us.

units.la: Ad vtram verò naturam nomen Domini pertinet? Resp. Ad vtramque: quemadmodum & nomen sacerdotis, regis, prophetæ, &c. Nomina enim officij, beneficiorum, dignitatis, beneficentiæ, quam Christus in nos exercet, tribuuntur toti personæ, non per communicationem idiomatum, vt nomina naturarum, vel proprietatum: sed proprie, ratione vtriusque naturæ. Vtraque enim natura Christi vult & exsequitur nostri redemptionem: humana fit precium redemptionis, moriendo pro nobis: diuina dat & offert Patri hoc precium, & nobis applicat. Itaque Christus est Dominus noster, non tantum respectu naturæ diuinæ, qua nos creauit: sed etiam respectu naturæ humanæ, qua resurrexit, & exaltatus est. Nam etiam, quatenus homo, Christus est omnium Angelorum & creaturarum Dominus.
units.tr: But to which nature does the name of Lord belong? Answer: to both, just as the names of priest, king, prophet, and so on do. For the names of office, of benefits, of dignity, and of the beneficence which Christ exercises towards us, are given to the whole person, not by communication of properties, as the names of the natures or of the properties are, but properly, by reason of both natures. For each nature of Christ wills and carries out our redemption: the human nature becomes the price of redemption by dying for us; the divine nature gives and offers this price to the Father and applies it to us. Thus Christ is our Lord, not only with respect to the divine nature, by which he created us, but also with respect to the human nature, by which he rose again and was exalted. For even as man Christ is the Lord of all angels and creatures.

units.la: II. Propter quas causas, & quot modis sit noster Dominus.
units.tr: II. For what reasons, and in how many ways, he is our Lord.

units.la: Christus non vna tantum ratione est Dominus noster, sed pluribus.
units.tr: Christ is our Lord not for one reason only, but for several.

units.la: 1. Iure creationis, sustentationis & gubernationis vniuersali, & sibi communi cum Patre & Spiritu sancto. Omnia mea tua sunt, & tua mea sunt. Estque hoc dominium generalissimum, quod se extendit non tantum ad nos, sed ad omnes homines, etiam ad impios, & ipsos diabolos, etsi non omnino eadem ratione ad nos, & istos. Nam 1. hos creauit ad mortem, nos ad vitam. 2. In impios & diabolos habet jus faciendi quod libet, vt præter nutum eius ne mouere quidem se possint, ac, si velit, possit eos in nihilum redigere, vt testatur historia obsessi in Euangelio. Sed præter hoc jus, quod in nos quoque habet, etiam est Dominus noster: quia custodit nos, tanquam peculium suum, & populum proprium, quem acquisiuit suo sanguine, & sanctificat suo Spiritu: præterea nos suo Spiritu regit & gubernat, in cordibus nostris fidem & obedientiam operans atque conseruans.
units.tr: (1) By the right of creation, of universal sustaining and governing, which he shares with the Father and the Holy Spirit. "All that is mine is yours, and yours is mine" (John 17:10). This dominion is the most general, extending not only to us but to all men, even the wicked, and to the devils themselves, although not in exactly the same way towards us and towards them. For (a) he created them for death, but us for life. (b) Over the wicked and the devils he has the right to do whatever he pleases, so that they cannot even stir without his nod, and if he wished he could reduce them to nothing, as the story of the demoniacs in the Gospel attests. But beyond this right, which he has over us too, he is also our Lord because he keeps us as his own property and his own people, whom he has acquired with his blood and sanctifies by his Spirit. Moreover, he rules and governs us by his Spirit, working and preserving faith and obedience in our hearts.

units.la: 2. Iure redemptionis sibi proprio: quia ipse solus est mediator, qui nos à peccato & morte suo sanguine redemit, à potestate Satanæ liberauit, & sibi proprios dicauit. Modus redemptionis est pretiosissimus: quia maius est, suo sanguine, quam pecunia redimere. Ergo jus possessionis, quod in nos habet, etiam est maximum. Quoniam verò nos liberauit, constat nos fuisse servos. Et quidem eramus serui & mancipia diaboli, à cuius tyrannide Christus nos liberauit. Hinc jam sumus serui Christi: quia nos natura hostes dignos, quos perderet, seruauit. Serui enim dicti sunt à seruando: quod cùm in bello capti ab hostibus possent interfici seruabantur. Hoc Christi dominium in nos est speciale, tantum ad Ecclesiam se extendens.
units.tr: (2) By the right of redemption, which is his own: because he alone is the mediator, who redeemed us from sin and death with his blood, freed us from the power of Satan, and dedicated us to himself as his own. The manner of redemption is most precious, because it is more costly to redeem with one's own blood than with money. Therefore the right of possession which he has over us is also the greatest. Since he has set us free, it is clear that we were slaves. Indeed we were slaves and chattels of the devil, from whose tyranny Christ freed us. Hence we are now servants of Christ, because he preserved us, who by nature were enemies worthy to be destroyed. For servants (servi) are so called from preserving (servando), since captives taken in war, who could have been killed by their enemies, were kept alive. This dominion of Christ over us is special, extending only to the Church.

units.la: Obiect. Si sumus redemti à potestate diaboli: ergo diabolo est datum pretium pro redemtione. Nam à cuius potestate redemti sumus, ei debetur pretium. At non datum est diabolo pretium à Christo. Ergo non sumus redemti à potestate diaboli. Resp.ad maiorem. A cuius potestate, scilicet tanquam supremi domini, & jure imperium in nos tenentis, redemti sumus, ei debetur pretium. Diabolus verò nequaquam, sed solus Deus est supremus noster Dominus, & solus jure imperium in nos tenet. Ergo pretium redemtionis nostræ non debebatur diabolo, sed Deo. Redegerat quidem nos Satan in suam potestatem, justo Dei judicio, propter peccatum rapiens ad se, & invadens possessionem alienam. Sed Christus fortior ille armatus, expiato peccato nostro, & fracta diaboli potentia, nos ab eius tyrannide liberauit. Respectu itaque Dei, Christus nos redemit: quia Deo persoluit pretium: respectu diaboli, nos liberauit, & in libertatem vindicauit.
units.tr: Objection. If we have been redeemed from the power of the devil, then a price was paid to the devil for our redemption. For to whoever holds power over us a price is owed when we are redeemed from it. But no price was paid to the devil by Christ. Therefore we were not redeemed from the power of the devil. Answer to the major premise. A price is owed to the one from whose power, that is, as supreme lord and holder of rightful dominion over us, we have been redeemed. But the devil is by no means such a one; God alone is our supreme Lord, and God alone rightfully holds dominion over us. Therefore the price of our redemption was owed not to the devil but to God. Indeed Satan had brought us under his power by the just judgment of God, seizing us for sin and invading another's possession. But Christ, that stronger armed man, after our sin was expiated and the power of the devil broken, freed us from his tyranny. Therefore, with respect to God, Christ redeemed us, because he paid the price to God; with respect to the devil, he set us free and claimed us into liberty.

units.la: 3. Iure conseruationis. Christus est noster Dominus: quia nos defendit usque ad finem, & custodit ad vitam æternam, non solum corpora ab injuriis tuendo, sed & animas à peccatis. Seruatio enim debet intelligi non tantum de prima ereptione à potestate diaboli, sed etiam de continua seruatione & summatione beneficiorum. De hoc dominio dicit ipse: Nemo periit ex istis, quos dedisti mihi. Omnes meas nemo rapiet, &c. Ego do eis vitam æternam. Omnem, qui ad me venit, non ejiciam foras. Impios conseruat ad interitum, & corporali defensione tantum.
units.tr: (3) By the right of preservation. Christ is our Lord because he defends us to the end and keeps us to eternal life, guarding not only our bodies from injury but also our souls from sin. For preservation must be understood not only of the first rescue from the power of the devil but also of the continual keeping and increase of benefits. Of this dominion he himself says: "None of those whom you gave me has perished. No one will snatch my own out of my hand, etc. I give them eternal life. Whoever comes to me I will not cast out" (John 6:39; 10:28; 6:37). He preserves the wicked only unto destruction, and only by bodily protection.

units.la: 4. Iure ordinationis: quia Pater λόγος, seu hanc personam Christum ad hoc ordinauit, vt per eum omnia in cœlo & in terra perficiat. Neque enim Christus tantum Dominus noster est: quia seruauit nos, hoc est, liberauit ab hostibus, & fecit ex hostibus filios Dei: sed etiam, quia nos Pater illi dedit, & eum nobis præfecit principem, regem, & caput. Constituit eum haeredem omnium. Tui erant, & dedisti mihi. Omne quod dat mihi Pater, ad me venit. Omnia subiecit eius pedibus, eumque constituit caput super omnia ipsi ecclesiæ, &c. Hunc Deus dextra sua exaltatum constituit principem ac seruatorem, vt det resipiscentiam Israeli, & remissionem peccatorum. Cùm Cum igitur Christus sit Dominus noster longè excellentiori modo, quàm aliorum, etiam longè magis nos ad obedientiam ei sumus obligati. Nam sic noster est Dominus, vt faciat quidem de nobis quod vult, & habeat absolutum jus in nos: eo verò vtatur ad nostram duntaxat salutem. Plura enim & infinitis partibus maiora beneficia ab hoc Domino accipimus, quàm vlli alij. Proinde dominium, quod in nos habet Christus, nunquam non debemus agnoscere. Agnitio autem eius dominij est 1. Professio tanti beneficij, quod ipse dignetur esse Dominus noster. 2. Confessio nostræ obligationis & officij: quoniam Christus Dominus noster tam clemens est, ergo debemus ei seruire, eum colere, & solum amare.
units.tr: (4) By the right of appointment: because the Father, the Word [λόγος], or this person, has appointed Christ to this end, that through him he may accomplish all things in heaven and on earth. For Christ is our Lord not only because he has kept us, that is, freed us from enemies and made sons of God out of enemies, but also because the Father has given us to him and set him over us as prince, king and head. "He has appointed him heir of all things" (Heb. 1:2). "They were yours, and you gave them to me" (John 17:6). "All that the Father gives me comes to me" (John 6:37). "He put all things under his feet and appointed him head over all things to the Church, etc." (Eph. 1:22). "God exalted him at his right hand as Prince and Saviour, to give repentance to Israel and forgiveness of sins" (Acts 5:31). Since Christ is therefore our Lord in a far more excellent way than others are, we are also bound to obey him far more. For he is our Lord in such a way that he indeed does with us what he wills and has absolute right over us, yet he uses that right only for our salvation. For we receive from this Lord benefits that are more numerous and greater by infinite degrees than from anyone else. Therefore we must always acknowledge the dominion which Christ has over us. Now the acknowledgement of this dominion consists in (1) a profession of so great a benefit, that he deigns to be our Lord; (2) a confession of our obligation and duty: since Christ our Lord is so merciful, we ought to serve him, worship him, and love him alone.

units.la: Quis igitur est sensus: Credo in Christum Dominum nostrum? Tres diuersæ locutiones sunt. 1. Credere Christum esse Dominum. Hoc credere non sufficit, nam etiam credimus, diabolum esse dominum: sed nec omnium, nec nostrum, sicut Christum credimus Dominum omnium nostrum. 2. Credere Christum esse Dominum omnium, & nostrum. Neque hoc satis est credere. Nam & diaboli credunt Christum esse Dominum suum, quatenus eis etiam inuitis dominatur. 3. Credere in Christum Dominum nostrum, hoc est, ita credere Christum Dominum nostrum, vt in eo fiduciam collocemus. Atque hoc est, quod præcipuè oportet nos credere. Cùm igitur dicimus, nos credere in Dominum nostrum, credimus 1. Filium Dei esse creatorem omnium rerum, ideoque ejus habere in omnes creaturas. Omnia quæ habet Pater, mea sunt. 2. Singulari autem modo esse dominum, defensorem & conseruatorem Ecclesiæ: quia redemit eam suo sanguine. 3. Filium Dei mihi quoque esse Dominum, & me quoque esse eius subditum, hoc est, me quoque eius sanguine esse redemtum, & seruari perpetuò, ac proinde me obligatum ei esse ad gratitudinem: Dominium eius mihi esse salutare: me seruari ab eo, tanquam possessionem charissimam, peculium maximo pretio emtum.
units.tr: What then is the meaning of "I believe in Christ our Lord"? There are three different expressions. (1) To believe that Christ is Lord. This belief is not enough, for we also believe that the devil is lord, but not of all things nor of us, whereas we believe Christ to be the Lord of all things and of us. (2) To believe that Christ is the Lord of all and of us. Nor is this enough to believe; for the devils too believe that Christ is their Lord, inasmuch as he rules over them even against their will. (3) To believe in Christ our Lord, that is, to believe Christ our Lord in such a way that we place our trust in him. This is what above all we ought to believe. Therefore when we say that we believe in our Lord, we believe: (a) that the Son of God is the creator of all things, and therefore has dominion over all creatures. "All that the Father has is mine" (John 16:15). (b) That he is Lord in a singular way, the defender and preserver of the Church, because he redeemed it with his blood. (c) That the Son of God is also my Lord, and that I too am subject to him, that is, that I too have been redeemed by his blood and am kept forever, and so I am bound to him in gratitude; that his dominion is salutary for me; that I am kept by him as his most dear possession, a property bought at the greatest price.

units.la: QVÆSTIO XXXV.
units.tr: QUESTION XXXV.

units.la: Quid credis, cùm dicis? Conceptus est per Spiritum sanctum, natus ex Maria virgine.
units.tr: What do you believe when you say: He was conceived by the Holy Spirit, born of the Virgin Mary?

units.la: RESPONSIO.
units.tr: ANSWER.

units.la: Quod ipse Filius Dei, qui est a & permanet verus ac æternus Deus b, naturam verè-humanam ex carne sanguine virginis Mariæ c, operatione Spiritus sancti assumsit d, vt simul sit verum semen Dauidis e, fratribus suis per omnia similis f, excepto peccato g.
units.tr: That the Son of God himself, who is and remains true and eternal God a b, assumed a truly human nature from the flesh and blood of the Virgin Mary c, by the operation of the Holy Spirit d, so that at the same time he is the true seed of David e, like his brothers in all things f, except sin g.

units.la: EXPLICATIO.
units.tr: EXPLANATION.

units.la: Huius quæstionis explicatio necessaria est propter hæreticos veteres & recentes, qui negarunt, & negant, carnem Christi ex substantia virginis assumtam esse. Eutychiani dicebant: Christus conceptus est de Spiritu sancto. Ergo caro Christi pro pagata est ex substantia diuinitatis, seu ex essentia Spiritus sancti: eoque natura diuina mutata est in humanam. Resp. Est fallacia figuræ dictionis. Particula enim ex, siue de Spiritu sancto hoc est, hic non significat materiam, sed efficientem causam, vim, efficaciam, virtutem seu operationem: & ex πνεύματος ἁγίου idem est, quod ἀπὸ πνεύματος ἁγίου: quia virtute & operatione Spiritus sancti Filius conceptus est in utero virginis, vt liquet ex verbis angeli: Spiritus sanctus superueniet in te, & virtus Altissimi obumbrabit te. Christus dicitur semen Abrahæ, filius Dauidis. Ergo carnem suam sumsit ex his patribus, non ex Spiritu sancto. Et sicut nos sumus ex Deo, quia fecit nos: sic Christus est è Spiritu sancto: quia Spiritus sancti virtute & operatione, non autem quia ex Spiritus sancti substantia conceptus est.
units.tr: An explanation of this question is necessary because of the ancient and recent heretics who denied, and still deny, that the flesh of Christ was assumed from the substance of the Virgin. The Eutychians said: Christ was conceived of the Holy Spirit. Therefore the flesh of Christ was produced from the substance of the Godhead, or from the essence of the Holy Spirit, and so the divine nature was changed into the human. Answer: this is a fallacy of figure of speech. The particle "of" (ex), or "of" (de) the Holy Spirit, here does not signify matter but the efficient cause, power, efficacy, virtue or operation; and "ex pneumatos hagiou" [ἐκ πνεύματος ἁγίου] means the same as "apo pneumatos hagiou" [ἀπὸ πνεύματος ἁγίου], that is, "from the Holy Spirit": because the Son was conceived in the womb of the Virgin by the power and operation of the Holy Spirit, as is clear from the words of the angel: "The Holy Spirit will come upon you, and the power of the Most High will overshadow you." Christ is called the seed of Abraham and the son of David. Therefore he took his flesh from these fathers, not from the Holy Spirit. And just as we are "of God" because he made us, so Christ is "of the Holy Spirit" because he was conceived by the power and operation of the Holy Spirit, not because he was conceived from the substance of the Holy Spirit.

units.la: Inst. Ergo etiam cum dicitur, Natus ex Maria virgine, particula ex non significabit materialem causam. Resp. Immo sibi significat materialem causam. Christum enim nasci oportuit ex semine Dauidis, vt esset filius Dauidis. Cum vero dicitur, Conceptus ex Spiritu sancto, non potest particula ex accipi de causa materiali. 1. Quia secus Christus non esset natus ex virgine, nec esset semen mulieris. 2. Quia Deus est immutabilis. Non igitur Spiritus sanctus mutatus est in carnem. 3. Quia λόγος assumsit carnem: non vero in eam mutatus est.
units.tr: Objection. Then, when it is said, "Born of the Virgin Mary," the particle "of" (ex) will not signify the material cause. Answer. On the contrary, it does signify the material cause there. For Christ had to be born of the seed of David, so that he might be the son of David. But when it is said, "Conceived of the Holy Spirit," the particle "of" cannot be taken as the material cause. (1) Because otherwise Christ would not have been born of a virgin, nor would he be the seed of the woman. (2) Because God is unchangeable; therefore the Holy Spirit was not changed into flesh. (3) Because the Word assumed flesh; he was not changed into it.

units.la: Quid igitur conceptio de Spiritu sancto significat? Tria complectitur. 1. Immediatam operationem Spiritus sancti in utero virginis miraculosè concipientis filium sine sanguine & semine virili, qua operatione caro Christi formata est ex sola matris virginis substantia, præter rerum finem à Deo in natura institutam. Obiect. Nos etiam formamur à Deo. Resp. Non immediatè à Deo, vt Christus, sed mediatè.
units.tr: What, then, does "conceived by the Holy Spirit" mean? It comprises three things. (1) The immediate operation of the Holy Spirit in the womb of the Virgin, who miraculously conceived the Son without blood or male seed, by which operation the flesh of Christ was formed from the substance of the mother alone, apart from the end of things established by God in nature. Objection. We too are formed by God. Answer. Not immediately by God, as Christ was, but mediately.

units.la: 2. Miraculosam sanctificationem fœtus in vtero materno, qua effecit Spiritus sanctus, ne peccatum originis in fœtum il-lum propagaretur. Non enim conueniebat λόγῳ, Filio Dei as-sumere naturam pollutam peccato. Oportuit igitur prohiberi, ne peccatum in eum transfunderetur. 1. Vt esset victima pura: quia pro peccatis nostris debuit satisfacere. 2. Vt etiam alios sanctificaret suasanctitate. 3. Vt sciremus, quicquid Filius loquitur, id esse veritatem. Quicquid enim natum est ex carne, peccatrice scilicet, & non sanctificata, caro est, mendacium & vanitas. Obiect. Natus est ex virgine peccatis obnoxia. Ergo & ipse habuit peccatum. Resp. Spiritus sanctus optimè novit separare peccatum à natura hominis; substantiam ab accidente. Peccatum enim non est de natura hominis, sed aliunde à diabolo naturæ accessit.
units.tr: (2) The miraculous sanctification of the foetus in the maternal womb, which the Holy Spirit effected, so that the sin of origin might not be propagated into that foetus. For it was not fitting that the Word, the Son of God, should assume a nature polluted by sin. It was therefore necessary that sin be prevented from being transfused into him: (a) so that he might be a pure victim, since he had to make satisfaction for our sins; (b) so that he might also sanctify others by his holiness; (c) so that we might know that whatever the Son speaks is truth. For whatever is born of flesh, that is, sinful and unsanctified flesh, is falsehood and vanity. Objection. He was born of a virgin subject to sin; therefore he too had sin. Answer. The Holy Spirit knows perfectly well how to separate sin from the nature of man, substance from accident. For sin is not of the nature of man, but came to nature from elsewhere, from the devil.

units.la: 3. Vnionem hypostaticam naturarum, diuinæ & humanæ, safctam ab eodem Spiritu sancto in vtero matris in ipso statim conceptionis articulo.
units.tr: (3) The hypostatic union of the natures, divine and human, sanctified by the same Holy Spirit in the womb of the mother, at the very moment of conception.

units.la: Est igitur sensus articuli: Conceptus de Spiritu sancto. 1. Spiritus sanctus autor fuit immediatus miraculosæ conceptionis carnis Christi. 2. Separauit à fœtu omnem impuritatem, & contagionem peccati originalis. 3. In ipso conceptionis momento vniuit carnem λόγῳ vnione hypostatica.
units.tr: The sense of the article, therefore, is this: Conceived by the Holy Spirit. (1) The Holy Spirit was the immediate author of the miraculous conception of Christ's flesh. (2) He separated from the foetus all impurity and contagion of original sin. (3) At the very moment of conception he united the flesh to the Word by the hypostatic union.

units.la: Natus ex Maria virgine. Messias debuit nasci ex virgine secundum vaticinia Prophetarum: vt esset Pontifex sine peccato: & figura spiritualis nostræ regenerationis, quæ non ex voluntate carnis, sed ex Deo est. Additur igitur in symbolo: Christum natum esse ex Maria virgine.
units.tr: Born of the Virgin Mary. The Messiah had to be born of a virgin according to the prophecies of the prophets: so that he might be a high priest without sin, and a figure of our spiritual regeneration, which is not of the will of the flesh but of God. Therefore it is added in the creed: that Christ was born of the Virgin Mary.

units.la: 1. Vt significetur veritas naturæ humanæ à Filio Dei assumtæ, Christum videlicet conceptum virtute Spiritus sancti, esse ex substantia Mariæ matris verum hominem natum. Ergo est sensus: etsi miraculosè concepta est caro Christi: tamen accepta & nata est ex virgine, &c.
units.tr: (1) So that it may be signified that the truth of the human nature assumed by the Son of God is this: that Christ, conceived by the power of the Holy Spirit, was born as a true man from the substance of his mother Mary. The sense, then, is: although the flesh of Christ was conceived miraculously, nevertheless it was received and born from the Virgin, and so on.

units.la: 2. Vt sciamus, eum esse ex iis patribus, ex quibus etiam Maria: verum Abrahæ semen, ex Abrahami semine propagatum, & filium Dauidis, ex Dauidis filia natum, juxta promissiones & vaticinia.
units.tr: (2) So that we may know that he is of those fathers from whom Mary also came: a true seed of Abraham, propagated from the seed of Abraham, and the son of David, born of the daughter of David, according to the promises and prophecies.

units.la: 3. Vt sciamus, impletam esse scripturam: Ecce virgo concipiet & pariet filium. Semen mulieris conteret caput serpentis. Ex hac impletione vaticiniorum, quibus prædictum erat, Christum natum ex virgine, & quidem nata è posteris Dauidis, & ex hoc miraculo similiter à prophetis prædicto, quod Christus è sola matre virgine est natus, certò constat, hunc hominem Iesum ex virgine natum esse promissum illum Christum seu Messiam, generis humani redemtorem.
units.tr: (3) So that we may know that the Scripture has been fulfilled: "Behold, a virgin shall conceive and bear a son" and "The seed of the woman shall bruise the head of the serpent." From this fulfilment of the prophecies, in which it was foretold that Christ would be born of a virgin, and indeed born of the posterity of David, and from this miracle likewise foretold by the prophets, that Christ was born from the mother alone, a virgin, it is certain that this man Jesus, born of a virgin, is that promised Christ or Messiah, the redeemer of the human race.

units.la: 4. Vt significetur, sanctificatum esse Christum in virginis utero virtute Spiritus sancti: ideo esse purum sine peccato.
units.tr: (4) So that it may be signified that Christ was sanctified in the womb of the virgin by the power of the Holy Spirit, and therefore is pure and without sin.

units.la: 5. Vt sciamus, esse analogiam inter Christi nativitatem & fidelium regenerationem. Generatio enim Christi ex virgine est signum spiritualis nostrae regenerationis, quae non ex sanguine, neque ex libidine carnis, neque ex libidine viri, sed ex Deo est.
units.tr: (5) So that we may know that there is an analogy between the nativity of Christ and the regeneration of believers. For the generation of Christ from a virgin is a sign of our spiritual regeneration, which is not of blood, nor of the lust of the flesh, nor of the lust of man, but of God.

units.la: QVÆSTIO XXXVI.
units.tr: QUESTION 36.

units.la: Quem fructum percipis ex sancta conceptione & nativitate Christi?
units.tr: What fruit do you receive from the holy conception and birth of Christ?

units.la: RESPONSIO.
units.tr: ANSWER.

units.la: Quod is noster sit mediator a, & sua innocentia, ac perfecta sanctitate, mea peccata, in quibus conceptus sum, tegat, ne in conspectum Dei veniant.
units.tr: That he is our mediator a, and by his innocence and perfect holiness covers my sins, in which I was conceived, so that they do not come into God's sight.

units.la: EXPLICATIO.
units.tr: EXPLANATION.

units.la: Duo sunt fructus sanctæ conceptionis & nativitatis Christi. 1. Confirmatio fidei, quod hic sit mediator. 2. Consolatio: quod huius Mediatoris puritate tecta sunt nostra peccata: ut per eum coram Deo justificemur. Ratio consequentiæ est: quia non poterat esse mediator inter Deum & homines: qui non idem esset homo purus, & sanctus, & natura Deus: qui salutem meritò nobis pararet, partamque efficacia conseruaret. Talis enim nobis conveniebat Pontifex, qui esset innocens, impollutus. Talis autem salus est Christus, ex Spiritu sancto conceptus: & ex virgine natus, absque peccato.
units.tr: There are two fruits of the holy conception and birth of Christ. (1) Confirmation of faith, that he is the mediator here. (2) Consolation: that our sins are covered by the purity of this Mediator, so that we are justified before God through him. The reasoning of the consequence is this: he could not be the mediator between God and men unless he were at once a pure and holy man and by nature God, one who would rightly obtain salvation for us and preserve the salvation obtained by his power. For such a high priest was fitting for us, one who was innocent and undefiled. Such a Saviour is Christ, conceived of the Holy Spirit and born of the virgin, without sin.

units.la: Quis igitur est sensus Articuli: Credo in Iesum Christum, conceptum de Spiritu sancto, natum ex Maria virgine? I. Credo hunc Filium Dei naturalem factum esse verum hominem: miraculoso modo, unum Christum, duabus naturis constantem: & esse à matris utero sanctificatum per Spiritum sanctum. II. Credo talem eum esse, ut me coram Deo justificet, & sanctificet: (quod non posset, nisi in ipso facta esset sanctificatio, & unio) & ut ego propropter hunc Filium sic conceptum & natum habeam vio apud Deum.
units.tr: What, then, is the sense of the Article: I believe in Jesus Christ, conceived by the Holy Spirit, born of the virgin Mary? (I) I believe that this Son of God, by nature, was made true man, in a miraculous manner, one Christ consisting of two natures, and that from his mother's womb he was sanctified by the Holy Spirit. (II) I believe that he is such that he justifies and sanctifies me before God (which he could not do unless sanctification and union had taken place in him), and that because of this Son thus conceived and born I have right before God.

units.la: DE DVABVS IN CHRISTO NATVRIS.
units.tr: Concerning the Two Natures in Christ.

units.la: Quia verò huc pertinet articulus de incarnatione, seu de duabus in Christo naturis, & de earum hypostatica vnione: aliquanto plenius explicandæ sunt quæstiones sequentes: I. An sint duæ naturæ in mediatore. II. An sint vna, an plures personæ. III. Si sit tantum vna persona, qualis igitur vnio. IV. Quare oportuerit vnionem hypostaticam fieri.
units.tr: Since the article on the incarnation, or on the two natures in Christ and their hypostatic union, belongs here, the following questions must be explained rather more fully: I. Whether there are two natures in the Mediator. II. Whether there are one or more persons. III. If there is only one person, what kind of union this is. IV.
