Si Christus pro omnibus satisfecit, omnes debent servari; respondit: Satisfecit pro omnibus, quoad sufficientiam λύτρε, sed non quoad applicationem: sequutus, ut apparet, vulgatam Scholarum distinctionem, quam & ego hactenus edi-tionibus superioribus retinui. Inventa ea videtur ad concilian-da quædam scripturarum loca, de hac quæstione in speciem repugnantia. Aliquando enim Christus dicitur mortuus esse pro omnibus, & pro toto mundo. Semetipsum degit redemptionis pretium pro omnibus, Est propitiatio pro peccatis nostris: nec pro nostris solùm: sed pro peccatis totius mundi. Vt beneficio Dei pro omnibus gustaret mortem. Si vnus pro omnibus mortuus est: ergo omnes mortui sunt; & pro omnibus mortuus est Christus, ut qui viuunt, posthac non sibi viuant, sed ei, qui pro ipsis mortuus est, & resurrexit. Aliquando contra, Christus dicitur mortuus esse & orasse, & se tradidisse, non pro omnibus, nec pro mundo: sed tantum pro multis, pro electis, pro credituris in eum: pro suo populo: pro Ecclesia: pro omnibus suis. Ego pro eis rogo: non pro mundo rogo, sed pro iis, quos dedisti mihi, quia tui sunt. Ego sanctifico me pro eis. Non pro eis autem rogo tantum, sed pro iis, qui per sermonem eorum credituri sunt in me. Filius hominis non venit, ut sibi ministraretur, sed ut ministraret, & animam suam daret redemptionis pretium pro multis. Ipse seruabit populum suum à peccatis eorum. Hoc est sanguis meus Noui Testamenti, qui pro multis effunditur in remissionem peccatorum. Christus oblatus est semel, ut peccata multorum tolleret. Seruus meus justus cognitione sui justificabit multos, quoniam iniquitates ipse portauit. Christus est seruator sui corporis: diligit Ecclesiam, & semetipsum tradidit pro ea. Ego animam pono pro quibus. Hæc & similia dicta in speciem contraria Scholastici conciliarunt distinctione Sufficientia & Efficacia mortis Christi: quòd secundum priora dicta Christus sit mortuus pro omnibus hominibus, tam infidelibus, quàm fidelibus, quantum ad sufficientiam pretij pro omnibus: secundum dicta posteriora pro solis electis credentibus, quantum ad efficaciam & fructum attinet: quoniam mors C H R I S T I in eis solis est efficax ad salutem, qui eam fide sibi applicant. Hoc autem soli electi credentes faciunt. L O M B A R D V S: Christus se obtulit DEO Trinitati pro omnibus, quantum ad pretij sufficientiam: sed pro electis tantum, quantum ad efficaciam: quia prædestinatis tantum salutem effecit.
units.tr: [I do not recall this question, nor have I found it explained by Dr Ursinus in any of his known manuscripts. For it had not yet been debated by anyone in our century. What he thought about it, however, is not unclear from what was said above, in the question on the passion of Christ (XXXVII), where, in answer to the fourth objection, If Christ satisfied for all, all ought to be saved, he replied: He satisfied for all as to the sufficiency of the ransom [λύτρον], but not as to its application. He evidently followed the common distinction of the schools, which I too have hitherto retained in the earlier editions. This distinction seems to have been devised to reconcile certain passages of Scripture that appear to conflict on this question. For at times Christ is said to have died for all and for the whole world: He gave himself a ransom for all; He is the propitiation for our sins, and not for ours only, but for the sins of the whole world; that by the grace of God he might taste death for every man; If one died for all, then were all dead; and he died for all, that those who live should no longer live to themselves, but to him who died for them and rose again. At other times, on the contrary, Christ is said to have died, and to have prayed, and to have delivered himself up, not for all, nor for the world, but only for many, for the elect, for those who would believe in him, for his people, for the Church, for all his own. I pray for them; I do not pray for the world, but for those whom thou hast given me, for they are thine. I sanctify myself for them. Nor do I pray for them only, but for those also who through their word shall believe on me. The Son of man came not to be ministered unto, but to minister, and to give his life a ransom for many. He shall save his people from their sins. This is my blood of the New Testament, which is shed for many for the remission of sins. Christ was offered once to bear the sins of many. My righteous servant shall justify many by his knowledge, for he shall bear their iniquities. Christ is the Saviour of his body; he loves the Church, and gave himself for it. I lay down my life for the sheep. The Schoolmen reconciled these and similar sayings, which seem to be contrary, by the distinction between the sufficiency and the efficacy of the death of Christ: that according to the former sayings Christ died for all men, both unbelievers and believers, as to the sufficiency of the price for all; but according to the latter sayings he died for the elect believers alone, as far as efficacy and fruit are concerned, since the death of Christ is effective for salvation only in those who apply it to themselves by faith. Only the elect believers do this. LOMBARD: Christ offered himself to God the Trinity for all, as to the sufficiency of the price, but for the elect only, as to efficacy, since he effected salvation only for the predestined.]

units.la: T H O M A S: Meritum Christi, quantum ad sufficientiam, æqualiter se habet ad omnes: non autem quantum ad efficaciam. quod accidit partim ex libero arbitrio, partim ex divina electione, per quam quibusdam misericorditer affectus meritorum Christi confertur, quibusdam verò justo Dei judicio subtrahitur.
units.tr: THOMAS: The merit of Christ, as to sufficiency, stands equally related to all; but not as to efficacy. This happens partly from free will and partly from divine election, through which the merit of Christ is conferred mercifully on some who are affected by it, while from others it is withheld by the just judgment of God.

units.la: Non dissimili distinctione olim A V G V S T I N V S est vsus adversus Pelagianorum calumniam: quod Dominum nostrum Iesum Christum non pro omnium hominum redemtione esse passum doceret, eò, quod contra Pelagianos docebat, non omnes homines esse prædestinatos: Quod, inquit, ad magnitudinem & potentiam pretij, & quod ad vnam pertinet causam generis humani: sanguis Christi redemtio est totius mundi: sed qui hoc saeculum sine fide Christi, & sine regenerationis sacramento pertranseunt, redemtionis alieni sunt; &c. Poculum quippe immortalitatis, quod confectum est de infirmitate nostra & virtute divina, (sic vocat passionem & mortem Domini) habet quidem in se vt omnibus prosit: sed si non bibitur, non proficit.
units.tr: By a distinction not unlike this, AUGUSTINE once answered the calumny of the Pelagians, who charged that he taught that our Lord Jesus Christ had not suffered for the redemption of all men, because he taught against the Pelagians that not all men are predestined. He says, as to the greatness and power of the price, and as to what pertains to the one cause of the human race: the blood of Christ is the redemption of the whole world; but those who pass through this age without the faith of Christ and without the sacrament of regeneration are strangers to the redemption; etc. For the cup of immortality, which has been prepared from our weakness and the divine power (so he calls the passion and death of the Lord), indeed has in itself that it may profit all; but if it is not drunk, it does not profit.

units.la: C A L V I N V S etiam distinctionem veram esse agnoscit: licet loco Johannes eam quadrare negat: eò quod Johannes ibi per totum mundum non intelligit singulos mundi homines, etiam infideles, (quorum propitiatio C H R I S T V S nequaquam est) sed omnes alias gentes, præter Iudæos in Christum credentes.
units.tr: CALVIN also acknowledges the distinction to be true, although he denies that it fits the passage in John, because John there does not by the whole world understand each and every man in the world, even unbelievers (for whom Christ is by no means the propitiation), but all nations other than the Jews who believe in Christ.

units.la: Hac igitur de causa ego etiam in Commentariis & Disputationibus meis hactenus distinctionem illam citra metum cavillationis retinui: existimans, nulla incommodo meritum mortis Christi (siue hæc in se absolutè, siue ad consilium Dei & voluntatem morientis Christi relatè consideretur) quoad sufficientiam quidem ad omnes homines extendi: idq; ne quisquam hominum meriti defectu causari posset, sed pereuntes sua ipsorum infidelitate reddantur ἀναπολόγητοι in Dei judicio: quoad fructum autem ctum vero & efficaciam ad solos credentes, juxta Euangelij doctrinam recte ac necessario adstringi.
units.tr: For this reason, in my Commentaries and Disputations I have hitherto retained that distinction without fear of cavil, judging that the merit of Christ's death, whether it is considered absolutely in itself or in relation to the counsel of God and the will of Christ dying, extends to all men as to sufficiency, so that no one could allege a lack of merit on the part of man, but that those who perish by their own unbelief are made without excuse [ἀναπολόγητοι] in the judgment of God; and that as to fruit and efficacy it is rightly and necessarily restricted to believers alone, according to the doctrine of the Gospel.

units.la: CÆTERVM quoniam dum vltimæ huic curæ incumbo, relatu non incerto accepi, in nupera prouinciali Synodo DORDRACENA Anno 1618. distinctionem hanc fratrum quorundam censuram non leuem, sub nomine meo, incurrisse, opportunamque aliquibus visam fuisse stabiliendis opinionibus, a veritate & a mente mea longè alienissimis: iccirco necessariam duxi, hoc loco de distinctionis eius vsu, atq; etiam abusu, commonefactionem breuem addere: quâ & fratribus omnis sinistræ suspicionis scrupulus eximatur, & scholis catecheticis nulla post fata mea errandi materia relinquatur.
units.tr: Moreover, since while I am engaged on this last care I have received, by a report not uncertain, that in the recent provincial Synod of Dordrecht in the year 1618 this distinction incurred, under my name, a censure from certain brethren that was not light, and that it seemed useful to some for establishing opinions very far removed from the truth and from my mind, I have therefore judged it necessary to add in this place a brief reminder about the use, and also the abuse, of that distinction; by which the scruple of any unfavourable suspicion may be removed from the brethren, and no matter for error may be left to the catechetical schools after my death.

units.la: Tenendum igitur:
units.tr: It must therefore be held:

units.la: I. Quòd manendo intra limites Symboli, seu in ordine causarum secundarum redemptionis nostræ, distinctio citra incommodum in Scholis obtinere possit: prout hactenus obtinuit.
units.tr: I. That, so long as it stays within the limits of the Creed, or within the order of the secondary causes of our redemption, the distinction can be retained in the schools without harm, as it has been retained hitherto.

units.la: II. Quòd ad scripturas in specie dissidentes conciliandas distinctio non sit omninò necessaria: quin etiam absque ea rectè conciliari possint: quandoquidem nulla reuera in eis est pugna: sed tam priora quàm posteriora dicta verè hoc volunt: Christum esse mortuum pro omnibus non solum Judæis, sed & gentibus in Christum credituris.
units.tr: II. That the distinction is not absolutely necessary for reconciling the Scriptures that seem to disagree. Indeed, they can be reconciled properly without it, since there is really no conflict between them. Both the earlier and the later statements mean truly this: that Christ died for all, not only for the Jews but also for the Gentiles who will believe in Christ.

units.la: III. Quòd rigidè vrgendo phrasin scripturæ (Mori pro alio) distinctio improprietate laboret, & quandam contradictionis difficultatem importet: quasi etiam pereuntes morte Christi seruentur. Nam mori pro alio in scripturis proprie est, 1. Moriali terius causa, & bono: quomodo Paulus dicit, se premi, pati, mori pro Corinthiis, Colossensibus, pro ecclesia, hoc est, eorum causa, & bono, seu (vt ipse interpretatur) pro ipsorum consolatione & salute. Sic Johannes nos debere animam ponere pro fratribus: hoc est, pro fratrum bono & salute. 2. Mori alterius vice & loco, ita, vt alius, pro quo quis moritur, à morte liberetur, & in vita seruetur: quomodo Dauid optabat mori pro Absolomo: Fili mi Absolom, quis dabit mihi mori pro te? pro: Vtinam ego morluus essem tuo loco, vt tu viueres. Sic Paulus dicit: pro iusto fortasse aliquem mori sustinere, h.e. justi vice & loco mori, & eum à morte seruare. Christus verò pro nobis impiis, peccatoribus, & (vt Petrus addit) iustum pro iniustis mortuum esse: h.e. nos impios, peccatores, mortis reos, morte sua à morte liberasse: & in vitam æternam seruasse. Ipse etiam optat fieri anathema à Christo pro fratribus: hoc est, à Christo damnari, fratrum Judæorum loco; vt ipsi per Christum stum seruarentur. Denique Christus pastor bonus reliquit vitam suam pro ouibus, vt nullam earum perire sit possibile. Neutro autem horum modorum proprie dici potest, Christum pro omnibus etiam infidelibus, hoc est, infidelium causa & bono, vel vice & loco, ita vt infideles per Christi mortem non moriantur, sed æternum viuant, siue sufficienter, siue efficienter mortuum esse, quin prædicta implicetur contradictio, percuntes morte Christi seruari.
units.tr: III. That if the phrase of Scripture (to die for another) is pressed rigidly, the distinction suffers from impropriety and implies a certain difficulty of contradiction, as though those who perish were also saved by the death of Christ. For to die for another in Scripture properly means: (1) to die for the sake and good of another, as Paul says that he suffers, endures and dies for the Corinthians, for the Colossians, for the Church, that is, for their sake and good, or (as he himself explains it) for their consolation and salvation. So John says that we ought to lay down our life for the brethren, that is, for the good and salvation of the brethren. (2) To die in the place and stead of another, so that the one for whom someone dies is freed from death and kept alive. So David wished to die for Absalom: My son Absalom, who will give me to die for you? that is, Would that I had died in your place, so that you might live. So Paul says: For a righteous man one would perhaps dare to die, that is, to die in the place of the righteous man and to save him from death. But Christ died for us, who were ungodly and sinners, and (as Peter adds) the just for the unjust: that is, by his death he freed us, the ungodly, sinners, guilty of death, from death and preserved us to eternal life. He himself also wishes to be made accursed by Christ for the brethren, that is, to be condemned by Christ in the place of the Jewish brethren, so that they might be saved through Christ. Lastly, Christ the good shepherd laid down his life for the sheep, so that it is impossible for any of them to perish. But in neither of these ways can it properly be said that Christ died for all, even for unbelievers, that is, for the sake and good of unbelievers or in their place and stead, so that unbelievers do not die through the death of Christ but live forever, whether he died sufficiently or efficiently, without the contradiction described above being involved: that those who perish are saved by the death of Christ.

units.la: IV. Quòd deniq; vel sola proprietate phrasεως, Mori pro alio, facile elidantur opiniones Pelagianæ, quæ distinctionis huius prætextu & abusu colorantur, de vniuersali electione, vel de vniuersali reconciliatione: vel de vniuersalis reconciliationis impetratione, vel de vniuersalibus mortis Christi fructibus: &c. Quæ omnes, sicut se intra limites distinctionis non continent: sic in vnum collimant pernitiosum scopum, vt hinc quidé æterna Dei prædestinatio, quâ ille saluandos à non saluandis certo consilio discreuit, & nouit, qui sint sui, subuertatur: inde verò idolum humani arbitrij stabiliatur; quasi ab eo, vel solo, vel maiorem partem sluat seruandorum & non seruandorum discretio: contra illud: Quis te discreuit?
units.tr: IV. That, finally, the Pelagian opinions, which are coloured by the pretext and abuse of this distinction, are easily overthrown by the proper sense of the phrase to die for another alone: opinions concerning a universal election, or a universal reconciliation, or the universal obtaining of reconciliation, or universal fruits of Christ's death, etc. All of these, just as they do not keep within the limits of the distinction, so aim at one pernicious goal: that from them the eternal predestination of God, by which he distinguished with a certain counsel those to be saved from those not to be saved, and knows who are his own, is overturned; and from them the idol of human free will is established, as though the distinction between those who are saved and those who are not flowed from that alone, or from the greater part of it. This is against the words: Who maketh thee to differ? [τίς σε διακρίνει]

units.la: Quibus ita præmonitis, jam per me vtatur distinctione, vel abstineat, qui volet. Nihil ad eam, vel ad me, Pelagianæ opiniones: quibus ea prætexi solet. Respondendum nunc est ad duas præcipuas obiectiones.
units.tr: With these things thus forewarned, let whoever wishes use the distinction through me, or abstain from it. The Pelagian opinions, under cover of which it is usually put forward, have nothing to do with it or with me. Now we must answer the two principal objections.

units.la: Obiectio I. Promissio Euangelij est vniuersalis, ad omnes pertinens: Ergo etiam fructus mortis Christi. Respond. Conceditur totum; sub conditione fidei ac pœnitentiæ. Omnibus enim debet annunciari promissio Euangelij, & fructus mortis Christus: omnesque percipiunt, qui credunt Euangelio, & agunt pœnitentiam. Qui verò non credunt, super eos manet ira Dei.
units.tr: Objection I. The promise of the Gospel is universal, pertaining to all. Therefore the fruits of Christ's death are also universal. Answer. The whole is granted, under the condition of faith and repentance. For the promise of the Gospel and the fruits of Christ's death ought to be announced to all, and all who believe the Gospel and repent receive them. But on those who do not believe, the wrath of God remains.

units.la: Obiectio II. Si Christus non est mortuus etiam pro infidelibus & reprobis, nihil habebunt isti, quod credant: aut falsum credunt: quod vtrumque absurdum. Resp. Neutrum absurdum: infidelis contra absurdum & falsum vtrumque, quod ponitur, infideles, reprobos, hoc est, eos, qui non credunt, nec credere volunt Euangelio, debere habere, quod credant, vel credere. Aut enim hi credunt Euangelio, aut non credunt. Si credunt, cadit vtrumque absurdum, quod prætenditur: quia non erunt infideles, neque probi: nec credent falsum: quia credent Euangelio. Si non credunt Euangelio, habebunt illi quidem, quod credere debent, Euangelium, Christum morte sua redemisse omnes in ipsum credentes: verum sine absurditate falsum crederent, si Christum, ipsos etiam non credentes, nec credere volentes, morte sua redemisse, sibi persuaderent: quia ipsi sibi contra Euangelium nefariè illuderent, non minus, quàm si cæci sine oculis se videre: vel ebrij, in crapula sua se bene sobrios contra sensum stultè somniarint.]
units.tr: Objection II. If Christ did not die also for unbelievers and the reprobate, they will have nothing to believe, or they believe what is false; both of which are absurd. Answer. Neither is absurd. The unbeliever is supposed to have something to believe, and to believe it, which is absurd and false in both respects, namely that unbelievers and the reprobate, that is, those who do not believe and are unwilling to believe the Gospel, ought to have something to believe. For either these men believe the Gospel or they do not. If they believe it, both absurdities alleged fall away: they will not be unbelievers or reprobate, nor will they believe what is false, since they will believe the Gospel. If they do not believe the Gospel, they will indeed have the Gospel to believe, that Christ by his death has redeemed all who believe in him; yet they would believe falsely, without any absurdity, if they persuaded themselves that Christ by his death had redeemed them, even though they do not believe and are unwilling to believe. For they would wickedly deceive themselves against the Gospel, no less than if the blind were to think they see without eyes, or the drunken, in their drunkenness, were foolishly to dream against their senses that they are quite sober.

units.la: QVÆSTIO XLI.
units.tr: QUESTION XLI.

units.la: Quare etiam sepultus est?
units.tr: Why was he also buried?

units.la: RESPONSIO.
units.tr: ANSWER.

units.la: Vt eo testatum faceret, se verè mortuum esse a.
units.tr: To show by this that he had truly died.

units.la: EXPLICATIO.
units.tr: EXPLANATION.

units.la: Causæ sepulturæ Christi sunt plures.
units.tr: There are several causes of Christ's burial.

units.la: 1. Sepeliri voluit, & debuit, in testimonium veræ mortis, vt cum verè mortuum esse constaret. Non enim sepeliri solent viui, sed mortui. Quemadmodum igitur post resurrectionem se videndum & contrectandum præbuit, vt constaret de veritate corporis resuscitati: sic post mortem præbuit se palpandum & sepeliendum, vt constaret, esse factum verum cadauer. Hue pertinent aliquot partes historiæ, quod mortuus est lancea perfossus, quod de cruce sublatus, quod vnctus, quod linteis inuolutus, &c. Quæ omnia veritatem mortis ostenderunt. Ex sepultura igitur certi sumus de vera ipsius morte: ex hac autem de vera nostri redemtione. Nam in eius morte, cuius testimonium est sepultura, consistit nostra salus.
units.tr: 1. He willed and ought to be buried, as a testimony to his true death, so that it might be established that he had really died. For the living are not usually buried, but the dead. Therefore, just as after the resurrection he presented himself to be seen and handled, so that the truth of his raised body might be established, so after death he presented himself to be touched and buried, so that it might be established that he had become a true corpse. To this pertain several parts of the history: that he was pierced with a lance when dead, that he was taken down from the cross, that he was anointed, that he was wrapped in linen cloths, and so on. All of these showed the truth of his death. From the burial, then, we are certain of his true death, and from his death, of our true redemption. For our salvation consists in his death, of which the burial is the testimony.

units.la: 2. Vt postrema pars humiliationis accederet. Erat enim hæc quoq; pars poenæ, maledictionis & ignominiæ, quam meriti eramus, videlicet sepultura, secundum dictum: In pulverè reuerteris. Est quidem corpus mortuum sensus expers. Nihilominus ignominiosum fuit, corpus ipsius in terram proijci, non minus quam aliud cadauer. Sicut igitur resurrectio ex sepulchro est pars gloriæ, sic sepultura, & demissio inter cadauera fuit pars humilitatis & ignominiarum, quas nostra causa sustinuit. Non enim decreuit cadauer fieri propter nos.
units.tr: 2. So that the final part of his humiliation might be added. For this too was a part of the punishment, curse and ignominy that we had deserved, namely burial, according to the saying: Dust you are, and to dust you shall return. A dead body is indeed without sensation. Nevertheless it was ignominious for his body to be cast into the earth, no less than any other corpse. Just as the resurrection from the tomb is a part of his glory, so his burial and lowering among the corpses was a part of the humiliation and ignominy that he endured for our sake. For he did not decree that a corpse should come into being on our account.

units.la: 3. Voluit sepeliri, ne nos exhorresceremus sepulchrum, sed sciremus; ipsius sepultura nostra sepulchra sanctificata esse, vt jam nobis non sint sepulchra, sed cubilia, in quibus placidè requiescamus, donec in vitam resuscitemur.
units.tr: 3. He willed to be buried so that we should not shrink from the grave, but know that by his burial our graves have been sanctified, so that they are no longer tombs to us but beds, in which we may rest peacefully until we are raised to life.

units.la: 4. Vt constaret de vera ipsius resurrectione; quod verè vicisset, atque sua ipsius virtute à se depulisset mortem: nec esset resurresurrectio phantastica, sed vera, reuiuiscentis cadaueris resuscitatio.
units.tr: 4. So that the truth of his own resurrection might be established: that he had truly conquered and by his own power had driven death away from himself, and that the resurrection would not be a phantom but a true raising of a revived body.

units.la: 5. Vt confirmaret in nobis spem resurrectionis, fore nimirum, vt ipsius exemplo & virtute nos quoque sepeliamur & resurgamus: scientes, Christum caput nostrum iter nobis aperuisse à sepulchro ad gloriam.
units.tr: 5. To strengthen in us the hope of resurrection: that by his example and power we too shall be buried and rise again, knowing that Christ our head has opened for us a path from the grave to glory.

units.la: 6. Vt nos spiritualiter mortui jam quiescamus à peccato: Sepulti sumus vna cum Christo per baptismum in mortem, vt sicut Christus à mortuis excitatus est ad gloriam Patris: ita & nos in nova vita ambulemus.
units.tr: 6. So that we, spiritually dead, may now rest from sin: We are buried together with Christ through baptism into death, so that just as Christ was raised from the dead to the glory of the Father, so we too may walk in newness of life.

units.la: 7. Deniq; vt veritas responderet typo Jonæ, & implerentur vaticinia de sepultura Messiæ. Non derelinques animam meam in sepulchro. Expositi improbis sepulchrum eius,
units.tr: 7. Finally, so that the truth might correspond to the type of Jonah, and the prophecies about the burial of the Messiah might be fulfilled: You will not leave my soul in the grave. His grave was appointed with the wicked.

units.la: QVÆSTIO XLII. At cum Christus pro nobis mortem oppetierit, cur nobis quoque est moriendum. RESPONSIO.
units.tr: QUESTION XLII. But since Christ underwent death for us, why must we also die?

units.la: Mors nostra non est pro peccatis nostris satisfactio , sed peccati abolitio, & transitus in vitam æternam .
units.tr: Our death is not a satisfaction for our sins, but the abolition of sin and a passage into eternal life.

units.la: a Marci 8, 37. Psal. 49, 8. b Phil. 3, 2. Iob. 8, 24. Rom. 7, 24.
units.tr: a Mark 8:37. Ps. 49:8. b Phil. 3:2. Job 8:24. Rom. 7:24.

units.la: EXPLICATIO.
units.tr: EXPLANATION.

units.la: Est explicatio obiectionis: Pro quo moritur alius, is non debet ipse mori; alioqui Deus videtur geminam satisfactionem exigere pro vna culpa. Pro nobis Christus est mortuus. Ergo nos non debemus mori. Resp. Concedo; non debemus mori, tamen satisfaciendi causa. Sic enim nos non morimur: sed sunt aliæ causæ, cur nobis sit moriendum: nimirum vt percipiamus bona alterius morte parta: vt expurgentur peccata, & fiat transitus ad viam. Mors igitur temporalis nostra non est satisfactio pro peccatis. Sed 1. admonitio de reliquiis peccatorum in nobis. 2. Admonitio de peccati magnitudine. 3. Purgatio à reliquiis peccati. 4. Requies à peccato. 5. Traductio in vitam æternam. Per mortem enim corporalem fit fidelium in vitam æternam transitus. Inst. Sublata causa tollitur effectus. In nobis sublata est causa mortis, peccatum. Ergo etiam effectus, mors ipsa tolli debet. Resp. ad maiorem: Effectus tollitur, vbi sublata est causa, scilicet omnis. In nobis verò non omnis causa mortis est sublata, quoad expurgexpurgationem peccati: etsi sublata est quoad peccati remissionem. Sublatum est peccati formale, reatus: materiale nondum est planè expurgatum, sed derelinquitur in nobis, paulatim expurgandum, vt habeamus exercitia poenitentiae & precum, donec in altera vita perfectè à peccatorum reliquiis liberemur.
units.tr: This is an explanation of an objection: whoever dies for another ought not himself to die; otherwise God would seem to demand a double satisfaction for one guilt. Christ died for us; therefore we ought not to die. Answer: I grant it: we ought not to die for the sake of satisfaction. For in this way we do not die; but there are other reasons why we must die, namely: to receive the benefits won by another's death, that sins may be purged and a passage to the way may be made. Our temporal death, therefore, is not a satisfaction for sins. But (1) it is a reminder of the remnants of sin in us; (2) a reminder of the greatness of sin; (3) a purging from the remnants of sin; (4) rest from sin; (5) a conveyance into eternal life. For it is through bodily death that the passage of believers into eternal life takes place. Objection: when the cause is removed, the effect is removed. In us the cause of death, sin, has been removed; therefore death itself too ought to be removed. Answer to the major premise: an effect is removed when its cause is wholly removed. In us, however, not every cause of death has been removed as regards the purging of sin, although it has been removed as regards the remission of sin. The formal element of sin, its guilt, has been taken away; the material element has not yet been fully purged, but is left in us, to be purged gradually, so that we have the exercises of repentance and prayer, until in the other life we are wholly freed from the remnants of sin.

units.la: QVÆSTIO XLIII.
units.tr: QUESTION 43.

units.la: Quid praeterea capimus commodi ex crucifixione, morte, & sepultura Christi? RESPONSIO.
units.tr: What further benefit do we receive from the crucifixion, death, and burial of Christ? ANSWER.

units.la: Quod virtute eius mortis, vetus noster homo vnà cum eo crucifigitur, interimitur, ac sepelitur a, ne prauae cupiditates & desideria carnis posthac in nobis regnent b, sed nos ipsos ei hostiam gratitudinis offeramus c.
units.tr: By the virtue of his death, our old man is crucified together with him, put to death, and buried, a so that wicked lusts and the desires of the flesh may no longer reign in us, b but that we may offer ourselves to him as a sacrifice of gratitude. c

units.la: a Rom. 6, 6. b Rom. 6,6. c Rom. 12,1.
units.tr: a Rom. 6:6. b Rom. 6:6. c Rom. 12:1.

units.la: EXPLICATIO.
units.tr: EXPLANATION.

units.la: Haec quaestio est de fructibus mortis Christi. Finis & fructus hic etiam iidem sunt, vt in passione: diuerso respectu. Quos enim Christus habuit fines in moriendo, ij nobis sunt fructus in percipiendo. Fructus igitur siue vtilitates mortis Christi, sunt totum opus redemtionis, videlicet:
units.tr: This question concerns the fruits of the death of Christ. The end and the fruit here are also the same as in the passion, though viewed in a different respect. For the ends that Christ had in dying are the fruits that we receive in being partakers of them. The fruits, or benefits, of the death of Christ are therefore the whole work of redemption, namely:

units.la: 1. Iustificatio & remissio peccatorum: quia iustitia postulat, vt Deus peccantem non bis puniat. In Christo autem puniuit nostra peccata. Ideo eadem in nobis non puniet. Sanguis Iesu Christi purgat nos ab omni peccato: nempe tam originali, quam actuali, tam facti, quam omissionis. Iustificati igitur, hoc est, absoluti sumus à reatu, tam poenae, quam culpae, propter Christi mortem. Huius effectus causa est mors Christi,
units.tr: 1. Justification and the remission of sins: because justice requires that God not punish a sinner twice. But in Christ he has punished our sins; therefore he will not punish the same sins in us. "The blood of Jesus Christ cleanses us from all sin" (1 John 1:7): namely original sin as well as actual, sins of commission as well as of omission. We are therefore justified, that is, absolved from the guilt both of punishment and of fault, on account of the death of Christ. The cause of this effect is the death of Christ.

units.la: 2. Regeneratio seu instauratio naturae, per Spiritum sanctum: quia Christus moriendo nobis meritus est, non tantum peccati condonationem, sed etiam peccati expurgationem per Spiritum sanctum: morte, inquam, sua impetrauit nobis non tantum peccatorum remissionem: sed etiam Dei in nobis habitationem & sanctificatio. Ego & Pater veniemus, & mansionem apud eum faciemus.
units.tr: 2. Regeneration, or the restoration of nature, through the Holy Spirit: because by dying Christ merited for us not only the forgiveness of sin but also the cleansing of sin through the Holy Spirit. By his death, I say, he obtained for us not only the remission of sins but also the indwelling of God in us and sanctification. "I and the Father will come, and make our abode with him" (John 14:23).

units.la: Est autem mors Christi tam justificationis, quàm regenerationis nostræ causa efficiens dupliciter. 1. Respectu Dei: quia Deus propter meritum & mortem Christi nobis remittit peccata, donat nos Spiritu sancto, & restituit in nobis suam imaginem. Justificati sanguine eius. Reconciliati Deo per mortem Filij eius. Quia estis filij, misit Deus Spiritum Filij sui in corda vestra, clamantem, Abba Pater. 2. Respectu nostri: quia nos, qui credimus, Christum nobis sua morte peperisse justitiam & Spiritum sanctum, facere non possumus, quin simus ipsi grati, & studeamus ita viuere, ut simus ei honori, quod fit novitate vitæ. Applicatio mortis Christi & eius consideratio, non sinit nos esse ingratos, sed pellit nos ad Christum redamandum, ad gratitudinem pro tanto beneficio præstandum. Ideo non est fingenda remissio peccatorum sine regeneratione. Qui hanc non habet, nec illam habet. Mentitur, qui gloriatur de fiducia mortis Christi sibi applicatæ, & non habet studium viuendi piè & sanctè: ita ut Christo sit honori & gratus. Omnes fide justificati se comparant ad grata Deo facienda; non potest enim studium obediendi Deo separari ab applicatione, nec beneficium regenerationis à justificationis beneficio. Omnes igitur justificati etiam regenerantur, & omnes regenerati sunt justificati.
units.tr: The death of Christ is the efficient cause of both our justification and our regeneration, in two ways. 1. With respect to God: because God, on account of the merit and death of Christ, forgives us our sins, grants us the Holy Spirit, and restores his image in us. "Justified by his blood" (Rom. 5:9); "reconciled to God by the death of his Son" (Rom. 5:10); "Because you are sons, God sent the Spirit of his Son into your hearts, crying, Abba, Father" (Gal. 4:6). 2. With respect to us: because we who believe cannot but be grateful to him, since Christ by his death has obtained for us righteousness and the Holy Spirit, and we strive to live in such a way that we bring honour to him, which is done by newness of life. The application and consideration of the death of Christ does not allow us to be ungrateful, but drives us to love Christ in return and to render gratitude for so great a benefit. Therefore the remission of sins must not be imagined without regeneration. Whoever does not have the one does not have the other. He lies who boasts of trust in the death of Christ applied to himself, and yet has no zeal to live piously and holily, so as to be an honour to Christ and pleasing to him. All who are justified by faith set themselves to do what is pleasing to God; for zeal to obey God cannot be separated from application, nor the benefit of regeneration from the benefit of justification. All who are justified are therefore also regenerated, and all who are regenerated are justified.

units.la: Obiect. Apostolus Rom. 6, 4. regenerationem tribuit resurrectioni; quomodo igitur hic tribuitur morti? Resp. Tribuitur utrique: morti quoad meritum: moriendo enim regenerationem nobis est meritus: & resurrectioni, quoad applicationem: resurgendo enim nobis applicat regenerationem, dans nobis Spiritum sanctum.
units.tr: Objection. The Apostle in Rom. 6:4 ascribes regeneration to the resurrection; how then is it ascribed here to the death? Answer. It is ascribed to both: to the death with respect to merit, for by dying he merited regeneration for us; and to the resurrection with respect to application, for by rising he applies regeneration to us, giving us the Holy Spirit.

units.la: 3. Vita æterna etiam est fructus mortis Christi. Sic Deus dilexit mundum, ut Filium suum unigenitum daret, (nempe in mortem) ut omnis qui credit, non pereat, sed habeat vitam æternam. Vitam æternam dedit nobis, & hæc vita in Filio eius est.
units.tr: 3. Eternal life is also a fruit of the death of Christ. "God so loved the world that he gave his only-begotten Son (namely to death), that whoever believes in him should not perish but have eternal life" (John 3:16). "He has given us eternal life, and this life is in his Son" (1 John 5:11).

units.la: Jam quid est credere in Christum mortuum? Est credere Christum pro me passum esse non modo summos cruciatus, sed ipsam etiam mortem: & moriendo mihi impetrasse remissionem peccatorum, reconciliationem cum Deo, & Spiritum sanctum, inchoantem in me novam vitam, ut denuo fiam templum Dei, tandemque vitam æternam consequar, in qua Deum in æternam celebrem.
units.tr: Now what is it to believe in Christ who died? It is to believe that Christ suffered for me not only the greatest torments but even death itself, and by dying obtained for me the remission of sins, reconciliation with God, and the Holy Spirit, who begins a new life in me, so that I may again become a temple of God, and at last obtain eternal life, in which I may praise God forever.

units.la: QVÆSTIO XLIV. Ctr additur? Descendit ad inferos.
units.tr: QUESTION XLIV. Why is this added? He descended into hell.

units.la: RESPONSIO.
units.tr: ANSWER.

units.la: Vt in summis doloribus & grauissimis tentationibus, me consolatione hac sustentem, quod Dominus meus Iesus Christus in narrabilibus animi sui angustiis, cruciatibus, & terroribus, in quos cùm antea a, tum maximè in cruce pendens fuerat demersus, me ab angustiis & cruciatibus inferni liberauit b.
units.tr: That in the greatest sorrows and the most grievous temptations I may sustain myself with this consolation: that my Lord Jesus Christ, in the unspeakable anguish of his soul, his sufferings and terrors, into which he had been plunged both before and above all while hanging on the cross, freed me from the anguish and torments of hell. a b

units.la: EXPLICATIO.
units.tr: EXPOSITION.

units.la: DE DESCENSU AD INFEROS.
units.tr: ON THE DESCENT INTO HELL.

units.la: Duo hic excutienda sunt: I. Verus sensus articuli. II. Vsus eiusdem.
units.tr: Two things must be examined here: I. The true sense of the article. II. Its use.

units.la: I. Quis sit verus sensus huius articuli: seu quid sit descensus Christi ad inferos.
units.tr: I. What is the true sense of this article, or what is the descent of Christ into hell?

units.la: Infernus in scriptura tripliciter accipitur. 1. Pro sepulchro: Deducetis canos meos cum dolore in infernum. Non derelinques animam meam in inferno. 2. Pro loco damnatorum, vt in historia diuitis & Lazari. Epulo in inferno sublatis oculis, cùm esset in tormentis, vidit Abraham procul. Si strauero lectum meum in inferno &c. 3. Pro summis angustiis & doloribus. Dolores mortis circumdederunt me, & angores inferni occupauerunt me. Dominus deducit in infernum & reducit, hoc est, in summos cruciatus, ex quibus denuo eripit.
units.tr: In Scripture "hell" is taken in three ways. (1) For the grave: "You will bring my grey hairs down with sorrow into hell" (Gen. 42.). "You will not leave my soul in hell" (Ps. 16.). (2) For the place of the damned, as in the story of the rich man and Lazarus: "In hell, lifting up his eyes, when he was in torments, Dives saw Abraham afar off" (Luke 16.). "If I make my bed in hell, behold, you are there" (Ps. 139.). (3) For extreme distress and pain: "The sorrows of death compassed me, and the pains of hell took hold upon me" (Ps. 116.). "The Lord brings down to hell and brings up again," that is, into the utmost torments, from which he again rescues.

units.la: In hoc articulo infernus accipitur tertia significatione, pro summis angustiis, &c. Nam prima significatione pro sepultura accipi non potest. 1. Quia praecedit: sepultus est. Si quis articulum posteriorem prioris exegesin dicat, nihil dixerit. Quoties enim duae locutiones rem eandem exprimentes coniunguntur, ita vt altera sit exegesis alterius: posteriorem priore clariorem esse conuenit. Hic vero contra fieret. Nam obscurius est, descendere ad inferos, quam sepeliri. 2. Non est verisimile, in symbolo tam breui & succincto eundem articulum bis poni, seu, idem bis dici verbis commutatis. Non etiam secunda, pro loco damnatorum, in
units.tr: In this article "hell" is taken in the third sense, for extreme distress, and so on. For it cannot be taken in the first sense, for burial. (1) Because it follows: "he was buried." If someone says that the later clause is an explanation of the earlier, he says nothing. For whenever two expressions that express the same thing are joined, so that one is the explanation of the other, the later ought to be clearer than the earlier. Here, however, the reverse would happen, for "to descend into hell" is more obscure than "to be buried." (2) It is not likely that in so brief and succinct a creed the same article would be stated twice, that is, the same thing said twice in changed words. Nor can the second sense, the place of the damned, be taken here either.

units.la: Q in quem Christus descenderit. Probatur divisione. Diuinitas non descendit: quia est & erat vbique. Neq; corpus: quia id triduum requieuit in sepulchro, juxta typum Jonæ: nec aliunde resurrexit, quam ex sepulchro.
units.tr: The question is into what place Christ descended. It is proved by division. The divinity did not descend, because it is and was everywhere. Nor did the body, because it rested for three days in the sepulchre, according to the type of Jonah, and it rose from nowhere but the sepulchre.

units.la: Neque anima Christi descendit.
units.tr: Nor did the soul of Christ descend.

units.la: 1. Quia scriptura nusquam hoc expressit.
units.tr: (1) Because Scripture nowhere expresses this.

units.la: 2. Quia de hac dicit Christus, moriens in cruce: Pater, in manus tuas depono spiritum meum. Et ad latronem: Hodie mecum eris in paradiso. Anima igitur Christi post mortem fuit in manu Patris, in paradiso, non in inferno. Nec valet cavillatio: Etiam in inferno erat in manu Patris, secundum illud: Si stravero lectum meum in inferno, tu illic es: hoc est, erat Deo curæ, custoditum, ne periret. Dictum enim prius: In manus tuas, &c. dedebatur, ne periret. Dictum enim prius: In manus tuas, &c. declarandum est per posterius: Hodie mecum eris in paradiso. Hoc autem loquitur de felicitate & liberatione, quæ non est in inferno: quia sensus est: Uterque qui jam patimur, hodie futuri sumus in paradiso, loco salutis & felicitatis sempiternæ, ab istis cruciatibus liberati. Paradisus autem non est infernus, nec in inferno, qui est locus tormenti. Hinc etiam liquet, Christum hoc dixisse latroni, non de divinitate, sed de anima, quæ cum corpore patiebatur. Nam divinitas jam erat cum latrone: sed sequeque Christus secundum eam patiebatur aut liberabatur, secundum animam.
units.tr: (2) Because Christ, dying on the cross, says of this soul: "Father, into your hands I commend my spirit." And to the thief: "Today you will be with me in paradise." Therefore the soul of Christ after death was in the hand of the Father, in paradise, not in hell. Nor does the quibble hold that it was also in the hand of the Father in hell, according to the words "If I make my bed in hell, you are there"; that is, it was under God's care and kept so that it should not perish. For the earlier words, "into your hands," must be explained by the later, "Today you will be with me in paradise." This speaks of happiness and deliverance, which is not in hell, because the sense is: we who now suffer will today be in paradise, in the place of salvation and eternal happiness, freed from these torments. Paradise, however, is not hell, nor is it in hell, which is the place of torment. Hence it is also clear that Christ said this to the thief not of the divinity but of the soul, which was suffering together with the body. For the divinity was already with the thief; but Christ, according to the soul, was suffering or being delivered.

units.la: 3. Si descendit in infernum anima, descendit, vel, ut ibi pateretur aliquid: vel, ut inde liberaret patres, ut asseruerunt pontifices. At non descendit passurus aliquid, quia in cruce pendens dixit: Consummatum est. Nec asseruit patres. 1. Quia hoc fecit patiendo pro ipsis in terra. 2. Fecit idem potentia & efficacia suæ divinitatis inde ab initio mundi, non animæ aut corporis locali descensu ad inferos. 3. Patres non fuerunt in inferno. Ergo non potuerunt inde liberari. Iustorum animæ in manu Dei sunt, & non attingit eas cruciatus. Inter nos & vos hiatus ingens constitutus est, ut illi, qui volunt huc transfire ad nos, non possint, neque ii huc hinc transfire. Et Lazarus etiam ante Christi ascensionem moriens portabatur ab angelis in sinum Abrahæ, locum solatij, seu paradisum, non in limbum inferni.
units.tr: (3) If the soul descended into hell, it descended either to suffer something there, or to deliver the fathers from there, as the Pontiffs have asserted. But it did not descend to suffer anything, because hanging on the cross he said: "It is finished." Nor did it deliver the fathers. (a) Because he did this by suffering for them on earth. (b) He did the same by the power and efficacy of his divinity from the beginning of the world, not by a local descent of his soul or body into hell. (c) The fathers were not in hell; therefore they could not be delivered from there. "The souls of the righteous are in the hand of God, and torment does not touch them. Between us and you a great gulf is fixed, so that those who wish to pass from here to us cannot, nor can those from there pass to us." And Lazarus, too, when he died before the ascension of Christ, was carried by angels into the bosom of Abraham, a place of comfort, or paradise, not into the limbo of hell.

units.la: Aliqui statuunt descensum animæ Christi ad inferos post mortem, non ut ibi pateretur, neque ut patres inde liberaret, sed ut ibi victoriam suam ostentaret, & incuteret terrorem diabolis. Sed quod eam ob causam descenderit ad inferos Christus, nusquam reperitur in scriptura.
units.tr: Some hold that the soul of Christ descended to hell after death, not in order to suffer there, nor to deliver the fathers from there, but to display his victory there and to strike terror into the devils. But that Christ descended into hell for this reason is nowhere found in Scripture.

units.la: Objciunt. 1. Locum Petri: Per quem etiam spiritibus, qui sunt in carcere, profectus prædicavit olim immorigeris. Resp. Petri alia est sententia, quam isti putant. Dicit enim Christum profectum, hoc est, inde ab initio missum à Patre ad ecclesiam, suo spiritu, hoc est, sua diuinitate, spiritibus iis, qui jam sunt in carcere, hoc est, in inferno, prædicasse olim, cùm adhuc viuebant, & erant immorigeri, nempe ante diluuium. Tunc enim prædicauit immorigeris, quando erant immorigeri. Erant autem immorigeri tempore Nohæ: ἀπειθοῦντες ποτέ. Ergo tempore Nohæ, hoc est, per patres prædicauit Christus, inuitans immorigeros ad resipiscentiam. Deinde, etsi loqueretur Petrus de descensu ad inferos: tamen hæc non esset sententia ipsorum, sed Papistarum, qui volunt, Christum apud inferos prædicasse patribus, & eos liberasse.
units.tr: They object: (1) the passage of Peter: "By whom also he went and preached to the spirits that are in prison, who formerly were disobedient." Answer: Peter's meaning is different from what they suppose. For he says that Christ, "having gone," that is, sent from the beginning by the Father to the Church, "by his Spirit," that is, by his divinity, "preached" to those spirits "who are now in prison," that is, in hell, "formerly" when they were still alive and "disobedient," namely before the flood. For then he preached to the disobedient when they were disobedient. They were disobedient in the time of Noah: [ἀπειθοῦντες ποτέ]. Therefore in the time of Noah, that is, through the fathers, Christ preached, inviting the disobedient to repentance. Moreover, even if Peter were speaking of the descent into hell, this would not be their opinion but that of the Papists, who hold that Christ preached to the fathers in hell and delivered them.

units.la: 1. Obiiciunt alium locum Petri: Mortuis quoque prædicatum est Euangelium. Resp. Est fallacia figuræ dictionis: Prædicatum est mortuis, hoc est, iis, qui nunc sunt mortui, vel, qui mortui erant, cùm Petrus illa scriberet: sed tunc cùm Euangelium eis prædicaretur, viuebant.
units.tr: (2) They object another passage of Peter: "The gospel was preached also to the dead." Answer: This is a fallacy of figure of speech. The gospel was preached to the dead, that is, to those who are now dead, or who were dead when Peter wrote these words; but when the gospel was preached to them, they were alive.

units.la: 3. Abutuntur etiam loco Pauli: Christus descendit ad inferiores partes terræ. Ergo ad inferos. Resp. Rursus est fallacia figuræ dictionis. Sensus enim phraseos est: Descendit ad inferiores partes terræ, hoc est, in terram, quæ est infima pars mundi, vel, quæ partes inferiores sunt terra, per appositionem, Hebraico more: quia non vna pars terra alteri, sed terra cælo opponitur: & significatur humiliatio Christi. Patet ex scopo Apostoli: quia facit antithesin summæ gloriæ & summæ humiliationis Christi. Sic Christus ascendit in superiores partes cæli, seu supra omnes cælos, hoc est, in cælum supremum, quod est beatorum.
units.tr: (3) They also misuse the passage of Paul: "Christ descended into the lower parts of the earth." Therefore into hell. Answer: Again this is a fallacy of figure of speech. The sense of the phrase is: he descended into the lower parts of the earth, that is, to the earth, which is the lowest part of the world; or, the lower parts are the earth, by apposition, in the Hebrew manner, because it is not one part of the earth set against another, but the earth is set against heaven; and the humiliation of Christ is signified. This is clear from the apostle's purpose, because he sets in antithesis the highest glory and the deepest humiliation of Christ. So Christ ascended into the higher parts of heaven, or above all the heavens, that is, into the highest heaven, which is the heaven of the blessed.

units.la: Nihil igitur hæc loca faciunt ad descensum animæ Christi ad inferos: & si maximè facerent: tamen, vt dictum est, non facerent pro ipsis, sed potius pro Pontificiis, docentibus, Christum apud inferos prædicasse, & patres liberasse. Quod si Pontificios hæc testimonia non iuuant, multo minus juuabunt istos. Nam inde non potest probari, Christum descendisse ad inferos, vt morti & diabolo terrorem incuteret. Nihil quidem impietatis habet per se hæc sententia, & est à multis Patribus approbata. Ideo non est odiosè dimicandum de ea cum quoquam. Interim certum est, eam non posse obtineri ex scriptura; nec nititur rationibus, & contrariæ rationes in promtu sunt. Nam post mortem, quando dixerat: consummatum est, anima Christi quiescere in manibus Patris, in quas illam commendauerat. Et si triumphandi causa descendit, esset hic articulus initium glorificationis. At non est verisimile, Christum glorificationis initium sumsumsisse in inferno. Nam omnes praecedentes articuli ad hunc usque, loquuntur de gradibus humiliationis, quorum extremus & infimus descensus est ad inferos, quod etiam ex antithesi constat. Ideo ab illa sententia discedo. Interim fateor, Christum diabolis magnum incussisse terrorem. Id vero morte sua fecit, quia diabolum, peccatum & mortem debellavit, & sine dubio sentit diabolus, se morte Christi victum esse.
units.tr: These passages therefore do nothing for the descent of the soul of Christ into hell; and even if they did very much, yet, as has been said, they would support not us but rather the Papists, who teach that Christ preached in hell and delivered the fathers. But if these testimonies do not help the Papists, they will help these men much less. For from them it cannot be proved that Christ descended into hell in order to strike terror into death and the devil. This opinion in itself has nothing of impiety, and it has been approved by many Fathers. Therefore one should not contend bitterly about it with anyone. Meanwhile it is certain that it cannot be established from Scripture; nor does it rest on reasons, and the contrary reasons are at hand. For after death, when he had said "It is finished," the soul of Christ rested in the hands of the Father, into which it had commended itself. And if he descended to triumph, this article would be the beginning of his glorification. But it is not likely that Christ took up the beginning of his glorification in hell. For all the preceding articles up to this one speak of the degrees of humiliation, of which the last and lowest is the descent into hell, as also appears from the antithesis. Therefore I depart from that opinion. Meanwhile I admit that Christ struck great terror into the devils. But he did this by his death, because he vanquished the devil, sin and death, and without doubt the devil feels that he has been conquered by the death of Christ.

units.la: Quid igitur significat iste descensus Christi ad inferos? 1. Summos cruciatus, angustias & dolores, quos Christus perpessus est in anima sua, quales damnati experiuntur, partim in hac, partim in altera vita. 2. Complectitur etiam ignominiam extremam, qua est affectus Christus in toto passionis actu. Ista significari per descensum ad inferos, docent testimonia scripturae supra citata: Angustia inferni invenerunt me. Dominus deducit ad inferos, & reducit.
units.tr: What then does this descent of Christ into hell signify? (1) The highest torments, anguish and pains which Christ suffered in his soul, such as the damned experience, partly in this life and partly in the next. (2) It also includes the utmost ignominy with which Christ was afflicted during the whole course of his passion. That these things are signified by the descent into hell is taught by the testimonies of Scripture cited above: "The pains of hell found me. The Lord brings down to hell and brings back up."

units.la: Christum vero ista debuisse pati, & perpessum esse, probatur testimoniis Davidis: Angustia inferni comprehenderunt me: quod de Christo dictum est in persona Davidis. Similia sunt: Dominus voluit eum conterere infirmitate. Tristis est anima mea usque ad mortem. Idem demonstrant terrores & cruciatus in horto, cum sudaret sanguinem: quia coniecit in eum omnes iniquitates nostras Domi-nus. Propterea exclamat: Deus meus, Deus meus, quare me dereliqui? Idem probatur argumentis.
units.tr: That Christ had to suffer these things and did suffer them is proved by the testimonies of David: "The pains of hell surrounded me," which is said of Christ in the person of David. Similar are: "The Lord was pleased to bruise him with infirmity," and "My soul is sorrowful even unto death." The terrors and torments in the garden, when he sweated blood, show the same thing: "because the Lord has laid on him the iniquities of us all." Therefore he cries out: "My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?" The same is proved by arguments.

units.la: 1. Christus non tantum corpora, sed etiam animas nostras debuit redimere. Ergo non tantum corpore, sed etiam anima debuit pati.
units.tr: (1) Christ was bound to redeem not only our bodies but also our souls. Therefore he had to suffer not only in body but also in soul.

units.la: 2. Debuit nos ab angustiis & cruciatibus inferni liberare. Ergo debuit ipse hoc experiri. Id fecit vel ante, vel post mortem. Non post mortem, ipsis Papistis fatentibus. Ergo ante mortem. At non in corpore. Huius enim passiones tantum fuerunt externae. Ergo in anima dolores illos est passus.
units.tr: (2) He had to free us from the anguish and torments of hell. Therefore he himself had to undergo these things. He did so either before or after death. Not after death, as the Papists themselves admit. Therefore before death. But not in the body, for his sufferings there were only external. Therefore he suffered those inner pains in his soul.

units.la: 3. Cruciatus & angustias animi summas, tanquam gravissimam passionis Christi partem, in symbolo non taceri, consentaneum est. Atqui tacerentur, si articulus de descensu ad inferos de iis non intelligeretur. Nam praecedentes articuli tantum de externis passionibus corporis loquuntur, quas Christus perpessus est. Non igitur est dubium, hoc articulo spirituales animae passiones significari. Hic est verus descensus Christi ad inferos. Itaque tenendum & defendendum est contra Papistas id, quod est certum: nempe CHRISTVM eo, quo dictum est, modo descendisse ad inferos. Si quis potest defendere, etiam alio sensu descendisse, bene est. Ego non possum.
units.tr: (3) It is fitting that the greatest torments and anguish of the spirit, as the most grievous part of Christ's passion, should not be passed over in the creed. Yet they would be passed over if the article on the descent into hell were not understood to refer to them. For the preceding articles speak only of the external sufferings of the body which Christ endured. There is therefore no doubt that spiritual sufferings of the soul are signified in this article. This is the true descent of Christ into hell. Thus against the Papists we must hold and defend what is certain: namely, that CHRIST descended into hell in the sense in which it has been said. If anyone can defend that he descended also in another sense, well and good. I cannot.

units.la: Quaest.XLIV. Obiect. 1. Articuli fidei debent proprie & sine tropo intelligi. Resp. Nisi articulus proprie acceptus pugnet cum aliis scripturæ locis. At hic articulus de descensu ad inferos proprie acceptus pugnaret inprimis cum hoc dicto Christi: Consummatum est. Nam si Christus omnes redemptionis partes in cruce compleuit & consummauit, nulla fuit causa, cur descenderet ad inferos, in locum damnatorum.
units.tr: Question 44. Objection 1: The articles of faith must be understood properly and without a trope. Answer: Only if an article taken properly conflicts with other passages of Scripture. But this article on the descent into hell, taken properly, would especially conflict with this saying of Christ: "It is finished." For if Christ accomplished and completed all parts of redemption on the cross, there was no reason for him to descend into hell, into the place of the damned.

units.la: Obiect. 2. Cruciatus & horrores animi in Christo præcesserunt sepulturam. Descensus ad inferos sequitur sepulturam. Ergo descensus ad inferos non potest notare illos cruciatus, &c. Resp. Fallacia non causæ est in minore. Descensus enim in symbolo sequitur sepulturam; non quod post sepulturam demum fit factus: sed quia est explicatio præcedentium de passione, morte & sepultura, ne quid iis adimatur, quasi dicat: non tantum passus est corpore, non tantum mortuus corporaliter, non tantum sepultus: sed etiam summos cruciatus & dolores infernales, quales impij omnes in æternum patientur, est perpessus animâ. Præcipua igitur & grauior pars passionis rectè sequitur. Nam symbolum à doloribus corporis ad dolores animi, & à passione visibili ad passionem invisibilem, tanquam à leuioribus ad graviora progreditur.
units.tr: Objection 2: The torments and terrors of soul in Christ came before the burial. The descent into hell follows the burial. Therefore the descent into hell cannot denote those torments, etc. Answer: The fallacy is not in the cause but in the minor premise. For the descent in the creed follows the burial, not because it happened only after the burial, but because it is an explanation of the preceding statements about passion, death and burial, lest anything be taken from them, as if it said: he suffered not only in body, not only died bodily, not only was buried, but he also suffered in soul the utmost torments and infernal pains, such as all the wicked will suffer forever. The principal and weightier part of the passion therefore rightly follows. For the creed proceeds from the pains of the body to the pains of the soul, and from the visible passion to the invisible passion, as from lighter things to heavier.

units.la: II. Fructus descensus Christi ad inferos.
units.tr: II. The fruit of Christ's descent into hell.

units.la: Christus descendit ad inferos. 1. Ne nobis esset descendendum, sed vt nos ab æternis angustiis & cruciatibus inferni liberaret. 2. Vt nos secum eueheret in cœlum.
units.tr: Christ descended into hell (1) not so that we would have to descend, but so that he might free us from the eternal anguish and torments of hell; (2) so that he might carry us with him up into heaven.

units.la: Credere igitur in Christum, qui descendit ad inferos, est, credere, Christum in anima sua pro nobis sustinuisse dolores & cruciatus infernales, & ignominiam summam impiis in inferno debitam: ne nos vnquam in infernum descenderemus, & dolores atque cruciatus inferni pati cogeremur, quos omnes diaboli & impij in æternum apud inferos passuri sunt: sed vt è contrario potius ascenderemus cum ipso in cœlum, atq; ibidem cum ipso summa felicitate & gloria in æternum frueremur. Hic est visus articuli de descensu Christi ad inferos.
units.tr: To believe in Christ, who descended into hell, is therefore to believe that Christ in his soul bore for us the pains and infernal torments, and the utmost ignominy due to the wicked in hell, so that we would never descend into hell and be compelled to suffer the pains and torments of hell, which all the devils and wicked will suffer forever in the depths; but on the contrary we would rather ascend with him into heaven and there enjoy with him supreme happiness and glory forever. This is the meaning of the article on Christ's descent into hell.

units.la: QVÆSTIO XLV.
units.tr: QUESTION XLV.

units.la: Quid nobis prodest resurrectio Christi? RESPONSIO.
units.tr: What benefit does the resurrection of Christ bring us? ANSWER.

units.la: Primùm suâ resurrectione mortem deuicit, vt nos posset eius justitiæ, quam nobis sua morte pepererat, parparticipes facere. Deinde, nos jam quoque eius potentiâ ad nouam vitam excitamur . Postremò, resurrectio capitis nostri CHRISTI, nobis gloriosæ resurrectionis nostræ pignus est .
units.tr: First, by his resurrection he overcame death, so that he might make us partakers of the righteousness which he had obtained for us by his death. Second, by his power we are now also raised up to a new life. Finally, the resurrection of Christ, our head, is a pledge of our own glorious resurrection.

units.la: EXPLICATIO.
units.tr: EXPLICATION.

units.la: Hactenus de humiliatione Christi; sequitur de eius gloria, ad quam tertia die resurrexit ex mortuis. Humiliatio enim mediatoris non debuit durare perpetuò: sed satis erat, eum semel passum & mortuum esse. Efficacia verò & potentia eius in conseruandis beneficiis in æternum durat.
units.tr: So far we have spoken of the humiliation of Christ. Next comes his glory, into which he rose from the dead on the third day. The humiliation of the Mediator did not need to last forever; it was enough that he suffered and died once. But his efficacy and power in preserving the benefits endure forever.

units.la: Sunt autem in resurrectione Christi duo potissimum consideranda: historia, & fructus. In historia rursus 1. Quis resurrexerit? Christus nempe, Deus & homo, secundum corpus illud, secundum quod mortuus erat. Id enim λόγῳ nunquam depositum. 2. Quomodo? Verè mortuus reuixit, anima ad corpus reuocata, & gloriosus e sepulchro egressus est tertio post sepulturam die, secundum scripturas: idq; tum Patris, tum suâ propria vi atque potentia, non quidem carnis, sed deitatis suæ. A Patre enim est suscitatus per seipsum, quia Pater agit per Filium. 3. Testimonia resurrectionis. Visendum se præbuit multis mulieribus, discipulis: quod testantur angeli, &c. Fructus recitantur in quæstione. Sed hæc uberius sunt explicanda.
units.tr: In Christ's resurrection two things chiefly deserve consideration: the history and the fruits. In the history there are again three points. Who rose? Christ indeed, God and man, according to that body in which he had died, for that was never laid aside [λόγῳ]. How? He truly rose from the dead, his soul being recalled to his body, and he came forth glorious from the tomb on the third day after the burial, according to the Scriptures. This was done both by the power of the Father and by his own proper power and might, not indeed of his flesh but of his deity. For he was raised by the Father through himself, because the Father works through the Son. Witnesses of the resurrection. He showed himself to be seen by many women and disciples, as the angels also testify, and so on. The fruits are set out in the question below. But these things must be explained more fully.

units.la: Quæstiones igitur de RESVRRECTIONE CHRISTI præcipuè considerentur: I. An Christus resurrexerit. II. Quomodo resurrexerit. III. Quare resurrexerit. IV. Quis sint fructus resurrectionis Christi.
units.tr: Therefore the questions concerning the RESURRECTION OF CHRIST should be considered chiefly as follows: I. Whether Christ rose. II. How he rose. III. Why he rose. IV. What are the fruits of Christ's resurrection.

units.la: I. An Christus resurrexerit.
units.tr: I. Whether Christ rose.

units.la: Infideles credunt Christum esse mortuum, sed non credunt eum resurrexisse à mortuis. Quod autem resurrexerit, probant testimonia angelorum, mulierum, euangelistarum, apostolorum, aliorumque sanctorum, qui post resurrectionem ipsum viderunt, palparunt, & eum ipso locuti sunt. Apostolis credendum esset propter authoritatem cœlestem, etiamsi eum non vidissent.
units.tr: Unbelievers believe that Christ died, but they do not believe that he rose from the dead. That he did rise is proved by the testimony of the angels, the women, the evangelists, the apostles, and other saints, who saw him after the resurrection, touched him, and spoke with him. The apostles would have deserved belief even if they had not seen him, on account of their heavenly authority.

units.la: II. Quomodo Christus resurrexerit.
units.tr: II. How Christ rose.

units.la: Modus resurrectionis sequentibus circumstantiis declaratur.
units.tr: The manner of the resurrection is made clear by the following circumstances.

units.la: 1. Verè Christus resurrexit, hoc est, verè anima ad corpus rediit, à quo fuit per mortem separata: & verè Christus ex sepulchro, custodibus inuitis ac stupore perculsis, exiuit.
units.tr: 1. Christ truly rose, that is, his soul truly returned to the body from which it had been separated by death; and Christ truly came out of the tomb, the guards being unwilling and struck with amazement.

units.la: 2. Resurrexit eadem persona, idem Iesus Christus, verus Deus & verus homo, qui erat mortuus: secundum eam naturam, secundum quam passus erat: nempe secundum humanam, & quidem veram, essentia & proprietatibus eandem quæ fuerat, non deificatam, sed glorificatam, depositis infirmitatibus. Videte manus meas & pedes meos, nam ego ipse sum. Contrectate me, & videte, nam spiritus carnem & ossa non habet prout me conspicitis habere. Et certè nihil aliud resurgere potuit, quam quod ceciderat. Idem ergo corpus, quod ceciderat, resurrexit: quod nobis est magno solatio. Nam oportuit esse eundem mediatorem, qui mereretur nobis bona, quæ perdideramus per peccatum, & qui eadem nobis restitueret, ac singulis applicaret. Si enim Christi caro non resurrexisset, etiam nostra caro non resurgeret ad beatam vitam.
units.tr: 2. The same person rose, the same Jesus Christ, true God and true man, who had died, according to that nature according to which he had suffered, namely the human nature, and indeed a true human nature, with the same essence and properties it had before, not deified but glorified, its weaknesses laid aside. See my hands and my feet, for it is I myself. Handle me and see, for a spirit does not have flesh and bones as you see me have. And certainly nothing else could rise than what had fallen. Therefore the same body that had fallen rose again, which is a great comfort to us. For it was necessary that the same Mediator should merit for us the goods that we had lost through sin, and should restore the same to us and apply them to each one. For if Christ's flesh had not risen, our flesh too would not rise to blessed life.

units.la: 3. Resurrexit propriâ potentiâ, hoc est, ipse à se depulit mortem, viuificauit corpus mortuum, animæ rursus copulauit corpus, & restituit sibi vitam beatam, cœlestem & gloriosam; idque diuina sua virtute & potentia. Destruite templum hoc, & ego tribus diebus erigam illud. Potestatem habeo ponendi animam meam, & potestatem habeo rursus eam assumendi. Sicut Pater excitat mortuos, & viuificat, ita & Filius, quos vult, viuificat.
units.tr: 3. He rose by his own power, that is, he himself drove death away from himself, quickened the dead body, joined the body again to the soul, and restored to himself a blessed, heavenly and glorious life; and this by his own divine virtue and power. Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up. I have power to lay down my life, and I have power to take it again. As the Father raises the dead and quickens them, so the Son also quickens whom he wills.

units.la: Obiect. Atqui Pater eum suscitauit. Si spiritus eius, qui excitauit à mortuis, &c. Ergo non ipse. Resp. Pater suscitauit Filium per Iesum Filium, non vt per instrumentum, sed vt per alteram personam eiusdem essentiæ cum Patre, & infinitæ potentiæ per metipsum: ipsemet suscitauit se suo spiritu. Quaecunque enim Pater facit, Filius similiter facit.
units.tr: Objection. But the Father raised him. If the Spirit of him that raised up from the dead, and so on. Therefore not he himself. Answer. The Father raised the Son through Jesus the Son, not as through an instrument, but as through another person of the same essence as the Father and of infinite power, through himself: he himself raised himself by his own Spirit. For whatever the Father does, the Son likewise does.

units.la: 4. Tertio die reuixit virtute Patris, & propriâ. 1. Secundum scripturas, sub quibus intelliguntur omnes prædictiones & typi, ostendentes Christum tertio die resurgere debuisse: vt typus Ionæ, &c. 2. Quia corpus incorruptum debuit suscitari: non tamen statim primo die, vt constaret, eum verè mortuum esse, sed tertio die post. Additur igitur circumstantia tertij diei in symbolo, vt veritas respondeat typo, idque ob nostri confirmationem, tionem, hunc esse Messiam patribus promissum: quia hic solus tertio die resurrexit.
units.tr: 4. He rose on the third day by the power of the Father and by his own. 1. According to the Scriptures, under which are understood all the predictions and types showing that Christ ought to rise on the third day, such as the type of Jonah, and so on. 2. Because his incorrupt body had to be raised, yet not immediately on the first day, so that it might be established that he had truly died, but on the third day after. The circumstance of the third day is therefore added in the creed, so that the truth may correspond to the type, and this for our confirmation, that this is the Messiah promised to the fathers, because he alone rose on the third day.

units.la: III. Quare Christus resurrexit?
units.tr: III. Why did Christ rise?

units.la: CHRISTVS resurrexit,
units.tr: CHRIST rose again:

units.la: 1. Propter suam & Patris gloriam. Declaratus Filius Dei per resurrectionem a mortuis. Pater glorifica Filium tuum, ut & Filius glorificet te. Nam gloria Filij est Patris gloria.
units.tr: 1. For the sake of his own glory and the Father's. He was declared the Son of God with power by the resurrection from the dead. Father, glorify your Son, that the Son may also glorify you. For the glory of the Son is the glory of the Father.

units.la: 2. Propter vaticinia propheratum de Christo morituro & resurrecturo edita. Non derelinques animam meam in inferno, nec dabis sanctum tuum videre corruptionem. Si posuerit pro peccato animam suam, videbit semen longaevum, pro eo, quod laboravit anima ipsius, videbit, & saturabitur. Signum non dabitur ei, nisi signum illud Ionae prophetae. Sicut enim Ionas fuit in ventre ceti tres dies & tres noctes: ita erit Filius hominis in corpore terrae tres dies & tres noctes. Nondum noverant scripturam, videlicet, oportere Christum a mortuis resurgere. Propter haec & alia vaticinia necesse fuit, Christum mori & resurgere: quia oportuit impleri scripturas. Quomodo implerentur scripturae, quae dicunt, sic oportere fieri? nempe propter immutabile decretum Dei in scripturis patefactum, de quo Apostolus in actis: Coacti sunt vere adversus sanctum Filium tuum Jesum, quem unxisti, Herodes & Pontius Pilatus cum gentibus & populis Israelis, ut facerent quaecunque manus tua & consilium tuum prius definierat facienda. Huc pertinent Christi praedictiones. Filium hominis trucidabunt, sed tertio die suscitabitur. Triduo readificabo illud.
units.tr: 2. On account of the prophecies published concerning the Christ who was to die and rise again. You will not leave my soul in hell, nor will you suffer your Holy One to see corruption. When he shall make his soul an offering for sin, he shall see a long-lived seed; and because his soul has laboured, he shall see and be satisfied. No sign shall be given to him except the sign of the prophet Jonah. For as Jonah was in the belly of the whale three days and three nights, so shall the Son of man be in the heart of the earth three days and three nights. They did not yet know the Scripture, namely that Christ must rise again from the dead. On account of these and other prophecies it was necessary that Christ die and rise, because the Scriptures had to be fulfilled. How would the Scriptures be fulfilled, which say that it must happen thus? Namely on account of the unchangeable decree of God, made known in the Scriptures, of which the Apostle speaks in Acts: Truly they were gathered together against your holy Son Jesus, whom you anointed, Herod and Pontius Pilate, with the Gentiles and the peoples of Israel, to do whatever your hand and your counsel had decided beforehand should be done. To this belong Christ's own predictions: The Son of man will be killed, but on the third day he will be raised up. In three days I will raise it up.

units.la: 3. Propter personae regentis dignitatem & potentiam. Propter hanc impossibile erat Christum a morte retineri, dicit Petrus. Quia erat Filius Dei dilectus & unigenitus. Pater diligit Filium suum, & omnia dedit in manus eius. Sic Deus dilexit mundum, ut Filium unigenitum daret. 2. Christus est verus Deus, author & fons vitae. Ego sum resurrectio & vita. Pater dedit Filio vitam habere in seipso, & sicut Pater excitat mortuos, & vivificat, ita & Filius quos vult, vivificat. Ego vitam aeternam do eis. Absurdum igitur fuisset, eum manere in morte, qui ipse hominibus dat vitam.
units.tr: 3. On account of the dignity and power of the person who was to rise. Because of this, as Peter says, it was impossible for Christ to be held by death. Because he was the beloved and only-begotten Son of God. The Father loves the Son and has put all things into his hands. For God so loved the world that he gave his only-begotten Son. 2. Christ is true God, the author and fountain of life. I am the resurrection and the life. The Father has given the Son to have life in himself; and as the Father raises the dead and gives them life, so the Son also gives life to whom he wills. I give them eternal life. It would therefore have been absurd for him to remain in death, he who himself gives life to men.

units.la: 3. Erat in se justus homo, & pro nostris peccatis, ipsi imputatis, moriendo satisfecerat. Ubi vero non est peccatum, ibi mors non amplius dominatur. Unica oblatione consecravit in perpetuum eos, qui sanctificantur. Quod mortuus est peccato mortuus est semel: quod autem vivit, vivit Deo.
units.tr: 3. He was in himself a just man, and by dying he had made satisfaction for our sins, which had been imputed to him. But where there is no sin, death no longer has dominion. By one offering he has perfected for ever those who are sanctified. For in that he died, he died to sin once; but in that he lives, he lives to God.

units.la: 4. Propter personae resurgentis officium, quod non poterat obire, manens in morte. Nam 1. Mediator, qui sit verus Deus in seculum & homo, debebat in aeternum regnare. Thronus tuus Deus in seculum culum seculi : virga rectitudinis virga regni tui. Stabiliam solium regni eius usque in seculum. Ego ero ei in patrem, & ipse erit mihi in filium. Semel juraui per sanctitatem meam, si Dauid mentiar : semen eius in aeternum manebit, & thronus eius sicut sol in conspectu meo, sicut luna stabilietur in seculum, & testis in cælo fidelis. Erunt mihi in populum : ego verò ero eis in Deum, & seruus meus Dauid erit rex super eos in perpetuum. Regnum autem & potestas, & magnitudo regni, quod est sub toto cœlo, detur populo sancti altissimi : regnum eius regnum æternum, & omnes potestates ei seruient, & obedient ei. Multi- plicationis regni & pacis non erit finis. Regni eius non erit finis. Opor- tuit ergo naturam humanam semen Dauidis resuscitari & re- gnare. 2. Mediator, qui sit frater noster, & verus homo, debebat semper pro nobis intercedere, & tanquam sacerdos æternus apparere coram Deo. Tu es sacerdos in aeternum secundum ordinem Melchisedech. Christus is est, qui mortuus est : immò verò etiam qui excitatus est : qui etiam est ad dexteram Dei : qui etiam postulat pro nobis. 3. Mediator, qui sit verus homo, debuit esse mediator merito & efficacia. Non enim sufficiebat eum pro nobis mori, sed etiam oportebat eum ecclesiæ & nobis omnibus potentiâ suâ conferre beneficia, quæ moriendo nobis impetrauerat, justitiam videlicet, Spiritum sanctum, vitam & gloriam æter- nam. Utrumque enim pertinebat ad mediatorem, mereri & con- ferre. Non potuisset autem conferre, si mansisset in morte : quia non fuisset. Qui non est, nihil agit. Ideo etiam hæc beneficia in eo deponuntur à diuinitate, vt ipsemet eorum nos faciat partici- pes. Ex plenitudine eius omnes accepimus, gratiam pro gratia. Neque mirum videri debet, Christum conferre nobis eadem beneficia hæc, quæ morte sua à diuinitate nobis impetrauit. Nam & homo potest altero alicui aliquid impetrare & conferre. Interce- da aliquis pro te apud principem propter donum mille coronatorum. Princeps hoc faciat in precantis gratiam, eique det donum, quod tibi conferat. Is à principe impetrabit donum, & simul conferet.
units.tr: 4. On account of the office of the person who rose, which he could not discharge while remaining in death. For first, the Mediator, who is true God and man, had to reign for ever. Your throne, O God, endures for ever and ever; the sceptre of uprightness is the sceptre of your kingdom. I will establish the throne of his kingdom for ever. I will be his Father, and he shall be my Son. Once have I sworn by my holiness, and I will not lie to David: his seed shall endure for ever, and his throne shall be before me as the sun, it shall be established for ever like the moon, and the witness in heaven is faithful. They shall be my people, and I will be their God, and my servant David shall be king over them for ever.
