units.tr: Objection: He also interceded for us on earth. Answer: That intercession was made with respect to his future intercession. For on this condition he first interceded, so that, once the sacrifice on earth was completed, he might appear perpetually as Mediator in the heavenly sanctuary.

units.la: 2. Vt & nos ascenderemus, & de nostra ascensione certi essemus. Parabo vobis locum. In domo Patris mei mansiones multæ sunt. hoc est, loca ad manendum perpetuò. Nam de duratione loquitur. Christus ascendit: ergo & nos ascendemus. Valet; quia ipse est caput, nos membra: item, est primogenitus inter multos fratres.
units.tr: (2) That we too might ascend, and be certain of our ascension. I go to prepare a place for you. In my Father's house are many mansions. That is, places to remain forever, for he speaks of duration. Christ ascended; therefore we too shall ascend. The inference holds, since he is the Head and we are the members; likewise he is the firstborn among many brethren.

units.la: 3. Vt missō Spiritu sancto, Ecclesiam vsque ad finem mundi colligat, consoletur ac defendat. Nisi abiero, consolator non veniet ad vos. Quem Spiritum suum effudit in nos copiose, per Iesum Christum seruatorem nostrum.
units.tr: (3) That, by sending the Holy Spirit, he might gather the Church until the end of the world, comfort it and defend it. Unless I go away, the Comforter will not come to you. Whom he poured out upon us abundantly, through Jesus Christ our Saviour.

units.la: Obiect. Ante & post resurrectionem dedit Spiritum sanctum. Ergo non ideo ascendit, vt eum mitteret. R. 1. Dederat quidem, sed non tanta copia, quanta in die pentecostes. 2. Illa missio Spiritus sancti facta ab initio mundi in Ecclesia, fiebat propter Christum venturum, qui aliquando regnaturus esset in humana natura, & largiter effusurus Spiritū sanctum. Ante ascensionem autem non dedit Spiritum S. tanta copia, propter decretum Dei: quia Deus constituerat vtrumq; per hominē glorificatum facere. Erat praecipua pars gloriæ Christi, missio Spiritus sancti. Ideo dicitur: Nondum erat Spiritus sanctus, hoc est, miraculosa & copiosa missio Spiritus sancti: quia Christus nondum erat glorificatus. Nisi abiero, Paracletus non veniet ad vos. Haec est causa, cur missio vsque ad ascensionem differretur.
units.tr: Objection: Before and after the resurrection he gave the Holy Spirit; therefore he did not ascend in order to send him. Answer: (1) He had indeed given the Spirit, but not in such abundance as on the day of Pentecost. (2) That sending of the Holy Spirit, made in the Church from the beginning of the world, was made on account of the Christ who was to come, who would one day reign in human nature and pour out the Holy Spirit abundantly. Before the ascension, however, he did not give the Spirit in such abundance, because of the decree of God: God had determined to make both glorified through a man. The chief part of Christ's glory was the sending of the Holy Spirit. Therefore it is said: The Holy Spirit was not yet, that is, the miraculous and abundant sending of the Holy Spirit, because Christ was not yet glorified. Unless I go away, the Paraclete will not come to you. This is the reason why the sending was deferred until the ascension.

units.la: IV. Quod sit discrimen inter ascensionem Christi & nostram.
units.tr: IV. In what respect the ascension of Christ differs from ours.

units.la: Conueniunt Christi & nostra ascensio, 1. Loco: quia in eundem locum nos ascendemus, in quem ipse ascendit. 2. Gloria, Volo vt vbi ego sum, etiam sint, quos dedisti mihi, vt videant gloriam meam.
units.tr: Christ's ascension and ours agree: (1) in place, since we shall ascend into the same place into which he ascended; (2) in glory. I will that where I am, those also whom you have given me may be, so that they may see my glory.

units.la: Differunt. 1. Christus ascendit propria potentia & virtute. Nemo ascendit in cœlum (nempe propria virtute) nisi Filius hominis. Nos ascendemus virtute Christi, per & propter ipsum. Vado paraturus vobis locum. Volo, vt quos dedisti mihi, sint vbi & ego. 2. Ipse ascendit, vt sit caput: nos, vt simus membra: ipse ad gloriam capiti conuenientem: nos ad gloriam membrorum ascendemus: ipse vt sedeat ad dextram Patris, nos vt sedeamus in throno ipsius participatione, non æqualitate dignitatis. Vincenti dabo sedere in throno meo, vt & ego vici, & sedeo cum Patre meo in throno eius. Erimus igitur participes gloriæ eius, seruata proportione membrorum & capitis. 3. Christi ascensio fuit causa nostræ ascensionis: nostra illius effectus. 4. Totus Christus ascendit, sed non totum Christi: quia tantum secundum naturam humanam ascendit, qua potuit mutare locum: non autem secundum diuinam, qua fuit & est immobilis, quia immensa. Nos toti ascendemus, & totum nostri ascendent: quia habemus tantum naturam vnam, & quidem finitam.
units.tr: They differ. (1) Christ ascended by his own power and virtue. No one ascends into heaven (namely by his own virtue) except the Son of man. We shall ascend by the virtue of Christ, through him and on account of him. I go to prepare a place for you. I will that those whom you have given me be where I am. (2) He ascended so that he might be the Head; we so that we might be the members. He ascends to the glory befitting the Head; we ascend to the glory of the members. He ascends so that he may sit at the right hand of the Father; we so that we may sit on his throne by participation, not by equality of dignity. To him who overcomes I will give a seat on my throne, as I also overcame and sit with my Father on his throne. We shall therefore be partakers of his glory, the proportion between members and Head being preserved. (3) Christ's ascension was the cause of our ascension; ours is its effect. (4) The whole Christ ascended, but not the whole of Christ's nature, since he ascended only according to his human nature, by which he could change place, and not according to his divine nature, by which he was and is immovable, because it is immense. We shall ascend wholly, and all of what we are will ascend, because we have only one nature, and that a finite one.

units.la: QVÆSTIO XLIX.
units.tr: QUESTION XLIX.

units.la: Quem fructum nobis adfert ascensio Christi in cælum?
units.tr: What fruit does the ascension of Christ into heaven bring to us?

units.la: RESPONSIO.
units.tr: ANSWER.

units.la: Primùm, quod in cœlo apud Patrem pro nobis intercedit a. Deinde, quod carnem nostram in cœlo habemus, vt eo tanquam certo pignore confirmemur, scilicet vt ipse, qui caput nostrum est, nos sua membra ad se extollat b. Tertio, quod nobis suum Spiritum mutui pignoris loco mittit c, cuius efficacia, non terrena, sed superna quærimus, vbi ipse est, ad dexteram Dei sedens d.
units.tr: First, that in heaven He intercedes for us before the Father a. Second, that we have our flesh in heaven, so that by this as a sure pledge we may be confirmed: namely, that He, who is our Head, will raise up His members to Himself b. Third, that He sends us His Spirit in place of a pledge of mutual surety c, and it is for His power, not earthly but heavenly, that we seek, where He Himself is, sitting at the right hand of God d.

units.la: EXPLICATIO.
units.tr: EXPLANATION.

units.la: V. Qui sint fructus ascensionis Christi.
units.tr: V. What are the fruits of the ascension of Christ?

units.la: Fructus ascensionis Christi præcipui sunt tres.
units.tr: The chief fruits of the ascension of Christ are three.

units.la: 1. Intercessio Christi pro nobis apud Patrem. Ea significat 1. Valorem sacrificij Christi perpetuum. 2. Voluntatem Christi vtramque, diuinam & humanam, erga nos propitiam, qua vult propter sacrificium suum nos recipi à Patre. 3. Assensum Patris acquiescentis in hac voluntate & in hoc λύτρῳ Fili j. Summa. Est voluntas Patris & Filij, vt valeat Christi oblatio pro nobis in perpetuum.
units.tr: 1. The intercession of Christ for us before the Father. This signifies: 1. the perpetual value of the sacrifice of Christ. 2. the will of Christ, both divine and human, favourable toward us, by which He wills that we be received by the Father on account of His sacrifice. 3. the assent of the Father, resting in this will and in this ransom [λύτρον] of the Son. Summary. It is the will of the Father and of the Son that the offering of Christ for us remain effective forever.

units.la: Obiect. Intercessio fuit ante ascensionem Christi, immò ante aduentum eius. Ergo non est ascensionis fructus. Resp. 1. Fuit: sed ita, vt penderet ab ea, quæ futura erat post ascensionem, hoc est, fiebat respectu futuræ intercessionis, sicut tota receptio in gratiam ab initio mundi. 2. Fuit: sed non talis, qualis nunc est. Olim enim intercedebat Mediator valore sacrificij sui præstandi: nunc vero intuitu sacrificij præstiti. Sic olim remittebantur peccata, donabatur Spiritus sanctus propter futurum sacrificium: nunc propter sacrificium peractum. Valor autem vnius sacrificij Christi continuatur in perpetuum; quia vnica oblatione consecrauit in perpetuum eos, qui sanctificantur. Neque imperfecti, sed perfecti sacrificij argumentum est cessatio ChriChristi à sacrificando. Si enim sæpius sacrificaret, more Leuiticorum sacerdotum, faceret id, quia vnico sacrificio non potuisset perficere eos, qui ad Deum accedunt. Sed omnes vnico sacrificio perfecit. Fungitur ergo nunc sacerdotio suo, non quidem sæpius offerendo, sed semper intercedendo, nec amplius merendo, sed semel meritum nobis semper applicando, gratiam, justitiam & Spiritum sanctum, æterno & infinito sacrificij sui vnici valore ac dignitate: quod multo est maius, quàm si sacrificium iteraret.
units.tr: Objection. The intercession was before the ascension of Christ, indeed before His coming. Therefore it is not a fruit of the ascension. Answer. 1. It was, but in such a way that it depended on what was to come after the ascension; that is, it was made with respect to the future intercession, just as the whole reception into grace from the beginning of the world. 2. It was, but not such as it is now. For formerly the Mediator interceded by the value of the sacrifice He was to render; but now He intercedes with regard to the sacrifice already rendered. So formerly sins were remitted and the Holy Spirit was bestowed on account of the future sacrifice; now on account of the sacrifice completed. Moreover, the value of the one sacrifice of Christ continues forever, because by one offering He has perfected forever those who are sanctified. The cessation of Christ from sacrificing is a proof not of an imperfect but of a perfect sacrifice. For if He sacrificed more often, after the manner of the Levitical priests, He would do so because by one sacrifice He could not have perfected those who draw near to God. But by one sacrifice He has perfected all. He therefore now exercises His priesthood, not by offering more often, but by interceding always, and no longer by merit, but by once for all applying the merit to us: grace, righteousness and the Holy Spirit, by the eternal and infinite value and dignity of His one sacrifice. This is far greater than if He repeated the sacrifice.

units.la: 2. Assensio nostra & glorificatio. Quia enim Christus caput nostrum ascendit, etiam nos, eius membra, certo ascendemus. Proficiscor paraturus vobis locum: & cum profectus fuero, & parauero vobis locum, rursus veniam, & assumam vos ad me. Obiect. Elias & Enoch ascenderunt ante Christum. Ergo Christi ascensio non est causa nostræ ascensionis. Resp. Ante quidem tempore, sed non virtute. Christus ascendit virtute sua. Illi ascenderunt & nos ascendemus virtute Christi. Christi ascensio nobis non tantum est exemplum, sed etiam causa ascensionis. Nisi enim ipse esset glorificatus, nos non glorificaremur. Omnia decreuit Pater nobis dare per Messiam & in ipso omnia deposuit. Quomodo autem Christus fuisset nobis regnum daturus, nisi prius hoc ipse tanquam progenitus occupasset? Quia igitur ascendit, & nunc ibi regnat etiam nos cives suos eò transferet. Vbi ego fuero, illic & minister meus erit. Assumam vos ad meipsum, vt vbi ego sum, & vos sitis.
units.tr: 2. Our assent and glorification. For since Christ our Head has ascended, we, His members, will certainly ascend too. I go to prepare a place for you; and when I have gone and prepared a place for you, I will come again and take you to myself. Objection. Elijah and Enoch ascended before Christ. Therefore the ascension of Christ is not the cause of our ascension. Answer. Indeed before in time, but not in power. Christ ascended by His own power; those others ascended, and we shall ascend, by the power of Christ. The ascension of Christ is not only an example to us, but also the cause of our ascension. For unless He Himself had been glorified, we would not be glorified. The Father decreed to give us all things through the Messiah, and placed all things in Him. But how would Christ have been going to give us the kingdom, unless He first, as the firstborn, had taken possession of it Himself? Because therefore He has ascended and now reigns there, He will also transfer us, His citizens, thither. Where I am, there also shall my servant be. I will take you to myself, that where I am, you may be also.

units.la: 3. Missio Spiritus sancti, per quem ad finem vsq; mundi Ecclesiam colligit, consolatur, & defendit. Dabatur quidem Spiritus sanctus piis etiam sub lege: sed 1. respectu ascensionis & glorificationis Christi futuræ, cuius non modo fructus, sed etiam pars est missio, atque effusio Spiritus sancti. 2. Post glorificationem Christi datur copiosius, vt in pentecoste: id quod prædictum erat; Et erit vltimis temporibus, dicit Dominus: effundam ex Spiritu meo in quamvis carnem. &c. Efficacia huius Spiritus superna quærimus: quia ibi est thesaurus noster; ibi sunt bona nostra: idque quia Christus ideò ascendit, vt bona, quæ ibi erant, nostra faceret. Et hoc argumentum Pauli Col. 3, 1.
units.tr: 3. The sending of the Holy Spirit, through whom He gathers, comforts and defends the Church until the end of the world. The Holy Spirit was indeed given even to the godly under the law; but 1. with respect to the future ascension and glorification of Christ, of which the sending and outpouring of the Holy Spirit is not only a fruit but also a part. 2. After the glorification of Christ He is given more abundantly, as at Pentecost; which had been foretold: And it shall come to pass in the last days, says the Lord: I will pour out of my Spirit upon all flesh, etc. We seek His power from above, because there is our treasure; there are our goods; and this because Christ ascended for this reason, that He might make our the goods which were there. And this is the argument of Paul, Col. 3:1.

units.la: Sunt & alij fructus ascensionis Christi.
units.tr: There are also other fruits of the ascension of Christ.

units.la: 4. Est testimonium, nobis credentibus esse peccata remissa perfectè. Nisi enim luisset pœnam pro peccatis, nequiuisset introire thronum Dei. Nam vbi peccatum est, ibi & mors. Iudicabit mundum de justitia, eò quod ad Patrem abeam.
units.tr: 4. It is a testimony that to us who believe, sins are fully forgiven. For unless He had paid the penalty for sins, He could not have entered the throne of God. For where sin is, there is death also. He will convict the world concerning righteousness, because I go to the Father.

units.la: 5. Est testimonium, Christum reuera mortis, peccati, & diaboli victorem esse.
units.tr: 5. It is a testimony that Christ is truly the conqueror of death, sin, and the devil.

units.la: 6. Est testimonium, nos nunquam destitutum iri consolatione: quia ideo ascendit, ut Ecclesiæ semper mitteret Spiritum suum. Nisi ego abiero, Consolator ille non veniet ad vos: sin autem profectus fuero, mittam eum ad vos. Cum ascendisset in sublime, captivitatem duxit captivitatem, & dedit dona hominibus.
units.tr: 6. It is a testimony that we shall never be left without consolation: for He ascended so that He might always send His Spirit to the Church. Unless I go away, that Comforter will not come to you; but if I depart, I will send him to you. When He had ascended on high, He led captivity captive, and gave gifts to men.

units.la: 7. Est testimonium, Christum nos perpetuò defensurum, quia caput gloriosum, & supra omnes principatus collocatum, non deseret membra sua.
units.tr: 7. It is a testimony that Christ will defend us forever, because as a glorious Head, placed above all principalities, He will not forsake His members.

units.la: Jam quid est; Credo in Iesum Christum, qui ascendit in cœlum? Resp. Est, credo 1. Christum ascendendo non disparuisse, sed verè ascendisse in cœlum, & jam ibi esse, & invocari velle ad dexteram Patris, donec inde redeat ad judicium. 2. Christum ascendisse mea, & tua causa, & nunc ibi in conspectu Dei apparere & incedere pro nobis, mittere nobis Spiritum sanctum, & tandem nos ad se assumturum esse.
units.tr: Now what is the meaning of: I believe in Jesus Christ, who ascended into heaven? Answer: It means that I believe 1. that Christ, by ascending, did not vanish, but truly ascended into heaven, and is now there, and is willing to be invoked at the right hand of the Father, until He returns thence to judgment. 2. that Christ ascended for my sake and for yours, and now appears in the presence of God and intercedes for us there, sends us the Holy Spirit, and at last will take us to Himself.

units.la: QVÆSTIO L.
units.tr: QUESTION 50.

units.la: Citr additur: Sedet ad dexteram DEI?
units.tr: Why is it added: He sits at the right hand of God?

units.la: RESPONSIO.
units.tr: ANSWER.

units.la: Quia Christus ideo in cœlum ascendit, ut se ibi caput suæ Ecclesiæ declararet, per quod Pater omnia gubernat.
units.tr: Because Christ ascended into heaven so that there he might declare himself the head of his Church, through whom the Father governs all things.

units.la: EXPLICATIO.
units.tr: EXPLANATION.

units.la: Differunt sedere ad dexteram Dei, & ascendere ad cœlos: quia unum potest esse sine altero. Ergo non sunt idem. Differunt autem hic articulus à præcedente tripliciter. 1: Quia hoc articulo finis prioris declaratur. Ideo enim Christus ascendit ad cœlos, ut sederet ad dexteram Dei. 2. Quia perpetuo Christus sedet ad dexteram Patris: at semel tantum ascendit ad cœlos, 3. Ascendunt etiam angeli, ascendemus & nos: sed neque tu, neque illi, vel nos sedebimus ad dexteram Patris. Ad quem enim angelorum dixit: sede ad dexteram meam, usque dum posuero inimicos tuos scabellum pedum tuorum? Multo minus hoc dixit ad ullum hominem excepto Christo.
units.tr: To sit at the right hand of God and to ascend into the heavens are different things, because one can exist without the other. Therefore they are not the same. This article differs from the preceding one in three ways. First, in this article the purpose of the previous one is declared: Christ ascended into the heavens in order to sit at the right hand of God. Second, Christ sits at the right hand of the Father perpetually, but he ascended into the heavens only once. Third, angels also ascend, and we shall ascend too, but neither you nor they nor we will sit at the right hand of the Father. For to which of the angels did he say: Sit at my right hand, until I make your enemies your footstool? Much less did he say this to any man except Christ.

units.la: De Sessione ad dexteram Dei præcipuè considerandum: I. Quid dextera Dei significet. II. Quid sit sedere ad dexteram Dei. III. Quid
units.tr: Concerning the sitting at the right hand of God, the following must chiefly be considered: I. What the right hand of God signifies. II. What it is to sit at the right hand of God. III. What

units.la: III. An semper Christus ad dexteram Dei sederit.IV. Qui sint fructus sessionis Christi ad dexteram Patris.Sed fructus sequenti quaestione explicantur.
units.tr: III. Whether Christ has always sat at the right hand of God. IV. What the fruits of Christ's sitting at the right hand of the Father are. But these fruits are explained in the following question.

units.la: I. Quid in scripturis sit dextera Dei.
units.tr: I. What the right hand of God is in Scripture.

units.la: Dextera tribuitur Deo improprie per ἀνθρωποπάθειαν, vt alia humana membra: & in scripturis duo significat. 1. Summam potentiam & virtutem, seu omnipotentiam Dei. Hunc Deus dextra sua exaltum constituit principem ac seruatorem. Dextera Domini fecit virtutem, Dextera tua Domine percussit inimicum. 2. Summam dignitatem & gloriam seu maiestatem. Hic sumitur secunda significatione.
units.tr: The right hand is attributed to God improperly, by anthropopatheia [ἀνθρωποπάθεια], as are other human members. In Scripture it signifies two things. 1. The highest power and virtue, that is, the omnipotence of God. This one God has exalted with his right hand as prince and savior. The right hand of the Lord has done valiantly; your right hand, O Lord, has dashed the enemy in pieces. 2. The highest dignity, glory, or majesty. It is taken in this second sense here.

units.la: II. Quid sit sessio, seu sedere ad dexteram Dei.
units.tr: II. What sitting, or sitting at the right hand of God, is.

units.la: Sedere ad dexteram Dei est esse personam Deo aequalem potentia & gloria, per quam Pater immediate agit & gubernat omnia. Vulgo definiunt, quod sit, aequali cum Patre potentia & gloria regnare. Verum id quidem est de Christo. Nam omnia facit similiter cum Patre; & praeditus est eadem cum Patre potentia. Sed Filius semper ita regnauit. Idem competit etiam Spiritui sancto, qui tamen ad dexteram Patris in scriptura non dicitur sedere, nec sedet: quia non per Spiritum sanctum, sed per Filium ἀνθρωπος, tanquam per caput & regem Ecclesiae Pater immediate omnia, praesertim Ecclesiam gubernat. Proinde ista vulgo recepta definitio non est sufficiens. Aliqui confundunt sessionem cum ascensione, & idem esse volunt. Sed discrimen prius est ostensum: & absurdum esset dicere, in tam brevi Symbolo ἀναλογίαν committi.
units.tr: To sit at the right hand of God is to be a person equal to God in power and glory, through whom the Father acts and governs all things immediately. Commonly it is defined as reigning with the Father in equal power and glory. This indeed is true of Christ. For he does all things in the same way as the Father and possesses the same power as the Father. But the Son has always reigned in this way. The same also belongs to the Holy Spirit, who nevertheless is not said in Scripture to sit at the right hand of the Father, and does not sit there, because the Father governs all things immediately, and especially the Church, not through the Holy Spirit but through the Son as man, as through the head and king of the Church. Therefore this commonly received definition is not sufficient. Some confuse sitting with ascension and want them to be the same. But the difference has been shown above, and it would be absurd to say that an inconsistency is committed in so short a Creed [ἀναλογία].

units.la: Sumta autem est phrasis ex consuetudine magnatum & regum, qui quos honorant, a dextris collocant, & suos faciunt assessores, quibus regendi partes committunt. Ita Christus dicitur exaltatus ad dexteram Patris, αὐθρωποπάθως: quia Pater eum post opus redemptionis nostrae in terris peractum, summa gloria & honore supra omnes angelos & homines in coelo coronauit, eumque Ecclesiae caput & regem declarauit, per quem immediate omnia in coelo & in terra gubernare, quemq; ab omnibus creaturis adorari velit. Est igitur haec sessio singularis & propria dignitas & gloria Mediatoris Christi ἀνθρωπου exaltati in suo sacerdotio & regno, post ascensionem eia Patre collata: quae secundum declarationem D. Vrsini, in hisce quatuor potissimum consistit.
units.tr: The phrase, however, is taken from the custom of great men and kings, who place at their right hand those whom they honor, and make them their assessors, to whom they entrust the duties of ruling. Thus Christ is said to be exalted to the right hand of the Father anthropopathōs [ἀνθρωποπαθῶς]: because the Father, after the work of our redemption had been accomplished on earth, crowned him in heaven with the highest glory and honor above all angels and men, and declared him the head and king of the Church, through whom he wills to govern all things in heaven and on earth immediately, and whom he wills to be adored by all creatures. This sitting is therefore the singular and proper dignity and glory of the mediator Christ, the exalted man, in his priesthood and kingdom, conferred by the Father after the ascension. According to the explanation of Dr. Ursinus, it consists chiefly in these four things.

units.la: 1. In aequalitate Λόγου seu personae Mediatoris cum Patre: quam quidem non tunc demum accepit, sed ab aeterno habuit. Eam vero toto humilitatis tempore carnis infirmitate tectam, in exaltatione tandem rursus exeruit, atque manifestauit, juxta Patris consilium. Ideo in humilitate precabatur, Ioh.17,5. Patet glorifica me apud teipsum eâ gloriâ, quam habui apud te, priusquam hic mundus exsisteret.
units.tr: 1. In the equality of the Word [Λόγου], that is, of the person of the Mediator, with the Father. He did not receive this only then, but had it from eternity. Yet during the whole time of his humiliation it was veiled by the weakness of the flesh, and in the exaltation it was at last brought out again and manifested, according to the counsel of the Father. Therefore in his humiliation he prayed: John 17:5. Father, glorify me with yourself, with the glory which I had with you before this world existed.

units.la: 2. In perfectione naturae humanae Christi: quam, cùm depositio ne omnium infirmitatum humanarum, post ascensionem est consecutus, hoc est, in excellentia donorum, sapientiae, potentiae, fulgoris, gloriae & maiestatis, omnium denique perfectionum, quae in naturam creatam, citra eius destructionem, cadere aut cogitari possunt: quibus nunc Christi humanitas in gloria coelesti omnes angelos & beatos homines in immensum antecellit. Gloriâ & honore coronasti eum. Ex plenitudine eius omnes accepimus. Non enim huic admetitur Deus spiritum.
units.tr: 2. In the perfection of the human nature of Christ, which, after the laying aside of all human infirmities, he obtained after the ascension; that is, in the excellence of gifts: of wisdom, power, splendor, glory and majesty, and finally of all perfections which can fall upon or be conceived in a created nature without its destruction. By these the humanity of Christ in heavenly glory now immeasurably surpasses all angels and blessed men. You have crowned him with glory and honor. From his fullness we have all received. For God does not give the Spirit to him by measure.

units.la: 3. In perfectione officij Mediatoris: quod jam gloriâ & honore coronatus, atque in sacerdotio suo & regno exaltatus, vt caput Ecclesiae glorificatum gloriosè exercet, intercedens pro nobis, mittens Spiritum sanctum, & Apostolos, Prophetas atque Doctores Ecclesiae, eamque seruans & defendens potenter contra hostes: juxta illud, quod dixit: Data est mihi omnis potestas in coelo & in terra. Ego do ouibus meis vitam aeternam: & nemo rapiet eas ex manu mea.
units.tr: 3. In the perfection of the office of Mediator, which he, now crowned with glory and honor and exalted in his priesthood and kingdom, exercises gloriously as the glorified head of the Church: interceding for us, sending the Holy Spirit, and the Apostles, Prophets and Teachers of the Church, and preserving and defending it powerfully against its enemies. This is according to what he said: All power is given to me in heaven and on earth. I give my sheep eternal life, and no one shall snatch them out of my hand.

units.la: 4. In perfectione honoris, reuerentiae & cultus, quod Christus Mediator in sacerdotio & regno suo exaltatus, Dominus & caput omnium ab omnibus creaturis agnoscitur & celebratur. Propterea exaltauit eum Deus, & donauit ei nomen super omne nomen, vt in nomine Iesu flectatur omne genu, coelestium, terrestrium, & subterraneorum. Hoc nomen non est nomen syllabicum, sed est praestantia personae & officij, & declaratio vtriusque per visibilem maiestatem, vt omnes agnoscant, & fateri cogantur, hunc hominem esse regem illum, per quem omnia Deus gubernat. Sic Stephanus eum vidit coelis apertis stantem à dexteris Dei, visibili maiestate & gloriâ coronatum, & adoravit eum.
units.tr: 4. In the perfection of honor, reverence and worship, since Christ the Mediator, exalted in his priesthood and kingdom, is acknowledged and celebrated as Lord and head of all by all creatures. Therefore God exalted him and gave him a name above every name, so that at the name of Jesus every knee should bow, of heavenly, earthly and subterranean beings. This name is not a syllabic name but the preeminence of the person and office, and a declaration of both through visible majesty, so that all may acknowledge and be compelled to confess that this man is that king through whom God governs all things. So Stephen saw him standing at the right hand of God with the heavens opened, crowned with visible majesty and glory, and adored him.

units.la: Obiect. 1. Etiam Pater & Spiritus sanctus sunt aequales Filio Deitate. Ergo recte diximus, etiam eos sedere ad dexteram Dei. Resp. Negatur consequentia ex mala definitione. Nam aequalitas Deitatis, etsi in Mediatore ad hanc sessionem requirebatur: non tamen est tota sessio ad dexteram Dei, vel pars eius, si absolutè consideretur: nisi quatenus ea carnis velo & infirmitatibus fuit humiliata, tursusque infirmitatum depositione manifestata & glorificata: qualis non est in Deo Patre & Spiritu sancto, sed in solo Filio mediatore. Vnde patet, aequalitatem personæ Mediatoris cum Patre & Spiritu sancto, non esse quidem ipsam sessionem ad dexteram Dei, esse vero sessionis huius fundementum & principium: quod in Mediatore necessariò requirebatur.
units.tr: Objection 1. The Father and the Holy Spirit are also equal to the Son in Deity. Therefore we rightly said that they too sit at the right hand of God. Answer: The consequence is denied, because it rests on a faulty definition. For equality of Deity, although it was required in the Mediator for this sitting, is not the whole sitting at the right hand of God, nor a part of it, if it is considered absolutely, except insofar as it was humbled under the veil of the flesh and its infirmities, and then manifested and glorified again by laying aside the infirmities; this is not so in God the Father and the Holy Spirit, but only in the Son as Mediator. Hence it is clear that the equality of the person of the Mediator with the Father and the Holy Spirit is not indeed the sitting at the right hand of God itself, but is the foundation and principle of this sitting, which was necessarily required in the Mediator.

units.la: Obj. 2. Christus ante ascensionem etiam fuit caput ecclesiæ, & rex gloriæ. Ergo non tunc demum cœpit sedere ad dexteram Dei. R. Est fallacia æquivocationis. Semper quidem fuit caput ecclesiæ, sed non semper fuit caput ecclesiæ exaltatum in suo officio. Semper etiam fuit rex gloriæ, ratione Deitatis: sed non semper fuit rex gloriæ gloriosus in carne assumta; nisi post eversionem ad dexteram Patris in cœlo.
units.tr: Objection 2. Christ was also head of the Church and king of glory before the ascension. Therefore he did not begin to sit at the right hand of God only then. Answer. This is the fallacy of equivocation. He was indeed always head of the Church, but he was not always the head of the Church exalted in his office. He was also always king of glory, by reason of the Deity, but he was not always king of glory glorified in the assumed flesh, except after his exaltation at the right hand of the Father in heaven.

units.la: Obiect. 3. Christus dicit: Si quis vicerit, dabo ei sedere in throno meo, &c. Resp. Ergo & nos sedebimus ad dexteram Patris. Resp. Nos sedebimus participatione gloriæ: concesso interim, quod idem sit Patris & Filij thronus. In eodem throno possunt multi sedere, alius superiori loco, alius inferiori, sed non eadem dignitate. Multi consiliarij sedent juxta Principem: Cancellarius verò sedet ad dexteram principis. Summam igitur illam dignitatem & gloriam à Patre sibi datam Christus non dabit alteri. Inst. Ad dexteram Dei sedere, est etiam gloriosè & beatè viuere. Hoc autem nobis comperit. Resp. Rursus non est sufficiens definitio: quia nobis & angelis competit vita, & gloria: sessio ad dexteram Dei non item.
units.tr: Objection 3. Christ says: If anyone overcomes, I will give him to sit on my throne, etc. Answer: Then we too shall sit at the right hand of the Father. Answer: We shall sit by participation in glory, while granting in the meantime that the throne of the Father and of the Son is the same. In the same throne many can sit, one in a higher place, another in a lower, but not with the same dignity. Many counselors sit beside a prince, but the chancellor sits at the prince's right hand. Christ therefore will not give that highest dignity and glory, given to himself by the Father, to another. Objection. To sit at the right hand of God is also to live gloriously and blessedly. But this belongs to us. Answer. Again, the definition is not sufficient, because life and glory belong also to us and to the angels, but sitting at the right hand of God does not.

units.la: III. An Christus semper ad dexteram DEI sederit.
units.tr: III. Whether Christ has always sat at the right hand of God.

units.la: Hæc quæstio non esset necessaria, nisi curiositas hominum eam, talem faceret. Ad eius verò explicationem opus est primò naturarum, deinde temporis distinctione.
units.tr: This question would not need to be raised at all, unless human curiosity had made it so. To explain it, we need to distinguish, first, the natures and, second, the times.

units.la: Ad diuinitatem quod attinet, Christus secundum eam sem-per sedit ad dexteram Dei. 1. Quatenus sedere ad dexteram est æquali potentia cum Patre regnare, & honore ac gloriâ prædi-tum esse. Natura enim diuina Christi ab æterno fuit æqualis Patri honore & potentiâ: item quatenus sedere ad dexteram Dei significat esse caput Ecclesiæ. Semper enim Filius fuit persona illa, per quam Pater omnia gubernauit, sicut per eandem omnia creauit. Hoc modo Christus nascendo ex Patre ab æternitate ad dexteram Patris esse collocatus, dici potest. 2. Semper sedere ad dexteram Dei, ordinatione ad officium Mediatoris ab æterno facta, 1 Pet. 1, 20. Ad hoc enim ab æterno fuit prædordinatus etiam secundum diuinitatem. 3. Execufione officij Mediatoris: quia λέγ&-Filius Dei inde ab initio ecclesiæ adfuit,
units.tr: As regards the divinity, Christ has always sat at the right hand of God according to it. (1) Sitting at the right hand means reigning with the Father with equal power, and being endowed with equal honour and glory. For the divine nature of Christ was from eternity equal to the Father in honour and power. Likewise, sitting at the right hand of God signifies being the head of the Church. For the Son was always that person through whom the Father governed all things, just as through him he created all things. In this way it can be said that Christ, being born of the Father from eternity, was placed at the Father's right hand. (2) He always sits at the right hand of God by the ordination to the office of Mediator made from eternity, 1 Pet. 1:20. For he was foreordained to this from eternity, even according to his divinity. (3) By the execution of the office of Mediator: because the Son of God, the [λόγος], has been present with the Church from the beginning,

units.la: Post ascensionem Christus juxta diuinitatem dici potest demum collocatus esse ad dexteram Dei, quatenus diuinam suam gloriam tunc coepit gloriosè exerere in carne assumta, sub cuius infirmitate prius in terris latuerat. Nam tunc etiam dicuntur res fieri, cùm incipiunt patefieri. Ideo in humanitate orauit: Nunc glorifica me Pater apud temetipsum eâ gloriâ, quam habui apud te, antequam hic mundus esset. Loquitur de gloria Deitatis, quam tunc apud homines non habebat. Itaque petit, vt sicut eam semper habuit apud Patrem: sic Pater illam deinceps patefaciat etiam apud homines. Proinde non accipiendum hoc est, quasi λόγος aliquam imminutionem aut mutationem diuinitatis suæ passus fuisset: sed eo, quod dictum est, modo.
units.tr: After the ascension, according to his divinity, Christ can be said to have been finally placed at the right hand of God, in that he then began to display his divine glory gloriously in the assumed flesh, under whose weakness he had previously lain hidden on earth. For things are then said to happen when they begin to be revealed. Hence he prayed in his humanity: Now glorify me, Father, with yourself, with the glory I had with you before the world existed. He speaks of the glory of the Godhead, which he did not then have among men. Accordingly he asks that, just as he always had it with the Father, so the Father would henceforth reveal it also among men. Therefore this is not to be taken as though the [λόγος] had suffered some diminution or change of his divinity, but in the manner that has been stated.

units.la: Ad humanam naturam quod attinet, secundum eam tunc demum collocatus est Christus ad dexteram Patris, cùm ascendit in cœlum. Tunc enim demum glorificationem est consecutus, cùm accepit, quod antea non habuit. Oportuit enim Christum pati, & sic ingredi in gloriam suam.
units.tr: As regards the human nature, it was according to this that Christ was finally placed at the right hand of the Father, when he ascended into heaven. For then at last he obtained the glorification, when he received what he had not had before. For it was necessary that Christ should suffer, and so enter into his glory.

units.la: Obiect. 1. Qui sedet ad dexteram Dei, est vbique. Christus sedet ad dexteram Dei. Ergo est vbique. Respond. Datur tum, per communicationem idiomatum. Sed si quis inferat, etiam secundum carnem, plus erit in conclusione, quàm in præmissis.
units.tr: Objection 1. He who sits at the right hand of God is everywhere. Christ sits at the right hand of God. Therefore he is everywhere. Answer. The major is granted, by the communication of attributes. But if someone infers that he is everywhere also according to the flesh, the conclusion will contain more than the premises.

units.la: Obiect. 2. Dextera Dei est vbique. Natura humana sedet ad dexteram Dei. Ergo natura humana est vbique. Resp. Negatur consequentia, quia sunt quatuor termini. Non enim sunt vnus, sed duo termini, dextera Dei, & sedere ad dexteram Dei. Minor esse debet: Natura humana est dextera Dei: sed sic erit falsa. Deinde, nec maior simpliciter est vera. Nam sessionis ad dexteram Dei pars non minima est illa visibilis gloria & maiestas, qua ornata est & refulget in cœlo humanitas Christi, & in qua stantem ad dexteram Dei Christum vidit Stephanus Act.7,56. Hæc verò non est vbique, sed in cœlo tantum.
units.tr: Objection 2. The right hand of God is everywhere. Human nature sits at the right hand of God. Therefore human nature is everywhere. Answer. The consequence is denied, because there are four terms. For they are not one term but two: the right hand of God, and sitting at the right hand of God. The minor ought to be: Human nature is the right hand of God; but so stated it would be false. Further, neither is the major simply true. For a no small part of sitting at the right hand of God is that visible glory and majesty with which the humanity of Christ is adorned and shines in heaven, and in which Stephen saw Christ standing at the right hand of God, Acts 7:56. But this is not everywhere, only in heaven.

units.la: Obiect. 3. Christus ascendit supra omnes cœlos, vt impleret omnia præsentiâ suæ carnis. Resp. Negatur hæc glossa. Ascendit vt donis suis impleret omnia, hoc est, totam Ecclesiam: vt explicatur Ephes.1,23. Ecclesia est complementum eius, qui implet omnia in omnibus: & Eph.4,8. Dedit dona hominibus. Et vers.11. Dedit igitur ipse alios, &c. Minimè verò, vt carne & cute, ossibus & corpore suo impleret omnia loca, cœlum, terram, inferos. Hæc sunt monstra & deliria, quibus diabolus gloriam Christi deridendam propinat mundo.
units.tr: Objection 3. Christ ascended above all the heavens, that he might fill all things with the presence of his flesh. Answer. This gloss is denied. He ascended that he might fill all things with his gifts, that is, the whole Church, as is explained in Eph. 1:23: the Church is the fulness of him who fills all in all; and Eph. 4:8: he gave gifts to men; and verse 11: he himself gave some, etc. By no means did he ascend so as to fill all places, heaven, earth and the underworld, with his flesh and skin, bones and body. These are monsters and delusions, with which the devil serves up the glory of Christ to the world to be mocked.

units.la: Obiect. 4. Natura, quæ accepit omnipotentiam, est vbique. Ergo, &c. Resp. ad maiorem. Humanitas Christi accepit omnipotentiam. maiorem: Natura vbique est, quæ accepit omnipotentiam, reali transfusione: non autem quæ accepit personali vnione. Sic verò humanitas accepit omnipotentiam: non quod ipsa formaliter facta sit omnipotens, sed quia personaliter vnita est omnipotenti Deitati, vt Christus homo sit omnipotens Deus.
units.tr: Objection 4. A nature that has received omnipotence is everywhere. Therefore, etc. Answer to the major. The humanity of Christ has received omnipotence. Answer to the major: a nature is everywhere which has received omnipotence by real transfusion; but not one which has received it by personal union. Now the humanity has received omnipotence not because it has itself been formally made omnipotent, but because it is personally united to the omnipotent Godhead, so that Christ as man is almighty God.

units.la: QVÆSTIO LI.
units.tr: QUESTION 51.

units.la: Quid nobis prodest hæc gloria nostri capitis Christi? RESPONSIO.
units.tr: What benefit do we receive from this glory of our head, Christ? ANSWER.

units.la: Primùm, quod per Spiritum sanctum in nos, sua membra, cœlestia dona effundit a. Deinde, quod nos sua potentia contra omnes hostes protegit ac defendit b.
units.tr: First, that through the Holy Spirit he pours heavenly gifts upon us, his members a. Second, that by his power he protects and defends us against all enemies b.

units.la: a Actor. 2. verf. 33. Ephes. 4. v. 10. b Psalm. 2, 9. & 110, 1. 2. Iohan. 10, 28. Ephes. 4. verf. 8.
units.tr: a Actor. 2. verf. 33. Ephes. 4. v. 10. b Psalm. 2, 9. & 110, 1. 2. Iohan. 10, 28. Ephes. 4. verf. 8.

units.la: EXPLICATIO.
units.tr: EXPLANATION.

units.la: Fructus sessionis Christi ad Patris dexteram, sunt omnia beneficia regni & sacerdotij Christi gloriosi, videlicet 1. Intercessio pro nobis: quæ quid sit, prius est dictum. 2. Collectio, gubernatio & conservatio ecclesiæ per verbum & Spiritum sanctum. 3. Defensio ecclesiæ contra hostes. 4. Abiectio & destructio hostium. 5. Glorificatio ecclesiæ, & abolitio omnium infirmitatum.
units.tr: The fruits of Christ's sitting at the right hand of the Father are all the benefits of his glorious kingly and priestly office, namely: (1) intercession for us, of which the nature has already been explained; (2) the gathering, governing and preserving of the Church through the Word and the Holy Spirit; (3) the defence of the Church against its enemies; (4) the casting down and destruction of its enemies; (5) the glorifying of the Church and the abolition of all its infirmities.

units.la: Hi fructus sessionis Christi ad dexteram sequuntur ex eius officio, quod gerit.
units.tr: These fruits of Christ's sitting at the right hand follow from the office which he exercises.

units.la: REGNI Christi glorificati beneficia sunt, quod nos regit per ministerium verbi, & Spiritum sanctum, quod ministerium conservat, ecclesiæ dat hospitia, efficax est per doctrinam in conuertendis electis: quod electos tandem suscitabit, omnes eorum infirmitates abolebit, eos glorificabit, abstergeт ab iis omnem lacrymam, collocabit eos in throno, eosque faciet Patri suo sacerdotes ac reges.
units.tr: The benefits of the kingly reign of the glorified Christ are these: he rules us through the ministry of the Word and the Holy Spirit; this ministry preserves us, gives the Church its shelter, and is effective through its teaching in converting the elect. Finally, he will raise up the elect, abolish all their infirmities, glorify them, wipe every tear from their eyes, set them on a throne, and make them priests and kings to his Father.

units.la: SACERDOTII Christi glorificati fructus est, quod pro nobis apparet & intercedit in cœlo, & quidem efficaciter, ita vt Pater nihil nobis neget propter valorem intercessionis eius. Hinc oritur consolatio. Quia rex noster, caput nostrum, caro nostra, & frater noster sedet ad dexteram Patris: ergo dabit ciuibus suis bona, Spiritum sanctum: ergo membra sua viuificabit & glorificabit: ergo effundet in nos cœlestia dona, hoc est, veram Dei agniagnitionem, fidem, pœnitentiam, omnes virtutes Christianas: idque facient tum ex amore fraterno, tum ex officio capitis. Quia talem habemus Pontificem, qui ad dexteram Patris consedit: non est, quod de salute dubitemus. Eam enim ipse tuto nobis conseruabit, ac tandem certissimè conferet. Nemo rapiet oves meas ex manu mea. Volo, ut ubi sum ego, & illi sint mecum, quos dedisti mihi.
units.tr: The fruit of the glorified priesthood of Christ is that he appears and intercedes for us in heaven, and does so effectively, so that the Father denies us nothing because of the worth of his intercession. Hence comes our comfort. Our king, our head, our flesh and our brother sits at the right hand of the Father; therefore he will give his citizens good things, the Holy Spirit; therefore he will quicken and glorify his members; therefore he will pour into us heavenly gifts, that is, the true knowledge of God, faith, repentance and all Christian virtues; and he will do this both from brotherly love and from the duty of a head. Since we have such a High Priest, who has sat down at the right hand of the Father, there is no reason for us to doubt our salvation. For he himself will keep it safe for us and at last most certainly bestow it. No one shall snatch my sheep out of my hand. I will that where I am, they also may be with me, whom thou hast given me.

units.la: Jam quæ est applicatio, & quid credis de sessione Christi ad dexteram Patris? Resp. Credo Christum in summa & divina maiestate pro me & omnibus electis intercedere, & applicare nobis sacrificium suum, ut per & propter eum, Pater mihi det vitam æternam: & in hac vita etiam me regere, & defendere contra diabolum & pericula omnia: tandemq; me esse glorificaturum, & donaturum vitâ æternâ.
units.tr: Now what is the application, and what do you believe concerning Christ's sitting at the right hand of the Father? Answer: I believe that Christ, in supreme and divine majesty, intercedes for me and for all the elect, and applies to us his sacrifice, so that through him and for his sake the Father gives me eternal life; and that in this life he also rules me and defends me against the devil and all dangers; and that at last he will glorify me and grant me eternal life.

units.la: QVÆSTIO LII. Quid te consolatur reditus Christi ad iudicandum vivos & mortuos?
units.tr: QUESTION 52. What comforts you concerning the return of Christ to judge the living and the dead?

units.la: RESPONSIO.
units.tr: ANSWER.

units.la: Quod in omnibus miseriis & persecutionibus, erecto capite, eundem illum, qui se prius pro me judicio statuit, & maledictionem omnem à me abstulit, judicem è cœlo exspecto a, qui omnes suos & meos hostes in æternas pœnas abijciat b: me verò cum omnibus electis ad se in cœlestia gaudia, & sempiternam gloriam traducat c.
units.tr: That in all miseries and persecutions I lift up my head and await from heaven that same One who previously presented himself to judgment for me and took from me every curse, as judge; he will cast all his enemies and mine into eternal punishments, and will bring me with all the elect to himself, into heavenly joys and everlasting glory a.

units.la: a Philip. 3. verf. 20. Luc. 21. verf. 28. Roman. 8. verf. 23. Tit. 2. verf. 13. 1 Thessalon. 4. v. 16. b Matthæi 25. v. 41. 2 Thessalon. 1. v. 6, 7. c Matth. 25. verf. 34.
units.tr: a Philippians 3, verse 20; Luke 21, verse 28; Romans 8, verse 23; Titus 2, verse 13; 1 Thessalonians 4, verse 16. b Matthew 25, verse 41; 2 Thessalonians 1, verses 6, 7. c Matthew 25, verse 34.

units.la: EXPLICATIO.
units.tr: EXPLANATION.

units.la: In hoc articulo coincidunt tres loci: de secundo adventu Christi, de fine mundi, & de iudicio extremo. De his continuo dicam, quia cohærent: ita tamen, ut postremus, de iudicio extremo, præcipuè tractetur. Nam parum esset, nos cogitare de Christi secundo adventu, nisi simul consideraretur, ad quid venturus sit.
units.tr: Three topics come together in this article: the second coming of Christ, the end of the world, and the last judgment. I shall speak of these in turn, because they cohere; yet the last, the last judgment, will be treated especially. For it would be of little use for us to think about Christ's second coming unless we considered at the same time for what purpose he will come.

units.la: QVÆST. LII. De Extremo Judicio
units.tr: QUESTION LII. On the Last Judgment

units.la: Quæstiones de Extremo Judicio potissimum considerandæ sunt istæ seqq.
units.tr: The questions chiefly to be considered concerning the Last Judgment are the following.

units.la: I. An sit futurum judicium.
units.tr: I. Whether there will be a judgment.

units.la: II. Quid sit illud judicium.
units.tr: II. What that judgment is.

units.la: III. Quis judex.
units.tr: III. Who the judge is.

units.la: IV. Unde & quo sit venturus judex.
units.tr: IV. Whence and whither the judge will come.

units.la: V. Quomodo venturus.
units.tr: V. How he will come.

units.la: VI. Quos sit judicaturus.
units.tr: VI. Whom he will judge.

units.la: VII. Qualis futura sententia & exsecutio judicij.
units.tr: VII. What the sentence and execution of the judgment will be.

units.la: IIX. Quare futura hæc exsecutio.
units.tr: VIII. Why this execution will take place.

units.la: IX. Quando.
units.tr: IX. When.

units.la: X. Cur de eo debeamus esse certi.
units.tr: X. Why we ought to be certain of it.

units.la: XI. Cur tempus incertum.
units.tr: XI. Why the time is uncertain.

units.la: XII. Cur differatur.
units.tr: XII. Why it is delayed.

units.la: XIII. An sit optandum.
units.tr: XIII. Whether it is to be desired.

units.la: I. An sit futurum iudicium.
units.tr: I. Whether there will be a judgment.

units.la: Hæc quæstio necessaria est. Nam scriptura prædixit, postremis temporibus venturos esse irrisores, qui sint hunc articulum habituri pro fabula: Ubi est pollicitatio adventus eius? Nam ex quo patres obdormiuerunt, omnia ita permanent ab initio creationis, &c. Ex philosophia quidem judicium extremum demonstrari non potest. Sed neque contra hoc est in ea quicquam pugnans. Certitudo autem tota pendet ex doctrina Ecclesiæ, & oraculis divinis. Quamuis enim philosophus aliquid fortasse per caliginem diceret, & ratio etiam judicet, bonis bene, malis male esse debere, necesse verisimile, hominem ad has miserias conditum esse: tamen propter amissam cognitionem justitiæ, bonitatis & veritatis divinæ, non potest satis certò concludere, quod vel quando sit futurum judicium: multò minus, quibus futurum sit circumstantiis. Oportet ergo accedere testimonia scripturæ. Argumenta quidem, quæ philosophia supponit, efficacia sunt per se, sed non explicantur, nisi in Theologia: proinde etiam tantum fiunt efficacia in Theologia. Probationes igitur futuri judicij.
units.tr: This question is necessary. For Scripture foretold that in the last times there would be scoffers who would count this article a fable: Where is the promise of his coming? For since the fathers fell asleep, all things continue as they were from the beginning of creation, etc. Indeed, the Last Judgment cannot be demonstrated from philosophy. But nothing in philosophy argues against it either. Its certainty, however, depends entirely on the teaching of the Church and the divine oracles. For although a philosopher might perhaps say something in the dark, and reason too may judge that good things should go well for the good and badly for the bad, and it is probable that man was not created for these miseries, yet because the knowledge of divine justice, goodness and truth has been lost, he cannot conclude with sufficient certainty that a judgment will come, or when; much less in what circumstances. It is necessary, therefore, to add the testimonies of Scripture. The arguments which philosophy assumes are effective in themselves, but they are not unfolded except in theology; therefore they become effective only in theology. Here, then, are the proofs of a future judgment.

units.la: 1. Sunt testimonia scripturæ ex veteri & novo Testamento, directè hoc asserentia. Ut prophetia Danielis: Aspiciebam in visione noctis, & ecce in nubibus cæli quasi filius hominis veniebat, & usque ad antiquum dierum pervenit, & in conspectu eius appropinquare fecerunt eum: & dedit ei potestatem, & honorem, & regnum: & omnes populi, tribus & linguæ ipsi servient: potestas eius potestas æterna, quæ non auferetur, & regnum eius, quod non corrumpetur. Et mox: Antiquus dierum sedit, vestimentum eius erat ut candidum: thronus thronus eius flamma ignis: fluuius igneus procedebat, egrediebaturque à conspectu eius: millies mille ministrabant ei. & decies millies centena millia coram eo stabant: postea judicium sedit: & libri aperti sunt: & infecta est bestia, & perditum corpus eius, & tradita incendio ignis. Item prophetia Enochi citata ab apostolo Juda: Ecce venit Dominus cum sanctis millibus suis, vt ferat judicium aduersus omnes, & redarguat quicunque ex iis sunt impij, de factis omnibus, quae impie patrauerint, deque omnibus duris, quae locuti fuerint aduersus ipsum peccatores impij. Item conciones Christi, maximè apud Matthaeum cap. 24. & 25. Similiter conciones Apostolorum: Diem statuit Dominus, quo iuste judicaturus est orbem terrarum, per eum virum, quem definiit, fide palam facta omnibus illo a mortuis excitato. Ipse Dominus, cum hortationis clamore & voce archangeli ac Dei tuba descendet e coelo: & qui mortui fuerint in Christo, resurgent primum: deinde nos viui, qui reliqui erimus, rapiemur simul cum eis, in nubes, in occursum Domini, in aera. Statutum est hominibus semel mori, post ea judicium. Et vidi, thronum magnum candidum, & quendam eum insidentem, &c. & vidi mortuos magnos & pusillos stantes in conspectu Dei, & libri aperti sunt: & alius liber apertus est, qui est liber vitae, judicati ex his, qui scripta sunt in libris, secundum opera ipsorum. Nec solum certitudo futuri judicij constat ex his & similibus distinctis scripturae testimoniis, sed etiam ex aliis, ex quibus bona consequentia deducitur.
units.tr: 1. There are testimonies of Scripture from the Old and New Testaments asserting this directly. Such is the prophecy of Daniel: I was watching in a vision of the night, and behold, one like the Son of man came with the clouds of heaven, and he came to the Ancient of days, and they brought him near before him. And there was given him dominion, and glory, and a kingdom; and all peoples, nations and languages shall serve him: his dominion is an everlasting dominion, which shall not pass away, and his kingdom that which shall not be destroyed. And soon after: The Ancient of days sat, his garment was white as snow, and the hair of his head like pure wool: his throne was a fiery flame, and its wheels burning fire. A fiery stream issued and came forth from before him; thousands of thousands ministered to him, and ten thousand times ten thousand stood before him: the judgment was set, and the books were opened. And the beast was slain, and its body destroyed, and given over to the burning of fire. Likewise the prophecy of Enoch, cited by the apostle Jude: Behold, the Lord comes with ten thousands of his saints, to execute judgment upon all, and to convict all the ungodly of all their ungodly deeds which they have committed in an ungodly way, and of all the harsh things which ungodly sinners have spoken against him. Likewise the sermons of Christ, especially in Matthew chapters 24 and 25. Similarly the sermons of the apostles: The Lord has appointed a day on which he will judge the world in righteousness, by the man whom he has appointed, having given assurance of this to all by raising him from the dead. The Lord himself will descend from heaven with a shout, with the voice of the archangel and the trumpet of God; and the dead in Christ will rise first; then we who are alive and remain will be caught up together with them in the clouds, to meet the Lord in the air. It is appointed for men once to die, and after this the judgment. And I saw a great white throne, and one sitting on it, etc. And I saw the dead, great and small, standing before God, and books were opened; and another book was opened, which is the book of life, and the dead were judged by what was written in the books, according to their works. Nor is the certainty of a future judgment established only by these and similar distinct testimonies of Scripture, but also by other arguments from which a sound inference is drawn.

units.la: 2. Ex decreto Dei. Deus ab aeterno ordinauit & proposuit excitare mortuos. Ergo cùm sit immutabilis, hoc decretum non antiquabit. Eius decreti typus & specimen exstat Ezech. 37. & exempla sunt Enoch, Elias, Christus, &c.
units.tr: 2. From the decree of God. God from eternity ordained and purposed to raise the dead. Therefore, since he is unchangeable, this decree will not be annulled. The type and pattern of this decree stands in Ezekiel 37, and there are examples in Enoch, Elijah, Christ, etc.

units.la: 3. Ex omnipotentia Dei: qua potest etiam rationi absurda seu erre. Hoc argumento Christus vtitur contra Sadducaeos: Erratis, nescientes scripturas, neque potentiam Dei.
units.tr: 3. From the omnipotence of God, by which he can even do what is absurd to reason, or to error. Christ uses this argument against the Sadducees: You are wrong, not knowing the Scriptures nor the power of God.

units.la: 4. Ex justitia Dei: quae postulat bonis bene, malis male esse, & quidem perfecte: quod cùm nunc non fiat, certum est, restare aliud seculum, in quo Deus illam justitiae normam exercebit. Sic Paulus se & omnes pios in cruce consolatur. Tolerantia in oppressionibus indicium est justi judicij DEI, &c. Siquidem qui vos affligunt, afflictionem, vobis verò, qui affligimini, relaxationem nobiscum, cùm patefiet Dominus Iesus de coelo, cùm angelus potentia sua, &c. Memento, fili, te bona tua accepisse in vita tua, & Lazarum similiter mala: nunc autem hic solatio fruitur, tu verò cruciaris.
units.tr: 4. From the justice of God, which requires that good things go well for the good and bad for the bad, and indeed perfectly. Since this does not now happen, it is certain that another age remains in which God will carry out that standard of justice. So Paul consoles himself and all the godly in the cross: Your endurance in the oppressions is a sign of the righteous judgment of God, etc.; since it is just for God to repay affliction to those who afflict you, and to give relief to you who are afflicted, along with us, when the Lord Jesus is revealed from heaven with his mighty angels, etc. Remember, son, that you received your good things in your life, and Lazarus likewise evil things; but now he is comforted here, and you are tormented.

units.la: 5. Ex fine: ad quem à Deo conditum est genus humanum. Deus necessariò assequitur suum finem. Ad hoc autem condidit genus humanum, vt esset templum, in quo habitaret, cui communimunicaret lætitiam & beatitudinem: quod cùm nunc non fiat, nec tamen præstantissimam creaturam Deus ad miseriam perpetuam crearit, certò colligimus futuram mutationem. Assequetur enim Deus suum finem, nec patietur, vt templum Spiritus sancti perpetua consumatur putredine. Felicitas est pars imaginis Dei, ad quam homo erat conditus. Sed hæc destructa est à Diabolo. Ergo Deus eam restituet, quia fortior est diabolo. Neque enim solum est verisimile (vt philosophus argumentatur) sed & longè certissimum, hominem non esse conditum ad has miserias, sed ad finem meliorem, qui licet in hac vita variis modis impediatur: cum tamen certo Deus in hominem tandem consequetur. Hoc argumento confirmatur etiam corporum nostrorum resurrectio & felicitas, juxta illud Pauli: An ignoratis, corpus vestrum esse templum Spiritus sancti, qui est in vobis?
units.tr: 5. From the end for which the human race was created by God. God necessarily attains his end. Now he created the human race for this, that there might be a temple in which he would dwell, and to which he would communicate joy and blessedness. Since this does not now happen, and yet God did not create the most excellent creature for perpetual misery, we confidently conclude that a change will come. For God will attain his end, nor will he suffer the temple of the Holy Spirit to be consumed by perpetual putrefaction. Happiness is part of the image of God, in which man was created. But this was destroyed by the Devil. Therefore God will restore it, because he is stronger than the Devil. For it is not only probable (as the philosopher argues) but by far most certain that man was not created for these miseries, but for a better end, which, although it is hindered in this life in various ways, God will at last certainly bring about in man. By this argument the resurrection of our bodies and their blessedness is also confirmed, according to the word of Paul: Do you not know that your body is the temple of the Holy Spirit who is in you?

units.la: 6. Ex Dei gloria. Deus hominem creavit, vt ipsum perpetuò celebret. Hoc autem non fieret sine resurrectione & judicio.
units.tr: 6. From the glory of God. God created man so that he might celebrate him forever. But this would not happen without resurrection and judgment.

units.la: Alia argumenta ad hæc referri possunt.
units.tr: Other arguments may be referred to these.

units.la: II. Quid sit iudicium extremum.
units.tr: II. What the Last Judgment is.

units.la: In omni mundano judicio sunt, reus, actor, judex, causa, accusatio causæ, lex secundum quam judicatur, sententia absolutionis, vel damnationis, & eius executio secundum leges. Iudicium mundanum in genere est inquisitio causæ, à judice ordinatio secundum leges facta, & sententiæ de reo vel absolutione vel plectendo latio & executio.
units.tr: Every worldly judgment involves a defendant, a plaintiff, a judge, a cause, the charge brought in the cause, the law by which the case is decided, the sentence of acquittal or condemnation, and the carrying out of that sentence according to the laws. A worldly judgment, in general, is an inquiry into a cause, an ordering of the matter by the judge according to the laws, and the pronouncing and carrying out of a sentence on the defendant, either of acquittal or of punishment.

units.la: Hinc facilè eruitur definitio iudicij extremi, quod Deus exercebit per Christum. Actoribus & testibus non egebit hic judex, quia ipse manifesta faciet opera omnium, cùm sit κρίσις, sed tantum erunt rei, lex, sententia, & executio sententiæ. Iudicium igitur extremum erit, quando in fine dierum Christus judex, in gloria & maiestate Patris & angelorum, visibiliter descendet de cœlo in nubes, & suscitabuntur omnes homines, qui mortui fuerunt ab initio mundi, reliqui autem subito immutabuntur, & sistentur omnes ante tribunal Christi, qui de omnibus sententiam, & impios cum diabolis abiicit in æternas pœnas, pios autem ad se assumet, vt cum ipso & beatis angelis in cœlo fruantur æterna felicitate & gloria. Ita veniet, quemadmodum conspexistis eum proficiscentem in cœlum. Breuius: Iudicium extremum erit retectio cordium, & patefactio omnium eorum, quæ homines fecerunt, & discretio ac separatio iustorum & iustorum, à iudice Deo per Christum futura, & latio sententiæ de omnibus, sententiaq; exsecutio secundum doctrinam legis & euangelij, quae erit perfecta liberatio ecclesiae, impiorum vero ac diabolorum in aeternas poenas abiectio.
units.tr: From this a definition of the last judgment, which God will hold through Christ, is easily drawn. This judge will need no plaintiffs or witnesses, because he himself will make manifest the works of all, since he is the judgment (κρίσις); there will be only the defendants, the law, the sentence, and the carrying out of the sentence. The last judgment, then, will take place when, at the end of days, Christ the judge, in the glory and majesty of the Father and of the angels, shall descend visibly from heaven in the clouds; all who have died from the beginning of the world will be raised, and the rest will be suddenly changed; all will be made to stand before the tribunal of Christ, who will pronounce sentence on all, casting the ungodly with the devils into everlasting punishment, and taking the godly to himself, so that with him and the blessed angels they may enjoy eternal happiness and glory in heaven. So he will come, just as you saw him going into heaven. More briefly: the last judgment will be the disclosure of hearts and the revealing of all that men have done, and the discerning and separating of the righteous and the unrighteous, to be carried out by God the judge through Christ; the pronouncing of sentence on all, and the execution of the sentence according to the doctrine of the law and the gospel. This will be the complete deliverance of the Church, and the casting of the ungodly and the devils into everlasting punishment.

units.la: Huius definitionis partes omnes confirmantur ex scriptura, 1. Detectio & patefactio omnium. Nam aperientur libri, ut manifesta fiant arcana cordium. 2. Fiet separatio iustorum & iniustorum. Judex enim separabit alios ab aliis, ut pastor separat oves ab haedis, & statuet oves ad dexteram suam, haedos ad sinistram. 3. Haec separatio fiet ab ipso Deo. Erit ergo judicium plane divinum & iustissimum. Si Deus iniustus, quomodo judex erit mundi? Per Christum fiet: quia Pater omne judicium dedit Filio. Deus constituit mundum judicare per virum. 4. Erit latio sententiae: quia judex stantibus ad dexteram dicet: Venite benedicti Patris mei, possidete regnum paratum vobis a jactis fundamentis mundi. Aliis ad sinistram: Ite maledicti in ignem aeternum, qui paratus est diabolo & angelis eius. 5. Fiet aeterna exsecutio: Et abibunt isti in ignem aeternum: justi vero in vitam aeternam. 6. Haec ratione secundum Legem & Euangelium pij & impij judicabuntur, hoc est, justi vel injusti declarabuntur coram tribunali Christi. Nam absolutio justorum fiet principaliter secundum Euangelium, confirmabitur per legem. Damnatio injustorum fiet principaliter per Legem, confirmabitur ab Euangelio. Sententia de piis feretur ex merito ipsorum: sententia de impiis feretur ex mertio Christi fide ipsis applicato, cuius fidei testimonium erunt eorum opera. Fatebuntur enim ipsi non secundum meritum suum, sed secundum gratiam sibi fieri retributionem praemiorum. Quando vidimus te esurientem, aut sitientem? Nam turaliter omnes irae DEI sumus obnoxij. Benedicti autem a DEO pronunciabimur, non in Adamo, sed in semine benedicto, CHRISTO. Proinde sententia haec erit secundum Euangelium.
units.tr: All parts of this definition are confirmed from Scripture: (1) the uncovering and revealing of all things, for the books will be opened so that the secrets of hearts become manifest; (2) there will be a separation of the righteous and the unrighteous, for the judge will separate one from another, as a shepherd separates the sheep from the goats, and will set the sheep at his right hand and the goats at his left; (3) this separation will be made by God himself. The judgment will therefore be plainly divine and most just. If God were unjust, how could he be the judge of the world? It will be done through Christ, because the Father has given all judgment to the Son, and God has appointed the world to be judged by a man; (4) there will be the pronouncing of sentence, for the judge will say to those on his right: Come, you blessed of my Father, inherit the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world; and to those on his left: Depart, you cursed, into everlasting fire, which is prepared for the devil and his angels; (5) there will be everlasting execution: And these shall go away into everlasting fire, but the righteous into life eternal; (6) in this way the godly and the ungodly will be judged according to the Law and the Gospel; that is, the righteous and the unrighteous will be declared so before the tribunal of Christ. For the acquittal of the righteous will take place chiefly according to the Gospel, and will be confirmed by the Law; the condemnation of the unrighteous will take place chiefly by the Law, and will be confirmed by the Gospel. The sentence on the godly will be pronounced on the basis of their own merit; the sentence on the ungodly will be pronounced on the basis of the merit of Christ applied to them by faith, and their works will be the testimony of that faith. For they themselves will confess that the reward is given not according to their own merit but according to grace. When did we see you hungry, or thirsty? For by nature we are all liable to the wrath of God. We shall be pronounced blessed by God, not in Adam, but in the blessed seed, Christ. Therefore this sentence will be according to the Gospel.

units.la: Obiect. At unicuique secundum opera sua reddetur. Ergo non secundum Euangelium, sed secundum Legem tantum judicabitur. Resp. Etiam electis reddetur secundum opera: non quod opera eorum sint merita vitae: sed quia erunt effecta & testimonia fidei, quae habita fuit Euangelio. Ergo etiam secundum Euangelium, quod requirit fidem & opera fidei, judicabuntur electi. Potius autem secundum effecta fidei, quam secundum ipsam fidem Christus judicabit. 1. Quia volet manifestum esse omnibus, quod juste judicet. Ne enim impij calumnientur eius justitiam, quasi credentibus vitam iniquè adjudicet: probabit ex fructibus fidei fidem eorum veram fuisse, ideoque tales esse eos, quibus juxta promissionem Euangelij, vita aeterna justè tribuitur. tribuatur. Monstrabit igitur impiis opera nostra, eaque ad refutandum illos proferet, tanquam testimonia, quod in hac vita applicuerimus nobis meritum tuum vera fide per dilectionem operante. 2. Vt in hac vita consolationem habeamus ex operibus, nos sistendos ad dextram.
units.tr: Objection. But to each one will be rendered according to his works. Therefore he will not be judged according to the Gospel, but according to the Law alone. Answer. The elect too will be rewarded according to their works; not because their works are the merits of life, but because they will be the effects and the testimonies of the faith which they had in the Gospel. Therefore the elect will be judged also according to the Gospel, which requires faith and the works of faith. Yet Christ will judge according to the effects of faith rather than according to faith itself: (1) because he wishes it to be manifest to all that he judges justly. For lest the ungodly accuse his justice, as if he unjustly adjudged life to believers, he will prove by the fruits of faith that their faith was true, and that they are therefore such persons as to whom eternal life is justly given according to the promise of the Gospel. He will therefore show our works to the ungodly, and will bring them forward as witnesses to refute them, that in this life we applied to ourselves your merit by true faith working through love; (2) so that in this life we may have comfort from our works, that we shall be set at the right hand.

units.la: III. Quis sit futurus iudex.
units.tr: III. Who the future judge will be.

units.la: Judex erit CHRISTVS, persona eadem, quae & mediator. Pater enim omne judicium dedit Filio: & authoritatem ei dedit judicium exercendi: quia filius hominis est. Non quod removeantur a judicio Pater & Spiritus sanctus, sed quia Christus in sua natura humana apparebit, loquetur & feret sententiam. Ipso autem loquente, Deus loquetur, & ipso judicante, Deus judicabit, non solum, quia ipse Deus est, sed etiam, quia Pater per ipsum loquetur & judicabit. Ipse definitus est a Deo judex vivorum & mortuorum. Iudicaturus est orbem terrarum juste, per eum visibilem actum, promulgationem & executionem sententiae. Itaque judicium erit totius individuae Trinitatis, quod ad consensum & authoritatem: Christi vero quod latam exsequetur. Ecclesia etiam judicabit, approbatione huius judicij, quomodo Christus dicit, apostolos sessuros super duodecim thronos, & judicaturos duodecim tribus Israel. Nos ergo judicabimus, hoc est, Christi sententiam approbabimus, eiq; subscribemus.
units.tr: The judge will be Christ, the same person who is also the mediator. For the Father has given all judgment to the Son and has given him authority to exercise judgment, because he is the Son of man. This does not mean that the Father and the Holy Spirit are removed from judgment, but that Christ will appear in his human nature, will speak and will pronounce sentence. When he speaks, God will speak, and when he judges, God will judge, not only because he is God himself, but also because the Father will speak and judge through him. He has been appointed by God as judge of the living and the dead. He will judge the world of the earth righteously, through that visible act, the promulgation and execution of the sentence. Thus the judgment will belong to the whole undivided Trinity as to consent and authority, but the execution of the sentence belongs to Christ. The Church also will judge, by approving this judgment, as Christ says, that the apostles will sit upon twelve thrones and judge the twelve tribes of Israel. We therefore will judge, that is, we will approve Christ's sentence and subscribe to it.

units.la: Sed quare Christus homo erit judex? 1. Quia debet judicare homines. Ergo necesse erit, eum ut judicem ab hominibus conspici. Nam Deus est invisibilis. 2. Quia per eundem mediatorem Deus vult glorificari Ecclesiam, per quem etiam est justificata, quique ei beneficia haec promeruit. Per eum virum Deus judicabit orbem terrarum, quem definiit. Videbunt Filium hominis venientem in nubibus coeli, cum potentia & gloria multa. Pater authoritatem dedit Filio judicium etiam exercendi, quatenus Filius hominis est. 3. Vt habeamus hanc consolationem, judicem hunc, cum sit redemptor & frater noster, & caput nostrum, nobis fore propitium, neque damnaturum eos, quos suo sanguine redemit, immo quos fratres & membra sua facere dignatus est. Consolatur igitur nos 1. Persona judicis. Est enim frater noster & caro nostra. 2. Promissio judicis. Promisit enim, & dixit: Qui credit in Filium, habet vitam aeternam, & in condemnationem non venit, sed transiit a morte in vitam. 3. Causa finalis: Ideo venit, ut Ecclesiam liberet, & impios abiiciat. 4. Propter justitiam Dei 1. Quia Christum mundus affecit contumelia repudiatis eius beneficiis: ideo videbunt, quem confixerunt, vt eò magis confundat hostes suos, qui eum cogentur videre judicem, cui restiterunt.
units.tr: But why will Christ be judge as man? (1) Because he ought to judge men, and so it is necessary that he be seen by men as judge, for God is invisible. (2) Because God wills that through the same mediator the Church be glorified, through whom she has also been justified, and who has merited these benefits for her. God will judge the world through that man whom he has appointed. They will see the Son of man coming in the clouds of heaven, with great power and glory. The Father has given the Son authority also to exercise judgment, insofar as he is the Son of man. (3) So that we may have this consolation: that this judge, since he is our redeemer, our brother and our head, will be merciful to us and will not condemn those whom he redeemed with his blood, indeed those whom he has deigned to make his brothers and members. He therefore comforts us by: (1) the person of the judge, for he is our brother and our flesh; (2) the promise of the judge, for he has promised and said: He who believes in the Son has eternal life, and does not come into condemnation, but has passed from death into life; (3) the final cause, for he came to deliver the Church and to cast off the wicked; (4) on account of God's justice. (1) Because the world has treated Christ with contumely and rejected his benefits, therefore they will see him whom they pierced, so that he may all the more confound his enemies, who will be compelled to see as judge the one they resisted.

units.la: Obiect. Christus dicit, se non venisse ad judicandum. Quomodo igitur erit judex? Resp. Loquitur de primo aduentu, in quo non venit ad judicandum, sed ad seruandum mundum. In secundo autem aduentu propterea veniet, vt sit judex viuorum & mortuorum.
units.tr: Objection: Christ says that he did not come to judge. How then will he be judge? Answer: He speaks of his first coming, in which he did not come to judge but to save the world. In his second coming, however, he will come for this very purpose, that he may be judge of the living and the dead.

units.la: IV. Vnde & quo sit venturus iudex.
units.tr: IV. From where and to where the judge will come.

units.la: E coelo exspectamus judicem nostrum Christum, venturum in nubes. Inde enim veniet, quo discipuli ascendentem viderunt. Patefecit Dominus Iesus de coelo cum angelis potentiis suis. Ab hoc tempore videbitis Filium hominis sedentem ad dexteram potentiae Dei, & venientem in nubibus coeli. Conuersatio nostra in coelis est, unde & seruatorem exspectamus Dominum nostrum Iesum Christum. E coelo igitur, vbi sedet ad dexteram Dei (non ex aere, aut mari, aut terra) descendet in nubes, hoc est, descendet e coelo visibiliter in hanc regionem aeris, sicut revera visibiliter per nubes ascendit in coelum. Sicut eum vidistis ascendentem, ita veniet. Haec necessario proponuntur, vt Ecclesia sciat, unde sit exspectandus judex & redemptor. Sicut enim Christus vult sciri, quonam ascenderit: ita etiam vult sciri, unde sit rediturus: vt simus certi, cum non deposuisse naturam humanam, quam assumserat.
units.tr: From heaven we await our judge, Christ, who will come in the clouds. For he will come from the place whence the disciples saw him ascend. The Lord Jesus will be revealed from heaven with his mighty angels. From this time you will see the Son of man sitting at the right hand of the power of God, and coming in the clouds of heaven. Our citizenship is in heaven, whence we also await the Saviour, our Lord Jesus Christ. Therefore he will descend from heaven, where he sits at the right hand of God (not from the air, or the sea, or the earth), in the clouds; that is, he will descend visibly from heaven into this region of the air, just as he truly ascended visibly through the clouds into heaven. As you saw him ascending, so he will come. These things are set forth necessarily, so that the Church may know from where the judge and redeemer is to be awaited. For just as Christ wills it to be known whither he ascended, so he also wills it to be known whence he is to return, so that we may be certain that he has not laid aside the human nature which he had assumed.

units.la: V. Quomodo venturus sit.
units.tr: V. How he will come.

units.la: 1. Veniet vere, visibiliter, & locali modo e coelo, non nudâ apparentiâ. Sic veniet, sicut vidistis eum ascendentem in coelum. Sed visibiliter & localiter ascendit. Ergo sic descendet. Videbunt Filium hominis venientem in nubibus coeli: & cognoscent eum esse Deum, ex visibili eius maiestate. Videbunt, quem transfixerunt. 2.
