Veniet instructus gloria Patris & maiestate diuina, cum omnibus angelis, cum voce & tuba archangeli, cum potentia diuina, ad excitandos mortuos, ad separandas oues ab haedis, ad liberandos pios, & abijciendos impios in poenas aeternas. Filius hominis veniet cum gloria Patris sui, & angelis suis, hoc est, venient in tali gloria, quae soli vero Deo conueniat: & gloriosus propter gloriosum comitatum & satellitium angelorum. 3. Veniet subito, impiis non exspectantibus. Cum dicent: pax, pax, veniet vt fur in nocte.
units.tr: (1) He will come truly, visibly and locally from heaven, not with a mere appearance. He will come in the same way as you saw him go up into heaven. But he ascended visibly and locally. Therefore he will descend in this way. They will see the Son of man coming in the clouds of heaven, and they will recognise from his visible majesty that he is God. They will see him whom they pierced. (2) He will come attended by the glory of the Father and divine majesty, with all the angels, with the voice and trumpet of the archangel, with divine power, to raise the dead, to separate the sheep from the goats, to deliver the godly, and to cast the wicked into eternal punishments. The Son of man will come in the glory of his Father and with his angels; that is, they will come in such glory as belongs to the true God alone, and he will be glorious on account of his glorious retinue and the attendance of his angels. (3) He will come suddenly, when the wicked are not expecting him. When they say, "Peace, peace," then he will come like a thief in the night.

units.la: VI. Quos sit iudicaturus.
units.tr: VI. Whom he will judge.

units.la: Judicabit omnes homines, tam viuos, quàm mortuos, tam bonos, quàm malos, etiam angelos malos. Homines autem dicuntur viui vel mortui, respectu status, qui praecedit judicium. Viui enim intelliguntur, qui ad judicium vsq; supervixerunt. Reliqui omnes dicuntur mortui: atq; hi tempore judicij resurgent: illi immutabuntur, quae immutatio illis erit mortis loco: & sic omnes sistemur apud tribunal Christi.
units.tr: He will judge all people, the living as well as the dead, the good as well as the wicked, and also the evil angels. People are called living or dead with respect to the state that precedes the judgment. Those are called living who survive until the judgment. All the rest are called dead, and these will rise again at the time of judgment. The living will be changed, and that change will take the place of death for them. So all of us will be presented before the tribunal of Christ.

units.la: Obiect.1. Qui credit, non venit in judicium. Ergo non omnes judicabuntur. Resp. Qui credit, non veniet in judicium condemnationis, sed veniet in judicium absolutionis. Omnes ergo judicabimur, latè sumendo vocabulum judicij pro toto actu judicij, damnationis & absolutionis simul. Sed non omnes judicabimur, quoad damnationem. Diaboli judicabuntur, non tantum quoad damnationem, sed etiam quoad exasperationem judicij.
units.tr: Objection 1. He who believes does not come into judgment; therefore not all will be judged. Answer. He who believes will not come into the judgment of condemnation, but will come into the judgment of absolution. So we will all be judged, if the word judgment is taken broadly for the whole act of judging, both condemnation and absolution together. But not all will be judged with respect to condemnation. The devils will be judged not only with respect to condemnation but also with respect to the increased bitterness of the judgment.

units.la: Obiect.2. Princeps mundi jam judicatus est. Ergo non tunc demum judicabitur diabolus. R. Diabolus jam judicatus est. 1. Decreto Dei. 2. In verbo. 3. Sua conscientia. 4. Inchoatione poenae. Tunc autem sic judicabitur, promulgata publicè sententia, ut nihil amplius in Deum & ecclesiam possit moliri.
units.tr: Objection 2. The prince of this world has already been judged; therefore the devil will not be judged only at that time. Answer. The devil has already been judged: (1) by the decree of God; (2) in the Word; (3) by his own conscience; (4) by the beginning of his punishment. But he will then be judged in such a way that, once the sentence is publicly pronounced, he can no longer plot anything against God and the Church.

units.la: VII. Qualis sit iudicij processus, sententia, & exsecutio futura.
units.tr: VII. What the course, sentence and execution of the judgment will be.

units.la: 1. Virtute divina Christi, & eiusdem voce humana fiet suscitatio mortuorum. Omnes enim, qui in monumentis sunt, audient vocem eius, & prodibunt. Viuentes immutabuntur, & ex mortalibus fient immortales. 2. Ministerio angelorum omnes sistentur tribunali. Per angelos enim tanquam per apparitores, Christus colliget pios & impios à quatuor plagis mundi, & omnes sistet judicio. Per angelos hoc faciet, non necessitate, sed imperio: non quod egeat eorum opera, sed ut se Dominum angelorum & omnium creaturarum declaret: pertinebitque id ad maiestatem & gloriam judicis. 3. Mundus, coelum, terra, igne liquescent, fietque mutatio praesentis status, & repurgatio creaturarum: non omnium abolitio. 4. Fiet piorum & impiorum separatio, & feretur de utrisq; sententia. De impiis principaliter secundum legem (ut quaestione secunda dictum) ita tamen, ut Euangelium eam approbet: de piis principaliter secundum Euangelium, ita tamen, ut lex ea sit contenta. Electi ergo audient sententiam ex Euangelio: Venite benedicti, possidete regnum, &c: Impij vero audient terribilem vocem legis: Ite maledicti in ignem aeternum, &c. dict in ignem aternum. 5. Tandem sequetur glorificatio perfecta piorum, & abiectio impiorum in sempiternos cruciatus. Pios enim Christus in gloriam ad se traducet. Rursum veniam, & assumam vos ad me. Rapiemur in occursum Domini in aera, & ita semper cum Domino erimus. Impij vero cum diabolis in ignem aeternum abijcientur.
units.tr: (1) By the divine power of Christ, and by his human voice, the raising of the dead will take place. For all who are in the tombs will hear his voice and will come forth. Those who are alive will be changed, and from mortal they will become immortal. (2) By the ministry of angels all will be brought before the tribunal. For the angels, as it were as officers, will gather the godly and the wicked from the four quarters of the world, and Christ will present them all to judgment. He will do this through the angels not out of necessity but by his command, not because he needs their work, but so that he may declare himself Lord of the angels and of all creatures; and this belongs to the majesty and glory of the Judge. (3) The world, heaven and earth will melt with fire, and the present state will be changed and the creatures purified, not destroyed entirely. (4) There will be a separation of the godly from the wicked, and sentence will be pronounced on both. The wicked are judged principally according to the law (as was said in the second question), yet in such a way that the Gospel approves that judgment. The godly are judged principally according to the Gospel, yet in such a way that the law is contained in it. The elect therefore will hear the sentence from the Gospel: Come, you blessed, inherit the kingdom, etc. But the wicked will hear the terrible voice of the law: Depart, you cursed, into the eternal fire, etc. (5) Finally, the complete glorification of the godly will follow, and the casting of the wicked into everlasting torments. For Christ will take the godly up to himself in glory: I will come again and take you to myself. We shall be caught up to meet the Lord in the air, and so we shall always be with the Lord. But the wicked will be cast into the eternal fire with the devils.

units.la: Obiect. Qui non credit, jam judicatus est. Ergo impij jam sunt condemnati, & non tunc demum condemnabuntur. Respond. Quemadmodum diaboli jam sunt judicati: ita & impij jam sunt condemnati. 1. Decreto Dei. 2. Verbo, in quo Dei decretum est revelatum. 3. Suis ipsorum conscientiis. 4. Inchoatione. Tunc vero impij judicabuntur cum diabolis, promulgatione & executione judicij. Nam tunc fiet 1. Manifestatio judicij Dei, quod juste pereant, qui pereunt. 2. Impij etiam patientur cruciatus corporis, quod nunc est sepulcrum. 3. Impiis & diabolis poenae exasperabuntur, sicque coercebuntur, ne possint amplius pios laedere, & Deum contumeliis afficere. Hiatus ille ingens inter salvatos & damnatos constitutus transitum illis intercludet, ut nocere desistant.
units.tr: Objection. He who does not believe is already judged; therefore the wicked are already condemned, and will not be condemned only at that time. Answer. Just as the devils have already been judged, so the wicked have already been condemned: (1) by the decree of God; (2) by the Word, in which God's decree has been revealed; (3) by their own consciences; (4) by a beginning of punishment. But the wicked will then be judged together with the devils, by the proclamation and execution of the judgment. For then there will be (1) a manifestation of the judgment of God, that those who perish justly perish; (2) the wicked will also suffer bodily torments, since the body is now in the grave; (3) punishments will be made more severe for the wicked and the devils, and so they will be restrained, so that they can no longer harm the godly or insult God. That vast chasm set between the saved and the damned will cut off their passage to us, so that they cease to do harm.

units.la: VIII. Quare futurum sit hoc iudicium.
units.tr: VIII. Why this judgment will take place.

units.la: Causa principalis est Dei decretum. Ideo enim futurum est, quia Deus decreuit, & praedixit futurum, Necesse igitur est, ut fiat. 2. Ut Deus assequatur finem creati hominis, & ab electis in aeternum celebretur. 3. Ut ostendat perfectam bonitatem & misericordiam suam erga electos, qui in hac vita affliguntur. 4. Propter perfectam justitiam & veritatem Dei, ut hanc etiam ostendat in puniendis impiis, qui hic florent. Oportet enim, ut perfecte tandem bonis bene, malis male sit, secundum corpus & animam. Summa: ut impios Deus abijciat, ecclesiam liberet, ut habitet in nobis, & sit omnia in omnibus.
units.tr: The principal cause is the decree of God. It will take place because God has decreed it and foretold that it will happen; it must therefore come to pass. (2) So that God may attain the end for which man was created, and be praised for ever by the elect. (3) So that he may show his perfect goodness and mercy toward the elect, who are afflicted in this life. (4) On account of the perfect justice and truth of God, so that he may also show this in punishing the wicked, who flourish here. For it is fitting that at last it be well with the good and ill with the evil, in both body and soul, perfectly. In sum: God will cast off the wicked, deliver the Church, dwell in us, and be all in all.

units.la: IX. Quando futurum sit iudicium.
units.tr: IX. When the judgment will take place.

units.la: 1. Futurum est judicium in fine dierum, seu in fine mundi, Nam tres sunt partes durationis mundi. 1. Ante legem. 2. Sub lege. 3. Sub Christo. Pars tertia sub Christo vocatur finis mundi, finis dierum, tempus extremum, ultima hora: duratio nempe a primo Christi adventu usque ad secundum. Ergo non erit tantum spacium inter adventum primum & secundum, quantum fuit ab initio mundi usque ad adventum primum. Nos enim in postremos dies incidimus, quotidie siquidem signa judicij praedicta conspicimus. Pueruli, ultimum tempus adest: & sicut audistis antichristum venturum, ita nunc multi antichristi facti sunt. antichristum venturum, & nunc antichristi multi coeperunt esse: unde scimus, ultimum tempus adesse.
units.tr: (1) The judgment will take place at the end of days, or at the end of the world. For there are three periods in the duration of the world: (1) before the law; (2) under the law; (3) under Christ. The third period, under Christ, is called the end of the world, the end of days, the last time, the last hour: that is, the duration from the first coming of Christ until the second. Therefore the interval between the first and second coming will not be as long as the time from the beginning of the world to the first coming. For we have fallen upon the last days, since daily we see the signs of judgment foretold. Little children, it is the last time; and as you have heard that antichrist is coming, so now many antichrists have appeared. Hence we know that the last time is at hand.

units.la: 2. Annus, mensis, dies, & hora ignoratur, etiam ab angelis, & ignorabatur ab ipso Christo in statu humilitatis. 1. Quoad naturam humanam. 2. Quoad officium mediatoris, quatenus videlicet illud non postulat, ut tempus judicij nobis declaret. De die illo & hora nemo scit, ne angeli quidem, qui in coelo sunt, nec ipse Filius, sed solus Pater.
units.tr: (2) The year, month, day and hour are unknown, even to the angels, and were unknown to Christ himself in the state of humiliation: (1) with respect to his human nature; (2) with respect to the office of mediator, inasmuch as that office did not require him to declare the time of judgment to us. Of that day and hour no one knows, not even the angels in heaven, nor the Son himself, but the Father alone.

units.la: X. Cur Deus velit nos esse certos de judicio.
units.tr: X. Why God wills us to be certain about the judgment.

units.la: Tempus quidem judicij futuri nobis est incognitum: sed ut certissimum est, judicium esse futurum: sic Deus de eo vult nos esse certos. 1. Propter gloriam suam, ut refutare possimus Epicureos, qui hanc de futuro judicio doctrinam habent pro fabula, & ex confusione, quae nunc est in mundo, inferunt, aut mundum non curari a DEO, aut si curetur a DEO, ipsum esse injustum. Justis, inquiunt, debet esse bene: hoc autem non fit. Ergo Deus aut non potest id praestare, aut non stat promissis, aut non est providentia. Resp. Sed opponenda est istorum cavillo certitudo judicij futuri ex DEI veritate & justitia, propter quam necessario tandem piis perfecte bene, impiis perfecte male erit. 2. Propter consolationem nostram, ut sciamus, secuturam aliquando huius miseri status commutationem. 3. Ut contineamus nos in timore DEI, atque officio nostro. Futurum est judicium: demus igitur operam, ut in hoc judicio consistere possimus. Vigilate omni tempore, rogantes, ut digni habeamini, qui effugiatis ista omnia, qua futura sunt, ut consistatis coram Filio hominis. Cum igitur haec omnia soluantur, quales oportet vos esse in sanctis conversationibus & pietatis officiis. 4. Ut impij reddantur ἀναπολόγητοι, inexcusabiles. Monentur enim satis, ut omnibus momentis sint parati: nimirum ne dicant, de improviso se oppressos esse.
units.tr: The time of the future judgment is unknown to us; but just as it is most certain that there will be a judgment, so God wills us to be certain of it. (1) For his own glory, so that we may be able to refute the Epicureans, who regard this doctrine of a future judgment as a fable, and from the present confusion in the world infer either that the world is not cared for by God, or, if it is cared for, that God is unjust. "It ought to go well with the just," they say, "but this does not happen. Therefore God either cannot bring it about, or does not keep his promises, or there is no providence." Answer: their quibble must be met with the certainty of the future judgment, grounded in the truth and justice of God, on account of which at last it will necessarily go perfectly well with the godly and perfectly ill with the wicked. (2) For our consolation, so that we may know that a change of this wretched state will follow at some time. (3) So that we may keep ourselves in the fear of God and in our duty. The judgment will come: let us therefore take pains to be able to stand in that judgment. "Watch at all times, praying that you may be counted worthy to escape all these things that are going to happen, and to stand before the Son of man." Since therefore all these things are to be resolved, what manner of persons you ought to be in holy conduct and the duties of godliness! (4) So that the wicked may be made ἀναπολόγητοι, without excuse. For they are warned sufficiently that they should be ready at every moment, lest they say that they were overtaken unawares.

units.la: XI. Cur velit diem judicij a nobis ignorari.
units.tr: XI. Why he wills that we should not know the day of judgment.

units.la: Licet certissimè sit judicium futurum, dies tamen huius judicij planè est incertus. De die illo ac hora nemo scit, ne angeli quidem, qui in coelo sunt, nec Filius, sed solus Pater. Causae, cur velit Deus nos latere, sunt: 1. Ut exerceat fidem, spem & patientiam nostram, ut credamus DEO, perseveremus in expectatione promissionum, tametsi ignoremus, quando futura sit liberatio. 2. Ut frenet nostram curiositatem. 3. Ut contineat nos in timore sui, in pietate & officij executione: ne simus securi, sed parati expectemus, quia nescimus, qua hora venturus sit Dominus.
units.tr: Although it is most certain that the judgment will come, the day of this judgment is altogether uncertain. "Of that day and hour no one knows, not even the angels who are in heaven, nor the Son, but the Father alone." The reasons why God wills that we be kept in the dark are these: (1) That he may exercise our faith, hope and patience, so that we may believe God and persevere in waiting for the promises, even though we do not know when the deliverance will come. (2) That he may curb our curiosity. (3) That he may keep us in the fear of himself, in godliness and in the performance of our duty, so that we may not be secure, but may wait prepared, because we do not know at what hour the Lord will come.

units.la: 4. Vt etiam impij pœnitentiam non differant, quia horam igno-rant, ne comprehendat eos imparatos dies judicij. Si sciret pater-familias, qua vigilia fur venturus sit, vigilaret. Vigilate, quia nescitis diem, neque horam, qua venturus sit Dominus. Negotiamini, donec veniam.
units.tr: (4) So that also the wicked may not postpone repentance, because they do not know the hour, lest the day of judgment overtake them unprepared. "If the householder knew in what watch the thief would come, he would watch. Watch, because you know neither the day nor the hour in which the Lord will come. Be busy until I come."

units.la: XII. Cur iudicium differat.
units.tr: XII. Why the judgment is delayed.

units.la: Differt Dominus aduentum & judicium suum. 1. Vt exerceat in piis fidem & patientiam, spem & invocationem. 2. Vt omnes electi aggregentur ad ecclesiam. Propter hos enim, non propter impios mundus consistit. Nam creaturæ sunt conditæ propter filios Dei. Impij iis vruntur sicut fures & latrones. Aggregatis vero aggregandis ad ecclesiam, erit finis. Vult autem Deus electos colligi mediis ordinariis in hac vita: vult eos audire verbum, ac per illud renasci & converti, ad quod requiritur tempus. 3. Vt omnibus concedat tempus pœnitentiæ, sicut tempore Nohæ, atq; vt dilatio impios & contumaces reddat inexcusabiles. Multa lenitate tulit vasa ira. An nescis te benignitate Dei adduci ad poenitentiam vocari? Dominus patiens est erga nos, nolens vllos perire, sed omnes ad resipiscentiam tendere.
units.tr: The Lord delays his coming and his judgment. (1) That he may exercise in the godly faith and patience, hope and prayer. (2) That all the elect may be gathered into the Church. For the world stands on account of these, not on account of the wicked; for creatures were made for the sons of God. The wicked use them as thieves and robbers do. But when those who are to be gathered have been gathered into the Church, there will be an end. Now God wills the elect to be gathered in this life by ordinary means: he wills them to hear the Word and through it to be born again and converted, and for this time is required. (3) That he may grant to all a time of repentance, as in the time of Noah, and so that the delay may make the wicked and obstinate inexcusable. "He endured with much patience the vessels of wrath. Or do you not know that the goodness of God leads you to repentance? The Lord is patient toward us, not wishing that any should perish, but that all should come to repentance."

units.la: XIII. An iudicium extremum sit optandum.
units.tr: XIII. Whether the final judgment is to be desired.

units.la: Est omninò: quia desiderium judicij est [?]ἀποκαραδοκίαν, discernens pios ab impiis. In judicio enim futura est justorum & injustorum discretio, quam discretionem pij vehementer expetunt. Perpetuò igitur suspirant cum Paulo: Quis me liberabit à corpore mortis huius? Cupio migrare, & esse cum Christo. quoniam Spiritus & sponsa id desiderium in cordibus eorum efficit, vt clament cum spiritu & sponsa: Veni Domine Iesu, & qui audit, dicat, veni. Impij vero ad mentionem huius judicij exhorrescunt: quia non faciunt in ipsorum rem. Germanicè: Es dienet jhnen nicht in jre Küchen. Hoc certum est signum impietatis. Nisi enim quis dicat, VENI, non est membrum sponsæ, nec habet Spiritum Christi, vocem illam piis suggerentem.
units.tr: Entirely so: because the longing for the judgment is an ἀποκαραδοκία [eager expectation], distinguishing the godly from the wicked. For in the judgment there will be a separation of the just and the unjust, which separation the godly earnestly desire. Therefore they constantly sigh with Paul: "Who will deliver me from this body of death? I desire to depart and be with Christ." Since the Spirit and the bride produce this longing in their hearts, they cry out with the Spirit and the bride: "Come, Lord Jesus, and let him who hears say, Come." But the wicked shudder at the mention of this judgment, because it does not concern their own affair. In German: "Es dienet jhnen nicht in jre Küchen" [it does not serve them in their kitchen]. This is a sure sign of impiety. For unless someone says COME, he is not a member of the bride, nor has he the Spirit of Christ, who suggests that voice to the godly.

units.la: Quid igitur est, Credo in Christum venturum ad judicandum vivos & mortuos? Resp. Credo 1. Quod Christus certò sit venturus, & quod in aduentu eius futura sit renouatio cœli & terræ. 2. Quod idem ille Christus venturus sit, qui pro nobis est passus, mortuus & resurrexit. 3. Quod venturus sit visibiliter & gloriosè ad liberandam ecclesiam, cuius ego sum membrum. 4. Quod venturus sit ad abijciendos impios in æternas pœnas.
units.tr: What, then, is the meaning of "I believe in Christ who will come to judge the living and the dead"? Answer: I believe (1) that Christ will certainly come, and that at his coming there will be a renewal of heaven and earth. (2) That the same Christ who suffered, died and rose again for us will come. (3) That he will come visibly and gloriously to deliver the Church, of which I am a member. (4) That he will come to cast the wicked into eternal punishments.

units.la: Ex his consolationem percipimus magnam simul & solidam, concipimus fiduciam, Nam quia futura est cœli terræque renouatio, concipimus fiduciam, ciam, fore & nostrum statum aliquando alium & meliorem; quia Christus veniet nobis judex propitius. Ipse enim veniet ad judicandum, qui nobis est meritus justitiam, qui noster est frater, redemtor, patronus. Quia veniet gloriosè, etiam feret sententiam justam, & satis potens erit ad nos liberandos. Quia veniet ad liberandam ecclesiam, est quod lætii ipsum expecte-mus. Quia abijciet impios in æternas pœnas, patienter feramus ipsorum tyrannidem. Denique quia liberabit pios, impios ab-ijciet, etiam nos aut liberabit, si pij, aut abijciet, si impij sueri-mus. Necesse est igitur, vt resipiscamus, & in hac vita grati si-mus, securitatem verò carnalem fugiamus, vt inueniamur in eo-rum numero, quos liberabit.
units.tr: From these things we receive a great and at the same time solid consolation; we conceive confidence. For since there will be a renewal of heaven and earth, we conceive confidence that our own state too will someday be other and better; because Christ will come to us as a gracious judge. For he who merited righteousness for us, who is our brother, redeemer and patron, will come to judge. Because he will come in glory, he will also pronounce a just sentence, and he will be powerful enough to set us free. Because he will come to deliver the Church, we have cause to await him joyfully. Because he will cast the wicked into eternal punishments, we may patiently bear their tyranny. Finally, because he will deliver the godly and cast off the wicked, he will either deliver us, if we have been godly, or cast us off, if we have been wicked. It is necessary therefore that we repent and be thankful in this life, and that we shun carnal security, so that we may be found among those whom he will deliver.

units.la: DE DEO SPIRITV SANCTO.
units.tr: CONCERNING GOD THE HOLY SPIRIT.

units.la: QVÆSTIO LIII.
units.tr: QUESTION 53.

units.la: Quid credis de Spiritu sancto?
units.tr: What do you believe concerning the Holy Spirit?

units.la: RESPONSIO.
units.tr: ANSWER.

units.la: Primùm, quod sit verus & coæternus Deus cum æter-no Patre & Filio a. Deinde, quod mihi quoq; datus sit b, vt me per veram fidem Christi & omnium eius benefi-ciorum participem faciat c, me consoletur d, & mecum in æternum maneat e.
units.tr: First, that he is a true God, coeternal with the eternal Father and Son a. Second, that he has also been given to me b, so that he may make me a partaker of true faith in Christ and of all his benefits c, may comfort me d, and may remain with me forever e.

units.la: a Iohan. 5. verf. 7. Genes. 1, 1. Esa. 48, 16. 1 Corinth. 3, 6. & 6, 19. Actor. 5, 34. b Galat. 24, 6. Matth. 28, 19. 20. 2 Cor. 1, 22. Eph. 1, 13. c Galat. 3, 14. 1 Pet. 1, 1. 2. 1 Cor. 6, 7. d Iohan. 15, 26. Actor. 9, 31. e Iohan. 14, 16. 1 Petri 4, 14.
units.tr: a Iohan. 5. verf. 7. Genes. 1, 1. Esa. 48, 16. 1 Corinth. 3, 6. & 6, 19. Actor. 5, 34. b Galat. 24, 6. Matth. 28, 19. 20. 2 Cor. 1, 22. Eph. 1, 13. c Galat. 3, 14. 1 Pet. 1, 1. 2. 1 Cor. 6, 7. d Iohan. 15, 26. Actor. 9, 31. e Iohan. 14, 16. 1 Petri 4, 14.

units.la: EXPLICATIO.
units.tr: EXPLANATION.

units.la: Tertia symboli parte quinque articuli continentur, quo-rum primus est de Spiritus sancti persona: alter de Ecclesia, quæ per Spiritum sanctum colligitur, confirmatur, & conseruatur: tres sequentes sunt de beneficiis Christi per Spiritum sanctum in ecclesiam collatis: remissione peccatorum, resurrectione carnis, & vita æterna.
units.tr: The third part of the creed contains five articles. The first concerns the person of the Holy Spirit; the second concerns the Church, which is gathered, confirmed and preserved by the Holy Spirit; the three that follow concern the benefits of Christ conferred upon the Church through the Holy Spirit: the forgiveness of sins, the resurrection of the flesh, and eternal life.

units.la: De Spiritu Sancto tria præcipuè in consideratione veniunt, persona, officium, & dona seu effecta: quorum vt plenior sit explicatio, hæc ordine considerentur: I. Quid nomen spiritus significet. II. Quis, & quid sit Spiritus sanctus. III. Quod eius officium. IV. Quæ & quotuplicia eius dona. V. A quo, & cur detur. VI. Quibus, & quatenus detur. VII. Quando, & quomodo detur, & accipiatur. VIII. Quomodo retineatur. IX. An, & quomodo amittatur. X. Quare sit necessarius. XI. Vnde agnoscatur eius habitatio in nobis.
units.tr: Three things chiefly come into consideration concerning the Holy Spirit: his person, his office, and his gifts or effects. So that the explanation may be fuller, these are to be considered in this order: (1) what the name spirit signifies; (2) who and what the Holy Spirit is; (3) what his office is; (4) what and how many his gifts are; (5) from whom and why he is given; (6) to whom and how far he is given; (7) when and how he is given and received; (8) how he is retained; (9) whether and how he is lost; (10) why he is necessary; (11) by what sign his indwelling in us is recognised.

units.la: I. Quid nomen Spiritus significet.
units.tr: I. What the name Spirit signifies.

units.la: SPIRITVS à spirando, vt πνεῦμα ἀπὸ πνέω, aliquando pro causa, aliquando pro effectu sumitur. Quando pro causa, significat naturam seu vim agitantem, & cientem aliquid. Quæ est vel increata, quomodo Deus essentialiter & personaliter dicitur Spiritus: Deus est Spiritus: Vel creata: eaque vel incorporea, vt venti, vapores geli boni, mali, animæ humanæ: vel corporea, vt venti, vapores impellentes: Spiritus vbi vult, flat. Quando pro effectu seu motu & cogitatione capitur, significat 1. Aerem impulsum. 2. Ipsam impulsionem & motus aeris. 3. Vapores aliunde impulsos. 4. Affectus & motus bonos vel malos: vt Spiritus timoris, sapientiæ, vertiginis, fornicationis. 5. Dona Spiritus sancti. Spiritum ne extinguite. Hic significat causam mouentem: tertiam personam Diuinitatis, quæ est efficax in mentibus & voluntatibus hominum.
units.tr: SPIRIT, from breathing [spirando], as pneuma from pneō [πνεῦμα ἀπὸ πνέω], is sometimes taken for a cause and sometimes for an effect. When taken for a cause, it signifies a nature or power that moves and stirs something. This is either uncreated, as God is called Spirit both essentially and personally: "God is Spirit"; or created, and this is either incorporeal, such as the winds, good and evil spirits, and human souls, or corporeal, such as winds and driving vapours: "The Spirit blows where he wills." When taken for an effect or motion and thought, it signifies: (1) air set in motion; (2) the very impulse and motion of the air; (3) vapours driven from elsewhere; (4) good or bad affections and motions, as the spirit of fear, of wisdom, of giddiness, of fornication; (5) the gifts of the Holy Spirit: "Do not quench the Spirit." Here it signifies the moving cause, the third person of the Godhead, who is effective in the minds and wills of men.

units.la: Vocatûr hæc tertia persona Spiritus. 1. Quia est spiritualis essentia incorporea, inuisibilis. 2. Quia spiratur à Patre & Filio immediatè efficiunt motus in cordibus electorum, seu, quia est agitator ac motor immediatus diuinorum operum. Pater & Filius mouent, sed per hunc Spiritum. 3. Quia ipse spirat & efficit motus immediatè in cordibus, vnde & virtus altissimi vocatur. 4. Quia est æqualis & idem cum Filio Deus. Deus autem Spiritus est. Sanctus dicitur. 1. Quia in se & sua natura sanctus est. 2. Quia est sanctificator, electos immediatè sanctificans. Pater & Filius per ipsum mediatè sanctificant.
units.tr: This third person is called Spirit: (1) because he is a spiritual, incorporeal, invisible essence; (2) because he is breathed forth [spiratur] from the Father and the Son, and immediately produces motions in the hearts of the elect; or because he is the immediate mover and agent of the divine works. The Father and the Son move, but through this Spirit; (3) because he himself breathes and produces motions immediately in the hearts, whence he is also called the power of the Most High; (4) because he is God, equal and the same with the Son. But God is Spirit. He is called holy: (1) because he is holy in himself and by his own nature; (2) because he is the sanctifier, sanctifying the elect immediately. The Father and the Son sanctify through him mediately.

units.la: II. Quis, & quid sit Spiritus sanctus.
units.tr: II. Who and what the Holy Spirit is.

units.la: Spiritus sanctus est tertia persona Deitatis, à Patre & Filio procedens, Patri Filioq; coæterna, æqualis & consubstantialis, quæ ab vtroque mittitur in corda electorum, vt eos ad vitam æternam sanctificet.
units.tr: The Holy Spirit is the third person of the Godhead, proceeding from the Father and the Son, coeternal with the Father and the Son, equal and consubstantial with them, who is sent by both into the hearts of the elect, so that he may sanctify them to eternal life.

units.la: Quæst.LIII.
units.tr: Question LIII.

units.la: Hæc descriptio vt confirmetur aduersus hæreticos, eadem de deitate Spiritus sancti ex scripturis ostendenda sunt, quæ prius de deitate filii demonstrata fuerunt, esse nimirum 1. ὑφιστάμενον seu personam. 2. ἄλλον à patre & filio. 3. Vtrique ἴσον. 4. ὁμοούσιον. Omnia hæc ostendit testimonium apostoli. Ea quæ sunt Dei, nemo novit, nisi spiritus Dei. Nos vero non spiritum mundi accepimus, sed spiritum, qui ex Deo est, vt sciamus, quæ Deus est nobis gratuitò donata. Item illud: Omnia hæc efficit unus ille & idem spiritus, dispertiens privatim illa singulis, sicut vult. Sed singula ordine sunt ostendenda.
units.tr: So that this description may be confirmed against the heretics, the same things must be shown from Scripture concerning the deity of the Holy Spirit that were previously demonstrated concerning the deity of the Son, namely that he is (1) a subsistent being [ὑφιστάμενον] or person; (2) another [ἄλλον] than the Father and the Son; (3) equal [ἴσον] to both; (4) of the same substance [ὁμοούσιον]. The testimony of the apostle shows all these things: "The things of God no one knows except the Spirit of God. But we have received not the spirit of the world, but the Spirit who is from God, so that we may know the things that God has freely given us." Likewise that: "One and the same Spirit works all these things, dividing them to each one individually as he wills." But the individual points must be shown in order.

units.la: Spiritum sanctum esse ὑφιστάμενον, probatur. 1. Ex apparitionibus eius: quia visibili specie apparuit. Descendit Spiritus sanctus super Christum σωματικῷ εἴδει, tanquam columba. Et visa sunt iis (apostolis) dispertita lingua instar ignis, qui etiam sedit super unumquemque eorum. Nulla autem qualitas, aut motus cordium creatus, assumit & gestat corpoream speciem. Nam accidens non modo nullam assumit speciem, sed & indiget alio, in quo ipsum hæreat. Neque vero sanctitatis, pietatis, amoris Dei, aliorumque motuum spiritualium subiectum est aer, sed mentes hominum. 2. Quia vocatur Deus. An nescitis vos esse templum Dei, & spiritum sanctum habitare in vobis? Cur implevit Satanas cor tuum, ut mentireris in Spiritum sanctum? Non es mentitus hominibus, sed Deo. Vide etiam Iesa.40.7.13. Act.26.25 Ephes.4.4.30.
units.tr: That the Holy Spirit is a subsistent being [ὑφιστάμενον] is proved: (1) from his appearances, since he appeared in visible form: "The Holy Spirit descended upon Christ in bodily form [σωματικῷ εἴδει], like a dove." And there appeared to them (the apostles) "tongues divided, like fire, which also sat upon each one of them." But no created quality or motion of the heart takes on and bears a bodily form. For an accident not only takes on no form, but also needs something else in which it may cling. Nor is the air the subject of holiness, piety, love of God, or other spiritual motions, but the minds of men are. (2) Because he is called God: "Do you not know that you are the temple of God, and that the Spirit of God dwells in you? Why has Satan filled your heart, that you should lie to the Holy Spirit? You have not lied to men, but to God." See also Isa. 40:7, 13; Acts 26:25; Eph. 4:4, 30.

units.la: Quocunque igitur modo hæretici dicant, Spiritum sanctum vocari Deum, fieri non potest, quin sit ὑφιστάμενον, seu persona subsistens: cum Deus sit τὸ ὄν: nostra autem pietas, bonitas, pii motus, & alii affectus spirituales, Deus dici non possint.
units.tr: Therefore, however the heretics may speak, if the Holy Spirit is called God, he cannot fail to be a subsistent being [ὑφιστάμενον], or a subsisting person, since God is "that which is" [τὸ ὄν]; but our piety, goodness, pious motions and other spiritual affections cannot be called God.

units.la: 3. Quia est author baptismi, & in nomen eius perinde atque in nomen patris & filii, hoc est, eius iussu, voluntate & authoritate, baptizamur. Rei autem mortuæ, vel non existentis, vel donorum Dei iussu, voluntate & authoritate neque quaquam baptizamur.
units.tr: 3. Because he is the author of baptism, and we are baptized into his name just as into the name of the Father and the Son, that is, by his command, will and authority. But we are in no way baptized by the command, will or authority of a dead thing, of something that does not exist, or of the gifts of God.

units.la: 4. Quia propria personæ ei tribuuntur. Vt, quod docet, ducat in omnem veritatem, & consoletur: quod distribuat dona prout vult: quod vocet, ac mittat Apostolos: & in iisdem loquatur. Spiritus sanctus vos docebit, quæ oportet dicere. Separate mihi Barnabam & Saulum. Tentabant ire in Bithyniam, sed non siuit eos ire Spiritus: quod annunciet futura: Luc. 2, 26.
units.tr: 4. Because personal properties are attributed to him: that he teaches, leads into all truth and comforts; that he distributes gifts as he wills; that he calls and sends the apostles and speaks through them. "The Holy Spirit will teach you what you ought to say." "Set apart for me Barnabas and Saul." "They tried to go into Bithynia, but the Spirit did not allow them to go." That he foretells the future: Luke 2, 26.

units.la: Quæ ventura sunt, annunciabit vobis. Quod det oracula, de Simeonis morte, de Iuda proditore, de profectione Petri ad Cornelium, de vinculis & afflictionibus manentibus Paulum Hierosolymæ, de apostasia & deceptoribus postremorum temporum, de significatione ingressus pontificis in sacrarium prioris tabernaculi, de fœdere novo, de Christi perpessionib. & gloria illas securitatis... cutura, &c. quod intercedat pro nobis gemitibus ineffabilibus, & clamet Abba Pater: quod tentetur à mentientibus, denique quod testetur in cœlo cum Patre & Filio. Hæc omnia sunt personæ exsistentis, viuentis, volentis & agentis consilio, &c. 5. Quia diserte à donis distinguitur. Discrimina donorum sunt, sed idem Spiritus. Omnia autem hic efficit vnus idemque Spiritus, distribuens illa priuatim singulis, sicut vult. Plurimum igitur dona differunt ab ipso Spiritu.
units.tr: "He will declare to you the things that are to come" (John 16:13). That he gives oracles about the death of Simeon, about Judas the traitor, about Peter's journey to Cornelius, about the chains and afflictions awaiting Paul at Jerusalem, about the apostasy and the deceivers of the last times, about the meaning of the high priest's entry into the inner sanctuary while the former tabernacle stood, about the new covenant, about the sufferings and glory of Christ ... and about that security ... to come, etc. That he intercedes for us with groanings that cannot be uttered, and cries "Abba, Father." That he is lied to by liars. Finally, that he bears witness in heaven together with the Father and the Son. All these things belong to a person who exists, lives, wills and acts by his own counsel, etc. 5. Because he is clearly distinguished from the gifts. "There are diversities of gifts, but the same Spirit. But all these things one and the same Spirit works, dividing to each one individually as he wills." Therefore the gifts differ greatly from the Spirit himself.

units.la: Obiect. Donum Dei non est persona. Spiritus sanctus dicitur donum Dei. Resp. Minor non est vniuersaliter vera. Nam & Filius est datus, & donum Dei: & tamen est persona. Vocatur autem Spiritus sanctus donum, propter missionem: quia mittitur à Patre & Filio. Consolatorem illum ego mittam vobis à Patre: & est tale donum, quod efficit sua virtute reliqua.
units.tr: Objection. A gift of God is not a person. The Holy Spirit is called a gift of God. Answer. The minor premise is not universally true. For the Son too is given, and is a gift of God, and yet he is a person. The Holy Spirit, however, is called a gift on account of his mission, because he is sent by the Father and the Son. "I will send that Comforter to you from the Father." And he is such a gift that by his own power he effects the rest.

units.la: "Ἀπὸ esse Spiritum sanctum, hoc est, distinctum à Patre & Filio, probatur aduersus illos, qui dicunt, eum esse Patris φῦσις ἀμφω, hoc est, Sabellianos: 1. Quia est Patris & Filij Spiritus. Nemo autem est suiipsius spiritus, sicut nemo est suiipsius pater, nemo suiipsius filius. Ergo ab vtroque est alius. 2. Expresse in scriptura Spiritus sanctus vocatur alius à Patre & Filio. Rogabo Patrem, & alium Paracletum mittet vobis. Quem ego vobis mittam à Patre. Sermo & Spiritus sanctus. Tres sunt in cœlo, qui testantur: Pater, Sermo & Spiritus sanctus. Est ergo ab vtroque distinctus. 3. Dicitur mitti à Patre & Filio. Est ergo ab vtroque distinctus. Nemo enim mittitur à seipso: sed à seipso. Potest quis accedere sua voluutate & à seipso: non potest. Ego mittam eum vobis à Patre. Pater mittet eum in nomine meo. 4. Ab attributis distinctis. Solus Spiritus sanctus procedit à Patre & Filio: solus apparuit in specie columbæ & ignis, non Pater aut Filius. Christus etiam non per Patrem aut Filium, sed per Spiritum sanctum conceptus esse dicitur, hoc est, immediata virtute atque efficacia Spiritus sancti: Spiritus sanctus superueniet in te, & virtus altissimi inumbrabit te. Est igitur alius à Patre & Filio. Hæretici his scripturæ argumentis conuicti, concedunt, Spiritum sanctum esse φῦσις ἀμφω sed Patris, & obijciunt seqq.
units.tr: That the Holy Spirit is distinct from the Father and the Son, that is, a separate person, is proved against those who say that he is of the nature of both [φύσει ἀμφω], that is, against the Sabellians. (1) Because he is the Spirit of the Father and of the Son. No one is the spirit of himself, just as no one is his own father or his own son. Therefore he is other than both. (2) Scripture expressly calls the Holy Spirit another than the Father and the Son: "I will pray the Father, and he shall give you another Comforter" (John 14:16); "whom I will send unto you from the Father" (John 15:26); "the Word and the Holy Spirit"; "there are three that bear record in heaven: the Father, the Word, and the Holy Spirit" (1 John 5:7). He is therefore distinct from both. (3) He is said to be sent by the Father and the Son. Therefore he is distinct from both. For no one is sent by himself but by another. One may come of his own will, but cannot be sent by himself: "I will send him unto you from the Father" (John 15:26); "the Father will send him in my name" (John 14:26). (4) He is distinguished by distinct attributes. Only the Holy Spirit proceeds from the Father and the Son; only the Holy Spirit appeared in the form of a dove and of fire, not the Father or the Son. Christ too is said to have been conceived not through the Father or the Son but through the Holy Spirit, that is, by the immediate power and efficacy of the Holy Spirit: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee" (Luke 1:35). He is therefore other than the Father and the Son. The heretics, convicted by these scriptural arguments, concede that the Holy Spirit is of the nature of both [φύσει ἀμφω], but say that he is of the Father's nature, and they raise the following objections.

units.la: Obiect. 1. Virtus Patris est ipse Pater. Spiritus sanctus vocatur virtus Patris. Ergo Spiritus sanctus est ipse Pater. Resp. 1. Sunt quatuor termini: quia in maiore virtus sumitur pro natura seu potentia Patris, in minore pro persona, per quam Pater exserit suam potentiam.
units.tr: Objection 1: The power of the Father is the Father himself. The Holy Spirit is called the power of the Father. Therefore the Holy Spirit is the Father himself. Answer 1: There are four terms here, because in the major premise "power" is taken for the nature or essence of the Father, but in the minor for the person through whom the Father exerts his power.

units.la: Obiect. 2. Quod est omnibus personis commune, non debet restringi ad vnam. Vocabulum spiritus est tribus personis commune. Ergo non debet restringi ad tertiam. Resp. Concedo totum. tum, si intelligatur spiritus de essentia: non autem, si de ordine exsistendi & operandi. Nam spiritus & spirans differunt: alius est procedens, alius à quo procedit: alia persona Deitatis tertia, alia prima vel secunda. At Spiritus sanctus vocatur tertia persona: idque non quod in Deo sit prius aut posterius tempore, sed propter ordinem siue modum exsistendi: quia videlicet Spiritus sanctus à Patre & Filio habet suam essentiam, quia ab utroque procedit: & utriusque est Spiritus. Pari ratione Filius secunda persona vocatur, quia est à Patre: Pater prima, quia est à nullo.
units.tr: Objection 2: What is common to all the persons should not be restricted to one. The word "spirit" is common to the three persons. Therefore it should not be restricted to the third. Answer: I grant the whole argument, if "spirit" is understood of the essence; but not if it is understood of the order of existing and acting. For spirit and the one who breathes differ: one is the one proceeding, the other the one from whom he proceeds; the third person of the Godhead is one thing, the first or second another. The Holy Spirit is called the third person, not because anything in God is earlier or later in time, but on account of the order or mode of existing: namely, because the Holy Spirit has his essence from the Father and the Son, since he proceeds from both, and is the Spirit of both. By the same reasoning the Son is called the second person, because he is from the Father, and the Father is the first, because he is from no one.

units.la: Ἰσον, hoc est, æqualem esse Spiritum sanctum Patri & Filio, probant hæc firmissima argumenta. Ipsi communicata est essentia Patris & Filij: quia ab utroque procedit, & utriusque est Spiritus. In Deo autem nihil est, quod non sit eius essentia. Ea igitur indiuisibilis cum sit, tota & eadem ipsi communicata sit necesse est. Sicut enim spiritus hominis, qui est in homine, est de essentia hominis, sic Spiritus Dei, qui est in Deo, est de essentia Dei. Hinc apparet, quid sit processio Spiritus sancti, nempe communicatio diuinæ essentiæ, qua sola tertia persona diuinitatis à Patre & Filio, tanquam Spiritus, ab eo, cuius est Spiritus, essentiam accepit eandem & integram, quam Pater & Filius habent & retinent: sicut generatio Filij est communicatio essentiæ diuinæ, qua sola secunda persona diuinitatis à sola prima, tanquam filius à Patre, essentiam accipit eandem & integram, quam habet & retinet.
units.tr: That the Holy Spirit is equal [ἴσον], that is, equal to the Father and the Son, is proved by these very strong arguments. The essence of the Father and the Son is communicated to him, because he proceeds from both and is the Spirit of both. Now in God there is nothing that is not his essence. Since that essence is indivisible, it must be necessarily communicated to him whole and the same. For just as the spirit of a man that is in him belongs to the essence of the man, so the Spirit of God that is in God belongs to the essence of God. From this it is clear what the procession of the Holy Spirit is: namely, the communication of the divine essence, by which the third person of the Godhead alone, from the Father and the Son, as Spirit, from him whose Spirit he is, receives the same and entire essence which the Father and the Son have and retain. Just as the generation of the Son is the communication of the divine essence, by which the second person of the Godhead alone, from the first alone, as Son from the Father, receives the same and entire essence which he has and retains.

units.la: Quod vero Spiritus sanctus etiam à Filio procedat, scripturæ rationibus ostenditur. Primò, quia dicitur etiam Filij Spiritus. Si quis Spiritum Christi non habet, is non est eius. Emisit Deus Spiritum Filij sui in corda vestra, clamantem Abba Pater. Spiritus filij dicitur non donatus Filio à Patre, sed sicut de Patris, sic de Filij quoque substantia exsistens & procedens, cùm Filius sit æqualis & consubstantialis Patri. Secundò, quia Filius eum dat vnà cum Patre. Ego mittam eum vobis à Patre. Accipite Spiritum sanctum. Tertiò, quia Spiritus sanctus accipit sapientiam à Filio, quam nobis revelat. De meo accipiet, & annunciabit vobis. Cùm autem sit verus Deus, consubstantialis Patri & Filio, vt mox ostendetur, non potest quicquam accipere, nisi ab eo, de cuius est substantia. Proinde ergo etiam de substantia Filij.
units.tr: That the Holy Spirit also proceeds from the Son is shown by scriptural reasons. First, because he is also called the Spirit of the Son: "If anyone has not the Spirit of Christ, he is none of his" (Rom. 8:9); "God hath sent forth the Spirit of his Son into your hearts, crying, Abba, Father" (Gal. 4:6). He is called the Spirit of the Son not because he was given to the Son by the Father, but because he exists and proceeds from the substance of the Son as well as of the Father, since the Son is equal to and consubstantial with the Father. Second, because the Son gives him together with the Father: "I will send him unto you from the Father" (John 15:26); "Receive ye the Holy Ghost" (John 20:22). Third, because the Holy Spirit receives wisdom from the Son, which he reveals to us: "He shall receive of mine, and shall shew it unto you" (John 16:14). Since he is true God, consubstantial with the Father and the Son, as will soon be shown, he cannot receive anything except from him whose substance he is. Therefore he also proceeds from the substance of the Son.

units.la: 2. Omnes proprietates seu attributa essentiæ diuinæ tribuuntur Spiritui sancto: vt, æternitas: quia fuit in creatione rerum, & quia Deus nunquam fuit absque suo Spiritu. Spiritus Domini ferebatur super aquas. Immensitas: quia habitat totus in omnibus electis. Spiritus Dei habitat in vobis. Per Spiritum sanctum. tum, qui habitat in vobis. Omnipotentia: quia cum Patre & Filio omnia creauit & consecrat. Verbo Iehouæ creati sunt cœli, & Spiritus, distribuens prinatim singulis sicut vult. Omniscientia. Spiritus omnia scrutatur, etiam profunditates Dei. Bonitas & sanctitas immensa, & causa bonitatis & sanctificationis in creaturis. Spiritus tuus bonus deducat me in viam rectam. Sanctificati estis per nomen Domini Iesu, & per Spiritum Dei nostri. Immutabilitas. Oportuit impleri scripturam, quam prædixit Spiritus sanctus. Veritas, de qua non liceat dubitare, & fons veritatis. Cum venerit ille Spiritus veritatis. Spiritus est veritas. Misericordia ineffabilis. Dilectio Dei diffusa est in corda nostra per Spiritum sanctum, qui datus est nobis. Similiter & Spiritus auxiliatur infirmitatibus nostris, &c. Ira aduersus peccata, etiam arcana, in æternas pœnas abijciens. Nolite contristare Spiritum sanctum, quo obsignati estis. Quare convenit inter vos, ut tentaretis Spiritum Domini? Qui dixerit blasphemiam in Spiritum sanctum, ei non remittetur.
units.tr: Second, all the properties or attributes of the divine essence are ascribed to the Holy Spirit: for example, eternity, since he was present at the creation of things, and because God never was without his Spirit: "The Spirit of God moved upon the face of the waters" (Gen. 1:2). Immensity, since he dwells wholly in all the elect: "The Spirit of God dwelleth in you" (1 Cor. 3:16); "through his Spirit that dwelleth in you" (2 Tim. 1:14). Omnipotence, since with the Father and the Son he created and sanctifies all things: "By the word of the Lord were the heavens made, and all the host of them by the breath of his mouth" (Ps. 33:6); "dividing to every man severally as he will" (1 Cor. 12:11). Omniscience: "The Spirit searcheth all things, yea, the deep things of God" (1 Cor. 2:10). Goodness and holiness immense, and the cause of goodness and sanctification in creatures: "Thy good Spirit shall lead me into the land of uprightness" (Ps. 143:10); "Ye are sanctified in the name of the Lord Jesus, and by the Spirit of our God" (1 Cor. 6:11). Immutability: "This Scripture must needs have been fulfilled, which the Holy Ghost by the mouth of David spake before" (Acts 1:16). Truth, which may not be doubted, and the fountain of truth: "When the Spirit of truth is come" (John 16:13); "The Spirit is truth" (1 John 5:6). Immeasurable mercy: "The love of God is shed abroad in our hearts by the Holy Ghost which is given unto us" (Rom. 5:5); "Likewise the Spirit also helpeth our infirmities" (Rom. 8:26). Wrath against sins, even hidden ones, casting them into eternal punishments: "Grieve not the Holy Spirit of God, whereby ye are sealed" (Eph. 4:30); "How is it that ye have agreed together to tempt the Spirit of the Lord?" (Acts 5:9); "Whosoever speaketh against the Holy Ghost, it shall not be forgiven him" (Matt. 12:32).

units.la: 3. Eadem opera diuina tribuuntur Spiritui sancto, quæ Patri & filio: tum vniuersalia, vt sunt creatio, conseruatio & gubernatio vniuersalis: Spiritus eius ornauit cœlos. Spiritus Dei fecit me, &c. Ego in Spiritu Dei eijcio dæmonia. Dius, tum singularia, vt miracula. Ego in Spiritu Dei eijcio dæmonia. Dei visiones operationum sunt: sed idem Spiritus. Item ea, quæ proprie ad salutem Ecclesiæ pertinent, vt vocatio & missio prophetarum & apostolorum. Dominus Iehoua misit me, & Spiritus eius. Separate mihi Barnabam & Paulum. Attendite gregi, in quo Spiritus sanctus vos constituit apostolos. Collatio donorum in ministros ad ministerium necessariorum. Spiritus sanctus docebit vos omnia. Promulgatio vnicuique datur manifestatio Spiritus ad vtilitatem. Doctrinæ propheticæ & apostolicæ. Spiritu Dei afflati, locuti sunt sancti Dei homines. Institutio sacramentorum. Baptizate eos in nomine Patris & Filij & Spiritus sancti. Hoc declarante Spiritu sancto (per vnum quotannis ingressum pontificis in sacrarium) nondum patefactam fuisse viam, &c. Prædictio & revelatio futurorum. Qua futura sunt, renunciabit vobis. Agabus per Spiritum sanctum significabat famem, &c. Spiritus diserte dicit, quod in posterioribus temporibus quidam defecisent à fide, &c. Collectio Ecclesiæ. In quo & vos ædificemini in habitaculum Dei per Spiritum. Per vnum Spiritum nos omnes in vnum corpus baptizati sumus. Illuminatio mentium. Spiritus sanctus docebit vos omnia. Ducet vos in omnem veritatem. Deus det vobis Spiritum sapientiæ & revelationis in agnitionem sui. Regeneratio & sanctificatio. Nisi quis renatus fuerit ex aqua & Spiritu. In eandem imaginem transformamur à gloria in gloriam, tanquam à Domini Spiritu. Gubernatio actionum & vitæ piorum. Quicunque agitur Spiritu Dei, sunt filij Dei. Spiritus sanctus prohibuit Paulum loqui sermonem in Asia. Consolatio in tentationibus. Paracletus autem ille Spiritus sanctus, quem mittet Pater in nomine meo. Ecclesiæ ædificabantur, & consolatione Spiritus sancti multiplicabantur. Effundam super domum Dauid Spiritum gratiæ & precum. Confirmatio & conseruatio renatorum aduersus vim tentationum in finem vsque. Requiescet super eum Spiritus fortitudinis. Alium Paracletum dabit vobis, vt maneat vobiscum in æternum. In quo etiam obsignati estis Spiritu illo promissionis sancto. Condonatio peccatorum, & adoptio in filios Dei. Accepistis Spiritum adoptionis. Vbi Spiritus Domini, ibi libertas. Iustificati estis per nomen Domini Iesu, & per Spiritum Dei nostri. Donatio vitæ & salutis æternæ. Spiritus est, qui vivificat. Si spiritus eius, qui Iesum excitauit à mortuis, habitat in vobis, viuificabit etiam mortalia corpora vestra, per inhabitantem in vobis spiritum eius. Iudicium aduersus peccata. Cum venerit Paracletus, arguet mundum de peccato. Qui dixerit blasphemiam in Spiritum sanctum, non remittetur ei.
units.tr: Third, the same divine works that are ascribed to the Father and the Son are ascribed to the Holy Spirit: both those that are universal, such as creation, preservation, and universal government: "By his Spirit he hath garnished the heavens" (Job 26:13); "The Spirit of God hath made me" (Job 33:4); and particular ones, such as miracles: "I cast out devils by the Spirit of God" (Matt. 12:28). The visions of the works of God are indeed works, but the same Spirit. Likewise those that properly pertain to the salvation of the Church, such as the calling and sending of prophets and apostles: "The Lord God hath sent me, and his Spirit" (Isa. 48:16); "Separate me Barnabas and Saul" (Acts 13:2); "Take heed unto yourselves, and to all the flock, over which the Holy Ghost hath made you overseers" (Acts 20:28). The bestowing of gifts on ministers, needed for the ministry: "The Holy Ghost shall teach you all things" (John 14:26); "But the manifestation of the Spirit is given to every man to profit withal" (1 Cor. 12:7). The teaching of prophetic and apostolic doctrine: "Holy men of God spake as they were moved by the Holy Ghost" (2 Pet. 1:21). The institution of the sacraments: "Baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost" (Matt. 28:19); the Holy Spirit signifying by this (that the way into the holy place was not yet opened while the first tabernacle was standing, shown by the high priest's entrance into the sanctuary once a year) (Heb. 9:8). The foretelling and revelation of future things: "He will shew you things to come" (John 16:13); "Agabus, by the Spirit, signified that there should be a great dearth" (Acts 11:28; 21:11); "The Spirit speaketh expressly, that in the latter times some shall depart from the faith" (1 Tim. 4:1). The gathering of the Church: "In whom ye also are builded together for an habitation of God through the Spirit" (Eph. 2:22); "For by one Spirit are we all baptized into one body" (1 Cor. 12:13). The illumination of minds: "The Holy Ghost shall teach you all things" (John 14:26); "He shall guide you into all truth" (John 16:13); "God give unto you the spirit of wisdom and revelation in the knowledge of him" (Eph. 1:17). Regeneration and sanctification: "Except a man be born of water and of the Spirit" (John 3:5); "We are transformed into the same image from glory to glory, even as by the Spirit of the Lord" (2 Cor. 3:18). The governance of the actions and life of the godly: "As many as are led by the Spirit of God, they are the sons of God" (Rom. 8:14); "They were forbidden of the Holy Ghost to preach the word in Asia" (Acts 16:6). Comfort in temptations: "But the Comforter, which is the Holy Ghost, whom the Father will send in my name" (John 14:26); "The churches were edified, and walking in the fear of the Lord, and in the comfort of the Holy Ghost, were multiplied" (Acts 9:31). "I will pour upon the house of David the spirit of grace and of supplication" (Zech. 12:10). The confirmation and preservation of the regenerate against the force of temptations to the end: "The Spirit of the Lord shall rest upon him" (Isa. 11:2); "He shall give you another Comforter, that he may abide with you for ever" (John 14:16); "In whom ye also were sealed with that Holy Spirit of promise" (Eph. 1:13). The forgiveness of sins and adoption as sons of God: "Ye have received the Spirit of adoption" (Rom. 8:15); "Where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is liberty" (2 Cor. 3:17); "But ye are justified in the name of the Lord Jesus, and by the Spirit of our God" (1 Cor. 6:11). The giving of life and eternal salvation: "It is the Spirit that quickeneth" (John 6:63); "If the Spirit of him that raised up Jesus from the dead dwell in you, he that raised up Christ from the dead shall also quicken your mortal bodies by his Spirit that dwelleth in you" (Rom. 8:11). Judgment against sins: "When he is come, he will reprove the world of sin" (John 16:8); "Whosoever speaketh against the Holy Ghost shall not be forgiven him" (Matt. 12:32).

units.la: 4. Æqualis & idem honor diuinus offertur Spiritui sancto, qui Patri & Filio. Nulli autem creaturæ, sed soli Deo tribuendus est honor & cultus diuinus. Æqualitas ergo honoris eiusdem est Deitatis æqualis argumentum. Tres sunt, qui testimonium dant in cœlo, Pater, Sermo & Spiritus sanctus, & hi tres vnum sunt. Spiritus sanctus igitur idem est cum Patre & Filio verus Deus. Profecti docete omnes gentes, & baptizate eos in nomine Patris, Filij & Spiritus sancti. Hoc testimonio docemur nos etiam in Spiritus sancti nomen, fidem, cultum & religionem baptizari & obligari.
units.tr: 4. The same divine honour is offered to the Holy Spirit as to the Father and the Son. Divine honour and worship, however, are to be given to no creature but to God alone. The equality of honour is therefore a sign of the equality of the same Deity. "There are three who bear witness in heaven, the Father, the Word and the Holy Spirit, and these three are one" (1 John 5:7). The Holy Spirit is therefore the same true God as the Father and the Son. "Go and teach all nations, and baptize them in the name of the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit" (Matt. 28:19). By this testimony we are taught that we are also baptized into the name, faith, worship and religion of the Holy Spirit, and bound to them.

units.la: 2. Etiam Spiritum sanctum esse autorem baptismi & ministerij. Sic & in Spiritum sanctum credimus, & spem atque fiduciam collocamus. Ne turbetur cor vestrum. Ego rogabo Patrem, & alium Paracletum mittet vobis, qui maneat vobiscum in æternum. Peccatum in Spiritum sanctum non remittitur. Ergo in eum peccantes. Nos sumus ipsius templum. Templum Dei estis, & Spiritus Dei habitat in vobis. Apostoli precantur ecclesiis gratiam & pacem à Spiritu sancto in epistolis. Communicatio Spiritus sancti sit cum omnibus vobis.
units.tr: 2. The Holy Spirit is also the author of baptism and of the ministry. So we believe in the Holy Spirit and place our hope and trust in him. "Let not your heart be troubled" (John 14:1). "I will ask the Father, and he will send you another Comforter, who will abide with you for ever" (John 14:16). "The sin against the Holy Spirit is not forgiven" (Matt. 12:31). Therefore those who sin against him... "We are his temple." "You are the temple of God, and the Spirit of God dwells in you" (1 Cor. 3:16). The apostles, in their epistles, pray that grace and peace be given to the churches by the Holy Spirit. "The communion of the Holy Spirit be with you all" (2 Cor. 13:13).

units.la: Obiect. 1. Qui accipit ab alio, non est æqualis ei, qui dat. Spiritus sanctus accipit à Patre & Filio. Ergo non est vtrique æqualis. R. 1. ad maiorem: qui accipit ab alio, pattem, non totum. 2. Qui accipit, in tempore, seu successiue, per donationem, vel gratiam, non autem per naturam. 3. Qui accipit ab alio, accipit omnia, ipsam etiam diuinam essentiam, a Patre & Filio, non dono vel gratia, sed per æternam & ineffabilem processionem.
units.tr: Objection 1. He who receives from another is not equal to him who gives. The Holy Spirit receives from the Father and the Son. Therefore he is not equal to both. Answer: First, to the major premise: he who receives from another is not equal to him as a part is not equal to the whole. Second, he who receives, receives in time, or successively, by donation or grace, and not by nature. Third, he who receives from another receives everything, even the divine essence itself, from the Father and the Son, not by gift or grace, but by an eternal and ineffable procession.

units.la: Obiectio 2. Pater per Filium omnia fecit. Ergo etiam Spiritum sanctum. Resp. Omnia, scilicet, quæ facta sunt, fecit per Filium: quia dicitur: Et absque eo factum est nihil, quod factum est. At Spiritus sanctus non est factus, sed procedit à Patre & Filio ab æterno.
units.tr: Objection 2. The Father made all things through the Son. Therefore he also made the Holy Spirit. Answer: He made through the Son all the things that have been made, because it is said: "And without him was not anything made that was made" (John 1:3). But the Holy Spirit has not been made; he proceeds from the Father and the Son from eternity.

units.la: Obiect. 3. Missus non est æqualis mittenti. Spiritus sanctus mittitur à Patre & Filio. Ergo non est utrique æqualis. Respond. Maior universaliter negatur: quia missus potest esse æqualis mittenti: ut si rex regem, princeps principem mittat. Sic nihil impedit, Christum à Patre missum & tamen eidem æqualem esse: & Spiritum sanctum missum ab utroque, & utrique simul æqualem esse. Unde à Cyrillo recte dictum: Missio & obedientia non tollit æqualitatem.
units.tr: Objection 3. One who is sent is not equal to the one who sends. The Holy Spirit is sent by the Father and the Son. Therefore he is not equal to both. Answer: The major premise is denied universally, because one who is sent can be equal to the one who sends, as when a king sends a king, or a prince sends a prince. Thus nothing prevents Christ, who was sent by the Father, from being equal to him; and the Holy Spirit, who is sent by both, from being equal to both at once. Hence Cyril rightly said: "Mission and obedience do not take away equality."

units.la: 'Ὁμοούσιον esse Spiritum sanctum Patri & Filio, hoc est, unum cum utroque Deum, probatur. 1. Quia est Patris & Filij Spiritus: procedit ab utroque: est Spiritus Dei: in Deo, & ex Deo. Ergo habet sibi communicatam essentiam divinam eandem, & totam, quæ est Patris & Filij: quia essentia Dei non potest multiplicari, nec dividi, nec alia creari. 2. Jehoua non est nisi unus. Spiritus sanctus est Jehoua. Nam quæ de Jehoua dicuntur, ad Spiritum sanctum accommodat scriptura. Leuit. 16. verf. 2. 34. Jehoua. Hebr. 9. v. 7. 8. Spiritus sanctus jussit pontificem semel in anno in sanctuario expiare populum. Leuit 26, 11. 12. Jehoua, 2 Corinth. 6, 19. Deus. 1 Cor. 6, 19. Spiritus sanctus habitat in nobis ut in templo. Psalm. 95. verf. 9. Jehoua. Hebr. 3, 7. Spiritus sanctus queritur se tentatum à patribus in deserto. Esaiæ 6. verf. 10. Jehoua. Actor. 28, 25. Spiritus sanctus dixit Prophetæ: Vade ad populum istum. Actor. 4, 24. Jehoua creator cœli & terræ. Ibidem verf. 25. & Actor. 1, 16. Spiritus sanctus locutus est per os Davidis. Est igitur Spiritus sanctus Jehoua, unus cum Patre & Filio Deus. Ideo & Deus absolutè vocatur à Petro Actor. 5, 4. Non hominibus, sed Deo mentitus es. Et verf. 3. 9. Ut mentireris Spiritui sancto: ut tentaretis Spiritum sanctum. Est igitur Spiritus sanctus Patri & Filio 'ὁμοούσιος.
units.tr: That the Holy Spirit is homoousios [ὁμοούσιον] with the Father and the Son, that is, one God with each, is proved as follows. First, because he is the Spirit of the Father and the Son; he proceeds from both; he is the Spirit of God, in God and from God. Therefore he has communicated to him the same divine essence, and the whole of it, which belongs to the Father and the Son, because the essence of God cannot be multiplied, divided, or created anew. Second, Jehovah is only one. The Holy Spirit is Jehovah. For Scripture applies to the Holy Spirit what is said of Jehovah. Lev. 16:2, 34: Jehovah. Heb. 9:7, 8: the Holy Spirit commanded the high priest to make atonement for the people once a year in the sanctuary. Lev. 26:11, 12: Jehovah. 2 Cor. 6:19: God. 1 Cor. 6:19: "The Holy Spirit dwells in us as in a temple." Ps. 95:9: Jehovah. Heb. 3:7: "The Holy Spirit says that he was tempted by the fathers in the wilderness." Isa. 6:10: Jehovah. Acts 28:25: "The Holy Spirit spoke to the prophet: Go to this people." Acts 4:24: Jehovah, creator of heaven and earth. The same, verse 25, and Acts 1:16: "The Holy Spirit spoke by the mouth of David." The Holy Spirit is therefore Jehovah, one God with the Father and the Son. Accordingly Peter also calls him God absolutely, Acts 5:4: "You have not lied to men, but to God." And verses 3 and 9: "That you should lie to the Holy Spirit," "that you should tempt the Holy Spirit." The Holy Spirit is therefore homoousios [ὁμοούσιος] with the Father and the Son.

units.la: Obiectio. Qui est ab alio, non est ei 'ὁμοούσιος, seu, non est idem cum eo, à quo est. Spiritus sanctus est à Patre & Filio. Ergo, &c. Resp. Totum datur, quoad personam, quæ non est idem, sed differt à Patre & Filio. Quoad essentiam infinitam Dei, quæ eadem & tota est tribus personis communis, Maior est falsa.
units.tr: Objection. He who is from another is not homoousios with him, or is not the same as him from whom he is. The Holy Spirit is from the Father and the Son. Therefore, etc. Answer: The whole is given with respect to the person, which is not the same as, but differs from, the Father and the Son. With respect to the infinite essence of God, which is the same and whole and common to the three persons, the major premise is false.

units.la: III. Quod sit officium Spiritus sancti.
units.tr: III. What the office of the Holy Spirit is.

units.la: Officium Spiritus sancti est sanctificatio: quæ fit immediatè per ipsum à Patre & Filio. Ideò Spiritus sanctificationis vocatur. Eius præcipuæ partes sunt, docere & regenerare, vnire cum Christo & Deo, regere, consolari, & confirmare: quæ hoc disticho comprehenduntur.
units.tr: The office of the Holy Spirit is sanctification, which is effected immediately by the Spirit himself from the Father and the Son. For this reason he is called the Spirit of sanctification. His chief parts are to teach and to regenerate, to unite us with Christ and God, to rule, to comfort, and to confirm; these are comprehended in the following couplet.

units.la: Spiritus ecce docet, renouat, copulatq;, regitque, Et consolatur arrha salutiferâ.
units.tr: Behold, the Spirit teaches, renews, joins us and rules, and comforts us with the saving pledge.

units.la: 1. Igitur Spiritus sanctus nos docet & illuminat: vt sciamus, & recte intelligamus ea, quæ ad salutem intelligere debemus: juxta promissionem Christi: Dorebit vos omnia. Ducet vos in omnem veritatem. Sic docuit apostolos in pentecoste rudes antea doctrinæ de morte & regno Christi: accendit in mentibus eorum nouam lucem: infudit iisdem cognitionem miraculosam linguarum, & impleuit oraculum Ioelis. Ideo vocatur in scriptura Spiritus sapientiæ & reuelationis, Spiritus intelligentiæ, consilij, scientiæ, &c.
units.tr: 1. The Holy Spirit therefore teaches and enlightens us, so that we may know and rightly understand those things which we must understand for salvation, according to the promise of Christ: He shall teach you all things. He shall lead you into all truth. So he taught the apostles at Pentecost, who were previously untrained in the doctrine of the death and kingdom of Christ: he kindled a new light in their minds, poured into them the miraculous knowledge of tongues, and fulfilled the oracle of Joel. Therefore in Scripture he is called the Spirit of wisdom and revelation, the Spirit of understanding, counsel, knowledge, and so on.

units.la: 2. Regenerat nos, cum indit nouas qualitates cordibus, hoc est, efficit fidem & conuersionem. Nisi quis renatus fuerit ex aquâ & Spiritu, non potest ingredi in regnum Dei. Ego baptizo vos aquâ in resipiscentiam, is vero, qui post me venit, baptizabit vos Spiritu sancto & igni. Hic baptismus, qui fit à Christo per Spiritum sanctum, est ipsa renouatio, eaque per externum Iohannis & aliorum ministrorum baptismum significata & obsignata.
units.tr: 2. He regenerates us when he implants new qualities in our hearts, that is, when he effects faith and conversion. Unless someone is born again of water and the Spirit, he cannot enter the kingdom of God. I baptize you with water unto repentance, but he who comes after me will baptize you with the Holy Spirit and with fire. This baptism, which is performed by Christ through the Holy Spirit, is the renewal itself, and it is signified and sealed by the external baptism of John and of the other ministers.

units.la: 3. Coniungit nos cum Christo: vt simus eius membra, ab eo viuificemur, omniumq; beneficiorum eius participes fiamus. Effundam de spiritu meo super omnem carnem. Sed abluti estis, sed sanctificati estis in nomine Domini Iesu, & per spiritum Dei nostri. Per vnum Spiritum nos omnes in vnum corpus baptizati sumus. Per hoc nouimus eum habitare in nobis, nempe ex spiritu, quem dedit nobis. Nemo potest dicere Iesum Dominum, nisi per Spiritum sanctum. Discrimina dorum sunt, sed idem spiritus.
units.tr: 3. He joins us with Christ, so that we may be his members, be quickened by him, and become partakers of all his benefits. I will pour out my Spirit upon all flesh. But you were washed, you were sanctified, in the name of the Lord Jesus and by the Spirit of our God. By one Spirit we were all baptized into one body. By this we know that he dwells in us, namely by the Spirit whom he has given us. No one can say that Jesus is Lord except by the Holy Spirit. There are diversities of gifts, but the same Spirit.

units.la: 4. Regit nos. Regi à Spiritu sancto est ab eo instrui consilio in actionibus vitæ & vocationis, & flecti ad sequendum recta, & ad faciendum officia dilectionis erga Deum & proximum. Sub hoc continentur omnes virtutes Christianæ primæ & secundæ tabulæ. Qui Spiritu DEI ducuntur, hi sunt filij DEI. Apostoli coeperunt loqui aliis linguis, prout Spiritus ille dabat eis eloqui.
units.tr: 4. He rules us. To be ruled by the Holy Spirit means to be instructed by him in counsel in the actions of life and of our calling, and to be turned to follow what is right and to perform the duties of love towards God and neighbour. Under this are contained all the Christian virtues of the first and second tables. Those who are led by the Spirit of God, these are the sons of God. The apostles began to speak in other tongues, as that Spirit gave them utterance.

units.la: 5. Consolatur nos in periculis & afflictionibus. Apostoli fugientes ac laetantes metu Judæorum, accepto Spiritu sancto proprodeunt in publicum: lætantur cum est patiendum propter confessionem Euangelij. Alium consolatorem dabit vobis, qui manebit vobiscum in æternum.
units.tr: 5. He comforts us in dangers and afflictions. The apostles, who had fled and trembled for fear of the Jews, after receiving the Holy Spirit boldly come forward in public; they rejoice when they must suffer for the confession of the gospel. He will give you another Comforter, who will abide with you for ever.

units.la: 6. Confirmat nos vacillantes in fide, & facit certos de salute, hoc est, continuat & conservat beneficia Christi vsque ad finem. Sic Apostolos duxit in omnem veritatem, & confirmauit, qui prius fuerant infirmi, multis dubitationibus inuolati: quod ostendit collatio concionis Petri in pentecoste, & orationis eius in Emaus. Nos autem sperabamus illum esse, qui redemturus esset Israelem, &c. De hoc loquitur Christus: Gaudebit cor vestrum, & gaudium vestrum nemo tollet à vobis. Manebit vobiscum in æternum. Hinc spiritus fortitudinis, & arrhabo hæreditatis vocatur.
units.tr: 6. He confirms us when we waver in faith, and makes us certain of salvation, that is, he continues and preserves the benefits of Christ until the end. Thus he led the apostles into all truth and strengthened them, who before had been weak and entangled in many doubts; this is shown by a comparison of Peter's sermon at Pentecost with his speech at Emmaus. But we were hoping that it was he who would redeem Israel, etc. Of this Christ speaks: Your heart shall rejoice, and no one shall take your joy from you. He will abide with you for ever. Hence he is called the Spirit of strength and the pledge of the inheritance.

units.la: Hæ sunt officii Spiritus sancti præcipuæ partes, quarum respectu varia habet in scripturis elogia. Hinc enim vocatur. 1. Spiritus viοθεσίας adoptionis, quia nos certos facit de paterna Dei erga nos bonitate, & nobis est testis gratuitæ adoptionis ac beneuolentiæ, qua nos pater complectitur in filio unigenito. Ideoque hunc spiritum clamamus, Abba pater. 2. Arrhabo & signum hæreditatis nostræ: quia nos certos reddit de salute nostra. Qui nos confirmat vobiscum in Christum: & qui unxit nos, Deus est, qui etiam obsignauit nos, & dedit arrhabonem spiritus in cordibus nostris. Postquam credidistis, obsignati estis spiritu illo promissionis sancto qui est arrhabo hæreditatis nostræ. 3. Vita seu spiritus vitæ: quia veterem hominem mortificat, nouum viuificat. Lex spiritus vitæ quia nos refrigerat sub æstu iræ Dei languentes in peccatis, expurgat peccata; & fœcundat nos, ut fructum iustitiæ feramus Deo. 5. Ignis: quia assidue glisicentes in nobis concupiscentias & vitia exurit, & corda nostra amore Dei & proximi accendit. 6. Fons aquæ viuæ: quia ex ipso & per ipsum omnes cœlestes diuitiæ ad nos manant. 7. Spiritus precum: quia ad precandum nos excitat & instruit. Effundam super domum Dauid & super habitatores Ierusalem spiritum gratiæ & precum, & aspicient ad me. Spiritus subleuat infirmitates nostras: quid enim precemur ut oportet non nouimus. 8. Oleum lætitiæ: quia lætos, alacres, & vegetos reddit. Propterea unxit te Deus, Deus tuus, oleo lætitiæ præ consortibus tuis. 9. Paracletus, consolator: quia per fidem de gratia Dei nos certos reddit, purificat conscientias & corda, & ita nos consolatur, ut in afflictionibus etiam gloriemur. 10. Aduocatus seu intercessor: quia interpellat pro nobis gemitibus ineffabilibus. 11. Denique spiritus veritatis, sapientiæ, consilij, gaudij, lætitiæ, fidei, timoris Dei, fortitudinis, gratiæ, &c.
units.tr: These are the chief parts of the office of the Holy Spirit, and in view of them Scripture gives him various titles. For he is called: 1. the Spirit of adoption [υἱοθεσία], because he makes us certain of the Father's goodness towards us, and is to us a witness of the free adoption and the favour by which the Father embraces us in the Only-begotten Son. Therefore we cry out this Spirit: Abba, Father. 2. The pledge and seal of our inheritance, because he makes us certain of our salvation. He who establishes us with you in Christ, and who anointed us, is God, who also sealed us and gave us the pledge of the Spirit in our hearts. After you believed, you were sealed with that Holy Spirit of promise, who is the pledge of our inheritance. 3. The life, or the Spirit of life: because he mortifies the old man and quickens the new. The law of the Spirit of life because he cools us, who languish under the heat of God's wrath in our sins, cleanses our sins, and makes us fruitful so that we may bear the fruit of righteousness to God. 5. Fire, because he constantly burns up the lusts and vices that flare up in us, and kindles our hearts with love of God and neighbour. 6. The fountain of living water, because from him and through him all heavenly riches flow to us. 7. The Spirit of prayers, because he stirs us up and teaches us to pray. I will pour out upon the house of David and upon the inhabitants of Jerusalem the Spirit of grace and of prayers, and they will look to me. The Spirit helps our infirmities, for we do not know how we ought to pray. 8. The oil of gladness, because he makes us glad, cheerful, and vigorous. Therefore God, your God, has anointed you with the oil of gladness above your fellows. 9. The Paraclete, the Comforter, because through faith he makes us certain of the grace of God, purifies consciences and hearts, and so comforts us that we glory even in afflictions. 10. The advocate or intercessor, because he intercedes for us with groanings that cannot be uttered. 11. Finally, the Spirit of truth, wisdom, counsel, joy, gladness, faith, fear of God, strength, grace, and so on.

units.la: Quaest. LIII.
units.tr: Question 53.

units.la: Obiect. 1. Istæ officij partes iam enumeratæ, sunt etiam patris & filij. Non ergo soli Spiritui sancto sunt assignandæ tanquam propriæ. Resp. Sunt etiam patris & filij, sed non immediate, vt sunt Spiritus sancti, per quem Pater & Filius eas operantur. Inst. Eadem ratione etiam tanquam propria officia Spiritui sancto viderentur tribuenda conseruatio rerum, artium inuentio, & similia. Nam etiam illa agit pater & filius per spiritum san-ctum, iuxta dictum : Spiritus Domini replet terras. Resp. Vt aliquod opus tanquam proprium assignetur Spiritui sancto, non tantum illud immediate ab eo fieri debet, sed etiam ita, vt agnoscatur. Agnoscitur autem per sanctificationem. Ibi igitur proprie operatur Spiritus sanctus, vbi sanctificat, cum & inde sanctus dicatur: per communia autem illa opera non sanctificat.
units.tr: Objection. 1. These parts of the office already listed also belong to the Father and the Son. Therefore they should not be assigned to the Holy Spirit alone as proper to him. Answer.
