They belong also to the Father and the Son, but not immediately as they are the Holy Spirit's, since it is through the Holy Spirit that the Father and the Son work them. Instance. By the same reasoning, the preservation of things, the invention of arts and similar works would also seem to be assigned to the Holy Spirit as proper offices, since the Father and the Son perform these too through the Holy Spirit, according to the saying: Spiritus Domini replet terras. Answer. For some work to be assigned to the Holy Spirit as his own, it must not only be done by him immediately, but must also be recognised as his. It is recognised, however, through sanctification. The Holy Spirit therefore properly works where he sanctifies, since he is called holy from that; but by those common works he does not sanctify.

units.la: Obiect.2. Saul & Iudas non obtinuerunt hæreditatem & tamen habuerunt Spiritum sanctum. Ergo Spiritus sanctus non est argabo hæreditatis nostræ.Resp. Saul & Iudas habuerunt Spiritum sanctum, quoad aliqua eius dona : sed non habuerunt spiritum adoptionis.Inst. Atqui est idem spiritus.Resp. Idem quidem spiritus est, sed non eadem efficitin omnibus. Adoptionem & conuersionem in solis electis efficit. Hic igitur de donis & eorum discrimine aliquid dicendum est.
units.tr: Objection. 2. Saul and Judas did not obtain the inheritance, and yet they had the Holy Spirit. Therefore the Holy Spirit is not the pledge of our inheritance. Answer. Saul and Judas had the Holy Spirit as to some of his gifts, but they did not have the Spirit of adoption. Instance. But it is the same Spirit. Answer. It is indeed the same Spirit, but he does not produce the same effects in everyone. He produces adoption and conversion only in the elect. Something must therefore be said here about the gifts and how they differ.

units.la: IV. Quæ & quot uplicia sint dona Spiritus sancti.
units.tr: IV. What and how many kinds of gifts of the Holy Spirit there are.

units.la: Omnia dona Spiritus sancti possunt referri ad partes officii prius enumeratas. Sunt autem duplicia. Quædam communia piis & impiis: quædam piorum & electorum propria. Quæ communia sunt piis & impiis, rursus sunt duplicia. Quædam dantur certis temporibus, vt facultas miraculosa linguarum, oracula, fides miraculorum, & quæ Apostolis & primitiuæ Ecclesiæ etant necessaria, cum primum esset spargendum Euangelium, iis dabantur eis miraculose. Quædam omnibus membris ac temporibus Ecclesiæ sunt necessaria, vt donum linguarum, interpretationis, scientiæ, artes, prudentia, eruditio, eloquentia, & alia, quæ ad conseruationem ministerij pertinent. Hæc etiam nunc accipiunt singuli juxta mensuram donationis Christi, pro necessitate vocationis suæ, licet non miraculose, vt apostoli, sed labore & studio. Dona vero piorum propria sunt ea omnia, quæ nomine sanctificationis & adoptionis comprehenduntur, vt iustificatus, regeneratio, inuocatio vera, dilectio Dei & proximi, spes, patientia, constantia, & alia dona salutaria. Hæc dantur solis electis in conuersione. Quem mundus non potest accipere. Spiritus contestatur spiritui nostro, quod sumus filij Dei. Rom. 8, 16. Intercedit pro nobis gemitibus inenarrabilibus. Hinc Spiritus adoptionis vocatur.
units.tr: All the gifts of the Holy Spirit can be referred to the parts of the office enumerated earlier. They are of two kinds. Some are common to the godly and the ungodly; others are proper to the godly and the elect. Those common to the godly and the ungodly are again of two kinds. Some are given at certain times, such as the miraculous gift of tongues, prophecy, the faith to work miracles, and the other things that were necessary for the apostles and the primitive Church when the gospel first had to be spread; these were given to them miraculously. Others are necessary for all the members and all the times of the Church, such as the gift of interpreting tongues, knowledge, skills, prudence, learning, eloquence, and the others that pertain to the preservation of the ministry. These too individuals now receive, according to the measure of Christ's gift and the needs of their calling, not miraculously as the apostles did, but through labour and study. The gifts proper to the godly are all those comprehended under the names of sanctification and adoption, such as justification, regeneration, true invocation, love of God and neighbour, hope, patience, constancy, and the other saving gifts. These are given only to the elect at conversion. "Which the world cannot receive. The Spirit itself beareth witness with our spirit, that we are the children of God." Rom. 8, 16. "He intercedes for us with groanings which cannot be uttered." Hence he is called the Spirit of adoption.

units.la: Obiect. Multi extra Ecclesiam calluerunt linguas, scientias, &c. Linguæ igitur & scientiæ non sunt inter dona Spiritus sancti numerandæ. Resp. Extra ecclesiam linguæ, &c. sunt dona Dei, exactione generali, quæ est sine vera Dei cognitione: in ecclesia verò sunt dona Spiritus sancti: quia in ea Spiritus sanctus agnoscitur.
units.tr: Objection. Many outside the Church have learned languages, sciences and so on. Therefore languages and sciences should not be counted among the gifts of the Holy Spirit. Answer. Outside the Church, languages and the rest are gifts of God by general providence, which is without true knowledge of God; but within the Church they are gifts of the Holy Spirit, because in the Church the Holy Spirit is recognised.

units.la: V. A quo detur Spiritus sanctus, & quare.
units.tr: V. By whom the Holy Spirit is given, and why.

units.la: Datur à Patre per Filium: quod confirmant testimonia. Denunciauit iis, vt exspectarent promissum Patris. Effundam de spiritu meo super omnem carnem. Rogabo Patrem, & alium consolatorem mittet vobis. Quem Pater mittet in nomine meo. Datur etiam à Filio: sed à Patre, à quo ipse Filius est & agit, secundum dicta. Quem ego vobis mittam à Patre. Sin autem profectus fuero, mittam illum ad vos. Dextera Dei exaltus, & promissum Spiritum sanctum adeptus effundit hoc, quod vos nunc spectatis & auditis, &c. Hinc firmum argumentum colligitur pro deitate CHRISTI. Nemo enim jus habet in Spiritum Dei, & potest eum dare, nisi Deus. Filius dat & mittit Spiritum Dei. Ergo, &c. Obiect. Etiam natura humana Christi mittit. Resp. Christus homo mittit Spiritum sanctum. Natura humana Christi tantum abest, vt jus habeat mittendi Spiritum sanctum, vt contrà Spiritus sanctus ipsam formarit & sanctificarit.
units.tr: He is given by the Father through the Son, as the testimonies confirm. He charged them to wait for the promise of the Father. "I will pour out my Spirit upon all flesh." "I will pray the Father, and he shall send you another Comforter." "Whom the Father will send in my name." He is also given by the Son, but from the Father, from whom the Son himself is and acts, according to the sayings: "Whom I will send unto you from the Father." "But if I depart, I will send him unto you." "Exalted at the right hand of God, and having received the promised Holy Spirit, he has poured out this which you now see and hear," and so on. From this a firm argument for the deity of Christ is drawn. For no one has the right over the Spirit of God and can give him, except God. The Son gives and sends the Spirit of God; therefore, etc. Objection. Christ's human nature also sends him. Answer. Christ as man sends the Holy Spirit. Christ's human nature is so far from having the right to send the Holy Spirit that, on the contrary, the Holy Spirit formed and sanctified it.

units.la: Dari autem Spiritum sanctum à Patre & Filio, sic est intelligendum, quod vterq; per illum est efficax, & quod Spiritus sanctus agit præeunte voluntate Patris & Filij. Notandus enim est operationis ordo in personis diuinis, qui talis est in agendo, qualis est in existendo. Præcedit voluntas Patris, sequitur voluntas Filij, vtriusque voluntatem consequitur voluntas Spiritus sancti, non tempore, sed ordine.
units.tr: That the Holy Spirit is given by the Father and the Son is to be understood in this way: each of them is effective through him, and the Holy Spirit acts at the prior will of the Father and the Son. For the order of operation in the divine persons must be noted; in acting it is the same as in existing. The will of the Father comes first, the will of the Son follows, and the will of the Holy Spirit follows the will of both, not in time but in order.

units.la: VI. Quibus, & quatenus detur.
units.tr: VI. To whom, and how far, the Holy Spirit is given.

units.la: Spiritus sanctus dicitur dari his, quibus dona sua communicat, quique eum agnoscunt. Datur igitur aliis atque aliis secundum diuersa dona, quorum alia communia, alia propria esse, dictum est. Datur tori Ecclesiæ vocatorum, hypocritis & electis, sed aliter his, aliter illis. Hypocritis, fidem non syncerè profitentibus, datur tantum, quoad dona communia, cognitionem doctrinæ, peritiam linguarum, virtutes miraculorum, donum prophetiæ, fidem temporalem, &c. Multi dicent in die illo, nomine tuo prophetauimus, &c. Non datur verò, quoad dona adoptionis, fidei sincerae, regenerationis, perseuerantiae, &c. Quem mundus non potest accipere, quia non nouit illum. Electis autem praeter dona communia, quae Spiritus sanctus cuique distribuit, sicut vult, etiam conferuntur dona singularia & salutaria, fidei, conuersionis, regenerationis, adoptionis, justificationis, sanctificationis, & perseuerantiae: & quidem sic dantur eis haec dona, vt inde Spiritum sanctum in se habitantem possint agnoscere, & de salute sua certò confidere. Dantur autem volentibus & petentibus, atque perseuerantibus, quae omnia tamen idem ille Spiritus in nobis efficit. Nemo potest IESVM appellare Dominum, nisi per Spiritum sanctum. Spiritus intercedit pro nobis gemitibus inenarrabilibus. Deus efficit in vobis, vt velitis, & vt perficiatis.
units.tr: The Holy Spirit is said to be given to those to whom he communicates his gifts and who acknowledge him. He is therefore given to different people in different ways, according to the diverse gifts, of which some, as has been said, are common and others proper. He is given to the whole body of the called, to hypocrites and to the elect, but in different ways. To hypocrites, who do not profess the faith sincerely, he is given only as regards the common gifts: knowledge of doctrine, skill in languages, powers of miracles, the gift of prophecy, temporary faith, and so on. Many will say on that day, we have prophesied in your name, etc. But he is not given as regards the gifts of adoption, sincere faith, regeneration, perseverance, and so on: whom the world cannot receive, because it does not know him. To the elect, however, besides the common gifts which the Holy Spirit distributes to each one as he wills, there are also conferred singular and saving gifts: of faith, conversion, regeneration, adoption, justification, sanctification and perseverance. These gifts are given to them in such a way that from them they can recognise the Holy Spirit dwelling in them and be certain of their salvation. They are given, moreover, to those who are willing and who ask, and who persevere; yet all these things that same Spirit effects in us. No one can call Jesus Lord except through the Holy Spirit. The Spirit makes intercession for us with groanings that cannot be uttered. God works in you both to will and to do.

units.la: Hinc apparet, quid cognitio linguarum, scientiarum & similia dona ethnicis collata differant ab iis, quae conferuntur ecclesiae. Nam qui inter ethnicos linguarum cognitione, & bonarum artium rerumq; vtilium scientia excelluerunt, habuerunt quidem dona Dei, sed non Spiritum sanctum, quippe quem nisi quos ipse sanctificat, & qui ipsum agnoscunt authorem donorum.
units.tr: Hence it is clear how the knowledge of languages, of the sciences and similar gifts bestowed on the heathen differ from those which are bestowed on the Church. For those among the heathen who excelled in knowledge of languages and in the learning of the liberal arts and useful things indeed had the gifts of God, but not the Holy Spirit, who is given only to those whom he himself sanctifies and who acknowledge him as the author of the gifts.

units.la: VII. Quando, & quomodo detur, atque accipiatur Spiritus sanctus.
units.tr: VII. When and how the Holy Spirit is given and received.

units.la: Datur Spiritus sanctus, quando dona sua communicat, vt prius dictum est. Datur autem vel visibiliter, symbolis adhibitis: vel inuisibiliter, sine symbolis.
units.tr: The Holy Spirit is given when he communicates his gifts, as was said before. He is given either visibly, with symbols employed, or invisibly, without symbols.

units.la: Visibiliter non semper, sed certis temporibus: praecipuè autem in nouo Testamento, juxta oraculum Joelis: Postremis diebus effundam de spiritu meo super omnem carnem. Sic datus fuit Apostolis, & viris apostolicis, aliisq; membris in primitiua Ecclesia. Visa sunt linguae eorum dispertitae instar ignis, &c. Et Spiritus sedit super vnumquemque. Spiritus sanctus decidit super eos. Vidi Spiritum descendentem de coelo, &c. Quae locutiones sunt intelligendae per metonymiam signi, quod symbolum accipiat nomen rei, & de re dicatur, quod symbolo conuenit: quia his symbolis Spiritus sanctus praesentiam atque efficaciam suam testabatur. Sic Joannes vidit Spiritum descendentem super Christum corporea specie, tanquam columbam, hoc est, vidit columbam, qua Deus Spiritus sui praesentiam demonstrabat. Non igitur motus locales cogitetur in Deo, sed praesentia & operatio, quam exercet in Ecclesia. Nam Spiritus sanctus essentiae immensitate vbiq; quidem diffusus est, coelum ac terram replens. Dicitur verò dari, mitti, effundi, &c. quando efficacia sua in Ecclesiae membris dona
units.tr: He was given visibly not always, but at certain times, especially in the New Testament, according to the oracle of Joel: In the last days I will pour out my Spirit upon all flesh. Thus he was given to the Apostles, to apostolic men and to other members in the primitive Church. There appeared to them tongues divided like fire, etc. And the Spirit sat upon each one. The Holy Spirit fell upon them. I saw the Spirit descending from heaven, etc. These expressions are to be understood by metonymy of the sign, since the symbol takes the name of the thing, and what belongs to the symbol is said of the thing: for by these symbols the Holy Spirit testified his presence and efficacy. So John saw the Spirit descending upon Christ in bodily form, as a dove, that is, he saw the dove by which God showed the presence of his Spirit. Therefore one should not think of local motions in God, but of the presence and operation which he exercises in the Church. For the Holy Spirit, by the immensity of his essence, is indeed diffused everywhere, filling heaven and earth. But he is said to be given, sent, poured out, etc., when by his efficacy he creates, arouses and perfects his gifts in the members of the Church.

units.la: Ioh. 14, 17. donasua creat, excitat, & perficit. Inuisibiliter semper datus est & datur ecclesiæ, inde ab initio vsque ad finem mundi: quia locutus est per prophetas. Qui spiritum Christi non habet, non est eius. Et sine Spiritu sancto nulla fuisset fides, nulla ecclesia. Multò tamen liberalius & pluribus in nouo Testamento confertur, quàm olim in veteri, juxta oraculum Ioelis & Zachariæ, & historiam nouæ Ecclesiæ.
units.tr: John 14:17. Invisibly he has always been given and is given to the Church, from the beginning until the end of the world, because he spoke through the prophets. He who does not have the Spirit of Christ is not his. And without the Holy Spirit there would have been no faith and no Church. Yet he is conferred much more liberally and upon more people in the New Testament than formerly in the Old, according to the oracles of Joel and Zechariah and the history of the new Church.

units.la: Datur autem per ministerium verbi & Sacramentorum. 1. Pa-tefaciendo sese nobis per euangelicæ doctrinæ cognitionem, studium & meditationem. Agnitus enim vult se nobis communicare: quia dum se nobis agnoscendum præbet, etiam corda nostra illustrat, renouat & reformat. Sic operabatur in electis per concionem Petri apostoli in die Pentecostes: & in Cornelio, ac reliquis, qui aderant, loquente Petro. Ita tamen per verbum & sacramenta operatur Spiritus sanctus, vt his mediis non sit alligatus. Neque enim omnes audientes conuertit, sed quos vult: & alios aliter: vt Paulum in itinere Damasceno: & Iohannem donis suis instruxit in vtero matris. Cum autem dicimus, cum dari per ministerium, loquimur de adultis, & de via ordinaria, deque missione inuisibili, qua singulis dona consueta in ecclesia contingunt, & de qua dicitur: Misit Spiritum Filij sui in corda vestra, &c. Qui Spiritum Christi non habet, non est eius. 2. Efficiendo in electis desiderium sui. Petentibus enim datur. Hinc sumitur argumentum efficax pro Deitate Spiritus sancti. Per ministerium enim operari efficaciter, est solius Dei. Neque is qui plantat, est aliquid, neque is, qui rigat, sed Deus, qui dat incrementum. Ego baptizo vos aqua ad resipiscentiam: is vero qui venit vos baptizabit Spiritu sancto & igni. Euangelium est potentia Dei, &c. Quia Spiritus est per illud efficax: vnde & ministerium Spiritus dicitur Euangelium. Accipitur autem Spiritus sanctus per fidem. In quo etiam, postquam credidistis, obsignati estis Spiritu sancto promissionis. Mundus non potest Spiritum illum veritatis accipere: quia non vidit eum, nec nouit eum.
units.tr: He is given, however, through the ministry of the Word and of the Sacraments. First, by making himself known to us through the knowledge, study and meditation of the evangelical doctrine. For the Spirit, being known, wishes to communicate himself to us: since while he presents himself to us to be acknowledged, he also illumines, renews and reforms our hearts. Thus he worked in the elect through the sermon of the apostle Peter on the day of Pentecost, and in Cornelius and the others who were present while Peter spoke. Yet the Holy Spirit works through the Word and the sacraments in such a way that he is not bound to these means. For he does not convert all who hear, but whom he wills, and others in other ways: as Paul on the road to Damascus, and he equipped John with his gifts in his mother's womb. When we say that he is given through the ministry, we are speaking of adults, and of the ordinary way, and of the invisible mission by which the usual gifts in the Church come to individuals, and of which it is said: He sent the Spirit of his Son into your hearts, etc. He who does not have the Spirit of Christ is not his. Second, by working desire for himself in the elect. For to those who ask it is given. From this an effective argument is drawn for the Deity of the Holy Spirit. For to work efficaciously through the ministry belongs to God alone: Neither is he who plants anything, nor he who waters, but God who gives the increase. I baptise you with water unto repentance; but he who comes after me will baptise you with the Holy Spirit and with fire. The gospel is the power of God, etc. Because the Spirit is efficacious through it; hence the ministry of the Spirit is also called the Gospel. The Holy Spirit is received through faith: In whom also, after you believed, you were sealed with the Holy Spirit of promise. The world cannot receive that Spirit of truth, because it neither sees him nor knows him.

units.la: Obiect. Atqui fides est donum & fructus Spiritus sancti. Gratia estis seruati, idq; non ex vobis, donum Dei est. Nemo potest dicere Iesum Dominum, nisi per Spiritum sanctum. Ergo Spiritus sanctus est prior fide. Quomodo igitur accipitur fide? Resp. Actio Spiritus sancti naturâ prior est fide, simul tempore: quia fidei initium est Spiritus sancti acceptio. 2. Fide autem inchoata, magis manet in nobis, per quam accipitur Spiritus sanctus, qui reliqua deinde per eisque operatur, sicut dicitur: Fides per charitatem operatur. Fide purificantur corda.
units.tr: Objection. Yet faith is a gift and fruit of the Holy Spirit: By grace you are saved, and that not of yourselves; it is the gift of God. No one can say that Jesus is Lord except through the Holy Spirit. Therefore the Holy Spirit is prior to faith. How then is the Spirit received by faith? Answer: The action of the Holy Spirit is prior to faith in nature, though simultaneous in time, because the beginning of faith is the reception of the Holy Spirit. Second, once faith is begun, it abides more in us, through which the Holy Spirit is received, who then works the remaining things through and by means of it, as it is said: Faith works through love. By faith hearts are purified.

units.la: VIII. Quomodo retineatur Spiritus sanctus.
units.tr: VIII. How the Holy Spirit is retained.

units.la: Iisdem modis retinetur, quibus datur & accipitur Spiritus sanctus. 1. Diligenti vsu ministerij ecclesiastici. Dedit alios apostolos, alios prophetas, &c. ad coagmentationem corporis Christi, donec euadamus omnes in vnitatem fidei. 2. Meditatione doctrinæ assidua, & studio in ea proficiendi. Qui in lege Domini meditatur die ac nocte, erit velut arbor plantata ad ripas aquarum. Sermo Christi inhabitet in vobis cum omni sapientia, docendo & commonefacientes vos mutuo. 3. Assidua pœnitentia, & studio cavendi lapsus contra conscientiam. Habenti dabitur. Iustus iustificetur adhuc. Ne tristitia afficite Spiritum illum sanctum Dei, per quem obsignati estis in diem redemptionis. Huc pertinet studium vitandi praua commercia, & peccatorum occasiones. Vitare enim peccata, est vitare occasiones peccatorum. 4. Assidua & seria invocatione. Quanto magis Pater meus cœlestis dabit Spiritum sanctum petentibus. Spiritum sanctum tuum ne auferas à me. Hoc genus non expellitur, nisi ieiunio & precibus. 5. Dona Dei conferendo ad vsuram, hoc est ad gloriam Dei, & proximi salutem. Et tu conuersus confirma fratres tuos. Negotiamini donec veniam. Habenti dabitur, à non habente etiam quod habet, auferetur. IX. An & quomodo amittatur Spiritus sanctus. Amittitur ab hypocritis & reprobis finaliter, hoc est, ita, vt nunquam recipiant, & totaliter, hoc est, prorsus: ita, vt nulla singularia, sed vix generalia dona retineant. Ab electis non amittitur totaliter, sed quoad multa dona, quia semper aliqua dona singularia retinent, vt testatur exemplum Dauidis: Redde mihi latitiam, &c. & Spiritum tuum sanctum ne auferas à me. Et Iohanes: Semen Dei manet in eo. Nec finaliter: quia tandem vi Spiritus Dei redeunt ad pœnitentiam. Obiect. Atqui Spiritus sanctus recessit à Saule, qui fuit electus. Ergo etiam ab electis recedere potest. Resp. Recessit à Saule non Spiritus regenerationis & adoptionis, quem nunquam habuit, sed Spiritus prophetiæ, prudentiæ, fortitudinis, & aliorum donorum, quibus fuerat ornatus. Fuit autem electus non ad vitam, sed ad regnum, sicut Judas ad apostolatum. Inst. Imò etiam Spiritus regenerationis recessit ab electis: quia Dauid peccatur: Redde mihi latitiam salutis tuæ. Resp. Sæpe amittitur à sanctis Spiritus regenerationis, quoad aliqua dona, vt dictum est, sed non quoad omnia, nec in vniuersum. Fieri enim non potest, vt electi nullas retineant fidei reliquias, cum non peccent ad mortem: sed ex infirmitate carnis, quatenus nondum sunt renati: quod expresse docet Johannes: Quisquis ex Deo natus est, non peccat, quoniam semen eius manet in eo, nec potest peccare, eo quod ex Deo natus est. Amiserat Dauid in lapsu laetitiam cordis, puritatem conscientiae, & multa alia dona, quae sibi petit restitui, sed Spiritum sanctum non amiserat penitus, alioqui non potuisset dicere: Spiritum tuum sanctum ne auferas a me. Hunc ergo non penitus amiserat. Homo nunquam in eodem statu manet, (inquit Bernhardus) aut deficit, aut proficit. Hoc discrimen tenendum est, ad soluendam quaestionem: Quomodo certa sit nihilominus electorum salus & perseuerantia, licet aliquando in lapsibus amittant Spiritum sanctum: quia scilicet totaliter & finaliter a Spiritu sancto non deseruntur.
units.tr: The Holy Spirit is retained in the same ways by which he is given and received. (1) By the diligent use of the ecclesiastical ministry. He gave some to be apostles, some prophets, etc., for the building up of the body of Christ, until we all attain to the unity of faith. (2) By constant meditation on doctrine and zeal to advance in it. Blessed is the one who meditates on the law of the Lord day and night; he will be like a tree planted by streams of water. Let the word of Christ dwell in you richly in all wisdom, teaching and admonishing one another. (3) By constant repentance and diligence in avoiding lapses against conscience. To the one who has, more will be given. Let the righteous still be made righteous. Do not grieve the Holy Spirit of God, by whom you were sealed for the day of redemption. To this belongs the effort to shun wicked dealings and occasions of sin, for to avoid sins is to avoid the occasions of sin. (4) By constant and earnest invocation. How much more will your heavenly Father give the Holy Spirit to those who ask him. Do not take your Holy Spirit from me. This kind is not cast out except by fasting and prayer. (5) By putting the gifts of God to use, that is, for the glory of God and the salvation of neighbour. And you, when you have turned back, strengthen your brothers. Engage in business until I come. To the one who has, more will be given, but from the one who has not, even what he has will be taken away. IX. Whether and how the Holy Spirit may be lost. He is lost finally by hypocrites and the reprobate, that is, so that they never recover him, and totally, that is, altogether: so that they keep no single gifts, but hardly even general ones. The elect do not lose him totally, but as to many gifts, because they always retain some particular gifts, as the example of David testifies: Restore to me the joy, etc., and do not take your Holy Spirit from me. And John: The seed of God remains in him. Nor do they lose him finally, because at last by the power of God's Spirit they return to repentance. Objection: Yet the Holy Spirit departed from Saul, who was elect. Therefore the elect too can depart. Answer: It was not the Spirit of regeneration and adoption, which he never had, that departed from Saul, but the Spirit of prophecy, prudence, fortitude, and the other gifts with which he had been adorned. Moreover, he was elected not to life but to kingdom, just as Judas was to apostleship. Objection: Indeed, even the Spirit of regeneration has departed from the elect, since David sinned: Restore to me the joy of your salvation. Answer: The Spirit of regeneration is often lost by the saints as to some gifts, as has been said, but not as to all, nor altogether. For it cannot happen that the elect retain no remnants of faith, since they do not sin unto death; rather, they sin from the weakness of the flesh, insofar as they are not yet reborn. John teaches this expressly: Whoever is born of God does not sin, because his seed remains in him, and he cannot sin, because he is born of God. In his fall David had lost the joy of his heart, the purity of his conscience, and many other gifts, which he asks to be restored to him, but he had not wholly lost the Holy Spirit, otherwise he could not have said: Do not take your Holy Spirit from me. Therefore he had not lost him entirely. A man never remains in the same state (says Bernard): he either falls back or advances. This distinction must be kept in order to resolve the question of how the salvation and perseverance of the elect are nonetheless certain, although at times in their falls they lose the Holy Spirit: namely because they are not wholly and finally forsaken by the Holy Spirit.

units.la: Potest autem amitti Spiritus sanctus multis modis, & quidem contrariis, iis quibus retinetur. 1. Contemptu ministerij ecclesiastici. 2. Neglectu studij & meditationis doctrinae. Ideo Paulus Timotheum jubet ἀναζωπυρεῖν τὸ χάρισμα τοῦ Θεοῦ: & quo pacto hoc fiat, etiam docet, attendendo scilicet lectioni, exhortationi, doctrinae. 3. Securitati carnali, proiiciendo scilicet conscientiam. 4. Neglectu precum & invocationis Dei. 5. Denique abusu donorum Spiritus sancti, quando non conferuntur ad ipsius gloriam & proximi salutem. Habenti dabitur, a non habente auferetur, quod habet.
units.tr: The Holy Spirit can be lost in many ways, and indeed in ways contrary to those by which he is retained. (1) By contempt of the ecclesiastical ministry. (2) By neglect of the study and meditation of doctrine. Therefore Paul orders Timothy to stir up the gift of God [ἀναζωπυρεῖν τὸ χάρισμα τοῦ Θεοῦ], and he also teaches how this is to be done, namely by attending to reading, exhortation, and doctrine. (3) By carnal security, namely by casting away conscience. (4) By neglect of prayer and of invoking God. (5) Finally, by abuse of the gifts of the Holy Spirit, when they are not directed to his glory and the salvation of neighbour. From the one who has, even what he has will be taken away, and to the one who has, more will be given.

units.la: X. Quare & quantopere sit necessarius Spiritus sanctus.
units.tr: X. Why the Holy Spirit is necessary, and how greatly.

units.la: Quam necessarius sit Spiritus sanctus, & quibus de causis, ex his dictis luculenter apparet. Nisi quis fuerit genitus ex aqua & spiritu, non poterit introire in regnum Dei. Caro & sanguis non poterit hereditatem regni Dei consequi. Non sumus idonei ad cogitandum quippiam boni ex nobis ipsis, velut ex nobis, sed quod idoneos sumus, id ex Deo est. Quod si quis Spiritum Christi non habet, is non est eius. Hinc ita licet concludere. Sine quo non possumus boni quid cogitare, nedum facere, nec regenerari, nec cognoscere DEVM, nec obedire Deo, nec regni coelestis hereditatem consequi, sine eo non possumus seruari. Sine Spiritu sancto illa fieri, propter nostrae naturae corruptionem & caecitatem, non possunt. Ergo sine Spiritu sancto fieri non potest, vt ita uemur, & per consequens, Spiritus sanctus nobis omnino necessarius est ad salutem.
units.tr: How necessary the Holy Spirit is, and for what causes, is clearly apparent from what has been said. Unless one is born of water and the Spirit, he cannot enter the kingdom of God. Flesh and blood cannot obtain the inheritance of the kingdom of God. We are not sufficient to think anything good of ourselves, as of ourselves, but our sufficiency is from God. If anyone does not have the Spirit of Christ, he is not his. Hence we may conclude thus: without whom we cannot think anything good, much less do it, nor be regenerated, nor know God, nor obey God, nor obtain the inheritance of the heavenly kingdom, without him we cannot be saved. Those things cannot be done without the Holy Spirit, on account of the corruption and blindness of our nature. Therefore, without the Holy Spirit it cannot come about that we are saved, so to speak, and consequently the Holy Spirit is wholly necessary to us for salvation.

units.la: XI. Vnde agnoscatur inhabitatio Spiritus sancti in nobis.
units.tr: XI. How the indwelling of the Holy Spirit in us is recognised.

units.la: Agnoscimus Spiritum sanctum nos habere ex effectis seu beneficiis ipsius in nobis: videlicet, ex vera DEI agnitione, regeneratione, fide, pace conscientiae, inchoatione nouae obedientiae, & promptitudine ad obediendum DEO. Iustificati fide pacem habemus cum Deo. Dilectio Dei diffusa est in cordibus nostris, per Spiritum sanctum, qui datus est nobis. Item ex testimonio, quod ipse dat spiritui nostro, nos esse filios DEI. Insuper certissima testimonia sunt & indicia Spiritus sancti in nobis habitantis, consolatio in media morte, laetitia in afflictionibus, propositum perseuerandi in fide, gemitus & preces ardentes, sincera denique professio Christianismi. Nemo potest dicere JESVM Dominum, nisi per Spiritum sanctum. Breuiter: Ex fide & poenitentia habitationem Spiritus sancti in nobis agnoscimus.
units.tr: We recognise that we have the Holy Spirit from His effects or benefits in us: namely, from the true knowledge of God, regeneration, faith, peace of conscience, the beginning of new obedience, and readiness to obey God. Being justified by faith, we have peace with God. The love of God has been poured out in our hearts through the Holy Spirit, who has been given to us. Likewise, we know it from the testimony which He gives to our spirit, that we are the sons of God. Moreover, the most certain testimonies and signs of the Holy Spirit dwelling in us are consolation in the midst of death, joy in afflictions, purpose to persevere in faith, groanings and fervent prayers, and, finally, sincere profession of Christianity. No one can say that Jesus is Lord, except through the Holy Spirit. In short: from faith and repentance we recognise the indwelling of the Holy Spirit in us.

units.la: QVÆSTIO LIV.
units.tr: QUESTION 54.

units.la: Quid credis de sancta & catholica Christi Ecclesia?
units.tr: What do you believe concerning the holy and catholic Church of Christ?

units.la: RESPONSIO.
units.tr: ANSWER.

units.la: Credo Filium DEI a, ab initio mundi ad finem vsque b, sibi ex vniuerso genere humano c, coetum ad vitam aeternam electum d, per Spiritum & verbum e, in vera fide consentientem f, colligere, tueri & seruare g: neque vnquam eius coetus membrum esse h, & perpetuò mansurum i.
units.tr: I believe that the Son of God, from the beginning of the world to its end, gathers, defends and preserves for himself, from the whole human race, a congregation chosen to eternal life, agreeing in the true faith, through the Spirit and the Word; and that no member of this congregation will ever be lost, but it will remain forever.

units.la: EXPLICATIO.
units.tr: EXPLANATION.

units.la: I. Quæstiones de Ecclesia præcipuæ sunt: II. Quid sit. Quotuplex sit. III. Qui
units.tr: I. The chief questions about the Church are these: II. What it is, and how many kinds there are.

units.la: III. Quæ sint notæ veræ ecclesiæ.
units.tr: III. What are the marks of the true church.

units.la: IV. Quare dicatur una, sancta & catholica.
units.tr: IV. Why it is called one, holy and catholic.

units.la: V. Quid differat ecclesia à politia.
units.tr: V. How the church differs from the state.

units.la: VI. Quæ sit causa discriminis inter ecclesiam & reliquum genus humanum.
units.tr: VI. What is the cause of the distinction between the church and the rest of the human race.

units.la: VII. An extra ecclesiam sit salus.
units.tr: VII. Whether there is salvation outside the church.

units.la: I. Quid sit Ecclesia.
units.tr: I. What the Church is.

units.la: Cùm quæritur, quid sit ecclesia, præsupponitur esse ecclesiam: ita vt quæraere, an sit ecclesia non sit necesse. Semper enim fuit & futura est aliqua ecclesia, aliàs maior, aliàs minor: quia semper fuit & futurus est Christus rex, caput, & sacerdos ecclesiæ, vt mox quæst. 4. fusius ostendetur.
units.tr: When we ask what the church is, it is presupposed that there is a church, so that to ask whether there is a church is unnecessary. For there always has been, and always will be, some church, sometimes larger, sometimes smaller, because Christ always has been and always will be the King, Head and Priest of the church, as will be shown more fully below in question 4.

units.la: Quod ad nomen ecclesiæ attinet, dicebatur apud Athenienses ἐκκλησια, cœtus ciuium, voce præconis è reliqua turba quasi nominatim & per centurias euocatus ad concionem, vel ad audiendam senatus sententiam, ab ἐκκαλεῖν, euocare. Hinc apodiendam senatus sententiam, ab ἐκκαλεῖν, euocare. Hinc apostoli nomen ecclesiæ, translulerunt ad suum institutum, propter similitudinem. Est enim ecclesia Dei cœtus non fortuito confluens, nec inordinatus, sed voce Domini, & præconio verbi euocatus à regno satanæ, ad audiendum & amplectendum Dei verbum. Et hoc modo differt ecclesia à συναγωγὴ qualemcunq; congregationem, etiam quæ sit communis & inordinata. At ecclesia ordinatum cœtum denotat, eumque certa causa euocatum, qualis est cœtus vocatorum à Deo ad Euangelij cognitionem. Hunc cœtum etiam Latini voce Græca vocant Ecclesiam. Germanicum nostrum Kirch factum videtur ex Græco κυριακὴ, hoc est, dominica, scilicet domus, Gotes hauss.
units.tr: As to the name church, among the Athenians the ekklesia [ἐκκλησια] was an assembly of citizens, summoned to the public meeting, or to hear the decision of the senate, by a herald's voice calling them by name and by centuries out of the rest of the crowd; the word comes from ekkalein [ἐκκαλεῖν], to call out. Hence the apostles transferred the name church to their own institution, because of the resemblance. For the church of God is an assembly that does not gather by chance, nor in disorder, but is called out of the kingdom of Satan by the voice of the Lord and the proclamation of the Word, to hear and embrace God's Word. In this way the church differs from a synagogue [συναγωγὴ], any sort of gathering, even one that is common and disorderly. The church denotes an ordered assembly, called together for a definite cause, such as the assembly of those called by God to the knowledge of the Gospel. This assembly the Latins also call by the Greek word Ecclesia. Our German Kirch seems to have been made from the Greek kyriakē [κυριακὴ], that is, dominica, namely domus, Gotes hauss [God's house].

units.la: Definitio ecclesiæ in quæstione talis continetur: Ecclesia est cœtus hominum ab æterno electus à Deo ad vitam æternam, quem inde ab initio mundi ad finem usque Filius Dei sibi ex vniuerso genere humano, per Spiritum suum & verbum, in fide vera consentientem colligit, tuetur & conseruat, tandemque glorificat gloria & vita æterna. Sic definitur vera Dei Ecclesia, de qua proprie agit symbolum.
units.tr: The definition of the church contained in the question is this: The church is the congregation of men chosen by God from eternity to eternal life, which the Son of God gathers, protects and preserves for himself from the whole human race, from the beginning of the world to its end, through his Spirit and Word, agreeing in the true faith, and at last glorifies with eternal glory and life. This is how the true Church of God is defined, which is what the creed properly deals with.

units.la: II. Quotuplex sit Ecclesia.
units.tr: II. How many kinds of Church there are.

units.la: Ecclesia est aut vera, aut falsa. Falsa improprie dicitur ecclesia, sicut malus grammaticus improprie dicitur grammaticus: & est omnis cœtus, arrogans sibi titulum ecclesiæ Christianæ, sed eam non sequens, verum persequens. Vera ecclesia est aut triumphans, aut militans. Triumphans, quæ & nunc cum beatis angelis in coelo triumphat, & post resurrectionem plenum triumphum aget. Militans, quæ in hoc mundo aduersus diabolum, carnem, & mundum sub Christi vexillo pugnat. Militans est duplex, visibilis & inuisibilis. Visibilis est cœtus in genere humano amplectentium & profitentium integram & incorruptam doctrinam legis & euangelij, & vtentium sacramentis secundum institutionem diuinam, & profitentium obedientiam erga doctrinam: in quo cœtu multi regenerantur à Spiritu sancto per verbum ad vitam æternam, multi etiam manent non renati vel hypocritæ, consentientes tamen de doctrina & ritibus externis. Seu, est cœtus consentientium de doctrina, habens etiam quosdam membra mortua, seu non regeneratos. Non omnis qui dixerit mihi, domine, domine, ingredietur in regnum cœlorum. Huc pertinet parabola de semine, & de zizaniis, & de sagena cogente bonos & putridos pisces. Inuisibilis, est cœtus electorum & regeneratorum, qui sunt de cœtu visibilis Ecclesiæ. Hæc enim ecclesia, quamdiu in terris adhuc militat, semper latet in ecclesia visibili. Alias dicitur ecclesia sanctorum. Qui sunt de hac ecclesia, nunquam pereunt: neque ulli in eam sunt hypocritæ, sed soli electi, de quibus dicitur. Oues meas nemo rapiet è manibus meis. Firmum stat fundamentum DEI, habens sigillum hoc: nouit Dominus qui sint sui. Inuisibilis autem dicitur, non quod homines sint invisibiles, sed quia fides & pietas hominum est inuisibilis: nec agnoscitur nisi ab ipsis, in quibus est: & quia vere pios ab hypocritis in ecclesia nos non possumus certo dignoscere.
units.tr: The church is either true or false. The false is improperly called a church, just as a bad grammarian is improperly called a grammarian; it is any assembly that arrogantly claims the title of the Christian church but does not follow it, rather persecutes it. The true church is either triumphant or militant. The triumphant church is the one that now triumphs in heaven with the blessed angels, and after the resurrection will have its full triumph. The militant church is the one that in this world fights against the devil, the flesh and the world under Christ's banner. The militant church is twofold, visible and invisible. The visible church is the assembly, in the human race, of those who embrace and profess the whole and uncorrupted doctrine of the law and the gospel, who use the sacraments according to divine institution, and who profess obedience to the doctrine. In this assembly many are regenerated by the Holy Spirit through the Word to eternal life; many also remain unregenerate or hypocrites, yet agree in doctrine and external rites. Or, it is an assembly agreeing in doctrine, which also has some dead members, that is, unregenerate ones. Not everyone who says to me, Lord, Lord, will enter the kingdom of heaven. To this belongs the parable of the seed and of the tares, and of the net gathering good and bad fish. The invisible church is the assembly of the elect and regenerate, who are part of the visible church. For this church, as long as it still fights on earth, always lies hidden within the visible church. Otherwise it is called the church of the saints. Those who belong to this church never perish, and no hypocrites belong to it, but only the elect, of whom it is said: No one will snatch my sheep out of my hands. The firm foundation of God stands, having this seal: the Lord knows those who are his. It is called invisible not because the men are invisible, but because the faith and piety of men are invisible: it is recognised only by those in whom it is, and because we cannot with certainty distinguish the truly godly from the hypocrites in the church.

units.la: Porro vtraque, visibilis & inuisibilis, est vel vniuersalis vel particularis. Ecclesia visibilis catholica est cætus omnium profitentium doctrinam per totum mundum sparsus. Visibilis ecclesia particularis, est cœtus profitentium doctrinam in certo loco. Visibilis est vniuersalis, quoad professionem vnius fidei in Christum, vniusque doctrinæ cultus: particularis verò, quod ad habitationes & diuersitatem rituum attinet. Sic & inuisibilis ecclesia est vniuersalis, quatenus omnes electi, vbicunque locorum sint, & quocunque tempore vixerint, vnam habent fidem. Rursum particularis est, quatenus in hoc vel illo loco eandem habet fidem. Omnes autem particulares Ecclesiæ sunt partes vniuersalis, & quidem visibiles visibilis, inuisibiles verò inuisibilis ecclesiæ. Atque de hac visibili ecclesia vniuersali agit proprie articulus symboli nostri: Credo sanctam Ecclesiam catholicam. Hæc enim proprie eo titulo insignitur, quod sit sancta: & in hac est vera communio sanctorum cum Christo & membris omnibus.
units.tr: Moreover, each of these, visible and invisible, is either universal or particular. The visible catholic church is the assembly of all who profess the doctrine, spread throughout the whole world. The visible particular church is the assembly of those who profess the doctrine in a certain place. The visible church is universal as regards the profession of one faith in Christ and the one worship of the doctrine, but particular as regards dwellings and the diversity of rites. So too the invisible church is universal, inasmuch as all the elect, wherever they are and whenever they have lived, have one faith; and again it is particular, inasmuch as it has the same faith in this or that place. All particular churches are parts of the universal church, and indeed visible ones of the visible church, and invisible ones of the invisible church. And it is of this visible universal church that the article of our creed properly speaks: I believe in the holy catholic Church. For this is the church properly marked with the title of being holy, and in it is the true communion of the saints with Christ and all the members.

units.la: Est autem inter visibilem & inuisibilem Ecclesiam idem fere discrimen, quod inter totum & partem. Inuisibilis enim latet in visibili, vt pars in toto: quod etiam ex loco Pauli constat: Quos elegit, hos vocauit. Vocatio autem, qua eos DEVS vocat, est duplex, interna, & externa. Internam Paulus dicit factam secundum propositum electionis: & vtraque vocantur electi, hypocritæ tantum externa. Huius autem externæ vocationis respectu, visibilis Ecclesia dicitur etiam Ecclesia vocatorum, in qua sunt etiam hypocritæ. Inuisibilis vero dicitur Ecclesia electorum.
units.tr: Between the visible and the invisible church there is almost the same distinction as between the whole and the part. For the invisible lies hidden in the visible, as the part in the whole; this also appears from the passage of Paul: Whom he elected, these he also called. The calling by which God calls them is twofold, internal and external. Paul says the internal calling is made according to the purpose of election; and both are called the elect, while the hypocrites have only the external. With respect to this external calling, the visible church is also called the church of the called, in which there are also hypocrites. The invisible church, however, is called the church of the elect.

units.la: Obiect. 1. Si totum est visibile, etiam pars est visibilis, &c. Resp. Est fallacia secundum quid. Totum est visibile, non simpliciter: sed r. quoad homines, quibus foris constat. 2. quoad formam ecclesiasticam, quam foris habet. Et, sic etiam pars est visibilis, in quantum electi etiam sunt homines visibiles, & ecclesiæ visibilis fidem veram profitentur. Sed totum non est visibile, quantum ad hypocritarum in eo simulatam, electorum vero in eo sinceram fidem & regenerationem. Solus enim Dominus novit, qui sint, vel non sint sui.
units.tr: Objection 1. If the whole is visible, the part is also visible, etc. Answer. It is a fallacy of qualification. The whole is visible, not absolutely, but (1) as regards men, who are known outwardly; (2) as regards the ecclesiastical form which it has outwardly. Thus the part too is visible, insofar as the elect are also visible men and profess the true faith of the visible church. But the whole is not visible as regards the feigned faith of the hypocrites in it, or the sincere faith and regeneration of the elect in it. For the Lord alone knows who are his and who are not.

units.la: Obiect. 2. Qui sunt in Ecclesia, non pereunt: vt habet definitio Ecclesiæ. Multi hypocritæ sunt in Ecclesia. Ergo aut hypocritæ non pereunt: aut falsum, quòd, qui sunt in Ecclesia, non pereant.
units.tr: Objection 2. Those who are in the Church do not perish, as the definition of the Church says. Many hypocrites are in the Church. Therefore either the hypocrites do not perish, or it is false that those who are in the Church do not perish.

units.la: Resp. Sunt quatuor termini. Qui sunt in Ecclesia inuisibili, non pereunt: & de his est definitio. Minor loquitur de Ecclesia visibili, in qua sunt multi hypocritæ pereuntes: nulli vero tales sunt in Ecclesia inuisibili.
units.tr: Answer. There are four terms here. Those who are in the invisible Church do not perish, and it is of these that the definition speaks. The minor premise speaks of the visible Church, in which there are many perishing hypocrites; but no such people are in the invisible Church.

units.la: Obiect 3. Vbi non est inuisibilis ecclesia, ibi nec visibilis. In Papatu non fuit inuisibilis Ecclesia: ergo nec visibilis.
units.tr: Objection 3. Where there is no invisible Church, there is no visible Church either. In the Papacy there was no invisible Church; therefore neither was there a visible one.

units.la: Resp. Minor negatur: quia Deus etiam in mediis fœcibus Papatus semper sibi seruauit aliquas reliquias, retinentes fundamentum: alias purius, alias minus pure.
units.tr: Answer. The minor premise is denied, because God, even in the dregs of the Papacy, always preserved for himself some remnants who retained the foundation: some more purely, others less purely.

units.la: Est etiam alia ecclesiæ diuisio, in Ecclesiam veteris & noui Testamenti. Ecclesia veteris Testamenti fuit cœtus amplectens doctrinam Mosis & Prophetarum: & professionem edens, se amplecti in Judæa cærimonias Mosaicas: & eas seruare velle: &tum in Judæa, tum extra eam fide amplecti res illis cærimoniis significatas: hoc est, credens in Messiam exhibendum.
units.tr: There is also another division of the Church, into the Church of the Old and of the New Testament. The Church of the Old Testament was an assembly that embraced the doctrine of Moses and the Prophets, and that made profession that it embraced the Mosaic ceremonies in Judea and wished to observe them, and that, whether in Judea or outside it, embraced by faith the realities signified by those ceremonies; that is, believing in the Messiah who was to be revealed.

units.la: Ecclesia noui Testamenti, non habet hæc discrimina: quia omnes in ea credunt in Messiam exhibitum: & est cœtus amplectens doctrinam Euangelij, vtens sacramentis à Jesu Christo institutis, & in eum exhibitum Messiam credens.
units.tr: The Church of the New Testament does not have these distinctions, because all in it believe in the Messiah who has been revealed. It is an assembly that embraces the doctrine of the Gospel, uses the sacraments instituted by Jesus Christ, and believes in him as the Messiah who has been revealed.

units.la: VI. Quæ sint signa, seu notæ verae Ecclesiæ.
units.tr: VI. What are the signs, or marks, of the true Church?

units.la: Tres sunt notæ verae Ecclesiæ. 1. Professio verae, incorruptæ, & rectè intellectæ doctrinæ legis & euangelij, seu prophetarum & apostolorum. 2. Rectus & legitimus vsus sacramentorum. Nam finis sacramentorum præter alios etiam hic est, vt coetus ecclesiæ ab aliis omnibus sectis & haereticis per ea discernatur. 3. Professio obedientiæ erga doctrinam & ministerium. Hæ notæ continentur in dicto Christi: Euntes docete omnes gentes, baptizantes eos in nomine Patris & Filij, & Spiritus sancti: docentes eos seruare omnia, quæcunque præcepi vobis. Et oportet vt eas teneamus, 1. Propter gloriam Dei, vt discernantur hostes à filiis. 2. Propter nostram salutem; vt possimus veræ ecclesiæ nos adjungere.
units.tr: There are three marks of the true Church. (1) The profession of the true, uncorrupted and rightly understood doctrine of the law and the Gospel, that is, of the Prophets and the Apostles. (2) The right and lawful use of the sacraments; for among other purposes, this is the purpose of the sacraments: that the assembly of the Church may be distinguished by them from all other sects and heretics. (3) The profession of obedience towards the doctrine and the ministry. These marks are contained in the saying of Christ: "Go and teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit, teaching them to observe all things whatsoever I have commanded you" (Matt. 28). And we ought to hold to them: (1) for the glory of God, so that enemies may be distinguished from the sons; (2) for our own salvation, so that we may be able to join ourselves to the true Church.

units.la: Obiect. 1. Omnibus temporibus magni errores fuerunt in ecclesia, priuati vel publici. Resp. Sed 1. retento fundamento: supra quod alij aurum, alij stipulas ædificarunt. 2. Errores in vera Ecclesia non defenduntur: ideo manente fundamento constat hæc nota, quamuis aliquæ stipulæ superstruantur. Cùm verò errores & stipulæ defenduntur, Ecclesia, quantum hoc facit, tantum de veritate sua deperdit.
units.tr: Objection 1. In all times there have been great errors in the Church, private or public. Answer. But (1) the foundation has been retained, upon which some built gold, others straw. (2) Errors are not defended in the true Church; therefore, while the foundation remains, this mark stands, although some straw is built upon it. But when errors and straw are defended, the Church, to the extent that it does this, loses that much of its truth.

units.la: Obiect. 2. In multis ecclesiis veram doctrinam profitentibus, etiam magna aliquando scelera grassantur. Ergo obedientia non potest esse nota verae Ecclesiæ. Resp. 1. Sed & multi sunt in illis, qui obedientiam in doctrina præstant, & præstare student. 2. Omnes obediunt saltem professione, agnoscentes, quòd non debeant defendi peccata: qui verò sceleribus Eccle- siam offendunt, censuris verbi diuini cohercentur. Peccata igi-tur in Ecclesia non defenduntur, sed deplorantur, & legitimè corripiuntur. Proinde obedientia Euangelij propter defectus non cessat esse nota Ecclesiæ. Necesse est autem hanc notam addere: quia alioqui Deum ludibrio haberent, qui quidem doctrinam Christi se recipere, sed nolle secundum eam viuere, dicerent.
units.tr: Objection 2. In many churches that profess the true doctrine, great crimes sometimes also flourish. Therefore obedience cannot be a mark of the true Church. Answer. (1) Indeed, there are many among them who render obedience in doctrine, and strive to render it. (2) All obey at least in profession, acknowledging that sins ought not to be defended; and those who offend the Church by their crimes are restrained by the censures of the divine Word. Sins in the Church, therefore, are not defended but are deplored and lawfully rebuked. Accordingly, the obedience of the Gospel does not cease to be a mark of the Church because of its defects. It is necessary, however, to add this mark, since otherwise they would make a mockery of God, who say indeed that they receive the doctrine of Christ, but are unwilling to live according to it.

units.la: Obiectio 3. Quæ omnes haeretici & schismatici sibi arrogant, ea non sunt notæ verae Ecclesiæ. Haec tria sibi arrogant omnes. Ergo, &c. Respond. Nego maiorem: quia non, an sibi arrogent, sed an habeant, videndum est: alioqui sequeretur etiam bona cœlestia non esse propria Ecclesiæ, quia etiam hæc illi sibi arrogant.
units.tr: Objection 3. Those things which all heretics and schismatics claim for themselves are not marks of the true Church. All claim these three things for themselves. Therefore, etc. Answer. I deny the major premise: for it must be considered not whether they claim these things for themselves, but whether they have them; otherwise it would follow that even the heavenly goods are not proper to the Church, since they too claim these for themselves.

units.la: Obiect. 4. Sine quo non potest consistere Ecclesia, id est, eius nota, sine ordinaria successione ministrorum non potest consistere Ecclesia in mundo. Ergo ordinaria successio est eius nota. Respond. Ordinaria successio in Minore, vt sit vera, intelligatur oportet de successione pastorum in doctrina verbi & sacramen-torum apostolica: quo sensu etiam conclusio non negatur. Talis enim successio sunt illæ ipsæ notæ, quas requirimus: vel certò eas supponit. Aduersarij verò intelligunt ordinariam successionem episcoporum in eodem officio & loco: siue retinuerint illi & rerineant sanam doctrinam apostolicam, siue non: quomodo pastori lapis etiam succedere potuit, & potest. Sic verò nos Assumptionem negamus. Secus enim neque Christus, neque Apostolorum, ac neque Prophetarum quidem Ecclesia fuisset vera Ecclesia.
units.tr: Objection 4. That without which the Church cannot exist, that is, its mark, is the ordinary succession of ministers; without it the Church cannot exist in the world. Therefore the ordinary succession is its mark. Answer. The ordinary succession in the minor premise, to be true, must be understood of the succession of ministers in the doctrine of the Word and the apostolic administration of the sacraments; in this sense the conclusion is not denied. For such a succession is those very marks which we require, or certainly presupposes them. But our opponents understand the ordinary succession of bishops in the same office and place, whether or not they have retained and retain the sound apostolic doctrine; in this way even a stone could succeed a pastor, and could do so. But we deny the assumption in this sense. Otherwise neither the Church of Christ, nor that of the Apostles, nor indeed that of the Prophets, would have been a true Church.

units.la: V. Cur Ecclesia dicatur vna, sancta, & catholica Ecclesia.
units.tr: V. Why the Church is called one, holy, and catholic.

units.la: Ecclesia est vna, non propter cohabitationem, aut rituum, & cæremoniarum identitatem: sed propter suæ doctrinæ & fidei consensum. Sancta: quia sanctificatur à Deo, sanguine & spiritu Christi: vt sit ei conformis: non quidem perfectione; sed 1. Imputatione: quia puritas Christi ei imputatur. 2. Incohatione: quia Spiritus sanctus eam indies magis à sordibus peccati repurgat, vt omnia eius membra, omnes obedientiæ debitæ partes ino-ehoent. 3. Segregatione à mundo: quia sancto cultui est consecrata, & ab impiis extra Ecclesiam separata. Catholica dicitur 1. Ratione locorum: non quia omnia, vel nulla regna mundi possidet (vt de sua catholica Ecclesia Romana gloriatur Antichristus) sed quia sparsa est, vel fuit per totum terrarum orbem, ad nullum certum locum, regnum, certamve successionem alligata. Hoc respectu catholica appellatio cœpit temporibus Apostolorum. Prius enim angustis terminis Ecclesia circumscripta erat. 2. Ratione hominum, quia collecta est ex omnium generum hominibus. 3. Ratione temporum, quia durabit omnibus temporibus in mundo. Ero vobiscum omnibus diebus, usque ad consummationem seculi: quia omnium temporum vna tantum est vera Ecclesia, quæ vnoquoque tempore sic est catholica, vt dispersa sit per totum mundum, nec vnquam sit certo loco alligata.
units.tr: The Church is one, not because of living together in one place or sameness of rites and ceremonies, but because of agreement in its doctrine and faith. It is holy, because it is sanctified by God through the blood and Spirit of Christ, so that it is conformed to him: not indeed in perfection, but (1) by imputation, because the purity of Christ is imputed to it; (2) by inchoation, because the Holy Spirit cleanses it more and more each day from the filth of sin, so that all its members begin to perform the obedience they owe; (3) by separation from the world, because it is consecrated to holy worship and set apart from the ungodly outside the Church. It is called catholic (1) with respect to places: not because it possesses all or none of the kingdoms of the world (as the Antichrist boasts of his Roman Church as catholic), but because it is, or has been, scattered throughout the whole world, bound to no certain place, kingdom, or succession. In this sense the name catholic began in the times of the apostles, for before that the Church was confined within narrow limits. (2) With respect to men, because it is gathered from men of every kind. (3) With respect to times, because it will endure in the world at all times: I am with you always, even to the end of the age. For there is only one true Church of all times, which at every time is so catholic that it is spread through the whole world, and is never bound to a certain place.

units.la: Quod autem vna sit omnium temporum ecclesia inde ab initio ad finem vsque, de eo non est dubitandum. Nam 1. Ecclesiam semper fuisse manifestum est. Nec obijci possunt Abrahami tempora, quasi ante ipsius vocationem nullus fuerit veri Dei cultus in ipsius familia, & post vocationem ipse fuerit solus. Nam & ante vocationem retinuit fundamenta de vero Deo, licet illa fuerint superstitionibus admixtis obscurata. Deinde Melchisedech eodem tempore vixit, qui fuit sacerdos Dei altissimi. Ideo etiam post vocationem Abraham non fuit solus, sed præter eum fuerunt & alij cultores veri Dei, quorum sacerdos fuit Melchisedech. 2. Ecclesiam quoque semper mansuram esse, testatur scriptura: Non recedet verbum meum ab ore tuo, nec ab ore seminis tui. Si nox & dies mutabitur, mutabitur etiam pactum meum. Ego vobiscum sum omnibus diebus, usque ad consummationem seculi. Præterea Christus semper fuit, & erit rex, caput, & sacerdos ecclesiæ: proinde nunquam non ecclesia fuit, & futura est. Unde etiam liquet, Ecclesiam utriusque Testamenti esse unam & eandem: quod etiam articulo sequenti confirmatur. Nam Christus est ecclesiæ sanctificator utriusque Testamenti hominibus communis.
units.tr: That the Church is one, the same from the beginning to the end of time, there is no doubt. For (1) it is plain that the Church has always existed. Nor can the times of Abraham be objected to, as if before his calling there was no true worship of God in his family, and after his calling he alone had it. For even before his calling he retained the foundations concerning the true God, although these had been obscured by superstitions mixed in. Moreover, Melchizedek lived at the same time, and he was the priest of the most high God. Therefore, even after Abraham's calling he was not alone, but besides him there were other worshippers of the true God, of whom Melchizedek was the priest. (2) Scripture also testifies that the Church will always remain: My word shall not depart from your mouth, nor from the mouth of your seed. If day and night change, my covenant too will change. I am with you always, even to the end of the age. Furthermore, Christ always was, and will be, the king, head, and priest of the Church; therefore the Church has never not existed, and will always exist. From this it is also clear that the Church of both Testaments is one and the same, which is confirmed also in the following article. For Christ is the sanctifier of the Church, common to men of both Testaments.

units.la: Quæstio de authoritate ecclesiæ huc pertineret, quam omitto.
units.tr: The question about the authority of the Church belongs here, but I omit it.

units.la: Papistæ dicunt, ecclesiæ authoritatem maiorem esse, quàm scripturæ: sed est falsum. Non enim ecclesia scripturam, sed scriptura Ecclesiam peperit. Objiciunt testimonium Augustini contra epistolam Manichæi cap. 5. vbi exponens, quomodo ad fidem catholicæ ecclesiæ perductus fuerit, dicit, se obtemperasse catholicis dicentibus: Crede Euangelio; ibiq; profert vulgatam illam sententiam: Ego verò Euangelio non crederem, nisi me catholica ecclesiæ commoveret authoritas. Ex ecclesiæ igitur testificatione commotus est, vt legeret Euangelium, & crederet doctrinam patefactam in illo esse veram. Resp. Quid tum? An verò postquam euangelio credidit, pollicetur se plus crediturum ecclesiæ quàm euangelio, si ipsa aliquid statuat vel proponat, quod sit contra euangelium, vel nullo scripturæ testimonio probari possit? Hoc certè noluit Augustinus. Immò alibi anathema dicit iis, qui annunciant aliquid, præterquam quod in scripturis legalibus & euangelicis accepimus. Et in illo ipso loco testatur, se non posse Manichæo credere, propterea quod in euangelio nihil legat de Manichæi apostolatu. Ergo traditiones deducunt nos ad scripturam, & ad vocem in scriptura sancitam nos alligant.
units.tr: The Papists say that the authority of the Church is greater than that of Scripture, but this is false. For it is not the Church that has brought forth Scripture, but Scripture that has brought forth the Church. They object the testimony of Augustine against the letter of Manichaeus, chapter 5, where, explaining how he was brought to the faith of the catholic Church, he says that he obeyed the catholics who said: Believe the Gospel; and there he quotes that well-known saying: But I would not believe the Gospel, unless the authority of the catholic Church moved me. So he was moved by the witness of the Church to read the Gospel and to believe that the doctrine revealed in it was true. Answer. So what? Did Augustine, after he believed the Gospel, promise that he would believe the Church more than the Gospel, if the Church itself set forth or proposed something contrary to the Gospel, or something that could not be proved by any testimony of Scripture? Augustine certainly did not wish this. Indeed, elsewhere he pronounces an anathema on those who announce anything beyond what we have received in the legal and evangelical Scriptures. And in that same passage he testifies that he cannot believe Manichaeus, because he reads nothing in the Gospel about Manichaeus's apostleship. Therefore traditions lead us back to Scripture, and bind us to the word established in Scripture.

units.la: Hic verò obseruandum, quàm candidè agant pontificij. Vbicunque in scriptura occurrit vocabulum traditionis, id mox detorquent ad suas traditiones, quæ ex scriptura probari non possunt. Vt cùm Paulus dicit: Tradidi vobis, quod acceperam: statim exclamat: audis traditiones? Audio; sed mox ibidem lege: Paulum scripto explicare, quæ essent illæ traditiones: Tradidi vobis, quod & accepi, quod Christus mortuus est pro peccatis nostris secundum scripturas, quod sepultus est, & resurrexit, secundum scripturas. Audis hic traditiones Pauli duplici modo esse ἀγράφως. Primò, quia sumtę sunt ex scriptura veteris testamenti. Deinde, quia ab ipso Paulo sunt literis consignatæ. Sic de cœna Domini Paulus inquit: Ego accepi à Domino, quod & tradidi vobis. Sed traditionem hanc post euangelistas ipse etiam scripto comprehendit. Jesuitæ citant dictum Pauli: Subducite vos ab omni fratre ambulante inordinatè, & non secundum traditionem, quam accepit à nobis. Sed mox in eodem capite describit, quam intelligat traditionem, sicut insipienti manifestum est. Et tamen inde volunt probare, multa esse credenda, quæ nullo scripturæ testimonio probari possunt. Eandem impudentiam produnt in alio testimonio ex Luca desumto. Tradebant eis custodienda dogmata, quæ ab apostolis & senioribus Hierosolymitanis decreta fuerant: cùm paulò ante testerutur Lucas, dogmata illa literis fuisse ab Apostolis consignata. Porrò dictum illud vulgatum: Ecclesia non errat, limitate verum est: quod non erret. 1. Tota: etiamsi aliqua membra, etiam multa errent. 2. Universaliter, licet in aliquibus doctrinæ partibus aliquando erret. 3. In fundamento. Intelligantur verò hæc de Ecclesia Christi, non de ecclesia Antichristi.
units.tr: Here we must observe how candidly the Papists deal. Wherever the word tradition occurs in Scripture, they immediately twist it to their own traditions, which cannot be proved from Scripture. So when Paul says: I delivered to you what I had received, they at once cry out: do you hear traditions? I hear them; but read immediately after in the same place how Paul explains in writing what those traditions were: I delivered to you what I also received, that Christ died for our sins according to the Scriptures, that he was buried, and that he rose again according to the Scriptures. Here you hear that Paul's traditions are unwritten [ἀγράφως] in two ways. First, because they were taken from the Scripture of the Old Testament; then, because they were committed to writing by Paul himself. Thus Paul says of the Lord's Supper: I received from the Lord what I also delivered to you. But this tradition he himself also later included in writing, after the evangelists. The Jesuits cite Paul's saying: Withdraw yourselves from every brother who walks disorderly, and not according to the tradition which he received from us. But in the same chapter he soon describes what he means by tradition, so that it is plain even to the foolish. Yet from this they wish to prove that many things must be believed which cannot be proved by any testimony of Scripture. They show the same shamelessness in another testimony taken from Luke: They delivered to them for keeping the decrees which had been decreed by the apostles and the elders of Jerusalem, although Luke had just before testified that those decrees had been committed to writing by the apostles. Moreover, the common saying: The Church does not err, is true only with limitations: that it does not err (1) wholly, even if some members, indeed many, err; (2) universally, although it may sometimes err in some parts of doctrine; (3) in the foundation. But these things are to be understood of the Church of Christ, not of the church of Antichrist.

units.la: V. Quid differat Ecclesia à politia.
units.tr: V. How the Church differs from the state (politia).

units.la: Præcipua discrimina sunt: 1. Politia est cœtus, qui obligatur certis legibus politicis, ad externam disciplinam, secundum utramque tabulam decalogi. Ecclesia est cœtus amplectentium Euangelium, & rectè utentium sacramentis, qui regitur Spiritu & verbo Dei, requirente internam & externam obedientiam. 2. In Ecclesia semper sunt aliqui sancti electi: in politia non semper. 3. Politiæ sunt multæ diversæ, locis, temporibus & legibus distinctæ: nec qui est civis unius, est alterius quoque vel omnium civis, nec est vna aliqua generalis politia, cuius aliæ omnes sunt partes. Ecclesia fuit, est, & erit vna omnibus temporibus & apud omnes: ideò dicitur catholica, habens multas partes. 4. Caput Ecclesiæ vnum & in cœlo est Christus. Politiæ multa, & quidem in terra. 5. Politia habet authoritatem præscribendi leges, quibus etiam propter conscientiam obtemperandum est. Ecclesia est alligata ad verbum Dei, nec habet potestatem condendi novos articulos fidei. Potest quidem instituere ordinem & decorum, sed sine obligatione conscientiarum, idque non authoritate prætoria, sed ex consensu. 6. Politia est armata potentia corporali contra delinquentes, & tuetur leges suas gladio. Ecclesia tantum habet gladium verbi, hoc est, denunciationem iræ Dei adversus contumaces. Aliquando in una & eadem persona concurrunt duo officia, ecclesiasticum & politicum, ut in prophetis & sacerdotibus olim: ideo diligenter discerni debent.
units.tr: The principal differences are these. (1) The state is a body bound by political laws to external discipline, according to both tables of the decalogue. The Church is a body of those who embrace the Gospel and rightly use the sacraments, and it is governed by the Spirit and the Word of God, requiring inward and outward obedience. (2) In the Church there are always some elect saints; in the state there are not always. (3) There are many states, distinguished by place, time and laws; nor is one who is a citizen of one state a citizen of another or of all, nor is there one general state of which all the others are parts. The Church was, is and will be one for all times and among all peoples; therefore it is called catholic, having many parts. (4) The one head of the Church is Christ, who is in heaven; states are many, and indeed on earth. (5) The state has authority to prescribe laws, which must be obeyed even for conscience' sake. The Church is bound to the Word of God and has no power to frame new articles of faith. It can indeed institute order and decency, but without binding consciences, and this not by princely authority but by consent. (6) The state is armed with bodily power against wrongdoers, and it defends its laws with the sword. The Church has only the sword of the Word, that is, the declaration of God's wrath against the obstinate. Sometimes two offices, the ecclesiastical and the civil, meet in one and the same person, as once in the prophets and priests; therefore they must be carefully distinguished.

units.la: VI. Quæ causa discriminis inter Ecclesiam, & reliquum humanum genus.
units.tr: VI. What is the cause of the difference between the Church and the rest of the human race.

units.la: Tria sunt hominum genera in mundo, plurimum inter se diuersa. Alii professione prorsus alieni sunt ab Ecclesia: vt qui negant fidem & pœnitentiam, eoq; sunt professi hostes Dei & ecclesiæ. Alij sunt vocati, sed non efficaciter, vt hypocritæ, profitentes fidem sine vera conuersione ad Deum. Alij deniq; vocati sunt efficaciter, electi videlicet, quorum est minima portio, juxta illud Christi: Multi vocati sunt, pauci electi.
units.tr: There are three kinds of men in the world, very different from one another. Some by profession are wholly alien from the Church, such as those who deny faith and repentance, and so are open enemies of God and the Church. Others are called, but not effectually, such as hypocrites, who profess faith without true conversion to God. Others, finally, are effectually called, namely the elect, who are the smallest portion, according to that saying of Christ: Many are called, but few are chosen.

units.la: Jam quæritur, quæ sit causa huius discriminis? Resp. 1. Discriminis huius causa efficiens est electio Dei volentis sibi colligere ecclesiam in his terris. 2. Filius Dei est huius consilii executor mediatus: Spiritus sanctus immediatus. 3. Verbum Dei est causa instrumentalis. Præteritis ætatibus siuit Deus omnes gentes suis ipsorum viis incedere. Deus cuius vult, miseretur: quem autem vult, indurat. Quicquid dat mihi Pater, ad me veniet. Quos præscivit, eosdem & prædestinauit, vt conformes fiant imagini Filij sui. Quos verò prædestinauit, hos & vocauit, &c. Hoc dicto docemur, promissionem gratiæ esse vniuersalem, respectu electorum seu credentium. Omnes quidem Deus vult saluos fieri, idque 1. Quod ad amorem salutis omnium. 2. Quod ad inuitationem omnium ad salutem. Sed electi tantum assequuti sunt, reliqui obcaluerunt.
units.tr: Now the question is, what is the cause of this difference? Answer: (1) The efficient cause of this difference is the election of God, who willed to gather for himself a church in these lands. (2) The Son of God is the mediate executor of this counsel; the Holy Spirit is the immediate executor. (3) The Word of God is the instrumental cause. In past ages God suffered all nations to walk in their own ways. God has mercy on whom he wills, and whom he wills he hardens. All that the Father gives me will come to me. Whom he foreknew, these he also predestined to be conformed to the image of his Son; and whom he predestined, these he also called, etc. By this saying we are taught that the promise of grace is universal, with respect to the elect or believers. God indeed wills all to be saved, and this (1) as regards his love for the salvation of all, and (2) as regards his invitation of all to salvation. But only the elect have obtained it; the rest were hardened.

units.la: VII. An extra Ecclesiam sit salus.
units.tr: VII. Whether there is salvation outside the Church.

units.la: Nemo extra Ecclesiam potest saluus fieri. 1. Quia extra Ecclesiam nullus est saluator. Ergo nec salus. Sine me nihil potestis facere. 2. Quia quoscunque Deus elegit ad finem, hoc est, ad vitam æternam, eos etiam elegit ad media, hoc est, vocationem internam & externam. Electi igitur etsi non semper sunt membra visibilis ecclesiæ: omnes tamen fiunt, antequam moriantur. Obiect. Ergo electio Dei non est libera. Resp. Est libera: quia libere elegit, & ad finem, & ad media, quos voluit: Miseretur, cuius vult. Postquam elegit, & destinauit ad vtrumque, non mutat decretum. Infantes nati in Ecclesia, sunt etiam de Ecclesia: contra anabaptistas.
units.tr: No one can be saved outside the Church. (1) Because outside the Church there is no saviour. Therefore neither is there salvation. Without me you can do nothing. (2) Because whomsoever God has elected to the end, that is, to eternal life, those he has also elected to the means, that is, internal and external calling. Therefore the elect, although they are not always visible members of the Church, nevertheless all become such before they die. Objection: Then God's election is not free. Answer: It is free, because he freely elected whom he willed, both to the end and to the means: he has mercy on whom he wills. Once he has elected and destined them to both, he does not change the decree. Infants born in the Church are also of the Church; against the Anabaptists.

units.la: Quid igitur est, Credere Ecclesiam sanctam catholicam? Est credere semper fuisse, & esse, & fore, talem ecclesiam in mundo, & in coetu visibili Ecclesiæ semper esse aliquos vere credentes, & me ex horum numero esse, proinde & esse viuum & invisibilis & visibilis Ecclesiæ membrum, ac perpetuò mansurum.
units.tr: What then is it to believe the holy catholic Church? It is to believe that such a Church has always been, is, and will be in the world, and that in the visible assembly of the Church there are always some who truly believe, and that I am of their number, and therefore a living and invisible and visible member of the Church, and that I shall remain so forever.

units.la: DE ÆTERNA PRÆDESTI-NATIONE Dei.
units.tr: On the Eternal Predestination of God.

units.la: Locus hic de æterna Dei prædestinatione, seu de electione & reprobatione oritur ex loco de ecclesia: ideo rectè cum illo conjungitur. Quæstiones præcipuæ sunt: I. An sit prædestinatio. II. Quid sit. III. Qua eius causa. IV. Qua effecta. V. An sit immutabilis. VI. Quatenus sit nobis nota. VII. An electi semper sint membra Ecclesiæ. VIII. An electi deficiant ab Ecclesia. IX. Quis sit visus huius doctrinæ.
units.tr: This locus, concerning the eternal predestination of God, or election and reprobation, arises from the locus on the Church, and so is rightly joined to it. The principal questions are: I. Whether there is predestination. II. What it is. III. What its cause is. IV. What its effect is. V. Whether it is unchangeable. VI. How far it is known to us. VII. Whether the elect are always members of the Church. VIII. Whether the elect can fall away from the Church. IX. What has been the view of this doctrine.

units.la: I. An sit prædestinatio.
units.tr: I. Whether there is predestination.

units.la: Cùm quæritur, an sit prædestinatio, hoc quæritur: an sit aliquod consilium Dei, quo ab æterno discreverit saluandos à non saluandis. Nonnulli dicunt, electionem, cùm eius fit mentio in scripturis, significare præstantiam, propter quam aliquis sit dignus, vt eligatur: sicut equus egregius dicitur electus, aurum sincerum dicitur electum. Sic & reprobationem interpretantur, sed falsò. Est enim æternum Dei consilium.
units.tr: When it is asked whether there is predestination, the question is whether there is some counsel of God by which, from eternity, he distinguished those to be saved from those not to be saved. Some say that election, whenever it is mentioned in the Scriptures, signifies an excellence on account of which someone is worthy to be chosen, just as an outstanding horse is called chosen, or pure gold is called chosen. They interpret reprobation in the same way, but wrongly. For it is an eternal counsel of God.

units.la: Esse igitur prædestinationem, hoc est, electionem & reprobationem in Deo, probant hæc scripturæ testimonia: Multi sunt vocati, pauci electi. Non vos me elegistis, sed ego elegi vos. Alias oves habeo, quae non sunt ex ovili hoc. Elegit nos in Christo, antequam jacerentur fundamenta mundi. Prædestinauit nos, quos adoptaret in filios, per Iesum Christum in sese, pro beneuolo affectu voluntatis sua. Populus mihi multus est in hac urbe. Et crediderunt, quotquot erant ordinati ad vitam æternam. Quos prædestinauit, hos & vocauit. De reprobatione speciatim loquuntur hæc dicta: Deus volens ostendere iram, & notam facere potentiam suam, pertulit multa lenitate vasa irae, coagmentata ad interitum. Iacob dilexi, Esau odio habui. Vobis datum est nosse mysteria regni &c. illis autem non est datum. In hoc judicium iam olim descripti. Confitebor tibi, Pater, Domine cœli & terræ, quod abscondethe hæc à sapientibus & intelligentibus, & revelasti ea infantibus: Etiam Pater, quia sic placuit tibi.
