Sed abluti estis, sed sanctificati estis, sed justificati estis in nomine Domini Iesu, & per Spiritum Dei nostri. Item ex eo, quod dicimur per baptismum cum Christo mori, & sepeliri, exuere corpus carnis peccatricis, Christum induere, &c. Utriusque ablutionis seu remissionis peccatorum, & regenerationis symbolum est baptismus: non tantum, quia similitudinem cum utroque beneficio habet: sed etiam, quia ista duo beneficia perpetuò coniuncta sunt, & neutrum potest esse sine altero. Nisi enim Christus nos abluerit, non habemus partem cum eo: & qui Spiritum Christi non habet, non est eius. Differunt autem justificatio, quæ fit sanguine Christi: & regeneratio, quæ fit Spiritu Christi: quod justificatio fit perfectè in hac vita, imputatione, sicut dicitur: Nulla est condemnatio iis, qui sunt in Christo Iesu. Regeneratio verò & mutatio naturæ prauæ in bonam, in hac vita non fit perfectè, sed tantum inchoatione: sic tamen, ut initium eius verè sit in omnibus piis, & sentiatur in omnibus conuersis, dum adhuc sunt in hac vita: quia omnes pij verè habent in voluntate & corde studium obediendi Deo: ita, ut maximè doleant propter reliquos defectus.
units.tr: That baptism signifies this twofold washing from sins is clear from what has been said: John preached the baptism of repentance for the remission of sins. But you have been washed, you have been sanctified, you have been justified in the name of the Lord Jesus and by the Spirit of our God. It is also clear from the fact that through baptism we are said to die and be buried with Christ, to put off the body of sinful flesh, to put on Christ, and so on. Baptism is the sign and seal of both the washing, that is, the forgiveness of sins, and the regeneration. It is so not only because it resembles both benefits, but also because these two benefits are always joined, and neither can exist without the other. For unless Christ has washed us, we have no part in him, and whoever does not have the Spirit of Christ is not his. Justification, which comes through the blood of Christ, and regeneration, which comes through the Spirit of Christ, do differ. Justification is made perfect in this life by imputation, as it is said: There is no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus. Regeneration, however, and the change of a corrupt nature into a good one, is not made perfect in this life but only begun. Yet its beginning is truly in all the godly and is felt in all who are converted, while they are still in this life, because all the godly truly have in their will and heart a zeal to obey God, so that they grieve most of all over their remaining failings.

units.la: QVÆSTIO LXXI. Vbi promisit Christus, se nos tam certo sanguine & Spiritu suo abluturum, quàm aquâ baptismi abluti sumus?
units.tr: QUESTION 71. Where did Christ promise that he would cleanse us by his blood and Spirit as surely as we are washed with the water of baptism?

units.la: RESPONSIO.
units.tr: ANSWER.

units.la: In institutione baptismi, cuius hæc sunt verba: Ite & docete omnes gentes, baptizantes eos in nomine Patris, & Filij, & Spiritus sancti. Qui crediderit & baptizatus fuerit, seruabitur: qui verò non crediderit, condemnabitur a. Hæc promissio repetitur, cùm scriptura baptismum nominat lauacrum regenerationis b, & ablutionem peccatorum c.
units.tr: In the institution of baptism, whose words are: "Go and teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. He who believes and is baptized will be saved; but he who does not believe will be condemned" a. This promise is repeated where Scripture calls baptism "the washing of regeneration" b and "the washing away of sins" c.

units.la: a Matth. 28,19. Marci 16,16. b Tit. 3,5. c Actor. 22,16.
units.tr: a Matt. 28:19. Mark 16:16. b Titus 3:5. c Acts 22:16.

units.la: EXPLICATIO.
units.tr: EXPLANATION.

units.la: Probatio definitionis, & præcipuorum finium baptismi, continetur verbis institutionis, quæ leguntur apud Matthæum & Marcum: Profecti docete omnes gentes, baptizantes eos in nomine Patris, & Filij, & Spiritus sancti. Qui crediderit & baptizatus fuerit, seruabitur, qui verò non crediderit condemnabitur. Hæc paucis explicanda sunt.
units.tr: The proof of the definition and of the chief ends of baptism is contained in the words of institution, which are read in Matthew and Mark: "Go, teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. He who believes and is baptized will be saved; he who does not believe will be condemned." These words must be explained briefly.

units.la: Profecti docete omnes gentes. Omnes, inquit, non aliquas tantum gentes docete, neq; tantum posteros Abrahami. Hic igitur Christus sustulit maceriem, quæ hactenus Iudæos ab omnibus aliis gentibus separauerat, & constituit discrimen sacramentorum veteris & noui Testamenti. Vetera enim solis Iudæis erant instituta: hoc nouum sacramentum Iudæis simul & gentibus omnibus Christus instituit.
units.tr: "Go, teach all nations." All, he says, not only some nations, nor only the descendants of Abraham. Here, then, Christ removed the wall which had hitherto separated the Jews from all other nations, and he established a distinction between the sacraments of the Old and New Testaments. For the old rites were instituted for the Jews alone; Christ instituted this new sacrament for the Jews and for all nations at once.

units.la: Baptizantes eos. Omnes nempe, qui vestra doctrina ad me accedunt, meiq; fient discipuli. Inter eos autem etiam numerandi sunt infantes accedentium ad Christum, seu discipulorum Christi. Nam & hi sunt Christi discipuli, nati in schola Christi. Nascitur enim in ecclesia, est infantibus loco professionis. Notandus est hic ordo. Iubet prius eos doceri, postea baptizari: quia loquitur de adultis conuertendis, & significat sacramenta non debere esse muta, sed addendam esse doctrinam, & quidem verbum debere præcedere, sacramenta sequi in adultis.
units.tr: "Baptizing them." Namely, all who come to me through your teaching and become my disciples. Among these must also be counted the infants of those who come to Christ, or of Christ's disciples. For they too are disciples of Christ, born in the school of Christ. For an infant is born in the Church, and birth serves infants in place of profession. The order here is to be noted: he commands that they be taught first and baptized afterwards, because he is speaking of adults who are to be converted, and he signifies that sacraments ought not to be mute, but that teaching must be added; indeed, in adults the word must go before and the sacraments follow.

units.la: In nomine Patris, & Filij, & Spiritus sancti. pro eodem sumuntur. Significat autem tutum i. iussu & authoritate communi horum trium institutum tutum esse baptismum, atque has tres personas mandare, vt qui velint esse membra ecclesiae, illi sic baptizentur. Idem ergo valet, quando minister baptizat, ac si Deus Pater, & Filius, & Spiritus sanctus baptizaret. Vnde porro liquet, hos tres esse tria ὑφιστάμενα diuina & ὁμοούσια, hoc est, tres personas eiusdem diuinitatis, & vnum verum Deum, in quem baptizamur. 2. Testificatione hac nobis has tres personas confirmare, quod ipsae nos in gratiam recipiant, & nobis verè praestent beneficia, quae baptismo significantur, si crediderimus. Et hic notatur principalis finis baptismi. 3. Baptizari in nomine patris, filij, & spiritus sancti, est baptizatum obligari ad agnitionem, fidem, cultum, fiduciam, honorem & invocationem huius veri Dei, qui est Pater, Filius & Spiritus sanctus. Et hic est secundus baptismi finis, quem & Paulus his verbis indicat: Num in nomen Pauli baptizati estis? quasi dicat, illius debetis esse, cui in baptismo nomen dedistis, & vos obligastis.
units.tr: "In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit." The words "in the name of" are taken here as equivalent to "by the authority of." It signifies that baptism is instituted by the command and common authority of these three, and that these three persons enjoin that those who wish to be members of the Church be baptized in this way. Therefore, when a minister baptizes, it is the same as if God the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit were baptizing. From this it further appears that these three are three divine subsistences [ὑφιστάμενα] and consubstantial [ὁμοούσια], that is, three persons of the same divinity, and one true God, into whom we are baptized. (2) By this testimony these three persons confirm to us that they themselves receive us into grace, and truly bestow on us the benefits which are signified by baptism, if we believe. And here the principal end of baptism is noted. (3) To be baptized in the name of the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit is for the one baptized to be bound to acknowledge, believe, worship, trust in, honour and call upon this true God, who is Father, Son and Holy Spirit. And this is the second end of baptism, which Paul also indicates in these words: "Were you baptized in the name of Paul?" as if he said: you ought to belong to him whose name you received in baptism, and to whom you bound yourselves.

units.la: Qui crediderit. Promissioni additur conditio fidei. Nam qui baptizantur, non nisi fide possunt percipere, quod baptismo promittitur & obsignatur, adeo vt sine fide nec promissio sit rata, nec baptismus prosit. Atque his verbis notatur breviter vsus baptismi legitimus, in quo legitimo vsu sacramenta sunt sacramenta, & sunt rata iis, qui ex vera fide accipiunt. In vsu autem illegitimo sacramenta non sunt sacramenta, nec prosunt.
units.tr: "He who believes." A condition of faith is added to the promise. For those who are baptized cannot receive what is promised and sealed in baptism except by faith; so much so that without faith the promise is not valid, nor does baptism profit. In these words the lawful use of baptism is briefly noted, and in this lawful use the sacraments are sacraments and are effective for those who receive them from true faith. In an unlawful use, however, the sacraments are not sacraments, nor do they profit.

units.la: Vsus igitur legitimus baptismi est: quando baptizantur conuersi, ritu & sine instituto, hoc est, 1. Quando non mutantur caeremoniae & ritus à Deo instituti in baptismo. Vnde manifestum est, abiiciendas esse sordes pontificias chrismatis, sputi, exorcismos, cereos, sal, & similes, quibus baptismum conspurcant. Sed haec, inquiunt, pertinent ad ordinem & decorum. Respond. Spiritus sanctus satis intellexit, quid ad ordinē & decorum baptismi faceret. At habent significationem & mysteria. Respon. Hominum non est, instituere mysteria, & signa voluntatis Dei. Idem de aliis huius farinae caeremoniis iudicandum est. 2. Quando baptismus confertur iis, quibus est institutus, nimirum conuersis & ecclesiae membris: & quando ab his vera fide accipitur, iuxta illud: Licet tibi baptizari, si credis toto corde. 3. Quando baptismus in eum finem vsurpatur, in quem est institutus, non ad curationem pecudum, consecrationem campanarum, vel similes abusus. His additur 4. vt baptismus administretur ab iis, quibus id Christus praecepit, hoc est, ministris ecclesiae, quos Christus misit ad docendum & baptizandum: non à mulieribus, aut aliis, quia à Deo non sunt missi, & nomine Dei nihil stipulari possunt. Et baptizatus fuerit. Christus etiam signo nos vult confirmare. Addit igitur hoc: & baptizatus fuerit, vt non tantum ex fide, sed etiam ex symbolo certissimus, nos esse è numero seruandorum.
units.tr: The lawful use of baptism, therefore, is when converts are baptized according to the rite and without addition, that is, (1) when the ceremonies and rites instituted by God in baptism are not changed. Hence it is clear that the papist filth of chrism, spittle, exorcisms, candles, salt and the like, by which they defile baptism, must be cast away. "But," they say, "these pertain to order and decorum." Answer: The Holy Spirit understood well enough what would serve the order and decorum of baptism. "But they have significance and mysteries." Answer: It is not for men to institute mysteries and signs of the will of God. The same judgment must be made of the other ceremonies of this sort. (2) When baptism is conferred on those for whom it was instituted, namely converts and members of the Church, and when it is received by them in true faith, according to that saying: "You may be baptized, if you believe with all your heart." (3) When baptism is used for the end for which it was instituted, and not for the healing of cattle, the consecration of bells, or similar abuses. To these is added (4) that baptism be administered by those whom Christ commanded to do so, that is, by the ministers of the Church whom Christ sent to teach and baptize; not by women or others, because they have not been sent by God and can make no covenant in the name of God. "And is baptized." Christ wills also to confirm us by a sign. He therefore adds this: and is baptized, so that we may be most certain, not only from faith but also from the symbol, that we are among those who are to be saved.

units.la: Seruabitur. Id est, baptizatus sciat, se habere beneficia, quae ritu significantur, hoc est, se iustificari & regenerari, si credat. Nam sine fide promissio non est rata, nec baptismus prodest. Vtriq; & fidei & baptismo additur promissio salutis, sed diuerso modo: fidei, tanquam medio necessario ad accipiendam salutem: baptismo, tanquam signo obsignanti acceptam salutem.
units.tr: "Will be saved." That is, let the one baptized know that he has the benefits which are signified by the rite, that is, that he is justified and regenerated, if he believes. For without faith the promise is not valid, nor does baptism profit. To both faith and baptism the promise of salvation is added, but in different ways: to faith as the necessary means of receiving salvation; to baptism as a sign sealing the salvation received.

units.la: Qui non crediderit, condemnabitur. Etiamsi baptizatus fuerit. Visus enim sacramenti sine fide non seruat: sicut priuatio sacramenti non damnat, si non accedat contemtus. Contemtus enim sacramenti non minus, quàm verbi, damnat: quia contemtus non potest esse cum fide. Atque hinc est, quod Christus in antithesi promissionis non retinet vtrumque membrum subiecti: Qui non crediderit, & baptizatus fuerit: quoniam non est eadem necessitas fidei & baptismi ad salutem. Fides simpliciter necessaria est ad salutem, necessitate medij, adeo vt sine ea nemo seruari possit: Sine fide enim impossibile est Deo placere. Sacramenta autem sunt necessaria necessitate praecepti, quando haberi possunt secundum institutionem diuinam. Haec est ratio, cur Christus cum discrimine salutem promittat credentibus & baptizatis: non admat vero salutem iis, quibus adimitur baptismus.
units.tr: "He who does not believe will be condemned." Even if he has been baptized. For the mere sight of the sacrament without faith does not save; just as the lack of the sacrament does not condemn, if contempt is not added. For contempt of the sacrament condemns no less than contempt of the word, because contempt cannot exist together with faith. And hence it is that Christ, in setting the promise against the threat, does not keep both parts of the subject: "He who does not believe and is baptized"; since faith and baptism are not equally necessary for salvation. Faith is simply necessary for salvation, by the necessity of means, so that no one can be saved without it: "For without faith it is impossible to please God." The sacraments, however, are necessary by the necessity of precept, when they can be had according to the divine institution. This is the reason why Christ promises salvation with a distinction to those who believe and are baptized, but does not likewise promise salvation to those from whom baptism is withheld.

units.la: QVAESTIO LXXII.
units.tr: QUESTION LXXII.

units.la: Estne ergo externus baptismus aquae ipsa peccatorum ablutio? RESPONSIO.
units.tr: Is external baptism with water therefore itself the washing away of sins? ANSWER.

units.la: Non est. a Nam solus sanguis Christi purgat nos ab omni peccato b.
units.tr: No. a For only the blood of Christ cleanses us from all sin b.

units.la: EXPLICATIO.
units.tr: EXPLANATION.

units.la: Sicut de totogenere sacramentorum verum est, locutiones de illis alias esse proprias, alias improprias, quas vocant sacramentales: sic etiam de baptismo formae loquendi sunt duplices, propriae & impropriae. Propriae sunt: 1. Cum accipientes signum dicuntur accipere rem significatam, vt: Qui crediderit, & baptizatus fuerit, salvus erit. 2. Cum signum dicitur significare rem, vt: Baptismus est signum ablutionis peccatorum. Dedit eis cir- cumcisione signum fœderis. Impropria seu figurata sunt: 1. Cùm signum dicitur esse res ipsa: vt, Baptismus est lauacrum regenerationis. 2. Cùm sacramentum dicitur conferre rem, aut ea, quæ sunt rei: vt, Baptismus nos saluos facit. Tres posteriores æquipollent prò-missioni: Qui crediderit, & baptizatus fuerit, saluus erit. Omnes autem habent hanc vnam sententiam: Baptismus est certum signum remissionis peccatorum & æternæ salutis credentibus. Nam figuratæ locutiones de sacramentis interpretandæ sunt, sicut locutiones figuratæ de sacrificiis. Sacrificia sæpissimè dicuntur expiatio peccatorum: & tamen Apostolus affirmat, sanguinem hircorum & taurorum non potuisse expiare peccata. Sic cùm dicitur: Baptismus nos saluat: est lauacrum regenerationis: est 1 Pet.3,21. ablutio peccatorum, idem est, ac si dicatur: Baptismus est signum horum omnium.
units.tr: Just as it is true of the whole class of sacraments that some ways of speaking about them are proper and others improper, which they call sacramental, so also with baptism there are two kinds of forms of speech, proper and improper. The proper ones are: 1. When those who receive the sign are said to receive the thing signified, as: He who believes and is baptized will be saved. 2. When the sign is said to signify the thing, as: Baptism is a sign of the washing away of sins. He gave them the sign of the covenant in circumcision. The improper or figurative ones are: 1. When the sign is said to be the thing itself, as: Baptism is the washing of regeneration. 2. When the sacrament is said to confer the thing, or the things that belong to the thing, as: Baptism saves us. The last three are equivalent to the promise: He who believes and is baptized will be saved. All of them, however, carry this one meaning: baptism is a sure sign of the forgiveness of sins and of eternal salvation to believers. For figurative expressions about sacraments must be interpreted in the same way as figurative expressions about sacrifices. Sacrifices are very often said to be the expiation of sins, and yet the Apostle affirms that the blood of goats and bulls could not expiate sins. So when it is said: Baptism saves us: it is the washing of regeneration: it is 1 Pet. 3,21 the washing away of sins, it is the same as if it were said: baptism is a sign of all these things.

units.la: QVÆSTIO LXXIII.
units.tr: Question 73.

units.la: Cur ergo Spiritus sanctus Baptismum appellat lauacrum regenerationis, & ablutionem peccatorum? RESPONSIO.
units.tr: Why then does the Holy Spirit call baptism "the washing of regeneration" and "the cleansing of sins"? ANSWER.

units.la: Deus non sine causa sic loquitur: videlicet, non solum, vt nos doceat, quemadmodum sordes corporis aquâ purgantur, sic peccata nostra sanguine & Spiritu Christi lauari a: Verum multo magis, vt nobis hoc divino symbolo ac pignore certum faciat, nos non minus verè à peccatis nostris interna lotione ablui, quàm externa & visibili aquâ abluti sumus b.
units.tr: God does not speak this way without cause. He wishes, first, to teach us that just as the filth of the body is washed away by water, so our sins are washed away by the blood and Spirit of Christ a. Much more, however, He wishes by this divine sign and pledge to assure us that we are washed from our sins by an inward cleansing no less truly than we are washed by outward and visible water b.

units.la: EXPLICATIO.
units.tr: EXPLANATION.

units.la: Cur scriptura sic loquatur, nomina signorum & rerum permutans, tres sunt causæ. 1. Analogia signi & rei significatæ. Tale enim quiddam est res significata in suo genere, quale quiddam est signum in suo genere, & contra. Vt enim aqua, hoc est, signum abluit sordes: sic sanguis & Spiritus Christi, hoc est, res significata abluit peccata: & sicut signum externè confertur à ministro: sic Deus internè, virtute sui Spiritus, rem signatam vult conferre iis, qui signum vera fide percipiunt. Vt enim ministri agunt foris, ita Deus agit intus. 2. Obsignatio rei per signum: seu conconfirmatio fidei in nobis per vsum signi. Signa enim testantur voluntatem Dei erga nos, propter promissionem additam, qua-lis est haec: Qui crediderit, & baptizatus fuerit, saluus erit. Sed quare ad confirmationem sic loquitur? Quia in vsu legitimo est coniuncta exhibitio & perceptio signorum & rerum. Vt ita-que doceat nos, quid det: & confirmet, quod dat: permutat nomina, quod rei est, tribuens signo, vel contra. Haec igitur est tertia causa ex superiore pendens, coniuncta nimirum cum signis exhibitio rerum.
units.tr: There are three reasons why Scripture speaks in this way, interchanging the names of signs and things. (1) The analogy between the sign and the thing signified. For the thing signified is, in its own kind, of the same sort as the sign is in its kind, and the reverse. Just as water, that is, the sign, washes away filth, so the blood and Spirit of Christ, that is, the thing signified, wash away sins. And just as the sign is conferred externally by the minister, so God confers the thing signified inwardly, by the power of His Spirit, on those who receive the sign with true faith. For as the ministers act outwardly, so God acts inwardly. (2) The sealing of the thing by the sign, or the strengthening of faith in us through the use of the sign. For signs attest God's will towards us, on account of the promise added, such as this: Whoever believes and is baptized will be saved. But why does Scripture speak thus for the sake of confirmation? Because in lawful use the exhibition and reception of the signs and of the things are joined together. So that it may teach us what God gives and confirm what He gives, it interchanges the names, ascribing to the sign what belongs to the thing, or the reverse. This, then, is the third reason, depending on the above: namely, the exhibition of the things joined with the signs.

units.la: QVÆSTIO LXXIV. Suntne etiam infantes baptizandi?
units.tr: QUESTION 74. Are infants also to be baptized?

units.la: RESPONSIO.
units.tr: ANSWER.

units.la: Omnino. Nam cùm æquè ac adulti ad fœdus & Ec-clesiam Dei pertineant a: cumque eis per sanguinem Christi, remissio peccatorum b, & Spiritus sanctus, fidei effector, non minus quàm adultis promittatur c: per baptismum Ecclesiæ Dei inserendi, & ab infidelium li-beris discernendi d: itidem vt in veteri fœdere per cir-cumcisionem fiebat e, cui in nouo fœdere substitutus est Baptismus f.
units.tr: Certainly. For since they belong to the covenant and the Church of God just as adults do a, and since remission of sins through the blood of Christ b, and the Holy Spirit, the author of faith, are promised to them no less than to adults c, they are to be admitted to the Church of God by baptism and distinguished from the children of unbelievers d. Likewise, as in the Old Covenant this was done by circumcision e, for which baptism has been substituted in the New Covenant f.

units.la: a Genef. 17. verf. 7. b Matth. 19, 14. c Luc. 1, 14.15. Psalm. 22, 11. Esa. 44, 1.2.3. Actor. 2, 39. d Actor. 10, 47. e Genes. 17, 14. f Coloss. 2, verf. 11, 12, 13.
units.tr: a Genef. 17. verf. 7. b Matth. 19, 14. c Luc. 1, 14.15. Psalm. 22, 11. Esa. 44, 1.2.3. Actor. 2, 39. d Actor. 10, 47. e Genes. 17, 14. f Coloss. 2, verf. 11, 12, 13.

units.la: EXPLICATIO.
units.tr: EXPLANATION.

units.la: Ad hanc quaestionem intelligendam obseruetur thesis, Qui debeant baptizari, & qui debeant petere baptismum. Qui non-dum sunt discipuli Christi, hoc est, ex numero vocatorum, non consentientes de doctrina, nec obedientes ministerio, non sunt admittendi ad baptismum. Qui sentiunt, se nondum esse discipulos Christi, non debent petere baptismum. Ratio vtriusque est: quia Christus dicit primo: Μαθητεύσατε πάντα τὰ ἔθνη: Facite mihi discipulos omnes gentes: & deinde eos baptizari præcipit. Vnde omnes ijque soli sunt baptizandi ex Christi mandato, qui sunt Christi discipuli, hoc est, qui sunt, & haberi debent membra visi-bilis Ecclesiæ, siue ij sint adulti profitentes fidem & pœniten-tiam, siue infantes in Ecclesia nati. Omnes enim fidelium liberi sunt in fœdere, & in Ecclesia Dei, nisi ipsi se excludant. Proinde etiam sunt discipuli Christi: quia nati sunt in ecclesia hoc est, in schola Christi: ideo eos etiam docet Spiritus sanctus pro ipsorum captu & ætatis modo.
units.tr: To understand this question, the following thesis should be noted: who ought to be baptized, and who ought to request baptism. Those who are not yet disciples of Christ, that is, not among those called, who do not agree with the doctrine nor obey the ministry, are not to be admitted to baptism. Those who perceive that they are not yet disciples of Christ ought not to request baptism. The reason for both is this: Christ says first, Μαθητεύσατε πάντα τὰ ἔθνη [Make disciples of all nations], and then commands that they be baptized. Hence all, and only those, are to be baptized by Christ's command who are Christ's disciples, that is, who are, and ought to be regarded as, members of the visible Church, whether they are adults professing faith and repentance or infants born in the Church. For all the children of believers are in the covenant and in the Church of God, unless they exclude themselves. Therefore they too are disciples of Christ, because they are born in the Church, that is, in the school of Christ; and so the Holy Spirit teaches them too, according to their capacity and age.

units.la: Hinc facile judicatur de hypothesi: an infantes baptizandi. Si enim sunt discipuli Christi, & de ecclesia, sunt baptizandi. Atqui illud. Ergo & hoc. Maior patet ex mandato Christi. Minor est manifestissima ex formula fœderis, & aliis locis. Rationes verò, quibus in catechesi probatur, infantes esse baptizandos, sunt quatuor.
units.tr: Hence it is easily judged by the hypothesis whether infants are to be baptized. For if they are disciples of Christ and of the Church, they are to be baptized. But that is so; therefore this also is so. The major premise is evident from Christ's command. The minor premise is most evident from the formula of the covenant and from other passages. The reasons by which it is proved in the catechism that infants are to be baptized are four.

units.la: Prima. Omnes pertinentes ad fœdus, & ecclesiam Dei, sunt baptizandi. Infantes Christianorum æquè ac adulti pertinent ad fœdus, & ecclesiam Dei. Infantes igitur Christianorum æquè ac adulti sunt baptizandi. Maior probatur: quia tota Ecclesia debet baptizari, juxta præceptum Christi: Profecti docete omnes Gentes, & baptizate eos, &c. & dictum Pauli: Per unum spiritum omnes in unum corpus baptizati sumus. Minor patet ex formula fœderis: Ero Deus tuus, & seminis tui. & ex Christi mandato: Sinite pueruulos ad me venire: quia talium est regnum Dei.
units.tr: First. All who belong to the covenant and the Church of God are to be baptized. The infants of Christians, just as much as adults, belong to the covenant and the Church of God. Therefore the infants of Christians, just as much as adults, are to be baptized. The major premise is proved: because the whole Church ought to be baptized, according to Christ's precept: Go and teach all nations, and baptize them, etc., and Paul's saying: By one Spirit we were all baptized into one body. The minor premise is evident from the formula of the covenant: I will be your God and the God of your seed, and from Christ's command: Suffer the little children to come to me, for of such is the kingdom of God.

units.la: Secunda. Ad quos pertinet beneficium remissionis peccatorum & regenerationis, ij non possunt arceri à baptismo. Ad infantes Ecclesiæ pertinet beneficium remissionis peccatorum & regenerationis, hoc est, infantibus æquè ac adultis remissio peccatorum per sanguinem Christi, & Spiritus sanctus fidei effector promittitur. Ergo infantes Christianorum debent baptizari. Maior confirmatur verbis Petri: Resipiscite, & baptizetur unusquisque vestrum in nomine Iesu Christi. Vobis enim facta est promissio & liberis vestris. Item: Num quis potest aquam prohibere, quo minus baptizentur isti, qui Spiritum sanctum acceperunt, sicut & nos?
units.tr: Second. Those to whom the benefit of the remission of sins and of regeneration belongs cannot be kept from baptism. To the infants of the Church belongs the benefit of the remission of sins and of regeneration; that is, remission of sins through the blood of Christ and the Holy Spirit, the author of faith, are promised to infants no less than to adults. Therefore the infants of Christians ought to be baptized. The major premise is confirmed by Peter's words: Repent, and let each of you be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ. For the promise is made to you and to your children. Likewise: Can anyone forbid water, so that these who have received the Holy Spirit, as we have, should not be baptized?

units.la: Probatur etiam evidenti ratione. Quibus debentur res significatæ, iis etiam symbolum debetur, nisi obstet aliqua conditio in modo utendi: vel, nisi sit aliqua circumstantia in institutione expressa, impediens usum ritus: ut olim sexus excludebat fœmellas à circumcisione, & hodie annunciatio mortis Domini, & probatio sui excludit infantes à cœna. Minor patet ex formula fœderis: Ero Deus tuus & seminis tui. Et ex promissione: Sinite parvulos ad me venire: quia talium est regnum Dei. Item ex dictis: Vobis & liberis vestris facta est promissio. Vos estis filii Prophetarum, & pacti quod pepigit Deus erga Patres vestros. Liberi vestri sancti sunt. Si radix sancta est, etiam rami sancti sunt. Sic baptista Iohannes sanctificatus fuit in utero. Qui hæc testimonia scripturæ diligenter expendet, videbit, non tantum licere, sed etiam debere infantibus baptismum conferri. Sunt enim sancti: ipsis facta est promissio: eorum est regnum Dei: & Deus se cose eorum quoque Deum esse dicit, qui certè non est extraneorum Deus. Necest vlla conditio in infantibus impediens vsum baptismi. Quis igitur aquam prohibere potest, quominus baptizentur isti, qui eorundem beneficiorum cum tota Ecclesia sunt participes?
units.tr: This is also proved by a clear reason. To those to whom the things signified are due, the sign is also due, unless some condition in the manner of use stands in the way, or unless there is some circumstance expressed in the institution that prevents the use of the rite; as formerly sex excluded females from circumcision, and today the proclamation of the Lord's death and self-examination exclude infants from the Supper. The minor premise is evident from the formula of the covenant: I will be your God and the God of your seed. And from the promise: Suffer the little children to come to me, for of such is the kingdom of God. Likewise from the sayings: The promise is made to you and to your children. You are the sons of the prophets, and of the covenant which God made with your fathers. Your children are holy. If the root is holy, the branches are holy too. So John the Baptist was sanctified in the womb. Whoever weighs these testimonies of Scripture diligently will see that baptism may not only lawfully, but ought to be conferred on infants. For they are holy; the promise is made to them; theirs is the kingdom of God; and God says that He is also the God of their seed, who is certainly not the God of strangers. Nor is there any condition in infants that hinders the use of baptism. Who then can forbid water, so that these should not be baptized, who with the whole Church are partakers of the same benefits?

units.la: Tertia. Sacramentum, quod à Deo in hunc finem est institutum, vt sit solemnis receptio in Ecclesiam, & discretio eius ab omnibus aliis sectis, debet communicari omnibus ætatibus, ad quas fœdus&receptio in ecclesiam,&discretio pertinet. Baptismus est tale sacramentum. Ergo debet omnibus ætatibus, proinde & infantibus tribui. Valet consequentia, à propria causa finali ad effectum. Quibus enim causa finalis conuenit, iisdem effectus recte & necessariò tribuitur.
units.tr: Third. The sacrament which God instituted for this end, that it might be the solemn reception into the Church and the distinction of its members from all other sects, ought to be administered at every age to which the covenant, reception into the Church, and distinction belong. Baptism is such a sacrament. Therefore it ought to be given at every age, and so also to infants. The inference holds, from the proper final cause to the effect. For to whatever things the final cause pertains, to those same things the effect is rightly and necessarily ascribed.

units.la: Quarta. Circumcisio pertinebat ad vtramq; ætatem. Circumcisioni in nouo fœdere successit baptismus, ita vt habeat eundem vsum, quem habuit in veteri fœdere circumcisio. Ergo baptismus pertinet tam ad infantes, quàm ad adultos. Maior pater. Minor probatur testimonio Apostoli: Circumcisi estis circumcisione non manu facta, dum exuistis corpus carnis peccatricis per circumcisionem Christi: consepulti cum eo per baptismum, per quem etiam cum eo resurrexistis. Baptismus igitur est nostra circumcisio, hoc est, sacramentum, quo confirmantur eadem, & iis omnibus, nunc in nouo Testamento, quæ, & quibus confirmabantur in veteri Testamento circumcisione.
units.tr: Fourth. Circumcision pertained to both ages. Baptism has succeeded circumcision in the New Covenant, so that it has the same use which circumcision had in the Old Covenant. Therefore baptism pertains to infants as much as to adults. The major premise is plain. The minor premise is proved by the testimony of the Apostle: You were circumcised with a circumcision not made by hand, when you put off the body of the sinful flesh by the circumcision of Christ, buried with Him in baptism, in which you were also raised with Him. Baptism, therefore, is our circumcision, that is, the sacrament by which the same things are confirmed, and to all those now in the New Testament, to whom and by which they were confirmed in the Old Testament by circumcision.

units.la: Anabaptistæ igitur negantes infantibus Ecclesiæ baptismum, non modo jure suo eos spoliant, sed & gratiam DEI, sobolem fidelium inde ab vtero inter Ecclesiæ membra censeri volentis, obscurant, immò gratiæ noui fœderis manifestè derogant, & angustiorem gratia veteris faciunt, negantes baptismum extendebatur: tendi ad infantes, ad quos olim circumcisio extendebatur: obtinet consolationem Ecclesiæ & fidelium parentum labefactant: obligationem solennem, qua DEVS sobolem populi sui inde ab infantia sibi vult obstringi, & à reliqua hominum multitudine discerni, tollunt: studium gratitudinis & seruandæ obligationis in parentibus & liberis languefaciunt: Apostolis affirmantibus, ab aqua non posse arceri Spiritu sancto donatos, impudenter contradicunt: infantes à Christo jubente eos ad se adduci petulanter repellunt: denique vniuersali CHRISTI mandato de baptizandis omnibus impiè derogant. Ex quibus omnibus manifestum est, impugnationem pædobaptismi non esse leue erratum, sed impium dogma, Verbo Dei & consolationi Ecclesiæ aduersum. Quo magis vitanda sunt hæc & similia deliria sectæ anabaptisticæ: quæ sine dubio à diabolo est exci-
units.tr: The Anabaptists, then, by denying baptism to the infants of the Church, not only deprive them of their right but also obscure the grace of God, which wishes the offspring of believers to be counted among the members of the Church from the womb. Indeed, they plainly detract from the grace of the new covenant and make the grace of the old covenant narrower, denying that baptism extends to infants, to whom circumcision once extended. They take away the comfort of the Church and undermine believing parents, and they remove the solemn obligation by which God wills the offspring of his people to be bound to himself from infancy and distinguished from the rest of mankind. They weaken the zeal for gratitude and for keeping the obligation, in parents and children alike. When the apostles affirm that those who have received the Holy Spirit cannot be kept from water, they contradict them shamelessly. When Christ bids infants be brought to him, they wantonly repel them. Finally, they impiously detract from Christ's universal command concerning the baptizing of all. From all these things it is plain that the attack on infant baptism is not a slight error but an impious dogma, opposed to the Word of God and to the comfort of the Church. All the more must these and similar delusions of the Anabaptist sect be avoided: a sect undoubtedly stirred up by the devil, and an execrable monster compounded of various heresies and blasphemies.

units.la: Anabaptistici dogmatis absurditates. excitata, & monstrum est exsecrabile, ex variis hæresibus & blasphemiis conflatum.
units.tr: The absurdities of the Anabaptist doctrine. Stirred up by the devil, and an execrable monster compounded of various heresies and blasphemies.

units.la: Obiect. 1. Dogma, cuius neque mandatum, neque exemplum exstat in scriptura, non est recipiendum. Pædobaptismi neque mandatum, neque exemplum exstat in scriptura. Pædobaptismus ergo non est in Ecclesia recipiendus. Resp. Negatur minor. Exstat mandatum vniuersale: Baptizate omnes gentes. Ad hos omnes etiam infantes Ecclesiæ pertinent. Exstant exempla, quod integræ familiæ ab Apostolis sint baptizatæ, non exclusis infantibus, ad familias illas pertinentibus. Baptizata est ipsa (Lydia purpuraria) & domus eius. Et baptizatus est ipse (commentariensis Philipporum) & omnes illius illico. Baptizaui etiam Stephana & familiam.
units.tr: Objection 1. A doctrine for which neither command nor example is found in Scripture is not to be received. Neither a command nor an example of infant baptism is found in Scripture. Therefore infant baptism is not to be received in the Church. Answer. The minor is denied. A universal command exists: Baptize all nations. Infants of the Church belong to this all as well. Examples exist of whole households baptized by the apostles, without infants of those households being excluded: She (Lydia the seller of purple) was baptized, and her household. He (the jailer of the Philippians) was baptized, he and all his immediately. I baptized also Stephanas and his household.

units.la: Inst. 1. Christus non expresse jubet baptizari infantes. Resp. Nec expresse jubet baptizari adultos, viros, fœminas, cives, rusticos, fullones, sartores, &c. Omnes baptizari mandat, cuiuscunque sint ætatis, sexus, conditionis, qui ad fœdus & ecclesiam Dei pertinent. Neq; requiritur in præceptis & legibus vniversalibus singularium enumeratio: quia leges præcipiunt de toto genere. De singularibus sub genere comprehensis volunt esse simile judicium. Anabaptistæ ipsi non arcent mulieres à Cœna: nec tamen eius facti habent expressum mandatum, vel exemplum in scriptura. De baptismo habemus mandatum generale. Docete omnes gentes, (inquit Christus) & baptizate eos, &c. Præcepit, ut baptizentur omnes, qui sunt discipuli. Infantes autem sunt discipuli: quia nascuntur in schola Christi, & docentur suo modo. Idem Petrus mandauit, inquiens: Facta est vobis & liberis vestris promissio. Ergo baptizetur vnusquisque vestrum in nomen Iesu Christi. Num quis aquam prohibere potest, quo minus baptizentur isti, qui acceperunt Spiritum sanctum, sicut & nos? Mandat hoc etiam Paulus, cum docet, nos esse circumcisos in Christo, & cum eo consepultos per baptismum. Substitutus ergo est baptismus noster circumcisioni, quæ substitutio est lomandati.
units.tr: Objection 2. Christ does not expressly command infants to be baptized. Answer. Nor does he expressly command adults, men, women, citizens, country folk, fullers, tailors, and so on, to be baptized. He commands all, of whatever age, sex or condition, who belong to the covenant and church of God, to be baptized. In universal precepts and laws an enumeration of individuals is not required, because laws prescribe for the whole kind, and they wish a similar judgment to be made about the individuals comprehended under the kind. The Anabaptists themselves do not exclude women from the Supper, and yet they have no express command or example of this in Scripture. For baptism we have a general command: Teach all nations (says Christ), and baptize them, etc. He commanded that all who are disciples be baptized. Infants, however, are disciples, because they are born in the school of Christ and are taught in their own way. Peter likewise commanded, saying: The promise is made to you and to your children. Therefore let each of you be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ. Can anyone forbid water, so that these may not be baptized, who have received the Holy Spirit as we have? Paul also commands this, when he teaches that we are circumcised in Christ and buried with him through baptism. Our baptism, therefore, has been substituted for circumcision, and this substitution is by command.

units.la: Inst. 2. Qui debent baptizari, debent prius doceri: Docete omnes gentes, baptizantes eos, &c. Ergo non debent baptizari. Resp. Maior est neganda, cum probatione ex impropria versione. Verbum enim μαθητεύσατε, quod vulgo redditur Docete, proprie est, Discipulos facite. De doctrina sequitur: Docentes eos seruare. Vbi est διδάσκοντες, docentes, à διδάσκειν, docere: vide supra ad Quæst. 69. fine tertio. 2. Esto tamen μαθητεύσατε, docete: vera erit tantum de adultis qui doctrinæ capaces sunt, ex qualibus fiebat prima Ecclesiæ collectio. Hos Christus jubet prius doceri, postea baptizari, & discerni ab aliis. De infantibus in Ecclesia natis, aut cum parentibus fidelibus in Ecclesiam transeuntibus, etiam negatur: quia hi etiam ante baptismum comprehenduntur in formula foederis: Ero Deus tuus, & seminis tui. Proinde ad eos etiam, antequam doceri possint, signum novi foederis baptismus pertinet. Unde sequitur, illud Docete, de adultis, non de infantibus intelligendum esse. Ergo, inquis, universalis omnes, non comprehendit infantes. Resp. Comprehendit adultos & infantes: quia refertur non modo ad verbum Docete: sed etiam ad participium sequens, Baptizantes. Et est sensus: Docete, quicunq; doceri possunt: hi sunt soli adulti. Baptizantes, quicunque baptizari possunt: hi sunt adulti & infantes simul: & propter infantes baptizatos Christus videtur addidisse: Docentes eos servare, &c.
units.tr: Objection 2 (continued). Those who ought to be baptized ought first to be taught: Teach all nations, baptizing them, etc. Therefore they ought not to be baptized. Answer. The major premise is to be denied, with proof from an improper translation. For the verb μαθητεύσατε [mathēteusate], which is commonly rendered teach, properly means make disciples. The teaching that follows is: teaching them to observe. Where there is διδάσκοντες [didaskontes, teaching], from διδάσκειν [didaskein, to teach]: see above at Question 69, near the end of the third point. 2. Even if μαθητεύσατε means teach, the statement will be true only of adults who are capable of doctrine, from whom the first gathering of the Church was made. Christ bids these be taught first, then baptized, and distinguished from others. Concerning infants born in the Church, or those who pass into the Church with believing parents, it is also denied, because these too are comprehended before baptism in the form of the covenant: I will be God to you and to your seed. Accordingly, baptism, as the sign of the new covenant, pertains to them too, even before they can be taught. Hence it follows that the word Teach is to be understood of adults, not of infants. Therefore, you say, the universal all does not comprehend infants. Answer. It comprehends both adults and infants, because it refers not only to the verb Teach but also to the following participle, baptizing. And the sense is: Teach, whoever can be taught: these are only adults. Baptizing, whoever can be baptized: these are adults and infants together. And on account of the infants who are baptized, Christ seems to have added: teaching them to observe, etc.

units.la: Inst. 3. In exemplis de totis familiis baptizatis est synecdoche, & intelliguntur fuisse baptizati, qui essent fidem professi. Non igitur inde sequitur paedobaptismus. Resp. Negatur antecedens: quia historia nullam facit exclusionem: & non est dedens: quia historia nullam facit exclusionem: & non est currendum ad figuram, ubi nulla est ratio, cur non retineatur sententia propria.
units.tr: Objection 3. In the examples of whole households baptized there is a synecdoche, and it is to be understood that only those who had professed faith were baptized. Therefore infant baptism does not follow from them. Answer. The antecedent is denied, since the history makes no exclusion; and there is no need to run to a figure where there is no reason why the proper sense should not be retained.

units.la: Instant. 4. Immo est duplex ratio synecdoches. Una; quod Apostoli non baptizarunt contra mandatum & institutionem CHRISTI. Altera, quod exemplorum illorum circumstantiae infantes excludunt; quia dicitur: Dixerunt verbum omnibus, qui in domo erant: cum tamen infantibus non dixerint. Tota domus Stephani ministrauit sanctis. Excludamus gausa est. Tota domus Stephani ministrauit sanctis. Excludantur igitur infantes. Resp. ad 1. Negatur, baptismum infantum pugnare cum institutione Christi, qui vult omnes, ad se & ad Ecclesiam pertinentes, baptismo insigniri, ut ostensum est: Non igitur est verum, Apostolos ex institutione CHRISTI abstinuisse a baptismo infantum. Ad 2. Negatur, ex illis circumstantiis sequi synecdochen in phrasibus de baptismo Potuerunt infantes baptizari cum parentibus, etsi non ipsi, sed parentes, & alij domestici adulti audirent verbum, & ministrarent Apostolis: quandoquidem aetas potuit quidem eos excludere ab auditu doctrinae, & a ministratione: sed a baptismo non magis, quam a salute ipsa. Ideo dicitur Cornelio: Petrus tibi ea dicturus est, per quae salvaberis & tu, & tota domus tua. Quare reiectis tam friuolis cauillationibus, certo est statuendum, paedobaptismum a Christo mandatum, & ab Apostolis, totaque Ecclesia semper usurpatum esse. Augustinus: Baptismum parvulorum traditum tenet universitas Ecclesia. Et ibi contra Don. concludit: Quod universa tenet Ecclesia, nec a Conciliis institutum, tum, sed semper retentum est: non nisi apostolica authoritate traditum, sed rectissimè credimus.
units.tr: Objection 4. Indeed there are two grounds for the synecdoche. One: the apostles did not baptize contrary to the command and institution of Christ. The other: the circumstances of those examples exclude infants, because it is said: They spoke the word to all who were in the house, whereas they did not speak it to infants. The whole household of Stephanas devoted themselves to the saints. Therefore let infants be excluded. Answer to the first: it is denied that infant baptism conflicts with the institution of Christ, who wishes all who belong to himself and to the Church to be marked with baptism, as has been shown. It is therefore not true that the apostles abstained from baptizing infants by the institution of Christ. Answer to the second: it is denied that a synecdoche follows in the phrases about baptism from those circumstances. Infants could be baptized with their parents, even if they themselves did not hear the word, but their parents and other adult members of the household did, and served the apostles. For age could indeed exclude them from hearing the doctrine and from service, but not from baptism any more than from salvation itself. So Cornelius is told: Peter will speak to you words by which you and your whole household will be saved. Therefore, these trivial cavils being rejected, it must be firmly established that infant baptism was commanded by Christ and always used by the apostles and the whole Church. Augustine: The universal Church holds the baptism of little children. And there, against the Donatists, he concludes: What the whole Church holds, and what was not instituted by councils but has always been retained, is rightly believed to have been handed down by apostolic authority.

units.la: Obiect. 2. Qui non credunt, non sunt baptizandi. Dicitur enim: Qui crediderit, & baptizatus fuerit, &c. Infantes non credunt. Ergo non sunt baptizandi. Ad vsum baptismi necessariò requiritur fides. Nam quicunque non crediderit, condemnabitur. Condemnandis autem non debet dari signum gratiae. Respond. 1. Maior vniuersaliter negatur. Potest opponi exemplum circumcisionis infantum per instantiam. Itaque vera est tantum de adultis. Non sunt baptizandi, qui non credunt, nempe adulti. Nec tamen pronunciari potest de adultis, quod credant. Si igitur infantes non sunt baptizandi, quia non credunt, neque grandes natu erunt baptizandi, quia etiam de his non potest sciri, an credant: ut Simon magus baptizatur, & tamen fuit hypocrita. Sed (inquiunt) sufficit professio fidei Ecclesiae. Fatemur ita esse: sed addimus, natum esse in Ecclesia infantibus esse loco professionis. 2. Ad vsum baptismi requiritur fides, nempe actualis in adultis: in infantibus sufficit inclinatiua, quam in iis operatur Spiritus Dei. Sunt igitur quatuor termini, vel fallacia à dicto secundum quid, &c. Qui non credunt, nempe simpliciter, nec professione, nec inclinatione, non sunt baptizandi. Infantes fidelium credunt inclinatione. Ergo, &c. De his Minor neganda est: quia licet non credant actu, sicut adulti, credunt tamen inclinatione. Sicut enim infantes impiorum extra Ecclesiam non habent quidem impietatem actualem, habent vero inclinationem ad impietatem: sic infantes piorum non habent quidem pietatem actualem, habent vero inclinationem ad pietatem: non quidem ex natura, sed ex gratia foederis. Habent etiam Spiritum sanctum, & ab eo regenerantur, pro modo aetatis suae, sicut Johannes baptista impletus fuit Spiritu sancto, cùm adhuc esset in utero matris. Et Jeremiae dicitur: Cùm nondum prodissem ex utero, sanctificaui te. Si infantes habent Spiritum sanctum, certè operatur in eis regenerationem, bonas inclinationes, nouos motus, pro aetatis modulo, & alia, quae eis ad salutem sunt necessaria: vel certè haec omnia ipse quasi supplet, & ad baptismum eis sufficit, juxta dictum Petri: Quis potest arcere aqua eos, qui Spiritum sanctum receperunt, sicut & nos? Propter hanc causam Christus parvulos vlnis complectitur, & benedicit, & numerat inter credentes: Qui offenderit vnum ex pusillis istis, qui credunt in me, &c. Cùm igitur infantes Ecclesiae baptizantur, non profanatur baptismus, vt calumniantur Anabaptistae. Obiect. 3. Si signum foederis pertinet ad omnes, ad quos pertinet promissio foederis, etiam Coena erit administranda infantibus: quia etiam Coena est signum foederis. At Coena non est infantibus administranda. Ergo, &c. Resp. Nos non concludimus: Ergo omne signum, sed, ergo aliquod signum dandum est infantibus: illud nimirum, 1. Quod non habet conditiones, quae excludant infantes. 2. Quod est initiatio. Tale autem nouo foedere est solus baptismus. Probatur: Baptismus tantum requirit Spiritum sanctum & fidem, siue actu, siue potentia: vt ex verbis Petri, Quis poterit, &c. Item, solus baptismus est receptio in Ecclesiam. Ergo, &c. Vel hoc modo: Si baptizandi sunt infantes, admittendi quoque sunt ad Coenam. Coena enim debetur toti Ecclesiae non minus quam baptismus. At non sunt admittendi ad coenam. Ergo. Resp. Negatur consequentia: quia est dissimilitudo in exemplis. Magnum discrimen est inter baptismum, & coenam. Nam 1. Baptismus est sacramentum initus & receptionis in Ecclesiam: quo fit, vt nemini sit coena concedenda, nisi prius baptizato. Coena vero est sacramentum mansionis in Ecclesia, seu confirmatio receptionis factae. Coena enim est instituta ad confirmationem nostri: vt sit signum, quo Deus nos confirmat, & obsignat, quod nos in Ecclesiam semel receptos velit in ea perpetuo conseruare, ne vnquam ab ea deficiamus, quod item velit continuare beneficia, semel nobis collata, & nos alere ac nutrire corpore & sanguine Christi ad vitam aeternam. Hac autem confirmatione indigent adulti, qui varie tentantur. 2. Ad baptismum satis est regeneratio per Spiritum sanctum, & fides, vel inclinatio ad fidem & poenitentiam. In coena vero additae sunt & requiruntur conditiones, quae ab eius usu infantes excludunt. Requiritur enim in Coena 1. vt vtentes signo annuncient mortem Domini. 2. Vt seipsos probent, an habeant fidem & poenitentiam. Haec cum non possit aetas infantum, manifestum est, quod infantes a coena excludantur, a baptismo non item. Proinde non sequitur, infantes, quia sunt baptizandi, statim etiam esse admittendos ad coenam. Nam ad ea tantum sacramenta admitti debent, quae sunt signa receptionis in foedus & ecclesiam, quaeq; non habent additam conditionem, qua eorum aetas excludatur. Tale autem sacramentum est baptismus in nouo Testamento: non Coena Domini.
units.tr: Objection 2. Those who do not believe are not to be baptized. For it is said: "Whoever believes and is baptized," and so on. Infants do not believe. Therefore they are not to be baptized. Faith is necessarily required for the use of baptism. For whoever does not believe will be condemned, and the sign of grace should not be given to those who are to be condemned. Answer: 1. The major premise is denied universally. The example of the circumcision of infants can be set against it as an instance. So the premise is true only of adults. Those who do not believe, namely adults, are not to be baptized. Yet it cannot be asserted of adults that they believe. If therefore infants are not to be baptized because they do not believe, neither will those grown up be baptized, since it cannot be known of them either whether they believe. Simon Magus was baptized, and yet he was a hypocrite. But (they say) the profession of faith made by the Church suffices. We grant that it is so, but we add that for those born within the Church, infants stand in place of a profession. 2. For the use of baptism faith is required: actual faith in adults; in infants an inclinational faith suffices, which the Spirit of God works in them. There are therefore four terms, or a fallacy arising from a statement made with a qualification, and so on. Those who do not believe, namely simply, neither by profession nor by inclination, are not to be baptized. Infants of believers believe by inclination. Therefore, and so on. The minor premise is to be denied concerning these infants: although they do not believe actually, as adults do, they nonetheless believe by inclination. For just as the infants of the impious outside the Church do not indeed have actual impiety, but do have an inclination to impiety, so the infants of the pious do not indeed have actual piety, but do have an inclination to piety: not indeed from nature, but from the grace of the covenant. They also have the Holy Spirit and are regenerated by him, according to the measure of their age, just as John the Baptist was filled with the Holy Spirit while he was still in his mother's womb. And of Jeremiah it is said: "Before you came forth from the womb, I sanctified you." If infants have the Holy Spirit, he certainly works regeneration in them, good inclinations, new motions, according to the measure of their age, and the other things that are necessary to them for salvation; or certainly he himself, as it were, supplies all these and suffices for them for baptism, according to the saying of Peter: "Can anyone forbid water for those who have received the Holy Spirit, just as we have?" For this reason Christ embraces little children in his arms, blesses them, and counts them among believers: "Whoever offends one of these little ones who believe in me," and so on. Since therefore the infants of the Church are baptized, baptism is not profaned, as the Anabaptists slander. Objection 3. If the sign of the covenant pertains to all to whom the promise of the covenant pertains, then the Supper too will have to be administered to infants, because the Supper is also a sign of the covenant. But the Supper is not to be administered to infants. Therefore, and so on. Answer: We do not conclude "therefore every sign," but "therefore some sign must be given to infants": namely one which 1. does not have conditions that exclude infants, and 2. which is an initiation. Such a sign in the New Covenant is baptism alone. This is proved: baptism alone requires the Holy Spirit and faith, either actually or potentially, as from the words of Peter, "Who can...?" Likewise baptism alone is reception into the Church. Therefore, and so on. Or in this way: if infants are to be baptized, they must also be admitted to the Supper. For the Supper is owed to the whole Church no less than baptism is. But they are not to be admitted to the Supper. Therefore... Answer: The consequence is denied, because there is a dissimilarity in the examples. There is a great difference between baptism and the Supper. For 1. baptism is the sacrament of entrance and reception into the Church, so that the Supper is to be granted to no one unless he has first been baptized. The Supper, however, is the sacrament of remaining in the Church, or the confirmation of a reception already made. For the Supper was instituted for our confirmation: it is a sign by which God confirms and seals that, having once received us into the Church, he wills to keep us in it perpetually, lest we ever fall away from it; likewise that he wills to continue the benefits once bestowed on us, and to feed and nourish us with the body and blood of Christ unto eternal life. Now adults, who are variously tempted, need this confirmation. 2. For baptism, regeneration through the Holy Spirit and faith, or an inclination to faith and repentance, is enough. In the Supper, however, conditions have been added and are required which exclude infants from its use. For in the Supper it is required 1. that those who use the sign proclaim the death of the Lord, and 2. that they examine themselves, whether they have faith and repentance. Since the age of infants cannot do these things, it is plain that infants are excluded from the Supper but not in the same way from baptism. Therefore it does not follow that infants, because they are to be baptized, are at once also to be admitted to the Supper. For they ought to be admitted only to those sacraments which are signs of reception into the covenant and the Church, and which have no added condition by which their age is excluded. Such a sacrament is baptism in the New Testament, not the Lord's Supper.

units.la: Obiect. 4. Si circumcisioni successit baptismus, etiam hodie masculi tantum erunt baptizandi, & quidem octauo die. At hoc est falsum. Ergo & illud. Resp. Negatur maior: quia baptismus successit circumcisioni, non in singulis circumstantiis, sed in regnisignificata, fine; & vsu, in quibus hæc duo sacramenta conue-niunt: tametsi circumstantia sexus & ætatis non sit vtriq; com-munis: Nam DEVS circumcisionem expresse restrinxerat ad masculos, fœmellis pepercerat. Interim in masculis eas com-plectebatur, vt eis nasci ex circumcisis parentibus, pro circum-cisione esset. Fœmellæ igitur in maribus circumcidebantur, hoc est, pro circumcisis habebantur. Hinc mulier sanata à Christo, vocatur filia Abrahami: & filij Jacob dicentes: Non possumus so-rorem nostram dare incircumciso: opponunt inter se hæc duo: Soror nostra, & incircumcisus. Fœmellas igitur Deus olim exceperat à circumcisione, & circumstantiam octaui diei determinauerat. In baptismo vero hæ circumstantiæ sexus & ætatis non sunt de-terminatæ: sed vniuersale mandatum est, quod liberi piorum omnes hoc symbolo debent inseri Ecclesiæ: siue id fiat octauo die, siue statim post partum.
units.tr: Objection 4. If baptism succeeded circumcision, then today too only males would have to be baptized, and indeed on the eighth day. But this is false. Therefore that too is false. Answer: The major premise is denied, because baptism succeeded circumcision not in every circumstance, but in the things signified, the end, and the use, in which these two sacraments agree, although the circumstances of sex and age are not common to both. For God had expressly restricted circumcision to males and had spared females. Yet in the males he included the females, so that for them to be born of circumcised parents took the place of circumcision. Females were therefore circumcised in the males, that is, they were regarded as circumcised. Hence the woman healed by Christ is called a daughter of Abraham, and the sons of Jacob, saying "We cannot give our sister to an uncircumcised man," set these two things against each other: our sister, and the uncircumcised. God therefore had formerly excepted females from circumcision and had fixed the circumstance of the eighth day. In baptism, however, these circumstances of sex and age are not fixed; rather there is a universal command that all the children of the pious must be incorporated into the Church by this sign, whether this is done on the eighth day or immediately after birth.

units.la: DE CIRCUMCISIONE.
units.tr: On Circumcision.

units.la: Cum dictum sit, Baptismum Circumcisioni in nouo fœdere substitutum esse: non alienum fuerit aliquid de Circumcisione etiam subijcere. De ea vero quæstiones potissimum considerandæ sunt hæ: I. Quid fuerit Circumcisio: II. Cur fuerit instituta. III. Cur rursus abolita. IV. Quid ei successerit. V. Quomodo Circumcisio & Baptismus conueniant & differant. VI. Cur Christus sit circumcisus.
units.tr: Since it has been said that Baptism was substituted for Circumcision in the New Covenant, it will not be out of place to add something about Circumcision itself. Concerning it, the following questions above all need to be considered: (1) What circumcision was; (2) why it was instituted; (3) why it was afterwards abolished; (4) what succeeded it; (5) how circumcision and baptism agree and differ; (6) why Christ was circumcised.

units.la: I. Quid fuerit Circumcisio.
units.tr: I. What Circumcision was.

units.la: Circumcisio erat ritus, quo circumcidebatur præputium ma-ribus in populo Israelitico ex DEI mandato: vt iste ritus esset sigillum initi fœderis cum posteritate Abrahami. Seu; erat am-putatio præputij omnibus masculis populi Israelitici mandata à Deo, vt esset signum fœderis initi cum Abrahamo, & eius posteris, significans & obsignans eis amputationem præputij cordium, propter nasciturum semen promissum, discernens eos à reliquis gentibus, & obligans eos ad fidem & obedientiam er-ga Deum. Hoc est fœdus meum inter me & vos, & inter semen tuum post te, quod seruabitis, vt circumcidatis omne masculum, &c. Circum-cisionem verò accepit sigillum iustitiæ fidei, &c. Iehoua circumcidet cor tuum, & cor seminis tui, vt diligas Dominum Deum tuum ex toto corde tuo, &c. Circumcisio igitur solos Judæos obligabat. Aliis gentibus liberum erat circumcidi, vel non, si ad ecclesiam Judaicam accederent.
units.tr: Circumcision was a rite in which the foreskin of males was cut away among the people of Israel by command of God, so that this rite would be the seal of the covenant made with the posterity of Abraham. Or: it was the amputation of the foreskin, commanded by God for all males of the Israelite people, to be the sign of the covenant made with Abraham and his posterity, signifying and sealing to them the cutting away of the foreskin of the heart, on account of the promised seed that was to be born; it distinguished them from the other nations and bound them to faith and obedience toward God. "This is my covenant between me and you, and between your seed after you, which you shall keep: every male among you shall be circumcised," etc. Moreover, he received circumcision as the seal of the righteousness of faith, etc. "The LORD will circumcise your heart and the heart of your seed, that you may love the LORD your God with all your heart," etc. Circumcision therefore obliged only the Jews. Other nations were free to be circumcised or not, if they came over to the Jewish church.

units.la: Notandum hic est, triplices fuisse cives veteris ecclesiae. 1. Erant Israelitae, ex semine Abrahae progeniti, qui tenebantur exlege observare circumcisionem, & reliquas caeremonias omnes. 2. Erant Proselyti, hoc est, advententij, qui ex Gentibus ad religionem Judaicam accedebant, & fidei suae confirmandae causa se circumcisioni & toti legi caeremoniali subijciebant. Horum fit mentio Act.2,10. Matth.23,15. 3. Erant viri religiosi, converši ex gentibus ad Judaeos, & doctrinam ac promissiones Dei amplexi, sed non circumcisi, nec observantes ceremonias: quia Gentibus liberum erat servare circumcisionem, & ceremonias. Tales fuerunt Naaman Syrus, Eunuchus, Ethiops, & alij, de quibus Act. 2, 5. Erant viri σεβομενοι, religiosi, &c.
units.tr: It must be noted here that there were three kinds of citizens of the old Church. (1) There were the Israelites, born of the seed of Abraham, who were bound by the law to observe circumcision and all the other ceremonies. (2) There were the Proselytes, that is, newcomers, who came over from the Gentiles to the Jewish religion and, to confirm their faith, submitted themselves to circumcision and to the whole ceremonial law. Mention of them is made at Acts 2:10 and Matt. 23:15. (3) There were the religious men, converted from the Gentiles to the Jews, who embraced the doctrine and promises of God but were not circumcised nor observed the ceremonies, because it was left free to the Gentiles whether they kept circumcision and the ceremonies. Such were Naaman the Syrian, the Eunuch, the Ethiopian, and others, of whom Acts 2:5 speaks. There were the men who were fearers of God [σεβόμενοι], religious, etc.

units.la: Obj. Soli mares circumcidebantur: ergo foeminae excludebantur a foedere gratiae. R. Foeminae comprehendebantur in circumcisione: quia Deus parcebat infirmiori sexui: satis erat eis ex circumcisis prognatas esse, ut in foedere, & semine Abrahami censerentur. Vide supra Obiect.4. de Anabapt.
units.tr: Objection. Only males were circumcised; therefore females were excluded from the covenant of grace. Answer. Females were included in circumcision, because God spared the weaker sex; it was enough for them to be born of circumcised parents to be counted in the covenant and in the seed of Abraham. See above, Objection 4, on the Anabaptists.

units.la: II. Qui fuerint circumcisionis fines.
units.tr: The purposes of circumcision.

units.la: Instituta fuit circumcisio. 1. Ut esset signum gratiae Dei erga posteros Abrahami, & quidem dupliciter. Primo, quod propter Messiam venturum Deus reciperet in foedus credentes. Deinde, quod terram Chanaan eis esset daturus, & ibi certam sedem ecclesiae usq; ad adventum Messiae concessurus. 2. Ut esset obligatio Abrahae, eiusque seminis, ad gratitudinem, seu, ad fidem & poenitentiam, adeoque ad servandum totam legem. 3. Ut esset sacra discretio illius populi ab aliis gentibus & sectis. 4. Ut esset signum ingressus & receptionis in visibilem ecclesiam. 5. Ut significaret, omnes homines naturali propagatione esse immundos & reos: seu: ut esset commonefactio de immunditie naturali: de abijcienda massa peccati, praesertim immunditie, pugnante cum lege castitatis: Circumcidite praeputium cordis vestri, & cervicem vestram ne obdurate amplius. Circumcidimini Domino, & auferte praeputia cordium vestrorum. 6. Ut esset signum, ostendens mo-dum liberationis a peccati immunditie & reatu, per & propter Christum ex semine Abrahae nasciturum. In semine tuo benedicentur omnes gentes.
units.tr: Circumcision was instituted: (1) to be a sign of God's grace toward the posterity of Abraham, and this in two ways. First, that on account of the Messiah who was to come, God would receive believers into the covenant. Then, that he would give them the land of Canaan and there grant to the Church a certain seat until the coming of the Messiah. (2) To be an obligation on Abraham and his seed to gratitude, that is, to faith and repentance, and so to keep the whole law. (3) To be a holy distinction of that people from the other nations and sects. (4) To be a sign of entrance into and reception into the visible Church. (5) To signify that all men are unclean and guilty by natural propagation; or: to be a reminder of natural uncleanness, of putting away the mass of sin, especially the uncleanness that conflicts with the law of chastity: "Circumcise the foreskin of your heart, and stiffen your neck no more." "Circumcise yourselves to the LORD, and take away the foreskins of your hearts." (6) To be a sign showing the way of deliverance from the uncleanness and guilt of sin through and on account of Christ, who was to be born of the seed of Abraham: "In your seed all the nations shall be blessed."

units.la: III. Cur abolita sit circumcisio.
units.tr: Why circumcision was abolished.

units.la: Abolita est circumcisio 1. Quia res significata est exhibita. Intermedia enim significabat Messiam venturum aliquando, & naturam assumpturum. 2. Quia instituta erat ad discretionem tionem populi Judaici ab aliis omnibus gentibus. Nunc vero ecclesia ex omnibus gentibus colligitur. Exhibito igitur Messia, & discrimine illo populorum sublato, typum circumcisionis aboleri oportuit. Nam causis mutatis, etiam leges & instituta ex illis pendentia tollere & mutare, sapientia legislatoris est.
units.tr: Circumcision was abolished: (1) because the thing signified has been exhibited. For the intermediate rite signified that the Messiah would come at some time and assume our nature. (2) Because it was instituted to distinguish the Jewish people from all other nations. But now the Church is gathered from all nations. Therefore, with the Messiah exhibited and that distinction between peoples removed, the type of circumcision had to be done away with. For when the causes have changed, it is the wisdom of the lawgiver to remove and change the laws and institutions that depend on them.

units.la: IV. Quid circumcisioni successerit.
units.tr: IV. What succeeded circumcision.

units.la: Circumcisioni successit baptismus in novo Testamento. Succedere sacramentum sacramento, est, uno abolito aliud in eius locum substitui, & quidem ita, ut sub diversis ritibus idem sit significatum, idem finis, & usus utriusque. Sic baptismum successisse circumcisioni, probatur 1. authoritate Apostoli: In quo etiam circumcisi estis, circumcisione non manu facta, dum corpus carnis peccatricis exuistis per circumcisionem Christi, consepulti cum eo per baptismum, per quem etiam cum eo resurrexistis per fidem Dei efficaciter agentis, qui excitavit eum ex mortuis, vosque mortuos in peccatis & praeputio carnis vestrae cum eo vivificavit, condonatis vobis omnibus peccatis, &c. Hic Apostolus duabus rationibus probat, externae circumcisionis nullum amplius esse usum, seu, circumcisionem non amplius esse servandam in nova Ecclesia. Primo; quia in Christo habemus circumcisionem non manu factam, seu spiritualem, cuius symbolum fuerat circumcisio corporalis, hoc est, quia in Christo jam est impletum, quod per eam fuit adumbratum. Deinde; quia baptismus eandem significationem, & eundem usum nunc habet, quem olim circumcisio habuit, nisi quod baptismus est signum rei exhibitae; quam exhibendam figurabat circumcisio. Itaque docemur hoc Pauli loco, baptismum idesse Christianis, quod olim Judaeis fuerat circumcisio. 2. Professionis sacramentum est tessera adoptionis in populum Dei, & sacramentum ingressus in Ecclesiam. Nam sicuti infantes Judaeorum & proselytorum tanquam nati cives Ecclesiae, mox octavo die circumcidebantur, adulti vero tum demum admittebantur ad circumcisionem, cum professi essent Judaismum: sic etiam Christianorum infantes baptizantur statim, adulti vero non nisi post professionem doctrinae Christi: cuius professionis loco infantibus est, quod nati sunt in Ecclesia.
units.tr: Baptism succeeded circumcision in the New Testament. For one sacrament to succeed another means that, when one is abolished, another is substituted in its place, and indeed in such a way that under different rites the meaning, the end, and the use of both are the same. That baptism succeeded circumcision is proved (1) by the authority of the Apostle: "In him you were also circumcised with a circumcision not made by hands, when you put off the body of the sinful flesh by the circumcision of Christ, buried with him in baptism, in which you were also raised with him through faith in the working of God, who raised him from the dead; and you, being dead in your sins and the uncircumcision of your flesh, he made alive together with him, having forgiven you all your sins," etc. Here the Apostle proves by two reasons that external circumcision no longer has any use, or that circumcision is no longer to be kept in the new Church. First, because in Christ we have a circumcision not made by hands, that is, a spiritual one, of which bodily circumcision was the symbol; that is, because what was foreshadowed by it has now been fulfilled in Christ. Then, because baptism now has the same meaning and the same use that circumcision had of old, except that baptism is the sign of the thing exhibited, which circumcision foreshadowed as something to be exhibited. Thus from this passage of Paul we are taught that baptism is to Christians what circumcision once was to the Jews. (2) The sacrament of profession is the token of adoption into the people of God and the sacrament of entrance into the Church. For just as the infants of Jews and proselytes, as born citizens of the Church, were circumcised straightaway on the eighth day, while adults were admitted to circumcision only when they had professed Judaism, so also the infants of Christians are baptized at once, but adults only after professing the doctrine of Christ; for infants, the profession takes the place of this, that they were born in the Church.

units.la: V. Quomodo circumcisio & baptismus conveniant, & differant.
units.tr: V. How circumcision and baptism agree and differ.

units.la: Conveniunt circumcisio & baptismus 1: Fine principali, quod utroque sacramento obsignatur promissio gratiae per & propter Christum, quæ omnibus temporibus est eadem. 2. Quod vtro- que significatur regeneratio, & stipulatio de fide & obedientia hominum erga Deum. 3. Quod vtrumque est sacramentum ingressus seu receptionis & insitionis in ecclesiam. Differunt autem 1. Ritu seu caremonia: quæ non est eadem in circumcisione & baptismo. 2. Circumstantia sexus & ætatis: quod circumcisio solis masculis erat præcepta octauo die: baptismus ad vtrumq; sexum ecclesiæ mox à natiuitate pertinet. 3. Modo significandi. Circumcisio (ex parte Dei) promittebat gratiam propter venturum Messiam; baptismus propter exhibitum. Circumcisi recipiebantur in gratiam propter exhibendum; baptizati recipiuntur propter exhibitum Christum. 4. Promissione particulari. Circumcisio habet promissionem de beneficio etiam corporali, hoc est, de certa sede ecclesiæ danda & seruanda in terra Chanaan, vsq; ad aduentum Messiæ. Baptismus in specie nullam habet promissionem temporalis beneficij. 5. Obligationis modo. Circumcisio (ex parte populi) obligabat ecclesiam ad obseruationem totius legis cæremonialis, forensis & moralis simul. Baptismus nos tantum obligat ad legem moralem: hoc est, ad fidem & pœnitentiam. 6. Obiectis & duratione. Circumcisio tantū fuit mandata posteris Abrahami, & vsq; ad exhibitionem Messiæ durare debuit. Baptismus omnibus gentibus est institutus, volentibus ad ecclesiæ sanctitatem accedere, & permanebit vsq; ad finem mundi.
units.tr: Circumcision and baptism agree: (1) in their principal end, because both seal the promise of grace through and on account of Christ, which is the same in all times; (2) because both signify regeneration and the covenant pledge of faith and obedience of humans toward God; (3) because both are the sacrament of entrance, that is, of reception and ingrafting into the Church. They differ: (1) in rite or ceremony, which is not the same in circumcision and baptism; (2) in the circumstances of sex and age: circumcision was commanded only for males on the eighth day, while baptism belongs to both sexes in the Church immediately from birth; (3) in the manner of signifying. Circumcision (on God's part) promised grace on account of the Messiah who was to come; baptism promises it on account of the Messiah who has been revealed. The circumcised were received into grace on account of the one to be exhibited; the baptized are received on account of Christ already exhibited; (4) in the particular promise. Circumcision carries a promise of a bodily benefit as well, that is, of a certain dwelling place of the Church to be given and kept in the land of Canaan until the coming of the Messiah. Baptism, as such, carries no promise of a temporal benefit; (5) in the mode of obligation. Circumcision (on the people's part) bound the Church to observe the whole law, ceremonial, judicial and moral alike. Baptism binds us only to the moral law, that is, to faith and repentance; (6) in the objects and duration. Circumcision was enjoined only on the posterity of Abraham and was to last until the Messiah was exhibited. Baptism has been instituted for all nations, for those who are willing to come to the holiness of the Church, and it will remain until the end of the world.

units.la: XI. Cur Christus circumcisus.
units.tr: XI. Why Christ was circumcised.

units.la: Nulla causa circumcisionis erat in Christo. Nihil enim poterat ei significari aut conferri, nec vlla immundities in eo hæreba t, cuius amputati o ei obsignaretur. Circumcidi tamen voluit propter consolationem & doctrinam Ecclesiæ. 1. Vt testaretur, se esse populi illius circumcisi membrum: sicut & ideo baptizari voluit, vt testaretur, se etiam populi baptizati esse membrum; Vtriusq; igitur ecclesiæ sacramento initiatorio insigniri voluit, vt, se vtriusque caput, seruatorem, & lapidem angularem esse, ex vtraq; vnam ecclesiam efficere velle, significaret. 2. Vt ostenderet, se omnia nostra peccata in se recepisse, vt pro iis satisfaceret, & nos ab omni reatu liberaret. Eum, qui peccatum non nouit, fecit pro nobis peccatum, vt nos efficeremur iustitia Dei in eo. Disciplina pacis nostræ super eum, & liuore eius sanati sumus. Posuit Dominus in eo iniquitatem omnium nostrum. 3. Vt testaretur, se nostro nomine esse factum legi obnoxium, & eam integrè ac perfectè implere, exsecrationem eius in se deriuando, vt nos ab ea redimeret. 4. Circumcisio Christi fuit etiam pars humiliationis & λύτρον pro nostris peccatis.
units.tr: There was no cause for circumcision in Christ. For nothing could be signified in him or conferred on him, nor was there any uncleanness in him that clung to him and that the cutting away of which would be sealed to him. Nevertheless he willed to be circumcised for the comfort and the teaching of the Church. (1) So that he might testify that he was a member of that circumcised people; just as he also willed to be baptized, so that he might testify that he is a member of the baptized people. By receiving the initiatory sacrament of both churches, he willed to be marked with both, signifying that he is the head and Saviour of both, and the cornerstone, and that he willed to make one Church out of both.
