(2) So that he might show that he had taken all our sins upon himself, in order to make satisfaction for them and to free us from all guilt: He who knew no sin he made to be sin for us, that we might be made the righteousness of God in him. The chastisement of our peace was upon him, and by his stripes we are healed. The Lord has laid on him the iniquity of us all. (3) So that he might testify that in our name he was made subject to the law, and fulfilled it entirely and perfectly, by taking upon himself its curse, so as to redeem us from it. (4) Christ's circumcision was also a part of his humiliation and a ransom [λύτρον] for our sins.

units.la: DE CÆNA DOMINI
units.tr: CONCERNING THE LORD'S SUPPER

units.la: QVÆSTIO LXXV.
units.tr: QUESTION LXXV.

units.la: Qua ratione in Cœna Domini admoneris & confirmaris, te vnici illius sacrificij Christi in cruce oblati, atque omnium eius bonorum participem esse?
units.tr: By what means in the Lord's Supper are you admonished and assured that you are a partaker of that one sacrifice of Christ offered on the cross, and of all his benefits?

units.la: RESPONSIO.
units.tr: ANSWER.

units.la: Quod Christus me atq; omnes fideles de hoc fracto pane edere, & de poculo distributo bibere iussit in sui memoriam, addita hac promissione a. Primum, corpus suum non minus certò pro me in cruce oblatum ac fractum, & sanguinem suum pro me fusum esse: quàm oculis cerno, panem Domini mihi frangi, & poculum mihi communicari. Deinde animam meam non minus certo ipsius corpore, quod pro nobis crucifixum, & sanguine, qui pro nobis fusus est, ad vitam æternam ab ipso pasci: quàm panem & vinum, symbola corporis & sanguinis Domini, è manu ministri accepta, ore corporis percipio.
units.tr: Because Christ commanded me and all the faithful to eat of this broken bread and to drink from the cup distributed, in remembrance of him, with this promise added: first, that his body was offered and broken for me on the cross, and his blood shed for me, no less surely than I see with my eyes that the bread of the Lord is broken for me and the cup shared with me; and then, that my soul is fed by him to eternal life no less surely with his body, which was crucified for us, and with his blood, which was shed for us, than I receive with my mouth the bread and wine, the signs of the body and blood of the Lord, taken from the hand of the minister.

units.la: EXPLICATIO.
units.tr: EXPLANATION.

units.la: De Cœna Domini præcipuè considerandum: I. Quid sit Cœna Domini. II. Qui sint eius fines. III. Quid à baptismo differat. IV. Quis sit sensus verborum institutionis. V. Quod discrimen Missa, & Cœna: & cur Missa sit abolenda. VI. Quis vsus legitimus cœnæ. VII. Quid accipiant impij in cœna. VIII. Qui ad cœnam accedere debeant. IX. Qui debeant admitti.
units.tr: Concerning the Lord's Supper the following should be chiefly considered: (1) what the Lord's Supper is; (2) what its ends are; (3) how it differs from baptism; (4) what the sense of the words of institution is; (5) what the difference is between the Mass and the Supper, and why the Mass is to be abolished; (6) what the lawful use of the Supper is; (7) what the wicked receive in the Supper; (8) who ought to approach the Supper; (9) who ought to be admitted.

units.la: Ex his tres priores pertinent ad quæst. Catech. LXXV, LXXVI. quarta ad LXXVII, LXXVIII, LXXIX. quinta ad LXXX. sexta, septima & octaua ad LXXXI.
units.tr: Of these, the first three pertain to Questions LXXV and LXXVI; the fourth to LXXVII, LXXVIII and LXXIX; the fifth to LXXX; the sixth, seventh and eighth to LXXXI.

units.la: I. Quid sit cœna Domini.
units.tr: I. What the Lord's Supper is.

units.la: Primùm videbimus, quibus nominibus appelletur Cœna Domini: postea quid sit, definiemus. Hæc actio, seu hic ritus à Christo ante mortem institutus, vocatur Cœna Domini, à circumstantia primæ institutionis, quæ inter cœnandum facta est: quam temporis circumstantiam Ecclesia pro libertate mutavit. Nam per accidens, hoc est, propter eum agni paschalis, qui ex lege inter duas vesperas celebrandus, & hoc novo sacramento abolendus erat, factum est, ut vesperæ sub tempus cœnæ potius, quàm mane aut meridie, hic ritus sit à Christo institutus. Vocatur etiam à Paulo mensa Domini. Deinde appellata est συνάξις, à conventu Ecclesiæ: quia in peragenda Cœna conuenire debent aliqui, multi, pauci, immò tota Ecclesia. Nam in prima actione erant discipuli omnes, & dicitur eis: Accipite hoc, & dividite inter vos. Bibite ex hoc omnes. Necesse est igitur, ibi plures fuisse: quod etiam apparet ex repetita institutione Apostoli: Cum convenitis in unum, hoc non est Dominicam cœnam edere: & ad extremum subiungit: Itaque, fratres mei, cum convenitis ad vescendum, alius alium expectate. Et plures conuenire oportere ad celebrandam cœnam, finis demonstrat, quem Apostolus ei tribuit: quod sit symbolum & vinculum dilectionis: Quoniam unus panis unum corpus multi sumus. Dicta est etiam εὐχαριστία, quia est ritus gratiarum actionis. A patribus sæpe vocatur sacrificium, non ἱλασκὴ, aut meritorium, ut fingunt Pontificij, sed ἱυχαρίστικον, quia est solennis commemoratio & celebratio sacrificij propitiatorij Christi. Tandem vocata est missa, ab oblatione, à dictioribus missa in vsum publicam, quæ de perum, vel à dimissione cœtus post λειτουργίαν reinfra. Nos appellatione in scriptura tradita Cœnam Domini vocamus.
units.tr: First we shall see by what names the Lord's Supper is called; afterwards we shall define what it is. This action, or rite, instituted by Christ before his death, is called the Lord's Supper from the circumstance of its first institution, which took place during a meal. The Church has changed this circumstance of time, as it was free to do. For by accident, that is, on account of the paschal lamb, which by law was to be eaten between the two evenings and was to be abolished by this new sacrament, it came about that Christ instituted this rite in the evening, at the time of supper, rather than in the morning or at midday. It is also called by Paul "the table of the Lord." Then it was called synaxis [συνάξις], from the assembly of the Church, because in celebrating the Supper some should gather, many or few, or indeed the whole Church. For at the first action all the disciples were present, and it is said to them: "Take this and divide it among you. Drink of this, all of you." It is necessary, therefore, that there were several there. This also appears from the repeated institution by the Apostle: "When you come together in one place, it is not to eat the Lord's Supper." And at the end he adds: "So, my brothers, when you come together to eat, wait for one another." That many ought to gather to celebrate the Supper, the purpose which the Apostle assigns to it makes clear: that it is a symbol and bond of love: "Since we, though many, are one bread, one body." It is also called eucharist [εὐχαριστία], because it is a rite of thanksgiving. The Fathers often call it "sacrifice," not "propitiatory" [ἱλαστική] or meritorious, as the Papists feign, but "eucharistic" [εὐχαριστικόν], because it is the solemn commemoration and celebration of Christ's propitiatory sacrifice. Lastly it was called mass, from the offering, or from the dismissal of the assembly after the liturgy [λειτουργία], when the people were dismissed; the word passed into public use. We, however, call it by the name handed down in Scripture: the Lord's Supper.

units.la: Definitio talis hac quæstione continetur. Cœna Domini, est instituta & mandata à Christo panis a finis distributio in sui memoriam, qua mihi & omnibus fidelibus Christus certò promittit & obsignat: primò, suum corpus pro me in cruce oblatum & sanguinem suum pro me effusum esse, tam verè, quàm oculis meis video, panem Domini mihi frangi & calicem mihi distribui. Deinde, se suo illo corpore crucifixo, & sanguine illo effuso, tam certo animam meam pascere ad vitam æternam, quàm certo meum corpus pascitur pane & calice Domini, ex manu ministri sumptis, quæ mihi tanquam certa corporis & sanguinis Christi sigilla porriguntur.
units.tr: The definition is contained in this question as follows. The Lord's Supper is the distribution of bread and cup, instituted and commanded by Christ, in remembrance of himself, by which Christ assures and seals to me and to all the faithful with certainty: first, that his body was offered for me on the cross and his blood shed for me, as truly as I see with my eyes the bread of the Lord broken for me and the cup distributed to me. Second, that by that crucified body and that shed blood he feeds my soul to eternal life as surely as my body is fed by the bread and cup of the Lord, received from the hand of the minister, which are held out to me as sure seals of the body and blood of Christ.

units.tr: Briefly:

units.la: Quaest. LXXV.
units.tr: Question LXXV.

units.la: Breuius hoc modo: Coena Domini est distributio & sumptio panis & vini, mandata à Christo fidelibus, vt his symbolis testentur, se corpus suum pro eis morti tradidisse, & sanguinem effudisse, hæcque eis dare edenda & bibenda in cibum ac potum vitæ æternæ, & se velle in eis habitare, eosque alere & viuificare in æternum.
units.tr: Briefly, in this way: the Lord's Supper is the distribution and reception of bread and wine, commanded by Christ to the faithful, so that by these symbols they may testify that he delivered his body to death for them and shed his blood, and that he gives these things to them to eat and drink as food and drink of eternal life, and that he wishes to dwell in them, and to nourish and quicken them forever.

units.la: Constat igitur hoc sacramentum ritu, & promissione ritui annexa. Ritus ac signa sunt panis fractus & manducatus, vinum distributum & sumtum: seu, panis fractio & manducatio, vini distributio & sumtio. Promissio ritui annexa: Hoc est corpus meum, pro vobis traditum. Hoc est sanguis meus pro vobis effusus in remissionem peccatorum: declarat rem ritu significatam, eamque sumentibus applicat in vsu legitimo: crucifixum Christi corpus, effusum Christi sanguinem, eorumque manducationem & haustionem, hoc est, vnionem nostri cum Christo per fidem, qua ipsius & omnium beneficiorum eius participes facti, ex eo, vt palmites ex vite, vitam æternam haurimus. De hac κοινωνία nostri cum Christo non sola promissio, sed etiam analogia signi & rei signatæ nos admonet. Analogia enim signi & rei externæ duo nobis proponit potissimum, sacrificium Christi, & κοινωνίαν cum Christo: quia non tantum panis frangitur, sed etiam nobis ad edendum datur. Fractio panis est pars cæremoniæ instituta: quia rei externæ respondet pars rei significatæ, fractio seu laceratio corporis Christi in cruce, de qua significatione Paulus testatur: Hoc est corpus meum, quod pro vobis frangitur. Vini separatio à pane significat mortis violentiam, qua sanguis eius à corpore diuulsus est.
units.tr: This sacrament therefore consists of a rite and of a promise attached to the rite. The rite and signs are the bread broken and eaten, and the wine distributed and drunk; or, the breaking and eating of the bread, the distribution and drinking of the wine. The promise attached to the rite is: "This is my body, which is given for you. This is my blood, which is shed for you for the forgiveness of sins." It declares the thing signified by the rite, and applies it to those who receive it in lawful use: the crucified body of Christ, the shed blood of Christ, and their eating and drinking, that is, our union with Christ through faith, by which, made partakers of him and of all his benefits, we draw eternal life from him as branches draw life from the vine. Concerning this communion [κοινωνία] of ourselves with Christ, not only the promise but also the analogy between the sign and the thing signified admonishes us. For the analogy between the outward sign and the thing signified sets before us chiefly two things: the sacrifice of Christ, and our communion [κοινωνίαν] with Christ. For the bread is not only broken but also given to us to eat. The breaking of the bread is a part of the ceremony instituted, because a part of the thing signified corresponds to the outward thing: the breaking or laceration of Christ's body on the cross, of which signification Paul bears witness: "This is my body, which is broken for you." The separation of the wine from the bread signifies the violence of death, by which his blood was torn from his body.

units.la: II. Quid sint fines Coenæ Domini.
units.tr: II. What are the ends of the Lord's Supper.

units.la: Fines, propter quos instituta est Coena Domini, sunt:
units.tr: The ends for which the Lord's Supper was instituted are these:

units.la: 1. Vt sit confirmatio fidei, seu, testificatio certissima communionis & vnionis nostræ cum Christo: quia Christus per hæc signa nobis restatur, quod ipse tam vere suo corpore & sanguine nos ad vitam æternam pascat, quam vere symbola è manu ministri accipimus: atque hæc testificatio dirigitur ad vnumquemque, vera fide symbola percipientem: Sic enim symbola è manu ministri accipimus, quasi ea ipse Dominus sua manu nobis porrigeret. Vnde & Christus dicitur plures baptizasse, quam Iohannes, cum id faceret per discipulos.
units.tr: 1. That it be a confirmation of faith, or a most certain testimony of our communion and union with Christ: because Christ, through these signs, assures us that he feeds us to eternal life with his body and blood as truly as we receive the symbols from the hand of the minister. And this testimony is directed to each one who receives the symbols with true faith. For thus we receive the symbols from the hand of the minister, as if the Lord himself held them out to us with his own hand. Hence also Christ is said to have baptized more than John, though he did so through his disciples.

units.la: 2. Vt sit testificatio nostra erga Christum & Ecclesiam, seu publica confessio fidei, & solennis gratiarum actio atque obligatio nostri, ad perpetuam gratitudinem, & celebrationem huius beneficii. De vtroque sine dictum est: Hoc facite in mei recordationem.
units.tr: 2. That it be our testimony toward Christ and the Church, that is, a public confession of faith, and a solemn thanksgiving and obligation of ourselves to perpetual gratitude and to the celebration of this benefit. Of both things it was said: "Do this in remembrance of me."
John 4. 1.

units.la: Luc. 22. 19. Et: Quotiescunque comederitis de pane isto, & biberitis de poculo isto, mortem Domini annunciate, donec veniat. Haec recordatio & commemoratio est primum ipsa fides in corde: deinde publica confessio & gratiarum actio.
units.tr: Luke 22. 19. "And: as often as you eat this bread and drink this cup, you proclaim the death of the Lord until he comes." This remembrance and commemoration is, first, faith itself in the heart; second, public confession and thanksgiving.

units.la: 3. Vt sit publica distinctio, seu nota discernens Ecclesiam ab aliis omnibus gentibus & sectis. Dominus enim discipulis suis, & non aliis, coenam suam instituit.
units.tr: 3. That it be a public distinction, or a mark distinguishing the Church from all other nations and sects. For the Lord instituted his Supper for his disciples, and not for others.

units.la: 4. Vt sit vinculum dilectionis: quoniam coena testatur, omnes legitimè eam sumentes, fieri membra unius corporis sub uno capite Christo: Quoniam unus panis unum corpus multi sumus: quia omnes de uno pane participamus. Membra autem eiusdem corporis se mutuò diligunt.
units.tr: 4. That it be a bond of love: since the Supper testifies that all who receive it lawfully become members of one body under one head, Christ: "Since we, though many, are one bread, one body, for we all partake of one bread." Members of the same body, moreover, love one another.

units.la: 5. Vt sit vinculum congressuum publicorum Ecclesiae: quia coena est instituta, ut fiat ac peragatur in congregatione, sive magna, sive parua. Ideo vocatur συναξις: & Christus praecipit: Bibite ex hoc omnes. Paulus item: Cùm convenitis ad vescendum, alij alios exspectate.
units.tr: 5. That it be a bond of public assemblies of the Church: since the Supper was instituted to be done and celebrated in a congregation, whether large or small. Therefore it is called synaxis [συνάξις], and Christ commands: "Drink of this, all of you." Paul likewise: "When you come together to eat, wait for one another."

units.la: Ex his colligitur, coenam Domini non debere privatim ab uno solo celebrari. 1. Quia est communio, & communionis symbolum. Priuata autem coena non communio. 2. Quia est solennis εὐχαριστία seu gratiarum actio: & omnes debemus Deo gratias agere. Qui ergo se judicat indignum, ut cum aliis communicer, fatetur, se non esse idoneum, ad gratias cum aliis Deo agendas. 3. Quia Christus cum suis beneficiis non est priuatim unius, sed omnium communis. Priuata igitur communio ex publico bono facit priuatum. 4. Quia Christus convocavit ad coenam omnes suos domesticos, etiam Judam. Ergo communio priuata est contra institutum Christi. 5. Denique, quod quidam à coena abstinent, vel eam usque in morbum differunt, fit haud dubiè ex malo quodam motu: vel quia cum aliis communicare nolunt, vel quia putant se nunquam satis dignos. Atqui omnes satis digni sunt, qui credunt, se morte CHRISTI ab aeterna damnatione liberatos esse, & in pietate proficere cupiunt. In summa: cùm ab uno tantum coena sumitur, id sit contra usum, appellationem, institutionem & naturam huius sacramenti.
units.tr: From these things it is gathered that the Lord's Supper ought not to be celebrated privately by one person alone. First, because it is a communion and a symbol of communion, and a private supper is not a communion. Second, because it is a solemn eucharist, that is, thanksgiving, and all of us ought to give thanks to God. Whoever therefore judges himself unworthy to communicate with others confesses that he is not fit to give thanks to God together with others. Third, because Christ, with his benefits, belongs not privately to one person but is common to all. A private communion therefore turns a public good into a private one. Fourth, because Christ invited to supper all his household, even Judas. Therefore private communion is contrary to the institution of Christ. Fifth, finally, that some abstain from the Supper, or defer it until sickness, arises undoubtedly from some evil motion: either because they are unwilling to communicate with others, or because they think they are never worthy enough. Yet all are worthy enough who believe that they have been freed from eternal damnation by the death of Christ, and desire to make progress in piety. In sum: since the Supper is received by one person alone, this is contrary to the custom, the name, the institution and the nature of this sacrament.

units.la: Obiectio. Christus ponit principalem finem coenae ἀνάμνησιν sui; hoc facite in mei recordationem. Ergo principalis finis non debet poni confirmatio fidei. Resp. A positione totius ad negationem partis, non valet consequentia. Recordatio Christi est totum, complectens ἀνάμνησιν fidei, & ἀνάμνησιν gratitudinis, tanquam partes. Est igitur collectio talis, ac si dicas. Petrus est homo: ergo non est corpus. Immò per inuersionem sic infero: quia est ἀνάμνησις, ideo est confirmatio fidei. Si enim Christus hanc cæremoniam nobis proponit in sui ἀνάμνησιν, utique proponit eam in confirmationem fidei, cùm fides nihil sit aliud, quàm fidelis recordatio Christi & beneficiorum eius. Inst. Spiritus sanctus confirmat nostram fidem. Ergo non cœna. Resp. A positione causæ principalis, ad remotionem instrumentalis, non valet consequentia. Vt si dicas. Deus nos pascit & nutrit: ergo non panis. Nam Spiritus sanctus confirmat nostram fidem, sed per verbum & sacramenta: sicut Deus nos pascit & nutrit, sed per panem.
units.tr: Objection. Christ names the chief end of the Supper as his remembrance [ἀνάμνησιν]: "Do this in remembrance of me." Therefore the chief end should not be stated as the confirmation of faith. Answer. The inference from the whole to the denial of a part is not valid. The remembrance of Christ is the whole, which comprises the remembrance of faith and the remembrance of gratitude as its parts. So the argument is like saying: "Peter is a man; therefore he is not a body." Indeed, I infer the reverse: because it is a remembrance, therefore it is a confirmation of faith. For if Christ sets this ceremony before us for his remembrance, he certainly sets it before us for the confirmation of faith, since faith is nothing other than the faithful remembrance of Christ and of his benefits. Objection. The Holy Spirit confirms our faith; therefore it is not the Supper. Answer. The inference from the positing of the principal cause to the removal of the instrumental cause is not valid. It is as if you said: "God feeds and nourishes us; therefore it is not bread." For the Holy Spirit confirms our faith, but through the Word and the sacraments, just as God feeds and nourishes us, but through bread.

units.la: III. Quid Cœna à Baptismo differat?
units.tr: III. How the Supper differs from Baptism?

units.la: Etsi eadem beneficia nobis porriguntur & obsignantur in baptismo & in cœna, spiritualis scilicet κοινωνία Christi, & totum salutationis beneficium, de quo dicit Apostolus: Per unum Spiritum nos omnes in unum corpus baptizati sumus, & omnes una potione potati sumus in unum spiritum: tamen varia & manifesta sunt horum sacramentorum discrimina. Differunt enim 1. Cæremoniis seu ritibus externis. 2. Cæremoniarum significationibus. Etsi enim eadem est Christi participatio, ablutio peccatorum per sanguinem Christi, quæ fit in baptismo, & manducatio ac haustio corporis & sanguinis Christi, quæ fit in cœna: tamen illa significatur mersione corporis in aquam baptismi: hæc manducatione ac haustione panis & vini pingitur & obsignatur in cœna. Ideo res sacramentorum non est diuersa: quia idem est, sanguine Christi ablui, & sanguinem Christi bibere. Modus autem significandi vnam eamdemque rem, est diuersus. 3. Finibus propriis. Baptismus est signum eiusdem fœderis continuandi: seu, est signum regenerationis & ingressus in Ecclesiam & fœdus Dei: cœna signum est nutritionis, mansionis & conseruationis eorum, qui semel in Ecclesiam sunt ingressi. Oportet hominem renasci spiritu: & huius renascentiæ signum est baptismus: renatum etiam oportet nutriri corpore & sanguine Christi, cuius nutritionis signum est cœna. Breuiter: In baptismo de receptione in ecclesiam: in cœna de conseruatione & incremento beneficiorum nos Deus confirmat. Interim est vnus & idem Christus, qui nos ad vitam æternam regenerat & nutrit. 4. Modo vtendi. Ad baptismi legitimum vsum sufficit regeneratio: ideo commodè petit omnibus, quos Ecclesia habet pro regeneratis: vt sunt omnes adulti profitentes fidem & pœnitentiam, & infantes in ecclesia nati: sed cœna requirit etiam probationem fidei sumendem: commemorationem mortis Domini, & gratiarum actionem: Hoc facite in mei recordationem. Mortem Domini annunciatis, donec. donec veniat. Probet quisque seipsum, &c. Baptismus igitur toti Ecclesiæ, hoc est, tam infantibus, quàm adultis debetur: cœna solis adultis, qui seipsos probare & mortem Domini annunciare possunt. §. Ordine sumtionis. Baptismus debet præcedere, cœna sequi: hoc est, cœna non debet conferri, nisi prius baptizatis, & quidem non illico, sed postquam ediderint confessionem fidei & pœnitentiæ. Ideo in veteri ecclesia, finita concione, ante λεγόμενοι, hoc τουχίων, dimittebantur excommunicati, item ἐπιζεύμενοι, hoc est, obsessi, & κατηχούμενοι, hoc est, discentes capita Christianæ fidei, & vel nondum baptizati, vel baptizati quidem in infantia, nondum tamen fundamenta religionis satis intelligentes. Sic olim non circumcisi non admittebantur ad sacrificia & cæremonias. Quod si baptizati priusquam fidei & pœnitentiæ confessionem ediderint, nondum ad cœnam sunt admittendi: multo minus admittendi sunt, qui baptizati porcorū & canum instar viuunt.
units.tr: Although the same benefits are offered and sealed to us in baptism and in the Supper, namely the spiritual communion [κοινωνία] with Christ and the whole benefit of salvation, of which the Apostle says: "By one Spirit we were all baptized into one body, and we have all drunk of one drink into one Spirit," nevertheless the differences between these sacraments are various and evident. They differ: (1) in their ceremonies, or external rites; (2) in the meanings of their ceremonies. For although the participation in Christ is the same, and the washing away of sins through the blood of Christ, which takes place in baptism, is the same as the eating and drinking of the body and blood of Christ, which takes place in the Supper, yet the former is signified by the immersion of the body in the water of baptism, while the latter is depicted and sealed in the Supper by the eating and drinking of bread and wine. So the thing signified by the sacraments is not different, for to be washed in the blood of Christ and to drink the blood of Christ are the same; but the manner of signifying one and the same thing is different. (3) In their proper ends. Baptism is the sign of the covenant to be continued, that is, the sign of regeneration, of entrance into the Church and of the covenant of God; the Supper is the sign of nourishment, of abiding and of preservation for those who have once entered the Church. A man must be born again of the Spirit, and the sign of this rebirth is baptism; the one who is reborn must also be nourished with the body and blood of Christ, and the sign of this nourishment is the Supper. In brief: in baptism God confirms us in reception into the Church; in the Supper, in the preservation and increase of the benefits. Yet it is one and the same Christ who regenerates us to eternal life and nourishes us. (4) In their manner of use. For the lawful use of baptism, regeneration is sufficient; therefore it is rightly given to all whom the Church holds to be regenerate, namely all adults who profess faith and repentance, and infants born in the Church. But the Supper also requires a proof of the faith with which it is to be received: the remembrance of the Lord's death and the giving of thanks. "Do this in remembrance of me." "You proclaim the Lord's death until he comes." "Let each man examine himself," etc. Baptism, therefore, is owed to the whole Church, that is, to infants as well as to adults; the Supper only to adults, who can examine themselves and proclaim the Lord's death. Concerning the order of reception: baptism must precede and the Supper follow; that is, the Supper must not be given except to those who have first been baptized, and even then not at once, but after they have made a confession of faith and repentance. Therefore in the ancient Church, when the sermon was finished, before the so-called [λεγόμενοι] hearers, that is, the hearers (τουχίων), were dismissed the excommunicated, likewise the possessed, that is, those troubled by evil spirits, and the catechumens, that is, those learning the heads of the Christian faith, who were either not yet baptized or were baptized in infancy but did not yet understand the foundations of religion sufficiently. Thus formerly the uncircumcised were not admitted to the sacrifices and ceremonies. But if those who have been baptized do not yet make a confession of faith and repentance, they are not yet to be admitted to the Supper; much less are those to be admitted who live like swine and dogs though baptized.

units.la: 6. Vsurpatione: cœnam sæpe debemus sumere: quia sæpe debemus commemorare mortem Domini. Ideo enim est instituta, ut fiat in ea publica commemoratio & annunciatio mortis Domini. Fidei item confirmatio de æterna duratione fœderis, quæ fit per cœnam, sæpe est necessaria. Ideo cœna sæpe est iteranda; sicut & pascha propter hanc causam quotannis iterabatur. Baptismus verò non debet iterari: sicut nec circumcisio olim iterabatur: tum quia est signum receptionis in ecclesiam & fœdus Dei. Fœdus enim semel initum non fit irritum, sed semper manet ratum agentibus pœnitentiam: quia dona & vocatio Dei sunt ἀμεταμέλητα. Neque enim pœnitentia post lapsus initur nouum fœdus, sed priusinitum reuocatur. Hinc de cœna dicitur: Hoc facite, quotiescunque ederitis panem hunc, & poculum hoc biberitis, in mei commemorationem. Quotiescunque ederitis panem hunc, & poculum hoc biberitis, mortem Domini annunciabitis, donec veniat. De baptismo: Quotquot baptizati sumus in Iesum Christum, in mortem eius baptizati sumus. Qui crediderit, & baptizatus fuerit, seruabitur.
units.tr: 6. By frequency of use: we ought often to take the Supper, because we ought often to remember the death of the Lord. For it was instituted so that in it there might be a public remembrance and proclamation of the Lord's death. Likewise the confirmation of faith concerning the eternal duration of the covenant, which takes place through the Supper, is often necessary. Therefore the Supper is to be repeated often, just as the Passover was also repeated every year for this reason. Baptism, however, ought not to be repeated, just as circumcision was not repeated formerly; both because it is the sign of reception into the Church and of the covenant of God. For a covenant once entered is not made void, but always remains valid for those who repent, because the gifts and calling of God are irrevocable [ἀμεταμέλητα]. For repentance after a fall does not enter into a new covenant, but the earlier one is renewed. Hence it is said of the Supper: "As often as you eat this bread and drink this cup, do it in remembrance of me. As often as you eat this bread and drink this cup, you proclaim the Lord's death until he comes." Of baptism: "As many of us as were baptized into Jesus Christ were baptized into his death." "He who believes and is baptized shall be saved."

units.la: QVÆSTIO LXXVI.
units.tr: QUESTION 76.

units.la: Quid est crucifixum corpus Christi edere, & fusum sanguinem bibere: illisque pasci?
units.tr: What is it to eat the crucified body of Christ and to drink his shed blood, and to be fed by them?

units.la: RESPONSIO.
units.tr: ANSWER.

units.la: Est non tantum totam passionem & mortem Christi, certa animi fiducia amplecti, ac per id remissionem peccatorum & vitam æternam adipisci: sed etiam per Spiritum ritum sanctum, qui simul in Christo & nobis habitat, ita sacrosancto eius corpori magis ac magis vniri: vt quamuis ipse in cœlo, nos verò in terra simus, nihilominus tamen caro simus de carne eius, & os de ossibus eius: atque vt omnia corporis membra ab vna anima, sic nos vno eodemq; Spiritu viuificemur, & gubernemur.
units.tr: It is not only to embrace the whole passion and death of Christ with a certain confidence of mind, and thereby to obtain the forgiveness of sins and eternal life; it is also, through the Holy Spirit, who dwells at once in Christ and in us, to be joined more and more to his most holy body, so that although he is in heaven and we are on earth, we are nevertheless flesh of his flesh and bone of his bones; and just as the members of the body are quickened and governed by one soul, so we are quickened and governed by one and the same Spirit.

a John 6:35, 40, 47, 48, 50, 51, 53, 54. b John 6:55, 56. c Colossians 3:1. Acts 3:21. 1 Corinthians 11:26. d Ephesians 5:30 and 3:16. 1 Corinthians 6:15. 1 John 3:24 and 4:13. e John 6:57 and 15:1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6. Ephesians 4:15, 16.

units.la: EXPLICATIO,
units.tr: EXPLANATION.

units.la: Pertinet ad declarationem rei signatæ sacramenti. Manducatio carnis, & bibitio sanguinis Christi, non est corporalis, sed spiritualis: & complectitur 1. fidem passionis & sanguinis Christi, 2. Acceptionem remissionis peccatorum, & vitæ æternæ per fidem. 3. Vnionem nostri cum Christo per Spiritum sanctum in Christo & in nobis habitantem, 4. Beneficium viuificationis per eundem Spiritum. Carnem igitur Christi manducare, & sanguinem Christi bibere, est credere, nos propter Christi meritum recipi à Deo in gratiam, & hac fide accipere remissionem peccatorum, seu, reconciliari Deo, & Filium Dei Λόγον, qui naturam humanam assumtam sibi vniuit personaliter, in nobis habitare, & nos sibi ac naturæ suæ assumtæ copulare, effuso in nos Spiritu sancto, per quem nos regenerat, & restituit in nobis lucem, iustiuiam & vitam æternam, qualis lucet in natura eius assumta. Breviter: Manducare est 1. credere: seu, fide accipere remissionem peccatorum, 2. vniri Christo, & participem fieri vitæ Christi: seu, Christo fieri conformem per Spiritum sanctum, qui eadem in Christo, & in nobis operatur.
units.tr: This pertains to the declaration of the thing signified by the sacrament. The eating of the flesh and the drinking of the blood of Christ are not bodily but spiritual, and they comprise: (1) faith in the passion and blood of Christ; (2) the receiving of the forgiveness of sins and of eternal life through faith; (3) the union of us with Christ through the Holy Spirit, who dwells in Christ and in us; (4) the benefit of quickening through the same Spirit. To eat the flesh of Christ and to drink the blood of Christ, therefore, is to believe that we are received into grace by God on account of the merit of Christ, and by this faith to receive the forgiveness of sins, or to be reconciled to God; and that the Son of God, the Word [Logos], who personally united to himself the human nature he assumed, dwells in us and joins us to himself and to his assumed nature, the Spirit being poured out upon us, through whom he regenerates us and restores in us light, righteousness and eternal life, such as shines in his assumed nature. In brief: to eat is (1) to believe, that is, to receive by faith the forgiveness of sins; (2) to be united to Christ and to become a partaker of the life of Christ; that is, to be made conformed to Christ through the Holy Spirit, who works the same things in Christ and in us.

units.la: Hæc manducatio est κοινωνία illa nostra cum Christo, quam scriptura docet, & quam in symbolo profitemur: nempe vnio spiritualis cum Christo, qualis est membrorum cum capite, palmitum cum vite. Hanc manducationem suæ carnis docet Christus Johan. 6. & confirmat in cœna externis signis. Sic manducationem exposuerunt veteres, Eusebius, Nazianzenus, Nyssenus, Hilarius, Augustinus, &c. Non igitur stabilitur ex verbis cœnæ (quæ manducationem corporis Christi promittunt) transsubstantiatio papistica, vel præsentia corporalis, aut manducatio oralis corporis Christi in pane: quam multi defendunt.
units.tr: This eating is that fellowship [koinonia] of ours with Christ which Scripture teaches and which we profess in the creed: namely, a spiritual union with Christ, such as that of the members with the head, or of the branches with the vine. Christ teaches this eating of his flesh in John 6, and confirms it in the Supper by external signs. The ancients expounded eating in this way: Eusebius, Nazianzen, Nyssen, Hilary, Augustine, etc. Therefore the Papist transubstantiation, or the bodily presence, or the oral eating of the body of Christ in the bread, which many defend, is not established from the words of the Supper (which promise the eating of the body of Christ).

units.la: QVÆSTIO LXXVII.
units.tr: QUESTION 77.

units.la: Quo loco promisit Christus, se credentibus tam certò corpus & sanguinem suum sic edendum & bibendum daturum, quàm fractam hunc panem edunt, & poculum hoc bibunt?
units.tr: At what place did Christ promise that he would give his body and blood to believers to be eaten and drunk as surely as they eat this broken bread and drink this cup?

units.la: RESPONSIO.
units.tr: ANSWER.

units.la: In institutione cœnæ, cuius hæc sunt verba a: Dominus noster Iesus Christus, in ea nocte, qua proditus est, accepit panem, & gratiis actis, fregit ac dixit: Accipite, hoc est corpus meum, quod pro vobis frangitur: hoc facite in mei recordationem. Itidem & poculum, postquam cœnassent, dicens: Hoc poculum est novum fœdus per meum sanguinem. Hoc facite, quotiescunque biberitis, in mei recordationem. Quotiescunq; enim ederitis panem hunc, & poculum hoc biberitis, mortem Domini annunciate, donec veniret. Hæc promissio à Paulo repetitur cùm inquit b: Poculum gratiarum actionis, quo gratias agimus, nonne communio est sanguinis Christi? Panis, quem frangimus, nonne communio est corporis Christi? Quoniam unus panis unum corpus multi sumus. Nam omnes unius panis participes sumus.
units.tr: In the institution of the Supper, whose words are these a: Our Lord Jesus Christ, on the night in which he was betrayed, took bread, and having given thanks, broke it and said: Take, this is my body, which is broken for you; do this in remembrance of me. Likewise also the cup, after supper, saying: This cup is the new covenant through my blood. Do this, as often as you drink it, in remembrance of me. For as often as you eat this bread and drink this cup, you proclaim the Lord's death until he comes. This promise is repeated by Paul when he says b: Is not the cup of thanksgiving, over which we give thanks, a communion in the blood of Christ? Is not the bread which we break a communion in the body of Christ? Because there is one bread, we who are many are one body, for we all partake of the one bread.

units.la: EXPLICATIO.
units.tr: EXPLANATION.

units.la: Institutio cœnæ Domini confirmat salutarem communionem corporis & sanguinis Christi. Sensus igitur verborum institutionis diligenter considerandus est. Matthæus, Marcus & Lucas institutionem præcipuè describunt: & præter hos etiam Apostolus ad Corinthios. Verba sunt:
units.tr: The institution of the Lord's Supper confirms the saving communion of the body and blood of Christ. The sense of the words of institution therefore needs to be carefully considered. Matthew, Mark and Luke describe the institution most fully, and besides these the Apostle to the Corinthians also. The words are:

units.la: MATTAEVS c.26. v.26. &c.
units.tr: MATTHEW ch. 26, v. 26, etc.

units.la: Vescentibus illis Iesus accepit panem, & cùm benedixisset (εὐλογήσας) fregit, & dedit discipulis suis, dicens: Accipite, comedite, Hoc est corpus meum, &c. Et accepto poculo gratias egit (εὐχαριστήσας) & dedit illis, dicens: Bibite ex hoc omnes: Hoc enim est sanguis meus novi testamenti, quipro multis effunditur, in remissionem peccatorum.
units.tr: While they were eating, Jesus took bread, and when he had blessed it [εὐλογήσας] he broke it and gave it to his disciples, saying: Take, eat; this is my body, etc. And taking the cup, when he had given thanks [εὐχαριστήσας], he gave it to them, saying: Drink from it, all of you; for this is my blood of the new testament, which is poured out for many for the forgiveness of sins.

units.la: MARCVS c.14. v.22. &c.
units.tr: MARK ch. 14, v. 22, etc.

units.la: Edentibus illis, sumpto pane cùm benedixisset (εὐλογήσας) fregit & dedit illis ac dixit: Accipite, comedite, Hoc est corpus meum. Et accepto poculo, cùm gratias egisset (εὐχαριστήσας) dedit illis: & biberunt ex eo omnes, & dixit illis: Hoc est sanguis meus novi testamenti, qui pro multis effunditur.
units.tr: While they were eating, he took bread, and when he had blessed it [εὐλογήσας] he broke it and gave it to them and said: Take, eat; this is my body. And taking the cup, when he had given thanks [εὐχαριστήσας], he gave it to them, and they all drank from it, and he said to them: This is my blood of the new testament, which is poured out for many.

units.la: LVCAS c.22. v.19. &c.
units.tr: LUKE ch. 22, v. 19, etc.

units.la: Et accepto pane, cùm gratias egisset (εὐχαριστήσας) fregit & dedit eis, dicens: Hoc est corpus meum, quod pro vobis dabitur. Hoc facite in mei recordationem. Similiter & poculum postquam cœnatum, dicens: Hoc poculum est novum testamentum in meo sanguine, quipro vobis effunditur.
units.tr: And taking bread, when he had given thanks [εὐχαριστήσας], he broke it and gave it to them, saying: This is my body, which is given for you. Do this in remembrance of me. Likewise also the cup after supper, saying: This cup is the new testament in my blood, which is poured out for you.

units.la: PAVLVS 1 Cor.11. v.23.
units.tr: PAUL, 1 Cor. ch. 11, v. 23.

units.la: Ego à Domino accepi, quod & tradidi vobis, quoniam Dominus Iesus ea nocte, qua prodebatur, accepit panem, & postquam gratias egisset, (εὐχαριστήσας) fregit ac dixit: Accipite, edite, Hoc est corpus meum, quod pro vobis frangitur. Hoc facite in mei commemorationem. Similiter & poculum peracta cœna, dicens: Hoc poculum est novum testamentum in meo sanguine: Hoc facite, quotiescunque feceritis, in mei commemorationem. Quotiescunque enim ederitis panem hunc, & poculum hoc biberitis, mortem Domini annunciate, donec veniat.
units.tr: I received from the Lord what I also delivered to you: that the Lord Jesus, on the night in which he was betrayed, took bread, and after he had given thanks [εὐχαριστήσας], he broke it and said: Take, eat; this is my body, which is broken for you. Do this in remembrance of me. Likewise also the cup, after supper was finished, saying: This cup is the new testament in my blood. Do this, as often as you do it, in remembrance of me. For as often as you eat this bread and drink this cup, you proclaim the Lord's death until he comes.

units.la: Dominus Iesus.] Hic est author, à quo vocatur cœna Domini. Videndum ergo, quid hic Dominus fecerit, dixerit, & præceperit, vt præclare monet Cyprianus: Si solus Christus audiendus est, Lib.1. epist.3 non debemus attendere, quid aliquis ante nos faciendum putauerit, sed quid, qui ante omnes est, Christus prior fecerit.
units.tr: The Lord Jesus.] He is the author from whom the Supper is called the Lord's. We must therefore consider what the Lord did, said and commanded here, as Cyprian rightly warns: If Christ alone is to be heard, we ought not to consider what anyone before us thought should be done, but what Christ, who is before all, first did.

units.la: Ea nocte, qua proditus est.] Hæc circumstantia additur, vt scia Christum voluisse in vltima cœna paschali cœnam suam instituisse.
units.tr: On the night in which he was betrayed.] This circumstance is added so that you may know that Christ willed to institute his Supper at the last Passover meal.

units.la: instituere, vt ostenderet 1. veteribus sacrificiis jam finem imponi & se nouum substituere sacramentum, quod succederet & seru̇aretur deinceps, illo paschali abolito, quodq; idem significaret; excepto temporis discrimine. Nam pascha significabat Christum venturum & immolandum: Cœna vero significat Christum immolatum. Obiect. Atqui cum cœna institueretur, Christus erat immolandus. Resp. Jam tum instabat immolatio, & paucis post horis immolatus est: & debebat cœna deinceps significare Christum immolatum. 2. Vt maiorem attentionem & consideratio-nem causæ, quare institueret, in discipulis & in nobis excitaret; & admoneremur, quam serio velit Christus nobis commendari & maximè sectam esse hanc cœnam: cum nihil ante mortem, nisi maximè serium egerit. Ideo in ipso articulo mortis instituit, vt esset veluti testamentum & extrema testatoris voluntas. Breuiter. Hoc Paulus addit, vt sciamus, Christum instituisse hanc cœnam tanquam μνημόσυνον sui jam morituri.
units.tr: He instituted it, first, to show that an end was now being put to the old sacrifices and that he was substituting in their place a new sacrament, which would succeed them and be kept from then on, the Passover being abolished, and which signifies the same thing, except for the difference of time. For the Passover signified Christ who was to come and be sacrificed; the Supper signifies Christ already sacrificed. Objection: but when the Supper was instituted, Christ was still to be sacrificed. Reply: the immolation was already at hand, and he was sacrificed a few hours later; and the Supper was to signify Christ as sacrificed from then on. Second, so that he might awaken greater attention and consideration in the disciples and in us as to why he instituted it, and so that we may be reminded how earnestly Christ wishes this Supper to be commended to us, and above all held sacred, since he did nothing before his death except with the utmost seriousness. Therefore he instituted it at the very point of death, so that it would be like a testament and the last will of the testator. In brief: Paul adds this so that we may know that Christ instituted this Supper as a memorial [μνημόσυνον] of himself, who was now about to die.

units.la: Accepit panem. Panis erat ἄζυμος: infermentatus, cibarius; quali tunc vescebantur in conuiuio paschali, quod non admittebat fermentum. Per accidens concurrebat institutio cœnæ, & panis azymus. Hæc igitur panis qualitas propriè non pertinet ad cœnam: sicut nec vespera, sub quam est instituta: ideo non potest ex ea necessitas panis azymi vrgeri: nec voluit Christus certam rationem coquendi vel adhibendi panis ad cœnam suam præscribere. Interim panis cœnæ vsu differt à pane communi. Hic enim sumitur ad nutritionem corporis: ille ad nutritionem animæ, hoc est, ad confirmationem fidei, & vnionis cum Christo. Notandum verò, quod Christus dicitur panem è mensa accepisse, nempe manu. Non igitur accepit suum corpus: nec accepit corpus cum pane, vel in pane, vel sub pane, nisi sacramentaliter. Nam corpus eius non jacebat in mensa, sed accumbebat mensæ.
units.tr: He took bread. The bread was unleavened [ἄζυμος]: without leaven, ordinary bread, such as they then ate at the Passover feast, which did not admit leaven. The institution of the Supper and the unleavened bread happened to coincide. This quality of the bread therefore does not properly belong to the Supper, any more than the evening under which it was instituted does; so the necessity of unleavened bread cannot be pressed from it, nor did Christ wish to prescribe a fixed method of baking or preparing the bread for his Supper. Meanwhile the bread of the Supper differs in use from common bread. For the latter is taken for the nourishment of the body, the former for the nourishment of the soul, that is, for the strengthening of faith and of union with Christ. It should be noted, moreover, that Christ is said to have taken the bread from the table, namely with his hand. He therefore did not take his own body; nor did he take the body with the bread, or in the bread, or under the bread, except sacramentally. For his body was not lying on the table; it was reclining at the table.

units.la: Gratiis actis. Matthæus & Marcus de pane dicunt εὐλογήσας, de poculo εὐχαριστήσας, gratias agens. Lucas & Paulus etiam de pane dicunt εὐχαριστήσας, gratias agens. Idem ergo hic significat benedicere, & gratias agere: nec latet in hoc participio mysterium magicæ consecrationis pontificiæ. Christus igitur benedixit, hoc est, gratias egit, nempe Patri suo, non pani, pro benecficiis spiritualibus, hoc est, pro animarum saturitate, quod videlicet peracto jam officio suo in terris (vltimo eius actu tantum restante) aduenisset tempus moriendi pro redemptione electorum: & quod Patri ita hominum redemptio placuisset: vel quod paschate typico abolito, jam verum & significatum pascha esset exhibitum, & eius μνημόσυνον: Ecclesiæ sanciendum; vel denique pro admirabili collectione & conseruatione Ecclesiæ gratias egit.
units.tr: Having given thanks. Matthew and Mark say of the bread εὐλογήσας [blessed], and of the cup εὐχαριστήσας [giving thanks]. Luke and Paul also say εὐχαριστήσας of the bread. Therefore here to bless and to give thanks mean the same thing, and no mystery of the Papist magical consecration is hidden in this participle. Christ therefore blessed, that is, gave thanks, namely to his Father, not to the bread, for spiritual benefits, that is, for the satisfying of souls: that is, because his work on earth was now finished (only his last act remaining), the time had come to die for the redemption of the elect; and because it had pleased the Father that men should be redeemed in this way; or because the typical Passover was now abolished and the true and signified Passover had been made manifest, and its memorial was to be sanctioned for the Church; or finally, he gave thanks for the wonderful gathering and preservation of the Church.

units.la: Fregit.] Panem scilicet: quem de mensa acceptum in frusta comminuit: & inter multos distribuit: non aliud aliquid inuisibile in pane latens. Corpus suum non fregit, sed panem. Unde Paulus: Panis, quem frangimus. Vnum vero panem inter multos distribuit: quoniam unus panis unum corpus multi sumus.
units.tr: He broke. That is, the bread: which he took from the table, broke into pieces, and distributed among many, with nothing else invisible lying hidden in the bread. He did not break his body, but the bread. Hence Paul says: The bread which we break. But he distributed one bread among many: because there is one bread, we who are many are one body.

units.la: Hæc fuit una causa, cur panem frangeret, vt commodè inter plures distribueret. Fuit vero & alia causa potior mystica, cur frangeret, & fractum distribueret: vt repræsentaret 1. Passionis suæ dolores & corporis sui lacerationem ab anima in cruce. 2. [illegible, ~4 letters] multorum cum vno suo fracto corpore: & vinculum vnionis ac dilectionis mutuæ. Hanc posteriorem mysticam dilectionis causam indicauit Paulus, dicens: Hoc est corpus meum, quod pro vobis frangitur. Et: Panis, quem frangimus, nonne communio est corporis Christi? quoniam vnus panis vnum corpus multi sumus: quia omnes de vno pane participamus.
units.tr: This was one reason why he broke the bread, so that he might distribute it conveniently among several. But there was also another, weightier mystical reason why he broke it and distributed it broken: to represent first, the pains of his suffering and the laceration of his body from his soul on the cross; second, [illegible] of many with his one broken body, and the bond of union and mutual love. Paul pointed out this latter mystical reason of love, saying: This is my body, which is broken for you. And: The bread which we break, is it not a communion in the body of Christ? Because there is one bread, we who are many are one body, since we all partake of the one bread.

units.la: Est igitur fractio panis in cœna Domini non adiaphora cæremonia, sed ob mysticam hanc significationem necessaria & retinenda. 1. Propter Christi exemplum, qui panem fregit. 2. Propter eius mandatum: Hoc facite, nempe, quod ego feci. 3. Propter exemplum Apostolicæ Ecclesiæ, quæ panem fregit, & à ritu fractionis totam actionem denominauit κλᾶσιν τοῦ ἄρτου: fractionem panis. 4. Propter nostram consolationem, vt sciamus, corpus Domini tam certo pro nobis crucifixum esse: quam certo videmus panem nobis frangi. 5. Vt ex animis opinio transsubstantiationis, vel latentiæ corpusculi alicuius in pane.
units.tr: Therefore the breaking of bread in the Lord's Supper is not an indifferent ceremony, but because of this mystical signification it is necessary and to be retained. (1) On account of Christ's example, who broke bread. (2) On account of his command: Do this, namely, what I have done. (3) On account of the example of the apostolic Church, which broke bread and named the whole action from the rite of breaking: breaking the bread [κλᾶσιν τοῦ ἄρτου]: the breaking of bread. (4) For our comfort, so that we may know that the body of the Lord was crucified for us as surely as we see the bread broken for us. (5) So that the opinion of transubstantiation, or of some hidden little body in the bread, may be banished from minds.

units.la: Accipite, comedite.] Hoc mandatum pertinet ad discipulos, & ad totam Ecclesiam noui Testamenti. Vnde liquet, 1. Missam pontificiam, in qua sacrificulus nihil dat accipiendum & manducandum ecclesiæ, non esse cœnam Domini, sed epulum priuatum missifici, & histrionicum lusum. 2. Nos non debere otiosos esse cœnæ spectatores, sed eam accipere & manducare. 3. Cœnam Domini non esse celebrandam, nisi in cœtu aliquo, vbi sint accipientes & manducantes. 4. Denique cœnam esse signum gratiæ ex parte Dei, exhibentis nobis certa beneficia fide accipienda, sicut symbola manu & ore accipimus.
units.tr: Take, eat.] This command pertains to the disciples and to the whole Church of the New Testament. From this it is clear that (1) the Papist Mass, in which the sacrificing priest gives nothing for the Church to take and eat, is not the Lord's Supper but a private feast of the celebrant and a theatrical show. (2) We ought not to be idle spectators of the Supper, but to take it and eat it. (3) The Lord's Supper is not to be celebrated unless in some assembly where there are those who take and eat. (4) Finally, the Supper is a sign of grace on God's part, offering us certain benefits to be received by faith, just as we receive tokens with the hand and the mouth.

units.la: Hoc est corpus meum, quod pro vobis, &c.] τοῦτο, Hoc, id est, hic τοῦτο, hoc, panis. At fuisset dicendum τοῦτος, non τοῦτο. Resp. τοῦτο, id est, panem notas haeres, quam habeo in manibus: ea vero erat panis. Sic esse intelligendum, constat his rationibus. 1. Christus nihil nisi panem accepit, panem fregit, fractum panem dedit discipulis mandendum. 2. Paulus disertè dicit: Panis, quem frangimus, est communio
units.tr: This is my body, which is given for you, etc.] Touto [τοῦτο], this, that is, here this [τοῦτο], bread. But it should have been said touton [τοῦτος], not touto [τοῦτο]. Answer: touto [τοῦτο] refers to the bread which I hold in my hands; and that was bread. That this is how it must be understood is clear from these reasons. (1) Christ took nothing but bread, broke the bread, and gave the broken bread to the disciples to eat. (2) Paul states plainly: The bread which we break is a communion

units.la: corporis Christi. 3. De vino dicitur: Hoc poculum est nouum illud testamentum, in sanguine meo. Eodem igitur modo dicitur: Hoc, id est, hic panis est corpus meum, quod pro vobis frangitur, ac traditur in mortem. Haec est literalis sententia, quae proprie accepta non potest aliter intelligi, quam sic: substantia huius panis est substantia corporis mei. Sed sic intelligere verba Domini absurdum est. Substantia enim panis est massa inanimis, ex tritico pista, neque unita λόγῳ, persónaliter, neque pro nobis crucifixa. Substantia vero corpotis Christi est animata, ex virgine nata, persónaliter vnita λόγῳ, & pro nobis tradita in mortem. Hoc igitur sensu literali panis non potest esse vel dici corpus Christi. Proinde cogitandum est, Christum sic loquendo instituisse Sacramentum. Panem igitur vocat corpus suum pro nobis traditum, non literaliter, sed sacramentaliter, hoc est, panem dicit esse sacramentum, siue sacrum signum sui corporis pro nobis traditi, iuxta simplicissimam & verissimam explicationem Augustini capit. 12. contr. Adim. Non dubitauit Dominus dicere, Hoc est corpus meum, cum daret signum sui corporis. Absit vero vt credamus, Christum dicendo: Hoc est corpus meum, pane mutasse, vel mutare voluisse in corpus suum. Nam sic panis Eucharistiae non esset corpus Christi pro nobis traditum, sed esset corpus ex pane factum, quale non est pro nobis traditum. Absit etiam, vt credamus, Christum accipiendo panem, & dicendo: Hoc est corpus meum, accepisse & dedisse corpus suum inuisibiliter in pane. Nam cum ea verba diceret, corpus eius non erat inuisibiliter in pane, sed visibiliter assidebat, & loquebatur discipulis. Ec obstant verba. Non enim dixit: In hoc pane est corpus meum, aut; hic panis est, vel continet corpus meum inuisibile. Haec commenta refutantur ex verbis: quod pro vobis traditur. Sed de sensu verborum plura erunt dicenda.
units.tr: of the body of Christ. (3) Of the wine it is said: This cup is the new covenant in my blood. In the same way, then, it is said: This, that is, this bread is my body, which is broken and delivered to death for you. This is the literal sense, which, taken properly, cannot be understood otherwise than thus: the substance of this bread is the substance of my body. But to understand the words of the Lord in this way is absurd. For the substance of bread is an inanimate mass, ground from wheat, and is not united to the Word personally, nor crucified for us. But the substance of the body of Christ is animate, born of the virgin, personally united to the Word, and delivered to death for us. Therefore, in this literal sense the bread cannot be, or be called, the body of Christ. Hence we must think that Christ instituted the sacrament by speaking in this way. He therefore calls the bread his body given for us not literally but sacramentally, that is, he says that the bread is a sacrament, or holy sign, of his body given for us, according to the most simple and most true explanation of Augustine, chapter 12 against Adimantus: The Lord did not hesitate to say, This is my body, when he gave the sign of his body. Far be it from us to believe that by saying, This is my body, Christ changed the bread into his body, or wished to change it. For then the bread of the Eucharist would not be the body of Christ given for us, but would be a body made from bread, which is not given for us. Far be it also from us to believe that Christ, in taking the bread and saying, This is my body, invisibly took and gave his body in the bread. For when he spoke those words, his body was not invisibly in the bread, but was visibly sitting there and speaking to the disciples. Nor do the words stand in the way of this: he did not say, In this bread is my body, or this bread is, or contains, my invisible body. These fancies are refuted by the words which is given for you. But more will be said about the sense of the words.

units.la: Nunc obseruetur, haec esse verba promissionis, declarantia; quae sit res signata huius sacramenti. Per hanc enim promissionem Christus panem Eucharistiae fecit sacramentum, siue signum sui corporis, pro nobis traditi; & corpus suum pro nobis traditum fecit rem signatam huius sacramenti. Promissio autem haec, est promissio noui testamenti, & promissio gratiae, requirens fidem. Quicunque igitur rem signatam huius sacramenti percipere volunt, ad sacramentum hoc fidem adferant necesse est.
units.tr: Now let it be observed that these are words of promise, declaring what the thing signified by this sacrament is. For by this promise Christ made the bread of the Eucharist a sacrament, or sign, of his body given for us, and made his body given for us the thing signified by this sacrament. This promise, moreover, is the promise of the New Testament and a promise of grace, requiring faith. Whoever therefore wishes to receive the thing signified by this sacrament must necessarily bring faith to this sacrament.

units.la: Quod pro vobis. ] nempe discipulis meis; pro, in vestram salutem.
units.tr: Which is for you.] namely, for my disciples; for, for your salvation.

units.la: Frangitur. ] Atqui corpus Christi non est fractum. Respon. Paulus tribuit corpori Christi, quod est proprium panis: quia fractio panis in coena repraesentat fractionem, hoc est, lacerat, onem corporis Christi, & diuulsionem animae a corpore, seu mortem Christi pro nobis in cruce. Sicut enim panis frangitur in partes: sic anima & corpus Christi ab inuicem diuulsa fuerunt. Metonymia igitur sacramentali proprium signi tribuitur rei signatae.
units.tr: Is broken.] But the body of Christ was not broken. Answer: Paul attributes to the body of Christ what is proper to the bread, because the breaking of bread in the supper represents the rending of the body of Christ, that is, the tearing apart of the body, and the separation of the soul from the body, or the death of Christ for us on the cross. For just as bread is broken into parts, so the soul and body of Christ were torn apart from one another. Therefore, by sacramental metonymy, what belongs to the sign is attributed to the thing signified.

units.la: Hoc facite. Praeceptum de obseruatione ritus instituti. Hoc, hoc est, quod vidistis me facere, facite & vos deinceps in ecclesia: congregati accipite panem, gratias agite, frangite, distribuite, credentibus, non Iudaeis, qui ipsum erant crucifixuri. In mei recordationem. Finis coenae esse debet ἀνάμνησις, recordatio Christi: quae non tantum est recordatio vel cogitatio historiae: sed praecipue fides & gratitudo. Fides enim est recordatio & applicatio mortis & beneficiorum Christi. Gratitudo est recordatio & celebratio amoris Dei & Christi erga Ecclesiam. Est ergo coena institu̅ta a Christo, ut sit ὑπόμνησις, hoc est, sacramentum monitorium, reuocans nobis in memoriam, quam diro mortis genere, & quantis cruciatibus, quanta bona ipse nobis acquisiuerit, eademq; nobis obsignans: proinde etiam nos excitans ad solennem eorum celebrationem & gratiarum actionem. Coena enim non tantum nos monet nostri officii, ut volunt fanatici, sed primo de beneficio Christi, postea de officio nostro nos commonefacit. Prius enim docet, Christum nobis dare hoc sui μνημόσυνον, in pignus amoris & beneficiorum suorum: postea nos monet de gratitudine. Nam pro non-beneficio non possemus esse grati. Sensus ergo est: Facite in mei recordationem: hoc est, cogitate beneficia mea, quae per hunc ritum vobis in memoriam revoco & obsigno: & pro his mihi gratias agite.
units.tr: Do this.] A command about the observance of the instituted rite. This, that is, what you have seen me do, do also yourselves hereafter in the Church: gathered together, take bread, give thanks, break, and distribute it to believers, not to the Jews, who were about to crucify him. In remembrance of me. The aim of the Supper ought to be anamnesis [ἀνάμνησις], remembrance of Christ, which is not merely the remembrance or thought of a history, but above all faith and gratitude. For faith is the remembrance and application of the death and benefits of Christ. Gratitude is the remembrance and celebration of the love of God and Christ toward the Church. The Supper was therefore instituted by Christ so that it might be a hypomnesis [ὑπόμνησις], that is, a sacrament that admonishes, recalling to our memory with what dreadful kind of death, and with what great torments, and what great blessings he himself has acquired for us, and at the same time sealing these things to us; and so also stirring us up to the solemn celebration of them and to thanksgiving. For the Supper does not merely remind us of our duty, as the fanatics would have it, but first reminds us of the benefit of Christ, and afterwards of our duty. For first it teaches that Christ gives us this memorial of himself as a pledge of his love and benefits; afterwards it admonishes us about gratitude. For we could not be grateful for a non-benefit. The sense, then, is: Do this in remembrance of me: that is, think of my benefits, which I recall to your memory and seal to you through this rite; and for these give thanks to me.

units.la: Bibite ex hoc omnes. Hoc mandatum opponitur sacrilegio Papae, eripientis calicem laicis, & figmento sophistarum de concomitantia sanguinis cum corpore sub specie panis. Christus iubet omnes comedere & bibere: Papa vult non omnes bibere, sed solos sacerdotes: laicos vero iubet tantum comedere, & persuadet illis, quod comedendo etiam bibant. Haec impudentia refutatur mandato Christi: Bibite ex hoc omnes. Sophistae cauillantur, mandatum pertinere tantum ad praesentes discipulos, qui non fuerunt sacerdotes. Sed r. ineptè ex discipulis faciunt sacrificulos missificos. 2. Discrimen sacerdotum & laicorum non est in scriptura, quae omnes fideles vocat sacerdotes Dei. Fecit nos re-
units.tr: Drink from this, all of you. This command is set against the sacrilege of the Pope, who takes the cup from the laity, and against the fiction of the sophists about the concomitance of the blood with the body under the appearance of bread. Christ commands all to eat and drink; the Pope wills that not all drink, but only the priests; and he commands the laity only to eat, and persuades them that by eating they also drink. This impudence is refuted by the command of Christ: Drink from this, all of you. The sophists quibble that the command pertains only to the disciples present, who were not priests. But first, they foolishly make priests who offer Mass out of the disciples. Second, the distinction between priests and laity is not in Scripture, which calls all the faithful priests of God: He made us [Fecit nos re-]

units.la: gnes & sacerdotes Deo & Patri suo. Vos estis regale sacerdotium, ad offerendas spirituales hostias acceptas Deo per Iesum Christum. 3. Hoc praeterea laicis tota coena posset eripi, praesertim foeminis, si veritas rum esset, tantum id hominum genus esse admittendum ad coenam, quod fuit in prima coena.
units.tr: kings and priests to God and his Father. You are a royal priesthood, to offer spiritual sacrifices acceptable to God through Jesus Christ. Third, moreover, the whole Supper could be taken away from the laity, especially from women, if it were true that only that class of men was to be admitted to the supper which was present at the first supper.

units.la: Concomitantiæ figmentum est impius sacrilegii prætextus, quem Christus refutat, dum seorsum panem vocat corpus suum, & poculum sanguinem suum, & utrumque seorsum discipulis exhibet manducandum & bibendum, & sic deinceps seorsum exhiberi præcipit.
units.tr: The figment of concomitance is an impious pretext for sacrilege, which Christ refutes when he calls the bread by itself his body and the cup by itself his blood, gives each to the disciples separately to eat and to drink, and commands that they be served separately from then on.

units.la: Hoc poculum est novum testamentum. sive fœdus. Græcè διαθήκη, quod respondet Hebraeo ברית fœdus novum, id est, renovatum & impletum, quod nihil aliud est, quàm reconciliatio cum Deo, communio Christi, & omnium beneficiorum eius, per fidem in Christi sacrificium jam peractum, sine observatione cæremoniarum veteris paschæ. Cœna vocatur hic novum fœdus, signifi-catione: quia est fœderis huius signum & sigillum, reconciliationem nostri cum Deo, nostramque cum Christo coniunctionem (quæ per fidem fit) nobis obsignans.
units.tr: This cup is the new testament, that is, the new covenant. In Greek it is διαθήκη [diathēkē], which corresponds to the Hebrew ברית [berith]: a new covenant, that is, renewed and fulfilled. This is nothing other than reconciliation with God and communion with Christ and all his benefits, through faith in the sacrifice of Christ already accomplished, without the observance of the ceremonies of the old Passover. The Supper is here called the new covenant by a figure of speech, because it is the sign and seal of this covenant, sealing to us our reconciliation with God and our union with Christ (which comes about through faith).

units.la: In meo sanguine, qui pro vobis effunditur in remissionem peccatorum. Sanguis Christi est mors Christi. In sanguine Christi, est, in morte, seu propter mortem Christi. Effusio sanguinis Christi est meritum Christi, propter quod fide apprehensum accipimus remissionem peccatorum. Synecdoche partis pro toto.
units.tr: In my blood, which is poured out for you for the remission of sins. The blood of Christ is the death of Christ. In the blood of Christ means in the death, or on account of the death, of Christ. The pouring out of Christ's blood is the merit of Christ, on account of which we receive the remission of sins, apprehended by faith. This is synecdoche, the part put for the whole.

units.la: Quotiescunque ederitis de pane hoc. Ergo cœna sæpius est iteranda: quod etiam ex scopo eius colligitur: quia debet fieri ad recordationem & celebrationem mortis Domini.
units.tr: As often as you shall eat of this bread. Therefore the Supper is to be repeated frequently, which is also gathered from its purpose, since it ought to be done in remembrance and celebration of the Lord's death.

units.la: Mortem Domini annunciate. Credite, Christum esse mortuum, & quidem pro vobis: deinde id celebrate publicè coram omnibus.
units.tr: Proclaim the Lord's death. Believe that Christ has died, and indeed for you; then celebrate it publicly before everyone.

units.la: Usquequo venerit. Ergo cœna debet observari usque ad finem mundi, nec est exspectanda alia forma externa cultus usq; ad judicium. Docet igitur usus cœnæ, Christum nondum venisse, neque adesse in terris corporaliter.
units.tr: Until he comes. Therefore the Supper ought to be observed until the end of the world, and no other outward form of worship is to be expected until the judgment. The practice of the Supper thus teaches that Christ has not yet come, nor is present on earth bodily.

units.la: Verba institutionis hactenus explicata, illustrantur verbis Apostoli: Poculum benedictionis, cui benedicimus, nonne est communio sanguinis Christi? Panis, quem frangimus, nonne est communio corporis Christi? Hæc paucis etiam explicabimus.
units.tr: The words of institution explained so far are illustrated by the words of the Apostle: The cup of blessing which we bless, is it not the communion of the blood of Christ? The bread which we break, is it not the communion of the body of Christ? We will also explain these briefly.

units.la: Poculum benedictionis ] εὐλογία & ἐυχαριστία in hac actione idem significare, collatio verborum institutionis ostendit. Poculum igitur benedictionis sive gratiarum actionis vocatur: quia in hunc finem accipitur, ut gratias agamus Christo pro passione & morte: seu, quia vtentes debemus nobis in memoriam revocare Christi beneficia, & pro his ei gratias agere.
units.tr: The cup of blessing. That the words εὐλογία [eulogia] and εὐχαριστία [eucharistia] mean the same thing in this action is shown by a comparison of the words of institution. The cup is therefore called the cup of blessing, or of thanksgiving, because it is taken for this end, that we may give thanks to Christ for his passion and death; or because, in using it, we ought to call to mind the benefits of Christ and give him thanks for them.

units.la: Est communio sanguinis Christi. Communio est participatio rei communis. Communio corporis & sanguinis Christi, est, nec fidem fieri participem Christi & omnium beneficiorum eius, sanguinis eodem spiritu in nobis existente, qui est in Christo, & eadem in Christi nobis efficiente, quae efficit in Christo: seu, est spiritualis sociatio fidelium cum Christo, tanquam membrorum cum capite, & palmitum cum vite. Panis & vinum sunt communio, Ephes. 5, 30 hoc est, symbolum & sigillum communionis nostrae cum Christo. 1 Ioh. 1, 3. Communio autem haec (ut declarat Apostolus) in eo consistit, quod unum corpus multi sumus. Unde colligitur, communionem Christi non esse manducationem corporalem. Illa enim communio tantum fit per fidem & Spiritum sanctum. Christus est caput, nos membra, & omnes, qui sumus membra, habemus communionem cum capite Christo, & omnibus eius beneficiis.
units.tr: It is the communion of the blood of Christ. Communion is the participation in a common thing. The communion of the body and blood of Christ is that faith makes us partakers of Christ and all his benefits, the same Spirit being in us which is in Christ, and effecting in us the same things which he effects in Christ; or it is the spiritual fellowship of believers with Christ, as members with the head and branches with the vine. The bread and wine are a communion, Eph. 5:30, that is, a symbol and seal of our communion with Christ. 1 John 1:3. This communion (as the Apostle declares) consists in this, that we who are many are one body. From this it is gathered that the communion with Christ is not a bodily eating. For that communion comes about only through faith and the Holy Spirit. Christ is the head, we are the members, and all of us who are members have communion with Christ the head and with all his benefits.

units.la: QVAESTIO LXXVIII. Num ergo panis & vinum naturaliter fiunt ipsum corpus & sanguis Christi? RESPONSIO.
units.tr: QUESTION 78. Do bread and wine therefore naturally become the very body and blood of Christ? ANSWER.

units.la: Nequaquam verum ut aqua baptismi in sanguinem Christi non convertitur, nec est ipsa peccatorum abluitio, sed symbolum & pignus earum rerum, quae nobis in baptismo significantur, & obsignantur b: ita nec panis Coenae Dominicae est ipsum corpus Christi c: quamquam pro ratione sacramentorum, & vsitata Spiritui sancto de his loquendi forma d, panis Christi corpus appellatur.
units.tr: By no means is it true that the water of baptism is converted into the blood of Christ, nor is it the washing away of sins itself, but it is a symbol and pledge of those things which are signified and sealed to us in baptism. So too the bread of the Lord's Supper is not the very body of Christ; yet, in keeping with the nature of the sacraments and the usual manner in which the Holy Spirit speaks of them, the bread is called the body of Christ.

units.la: a Matth. 26. vers. 29. b Ephes. 5, 26. c 1 Cor. 10, 16. & 11, 18. d Genes. 17, 10. 11. Exod. 12, 11. 13. & 13, 9. Tit. 3, 5. 1 Petri 3. vers. 21. 1 Corinth. 10. vers. 4.
EXPLICATIO.
units.tr: EXPLANATION.

units.la: Hic reijicitur transsubstantiatio Papistarum, sub qua etiam comprehenditur consubstantiatio, quam ubiquitarij defendunt: & explicatur locutio sacramentalis, & vera sententia verborum Christi: Hoc est corpus meum. De locutione sacramentali & vera sententia verborum prius dicendum: postea de controversia transsubstantiationis & consubstantiationis: Quae igitur supra de locutionibus sacramentalibus in genere dicta sunt, etiam ad hoc sacramentum pertinent, sicut & Augustinus generali regulae loculocutionum sacramentalium exemplum de manducatione carnis Christi expressè subiecit: Iste omninò modus est (inquit) innuendæ locutionis, propriáne an figurata sit, vt quicquid in sermone divino neque ad morum honestatem, neque ad fidei veritatem propriè referri potest, figuratum esse cognoscas. Et paulò post dat hoc exemplum: Nisi manducaveritis carnem filij hominis, & sanguinem biberitis, non habebitis vitam in vobis. Flagitium videtur iubere. Figurâ est ergò, præcipiens passioni Domini esse communicandum, & suaviter ac utiliter recondendum in memoria, quod pro nobis caro eius crucifixa & vulnerata sit. Quemadmodum igitur de baptismo scriptura modo proprie loquitur, modo figuratè, vt supra ostensum est; sic etiam de cœna, modo figuratè, modo proprie loquitur. Figurata locutio est, cùm Christus dicit de pane: Hoc est corpus meum: & de poculo: Hoc est sanguis meus. Item Paulus: Hoc poculum est novum testamentum in meo sanguine. Signo enim tribuitur nomen rei signatæ, per metonymiam sacramentalem. Figuratè etiam loquitur Paulus, cùm dicit: Hoc est corpus meum, quod pro vobis frangitur: quia proprium signi (quod est frangi) tribuitur rei signatæ. Sic & Cyprianus: Bibentes calicem cruci haremus, sanguinem fugimus, & intra ipsa redemptoris nostri vulnera linguam figimus. Et Chrysostomus: Sanguis Christi est in calice: corpus Christi, quod in cœlis est, in terra nobis videndum proponitur: nec tantum videtur, sed tangitur: nec solum tangitur, sed comeditur: à nobis tenetur, mordetur, & manducatur in signum dilectionis: sicut quos amamus, nonnunquam etiam morsu petimus: carnem eius linguâ attingimus, &c. Hæc non nisi per tropum sacramentalem vere dicuntur, & intelligi possunt de corpore Christi. Sed propria locutio est, cùm Christus dicit: Hoc facite in mei memoriam: & patres passim dicunt: Fractio panis est recordatio, ... panis significat corpus Christi: est figura, signum, sacramentum corporis Christi.
units.tr: Here the transubstantiation of the Papists is rejected, under which is also included the consubstantiation which the ubiquitarians defend. The sacramental manner of speaking and the true sense of the words of Christ, This is my body, are explained. The sacramental manner of speaking and the true sense of the words must be discussed first; afterwards the controversy about transubstantiation and consubstantiation. What has been said above about sacramental forms of speech in general also pertains to this sacrament, just as Augustine expressly added, as an example of the general rule about sacramental forms of speech, the eating of the flesh of Christ: This is altogether the way (he says) to discern whether an expression is proper or figurative: whatever in divine speech cannot be referred properly either to the goodness of morals or to the truth of faith, you may know to be figurative. And a little later he gives this example: Unless you eat the flesh of the Son of man and drink his blood, you will not have life in you. It seems a crime to command this. It is therefore a figure, enjoining that we should communicate in the passion of the Lord, and sweetly and profitably lay up in memory that his flesh was crucified and wounded for us. Just as, therefore, Scripture speaks of baptism sometimes figuratively and sometimes properly, as has been shown above, so also it speaks of the Supper sometimes figuratively and sometimes properly. The manner of speaking is figurative when Christ says of the bread, This is my body, and of the cup, This is my blood. Likewise Paul: This cup is the new testament in my blood. For the name of the thing signified is given to the sign, by sacramental metonymy. Paul also speaks figuratively when he says, This is my body, which is broken for you, because the property of the sign (which is to be broken) is attributed to the thing signified. So also Cyprian: Drinking the cup, we cleave to the cross, we flee from blood, and we fix our tongue within the very wounds of our Redeemer. And Chrysostom: The blood of Christ is in the cup; the body of Christ, which is in heaven, is set before us on earth to be seen; not only is it seen, but it is touched; not only is it touched, but it is eaten; it is held by us, bitten, and eaten as a sign of love, as we sometimes seek to bite those whom we love; we touch his flesh with the tongue, etc. These things are truly said, and can be understood of the body of Christ, only by a sacramental trope. But the manner of speaking is proper when Christ says, Do this in remembrance of me, and the Fathers everywhere say, The breaking of bread is a remembrance ... the bread signifies the body of Christ; it is a figure, a sign, a sacrament of the body of Christ.

units.la: DE CONTROVERSIA VERBORUM COENÆ.
units.tr: On the Controversy Concerning the Words of the Supper.

units.la: Quoniam verò adversarij Papistæ, & alij, negant, in verbis Christi esse locutionem sacramentalem: & contendunt, retinendum esse τὸ ῥητόν: ideo de controversia ῥητῶν καὶ ἀλληγοριῶν, aliquid addendum est.
units.tr: Since our opponents, the Papists and others, deny that there is a sacramental figure of speech in the words of Christ, and contend that the literal sense (τὸ ῥητόν) must be retained, something must be added concerning the controversy between the literal and the allegorical (ῥητῶν καὶ ἀλληγοριῶν).

units.la: Papistæ fingunt, vt consecrationis fieri μεταρύσιν, seu conversionem panis in corpus Christi, remanentibus tantùm accidentibus, & vocant transubstantiationem. Alij contendunt de συνουσίᾳ seu coexistentia corporis in vel cum pane. Metusiastæ cum synusiastis pariter gloriantur, se Christi verba simpliciter accipeaccipere: sed neutri id præstant, quod venditant. Ea enim verborum est simplicitas & proprietas, cui ad justam intelligentiam neq; addendum est quicquam, neque adimendum, & nihil etiam in litera immutandum. Illi verò, qui corpus Christi cum, in, sub pane adesse dicunt, Christi verbis addunt, & à simplicitate recedunt. Nam si simpliciter est retinendum, quod Christus dixit, & non admittendum, quod non dixit: vtique non est dicendum: Panis est simul panis, & corpus Christi. Hoc enim Christus non dixit: multò minus: Corpus Christi est in, cum, sub pane. Neque addendum, quod addunt de suo: realiter, substantialiter, corporaliter. Nuda enim ista verba sua protulit de pane: Hoc est corpus meum.
