Lombard puts it differently: Mass (he says) is so called because the heavenly messenger comes to consecrate the life-giving body, according to the words of the priest saying: Almighty God, command that these things be carried by the hands of your holy Angel to your high altar, etc. Therefore, unless an angel comes, the Mass cannot rightly be called by that name at all. See the absurdities! The same writer: Mass is so called either because the victim was sent, whose memorial is made in that office; hence it is said: Go, it is the dismissal, follow the victim, which was sent to heaven, going after it; or because a heavenly messenger comes to consecrate the Lord's body, through whom the victim is carried to the heavenly altar; hence it is said: Go, it is the dismissal.

units.la: Nos abijcimus missam cum vocabulo: quia coenae dominicae non competit, cui cum missa nihil est commune, quamvis eo veteres scriptores aliqui sint usi. Nec isto vocabulo nobis est opus. Habemus alias appellationes, huic mysterio convenientissimas, quae in scripturis exstant. Vocatur enim coena Domini, mensa Domini, fractio panis, &c.
units.tr: We reject the Mass together with the word, because it does not suit the Lord's Supper, with which the Mass has nothing in common, although some ancient writers have used it. Nor do we need this word. We have other appellations, most suitable to this mystery, which are found in the Scriptures. For it is called the Lord's Supper, the Lord's table, the breaking of bread, etc.

units.la: Jam videamus discrimina coenae Domini & Missae Papisticae, eaque prorsus inuicem contraria: Propter quae Missa omnino aboleri debet. Sunt autem tria praecipua, quae in catechesi explicantur.
units.tr: Now let us see the differences between the Lord's Supper and the Papistical Mass, which are wholly contrary to each other, and on account of which the Mass must altogether be abolished. There are, however, three chief ones, which are explained in the catechism.

units.la: I. Coena Domini testatur, nos habere plenariam remissionem peccatorum, & justificationem gratis per fidem, propter unicum sacrificium Christi in cruce peractum, juxta dicta: Panis est corpus Christi pro nobis traditum: poculum sanguis Christi pro nobis effusum in remissionem peccatorum. Hoc facite in mei recordationem. Mortem Domini annunciate, donec veniat. Id fecit semel, cum semetipsum obtulit. Per proprium sanguinem ingressus est semel sacrarium, aeterna redemtionem nactus. Alioqui oportuisset eum saepe passum esse à condito mundo: nunc autem semel in consummatione mundi ad abolendum peccatum per immolationem suiipsius patefactus est. Qua voluntate sanctificati sumus per oblationem corporis Iesu Christi semel factam. Hic verò una pro peccatis oblata victima, in perpetuum sedet ad dexteram Dei. Vnica enim oblatione consecrauit in perpetuum eos, qui sanctificantur.
units.tr: First, the Lord's Supper testifies that we have full remission of sins and justification freely through faith, on account of the one sacrifice of Christ accomplished on the cross, according to the words: The bread is the body of Christ, given for us; the cup is the blood of Christ, poured out for us for the remission of sins. Do this in remembrance of me. Proclaim the death of the Lord until he comes. He did this once, when he offered himself. Through his own blood he entered the sanctuary once, having obtained eternal redemption. Otherwise he would have had to suffer often since the foundation of the world; but now once, at the consummation of the world, he has been revealed to abolish sin by the sacrifice of himself. By that will we have been sanctified through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ made once. But this one, having offered one victim for sins, sits forever at the right hand of God. For by one offering he has perfected forever those who are sanctified.

units.la: ANTITHESIS.
units.tr: ANTITHESIS.

units.la: Contra verò Missa negat, viuos & mortuos habere remissionem peccatorum per & propter vnicam Christi oblationem nisi etiamnum quotidie à sacrificulis Christus Deo offeratur. Sic enim habet Canon, quem vocant minorem: Suscipe sancte Pater, omnipotens æterne Deus, hanc immaculatam hostiam, quam ego indignus famulus tuus offero tibi Deo meo, viuo & vero, pro innumerabilibus peccatis, & offensionibus, & negligentiis meis, & pro omnibus circumstantibus: sed & pro omnibus fidelibus Christianis, viuis atque defunctis, vt mihi & illis proficiat ad salutem in vitam æternam. Et Canon maior: Memento famulorum famularumque tuarum N. N. & omnium circumstantium, quorum tibi fides cognita est, & nota devotio, pro quibus tibi offerimus, vel qui tibi offerunt hoc sacrificium laudis, pro se suisque omnibus, pro redemptione animarum suarum, pro spe salutis & incolumitatis, &c. Quid verò opus fuit Christum seipsum offerre, si oblatio sacrificuli valet pro redemptione animarum?
units.tr: The Mass, on the other hand, denies that the living and the dead have forgiveness of sins through and on account of the one oblation of Christ, unless Christ is also offered to God every day by the sacrificing priests. For the so-called Lesser Canon says: Receive, holy Father, almighty eternal God, this immaculate host, which I, your unworthy servant, offer to you, my God, living and true, for my countless sins, offences and negligences, and for all who stand around; but also for all faithful Christians, living and dead, that it may profit me and them for salvation unto eternal life. And the Greater Canon: Remember your servants, men and women, N. N., and all who stand around, whose faith is known to you and whose devotion is noted, for whom we offer to you, or who offer to you this sacrifice of praise, for themselves and all their own, for the redemption of their souls, for the hope of salvation and safety, etc. But why was it necessary for Christ to offer himself, if the oblation of a sacrificing priest avails for the redemption of souls?

units.la: II. Cœna testatur, Christum juxta articulos fidei humanitate sua esse in cœlo ad dextram Patris, nec delitescere sub accidentibus elementorum, sed exhibere nobis corpus & sanguinem suum in sacra cœna manducandum & bibendum fide, & nos sibi inserere per Spiritum sanctum, vt nos in ipso maneamus, & ipsum manentem in nobis habeamus, juxta dicta: Qui agglutinatur Domino, vnus est spiritus. Panis, quem frangimus, nonne est communio corporis Christi? Talem habemus pontificem, qui consedit ad dexteram throni maiestatis in cœlestibus. Nam si esset in terra, nec sacerdos quidem esset.
units.tr: II. The Supper testifies that Christ, according to the articles of faith, is in heaven at the right hand of the Father in his humanity, and does not lie hidden under the accidents of the elements; rather he sets forth his body and blood to us in the holy Supper to be eaten and drunk by faith, and joins us to himself through the Holy Spirit, so that we may remain in him and have him remaining in us, according to the words: He who is joined to the Lord is one spirit. The bread which we break, is it not the communion of the body of Christ? We have such a high priest, who sat down at the right hand of the throne of the Majesty in the heavens. For if he were on earth, he would not even be a priest.

units.la: ANTITESIS.
units.tr: ANTITHESIS.

units.la: In Missa contra docetur, panem & vinum, vi consecrationis mutari in corpus & sanguinem Christi, & hæc in actu consecrationis ab angelo deferri è cœlo, latere corporaliter sub speciebus panis & vini, manibus sacerdotis realiter gestari, tractari, & a communicantibus oraliter sumi. Hæc figmenta pugnant cum articulis fidei de incarnatione, de ascensione, de intercessione, de reditu ad judicium, & cum natura sacramentorum, in quibus necesse est symbola manere, non naturam amittere, vt supra demonstratum.
units.tr: In the Mass, on the contrary, it is taught that the bread and wine, by the power of consecration, are changed into the body and blood of Christ; that in the act of consecration this body is brought down from heaven by an angel; that it lies corporeally under the appearances of bread and wine; that it is physically carried and handled by the hands of the priest, and is taken orally by the communicants. These fictions clash with the articles of faith concerning the incarnation, the ascension, the intercession, and the return to judgment, and with the nature of the sacraments, in which the signs must remain and not lose their nature, as has been shown above.

units.la: III. Cœna docet, Christum esse adorandum in cœlo ad dextram Patris. Cœna enim non convellit, sed confirmat articulos fidei, & doctrinam totius Euangelij, Christum esse quaerendum SVRSVM: Quarite quae SVRSVM sunt, VBI Christus est ad dextram Dei sedens. Stephanos cum lapidaretur, Christum vidit, & adoravit SVRSVM ad dextram Dei stantem. Vetus quoque Ecclesia cecinit in Liturgia: SVRSVM CORDA habemus ad Dominum. Ibi igitur adorandus est.
units.tr: III. The Supper teaches that Christ is to be adored in heaven at the right hand of the Father. For the Supper does not overturn but confirms the articles of faith and the teaching of the whole Gospel, that Christ is to be sought ABOVE: Seek those things which are ABOVE, where Christ is sitting at the right hand of God. Stephen, when he was being stoned, saw Christ and adored him standing ABOVE at the right hand of God. The ancient Church also sang in the Liturgy: We have our hearts ABOVE lifted up to the Lord. There, therefore, he is to be adored.

units.la: ANTITHESIS.
units.tr: ANTITHESIS.

units.la: Missa contra docet, Christum esse adorandum in hostia panis: quae adoratio haud dubie est idololatrica. Est enim adorare ad panem, dirigere adorationem animo, mente, cogitatione, & (quantum fieri potest) gestu corporis ad locum, in quo est praesenti magis quam alibi. Sicut olim Judaei adorabant Deum ad arcam, conversi ad eam animis, & quantum fieri potuit, etiam gestu corporis, ex Dei mandato. Sine Dei autem mandato hoc facere, idololatricum esse patet. 1. Quia nulla creatura potestatem habet alligandi adorationem ad villam rem aut locum, in quo, vel ad quam, Deus non jussit expresso verbo se adorari, & exauditionem promisit. Hinc manifesta est causa discriminis, cur Judaei dirigentes adorationem ad propitiatorium, simul tamen in spiritu adorantes, verum Deum recte colebant, & promissione certi erant de exauditione. Adorantes autem in Dan & Bethel, & in excelsis, & in templo Samariae, erant idololatrae nescientes quid adorarent: & huius rei causa fusius explicatur 2 Reg. 17, 9. 2. Quia in novo Testamento omnis adoratio, quae sit alligata ad certum locum in terra, omnino sublata est, tantumque spiritualis requiritur: excitata a Spiritu sancto, facta in vera cognitione & fide. Haec docet Christus Johannis 4. Vos adoratis, quod nescitis: nos adoramus, quod scimus. Sed venit hora, quando neque in monte hoc, neque Hierosolymis adorabitis Patrem: sed veri adoratores adorabunt eum in Spiritu & veritate. Cum dicit, in spiritu, non in monte hoc, non Hierosolymis, tollit adorationem alligatam loco in terris. Itaque tollere ac detestari nos quoque oportet impium istud commentum, quod idololatricae adorationis est fundamentum. Ponitur enim, quod Christus sit corpore praesens in pane, (sive id fieri dicatur μετουσία sive σωουσία) stat adoratio Papistica. Sicut enim olim ante ascensionem, non tantum licebat, sed etiam oportebat adorare Christum, quocunque erat loco: ita nunc, si est in pane, ad panem oportet adorari, sive videatur, sive non. Magis enim voci divinae, quam villis sensibus credendum esset, si verbum Dei praesentiam corporalem docerer. Sed & vice versa tollitur corporalis praesentia Christi in pane, sublata, ex ipsius Domini mandato, hac tetra Papistarum adoratione Christi, sub panis & vini speciebus, eorum opinione, latentis.
units.tr: The Mass, on the contrary, teaches that Christ is to be adored in the host of bread; and this adoration is undoubtedly idolatrous. For to adore toward the bread is to direct the adoration with the soul, mind and thought, and (as far as possible) with the posture of the body, to the place where he is present more than elsewhere. Just as the Jews of old adored God toward the ark, turned to it in their hearts and, as far as they could, with the posture of their bodies, by God's command. But that to do this without God's command is idolatrous is plain. 1. Because no creature has the power to tie adoration to any thing or place to which God has not commanded, by an express word, that he be adored, and promised to hear. Hence the cause of the difference is clear: why the Jews, directing their adoration toward the mercy seat yet at the same time adoring in spirit, worshipped the true God rightly and were certain of being heard through the promise; but those who adored at Dan and Bethel, and on the high places, and in the temple of Samaria, were idolaters, not knowing what they adored; and the reason for this is explained more fully at 2 Kings 17:9. 2. Because in the New Testament all adoration that is bound to a certain place on earth has been wholly abolished, and only spiritual adoration is required: stirred up by the Holy Spirit, made in true knowledge and faith. Christ teaches this in John 4: You adore what you do not know; we adore what we know. But the hour comes when neither on this mountain nor at Jerusalem will you adore the Father; but the true worshippers will adore him in Spirit and truth. When he says in spirit, not on this mountain, not at Jerusalem, he removes adoration tied to a place on earth. Therefore we too ought to abhor and detest that impious invention, which is the foundation of idolatrous adoration. For if it is posited that Christ is present in body in the bread (whether this is called μετουσία [metousia] or σωουσία [sōousia]), the Papist adoration stands. For just as before the ascension it was not only permitted but even necessary to adore Christ wherever he was, so now, if he is in the bread, he must be adored toward the bread, whether it is seen or not. For it would be more necessary to believe the divine voice than our senses, if the Word of God taught a bodily presence. But conversely, the bodily presence of Christ in the bread is also overturned, by the Lord's own command, when this foul adoration of Christ by the Papists, supposedly hidden under the appearances of bread and wine, is removed.

units.la: Vbiquitarij excipiunt, Christum adesse in pane, non vt adoretur, sed vt manducetur: nec jussisse se adorari in pane, sed mandu-cari. Resp. Est petitio principij in utroque. Neutrum jussit. Si enim est in pane, oportet eum ibi adorari, propter mandatum generale, Adorent eum omnes sancti angeli eius. Dominum Deum tuum adorabis. Fingunt ergo Christum in pane, quem non liceat adorare. Haec est manifesta impostura. Ideo Andreas Musculus & alij, vt hunc nodum soluant, procidunt coram pane, & in eo Christum adorant. Instat Heshusius, divinitatem non adorari in omnibus creaturis, licet in omnibus sit praesens: Ergo nec humanitatem necesse esse adorari in pane, licet in eo sit praesens corporaliter. Respond. Est dissimilitudo in exemplis. Adoratio divinitatis non est alligata omnibus creaturis, est verò alligata humanitati assumptae tanquam proprio templo. Vbicunque igitur est Christi humanitas, ibi divinitas in ea, & cum ea vult adorari. Et quidem hoc certissimo argumento vbiquitas humanitatis evertitur. Cùm enim humanitas in omnibus creaturis & vbique non sit adoranda: sequitur non esse vbique praesentem in omnibus piris, pomis, funibus, caseis, cantharis; vt scripserunt Vbiquitarij.
units.tr: The Ubiquitarians object that Christ is present in the bread not so that he may be adored, but so that he may be eaten; and that he did not command himself to be adored in the bread, but to be eaten. Answer. Both are begging the question. He commanded neither. For if he is in the bread, he must be adored there, on account of the general command: Let all his holy angels adore him. You shall adore the Lord your God. They therefore feign Christ in the bread, whom it is not lawful to adore. This is a manifest imposture. Therefore Andreas Musculus and others, to loosen this knot, fall down before the bread and adore Christ in it. Heshusius presses: the divinity is not adored in all creatures, although it is present in all; therefore neither is it necessary for the humanity to be adored in the bread, although it is bodily present in it. Answer. There is a dissimilarity in the examples. The adoration of the divinity is not tied to all creatures, but it is tied to the assumed humanity as to its proper temple. Wherever, therefore, the humanity of Christ is, there the divinity is in it, and wishes to be adored with it. And indeed by this most certain argument the ubiquity of the humanity is overthrown. For since the humanity is not to be adored in all creatures and everywhere, it follows that he is not present everywhere in pears, apples, ropes, cheeses, and tankards, as the Ubiquitarians have written.

units.la: Eadem discrimina D. Vrsinus anno 69. sic tradidit.
units.tr: The same differences were set out by Dr. Ursinus in the year 69, as follows.

units.la: 1. Coena testatur, solum sacrificium Christi justificare. Sacrificuli dicunt, suam Missam justificare ex opere operato.
units.tr: 1. The Supper testifies that the sacrifice of Christ alone justifies. The little sacrificers say that their Mass justifies by the work worked (ex opere operato).

units.la: 2. Coena docet, CHRISTVM seipsum offerendo nos redemisse. Sacrificuli dicunt, nos redemi per Christum ab ipso oblatum.
units.tr: 2. The Supper teaches that Christ redeemed us by offering himself. The little sacrificers say that we are redeemed through Christ, offered by the priest.

units.la: 3. Coena docet, salutem nostram vnico sacrificio Christi perfectam esse. Sacrificuli dicunt, eam perfici infinitis Missis.
units.tr: 3. The Supper teaches that our salvation was made perfect by the one sacrifice of Christ. The little sacrificers say that it is made perfect by endless Masses.

units.la: 4. Coena docet, nos Christo inseri mediante Spiritu sancto per fidem. Missa mentitur, Christum in nos ingredi corporaliter, seu nos Christo inseri per corporalem illapsum.
units.tr: 4. The Supper teaches that we are grafted into Christ through faith, by the mediation of the Holy Spirit. The Mass lies, claiming that Christ enters into us bodily, or that we are grafted into Christ by a bodily inflowing.

units.la: 5. Coena docet, Christum sacrificio suo peracto ascendisse in coelum. Missarij volunt, eum corpore suo etiam nunc esse in altari.
units.tr: 5. The Supper teaches that Christ, having finished his sacrifice, ascended into heaven. The Missarii want him to be now in the altar in his body.

units.la: 6. In Coena panis & vinum manent, & non mutant substantiam: quia sacramenta retinent, & non mutant substantiam aboleri, manen-tibus tantum accidentibus.
units.tr: 6. In the Supper the bread and wine remain and do not change their substance. For the sacraments retain their substance and are not abolished, only the accidents remaining.

units.la: 7. Finis cœnæ est confirmatio fidei in Christum, & eius vnicum sacrificium. Missæ finis est confirmatio opinionis de opere operato, & abnegatio sacrificii Christi.
units.tr: 7. The purpose of the Supper is the confirmation of faith in Christ and in his one sacrifice. The purpose of the Mass is the confirmation of the opinion about the work worked, and the denial of the sacrifice of Christ.

units.la: 8. Cœna docet, Christum esse adorandum sursum in cœlo. Missarii adorant sub speciebus panis & vini.
units.tr: 8. The Supper teaches that Christ is to be adored above in heaven. The Missarii adore him under the appearances of bread and wine.

units.la: Hæc discrimina ostendunt, missam Papisticam in fundamento nihil esse aliud, quam abnegationem vnici sacrificii Christi, & horribilem idololatriam. Hæc porro discrimina grauissimas ostendunt causas, propter quas Missa Papistica debeat aboleri, & procul ex Ecclesia eliminari: videlicet
units.tr: These differences show that the Papist Mass is, at its foundation, nothing other than a denial of the one sacrifice of Christ and a horrible idolatry. Moreover, these differences show the most serious causes on account of which the Papist Mass ought to be abolished and driven far out of the Church, namely:

units.la: 1. Missa Papistica est multiplex depravatio, imo abolitio ritus à Christo instituti, hoc est, cœnæ Domini. Eripit enim calicem populo, & addit multas ineptissimas nugas, ignotas Apostolis, & piæ antiquitati: cum nulla creatura haberet potestatem commutandi aut abolendi constitutiones diuinas.
units.tr: 1. The Papist Mass is a manifold corruption, indeed an abolition, of the rite instituted by Christ, that is, of the Lord's Supper. For it takes the cup from the people, and adds many most foolish trifles, unknown to the Apostles and to the pious antiquity, although no creature has the power of changing or abolishing divine ordinances.

units.la: 2. Missa tollit sacramentum: quia transformat signum in rem signatam, dicens, panem & vinum non esse panem, vinum, sed esse carnem & sanguinem Christi substantialiter: quod pugnat cum natura sacramentorum, quæ non patitur aboleri signorum substantiam.
units.tr: 2. The Mass destroys the sacrament, because it transforms the sign into the thing signified, saying that the bread and wine are not bread and wine but are substantially the flesh and blood of Christ. This conflicts with the nature of the sacraments, which does not allow the substance of the signs to be abolished.

units.la: 3. Missa fingitur esse sacrificium ἱλαστικὸν, propitiatorium, quod sua dignitate mereatur remissionem peccatorum ipsis & aliis, ex opere operato: cum hoc nequidem Mosaicis sacrificiis, sed vnico sacrificio filii Dei semel facto competat, ad quod cœna Dominini nos deducit, & remittit: Missa vero abducit & auocat. Patres quidem cœnam aliquando vocant sacrificium, sed ευχαριστικὸν, non ἱλαστικὸν, vt volunt pontificii. Et est quidem cœna illud ipsum sacrificium, quod Christus obtulit, sicut panis est illud ipsum corpus, quod Christus tradidit pro nobis; verum sacramentaliter. Missarii vero Missam faciunt sacrificium, non ipsum, quod Christus obtulit, sed diuersum: quia dicunt suum sacrificium esse incruentum. Ergo sacrificium Christi cruentum vere expiatorium omnium peccatorum nostrorum reuera abnegant, fingentes aliud sacrificium pro peccatis; quantumuis dicant se non offerre aliam victimam quam Christus obtulit. Nam aliud est, vnam victimam semel offerri, & quidem sufficientem ad tollenda omnia peccata, quod de Christi victima dicit scriptura; aliud, eandem victimam sæpius offerri, quod victimæ Christi non competit. Contradictoria enim sunt dicere, & hoc sacrificium solum sufficit ad remissionem peccatorum; & hoc sacrificium non sufficit, nisi cum aliis offeratur pro peccatis.
units.tr: 3. The Mass is made out to be a sacrifice that is propitiatory (ἱλαστικὸν), which by its own worth merits forgiveness of sins for itself and others, by the work worked. Yet this does not belong even to the Mosaic sacrifices, but to the one sacrifice of the Son of God, made once; to this the Lord's Supper leads us and sends us back, whereas the Mass draws us away and diverts us. The Fathers indeed sometimes call the Supper a sacrifice, but a eucharistic one (εὐχαριστικὸν), not a propitiatory one (ἱλαστικὸν), as the Papists maintain. The Supper is indeed that very sacrifice which Christ offered, just as the bread is that very body which Christ delivered for us, but sacramentally. The Missarii, however, make the Mass a sacrifice that is not the very one Christ offered, but a different one, because they say their sacrifice is unbloody. Therefore they really deny the bloody sacrifice of Christ, which truly expiates all our sins, inventing another sacrifice for sins, although they say they do not offer any other victim than the one Christ offered. For it is one thing for one victim to be offered once, and indeed sufficient to take away all sins, which Scripture says of the victim of Christ; it is another for the same victim to be offered over and over, which does not belong to the victim of Christ. For it is contradictory to say both that this sacrifice alone suffices for the forgiveness of sins, and that this sacrifice does not suffice unless it is offered together with others for sins.

units.la: 4. In hoc errore latet alius, quod fingunt se etiam absentibus, vel mortuis, & in purgatorio exsistentibus, impetrare remissionem peccatorum, & redemtionem animarum: cum verbum Dei dicat, nos superinduendos esse in coelis, si induti, non nudi reperiemur in terris, & judicandos, quales reperti fuerimus in huius vitae excessu. Quando enim istinc excessum fuerit (dicit Cyprianus) nullus jam poenitentiae locus est, nullus satisfactionis effectus: hic vita aut amittitur, aut tenetur; hic salutis aeterna cultu Dei & fructu fidei providetur.
units.tr: 4. Another error lies hidden in this one: they pretend that they can obtain forgiveness of sins and the redemption of souls even for the absent, or the dead, who exist in purgatory; yet the Word of God says that we must be clothed upon in heaven, that if we are found clothed, and not naked, on earth, we will be judged as we were found at the departure from this life. For when one has departed from here (says Cyprian), there is no longer any place for repentance, no effect of satisfaction; here life is either lost or kept; here provision is made for eternal salvation by the worship of God and the fruit of faith.

units.la: 5. Item alius, quod fingunt, se opere illo non tantum mereri remissionem peccatorum, sed etiam alia beneficia: ut sanationem aegrotantium hominum, pecorum, equorum, boum, porcorum, &c. Fingunt igitur in Missa conferri bona, toto genere diversa ab iis, quae in Evangelio promittuntur, & sacramentis obsignantur.
units.tr: 5. Likewise, another error is that they pretend that by that work they merit not only forgiveness of sins but also other benefits: such as the healing of sick men, flocks, horses, oxen, pigs, and so on. They therefore imagine that goods conferred in the Mass are entirely different in kind from those promised in the Gospel and sealed by the sacraments.

units.la: 6. Missa pugnat cum sacerdotio Christi. Solus Christus habet potestatem seipsum offerendi. Contra Missarij fingunt Filium Dei posse offerri etiam ab alio, quam a seipso, & se eum offerre Deo Patri, cum nulla creatura sit eius dignitatis, ut possit sacrificare Filium Dei. Sacerdos enim superior est victimâ. Qui ergo volunt esse sacerdotes, offerentes Christum, ij se supra Christum efferunt, atq; hoc ipso sunt Antichristi. Excipiunt: se non mactare, sed tantum offerre, & exhibere Filium Patri, ut propter ipsum remittat peccata: atq; ita applicare tantum unicum illud sacrificium. Resp. Satis est, quod dicunt, se Christum suis manibus offerre. Manet enim, quod se constituant sacerdotes, qui Filium Dei offerant victimam: & sic se supra Filium Dei constituunt. Nec refert, quod negant, se eum mactare. Offerebantur olim à sacerdotibus multa, quae non mactabantur, sed duntaxat immolabantur, ut placentae, liba, &c. sed viua animantia non poterant offerri, nisi mactata. Ergo vel mactant Christum, Missarij, vel non offerunt. Judaei quidem mactarunt Christum, sed non sacrificarunt: quia non mactarunt, ut sacerdotes, sed vt carnifices. Ipse vero volens ab eis mactatus, seipsum per Spiritum aeternum obtulit inculpatum Deo: & quidem semel se obtulit victimam Patri pro nobis. Semel oblatus est, ut peccata multorum tolleret: altera vice absque peccato conspicietur iis, qui ipsum expectant ad salutem. Vna pro peccatis oblata victima in perpetuum sedet ad dextram Dei. Contra haec manifesta scripturae testimonia Missarij volunt Christum saepius offerre: volunt eum sacrificare: non autem mactare pro expiandis peccatis. At sacrificium pro expiandis peccatis sine mactatione non potest esse: Nam absque sanHeb. 9, 14. Heb. 9, 28. Hebr. 10, 12. Heb. 9, 22. sanguinis effusione nulla fit remissio. Ergo sacrificium Missæ est impostura.
units.tr: 6. The Mass conflicts with the priesthood of Christ. Christ alone has the power of offering himself. On the contrary, the Missarii pretend that the Son of God can be offered by another than himself, and that they offer him to God the Father, although no creature has such dignity that it can sacrifice the Son of God. For the priest is superior to the victim. Therefore those who want to be priests, offering Christ, exalt themselves above Christ, and by this very fact they are of Antichrist. They object: that they do not slaughter him, but only offer and present the Son to the Father, so that for his sake he may forgive sins; and thus they apply only that one sacrifice. Answer. It is enough that they say they offer Christ with their own hands. For it remains that they make themselves priests who offer the Son of God as a victim, and so they set themselves above the Son of God. Nor does it matter that they deny that they slaughter him. Many things were formerly offered by priests which were not slaughtered but merely sacrificed, such as cakes, offerings of flour, and so on; but living animals could not be offered unless they were slaughtered. Therefore the Missarii either slaughter Christ, or they do not offer him. The Jews indeed slaughtered Christ, but did not sacrifice him, because they slaughtered him not as priests but as executioners. He himself, being willing to be slaughtered by them, offered himself through the eternal Spirit, without blemish, to God; and indeed he once offered himself as a victim to the Father for us. He was offered once to bear the sins of many; and a second time, without sin, he will be seen by those who wait for him unto salvation. The one victim offered for sins sits forever at the right hand of God. Against these clear testimonies of Scripture the Missarii want Christ to be offered more often; they want him to be sacrificed, but not slaughtered for the expiation of sins. But a sacrifice for the expiation of sins cannot be without slaughter: for without the shedding of blood there is no forgiveness. Heb. 9, 14. Heb. 9, 28. Heb. 10, 12. Heb. 9, 22. Therefore the sacrifice of the Mass is an imposture.

units.la: 7. Missa pugnat cum articulis fidei, de veritate naturæ humanæ Christi, de vera ascensione in cœlum: de reditu eius ad judicium. Affingit enim Christo corpus invisibile ex pane factum, latens sub speciebus panis & vini, quod nec natum est ex virgine, neq; ascendit, nec rediturum est.
units.tr: 7. The Mass conflicts with the articles of faith concerning the truth of the human nature of Christ, concerning his true ascension into heaven, and concerning his return to judgment. For it attributes to Christ an invisible body made from bread, lying hidden under the appearances of bread and wine, which was neither born of the Virgin, nor ascended, nor will return.

units.la: 8. Missa pugnat cum communione sanctorum cum Christo: Fingit enim execrabili commento, Christi corpus in nostra corpora illabi, & tamdiu in ventriculo nostro manere, quamdiu manent indigestæ species panis & vini. Cœna vero docet, nos non esu corporali, sed communione spirituali, per Spiritum sanctum fieri membra Christi, & Christo inseri.
units.tr: 8. The Mass conflicts with the communion of the saints with Christ. For by an execrable invention it pretends that the body of Christ glides into our bodies and remains in our stomach as long as the undigested appearances of bread and wine remain. The Supper, on the other hand, teaches that we become members of Christ and are grafted into Christ not by bodily eating, but by spiritual communion, through the Holy Spirit.

units.la: 9. Denique Missa pugnat cum vero Dei cultu: quia statuit adorationem idololatricam in pane, de qua supra est dictum. Alligant enim potificij adorationem ad rem, ad quam ipse Christus eam expresso verbo non alligauit: & sic profitentur se idolatras: non minus, quàm si ad parietem, aut coram columna procidentes Christum adorarent.
units.tr: 9. Finally, the Mass conflicts with the true worship of God, because it establishes an idolatrous adoration in the bread, of which we have spoken above. For the Papists tie the adoration to the thing to which Christ himself did not tie it by any express word; and so they profess themselves idolaters, no less than if they were falling prostrate before a wall or in front of a pillar to adore Christ.

units.la: Ex his constat, Missam esse idolum, ex variis iisque horrendis erroribus & blasphemiis ab Antichristo conflatum, & in locum cœnæ Dominicæ substitutum: proinde recte ac necessario rursus aboleri.
units.tr: From these things it is clear that the Mass is an idol, forged by Antichrist out of various and horrible errors and blasphemies, and substituted in place of the Lord's Supper; therefore it must rightly and necessarily be abolished again.

units.la: Obiect. 1. Missa est applicatio sacrificij Christi: Ergo non tollenda. Resp. Negatur antecedens: quia sola fide applicatur nobis meritum Christi: sicut ipse Christus per fidem habitat in cordibus nostris.
units.tr: Objection 1. The Mass is an application of Christ's sacrifice; therefore it is not to be abolished. Reply: The antecedent is denied, because the merit of Christ is applied to us by faith alone, just as Christ himself dwells in our hearts through faith.

units.la: Obiect. 2. Oportet esse sacrificium perpetuum in Ecclesia, quia Esaias prædixit futurum sabbathum ex sabbatho: & Malachias: Offerent munus purum omni loco, &c. Resp. Sacrificia novæ Ecclesiæ sunt eucharistica: & de tali sacrificio jugi ac puro loquuntur prophetæ. Tale sacrificium, nempe gratiarum actionis, patres vocarunt eucharistiam. 1. Quia est recordatio sacrificij Christi. 2. Quia in primitiva Ecclesia eleemosynæ offerebantur, & dabantur pauperibus, peracta cœna, quæ erant sacrificium. Cœnam verò sacrificium propitiatorium esse, patres nunquam somniarunt. Hic tria sunt explicanda. 1. Qui ad coenam debeant accedere. 2. Quid accipiant impij, si accedant. 3. Quis sit coenae legitimus visus.
units.tr: Objection 2. There must be a perpetual sacrifice in the Church, because Isaiah foretold that there would be sabbath after sabbath, and Malachi says: "They shall offer a pure offering in every place," etc. Reply: The sacrifices of the New Church are eucharistic, and the prophets speak of this continual and pure sacrifice. The Fathers called this sacrifice, namely the sacrifice of thanksgiving, the Eucharist. (1) Because it is a remembrance of Christ's sacrifice; (2) because in the primitive Church alms were offered and given to the poor after the supper was finished, and these were the sacrifice. But the Fathers never dreamed that the supper was a propitiatory sacrifice. Three things must be explained here: (1) who ought to come to the supper; (2) what the wicked receive if they come; (3) what is the lawful use of the supper.

units.la: QVÆSTIO LXXXI. Quibus accedendum est ad mensam Domini?
units.tr: QUESTION 81. To whom must one come to the Lord's table?

units.la: RESPONSIO.
units.tr: ANSWER.

units.la: Iis tantum, qui verè dolent, se suis peccatis DEVM offendisse: confidunt autem, sibi ea propter Christum remissa esse: & quas reliquas habent infirmitates, eas passione & morte illius obtectas esse, quique desiderant magis ac magis in fide & integritate vitæ proficere. Hypocritæ autem, & qui non verè resipiscunt, damnationem sibi edunt & bibunt a.
units.tr: Only to those who truly grieve that they have offended God by their sins, who trust that these have been forgiven them for Christ's sake, who believe that whatever infirmities they still have are covered by his passion and death, and who desire more and more to make progress in faith and in integrity of life. But hypocrites, and those who do not truly repent, eat and drink damnation to themselves a.

units.la: EXPLICATIO.
units.tr: EXPLANATION.

units.la: Hic tria sunt explicanda. 1. Qui ad coenam debeant accedere. 2. Quid accipiant impij, si accedant. 3. Quis sit coenæ legitimus vsus.
units.tr: Three things must be explained here: (1) who ought to come to the supper; (2) what the wicked receive if they come; (3) what is the lawful use of the supper.

units.la: I. Qui ad coenam accedere debeant.
units.tr: I. Who ought to come to the supper.

units.la: Distincta sunt quæstiones, qui debeant accedere, & qui debeant admitti ad coenam. Prior loquitur de officio vtentium: Posterior de officio Ecclesiæ, & ministrorum. Prior est angustior: posterior est latior & generalior: quia tantum pij debent accedere: sed non tantum pij, verum etiam hypocritæ nondum patefacti sunt ab Ecclesia admittendi. Omnes igitur, qui debent accedere, etiam debent admitti: sed non contra, omnes qui peccata sua agnoscunt, & verè de his dolent. 2. Qui confidunt ea sibi remissa esse, per & propter Christum. 3. Qui habent serium propositum in fide & vitæ integritate magis ac magis proficiendi: hoc est, ij tantum debent accedere ad coenam, & sunt digni conuiuæ Christi, qui viunt in fide & vera poenitentia. In his consistit vera probatio sui, de qua Paulus: Homo (inquit) probet seipsum, & sic edat de pane hoc. Probare seipsum, est explorare, an habeas fidem & poenitentiam, sicut dicitur: Explorate vosipsos, an sitis in fide: an Christus habitet in vobis. Sed vnde quis potest cognoscere, quod hæc habeat? 1. Ex fiducia & tranquillitate conscientiæ: quia Iustificati fide pacem habemus. Spes non confundit. Nam charitas Dei diffusa est in cordibus nostris per Spiritum sanctum, qui datus est nobis. 2. Ex effectis, hoc est, ex initiis veræ obedientiæ interinternæ & externæ, & ex serio proposito obediendi Deo secun-dum omnia mandata. Hæc in se habentes & sentientes debent accedere: seu habentes fidem & pœnitentiam, non modo potentiâ, sed etiam actu. Infantes nondum sunt capaces cœnæ: quia nondum fidem habent actu, sed tantum inclinatione. Hic requiritur fides actualis, initiû nouæ obedientiæ, propositum piè viuendi: probatio suiipsius, & commemoratio mortis Domini: quæ non sunt infantum, sed adultorum.
units.tr: The questions of who ought to come and who ought to be admitted to the supper are distinct. The first concerns the duty of those who partake; the second concerns the duty of the Church and its ministers. The first is narrower; the second is broader and more general. For only the godly ought to come, but not only the godly are to be admitted by the Church, since hypocrites are not yet exposed. Therefore all who ought to come also ought to be admitted, but not conversely: all who acknowledge their sins and truly grieve over them. (2) Those who trust that these have been forgiven them, through and for Christ. (3) Those who have a serious purpose of making progress in faith and in integrity of life. That is, only those who live in faith and true repentance ought to come to the supper, and they are worthy guests of Christ. In this lies the true self-examination of which Paul speaks: Let a man (he says) examine himself, and so let him eat of this bread. To examine oneself is to test whether one has faith and repentance, as it is said: Test yourselves, whether you are in the faith; whether Christ dwells in you. But how can anyone know that he has these? (1) From confidence and tranquillity of conscience, because being justified by faith we have peace. Hope does not disappoint. For the love of God has been poured out in our hearts through the Holy Spirit, who has been given to us. (2) From the effects, that is, from the beginnings of true obedience, inward and outward, and from a serious purpose of obeying God in all his commandments. Those who have and feel these things in themselves ought to come, that is, those who have faith and repentance not merely potentially but also actually. Infants are not yet capable of the supper, because they do not yet have faith actually, but only by inclination. Here actual faith is required, the beginning of new obedience, the purpose of living piously, self-examination, and the remembrance of the Lord's death, which belong not to infants but to adults.

units.la: Impiis & hypocritis, qui non habent veram fidem & pœnitentiam, non licet accedere. 1. Quia sacramenta tantum sunt instituta fidelibus & conuersis, vt his promissionem Euangelij obsignent, & fidem confirment. Verbum quidem est conuersis, & non conuersis commune, vt conuersi confirmentur, nondum conuerti conuertantur: sacramenta verò ad solos fideles pertinent. Ideo Christus cœnam solis suis discipulis instituit, dicens: Desiderio desideraui manducare hoc pascha vobiscum. Ex subiecto igitur sacramentorum sumitur demonstratiua probatio. Quod Deus instituit suis domesticis & filiis, id non debent accipere hypocritæ & alieni ab ecclesia. 2. Paulus omnes impios & hypocritas verbis authenticis à cœna arcet, cum præcipit, vt quisque probet seipsum, & sic edat de pane hoc, & bibat de poculo hoc. 3. Quia hypocritæ vel impij huc se ingerentes, manducant & bibunt sibi judicium, & rei fiunt corporis & sanguinis Christi. Qui enim indignè manducat panem hunc, & bibit de poculo hoc, manducat & bibit sibi judicium, reus est corporis & sanguinis Domini. 4. Accedant generalia scripturæ testimonia, quibus vsus sacramentorum, qui fit ab inconuersis, damnatur: Omitte munus tuum ad altare, & abi prius, reconciliare fratri tuo. Qui mactat bouem, est quasi qui mactat canem. Si legis transgressor fueris, circumcisio tua facta est præputium.
units.tr: It is not lawful for the ungodly and hypocrites, who do not have true faith and repentance, to come. (1) Because the sacraments are instituted only for the faithful and the converted, so that they may seal to them the promise of the gospel and confirm their faith. The Word indeed is common to the converted and the unconverted, so that the converted may be confirmed and the not yet converted may be converted; but the sacraments pertain to the faithful alone. Therefore Christ instituted the supper for his disciples alone, saying: With desire I have desired to eat this Passover with you. From the subject of the sacraments, then, a demonstrative proof is drawn: what God instituted for his household and sons, hypocrites and strangers to the Church ought not to receive. (2) Paul, in authentic words, keeps all the ungodly and hypocrites from the supper, when he commands that each one examine himself, and so eat of this bread and drink of this cup. (3) Because hypocrites or the ungodly who thrust themselves in here eat and drink judgment to themselves, and become guilty of the body and blood of Christ: For whoever eats this bread unworthily and drinks this cup, eats and drinks judgment to himself, being guilty of the body and blood of the Lord. (4) The general testimonies of Scripture also come in, by which the use of the sacraments made by the unconverted is condemned: Leave your gift there before the altar, and go first and be reconciled to your brother. He who slaughters an ox is like one who kills a dog. If you are a transgressor of the law, your circumcision has become uncircumcision.

units.la: Impiis & hypocritis non licet accedere ad cœnam. Luc. 22, 1. 1 Cor. 11, 29. Matt. 5, 24. Esa. 66, 3. Rom. 2, 25.
units.tr: It is not lawful for the ungodly and hypocrites to come to the supper. Luke 22:1. 1 Cor. 11:29. Matt. 5:24. Isa. 66:3. Rom. 2:25.

units.la: Obiect. 1. Deus mandat omnibus, vt vtantur sacramentis: & Christus dicit: Accipite, bibite ex hoc omnes. Ergo impij accedentes non peccant. Resp. ad antecedens. Mandat omnibus vsum sacramentorum, sed legitimum, qui non est sine fide & pœnitentia. Mandat, vt omnes baptizentur, & vtantur cœna: sed & mandat, vt omnes credant, & agant pœnitentiam. Resipiscite & baptizamini. Quisque probet seipsum.
units.tr: Objection 1. God commands everyone to use the sacraments, and Christ says: Take, drink of this, all of you. Therefore the ungodly who come do not sin. Reply to the antecedent: He commands everyone the use of the sacraments, but the lawful use, which is not without faith and repentance. He commands that everyone be baptized and partake of the supper, but he also commands that everyone believe and repent: Repent and be baptized. Let each one examine himself.

units.la: Obiectio 2. Omnes sumus indigni. Ergo omnibus est abstinendum. Resp. ad antecedens. Omnes sumus indigni naturâ, & in nobis: sed digni reddimur gratiâ Christi, modò afferamus fidem & bonam conscientiam. Augustinus: Securus accede, panis est, non venenum. Non igitur quenquam indignitas sua abstin-ere debet, quia digni sunt afferentes fidem & pœnitentiam.
units.tr: Objection 2. We are all unworthy; therefore one should abstain from it altogether. Reply to the antecedent: We are all unworthy by nature and in ourselves, but we are made worthy by the grace of Christ, provided we bring faith and a good conscience. Augustine: Come near securely; it is bread, not poison. Therefore no one's unworthiness ought to keep him away, because those who bring faith and repentance are worthy.

units.la: Acts 2, 38. 1 Cor. 11, 28. In Iohannem tract. 28. Esa. 66, 2. Ad quem respiciam, nisi ad pauperculum, & contritum spiritu, & tre-mentem sermones meos?
units.tr: Acts 2:38. 1 Cor. 11:28. Augustine, On John, tractate 28. Isa. 66:2. To whom shall I look, but to the poor man, and the one who is contrite in spirit and trembles at my words?

units.la: Obj. 3. Qui vitant profanationem cœnæ, recte faciunt. Abstinentes à cœna propter odia, aut alia peccata, vitant profanationem cœnæ. Ergo recte faciunt. Resp. ad maiorem, per dist. Qui vitant profanationem cœnæ, eo modo, quo vitare debent, nempe, agendo pœnitentiam, recte faciunt: pessime vero, qui persequerando in peccatis, hypocrisi, vel odiis, vitare volunt. Hi enim peccatum peccato cumulant, & profanationi contemtum addunt: nec facunt facienda mala, ut eueniant bona.
units.tr: Objection 3. Those who avoid profaning the supper do right. Those who abstain from the supper because of hatreds or other sins avoid profaning the supper. Therefore they do right. Reply to the major premise, with a distinction: Those who avoid profaning the supper in the way they ought to avoid it, namely by repenting, do right; but those who want to avoid it while persisting in sins, hypocrisy, or hatreds do very wrongly. For these heap sin upon sin and add contempt to profanation; nor do they do evil that good may come.

units.la: II. Quid in cœna accipiant impij.
units.tr: II. What the wicked receive in the Supper.

units.la: Impij & hypocritæ accedentes ad cœnam, non accipiunt res signatas, corpus & sanguinem Christi, &c. sed nuda symbola, & quidem ad judicium.
units.tr: The wicked and hypocrites who come to the Supper do not receive the things signified, the body and blood of Christ, etc., but only the bare symbols, and that to their judgment.

units.la: Probatur: 1. à definitione manducationis. Manducare Christum, est fieri participem essentiæ, meriti, efficaciæ, & omnium beneficiorum Christi, sicut dicitur: Qui manducat me, viuet propter me: manet in me, & ego in ipso. Impij & infideles non fiunt participes Christi. Non ergo manducant Christum.
units.tr: It is proved: 1. From the definition of eating. To eat Christ is to become a partaker of his essence, merit, efficacy, and all the benefits of Christ, as it is said: He who eats me will live because of me. He abides in me, and I in him. The wicked and unbelievers do not become partakers of Christ. Therefore they do not eat Christ.

units.la: 2. A modo & organo manducationis. Corpus Christi manducatur sola fide. Christum enim cum suis beneficiis accipimus sola fide: & corpus Christi est cibus mentis, non ventris: cordis, non oris, ut recte dicitur in catech. Lutheri: Hæc verba, pro vobis, requirunt corda credentia. Impij & hypocritæ destituuntur fide. Ergo non percipiunt corpus Christi.
units.tr: 2. From the mode and organ of eating. The body of Christ is eaten by faith alone. For we receive Christ with his benefits by faith alone, and the body of Christ is food of the mind, not of the belly; of the heart, not of the mouth, as is rightly said in Luther's Catechism: These words, "for you," require believing hearts. The wicked and hypocrites lack faith. Therefore they do not receive the body of Christ.

units.la: 3. Christus in cœna suum corpus iis solis offert manducandum, pro quibus se obtulit in cruce. Obtulit autem se pro sodum, pro quibus se obtulit in cruce. lis credentibus, non pro impiis, vel hypocritis. Rogo non pro mundo, sed pro crediturs. Hoc est corpus meum, quod pro vobis traditur.
units.tr: 3. Christ in the Supper offers his body to be eaten only by those for whom he offered himself on the cross. But he offered himself for his own, for whom he offered himself on the cross, that is, for believers, not for the impious or hypocrites. I do not pray for the world, but for those who will believe. This is my body, which is given for you.

units.la: 4. Corpus Christi est panis viuificus, quem quicunque percipiunt, vitam simul percipiunt. Spiritus enim Christi à suo corpore non separatur. Qui manducat carnem meam, in me manet, & ego in eo. Impij percipientes symbola non percipiunt vitam. Impij igitur symbola percipiunt sine rebus.
units.tr: 4. The body of Christ is the living bread, and whoever receives it at the same time receives life. For the Spirit of Christ is not separated from his body. He who eats my flesh abides in me, and I in him. The wicked, receiving the symbols, do not receive life. Therefore the wicked receive the symbols without the things.

units.la: 5. Infideles edunt & bibunt sibi judicium. Ergo non edunt corpus & sanguinem Christi. Valet à contrariis. Nam edere sibi judicium, est per incredulitatem & abusum sacramenti à Christo & omnibus eius bonis alienari & repelli, seu, per abusum sacramenti sine fide & pœnitentia sumti, Deum grauiter offendere, atque ita sibi pœnas temporales & æternas attrahere, nisi resipiscant. Contra, manducare Christum, est fide fieri participem Christi & sti & omnium eius bonorum. Nemo enim potest manducare Christum, & non simul particeps fieri ipsius meriti, efficaciae & bonorum. Nemo igitur potest manducare Christum, & edere sibi judicium.
units.tr: 5. Unbelievers eat and drink judgment to themselves. Therefore they do not eat the body and blood of Christ. The inference holds by contraries. For to eat judgment to oneself is, through unbelief and abuse of the sacrament, to be alienated and cut off from Christ and all his goods; or, by abusing a sacrament taken without faith and repentance, to offend God grievously and so draw upon oneself temporal and eternal punishments, unless they repent. On the contrary, to eat Christ is, by faith, to become a partaker of Christ and of all his goods. For no one can eat Christ and not at the same time become a partaker of his merit, efficacy, and goods. Therefore no one can both eat Christ and eat judgment to himself.

units.la: 6. Paulus cum dicit; Non potestis participes esse mensae Domini, & mensae daemoniorum, impiis aliquid adimit in mensa Domini, de quo non possint participare. Sed fiunt in mensa Domini participes symbolorum panis & vini. Ergo adimit eis participationem rerum signatarum corporis & sanguinis Christi, &c. Obiect. Non potestis, nempe bona conscientia, & ad salutem. Resp. Est falsa glossa. Apostolus non argumentatur ab inutili, sed ab impossibili. Non debetis participare idolothytis: quare? quia hoc est participare daemoniis. At impossibile est, vos simul participes esse mensae daemoniorum, & mensae Domini: quia impossibile est, simul duobus dominis servire, sicut Christus dicit: Nemo potest duobus dominis servire. Non potestis Deo servire & mammonae. Sic Apostolus: Non potestis mensae Domini participes esse, & mensae daemoniorum.
units.tr: 6. When Paul says, You cannot be partakers of the table of the Lord and of the table of demons, he takes away from the wicked something at the table of the Lord of which they cannot partake. But in the Lord's table they become partakers of the symbols of bread and wine. Therefore he takes from them participation in the things signified, the body and blood of Christ, etc. Objection: "You cannot," that is, with a good conscience and unto salvation. Answer: This gloss is false. The Apostle does not argue from what is useless but from what is impossible. You must not partake of idol meats; why? Because this is to partake of demons. But it is impossible for you to be at once partakers of the table of demons and of the table of the Lord, just as it is impossible to serve two masters at once, as Christ says: No one can serve two masters. You cannot serve God and mammon. So the Apostle says: You cannot be partakers of the table of the Lord and of the table of demons.

units.la: 7. Christus dicit: Non est honestum, panem filiorum objcere canibus. Corpus Christi est panis filiorum: hoc est, fidelium. Ergo Christum suum corpus non obijcit canibus, hoc est, impiis, contra suam ipsius doctrinam: Ne sanctum detis canibus, nec margaritas porcis, &c.
units.tr: 7. Christ says: It is not right to take the children's bread and throw it to the dogs. The body of Christ is the children's bread, that is, of the faithful. Therefore Christ does not throw his body to the dogs, that is, to the impious, which would contradict his own teaching: Do not give what is holy to the dogs, nor pearls to the swine, etc.

units.la: 8. Ab authoritate patrum, qui idem docuerunt. Augustinus lib.21.cap.25. de civitate Dei, & in Johannem tract.26. & 59. & in sentent. Prosperi cap.339. Ambros.serm. de coena: Quamuis ab indignis se sumi, vel contingi sacramenta permittant: non possunt tamen spiritus esse participes: quorum infidelitas, vel indignitas tantae sanctitudini contradicit. Et mox: Verum his, qui verbotenus corde sicci & mente aridi sacris intersunt, vel etiam participant de donis: lambunt quidem petram, sed inde nec mel sugunt, nec oleum: quia nec aliqua charitatis dulcedine, nec Spiritus sancti pinguedine vegetantur, nec se judicant: nec sacramenta dijudicant: sed sicut cibis communibus irreuerenter sacris utuntur muneribus: & dominicae mensae in veste luculenta se ingerunt impudenter: quibus melius erat mola asinaria collo alligata mergi in pelagus: quam illota conscientia de manu domini buccellam accipere, qui usq; hodie hoc veracissimum & sanctissimum corpus suum creat, & sanctificat, & benedicit, & pie sumentibus dividit.
units.tr: 8. From the authority of the Fathers, who taught the same. Augustine, City of God book 21, chapter 25, and on John, tractates 26 and 59, and in the Sentences of Prosper, chapter 339. Ambrose, sermon on the Supper: Although they allow the sacraments to be taken or touched by the unworthy, yet they cannot be partakers of the Spirit, whose unbelief or unworthiness contradicts such holiness. And shortly after: But those who attend the sacred rites dry in word and arid in mind, or even partake of the gifts, indeed lick the rock, but from it they suck neither honey nor oil, because they are not quickened by any sweetness of charity nor by the fatness of the Holy Spirit, nor do they judge themselves or discern the sacraments; but as they use common food, so they use the sacred gifts irreverently, and shamelessly thrust themselves into the Lord's table in fine clothing. For them it would be better to be sunk in the sea with a millstone hung about the neck than to take a morsel from the hand of the Lord with an unclean conscience. He who even today creates, sanctifies, and blesses this most true and most holy body of his, and divides it to those who receive it piously.

units.la: Cur vero infideles & impij edendo & bibendo sibi attrahant judicium, causae sunt. 1. Quia profanant sacra symbola, trahendo ad se, quae non ipsis, sed discipulis Christi sunt instituta.
units.tr: The causes why the unbelieving and wicked, by eating and drinking, draw judgment upon themselves are these. 1. Because they profane the holy symbols, taking to themselves what was instituted not for them but for the disciples of Christ.

units.la: 2. Quia profanant foedus Dei, usurpando sibi signa foederis, ut videanvideantur esse confoederati Deo, cùm sint confoederati diabolo, non Deo, quem quantum in ipsis est, socium impiorum constituunt.Quia non discernunt corpus Domini, & sanguinem eius conculcant. Offeruntur quidem eis beneficia: sed cum ea non accipiant fide, derident Deum, dum profitentur se accipere, cum nihil minus faciant, aut velint, & aliis peccatis novum hoc addant.Quia suo se judicio condemnant. Accedentes enim profitentur, se approbare hanc doctrinam, & se credere, extra Christum non esse salutem. Interea sibi sunt conscij: quod sint hypocritæ. Sic ergo damnant seipsos.
units.tr: 2. Because they profane the covenant of God, usurping for themselves the signs of the covenant so that they may seem to be in covenant with God, when they are in covenant with the devil and not with God; and so, as far as they are concerned, they make God a partner of the impious. Because they do not discern the body of the Lord and trample his blood underfoot. Benefits are indeed offered to them, but since they do not receive them by faith, they mock God while they profess that they receive, when they do nothing less or wish nothing less, and add this new sin to their other sins. Because they condemn themselves by their own judgment. For in coming they profess that they approve this doctrine and believe that there is no salvation outside Christ, yet meanwhile they are conscious that they are hypocrites. Thus they condemn themselves.

units.la: Vana igitur est eorum obiectio, qui dicunt: Impij sibi edunt judicium: Ergo edunt corpus Christi. Resp. Contrarium sequitur. Edunt judicium: Ergo non corpus Christum, & edere judicium, sunt contraria: quæ non consistunt simul. Inst.1. Edunt indignè. Ergo tamen edunt. Resp. Concedo: edunt indignè panem sacramenti, sed non Christum. Expressè enim dicitur: Quisquis ederit hunc panem indignè. Inst.2. Christus non tantum est salvator, sed etiam judex. Resp. Est judex, non eorum, à quibus manducatur: sed eorum, à quibus respuitur. Nam de manducantibus dicit: Qui manducat me, vivet propter me. De profanatoribus verò: Discedite à me omnes, qui operamini iniquitatem. Sicut igitur Euangelium creditum, est odor vitæ ad vitam: contemtum, est odor mortis ad mortem: ita Christus manducatus vivificat, spretus judicat. Spernitur autem, dum in verbo & sacramentis infidelibus offertur, sed infidelitate respuitur. Inst.3. Iuntrei corporis Christi. Resp. Causa reatus eorum non est manducatio Christi, sed manducatio panis sine Christo, quia dicitur: Qui indignè edit de pane hoc, &c. Abusus ergo symboli est contemtus ipsius Christi: sicut violatio diplomatis vel sigilli principis, est læsio ipsius principis, & crimen læsæ maiestatis. Inst.4. Quomodo edunt judicium, & fiunt rei, cùm sit bonum opus accipere sacramenta? Resp. Sumtio sacramentorum est bonum opus per se, & cum accedit verus & legitimus usus: extra hunc usum fit opus non mandatum, sed prohibitum à Deo, de quo Deus dicit: Qui macIat bovem, est quasi mactet canem. Et: Si transgressor fueris legis, circumcisio tua facta est præputium. Alioqui etiam liceret colligere: Sumtio corporis Christi est res bona. Ergo impij ea sumtione non possunt fieri rei corporis Christi.
units.tr: Therefore vain is their objection who say: The wicked eat judgment to themselves; therefore they eat the body of Christ. Answer: The opposite follows: they eat judgment, therefore not the body of Christ; and to eat judgment and to eat Christ are contraries, which cannot exist together. Objection 1: They eat unworthily; therefore they do eat. Answer: I grant it: they eat the bread of the sacrament unworthily, but not Christ. For it is expressly said: Whoever eats this bread unworthily. Objection 2: Christ is not only Savior but also Judge. Answer: He is judge not of those by whom he is eaten, but of those by whom he is rejected. For of those who eat he says: He who eats me will live because of me. But of the profaners: Depart from me, all you workers of iniquity. As therefore the gospel believed is a fragrance of life unto life, but scorned a fragrance of death unto death, so Christ eaten quickens, and Christ scorned judges. He is scorned when he is offered to unbelievers in word and sacraments, but is rejected through unbelief. Objection 3: They are guilty of the body of Christ. Answer: The cause of their guilt is not the eating of Christ but the eating of bread without Christ, since it is said: Whoever eats this bread unworthily, etc. The abuse of the symbol is therefore contempt of Christ himself, just as the violation of a prince's diploma or seal is an injury to the prince himself and the crime of high treason. Objection 4: How do they eat judgment and become guilty, since receiving the sacraments is a good work? Answer: The taking of the sacraments is a good work in itself, and it is so when a true and lawful use accompanies it. Outside this use it becomes a work not commanded but forbidden by God, of which God says: He who slaughters an ox is as if he slew a dog. And: If you are a transgressor of the law, your circumcision has become uncircumcision. Otherwise one could also infer: the taking of the body of Christ is a good thing; therefore the wicked cannot by that taking become guilty of the body of Christ.

units.la: III. Quis sit cænæ legitimus usus.
units.tr: III. What the lawful use of the Supper is.

units.la: Legitimus usus cænæ est, cum fideles in Ecclesia sumunt panem & poculum Domini, & annunciant mortem eius, ut ea sumtio
units.tr: The lawful use of the Supper is when the faithful in the Church take the bread and cup of the Lord and proclaim his death, so that this partaking

units.la: Ioh. 6, 57. Matt. 7, 23. Esa. 66, 3. 1 Cor. 11, 2. Rom. 2, 26. sumtio sit pignus vnionis suae cum Christo, & applicatio totius beneficij redemtionis & salutionis nostrae. In tribus igitur consistit.
units.tr: John 6:57. Matt. 7:23. Isa. 66:3. 1 Cor. 11:2. Rom. 2:26. is a pledge of their union with Christ and the application of the whole benefit of our redemption and salvation. It therefore consists in three things.

units.la: 1. Quando ritus à Christo instituti retinentur, & observantur, & quidem observantur, non ludicrè, vel ab vno priuatim, sed in legitimo Ecclesiæ conuentu, siue magno, siue parvo. Ritus autem instituti sunt, vt panis Domini frangatur, distribuatur & sumatur: poculum Domini detur omnibus communicantibus, cum recordatione mortis Domini. 2. Quando ritus seruantur ab iis personis, quibus eos Christus instituit, hoc est, quando paminus sumi voluit: nempe non ab hostibus, sed à discipulis suis, hoc est, à fidelibus. Obseruatio enim ritus sine fide & poenitentia, non est vsus, sed abusus & hypocrisis. 3. Quando coena sumitur, & tota actio dirigitur in finem à Christo institutum, nempe in memoriam mortis Domini, hoc est, ad confirmationem infirmæ fidei, & gratitudinem Deo præstandam.
units.tr: (1) When the rite instituted by Christ is retained and observed, and observed not in jest or privately by one person, but in a lawful assembly of the Church, whether large or small. The rite was instituted so that the bread of the Lord is broken, distributed and eaten, and the cup of the Lord is given to all who communicate, with remembrance of the Lord's death. (2) When the rite is observed by those persons to whom Christ gave it, that is, when he wished it to be taken by those for whom it was intended: not by enemies, but by his disciples, that is, by the faithful. For observance of the rite without faith and repentance is not use but abuse and hypocrisy. (3) When the Supper is taken and the whole action is directed to the end appointed by Christ, namely in remembrance of the Lord's death, that is, for the strengthening of weak faith and for the thanks to be rendered to God.

units.la: QVÆSTIO LXXXII.
units.tr: QUESTION LXXXII.

units.la: Suntne illi etiam ad hanc cœnam admittendi, qui confessione & vita se infideles & impios esse declarant?
units.tr: Are those also to be admitted to this supper who declare by their confession and their life that they are unbelieving and impious?

units.la: RESPONSIO.
units.tr: ANSWER.

units.la: Nequaquam. Nam eo pacto fœdus Dei profanatur, & ira Dei in universum cœtum concitatur 4. Quocirca Ecclesia, ex præscripto Christi & Apostolorum, hos, clauibus regni cœlorum vtens, à cœna arcere debet, quoad resipuerint, & mores mutauerint.
units.tr: By no means. For in that way the covenant of God is profaned, and the wrath of God is stirred up against the whole assembly. Therefore the Church, following the precept of Christ and the Apostles and using the keys of the kingdom of heaven, ought to keep such people from the supper until they repent and change their ways.

units.la: EXPLICATIO.
units.tr: EXPLANATION.

units.la: Ad cœnam ab Ecclesia sunt admittendi: 1. Quorum ætas est idonea ad probationem sui, & ad commemorationem mortis Domini, juxta præceptum: Hoc facite in mei commemorationem. Homo probet seipsum, & sic edat de pane hoc. Mortem Domini annunciate, donec venerit. Infantes igitur Ecclesiæ, etsi pro fidelibus censentur, ab vsu huius sacramenti exiluntur. 2. Qui sunt baptizati, & per baptismum facti membra ecclesiæ. In cœna enim fœdus cum Deo initum in baptismo renouatur. tur. Ideo olim de paschate non licebat edere, nisi prius circumcisis. Turcæ igitur, Iudæi, & alii ab ecclesia alieni à cœna arcen-di sunt.
units.tr: The Church is to admit to the supper: (1) those whose age is suitable for self-examination and for remembrance of the Lord's death, according to the command: Do this in remembrance of me. Let a man examine himself, and so eat of this bread. Proclaim the Lord's death until he comes. Infants of the Church, therefore, although they are counted among the faithful, are excluded from the use of this sacrament. (2) Those who have been baptized and have become members of the church through baptism. For in the supper the covenant entered into with God is renewed, as it was in baptism. For this reason, in former times, one might not eat of the Passover unless he had first been circumcised. Turks, Jews, and others foreign to the church are therefore to be kept from the supper.

units.la: 3. Qui verbis & factis veram pœnitentiam & fidem profiten-tur, seu, qui professionem fidei & pœnitentiæ, etiam vitæ actioni-bus exprimunt: siue id vere & sincere, siue per occultam hypo-crisin faciant. De occultis enim non iudicat ecclesia. Admittit ergo omnes, quos potest iudicare esse membra Christi, hoc est, quos audit & videt confessione & factis externis fidem & resi-piscentiam profiteri, siue sint vere pij, siue hypocritæ nondum patefacti.
units.tr: (3) Those who profess true repentance and faith by words and deeds, that is, who express their profession of faith and repentance also in the actions of their lives, whether they do so truly and sincerely or through hidden hypocrisy. For the Church does not judge hidden things. It therefore admits all whom it can judge to be members of Christ, that is, whom it hears and sees professing faith and repentance by confession and external deeds, whether they are truly godly or hypocrites not yet exposed.

units.la: Non sunt autem admittendi, qui quidem simpliciter se omnia credere dicunt, sed scelerate viuunt. Nam qui dicit se credere, & non habet opera, mentitur, & re ipsa negat, quod verbis affir-mat, iuxta illud apostoli: DEVM profitentur se scire, sed factis ne-gant, cum sint abominandi & rebelles, & ad omne opus bonum reprobi. Sic & Iacobus demonstrat, fidem, quæ est absque operibus, mor-tuam esse.
units.tr: Yet those are not to be admitted who indeed say that they simply believe everything, but live wickedly. For whoever says he believes, and has no works, is lying, and in fact denies by his deeds what he affirms in words, according to the saying of the Apostle: they profess that they know God, but they deny him by their works, being abominable and disobedient, and reprobate for every good work. So also James shows that faith without works is dead.

units.la: Rationes vero, cur tantum sint admittendi, qui confessione & vita fidem & pœnitentiam profitentur, sunt:
units.tr: The reasons why only those who profess faith and repentance by confession and life are to be admitted are these:

units.la: 1. Ecclesia profanaret fœdus Dei, si sciens admitteret incredu-los & impœnitentes. Faciens enim & consentiens eadem lege te-nentur. Profanare fœdus Dei est, venditare vel agnoscere eos pio confœderatis, aut sociis Dei, qui sunt hostes Dei, ac proinde Deum talem fingere, qui obliget se hypocritis & impiis. Prosa-natur ergo fœdus Dei, tam communicando symbola fœderis iis quibus Deus nihil promittit, quam vsurpando symbola sine fide & pœnitentia: non tantum, inquam, profanant fœdus, qui symbola fœderis impœnitentes ad se rapiunt, sed etiam, qui sci-entes & volentes dant iis, quos Deus à suo fœdere exclusit. Fa-ciunt enim Deum socium impiorum, & filios diaboli faciunt fi-lios Dei, quicunq; symbola dant impiis.
units.tr: (1) The Church would profane the covenant of God if, knowing it, it admitted unbelievers and the unrepentant. For the one who does the deed and the one who consents are bound by the same law. To profane the covenant of God is to pass off or acknowledge as allies or partners of God those who are enemies of God, and thus to imagine a God who binds himself to hypocrites and the impious. The covenant of God is therefore profaned both by sharing the signs of the covenant with those to whom God promises nothing, and by seizing the signs without faith and repentance. Not only do those profane the covenant who unrepentantly snatch the signs of the covenant for themselves, but also those who knowingly and willingly give them to those whom God has excluded from his covenant. For they make God a partner of the impious, and those who give the signs to the impious make the sons of the devil into sons of God.

units.la: 2. Ecclesia iram Dei in se concitaret, si sciens & volens ad cœnam admitteret impœnitentes. Testatur hoc apostolus, di-cens: Propterea inter vos multi sunt debiles, & infirmi, & multi dormiunt. Etenim si nos ipsi diiudicaremus, non puniremur: Con-sentientibus igitur vel conniuentibus ad profanationem sacra-menti Deus irascitur, eosque punit non minus, quam punitipsos impios, à conniuentibus admissos. Ab utrisq; enim cœna æque profanatur.
units.tr: (2) The Church would stir up the wrath of God against itself if, knowingly and willingly, it admitted the unrepentant to the supper. The Apostle bears witness to this, saying: For this reason many among you are weak and sickly, and many sleep. For if we judged ourselves, we would not be punished. Therefore, by consenting to or conniving at the profanation of the sacrament, God is angry and punishes those who connive no less than the impious themselves whom they have admitted. For the supper is profaned equally by both.

units.la: 3. Christus mandauit, vt impii non admittantur: Si quis neget extare tale mandatum de cœna, sententia tamen mandati facile probabitur. Christus enim cœnam suam instituit discipu-lis jis suis, & his solis dixit: Desiderio desideraui VOBISCVM manducare hoc pascha. accipite hoc, & partimini inter vos. Hoc poculum est nouum illud fœdus, per meum sanguinem, qui effunditur pro VOBIS. Solis vero discipulis CHRISTI cœna instituta est, & ad hos someos pertinet mandatum: Accipite, &c. reliqui omnes, pro quibus Christus non effudit sanguinem suum, excluduntur. His addi potest.
units.tr: (3) Christ commanded that the impious not be admitted. If someone should deny that such a command exists concerning the supper, the sense of the command can nonetheless easily be proven. For Christ instituted his supper for his own disciples, and said to them alone: With desire I have desired to eat WITH YOU this Passover. Take this and divide it among yourselves. This cup is the new covenant in my blood, which is poured out FOR YOU. The Lord's supper was instituted for the disciples of Christ alone, and the command: Take, etc., pertains to these alone. All the others, for whom Christ did not pour out his blood, are excluded. To these can be added:

units.la: 4. Demonstratio euidens. Qui abnegant fidem, non sunt habendi pro membris ecclesiæ, ne visibilis quidem. Omnes negantes pœnitentiam abnegant fidem; iuxta illud Apostoli: Deum profitentur se scire, sed facto negant, cum sint abominandi & rebelles, ad omne opus bonum reprobi. Ergo negantes pœnitentiam non sunt habendi pro membris ecclesiæ, nequidem visibilis. Proinde neque ad sacramenta ecclesiæ admitti, sed tanquam alieni ab illis arceri debent, quoad resipuerint & mores mutauerint. Admitti qui-dem debent cum piis hypocritæ nondum patefacti, vt qui confessione & factis externis fidem & resipiscentiam profitentur; Accedere vero nulli debent, nisi veri fideles. Nam præter hos alii omnes, etiam hypocritæ nondum patefacti, damnationem sibi edunt & bibunt, ac cœnam Domini profanant.
units.tr: (4) A clear demonstration. Those who deny faith are not to be regarded as members of the church, not even as visible members. All who deny repentance deny faith, according to the saying of the Apostle: They profess that they know God, but they deny him by their works, being abominable and disobedient, and reprobate for every good work. Therefore those who deny repentance are not to be regarded as members of the church, not even visible ones. Consequently they must not be admitted to the sacraments of the church, but kept away as strangers to them, until they repent and change their ways. Indeed, hypocrites not yet exposed, who profess faith and repentance by confession and external deeds, ought to be admitted along with the godly; but only true believers ought to approach. For all others, besides these, even hypocrites not yet exposed, eat and drink judgment to themselves and profane the Lord's supper.

units.la: Obiect. Ecclesia non profanat fœdus admittens hypocritas: Ergo nec profanat admittens impœnitentes. Respond. ad antecedens. Non peccat admittens hypocritas, nempe occultos & non-dum patefactos, quos quia ore profitentur fidem, & simulant pœnitentiam, cogitur pro sinceris agnoscere. Peccaret autem, si sciens & volens admitteret hypocritas iam detectos, fidem vel pœnitentiam ore vel factis negantes. Inst. At multi impœnitentes se ingerunt, & fœdus profanant; præsertim vbi non viget vsus disciplinæ ecclesiasticæ, & hos ecclesia admittit sine peccato. Ergo etiam non peccat admittens alios pœnitentiam negantes. Respond. Ecclesia tunc non peccat, non quod non sit peccatum, admittere impœnitentes, sed quia admittit, ignoras eos tales esse. Ipsi vero impœnitentes, qui se ingerunt, & ecclesiam fallunt, profanant fœdus, non ecclesiæ, aut piis vna communicantes, sibi. Sibi enim accersunt iudicium. Interim ecclesiæ est diligenter obseruare, quos & quales admittat; & minister non volens det cœnam abutentibus, sed instet monendo, & cüm piat cauere abusus. Beati enim qui esuriunt, & sitiunt iustitiam; Peccatum vero erit penes alios, nempe eos, qui abutuntur, vel commiment.
units.tr: Objection. The Church does not profane the covenant by admitting hypocrites; therefore neither does it profane it by admitting the unrepentant. Answer to the antecedent: one does not sin by admitting hypocrites, namely those who are hidden and not yet exposed, whom the Church is compelled to acknowledge as sincere because they profess faith with their mouths and feign repentance. But it would sin if, knowingly and willingly, it admitted hypocrites already detected, who deny faith or repentance by word or deed. Objection. But many unrepentant people thrust themselves in and profane the covenant, especially where the practice of ecclesiastical discipline does not flourish, and the Church admits them without sin. Therefore one who admits others who deny repentance does not sin either. Answer. The Church does not sin in that case, not because it is no sin to admit the unrepentant, but because it admits them without knowing that they are such. But the unrepentant themselves, who thrust themselves in and deceive the church, profane the covenant, not the church, nor the godly who communicate together with it, but themselves; for they bring judgment upon themselves. Meanwhile it is the duty of the church to observe carefully whom and what sort of people it admits; and the minister, unwilling to give the supper to those who abuse it, should press on by admonishing and take care to avoid abuses. Blessed are those who hunger and thirst after righteousness. The sin, however, will rest upon others, namely those who abuse it or permit it.

units.la: DE PASCHATE.
units.tr: ON THE PASSOVER.

units.la: Cum supra dictum sit, coenam Domini substitutam esse paschati: non abs re fuerit, breviter etiam explicare de paschate. I. Quid fuerit. II. Qui fuerint eius fines seu visus. III. Quae sint allegoriae ritIuum agni paschalis. IV. An sit abrogatum, & quid ei successerit.
units.tr: Since it has been said above that the Lord's Supper was substituted for the Passover, it will not be out of place to explain briefly the Passover also. I. What it was. II. What were its ends or uses. III. What are the allegories of the rites of the paschal lamb. IV. Whether it has been abrogated, and what has succeeded it.

units.la: I. Quid fuerit Pascha.
units.tr: I. What the Passover was.

units.la: Pascha erat solennis manducatio agni, à Deo Israelitis mandata, vt is ritus quotannis per familias iteratus, esset recordatio liberationis populi ex Ægypto, ac praecipuè significaret fidelribus liberationem spiritualem à peccato & morte per Christum mactandum in cruce, & fide manducandum. Seu, erat alterum veteris Ecclesiae sacramentum, anniversaria mactatione & commemoratione agni anniculi in singulis Judaeorum familiis ex DEI beneficij mandato peragendum, vt esset memoriale praestiti beneficij gratiae de liberationis ex Ægypto, & sigillum promissionis gratiae de emissione peccatorum propter victimam Messiae. Pascha Graece πάσχα vox ex Hebraeo Pesach transitus, à palach transfire, vel transsilire: Sic autem dictum fuit sacramentum, & totum festum, à transitu angeli, qui conspecto sanguine agni in superliminari Judaeorum, transiit, & pepercit eorum primogenitis, cum omnia primogenita Aegyptiorum trucidaret. Historia institutiprm paschatis exstat Exod.12. Praecepit Deus, hanc mactationem fieri certo ac vario ritu. Agnus anniculus, masculus, integer, segregandus erat à grege per familias, decima die primae mensis Nisan siue Abib: mactandus verò quatriduo post, inter duas vesperas, seu sub vesperam decimae quartae lunae exeuntis: sanguine eius aspergendi postes & superliminaria forium: tum assandus igne, & comedendus totus, & festinanter, adhibitis panibus azymis & herbis amaris. Comedentes verò stabant succincti lumbis, calceati & baculo subnixi. De hoc ritu inquit Deus: Pesach est Iehova. Sanguis ille erit pro vobis in signum, super illas domos, vbi eritis, vt videns sanguinem illum transeam praeter vos.
units.tr: The Passover was the solemn eating of a lamb, commanded by God to the Israelites, so that this rite, repeated yearly by households, would be a remembrance of the deliverance of the people from Egypt, and would especially signify to the faithful their spiritual deliverance from sin and death through Christ, who was to be slain on the cross and eaten by faith. Or, it was the second sacrament of the old Church, to be carried out each year in every Jewish household by the slaying and commemoration of a yearling lamb, by God's command of benefit, so that it might be a memorial of the grace bestowed in the deliverance from Egypt, and a seal of the promise of grace concerning the remission of sins on account of the sacrifice of the Messiah.
