The Greek word πάσχα [Pascha] comes from the Hebrew Pesach [פֶּסַח], passover, from the verb pasach, to pass over or leap over. The sacrament and the whole feast were so named from the passing over of the angel, who, when he saw the blood of the lamb on the lintel of the Jews, passed over and spared their firstborn, when he slew all the firstborn of the Egyptians. The account of the institution of the Passover is found in Exod. 12. God commanded that this slaughter be done with a fixed and particular rite. A yearling, male, unblemished lamb was to be set apart from the flock by households on the tenth day of the first month, Nisan or Abib; it was to be slain four days later, between the two evenings, that is, toward evening on the fourteenth day of the moon as it rose; its blood was to be sprinkled on the doorposts and lintels of the doors; then it was to be roasted with fire and eaten whole, and in haste, with unleavened bread and bitter herbs. Those who ate were to stand with their loins girded, shod, and leaning on a staff. Concerning this rite God says: "It is the Passover of Jehovah" [הוּא פֶּסַח לַיהוָה]. "That blood shall be for you a sign upon those houses where you are, so that when I see the blood I will pass over you."

units.la: Voluit autem Deus hoc festum esse anniversarium, hoc est, semel quotannis per totos dies septem summa solennitate celebrari. Esto dies iste vobis in monumentum, vt celebretis eum diem festum Iehova, per aetates vestras: statuto perpetuo celebrate eum. Septem dias dies panes azymos comeditote. Vide Exod. 23. v.5. Leuit. 23. v.5. Deut. 16. v.1.
units.tr: God willed that this feast be yearly, that is, celebrated once a year with the greatest solemnity over seven whole days. "Let this day be to you a memorial, that you may keep it as a feast to Jehovah throughout your generations; keep it as a perpetual statute. For seven days you shall eat unleavened bread." See Exod. 23. v.5. Lev. 23. v.5. Deut. 16. v.1.

units.la: II. Qui fuerint fines seu vsus paschatis.
units.tr: II. What the ends or uses of the Passover were.

units.la: Fines instituti paschatis quinque indicantur. Exod.12.
units.tr: The ends for which the Passover was instituted are five, see Exod. 12.

units.la: I. Vt sanguis agni in postibus esset signum transituri angeli, & conseruandorum primogenitorum. Erit autem sanguis ille pro vobis in signum super illas domos, vbi eritis, vt videns illum sanguinem transeam praeter vos. Hic finis respectu ritus & transitus semel facti postea desiit, etsi analogia perpetuo manet. Nam propter sanguinem Christi Deus & olim pepercit fidelibus, & nunc parcit, hoc est, remittit peccata, vt in secundo fine docetur.
units.tr: I. That the blood of the lamb should be a sign on the doorposts of the passing angel, and of the preservation of the firstborn. The blood shall be a sign for you on the houses where you are, and when I see the blood I will pass over you. This end, with respect to the rite and the passage once made, later ceased, although the analogy remains perpetually. For on account of the blood of Christ God both spared the faithful of old and still spares them, that is, forgives sins, as is taught in the second end.

units.la: II. Vt esset typus futuri sacrificij Messiae, seu signum praestan- dae liberationis per Christum: atque ita signum gratiae Dei erga ecclesiam. Hic fuit primarius finis paschatis annuersarij. Proba- tur. Os non confringetis in illo. Hunc typum Johannes dicit esse impletum, cum ossa Christi in cruce non frangerentur. Ergo agnus fuit typus Christi, & victimae eius. Item: Pascha nostrum pro nobis immolatum est Christus. Agnus ergo paschalis significabat Christum, & immolatio eius immolationem Christi. Item: Ecclesia intelligebat significationes aliorum sacrificiorum, quod essent typi victimae Messiae. Neque enim tam bruti erant patres, vt remissionem peccatorum in sanguine taurorum quaererent. Multo igitur magis in agno paschali fide intuebantur Messiam & victimam eius. Denique Iohannes Christum vocat agnum Dei, & quidem mactatum ab origine mundi: quia nimirum per agnum illum mactatum fuit significatus.
units.tr: II. That it should be a type of the future sacrifice of the Messiah, or a sign of the deliverance to be accomplished through Christ, and so a sign of God's grace toward the Church. This was the primary end of the yearly Passover. It is proved thus: "A bone of him shall not be broken." John says this type was fulfilled when the bones of Christ were not broken on the cross. Therefore the lamb was a type of Christ and of his sacrifice. Likewise: "Christ our Passover is sacrificed for us." The paschal lamb therefore signified Christ, and its slaughter signified the slaughter of Christ. Likewise: the Church understood the meaning of the other sacrifices, that they were types of the sacrifice of the Messiah. For the fathers were not so dull as to seek the forgiveness of sins in the blood of bulls; much more, then, did they behold the Messiah and his sacrifice by faith in the paschal lamb. Finally, John calls Christ "the Lamb of God, slain from the beginning of the world", because surely through that slain lamb he was signified.

units.la: III. Vt esset memoriale primi transitus & liberationis ex Aegypto proprio populo, ne posteri essent ingrati: Septem diebus comedes panem paupertatis: cum festinatione enim exiuisti ex Aegypto, vt recorderis diei exitus tui e terra Aegypti omnibus diebus vitae tuae.
units.tr: III. That it should be a memorial of the first passage and deliverance from Egypt for his own people, lest their descendants be ungrateful: Seven days you shall eat the bread of affliction, for in haste you came out of Egypt, so that you may remember the day of your departure from the land of Egypt all the days of your life.

units.la: IV. Vt esset nerus conuentuum publicorum & conseruatio- nis ministerij ecclesiastici. In primo autem die illorum erit conuo- catio sancta.
units.tr: IV. That it should be the bond of public assemblies and the preservation of the ecclesiastical ministry. And on the first day there shall be a holy convocation.

units.la: V. Vt esset sacramentum, distinguens populum Dei ab aliis gentibus. Nullus alienigena vescetur illo: Quod si peregrinus, qui facere velit pascha IEHOVAE, circumcidetur ei omnis mas: tum demum accedito ad faciendum ipsum: & esto sicut indigena terrae. At nullus praeputiatus vesci- tur illo.
units.tr: V. That it should be a sacrament distinguishing the people of God from the other nations. No foreigner shall eat of it. But if a stranger wishes to keep the Passover to the LORD, let every male of his be circumcised; then let him come near and keep it, and he shall be as a native of the land. But no uncircumcised person shall eat of it.

units.la: III. Analogia agni paschalis & Christi. Ad confirmationem & illustrationem finis principalis plurimum facit consideratio analogiæ rituum, quos Deus observari circa agnum præceperat, & passionis Christi. Collatio typi & rei significata. Typus | Res Significata 1. Agnus ex grege. | 1. Christus verus homo. Esa.53. Ioh.1. 2. Integer separatus. | 2. Sine peccato. Esa.53. Heb.7. 3. Mactandus & assandus. | 3. Passus & mortuus. 1 Cor.5. 4. Non fractis ossibus. | 4. Sine fractura ossium mortuus. Ioh.19. 5. Circa vesperam. | 5. In fine mundi. Heb.1. & 9. 6. Aspergendi postes eius sanguine. | 6. Eius satisfactio nobis imputata. Esa.53. Rom.3. 7. Ut transfiliret interfector. | 7. Ut liberemur à morte æterna. Heb.2. Ro.1. Io.6. 8. Manducandus, & quidem in singulis familiis. | 8. Applicatio singulis per fidem. 2 Tim.3. 9. Totus. | 9. Iuxta omnes articulos fidei. 1 Cor.5. 10. Sine fermento. | 10. Sine hypocrisi. 1 Cor.5. Matth.10. 11. Cum herbis amaris. | 11. Cum tolerantia crucis. Matth.10. 12. Festinanter, & peregrinantium habitu. | 12. Studio proficiendi, & exspectatione cœlestis vitæ. Matth.13. Heb.13. 13. A solis circumcisis. | 13. Soli renati edunt eum, & hi soli pro-desft, & soli isti non usurpant sacramenta ad judicium. Ioh.6. Heb.13. 1 Cor.11. IV. An vetus pascha sit abrogatum. Pascha vetus adventu Christi abrogatum esse cum aliis typis Messiam venturum significantibus, constat. 1. Ex tota disputatione Apostoli ad Hebræos de umbrarum legalium abolitione in novo Testamento. Mutato sacerdotio, necesse est, ut legis quoque mutatio fiat. Dum novum dicit, antiquauit prius. 2. Ex impletione. Facta sunt hæc, ut scriptura impleretur: Non confringetur os ipsius. Pascha nostrum pro nobis immolatum est Christus. 3. Ex sublitutione novi Testamenti. Christus enim moriturus, tanquam verum pascha seipsum immolaturus, solenni convivio ritum paschalem clausit, & eius loco cœnam suam ecclesiæ deinceps observandam instituit & mandavit. Desiderio desideravi vobiscum comedere hoc pascha, antequam patiar. Hoc facite in mei commemorationem. Jubet cœnam in sui ἀνάμνησιν celebrari, non vetus pascha. Ut igitur circumcisionem baptismus: sic paschati cœna successit in novo Testamento.
units.tr: III. The analogy between the paschal lamb and Christ. To confirm and illustrate the principal end, the comparison of the rites God commanded to be observed concerning the lamb with the passion of Christ is of great help. Comparison of type and thing signified. Type | Thing signified: (1) The lamb from the flock | Christ the true man. Isa. 53; John 1. (2) Whole and set apart | Without sin. Isa. 53; Heb. 7. (3) To be slain and roasted | Suffered and died. 1 Cor. 5. (4) Its bones not broken | Died without breaking of his bones. John 19. (5) Toward evening | At the end of the world. Heb. 1 and 9. (6) Its blood sprinkled on the doorposts | His satisfaction imputed to us. Isa. 53; Rom. 3. (7) That the destroyer might pass over | That we might be freed from eternal death. Heb. 2; Rom. 1; John 6. (8) To be eaten, and that in each household | Application to each person through faith. 2 Tim. 3. (9) Whole | According to all the articles of faith. 1 Cor. 5. (10) Without leaven | Without hypocrisy. 1 Cor. 5; Matt. 10. (11) With bitter herbs | With endurance of the cross. Matt. 10. (12) Eaten hastily, in the dress of travellers | With zeal to advance, and expectation of heavenly life. Matt. 13; Heb. 13. (13) Eaten only by the circumcised | Only the reborn eat him, and only they profit, and only they do not take the sacraments to their judgment. John 6; Heb. 13; 1 Cor. 11. IV. Whether the old Passover has been abrogated. That the old Passover was abrogated at the coming of Christ, together with the other types signifying the Messiah's coming, is established. (1) From the whole argument of the Apostle to the Hebrews on the abolition of the legal shadows in the New Testament: since the priesthood is changed, the law must of necessity be changed too; in calling it new, he has made the first old. (2) From fulfilment: "These things were done that the Scripture might be fulfilled: a bone of him shall not be broken"; "Christ our Passover is sacrificed for us." (3) From the substitution of the New Testament: Christ, about to die and to offer himself as the true Passover, closed the paschal rite with a solemn meal, and in its place instituted and commanded his Supper to be observed by the Church from then on. "With desire I have desired to eat this Passover with you before I suffer." "Do this in remembrance of me." He commands the Supper to be celebrated in remembrance [ἀνάμνησιν] of himself, not the old Passover. Therefore, as baptism took the place of circumcision, so the Supper of the Lord took the place of the Passover meal in the New Testament.

units.la: QVÆSTIO LXXXIII.
units.tr: QUESTION 83.

units.la: Quid sunt claues regni cœlorum? RESPONSIO.
units.tr: What are the keys of the kingdom of heaven? ANSWER.

units.la: Prædicatio Euangelij, & ecclesiastica disciplina: quibus cœlum credentibus apperitur: infidelibus autem clauditur.
units.tr: The preaching of the Gospel and ecclesiastical discipline, by which heaven is opened to believers but shut against unbelievers.

units.la: QVÆSTIO LXXXIV.
units.tr: QUESTION 84.

units.la: Quo pacto aperitur & clauditur regnum cœlorum prædicatione Euangelij? RESPONSIO.
units.tr: In what way is the kingdom of heaven opened and shut by the preaching of the Gospel? ANSWER.

units.la: Cùm ex mandato Christi, credentibus vniuersis & singulis, publicè annunciatur, omnia peccata ipsis diuinitus propter meritum Christi condonari, quoties promissionem Euangelij vera fide amplectuntur. Contrà verò omnibus infidelibus & hypocritis denunciatur, tantisper ipsis iram Dei, & æternam condemnationem incumbere, dum in suis sceleribus perseuerant : secundum quod euangelij testimonium, Deus tam in præsenti, quàm in futura vita judicaturus est.
units.tr: When, by Christ's command, it is publicly announced to all and each of the believers that all their sins are forgiven them by God for the sake of Christ's merit, as often as they embrace the promise of the Gospel with true faith. On the contrary, it is declared to all unbelievers and hypocrites that, for as long as they persist in their wickedness, the wrath of God and eternal condemnation rest upon them, according to the testimony of the Gospel, by which God will judge both in the present life and in the life to come.

units.la: QVÆSTIO LXXXV.
units.tr: QUESTION 85.

units.la: Quo pacto clauditur & aperitur regnum cœlorum per disciplinam ecclesiasticam? RESPONSIO.
units.tr: In what way is the kingdom of heaven shut and opened by ecclesiastical discipline? ANSWER.

units.la: Cùm ex mandato Christi, ij, qui nomine quidem sunt Christiani, verùm doctrina, aut vita, se ostendunt à Christo alienos, postquam aliquoties fraternè admoniti, ab erroribus aut flagitiis discedere nolunt, Ecclesiæ indicantur, aut iis, qui ab Ecclesia ad eam rem sunt constituti: ac si ne horum quidem admonitioni papareant, ab iisdem interdictione sacramentorum, ex coetu Ecclesiæ, & ab ipso Deo ex regno Christi exclu-duntur: rursum, si emendationem profiteantur, & recipiuntur: rursum, si emendationem profiteantur, & reduntur: rursum, si emendationem profiteantur, & reduntur: ipsa declarent, tanquam Christi & Ecclesiæ membra recipiuntur.a
units.tr: When, by Christ's command, those who indeed bear the name of Christians but show by their teaching or their life that they are alien to Christ, after being admonished several times in a brotherly way and refusing to turn from their errors or wickednesses, are reported to the Church or to those appointed by the Church for this purpose; and if they do not heed even the admonition of these, they are shut out by the same from the sacraments, from the assembly of the Church, and by God himself from the kingdom of Christ. Again, if they profess amendment, they are received back; and, if they show repentance, they are received as members of Christ and of the Church.a

units.la: EXPLICATIO.
units.tr: EXPLANATION.

units.la: Quoniam proximè fuit ostensum, quinam admittendi sint ab Ecclesia ad cœnam Domini: nunc commodè sequitur doctrina de potestate clavium, qua docetur, quomodo, qui non sunt admittendi, coerceri debeant: ne sacramenta accedentes profanent.
units.tr: Since it was shown just above who are to be admitted by the Church to the Lord's Supper, it now properly follows the teaching on the power of the keys, which teaches how those who are not to be admitted ought to be restrained, so that they do not profane the sacraments by coming to them.

units.la: De Potestate Clavium & Excommunicatione præcipuè quæritur:
units.tr: The following questions are chiefly treated concerning the power of the keys and excommunication:

units.la: I. Quid sit potestas clavium Ecclesiæ data, & quæ eius partes.
units.tr: I. What the power of the keys given to the Church is, and what its parts are.

units.la: II. An sit necessaria disciplina ecclesiastica & excommunicatio.
units.tr: II. Whether ecclesiastical discipline and excommunication are necessary.

units.la: III. Quibus hac potestas sit commissa: contra quos, & quo ordine sit exercenda.
units.tr: III. To whom this power has been committed, against whom it is to be exercised, and in what order.

units.la: IV. Ad quos fines sit dirigenda, & qui abusus vitandi.
units.tr: IV. To what ends it is to be directed, and what abuses are to be avoided.

units.la: V. Quid potestas clavium differat à potestate civili.
units.tr: V. How the power of the keys differs from the civil power.

units.la: I. Quid sit potestas clavium data Ecclesiæ: & quæ sint eius partes.
units.tr: I. What the power of the keys given to the Church is, and what its parts are.

units.la: Potestas clavium, quas Christus ecclesiæ tradidit, est prædicatio euangelij, & ecclesiastica disciplina, quibus cœlum credentibus aperitur, infidelibus clauditur. Seu: est officium ecclesiæ mandatum à Christo per prædicationem euangelij, & disciplinam ecclesiasticam, denunciandi voluntatem Dei, hoc est, gratiam Dei, & remissionem peccatorum iis, qui viuunt in vera fide & pœnitentiâ: impiis verò iram Dei, & exclusionem ex regno Christi & ecclesia, quamdiu se doctrina, vel vita, alienos à Christo ostenderint: vbi verò resipuerint, receptionem in ecclesiam, & in regnum Dei. Vocatur potestas clavium, metaphora ducta ab œconomia. Oeconomis enim traduntur claues: & claues significant officium œconomicum, per metonymiam signati, vt ministri ptrum pro regno. Ecclesia est domus Dei viuentis. Ministri ecclesiæ sunt œconomi Dei. Quod enim œconomus fidelis est in domo, administrans omnia ad nutum sui domini, hoc minister fidelis est in ecclesia. Denunciatio igitur voluntatis Dei in ecclesia fit à ministris, vt ab œconomis, Dei nomine. Authorest Christus, qui potestatem hanc dedit ecclesiæ, & clavium nomine.
units.tr: The power of the keys, which Christ handed over to the Church, is the preaching of the Gospel and ecclesiastical discipline, by which heaven is opened to believers and shut to unbelievers. Or: it is the office of the Church, commissioned by Christ, through the preaching of the Gospel and ecclesiastical discipline, of declaring the will of God, that is, the grace of God and the forgiveness of sins to those who live in true faith and repentance; but to the ungodly, the wrath of God and exclusion from the kingdom of Christ and from the Church, for as long as they show themselves alien to Christ in their teaching or their life; and, when they come to their senses, reception into the Church and into the kingdom of God. It is called the power of the keys by a metaphor taken from household management. For the keys are entrusted to stewards, and the keys signify the stewardly office, being named by metonymy, just as the ministers stand for the kingdom. The Church is the house of the living God. The ministers of the Church are the stewards of God. For just as a steward is faithful in the house, managing everything at the nod of his master, so the minister is faithful in the Church. The declaration of the will of God in the Church is therefore made by the ministers, as by stewards, in God's name. Christ is the author, who conferred this power on the Church and marked it with the name of keys, saying to Peter: I will give you the keys of the kingdom of heaven; that is, the power of opening and shutting the kingdom of God. He gave this also to all the disciples: Whatever you bind on earth shall be bound in heaven, and whatever you loose on earth shall be loosed in heaven. The keys are therefore the power of opening, shutting, binding and loosing, and they are so called because they are an effective power. For the Church opens, shuts, binds and loosens through the Word of God, in the name of Christ, whose stead the ministers fill; the Holy Spirit is effective through his Word, as Christ promised: Whose sins you forgive, they are forgiven them; whose sins you retain, they are retained.

units.la: 1 Tim.3,15. 1 Cor.4,1. mine insigniuit, dicens Petro: Dabo tibi claues regni cœlorum: hoc est, potestatem aperiendi & claudendi regnum Dei: quam etiam dedit omnibus discipulis: Quæcunque ligaueritis super terram, ligata erunt in cœlo: & quæcunque solueritis super terram, soluta erunt in cœlo. Claues igitur sunt potestas aperiendi, claudendi, ligandi, soluendi: & sic vocantur, quia sunt potestas efficax. Ecclesia enim aperit, claudit, ligat, soluit per verbum Dei, Christi nomine, cuius vice funguntur ministri: Spiritus sanctus per verbum suum est efficax; sicut Christus promisit: Quorum remiseritis peccata, remittuntur eis: si quorum retinueritis, retenta sunt.
units.tr: 1 Tim. 3:15; 1 Cor. 4:1. He marked this out when he said to Peter: "I will give you the keys of the kingdom of heaven"; that is, the power of opening and shutting the kingdom of God. He gave the same power to all the disciples: "Whatever you bind on earth shall be bound in heaven, and whatever you loose on earth shall be loosed in heaven." The keys, then, are the power of opening, shutting, binding and loosing, and they are so called because they are an effective power. For the Church opens, shuts, binds and looses through the Word of God, in the name of Christ, whose place the ministers take. The Holy Spirit is effective through his Word, as Christ promised: "Whose sins you remit, they are remitted to them; whose you retain, they are retained."

units.la: Clauiū partes sunt duæ: Prædicatio euangelij, seu ministerium verbi: & judicium ecclesiasticum, quod vocatur disciplina, vel jurisdictio spiritualis, ad quam excommunicatio pertinet. Vtraq; parte Ecclesia claudit & aperit, ligat & soluit. Prædicatione verbi claudit & ligat, cum infidelibus & hypocritis denunciat iram Dei & æternam damnationem, donec resipiscant: aperit verò & soluit, cum fidelibus & pœnitentiam agentibus annunciat remissionem peccatorum, & gratiam propter Christum. Iudicio ecclesiastico claudit & ligat, cum facinorosos & contumaces excommunicat, hoc est, excludit à communione sacramentorum, ecclesiæ, & regni Dei: aperit verò & soluit, cum eosdem, si resipiscant, tanquam Christi & ecclesiæ membra recipit.
units.tr: The keys have two parts: the preaching of the gospel, or the ministry of the Word; and ecclesiastical judgment, which is called discipline, or spiritual jurisdiction, to which excommunication belongs. By either part the Church shuts and opens, binds and looses. By the preaching of the Word it shuts and binds, when it declares to unbelievers and hypocrites the wrath of God and eternal damnation until they repent; but it opens and looses, when it announces to believers and to those who repent the forgiveness of sins and grace on account of Christ. By ecclesiastical judgment it shuts and binds, when it excommunicates the wicked and the obstinate, that is, excludes them from communion in the sacraments, the Church, and the kingdom of God; but it opens and looses, when, if they repent, it receives the same people again as members of Christ and of the Church.

units.la: Discrimen notandum est in ordine. In prædicatione Euangelij claues prius soluunt, deinde ligant. In disciplina ecclesiastica prius ligant, deinde soluunt. Et quidem in illa soluunt & ligant eosdem vel diuersos: in hac ligant & soluunt eosdem.
units.tr: The difference must be noted in the order. In the preaching of the gospel the keys first loose and then bind; in ecclesiastical discipline they first bind and then loose. Moreover, in the former they loose and bind the same or different persons; in the latter they bind and loose the same persons.

units.la: Excommunicatio vocatur eiectio facinorosi & contumacis è societate fidelium, judicio presbyterij, & totius Ecclesiæ nomine, authoritate Christi, & Spiritus sancti facta, vt pudefactus resipiscat, & scandala caveantur. Fit hæc exclusio non tantum à sacramentis, sed à tota communione fidelium, ad quam contumaces non pertinent. Est autem duplex: interna, quæ ad solum DEVM, & externa, quæ ad Ecclesiam pertinet. Illa per hanc declaratur in terra, hæc per illam habetur rata in cœlo, juxta promissionem Christi: Quicquid ligaueritis in terra, ligatum erit in cœlo.
units.tr: Excommunication is the casting out of a wicked and obstinate person from the fellowship of the faithful, done by the judgment of the elders and in the name of the whole Church, by the authority of Christ and the Holy Spirit, so that the shamed person may repent and scandals may be avoided. This exclusion is made not only from the sacraments but from the whole communion of the faithful, to which the obstinate do not belong. It is twofold: internal, which pertains to God alone, and external, which pertains to the Church. The latter is declared on earth through the Church, and the former is held as ratified in heaven through God, according to the promise of Christ: "Whatever you bind on earth shall be bound in heaven."

units.la: II. An disciplina & excommunicatio sit necessaria Ecclesiæ.
units.tr: II. Whether church discipline and excommunication are necessary for the Church.

units.la: De ministerio verbi non est dubium, quin omnes Prophetæ, Christus, & Apostoli sint concionati. Cum ministerio autem verbi necessariò cohæret judicium Ecclesiasticum, de quo etiam
units.tr: There is no doubt that all the Prophets, Christ, and the Apostles preached the Word. But ecclesiastical judgment is necessarily bound up with the ministry of the Word, and about this too there can be no doubt, since God himself, Christ, and the Apostle established it by precepts and examples.

units.la: Matt.18,15. 2Thess.3,14. 1Cor.5,1. etiam non potest esse dubium: siquidem illud Deus ipse, & Christus, & Apostolus, praeceptis & exemplis stabiliuerunt. Et sanè si nullus pagus, nullaq; vrbs sine disciplina, legibus & poenis stare potest: certè Ecclesia, quae est domus Dei viuentis, sua etiam spirituali politia & disciplina indiget, licet ea à ciuili iurisdictione multum differat.
units.tr: Matt.18,15. 2Thess.3,14. 1Cor.5,1. For indeed, if no village and no city can stand without discipline, laws and penalties, then certainly the Church, which is the house of the living God, needs its own spiritual polity and discipline, although this differs greatly from civil jurisdiction.

units.la: Necessaria igitur est disciplina Ecclesiae.
units.tr: Church discipline is therefore necessary.

units.la: 1. Propter mandatum Dei generale, de cauenda profanatione sacramentorum in veteri & nouo Testamento. In veteri Testamento contumaces, ne membra quidem populi Deus esse voluit, sed tolli è medio: multo minus ad sacramenta admitti. Anima, quae commiserit elata manu (hoc est proterue siue ex indigenis, siue ex peregrinis: Iehouam affecit probro: omnino exterminatur anima illa è medio populi sui. Quoniam aduersus Dominum rebellis fuit, peribit de populo suo. Omnes quidem venire volebat ad pascha, id est, omnia membra populi: sed contumaces nolebat esse membra populi. Ergo hos non volebat venire. Qui autem superbierit, nolens obedire sacerdoti, qui eo tempore ministrat Domino suo, aut summo judici, omnino moritor vir ille, & tollito malum ex Israele. Duobus istis locis Deus contumaces jubet tolli ex populo Israel, nec esse membra populi sui permittit. Multo igitur minus vult eos haberi pro membris Ecclesiae visibilis, & ad sacramenta admitti. Forensis quidem lex sublata est, sicut & caeremoniae: sed praecipuum illud discrimen ciuium Ecclesiae & aliorum, non est sublatum. Esaiae cap.1. exstat tota concio aduersus eos, qui scelerati offerebant sacrificia: nec vult Deus ab his sibi sacrificari. Ergo neq; nunc vult tales ad sacramenta admitti: Ne offeratis vltra sacrificium frustra, &c.
units.tr: (1) On account of God's general command to guard against the profanation of the sacraments in the Old and New Testaments. In the Old Testament God would not even have the contumacious counted as members of the people, but wanted them cut off from the midst of it, much less admitted to the sacraments. "The soul that does anything with a high hand, whether he be born in the land or a stranger, the same reproacheth the LORD; and that soul shall be cut off from among his people. Because he hath despised the word of the LORD, and hath broken his commandment, that soul shall utterly be cut off." God wanted all to come to the Passover, that is, all the members of the people, but he did not want the contumacious to be members of the people. Therefore he did not want them to come. "And the man that will do presumptuously, and will not hearken unto the priest that standeth to minister there before the LORD thy God, or unto the judge, that man shall die: and thou shalt put away the evil from Israel." In these two passages God commands that the contumacious be cut off from the people of Israel and does not permit them to be members of his people. Much less, then, does he wish them to be regarded as members of the visible Church and admitted to the sacraments. The forensic law has indeed been abrogated, as have the ceremonies, but that chief distinction between the citizens of the Church and others has not been abrogated. In Isaiah 1 there is a whole sermon against those who offered sacrifices while wicked, and God does not want sacrifices offered to him by them. Therefore he does not want such people admitted to the sacraments now either: "Bring no more vain oblations; incense is an abomination unto me..."

units.la: Inst. Vult omnes celebrare pascha. Ergo etiam admitti sceleratos. Resp. Omnes, quos praecipit haberi pro membris populi. Ergo non contumaces, quos praecipit ex populo tolli. Esaiae 66. exsecratur eos, qui in sceleribus perseuerantes offerebant sacrificia. Qui immolat bouem, est quasi qui interficiat virum; qui mactat pecus, quasi qui excerebret canem: qui offert oblationem, quasi qui sanguinem suillum offerat: qui recordatur thuris, quasi benedicat idolo, &c. Ieremiae 6. increpat eos, qui polluti sceleribus, audebant venire in templum. Ergo non vult eos admitti ad sacramenta. Ezechielis 20. non vult responderi iis, qui post alienos Deos iuerant, & tunc ad templum Dei venicbant, cum polluti essent. Ibidem dicit, eos profanare sabbatha, & polluere sanctuarium, qui cum idolis fornicati veniebant in templum. Amos 5. reijcit facinorosorum sacrificia & cultum: Odi & proiecti festiuitates vestras, & non capiam odorem coetuum vestrorum. Hagg.2. contaminaminatum in anima vetat attingere sacrum : vbi de immunditie morali & cæremoniali loquitur. Prouerb.15. Victima impiorum abominabiles Domino.
units.tr: Objection. He wants all to celebrate the Passover. Therefore wicked people are to be admitted too. Answer. All whom he commands to be regarded as members of the people. Not the contumacious, whom he commands to be cut off from the people. In Isaiah 66 he curses those who, persevering in wickedness, offered sacrifices: "He that killeth an ox is as if he slew a man; he that sacrificeth a lamb, as if he cut off a dog's neck; he that offereth an oblation, as if he offered swine's blood; he that burneth incense, as if he blessed an idol..." In Jeremiah 6 he rebukes those who, polluted by their crimes, dared to come into the temple. Therefore he does not want them admitted to the sacraments. In Ezekiel 20 he does not want an answer given to those who had gone after strange gods and then came to the temple of God while still defiled. In the same place he says that those who came into the temple after committing fornication with idols profane the sabbaths and pollute the sanctuary. In Amos 5 he rejects the sacrifices and worship of evildoers: "I hate, I despise your feast days, and I will not smell in your solemn assemblies." Haggai 2 forbids touching the holy thing by one who is unclean in soul; there he is speaking of moral and ceremonial uncleanness. Proverbs 15: "The sacrifice of the wicked is an abomination to the LORD."

units.la: In nouo Testamento Johannes admisit ad baptismum tantum confitentes peccata, & agentes pœnitentiam. Facite fructus pœnitentiæ dignos. Relinque munus tuum ad altare, & abi prius, ac reconciliare fratri tuo, & tum veniens offer munus tuum. Ergo qui non priusse reconciliat fratri, est arcendus à sacramentis. Vult, vt omnes se subijciant Deo, secundum omnia mandata, antequam accedant ad vllum sacramentum. Altaris enim nomine quælibet sacramenta hoc loco intelliguntur. Agite pœnitentiam, & baptizetur vnusquisque. Si credis toto corde, licet tibi baptizari. Ergo si non credis, non licet. Gentes, quæ immolant, dæmoniis immolant. Non potestis participare mensæ Domini, & mensæ dæmoniorum. Qui indignè edit, reus est. Impij edentes sine fide & pœnitentia, indignè edunt. Ergo, &c. Non debemus communicare alienis peccatis: neque committere, vt nobis conniuentibus aliquis pereat. Ergo non debemus admittere sceleratos, ne judicium sibi edant.
units.tr: In the New Testament John admitted to baptism only those who confessed their sins and were doing repentance. "Bring forth therefore fruits meet for repentance." "Leave there thy gift before the altar, and go thy way; first be reconciled to thy brother, and then come and offer thy gift." Therefore one who is not first reconciled to his brother is to be kept from the sacraments. He wants everyone to submit himself to God in all the commandments before he approaches any sacrament; for by the name of altar any sacraments are meant here. "Repent, and let every one of you be baptized." "If thou believest with all thine heart, thou mayest." Therefore if you do not believe, it is not lawful. "The things which the Gentiles sacrifice, they sacrifice to devils... Ye cannot be partakers of the Lord's table, and of the table of devils. Whosoever eateth and drinketh unworthily, is guilty..." The impious who eat without faith and repentance eat unworthily. Therefore, etc. We ought not to share in others' sins, nor to bring it about, by our connivance, that anyone perish. Therefore we ought not to admit evildoers, lest they eat judgment to themselves.

units.la: 2. Propter speciale mandatum Christi & Apostolorum: Si peccauerit in te frater tuus, veni & argue eum inter te & ipsum solum; si te audierit, lucratus es fratrem tuum: sin vero te non audierit, accipe tecum adhuc vnum aut duos, vt in ore duorum aut trium testium stabile sit omne verbum. Quod si neglexerit eos audire, dic Ecclesiæ: quod si Ecclesiam audire neglexerit, sit tibi velut ethnicus et publicanus. Amen dico vobis, quæcunque ligaueritis in terra, erunt ligata in cœlo: & quæcunque solueritis in terra, erunt soluta in cœlo. Ethnico autem & publicano Dominus non vult sacramenta communicari, quæ solis fidelibus instituit. Ac ne de priuato judicio mandatum intelligatur, additur expresse: Quæcunque ligaueritis, &c. quod non potest nisi de publica clauium potestate intelligi. Enimuero ego, vt absens corpore, præsens autem spiritu, iam vt præsens judicaui, vt is, qui hoc ita perpetrauit, vobis & meo spiritu in nomine Domini nostri Iesu Christi: eiusmodi, inquam, homo tradatur Satanæ ad interitum carnis, vt spiritus saluus sit die illo Domini Iesu. Et: Cùm eiusmodi ne edatis quidem. Tollite igitur istum sceleratum ex vobis ipsis. Quæ enim communio Christo & Belial? Denunciamus vobis, fratres, per nomen Domini nostri Iesu Christi, vt subducatis vos ab omni fratre, qui inordinatè se gerit, & non ex traditta doctrina, quam accepit à nobis. Quod si quis non auscultet nostro per epistolam sermoni, hunc notate, & ne commercium habete cum eo, vt eum pudeat. Si quis venit ad vos, & hanc doctrinam non affert: ne recipite eum domum, domum, ne aue ei dicite: qui enim dicit illi aue, communicat operibus eius malis.
units.tr: (2) On account of the special command of Christ and the apostles: "Moreover if thy brother shall trespass against thee, go and tell him his fault between thee and him alone: if he shall hear thee, thou hast gained thy brother. But if he will not hear thee, then take with thee one or two more, that in the mouth of two or three witnesses every word may be established. And if he shall neglect to hear them, tell it unto the church: but if he neglect to hear the church, let him be unto thee as an heathen man and a publican. Verily I say unto you, Whatsoever ye shall bind on earth shall be bound in heaven: and whatsoever ye shall loose on earth shall be loosed in heaven." Now the Lord does not want the sacraments, which he instituted for the faithful alone, to be shared with a heathen man or a publican. And lest the command be understood as referring to private judgment, it is expressly added: "Whatsoever ye shall bind, etc." which can only be understood of the public power of the keys. Indeed I, "as absent in body but present in spirit, have already judged, as though I were present, him that hath so done this deed, in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, to deliver such an one unto Satan for the destruction of the flesh, that the spirit may be saved in the day of the Lord Jesus." And: "With such an one, no, not to eat. Therefore put away from among yourselves that wicked person. For what communion hath light with darkness, and what concord hath Christ with Belial? We command you, brethren, in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, that ye withdraw yourselves from every brother that walketh disorderly, and not after the tradition which he received of us. And if any man obey not our word by this epistle, note that man, and have no company with him, that he may be ashamed. Yet count him not as an enemy, but admonish him as a brother. If there come any unto you, and bring not this doctrine, receive him not into your house, neither bid him God speed: for he that biddeth him God speed is partaker of his evil deeds."

units.la: 3. Propter gloriam Dei opus est clauium potestate. Nam Deus afficitur contumelia, si sine discrimine omnes pro filiis Dei habeantur, etiam impij & blasphemi, & regnum Dei atque diaboli confundantur.
units.tr: (3) On account of the glory of God, the power of the keys is necessary. For God is dishonoured if all are regarded without distinction as children of God, even the impious and blasphemers, and the kingdom of God and of the devil are confused.

units.la: 4. Ne profanentur sacramenta, & quod impiis negatur in verbo, eis detur in coena.
units.tr: (4) So that the sacraments are not profaned, and what is refused to the impious in the Word is not given to them at the Supper.

units.la: 5. Vt puritas doctrinæ & cultus conseruetur.
units.tr: (5) So that the purity of doctrine and worship may be preserved.

units.la: 6. Propter salutem Ecclesiæ: quæ punitur, si sciens & volens sacramenta profanet, vel profanari sinat.
units.tr: (6) For the salvation of the Church, which is punished if it knowingly and willingly profanes the sacraments, or allows them to be profaned.

units.la: 7. Propter salutem peccantium, vt ij sæpius moniti & pudefactiredeant ad pœnitentiam.
units.tr: (7) For the salvation of sinners, so that those who have been admonited often and put to shame may return to repentance.

units.la: 8. Vt vitentur scandala in Ecclesia, nec infirmi corrumpantur exemplis. An nescitis paululo fermenti totam massam fermentari.
units.tr: (8) So that scandals in the Church may be avoided, and the weak not be corrupted by examples. "Know ye not that a little leaven leaveneth the whole lump?"

units.la: 6. Vt vitentur scandala extra Ecclesiam, ne, qui nondum sunt membra Ecclesiæ, ad eam non accedant.
units.tr: 6. So that scandals outside the Church may be avoided, lest those who are not yet members of the Church approach it.

units.la: 10. Ne nomen Dei apud alios blasphemetur, & fœdus ipsius afficiatur contumelia.
units.tr: 10. So that the name of God is not blasphemed among others, and his covenant is not dishonoured.

units.la: 11. Vt a ipsis peccantibus auertatur pœna: siquidem impij accedentes judicium sibi sumunt. Hoc ne fiat, Ecclesia debet auerte, vt istiusmodi non accedant.
units.tr: 11. So that punishment is averted from the sinners themselves; for the impious who approach take judgment to themselves. To prevent this, the Church ought to turn such people away, so that they do not approach.

units.la: 12. Qui negant fidem & doctrinam, excludendi sunt ab Ecclesia, & ab vsu sacramentorum. Non enim confundendi sunt fideles cum palam impiis, blasphemis, deficientibus ad Arianismum, & Mahumetismum, &c. Atqui negantes se pœnitentiam acturos, abnegant fidem & doctrinam: Deum profiteatur se scire, sed factis negant. Qui vero fidem abnegat, est infideli deterior. Ergo perseuerantes in sceleribus, & negantes, se pœnitentiam acturos, excludendi sunt ab Ecclesia, & vsu sacramentorum arcendi.
units.tr: 12. Those who deny the faith and doctrine are to be excluded from the Church and from the use of the sacraments. For the faithful must not be confused with the openly impious, the blasphemers, those who defect to Arianism and Mahometanism, etc. But those who refuse to repent deny the faith and doctrine: "They profess that they know God, but in works they deny him." Now one who denies the faith is worse than an unbeliever. Therefore those who persevere in wickedness and refuse to repent are to be excluded from the Church and kept from the use of the sacraments.

units.la: 13. Hic etiam locum habet illud Christi: Nolite sanctum obijcere canibus, neq; margaritas porcis. Sed perseuerantes in sceleribus, ridentes Ecclesiam, & Deum ipsum, reuera sunt canes & porci. Non igitur admittendi sunt ad sacramenta. Si enim Christus hoc dixit de verbo audibili, quod tamen institutum est conuertendis: multo magis hoc dicetur de verbo visibili, hoc est, de sacramentis, quæ tantum conuersis sunt instituta.
units.tr: 13. Here also applies that saying of Christ: "Do not give what is holy to dogs, nor cast your pearls before swine." But those who persist in their sins, mocking the Church and God himself, are in truth dogs and swine. They are therefore not to be admitted to the sacraments. For if Christ said this of the audible word, which nevertheless was instituted for the converting of sinners, much more will it be said of the visible word, that is, of the sacraments, which were instituted only for the converted.

units.la: 14. Palam increduli, impij, blasphemi non debent baptizari. Non enim baptizari debent, qui non credunt toto corde. Vnde Et
units.tr: 14. Those who are openly unbelieving, impious, and blasphemous ought not to be baptized.

units.la: Philippus dicit Eunucho: Licet tibi baptizari, si credis toto corde. Et Johannes nullos baptizabat, nisi confitentes sua peccata. Si ergo increduli, & blasphemi non debent baptizari: consequitur eos etiam non admittendos ad coenam. Qui enim non debent baptizari, ij nec debent admitti ad coenam: quia eadem vtrobique est ratio.
units.tr: For those who do not believe with their whole heart ought not to be baptized. Hence Philip says to the eunuch: "You may be baptized if you believe with your whole heart." And John baptized none except those who confessed their sins. If therefore unbelievers and blasphemers ought not to be baptized, it follows that they are not to be admitted to the Supper either. For those who ought not to be baptized ought not to be admitted to the Supper, since the reason is the same in both cases.

units.la: 15. Nondum baptizati, ad coenam non sunt admittendi. At deficientibus à suo baptismo, baptismus non est baptismus: juxta illud Apostoli: Circumcisio tua facta est praeputium, si fueris transgressor legis, si in transgressione perseueraueris sine poenitentia. Ergo deficientes à suo baptismo, non sunt admittendi ad coenam.
units.tr: Objection: Then those who have fallen away from their baptism must also be baptized again after they have returned. Answer: Reception through baptism remains valid for those who repent, even without repeating the sign. But since baptism is the entrance into the Church, those who have fallen away from it are not in the Church; therefore, as long as they remain such, they belong neither to the Church nor are they to be admitted to the Supper.

units.la: Obiect. Ergo qui à suo baptismo defecerunt, etiam baptizandi sunt post receptionem. Resp. Receptio per baptismum rata est agentibus poenitentiam, etiam sine iteratione signi. Baptismus autem cum sit ingressus in Ecclesiam, qui ab eo defeciunt, non sunt in Ecclesia, ideoq; quamdiu tales manent, nec ad Ecclesiam pertinent, nec ad coenam sunt admittendi.
units.tr: 16. Those to whom the promise of grace does not pertain, to them the signs of grace ought not to be extended either; otherwise the Church would be deceitful, admitting those whom God excludes, and would be at odds with itself. For it would absolve by the visible word those whom it condemns by the audible word. The promise of grace does not pertain to the wicked and blasphemous. Therefore the signs of grace ought not to be extended to them either.

units.la: 16. Ad quos promissio gratiae non pertinet, ad eos nec signa gratiae extendi debent: alioqui Ecclesia esset falsaria, admittens quos Deus excludit, & pugnaret secum. Nam verbo visibili absoluerret, quos verbo audibili damnaret. Ad sceleratos & blasphemos non pertinet promissio gratiae. Ergo nec signa gratiae ad hos extendi debent.
units.tr: 16. Those to whom the promise of grace does not pertain, to them the signs of grace ought not to be extended; otherwise the Church would be a deceiver, admitting those whom God excludes, and would be at odds with itself. For it would absolve by the visible word those whom it condemns by the audible word. The promise of grace does not pertain to the wicked and blasphemous. Therefore the signs of grace ought not to be extended to them either.

units.la: 17. Denique institutio sacramentorum, seu, conditio, qua accedendum est ad sacramenta, postulat fidem & poenitentiam. Ergo infideles, & non agentes poenitentiam, non sunt admittendi ad sacramenta. Valet argumentum à contrariis. Habentes poenitentiam & fidem sunt admittendi. Ergo non habentes non sunt admittendi.
units.tr: 17. Finally, the institution of the sacraments, or the condition on which one must approach the sacraments, requires faith and repentance. Therefore unbelievers, and those not repenting, are not to be admitted to the sacraments. The argument holds from the contraries: those having repentance and faith are to be admitted; therefore those not having them are not to be admitted.

units.la: III. A quibus, aduersus quos, & quo ordine potestas clauium sit exercenda.
units.tr: III. By whom, against whom, and in what order the power of the keys is to be exercised.

units.la: Quibus annunciatio verbi diuini delegata est, iisdem & potestas clauium est commissa. Denunciatio irae & gratiae Dei, quae in Euangelij praedicatione, ministris est commissa. Nam his solis Euangelij praedicatio commendatur. Denunciatio verò, quae fit in Ecclesiastica disciplina, est totius Ecclesiae. Ad totam enim Ecclesiam pertinet disciplina, & jurisdictio spiritualis: sed alio modo fit illa denunciatio in verbi ministerio, quam in Ecclesiae judicio. In ministerio verbi à solis & singulis pastoribus & verbi ministris ira Dei, verbo diuino praeeunte, denunciatur omnibus impiis & non resipiscentibus; ipsos esse alienos a regno Christi, quamdiu non resipiscunt, & ad euangelicae doctridoctrinæ præscriptum viuunt. Si resipuerint, rursus eis ex verbo Dei annunciatur ab iisdem gratia Dei, & remissio peccatorum. Obiect. Ergo homines habent potestatem damnandi? Resp. Habent potestatem ministerialem, hoc est, officium denunciandi ex verbo Dei, quod Deus remittat peccata vel non remittat: & hoc fit duplicater. Primò, & generaliter, cum in prædicatione euangelij denunciant, omnes credentes saluari: omnes non credentes condemnari. Deinde, cùm priuatim erga singulos & vnumquemque vtuntur hoc officio denunciandi: vt cum certæ personæ pœnitenti promittitur remissio peccatorum, certæ item personæ non agenti pœnitentiâ denunciatur ira Dei, quantisper talis manet: sicut Petrus dicebat Simoni mago: Non est tibi pars, neq; sors in hoc negotio. Idem omnibus nominatim dicendum est, quoties necessitas requirit, non nostro quidem arbitratu, sed juxta Dei verbum. Atque hæc est potestas clauium, pastoribus ecclesiæ concessa, & verbi ministerio annexa. Denunciationem vero exsequi est solius Dei. In ecclesiastico judicio gratiæ & iræ Dei denunciatio non fit ab vno priuatim, sed à tota ecclesia, aut nomine totius ecclesiæ, ab iis, qui ad hoc delecti sunt communi omnium consensu: & quidem fit illa denunciatio propter certas causas, & ad certas personas, adhibita etiam exclusione ab vsu sacramentorum, quando necessitas postulat.
units.tr: The power of the keys has been committed to the same persons to whom the proclamation of the divine Word has been entrusted. The proclamation of God's wrath and grace, which occurs in the preaching of the Gospel, has been committed to the ministers, for the preaching of the Gospel is entrusted to them alone. But the proclamation which takes place in ecclesiastical discipline belongs to the whole Church, for discipline and spiritual jurisdiction pertain to the whole Church. Yet that proclamation takes place in one way in the ministry of the Word and in another way in the judgment of the Church. In the ministry of the Word, the wrath of God is proclaimed, with the divine Word going before, by the ministers alone and by each of the pastors and ministers of the Word to all the impious and those who do not repent: that they are strangers to the kingdom of Christ as long as they do not repent and live according to the rule of evangelical doctrine. If they repent, the grace of God and the remission of sins are again announced to them from the Word of God by the same ministers. Objection. Therefore men have the power of condemning? Answer. They have a ministerial power, that is, the office of declaring from the Word of God that God forgives sins or does not forgive them; and this is done in two ways. First, and in general, when in the preaching of the Gospel they declare that all who believe are saved and all who do not believe are condemned. Second, when they exercise this office of declaring privately toward individuals and each person: as when remission of sins is promised to a certain person who repents, and likewise the wrath of God is declared to a certain person who does not repent, for as long as he remains such, as Peter said to Simon the magician: You have no part or lot in this matter. The same must be said to people by name whenever necessity requires, not indeed at our own discretion, but according to the Word of God. And this is the power of the keys, granted to the ministers of the Church and joined to the ministry of the Word. But to carry out the declaration itself belongs to God alone. In ecclesiastical judgment, the declaration of God's grace and wrath is not made by one person privately, but by the whole Church, or in the name of the whole Church, by those who have been chosen for this purpose by the common consent of all; and that declaration is made for certain causes and to certain persons, with exclusion from the use of the sacraments also, when necessity demands it.

units.la: Qui verò sint excludendi, satis ex præcedentibus cognoscitur, nempe qui aut pertinaciter negant aliquem articulum fidei, aut ostendunt, se nolle pœnitentiam agere, & se subijcere voluntati Dei, secundum omnia præcepta, neque dubitant in manifestis scelaribus contumaciter perseuerare. Omnes eiusmodi non sunt admittendi ad Ecclesiam: quod si sint ad Ecclesiam admissi in baptismo, non tamen est pergendum exhibitione sacræ cœnæ.
units.tr: Who ought to be excluded is sufficiently known from what has gone before: namely those who either obstinately deny some article of faith, or show that they are unwilling to repent and to submit themselves to the will of God in all his commandments, and who do not hesitate to persist stubbornly in manifest crimes. All such persons are not to be admitted to the Church; and if they have been admitted to the Church in baptism, nevertheless they must not be admitted to the administration of the holy Supper.

units.la: Ordo autem in exercenda clauium potestate obseruari debet is, quem Christus ipse Matth.18. præscripsit. Cùm quis admiserit priuatum aliquod delictum, is primum ab vno humaniter admoneri debet, juxta mandatum Christi: Si peccauerit in te frater tuus, veni, & argue eum inter te & eum solum. Si te audierit, lucratus es fratrem tuum. Deinde si ab vno admonitus nondum resipiscat, assumto vno & altero rursum admoneri priuatim debet: atque admonitiones eiusmodi fieri debent secundum Dei verbum, cum significatione benevolentiæ, nec non justis, gravibus & necessariis de causis: Sin vero te non audierit, accipito tecum adhuc vnum aut duos, vt in ore duorum aut trium testium stabile sit omne verbum. Quod si sic admonitus ab vno atque altero, nec dum resipiscere velit, ab Ecclesia corrigendus est; quod Christus præcepit, inquiens:
units.tr: The order to be observed in exercising the power of the keys is the one which Christ himself prescribed in Matthew 18. When anyone has committed some private offence, he ought first to be admonished kindly by one person, according to the command of Christ: If your brother sins against you, go and tell him his fault between you and him alone. If he hears you, you have gained your brother. Then, if he, having been admonished by one, does not yet repent, he ought to be admonished again privately, with one or two others added; and such admonitions ought to be given according to the Word of God, with a sign of goodwill, and for just, weighty and necessary causes: But if he does not hear you, take with you one or two more, so that by the mouth of two or three witnesses every word may be established. But if, admonished in this way by one and another, he is still unwilling to repent, he is to be corrected by the Church, as Christ commanded, saying:

units.la: Matt.18,15. Ibid.v.16. quiens: Quod si neglexerit eos audire, dic Ecclesiae. Cum autem quis palam peccauerit cum offensione totius ecclesiae, is etiam publicè ab Ecclesia corrigi debet pro modo delicti. Si etiam admonitus & castigatus ab ecclesia resipiscere nolit, siue is, qui priuatim admisit peccatum, siue is, qui delictum admisit publicum: extremum remedium ad corrigendos impoenitentes excommunicatio ab Ecclesia adhiberi debet, juxta praeceptum Christi: Quod si Ecclesiam audire neglexerit, sit tibi velut Ethnicus aut publicanus. Haec igitur est legitima via corrigendi errantes, & coercendi contumaces in Ecclesia Christi, si gradus praescripti correctionum seruentur. Gradus autem praescripti sunt quatuor. 1. Admonitio fraterna priuata. 2. Admonitio per plures. 3. Admonitio per Ecclesiam. 4. Judicium publicum Ecclesiae. Primus & secundus gradus in peccatis priuatis: tertius in peccatis notoriis & grauibus, quartus demum in casu contumaciae locum habet, in quo solo Ecclesia ad conclusionem procedit, habens contumacem pro Ethnico & publicano, hoc est, pro alieno ab Ecclesia & regno Dei, quoad resipiscat.
units.tr: Matt. 18:15; ibid. v. 16. And if he refuses to hear them, tell it to the Church. When someone has sinned openly, to the offence of the whole Church, he too ought to be corrected publicly by the Church, according to the measure of the offence. If, moreover, the one who committed a private sin, or the one who committed a public offence, refuses to repent even when admonished and rebuked by the Church, the last remedy for correcting the impenitent is to be applied, excommunication from the Church, according to the precept of Christ: But if he refuses to hear the Church, let him be to you as a Gentile and a tax collector. This, then, is the lawful way of correcting those who err and restraining the stubborn in the Church of Christ, if the prescribed steps of correction are observed. The prescribed steps are four: (1) private fraternal admonition; (2) admonition by several; (3) admonition by the Church; (4) public judgment of the Church. The first and second steps apply to private sins; the third to notorious and grave sins; the fourth, finally, has its place in the case of obstinacy, and only in this case does the Church proceed to a conclusion, regarding the stubborn person as a Gentile and a tax collector, that is, as a stranger to the Church and the kingdom of God, until he repents.

units.la: Excommunicationem igitur necessariò praecedit cognitio erroris seu lapsus, & cognitio contumaciae. Si itaque quis fiat Papista, vel Arianus, vel Davidianus, vel alius apostata, non est habendus pro membro Ecclesiae, etiamsi dicat, se esse membrum, & velit in Ecclesia manere, nisi abijciat, & detestetur errorem, viuat secundum doctrinam Euangelij. Ratio est: quia Deus vult suam ecclesiam segregari ab aliis omnibus sectis & membris diaboli. Qui autem rescindunt juramentum baptismi, sunt membra diaboli. Itaque rescindendi sunt ab Ecclesia, etiamsi dicant, se esse Christianos. Nam factis negant, quod ore profitentur, & eos mentiri patet. Fides enim & vita Christiana non possunt separari. Qui separant, Deum & Ecclesiam rident. Est verò apostata, non qui aliquando, vel etiam saepe in doctrina & vita peccat, & resipiscit: sed qui conuictus de erroribus & sceleribus negat se velle desistere. Si autem quis profiteatur poenitentiam, & externè etiam declaret, etsi intus sit hypocrita, eum Ecclesia tenetur admittere, donec ipse se prodat. Nam non est Ecclesiae de arcanis judicare.
units.tr: Excommunication is therefore necessarily preceded by the recognition of error or lapse, and by the recognition of obstinacy. Accordingly, if anyone becomes a Papist, or an Arian, or a Davidian, or another apostate, he is not to be regarded as a member of the Church, even if he says that he is a member and wishes to remain in the Church, unless he casts off and detests his error and lives according to the doctrine of the Gospel. The reason is that God wills his Church to be separated from all other sects and from the members of the devil. Those who break the covenant of baptism are members of the devil; therefore they are to be cut off from the Church, even if they say that they are Christians. For they deny by their deeds what they profess with their mouths, and it is plain that they lie. For faith and Christian life cannot be separated. Those who separate them mock God and the Church. He is truly an apostate, however, not someone who sometimes, or even often, sins in doctrine and life and then repents, but someone who, when convicted of errors and crimes, denies that he wishes to desist. If, on the other hand, someone professes repentance and also declares it outwardly, even if he is inwardly a hypocrite, the Church is bound to admit him until he himself betrays himself. For it is not the Church's business to judge secret things.

units.la: IV. Qui sint disciplinae Ecclesiasticae fines spectandi, quisque abusus cauendi.
units.tr: IV. Which limits of ecclesiastical discipline are to be observed, and which abuses are to be guarded against.

units.la: Potestatem excommunicandi Christus Ecclesiae dedit, non ad destructionem peccatoris, sed ad eius aedificationem, & salutem. Finis igitur disciplinae nequaquam est, ut stabiliatur potentia vel tyrannis ministrorum: Potentes dominantur, vos autem antem non sic. Ministri debent vel maximè disciplinæ subiecti esse, & hoc fræno cumprimis intra limites vocationis suæ continentur: quia claues non sunt ministrorum tantum, sed totius Ecclesiæ. Multo minus hic finis est vt vexentur, premantur, aut ad desperationem adigantur miseri peccatores. Hæ sunt calumniæ hostium disciplinæ. Fines verò sunt, quos Apostolus tradit, & ostendit.
units.tr: Christ gave the Church the power of excommunication not for the destruction of the sinner but for his building up and salvation. The purpose of discipline is therefore by no means to establish the power or tyranny of the ministers: "The kings of the nations lord it over them, but you shall not be so." Ministers ought above all to be subject to discipline, and this bridle chiefly keeps them within the limits of their calling, because the keys belong not to the ministers alone but to the whole Church. Still less is it the purpose that wretched sinners should be harassed, oppressed, or driven to despair. These are the slanders of the enemies of discipline. The true ends are those which the Apostle hands down and shows.

units.la: 1. Vt contumaces hoc medio pudefacti & territi in se redeant, & resipiscant: Eiusmodi homo tradatur Satanæ ad interitum carnis, vt spiritus salvus sit in die illo Domini Iesu.
units.tr: 1. That the obstinate, shamed and terrified by this means, may come to themselves and repent: "Such a one is to be delivered to Satan for the destruction of the flesh, that the spirit may be saved in the day of the Lord Jesus."

units.la: 2. Ne alij Christiani conuersione & exemplis facinorosorum corrumpantur. Nam vna morbida pecus, nisi curetur, vel secludatur, poterit totum gregem contagione sua inficere, & modicum fermenti fermentat magnam massam. Non estis bona gloriatio vestra. An nescitis, paululo fermenti totam massam fermentari?
units.tr: 2. That other Christians may not be corrupted by the company and examples of wicked men. For one diseased sheep, unless it is cured or isolated, can infect the whole flock with its contagion, and "a little leaven leavens the whole lump." "Your boasting is not good. Do you not know that a little leaven leavens the whole lump?"

units.la: 3. Vt alij à peccatis absterreantur. Eos qui peccant, coram omnibus argue, vt & reliqui timeant.
units.tr: 3. That others may be deterred from sin. "Those who sin, rebuke before all, that the rest also may fear."

units.la: 4. Ne Ecclesia scandalis deformetur: & vt profanatio sacramentorum, & ira Dei caueatur. Expurgate vetus fermentum, vt sitis noua massa: sicut estis fermenti expertes. Etenim pascha nostrum pro nobis immolatum est Christus, &c. Hi igitur sunt fines siue vsus disciplinæ.
units.tr: 4. That the Church may not be disfigured by scandals, and that the profanation of the sacraments and the wrath of God may be avoided. "Purge out the old leaven, that you may be a new lump, as you are unleavened. For Christ our passover is sacrificed for us, etc." These, then, are the ends or uses of discipline.

units.la: Abusus verò in excommunicatione vitandi sunt.
units.tr: But the abuses in excommunication must be avoided.

units.la: Primò, ne negligantur admonitionum gradus, nec initium fiat à summo, sed à primo. Præcedat igitur admonitio priuata, & primò humaniter admoneatur, qui deliquit: & admonitio detectio & reprehensio erroris vel peccati ex verbo Dei, & hortatio ad emendationem.
units.tr: First, the steps of admonition must not be neglected, nor should one begin at the highest step but at the first. Let private admonition therefore come first, and let the one who has erred be admonished kindly at first. Admonition is the disclosure and rebuke of error or sin from the Word of God, together with exhortation to amendment.

units.la: Secundò, fiat eo modo, quo debet, hoc est, secundum verbum Dei, cum significatione fraternæ beneuolentiæ: & studij iuuandi errantes, & ad eorum salutem. Deus enim non vult esse executor sententiæ alienæ, sed suæ. Peccans igitur frater, non mox habeatur pro hoste, vel alieno, sed moneatur, vt frater: juxta illud Apostoli: Neque vt inimicum ducite, sed admonete vt fratrem.
units.tr: Second, it should be done in the manner it ought to be done, that is, according to the Word of God, with a sign of brotherly goodwill, and with zeal to help the erring and to save them. For God does not wish to be the executor of another's sentence but of his own. A brother who sins, therefore, should not at once be regarded as an enemy or a stranger, but admonished as a brother, according to the saying of the Apostle: "Do not count him as an enemy, but admonish him as a brother."

units.la: Tertiò, fiat justis, grauibus & necessariis de causis, non propter injustas, incertas, aut non satis graues: non temerè ex suspicione vel affectu descendatur ad exclusionem, sed extrema cogente necessitate, exemplo medicorum, qui non prius veniunt ad sectionem, quam necessitas flagitet. Est autem necessitas, cum errores contra fundamentum, & manifesta scelera, contumaciter defenduntur, & totus coetus, vel aliqui periclitantur. Quarto, attentè expendatur causa à toto presbyterio, judicium probetur ab Ecclesia, non suscipiatur priuata authoritate ab vno solo, vel à ministris solis. Potestas enim à Christo non est tradita paucis, vel solis ministris, (etsi executio paucis, vel vni ministro ab Ecclesia committitur) sed toti Ecclesiæ: Si te & alios non audierit: dic Ecclesiæ. Potentes dominantur, vos autem non sic. Accedat igitur Ecclesiæ consensus & judicium. 1. Propter mandatum Dei. 2. Vt nemini fiat injuria. 3. Vt actio plus habeat authoritatis. 4. Ne ministerium Ecclesiæ conuertatur in ἀλιγαρχίαν, vel tyrannidem Papisticam. 5. Vt justior sit damnatio pertinacium.
units.tr: Third, it should be done for just, weighty and necessary causes, not for unjust, uncertain, or insufficiently weighty ones. One should not rashly proceed to exclusion out of suspicion or feeling, but only when extreme necessity compels, after the example of physicians, who do not resort to surgery until necessity demands it. Necessity exists when errors against the foundation and manifest crimes are obstinately defended, and the whole congregation or some of its members are in danger. Fourth, the cause should be carefully weighed by the whole eldership, and the judgment approved by the Church; it should not be undertaken on private authority by one alone, or by the ministers alone. For the power was not given by Christ to a few, or to the ministers alone (although the execution is committed by the Church to a few, or to one minister), but to the whole Church: "If he will not hear you and the others, tell it to the Church. The mighty lord it over them, but you shall not be so." Let the consent and judgment of the Church therefore be added: 1. because of God's command; 2. so that no one is wronged; 3. so that the action may carry more authority; 4. so that the ministry of the Church is not turned into oligarchy [ὀλιγαρχίαν] or Papist tyranny; 5. so that the condemnation of the obstinate may be more just.

units.la: Denique cauendum, ne excitentur schismata aut scandala in Ecclesia, si videant boni, multos inter se dissentire, sequi maiora mala, scindi Ecclesiam.
units.tr: Finally, care must be taken that schisms or scandals are not stirred up in the Church, lest good men, seeing many dissent among themselves, and greater evils follow, see the Church torn apart.

units.la: Hæc mala si videant, aut metuant ministri, non debent procedere, sed priuatim & publicè monere & hortari. Si nihil prosi-ciant, sunt excusati. Beati qui esuriunt & sitiunt justitiam, quia saturabuntur. Cæteri pertinaciæ suæ poenas dabunt.
units.tr: If ministers see, or fear, these evils, they ought not to go forward, but to admonish and exhort privately and publicly. If they accomplish nothing, they are excused. "Blessed are those who hunger and thirst for righteousness, for they shall be filled." The rest will pay the penalty of their obstinacy.

units.la: IV. Quid differat clavium potestas Ecclesiæ delegata à potestate politica.
units.tr: IV. How the power of the keys delegated to the Church differs from political power.

units.la: Discrimina sunt multa & manifesta.
units.tr: The differences are many and plain.

units.la: 1. Ecclesiastica disciplina exercetur ab Ecclesia. Potestas civilis à præture, vel magistratu.
units.tr: 1. Ecclesiastical discipline is exercised by the Church; civil power by the praetor or magistrate.

units.la: 2. Politia judicat secundum leges civiles & positivas. Ecclesia secundum leges divinas, seu verbum Dei.
units.tr: 2. The civil polity judges according to civil and positive laws; the Church according to divine laws, or the Word of God.

units.la: 3. Potestas clavium Ecclesiæ commissa nititur verbo Dei, & Ecclesia jus suum exercet verbo, denuncians iram Dei impœnitentibus: punit contumaces solo Dei verbo: ita tamen, vt hæc pœna penetret ad conscientias vsque. Politica potestas armata est gladio, & coercet contumaces pœna tantum corporali.
units.tr: 3. The power of the keys committed to the Church rests on the Word of God, and the Church exercises its right by the Word, declaring the wrath of God to the impenitent. It punishes the obstinate by the Word of God alone, yet in such a way that this penalty reaches even to the conscience. Political power is armed with the sword and restrains the obstinate with bodily penalty only.

units.la: 4. Ecclesia præmittit gradus admonitionum, & interuenien-te pœnitentia, non procedit ad executionem. Magistratus procedit ad pœnam, licet peccans resipiscat.
units.tr: 4. The Church sends ahead the steps of admonition, and, if repentance intervenes, does not proceed to execution. The magistrate proceeds to punishment even though the offender repents.

units.la: 5. Ecclesia spectat emendationem peccantium. Magistratus executionē justitiæ, & pacem publicam, hoc est: Wil der Dieb nicht zu unserm Herrn Gott fahren, so fahr er zum Bösen. Nisi fur velit vadere ad Deum, vadat ad diabolum.
units.tr: 5. The Church looks to the amendment of sinners; the magistrate to the execution of justice and public peace. That is: "If the thief will not go to our Lord God, let him go to the devil."

units.la: 6. Sicut Ecclesia tantum procedit aduersus contumaces: ita judicium & pœnam tenetur retractare, si interueniat resipiscentia. Magistratus vero, postquam puniuit, non retractat judicium & pœnas: Wann schon ein Verbrecher wer fromb worden in einem alterum Land. Hoc est: tametsi pulsus à civitate in alio solo resipuerit. Latro resipiscit in cruce, & recipitur à Christo in paradisum, nihilominus magistratus pœnam exsequitur, & excludit eum ex politia. Sic sæpe locum habet ecclesiasticum judicium, ubi non est locus judicio politico: ut cum Ecclesia ex coetu suo eijcit, nec agnoscit amplius pro membris suis non agentes pœnitentiam: quos tamen magistratus civilis tolerat: & contra, sæpe politia eijcit, quos Ecclesia recipit: ut cum magistratus pœnâ capitali plectit adulteros, latrones, fures: quos tamen Ecclesia, si agant pœnitentiam, non excommunicat, sed recipit. Manifestum est igitur discrimen Ecclesiasticæ & politicæ potestatis.
units.tr: 6. Just as the Church proceeds only against the obstinate, so it is bound to reconsider its judgment and penalty if repentance intervenes. The magistrate, however, after he has punished, does not reconsider judgment and penalties, even though a criminal has become pious in another land. That is: "although, driven from the city, he has repented in another land." The robber repents on the cross and is received by Christ into paradise; nevertheless the magistrate carries out the penalty and excludes him from the polity. So ecclesiastical judgment often has a place where there is no room for political judgment: as when the Church casts out of its assembly, and no longer acknowledges as its members, those who do not repent, whom the civil magistrate nevertheless tolerates. And conversely, the polity often casts out those whom the Church receives: as when the magistrate punishes adulterers, robbers and thieves with capital punishment, whom the Church nevertheless, if they repent, does not excommunicate but receives. The difference between ecclesiastical and political power is therefore plain.

units.la: Supersunt obiectiones adversariorum disciplinæ ecclesiasticæ, ad quas paucis respondebimus.
units.tr: The objections of the opponents of ecclesiastical discipline remain, to which we shall reply briefly.

units.la: Obiect. 1. Nusquam est mandatum officium clavium. Ergo nemo debet excludi à sacramentis. Resp. Negatur antecedens: quia passim extant in scriptura divini mandati testimonia manifesta: Tibi dabo claves regni cœlorum: & quicquid ligaueritis super terram, erit ligatum in cœlis, &c. Hic distertis verbis exprimitur potestas clavium omnibus verbi ministris delegata. Quomodo etiam Ecclesia fungi debeat hoc officio clavium, Christus disertè præcipit & explicat: Quod si neglexerit eos audire, dic Ecclesiæ: quod si Ecclesiam audire neglexerit, sit tibi velut ethnicus & publicanus. Amen dico vobis, quæcunq; ligaueritis in terra, erunt ligata in cœlo, &c. Hæc à Christo præcepta Paulus reipsa confirmat: Huiusmodi tradatur Satanæ, ad interitum carnis, ut spiritus salvus sit die illo Domini Iesu. Cùm convenientis in unum, hoc non est cœnam Domini edere. Quod si quis non auscultat nostro per epistolam sermoni, hunc notate, & ne commercium habete cum eo, ut eum pudeat discant non blasphemare. Ex quibus sunt Alexander & Hymenaus, quos ego tradidi Satanæ, ut In Prophetis etiam manifesta sunt testimonia, quibus hoc à Deo mandatum esse constat: Quò mihi victimarum vestrarum multitudo? dicit Dominus. Plenus sum holocaustis arietum, &c. Qui immolat bovem, est quasi qui interficiat virum, &c. Non sum locutus cum patribus vestris, & non præcepi eis de verbo holocaustorum & victimarum. Peccatori autem dixit Deus: Quare tu enarras justitias meas, & assumis testamentum per os tuum? Hinc & Christus ait: Omitte illic munus tuum coram altari, & abi, & reconciliatorfratri tuo primum, & tunc veniens offer munus tuum. Sunt & alia scripturæ loca, quibus mandatum est, ut omnes palàm impij excludantur ab Ecclesia, & usu sacramentorum: ubicunque nimirum reprehenditur illegitimus sacramentorum usus: item, ubicunque jubentur ministri pro membiis Ecclesiæ recipere tantum profitentes fidem & pœnitentiam. Inst. Deus quidem impios ad sacramenta accedere vetat, sed non præcipit, vt Ecclesia eos prohibeat. Resp. Quæ Deus prohibet in Ecclesia fieri, ea vult Ecclesiæ iudicio vitari: & quod præceperit Dominus Ecclesiæ, vt prohibeat, & excludat palam impios, ex locis allegatis manifeste euincitur.
units.tr: Objection 1. Nowhere is the office of the keys commanded. Therefore no one ought to be excluded from the sacraments. Answer. The antecedent is denied, because throughout Scripture there are plain testimonies of divine command: "I will give you the keys of the kingdom of heaven; and whatever you bind on earth shall be bound in heaven, etc." Here the power of the keys is expressed in plain words as delegated to all ministers of the Word. Christ also plainly commands and explains how the Church ought to exercise this office of the keys: "But if he neglects to hear them, tell the Church; but if he neglects to hear the Church, let him be to you as a heathen and a tax collector. Truly I say to you, whatever you bind on earth shall be bound in heaven, etc." Paul actually confirms these precepts of Christ: "Such a one is to be delivered to Satan for the destruction of the flesh, that the spirit may be saved in the day of the Lord Jesus." When you come together into one place, this is not to eat the Lord's Supper. "And if anyone does not obey our word by this letter, note that man, and have no company with him, that he may be ashamed" and learn not to blaspheme. "Of these are Alexander and Hymenaeus, whom I have delivered to Satan, that they may..." There are also plain testimonies in the Prophets, by which it is clear that this was commanded by God: "What is the multitude of your sacrifices to me? says the Lord. I am full of the burnt offerings of rams, etc. He who slaughters an ox is as if he killed a man, etc. I did not speak with your fathers, nor command them concerning the word of burnt offerings and sacrifices." But God said to the sinner: "Why do you declare my statutes, and take my covenant into your mouth?" Hence Christ also says: "Leave your gift there before the altar, and go; first be reconciled to your brother, and then come and offer your gift." There are also other passages of Scripture by which it is commanded that all the openly wicked be excluded from the Church and from the use of the sacraments: wherever, that is, the unlawful use of the sacraments is rebuked; and likewise wherever ministers are commanded to receive into the membership of the Church only those who profess faith and repentance. Further objection. God indeed forbids the impious to approach the sacraments, but he does not command that the Church prohibit them. Answer. What God forbids to be done in the Church, he wills to be avoided by the judgment of the Church; and that the Lord commanded the Church to prohibit and openly exclude the impious is clearly proved from the passages cited.

units.la: Obiect. 1. Homines non possunt discernere dignos ab indignis, nec scire, qui verè resipiscant, & qui in impietate perseverent: quia non possunt inspicere corda: nec possunt aliquem ingehenam abiicere. Ergo Ecclesiæ non est mandatum illud iudicium, quo impii discernuntur à piis. Resp. Ecclesia non iudicat de arcanis, aut occultis, sed de manifestis; de iis nempe, quæ in exteriori vita & professione apparent: idq; cum de iis iudicio Dei subscribit, id est, cum de iis iudicat secundum verbi Dei præscriptū; vt cum ex verbo Dei condemnatos esse pronunciat contumaces, quamdiu tales manent; & cum ex verbo Dei pœnitentiam agentes absoluit. Occultos autem ab aliis discernere, sicut non potest Ecclesia, sic nec sibi tribuit.
units.tr: Objection 1. Men cannot distinguish the worthy from the unworthy, nor know who truly repent and who persist in impiety, since they cannot see into hearts; nor can they cast anyone into hell. Therefore the Church has not been commanded that judgment by which the impious are distinguished from the pious. Answer: The Church does not judge hidden or secret things but manifest ones, namely those that appear in outward life and profession; and it does so when it pronounces in accordance with God's judgment, that is, when it judges by the prescription of God's Word: as when it declares, from the Word of God, that the obstinate are condemned as long as they remain such, and when it absolves those who repent according to the Word of God. But to distinguish the secret from others, as the Church cannot do, so it does not claim this for itself.

units.la: Obiect. 3. Christus ait in illa parabola de zizaniis; Sinite simul utraque crescere vsque ad messem. Ergo nullus debet excludi. Resp. Christus loquitur ibi de hypocritis, qui non possunt discerni à veris piis. Itaque sensus est, non debere tolli vel segregari hypocritas ab Ecclesia, quos videlicet nos non nouimus, sed id facturos dicit angelos in nouissimo die. 2. Discernit officium ministrorum & magistratus: Sinite crescere, id est, ne intersicite alienos ab Ecclesia; ministri siquidem non debent quenquam afficere vi corporali, sicut magistratus. Hoc autem discrimine posito, non tollitur discrimen inter Ecclesiam, & regnum Diaboli.
units.tr: Objection 2. Christ says in that parable about the tares: "Let both grow together until the harvest." Therefore no one ought to be excluded. Answer: Christ is speaking there of hypocrites, who cannot be distinguished from true believers. So the meaning is that hypocrites are not to be removed or separated from the Church, namely those whom we do not know; this he says the angels will do on the last day. Second, he distinguishes the office of ministers and of the magistrate: "Let them grow," that is, do not slay those who are foreign to the Church; for ministers ought not to inflict any bodily force, as the magistrate does. Yet with this distinction laid down, the distinction between the Church and the kingdom of the Devil is not removed.

units.la: Obiect. 4. Homines cogendi sunt ad bona opera. Sacramentorum vsus est bonum opus. Ergo nemo ab eo est arcendus, sed omnes potius ad eum cogendi sunt. Resp. 1. Minor non est vera, nisi intelligatur de vsu, qui fit à fidelibus; cum vero ab infidelibus sacramenta vsurpantur, vsus eorum non est bonum opus, sed est abusus, & profanatio sacramentorum. Ideo Christus dehortatur impios ab hoc opere bono, cum ait: Relinque munus tuum ad altare, & abi, &c. 2. Maior est distinguenda.
