Answer 1 to the antecedent: it is lawful to show honour to the monuments of outstanding men, namely by keeping their memory gracious and honourable, and by using those things which they left behind as monuments for the purpose for which they were rightly intended. If necessity demands a change, they may be altered or destroyed, provided this is done without any intention or wish to insult those men. But it is by no means lawful to give them divine honour, such as that which these men give to idols under the name of either latreia [λατρείας] or douleia [δουλείας]. 2. Those monuments too must be of such a kind that they have not been turned to idolatry; otherwise they are not to be honoured but must be abolished altogether, as with the bronze serpent which Hezekiah broke in pieces when it had led to idolatry, although before this it had been preserved as a monument of God's benefit granted in the wilderness.

units.la: QVÆSTIO XCVIII. An autem in templis imagines tolerari non possunt, quæ pro libris sint imperitæ multitudini? RESPONSIO.
units.tr: QUESTION 98. But are images in churches not to be tolerated when they serve as books for the unlearned multitude? ANSWER.

units.la: Minimè. Neque enim decet nos sapientiores esse Deo, qui suam Ecclesiam non mutis simulacris a, sed viua prædicatione verbi sui vult erudiri b.
units.tr: By no means. For it is not fitting that we should be wiser than God, who wishes his Church to be taught not by dumb images a, but by the living preaching of his word b.

units.la: a Ieremiæ 10. verf. 8. Hebr. 2. verf. 18, 19. b Rom. 1. v. 17. 2 Pet. 1. verf. 19. 2 Timoth. 3, 16, 17.
units.tr: a Jeremiah 10:8. Habakkuk 2:18, 19. b Romans 1:17. 2 Peter 1:19. 2 Timothy 3:16, 17.

units.la: EXPLICATIO.
units.tr: EXPLANATION.

units.la: Hæc est obiectio eorum, qui quidem imagines & statuas Dei & sanctorum concedunt non esse adorandas: contendunt vero esse retinendas in templis Christianorum, tanquam libros Laicorum. Hoc prætextu Gregorius Papa iussit Serenum Episcopum Massiliensem idola Ethnicorum non simpliciter abolere, sed statuis sanctorum commutare: quia sint libri Laicorum. Catechesis vero simpliciter negat. Negationis plures adferri poterant causæ, sed vna sufficientissima est, à sapientissima Dei ordinatione, qua suam Ecclesiam non mutis simulacris, sed viua prædicatione verbi sui erudiri præcepit. Fides enim non est ex aspectu sculptilium (quæ sunt doctor mendacij) sed ex auditu verbi Dei.
units.tr: This is the objection of those who grant that images and statues of God and the saints are not to be worshipped, but maintain that they should be kept in the churches of Christians as books for laymen. On this pretext Pope Gregory ordered Serenus, Bishop of Marseilles, not simply to abolish the idols of the heathen but to replace them with statues of the saints, because they are books for laymen. The Catechism, however, flatly denies this. Several reasons could be given for the denial, but one is most sufficient: the wisest ordering of God, by which he commanded that his Church be taught not by dumb images but by the living preaching of his word. Faith comes not from the sight of carved images (which are a teacher of lies) but from hearing the word of God.

units.la: III. Quare Imagines & statuæ è templis & compitis Christianorum tollendæ sint.
units.tr: III. Why images and statues are to be removed from the temples and streets of Christians.

units.la: Causæ, propter quas imagines & statuæ, quæ aliquando adoratæ sunt, vel adorari possunt, vt sunt statuæ religiosæ Dei, Christi, vel sti, vel SANCTORVM, in templis, aut viarum compitis non sint ferendæ, sed abolendæ: præcipuæ sunt:
units.tr: The reasons why images and statues, which have at some time been worshipped or could be worshipped, such as religious statues of God, of Christ, or of the saints, should not be tolerated in the churches or at the crossroads of the streets, but abolished, are chiefly these:

units.la: 1. Quia contra expressum Dei mandatum factæ, & in templis positæ sunt. Cum vero Deus nolit imagines fieri, quibus ipse præsentetur, vel ad quas ipse colatur: non vult etiam ab aliis factas retineri, sed tolli, & aboleri.
units.tr: 1. Because they have been made and placed in churches against the express command of God. Since God does not wish images to be made by which he himself is represented, or by which he himself is worshipped, he does not wish images made by others to be kept either, but removed and abolished.

units.la: 2. Quia fuerunt occasio & instrumenta horribilis idololatriæ in papatu.
units.tr: 2. Because they have been the occasion and the instruments of dreadful idolatry in the papacy.

units.la: 3. Quia Deus expresse mandauit aboleri ac tolli idola, & omnes veri cultus Dei & veræ doctrinæ corruptelas, vt iram suam aduersus idololatriam testetur.
units.tr: 3. Because God has expressly commanded that idols be abolished and removed, along with all corruptions of the true worship of God and of true doctrine, so that he may show his wrath against idolatry.

units.la: 4. Propter confessionem sinceri cultus Dei, & odij aduersus idololatriam, quæ confessio non tantum in verbis, sed etiam in actionibus, specie & signis externis consistit: Statuas eorum confringetis, & sculptilia comburetis igni. nam populus sanctus es Iehoua Deo tuo. Fugite ab idololatria, nempe animo, professione & signis.
units.tr: 4. For the sake of confessing the pure worship of God and hatred of idolatry; a confession that consists not only in words but also in deeds, in appearance and in outward signs: You shall break their statues, and burn their carved images with fire; for you are a holy people to Jehovah your God. Flee from idolatry, that is, in mind, in profession and in signs.

units.la: 5. Quia propter idolorum destructionem laudantur pij reges in scriptura, Assa, Iehu, Ezechias, Iosias, &c.
units.tr: 5. Because on account of the destruction of idols the godly kings are praised in Scripture: Asa, Jehu, Hezekiah, Josiah, etc.

units.la: 6. Propter vitationem scandali, & periculi superstitionis & idololatriæ, ne videlicet veteribus statuis retentis, ac novis substitutis vel additis, idem periculum creetur Ecclesiæ & rudi populo, quod olim ex hac re maioribus nostris creatum esse vidimus.
units.tr: 6. For the avoiding of scandal and of the danger of superstition and idolatry; namely, lest, if old statues are kept and new ones substituted or added, the same danger should arise for the Church and for the untaught people which we have seen arise from this very thing for our forefathers in the past.

units.la: 7. Ne hostes Ecclesiæ hoc spectaculo, magnam idololatriæ speciem habente, ab Ecclesia magis abalienentur, & veritatem diuinam afficiant contumelia. De hoc periculo Deus ipse monuit: Propterea dixi, non expellam eos à facie vestra, sed erunt vobis sicut muli in lateribus, & dij eorum erunt vobis in laqueum. Et certè Iudæi & Turcæ & Pagani, qui vident statuas & idola in templis Christianorum, maximè offenduntur, vt à religione Christiana magis abhorreant.
units.tr: 7. Lest the enemies of the Church, offended by this spectacle, which has a great appearance of idolatry, become further alienated from the Church and cast contempt upon divine truth. God himself warned of this danger: Therefore I said, I will not drive them out from before you, but they shall be as thorns in your sides, and their gods shall be a snare to you. And certainly the Jews, the Turks and the pagans, who see statues and idols in the churches of Christians, are greatly offended and shrink all the more from the Christian religion.

units.la: 8. Denique vidimus, simulacra nunquam recte cessisse iis, qui ea habuerunt: plerunque populum DEI seduxerunt: vt passim in historia sacra, præsertim in libris Iudicum, Regum & Prophetarum videre est. Adeo procliuis est natura nostra ad idololatriam. Postea secutæ sunt horribiles pœnæ, quales passim DEVS per Mosen minatur: Destruam excelsa vestra, & simulacra vestra confringam, cadetis inter ruinas idolorum vestrorum. Et angelus exprobrans Israelitis, quod cum Chanaanis fœdus fecissent, inquit: Quamobrem noluit eos delere à facie vestra, vt haberetis hostes, & dij ipsorum essent vobis in ruinam.
units.tr: 8. Finally, we have seen that images have never turned out well for those who have kept them: they have for the most part led the people of God astray, as may be seen everywhere in sacred history, especially in the books of Judges, Kings and the Prophets. So prone is our nature to idolatry. Afterwards dreadful punishments followed, such as God threatens everywhere through Moses: I will destroy your high places and break your images, and you shall fall among the ruins of your idols. And the angel rebuking the Israelites, because they had made a covenant with the Canaanites, said: Wherefore he would not drive them out from before you, that you might have enemies, and their gods might be a ruin to you.

units.la: His igitur de causis statuæ & imagines in templis Christianorum rum ferri non debent: sed tolli, & aboleri, quantumuis non adorentur.
units.tr: For these reasons, therefore, statues and images ought not to be tolerated in the churches of Christians, but removed and abolished, even if they are not worshipped.

units.la: IV. Quomodo & à quibus imagines sint abolenda.
units.tr: IV. How and by whom images are to be abolished.

units.la: In abolitione imaginum & statuarum duo sunt diligenter obseruanda.
units.tr: In the abolition of images and statues two things are to be carefully observed.

units.la: 1. Vt praemittatur doctrina de vero Dei cultu ante idolorum abolitionem. Sic legimus fecisse Josuam, qui prius legem diuinam toti populo iussit recitari, postea ad eius executionem progressus est. Mutatio enim in rebus externis sine doctrina & intellectu causarum, propter quas mutatio fieri debeat, aut hypocritas facit, aut animos à facientibus mutationem alienat atque abster ret. Praecedat igitur doctrina, & idola sponte concident.
units.tr: 1. That the doctrine concerning the true worship of God be set forth before the abolition of idols. Thus we read that Joshua acted: he first ordered the divine law to be read to the whole people, and only afterwards proceeded to carry it out. For a change in external things without teaching and understanding of the causes that ought to bring about the change either makes hypocrites or alienates and turns away the minds of those who would make the change. Let doctrine therefore go first, and idols will fall of their own accord.

units.la: 2. Statuae & statuarum cathedrae, altaria aliaq; idololatriae instrumenta tolli debent non à priuatis, sed auctoritate publica siue magistratuum, siue populi, si penes eum sit potestas publica, & in iis locis, in quibus ecclesia tenet imperium. Sic enim praecepit Deus Israelitis; sic item ab Israelitis & piis regibus factum esse legimus. Contra Paulus cum priuatus esset, videns & improbans idola Atheniensium, Ephesiorum & aliorum, non tamen ea ipse deturbauit, nec Christianos ad deturbanda, sed tantum ad fugienda ea est hortatus: quia videlicet nec ipse fuit magistratus, nec ecclesia ibi tenuit imperium: & regulam addidit: Quid mea interest etiam de extraneis iudicare? Non de iis, qui intus sunt, vos iudicatis? De extraneis vero Deus iudicat.
units.tr: 2. Statues, the seats of statues, altars and other instruments of idolatry ought to be removed not by private persons but by public authority, whether of the magistrates or of the people, if the public power lies with them, and in those places where the Church holds authority. For thus God commanded the Israelites; and thus we read it was done by the Israelites and by godly kings. On the other hand, when Paul was a private person, seeing and disapproving of the idols of the Athenians, the Ephesians and others, he did not himself overthrow them, nor did he urge Christians to overthrow them, but only to flee from them; because clearly he was not a magistrate, and the Church did not hold authority there. And he added a rule: What have I to do with judging those outside? Do you not judge those who are inside? But God judges those outside.

units.la: Obiect. 1. Libri laicorum in templis sunt vtiles & retinendi. Imagines & statuae sunt libri laicorum. Ergo in templis vtiliter relinqui possunt. Resp. 1. ad maiorem. Libri laicorum sunt vtiles, nempe qui eis sunt traditi à Deo; simulacra verò sunt libri à Deo prohibiti. 2. Negatur minor. Nam longe aliter docent Prophetae: Sculptile doctor mendacy. Simulacra locuta sunt vanitatem. Hinc ita licet argumentari. De Deo nec vana loqui, nec mentiri debemus verbis vel gestibus. Ligna seu sculptilia sunt mendacium de Deo, quia non possunt Deum repraesentare, immò quia tantum discedunt, & simul nos auertunt à Deo, quantum à Deo abest eorum figura: & per consequens faciunt, vt nos de Deo mentiamur. Si igitur nolimus mentiri de Deo, imagines & sculptilia nec faciamus, nec habeamus necesse est. Nam vt Jeremias ait, lignum est eruditio vanitatum. Atque hoc modo concedemus, statuas & imagines esse libros idiotarum: nempe vanos & mendaces: partim quia falsum de Deo docent & significant: partim quia rei significatae & loci reuerentia, quando in templis & alibi proprostant, facilime ad superstitionem alios rapiunt, & populum docent idololatriam, sicut experientia testatur. 3. Negatur con-sequentia, quia est fallacia non causæ. Licet enim imagines docerent idiotas; non tamen sequeretur, eas ideo in templis, tanquam libros vtiles, retinendas esse. Nam Deus non vult Ecclesiam suam per muta simulacra, sed per viuam prædicationem fui verbi erudire: quia fides non est ex aspectu statuarum, sed ex auditu verbi Dei.
units.tr: Objection 1. Books for laymen are useful and are to be kept in churches. Images and statues are books for laymen. Therefore they can usefully be left in churches. Answer 1, to the major premise: books for laymen are useful, namely those given to them by God; but images are books forbidden by God. 2. The minor premise is denied. For the prophets teach quite differently: A carved image is a teacher of lies. Images have spoken vanity. From this we may argue thus: we must neither speak vain things nor lie about God, by words or by gestures. Wood or carved images are a lie about God, because they cannot represent God; indeed, because the more their figure departs from God, the more it both draws us away from him and turns us from him, and consequently makes us lie about God. If therefore we do not wish to lie about God, we must not make images and carved figures, nor need we have them. For, as Jeremiah says, the wood is a teaching of vanities. In this way we may grant that statues and images are books of the unlearned, namely vain and lying books: partly because they teach and signify falsehood about God, and partly because the reverence paid to the thing signified, when they are displayed in churches and elsewhere, very easily draws others into superstition and teaches the people idolatry, as experience bears witness. 3. The consequence is denied, because it is a fallacy of non-cause. For even if images did teach the unlearned, it would not follow that they are therefore to be kept in churches as useful books. For God does not wish to teach his Church by dumb images, but by the living preaching of his word: because faith does not come from the sight of statues, but from the hearing of the word of God.

units.la: Obiect. 2. Præceptum de abolendis statuis est cæremoniale. Ergo non pertinet ad Christianos, sed tantum ad Judæos. Resp. Negatur antecedens. Neq; enim cæremonia est, abolere idololatriæ organa, occasiones, & signa: neq; immutatæ sunt huius præcepti causæ, propter quas olim lata fuit, vt nimirum gloria Dei aduersus idololatras & hostes ecclesiæ vindicetur, & non tentetur Deus, objiciendo infirmis & rudibus occasiones & incitamenta superstitionum & idololatriæ, ad quam homines alioqui natura propendent. Est igitur præceptum de statuis non habendis, sed tollendis, morale, & perpetuum.
units.tr: Objection 2. The precept concerning the abolition of statues is ceremonial. Therefore it does not pertain to Christians, but only to the Jews. Answer. The antecedent is denied. For it is not ceremonial to abolish the implements, occasions and signs of idolatry; nor have the causes of this precept, for which it was once given, been changed: namely, that the glory of God be vindicated against idolaters and the enemies of the Church, and that God not be tempted by setting before the weak and the untaught occasions and incitements to superstition and idolatry, to which men are otherwise naturally inclined. The precept concerning not having statues, but removing them, is therefore moral and perpetual.

units.la: Obj. 3. Salomon in templo jussu Dei posuit statuas Cherubinorum, leonum, boum, palmarum. Ergo etiam in nostris templis statuæ possunt tolerari. Resp. Est dissimilitudo in exemplis. 1. Figuræ variarum rerum & animalium, vt boum, leonum, palmarum, Cherubinorum & similium in Salomonis templo, nitebantur Dei verbo seu mandato speciali, quod statuis & imaginibus in templis nostris prorsus aduersatur. 2. Statuæ Salomonis tales erant, quæ in vsum superstitiosum non facile trahi poterant. Dei verò & sanctorum statuæ non modo in superstitionem abire facilè possunt, sed nimis fœdæ, proh dolor, idololatriæ causa in papatu hactenus fuerunt. 3. Causam, cur vellet Deus imagines illas in templo exstare, hanc habuit, vt essent typi rerum spiritualium. Hæc verò causa nunc est per Christum sublata. Nostræ igitur statuæ hoc exemplo non possunt defendi: Est verò nobis vniuersali mandato parendum, quo imagines tales ac tali loco statuere prohibemur, quæ & vbi scandalo ecclesiæ membris aut hostibus esse possunt.
units.tr: Objection 3. Solomon, by God's command, set up in the temple statues of cherubim, lions, oxen and palm trees. Therefore statues may also be tolerated in our churches. Answer. The examples differ. 1. The figures of various things and animals, such as oxen, lions, palm trees and cherubim in Solomon's temple, rested on God's word or special command, which is entirely opposed to statues and images in our churches. 2. Solomon's statues were of a kind not easily turned to superstitious use. But statues of God and of the saints not only can easily slide into superstition, but, alas, in the papacy they have so far been a very foul cause of idolatry. 3. God had this reason for wanting those images to stand in the temple: they were to be types of spiritual things. But that reason has now been removed through Christ. Our statues therefore cannot be defended by this example. Rather, we must obey the universal command which forbids us to set up such images, in such places, as can be a scandal to the members of the church or to its enemies.

units.la: Obiect. 4. Statuæ & imagines in templis reformatis non adorantur. Ergo possunt tolerari. Resp. Deus non tantum vetat statuas adorari, sed etiam fieri, & factas haberi circa cultum Dei, seu in locis, vbi colitur Deus: Non facies tibi sculptile, &c. 2. Rudibus semper sunt occasio superstitionum & idololatriæ, reste superiorum & præsentium temporum experientia. 3. Judæis, Turcis, paganis, & aliis hostibus scandalum & materiam blasphemandi Euangelium objiciunt.
units.tr: Objection 4. Statues and images in the reformed churches are not worshipped. Therefore they may be tolerated. Answer. God forbids not only that statues be worshipped, but also that they be made and kept in connection with the worship of God, or in places where God is worshipped: "You shall not make for yourself a carved image," etc. 2. They are always an occasion of superstition and idolatry for the unlearned, as the experience of former and present times clearly shows. 3. They offer the Jews, Turks, pagans and other enemies a scandal and a material for blaspheming the Gospel.

units.la: Obiect. 5. Statuæ sunt ornatus templorum. Ergo tolerari possunt. Resp. 1. Verus ornatus templorum est pura doctrina Euangelij, legitimus sacramentorum vsus, vera inuocatio, & cultus secundum verbum Dei. 2. Templa sunt condita, vt in eis conspiciantur viuæ imagines Dei, non vt sint stabula idolorum, & mutarum statuarum. 3. Ornatus ecclesiasticus non debet esse membris ecclesiæ periculosus, aut hostibus scandalosus. gnare cum Dei mandato. 4. Nec debet esse membris ecclesiæ
units.tr: Objection 5. Statues are the adornment of churches. Therefore they may be tolerated. Answer. 1. The true adornment of churches is the pure doctrine of the Gospel, the lawful use of the sacraments, true invocation, and worship according to the Word of God. 2. Churches were built so that in them the living images of God might be seen, not so that they become stables of idols and dumb statues. 3. Church ornament should not be dangerous to the members of the church, nor scandalous to its enemies, and it should agree with God's command. 4. Nor should it be a danger to the members of the church.

units.la: Inst. Propter accidens seu abusum non est tollenda res ipsa & vsus rei. Statuæ per accidens tantum sunt periculosæ vel scandalosæ. Ergo non sunt ex templis remouendæ. Resp. ad maiorem, quæ vera est, si res sit per se bona, & vsus eius licitus, & accidens, indiuiduè cum ea cohærens, non fit à Deo damnatum. Secus enim & res & vsus rei est illicitus & vitandus. Jam autem statuæ Dei & sanctorum in templis religionis causa positæ, nec bonæ sunt, nec vsus earum licitus, sed expresso Dei mandato vetitus. Accidens quoque, nempe superstitio vel idololatria, perpetuo eas apud rudiores comitatur, quicquid alij firmiores de sua scientia præxtexant, & pariter Dei præcepto damnatur.
units.tr: Instance. Because of an accident or an abuse, the thing itself and its use should not be removed. Statues are dangerous or scandalous only by accident. Therefore they are not to be removed from churches. Answer to the major premise, which is true if the thing is good in itself and its use lawful, and the accident, which is inseparably joined to it, is not condemned by God. Otherwise both the thing and its use are unlawful and to be avoided. But statues of God and of the saints, set up in churches for the sake of religion, are neither good, nor is their use lawful; rather, they are forbidden by an express command of God. The accident as well, namely superstition or idolatry, always goes with them among the more unlearned, whatever the stronger sort may put forward from their own knowledge; and it is likewise condemned by God's command.

units.la: Inst. 2. Satis est eas per doctrinam eximi mentibus hominum. Ergo non necesse est eas è templis eijci. Resp. 1. Negatur antecedens, quia Deus non tantum in mentibus, sed etiam in oculis hominum eas existere vetat; quandoquidem vult nos non modo non esse, sed ne quidem videri idololatras: Ab omni specie mali abstinete. 2. Tanta est humani cordis peruersitas, & ad superstitiones propensio, vt idola, præsertim comta, polita & ornata, in oculis relicta, animis rudiorum vltro insideant, & religione quadam eas afficiant, quicquid ab aliis contra doceatur. 3. Per inuer-sionem. Sunt per doctrinam eximenda mentibus. Ergo etiam eijcienda ex templis. Jubet enim doctrina cœlitus patefacta, ca non tantum non adorare & colere, sed ne quidem facere aut habere. Hactenus de præcepto.
units.tr: Instance 2. It is enough to remove them from people's minds by teaching. Therefore it is not necessary to cast them out of churches. Answer. 1. The antecedent is denied, because God forbids them to exist not only in men's minds but also in men's sight; since he wills that we be not only not idolaters, but not even seen to be idolaters: "Abstain from every appearance of evil." 2. The perversity of the human heart and its tendency toward superstition are so great that idols, especially if adorned, polished and decked out, left in view, will of their own accord settle in the minds of the unlearned and invest them with a certain religious feeling, whatever is taught to the contrary by others. 3. By inversion. They are to be removed from minds by teaching. Therefore they are also to be cast out of churches. For the doctrine revealed from heaven commands that they not only not be adored and worshipped, but not even be made or kept. So much for the command.

units.la: Hortatio addita secundo præcepto.
units.tr: The exhortation added to the second commandment.

units.la: Hortatio præcepto addita: Ego sum Dominus Deus tuus, fortis, zelotes, vindicans peccata patrum in filiis, &c. continet quinque; Dei attributa, quæ nos ad obedientiam excitare debent. 1. Deum nostrum vocat se, hoc est, conditorem & seruatorem nostrum, ac bonorum omnium largitorem. Itamonet, quam detestanda sit ingratitudo, huic benefactori nostro non præstare obedientiam, vel ab eius cultu deficere ad idololatriam. 2. Deum fortem, nempe tam ad puniendum contumaces, quam ad benefaciendum obtemperantibus. Est igitur super omnia timendus colendus. 3. Zelotem seu Zelotypum, hoc est, acerrimum sui honoris defensorem & vindicem, horribiliter irascentem deficientibus ab ipso, aut honorem & cultum ipsius violantibus: cum autem zelus siue indignatio propter injuriam & turpitudinem oriatur ex amore eius, qui laeditur, simul indicat, se ardenter suos amare. 4. Vindicantem peccata parentum in filiis in tertia & quarta generatione eorum, qui ipsum oderunt. Exaggerat irae & poenarum grauitatem, dum etiam filiis & nepotibus & nepotibus hostium suorum minatur vindicare in illis maiorum peccata, nempe, si maiorum suorum peccatis ipsi communicent.
units.tr: The exhortation added to the commandment: "I am the LORD your God, a jealous God, visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children," etc., contains five attributes of God which ought to stir us up to obedience. 1. He calls himself our God, that is, our creator and preserver and the giver of all good things. He thereby warns how detestable ingratitude is, not to render obedience to this benefactor of ours, or to fall away from his worship into idolatry. 2. A strong God, namely, strong both to punish the stubborn and to bless those who obey. He is therefore to be feared and worshipped above all things. 3. A jealous God, that is, the most fierce defender and avenger of his own honor, who is terribly angry with those who fall away from him or violate his honor and worship. Since zeal or indignation arises from an injury and a disgrace done to one who is loved, it also shows that he ardently loves his own people. 4. Visiting the sins of the fathers upon the children, to the third and fourth generation of those who hate him. He magnifies the wrath and the gravity of the punishments, since he threatens to visit upon the children and grandchildren, and even the grandchildren of his enemies, the sins of their forebears, namely if they share in the sins of their forebears.

units.la: Obiectio. Filius non portabit iniquitatem Patris. Ezechielis 18. vers. 14. 20. Resp. Conciliatio ibidem additur: Si impius genuerit filium, qui viderit omnia peccata patris sui, & non fecerit similia: hic non morietur propter iniquitatem patris, sed viuendo viuet. Ergo minatur, se punituram peccata maiorum in posteris, scilicet perseuerantibus in maiorum peccatis, quos etiam poenarum participes esse iustum est. Inst. 1. Hoc modo posteri non maiorum, sed tantum sua peccata luerent. Resp. Negatur consequentia. Possunt enim vnius effectus plures esse causae impulsiuae, & vnius poenae causa possunt esse plura peccata, tam diuersorum, quam eorundem hominum. Inst. 2. Sensus poenarum, quas posteri perferunt, non possunt pertingere ad maiores. Ergo, &c. Resp. Negatur antecedens. Nam posteri sunt pars maiorum. Sentiunt igitur maiores in ipsis, tanquam in parte aliqua sui, quod posteri patiuntur.
units.tr: Objection. "The son shall not bear the iniquity of the father," Ezekiel 18, verses 14 and 20. Answer. The reconciliation is added in the same place: "If a wicked man begets a son who sees all the sins of his father and does not do likewise, this one shall not die for the iniquity of his father, but living he shall live." Therefore he threatens that he will punish the sins of the forebears in their posterity, namely those who persevere in their forebears' sins, and it is just that these also share in the punishments. Instance 1. In this way the posterity would suffer not the sins of their forebears but only their own. Answer. The consequence is denied. For one effect may have several impelling causes, and one punishment may have several causes, sins both of different persons and of the same persons. Instance 2. The feelings of the punishments which the posterity endure cannot reach the forebears. Therefore, etc. Answer. The antecedent is denied. For the posterity are a part of their forebears. The forebears therefore feel in them, as in some part of themselves, what the posterity suffers.

units.la: §. Deum se esse dicit, qui misericordia vtatur erga millesimam generationem eorum, qui diligunt ipsum, & mandata eius seruant: qua promissione amplificat misericordiam suam, vt nos beneficentiae diuinae amplitudine, & nostrae ac nostrorum posterorum salutis desiderio, ad obedientiam inuitet. Et cum tamen poenas minetur tantum in quartam generationem, misericordiam extendit in millesimam: vt significet, se magis propensum esse ad misericordiam, quam ad iram, & hoc nomine ad se magis diligendum nos alliciat.
units.tr: He says that he is the God "who shows mercy to the thousandth generation of those who love him and keep his commandments." By this promise he magnifies his mercy, so that he may invite us to obedience by the greatness of the divine kindness and by our desire for the salvation of ourselves and our posterity. And since he threatens punishment only to the fourth generation, he extends mercy to the thousandth, to signify that he is more inclined to mercy than to wrath, and so by this means draws us to love him more.

units.la: Obiect. 1. Atqui multorum piorum soboles male periit. Resp. Promissio est conditionalis. Sic enim Deus ipse exponit, se besetaturum posteris piorum, si in pietate maiorum perseuerent: si ab ea deficiant, se eos puniturum. Inst. Sed cur Deus non ominus ipsorum posteros conuertit, cum sine ipsius misericordia pietatem parentum nou possint imitari? Resp. Quia non astringit suam misericordiam ad singula indiuidua posteritatis pio-rum: sed liberam sibi seruat electionem suam, vt sicut ex impio-rum rum posteris aliquos conuertit & seruat, sic ex priorum posterioris aliquos relinquit in prauitate naturali & exitio, quod omnes natura merentur: idque vt suam misericordiam gratuitam esse, tam in piorum, quam in impiorum posteris eligendis ostendat, &c.
units.tr: Objection 1. Yet the offspring of many pious people have perished badly. Answer. The promise is conditional. For God himself thus explains it: he will show mercy to the posterity of the pious if they persevere in the piety of their forebears; if they fall away from it, he will punish them. Instance. But why does God not also convert their posterity, since without his mercy they cannot imitate the piety of their parents? Answer. Because he does not bind his mercy to each individual of the posterity of the pious, but keeps his election free, so that just as he converts and saves some from the posterity of the wicked, so he leaves some of the posterity of the former in natural depravity and ruin, which all deserve by nature; and this so that he may show that his mercy is free, in choosing both the posterity of the pious and that of the impious, etc.

units.la: Obj.2. Qui præcepta Dei seruant, misericordiam consequuntur. Ergo de Deo aliquid meremur nostra obedientia. R. Contrarium sequitur. Deus dicit: Faciam iis misericordiam. Ergo non facit ex merito. Namquod fit ex misericordia, non fit ex merito, & contra. Est igitur fallacia non causæ.
units.tr: Objection 2. Those who keep God's commandments obtain mercy. Therefore our obedience merits something from God. Answer. The contrary follows. God says: "I will show mercy to them." Therefore he does not act from merit. For what is done from mercy is not done from merit, and conversely. So this is the fallacy of the non-cause.

units.la: Obiect.3. Hæc promissio & comminatio pertinet ad totum decalogum: cur igitur huic præcepto annectitur? Resp. Annexa est secundo præcepto, non quod ad id solum pertineat, sed vt sciamus, primum & secundum præceptum esse aliorum omnium fundamentum, & vt Deus ostendat, se præcipuè cultus sui desiderare, ideoq; hoc peccati genus in ipsis & in posteris ultiscitur: contra vero etiam posteritati religionem puram diligenter custodientium benefacere velle.
units.tr: Objection 3. This promise and threat apply to the whole Decalogue, so why is it attached to this commandment? Answer. It is attached to the second commandment, not because it pertains to that alone, but so that we may know that the first and second commandments are the foundation of all the others, and so that God may show that he especially desires his worship. For this reason he punishes this kind of sin in the offenders and in their posterity, and on the other hand he is willing to do good to the posterity of those who diligently keep pure religion.

units.la: QVÆSTIO XCIX.
units.tr: QUESTION 99.

units.la: Quid sancit Deus in tertio præcepto? RESPONSIO.
units.tr: What does God enjoin in the third commandment? ANSWER.

units.la: Vt non solum exsecrando a, aut peierando b, verùm etiam temerè iurando c, nomen Dei contumeliosè aut irreuerenter ne vsurpemus: neue tacendo, aut conniuendo, horrendis istis sceleribus communicemus d: sed sacrosancto Dei nomine non nisi summa cum religione & veneratione vtamur e: vt verâ & constanti confessione f, inuocatione g, omnibus denique verbis & actionibus nostris, ipse celebretur h.
units.tr: That we not use the name of God contemptuously or irreverently, by cursing a, or by perjury b, but also not by rash swearing c; nor by silence or connivance may we share in these horrible crimes d; but we use the most holy name of God only with the highest reverence and veneration e; so that he himself may be celebrated by true and steadfast confession f, by invocation g, and finally by all our words and actions h.

units.la: a Leuit.24 verf.15.16. b Leuit.19,12. c Matth.5,37. Iacobi 9,12. d Leuit. 5,1. Proverb.29,24. e Ierem.4,7. Esa.45,23. f Matth.10. v.32. Rom.10,9-10. g Psal.50,51. 1 Tim.2,8. h Coloss.3,17. Rom.2. v.14. 1 Tim.6,1.
QVÆSTIO C.
units.tr: QUESTION 100.

units.la: Estne igitur adeo graue peccatum, iurando, aut dira imprecando, nomen Dei temerare, vt Deus etiam iis succenseat, qui quantum in se est, illud non prohibent, aut impediunt?
units.tr: Is it therefore so grave a sin to profane the name of God by swearing or by uttering dire imprecations, that God is angry even with those who, so far as in them lies, do not forbid or prevent it?

units.la: RESPONSIO.
units.tr: ANSWER.

units.la: Certè grauissimum a. Neque enim vllum est peccatum maius, aut quod Deum grauius offendat, quàm sancti ipsius nominis contumelia. Quocirca etiam id scelus morte multari voluit b.
units.tr: Certainly it is most grave. For there is no sin greater, or one that offends God more seriously, than insult to his holy name. Therefore he also wished this crime to be punished by death.

units.la: a Proverb. 29, 42. Leuit. 5, 1. b Leuit. 24, 16.
EXPLICATIO.
units.tr: EXPLANATION.

units.la: In primo & secundo præcepto Deus formauit mentes & corda ad verum sui cultum: iam in tertio & quarto præcepto etiam format externa membra & actiones.
units.tr: In the first and second commandments God formed minds and hearts for the true worship of himself; now in the third and fourth commandments he also forms the outward members and actions.

units.la: Duæ sunt partes tertij præcepti: prohibitio, & comminatio.
units.tr: The third commandment has two parts: a prohibition and a threat.

units.la: Prohibetur vsus nominis diuini temerarius, & omnis abusus in quacunq; re falsa, vana aut leui, quæ ad ignominiam, vel saltem non ad gloriam Dei spectat. Nomen autem Dei in scriptura significat 1. Attributa Dei. Cur quaris nomen meum, quod est mirabile? Iehoua Deus patrum vestrosum, Deus Abraham, Deus Isaac, Deus Iacob, misit me ad vos. Hoc nomen mihi est in æternum, & hoc memoriale meum in generatione & generationē: Dominus quasi vir pugnator, omnipotens nomen eius. 2. Ipsum Deum. Qui diligunt nomen tuum, hoc est, teipsum. Calicem salutis accipiam, & nomen Domini inuocabo. Psallam nomini altissimi. Immolabisq; Domino Deo tuo de ouibus, & de bobus in loco, quem elegerit Dominus Deus tuus, vt habitet nomen eius ibi. Cogito & ædificare templum nomini Domini Dei mei. 3. Voluntatem siue mandatum Dei, idq; vel patefactum & verum, vel ab hominibus effictum & simulatum. Quicunq; non audierit verba mea, quæ loquetur propheta ille in nomine meo, ego requiram ab eo. Ego venio ad te in nomine Domini exercituum. 4. Cultum, fiduciam, inuocationem, celebrationem & professionem Dei. Omnes populi ambulabunt, vnusquisq; in nomine Domini Dei nostri in æternum & vltra. Baptizantes eos in nomine Patris, & Filij & Spiritus sancti. Ego non solum vinciri, sed etiam mori paratus sum in Hierusalem pro nomine Domini Iesu.
units.tr: The rash use of the divine name is forbidden, and every abuse of it in any matter that is false, vain or frivolous, and which tends to dishonour God or at least does not tend to his glory. In Scripture the name of God signifies: 1. The attributes of God. "Why do you ask my name, seeing it is wonderful?" "I am Jehovah, the God of your fathers, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac and the God of Jacob, who has sent me to you. This is my name for ever, and this is my memorial from generation to generation. The Lord is a man of war; Almighty is his name." 2. God himself. "Those who love your name," that is, you yourself. "I will take the cup of salvation and call upon the name of the Lord. I will sing praise to the name of the Most High. You shall sacrifice to the Lord your God sheep and oxen in the place which the Lord your God shall choose, that his name may dwell there. I intend to build a temple for the name of the Lord my God." 3. The will or command of God, either revealed and true, or feigned and counterfeited by men. "Whoever does not hear my words, which that prophet shall speak in my name, I will require it of him." "I come to you in the name of the Lord of hosts." 4. The worship, trust, invocation, celebration and profession of God. "All peoples will walk, each in the name of the Lord our God, for ever and ever." "Baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit." "I am ready not only to be bound but also to die at Jerusalem for the name of the Lord Jesus."

units.la: Assumere nomen Dei, seu nominare, vel vsurpare, non quidem Deus prohibet, sed vetat illud temere, hoc est, leuiter, falso, vel
units.tr: To take up the name of God, that is, to name or use it, God does not forbid as such, but he forbids doing so rashly, that is, lightly, falsely, or contumeliously.

units.la: Iud. 13, 18. Exod. 3, 15. Exod. 15, 3. Psalm. 5, 12. Psal. 116, 4. Psal. 7, 18. Deut. 16, 2. 1 Reg. 5, 5. Deut. 18, 19. 1 Sam. 17, 45. Mich. 4, 5. Mat. 28, 19. Act. 21, 13. contumeliose vsurpari. Leuiter, vt in quotidiano sermone con tra regulam Christi: Sermo vester sit, est, est, non, non. Falso, vt in iuramentis illicitis & perjuriis. Contumeliose, vt in exsecrationibus, blasphemiis, & incantationibus, quibus opera diaboli nobis mine Dei palliantur. Sensus ergo est: Non assumes nomen Dei tui temere, hoc est, non tantum non peierabis, sed nec facies vllam mentionem nominis diuini non honorificam.
units.tr: Judg. 13:18. Exod. 3:15. Exod. 15:3. Ps. 5:12. Ps. 116:4. Ps. 7:18. Deut. 16:2. 1 Kings 5:5. Deut. 18:19. 1 Sam. 17:45. Mic. 4:5. Matt. 28:19. Acts 21:13. Lightly, as in everyday speech, contrary to the rule of Christ: "Let your speech be, Yes, yes; no, no." Falsely, as in unlawful oaths and perjuries. Contumeliously, as in curses, blasphemies and incantations, by which the works of the devil are covered over with the name of God. The sense, therefore, is: "You shall not take up the name of your God rashly," that is, you shall not only not commit perjury, but you shall not make any mention of the divine name that is not honourable.

units.la: Praeceptum hoc negatiuum habet inclusum affirmatiuum. Sicut igitur prohibetur nominis diuini abusus: ita vice versa praecipitur legitimus & honorificus nominis diuini vsus, vt religiose, pie, sancte & honorifice nomine Dei vtamur, & in sermone nostro mentionem Dei & operum ac patefactionem eius non nisi honorificam & maiestate eius dignam faciamus. Proinde finis huius tertij praecepti est, vt Deo cultu immediatum externum, vera nominis ipsius confessione ac celebratione priuatim & publice omnes deferamus.
units.tr: This negative precept includes an affirmative one. Just as the abuse of the divine name is forbidden, so conversely the lawful and honourable use of it is commanded: that we use the name of God religiously, piously, holily and honourably, and that in our speech we make mention of God, of his works and of his revelation only in a manner that is honourable and worthy of his majesty. Accordingly, the aim of this third commandment is that we all render to God, privately and publicly, the immediate outward worship of true confession and celebration of his name.

units.la: Comminatio ideo est adiecta, vt ostendat Deus hanc etiam obedientiae partem ex iis esse, quorum violationem praecipue detestetur, & punire velit. Cum enim celebratio Dei sit vltimus & principalis finis, ad quem homo est conditus: merito id Deus exigit a nobis seuerissime, propter quod alia nobis praecipit: cumq; summum bonum sit in homine celebratio: consequitur summum malum esse, Deum afficere contumelia, ideoque summam poenam huic peccato deberi, secundum dicta: Quandoquidem Deum agnitum, non vt Deum glorificauerunt, propterea tradidit eos Deus in reprobam mentem. Homo qui maledixerit Deo suo, portabit scelus suum: & qui contumelia affecerit nomen Iehoua, morte moriatur.
units.tr: The threat is added so that God may show that this part of obedience is among those whose violation he especially detests and wishes to punish. For since the celebration of God is the ultimate and principal end for which man was created, God rightly requires this from us most strictly, and on account of this he commands us other things. And since the highest good in man is the celebration of God, it follows that the highest evil is to insult God, and therefore the highest punishment is owed to this sin, according to the words: "Since they knew God, they did not glorify him as God; therefore God gave them up to a reprobate mind." "Whoever curses his God shall bear his sin; and whoever insults the name of Jehovah shall surely die."

units.la: Virtutes huius praecepti consistunt in legitima atq; honorifica nominis diuini vsurpatione; cuius haec sunt partes:
units.tr: The virtues of this precept consist in the lawful and honourable use of the divine name, whose parts are these:

units.la: I. PROPAGATIO VERAE DOCTRINAE de Dei essentia, voluntate & operibus: non quidem illa, quae fit publico officio docendi in Ecclesia, & quarto praecepto sancitur: sed qua priuatim quisque suo loco tenetur alios erudire, & ad veram Dei agnitionem ac celebrationem adducere, secundum dicta: Doceas ea filios tuos, & filios filiorum. Adhortamini alij alios, & aedificate singuli singulos. Et tu conuersus confirma fratres tuos. Sermo Christi habitet in vobis copiose, cum omni sapientia, docendo & commonefaciendo vos mutuo psalmis, hymnis, & cantionibus spiritualibus.
units.tr: I. The propagation of true doctrine concerning the essence, will and works of God: not indeed that which is done by the public office of teaching in the Church, which is enjoined in the fourth commandment, but that by which each person, privately and in his own place, is bound to instruct others and to lead them to the true knowledge and celebration of God, according to the words: "Teach these things to your sons, and to the sons of your sons." "Exhort one another, and build up each other." "And you, when you have turned again, strengthen your brothers." "Let the word of Christ dwell in you richly, with all wisdom, teaching and admonishing one another with psalms, hymns and spiritual songs."

units.la: Huic repugnat 1. omissio siue neglectus occasionum & facultatis erudiendi alios & veram doctrinam propagandi: Timens abij & occultauit talentum tuum in terra, &c. 2. Ta2. Tædium, seu fuga colloquiorum de Deo & rebus diuinis. est ab impiis salus, quia statuta tua non inquirunt.
units.tr: Opposed to this are: 1. The omission or neglect of opportunities and of the means of instructing others and propagating true doctrine: "I was afraid, and went and hid your talent in the earth," etc. 2. Weariness of, or flight from, conversations about God and divine things: "Salvation is far from the wicked, for they do not seek your statutes."

units.la: 3. Corruptela religionis & doctrinæ cœlestis, quibus falsa dogmata de Deo, & ipsius voluntate, & operibus asseuerantur aut spargantur: Falsum vates vaticinantur eis in nomine meo.
units.tr: 3. The corruption of religion and of heavenly doctrine, by which false dogmas about God, and about his will and works, are asserted or spread abroad: "They prophesy a lie to you in my name."

units.la: II. PRÆDICATIO seu CELEBRATIO Dei, quæ est commemoratio proprietatum & operum diuinorum, coniuncta cum eorum approbatione & admiratione coram ipso Deo, & coram creaturis, eo fine, vt significemus approbationem nostram, & reuerentiam erga Deum, vt Deus supra omnia emineat, & nostra subiectio ostendatur, Narrabo nomen tuum fratribus meis, in medio congregationis laudabo te. Iehoua Dominus noster, quam admirabile est nomen tuum in vniuersa terra? Laudent eum cœli & terra, &c.
units.tr: II. The PREACHING or CELEBRATION of God, which is the recounting of the divine properties and works, joined with approval and admiration of them, before God himself and before creatures, with the aim that we may show our approval and reverence towards God, that God may be exalted above all things, and that our subjection may be displayed: "I will declare your name to my brothers; in the midst of the congregation I will praise you." "O Lord, our Lord, how excellent is your name in all the earth! Let heaven and earth praise him," etc.

units.la: Huic contraria sunt: 1. Contemtus & omissio celebrationis Dei, & operum diuinorum. Non vt Deum glorificarunt.
units.tr: The opposite of this is: 1. Contempt and neglect of the worship of God and of his works, not glorifying him as God.

units.la: 2. Blasphemia, quæ est, de Deo pugnantia cum ipsius natura & voluntate dicere, siue ex ignorantia, siue ex odio veritatis, & ipsius Dei: Quicunque maledixerit Iehoua Deo suo, portabit iniquitatem suam.
units.tr: 2. Blasphemy, which is saying things about God that are inconsistent with his nature and will, whether from ignorance or from hatred of the truth and of God himself: Whoever curses Jehovah his God shall bear his iniquity.

units.la: 3. Exsecratio seu imprecatio omnis: qua impia de Deo dicuntur contra proximum, & Deus quasi carnifex statuitur, ad exequendam hominum vindictæ cupiditatem. Est autem Exsecrari, alicui malaimprecari à Deo. Injusta est omnis exsecratio vel imprecatio, quæ fit ex odio & vindicta priuata in perniciem proximi: quia petitur, vt Deus sit exsecutor nostrorum affectuum, & praua rum cupiditatum. Occurrunt in psalmis, & alibi, quædam exsecrationes sanctorum aduersus hostes: sed hæ non simpliciter damnandæ sunt, quia magna ex parte sunt propheticæ denunciationes pœnarum aduersus hostes non resipiscentes. Earum exemplo licitæ aliquando esse possunt execrationes, sed cum his conditionibus: 1. Si mala imprecemur iis, quib. Deus ea denunciat, nempe hostib. Dei. 2. In causa Dei, sine priuato odio & cupiditate vindictæ. 3. Cum conditione, si sint insanabiles. 4. Sic tamen, ne exitio eorum lætemur, sed tantum gloriæ Dei vindicationem, & ecclesiæ liberationem expetamus.
units.tr: 3. Every kind of cursing or imprecation, by which impious things are said about God against a neighbour, and God is set up as an executioner to satisfy the desire of men for vengeance. To curse (exsecrari) is to call down evil on someone from God. Every curse or imprecation that arises from hatred and private vengeance, to the destruction of a neighbour, is unjust, because it asks that God be the executor of our passions and wicked desires. Some curses of the saints against enemies occur in the Psalms and elsewhere, but these are not simply to be condemned, since for the most part they are prophetic denunciations of punishments against enemies who do not repent. On their example, curses may sometimes be lawful, but under these conditions: 1. that we pray evil on those on whom God pronounces it, namely the enemies of God; 2. that it be in God's cause, without private hatred and desire for vengeance; 3. on the condition that they are incurable; 4. yet in such a way that we do not rejoice in their destruction, but seek only the vindication of God's glory and the deliverance of the Church.

units.la: III. CONFESSIO VERITATIS de Deo cognitæ: quæ est ostensio nostræ sententiæ de Deo, & eius voluntate, ex verbo Dei certo cognitæ, pro ratione officij nostri, ad illustrandam Dei gloriam, & promouendam aliorum salutem. Corde creditur ad iustitiam, & ore fit confessio ad salutem. Estote semper parati ad responsum cuilibet petenti rationem eius spei, quæ in vobis est, cum lenitate & reuerentia, &c. Huic aduersatur 1. Negatio veritatis, siue sententiæ suæ de religione, propter metum odij, aut crucis, aut ignominiæ. Hæc est duplex. Alia est vniuersalis defectio à vera religione, quæ est, professionem veritatis certò vel dubitanter cognitæ & acceptæ abijcere, destinato consilio, & toto affectu cordis repugnandi Deo, & sine dolore hanc abiectionem refugiente, & sine vllo propósito obediendi Deo in applicanda sibi promissione gratiæ & agenda pœnitentia. Hæc est negatio reproborum & hypocritarum, de qua dicitur: Ex nobis egressi sunt, quia ex nobis non erant. Nam si fuissent ex nobis, mansissent utique nobiscum. Ad temptus credunt, & tempore tentationis abscedunt. Ac si fiat post veritatem certò agnitam, est peccatum in Spiritum sanctum, ex quo nulli resipiscunt, ideo non remittitur, neque in hoc, neque in futuro seculo.
units.tr: III. CONFESSION OF THE TRUTH known about God: which is the declaration of our opinion about God and his will, known with certainty from the Word of God, according to the duty of our office, for illustrating God's glory and promoting the salvation of others. With the heart one believes unto righteousness, and with the mouth confession is made unto salvation. Be always ready to give an answer to everyone who asks you for a reason for the hope that is in you, with gentleness and reverence, etc. Opposed to this is 1. denial of the truth, or of one's opinion about religion, out of fear of hatred, or of the cross, or of disgrace. This is of two kinds. One is total apostasy from true religion, which is to cast off the profession of a truth known and accepted, whether certainly or doubtfully, with settled purpose and with the whole affection of the heart resisting God, fleeing this rejection without grief, and with no intention of obeying God by applying to oneself the promise of grace and performing repentance. This is the denial of the reprobate and hypocrites, of whom it is said: They went out from us, but they were not of us; for if they had been of us, they would have remained with us. They believe for a while, and in time of temptation they fall away. And if it happens after the truth has been certainly recognised, it is the sin against the Holy Spirit, from which no one repents, and therefore it is not forgiven, either in this age or in the age to come.

units.la: Alia est particularis negatio infirmiorum, quæ fit ex errore non affectato, aut ex metu crucis manente in corde, inclinatione & dolore illam infirmitatem & negationem auersante, & aliquo proposito ex ea eluctandi & assentiendi atq; obtemperandi Deo, applicandi sibi promissionem gratiæ, & agendi pœnitentiam. In hanc labi possunt etiam electi & renati, sed ex ea eluctantur & redeunt ad confessionem in hac vita: vt Petrus ter negat Christum ex infirmitate, sed resipiscit.
units.tr: Another is particular denial by the weak, which happens through error not deliberately chosen, or through fear of the cross that remains in the heart, with an inclination and grief turning away from that weakness and denial, and with some purpose of struggling out of it, of assenting to and obeying God, applying to oneself the promise of grace, and performing repentance. The elect and the reborn may also fall into this, but they struggle out of it and return to confession in this life, as Peter, who denied Christ three times out of weakness, repented.

units.la: 2. Dissimulatio veritatis, vbi gloria Dei, & salus proximi constitutionem postulat. Tum autem postulat, cum falsæ opinionés de Deo, de ipsius verbo, aut de ecclesia in animis nostro silentio confirmari videntur: aut ea manent occulta, quæ ad vindicandam Dei gloriam ab obtrectationibus impiorum, ad conuincendos pertinaces, & erudiendos dociles, vult Deus esse nota: aut silentium nos de approbatione malorum suspicios facit. Sic dissimulabant veritatem parentes cæci, & primores illi, nolentes Christum confiteri metu Judæorum, ne fierent ἀποσυνάγωγοι.
units.tr: 2. Dissembling of the truth, where the glory of God and the salvation of a neighbour require confession. It requires it when false opinions about God, his Word, or the Church seem to be confirmed in men's minds by our silence; or when things remain hidden which God wills to be known, for vindicating his glory against the slanders of the impious, for convicting the obstinate and instructing the teachable; or when our silence makes us seem to approve of evil. Thus the parents of the blind man dissembled the truth, and those leaders who would not confess Christ for fear of the Jews, lest they be made excommunicated [ἀποσυνάγωγοι].

units.la: 3. Abusus libertatis Christianæ, seu scandalum datum in rebus adiaphoris: quod est, vsu adiaphororum errores in animis aduersariorum confirmare, aut eos à vera religione abalienare, aut exemplo ad mutationem cum mala conscientia coinuitam prouocare, de quo prolixè agit Apostolus Rom. 14, 1. & 1 Cor. 8. & 10.
units.tr: 3. Abuse of Christian liberty, or scandal given in matters indifferent: that is, using indifferent things to confirm errors in the minds of opponents, or to alienate them from true religion, or by example to provoke a change made with an evil conscience. The Apostle treats of this at length in Rom. 14:1 and 1 Cor. 8 and 10.

units.la: 4. Omnia scandala in moribus: cum videlicet ij, qui veram religionem profitentur, vitam flagitiosam agunt, fidem, quam verbis profitentur, actis negantes, & ecclesiam calumniis, Dei nomen blasphemiis infidelium exponentes. Deum profitentur se scire, sed factis negant: quasi dicat; sine fide de Deo garriunt. Dei nomen
units.tr: 4. All scandals in conduct: namely, when those who profess the true religion live a shameful life, denying by their deeds the faith they profess in words, and exposing the Church to slanders and the name of God to blasphemies by unbelievers. They profess that they know God, but by their works they deny him: as if to say, they chatter about God without faith. The name of God
1 John 2:19. Luke 8:13.

units.la: Tit. 1, 16. nomen propter vos blasphematur inter gentes. Vide Psalmo 50, 17. Esa.52.3. 2 Tim.3,5.1.
units.tr: Titus 1:16. The name of God is blasphemed among the Gentiles because of you (Rom. 2:24). See Psalm 50:17; Isa. 52:3; 2 Tim. 3:5, 1.

units.la: 5. Confessio intempestiua, qua sine gloriæ Dei illustratione, & salutis cuiusquam promotione, & sine vocationis siue officij faciendi necessitate irritatur vel derisio, & exagitatio veritatis, vel sævitia hostium aduersus pios. Hæc prohibetur à Christo: Ne date, quod sanctum est, canibus, &c. Et à Paulo: Hæreticum hominem post unam & alteram admonitionem reijce, vt qui noris euersum esse eum, qui sit eiusmodi, & peccare, suopte judicio condemnatum.
units.tr: 5. Ill-timed confession, by which, without any illustration of God's glory or promotion of anyone's salvation, and without any necessity arising from one's calling or office, the truth is provoked to ridicule and abuse, or the enemies' cruelty against the pious is roused. This is forbidden by Christ: Do not give what is holy to dogs, etc. And by Paul: Reject a heretical man after one or two admonitions, knowing that such a man is perverted and sins, being condemned by his own judgment.

units.la: Obiectio. Petrus vult nos semper paratos esse, ad respondendum omni petenti rationem eius spei, quæ in nobis est. Ergo nulla confessio potest esse intempestiua. Resp. Petrus jubet nos semper esse paratos, hoc est, instructos & promptos, ad respondendum de summa & fundamentis doctrinæ, & ad repellendas obtrectationes & calumnias, quibus deformatur doctrina Euangelij ab aduersariis. Non autem jubet semper, & apud quosuis omnia expromere, aut profiteri, sed apud omnes rationem, seu defensionem fidei nostræ postulantes, nempe discendi, vel cognoscendi, vel judicandi causa: non autem apud deridentes aut conuitiantes: postquam doctrina satis expositæ est, & confirmata. Sic ipse Christus, postquam satis confessus esset, & confirmassetsuam doctrinam, pontificibus & Pilato respondere noluit.
units.tr: Objection. Peter wants us always to be ready to answer everyone who asks a reason for the hope that is in us; therefore no confession can be ill-timed. Answer: Peter bids us always to be ready, that is, instructed and prompt, to answer concerning the sum and foundations of doctrine, and to repel the slanders and calumnies by which adversaries disfigure the doctrine of the Gospel. But he does not bid us always and before anyone at all to set forth or profess everything, but before all who ask for a reason or defence of our faith, namely for the sake of learning, knowing, or judging; not before those who mock or revile, once the doctrine has been sufficiently expounded and confirmed. So Christ himself, after he had sufficiently confessed and confirmed his doctrine, refused to answer the high priests and Pilate.

units.la: IV. Gratiarum actio: quæ est, cognoscere, & fateri, quæ, & quanta beneficia à Deo acceperimus, & ad quam obedientiam erga DEVM pro illis obligati ad parendum simus, ideoque velle illi ex animo obedientiam præstare, quoad possumus. De hac dicitur: Quicquid egeritis sermone aut facto, in nomine Domini Iesu facite, gratias agentes Deo, & Patri per eum. In omnibus gratias agite: hæc enim est voluntas Dei per Christum Iesum erga vos. Confitemini Domino, quoniam bonus, quoniam in seculum misericordia eius.
units.tr: IV. Thanksgiving: which is to acknowledge and confess what and how great benefits we have received from God, and to what obedience towards God we are bound for them, and therefore to wish from the heart to render him obedience as far as we can. Of this it is said: Whatever you do in word or deed, do all in the name of the Lord Jesus, giving thanks to God the Father through him. In all things give thanks; for this is the will of God in Christ Jesus toward you. Confess to the Lord, for he is good, for his mercy endures for ever.

units.la: Huic contraria est, 1. omissio gratiarum actionis, quæ vel raro, vel nunquam cogitat, & celebrat beneficia Dei, aut frigidè, & simulatè, hoc est, ita, vt non accendatur dilectio Dei, & desiderium præstandi gratitudinem erga Deum: Deum cognouerunt, sed non vt Deum glorificauerunt, neq; gratias ei egerunt.
units.tr: Opposed to this is 1. the omission of thanksgiving, which rarely or never thinks about and celebrates God's benefits, or does so coldly and insincerely, that is, in such a way that love of God and desire to render gratitude to God is not kindled. They knew God, but did not glorify him as God, nor give thanks to him.

units.la: 2. Beneficiorum Dei negatio, & extenuatio: vel seipsum, aut alios eorum autores fingere. Quid habes, quod non accepisti? quod si accepisti, quid gloriaris, vt qui non acceperis?
units.tr: 2. Denial and belittling of God's benefits, or claiming them for oneself or for others as their authors. What have you that you did not receive? And if you received it, why do you boast, as if you had not received it?

units.la: 3. Neglectus donorum DEI, quando non ad gloriam DEI: vel abusus, quando ad ignominiam DEI conferuntur. Serue male & cunctator, oportuit te committere pecuniam meam nummulariis, &c.
units.tr: 3. Neglect of God's gifts, when they are not directed to God's glory; or abuse, when they are turned to God's dishonour. Wicked and slothful servant, you ought to have committed my money to the bankers, etc. (Matt. 25.)

units.la: V. Zelus gloriæ Dei, qui est ardens amor Dei, & dolor propter contumeliam aut contemptum Dei, & conatus suo loco hunc prohibendi. Pinehas auertit furorem meum a filiis Israel, cum zelatus est ipse zelum meum in medio eorum. Zelando zelatus sum pro Iehoua Deo exercituum. Derelinquunt enim pactum tuum filij Israel. De hoc zelo quæst.catech. 110.
units.tr: V. Zeal for God's glory, which is ardent love of God, and grief at the reproach or contempt of God, and an effort to prevent it in its proper place. Phinehas turned away my wrath from the children of Israel, when he was zealous with my zeal among them. I have been zealous for Jehovah God of hosts with zeal; for the children of Israel have forsaken your covenant. On this zeal, see the Catechism, question 110.

units.la: Zelo Dei repugnat in defectu lenitas, non curans Dei gloriam, vel zelum dissimulans, quæ est, vel non affici dolore propter contumeliam Dei, vel non habere, vel non ostendere dictis & factis studium, eam pro sui officij ratione prohibendi. In hoc vitium incurrunt, qui non prohibent, cum possint, deierationes & blasphemias nominis diuini, quia non ducuntur zelo gloriæ Dei. In excessu repugnat zelus errans, quem Paulus vocat zelum Dei non secundum scientiam: qui est irasci dictis aut factis, quibus gloria Dei lædi falso existimatur. Hoc autem fit, cum vel id, quod gloria Dei non est, nec defendi debet, existimamus esse gloriam Dei, ac defendere conamur: vel id, quod non est gloriæ Dei læsionem, nec debet depelli, arbitramur esse læsionem Dei, & depellere studemus. Item, cum vel gloria Dei aliter defenditur, quàm defendi debet: vel cum gloriæ Dei læsio aliter propulsatur, quàm propulsari debet.
units.tr: Lenity in defect is opposed to the zeal of God, when a person does not care for God's glory or conceals his zeal. This happens either when he is not moved by grief at an insult to God, or when he has no eagerness, and shows none by word or deed, to prevent it in keeping with his office. Those fall into this vice who do not prevent oaths and blasphemies of the divine name when they can, because they are not led by zeal for God's glory. In excess is opposed the erring zeal, which Paul calls "zeal of God not according to knowledge." This is to be angry at words or deeds by which God's glory is falsely thought to be injured. This happens when we think that something which is not God's glory and ought not to be defended is God's glory, and we try to defend it; or when we judge that something which does not injure God's glory and ought not to be repelled is an injury to God, and we are eager to repel it. Likewise it happens when God's glory is defended otherwise than it ought to be defended, or when an injury to God's glory is repelled otherwise than it ought to be repelled.

units.la: VI. Invocatio seu Precatio, quæ est petitio à vero Deo illorum bonorum, quæ Deus à se peti iussit, profecta ex vero sensu necessitatis nostræ, & desiderio beneficentiæ diuinæ, facta in vera ad Deum conuersione, & fiducia promissionum diuinarum, propter mediatorem. Confitemini Domino, invocate nomen eius. Petite, & dabitur vobis. Hæc est fiducia, quam apud Deum habemus: ipsum, si quid petierimus secundum voluntatem eius, audire.
units.tr: VI. Invocation, or prayer, is a petition made to the true God for those good things which God has commanded us to ask of him. It proceeds from a true sense of our need and a desire for divine kindness, is made in a true conversion to God, and rests on trust in the divine promises, through the mediator. Confess to the Lord, call upon his name. Ask, and it will be given you. This is the confidence we have toward God: that if we ask anything according to his will, he hears us.

units.la: Huic repugnat, 1. Neglectus siue omissio invocationis, quæ tantum non totius impietatis fons reprehenditur: Dominum non invocant, Psalm.144.
units.tr: This is opposed by: (1) neglect or omission of invocation, which is rebuked as nearly the source of all impiety: They do not call upon the Lord, Ps. 144.

units.la: 2. Invocatio omnis illegitima, in qua nimirum desideratur aliqua conditio ex iis, quæ ad legitimam invocationem requiruntur: vt, invocatio idololatrica, quæ vel ad commentitia numina, vel ad creaturas dirigitur: vel exauditionem & præsentiam diuinam ad locum, vel rem certam alligat, sine verbo, hoc est, sine mandato, & promissione diuina. Talis est invocatio Ethnicorum, Turcarum, Judæorum, & omnium, qui aliud numen præter patefactum Deum sibi fingunt: Vos nescitis quid adoretis. Item eorum, qui angelos, vel mortuos sansanctos inuocant in papatu, & his tribuunt honorem soli Deo debitum.
units.tr: (2) Any illegitimate invocation, in which some condition is lacking from those required for lawful invocation. Such is idolatrous invocation, which is directed either to fictitious deities or to creatures, or which ties God's hearing and presence to a place or a particular thing, without the word, that is, without the divine command and promise. Such is the invocation of the heathen, the Turks, the Jews, and of all who make for themselves some deity other than the revealed God: You do not know what you worship. Likewise it is the invocation of those in the papacy who call upon angels or dead saints and give to them the honour due to God alone.

units.la: 3. Petitio earum rerum à Deo, quae diuinae voluntati ac legi repugnant: Petitis & non accipitis, eo quod male petitis, vt in voluptates vestras insumatis.
units.tr: (3) Petition for things that are opposed to the divine will and law: You ask and do not receive, because you ask amiss, that you may spend it on your pleasures.

units.la: 4. Battologia, seu preces conceptae sine vero cordis affectu & desiderio diuinae beneficentiae, tantum verbis aut gestu corporis, vel sine vera poenitentia, sine fiducia exauditionis, sine subiectione voluntatis nostrae erga Deum, sine cogitatione diuinarum promissionum, sine fiducia solius mediatoris Christi, & agnitione indignitatis nostrae. Precantes ne sitis loquaces, vt ethnici, putant enim fieri, vt sua illa loquacitate exaudiantur. Cum exaudiam etiam cum multiplicabitis orationem, non exaudiam. Non igitur existimet homo ille, se accepturum esse quicquam à Domino.
units.tr: (4) Battology, or prayers offered without true affection of heart and desire for divine kindness, only with words or bodily gesture; or without true repentance, without confidence of being heard, without submission of our will to God, without thought of the divine promises, without trust in Christ alone as mediator, and without acknowledgment of our unworthiness. When you pray, do not be babblers, as the heathen are, for they think they will be heard for their much speaking. Though you multiply prayer, I will not hear. Therefore let not that man think that he will receive anything from the Lord.

units.la: Pro inuocatione sanctorum obiectiones Papistarum.
units.tr: The objections of the Papists against the invocation of saints.

units.la: Obiect. 1. Sancti propter virtutes & dona sua sunt venerandi cultu vel λατρείας vel δουλείας: sed non cultu λατρείας. Hic enim soli Deo debetur, vtpote tribuens ei, cui defertur, vniuersalem potentiam, prouidentiam & dominium. Ergo sanctis debetur δουλεία, hoc est, talis veneratio, qua sanctos propter ipsorum sanctitatem veneremur. Resp. 1. Negatur consequentia: quia in maiore non est sufficiens enumeratio. Nam praeter cultum λατρείας & δουλείας, vt quidem illi distinguunt, alia est veneratio nis species sanctis conueniens, nempe agnitio & celebratio fidei, sanctitatis & donorum, quibus excelluerunt, obedientia doctrinae, denique imitatio vitae, & pietatis ipsorum, de qua Augustinus: Honorandi (inquit) sunt propter imitationem, non propter adorationem. Haec veneratio debetur sanctis, quam nos nec viuis nec mortuis sanctis detrahimus, iuxta praeceptum apostoli: Memores estote ducum vestrorum, qui loquuti sunt vobis sermonem Dei, quorum imitamini fidem, considerantes qui fuerit exitus conuersationis ipsorum. 2. Negatur maior, quia cultus λατρείας & δουλείας non est diuersus, sed vnus & idem, non sanctis vel creaturis vllo loco & tempore conueniens, nempe, quod intelligat & exaudiat cogitationes, & gemitus, & vota invocantium, & eorum necessitatibus succurrat. Invocantes exaudire non nisi solus Deus potest: proinde soli Deo hic cultus debet, quod invocantes exaudiat: sicut & soli Christo hic honor conuenit, quod propter ipsius meritum & intercessionem nobis à Deo detur remissio peccatorum, vita aeterna, & alia bona. na. Ad sanctos ergo non sine manifesto sacrilegio & idololatria transferri potest, siue δελείας, siue λατρείας, siue quocunque alio nomine appelletur.
units.tr: Objection 1. The saints, on account of their virtues and gifts, are to be venerated with the worship of latreia [λατρεία] or of douleia [δουλεία]. But not with the worship of latreia, for this is due to God alone, since it ascribes to him to whom it is paid universal power, providence and dominion. Therefore the saints are owed douleia, that is, such veneration by which we honour the saints on account of their holiness. Answer: (1) The consequence is denied, because the enumeration in the major premise is not sufficient. For besides the worship of latreia and douleia, as they distinguish them, there is another kind of veneration fitting for saints: namely, the acknowledgment and celebration of the faith, holiness and gifts in which they excelled, obedience to their teaching, and finally imitation of their life and piety. Augustine says of this: They are to be honoured, he says, on account of imitation, not on account of adoration. This veneration is due to the saints, and we do not withhold it from the saints, living or dead, according to the apostle's precept: Remember your leaders, who spoke the word of God to you, whose faith imitate, considering the outcome of their conduct. (2) The major is denied, because the worship of latreia and douleia is not different but one and the same. It is fitting for no saint or creature at any place or time, namely that he understands and hears the thoughts, groans and vows of those who invoke him, and succours their necessities. Only God can hear those who invoke him; therefore this worship is due to God alone, because he hears those who call upon him. Just as honour belongs to Christ alone, that on account of his merit and intercession remission of sins, eternal life and other goods are given to us by God. Therefore it cannot be transferred to the saints without manifest sacrilege and idolatry, whatever name it is called by, whether douleia, latreia, or anything else.

units.la: Est autem distinctio hæc admodum friuola: quia λατρεύω & δελεύειν, λατρεύς & δοῦλος, λατρεία & δουλεία, tam in scriptura, quam in profanis scriptoribus, promiscuè idem significant. De Deo dicitur: Dominum Deum tuum adorabis, & illi soli seruies, Non potestis Deo & mammonæ seruire, δουλεύειν λατρεύσεις. Et: Non potestis Deo & mammonæ seruire, Item: Vt seruiretis Deo viuo & vero, δουλεύειν Θεῷ ζῶντι. De Christo: Qui eiusmodi sunt, Domino nostro Iesu Christo non seruiunt: οὐ δουλεύουσιν. Et Paulus passim se vocat δοῦλον Θεοῦ.
units.tr: This distinction, however, is quite frivolous, because latreuō [λατρεύω] and douleuein [δουλεύειν], latreus [λατρεύς] and doulos [δοῦλος], latreia [λατρεία] and douleia [δουλεία], both in Scripture and in profane writers, mean the same thing indiscriminately. Of God it is said: You shall worship the Lord your God and serve him alone [λατρεύσεις, δουλεύειν]. And: You cannot serve God and mammon; and: That you may serve the living and true God [δουλεύειν Θεῷ ζῶντι]. Of Christ: Those who are such do not serve our Lord Jesus Christ [οὐ δουλεύουσιν]. And Paul everywhere calls himself servant of God [δοῦλον Θεοῦ].

units.la: In Græco Bibliorum textu, opus seruile passim vocatur λατρευτόν. Suidas λατρεύειν scribit idem esse, quod mercede seruire. Valla ostendit, λατρεύειν esse tam hominibus, quàm Deo seruire, adducens locum ex Xenophonte, vbi maritus dicit, se paratum esse vita redimere, ne vxor cuiquam λατρεύῃ, seruiat. Et vicissim vxor dicit, se vita redimere velle, ne maritus δουλεύῃ, seruiat. Non magis igitur λατρεία & δουλεία differunt, quàm gladius & ensis.
units.tr: In the Greek text of the Bible, servile work is everywhere called latreuton [λατρευτόν]. Suidas writes that latreuein [λατρεύειν] means the same as to serve for wages. Valla shows that latreuein means to serve men as much as to serve God, adducing a passage from Xenophon, where a husband says he is ready to redeem with his life that his wife should not serve anyone [λατρεύῃ]. And conversely the wife says she is willing to redeem with her life that her husband should not serve [δουλεύῃ]. Therefore latreia and douleia differ no more than gladius and ensis (sword and blade).

units.la: Obiect. 1. Quos Deus honorat, etiam nos debemus honorare. Sanctos Deus honorat: Sedebitis super duodecim sedia, &c. Ergo etiam à nobis sunt honorandi. Resp. Concedimus de honore, quem Deus ipsis tribuit. In eo autem nusquam inuocatio nomen, & gloriam tatur, sed de hac dicitur: Ego Iehoua, hoc est nomen meum, & gloriam meam alteri non dabo, nec laudem meam idolis.
units.tr: Objection 1. Those whom God honours, we too ought to honour. God honours the saints: You shall sit upon twelve thrones, etc. Therefore they too are to be honoured by us. Answer: We grant this regarding the honour which God gives them. But in that honour the invocation of the name and the glory are nowhere transferred. Of this it is said: I am the Lord, that is my name, and I will not give my glory to another, nor my praise to idols.

units.la: Obiect. 3. Sanctis exauditio arcanorum gemituum communicatur per gratiam, quam Deus habet per naturam. Ergo sunt inuocandi. Resp. Negatur antecedens. Deus enim proprietates illas, per quas vult à creaturis discerni, vt immensitatem, omnipotentiam, infinitam sapientiam, inspectionem cordium, ac proinde exauditionem inuocantium, neque per naturam, neque per gratiam vlli creaturæ communicat. Tu nouisti solus cor omnium hominum.
units.tr: Objection 3. The hearing of secret groans is communicated to the saints through grace, which God has by nature. Therefore they are to be invoked. Answer: The antecedent is denied. For God does not communicate to any creature, either by nature or by grace, those properties by which he wills to be distinguished from creatures, such as immensity, omnipotence, infinite wisdom, the inspection of hearts, and consequently the hearing of those who invoke him. You alone know the hearts of all men.

units.la: Obiect. 4. Deus communicauit sanctis facultatem edendi miracula, quæ tamen proprietas est solius Dei. Ergo aliquas proprietates suas, quibus à creaturis discernitur, sanctis communicat, ac proinde etiam notitiam, agnitionem, & affectum inuocantium. R.1. Negatur consequentia à genere particulariter ad certam speciem. 2. Neq; valet ratio: quia miraculorum notitia, nec præditi sunt sancti: ideo eos etiam pollere affectuum notitia. Non enim transfunditur in sanctos vis edendi miracula: neque propria virtute, sed vt ministri miracula faciunt sancti. Proinde dicuntur ea facere μιπωνυμικῶς, cum eos Deus tanquam ministros. stros suæ præsentiæ, potentiæ, & voluntatis suæ signum ad miraculi effectionem adhibet.
units.tr: Objection 4. God has communicated to the saints the faculty of working miracles, which nevertheless is a property of God alone. Therefore he communicates to them some of his properties by which he is distinguished from creatures, and consequently also knowledge, acknowledgment and affection of those who invoke. Answer: (1) The consequence is denied, as it moves from a genus, in particular, to a certain species. (2) Nor does the reasoning hold. The saints are not endowed with knowledge of miracles, therefore they are also endowed with knowledge of affections: for the power of working miracles is not transfused into the saints, nor do they work miracles by their own virtue, but as ministers. Therefore they are said to do them metonymically [μετωνυμικῶς], since God uses the saints as ministers, as signs of his presence, power and will, in bringing about the miracle.

units.la: Obiect. 5. Prophetæ aliqui viderunt cogitationes & consilia aliorum: vt Abias cogitationes vxoris Ieroboami, Elisæus regis Syriæ cogitationes: Petrus cogitationes Ananiæ & Sapphiræ. Ergo sanctis communicatur à Deo cordium cognitio. Respond. Exempla pauca extraordinaria non constituunt regulam. 1. Sciebant illi hæc ex dono prophetiæ: nec tamen sciebant semper, sed tantum eo tempore, quo id postulabat vtilitas ecclesiæ: nec ex aliqua sibi indita facultate intuendi corda & animos, sed ex reuelatione diuina: nec omnia, sed tantum ea, quæ ipsis Deus reuelare voluit. Hinc vero non sequitur, sanctos etiam post mortem dono prophetiæ præditos esse, cum eo non sit opus in vita æterna.
units.tr: Objection 5. Some prophets saw the thoughts and counsels of others: Abijah saw the thoughts of Jeroboam's wife, Elisha the thoughts of the king of Syria, and Peter the thoughts of Ananias and Sapphira. Therefore God communicates knowledge of hearts to the saints. Answer: A few extraordinary examples do not establish a rule. (1) They knew these things through the gift of prophecy, and not always, but only at the time when the usefulness of the Church required it. They did not know them by any faculty implanted in them for seeing hearts and minds, but by divine revelation, and not everything, but only what God chose to reveal to them. It does not follow from this that the saints, even after death, are endowed with the gift of prophecy, since there is no need of it in eternal life.

units.la: Obiect. 6. Angeli in cœlis lætantur de resipiscentia peccatorum. Ergo vident pœnitentiam in cordibus hominum, & desiderantium inuocantium. Resp. Male colligitur causa ex effectu, qui potest ex aliis causis existere. Non necesse est, angelos pœnitentiam peccatorum scire per inspectionem cordium, cum possint eam vel ex effectibus & signis, vel ex diuina patefactione cognoscere.
units.tr: Objection 6. The angels in heaven rejoice over the repentance of sinners. Therefore they see repentance in the hearts of men, and of those who desire and call upon God. Answer: The cause is badly inferred from the effect, which can exist from other causes. It is not necessary for the angels to know the repentance of sinners by inspecting hearts, since they can know it either from effects and signs, or from divine disclosure.

units.la: Obiect. 7. Anima Epulonis ex inferno vidit in cælo, & inuocauit Abrahamum, quam & Abrahamus exaudiuit, & Epulo sciebat statum quinque fratrum in hac vita. Ergo sancti in cælo viventes statum & vota versantium in terra, & sunt inuocandi. Resp. Ex allegoriis & parabolis non possunt constitui dogmata.
