There was a particular reason for the sabbath, which was commanded not through Moses but from the beginning, and therefore bound all people up to the Messiah; although this precept had so fallen into disuse among other nations that they counted it among the chief reproaches with which they mocked and harassed the Jews, calling them sabbatarians, because they kept the sabbath too scrupulously.

units.la: Ad tertiam responderetur, sabbatum infidelibus non fuisse sacramentum, etiamsi cum fidelibus à labore quiescerent: quia nec ad illos pertinebat promissio, quod Iehoua esset sanctificator ipsorum, nec ad huius promissionis testificationem aut professionem, sed tantum ad scandalum & occasionem peccandi, quæ populo Dei per ipsos dari poterat, cavendam, cessare ab vsitatis operibus cogebantur.
units.tr: To the third objection it may be answered that the sabbath was not a sacrament for unbelievers, even though they rested from labour together with the believers. For the promise, that Jehovah would be their sanctifier, did not pertain to them, nor was it a testimony to or profession of this promise; they were compelled to cease from their customary works only to avoid the scandal and the occasion of sinning that they might otherwise give to the people of God.

units.la: Neque iumentum tuum.] Hinc magis intelligitur, sabbatum non fuisse sacramentum infidelibus, quia etiam iumenta quiescere iubentur, quorum quies, neque cultus Dei, neque sacramentum est, sed propter homines erat mandata. 1. Vt ipsis laborandi occasio præcideretur, interdicto iumentorum labore, seu vsu. 2. Vt etiam brutis animalibus parcentes discerent, quantum Deus clementiæ & æquitatis erga homines rationem haberi vellet.
units.tr: Nor your beast.] From this it is understood more clearly that the sabbath was not a sacrament for unbelievers, because even the beasts of burden are commanded to rest. Their rest is neither the worship of God nor a sacrament, but was commanded on account of men. (1) So that the occasion for labour would be taken away from them, by forbidding the labour, or use, of the beasts. (2) So that also, by sparing the brute animals, they might learn how much God wishes mercy and fairness toward men to be taken into account.

units.la: Nam sex diebus fecit Deus] Ratio præcepti à quiete Dei, pertinet ad partem præcepti cæremonialem de septimo die, vt prius dictum est.
units.tr: For in six days God made] The reason for the precept, drawn from the rest of God, belongs to the ceremonial part of the precept concerning the seventh day, as was said earlier.

units.la: Quievit die septimo] hoc est, Deus desiit nouas mundi partes creare: vt qui iam esset absolutus, & talis, qualem esse volebat. Eam diem dedicauit cultui diuino. 1. Vt hæc diei septimi quies esset monimentum perfectæ & absolutæ à Deo creationis: continuatæ autem eo die perpetuæ conseruationis & gubernationis operum suorum, ad suam gloriam, & electorum salutem: ac proinde stimulus ad considerationem ac celebrationem horum operum & beneficiorum Dei erga genus humanum, propter quod omnes aliæ res sunt conditæ, & conseruantur à Deo. 2. Vt suæ imitationem sui hortaretur in operibus consuetis sex dierum septimo die intermittendis. Est autem duplex quietis diuina imitatio: cæremonialis & moralis: vt supra est dictum. Sic & opera nostra, à quibus cessare iubemur, duplicia sunt: alia sunt præcepta quiquidem à Deo, sed non facienda cum impedimento cultus Dei, vt sunt labores vocationis nostræ proprij: alia prohibita à Deo, vt peccata. Vtraq; prohibentur sabbato, sed triplici prohibitionis discrimine: 1. Labores prohibentur secundum quid, quatenus impediunt ministerium, vel præbent scandalum: peccata verò simpliciter. 2. Labores omitti jubentur tantum die sabbati: peccata omni tempore. 3. Laborum omissio est typus: omissio verò peccatorum res per typum illum significata.
units.tr: He rested on the seventh day] that is, God ceased to create new parts of the world, since he was now complete and was such as he wished to be. He dedicated that day to divine worship. (1) That this rest of the seventh day might be a memorial of the perfect and finished creation by God; and, since on that day his works were continually preserved and governed, a memorial of his perpetual preservation and government, for his own glory and the salvation of the elect. And so it is a spur to the consideration and celebration of these works and of God's benefits toward the human race, for the sake of which all other things were created and are preserved by God. (2) That he might urge them to imitate him, by setting aside their customary works on the seventh day of the six days. Now there is a twofold imitation of the divine rest: ceremonial and moral, as was said above. Likewise our works, from which we are commanded to cease, are of two kinds: some are commanded by God, yet not to be done to the hindrance of the worship of God, such as the labours of our own calling; others are forbidden by God, such as sins. Both are forbidden on the sabbath, but with a threefold distinction of prohibition: (1) Labours are forbidden in a certain respect, insofar as they hinder the ministry or give offence; but sins absolutely. (2) The omission of labours is commanded only on the day of the sabbath; sins at all times. (3) The omission of labour is a type; but the omission of sins is the thing signified by that type.

units.la: DE SABBATO.
units.tr: DE SABBATO.

units.la: Explicatis præcepti verbis, vt doctrina de sabbato, & vera eius sanctificatione, rectius intelligatur, considerandum est porrò de sabbato: I. Quid sit sabbatum, & quotuplex. II. Qua ratione ad nos pertineat. III. Quare sit institutum. IV. Quomodo seruetur, & violetur sabbatum.
units.tr: Having explained the words of the commandment, so that the doctrine of the Sabbath and its true sanctification may be understood more correctly, we must next consider the Sabbath: I. What the Sabbath is, and how many kinds there are. II. In what way it pertains to us. III. Why it was instituted. IV. How the Sabbath is kept and how it is violated.

units.la: I. Quid sit sabbatum, & quotuplex.
units.tr: I. What the Sabbath is, and how many kinds there are.

units.la: Sabbatum Hebraeis est schabbat, schebbet, & schabbaton, hoc est, cessatio, quies, seu vacatio à labore. Sic Deus appellauit diem cultui suo publico dicatum. 1. Quia Deus ipse eo die requieuit à creatione nouarum specierum: licet non ab earum conseruatione, & propagatione, per continuam indiuiduorum generationem. 2. Quia sabbatum est imago requiei spiritualis à peccatis, & futurae in vita æterna. 3. Quia & nos eo die vacare debemus ab operibus œconomicis, politicis, & aliis eiusmodi: 4. Quia etiam familiæ & jumenta nostra debent quiescere. Est igitur sabbatum temporaliter dicatum cessationi ab operibus externis, seu moraliter, seu cæremonialiter prohibitis, hoc est, à peccatis, & laboribus vocationis, ad vsum huius vitæ pertinentibus, & exsecutioni earum rerum, quæ ad cultum Dei pertinent.
units.tr: Among the Hebrews the Sabbath is shabbat, shebbet, and shabbaton, that is, cessation, rest, or abstinence from labour. God called by this name the day dedicated to his public worship. (1) Because God himself rested on that day from the creation of new kinds of things, though not from their preservation and propagation through the continual generation of individuals. (2) Because the Sabbath is an image of spiritual rest from sins, and of the rest that is to come in eternal life. (3) Because we too ought to abstain on that day from economic, political and similar works. (4) Because our households and our beasts of burden also ought to rest. The sabbath is therefore a time set apart for ceasing from external works forbidden either morally or ceremonially, that is, from sins and from the labours of one's calling which pertain to the use of this life, and set apart for the performance of those things which pertain to the worship of God.

units.la: Est autem duplex sabbatum: aliud morale, & internum, seu spirituale, est studium agnitionis Dei, & operum eius, vitandi peccata, celebrandi Deum confessione & obedientia. Breviter: Est cessatio à peccatis, & exercitatio operum Dei. Hoc sabbatum licet continuum & perpetuum esse debeat in conuersis: tamen in hac vita tantùm inchoatur: & nominatur sabbatum, tum quia hæc demum vera est quies à laboribus & miseriis, & nostri ad colendum Deum consecratio: tum quia cæremoniali sabbato olim significacabatur. Sabbata mea dedi eis in signum, vt scirent, quod sim Iehoua, sanctificans eos. Perfectè autem, & perpetuo continuabitur hoc spirituale sabbatum in vita æterna, in qua erit perpetua Dei celebratio, omnibus illis relictis, & omissis, quibus nunc occupamur: Et erit, vt de mense in mensem, & de sabbato in Sabbatum eius veniat omnis caro, vt incurvet se coram me.
units.tr: There is, however, a twofold sabbath. The one is moral and internal, or spiritual: it is the zeal to know God and his works, to avoid sins, and to honour God by confession and obedience. In brief: it is a cessation from sins and a practice of the works of God. This sabbath ought to be continual and perpetual in the converted, yet in this life it is only begun; and it is called a sabbath both because this alone is the true rest from labours and miseries, and the dedication of ourselves to the worship of God, and because it was formerly signified by the ceremonial sabbath: I gave them my sabbaths as a sign, that they might know that I am the LORD who sanctifies them (Ezek. 20). But this spiritual sabbath will be carried on perfectly and perpetually in eternal life, in which there will be perpetual celebration of God, with all those things set aside and laid down with which we are now occupied: And it shall come to pass that from new moon to new moon, and from sabbath to sabbath, all flesh shall come to bow down before me (Isa. 66).

units.la: Cæremoniale seu externum sabbatum, est certum tempus, destinatum in ecclesia ministerio verbi, & administrationi sacramentorum, seu publico cultui diuino, & vacationi ab aliis omnibus. Et hoc est duplex, immediatum, & mediatum. Immediatum, quod immediatè erat à Deo institutum & præceptum ecclesiæ in veteri testamento: quod rursus erat varium.
units.tr: The ceremonial or external sabbath is a fixed time, set apart in the Church for the ministry of the Word and the administration of the sacraments, or for public divine worship, and for abstaining from all other things. And this is of two kinds, immediate and mediate. The immediate sabbath is that which was instituted and prescribed by God himself immediately for the Church in the Old Testament, and which was in turn of various kinds.

units.la: 1. Sabbatum dierum erat septimus quisque dies septimanæ, qui peculiariter dicebatur sabbatum, propter quietem Dei à creatione mundi, & propter quietem populo Dei mandatam eo die seruandam. Inde tota hebdomada siue septimana dierum per synecdochen apud Hebræos dicebatur sabbatum vel sabbata. Similiter sabbata dierum erant alij dies festi, vt festum paschatis, pentecostes, tabernaculorum, expiationis, seu jejunij, tubarum, &c. quoniam his festis non minus populo quiescendum erat, quam die septimo.
units.tr: 1. The sabbath of days was the seventh day of every week, which was specifically called the sabbath, both because of God's rest since the creation of the world and because of the rest commanded to the people of God to be kept on that day. Hence the whole week, or seven days, was called among the Hebrews by synecdoche sabbath or sabbaths. Likewise, the other festival days were sabbaths of days, such as the feast of the passover, of pentecost, of tabernacles, of atonement, or of fasting, of trumpets, and so on, since on these feasts the people were required to rest no less than on the seventh day.

units.la: 2. Sabbatum mensium erant neomeniæ.
units.tr: 2. The sabbath of months was the new moons.

units.la: 3. Sabbatum annorum erat septimus quisque annus, quo populus Judaicus jubebatur agrorum culturam intermittere: inde per synecdochen hebdomades annorum dicebantur sabbata.
units.tr: 3. The sabbath of years was every seventh year, in which the Jewish people were commanded to cease tilling their fields. Hence, by synecdoche, the weeks of years were called sabbaths.

units.la: Mediatum sabbatum externum est, quod Deus mediatè per ecclesiā constituit in nouo testamento, cuiusmodi est dies primus hebdomadis, qui dicitur solis vel rectius dominicus, quem ecclesia Christiana jam inde à tempore Apostolorum observat die septimo, propter resurrectionem Domini: vt patet ex illo Joannis: Fui spiritu correptus die dominico, &c.
units.tr: The mediate external sabbath is that which God established through the Church mediately in the New Testament, such as the first day of the week, which is called the day of the sun, or more correctly the Lord's day. The Christian Church has observed it instead of the seventh day from the time of the Apostles onward, on account of the resurrection of the Lord, as is evident from that saying of John: I was caught up in the Spirit on the Lord's day, etc. (Rev. 1).

units.la: Breuius: Sabbatum cæremoniale est duplex: aliud veteris, aliud noui testamenti. Vetus erat adstrictum ad diem septimum, & eius observatio erat necessaria, & cultus Dei. Nouum pendet ex arbitrio ecclesiæ, quæ elegit diem primum, propter certas causas: & is est observandus, ordinis causa: sed sine opinione necessitatis, quasi ab ecclesia oporteat eum observari, & non alium: de quo discrimine in sequentibus dicetur.
units.tr: More briefly: the ceremonial sabbath is twofold: one belongs to the Old Testament, the other to the New. The old was bound to the seventh day, and its observance was necessary and a part of the worship of God. The new depends on the judgment of the Church, which chose the first day for certain reasons; and it is to be observed for the sake of order, but without any opinion of necessity, as if the Church required it to be observed and no other day. This distinction will be discussed in what follows.

units.la: Typus distinctionis Sabbati.
units.tr: Table of the distinction of the Sabbath.

units.la: Sabbatū, hoc est, cessatio ab operibus, est vel internum, morale, & spirituale: quies à peccatis. externum, cæremoniale, institutum à Deo, vel immediatè in veteri testamento: ut sabbatū dierum: dies septimus, dies festi, pascha, pentecoste, Scenopegia. Sabbatum mensium: neomeniæ: Sabbatum annorum: septimus quisque annus. mediatè per ecclesiam in nouo testamento: dies dominicus.
units.tr: The sabbath, that is, cessation from works, is either internal, moral and spiritual: rest from sins; or external, ceremonial, instituted by God, either immediately in the Old Testament, as the sabbath of days: the seventh day, festival days, passover, pentecost, tabernacles; the sabbath of months: new moons; the sabbath of years: every seventh year; or mediately through the Church in the New Testament: the Lord's day.

units.la: II. Quatenus ad nos Christianos sabbatum pertineat.
units.tr: II. How far the Sabbath pertains to us Christians.

units.la: Sabbatum septimi diei inde ab initio designatum fuit à Deo, ad significandum, homines exemplo eius quiescere debere à suis operibus, præsertim à peccatis. Postea in lege Mosaica repetitum est præceptum, & cæremonia feriandi septimo die facta est sacramentum sanctificationis, quo Deus significabat, se esse sanctificatorem ecclesiæ, hoc est, se remittere ei peccata, & reciprocare eam in gratiam propter Messiam, patribus promissum, & suo tempore exhibendum. Hæc est ratio, cur sabbatum cæremoniale septimi diei nunc sit abolitum: quia fuit typicum, significans beneficia Messiæ, & admonens populum de suo officio: quam ob causam omnia reliqua sacramenta, sacrificia, & cæremoniæ ante & post legem institutæ, fuerunt abolitæ, aduentu Christi, per quem est impletum, quod illæ significabant. Quamuis autem abrogatum sit in nouo testamento sabbatum cæremoniale, morale tamen durat adhuc, & ad nos pertinet, ipsumque genus sabbati cæremonialis, nempe tribuendum esse certum aliquod tempus ministerio. Oportet enim non minus nunc in Christiana, quam olim in Judaica ecclesia esse certū aliquem diem, quo verbum Dei doceatur, & sacramenta publicè administrentur. Interim non sumus alligati, vt diem septimanæ tertium, quartum, quintum, vel quemuis alium certum habeamus. Apostolica igitur ecclesia, vt se à Iudaica synagoga discerneret: pro libertate sibi à Christo donata, pro septimo die elegit diem primum propter probabilem causam, quia eo die facta est Christi resurrectio, per quam spirituale & internum sabbatum in nobis inchoatur. Breuiter: alligati sumus sabbato moraliter, & caeremonialiter in genere, sed non in specie, hoc est, oportet nos habere aliquem diem, quo doceatur ecclesia, & administrentur sacramenta, sed non sumus alligati certo diei.
units.tr: God designated the Sabbath of the seventh day from the beginning, to signify that human beings should, by his example, rest from their works, especially from sins. Later, in the Mosaic law, the precept was repeated, and the ceremony of keeping the seventh day holy became a sacrament of sanctification, by which God signified that he is the sanctifier of the Church, that is, that he forgives her sins and restores her to favour for the sake of the Messiah, promised to the fathers and to be exhibited in his time. This is the reason why the ceremonial Sabbath of the seventh day has now been abolished: it was typical, signifying the benefits of the Messiah and reminding the people of their duty. For this reason all the other sacraments, sacrifices and ceremonies, whether instituted before or after the law, were abolished at the coming of Christ, through whom what they signified has been fulfilled. Although the ceremonial Sabbath has been abrogated in the New Testament, the moral Sabbath still endures and pertains to us, and so does the kind of the ceremonial Sabbath itself, namely that some definite time should be assigned to the ministry. For it is necessary now in the Christian Church, no less than of old in the Jewish Church, that there be a certain day on which the Word of God is taught and the sacraments are publicly administered. Yet we are not bound to hold the third, fourth, fifth or any other particular day of the week. The apostolic Church, therefore, in order to distinguish itself from the Jewish synagogue, and in the liberty given to it by Christ, chose the first day instead of the seventh, for a probable reason: because on that day Christ rose, and through that resurrection the spiritual and inward Sabbath begins in us. In brief: we are bound to the Sabbath morally and ceremonially in general, but not in particular; that is, we must have some day on which the Church is taught and the sacraments are administered, but we are not bound to a particular day.

units.la: Iudai contra abrogationem sabbati caeremonialis obiiciunt.
units.tr: The Jews object against the abrogation of the ceremonial Sabbath as follows.

units.la: 1. Sabbatum est pars decalogi. Ergo est lex perpetua. Resp. ad maiorem. Decalogus est lex perpetua, quatenus est moralis. Appendices autem, sive determinationes moralium praeceptorum significationis causa, usq; ad Messiam seruandae fuerunt.
units.tr: 1. The Sabbath is part of the Decalogue; therefore it is a perpetual law. Reply to the major. The Decalogue is a perpetual law insofar as it is moral. But its appendages, or the determinations of the moral precepts for the sake of signification, were to be kept only until the Messiah.

units.la: Obiect. 2. Praecepta decalogi ad omnes pertinent. Hoc est praeceptum decalogi. Ergo ad omnes pertinet. Resp. Conceditur, quatenus est morale. Est autem ex parte caeremoniale, & sic ad nos non pertinet, nisi quoad genus. Rationes sunt euidentes. 1. Paulus dicit Col. 2. 16. Nemo vos iudicet in cibo & in potu, aut in parte diei festi 2. Apostoli ipsi mutarunt sabbatum septimi diei, fine legis. Erat typus rerum implendarum à Christo, nempe sanctificationis, &c. Typus autem cedit rei exhibitae. Item, erat discretio populi Iudaici à reliquis gentibus. Haec autem discretio per Christum sublata est.
units.tr: Objection 2. The precepts of the Decalogue pertain to all. This is a precept of the Decalogue; therefore it pertains to all. Reply: This is granted insofar as it is moral. But it is partly ceremonial, and so it does not pertain to us, except as to its genus. The reasons are evident. 1. Paul says in Colossians 2:16: Let no one judge you in food or drink, or in respect of a feast day. 2. The apostles themselves changed the Sabbath of the seventh day, once the law had ended. It was a type of things to be fulfilled by Christ, namely sanctification, and so on. A type, however, gives way to the thing exhibited. Likewise, it was a distinction of the Jewish people from the other nations. This distinction has been removed through Christ.

units.la: Obiect. 3. Dominus dicit de sabbato: Pactum est sempiternum inter me & filios Israel signum, & perpetuum. Ergo sabbatum septimi diei nunquam est abolendum. Resp. 1. Caeremoniale sabbatum est perpetuum usque ad Christum, qui est caeremoniarum finis. 2. Sabbatum est aeternum, quoad rem significatam, quae est cessatio à peccatis, & quies in Deo. Sic enim omnes typi veteris testamenti sunt aeterni, etiam ipsum regnum Dauidicum, quod tamen ante aduentum Messiae erat destruendum. Vide supra
units.tr: Objection 3. The Lord says of the Sabbath: It is an everlasting covenant between me and the children of Israel, a sign, and a perpetual one. Therefore the Sabbath of the seventh day must never be abolished. Reply: 1. The ceremonial Sabbath was perpetual only until Christ, who is the end of the ceremonies. 2. The Sabbath is eternal as to the thing signified, which is cessation from sins and rest in God. For in this way all the types of the Old Testament are eternal, even the Davidic kingdom itself, which nevertheless was to be destroyed before the coming of the Messiah. See above.

units.la: Quaest. de abrogatione legis, obiect. 1 & 2.
units.tr: The question on the abrogation of the law, objections 1 and 2.

units.la: Obiect. 4. Leges ante Mosen latae sunt immutabiles. Praeceptum de sabbato septimi diei ante Mosen fuit datum. Ergo sabbatum septimi diei est immutabile; ut maxime concederetur, caeremonias Mosaicas esse mutabiles. Resp. Maior est particularia negatur. Nam caeremoniae etiam ante Mosen à Deo institutae, cum typi fuerint beneficiorum Messiae, huius aduentu sunt abolitae, ut circumcisio Abrahamo data: item sacrificia primis parentibus mandata.
units.tr: Objection 4. Laws given before Moses were unchangeable. The precept about the Sabbath of the seventh day was given before Moses; therefore the Sabbath of the seventh day is unchangeable. Even if it were granted that the Mosaic ceremonies are changeable. Reply: The major is denied in its particular application. For ceremonies instituted by God even before Moses, since they were types of the benefits of the Messiah, were abolished at his coming, as was the circumcision given to Abraham, and likewise the sacrifices enjoined on our first parents.

units.la: Obiect. 5. Leges ante lapsum à Deo latae, non sunt typi beneficiorum Messiae, & omnes homines obligant: tunc enim nondum erat data promissio de Meffia : & vna eademque erat totius generis humani in primis parentibus conditio. Sabbatum septimi diei institutum est à Deo ante lapsum generis humani. Ergo est viuerfale & perpetuum. Resp. per distinctionem Maioris, quæ vera est de legibus moralibus, quarum notitiæ naturales menti humanæ sunt impressæ in creatione, non autem cæremonia septimi diei, quæ post lapsum in lege Mofaica est facta typus beneficiorum Meffiæ, ac proinde, sicut aliæ cæremoniæ, five tunc demum, five antea institutæ, mutationi per Meffiam est facta obnoxia. Noluit enim Deus vmbras rerum manere, ipsis rebus exhibitis.
units.tr: Objection 5. Laws given by God before the Fall are not types of the benefits of the Messiah, and they bind all human beings; for at that time the promise about the Messiah had not yet been given, and the condition of the whole human race was one and the same in our first parents. The Sabbath of the seventh day was instituted by God before the fall of the human race; therefore it is universal and perpetual. Reply by distinguishing the major, which is true of moral laws, whose knowledge is naturally impressed on the human mind at creation, but not of the ceremony of the seventh day, which after the Fall was made, in the Mosaic law, a type of the benefits of the Messiah. Consequently, like the other ceremonies, whether instituted at that time or earlier, it became subject to change through the Messiah. For God did not will that the shadows remain once the realities had been exhibited.

units.la: Obiect. 6. Causa legis perpetua facit legem perpetuam. Memoria & celebratio creationis, atque operum Dei meditatio, est perpetua causa consecrati septimi diei. Ergo lex de septimo die etiam post Christum exhibitum est immutabilis. Refpond. Rursus distinguenda est maior : legem esse immutabilem, propter causam immutabilem, fi causa illa, seu finis ille, necessario & perpetuò hanc legem, tanquam effectum aut medium, requirat : non tantum fi aliis temporibus, aliis mediis, ad eundem finem non minus consequi legislator possit. Atqui meditatio & celebratio operum Dei non minus alio die, quam septimo fieri potest. Ea igitur legem de septimo die non facit perpetuam.
units.tr: Objection 6. The cause of a perpetual law makes the law perpetual. The remembrance and celebration of creation, and the meditation on the works of God, are the perpetual cause for hallowing the seventh day; therefore the law concerning the seventh day remains unchangeable even after Christ has been exhibited. Reply: Again the major must be distinguished: a law is unchangeable because of an unchangeable cause if that cause, or that end, necessarily and perpetually requires this law as its effect or means, and not merely if the lawgiver could attain the same end no less by other times and other means. But meditation and celebration of the works of God can be carried out on another day no less than on the seventh. Therefore they do not make the law concerning the seventh day perpetual.

units.la: Anabaptista vero contra obseruationem diei primi objiciunt dicta, quibus prohibentur discrimina dierum in nouo testamento: Dies obseruatis & mensec & to: Nemo vos judicet in parte diei festi. tempora. Qui non curat diem, Domino non curat, &c. Ergo, inquiunt, obseruatio primi diei non minus improbatur, quam septimi. Resp. ad antecedens : Prohibetur Christianis discrimen dierum non simpliciter, sed cum opinione cultus, vel necessitatis, obseruatum. Sic autem non obseruatur ab ecclesia dies primus. Nam duplicitep differt obseruatio primi diei à sabbato Judaico. 1. Sabbatum septimi diei, tanquam partem cultus diuini cæremoniarum, non licebat Judeis omittere aut mutare, propter expressum Dei mandatum. Ecclesia verò Christiana primũ vel alium diem tribuit ministerio, salua sua libertate : Sine opinione necessitatis, aut cultus. 2. Sabbatũ vetus erat typus rerum in veteri testamento per Christum implendarum. In nouo autem testamento illa significatio cessauit, & tantum ordinis atque decori ratio habetur, sine quo ministerium ecclesiæ vel nullum, vel saltem non bene constitutum esse potest.
units.tr: The Anabaptists, on the other hand, object against the observance of the first day the sayings by which distinctions of days are forbidden in the New Testament: You observe days and months and times (Gal. 4:10); Let no one judge you in respect of a feast day (Col. 2:16); He who does not regard the day, does not regard it for the Lord (Rom. 14:6), and so on. Therefore, they say, the observance of the first day is condemned no less than that of the seventh. Reply to the antecedent: the distinction of days is forbidden to Christians not absolutely, but when it is observed with the opinion of worship or of necessity. The Church, however, does not observe the first day in that way. For the observance of the first day differs from the Jewish Sabbath in two ways. 1. The Sabbath of the seventh day, as a part of the ceremonial divine worship, was not lawful for the Jews to omit or change, because of the express command of God. The Christian Church, however, assigns the first or another day to the ministry, saving its own liberty, without any opinion of necessity or of worship. 2. The old Sabbath was a type of things in the Old Testament to be fulfilled through Christ. In the New Testament that signification has ceased, and only the consideration of order and decency is kept, without which the ministry of the Church either cannot exist or at least cannot be well ordered.

units.la: Coloss. 2. 16. Galat. 4, 6. Rom. 14, 6.
III. Causa, propter quas institutum sit sabbatum.
units.tr: III. The causes for which the Sabbath was instituted.

units.la: Causae finales instituti sabbati praecipuae sunt haec:
units.tr: The principal final causes of the institution of the Sabbath are these:

units.la: 1. Publica celebratio Dei in ecclesia.
units.tr: 1. The public worship of God in the Church.

units.la: 2. Conseruatio ministerij ecclesiastici, quod est officium diuinitus institutum docendi ecclesiam de Deo & eius voluntate ex verbo Dei per Prophetas & Apostolos tradito, atque administrandi sacramenta secundum institutionem diuinam. Finis huius instituti sabbati non est postremus: siquidem publica & ordinaria haec praedicatio doctrinae coniuncta cum recitatione precum, & gratiarum actione, & vsurpatione rituum diuinorum est exercitium publicum, excitans & fouens fidem & poenitentiam in electis.
units.tr: 2. The preservation of the ministry of the Church, which is an office divinely instituted to teach the Church about God and his will from the Word of God delivered through the Prophets and Apostles, and to administer the sacraments according to divine institution. The purpose of this institution of the Sabbath is not the least important: for this public and ordinary preaching of doctrine, joined with the recitation of prayers, the giving of thanks, and the use of the divine rites, is a public exercise that stirs up and nourishes faith and repentance in the elect.

units.la: 3. Vt in veteri testamento esset typus, significans sabbatum spirituale. Sabbata mea dedi eis, vt essent signum inter me & eos, & scirent, quia ego Dominus sanctificans eos.
units.tr: 3. That in the Old Testament there might be a type signifying the spiritual Sabbath. I gave them my Sabbaths, that they might be a sign between me and them, and that they might know that I, the Lord, sanctify them.

units.la: 4. Vt esset publicum & ordinarium exercitium precum, confessionis & obedientiae erga Deum.
units.tr: 4. That there might be a public and ordinary exercise of prayer, confession and obedience toward God.

units.la: 5. Propter circumstantiam septimi Diei, vt nimirum is admoneret homines de creatione mundi, & de meditatione operum diuinorum sex diebus à Deo conditorum.
units.tr: 5. On account of the circumstance of the seventh day, namely that it might remind people of the creation of the world and lead them to meditate on the works of God, who made them in six days.

units.la: 6. Vt eo die maxime exercerentur opera dilectionis, beneficentiae & benignitatis erga proximum.
units.tr: 6. That on that day works of love, beneficence and kindness toward one's neighbour might be practised especially.

units.la: 7. Propter quietem corporalem, tam brutorum, quam hominum, & quidem brutorum propter homines.
units.tr: 7. For bodily rest, both of animals and of men, and indeed of animals for the sake of men.

units.la: 8. Vt populus Israeliticus hoc symbolo ab aliis gentibus discernetur.
units.tr: 8. That the Israelite people might be distinguished from the other nations by this sign.

units.la: IV. Quomodo seruetur & violetur sabbatum, seu, quae sint opera sabbato praecepta, vel prohibita.
units.tr: IV. How the Sabbath is kept and violated, or, what works are commanded or forbidden on the Sabbath.

units.la: Sabbati seu temporis ministerio destinati sanctificatio siue sanctus vsus est, cum opera sancta, quae Deus fieri iussit, eo die exercentur. Contra profanatio est, cum vel opera sancta omittuntur, vel exercentur profana, ministerium impedientia, ac operibus ad sanctificationem pertinentibus contraria.
units.tr: The sanctification or holy use of the Sabbath, that is, of the time set apart for the ministry, takes place when the holy works that God commanded to be done are performed on that day. Profanation, on the other hand, is when either the holy works are omitted, or profane works are performed that hinder the ministry and are contrary to the works belonging to sanctification.

units.la: Sunt autem opera, quibus sabbatum sanctificatur, & eorum contraria, quibus profanatur, praecipuè haec:
units.tr: The works by which the Sabbath is sanctified, and their opposites by which it is profaned, are chiefly these:

units.la: 1. RECTE DOCERE ecclesiam de Deo & eius voluntate.
units.tr: 1. TO TEACH THE CHURCH RIGHTLY about God and his will.

units.la: Etiam in tertio praecepto sancitur propagatio verae doctrinae, sed priuata, quae priuatim est singulorum. Hic certarum personarum proprium docendi munus sancitur, quae donis necessariis diuinitus instructæ ab ecclesia legitimè ad docendum sunt vocatæ. His præcipitur, vt sanam doctrinam tum publicè in concionibus ecclesię fideliter proponant, tum priuatim singulis pro necessitate & occasione explicent, ad publicam ædificationem, & singulorum salutem. Pertinent huc dicta: Leuit.10,11. Act.13, 15. & 17,2.17.2 Tim.4,2.
units.tr: The third commandment also enjoins the spreading of true doctrine, but as a private matter, which belongs to each individual privately. Here the proper teaching office of certain persons is enjoined, who, equipped with the necessary gifts from God, have been lawfully called by the Church to teach. They are commanded to set forth sound doctrine faithfully, both publicly in the sermons of the Church and privately to individuals as need and occasion require, for the public edification and the salvation of individuals. To this belong the passages: Lev. 10:11; Acts 13:15 and 17:2, 17; 2 Tim. 4:2.

units.la: Huic contraria est 1. omissio, aut neglectus officii docendi, siue priuatim, siue publice: de qua conqueritur Deus apud Prophetam: Spectatores eius vniuersi sunt canes muti. Væ pastoribus, qui pauerunt semetipsos, &c.
units.tr: Contrary to this is 1. the omission or neglect of the duty to teach, whether privately or publicly, over which God complains through the Prophet: All its watchmen are dumb dogs. Woe to the shepherds who feed themselves, etc.

units.la: 1. Depravatio aut mutilatio doctrinæ, aut eius administrorum magistratuum, vel aliorum opiniones, affectus, cupiditates, aut ad commoda priuata inflexio: Non vt plerique cauponamur sermonem Dei.
units.tr: 1. The corruption or mutilation of doctrine, or of its ministers, or of the magistrates, through opinions, passions, desires, or a bending of it toward private advantage: Not, as many do, peddling the word of God.

units.la: II. ADMINISTRARE SACRAMENTA secundū institutionem diuinam: quod item ab ecclesiæ ministris ad hoc munus obeundū legitimè vocatis fieri debet. Vt autem doctrina, sic etiam sacramentorū administratio non est alligata ad illos dies, quibus conuentus ecclesiastici fiunt, sed sufficit, si administratio sit publica, & fiat per ministros, publicam personam, & vices Dei gerentes. Præcipuè tamen sabbato administratio sacramentorū vigere debet: Cum conuenitis in vnum, hoc non est dominicam cœnam edere. Itaque fratres mei, cum conuenietis ad vescendum, alius alium expectate. Erantque perdurantes in doctrina Apostolorum, & communicatione & fractione panis, & precatione. Huic aduersatur omissio vel neglectus hortationis ecclesiæ ad vtendum sacramentis: & administratio illegitima, cum vel detrahitur, vel additur cæremoniis diuinitus institutis, vel in eis aliquid mutatur, vel excluduntur à sacramentis ij, qui debent admitti, vel admittuntur, qui ex instituto Dei debent arceri, vel non docetur populus de legitimo eorum vsu. III. Diligenter DISCERE DOCTRINAM, hoc est, frequentare congressus ecclesiæ, ad audiendā & discendam doctrinam cœlestem, & auditam assiduè meditari & inquirere: præsertim autem dies ministerio dicatos lectioni, meditationi & tractationi rerum diuinarum impendere. Hoc ex natura correlatorum patet. Si enim Deus vult esse, qui sabbato diligenter doceant, etiam vult esse, qui sabbato diligenter discant doctrinam cœlestem. Requiritur ad studiū discendi priuata meditatio. Ideo laudantur Beroenses quotidie scrutantes scripturas, an hæc ita se haberent. Præsertim autem seruientibus, aut seruituris aliquando ecclesiæ, diligens studium cognoscendi doctrinam cœlestem injungitur. Attende lectioni, adhortationi, doctrinæ.
units.tr: II. TO ADMINISTER THE SACRAMENTS according to divine institution: which also must be done by the ministers of the Church who have been lawfully called to discharge this office. But just as with doctrine, the administration of the sacraments is not bound to those days on which the ecclesiastical assemblies are held; it is enough if the administration is public and is carried out by ministers who act as a public person and in the place of God. Yet the administration of the sacraments ought to flourish especially on the Sabbath: When you come together in one place, it is not to eat the Lord's Supper. So, my brothers, when you come together to eat, wait for one another. And they were devoted to the doctrine of the Apostles, and to fellowship, and to the breaking of bread, and to prayer. Opposed to this are the omission or neglect of exhorting the Church to use the sacraments, and an illegitimate administration, when something is taken away from, added to, or changed in the ceremonies divinely instituted, or when those who ought to be admitted are excluded from the sacraments, or those who by God's institution ought to be kept away are admitted, or the people are not taught about the lawful use of them. III. To LEARN DOCTRINE DILIGENTLY, that is, to attend the assemblies of the Church in order to hear and learn heavenly doctrine, and to meditate on and inquire into what has been heard continually; and especially to devote the days set apart for the ministry to reading, meditation and treatment of divine matters. This is clear from the nature of the correlatives. For if God wills that there be those who teach diligently on the Sabbath, he also wills that there be those who diligently learn heavenly doctrine on the Sabbath. Private meditation is required for the study of learning. Therefore the Bereans are praised for searching the Scriptures daily, to see whether these things were so. Especially for those who serve, or will at some time serve, the Church, a diligent study of knowing heavenly doctrine is enjoined. Attend to reading, to exhortation, to doctrine.

units.la: Huic aduersatur 1. Contemtus & neglectus doctrinæ, hoc est, vel non adesse sacris concionibus, non obstante legitima causa, & opera, quæ differri poterant, sabbato facere: vel concionibus sacris non auscultare: vel doctrinam ecclesiæ non meditari & inquirere.
units.tr: Opposed to this are 1. contempt and neglect of doctrine, that is, either not being present at the sacred sermons, without any lawful cause, and doing on the Sabbath work that could have been postponed; or not listening to the sacred sermons; or not meditating on and inquiring into the doctrine of the Church.

units.la: 2. Negligentia cognoscendi doctrinam in ministris, aut in iis, qui ad studia doctrinarum à Deo sunt vocati, & vel seruire aliquando debent propagationi doctrinæ, vel maiorem, quam alij, habent occasionem & facultatem discendi: Cui multum est datum, ab eo multum repetetur, &c.
units.tr: 2. Negligence in learning doctrine in ministers, or in those who have been called by God to the study of the doctrines, and who either ought at some time to serve the spread of doctrine, or have a greater opportunity and ability to learn than others: From him to whom much has been given, much will be required, etc.

units.la: 3. Curiositas: quæ est studium cognoscendi, vel audiendi, non patefacta à Deo, non necessaria, vel noua. Inuestigatio gloriæ diuinarum rerum non est gloria. Difficiliora quam quibus par sis, inconsiderate ne quæras. Quæ tibi mandata sunt à Deo, ea sanctè meditare. Sic 1 Tim.4,7. & 1 Tim.4,3. Tit.3,9.
units.tr: 3. Curiosity: which is the desire to know or hear what has not been revealed by God, what is not necessary, or what is new. The investigation of the glory of divine things is not glory. Do not inconsiderately seek things too difficult for you. Meditate faithfully on what has been commanded you by God. So 1 Tim. 4:7; 1 Tim. 4:3; Titus 3:9.

units.la: IV. Vti Sacramentis secundum institutionem diuinam.
units.tr: IV. On using the Sacraments according to the divine institution.

units.la: Primo die hebdomadis, cum discipuli convenissent ad frangendum panem, Paulus differebat, &c. Sic in solenni conuentu populi pascha Deus celebrari jusserat, ac reliquis festis & sabbatis certa sacrificia assignauerat. Et vultparem in modum Deus, quemadmodum doctrinam veram exaudiri, sic legitimum vsum sacramentorum conspici in congressibus publicis ecclesiæ; quia vtrumq; horum vult esse notum, quo agnoscatur & discernatur ecclesia ab aliis sectis & gentibus. Sunt item sacramenta, sicut verbum, fidei & pietatis in nobis excitandæ & fouendæ organa, & pars cultus Dei publici in ecclesia. Maxime igitur eorum vsurpatio congruit sabbato.
units.tr: "On the first day of the week, when the disciples came together to break bread, Paul preached to them, etc." (Acts 20:7). So in the solemn assembly of the people God had commanded the Passover to be celebrated, and he had appointed certain sacrifices for the other feasts and sabbaths. Just as God wills that sound doctrine be heard, so in the public gatherings of the church he wills that the lawful use of the sacraments be seen, for he wants both to be known, so that the church may be recognized and distinguished from other sects and nations. The sacraments, like the Word, are also instruments for kindling and fostering faith and piety in us, and a part of the public worship of God in the church. Their proper use therefore especially fits the sabbath.

units.la: Huic repugnat 1. Omissio & contemtus sacramentorum.
units.tr: Opposed to this are: 1. The omission and contempt of the sacraments.

units.la: 2. Profanatio sacramentorum, cum non eo modo, quo Deus jussit, aut non ab iis, quibus instituta sunt, vsurpatur.
units.tr: 2. The profanation of the sacraments, when they are used not in the manner God commanded, or not by those for whom they were instituted.

units.la: 3. Vsus superstitiosus, cum rituum obseruationi alligatur salus, & gratia Dei, aut in eos fines vsurpantur, ad quos non à Deo sunt instituta: Incircumcisus exterminabitur. Qui immolat bouem, perinde peccat, ac qui interficit virum.
units.tr: 3. Superstitious use, when salvation or the grace of God is tied to the observance of rites, or when the sacraments are used for ends for which God did not institute them: "The uncircumcised shall be cut off." "He who sacrifices an ox sins no less than he who kills a man."

units.la: V. Invocatio Dei publica, qua coniungimus confessionem, gratiarum actionem, & vota nostra cum ecclesia. Vult enim Deus non tantum priuatim à singulis, sed etiam publicè ab ecclesia invocari propter suam gloriam, & nostram consolationem. Ideo Christus peculiarem promissionem addidit communibus precibus: Si duo ex vobis consenserint in terra, quodcunq; petierint, fiet iis a Patre meo, qui est in cœlis. Vbi enim duo vel tres, coacti sunt in nomine meo, illic sum in medio eorum. Neque verò publicas preces, sed ostentationem & hypocrisin damnat, quæ est simulatio pietatis, cum dicit: Cum precaris, introito in conclaue tuum, & clauso ostio tuo precare Patrem tuum, qui est in occulto, & Pater tuus, qui te aspicit in occulto, reddet tibi in propatulo. Id enim praecedentia verba ostendunt: Cum precaris, ne sis vt hypocrita: Amant enim in conuentib. &c. Hic igitur inuocatio praecipitur, vt est publica totius ecclesiae: in tertio praecipitur inuocatio, vt est priuata singulorum.
units.tr: V. Public invocation of God, by which we join our confession, thanksgiving and prayers with those of the church. For God wills to be called upon not only privately by individuals but also publicly by the church, for his own glory and our comfort. Therefore Christ added a special promise to common prayers: "If two of you agree on earth about anything they ask, it will be done for them by my Father who is in heaven. For where two or three are gathered together in my name, there I am in the midst of them." Nor does he condemn public prayers, but ostentation and hypocrisy, which is the pretence of piety, when he says: "When you pray, go into your room, shut the door, and pray to your Father who is in secret; and your Father who sees in secret will reward you openly." The preceding words make this clear: "When you pray, do not be like the hypocrites, for they love to pray standing in the synagogues, etc." Here, then, invocation is commanded as the public act of the whole church; in the third passage, invocation is commanded as the private act of individuals.

units.la: Huic repugnat 1. Neglectus precum ecclesiae.
units.tr: Opposed to this are: 1. Neglect of the prayers of the church.

units.la: 2. Hypocritica praesentia in precibus ecclesiae, sine attentione & affectu.
units.tr: 2. Hypocritical presence at the prayers of the church, without attention or feeling.

units.la: 3. Recitatio precum, aedificationi ecclesiae non seruiens: Nam tu quidem gratias agis, sed alius non aedificatur.
units.tr: 3. Recitation of prayers that does not serve the edification of the church: "For you indeed give thanks well, but the other person is not edified."

units.la: VI. CHARITAS ET BENEFICENTIA
units.tr: VI. CHARITY AND BENEFICENCE

units.la: in pauperes, hoc est, date eleemosynas, & exercere opera dilectionis erga egentes, ad ostendendam obedientiam nostram, quam praestamus doctrinae. Huc pertinet concio Christi de sabbato, in qua contra Judaeos explicat, an liceat sabbato benefacere.
units.tr: toward the poor; that is, give alms and practise works of love toward the needy, to show our obedience to the doctrine we profess. To this belongs Christ's discourse on the sabbath, in which, against the Jews, he explains whether it is lawful to do good on the sabbath.

units.la: Repugnat ei 1. Neglectus vel contemtus pauperum. 2. Ostentatio in dandis eleemosynis, quam Christus damnat.
units.tr: Opposed to this are: 1. Neglect or contempt of the poor. 2. Ostentation in giving alms, which Christ condemns.

units.la: VII. HONOR MINISTERII
units.tr: VII. THE HONOUR OF THE MINISTRY

units.la: ecclesiastici, qui multa complectitur. 1. Reverentiam: hoc est, agnitionem ordinis & voluntatis diuinae in ministerij institutione, conseruatione & ecclesiae per illud collectione, & huius iudicij nostri de ministerio in dictis & factis declarationem. Sic de nobis reputet homo, vt de ministris Christi & dispensatoribus mysteriorum Dei. Nomine Christi legatione fungimur.
units.tr: of the ecclesiastical ministry, which embraces several things. 1. Reverence: that is, recognition of the order and will of God in the institution and preservation of the ministry, and in the gathering of the church through it, and the declaration of our judgment about the ministry in words and deeds. "Let a man regard us in this way, as ministers of Christ and stewards of the mysteries of God." We serve in the name of Christ as ambassadors.

units.la: 2. Amorem: quo & libenter frequentamus coetus ecclesiae, & bene volumus audimus atque disimus doctrinam ecclesiae, & bene volumus fidelibus ecclesiae ministris, non tantum propter dilectionis officium, sed etiam propter munus, quo funguntur. Quam amabilia tabernacula tua Iehoua exercituum! Concupiscit anima mea ad atria Iehoua. Laetatus sum cum dicentibus mihi: in domum Domini ibimus.
units.tr: 2. Love: by which we gladly attend the assemblies of the church, willingly hear and learn its doctrine, and wish well to the faithful ministers of the church, not only out of the duty of love but also on account of the office they discharge. "How lovely are your tabernacles, Jehovah of hosts! My soul longs for the courts of Jehovah. I rejoiced when they said to me: Let us go into the house of the LORD."

units.la: 3. Obedientiam in iis, quae sunt ministerij: Obedite praepositis vestris. Huc pertinent opera dilectionis erga Deum & proximum, hoc est, tota vita Christiana, quae est sabbatum spirituale. Agere enim sabbatum spirituale, nihil aliud est, quam in vita instituenda obedire voci diuinae sonanti per ministrum ecclesiae.
units.tr: 3. Obedience in those matters which belong to the ministry: "Obey your leaders." To this belong works of love toward God and neighbour, that is, the whole Christian life, which is the spiritual sabbath. For to keep the spiritual sabbath is nothing other than, in ordering one's life, to obey the divine voice sounding through the minister of the church.

units.la: 4. Gratitudinem: hoc est, officia ad conseruationem ministerij & ministrorum pertinentia. Si enim Deus vult ministerium esse, vult etiam illud conseruari, & a singulis ad id aliquid conferri. Huc pertinent leges Mosaicae de primogenitis, primitiis, decimis, & pluribus oblationibus, quae sacerdotibus & Leuitis erant attributae loco stipendij, quarum legum etsi circumstantiae sunt abolitæ : tamen genus perpetuo manet, quia vult Deus vsque ad finem mundi ministerium conseruari. Caue autem, ne derelinquas Leuitam omnibus diebus tuis super terram, &c. Quis mi-litat propriis stipendiis vnquam? quis plantat vineam, & de fructu eius non edit? Item Galat.6,6. 1 Tim.5,17. Matth.10,24. Conti-netur hac parte honoris erga ministerium, etiam scholarum conseruatio: siquidem sine studiis literarum & artium nec idonei fiunt homines ad docendum, nec puritas doctrinæ conseruari, & contra hæreticos defendi potest.
units.tr: 4. Gratitude: that is, the duties pertaining to the maintenance of the ministry and of ministers. For if God wills there to be a ministry, he also wills that it be preserved, and that individuals contribute something to it. To this belong the Mosaic laws concerning firstborn sons, firstfruits, tithes and the many offerings that were assigned to priests and Levites in place of wages. Although the particular circumstances of these laws have been abolished, their kind nevertheless remains permanently, because God wills the ministry to be preserved until the end of the world. "Take care that you do not forsake the Levite all your days upon the earth," etc. "Who ever serves as a soldier at his own expense? Who plants a vineyard and does not eat its fruit?" Likewise Gal. 6:6; 1 Tim. 5:17; Matt. 10:24. Under this part of honour toward the ministry is also included the maintenance of schools: for without the study of letters and the arts men do not become fit to teach, nor can the purity of doctrine be preserved and defended against heretics.

units.la: 5. Ἐπιείκεια seu æquitatem in tolerandis infirmitatibus mi-nistrorum, quæ non enormiter & manifeste corrumpunt, aut impediunt officium, & scandalo ecclesiam lædunt: Aduersus presbyterum accusationem ne admittito, nisi sub duobus, aut tribus testibus.
units.tr: 5. Epieikeia [ἐπιείκεια], that is, fairness in bearing with the weaknesses of ministers, which do not grossly and manifestly corrupt or impede their office, or wound the church with scandal: "Do not admit an accusation against an elder except on the evidence of two or three witnesses."

units.la: Honori erga ministerium ecclesiasticum contrarius est con-temptus ministerij: quando vel aboletur ministerium ecclesiæ: vel indignis committitur: vel negatur esse organum, quo Deus ad collectionem ecclesiæ vti velit. Item cum afficiuntur mini-stri contumeliis: cum doctrinæ auditæ non obeditur in insti-tuenda vita: cum negliguntur opera dilectionis: cum rebus in-anibus aut malis vacatur; cum non dantur alimenta necessaria ministris, cum defensio, & alia gratitudinis officia ministris non præstantur: cum scholarum, studiosorumq; & doctrinæ conser-uatio negligitur: cum defectus tolerabiles ministrorum non feruntur, & propter eos ministerium contumelia afficitur.
units.tr: Contrary to honour toward the ecclesiastical ministry is contempt for the ministry: when the ministry of the church is either abolished, or committed to unworthy men, or is denied to be the instrument through which God wills to gather his church. Likewise when ministers are assailed with insults; when the doctrine heard is not obeyed in ordering one's life; when works of love are neglected; when men are occupied with empty or evil things; when necessary support is not given to ministers; when defence and other duties of gratitude are not rendered to ministers; when the maintenance of schools, students and doctrine is neglected; when the tolerable weaknesses of ministers are not borne, and because of them the ministry is subjected to insult.

units.la: DE MINISTERIO ECCLESIASTICO.
units.tr: DE MINISTERIO ECCLESIASTICO. (On the Ecclesiastical Ministry)

units.la: Cum hoc præcepto publicus Dei cultus externus, ac proinde ipsum ecclesiæ ministerium eiusq; vsus & honor sanciatur, vt ex præcedentibus patet: doctrina de ministerio breuiter hic est re-petenda. Deo igitur præcipue quæritur: I. II. Quid sit ministerium ecclesiæ. III. Quare sit institutum. IV. Qui sint ministrorum gradus. V. Quæ sint officia. Quibus sit committendum.
units.tr: Since this precept sanctions the public external worship of God, and therefore the ministry of the Church itself, along with its use and honour, as is clear from what has gone before, the doctrine of the ministry should be briefly repeated here. Accordingly, the following points are chiefly to be considered: I. II. What the ministry of the Church is. III. Why it was instituted. IV. What the grades of ministers are. V. What the duties are, and to whom the ministry is to be committed.

units.la: I. Quid sit ministerium ecclesiæ.
units.tr: I. What the ministry of the Church is.

units.la: Ministerium ecclesiasticum est officium à Deo in ecclesia insti-tutum, prædicandi verbum Dei, & administrandi sacramenta, secundum institutionem diuinam.
units.tr: The ecclesiastical ministry is the office instituted by God in the Church, of preaching the Word of God and administering the sacraments, according to the divine institution.

units.la: Partes igitur ministerij sunt duæ: 1. Prædicatio verbi. 2. Sa-cramentorum administratio.
units.tr: The parts of the ministry are therefore two: (1) the preaching of the Word; (2) the administration of the sacraments.

units.la: II. Quare ministerium sit institutum.
units.tr: II. Why the ministry was instituted.

units.la: Causæ ministerii à Deo instituti sunt:
units.tr: The causes of the ministry instituted by God are these:

units.la: 1. Gloria Dei: quia vult Deus in genere humano non tantum priuatim à singulis, sed etiam publica voce totius ecclesiæ in hac vita celebrari & inuocari: In congregationibus benedicite Deo.
units.tr: 1. The glory of God: because God wishes to be celebrated and called upon in this life not only privately by individuals, but also by the public voice of the whole Church, among the human race: Bless God in the congregations.

units.la: 2. Vt sit instrumentum conuertendi homines ad Deum: Dedit alios apostolos, alios prophetas, &c. ad coagmentationem sanctorum.
units.tr: 2. That it may be an instrument for converting people to God: He gave some apostles, some prophets, etc., for the equipping of the saints.

units.la: 3. Vt Deus accommodet sese nostræ infirmitati, homines per homines docendo.
units.tr: 3. That God may accommodate himself to our weakness, teaching men through men.

units.la: 4. Vt alij alios suo exemplo ad pietatem & celebrationem Dei provocent: Narrabo nomen tuum fratribus meis.
units.tr: 4. That people may stir one another, by their example, to piety and to the celebration of God: I will declare your name to my brethren.

units.la: 5. Vt ostendat Deus suam φιλανθρωπίαν, quod velit homines esse ministros summi illius operis, & ministerii reconciliationis, quo ipse etiam Filius Dei functus est.
units.tr: 5. That God may show his love for mankind (φιλανθρωπία), in that he wishes human beings to be ministers of that great work and of the ministry of reconciliation, which the Son of God himself also performed.

units.la: 6. Vt possit ecclesia conspici in hoc mundo, & reprobi sint inexcusabiles.
units.tr: 6. That the Church may be seen in this world, and the reprobate may be left without excuse.

units.la: III. Qui sint ministrorum gradus.
units.tr: III. What the grades of ministers are.

units.la: Ministri alii sunt immediatè vocati à Deo, alii mediatè ab ecclesia. Immediatè vocati erant prophetæ & apostoli. Prophetæ erant ministri immediatè vocati à Deo ad docendam, & illustrandam doctrinā Mosis, & promissiones de Messia, ad corrigendos errores in ecclesia, & politia Mosaica, & ad edenda oracula de euentibus in ecclesia, & extra eam, habentes testimonium à Deo, quod non errarent in doctrina. Apostoli erant ministri immediatè vocati à Christo ad prædicandam doctrinam de Messia exhibito, & spargendam in totum terrarum orbem, habentes similiter testimonium à Deo, quod non errarent in doctrina. Mediatè vocati sunt 1. Euangelistæ, qui erant adjutores apostolorum, & mittebantur ab apostolis ad docendum varias ecclesias. 2. Episcopi seu pastores, qui sunt ministri, vocati ab ecclesia, ad docendum verbum, & administranda sacramenta, in certa ecclesia. 3. Doctores, qui sunt ministri, vocati ab ecclesia, ad docendum in certa ecclesia, 4. Gubernatores, qui sunt ministri, ecclesiæ judicio electi ad gubernandam disciplinam, & ad ordinanda necessaria ecclesiæ. 5. Diaconi, qui sunt ministri, ab ecclesia electi, adgerendam curam pauperum, & ad distribuendas eleemosynas.
units.tr: Some ministers are called immediately by God, others mediately by the Church. The prophets and apostles were called immediately. The prophets were ministers called immediately by God to teach and illustrate the doctrine of Moses and the promises concerning the Messiah, to correct errors in the Church and in the Mosaic polity, and to deliver oracles about events in the Church and outside it, having the testimony from God that they did not err in doctrine. The apostles were ministers called immediately by Christ to preach the doctrine of the Messiah now revealed and to spread it throughout the whole world, likewise having the testimony from God that they did not err in doctrine. Those called mediately are: (1) the Evangelists, who were helpers of the apostles and were sent by the apostles to teach various churches; (2) the bishops, or pastors, that is, ministers called by the Church to teach the Word and administer the sacraments in a particular church; (3) the teachers, that is, ministers called by the Church to teach in a particular church; (4) the governors, that is, ministers chosen by the judgment of the Church to govern discipline and to arrange what the Church needs; (5) the deacons, that is, ministers chosen by the Church to attend to the care of the poor and to distribute alms.

units.la: IV. Quæ sint ministrorum officia.
units.tr: IV. What the duties of ministers are.

units.la: Officia ministrorum ecclesiæ in genere sunt 1. veram & integram doctrinam legis & euangelii fideliter & dextrè proponere, vt ecclesia possit intelligere. 2. Rectè administrare sacramenta, secundum institutionem diuinam. 3. Præire ecclesiæ bono exemplo plo vitæ Christianæ : Per omnia teipsum præbens exemplar bonorum operum. 4. Diligenter attendere gregi : Attendite vos ipsos, & totum gregem. 5. Seruire judiciis ecclesiæ. 6. Dare operam, vt habeatur ratio pauperum.
units.tr: The duties of the ministers of the Church in general are: (1) to set forth faithfully and skilfully the true and entire doctrine of the law and the gospel, so that the Church may understand it; (2) to administer the sacraments rightly, according to the divine institution; (3) to go before the Church with a good example of Christian life: In all things showing yourself a pattern of good works; (4) to attend diligently to the flock: Take heed to yourselves and to the whole flock; (5) to serve the judgments of the Church; (6) to take care that account is kept of the poor.

units.la: V. Quibus sit committendum ministerium.
units.tr: V. To whom the ministry is to be committed.

units.la: Quibus & qualibus ab ecclesia ministerium debeat committi, disserè Paulus docet in epistola ad Timotheum & Titum. Summa est: ecclesiæ ministerium debet committi i. Viris, non mulieribus : Mulieres in ecclesia docere non permitto. 2. Habenti bonum testimonium in ecclesia, & extra eam. Oportet episcopum esse irreprehensum: & habere bonum testimonium ab extraneis, ne in probrum incidat, & laqueum diaboli. 3. Διδακτικὸν, hoc est, recte intelligentibus doctrinam, & habentibus mediocria dona ad eam rectè proponendam, & docendam publicè in ecclesia. Oportet episcopum esse διδακτικὸν, hoc est, idoneum ad docendum: qui non erubescat, & qui rectè sermonem veritatis secare possit: ἀντεχόμενον τοῦ κατὰ τὴν διδαχὴν πιστοῦ λόγου τῆς ἀληθείας : Tenacem fidelis illius sermonis, qui ad doctrinam facit: vt possit etiam exhortari per doctrinam sacram, & contradicentes convincere.
units.tr: Paul teaches clearly in his epistles to Timothy and Titus by whom and of what sort of people the ministry of the Church ought to be committed. The sum is this: the ministry of the Church ought to be committed (1) to men, not to women: I do not permit women to teach in the Church. (2) To one who has a good testimony both within the Church and outside it: A bishop must be blameless, and must have a good testimony from outsiders, lest he fall into reproach and the snare of the devil. (3) To one who is didaktikon [διδακτικὸν], that is, who understands the doctrine rightly and has at least moderate gifts for setting it forth correctly and teaching it publicly in the Church: A bishop must be didaktikon [διδακτικὸν], that is, apt to teach, who is not ashamed, and who can rightly divide the word of truth, holding firm to the faithful word of the teaching [ἀντεχόμενον τοῦ κατὰ τὴν διδαχὴν πιστοῦ λόγου τῆς ἀληθείας], so that he may also exhort by sound doctrine and convince those who contradict.

units.la: DE CÆREMONIIS.
units.tr: ON CEREMONIES.

units.la: Quoniam pars altera quarti præcepti est cæremonalis ; non incommodè aliquid de cæremoniis hoc loco subjicitur. I. II. Quid sint cæremoniæ. III. Quid differant à moralibus. IV. Quotuplices sint. An ecclesia cæremonias instituere liceat.
units.tr: Since the second part of the fourth commandment is ceremonial, something about ceremonies may fittingly be added here. I. What ceremonies are. II. How ceremonies differ from moral works. III. How many kinds of ceremonies there are. IV. Whether the Church may institute ceremonies.

units.la: I. Quid sint cæremoniæ.
units.tr: I. What ceremonies are.

units.la: Cæremonia, vel cærimonia, Græcè θρησκεία omnis divinus cultus Romanis appellatus est, ab oppido Cære, in quo simulacra Deorum contra Gallos seruata fuerant, teste Liu. l. 5. Macrobius à cærendo deducit. In ecclesia cæremoniæ vocantur actiones externæ & solennes, institutæ in ministerio ecclesiastico, ordinis, vel significationis causa.
units.tr: Among the Romans, caeremonia or caerimonia (in Greek threskeia [θρησκεία]) was the name for all divine worship. Livy, book 5, says it came from the town of Caere, where images of the gods had been kept safe against the Gauls. Macrobius derives it from cærere. In the Church, ceremonies are called the external and solemn actions instituted in the ecclesiastical ministry for the sake of order or signification.

units.la: II. Quomodo cæremoniæ ab operibus moralibus differant.
units.tr: II. How ceremonies differ from moral works.

units.la: Differunt cæremoniæ à moralib. 1. Cæremoniæ sunt temporariæ: moralia perpetua. 2. Moralia semper fiunt similiter: cæremoniæ non semper similiter: quia sæpe variant secundū ædificationem. 3. Cæremoniæ significant, moralia significatur. 4. Moralia habent fines & scopus cæremonialium: cæremonialia sunt determinata in specie. 5. Moralia ut genus: cæremonialia subserviunt moramoralibus. De discriminibus legum caeremonialium & moralium Mosaicarum, vide supra quaest. 2. de lege.
units.tr: Ceremonies differ from moral works in the following ways: (1) ceremonies are temporary, moral works are perpetual; (2) moral works are always done in the same way, ceremonies are not always done in the same way, because they often vary according to what builds up the Church; (3) ceremonies signify, moral works are what is signified; (4) moral works are the ends and scope of ceremonial things, whereas ceremonial things are determined in their particular form; (5) moral works are as the genus, while ceremonial works serve the moral works. For the differences between the ceremonial and moral laws of Moses, see above, question 2 on the law.

units.la: III. Quotuplices sint caeremoniae.
units.tr: III. How many kinds of ceremonies there are.

units.la: Caeremoniae sunt duplices: alia ab ipso Deo praeceptae, alia ab hominibus traditae. A Deo praecepta caeremonia sunt cultus Dei, & non nisi ab ipso Deo mutari possunt. Suntq; vel sacrificia, vel sacramenta. Sacrificia sunt caeremoniae diuinitus institutae, quibus nos certam obedientiam offerimus & praestamus Deo. Sacramenta, sunt caeremoniae diuinitus institutae, quibus Deus nobis certa beneficia testatur ac praestat. Ab Ecclesia instituta caeremoniae non sunt cultus Dei, & mutari possunt ecclesiae consilio, si sint probabiles causae.
units.tr: Ceremonies are of two kinds: some are commanded by God himself, others are handed down by men. Ceremonies commanded by God are the worship of God, and they can be changed only by God himself. These are either sacrifices or sacraments. Sacrifices are ceremonies divinely instituted, by which we offer and render to God the obedience due to him. Sacraments are ceremonies divinely instituted, by which God attests and bestows certain benefits upon us. Ceremonies instituted by the Church are not the worship of God, and they may be changed by the counsel of the Church if there are probable reasons.

units.la: IV. An ecclesiae caeremonias instituere liceat.
units.tr: IV. Whether the Church may institute ceremonies.

units.la: Potest ac debet ecclesia quasdam caeremonias instituere: quia sine determinatione circumstantiarum non potest observari genus, hoc est, moralis cultus Dei. Adhibitis tamen conditionibus Ecclesia caeremonias instituere debet: quae 1. non sint impia, sed conformes verbo Dei. 2. non sint superstitiosa, quibus affingatur vel cultus, vel meritum, vel necessitas, vel quae fiant cum scandalo. 3. non sint nimia, hoc est, non nimis multae, nec nimis operosae & graves. 4. non inutiles aut otiosa, sed quae spectent ad aedificationem.
units.tr: The Church can and should institute certain ceremonies, because the genus, that is, the moral worship of God, cannot be observed without the determination of circumstances. Yet when the Church institutes ceremonies it ought to observe these conditions: (1) they must not be impious, but conformable to the Word of God; (2) they must not be superstitious, that is, they must not have attached to them worship, merit or necessity, nor be performed with offence; (3) they must not be excessive, that is, not too many, nor too laborious and burdensome; (4) they must not be useless or idle, but such as tend to edification.

units.la: QVAESTIO CIV. Quid nobis iniungit Deus in quinto praecepto?
units.tr: QUESTION 104. What does God enjoin on us in the fifth commandment?

units.la: RESPONSIO.
units.tr: ANSWER.

units.la: Vt parentibus, atque adeo omnibus, qui nobis praesunt, debitum honorem, amorem & fidem praestemus, nosque ipsorum fidelibus praeceptis & castigationibus ea, qua par est, obedientia submittamus: Tum etiam, vt eorum vitia & mores nostra patientia toleremus, illud semper cogitantes, Deum nos illorum manu velle {c}ducere ac regere.
units.tr: That we should show the honour, love and faithfulness due to parents, and indeed to all who rule over us, and submit ourselves to their faithful commands and corrections with the obedience that is fitting. Also, that we should bear their faults and manners with patience, always remembering that God wishes to lead and govern us through their hand.

units.la: EXPLICATIO.
units.tr: EXPLANATION.

units.la: Sequuntur leges secundae tabulae, quarum obedientia quidem aeque ad Deum spectat, atque primae tabulae praecepta, sed opera immediate circa homines versantur. Obiectum enim eius immediatum est proximus, mediatum Deus.
units.tr: Next come the laws of the second table. Obedience to them concerns God just as much as the precepts of the first table do, but these duties are directed immediately towards human beings. For their immediate object is the neighbour, and their mediate object is God.

units.la: Summam obedientiae secundae tabulae Christus complexus est: Diliges proximum tuum sicut teipsum: Regulam intelligendi praecepta secundae tabulae idem hanc tradit: Quaecunque volueritis ut faciant vobis homines, ita & vos facite eis: ista est lex & prophetae. De tota secunda tabula idem Christus dicit: secundum praeceptum est simile primo, hoc est, secunda tabula est similis primae: quod intelligendum est 1. de eodem genere cultus praecipui, qui in utraque tabula praecipitur, & anteponitur caeremoniis. 2. de eodem genere poena, nempe aeternae, quae utriusque tabulae violatoribus infligitur. 3. de coherentia dilectionis Dei & proximi, tanquam causae & effectus, qua fit, ut neutra sine altera praestari possit.
units.tr: Christ summed up the whole obedience of the second table: You shall love your neighbour as yourself. The same Christ gives the rule for understanding the precepts of the second table: Whatever you wish that men would do to you, do so to them; for this is the law and the prophets. Concerning the whole second table, the same Christ says: The second commandment is like the first, that is, the second table is like the first. This must be understood (1) of the same kind of worship, which is commanded in both tables and is placed above ceremonies; (2) of the same kind of punishment, namely eternal punishment, which is inflicted on the violators of both tables; (3) of the connection between love of God and love of neighbour, as cause and effect, by which it comes about that neither can be rendered without the other.

units.la: Est igitur obedientia secundae tabulae necessaria, & Deus eam non minus flagitat, quam obedientiam primae tabulae. 1. Ut hac obedientia etiam ipse colatur, & dilectio ipsius dilectione proximi propter ipsum exerceatur. 2. Ut per dilectionem proximi ostendatur conformitas hominum cum Deo. 3. Ut conservetur humana societas à Deo propter sui nominis celebrationem ordinata.
units.tr: The obedience of the second table is therefore necessary, and God demands it no less than the obedience of the first table: (1) so that by this obedience God himself is also worshipped, and love of neighbour is exercised for his sake; (2) so that through love of neighbour the conformity of men with God is shown; (3) so that human society, ordained by God for the celebration of his name, may be preserved.

units.la: QUINTUM
units.tr: THE FIFTH

units.la: porro praeceptum de honore parentum (quod Hieronymus diserte vocat quintum in ordine) in secunda tabula la primum ponitur. 1. Quia est fundamentum & nervus obedientiae reliquorum praeceptorum secundae tabulae. Stante enim obedientia inferiorum erga superiores, qui obedientiam sequentium praeceptorum Dei nomine aliis praecipere, & tueri debent: stabit etiam obedientia reliqua. 2. Quia additam habet specialem promissionem longaevitatis, tanquam singularis beneficii, obtemperantibus huic praecepto praestandi.
units.tr: Moreover, the precept concerning the honour of parents (which Jerome expressly calls the fifth in order) is placed first in the second table. (1) Because it is the foundation and sinew of the obedience owed to the other precepts of the second table. For if the obedience of inferiors towards superiors stands firm, those who must enjoin and protect the obedience of the following precepts in God's name over others, then the remaining obedience will also stand. (2) Because it carries an added special promise of long life, as a singular benefit for those who obey this precept.

units.la: Duas vero habet partes: praeceptum & promissionem. Praeceptum est: Honora patrem & matrem. Finis praecepti est, ut conservetur ordo politicus, qui est ordo sancitus à Deo in officiis mutuis superiorum & inferiorum. Superiores sunt omnes, quos Deus aliis regendis & defendendis praefecit. Inferiores sunt, quos regendos & defendendos aliis subiecit. Superiores comprehenduntur nomine patris & matris, & sunt 1. Parentes ipsi, qui nos genuerunt. 2. Tutores & curatores pupillorum. 3. Praeceptores, doctores, ministri ecclesiae. 4. Magistratus superiores & inferiores. 5. Seniores. Hi igitur omnes, aut quicunque alii nobis praesunt, parcenparentum nomine intelliguntur: & sunt à nobis honorandi: quia hos omnes Deus nobis dat parentum loco, & ipsi parentum munere funguntur, & sunt quasi vicarij Dei in nobis regendis & tutandis, substituti à Deo in locum parentum: cum crescere coepisset hominum malitia.
units.tr: The precept has two parts: the command and the promise. The command is: Honour your father and your mother. The purpose of the precept is that the political order be preserved, which is the order sanctioned by God in the mutual duties of superiors and inferiors. Superiors are all those whom God has set over others to rule and defend. Inferiors are those whom he has subjected to others to be ruled and defended. Superiors are comprehended under the name of father and mother, and they are (1) parents themselves, who begot us; (2) guardians and curators of orphans; (3) teachers, doctors and ministers of the Church; (4) higher and lower magistrates; (5) elders. All these, then, or whoever else rules over us, are understood under the name of parents, and they are to be honoured by us. For God gives all of them to us in the place of parents, and they perform the office of parents, and they are as it were God's vicars in governing and protecting us, substituted by God in the place of parents, since the malice of men had begun to grow.

units.la: Parentes autem potius quam alios gubernatores Deus nominat & honorari jubet. 1. Quia patria potestas & gubernatio prima & antiquissima est in genere humano. 2. Quia haec est maxime amabilis hominibus, ut ei & propter eam se facile submittant. 3. Cum erga parentes sit maxima obligatio: atrocior est horum contemptus, & severius à Deo damnatur & punitur.
units.tr: God names parents, rather than other rulers, and commands that they be honoured, for these reasons: (1) because paternal power and government is the first and most ancient in the human race; (2) because this is the most lovable to men, so that they readily submit to it and for its sake; (3) since the obligation towards parents is greatest, their contempt is more monstrous, and it is condemned and punished more severely by God.

units.la: Sanciturigitur hoc praecepto non tantum honor perentum, sed omnium superiorum: vicissim occidentia non tantum liberorum: sed omnium inferiorum.
units.tr: By this precept, therefore, not only the honour of parents is enjoined, but that of all superiors; and conversely, not only the duty of children, but that of all inferiors.

units.la: Sanciuntur etiam officia mutua utrorumq;. Dum enim Deus jubet parentes honorari, jubet etiam eos esse, & quidem honore dignos esse, hoc est, officium parentum facere: & quia parentum etiam aliorum, qui praesunt, officia praecipit, quoniam parentum nomine sunt comprehensi. Sic & liberorum officia praecipit, dum honorem perentibus tribui jubet: ac non tantum liberorum, sed omnium inferiorum: quia omnes superiores ab inferioribus vult honorari.
units.tr: The mutual duties of both parties are also enjoined. For when God commands that parents be honoured, he also commands that they be such as are worthy of honour, that is, that they perform the duty of parents. And since he also prescribes the duties of other parents, that is, of those who rule, inasmuch as they are included under the name of parents, so too he prescribes the duties of children, when he commands that honour be given to parents; and not only of children, but of all inferiors, since he wills that all superiors be honoured by their inferiors.

units.la: Hinc ad objectionem facilis est responsio. Deus hoc praecepto tantum jubet honorari parentes, quod est officium inferiorum. Ergo hic nihil praecipit superioribus. Resp. per inuersionem. Ideo quia jubet parentes honorari, etiam de officiis superiorum praecipit. Nam cum superioribus tribuit nomen, etiam tribuit eis rem, seu id, à quo nomen habet: & si vult eos honore affici, vult etiam eos honore digna facere. Etsi autem interdum praesunt etiam mali, & honore indigni: tamen officium à personis discernendum, & quorum vitia detestari debemus, eorum officium propter divinam ordinationem honorandum est. Et quia propter officium honorandi sunt, quod est inferiores regere secundum voluntatem Dei, cuius sunt ministri: manifestum est, non nisi eatenus illis parendum esse, quatenus huius officij limites non egrediuntur.
units.tr: From this, the answer to an objection is easy. God, by this precept, commands only that parents be honoured, which is the duty of inferiors. Therefore here he prescribes nothing to superiors. Reply, by inversion. Because he commands that parents be honoured, he also prescribes the duties of superiors. For when he gives superiors the name, he also gives them the thing, or that from which the name derives; and if he wills them to be held in honour, he also wills them to make themselves worthy of honour. Although sometimes evil men, unworthy of honour, also rule, nevertheless the office must be distinguished from the persons, and though we ought to detest their vices, their office is to be honoured because of divine ordination. And because they are to be honoured for the sake of their office, which is to rule inferiors according to the will of God, whose ministers they are, it is clear that they are to be obeyed only so far as they do not step beyond the limits of this office.

units.la: Promissio est: Ut dies vivas in terra, quam Dominus Deus tuus dat tibi. Hanc promissionem Deus huic praecepto addidit, 1. Ut nos singulari beneficio, quasi praemio proposito, ad eius observationem magis invitet. 2. Ut testetur, quanti faciat honorem parentum, & quam graviter velit puniri honorem parentibus suum non tribuentes. 3. Quam denique obediencia tia huius praecepti sit necessaria, quandoquidem obedientia erga parentes ad totam reliquae legis obedientiam praeparatio est, & causa impulsiva. Hanc promissionem allegans Paulus ait, hoc praeceptum esse primum cum promissione, nempe speciali seu certi beneficij, quod praestantibus hanc obedientiam Deus promittit. Beneficium vero id, quod promittit, est longaevitas super terram.
units.tr: The promise is: That you may live long in the land which the Lord your God gives you.
