And forgive us our debts, as we also forgive our debtors. And lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil. For thine is the kingdom, and the power, and the glory, for ever. Amen.

units.la: EXPLICATIO.
units.tr: EXPLANATION.

units.la: Precationis à Christo nobis præscriptæ formula, quæ recitatur à duobus Euangelistis, Matthæo & Luca: est haud dubiè optima, certissima & perfectissima. Nam tradita est à Christo, qui vi et sapientia Dei, & cuius verba cœlestis Pater semper agnoscit & exaudit. Continet etiam breuissime omnes res petendas animæ & corpori necessarias. Denique est regula, ad quam omnes nostras preces congruere oportet.
units.tr: The form of prayer prescribed to us by Christ, which is recited by the two evangelists Matthew and Luke, is beyond doubt the best, most certain and most perfect. For it was delivered by Christ, who is the power and wisdom of God, and whose words the heavenly Father always acknowledges and heeds. It also contains, in the briefest compass, all the things needful to be asked for soul and body. Finally, it is the rule to which all our prayers ought to conform.

units.la: Quaritur verò, an sic alligati simus huic formulæ, vt inter prenostras preces congruere oportet.
units.tr: It is asked, however, whether we are so bound to this form that, in our prayers, we must agree with it, and may not use other words.

units.la: candum aliis verbis vti non liceat. Resp. Christus hanc formam nobis tradidit, non vt his verbis simus alligati, sed vt sciamus 1. quæ res: 2. quomodo petendæ sint. Est enim forma generalis de modo & de rebus petendis. Sæpe autem necessaria nobis sunt particularia, quæ in specie petere à Deo oportet, juxta dicta: Quicquid petieritis Patrem in nomine meo, dabit vobis. Qui non habet sapientiam, petat, & dabitur ei. Orate, ne fuga vestra fiat in hyeme. Hæc autem, quoad verba, non sunt in ista petitione. Idem ostendunt multa exempla precum in veteri & novo testamento, quæ quoad verba, ab hac formula variant, vt Josaphati, Salomonis, Danielis, ipsius Christi, apostolorum, &c. & sunt tamen exaudita à Deo. Vnde sequitur, formulam à Christo præscriptam quoad verba, esse indifferentem.
units.tr: Answer. Christ gave us this form not so that we should be bound to these words, but so that we might know (1) what things to ask for and (2) how they are to be asked. For it is a general form concerning the manner and the matters of prayer. Often, however, we need particular things, which we ought to ask of God in specific terms, according to the sayings: Whatever you ask the Father in my name, he will give you. If anyone lacks wisdom, let him ask, and it will be given him. Pray that your flight may not be in winter. These things, as to their wording, are not in that petition. Many examples of prayers in the Old and New Testaments show the same, which differ in wording from this form, such as those of Jehoshaphat, Solomon, Daniel, Christ himself, the apostles, and so on; and yet they were heard by God. Hence it follows that the form prescribed by Christ is indifferent as to its words.

units.la: Obiect. Nos non debemus esse sapientiores Christo. Ergo cum Christus nobis præscripserit certam formam precationis, nos contentos esse oportet, ac proinde malè facimus vrentes aliis precationum formulis. Resp. Non debemus discedere ab hac formula, si Christus ad eam velit nos esse alligatos. Sed ad hæc verba non vult nos alligatos esse: quia institutum eius, cum doceret discipulos orare, fuit, tradere breuem summam earum rerum, quæ nobis à Deo petendæ sunt.
units.tr: Objection. We ought not to be wiser than Christ. Therefore, since Christ has prescribed a certain form of prayer, we ought to be content with it, and accordingly we do wrong when we use other forms of prayer. Answer. We ought not to depart from this form if Christ had wished us to be bound to it. But he does not wish us to be bound to these words, because his purpose, when he taught the disciples to pray, was to hand down a brief summary of the things that we are to ask of God.

units.la: Inst. Quo nihil melius inueniri potest, illud est retinendum. Nos nec meliorem formam, nec meliora verba possumus inuenire, quàm sunt ipsius Christi. Ergo oportet nos & formam & verba Christi retinere. Resp. Non possumus meliorem formam inuenire, nec meliora verba, ad exprimendâ videlicet hanc eandem summam, quæ est tanquam genus omnium rerum petendarum. Genera enim hæc beneficiorum, quæ hic Christus præscripsit nobis petenda, non possunt meliori forma proponi. Sed Christus nos vult etiâ ad species descendere, & particularia beneficia petere pro necessitate. Est enim Christi formula nihil aliud, nisi series certarum classium seu generum, sub quam omnia beneficia spiritualia & corporalia referantur. Itaque jubens nos petere genera, jubet etiam petere species: & quæ hic sunt posita in genere, debemus eadem de causa explicare per species, vt inducamur in cogitationem necessitatis nostræ, & in desiderium petendi, vt necessitati nostræ subueniat Deus. Vt autem id possimus, opus est etiam specialibus formis precandi. Nam ad explicationem generum per species, alia forma opus est. Aliæ tamen precanprecandi formulæ debent omnes ad formulam à Christo præscriptam congruere. Hinc Augustinus ad Prob. dicit, omnes sanctorum preces, quæ in scriptura exstant, orationedominica contineri. Et addit esse liberum, aliis atq; aliis verbis, eadem tamen in orando dicere: sed non esse liberum, alia dicere.
units.tr: Inference. Whatever cannot be found better should be retained. We can find neither a better form nor better words than those of Christ himself. Therefore we must retain both the form and the words of Christ. Answer. We cannot find a better form, nor better words, for expressing, namely, this same summary, which is like the genus of all the things to be asked. For these general headings of benefits, which Christ here prescribes for us to ask, could not be set forth in a better form. But Christ wills us also to descend to the species, and to ask for particular benefits as need requires. For the formula of Christ is nothing other than a series of fixed classes or genera, under which all spiritual and bodily benefits are comprised. Therefore, in commanding us to ask for the genera, he also commands us to ask for the species; and what is put here in general we ought, for the same reason, to explain through particulars, so that we may be led to consider our need and to desire to ask, that God may come to our aid in our necessity. To do this, however, we also need particular forms of prayer. For a different form is needed for the explanation of the genera through the species. Yet all other forms of prayer ought to agree with the form prescribed by Christ. Hence Augustine, in his letter to Proba, says that all the prayers of the saints which exist in Scripture are contained in the Lord's Prayer. And he adds that it is free to say the same things in prayer in different words and different ways, but not free to say other things.

units.la: QVÆSTIO CXX.
units.tr: QUESTION CXX.

units.la: Cur præcipit Christus, vt ita DEVM compellemus: Pater noster?
units.tr: Why does Christ command us to address God thus: Our Father?

units.la: RESPONSIO.
units.tr: ANSWER.

units.la: Vt statim in ipso precationis exordio, conuenientem Dei filiis reuerentiam & fiduciam erga Deum in nobis excitet, quæ nostræ precationis fundamentum esse debet: nimirum, Deum propter Christum nobis patrem factum esse, & quæ vera fide ab eo petimus, nobis multo minus negare, quam parentes nostri nobis bona terrena denegant a.
units.tr: So that at the very beginning of the prayer he may stir up in us a reverence and confidence towards God fitting for the children of God, which ought to be the foundation of our prayer: namely, that God has become our Father for Christ's sake, and that he will much less deny us the things which we ask of him in true faith than our parents deny us earthly goods a.

units.la: EXPLICATIO.
units.tr: Explanation.

units.la: Orationis dominicæ tres sunt partes: exordium, petitiones, & clausula.
units.tr: The Lord's Prayer has three parts: the introduction, the petitions, and the closing words.

units.la: Exordium est: [Pater noster, qui es in cœlis.] Huius duæ sunt partes. 1. Compellatio veri Dei: Pater noster. 2. Et eius descriptio: qui es in cœlis. Sic vero præfari nos docuit Christus, quia DEVS debito honore & reuerentia vult inuocari. Honor iste consistit 1. in vera agnitione. 2. fiducia. 3. obedientia. Obedientia complectitur veram dilectionem, timorem, spem, humilitatem & patientiam.
units.tr: The introduction is: Our Father, who art in heaven. It has two parts. (1) The address to the true God: Our Father. (2) His description: who art in heaven. Christ taught us to begin in this way because God wishes to be called upon with due honour and reverence. This honour consists (1) in true knowledge, (2) in trust, and (3) in obedience. Obedience includes true love, fear, hope, humility and patience.

units.la: Pater noster.] Deus Pater noster est, 1. ratione creationis. Qui fuit Adam, qui fuit Dei. 2. Ratione redemtionis ac receptionis in gratiam per Filium mediatorem. Christus est vnigenitus & naturalis Dei filius: nos naturâ filij iræ, à Deo propter Christum in filios adoptati sumus. 3. Ratione sanctificationis seu regenerationis per Spiritum in Christo.
units.tr: Our Father. God is our Father (1) by right of creation, since Adam, who was made, was God's. (2) By right of redemption and reception into grace through the Son as Mediator. Christ is the only-begotten and natural Son of God; we, by nature children of wrath, have been adopted as sons by God for Christ's sake. (3) By right of sanctification, or regeneration, through the Spirit in Christ.

units.la: Deus ergo à nobis vult inuocari, Pater. 1. Propter agnitionem & inuocationem veram: vt agnoscamus & inuocemus verum Deum, qui est Pater Domini nostri Iesu Christi, qui per & propter Filium mediatorem nos adoptauit in filios, cum essemus hostes ipsius:
units.tr: God therefore wishes to be called upon by us as Father. (1) On account of true knowledge and invocation, so that we may acknowledge and call upon the true God, who is the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who through and for the sake of the Son as Mediator adopted us as sons when we were his enemies.

units.la: Asscendo ad Patrem meum, & Patrem vestrum: & qui nos per Spiri- tum sanctum regenerat, & omnibus necessariis donat. 2. Propter reuerentiam: vt excitetur in nobis vera erga ipsum reuerentia: quoniam ipse pater est noster, ideo nos tali erga eum reuerentia affecti simus, quali erga patre affectos decet esse liberos, & quidem gratuito adoptatos, atq; indignos beneficiis Dei. 3. Propter fiduciam: vt accendatur in nobis certa exauditionis fiducia, quod nobis daturus sit omnia, quae ad salutem nostram pertinent. Quoniam enim Deus, quem inuocamus, est pater noster, & quidem tantopere nos diligens, vt Filium suum vnigenitum tradiderit pro nobis in mortem, quomodo nobis cum eodem non daret omnia ad salutem nostram necessaria? 4. Propter memoriam creationis. Solos autem sic orantes vult exaudire, quia in iis solis assectionis finem suorum beneficiorum.
units.tr: "I ascend to my Father and your Father; and he who regenerates us through the Holy Spirit and gives us all necessary things." (2) On account of reverence, so that true reverence towards him may be stirred up in us. Since he is our Father, we ought to be disposed towards him with that reverence which children ought to have towards a father, and indeed children who have been adopted freely and are unworthy of God's benefits. (3) On account of trust, so that a firm confidence of being heard may be kindled in us, that he will give us all things that pertain to our salvation. For since God, whom we invoke, is our Father, and loves us so greatly that he gave his only-begotten Son to death for us, how would he not give us with him all things necessary for our salvation? (4) On account of the memory of creation. He wishes to hear only those who pray in this way, because in them alone he finds the end of his benefits, that is, love.

units.la: Obiect. 1. Inuocamus Patrem: ergo non Filium & Spiritum sanctum. Resp. Nego consequentiam, quia in operibus externis & in cultu, nominata vna Trinitatis persona, non excluduntur aliae. Deinde nomen Patris, vt & nomen Dei, quando opponitur creaturis, accipitur essentialiter: quando autem ponitur loco alia persona diuinitatis, sumitur personaliter. Hoc igitur loco nomen Patris essentialiter sumitur, & rationes manifestae sunt. 1. Quia hic non cum alia diuinitatis persona ponitur nomen Patris, sed opponitur creaturis, a quibus inuocatur. Sic & ab Esaia Christus dicitur Pater aeternitatis, siue seculi. 2. Quia si maxime personaliter intelligatur nomen patris, nominata vna persona, non excluduntur aliae, & de operibus externis & cultu fit mentio, vt dictum est. 3. Non possumus cogitare Dum Patrem, nisi in Filio mediatore. Filius autem fecit nos filios per Spiritum sanctum, qui ideo dicitur Spiritus vivificans. 4. Christus jubet se inuocare: Si quid petieritis in nomine meo, ego faciam 5. Christus etiam dat Spiritum sanctum. Ergo est ille ipse, a quo petimus.
units.tr: Objection 1. We invoke the Father; therefore not the Son and the Holy Spirit. Answer. I deny the consequence, because in external works and in worship, the naming of one person of the Trinity does not exclude the others. Further, the name Father, like the name God when it is set against creatures, is taken essentially; but when it is put in place of another person of the Godhead, it is taken personally. Here, then, the name Father is taken essentially, and the reasons are plain. (1) Because here the name Father is not set alongside another person of the Godhead, but is set against creatures, by whom he is invoked. Thus Christ is also called by Isaiah Father of eternity, or of the age. (2) Because even if the name Father is understood most of all personally, when one person is named the others are not excluded, and external works and worship are being mentioned, as has been said. (3) We cannot think of the Father except in the Son the Mediator. But the Son made us sons through the Holy Spirit, who for this reason is called the Spirit who gives life. (4) Christ commands us to invoke him: If you ask anything in my name, I will do it. (5) Christ also gives the Holy Spirit. Therefore he is that very one from whom we ask.

units.la: Obi.2. Christus dicitur & est noster frater. Ergo non est pater. R. Est frater noster, quatenus homo: pater vero, quatenus Deus, conditor & redemtor noster. Pater aeternitatis.
units.tr: Objection 2. Christ is called and is our brother. Therefore he is not Father. Answer. He is our brother as he is man; but Father as he is God, our creator and redeemer. Father of eternity.

units.la: Objecti 3. Propter quem Pater nos recipit in gratiam, is non est Pater, quia recipiens & propter quem recipit, non est idem. Propter Filium Pater nos recipit in gratiam. Ergo Filius non est Pater, seu idem Deus, qui Pater. Resp. De identitate personae maior est vera, & totum argumentum. De identitate essentiae maior est falsa. Essentia enim idem est recipiens nos, & propter quem recipimur: etsi persona alius est recipiens Pater, alius, propter quem recipimur, Filius. Inst. Etiam respectu essentiae non potest idem esse recipiens, & propter quem recipit. Resp. Non potest idem esse, eodem respectu. Filius autem est reci- piens, & propter quem recipit, diverso respectu. In quantum enim Filius est idem cum Patre Deus ὑμογνητος, est is, qui recipit. In quantum vero est mediator μεσίτης, est is, propter quem recipimur in gratiam.
units.tr: Objection 3. He on account of whom the Father receives us into grace is not the Father, because the one receiving and the one on account of whom he receives are not the same. The Father receives us into grace on account of the Son. Therefore the Son is not the Father, or the same God who is the Father. Answer. As to identity of person, the major premise is true and the whole argument is valid. As to identity of essence, the major premise is false. For the one receiving us and the one on account of whom we are received are the same in essence, although in person the receiving Father is one and the one on account of whom we are received, the Son, is another. Objection (further). Even with respect to essence, the one receiving and the one on account of whom he receives cannot be the same. Answer. They cannot be the same in the same respect. But the Son is both the one receiving and the one on account of whom he receives, in different respects. For insofar as the Son is God of the same essence [ὁμοούσιος] with the Father, he is the one who receives; but insofar as he is Mediator [μεσίτης], he is the one on account of whom we are received into grace.

units.la: Noster. Curron Pater meus? sed noster?
units.tr: Our. Why not "my Father"? But "our"?

units.la: 1. Ut excitet in nobis fiduciam exauditionis. Quia enim nos non oramus soli, sed tota ecclesia unanimiter orat: Deus preces totius ecclesiæ non reijcit, sed exaudit, juxta promissionem: Vbi duo aut tres sunt congregati in nomine meo, illic sum in medio eorum. Atque ideo domi oras ecclesia nesciente. Re. Pij & tota ecclesia sem- per orant pro se, & pro omnibus membris affectu ac desiderio. Amor & desiderium est qualitas habitualis, manens etiam, cum dormis: non est passio cito transiens. Ergo etiam tunc, cum tu solus domi oras verbis, tota ecclesia tecum orat affectu. 2. Ut nos admoneat dilectionis mutuæ, qua prædicti Christiani pro se invicem orare debent. Ideo autem hac voce in ipso precationis exordio nos dilectionis mutuæ admonuit. 1. Quia sine vera proximi dilectione non est vera precatio, neq; possumus statuere, nos à Deo exaudiri. Si enim accedimus ad Deum non habentes proximi dilectionem, neq; ipse nos habebit pro fratribus, filiosque Dei. 2. Quia sine proximi dilectione non est vera fides: sine fide non est vera precatio. Quicquid enim non est ex fide, peccatum est.
units.tr: (1) That he may stir up in us confidence of being heard. For since we do not pray alone, but the whole Church prays with one accord, God does not reject the prayers of the whole Church, but hears them, according to the promise: Where two or three are gathered in my name, there I am in the midst of them. And so you pray at home while the Church does not know it. Answer: the godly and the whole Church always pray for themselves and for all the members, with feeling and desire. Love and desire are a habitual quality, which remains even when you sleep; they are not a passion that quickly passes. Therefore, even then, when you alone pray at home in words, the whole Church prays with you in feeling. (2) That he may remind us of the mutual love by which Christians so endowed ought to pray for one another. He admonished us of mutual love in this very word at the beginning of the prayer. (a) Because without true love of neighbour there is no true prayer, and we cannot be sure that we are heard by God. For if we come to God without love of neighbour, he will not hold us as brothers and sons of God. (b) Because without love of neighbour there is no true faith, and without faith there is no true prayer. For whatever is not of faith is sin.

units.la: Obiect. Patris est nihil denegare liberis. Deus nobis multa denegat. Ergo non est pater noster. Resp. ad maiorem. Patris est nihil denegare liberis, quod sit necessarium & salutare: est vero patris denegare liberis, non necessaria, inutilia, noxia. Nihil salutare nobis denegat Deus. Dat enim nobis bona spiritualia & corporalia necessaria, vtilia & salutaria.
units.tr: Objection. It is the father's part to deny his children nothing. God denies us many things. Therefore he is not our Father. Answer to the major. It is the father's part to deny his children nothing that is necessary and salutary; but it is the father's part to deny his children what is not necessary, useless or harmful. God denies us nothing that is salutary. For he gives us spiritual and bodily goods that are necessary, useful and salutary.

units.la: QVÆSTIO CXXI.
units.tr: QUESTION 121.

units.la: Cur additur: Qui es in cœlis? RESPONSIO.
units.tr: Why is it added: Who art in heaven? ANSWER.

units.la: Ne de cœlesti maiestate Dei humile quippiam aut terrenum cogitemus a, simul etiam, vt ab eius omnipotentia, quæcunque animo & corpori sunt necessaria, expectemus b.
units.tr: Lest we think anything low or earthly about the heavenly majesty of God, and at the same time, that we may look to his omnipotence for everything necessary for soul and body.

units.la: EXPLICATIO.
units.tr: EXPLICATIO.

units.la: Altera pars exordij: Qui es in cœlis, id est, cœlestis. Cœlum hic significat habitaculum Dei, sanctorum angelorum, & beatorum hominum, de quo DEVS apud prophetam: Cœlum mihi thronus est. Et Christus: In domo Patris mei mansiones multæ sunt. Est quidem Deus immensa sua essentia ubique. Sed in cœlo esse & habitare dicitur, quia ibi est gloriosus magis, quam in mundo, & ibi immediatè se patefacit. Jubet autem nos Dominus Patrem sic compellare: Qui es in cœlis. 1. Vt ostendat antithesin patrum terrenorum, & huius patris, seu vt separet eum à patribus terrenis, & nos cogitemus esse talem Patrem, 1. Qui non sit terrenus, sed cœlestis, gloriosè habitans in cœlo. 2. Qui cœlestigloria & maiestate ubique regnet, præsideat omnibus rebus atque universum orbem à se conditum sua providentia gubernet. 3. Qui sit omnis corruptionis & mutationis expers. 4. Qui etiam ibi, hoc est in cœlo potissimum se coram angelis patefaciat, atque ostendat, qualis sit Pater, quam bonus, quamque potens ac dives.
units.tr: The second part of the introduction: Who art in heaven, that is, heavenly. Here "heaven" signifies the dwelling place of God, of the holy angels and of blessed men, of which God speaks through the prophet: Heaven is my throne. And Christ says: In my Father's house there are many mansions. God indeed is everywhere present by his immense essence. But he is said to be in heaven and to dwell there, because there he is more glorious than in the world, and there he reveals himself immediately. The Lord bids us address the Father thus: Who art in heaven. (1) So that he may show the contrast between earthly fathers and this Father, or so that he may separate him from earthly fathers, and we may think of such a Father: (a) who is not earthly but heavenly, dwelling gloriously in heaven; (b) who by heavenly glory and majesty reigns everywhere, presides over all things, and governs by his providence the whole world created by him; (c) who is free from all corruption and change; (d) who also there, that is, chiefly in heaven, reveals himself before the angels and shows what the Father is like, how good, how powerful and how rich.

units.la: 2. Propter fiduciam: vt excitet in nobis fiduciam exauditionis: quia si pater est noster, & quidem summa præditus bonitate, quam in cœlis patefacit maximè, ergo vult etiam omnia ad salutem necessaria nobis dare: & si hic pater noster est in cœlo, Dominus, omnipotentia præditus, qua nos possit juvare, ergo facilime nobis dare poterit, quæ ab ipso petimus.
units.tr: (2) On account of confidence: so that he may stir up in us confidence that we shall be heard. For if he is our Father, and indeed endowed with the highest goodness, which he reveals most of all in heaven, then he certainly wishes to give us all things necessary for salvation; and if this our Father is in heaven, a Lord endowed with omnipotence by which he can help us, then he will be able most easily to give us the things we ask of him.

units.la: 2. Propter reverentiam: vt reverentiam sui in nobis excitet. Quoniam enim Pater hic noster tantus est Dominus cœlestis, ubiq; regnans, qui corpus & animam abijcere potestin gehennam: reveremur ergo eius maiestatem, & summa animi & corporis demissione ad ipsum accedamus.
units.tr: (3) On account of reverence: so that he may stir up reverence for himself in us. For since this our Father is so great a Lord, a heavenly one, reigning everywhere, who has power to cast body and soul into hell, we therefore revere his majesty and approach him with the utmost humility of mind and body.

units.la: QVÆSTIO CXXII.
units.tr: QUESTION 122.

units.la: Quæ est prima petitio.
units.tr: What is the first petition?

units.la: RESPONSIO.
units.tr: ANSWER.

units.la: Sanctificetur nomen tuum: hoc est; Da principio, vt te recte agnoscamus a, & lucentem in omnibus operibus tuis omnipotentiam, sapientiam, bonitatem, justitiam, misericordiam & veritatem tuam veneremur, prædicemus & celebremus b: Deinde, vt vniuersam vitam nostram,
units.tr: Hallowed be thy name: that is, grant first that we may rightly acknowledge you a, and that we may worship, proclaim and celebrate your omnipotence, wisdom, goodness, justice, mercy and truth, which shine forth in all your works b. Then grant that we may always direct our whole life, our thoughts, words and actions, to this end, so that your most holy name is not dishonoured on our account, but is rather made illustrious with honour and praise.

units.la: a Psal. 8. b Psal. 145. stram, cogitationes, sermones & actiones, eò semper dirigamus, ne sanctissimum nomen tuum propter nos contumelia afficiatur, sed honore potius & laudibus illustretur.
units.tr: a Psal. 8. b Psal. 145. ...so that all our life, our thoughts, words and actions may always be directed to this end, that your most holy name be not dishonoured on our account, but rather be made illustrious with honour and praise.

units.la: EXPLICATIO.
units.tr: EXPLICATIO.

units.la: Sequitur altera pars precationis, sex petitiones continens. In hac petitio de sanctificatione nominis Dei primum locum obtinet, quia est finis & scopus reliquarum. Omnium enim actionum & precum nostrarum finis debet esse gloria Dei. Finis autem est primus in cogitatione, licet ultimus in executione. Primo igitur finis reliquarum petitionum petendus est, si velimus recte petere reliqua, juxta praeceptum: Quaerite primum regnum Dei, & justitiam eius; & cetera adjicientur vobis.
units.tr: There follows the second part of the prayer, which contains six petitions. In this one, the petition for the sanctification of God's name holds the first place, because it is the end and aim of the rest. For the end of all our actions and prayers ought to be the glory of God. The end is first in thought, although last in execution. Therefore, if we want to pray rightly for the rest, we must first ask for the end of the other petitions, according to the precept: Seek first the kingdom of God and his righteousness, and all these things will be added to you.

units.la: Videndum verò hic: I. Quid sit nomen Dei. II. Quid sanctum, & sanctificare.
units.tr: Here we must consider: I. What the name of God is. II. What holy and sanctify mean.

units.la: I. Quid sit Nomen Dei.
units.tr: I. What the Name of God Is.

units.la: Nomen Dei significat 1. Deum ipsum: Qui diligunt nomen tuum. Psallam nomini Domini. invocabo nomen tuum. aedificabit domum nomini meo. 2. Attributa & opera Dei. Omnipotens nomen eius Iehova Zelotes nomen eius. 3. Mandatum Dei, seu voluntatem & authoritatem divinam. Venio ad te in nomine Iehova Dei nostri. Baptizate eos in nomine Patris, Filij, & Spiritus sancti. 4. Cultum, fiduciam, celebrationem & professionem Dei. Mori paratus sum pro nomine Domini Iesu. Baptizetur unusquisque in nomine Iesu Christi: Matth.28. nomen Dei utrumque significat, mandatum & professionem. Hic prima & secunda significatione accipitur pro ipso Deo, & pro omnibus eius attributis atque operibus, in quibus maiestas Dei elucet.
units.tr: The name of God signifies (1) God himself: Those who love your name. I will sing to the name of the Lord. I will call upon your name. He shall build a house for my name. (2) The attributes and works of God: His name is Almighty; his name is Jehovah, the Zealous. (3) The command of God, or the divine will and authority: I come to you in the name of Jehovah our God. Baptize them in the name of the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit. (4) The worship, trust, celebration and profession of God: I am ready to die for the name of the Lord Jesus. Let each one be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ (Matt. 28). The name of God signifies both the command and the profession. Here it is taken in the first and second senses, for God himself, and for all his attributes and works, in which the majesty of God shines forth.

units.la: II. Quid sit sanctum, & sanctificare.
units.tr: II. What Holy and Sanctify Mean.

units.la: Sanctum significat 1. Ipsum Deum sanctissimum & purissimum, seu sanctitatem essentialem increatam, quae est Deus ipse. Omnes enim Dei virtutes & attributa sunt essentialis sanctitas. Sic angeli acclamant Deo: Sanctus, sanctus, sanctus DEVS Zebaoth. 2. Sanctitate in creaturis, hoc est, conformitatem cum Deo, quae in piis est inchoata, in angelis integra. 3. Ordinationem nem ad vsus sacros : hoc modo sanctum dicitur, quod est vsui sacro distinatum, vt templum Hierosolymitanum, altare, vasa, sacerdotes.
units.tr: Holy signifies (1) God himself, most holy and most pure, or the uncreated essential holiness, which is God himself. For all the virtues and attributes of God are essential holiness. So the angels cry out to God: Holy, holy, holy is the LORD God of hosts. (2) Holiness in creatures, that is, conformity to God, which is begun in the godly and complete in the angels. (3) Dedication to sacred uses: in this way that is called holy which is set apart for sacred use, such as the temple at Jerusalem, the altar, the vessels, the priests.

units.la: His tribus modis & verbū sanctificandi sumitur. Primo sanctificare est id, quod jam in se sanctum est, sanctū agnoscere, venerari, celebrare. Hoc significato nos Deum, qui est ipsa sanctitas, sanctificamus. 1. Cum eum agnoscimus talem, qualem se patefecit verbo & operibus, hoc est, quando ea de essentia, voluntate, operibus, on nipotentia, bonitate, sapientia & reliquis attributis eius cognoscimus ac sentimus, quæ de iis cognoscere & sentire in verbo suo ipse præcepit. 2. Cum Deum esse sanctū non modo cognoscimus, sed etiam profitemur & celebramus, idq; tum verbis & confessione, tum factis & vita sancta. 3. Cum veram doctrinam, agnitionem & professionem sanctitatis Dei, item preces & actiones omnes referimus ad eum finem, ad quem Deus vult referri, nempe ad ipsius celebrationem & gloriam.
units.tr: The verb to sanctify is also used in three ways. First, to sanctify is to acknowledge, venerate and celebrate what is already holy in itself. In this sense we sanctify God, who is holiness itself. (1) When we acknowledge him as he has revealed himself by word and works, that is, when we know and feel those things about his essence, will, works, omnipotence, goodness, wisdom and other attributes which he himself has commanded us in his word to know and feel about them. (2) When we not only know God to be holy, but also profess and celebrate it, both in words and confession and in deeds and a holy life. (3) When we refer true doctrine, the knowledge and profession of God's holiness, and likewise all our prayers and actions, to the end to which God wills them to be referred, namely, his own celebration and glory.

units.la: Secundo, sanctificare est id, quod in se sanctum non est, sed pollutum, sanctum facere, & a sordibus segregare. Sic λέγ& sanctificauit massam humanam, quam assumsit, naturam eam, quæ in nobis est polluta, in se præseruans à contagio peccati, & perfecta sanctitate exornans. Sic Deus & Christus sanctificant ecclesiam, condonatione peccatorum & sanctificatione per Spiritum sanctum, & continuatione vtriusque. Sic nos jubemur nos sanctificare, hoc est, præseruare ab omni inquinamento catnis. Estote sancti.
units.tr: Second, to sanctify is to make holy what is not holy in itself but polluted, and to separate it from defilement. Thus Christ sanctified the human nature which he assumed, preserving it from the contagion of sin, which is polluted in us, and adorning it with perfect holiness. Thus God and Christ sanctify the Church, by the forgiveness of sins, by sanctification through the Holy Spirit, and by the continuing of both. Thus we are commanded to sanctify ourselves, that is, to preserve ourselves from every pollution of the flesh: Be holy.

units.la: Tertio, sanctificare est id, quod in se, siue sanctum, siue mendium est, in vsum sanctum destinare. Sic Pater sanctificauit Filium, hoc est, ad officium mediatoris ordinauit & misit in mundum. Et Deus sanctificauit diem sabbati, templum, victimas, sacerdotes: & Christus seipsum sanctificauit pro electis, hoc est, sanctam hostiam tradidit: & cibus sanctificatur per verbum Dei & preces.
units.tr: Third, to sanctify is to set apart for holy use what is holy or unclean in itself. Thus the Father sanctified the Son, that is, appointed him to the office of mediator and sent him into the world. And God sanctified the Sabbath day, the temple, the sacrifices, the priests; and Christ sanctified himself for the elect, that is, he offered himself as a holy sacrifice; and food is sanctified by the word of God and prayer.

units.la: Ex his prima & secunda significatio huc pertiner. Petimus enim sanctificationem Dei, non modo à nobis, sed etiam in nobis: hoc est, petimus: 1. Vt Deus agnitione sanctitatis, & sanctissimi sui nominis nos illustret: seu, (vt habet catechesis) vt ipsum rete agnoscamus, & lucentem in omnibus operibus eius omnipotentiam, sapientiam, bonitatem, justitiam, misericordiam, & veritatem eius veneremur, prædicemus & celebremus. 2. Vt nomen suum etiam in nobis sanctum faciat, & nos magis ac magis sanctificer ac regeneret, vt in vniuersa vita nostra omne contumeliam sanctissimi nominis ipsius auertamus : omnibus verò modis illud honore ac laudibus illustremus.
units.tr: Of these, the first and second senses pertain here. For we ask for the sanctification of God not only from us but also in us. That is, we ask: (1) That God would enlighten us by the knowledge of his holiness and of his most holy name; or, as the catechism puts it, that we may rightly know him, and venerate, proclaim and celebrate his omnipotence, wisdom, goodness, justice, mercy and truth, shining forth in all his works. (2) That he would make his name holy in us also, and sanctify and regenerate us more and more, so that in our whole life we may turn away every reproach to his most holy name, and in every way honour and praise it.

units.la: Summa: petimus 1. Vt vera agnitione sanctitatis suæ nos illustret. 2. Vt nos doceat verafide & pœnitentia, & regeneret spiritu suo, vt simus sancti, sicut ipse sanctus est. 3. Vt det nobis animum taprofitendi illam nominis diuini sanctitatem verbis ac factis, ad suam ipsius laudem & gloriam, vt vera agnitione, confessione & conformitate vitæ per nos glorificetur, & ab omnibus idolis ac rebus profanis separetur.
units.tr: In sum, we ask: (1) That he would enlighten us with the true knowledge of his holiness. (2) That he would teach us true faith and repentance, and regenerate us by his Spirit, so that we may be holy as he himself is holy. (3) That he would give us the mind to profess that holiness of the divine name by words and deeds, to his own praise and glory, so that through us he may be glorified by true knowledge, confession and conformity of life, and be set apart from all idols and profane things.

units.la: Obiectio 1. Quod per se est sanctum, non potest sanctificari. Nomen Dei per se est sanctum. Non est ergo, cur illud petamus sanctificari. Resp. ad maiorem per distinct. Non potest sanctificari secundo significato, hoc est, sanctum ex non sancto effici, quod per se sanctum est. Potest vero sanctificari primo & tertio significato: hoc est, pro sancto agnosci, laudari & celebrari, in sanctum vsum dirigi, quod in se est sanctum vel ἀδιάφορον. Sic nos petimus sanctificari nomen Dei, vt quod in se est sanctum, etiam sanctum agnoscatur & celebretur. Deus sanctificat nos faciendo sanctos ex non sanctis. Nos sanctificamus Deum non faciendo eum sanctum, sed de ipso cognoscendo & prædicando, quæ de sua sanctitate vult nos scire ac prædicare.
units.tr: Objection 1. What is holy in itself cannot be sanctified. The name of God is holy in itself. Therefore there is no reason to ask that it be sanctified. Answer to the major premise, with a distinction: it cannot be sanctified in the second sense, that is, made holy out of what is not holy, since what is holy in itself already is. But it can be sanctified in the first and third senses: that is, acknowledged as holy, praised and celebrated, and directed to holy use, as with what is holy in itself or indifferent [ἀδιάφορον]. So we ask that the name of God be sanctified, so that what is holy in itself may also be acknowledged and celebrated as holy. God sanctifies us by making us holy out of what is not holy. We sanctify God not by making him holy, but by knowing and proclaiming about him what he wills us to know and proclaim about his holiness.

units.la: Obiect. 2. Quod nostrum est facere, id non debemus petere, vt faciat alius. Nostrum est sanctificare nomen Dei. Ergo non debemus petere, vt Deus sanctificet. Perinde enim videmur facere, atque si discipulus jussus à præceptore, vt diligenter studeat, oret præceptorem, vt ipse pro se hoc faciat. Resp. ad maiorem per distinctionem. Quod est nostrum facere, non debemus petere, vt faciat alius, si id per nos & viribus nostris facere possimus. Quod vero non possumus, recte à Deo petimus, vt vires id faciendi nobis suggerat. Nomen Dei sanctificare ipsi non possumus. Recte igitur petimus à Deo, vt nobis vires suggerat, quo nomen ipsius à nobis sanctificetur, & ipse nomen suum sanctum in nobis sanctificet.
units.tr: Objection 2. What is our task to do, we ought not to ask another to do for us. Sanctifying the name of God is our task. Therefore we ought not to ask God to sanctify it. For we would seem to act just as if a pupil, ordered by his teacher to study diligently, were to beg the teacher to do this for him. Answer to the major premise, by distinction: what is our task we ought not to ask another to do, if we can do it through ourselves and by our own powers. But what we cannot do, we rightly ask of God, that he would supply us with the power to do it. We cannot sanctify the name of God ourselves. Therefore we rightly ask God to supply us with the power, so that his name may be sanctified by us, and that he himself may sanctify his holy name in us.

units.la: QVÆSTIO CXXIII. Quæ est secunda petitio?
units.tr: QUESTION CXXIII. What is the second petition?

units.la: RESPONSIO.
units.tr: ANSWER.

units.la: Veniat regnum tuum: hoc est; Regas nos ita verbo & spiritu tuo, vt nos tibi magis magisque subijciamus a: Conserua & auge Ecclesiam tuam b, destrue opera diaboli, omnemque potentiam se aduersus maiestatem tuam esse-rentem c. rentem: irrita fac omnia consilia, quæ contra verbum tuum capiuntur e, quoad plene tandem ac perfecte regnes d, cum eris omnia in omnibus e.
units.tr: Thy kingdom come: that is, rule us by your word and your Spirit, so that we submit ourselves to you more and more. Preserve and increase your Church, destroy the works of the devil and every power that raises itself against your majesty, and make void all the counsels that are devised against your word, until at last you reign fully and perfectly, when you are all in all.

units.la: a Psalm.143. verf.10. & 119,4. Matth.6,31. b Psalm.51. verf.20, & 122, 6. c1 Ioh.3, 8. Rom.16, 20. d Apoc.22, 20. Rom.8, 22.23, c1 Corinth.15. verf.28.
units.tr: a Psalm.143. verf.10. & 119,4. Matth.6,31. b Psalm.51. verf.20, & 122, 6. c1 Ioh.3, 8. Rom.16, 20. d Apoc.22, 20. Rom.8, 22.23, c1 Corinth.15. verf.28.

units.la: EXPLICATIO.
units.tr: EXPLICATIO.

units.la: Adueniat regnum tuum: sensus est: per continuos progressus inter nos vigeat, augeatur, semperque noua accessione dilaretur ac multiplicetur regnum tuum, quod tu, ô Deus, habes in ecclesia.
units.tr: Thy kingdom come: the sense is that your kingdom, which you, O God, have in the Church, may flourish among us through continual progress, may grow, and may be continually enlarged and multiplied by fresh accessions.

units.la: Quæstiones de Regno Dei præcipuæ sunt: I. Quid sit regnum Dei. II. Quotuplex sit regnum Dei. III. Quis huius regni sit caput seu rex. IV. Qui eius cives & subditi. V. Qua leges. VI. Qua bona. VII. Qui hostes. VIII. Vbi administretur. IX. Quamdiu duret. X. Quomodo ad nos veniat. XI. Quare orandum, vt veniat.
units.tr: The chief questions concerning the Kingdom of God are: I. What the kingdom of God is. II. How many kinds of kingdom of God there are. III. Who is the head or king of this kingdom. IV. Who are its citizens and subjects. V. What are its laws. VI. What are its goods. VII. Who are its enemies. VIII. Where it is administered. IX. How long it lasts. X. How it comes to us. XI. Why we must pray that it comes.

units.la: I. Quid sit regnum Dei.
units.tr: I. What the kingdom of God is.

units.la: Regnum in genere est politiæ forma, in qua summa potestas est penes vnam personam, quæ donis & virtutibus præ cæteris ornata omnibus præest, secundum iustas, honestas, ac certas leges, defendendo bonos, & puniendo malos. Regnum Dei est, in quo solus Deus regnat, & dominium exercet in omnes creaturas, præcipuè vero ecclesiam gubernat & seruat. Hoc regnum est vniuersale. Regnum verò speciale, quod in ecclesia exercet, est missio Filij à Patre, inde ab initio mundi, vt instituat & colligat ecclesiam ex genere humano per verbum & Spiritum sanctum, regat, seruet, ac defendat eam contra hostes, suscitet ex morte, tandemque hostibus in æternas pœnas abiectis, eam ornet cœlesti gloria, vt sit DEVS omnia in omnibus, & ab ecclesia in æternum celebretur.
units.tr: In general, a kingdom is a form of polity in which supreme power rests with one person, who, adorned with gifts and virtues beyond others, presides over all, governing by just, honourable and certain laws, defending the good and punishing the wicked. The kingdom of God is that in which God alone reigns and exercises dominion over all creatures, and especially governs and preserves the Church. This kingdom is universal. The special kingdom, however, which he exercises in the Church, is the mission of the Son from the Father, from the beginning of the world, to institute and gather the Church from the human race through the Word and the Holy Spirit, to rule, preserve and defend it against its enemies, to raise it from death, and at last, when its enemies have been cast into eternal punishments, to adorn it with heavenly glory, so that God may be all in all and may be praised by the Church for ever.

units.la: Hæc descriptio ex partibus collecta est: quæ sunt 1. Missio Filij mediatoris in mundum, 2. Institutio & conseruatio ministerij per eum. 3. Collectio ecclesiæ ex genere humano voce euangelij & efficacia Spiritus sancti operantis in electis veram fidem & pœnitentiam. 4. Gubernatio ecclesiæ perpetua. 5. Conseruatio eius in hac vita, & defensio contra hostes. 6. Abiectio hostium in æternas pœnas. 7. Resuscitatio ecclesiæ ad vitam æternam. 8. Glorificatio eius in vita æterna, cum Deus erit omnia in omnibus. De hoc regno dicitur: Constitui regnum meum super Sion montem sanctum meum. Dominare in medio inimicorum tuorum. Regnum meum non est de hoc mundo.
units.tr: This description is gathered from its parts, which are: 1. the mission of the Son, the Mediator, into the world; 2. the institution and preservation of the ministry through him; 3. the gathering of the Church from the human race by the voice of the gospel and by the efficacy of the Holy Spirit working in the elect true faith and repentance; 4. the perpetual government of the Church; 5. its preservation in this life and its defence against enemies; 6. the casting of the enemies into eternal punishments; 7. the raising of the Church to eternal life; 8. its glorification in eternal life, when God will be all in all. Of this kingdom it is said: I have set my king upon my holy hill of Zion. Rule in the midst of your enemies. My kingdom is not of this world.

units.la: Ex quibus intelligitur, regnum Dei non esse mundanum sed spirituale, quod etiam variis in euangelio parabolis docetur, & Dominus ostendit, respondens Pilato: Regnum meum non est de hoc mundo. Hoc regnum venire, propagari & defendi hic petimus.
units.tr: From these things it is understood that the kingdom of God is not worldly but spiritual, which is also taught by various parables in the gospel, and which the Lord showed when he answered Pilate: My kingdom is not of this world. It is this kingdom that we here pray may come, be propagated and be defended.

units.la: II. Quotuplex sit regnum Dei.
units.tr: II. How many kinds of kingdom of God there are.

units.la: Vnum quidem est regnum Dei reipsa: sed differt modo administrationis. Aliter enim in hac vita administratur, aliter in cælo. Vulgo igitur distinguitur in regnum gratia & gloria. Idem est, si dicatur, aliud esse inchoatum in hac vita, aliud consummatum post hanc vitam. Vtrumq; hic petimus, vt regnum Dei inchoetur in nobis in hac vita, & tandem consummetur in nobis post hanc vitam. Est tamen idem regnum, gradib. distinctum, & gubernationis modo. Inchoatum regnum opus habet mediis, & turbatur ab hostibus: in consummato regno cessabunt media & hostes: quia ecclesia erit perfectè glorificata, sine malo culpæ & pœnæ, & Deus erit omnia in omnibus.
units.tr: There is indeed one kingdom of God in reality, but it differs in the mode of its administration. For it is administered one way in this life and another way in heaven. Commonly, therefore, it is distinguished into the kingdom of grace and the kingdom of glory. It is the same thing if one says that one part is begun in this life and another part is consummated after this life. Here we pray for both: that the kingdom of God may be begun in us in this life, and at last be consummated in us after this life. Yet it is the same kingdom, distinguished by degrees and by the mode of government. The begun kingdom has need of means and is disturbed by enemies; in the consummated kingdom the means and the enemies will cease, because the Church will be perfectly glorified, without the evil of guilt and punishment, and God will be all in all.

units.la: Hinc soluitur quæstio ex loco Pauli: Tradet regnum Deo & Patri. Quod attinet ad formam administrationis, Christus Patri tradet regnum post glorificationem ecclesiæ, id est, desinet facere officium mediatoris. Non erit opus conuersione, expurgatione peccati, defensione contra hostes, non colliget ecclesiam, non suscitabit mortuos, non glorificabit, non perficiet, quia erunt perfecti: non docebit, quia omnes erunt θεοδίδακτοι: prophetiæ abolebuntur, linguæ desinent, cognitio abolebitur: quia postquam aduenerit, quod perfectum est, tunc quod ex parte est, cessabit. His igitur mediis, quib. nunc colligitur & seruatur ecclesia, non erit opus. Nullus erit hostis amplius: ecclesia gloriosè regnabit cum Christo, & Deus erit omnia in omnibus, hoc est, patefaciet & communicabit se beatis immediatè. In ea urbe (quæ est regnū illud consummatum) templum non vidi. Dominus enim Deus omnipotens templum illius est, id est, agnus. Neque vrbs ista eget sole vel luna, vt luceant in ea. Nam gloria Dei illustrauit eam, & lucerna eius est agnus.
units.tr: Hence the question raised from the passage of Paul is resolved: He will deliver up the kingdom to God and the Father. As far as the form of administration is concerned, Christ will deliver up the kingdom to the Father after the glorification of the Church, that is, he will cease to perform the office of Mediator. There will be no need of conversion, of the purging away of sin, of defence against enemies; he will not gather the Church, will not raise the dead, will not glorify, will not perfect, because all will be perfect; he will not teach, because all will be taught by God (theodidaktoi [θεοδίδακτοι]); prophecies will be abolished, tongues will cease, knowledge will be abolished, because when that which is perfect has come, then that which is in part will cease. Therefore, these means by which the Church is now gathered and preserved will not be needed. There will be no enemy any more; the Church will reign gloriously with Christ, and God will be all in all, that is, he will reveal and impart himself immediately to the blessed. In that city (which is that consummated kingdom) I saw no temple. For the Lord God Almighty is its temple, that is, the Lamb. Nor does that city need the sun or the moon to shine in it. For the glory of God has illumined it, and its lamp is the Lamb.

units.la: III. Quis
units.tr: III. Who is the king and head in the kingdom of God.

units.la: III. Quis sit rex & caput in regno Dei.
units.tr: III. Who is the king and head in the kingdom of God.

units.la: Huius regni caput & rex vnus est, quia vnus est Deus Pater, Filius & Spiritus sanctus. Pater regnat per Filium & Spiritum sanctum. Singulari modo regni huius caput est Christus. Quia est Deus sedens ad dextram Patris, hoc est, pari potentia & gloria cum Patre omnia gubernans. 2. Quia est mediator, hoc est, illa persona, per quam Pater immediatè agit, & dat Spiritum sanctum. Ego mittam vobis eum à Patre. Constituit eum caput super omnia ipsi ecclesiæ.
units.tr: The head and king of this kingdom is one, because there is one God, Father, Son and Holy Spirit. The Father reigns through the Son and the Holy Spirit. In a singular way the head of this kingdom is Christ, (1) because he is God sitting at the right hand of the Father, that is, governing all things with equal power and glory with the Father; (2) because he is the Mediator, that is, that person through whom the Father acts immediately and gives the Holy Spirit. I will send you him from the Father. He has appointed him head over all things for the Church.

units.la: IV. Qui cives ac subditi in regno Dei.
units.tr: IV. Who are the citizens and subjects in the kingdom of God.

units.la: Cives huius regni sunt 1. Angeli sancti & confirmati in cœlo, 2. Homines beati in cœlo, qui vocantur ecclesia triumphans. 3. Homines pij seu conuersi in hac vita, habentes adhuc multas carnis & peccatorum reliquias: & dicuntur ecclesia militans. 4. Hypocritæ: cives quidem visibilis ecclesiæ, vocati, sed non electi: non reuera cives regni Dei, sed potius mancipia diaboli: sicut Judæi à Christo cives recusati. De his dicitur: Multi primi erunt vltimi, hoc est, qui volunt haberi pro primis, & tamen non sunt, erunt vltimi, hoc est, declarabuntur esse nulli in regno Dei.
units.tr: The citizens of this kingdom are: (1) the holy angels, confirmed in heaven; (2) the blessed men in heaven, who are called the Church triumphant; (3) the godly, or converted men in this life, who still have many remnants of the flesh and of sins, and who are called the Church militant; (4) hypocrites: citizens indeed of the visible Church, called, but not chosen; not truly citizens of the kingdom of God, but rather slaves of the devil, just as the Jews were rejected as citizens by Christ. Of these it is said: Many who are first will be last, that is, those who want to be considered first, and yet are not, will be last, that is, will be declared to be nothing in the kingdom of God.

units.la: V. Quæ leges huius regni,
units.tr: V. What are the laws of this kingdom.

units.la: Leges, quibus administratur hoc regnum, sunt I. Verbum Dei seu doctrina legis & euangelij. II. Efficacia Spiritus sancti per verbum in cordibus electorum operantis & regnantis.
units.tr: The laws by which this kingdom is governed are: I. the Word of God, or the doctrine of the law and of the gospel; II. the efficacy of the Holy Spirit working and reigning in the hearts of the elect through the Word.

units.la: VI. Qua bona rex subditis suis communicet.
units.tr: VI. What good things the king communicates to his subjects.

units.la: Nullum est regnum, quod non spectet ad commodum subditorum. Ideo Aristoteles scribit ad Alexandrum: regnum non esse ὕβριν, sed ὠφέλιμον. Hoc igitur regnum habet sua etiam bona. Ea sunt spiritualia & æterna Christi beneficia, vera fides, conuersio, remissio peccatorum, justitia, conseruatio in ea, Spiritus sanctus, lætitia in Deo, glorificatio, vita æterna. Si Filius vos liberauerit, verè liberi eritis. Regnum Dei est justitia, & pax, & gaudium per Spiritum sanctum. Pacem meam relinquo vobis, pacem meam do vobis, non prout mundus dat, ego do vobis.
units.tr: No kingdom exists that does not aim at the advantage of its subjects. Therefore Aristotle writes to Alexander that kingship is not hybris but ōphelimon [ὕβρις, ὠφέλιμον]. This kingdom therefore has its own good things as well. These are the spiritual and eternal benefits of Christ: true faith, conversion, forgiveness of sins, righteousness, preservation in it, the Holy Spirit, joy in God, glorification, and eternal life. If the Son shall make you free, you will be truly free. The kingdom of God is righteousness, and peace, and joy in the Holy Spirit. My peace I leave to you, my peace I give to you; not as the world gives, do I give to you.

units.la: VII. Qui hostes regni Dei.
units.tr: VII. Who are the enemies of the kingdom of God.

units.la: Hostes regni Dei sunt diaboli & homines impij: quorum alij sunt in ecclesia: vt hypocritæ, qui sibi nomen ciuium regni arrogant, cum nihil minus sint: alij extra ecclesiam, & palam hostes, stes, vt Turcæ, Judæi, Samosatenians, Arriani, & quotquot erro-res defendunt contra fundamentum.
units.tr: The enemies of the kingdom of God are the devils and wicked men. Of these, some are in the Church, such as hypocrites, who arrogate to themselves the name of citizens of the kingdom, though they are anything but; others are outside the Church and are openly enemies, such as the Turks, the Jews, the Samosatenes, the Arians, and as many as defend errors against the foundation.

units.la: VIII. Vbi hoc regnum administretur.
units.tr: VIII. Where this kingdom is administered.

units.la: Regnum hoc, quoad inchoationem & collectionem in his terris sic administratur, vt non sit inclusum in certo loco, insula, provincia, populo: sed sparsum per totum terrarum orbem. Volo viros precari quolibet loco. Vbicunque sunt duo vel tres congregati in nomine meo, illic suam in medio eorum. Ex hoc regno nunquam egredimur, si maneamus in vera fide. In coelo administratur hoc regnum quoad consummationem & perfectionem. Cum profectus fuero, & paravero vobis locum, rursum veniam, & assumam vos ad meipsum, vt, vbi ego sum, & vos sitis. Vbi ego fuero, ibi & minister meus erit. Pater, quos dedisti mihi, velim, vt vbi ego sum, & illi sint mecum. Obviam ei rapiemur, & erimus cum Domino semper.
units.tr: As regards its beginning and gathering on these earths, this kingdom is administered in such a way that it is not enclosed in a certain place, island, province or people, but is spread through the whole orb of the earth. I want men to pray in every place. Wherever two or three are gathered together in my name, there I am in the midst of them. We never go out of this kingdom, if we remain in the true faith. As regards its consummation and perfection, this kingdom is administered in heaven. When I have gone and prepared a place for you, I will come again and take you to myself, so that where I am, you may be also. Where I shall be, there also my minister will be. Father, those whom you have given me, I desire that where I am, they also may be with me. We shall be caught up to meet him, and we shall always be with the Lord.

units.la: IX. Quamdiu duret regnum Dei.
units.tr: IX. How long the kingdom of God lasts.

units.la: Inchoatio seu collectio huius regni durat ab initio mundi usque ad finem, quia omnibus temporibus fuerunt, sunt, & erunt aliqua membra verae ecclesiae, sive multa, sive pauca, ex hoc mundo ad regnum Dei aggregenda. Consummatio seu perfectio durabit inde a glorificatione piorum in aeternum usque. Deinde erit finis, cum tradiderit Filius regnum Deo & Patri: nempe quoad formam administrationis regni. Vide supra qu. 2.
units.tr: The beginning or gathering of this kingdom lasts from the beginning of the world until its end, because in all times there have been, are, and will be some members of the true Church, whether many or few, to be gathered from this world into the kingdom of God. The consummation or perfection will last from the glorification of the godly onward into eternity. Then will come the end, when the Son shall have delivered up the kingdom to God and the Father, namely as regards the form of the administration of the kingdom. See above, question 2.

units.la: X. Quomodo ad nos veniat.
units.tr: X. How it comes to us.

units.la: Regnum Dei ad nos venit quatuor modis: 1. Praedicatione evangelii, qua patefit lux verae ac coelestis doctrinae. 2. Conversione, cum aliqui convertuntur ad Deum, fideque & poenitentia a Deo donantur. 3. Profectu seu incremento, quando pij capiunt incrementa: seu dona fidelium propria perpetuo augmento augentur in conversis. Qui justus est, justificetur adhuc: qui sanctus est, sanctificetur adhuc. 4. Consummatione, & glorificatione ecclesiae in secundo Christi adventu. Etiam veni, Domine Iesu.
units.tr: The kingdom of God comes to us in four ways: (1) by the preaching of the gospel, by which the light of the true and heavenly doctrine is revealed; (2) by conversion, when some are converted to God and are given faith and repentance by God; (3) by progress or increase, when the godly make advances, or the gifts of the faithful are continually increased in the converted: He who is righteous, let him be justified still; he who is holy, let him be sanctified still; (4) by consummation and glorification of the Church at the second coming of Christ. Even so, come, Lord Jesus.

units.la: XI. Quare orandum, vt veniat.
units.tr: XI. Why we ought to pray that it may come.

units.la: Petere debemus, vt veniat regnum Dei, inchoatum & consummatum. 1. Propter gloriam Dei, seu propter sanctificationem nominis Dei. Vt enim sanctificemus nomen Dei, necesse est, vt ipse nos regat verbo & Spiritu. Nisi enim regnum suum Deus in nobis erigat, & eripiat nos e regno diaboli, nunquam sanctificabimus nomen eius, sed potius polluemus. Est igitur necessaria hæc secunda petitio propter primam. 2. Propter salutem & consolationem nostram: quia Deus tantum petentibus dare vult hoc regnum, sicut & solis petentibus dat Spiritum sanctum.
units.tr: We ought to ask that the kingdom of God may come, both begun and completed. (1) For the glory of God, or for the sanctification of God's name. For us to sanctify the name of God, he himself must rule us by his Word and Spirit. Unless God establishes his kingdom in us and rescues us from the kingdom of the devil, we will never sanctify his name but rather defile it. This second petition is therefore necessary for the sake of the first. (2) For our salvation and consolation, because God is willing to give this kingdom only to those who ask, just as he gives the Holy Spirit only to those who ask.

units.la: Ex his intelligitur, quid hic petamus. Petimus 1. Vt Deus person filium meditatorem in hunc mundum inde ab initio missam conseruet institutum ministerium. 2. Colligat ecclesiam ministerio verbi & virtute Spiritus sancti. 3. Regat ecclesiam, & nos eius membra, spiritu suo sancto emolliat corda nostra, regenerat voluntates nostras, nosq; totos sibi conformes faciat. 4. Defendat nos totamque ecclesiam contra hostes tyrannos. 5. Abiiciat hostes in æternas poenas. 6. Tandem liberet ecclesiam & nos omnes ab omnibus malis & in æterna vita glorificet.
units.tr: From these things it is clear what we ask for here. We ask (1) that God the Father preserve the Mediator Son, sent into this world from the beginning, and the ministry he instituted; (2) that he gather the Church by the ministry of the Word and the power of the Holy Spirit; (3) that he rule the Church, and us as its members, soften our hearts by his Holy Spirit, regenerate our wills, and make us wholly conformed to himself; (4) that he defend us and the whole Church against tyrannical enemies; (5) that he cast these enemies into eternal punishments; (6) that he finally free the Church and all of us from every evil and glorify us in eternal life.

units.la: Obiect. Quod propter preces nostras nec citius nec tardius fit, frustra petitur, eoque non est petendum. Regnum Dei, seu liberatio ecclesiæ ab omnibus malis & miseriis, nec citius nec tardius propter preces nostras futura est, quam Deus decreuit. Ergo liberatio ecclesiæ frustra petitur. Resp. Maior negatur. Sic enim de omnibus beneficiis liceret statuere, seu ratiocinari, non esse petenda, cum omnia sint in Dei consilio posita.
units.tr: Objection. What is done neither sooner nor later because of our prayers is asked for in vain, and so it is not to be asked. The kingdom of God, or the deliverance of the Church from all evils and miseries, will come neither sooner nor later because of our prayers than God has decreed. Therefore the deliverance of the Church is asked for in vain. Answer. The major premise is denied. For by this reasoning one could decide that no benefits are to be asked for, since all things are placed within God's counsel.

units.la: Inst. 1. Sed alia beneficia Deus promisit cum conditione petitionis. Resp. Etiam liberatio ab omnibus malis, tantum contingeris in illa die, qui sub cruce gementes illam expectunt, & desideRant: & quidem vt hæc liberatio quam primum eueniat secundum Dei decretum, & nullus electus excludatur.
units.tr: Objection 1. But God has promised other benefits on the condition that they be asked for. Answer. Deliverance from all evils also comes only on that day to those who groan under the cross and long for it; and indeed it comes so that this deliverance may arrive as soon as possible according to God's decree, and no elect person is shut out.

units.la: Inst. 2. At non debemus petere, vt liberationem ecclesiæ Deus maturet, quia id fieret cum iactura multorum electorum, qui nondum sunt nati. Resp. Cum petimus, vt liberationem ecclesiæ Deus maturet, petimus etiam, vt quicunq; adhuc sunt reliqui electi, ad vnum omnes cito congregentur: idque 1. vt cito liberetur ecclesia & quiescant pii omnes à laboribus suis. 2. vt cito fiat finis scelerum & impietatum, & hostes abiiciantur in poenas. 3. vt cito gloria Dei, liberatione ecclesiæ & hostium abiectione, manifestetur. Hanc liberationem nostri & totius ecclesiæ petere debemus, modo & nos cum ecclesia liberari tandem velimus. Qui vero aduentum Domini non expectunt, illis etiam non venient.
units.tr: Objection 2. But we ought not to ask that God hasten the deliverance of the Church, because that would happen at the cost of many of the elect who are not yet born. Answer. When we ask that God hasten the deliverance of the Church, we also ask that all the elect who still remain be gathered together quickly, every one of them; and this (1) so that the Church may quickly be delivered and all the godly may rest from their labours; (2) so that the end of crimes and impieties may quickly come and the enemies be cast into punishment; (3) so that the glory of God may quickly be made manifest through the deliverance of the Church and the overthrow of its enemies. We ought to ask for this deliverance of ourselves and of the whole Church, provided that we too are at last willing to be delivered with the Church. But those who do not await the coming of the Lord, for them it will not come either.

units.la: QVÆSTIO CXXIV. Quæ est tertia petitio?
units.tr: QUESTION 124. What is the third petition?

units.la: RESPONSIO.
units.tr: ANSWER.

units.la: Fiat voluntas tua, quemadmodum in cælo, sic etiam in terra: hoc est; Da, vt nos & omnes homines, voluntati propriæ renunciantes a, tuæ voluntati, quæ sola est sancta, prompte & sine vllo murmure pareamus b: atque ita singuli mandatum nobis munus fideliter & alacriter exsequamur c, quemadmodum faciunt angeli in cœlo d.
units.tr: Thy will be done, on earth as it is in heaven: that is, grant that we and all men, renouncing our own willa, may promptly and without any murmuring obey thy will, which alone is holyb, and so each of us may faithfully and eagerly carry out the duty entrusted to usc, just as the angels do in heavend.

units.la: EXPLICATIO.
units.tr: EXPLANATION.

units.la: I. Hic considerandum: II. Quid sit Dei voluntas. III. Quid hic petamus: & quomodo hæc petitio differat à secunda. IV. Quare necessaria hæc petitio. V. Cur addatur: sicut in cœlo.
units.tr: I. Here we must consider: II. What the will of God is. III. What we ask for here, and how this petition differs from the second. IV. Why this petition is necessary. V. Why "as in heaven" is added.

units.la: I. Quid sit Dei voluntas?
units.tr: I. What is the will of God?

units.la: Voluntas Dei in scriptura significat 1. Mandatum Dei. Ministri facientes voluntatem eius. Hæc est voluntas Dei, sanctificatio vestra, vt abstineatis à fornicatione. 2. Euentus vel potius decretum Dei de futuris euentibus, in quibus illud quotidie reuelatur: Non mea, sed tua voluntas fiat. Consilium meum stabit, & omnem voluntatem meam faciam. Voluntati eius quis resistet?
units.tr: In Scripture the will of God signifies: 1. The commandment of God: "Ministers doing his will"; "This is the will of God, your sanctification, that you abstain from fornication." 2. The event, or rather the decree of God concerning future events, in which that will is revealed every day: "Not my will, but thine, be done"; "My counsel shall stand, and I will do all my pleasure"; "Who shall resist his will?"

units.la: II. Quid hic petamus, & quomodo hæc petitio differat à secunda.
units.tr: II. What we ask for here, and how this petition differs from the second.

units.la: Fiat voluntas tua: sensus est: Effice, & da, vt nos homines faciamus voluntatem, non nostram, quæ est prava: sed tuam, quæ sola est iusta & sancta, tibique obtemperemus. Petimus igitur
units.tr: Thy will be done: the sense is: Bring it about and grant that we men may do the will, not our own, which is depraved, but thine, which alone is just and holy, and that we may obey thee. We therefore ask

units.la: 1. Abnegationem nostri, quæ duabus constat partibus. 1. Vt simus parati ad renunciandū omnibus affectib. nostris repugnantibus cum lege diuina. 2. Vt etiam ad suscipiendam crucem nostram simus parati, ac libenter in omnibus Deo subscribamus. Petimus ergo, vt Deus nobis largiatur gratiam suam, qua possimus abnegare gare voluntatem nostram prauam, atque omnia abiicere, quae voluntati eius repugnant.
units.tr: 1. For self-denial, which consists of two parts. (a) That we may be ready to renounce all our affections that resist the divine law. (b) That we may also be ready to take up our cross and gladly submit to God in all things. We therefore ask that God would bestow on us his grace, by which we may deny our depraved will and cast off all that opposes his will.

units.la: 2. Exsecutionem officii nostri rectam & promtam: vt quisque in sua vocatione possit Deo alacriter seruire, & voluntatem eius exsequi tam in communi, quam in proprio suo officio. Commune officium est, quod non à nobis solis sed pariter ab omnibus Christianis requiritur, & virtutes omnibus piis necessarias complectitur, vt sunt fides, conuersio, pietas, caritas, temperantia, &c. Proprium est, quod nostram, & cuiusque propriam vocationem concernit. De vtroque hic petimus, vt singuli in mandata sibi vocatione communi & propria permaneant, & officium faciant, Deo commissa cura de euentibus nostris: nobis autem, vt proprios labores faciamus.
units.tr: 2. For the right and prompt performance of our duty: that each in his own calling may serve God eagerly and carry out his will both in the common duty and in his own particular office. The common duty is that which is required not of us alone but equally of all Christians, and embraces the virtues necessary for all the pious, such as faith, conversion, godliness, love, temperance, etc. The particular duty is that which concerns our own calling and that of each person. For both we ask here that each may remain in the commands given him in his common and particular calling and perform his duty, the care of events being committed to God, while we ourselves do our own labours.

units.la: 3. Euentus diuinae voluntati non contrarios, vt scilicet eueniant ea, quae Deo placent.
units.tr: 3. Events not contrary to the divine will, namely that those things come to pass which are pleasing to God.

units.la: 4. Felices actionum & consiliorum successus, hoc est, vt pro immensa sua bonitate actiones, & studia, consilia, & labores nostros sic dirigere ac fortunate dignetur, vt eos non alii secundus quantus euentus quam quos ipse nouit suae gloriae & nostrae salutis maxime seruire posse. Vult enim Deus, nos etiam hoc a se petere, & sibi euentus committere: interim nos sedulo officium facere.
units.tr: 4. Happy success of actions and counsels: that is, that God in his immense goodness would deign so to direct and prosperously guide our actions, endeavours, counsels and labours, that they may have no other outcome than that which he himself knows can most serve his glory and our salvation. For God wills that we ask this of him too, and commit the outcomes to him, while meanwhile we diligently perform our duty.

units.la: Summa: petimus, vt Deus sepeliat in nobis prauas cupiditates, ipse vero solus agat in nobis suo spiritu, vt diuina gratia freti, officio nostro satisfaciamus.
units.tr: Summary: we ask that God would bury in us our depraved desires, and that he alone would act in us by his Spirit, so that, relying on divine grace, we may satisfy our duty.

units.la: Obiect. Praecedens petitio etiam petit, vt recte faciamus officium. Ergo haec est superuacanea. Resp. Non simpliciter idem hic petimus, quod prius. In priore petimus, vt Deus regnum suum in nobis inchoet, nos regendo per Spiritum sanctum, qui regeneret voluntatem nostram, vt officium nostrum recte facientes omnem obedientiam praestemus regi, sicut subditos regni Dei decet: In hac vero petimus, vt singuli officium suum recte faciant, conseruetur, & glorificetur ecclesia: hic, vt in ea vnusquisque recte officium faciat.
units.tr: Objection. The preceding petition also asks that we perform our duty rightly. Therefore this one is superfluous. Answer. We do not here ask simply the same thing as before. In the former we ask that God begin his kingdom in us, ruling us through the Holy Spirit, who regenerates our will, so that, performing our duty rightly, we may render all obedience to the King, as becomes subjects of God's kingdom. In this one, however, we ask that each person perform his duty rightly, that the Church may be preserved and glorified; the former asks that we may do our duty, this one asks that each may do his duty here, in the Church.

units.la: Obiter hic obseruetur trium petitionum cohaerentia, & discrimen. Sic cohaerent, vt vna sine altera non consistat, sed secunda seruiat primae, & tertia secundae. Non enim sanctificetur nomen Dei, nisi regnum eius veniat. Non venit regnum Dei, nisi positis mediis, quibus illud promouetur. Media vero sunt officia vocationis vnius cuiusque. Differunt vero hoc modo: In prima petimus sanctificationem siue veram agnitionem, & celebrationem Dei omniumq; operum & consiliorum eius. In secunda collectionem. nem, conseruationem & gubernationem ecclesiæ, vt Deus nos regat suo Spiritu & verbo, defendat & eripiat ab omnibus malis culpæ & pœnæ. In tertia, vt speciatim singuli in vocatione sua obtemperent Deo, hoc est, vnusquisque in proprio munere diligenter versetur, omnia ad Dei gloriam dirigat, & boni consulat, quicquid ipsi Deus immittit.
units.tr: Incidentally, the coherence and the distinction of the three petitions should be observed. They cohere so that one cannot stand without the other: the second serves the first, and the third serves the second. For the name of God is not sanctified unless his kingdom comes, and the kingdom of God does not come unless the means by which it is advanced are put in place; and the means are the duties of each one's calling. They differ thus: In the first we ask for the sanctification, that is, the true knowledge and celebration of God and of all his works and counsels. In the second, the gathering, preservation and governance of the Church, that God may rule us by his Spirit and Word, and defend and deliver us from all evils of guilt and punishment. In the third, that each person in particular may obey God in his calling, that is, that each may diligently engage in his own office, direct everything to the glory of God, and accept in good part whatever God sends upon him.

units.la: III. Quare necessaria sit hæc petitio.
units.tr: III. Why this petition is necessary.

units.la: Necessaria est hæc petitio, 1. Vt possit regnum Dei aduenire, quod secunda petitione optamus. Nisi enim Deus ipse efficiat, vt voluntatem eius quisque in suo officio faciat diligenter, non potest constitui, vigere, & conseruari inter nos regnū Dei. 2. Vt possumus esse cines regni eius. Non autem possumus ex nobis, propter naturæ nostriæ prauitatem, voluntatem Dei facere, si Deus ipse vires non suggerat. Non suggerit autem vires, nisi petamus. Ergo necesse est, vt petamus.
units.tr: This petition is necessary: (1) so that the kingdom of God, which we desire in the second petition, can come. Unless God himself brings it about that each person faithfully does his will in his own office, the kingdom of God cannot be established, flourish and be preserved among us. (2) So that we may be citizens of his kingdom. But we cannot do the will of God of ourselves, because of the wickedness of our nature, unless God himself supplies the strength. He does not supply that strength unless we ask. Therefore we must ask.

units.la: Obiect. Quod semper fit, & certo fiet, etiam nobis non petentibus, id non necesse est petere. Voluntas Dei semper fit, & certo fiet, etiam nobis non petentibus. Ergo non necesse est petere, vt fiat. Resp. 1. In maiore est fallacia non causæ. Non enim ideo petimus, vt voluntas Dei fiat, quasi nobis non petentibus ea non fieret, sed propter alias causas, nimirum vt fiat à nobis, & vt euentus à Deo decreti nobis sint salutares. Non enim salutares erunt nobis euentus, nisi voluntati diuinæ nos subijciamus, & illud tantum fieri petamus, quod ipse decreuit, & vult fieri. 2. Minor negatur, quæ est falsa, 1. de vocatione vniuscuiusque: quia qui non petunt, vt officium in sua vocatione facere possint rectè, fideliter & feliciter: ij nunquam illud facient. 2. De decretis diuinis: quia multos euentus decreuit Deus, sed ita, vt media etiam decreuerit.
units.tr: Objection. What will certainly happen always, even without our asking, need not be asked for. The will of God always happens and will certainly happen even if we do not ask. Therefore it is not necessary to ask that it be done. Answer. 1. The major premise contains the fallacy of non-cause. We do not ask so that the will of God may be done, as if it would not be done unless we asked, but for other reasons, namely that it may be done by us, and that the events decreed by God may be salutary for us. Events will not be salutary for us unless we submit ourselves to the divine will, and ask only for what he has decreed and wills to happen. 2. The minor premise is denied, because it is false: (1) concerning the calling of each person, since those who do not ask that they may perform their office in their calling rightly, faithfully and successfully will never do so; (2) concerning the divine decrees, since God has decreed many events, but in such a way that he has also decreed the means.

units.la: Inst. Decreta Dei sunt immutabilia. Ergo fient quæ Deus decreuit, etiam sine precibus nostris. Resp. ad antecedens. Decreta Dei non euentuum tantum seu finium, sed & mediorum ad fines sunt immutabilia. Finem enim Deus decreuit dare, sed per medium: hac videlicet conditione, vt petamus.
units.tr: Objection. The decrees of God are unchangeable. Therefore what God has decreed will happen even without our prayers. Answer to the antecedent. The decrees of God are unchangeable not only as to the events or ends, but also as to the means to the ends. For God has decreed to give the end, but through the means, namely on this condition, that we ask.

units.la: IV. Cur addatur, Sicut in cœlo.
units.tr: IV. Why 'as in heaven' is added.

units.la: Christus hanc particulam: sicut in cœlo, addit duabus de causis. 1. Vt proponat nobis exemplum perfectionis, ad quod contendere debemus. 2. Vt ex perfectionis desiderio certi simus, Deum nobis daturum esse hic inchoationem, in altera vita perfectionem: Habenti dabitur. Vtriusque ratio est, quia in cœlo volun-
units.tr: Christ adds this phrase, as in heaven, for two reasons. (1) To set before us an example of perfection, toward which we ought to strive. (2) So that, from our desire for perfection, we may be certain that God will give us here a beginning, and in the other life perfection: To him who has, more will be given. The reason for both is that in heaven the will

units.la: Vu voluntas Dei fit perfectissimè. A quibus? 1. A ipso Filio Dei, qui facit omnem voluntatem Patris: Ecce adsum, Deus, ut faciam voluntatem tuam. Ut faciam voluntatem, non meam, sed eius, qui misit me. 2. A sanctis angelis, & hominibus beatis. Ab angelis ita fit voluntas Dei in coelis, ut vnusquisque angelus stet in conspectu Dei promptus ad exequendum, quicquid Deus praeceperit. Faciunt voluntatem Dei generalem & specialem promtissimè: nullus ministerium suum detrectat, nullus in alienas partes inuolat, nullum pudet nobis seruire, etiamsi eos laedamus foetore peccatorum, & Deum offendamus. Sunt enim spiritus administratorij. Sic igitur petimus, ut nos etiam Deo obtemperemus, & voluntatem eius exsequamur in terra, sicut sancti angeli exsequuntur in coelo.
units.tr: of God is done most perfectly. By whom? (1) By the Son of God himself, who does all the will of the Father: Behold, I come, O God, to do your will. That I should do the will, not of myself, but of him who sent me. (2) By the holy angels and the blessed people. In heaven the will of God is done by the angels in such a way that each angel stands ready in the sight of God to carry out whatever God has commanded. They perform the general and the special will of God most readily; no one shirks his service, no one intrudes into another's part, and no one is ashamed to serve us, even though we offend them by the stench of our sins and displease God. For they are ministering spirits. So we ask that we too may obey God and carry out his will on earth, as the holy angels carry it out in heaven.

units.la: Obiect. Impossibilia non sunt petenda. Ut fiat Dei voluntas in terra, sicut in coelo, seu, ut nos faciamus officium in terra, sicut faciunt angeli in coelo, est impossibile: immò est petere contra decretum Dei. Ergo non est petendum, cum Deus statum percertè eam nullo tempore consequetur. Aliud est, non posse consequi consummationem: aliud non desiderare illam. Nego minorem, in qua est fallacia à non causa ut causa. Non enim petimus, ut in hac vita fiat consummatio obedientiae nostrae erga Deum: sed ut hic fiat eius inchoatio, & continuatio, & incrementū, ac deinde post hanc vitam continuis incrementis aucta, tandem perficiatur & consummetur, atque ita tunc nos faciemus voluntatem Dei non minus, quam ea semper fit ab angelis in coelo. Cum ergo precamur, ut in terra fiat voluntas Dei, sicut in coelo: Sicut non significat gradum, sed speciem obedientiae, scilicet, inchoationem. Hanc autem petere & consequi à Deo, non est contra Dei decretum. Quantum ad consummationem, nostrum est quoque singulis momentis petere, ut omnino liberemur à peccato. Vult enim Deus nos id optare, etsi nolit in hac vita nobis praestare.
