Quinta igitur petitio est reliquarum petitionum fundamentum, quo destructo reliquae concidunt. Si enim non statuas te habere Deum propitium, quomodo eum agnosces misericordem? quomodo in ea agnitione permanebis, quam non habes? quomodo officium tuum facies, ac voluntate Dei, cum sis ipsius hostis, & contrario studeas? quomodo adscribes omnia Deo? quomodo erunt illa tibi salutaria? 6. Post petitionem bonorum spiritualium & corporalium, sequitur extrema petitio liberationis a malis praesentibus & futuris. Ab hac petitione ultima reuertimur rursum ad primam: Libera nos ab omnibus malis culpa & poena, praesentibus ac futuris, ut agnoscamus te perfectum servatorem nostrum, ac proinde a nobis nomen tuum sanctificetur.
units.tr: Now we must observe the order and connection of all these petitions. (1) The Lord bade us ask for the true knowledge and profession of God, which is the cause of the other benefits. (2) That he would govern us by his Spirit, and so keep and confirm us in that knowledge perpetually. (3) That each one may perform and carry out his duty in his calling through it. (4) That he would give us those things by which each one may be able to perform his duty, namely bodily goods. Since we are to trust, with the former petitions, that we are in our calling, we must live and have what is necessary for life; therefore the fourth petition also coheres. For as spiritual goods and bodily goods pertain to us, (5) he added to the petition for spiritual and bodily goods a fitting objection from our unworthiness: that you may be able to give us spiritual and bodily goods, forgive us our debts. The fifth petition therefore is the foundation of the remaining petitions, and when it is destroyed the rest fall. For if you do not hold that you have a propitious God, how will you acknowledge him as merciful? How will you persevere in that knowledge which you do not have? How will you perform your duty and the will of God, when you are his enemy and strive against him? How will you ascribe all things to God? How will those things be salutary to you? (6) After the petition for spiritual and bodily goods there follows the final petition for deliverance from present and future evils. From this last petition we return again to the first: Deliver us from all evils, guilt and punishment, present and future, so that we may acknowledge you as our perfect Saviour, and so that your name may be sanctified among us.

units.la: QVAESTIO CXXVIII.
units.tr: QUESTION CXXVIII.

units.la: Quomodo concludis precationem tuam? RESPONSIO.
units.tr: How do you conclude your prayer? ANSWER.

units.la: Quia tuum est regnum, & potentia, & gloria in secula: hoc est, Omnia haec à te petimus, quia cum & Rex noster & omnipotens sis, omnia nobis & vis & potes largiri a. Atq; haec quidem ideo petimus, vt ex iis, non ad nos, sed ad sanctum nomen tuum omnis gloria redeat b.
units.tr: Because yours is the kingdom, and the power, and the glory for ever: that is, we ask all these things from you, since you are both our King and almighty, and you both will and are able to bestow all things upon us. a We ask these things so that all glory may return from them not to us but to your holy name. b

units.la: EXPLICATIO.
units.tr: EXPLANATION.

units.la: Haec precationis clausula seruit confirmandae nostrae fidei seu fiduciae exauditionis, quod Deus velit & possit nobis dare, quae petimus.
units.tr: This closing clause of the prayer serves to strengthen our faith, or our confidence, that God is willing and able to give us what we ask.

units.la: Tuum est regnum. Ratio 1. ab officio regis, quod est exaudire suos subditos, tueri & conseruare. Ergo tu Deus, cum sis Rex noster: potentior omnibus hostibus, habens omnia in tua potestate, bona & mala: mala, vt possis compescere: bona, vt nullum sit tantum, quod non possis dare, conueniens tuae naturae: nos autem cum simus tui subditi: adsis nobis tua potentia, nosq; conserua: quia amans es tuorum subditorum: & tua solius defensio ae tutela salutaris est.
units.tr: Thine is the kingdom. Reason 1, from the office of a king, which is to hear his subjects and to protect and preserve them. So you, God, since you are our King, are more powerful than all enemies and have all things in your power, both good and evil: evil, so that you can restrain it; good, so that there is nothing so great that you cannot give it, as befits your nature. But we, being your subjects, pray that you, by your power, would be present to us and preserve us, because you love your subjects, and your sole defence and protection is salutary.

units.la: Et potentia. Ratio 2. à Dei potentia. Exaudi nos Deus, & largire quae petimus, quoniam potes, & quidem solus potes. Penes te solum residet haec potentia cum summa bonitate coniuncta.
units.tr: And the power. Reason 2, from the power of God. Hear us, God, and grant what we ask, since you can, and indeed you alone can. This power resides in you alone, joined with the highest goodness.

units.la: Et gloria. Ratio 3. à causa finali. Petimus haec propter tuam gloriam: abs te solo vero Deo & Rege summo petimus & expectatio bonorum: te profitemur authorem ac fontem omnium bonorum: & quidem, quia haec gloria tibi debetur, ideo abs te petimus. Ergo exaudi nos propter gloriam tuam. Haec enim petitio & expectatio bonorum abs te, nihil aliud est, quam gloriae & honoris attributio: maxime, quia etiam vis propter gloriam tuam illa nobis dare, quae petimus. Nam quae seruiunt gloriae tuae, ea vis facere: sed quae petimus, seruiunt gloriae tuae. Ergo ea nobis vis dare. Des itaque nobis, quae petimus, & ad te redibit gloria, si nos liberes. Etenim hoc modo regnum tuum, & potentia, & gloria manifestabitur.
units.tr: And the glory. Reason 3, from the final cause. We ask these things for your glory. We look to you alone, the true God and supreme King, both for petition and for expectation of good things. We profess you to be the author and fountain of all good things. And indeed, because this glory is owed to you, therefore we ask it from you. So hear us for the sake of your glory. For this petition and expectation of good things from you is nothing other than the ascribing of glory and honour to you, especially since you also wish, for the sake of your glory, to give us the things we ask. For you wish to do those things that serve your glory, and the things we ask serve your glory. Therefore you wish to give them to us. Grant us, then, what we ask, and the glory will return to you if you free us. For in this way your kingdom, your power and your glory will be made manifest.

units.la: Obiect. Videmur argumenta suasoria afferre Deo, quibus impellamus eum ad faciendum, quae petimus: Verum qui est immutabilis, ei frustra adhibeatur rationes. Deus est immutabilis: Ergo &c. Resp. Concedo argumentum, frustra adhiberi rationes respectu Dei: sed non respectu nostri. Vel est fallacia non causae. Non enim adhibemus rationes, vt Deum moueamus, aut ipsi persuadeamus, vt hoc faciat: sed vt persuadeamus nobis ipsis, quod Deus sit hoc facturus, confirmemus nos de exauditione, & agnoscamus nostram necessitatem, Dei verò potentiam & veritatem. Itaque nequaquam ad permouendum Deum rationes istæ sunt precibus additæ: sed ad nos duntaxat confirmandos, quod Deus sit facturus, quæ petimus: quia hæ sunt causæ, cur id faciat: Tu es Rex optimus. Ergo dabis tuis subditis necessaria & salutaria. Tu es potentissimus. Ergo tuam potentiam ostentes in dandis his donis, quæ sunt maxima, & quæ à nullo alio, quam à te solo possunt dari. Denique tua gloria seruiet. Ergo facies: quia gloria tua tibi est curæ.
units.tr: Objection. We seem to bring persuasive arguments to God, by which we urge him to do what we ask. But reasons are used in vain with one who is unchangeable, and God is unchangeable. Therefore, etc. Answer. I grant the argument: reasons are used in vain with respect to God, but not with respect to us. Or it is the fallacy of a non-cause. For we do not adduce reasons in order to move God or to persuade him to do this, but in order to persuade ourselves that God is going to do it, to confirm ourselves regarding the answer, and to acknowledge our own need and God's power and truthfulness. Thus these reasons are by no means added to the prayers to move God, but only to confirm us that God is going to do what we ask, because these are the causes why he will do it: You are the best King. Therefore you will give your subjects what is necessary and salutary. You are most powerful. Therefore you will display your power in giving these gifts, which are very great and which can be given by no one other than you alone. Finally, your glory will be served. Therefore you will act, because your glory is your concern.

units.la: QVÆSTIO CXXIX.
units.tr: QUESTION CXXIX.

units.la: Quid sibi vult particula, Amen?
units.tr: What does the particle Amen mean?

units.la: RESPONSIO.
units.tr: ANSWER.

units.la: Rem certam ac ratam esse. Nam precatio mea multò certius à Deo est exaudita, quam ego in corde meo sentio, me illud ex animo cupere. a
units.tr: That the matter is certain and sure. For my prayer has been heard by God far more certainly than I feel in my heart that I desire it from my soul. a

units.la: a 2 Corinth. 1. verf. 20. 1 Tim. 2, 12.
units.tr: a 2 Corinthians 1, vers. 20; 1 Timothy 2, 12.

units.la: EXPLICATIO.
units.tr: EXPLANATION.

units.la: Hæc particula non adiungitur vt pars precationis: sed notat 1. Votum, seu desiderium verum & sincerum, quo optamus, vt exaudiamur, vt ratum certumque sit, quod petimus, vt quo petitioni respondeat. 2. Professionem fiduciæ: seu confessionem fidei nostræ, qua confidimus, nos exauditum iri. Amen igitur significat 1. Fiat, quod petimus. 2. Verè ac certò nos Deus, suæ promissionis memor, exaudiet.
units.tr: This particle is not attached as a part of the prayer, but signifies (1) a vow, or a true and sincere desire by which we wish to be heard, that what we ask may be fixed and certain, so that it corresponds to the petition; (2) a profession of confidence, or a confession of our faith, by which we trust that we shall be heard. Amen, therefore, means (1) let what we ask be done; (2) God, mindful of his promise, will truly and certainly hear us.

units.la: NOVAE Editioni huic CORPORIS DOCTRINAE ecclesiarum à Papatu Romano reformatarum constitueram quidē subnectere PARALIPOMENA CATECHETICA, è praelectionibus paternis, quas in aduersariis suis mihi reliquit: sed tempore nunc exclusus in reliquam Editionem operum Theologicorum illa reseruare volui. Interea certo consilio visum fuit noua quaedam MISCELLANEA Catechetica proferre: idque tuo, vt planissimè persuasum habemus, immò adeò vniuersae ecclesiae commodo haud poenitendo. Nam cùm singula illa, quae prioribus editionibus ex indulgentia venerandi senis Doctoris PAREI, quasi per traducem Typographorum, toties Orthodoxae Theologiae hoc Syntagma recudentiū, adiuncta fuerunt Miscellanea, partim propriè non agant de capitibus controuersis inter Theologos reformatos, & haereterodoxos, partim plaeraque omnia extent, legiq; possint in voluminibus Theologicis magni Theologi ZACHARIAE VRSINI; praesens Ecclesiae afflictae con. [?]tæ conditio aurem nobis vellicauit, nihil præ- ter votum piorum nos facturos, si priorem Mi- scellaneorum vicem suppleremus additione grauissimarum meditationum sacrarum, de iis inprimis Religionis capitibus, quæ hinc inde Ecclesias reformatas pluribus jam annis mi- rum quantum vexarunt: atque à venerabili Patre D. Davide Pareo, Ecclesiasticæ pacis & tranquillitatis incredibili sititore, ea judicii dexteritate examinata sunt, ut nihil exactius, nihil sanctius in hoc genere desiderari posse videatur. Quare, Christiane Lector, nihil du- bitamus, hocce officium nostrum tibi fore pergratum. Rogamus Deum Patrem Domini nostri Iesu Christi, ut deficientibus operariis alios in messem velit mittere, ac tandem par- vuli sui gregis sub cruce salutem & liberatio- nem ingemiscentis clementer misereri.
units.tr: Although I had intended to append to this new edition of the Corpus Doctrinae of the Churches Reformed from the Roman Papacy the Catechetical Paralipomena, drawn from my father's lectures which he left me among his papers, I have for the present been shut out of that task, and I have preferred to reserve them for the remaining edition of his theological works. Meanwhile, after careful deliberation, it seemed right to bring forth some new Catechetical Miscellanea, and we are fully persuaded that this will be of benefit to you, and indeed to the whole Church, and that you will have no cause for regret. For although those separate Miscellanea which, in earlier editions, were added to this Syntagma by the indulgence of the venerable old doctor Pareus, and which the printers, as it were by an inherited habit, have reproduced each time they reprinted this summary of orthodox theology, partly do not properly deal with the chief points of controversy between the reformed theologians and the heterodox, and partly are all found, and may be read, in the theological volumes of the great theologian Zacharias Ursinus; the present condition of the afflicted Church has pricked our ears, so that we considered we would do nothing but what the godly wish, if we supplied the place of the former Miscellanea by adding most weighty sacred meditations on those chief heads of religion which, here and there, have for many years now sorely troubled the reformed Churches; and which have been examined by the venerable Father David Pareus, an incredible lover of ecclesiastical peace and tranquillity, with such skill in judgment that nothing more exact and nothing holier in this kind could seem to be desired. Wherefore, Christian reader, we do not doubt that this service of ours will be very pleasing to you. We pray God the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ that, since the workers are failing, he will send others into the harvest, and at last graciously have mercy on the groaning salvation and deliverance of his little flock under the cross.

units.la: NOBILISS. REVERENDISSIMIS Q. SACRÆ Curiæ Præsidi: & Assessoribus: Collegis suis honorandis,
units.tr: To the most noble and most reverend President and Assessors of the Holy Court, and my honoured colleagues:

units.la: DAVID PAREVS.
units.tr: DAVID PAREUS.

units.la: NOn minus verè, quàm piè dictum esse à Salomone: Cor hominis disponit viam suam, sed Domini est dirigere gressus eius: vel exemplo meo nunc experior. Licet enim hactenus mihi aliquoties nec præclaræ occasiones, nec hortatus amicorum, nec alia, quæ me de sententia nunc dimouent, defuerint: semper tamen animo meo firma stetit πρόαιρεσις nunquam faciendi id, quod nunc faciendum suscipio. Obstitit non modo conscientia tenuitatis mea, sed & infelix Theologiæ hoc tempore conditio. Qui enim se Theologos profitentur, vel sunt magna ex parte acerbissimi Theologiæ hostes, & infectatores veritatis mordacissimi: vt inter hos, quanto quis est ad maledicendum paratior, tanto habeatur Theologus maior: vel certè, si verè id esse, quod audiunt, volunt, mox rabiem & dentes illorum sibi infigi acerbissimo suo cum dolore, & ecclesiæ scandalo sentiunt, quasi ad scopum facti videntur. Sic quidem ego.
units.tr: It was no less truly than piously said by Solomon: "A man's heart deviseth his way, but the LORD directeth his steps." I now learn this from my own experience. For although hitherto there have been several fine opportunities, the urging of friends, and other things that now move me to change my mind, my settled purpose [πρόαιρεσις] has always stood firm never to undertake what I now take in hand. What stood in the way was not only my awareness of my own slightness but also the unhappy condition of theology at this time. Those who profess themselves theologians are for the most part the bitterest enemies of theology and the most biting persecutors of the truth. Among them, the readier someone is to slander, the greater a theologian he is thought to be. Or, if anyone wishes to be what they hear him called, he soon feels their rage and teeth sunk into him, to his own bitter pain and the scandal of the Church, as if he had been made their target. So much for me.

units.la: Sed ecce Dominum dirigentem hæc aliter: vt quæ me absterruerant, nunc non morentur: quæ non induxerant, nunc rapiant fortissime.
units.tr: But see, the Lord directs these things otherwise: what frightened me off no longer holds me back, and what did not draw me now carries me away most strongly.

units.la: Manet conscientia imbecillitatis. Sed cogito illud: Discrimina donorum esse: & unumquemque prophetare pro modulo fidei & gratia sibi à Domino donata. Malè audit S. Theologia, quasi sit ovxo Quælxv [?]: sed aptiùs malos: nec vitio suo, sed Satana artificio, & malorum perversitate. Scio verò etiam Dominum nostrum in signum contradictionis positum fuisse atque etiamnum esse.
units.tr: The awareness of my weakness remains. But I think on this: there are diversities of gifts, and each one prophesies according to the measure of faith and grace given him by the Lord. Holy Theology is ill spoken of, as if it were [illegible]; but it is rather the wicked who deserve this, not through any fault of its own but by the craft of Satan and the perversity of evil men. I know too that our Lord was set for a sign to be spoken against, and still is.

units.la: Aliquot nunc annos in illustri hoc Collegio provinciam eam, Dei & Magistratus voluntate, sustineo, quæ sue quodam jure, & maiorum exemplo, quæ tandem consilium mutare cogit. Ornarunt eam ante me, magna sua laude & Ecclesiæ commodo Doctores clarissimi, partim præceptores mei, partim Collegæ venerandi, OLEVIANUS, VRSINVS, SOHNIVS, KIMEDONCIVS: quos honoris causa nomino. Ego primus provinciam tam nobilis dignitatem imminuerem? ordinem Scholæ tam clarum, tamq; laudatum connellerem? successoribus exemplum haud fatis Collegio honorificum, immò adeò injurium relinquerem? Huic, instante nunc actu Academia longè augustissimo, quo XVII. viris Doctissimis insignia honorum in Iure & Medica facultate conferentur, tum denuo accesserunt, tum aliorum amicorum hortationes plurima, tum vestra, Collegæ honorandi, rationes gravissimæ, quibus institutum meum non approbastis modo, sed & planè ita mihi confirmastis, ut nusquam quoquam divino huc me trahi nunc totus non dubitem. Pergat, oro, clementissimus ille Pater gressus meos in viis suis dirigere, ut nusquam de tramite exorbitent: & cœptum hoc meum Schola huic cumprimis, universaq; Ecclesiæ salutare suxit.
units.tr: For some years now, by the will of God and the magistrate, I have sustained this office in this illustrious College, an office which by its own right and the example of our forebears now compels me to change my plan. Before me it was adorned, to its great credit and to the benefit of the Church, by very distinguished teachers, some my own tutors and some my venerable colleagues: OLEVIANUS, URSINUS, SOHNIUS, and KIMEDONCIUS, whom I name out of respect. Should I, the first, diminish the dignity of so noble an office? Should I disturb the order of the School, so bright and so praised? Should I leave to successors an example not very honourable to the College, indeed so harmful? To this (now that the most august academic act is taking place, in which insignia of honour in law and medicine are conferred on seventeen most learned men) have been added, once again, the many exhortations of other friends, and your own most weighty reasons, honoured colleagues. By these you not only approved my plan but so confirmed it for me that I no longer doubt at all that I am being drawn here by God's hand. May that most merciful Father, I pray, continue to direct my steps in his ways, so that they never stray from the path; and may this undertaking of mine bring salvation above all to this School and to the whole Church.

units.la: Repetitionem Doctrinæ Ecclesiarum nostrarum, de quibusdam capitibus maximè nunc controversis, non integram, sed brevem ex Verbo Dei instituere placuit: ut studiosæ juventuti verrimam disputandi quasi segetem vel potius messem exhiberem: tum etiam, ut summa sententia Orthodoxa de illis, adversus infectatores harum Ecclesiarum omnibus [illegible, ~5 letters] in conspectu esset.
units.tr: I decided to set out, from the Word of God, not a complete but a brief repetition of the doctrine of our Churches on certain chief points that are now most controverted: so that I might offer studious youth, as it were, a crop, or rather a harvest, of disputation; and also so that the orthodox summary view on these matters would lie open against the assailants of these Churches [illegible, ~5 letters].

units.la: Vobis autem Viri honorandi, eam iure consecro, qui & sana doctrina in his Ecclesiis vigilantissimi custodes constituti, & studiorum meorum fautores estis humanissimi. Dominus JESVS diu vos servet Ecclesiæ. Amen. Heidelbergæ è Collegio Sapientiæ Calendis Iunij, Anno salutis reparatæ
units.tr: To you, honoured gentlemen, I dedicate this by right, since you have been appointed most watchful guardians of sound doctrine in these Churches and most kindly patrons of my studies. May the Lord Jesus preserve you long for the Church. Amen. From the College of Wisdom at Heidelberg, on the Kalends of June, in the year of salvation restored,

D. DAVID PAREVS

units.la: ROGATV plurimorum piorum hanc Orthodoxæ reformatæ Religionis Christianæ Epitomen è Latino transtuli in sermonem vernaculum, non sine aliquo auctario, & uberiori explicatione: additis item testimoniis Scripturæ, Symbolorum item Oecumenicorum, & Patrum. In hac igitur Epitome Lector Christianus summatim intelliget; quæ sit doctrina Ecclesiarum & Scholarum in Archi-Palatinatu, immo adeo omnium aliarum ecclesiarum Reformatarum, & à fermento Papistico exauthoratarum per Galliam, Angliam, Scotiam, Belgium, Helvetiam, Moraviam, Bohemiam, Poloniam, Vngariam & alibi. Dehinc cognoscet quoque, num, uti importune nonnulli clamitant, hæc doctrina sit Calviniana, & hæretica: an potius Apostolica & Christiana, atq; in Sacris litteris probe fundata. Homines vero pietatis zelo acti, quibus curæ est salus animæ suæ, nequicquam movebuntur insanis istis clamoribus: quin potius exemplo ingenuorum Iudæorum Thessalonicensium in timore Domini hanc doctrinam perpendent, ut exinde discant, quæ sit vera Religio Christiana: examinabunt quoque testimonia Sacræ Scripturæ, quibus doctrina orthodoxa Reformatæ Religionis confirmatur: quam tuemur, quamque coram Concilio legitime congregato, imo coram tribunali supremi & iustissimi Iudicis IESV CHRISTI, defendere non verecundabimur. Fecerunt idem Beroenses illi, attendentes, quam doctrinam illis annunciaret D. Paulus: & num ita se haberet, in verbo Dei studiose inquirentes. Quo factum est, ut multi ex iis, qua viri qua feminæ, crederent in Iesum Christum.
units.tr: REQUESTED by many godly people, I have translated this Epitome of the orthodox reformed Christian religion from Latin into the vernacular, with some addition and a fuller explanation, and with the testimonies of Scripture, of the ecumenical creeds, and of the Fathers also added. In this Epitome the Christian reader will understand in summary what the doctrine is of the churches and schools in the Upper Palatinate, indeed of all the other reformed churches that have been freed from the leaven of the Papacy throughout France, England, Scotland, Belgium, Switzerland, Moravia, Bohemia, Poland, Hungary and elsewhere. Next he will also learn whether this doctrine, as some clamour without restraint, is Calvinian and heretical, or rather apostolic and Christian, and soundly grounded in the Holy Scriptures. Men moved by zeal for piety, who care for the salvation of their souls, will not be stirred in vain by those frenzied outcries; rather, following the example of the noble Jews of Thessalonica, they will weigh this doctrine in the fear of the Lord, so that from it they may learn what the true Christian religion is. They will also examine the testimonies of Holy Scripture by which the orthodox doctrine of the reformed religion is confirmed. This doctrine we uphold, and we shall not be ashamed to defend it before a lawfully gathered council, indeed before the judgment seat of the supreme and most just Judge, Jesus Christ. The Bereans did the same, attentively considering what doctrine Paul proclaimed to them, and searching diligently in the Word of God whether it was so. As a result, many of them, both men and women, believed in Jesus Christ.

units.la: Secus hodie sentiunt ii, qui quicquid ab opinionibus suis discrepat, aut adeo alienum est, CALVINIANVM id esse vociferantur. Quā quidem intemperie sua ipsum Christum & Paulum refutare facile mè poterunt. Idem omnino haud dubio accidet his quoque Aphorismis meis. At vero si CALVINIANA illa est doctrina, profecto tota Sacra Scriptura, immo adeo vniuersa Ecclesia primitiua CALVINIANA dicenda fuerit. Adsunt enim testimonia, quibus irrefragabiliter contradicere nequit. Quin immo prudentiores Papistæ & Iesuitæ, qui sequuntur doctrinam Scholasticorū, CALVINIANI quoq; erunt appellandi. In medio namq; PAPATV DEVS, propter electos, per Scholasticos sartam testam tectam conseruauit doctrinam de persona Christi: de morte & merito Christi: de Ascensione ad coelos: de sessione Christi ad dextram Dei: de praedestinatione Dei: planissimè, vt à nobis illa explicatur in hisce Aphorismis. Reliqui verò Articuli, de fide, de ministerio Ecclesiastico, & de Sacramentis maturè fuerunt depravati in Papatu.
units.tr: Those who call everything that differs from their own opinions, or is even remote from them, Calvinian, think otherwise today. By this intemperance they could easily refute Christ and Paul themselves. The same will undoubtedly happen to these Aphorisms of mine. But if that doctrine is Calvinian, then surely the whole of Holy Scripture, and indeed the whole primitive Church, must be called Calvinian. For there are testimonies which they cannot contradict without refutation. Nay, the more prudent Papists and Jesuits, who follow the doctrine of the Schoolmen, will also have to be called Calvinists. For in the midst of the Papacy, God, on account of the elect, preserved through the Schoolmen, intact and secure, the doctrine concerning the person of Christ, concerning the death and merit of Christ, concerning the ascension into heaven, concerning the sitting of Christ at the right hand of God, concerning the predestination of God, just as it is clearly explained by us in these Aphorisms. The remaining articles, concerning faith, the ecclesiastical ministry, and the sacraments, were soon corrupted in the Papacy.

units.la: Dolendum verò est, eos, qui sepposito ac spreto nomine CHRISTIANORVM & CHRISTI, ab hominum sese nominibus appellari satagunt, in articulis hisce fidei tradendis longius recessisse à consensu primitiuæ Ecclesiæ: & magis ac magis indies ab eiusdem simplicitate deflectere.
units.tr: It is to be lamented that those who, setting aside and rejecting the name of Christians and of Christ, strive to be called by the names of men, have in teaching these articles of faith departed far from the consensus of the primitive Church, and deviate more and more every day from its simplicity.

units.la: Quid mirum autem? Deus namque mundum punit erroribus efficacibus: immissis: quia scilicet veritatem non amat. Ac quoniam, teste Chrysostomo, ERROR est res varia & intricata, eamq; habet vim, vt nesciat quiescere, aut subsistere, nihil mirum, si ex vno errore plures alij nati sint: & ex vna controuersia decem aliæ suboriantur. Initio controuertebatur duntaxat de X. Articulo, nempe de CORPORE Christi, latente sub pane: itemque de orali manducatione in Coena. Quam controuersiam Evangelici diu inter se agitarunt. Consensus verò summus fuit in exteris Articulis, à nobis hic propositis: sicuti testantur Acta Colloquii Marpurgensis Anno 1529. Immo verò & in doctrina de Coena Domini Concordia quoque fuit inita inter Theologos Anno 1536. Qua postmodum dissoluta, cum nonnulli, præsertim post obitum D. Lutheri, opinionem suam de corporali præsentia in pane defendere commodè non possent, quod nullus Evangelistarum verba Christi, HOC EST CORPVS MEVM, sic efferret: Hic est corpus meum: vel; sub pane, aut, sub specie panis latet meum corpus: ac præterea de Fidei Catholicæ sententia Christus suo corpore nunc non sit in terris, in hostia aut ciborio missæ inclusus, sed supra in coelo ad dextram Dei sedens, unde rediturus est ad judicandum vivos & mortuos: sperarunt sese opinionis suæ præsidium in aliis articulis fidei repertur os: ac primum ex Articulo de Vnione personali duarum naturarum in Christo: vnde VBIQVITATEM, siue omnipræsentiam eius, antequidem quærentes: Si corpus Christi est VBIQVE: erit quoque in omnibus hostiis. Si in omnibus hostiis: VBIQVE etiam erit. Tum stultè sibi imaginati sunt, Articulum de sessione ad dextram Dei eiusdem esse sententiæ cum primo De personali vnione duarum naturarum, ac si diceretur: Humanitas Christi cum Filio Dei, qui est ipsa dextra Dei vbique præsens, personaliter est vnita, & replet coelum ac terram. Tertio, quia viderunt, Ascensionem ad coelos cuertere vbi-
units.tr: And why should this be surprising? God punishes the world with effective errors sent in, because it does not love the truth. And since, as Chrysostom testifies, ERROR is a varied and intricate thing, and has the power that it cannot rest or stand still, it is no wonder that from one error several others are born, and from one controversy ten others arise. At first the dispute concerned only the tenth article, namely the body of Christ lying hidden under the bread, and likewise the oral eating in the Supper. The Evangelicals long debated this controversy among themselves. But there was the highest agreement on the other articles proposed here by us, as the Acts of the Colloquy of Marburg in the year 1529 bear witness. Indeed, a concord also concerning the doctrine of the Lord's Supper was entered into among the theologians in the year 1536. When this was afterwards dissolved, since some, especially after the death of Dr. Luther, could not conveniently defend their opinion concerning the bodily presence in the bread, because none of the evangelists rendered the words of Christ, THIS IS MY BODY, in this way: This is my body here; or under the bread, or my body lies hidden under the appearance of bread; and moreover, contrary to the view of the Catholic faith, that Christ with his body is not now on earth, enclosed in the host or the pyx of the Mass, but sits above in heaven at the right hand of God, whence he will return to judge the living and the dead, they hoped to find support for their opinion in other articles of faith; and first from the article on the personal union of the two natures in Christ, from which, seeking indeed his UBIQUITY, or omnipresence: If the body of Christ is EVERYWHERE, it will be in all the hosts. If in all the hosts, it will also be EVERYWHERE. Then they foolishly imagined that the article on the sitting at the right hand of God had the same meaning as the first, on the personal union of the two natures, as if it were said: The humanity of Christ is personally united with the Son of God, who is himself the right hand of God, present everywhere, and fills heaven and earth. Thirdly, because they saw that the ascension into heaven overturns the ubiquity-

units.la: {y} Lutheranorum primarium ἀξιωματικὸν circulare. Vbiquitatem, & corporalem præsentiam in pane: inaudito & allegorico prorsus modo illam interpretati sunt, quasi ASSCENDERE nihil aliud fit, quam euanescere in auras, in diuinitatem extolli, & vbique esse.
units.tr: {y} The chief axiomatic [ἀξιωματικὸν] circular argument of the Lutherans. They interpreted ubiquity and the bodily presence in the bread in an unheard-of and entirely allegorical way, as if to ASCEND were nothing other than to vanish into thin air, to be exalted into the divinity, and to be everywhere.

units.la: Nouis hisce opinionum portentis tam Pontificij Doctores, quam nostri, pluresque alij Euangelici Theologi sese strenuè opposuerunt, asserentes veterem simplicitatem ac veritatem istorum Articulorum fidei.
units.tr: Both the Papist doctors and our own, and many other Evangelical theologians, vigorously opposed these new monstrosities of opinion, asserting the old simplicity and truth of these articles of faith.

units.la: Quo viso, noui isti VBIQVITATIS Architecti, aquam sibi hærere deprehenderunt: eoque nouas machinas excogitantes, coperunt CALVINISTAS, quos vocant, alios insuper impingere errores, eos ad Colloquia prouocare, quibus cum non de persona Christi duntaxat, & Cœna Domini conferrent, sed in præcipuis articulis fidei errorum eos conuincerent. Prætendebant namq; à reformatis Ecclesiis doceri
units.tr: Seeing this, these new architects of UBIQUITY found that the water was stuck fast for them; and so, devising new machines, they began to fasten upon the so-called Calvinists also other errors, and to challenge them to colloquies, in which they might confute them not only concerning the person of Christ and the Lord's Supper, but also in the chief articles of faith. For they claimed that it was taught by the reformed churches

units.la: DE PRÆDESTINATIONE:
units.tr: ON PREDESTINATION:

units.la: Non omnes homines esse electos: sed a multos vocatos, & paucos electos.
units.tr: That not all men are elect, but many are called and few are elect.

units.la: DE MERITO MORTIS CHRISTI:
units.tr: ON THE MERIT OF CHRIST'S DEATH:

units.la: impios & incredulos, quoad tales manent, illius non fieri participes: sed duntaxat b electos credentes. Item: Promissiones Euangelij vniuersales esse, ratione c fidelium, non autem infidelium & Epicurorum.
units.tr: That the impious and unbelieving, as long as they remain such, do not become partakers of it, but only the elect who believe. Likewise: that the universal promises of the Gospel apply to believers, with respect to the faithful, and not to unbelievers and Epicureans.

units.la: DE FIDE:
units.tr: ON FAITH:

units.la: Esse singulare d Dei donum; dari solis electis, in quibus solis radices agat, & constans sit: eandem nunquam amitti finaliter: quod proficiscatur ex incorruptibili semine Verbi Dei.
units.tr: That it is a singular gift of God, given only to the elect, in whom alone it takes root and remains steadfast; that it is never finally lost; and that it springs from the incorruptible seed of the Word of God.

units.la: DE MINISTERIO ECCLESIASTICO:
units.tr: ON THE ECCLESIASTICAL MINISTRY:

units.la: e Ministros esse tantum externos VERBI dispensatores: DEVM verò interne operari per Spiritum sanctum.
units.tr: That ministers are only the external dispensers of the WORD, but that GOD works inwardly through the Holy Spirit.

units.la: DE SACRAMENTIS:
units.tr: ON THE SACRAMENTS:

units.la: f CHRISTVM esse heri & hodie, & in omnem æternitatem, ac proinde materiam omnium Sacramentorum, tam veteris, quàm noui Testamenti. Itemque tam in Sacramentis, quàm verbo, neminem absque fide Christi fieri participem.
units.tr: That CHRIST is "yesterday and today, and the same for ever," and therefore the matter of all sacraments, of both the Old and the New Testament. Likewise, that whether in the sacraments or in the word, no one becomes a partaker without faith in Christ.

units.la: DE BAPTISMO:
units.tr: ON BAPTISM:

units.la: g Duplicem esse ablutionem, vnam externam aquæ, quæ abluat sordes corporis: Alteram internam sanguinis & Spiritus Christi: quæ sit pactum bonæ conscientiæ cum DEO. Ministrum insuper sola aqua baptizare: CHRISTVM vero in vera baptismi administratione baptizare Spiritu sancto. Item: Infideles per baptismum non regenerari. Item: Liberos Christianorum esse liberos promissionis ac fœderis, etiam ante Baptismum: eamque ipsam ob causam esse baptizandos.
units.tr: That there is a twofold washing: one external, with water, which cleanses the filth of the body; the other internal, of the blood and Spirit of Christ, which is the covenant of a good conscience with God. Further, that the minister baptizes only with water, but that Christ, in the true administration of baptism, baptizes with the Holy Spirit. Likewise: that unbelievers are not regenerated through baptism. Likewise: that the children of Christians are children of the promise and covenant even before baptism, and that for this very reason they are to be baptized.

units.la: Doctrinam hanc jam inde ab Anno 1586. non tantum vt Calvinisticam & haereticam damnarunt, sed & diris calumniis ac depravationibus exceperunt ij, qui Lutheranorum nomine gaudent. Ac cum apud imperitam plebem Articulos illos strenuè traducunt vt Caluinianos errores, egregiè se causam suam in defendendis figmentis de Vbiquitate & corporali praesentia carnis in Coena egisse arbitrantur. Quod quidem suo loco nunc relinquimus, Deo rem omnem commendantes.
units.tr: This doctrine, from the year 1586 onward, has been condemned not only as Calvinistic and heretical, but has also been received with harsh calumnies and distortions by those who take pride in the name of Lutherans. And while they vigorously misrepresent those articles among the untaught common people as Calvinist errors, they think they have pleaded their cause admirably in defending their fictions about ubiquity and the bodily presence of the flesh in the Supper. This we now leave for its proper place, commending the whole matter to God.

units.la: Certum tamen est, eo ipso in Pelagianas & Papisticas lacunas illos relapsos esse: vt valde metuendum sit, ne graviores tenebrae Ecclesias Euangelicas sint obruturae, quam unquam antehac. Attamen, proh dolor! hanc veram Euangelicam, & Augustanae Confessionis doctrinam appellare non dubitant, docentes:
units.tr: It is certain, however, that by this very act they have relapsed into Pelagian and Papistical pitfalls, so that there is great reason to fear that darker shadows will overwhelm the Evangelical Churches than ever before. Yet, alas! they do not hesitate to call this the true Evangelical doctrine and that of the Augsburg Confession, teaching:

units.la: DE PRAEDESTINATIONE: In Deo nullam esse electionem: sed promiscuè omnes homines Deum elegisse.
units.tr: ON PREDESTINATION: That there is no election in God, but that God has chosen all men indiscriminately.

units.la: DE MORTE CHRISTI: Christum sua morte omnes homines redemisse, & Deo reconciliasse, in sinum gratiae Dei reposuisse, sanctificasse, sive credant, sive non.
units.tr: ON THE DEATH OF CHRIST: That Christ by his death redeemed all men and reconciled them to God, placed them in the bosom of the grace of God, and sanctified them, whether they believe or not.

units.la: DE REMISSIONE PECCATORVM: Generali remissione omnibus hominibus remissa esse sua peccata tam fidelibus, quàm infidelibus.
units.tr: ON THE FORGIVENESS OF SINS: That by a general forgiveness, their sins are forgiven to all men, both believers and unbelievers.

units.la: DE PROMISSIONIBVS EVANGELII: Pertinere ad omnes omnino homines tam fideles quàm impios.
units.tr: ON THE PROMISES OF THE GOSPEL: That they pertain to all men absolutely, both the faithful and the impious.

units.la: DE FIDE: Esse causam electionis. Deum enim prius praevidisse, quinam essent credituri ac perseveraturi. Fidem quidem non esse in viribus nostris: esse tamen opus, quod Deus in nobis promoveat: esse inconstantem, & communem hypocritis.
units.tr: ON FAITH: That it is the cause of election, for God foresaw beforehand who would believe and persevere. Faith indeed is not in our own powers, yet it is a work which God promotes in us; it is inconstant and common to hypocrites.

units.la: DE MINISTERIO ECCLESIASTICO: Ministros suo praeconio quoque efficaciam divinam conferre: dispensare rem externam & internam simul.
units.tr: ON THE ECCLESIASTICAL MINISTRY: That ministers by their preaching also confer divine efficacy, dispensing the external and the internal thing at the same time.

units.la: DE SACRAMENTIS: Sacramenta veteris Testamenti fuisse umbras duntaxat absque corpore Christo.
units.tr: ON THE SACRAMENTS: That the sacraments of the Old Testament were merely shadows, without the body of Christ.

units.la: DE BAPTISMO: Mysticam vim annexam esse aquae abluendi peccata, & regenerandi. Spiritū sanctum & efficaciam eius aquae esse affixam. Aquae & Spiritus eundem esse effectum. Hypocritas & infideles in Baptismo regenerari per Spiritum sanctum. Ministrum non tantum aqua baptizare, sed & conferre Spiritum sanctum. Infantes Christianorum ante Baptismum non magis pertinere ad foedus Dei, quàm Turcarum. Item: Esse à diabolo obsessos, qui ante baptismum certis verbis ac crucibus sit exorcizandus. Et id genus alia. Quae sanè doctrina & repugnat sacro evangelio: nec in Augustana confessione, quam tanto opere jactitant[?]. tant, vel verbo reperitur: à D. Luthero verò magno zelo est reiecta & refutata. Vide, Christiane Lector, quò res tandem redierit? Sed quorsum prodest nosse originem controuersiarum? In eo nobis potius laborandum, quei ab illis liberemur. Orandus igitur Deus, vt afflictæ Ecclesiæ suæ succurrat, in veritate VERBI eam sanctificet: Doctores ac ministros Euangelij in vera moderatione flectat ad amorem pacis & concordiæ. Ac tum errores ipsi citra operosiorem refutationem facilè concident, ac VERITAS locum obtinebit. Nihil est errore magis imbecillum, ait Chrysostomus, suis ipsius alis implicatur, nec oppugnatione aliunde est opus. Idem: Talis est conditio erroris: etiam nullo sibi obsistente consenescit ac defluit. Talis autem è diuerso Veritatis status: etiam multis impugnantibus suscitatur ac crescit. Proinde nihil mirabimur, infelix lolium succrescere in agro Domini. Veritas filia temporis est, vt fideles Dei serui virulentis istis aduersariorum libellis refutandis se se multum fatigent. Nihil quippe ad pacem id facit. Solus ad victoriam & concordiam gradus restat, si cum infirmitate, cum timore ac tremore, cum modestia ac tolerantia, cum demonstratione spiritus, cum potentia verbi propugnemus veritatem. Idq; vnice operam quoq; dabo in Aphorismis hisce explicandis. Spiritus namq; Christi tandem fortior erit, quàm spiritus Satanæ. Et regnum Christi potentius erit, quàm regnum diaboli. Ad iustitiam reuertetur iudicium: & post ipsum ibunt omnes recto corde: ait Dauid Psal. 94. v. 15.
units.tr: ON BAPTISM: That a mystical power is attached to the water for washing away sins and for regeneration; that the Holy Spirit and the efficacy of that water are joined together; that water and Spirit have the same effect; that hypocrites and unbelievers are regenerated in baptism through the Holy Spirit; that the minister not only baptizes with water but also confers the Holy Spirit; that the infants of Christians before baptism pertain no more to the covenant of God than those of the Turks; likewise, that those possessed by the devil must be exorcised before baptism with certain words and signs of the cross; and other things of this kind. This doctrine certainly contradicts the holy Gospel, and is not found, either in word or in sense, in the Augsburg Confession, which they boast of so greatly; it was rejected and refuted by Dr. Luther with great zeal. See, Christian reader, where the matter has finally come to! But what does it profit to know the origin of the controversies? We should rather labor for this, that we be delivered from them. Let God therefore be entreated to help his afflicted Church, to sanctify it in the truth of the WORD, and to turn the teachers and ministers of the Gospel, in true moderation, to love of peace and concord. Then the errors themselves will easily fall without a more laborious refutation, and the TRUTH will obtain its place. Nothing is weaker than error, says Chrysostom; it is entangled in its own wings, and needs no assault from elsewhere. The same: Such is the condition of error: even with no one opposing it, it grows old and falls away. On the other hand, such is the state of Truth: even when many attack it, it is raised up and grows. Therefore we shall not wonder that the unhappy darnel springs up in the Lord's field. Truth is the daughter of time, so that the faithful servants of God weary themselves greatly in refuting the venomous pamphlets of their adversaries. Indeed, this contributes nothing to peace. Only one way to victory and concord remains: if we defend the truth with gentleness, with fear and trembling, with modesty and tolerance, with demonstration of the Spirit, and with the power of the word. And to this end I shall devote my effort in explaining these Aphorisms. For the Spirit of Christ will at last be stronger than the spirit of Satan, and the kingdom of Christ will be more powerful than the kingdom of the devil. Judgment shall return unto righteousness, and all the upright in heart shall follow it, says David, Psalm 94:15.

units.la: Tertullianus contra Valentin.
units.tr: Tertullian against Valentinus.

units.la: Nihil VERITAS erubescit, nisi solummodo abscondi.
units.tr: Truth blushes at nothing, except only to be hidden.

units.la: APHORISMI DOCTRINÆ ORTHODOXÆ reformatarum Ecclesiarum.
units.tr: APHORISMS OF THE ORTHODOX DOCTRINE of the Reformed Churches.

units.la: ARTICVLVS PRIMVS DE PERSONA CHRISTI.
units.tr: ARTICLE THE FIRST, CONCERNING THE PERSON OF CHRIST.

units.la: I.
units.tr: I.

units.la: CREDIMVS ac profitemur ore & pectore coram Deo & hominibus: & hac ipsa cõfessione discerni volumus ab omnibus infidelibus & hypocritis, IESVM CHRISTVM esse personam verè ἀνθρώπων, subsistentem duabus naturis veris & perfectis, Divina & Humana, personaliter vnitis a. Proinde & verum Deum
units.tr: We believe and profess, with mouth and heart, before God and men, and by this very confession we wish to be distinguished from all unbelievers and hypocrites, that Jesus Christ is one true person, subsisting in two true and perfect natures, divine and human, personally united. Therefore we also confess him to be true God,

units.la: a. Sic Deum {b}: Patri ὁμοούσιον {c}: & coæternum secundum diuinitatem {d}: Et verum Hominem {e}, nobis ὁμοούσιον per omnia {f}: excepto peccato: natum ex Maria virgine MARIA in tempore natum secundum Humanitatem {g}: vnum & vnum {h} & vnigenitum DEI {i}, & Hominis Filium {k}: vnum & solum DEI & hominum Mediatorem {l}: non duos, sed vnum Christum {m}.
units.tr: a. Thus God {b}: consubstantial [ὁμοούσιον] with the Father {c}, and co-eternal according to the divinity {d}; and true man {e}, consubstantial with us in all things {f} except sin, born of the virgin Mary {g}, born in time according to the humanity; one and only-begotten {h} of God {i} and Son of man {k}; the one and only Mediator between God and men {l}; not two, but one Christ {m}.

units.la: TESTIMONIA SCRIPTVRÆ ET SYMBOLORVM.
units.tr: TESTIMONIES OF SCRIPTURE AND OF THE CREEDS.

units.la: {a}] Coloss. 2, 9. In eo inhabitat omnis plenitudo Deitatis corporaliter. 1 Tim. 3, 16. Sine controuersia magnum est pietatis mysterium: Deus conspicuus factus est in carne.
units.tr: {a}] Col. 2, 9. In him dwells all the fullness of the Godhead bodily. 1 Tim. 3, 16. Without controversy, great is the mystery of godliness: God was manifested in the flesh.

units.la: Johan. 1, 14. Et Sermo ille factus est caro.
units.tr: John 1, 14. And that Word was made flesh.

units.la: {b}] 1 Joh. 5, 20. Hic est verus ille Deus, & vita æterna.
units.tr: {b}] 1 John 5, 20. This is the true God, and eternal life.

units.la: {c}] Joh. 1, 14. Spectauimus gloriam eius, vt vnigeniti egressi à Patre.
units.tr: {c}] John 1, 14. We beheld his glory, the glory as of the only begotten of the Father.

units.la: Psal. 2, 7. Filius meus es tu: hodie genui te.
units.tr: Ps. 2, 7. You are my Son; today I have begotten you.

units.la: Prou. 8, 24. Quum nondum essent voragines, formata sum.
units.tr: Prov. 8, 24. When there were no depths, I was brought forth.

units.la: Mich. 5, 2. Egressus eius ab initio à diebus seculi.
units.tr: Mic. 5, 2. His goings forth have been from of old, from everlasting.

units.la: {d}] Philip. 2, 6. Qui, cum esset in forma Dei, non duxit rapinam parem esse cum Deo.
units.tr: {d}] Phil. 2, 6. Who, being in the form of God, did not consider it robbery to be equal with God.

units.la: Heb. 1, 3. Est effulgentia gloriæ Patris, & character personæ illius.
units.tr: Heb. 1, 3. He is the brightness of the Father's glory and the express image of his person.

units.la: Col. 1, 15. 17. Est imago Dei inuisibilis, & primogenitus omnis creaturæ. Et ipse est ante omnia, & omnia per eum consistunt.
units.tr: Col. 1, 15, 17. He is the image of the invisible God, the firstborn of every creature. And he is before all things, and by him all things consist.

units.la: {e}] Phil. 2, 7. Ipse seipsum exinaniuit forma serui accepta, similis hominibus factus, & habitu compertus vt homo.
units.tr: {e}] Phil. 2, 7. He emptied himself, taking the form of a servant, made in the likeness of men, and found in fashion as a man.

units.la: Hebr. 2. vers. 14. Quoniam igitur pueri participes sunt carnis & sanguinis, ipse quoque consimiliter participeps factus est eorundem. Non vtique Angelos assumsit, sed semen Abrahami assumsit.
units.tr: Heb. 2, 14. Since therefore the children are partakers of flesh and blood, he himself likewise took part of the same. For verily he took not on him the nature of angels, but he took on him the seed of Abraham.

units.la: {f}] Rom. 1, 3. Et filio suo, facto ex semine Dauidis secundum carnem. Heb. 2, 17. Vnde debuit per omnia fratribus similis fieri, vt misericors esset, & fidelis pontifex in iis, quæ apud Deum agenda forent ad expiandum peccata populi.
units.tr: {f}] Rom. 1, 3. Concerning his Son, who was made of the seed of David according to the flesh. Heb. 2, 17. Wherefore he ought in all things to be made like unto his brethren, that he might be a merciful and faithful high priest in things pertaining to God, to make reconciliation for the sins of the people.

units.la: {g}] Galat. 4, 4. Postquam venit plenum tempus, emisit Deus Filium suum, factum ex muliere.
units.tr: {g}] Gal. 4, 4. When the fullness of the time was come, God sent forth his Son, made of a woman.

units.la: Matthæi 1, 23. ex Esaiæ 7, 14. Ecce virgo illa pragnans erit, & pariet filium.
units.tr: Matt. 1, 23, from Isa. 7, 14. Behold, a virgin shall be with child, and shall bring forth a son.

units.la: Luc. 2, 7. Maria peperit filium suum primogenitum.
units.tr: Luke 2, 7. Mary brought forth her firstborn son.

units.la: {h}] Rom. 8, 32. Qui proprio Filio non pepercit, sed pro nobis omnibus tradidit eum.
units.tr: {h}] Rom. 8, 32. He who did not spare his own Son, but delivered him up for us all.

units.la: {i}] Joh. 3, 16. Sic Deus dilexit mundum, vt daret Filium suum vnigenitum.
units.tr: {i}] John 3, 16. God so loved the world that he gave his only begotten Son.

units.la: {k}] Matth.
units.tr: {k}] Matt.

units.la: Vt sciatis authoritatem habere Filium hominis in terra remittendi peccata.
units.tr: That you may know that the Son of man has authority on earth to forgive sins.

units.la: Vnus Deus, & vnus Mediator inter Deum & homines: nempe Homo Christus Iesus,
units.tr: There is one God, and one Mediator between God and men: the man Christ Jesus,

units.la: Nec in alio quoquam salus, nec enim aliud nomen est sub cælo, quod datum sit inter homines, per quod oporteat nos seruari.
units.tr: Neither is there salvation in any other, for there is no other name under heaven given among men by which we must be saved.

units.la: Est ergo fides recta, vt credamus, & confiteamur, quod Dominus noster Iesus Christus Dei Filius sit, Deus & Homo. Deus est, ex substantia Patris, ante sæcula genitus: & Homo, ex substantia matris in sæculo natus. Perfectus Deus, perfectus homo, ex anima rationali, & humana carne subsistens. Æqualis Patri secundum diuinitatem: minor Patri secundum humanitatem. Qui, licet Deus sit & homo, non duo tamen, sed unus est Christus.
units.tr: Therefore the true faith is that we believe and confess that our Lord Jesus Christ, the Son of God, is God and man. He is God, begotten of the substance of the Father before the ages, and man, born in time of the substance of his mother. Perfect God, perfect man, subsisting of a rational soul and human flesh. Equal to the Father according to his divinity, less than the Father according to his humanity. Who, although he is God and man, is nevertheless not two but one Christ.

units.la: II.
units.tr: II.

units.la: VNIO autem personalis duarum naturarum in Christo, juxta distinctionem Apostoli a, est inhabitatio corporalis omnis plenitudinis Deitatis in Christo: juxta declarationem Ecclesiæ, arcana & adoranda consociatio Deitatis θλόγω, & humanitatis assumptæ in unam personam siue ἕνωσιν, facta in utero matris βασυγχύτως, inconfusè, ἀτρέπτως, inconuertibiliter, ἀδιαιρέτως, indiuisè, ἀχωρίστως, & inseparabiliter: hoc est, saluis & distinctis manentibus naturis & naturarum proprietatibus: nullo nunc loco nec tempore separabilis.
units.tr: The personal union of the two natures in Christ, according to the Apostle's distinction, is the bodily indwelling of all the fullness of the Godhead in Christ. According to the declaration of the Church, it is the secret and adorable conjunction of the Godhead and the assumed humanity into one person, or union [ἕνωσις], made in the mother's womb: [θεολογικῶς] theologically, unconfusedly [ἀσυγχύτως], unchangeably [ἀτρέπτως], inconvertibly, indivisibly [ἀδιαιρέτως], undividedly, inseparably [ἀχωρίστως]. That is, the natures remain unimpaired and distinct, with their properties preserved, and the union is separable at no place or time.

units.la: TESTIMONIA SCRIPTVRÆ, ET SYMBOLORVM.
units.tr: TESTIMONIES OF HOLY SCRIPTURE AND OF THE ANCIENT TEACHERS.

units.la: In ipso (Christo) inhabitat omnis plenitudo Deitatis corporaliter.
units.tr: In him (Christ) dwells all the fullness of the Godhead bodily.

units.la: 2 Cor. 5, 19. Deus erat in Christo mundum reconcilians sibi.
units.tr: 2 Cor. 5, 19. God was in Christ, reconciling the world to himself.

units.la: Hebr. 2, 16. Non enim vtiq; Angelos assumsit, sed semen Abrahami assumsit.
units.tr: Hebr. 2, 16. For verily he took not on him the nature of angels, but he took on him the seed of Abraham.

units.la: Johan. 1, 14. Et Sermo ille factus est caro, & commoratus est inter nos.
units.tr: John 1, 14. And that Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us.

units.la: Spiritus sanctus superueniet in te, & virtus Altissimi obumbrabit te: propterea id etiam quod nascetur ex te sanctum, vocabitur Filius Dei.
units.tr: The Holy Spirit shall come upon you, and the power of the Most High shall overshadow you; therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of you shall be called the Son of God.

units.la: Deus & Homo vnus est Christus, non conuersione diuinitatis in carnem, sed assumtione humanitatis in Deum.
units.tr: God and man is one Christ, not by the conversion of the Godhead into flesh, but by the assumption of the manhood into God.

units.la: Item: In symbolo Oecumenico Concilij Chalcedonensis contra Eutychen ab Imperatore Martiano instituti Anno Christi ccccliii. Credimus Iesum Christum esse unicum & unigenitum Filium Dei, & Dominum in duabus naturis ἀσυγχύτως, ἀτρέπτως, ἀδιαιρέτως, χωρίστως: nusquam duarum naturarum diuersitate sublata propter unionem: salua magis proprietate utriusque naturae in unam personam concurrentibus: non in duas diuisum, aut segregatum, sed unum eundemque unigenitum Filium, Deum Verbum JESVM CHRISTVM.
units.tr: Likewise, in the ecumenical creed of the Council of Chalcedon, drawn up against Eutyches by the Emperor Marcian in the year of Christ 453: We believe that Jesus Christ is the one and only-begotten Son of God, and Lord, in two natures [ἀσυγχύτως], unchangeably [ἀτρέπτως], indivisibly [ἀδιαιρέτως], inseparably [χωρίστως]: the difference of the two natures being in no way taken away by the union, but rather the property of each nature being preserved, and both concurring into one person and one subsistence, not divided or separated into two persons, but one and the same only-begotten Son, God the Word, the Lord Jesus Christ.

units.la: III.
units.tr: III.

units.la: Propter hanc unionem personalem credimus, hanc personam JESVM CHRISTVM vere & proprie (non tropice aut figurate) esse Deum & Hominem: & de hac persona tum naturas ipsas, tum naturarum propria, & actiones vere & proprie vicissim praedicari in concreto de tota persona. Vere enim & proprie Christus Deus est homo{a}, natus ex virgine Maria{b}: ex semine Dauidis{c}: profecit aetate & sapientia{d}: est passus, mortuus, &c. Christus secundum suam humanitatem{e}: Vere item ac proprie Christus homo est Deus{f}: genitus a Patre{g}, ante Abrahamum existens{h}: immortalis{i}, omniscius{k}, omnipotens{l}, omniprasens{m}, creans & gubernans omnia cum Patre, &c. secundum suam diuinitatem{n}: non minus atque homo vere & proprie est rationalis, & immortalis secundum animam: irrationalis vero & mortalis secundum corpus{o}. Nam sicut anima rationalis (inquit Athanasius in symbolo) & caro vnus est homo, ita Deus & homo vnus est Christus. Quemadmodum igitur homini reipsa communes sunt proprietates corporis atque animae: ita personae Christi reipsa communes quoque sunt proprietates: quae & illi re ac nomine attribuuntur: non tamen secundum vtramque naturam, sed secundum eam, cui proprie competunt. Quod vocant Communicationem idiomatum. Et Damascenus περιχώρησιν ἀντιδόσεως, hoc est, Modum alternae attributionis.
units.tr: On account of this personal union, we believe that this person, Jesus Christ, is truly and properly (not tropically or figuratively) God and man; and that of this person both the natures themselves and the properties and actions of the natures are truly and properly predicated, in the concrete, of the whole person. For Christ is truly and properly God, man, born of the Virgin Mary, of the seed of David, grew in age and wisdom, suffered, died, etc., according to his humanity. Likewise, truly and properly, Christ as man is God, begotten of the Father, existing before Abraham, immortal, all-knowing, almighty, omnipresent, creating and governing all things with the Father, etc., according to his divinity. Just as man is truly and properly rational and immortal according to the soul, but irrational and mortal according to the body, so too: as the rational soul and the flesh are one man (says Athanasius in the creed), so God and man are one Christ. Therefore, just as the properties of body and soul are really common to a man, so the properties of the person of Christ are really common as well, and are attributed to him both in reality and in name; yet not according to each nature, but according to that nature to which they properly belong. This they call the communication of idioms. And Damascene calls it [περιχώρησιν ἀντιδόσεως], that is, the mode of mutual attribution.

units.la: TESTIMONIA SACRÆ SCRIPTVRÆ ET ANTIQVORVM DOCTORVM.
units.tr: TESTIMONIES OF HOLY SCRIPTURE AND OF THE ANCIENT TEACHERS.

units.la: {a} Phil. 2, 6. Christus similis hominibus factus. {b} Gal. 4, 4. Emisit Deus Filium suum factum ex muliere. {c} Rom. 1. vers. 3. Filius Dei factus est ex semine Danidis secundum carnem. {d} Lucae 2, 52. Iesus proficiebat sapientia & statura ac gratia apud Deum & homines.
units.tr: {a} Phil. 2, 6. Christ made like unto men. {b} Gal. 4, 4. God sent forth his Son, made of a woman. {c} Rom. 1, vers. 3. The Son of God was made of the seed of David according to the flesh. {d} Luke 2, 52. Jesus advanced in wisdom and stature, and in grace with God and men.

units.la: Justinus Martyr in Expositione fidei. Quemadmodum homo, cum sit unus, habet in se duas diversas naturas, & alia sui parte consulit, alia consultum exsequitur, animo decernens navis structuram, manibus vero opus decretum conficiens: sic Filius unus cum sit natura gemina, juxta alteram patrat miracula, juxta alteram humilia quaeque in se recipit. Quatenus enim ex Patre & Deus, fecit prodigia: quatenus e virgine & homo, crucem, passionem, & similia ultro pertulit naturaliter.
units.tr: Justin Martyr, in his Exposition of the Faith. As a man, though he is one, has within himself two different natures, and one part of him deliberates while another carries out what has been deliberated, the mind deciding on the structure of a ship while the hands complete the work decided upon; so the one Son, though his nature is twofold, performs miracles according to one nature and undergoes lowly things according to the other. For in so far as he is God from the Father, he worked wonders; in so far as he is man from the virgin, he willingly endured the cross, the passion, and similar things, naturally.

units.la: IV.
units.tr: IV.

units.la: Eodem modo nomina & actiones Mediatoris toti personae Nomina & tribuuntur: ac de ea vere ac proprie dicuntur in concreto (hoc actiones ossi- est nominibus personae) & quidem secundum utramque natu- cij Mediato- ram: quia ambae naturae una cum suis proprietatibus & actio- ris toti per- nibus requiruntur ad officium Mediatoris: in cuius execu- sone conue- tione unaquaeque natura communicatione alterius, operatur niunt secun- eas, quae illi proprie conveniunt a. Nam Christus secundu Dei- dumutram- tatem pariter & humanitatem suam noster est Mediator, servua- que natu- tor, intercessor, Salvator, Rex, Sacerdos, caput, Dominus, & ram. judex Mundi, qui omnia secundum utramque naturam novit, & per unamquamque naturam operatur ea, quae illi proprie conveniunt.
units.tr: In the same way, the names and actions of the Mediator are attributed to the whole person, and are truly and properly said of him in the concrete (that is, by the names of the person), and indeed according to both natures; because both natures, together with their properties and actions, are required for the office of Mediator. In the execution of that office, each nature, in communion with the other, works those things which belong properly to it. For Christ, according to his Godhead as well as his manhood, is our Mediator, Preserver, Intercessor, Saviour, King, Priest, Head, Lord, and Judge of the world, who knows all things according to both natures, and through each nature performs those things which belong properly to it.

units.la: TESTIMONIA ANTIQVORVM DOCTORVM.
units.tr: TESTIMONIES OF THE ANCIENT TEACHERS.

units.la: a] Damascenus lib. 3. cap. 15. de Orthodoxa fide: Christus agit secundum vtramque naturam. Et: Agit vtraque in ipso natura cum alterius communicatione: Verbo quidem operante, quae sunt verbi: propter authoritatem & potestatem diuinitatis, quaecunque sunt praecipua & regia: Corpore vero absoluente, quae sunt corporis munia, ad voluntatem verbi, quod ipsi counitur, cuius & factum est proprium.
units.tr: a] Damascene, book 3, chapter 15, On the Orthodox Faith: Christ acts according to each nature. And: Each nature acts in him with communion of the other: the Word indeed working what belongs to the Word, by reason of the authority and power of the divinity, whatever is excellent and royal; but the body carrying out what belongs to the body, at the will of the Word, to which it is united, and of which it is also the proper work.

units.la: Leo ad Flauianum cap. 4. Agit in vtraque forma cum alterius communione, quod proprium est: verbo scilicet operante, quod verbi est: & carne exsequente, quod carnis est.
units.tr: Leo, to Flavian, chapter 4: He acts in each form with communion of the other what is proper to it: namely, the Word working what belongs to the Word, and the flesh carrying out what belongs to the flesh.

units.la: Idem ad Leon. Augustt. epist. 95. Licet igitur in vno Domino Iesu Christo vero Dei atque hominis Filio, verbi & carnis vna persona sit, quae inseparabiliter atque indiuise communes habeat actiones: intelligenda tamen sunt ipsorum qualitates, & sincera fidei contemplatione cernendum est, ad quae proue-hatur humilitas carnis, & ad quae inclinetur altitudo diuinitatis: quid sit, quod caro sine verbo non agit, & quid sit, quod verbum sine carne non efficit.
units.tr: The same, to the Augusti Leo, letter 95: Therefore, although in the one Lord Jesus Christ, true Son of God and of man, there is one person of the Word and the flesh, which has its actions in common inseparably and undividedly, yet their qualities are to be understood, and by a sincere contemplation of faith we must discern to what the lowliness of the flesh is raised, and to what the loftiness of the divinity stoops: what it is that the flesh does not do without the Word, and what it is that the Word does not effect without the flesh.

units.la: Cyrillus Thesaur. lib. x. cap. 11. Quemadmodum igitur quando per carnem miracula efficiebat, non ipsi, vt homini hoc, sed vt DEO attribuimus: sic quando humano more aliquid de seipso dicit, quod alienum à Deitate sua videatur, carni idipsum accommodare debemus. Sic enim singula factorum atque dictorum congruè distribuentes à vera cognitione Saluatoris non aberramus.
units.tr: Cyril, Thesaurus, book 10, chapter 11: Just as, therefore, when he worked miracles through the flesh, we attribute them not to him as man, but to him as God, so when he says something of himself in a human manner which seems foreign to his Deity, we ought to apply that same thing to the flesh. For by distributing each of the deeds and words fittingly in this way, we do not stray from the true knowledge of the Saviour.

units.la: V.
units.tr: V.

units.la: Vtriusque autem naturae, etiam in personali vnione, consideratae (extra hanc enim non sunt) proprietates in abstracto, hoc est, nominibus naturarum, non possunt permutari, sicut nec ipsae naturae. Neque enim recte dicitur: Deitas est humanitas: siue homo: est creata, corporea, visibilis, finita, & circumscripta, mortua, sepulta, &c. Neque item recte dicitur: Humanitas est Deitas, siue Deus, est aeterna, increata, incorporea, inuisibilis, infinita & omnipraesens, omnipotens, &c. Verum vnicuique naturae tribuendum est, quod illi proprie competit: Diuinitati proprietates diuinae, humanitati humanae. Id nisi fiat, essentialis differentia naturarum confunditur, ac mutatur in Eutychia-nam & Syncksfeldianam naturarum permistionem. Quia in distincdistinctione proprietatum consistit distinctio naturarum: atque ita duae naturae, quae eaedem habent proprietates (siue natura siue per communicationem) non erunt amplius duae naturae, sed vna duntaxat natura a. Fieri etiam non potest, vt vna natura simul duas contrarias in se contineat proprietates b.
units.tr: The properties of each nature, considered even in the personal union (for outside it they do not exist), cannot be interchanged in the abstract, that is, in the names of the natures, any more than the natures themselves can be. For it is not right to say: "The Deity is humanity," or "man is created, corporeal, visible, finite and circumscribed, dead, buried," etc. Nor again is it right to say: "The humanity is Deity," or "God is eternal, uncreated, incorporeal, invisible, infinite and omnipresent, omnipotent," etc. Rather, to each nature must be attributed what properly belongs to it: to the Deity the divine properties, to the humanity the human. If this is not done, the essential difference of the natures is confused and changed into the Eutychian and Schwenckfeldian mixing of the natures. For the distinction of the natures consists in the distinction of the properties; and so two natures which have the same properties (whether by nature or by communication) will no longer be two natures, but only one nature. Nor can it happen that one nature contains two contrary properties at the same time.a b

units.la: TESTIMONIA ANTIQVORVM DOCTORVM.
units.tr: TESTIMONIES OF THE ANCIENT TEACHERS.

units.la: a Damascenus lib. III. cap. 14. & 15. ὢν γὰρ ἡ ὑπόστασις αὐτῆ, πάντων τῆς φύσεως καὶ ἡ ἐνέργεια αὐτοῦ. ὧν δὲ ἀλλὰ φύσεως ἡ οὐσία, πάντων ἀλλὰ φύσεως καὶ ἡ φύσις καὶ ἡ ἐνέργεια. ἡ τὸ ἀπαράλλαξ, ἀν φύσεως καὶ ἡ ἐνέργεια ἡ αὐτὴ, πάντων τῆς ἡ ὑπόστασις ἡ αὐτή. ἀν δὲ ἀλλαχοῦ φύσεως καὶ ἐνέργεια, πάντων τῆς ἡ οὐσία διαφορά. Hoc est: Quorum natura est eadem, horum & voluntas & actio est eadem. Quorum vero natura est diuersa, horum quoque voluntas & actio est diuersa: & rursum, quorum voluntas & actio est eadem, horum & natura est eadem: quorum vero diuersa est voluntas, & actio est diuersa, horum quoque natura est diuersa.
units.tr: a Damascene, book III, chapters 14 and 15: [ὢν γὰρ ἡ ὑπόστασις αὐτῆ, πάντων τῆς φύσεως καὶ ἡ ἐνέργεια αὐτοῦ. ὧν δὲ ἀλλὰ φύσεως ἡ οὐσία, πάντων ἀλλὰ φύσεως καὶ ἡ φύσις καὶ ἡ ἐνέργεια. ἡ τὸ ἀπαράλλαξ, ἀν φύσεως καὶ ἡ ἐνέργεια ἡ αὐτὴ, πάντων τῆς ἡ ὑπόστασις ἡ αὐτή. ἀν δὲ ἀλλαχοῦ φύσεως καὶ ἐνέργεια, πάντων τῆς ἡ οὐσία διαφορά.] That is: Those whose nature is the same, their will and their action are also the same. Those whose nature is different, their will and action are also different. And again, those whose will and action are the same, their nature is also the same; but those whose will is different and whose action is different, their nature is also different.

units.la: b Ibid. lib. 3. cap. 3. Quomodo possibile est eandem naturam secundum idem creatam esse & increatam, mortalem & immortalem, circumscriptam & incircumscriptam?
units.tr: b Ibid., book 3, chapter 3: How is it possible for the same nature, in the same respect, to be both created and uncreated, mortal and immortal, circumscribed and uncircumscribed?

units.la: Theodoretus Dial. II. Si Christus vna tantum est natura, quomodo ei contraria accommodari possunt? Nam esse in principio, & ab Abrahamo & Dauide originem ducere, contraria utique sunt.
units.tr: Theodoret, Dialogue II: If Christ is only one nature, how can contrary attributes be ascribed to him? For to be in the beginning, and to derive origin from Abraham and David, are certainly contraries.

units.la: VI.
units.tr: VI.

units.la: Hinc patet, Humanitatē Christi reipsa non manere humanitatem, sed mutari in Deitatem, atque ita naturam eius confundi: in Christo item non permanere duas distinctas naturas, sed duas miscerii in vnam, positis his sententiis: Humanitatem in & propter vnionem personalem assumpsisse cum λόγῳ omnes quoque proprietates & operationes ἑ λόγος, esse & operari omnia, quae λόγῳ & quocunque tandem modo sententiae istae palliantur. Quin immo multo magis, si statuatur, humanitatem triplices in se habere proprietates, naturales scilicet, supernaturales, praeternaturales ac diuinas.
units.tr: From this it is plain that the humanity of Christ, in reality, does not remain humanity but is changed into deity, and so its nature is confused; likewise that in Christ two distinct natures do not remain, but two are mixed into one. These assertions are laid down: that the humanity, in and on account of the personal union, has assumed with the Word all the properties and operations of the Word, so as to be and to do all things that the Word is and does, and whatever way these opinions are dressed up. Nay, much more so, if it is maintained that the humanity has in itself threefold properties, namely natural, supernatural, preternatural and divine.

units.la: Proinde reijcimus haec à scriptura & fide Catholica aliena dogmata haereticorum veterum & recentium.
units.tr: Therefore we reject these doctrines of old and recent heretics, which are alien to Scripture and to the Catholic faith.

units.la: 1. Quod Christus non sit verus Deus, sed purus homo.
units.tr: 1. That Christ is not true God, but a mere man.

units.la: 2. Quod Christus secundum Deitatem sit tantum spiritus creatus ante omnia, ὁ κ μὴ ὢν ἀγέννητον.
units.tr: 2. That Christ, according to his Deity, is only a created spirit before all things, [ὁ κ μὴ ὢν ἀγέννητον], and not unbegotten.

units.la: 3. Quod non sit verus ac perfectus homo, animo & corpore nobis ὁμοούσιος, manens etiam in gloria.
units.tr: 3. That he is not a true and perfect man, consubstantial with us [ὁμοούσιος] in soul and body, remaining so even in glory.

units.la: 4. Quod alia sit Filij Dei, alia Filij Mariæ in CHRISTO ὑπόστασις.
units.tr: 4. That the hypostasis of the Son of God is one, and that of the Son of Mary another, in CHRIST.

units.la: 5. Quod vnio personalis in vtero matris coeperit: per resurrectionem vero & ascensionem & sessionem ad dextram Maiestatis Dei penitus absoluta fuerit, facta naturarum exaquatione in gloria: ita vt corpus, caro, & sanguis CHRISTI perfecte vnius sint essentiæ, potentiæ, & efficaciæ cum DEO & cum λόγῳ.
units.tr: 5. That the personal union began in the womb of the mother, but was completely finished through the resurrection, the ascension and the sitting at the right hand of the Majesty of God, the natures having been made equal in glory; so that the body, flesh and blood of Christ are perfectly one in essence, power and efficacy with God and with the Word.

units.la: 6. Quod humanitas Christi per communicatam gloriam & maiestatem exæquata sit Deo: in natura autem Deus non sit.
units.tr: 6. That the humanity of Christ, through the communicated glory and majesty, has been made equal to God, yet is not God in nature.

units.la: 7. Quod vnionis differentia specifica sit omnium diuinæ naturæ proprietatum realis cum humanitate communicatio, ita vt in Filium hominis realiter effusa sit ἔλαχε omnipotentia, omnipræsentia, iustitia & maiestas.
units.tr: 7. That the specific difference of the union is a real communication of all the divine properties to the humanity, so that omnipotence, omnipresence, justice and majesty have been really poured out into the Son of man [ἔλαχε].

units.la: 8. Quod in Christo sit duplex diuinitas: Communicans, & communicata, siue participans, & participata.
units.tr: 8. That in Christ there is a twofold deity: the communicating and the communicated, or the participating and the participated.

units.la: 9. Quod differentia specifica inhabitationis ἔλαχε in homine Christo, & aliis sanctis hominibus, in eo sit posita, quod sanctis aliquot tantum proprietates diuinæ reipsa sint communicatæ, homini vero Christo omnes simul.
units.tr: 9. That the specific difference of the indwelling [ἔλαχε] in the man Christ, and in other holy men, lies in this: that to some saints only some divine properties have really been communicated, but to the man Christ all of them at once.

units.la: 10. Quod humanitas Christi realiter sit vbique: non tamen essentia corporis & animæ suæ.
units.tr: 10. That the humanity of Christ is really everywhere, yet not the essence of his body and soul.

units.la: 11. Quod caro Christi sit Deus.
units.tr: 11. That the flesh of Christ is God.

units.la: 12. Quod Christus homo non sit Deus naturalis.
units.tr: 12. That Christ as man is not natural God.

units.la: 13. Quod humana natura Christi Jerosolymis visibiliter mortua fuerit in cruce: simul vero inuisibiliter vbiq; viua & mortua, intra & extra sepulchrum, ante & post resurrectionem.
units.tr: 13. That the human nature of Christ died visibly on the cross at Jerusalem, yet at the same time is invisibly alive and dead everywhere, within and outside the sepulchre, before and after the resurrection.

units.la: 14. Quod caro Christi respectu vnionis cum λόγῳ illocali, omnem localitatem altissimè transcenderit, & in λόγῳ illocalem existendi modum vere sortiatur.
units.tr: 14. That the flesh of Christ, with respect to its union with the Word, is illocal, transcends all locality most highly, and truly obtains an illocal mode of existence in the Word.

units.la: 15. Et hoc Vbiquitariorum ψεῦδος: Quod non totus, sed dimidius tantum Christus sit, patiatur & agat id, quod Christus est, patitur, & agit secundum alteram naturam, & non secundum vtramque.
units.tr: 15. And this is the falsehood of the Ubiquitarians: that Christ is not whole, but only half; that what Christ is suffers and acts according to one nature only, and not according to both.

units.la: E quo fundamento Nestorianismum falsò impegerunt reformatis Ecclesiis. Necessariò namque sequeretur, dimidium tantum Christū ab æterno esse à Patre genitum, natum ex Maria, in terris ambulasse, pro nobis mortuum, sepultum, resurrexisse, adscendisse ad cœlum. Quas hæreticas opiniones damnamus & reijcimus.
units.tr: From this foundation they falsely charged the reformed Churches with Nestorianism. For it would necessarily follow that only half of Christ was begotten of the Father from eternity, was born of Mary, walked on earth, died for us, was buried, rose again and ascended to heaven. These heretical opinions we condemn and reject.

units.la: ARTICVLVS II.
units.tr: ARTICLE II.

units.la: DE MORTE CHRISTI ET EIVS MERITO.
units.tr: On the Death of Christ and Its Merit.

units.la: I.
units.tr: I.

units.la: Credimus CHRISTVM redemtorem nostrum verè mortuum esse carne : propter peccata nostra : & vnica oblatione in perpetuum consecrauisse eos, qui sanctificantur .
units.tr: We believe that CHRIST our Redeemer truly died in the flesh for our sins, and by one offering has consecrated for ever those who are sanctified.

units.la: TESTIMONIA SCRIPTVRÆ.
units.tr: Testimonies of Scripture.

units.la: Iesus autem cum rursum clamasset voce magna, emisit spiritum.Christus mortificatus est carne. Cum igitur Christus passus sit pro nobis carne.Christus traditus est in mortem, propter lapsus nostros.Christus unica oblatione consecrauit in perpetuum eos, qui sanctificantur.
units.tr: Jesus, when he had cried again with a loud voice, yielded up the spirit. Christ was put to death in the flesh. Since therefore Christ suffered for us in the flesh. Christ was delivered up to death for our transgressions. By one offering Christ has perfected for ever those who are sanctified.

units.la: II.
units.tr: II.

units.la: Credimus quoque, hanc mortem Filij Dei solam, perfectum & sufficiens λύτρον esse expiandis & delendis omnibus totius mundi peccatis : meritum immensum Justitiæ: medicinam Catholicam mortis: fontem perennem & inexhaustum vitæ æternæ .
units.tr: We believe also that this death of the Son of God alone is a perfect and sufficient ransom [λύτρον] for expiating and blotting out all the sins of the whole world; an immense merit of righteousness; the Catholic medicine of death; and a perpetual and inexhaustible fountain of eternal life.

units.la: TESTIMONIA SCRIPTVRAE.
units.tr: Testimonies of Scripture.

units.la: Nec est in alio quoquam salus: nec est aliud nomen sub cælo, quod datum sit inter homines, per quod oporteat nos saluari.Ecce agnus ille Dei, qui tollit peccatum mundi. 1 Joh. 2,2. Christus est propitiatio pro peccatis nostris: nec pro nostris solum, sed etiam pro totius mundi peccatis.
units.tr: Neither is there salvation in any other, for there is no other name under heaven given among men by which we must be saved. Behold the Lamb of God, who takes away the sin of the world. 1 John 2:2. Christ is the propitiation for our sins, and not for ours only, but also for the sins of the whole world.

units.la: III.
units.tr: III.

units.la: Sed & scimus, immotam & Catholicam hanc Euangelij voluntatem esse. Johan. 3. v. 18. 38. Qui credit in Filium Dei, habet vitam æternam. Qui non credit Filio, non videbit vitam, sed ira Dei manet super eos.
units.tr: But we also know that this Catholic will of the Gospel is unchanging. John 3:18, 38. He who believes in the Son of God has eternal life. He who does not believe the Son shall not see life, but the wrath of God abides on him.

units.la: IV.
units.tr: IV.

units.la: Licet itaque diuinissima hæc quasi [?] omnibus in Euangelio sit proposita : nullam tamen vim eius in homines transtransfundi credimus, nisi fiat applicatio per fidem in Filium Dei : perinde vt nulla vis artis medicæ & pharmacorum in ægros redundat, nisi audiatur medicus, & fiat applicatio medicinæ : Qua metaphora Spiritum sanctum in hoc negotio vsum videmus .
