units.tr: Although, therefore, this most divine [?] is set forth to all in the Gospel, we believe that its power is not transfused into men unless application is made through faith in the Son of God; just as the power of the medical art and of medicines does not flow into the sick unless the physician is heard and the medicine is applied. In this metaphor we see the Holy Spirit also using the matter.

units.la: TESTIMONIA SCRIPTVRÆ, ET ALIORVM.
units.tr: Testimonies of Scripture and of Others.

units.la: Matth.11,28. Venite ad me omnes, qui fatigati estis, & onerati, nam ego faciam, vt requiescatis.
units.tr: Matt. 11:28. Come to me, all you who are weary and heavy laden, for I will give you rest.

units.la: Marci 16,15. Prædicate Euangelium omni creaturæ.
units.tr: Mark 16:15. Preach the Gospel to every creature.

units.la: Joh. 3,36. Qui credit in Filium, habet vitam æternam: qui verò non obtemperat Filio, non videbit vitam, sed ira Dei manet super eum.
units.tr: John 3:36. He who believes in the Son has eternal life; but he who does not obey the Son shall not see life, but the wrath of God abides on him.

units.la: Johan.8, 24. Nisi credideritis, me eum esse, moriemini in peccatis vestris.
units.tr: John 8:24. Unless you believe that I am he, you will die in your sins.

units.la: Esaiæ 7. vers. 9. Si non credatis verbis meis, id fit, quia non estis stabiles.
units.tr: Isaiah 7:9. If you do not believe my words, it is because you are not steadfast.

units.la: Marci 16,16. Qui crediderit & baptizatus fuerit, seruabitur: qui vero non crediderit, condemnabitur.
units.tr: Mark 16:16. He who believes and is baptized will be saved; but he who does not believe will be condemned.

units.la: Chemnitius Harmonia Euangel. lib. 2. pag. 83. Sicut herba ægro non medetur, nisi verè vsurpetur & applicetur: ita virtus passionis Christi SVFFICIENS est ad tollenda peccata totius mundi: sed illis solis prodest, qui agnum hunc recipiunt.
units.tr: Chemnitz, Harmony of the Gospels, book 2, p. 83. As an herb does not heal the sick unless it is truly taken and applied, so the power of Christ's passion is SUFFICIENT to take away the sins of the whole world, but it benefits only those who receive this Lamb.

units.la: Esa.53,5. Liuor eius sanitas fuit nobis.
units.tr: Isa. 53:5. By his bruise we were healed.

units.la: 1 Pet.2,24. Cuius vibicibus sanati estis.
units.tr: 1 Pet. 2:24. By whose stripes you were healed.

units.la: V.
units.tr: V.

units.la: Proinde dubium esse non potest, quin ij omnes, & soli, efficacitatem mortis Christi, hoc est, redemtionem, reconciliationem cum Deo, remissionem peccatorum, iustitiam, & salutem æternam percipiant, quotquot hæc beneficia in Euangelio fide amplectuntur : cæteri ab hac efficacitate & beneficiis in æternum exclusi manent, quotquot sine fide hoc sæculum pertranseunt .
units.tr: Therefore there can be no doubt that all those, and only those, who embrace these benefits in the Gospel by faith receive the efficacy of Christ's death, that is, redemption, reconciliation with God, forgiveness of sins, righteousness, and eternal salvation; while all the rest, as many as pass through this age without faith, remain excluded from this efficacy and these benefits for ever.

units.la: TESTIMONIA SCRIPTVRÆ.
units.tr: Testimonies of Scripture.

units.la: Joh.1,12. Quotquot exceperunt, dedit eis hoc ius, vt filij Dei sint scilicet, nempe iis, qui credunt in nomen eius.
units.tr: John 1:12. As many as received him, to them he gave the right to become children of God, namely to those who believe in his name.

units.la: Joh.5,24. Amen, amen dico vobis: qui sermonem meum audit, & credit ei, qui misit me, habet vitam æternam.
units.tr: John 5:24. Verily, verily, I say to you, he who hears my word and believes him who sent me has eternal life.

units.la: a] Joh.1,12 ... (marginal citation as printed, see above)
units.tr: a] John 1:12 ... (marginal citation as printed, see above)

units.la: Haec est autem voluntas eius, qui misit me: ut omnis, qui conspicit Filium, & credit in eum, habeat vitam aeternam.
units.tr: For this is the will of him who sent me, that everyone who sees the Son and believes in him should have eternal life.

units.la: Huic omnes Prophetæ testimonium dant, remissionem peccatorum accepturum per nomen eius quemvis, qui credit in eum.
units.tr: To him all the prophets bear witness, that everyone who believes in him will receive forgiveness of sins through his name.

units.la: Et consecratus factus est author salutis æternæ omnibus, qui ipsi auscultant.
units.tr: And, having been made perfect, he became the author of eternal salvation to all who obey him.

units.la: Qui non credit in eum, jam condemnatus est: quia non credit in nomen unigeniti Filij Dei.
units.tr: He who does not believe in him is already condemned, because he does not believe in the name of the only-begotten Son of God.

units.la: Qui non obtemperat Filio, non videbit vitam, sed ira Dei manet super eum.
units.tr: He who does not obey the Son shall not see life, but the wrath of God abides on him.

units.la: An ignoratis injustos non esse Dei hereditatem possessuros?
units.tr: Do you not know that the unrighteous will not inherit the kingdom of God?

units.la: Foris erunt canes, & scortatores.
units.tr: Outside are the dogs and the sorcerers.

units.la: Eijce ancillam & filium eius: nequaquam enim heres erit filius ancillæ cum filio liberæ.
units.tr: Cast out the bondwoman and her son, for the son of the bondwoman shall by no means be heir with the son of the free woman.

units.la: VI.
units.tr: VI.

units.la: Accipimus quidem, promissiones evangelij universales esse, & ad omnes pertinere: verum non ad incredulos & non conversos Turcas, Judæos, Ethnicos, Epicureos, quamdiu tales manent, sed ad omnes credentes. Est enim omnibus promissionibus annexa conditio fidei in Christum expressa vel subintellecta: id quod apertus scripturæ textus ostendit .
units.tr: We indeed accept that the promises of the Gospel are universal and pertain to all; yet not to unbelievers and unconverted Turks, Jews, heathens, and Epicureans, so long as they remain such, but to all who believe. For a condition of faith in Christ, either expressed or understood, is attached to all the promises, as the plain text of Scripture shows.

units.la: TESTIMONIA SCRIPTVRÆ.
units.tr: TESTIMONIES OF SCRIPTURE.

units.la: Ut quisquis credit in eum, non pereat, sed habeat vitam æternam.
units.tr: That whoever believes in him should not perish, but have eternal life.

units.la: Iustitia Dei per fidem Iesu Christi in omnes & super omnes, qui credunt.
units.tr: The righteousness of God through faith in Jesus Christ, unto all and upon all who believe.

units.la: Huic omnes Prophetæ testimonium dant, remissionem peccatorum accepturum per nomen eius quemvis, qui crediderit in eum.
units.tr: To him all the prophets bear witness, that everyone who believes in him will receive forgiveness of sins through his name.

units.la: Conclusit scriptura omnia sub peccatum, ut promissio ex fide Iesu Christi daretur credentibus.
units.tr: Scripture has shut up all things under sin, so that the promise by faith in Jesus Christ might be given to those who believe.

units.la: VII.
units.tr: VII.

units.la: Quoties igitur scriptura dicit, Christum pro omnibus esse mortuum , dedisse semetipsum ἀντίλυτρον pro omnibus : gustasse mortem pro omnibus : esse ἱλασμὸν pro peccatis totius mundi : id vel de magnitudine pretij, seu de meriti sufficientia pro omnibus, vel de efficaci redemtione omnium quotquot ex Judæis & gentibus mortis eius beneficia fide amplectuntur, necessacessario intelligendum est. In his enim, inquit Ambrosius, specialis quaedam VNIVERSITAS censetur. Nihil vero magis illud aduersabitur Euangelij doctrinae, quam si dicant nonnulli, Christum sua morte promiscuè redemisse & Deo conciliasse fideles Christianos, & infideles, Turcas, Ethnicos, Epicureos, hypocritas, &c. quamuis meritum mortis CHRISTI fide non acceperint. Quae sententia plane impia est, & Verbo DEI contraria.
units.tr: Whenever, therefore, Scripture says that Christ died for all, gave himself as a ransom [ἀντίλυτρον] for all, tasted death for all, and is the propitiation [ἱλασμός] for the sins of the whole world, this must necessarily be understood either of the greatness of the price, or of the sufficiency of his merit for all, or of the effective redemption of all who, whether from the Jews or from the Gentiles, embrace with faith the benefits of his death. For in these passages, says Ambrose, a certain special universality is meant. Nothing, however, is more opposed to the doctrine of the Gospel than when some say that Christ by his death redeemed and reconciled to God, without distinction, Christian believers and unbelievers, Turks, Gentiles, Epicureans, hypocrites, and so on, even though they have not received the merit of Christ's death by faith. That opinion is plainly impious and contrary to the Word of God.

units.la: TESTIMONIA SCRIPTVRAE ET ANTIQVORVM DOCTORVM.
units.tr: TESTIMONIES OF SCRIPTURE AND OF THE ANCIENT TEACHERS.

units.la: 2 Corinth.5,15. Christus pro omnibus mortuus est, vt qui viuunt, posthac non sibi viuant, sed ei, & qui pro ipsis mortuus est, & suscitatus est.
units.tr: 2 Corinthians 5:15. Christ died for all, that those who live should no longer live to themselves, but to him, and to him who died for them and was raised again.

units.la: 1 Tim. 2, 6. Christus seipsum dedit redemptionis pretium pro omnibus.
units.tr: 1 Timothy 2:6. Christ gave himself as a ransom for all.

units.la: Heb.2,9. Vt gratia Dei pro omnibus mortem gustaret.
units.tr: Hebrews 2:9. That by the grace of God he should taste death for all.

units.la: 1 Joh. 2,2. Ipse est propitiatio pro peccatis nostris, nec pro nostris solum, sed pro totius mundi peccatis.
units.tr: 1 John 2:2. He himself is the propitiation for our sins, and not for ours only, but for the sins of the whole world.

units.la: Ambros. de vocatione gentium l.1. cap.3. Habet populus Dei plenitudinem suam: & quamuis magna pars hominum saluantis gratiam aut repellat, aut negligat: in electis tamen & praescitis, atque ab omnium generalitate diferetis, specialis quaedam censetur vniuersitas: vt de toto mundo totus mundus liberatus, & de omnibus hominibus omnes homines videantur assumti.
units.tr: Ambrose, On the Calling of the Gentiles, book 1, chapter 3. The people of God has its fullness; and although a great part of mankind either rejects or neglects the grace that saves, nevertheless among the elect and foreknown, and set apart from the generality of all, a certain special universality is reckoned: so that from the whole world the whole world is seen to be delivered, and from all men all men are seen to be taken up.

units.la: VIII.
units.tr: VIII.

units.la: Hinc recepta est vetus, nec incommoda distinctio: Mortuum esse Christum pro omnibus hominibus, quantum ad meriti sufficientiam, seu pretij magnitudinem: pro omnibus & solis credentibus, quantum ad efficaciam, seu efficientiam, seu fructum mortis: quem non omnes, sed soli credentes percipiunt: caeteri vero infidelitate sua respuunt.
units.tr: Hence has come the old and not inconvenient distinction: that Christ died for all men as to the sufficiency of his merit, or the greatness of the price; for all and only believers as to the efficacy, or efficiency, or fruit of his death, which not all but only believers receive, while the rest reject it through their unbelief.

units.la: TESTIMONIA SCHOLASTICORVM ET PATRVM.
units.tr: Testimonies of the Schoolmen and the Fathers.

units.la: Innocentius III. lib.2. Myst. Missae, cap.4. Anno Christi 1200. Pro solis praedestinatis effusus est, quantum ad efficientiam: sed pro cunctis hominibus effusus est, quantum ad sufficientiam. Effusio quippe sanguinis justi pro injustis tam fuit dives ad pretium, vt si vniuersitas crederet in Redemptorem, nullum omnino diaboli vincula retinerent: quia, sicut Apostolus ait: Vbi abundauit peccatum, superabundauit & gratia. Thomas Aquinas de veritate mat. Art. 26. q. 7. An. Christi 1270. Meritum Christi, quantum ad sufficientiam & qualiter se habet ad omnes: non autem ad efficaciam. Quod accidit partim ex libero arbitrio, partim ex divina electione: per quam quibusdam misericorditer effectus meritorum Christi confertur: quibusdam vero justo Dei judicio subtrahitur.
units.tr: Innocent III, Mysteries of the Mass, bk 2, ch. 4, in the year of Christ 1200: He was poured out for the predestined alone as regards efficacy, but he was poured out for all men as regards sufficiency. For the shedding of the blood of the just for the unjust is so rich in price that, if the whole world believed in the Redeemer, the chains of the devil would hold no one at all; because, as the Apostle says, where sin abounded, grace did much more abound. Thomas Aquinas, De veritate, art. 26, q. 7, in the year of Christ 1270: The merit of Christ, as regards sufficiency, relates to all men, but not as regards efficacy. This happens partly from free will and partly from divine election, by which the effect of Christ's merits is mercifully conferred on some, but withdrawn from others by the just judgment of God.

units.la: Idem in cap. V. Apocal. De redemtione facta per passionem Dei est loqui dupliciter. Aut secundum sufficientiam: & sic passio redemit omnes, quia quantum est ex se, omnes liberavit. Omnibus enim redimendis & salvandis sufficiens est: etiamsi essent infiniti mundi: ut dicit Anshelmus lib. 2. Cur Deus homo, &c. cap. 14. Aut secundum efficientiam: & sic non omnes redimit per passionem: quia non omnes adhærent redemptori: & ideo non omnes habent efficaciam redemptionis.
units.tr: The same, on Revelation ch. 5: Concerning the redemption made by the passion of God, one may speak in two ways. Either according to sufficiency, and so the passion redeemed all, because, as far as it lies in itself, it has freed all. For it is sufficient to redeem and save all men, even if there were infinite worlds, as Anselm says in bk 2 of Cur Deus homo, ch. 14. Or according to efficacy, and so it does not redeem all by the passion, because not all cling to the Redeemer, and therefore not all have the efficacy of redemption.

units.la: Petrus Lombardus, Thomæ Aquinatis in Scholasticis suffraganeus, l. 3. dist. 22. Christus se Deo Trinitati obtulit pro omnibus, quantum ad pretij sufficientiam: sed pro electis tantum, quantum ad efficaciam: quia prædestinatis tantum salutem effecit.
units.tr: Peter Lombard, a supporter of Thomas Aquinas among the Schoolmen, bk 3, dist. 22: Christ offered himself to the triune God for all, as regards the sufficiency of the price, but for the elect only, as regards efficacy, because he effected salvation only for the predestined.

units.la: Petrus Galatinus celebris Scriptor inter Pontificios de Arcanis Catholicæ veritatis lib. 8. cap. 14. super locum Esaiæ cap. 53. Seruus meus justus justificabit multos. Licet passio Christi ad delenda omnium peccata sufficiens esse debeat, non tamen omnium peccata deletura erat: sed eorum duntaxat, qui in eum crediturí essent, atq; pœnitentiam acturi. Eam ob rem dicit: Et ipse peccata multorum tulit.
units.tr: Peter Galatinus, a celebrated writer among the Papists, On the Secrets of Catholic Truth, bk 8, ch. 14, on Isaiah 53: "My righteous servant shall justify many" [Isa. 53:11]. Although the passion of Christ ought to be sufficient to blot out the sins of all, it was not going to blot out the sins of all, but only of those who were going to believe in him and repent. For this reason he says: "And he himself bore the sins of many" [Isa. 53:12].

units.la: IX.
units.tr: IX.

units.la: Sic præter Scholasticos etiam Orthodoxi Patres docent. Ita Prosper Aquitanicus Anno Christi 460. Resp. ad obiect. Vicent. Obiect. 1. Cum rectè dicatur Saluator pro totius Mundi redemtione crucifixus, propter rerum naturæ humanæ susceptionem, & propter commune in primo homine perditionem: potest tamen dici PRO HIS TANTVM CRVCIFIXVS, quibus mors ipsius profuit. Et Cyrillus in Ioh. lib. 11. cap. 19. dicit, Christum esse paracletum propeccatis totius mundi: hoc est, non Iudæis tantum, sed etiam pro aliis gentibus, seu, pro omnibus, qui per fidem vocati ad justitiam & sanctificationem perveniunt: & Mediatoris bonum non injuria HIS TANTVMMODO attribui, quorum est Mediator & Pontifex.
units.tr: Thus, besides the Schoolmen, the orthodox Fathers also teach this. So Prosper of Aquitaine, in the year of Christ 460, in his reply to the objections of Vincent, objection 1: Although it is rightly said that the Saviour was crucified for the redemption of the whole world, on account of the assumption of human nature and the common perdition in the first man, yet he can be said to have been CRUCIFIED FOR THOSE ALONE to whom his death profited. And Cyril, on John, bk 11, ch. 19, says that Christ is the paraclete for the sins of the whole world, that is, not for the Jews only but also for the other nations, or for all who, called through faith, come to righteousness and sanctification; and the good of the Mediator is not wrongly attributed to THOSE ALONE of whom he is Mediator and Priest.

units.la: X.
units.tr: X.

units.la: Omnium autem clarissimè Augustinus: cuius sententiam, quoniam tota nostra est, hoc loco Sycophantis quibusdam ponendam duximus. Sic igitur ille Tom. I. ad Attic. falso imp. Art. 1. Quod ad MAGNITVDINEM & POTENTIAM PRETII, & quod ad vnam pertinet causam generis humani: sanguis Christi redemtio est totius mundi. Sed qui hoc saeculum SINE FIDE & sine regeneratio-nis sacramento pertranseunt, REDEMTIONIS ALIENI SVNT. Cum itaque propter vnam omnium naturam, & vnam omnium causam à Domino nostro in veritate suscepta recte OMNES dicantur REDEMTI, & tamen NON OMNES à CAPTIVITATE sint erutI; Redemtionis proprietas haud dubie PENES ILLOS est de quibus princeps mundi missus est foras, & jam non vasa diaboli, sed membra sunt Christi. Cuius mors non ita impensa est generi humano, vt ad redemtionem eius etiam, qui regenerandi non erant, pertinerent: sed ita, vt quod per vnicum exemplum gestum est pro vniuersis, per singulare sacramentum celebraretur in singulis. Poculum quippe im-mortalitatis, quod confectum est de infirmitate nostra, & veritate nostra, & veritate divina, habet quidem in se, vt omnibus prosit, sed si non bibitur, non medetur.
units.tr: But Augustine most clearly of all, whose opinion, since it is wholly ours, we have thought fit to set down here against certain sycophants. Thus he writes in Tom. I, to Attic., falsely called imperfect, art. 1: As regards the GREATNESS AND POWER OF THE PRICE, and as far as it pertains to the one cause of the human race, the blood of Christ is the redemption of the whole world. But those who pass through this age WITHOUT FAITH and without the sacrament of regeneration ARE STRANGERS TO REDEMPTION. Therefore, since on account of the one nature of all and the one cause of all, which our Lord truly assumed, all are rightly said to be REDEEMED, and yet NOT ALL have been rescued from CAPTIVITY, the proper possession of redemption undoubtedly lies WITH THOSE of whom the prince of the world has been cast out, and who are no longer vessels of the devil but members of Christ. His death was not so bestowed on the human race that those who were not to be regenerated also belonged to its redemption; rather, what was done for all through the one example is celebrated in individuals through a particular sacrament. For the cup of immortality, which has been prepared from our weakness, our truth, and divine truth, indeed has in itself that it benefits all; but if it is not drunk, it does not heal.

units.la: PHILIPPI PAREI MONITIO AD LECTOREM.
units.tr: A Notice from Philip Pareus to the Reader.

units.la: Hanc doctrinam de mortis Christi efficacia D. PAREVS paulo fusius tractauit in Scalae aureae salutis parte I. vbi sin-gularem de ea scripsit Diatriben: nec non in Epitome Arminia-nismi, siue Examine quinque Articulorum Ministrorum Remon-strantium in Belgio: vt & corpore doctrinae Christianae ad quaestio-nem XL. Edit posthumae: itemque Collegio XVIII. Disp. XXIII. De morte Christi pro omnibus: ac denique Oratione peculiari, quam posuimus inter ORATIONES, habitas in Academia, Tomo II. Oper. Theolog. D. PAREI. In quibus scriptis distinctionem hanc Scholasticorum & antiquorum patrum, sufficientiae, inquam, & efficientiae, cum aliis orthodoxis Theologis defendit ac retinet: sed paulo ante obitū suum optimus senex, cum intelligeret, in synodo Provinciali Dordracena distinctionem illam sub nomine & autori-tate PAREI in discrimen a fratribus nonnullis imprudenter fuisse vocatam, accuratius nonnihil de ea cogitare coepit: arbitratus, illam non vsquequaq; esse necessariam: cum & absq; illa scriptura dicta εὐαγγελφων videantur commodè posse conciliari.
units.tr: Pareus treated this doctrine of the efficacy of Christ's death somewhat more fully in part I of his Scala aurea salutis, where he wrote a separate Diatribe on it; also in the Epitome of Arminianism, or Examination of the Five Articles of the Remonstrant Ministers in Belgium; likewise in his Corpus doctrinae Christianae, at question XL (posthumous edition); also in his Collegium, disputation XXIII, On the death of Christ for all; and finally in a special oration, which we have placed among the Orationes delivered in the Academy, in volume II of Pareus's Opera theologica. In these writings he defends and keeps the distinction of the Schoolmen and the ancient Fathers between sufficiency and efficiency, along with other orthodox theologians. Shortly before his death, however, that excellent old man learned that at the provincial synod of Dordrecht this distinction had been imprudently brought into dispute by some of the brethren, under Pareus's name and authority. He began to think about it more carefully, judging that it was not altogether necessary, since the sayings of the Gospel [εὐαγγελίων] seem to be reconcilable without it.

units.la: XI.
units.tr: XI.

units.la: Toto pectore igitur auersamur Epicureas blasphemias recentium Pelagianorum, Huberi, Puccij & similium: quibus fides Christiana funditus conuellitur,
units.tr: We therefore with our whole heart reject the Epicurean blasphemies of the recent Pelagians, Huber, Puccius and their like, by which the Christian faith is utterly overthrown:

units.la: I. Christum sic mortuum esse pro omnibus, vt per mortem eius verè & indubitanter omnes simul ab omni peccato & condemnatione liberati sint, siue credant, siue non.
units.tr: I. That Christ died for all in such a way that, through his death, all men are truly and undoubtedly freed at once from all sin and condemnation, whether they believe or not.

units.la: II. Morte Christi Deum cum vniuerso genere humano fuisse reconciliatum: & reipsa totum genus humanum (siue sint Turcæ, siue Iudæi & Epicurei) in gratiam & sinum suum recepisse.
units.tr: II. That by the death of Christ God was reconciled to the whole human race, and that in fact the whole human race (whether they are Turks, Jews or Epicureans) has been received by him into favour and into his bosom.

units.la: III. Et quidem etiam eos recepisse, qui ante mortem ipsius in gehennam iam inciderant. Nam & pro his Huberus Thes. 66. dicit Christum EFFICACITER esse mortuum.
units.tr: III. And indeed that even those who had already fallen into hell before his death have been received; for Huber, Thes. 66, says that Christ died efficaciously for these too.

units.la: IV. Omnibus ex æquo condonata esse peccata. Idem Thes. 270.
units.tr: IV. That sins have been forgiven to all alike. Same work, Thes. 270.

units.la: V. Remissionem peccatorum esse generalem. Ibid.
units.tr: V. That the remission of sins is general. Ibid.

units.la: VI. Reprobos per Christum æque fuisse salvatos ac quoslibet alios. Ibid.
units.tr: VI. That the reprobate were saved by Christ just as equally as any others. Ibid.

units.la: VII. Omnes & singulos homines beneficio & gratia vniuersali summi Patris esse per Christum seruatos. Puccius de effic. pag. 7.
units.tr: VII. That all and each of men have been preserved through Christ by the benefit and universal grace of the highest Father. Puccius, On efficacy, p. 7.

units.la: VIII. Christum pariter omnium & singulorum hominum vt conditorem, ita & redemtorem esse. Idem lib. MS. cap. 24.
units.tr: VIII. That Christ is equally the creator and the redeemer of all and each of men. The same, manuscript book, chap. 24.

units.la: CORONIS.
units.tr: Conclusion.

units.la: An verò ouum ouo similius, quam Huberus Puccio? Fundamentum vnum vtriusque de generali redemtione, remissione peccatorum, & salute per Christi mortem, etiam sine fide speciali: qua tamen infideles rursum excidant. Hoc solum discriminis adhuc quidem: quod Huberus sophisticè tegit, Puccius rotundè profitetur Pelagianismum necessariò inde consequentem, (vt in Margarita aurea ostensum est) nullum esse peccatum Originis: siquidem efficacitate Seruatoris omnes & singuli homines, iuxta Puccium quidē, quatenus homines: iuxta Huberum vero, quatenus redemti sunt, nascuntur: iuxta illum, in statu salutis & gratiæ Christi, iuxta hunc, in sinu & gratia Dei; ac proinde felices, modo non accersant sibi exitium sua infidelitate. Iudicet Ecclesia: Immò iudicet Deus inter hos duos, & inter Osiandrum, qua conscientia hic neget, controuersiam de eo esse: An Deus Filium suum toti mundo, id est omnibus & singulis hominibus donauerit, vt sit saluator vsque ad extremum terræ, omnium, qui cumque eum FIDE AMPLECTUNTUR: cum nos quidem hoc ipsum ex ore Filii Dei sententiamus & docemus: Puccius vero, & Huberus contra vociferentur: Christum donatum esse salvatorem omnibus absolute: & seruasse efficaciter omnes, SIVE CREDANT SIVE NON. Bene est ergo, quod Osiander pro nobis pugnat, & ipse fratercu- los suos refutat.
units.tr: Is one egg ever more like another than Huber is to Puccius? Both rest on one foundation: a general redemption, the remission of sins and salvation through Christ's death, even without special faith, from which unbelievers nevertheless fall away again. There is still this one difference: Huber cloaks it with sophistry, while Puccius openly professes the Pelagianism that necessarily follows from it (as shown in the Margarita aurea), namely that there is no original sin. For if by the efficacy of the Saviour all and each of men are, according to Puccius, so far as they are men, and according to Huber, so far as they have been redeemed, born, the former in a state of salvation and of Christ's grace, the latter in the bosom and grace of God; and therefore happy, provided they do not bring ruin on themselves by their unbelief. Let the Church judge; indeed, let God judge between these two and Osiander, with what conscience the latter denies that there is a controversy over this: Whether God has given his Son to the whole world, that is, to all and each of men, so that he is the Saviour to the end of the earth for all who embrace him in FAITH. We indeed teach and declare this very thing from the mouth of the Son of God, while Puccius and Huber cry out against it: that Christ has been given as Saviour to all absolutely, and has saved all efficaciously, WHETHER THEY BELIEVE OR NOT. It is good, then, that Osiander fights on our side and refutes his own little brothers.

units.la: ARTICVLVS III. DE ADSCENSV CHRISTI IN COELVM.
units.tr: ARTICLE III. OF THE ASCENSION OF CHRIST INTO HEAVEN.

units.la: I.
units.tr: I.

units.la: Credimus, proprie & sine tropo, Christum vero & locali motu corporis sui, diuina sua virtute, adspectantibus discipulis de terra adscendisse sursum in coelum: & ibidem nostra causa etiamnum esse, donec inde redeat ad judicandum viuos & mortuos.
units.tr: We believe, properly and without a figure, that Christ, by his divine power and by a local motion of his body, ascended from the earth upward into heaven while his disciples looked on, and that he is there for our sake until he returns from there to judge the living and the dead.

units.la: TESTIMONIA SCRIPTVRAE.
units.tr: TESTIMONIES OF SCRIPTURE.

units.la: Actor. 1, 9. 10. 11. Et cum haec dixisset, aspicientibus ipsis elevatus est, & nubes suscepit eum abstulit ab oculis eorum. Et cum intentis in coelum oculis eo proficiscente, ecce viri duo astiterunt illis albo vestitu: qui & dixerunt: Viri Galilei, quid statis intuentes in coelum? ita veniet, quemadmodum conspexistis eum proficiscentem in coelum.
units.tr: Acts 1:9, 10, 11. And when he had said these things, while they watched, he was lifted up, and a cloud received him and took him out of their sight. And while they were gazing intently into heaven as he went, behold, two men in white apparel stood beside them, who also said: Men of Galilee, why do you stand looking into heaven? This same Jesus, who has been taken up from you into heaven, will come in the same way as you saw him go into heaven.

units.la: Heb. 8, 4. Si Christus esset in terra, ne sacerdos quidem esset. Heb. 9, 24. Non in manufactum sacrarium ingressus est Christus, quod sit exemplar vero sacrario respondens, sed in ipsum coelum, ut compareat nunc faciei Dei pro nobis.
units.tr: Heb. 8:4. If Christ were on earth, he would not even be a priest. Heb. 9:24. Christ has not entered a sanctuary made with hands, which is a copy corresponding to the true sanctuary, but heaven itself, so that he may now appear before the face of God for us.

units.la: Coloss. 3. vers. 1. Superna quaerite, ubi Christus est ad dextram Dei sedens.
units.tr: Col. 3:1. Seek the things that are above, where Christ is, seated at the right hand of God.

units.la: Act. 3, 21. Christum oportet coeli capiant usq; ad tempora restitutionis omnium, de quibus loquutus est Deus à seculo per os omnium sanctorum suorum Prophetarum.
units.tr: Acts 3:21. Heaven must receive Christ until the times of the restoration of all things, of which God spoke from the beginning by the mouth of all his holy prophets.

units.la: Actor. 1, 11. Hic Iesus, qui sursum receptus est à vobis in coelum, ita veniet, quemadmodum conspexistis eum proficiscentem in coelum.
units.tr: Acts 1:11. This Jesus, who has been taken up from you into heaven, will come in the same way as you saw him go into heaven.

units.la: Matth. 24, 30. Tunc apparebit signum Filij hominis in coelo, & videbunt eum venientem in nubibus coeli cum potentia & gloria multa.
units.tr: Matt. 24:30. Then the sign of the Son of Man will appear in heaven, and they will see the Son of Man coming on the clouds of heaven with power and great glory.

units.la: Matt. 25, 31. Cum autem venerit Filius hominis cum gloria, & omnes sancti angeli cum eo, tunc sedebit in throno gloriae suae.
units.tr: Matt. 25:31. But when the Son of Man comes in his glory, and all the holy angels with him, then he will sit on the throne of his glory.

units.la: 1 Thess. 4, 16. Nam ipse Dominus cum hortationis clamore, cum voce Archangeli & cum Dei tuba descendet è coelo.
units.tr: 1 Thess. 4:16. For the Lord himself, with a shout of command, with the voice of the archangel and with the trumpet of God, will descend from heaven.

units.la: Philip. 3, 20. Nos vt municipes coelorum nos gerimus: unde etiam Seruatorem exspectamus Dominum Iesum Christum.
units.tr: Phil. 3:20. We conduct ourselves as citizens of heaven; whence we also await the Saviour, the Lord Jesus Christ.

units.la: II.
units.tr: II.

units.la: Id coelum, in quod Christus descendit, quale sit, & qualis locus sit, minimè inquirimus, sed curiosis relinquimus: cum sit scriscriptum : Oculus non vidit, auris non audiuit, nec in mentem hominis adscenderunt, quæ paravit Deus iis, qui ipsum diligunt: tamen 1 Cor.2, 9. Piè & cum Scriptura sacra credimus, quod sit locus a, non in his terris b, nec in inferis c, nec ubique: sed supra & extra hunc mundum adspectabilem d, cœlum cœlorum e, habitaculum, & thronus Dei f, in luce inaccessa g, domus Patris h, civitas Dei viui i, patria Sanctorum k, vbi Christus nunc est l, ad dextram Dei interpellans pro nobis m, & parans nobis locum n, vnde & rediturum exspectamus o, deorsum in nubes p, vt nos ad se adsumat q.
units.tr: As to what heaven is into which Christ descended, what sort of place it is, we do not inquire at all, but leave such curiosity to others, since it is written: "The eye has not seen, nor the ear heard, nor has it entered into the mind of man, what God has prepared for those who love him" (1 Cor. 2:9). Nevertheless, devoutly and with the holy Scripture we believe that it is a place a, not in these lands b, nor in the underworld c, nor everywhere; but above and beyond this visible world d, the heaven of heavens e, the dwelling place and throne of God f, in light inaccessible g, the house of the Father h, the city of the living God i, the homeland of the saints k, where Christ now is l, at the right hand of God, interceding for us m, and preparing a place for us n, whence we also await him to return o, down into the clouds p, to take us up to himself q.

units.la: TESTIMONIA SCRIPTVRAE.
units.tr: TESTIMONIES OF SCRIPTURE.

units.la: a 1 Reg. 8,30 Exaudias deprecationem serui tui & populi tui Israelis, qui orauerit in loco isto: tu quidem exaudias de loco habitationis tuæ, id est, de cœlis, exaudias & parcas.
units.tr: a 1 Kings 8:30. Hear the supplication of your servant and of your people Israel, who pray in this place; hear from the place of your dwelling, that is, from heaven, and hear and forgive.

units.la: Ioh. 14,2. In domo Patris mei habitationes multæ sunt: alioquin dixissem vobis: Proficiscor paraturus vobis locum.
units.tr: John 14:2. In my Father's house there are many dwelling places; otherwise I would have told you. I go to prepare a place for you.

units.la: Phil. 3,20. Nos vt municipes cœlorum nos gerimus: vnde etiam seruatorem exspectamus Dominum Iesum Christum.
units.tr: Phil. 3:20. We conduct ourselves as citizens of heaven; whence we also await the Saviour, the Lord Jesus Christ.

units.la: b Jer. 31, 37. Sic dixit Iehouah: Si mensurari possint cœli sursum, & inuestigari fundamenta terra deorsum, &c.
units.tr: b Jer. 31:37. Thus says the LORD: If the heavens above can be measured, and the foundations of the earth below can be searched out, etc.

units.la: c Luc. 16,26. Ad hæc omnia inter nos & vos hiatus ingens constitutus est, vt ij, qui volunt hinc transire ad vos, non possint, neque illinc huc transire.
units.tr: c Luke 16:26. Between us and you a great chasm has been fixed, so that those who wish to pass from here to you cannot, nor can anyone cross from there to us.

units.la: d Ephes. 4,10. Qui descendit, ipse est, qui etiam adscendit longè supra omnes cœlos, vt impleret omnia.
units.tr: d Eph. 4:10. He who descended is the same who also ascended far above all the heavens, that he might fill all things.

units.la: Heb. 4,14. Habentes igitur pontificem magnum, qui penetrauit cœlos, Iesum Filium Dei.
units.tr: Heb. 4:14. Since then we have a great high priest who has passed through the heavens, Jesus the Son of God.

units.la: e 1 Reg. 8, 27. Cœlum & cœli cœlorum te non continent.
units.tr: e 1 Kings 8:27. The heaven and the heaven of heavens cannot contain you.

units.la: Psal. 115,16. Cœlum, cœlum, inquam, Iehouæ est, terram autem dedit filiis hominum.
units.tr: Ps. 115:16. The heavens, even the heavens, are the LORD's, but the earth he has given to the sons of men.

units.la: f 1 Reg. 8,19. Exaudias de cœlo, de loco habitationis tuæ orationem eorum.
units.tr: f 1 Kings 8:39. Hear from heaven, from the place of your dwelling, their prayer.

units.la: g 1 Tim. 6,15. Rex regum, & Dominus dominorum lucem habitat inaccessam.
units.tr: g 1 Tim. 6:15. The King of kings and Lord of lords, who dwells in light inaccessible.

units.la: h Joh. 14,2. In domo Patris mei habitationes multæ sunt. Proficiscor paraturus vobis locum.
units.tr: h John 14:2. In my Father's house there are many dwelling places. I go to prepare a place for you.

units.la: i Heb. 11,10. Abraham exspectabat vrbem habentem fundamenta, cuius artifex & conditor est Deus.
units.tr: i Heb. 11:10. Abraham was looking for the city that has foundations, whose architect and builder is God.

units.la: Hebr. 12, 22. Accessistis ad montem Sion, & ciuitatem Dei viui, Hierusalem cœlestem, & myriadas angelorum.
units.tr: Heb. 12:22. You have come to Mount Zion and to the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem, and to myriads of angels.

units.la: k Heb. 11, vers. 14. Nam qui hæc dicunt, palam ostendunt, se patriam quærere.
units.tr: k Heb. 11:14. For those who say such things make it plain that they are seeking a homeland.

units.la: l Heb.
units.tr: l Heb.

units.la: Non in manu factum sacrarium ingressus est Christus (quod sit exemplar vero sacrario respondens) sed in ipsum cœlum, vt appareat NVNC in conspectu Dei pro nobis.
units.tr: Christ has not entered a sanctuary made with hands (which is a copy corresponding to the true sanctuary), but heaven itself, to appear NOW before the face of God for us.

units.la: Quis est, qui condemnet? Christus is est, qui mortuus est, imò vero qui etiam excitatus est, qui etiam est ad dextram Dei, qui etiam postulat pro nobis.
units.tr: Who is it that condemns? It is Christ who died, or rather who was also raised, who is also at the right hand of God, who also makes intercession for us.

units.la: Proficiscor paraturus vobis locum.
units.tr: I go to prepare a place for you.

units.la: Nos vt municipes cœlorum nos gerimus: vnde etiam seruatorem exspectamus Dominum Iesum Christum.
units.tr: We conduct ourselves as citizens of heaven; whence we also await the Saviour, the Lord Jesus Christ.

units.la: Hic Iesus, qui sursum receptus est à vobis in cœlum, ita veniet, quemadmodum conspexistis eum proficiscentem in cœlum.
units.tr: This Jesus, who has been taken up from you into heaven, will come in the same way as you saw him go into heaven.

units.la: 1 Thess. 4, 16. 17. Ipse Dominus cum hortationis clamore & voce Archangeli ac Dei tuba descendet è cœlo: & qui mortui fuerint in Christo, resurgent primum: deinde nos viui, qui reliqui erimus, rapiemur simul cum eis in nubes, in occursum Domini, in aerem: & ita semper erimus cum Domino.
units.tr: 1 Thess. 4:16, 17. The Lord himself will descend from heaven with a shout, with the voice of the archangel and the trumpet of God; and the dead in Christ will rise first; then we who are alive and remain will be caught up together with them in the clouds, to meet the Lord in the air; and so we shall always be with the Lord.

units.la: Rursum veniam, & assumam vos ad meipsum: vt vbi ego sum, & vos sitis.
units.tr: I will come again and take you to myself, so that where I am, you may be also.

units.la: Joh. 17, 24. Pater, velim, vt vbi sum ego, & illi sint mecum: vt conspiciant gloriam meam, quam dedisti mihi.
units.tr: John 17:24. Father, I desire that where I am, they also may be with me, so that they may see my glory, which you have given me.

units.la: III.
units.tr: III.

units.la: Eo autem non saepius, sed semela: non in vtero Matris, sed quadragesimo die post resurrectionemb: non vbique, sed in monte Oliuarumc: non apparenter, sed verò corporis motud: non inuisibiliter, sed adspectantibus discipulis, & eum deducentibus, videndo, non sequendo adscendite, ac reliquit mundumf, corporali discessione corpus suum cœlo inferens: maiestatem mundo non auferensg: quoniam licet corpore absit, habitat tamen in Patri pro nobis apparens, & à dextris sedens, vt pia sanctis per spiritum, neque patitur illos orphanos esse: vt vetustas loquiturh.
units.tr: He ascended thither, moreover, not repeatedly but oncea; not in the womb of his mother but on the fortieth day after the resurrectionb; not everywhere but from the Mount of Olivesc; not in mere appearance but by a real movement of his bodyd; not invisibly but while the disciples watched and escorted him, ascending by being seen, not by following, and he left the world, carrying his body to heaven by a bodily departure, yet not taking his majesty away from the world. For although he is absent in body, he nevertheless dwells in the Father, appearing for us and sitting at the right hand, so that by the Spirit he may bestow his kindnesses on the saints, and he does not allow them to be orphans, as antiquity puts it.

units.la: TESTIMONIA SCRIPTVRÆ ET ANTIQVORVM PATRVM.
units.tr: TESTIMONIES OF SCRIPTURE AND OF THE ANCIENT FATHERS.

units.la: Christus per proprium sanguinem ingressus est semel in sacrarium, aeternam redemptionem nactus.
units.tr: Christ entered once into the holy place through his own blood, having obtained eternal redemption.

units.la: Christus sese, postquam passus fuit, Apostolis suis exhibuit viuum cum multis certissimis signis, per dies quadraginta conspectus ab eis.
units.tr: After his passion, Christ showed himself alive to his apostles with many most certain proofs, being seen by them over forty days.

units.la: Actor. 1,11. Tunc Apostoli reuersi sunt Hierosolymam à monte, qui vocatur Oliveti, qui est prope Hierosolymam, distans itinere Sabbati.
units.tr: Acts 1:11. Then the apostles returned to Jerusalem from the mount called Olivet, which is near Jerusalem, a sabbath day's journey away.

units.la: Act. 1, 9. Et cum dixisset, adspicientibus ipsis elevatus est, & nubes suscepit eum abstulit ab oculis eorum. Et cum essent intentis in eum oculis.
units.tr: Acts 1:9. And when he had said this, as they watched, he was lifted up, and a cloud took him up and hid him from their eyes. And while they were gazing intently into heaven after him.

units.la: Augustin. Tractatu in Joh. 50. Secundum carnem, quam verbum assumsit: secundum id, quod de virgine natus est: secundum id, quod à Iudæis prehensus est, quod ligno confixus, quod de cruce depositus, quod linteis involutus, quod in sepulcro conditus, quod in resurrectione manifestatus, non semper habebitis vobiscum. Quare? Quoniam conversatus est secundum corporis præsentiam 40. diebus cum discipulis: & eis deducentibus videndo, non sequendo ascendit in cœlum, & non est hic.
units.tr: Augustine, Tractate 50 on John. According to the flesh, which the Word assumed; according to that which he was born of the virgin; according to that which he was seized by the Jews, which he was fastened to the wood, which he was taken down from the cross, which he was wrapped in linen cloths, which he was laid in the tomb, which he was made manifest in the resurrection, you will not always have with you. Why? Because he conversed with his disciples for forty days in bodily presence, and, while they led him on, he ascended into heaven by being seen, not by being followed, and he is not here.

units.la: Chrysost. sermone de Adscens. Domini, Tomo II. pag. 328. Quia longum spacium de terra tenebatur ad cœlum: & oculorum acies portatum corpus ad illam altitudinem minimè poterat peruidere: sed sicut auem si altiora postulat, deficiet aspectus inspicere, & noster oculus vincitur à celsiore: sic & illud corpus quanto ferebatur ad summa, tanto oculos videntium aspectus imbecillitate incidebat, deficiente natura altiora conspicere: ideo stabant Angeli, iter cœleste monstrantes, ne quis arbitraretur, quin tanquam Helias sic in cœlum ascenderit, qui elevatus est à vobis ad cœlum.
units.tr: Chrysostom, sermon on the Ascension of the Lord, vol. II, p. 328. Because a long stretch of space lay between earth and heaven, and the sight of the eyes could by no means follow the body carried up to that height; but just as a bird, if it attempts higher flight, the eye fails to see it and our sight is overcome by the loftier object, so that body, the higher it was carried to the heights, the more it escaped the sight of those looking on, since nature fails to behold higher things. Therefore angels stood by, showing the heavenly road, lest anyone should suppose that he had ascended into heaven as Elijah did; he who was taken up from you into heaven.

units.la: Ibid. Vide quo spacio cœlum separatur à terra, immò terra, quantò ab inferis est, & ipsum cœlum quantum ab altiore cœlo separatur: & de altiore cœlo ad angelos quantum spatii est: ad superiores etiam potestates ad ipsam quoq; dominicam sedem. Per hac omnia natura nostra elevata est, ut homo, qui loco tam humili tenebatur, ut descendere non posset ulterius, ad tam excelsam sedem elevaretur, ut altius non posset ascendere. Ideo dixit Paulus: Qui descendit, ipse est, qui etiam ascendit.
units.tr: Ibid. Consider what a distance separates heaven from earth, or rather earth from the lower regions, and how far heaven itself is from the higher heaven; and how great the space is from the higher heaven to the angels, and also to the higher powers, and even to the Lord's own throne. Through all these things our nature has been raised, so that man, who was held in a place so low that he could not descend any further, has been lifted up to so lofty a seat that he could not ascend any higher. Therefore Paul said: He who descended is the same who also ascended.

units.la: Ibidem. Descendit in infima loca terræ, & ascendit supra omnes cœlos.
units.tr: Ibid. He descended into the lowest parts of the earth, and ascended above all the heavens.

units.la: Johan. 16. vers. 28. Iterum relinquo Mundum, & proficiscor ad Patrem.
units.tr: John 16:28. Again I leave the world, and I go to the Father.

units.la: Augustin. Tract. in Joh. 102. Reliquit mundum corporali discessione. Perrexit ad Patrem corporali adscensione: nec mundum deseruit præsentiæ gubernatione.
units.tr: Augustine, Tractate 102 on John. He left the world by a bodily departure. He went to the Father by a bodily ascension; nor did he forsake the world in governing it by his presence.

units.la: Idem Tractatu in Joh. 50. Derant Pontifices mandatum, ut si quis cognouerit, ubi sit, indicet, ut apprehenderent eum. Nos (inquit) indicemus modo Iudæis, ubi sit Christus. Vtinam ve-lint audire, & apprehendere, quicunque sunt ex semine illorum, qui dederant mandatum, vt indicaretur eis, vbi esset Christus: Veniant ad Ecclesiam, audiant, vbi sit Christus, & apprehendant eum. A nobis audiant, ex Euangelio audiant. Occisus est ante oculos eorum, sepultus est, resurrexit, à discipulis agnitus, ascendit in cœlum: ibi sedet ad dextram Patris, qui judicatus est: venturus est Iudex: audiant, & teneant. Respond. Quem tenebo? absentem? Fidem mitte, & tenuisti. Parentes tui tenuerunt carne, tu tene corde: quoniam Christus absens etiam praesens est. Nisi praesens esset, à nobis ipsis teneri non posset. Sed quoniam verum est, quod ait: Ego vobiscum sum vsque ad consummationem seculi: & abiit, & hic est, & reliquit, & nos non deseruit: CORPVS enim suum intulit coelo: MAIESTATEM non abstulit mundo.
units.tr: Augustine, the same, Tractate 50 on John. The chief priests had given an order that, if anyone knew where he was, he should report it, so that they might seize him. We, he says, will now tell the Jews where Christ is. Would that they were willing to hear and to seize him, all who are of the seed of those who gave the order that it should be reported to them where Christ was! Let them come to the Church, let them hear where Christ is, and let them lay hold of him. Let them hear him from us, let them hear him from the Gospel. He was killed before their eyes, he was buried, he rose again, he was recognised by the disciples, he ascended into heaven; there he sits at the right hand of the Father, he who was judged; he is to come as judge. Let them hear and hold fast. The answer: Whom shall I hold? One who is absent? Send forth faith, and you have held him. Your parents held him in the flesh; you hold him in the heart, for Christ, though absent, is also present. If he were not present, he could not be held by us at all. But since what he said is true: I am with you always, even to the end of the age; and he has gone away, and yet he is here, and he has left us, and yet has not forsaken us. For he carried his BODY into heaven, but did not take his MAJESTY away from the world.

units.la: Cyrillus super Joh. l. 11, c. 3. Nam etsi abest corpore, Patri pro nobis apparens, ac à dextris eius sedens: habitat tamen in Sanctis per spiritum, nec patitur illos orphanos esse.
units.tr: Cyril, on John, book 11, chapter 3. For although he is absent in body, appearing before the Father for us and sitting at his right hand, yet he dwells in the saints through the Spirit, and does not allow them to be orphans.

units.la: IV.
units.tr: IV.

units.la: Haec sola Orthodoxa fide scimus, vbi sit quaerendus & invocandus Dominus Iesus thesaurus noster: nempe sursum in coelis, ad dextram Dei . Vbi enim thesaurus noster, ibi cor nostrum . Vnde sit exspectandus, nempe è coelo : vbi denique nostra sit mansio futura post hanc vitam, nempe in coelo, vbi à Domino nobis paratus est locus .
units.tr: By the orthodox faith alone we know where our treasure, the Lord Jesus, is to be sought and invoked: namely, upward in heaven, at the right hand of God. For where our treasure is, there our heart is also. From there he is to be awaited, namely from heaven. Finally, where our dwelling is to be after this life, namely in heaven, where a place has been prepared for us by the Lord.

units.la: TESTIMONIA SCRIPTVRÆ.
units.tr: TESTIMONIES OF SCRIPTURE.

units.la: Coloss. 3, 1. Superna quarite, vbi Christus est ad dextram Dei sedens.
units.tr: Col. 3:1. Seek the things above, where Christ is, sitting at the right hand of God.

units.la: Matth. 6, 21. Vbi thesaurus vester, ibi cor vestrum.
units.tr: Matt. 6:21. Where your treasure is, there your heart will be also.

units.la: Philip. 3, 20. Nos vt municipes coelorum nos gerimus: vnde etiam Seruatorem exspectamus, Dominum Iesum Christum.
units.tr: Phil. 3:20. We conduct ourselves as citizens of heaven, and from there we also await the Saviour, the Lord Jesus Christ.

units.la: Joh. 14, 3. Proficiscor paraturus vobis locum: & rursum veniam, & assumam vos ad meipsum.
units.tr: John 14:3. I go to prepare a place for you, and I will come again and take you to myself.

units.la: Joh. 17, 24. Pater, velim, vt vbi sum ego, & illi sint mecum: vt conspiciant gloriam, quam dedisti mihi.
units.tr: John 17:24. Father, I desire that where I am, they also may be with me, so that they may behold the glory which you have given me.

units.la: 1 Thess. 4, 17. Rapiemur in nube, in occursum Domini, in aere: & ita semper erimus cum Domino.
units.tr: 1 Thess. 4:17. We shall be caught up in the clouds, to meet the Lord in the air, and so we shall always be with the Lord.

units.la: V.
units.tr: V.

units.la: Auersamur vero aliena illa à fide Christiana, & piis mentibus plane φοξικὰ commenta Vbiquitariorum de Coelo & Ascensu Christi, pleraque vix Luciano digna, quae in libris ipsorum continentur, vt nimirum habeat, de quo ingemiscat, & efficiam erroris mitetur pia posteritas.
units.tr: We reject, as alien to the Christian faith, and to pious minds utterly ridiculous, the inventions of the Ubiquitarians about heaven and the ascension of Christ. Most of them are scarcely worthy of Lucian, yet they are contained in their books, so that pious posterity may have something to groan over and may be warned against the error.

units.la: i. Cor.
units.tr: 1 Cor.

units.la: 1. Coelum supramundanum esse anile delirium, quod Brentius se ridere ait: esse phãtasias Thalmudicas, Mahumedanas &c.
units.tr: 1. That the heaven above the world is an old wives' delusion, which Brenz says he laughs at; that they are Talmudic and Mohammedan fantasies, etc.

units.la: 2. Coelum, in quod Christus ascendit, non esse locum, non sursum, sed esse DEVM IPSVM (quia scilicet etiam coelum est infernus: ac non tantum Sancti homines, verum etiam Satan & angeli eius inveniantur.
units.tr: 2. That the heaven into which Christ ascended is not a place, nor above, but is God himself (because, of course, heaven is also hell, and not only holy men but also Satan and his angels are found there).

units.la: 3. Saepius Christum ascendisse in coelum: Inuisibiliter in vtero matris, vbi verbum est caro factum: In cruce, vbi emisso spiritu depositit formam serui: In resurrectione à mortuis: visibiliter denique in monte Oliveti.
units.tr: 3. That Christ ascended into heaven many times: invisibly in the womb of his mother, where the Word was made flesh; on the cross, where, having breathed out his spirit, he laid aside the form of a servant; in the resurrection from the dead; and finally visibly on the Mount of Olives.

units.la: 4. Postremum hunc ascensum non fuisse verum ascensum in coelum: sed mirandam elevationem corporis Christi VSQVE AD NVBES, dispensatorium spectaculum, ac visibilem disparentiam.
units.tr: 4. That this last ascent was not a true ascent into heaven, but a marvellous lifting up of the body of Christ UP TO THE CLOUDS, a dispensational spectacle and a visible disappearance.

units.la: 5. Christum in transitu ad patrem, h. e. ascensu in coelum, delatum quidem pilum de terra mouisse corpus suum.
units.tr: 5. That Christ, in his passage to the Father, that is, in his ascent into heaven, when indeed carried a hair's breadth from the earth, moved his body.

units.la: 6. Ascendere in coelum esse idem, quod exuere infirmitates, transfire in statum coelestem ac immortalem: disparere: vniri cum Deo: sedere ad dextram Dei: emergere ad summos honores &c.
units.tr: 6. That to ascend into heaven is the same as to cast off infirmities, to pass into a heavenly and immortal state: to disappear, to be united with God, to sit at the right hand of God, to rise to the highest honours, etc.

units.la: 7. Christum in ascensu tenebrionem factum: occuluisse se nebula: ac Protei more se vertisse in formas: siue, vt loquuntur, induisse nebulosum cucullum: quemadmodum Poetae fabulantur de Venere Paridem libetante. Homer Iliad. γ. v. 380. ... Illum vero eripuit Venus, obtexitq; nebula spissa. Sic Threni Ieremiae cap. 3. v. 44. Opposuisti nubem tibi, ne transfiret oratio.
units.tr: 7. That Christ in the ascent became a shadow-dweller: he hid himself in a cloud and, in the manner of Proteus, changed himself into shapes; or, as they say, he put on a cloudy hood, just as the poets fable of Venus when Paris made his libation. Homer, Iliad 3, v. 380: "But Venus snatched him away and covered him with a thick cloud." So Lamentations of Jeremiah, ch. 3, v. 44: "You have covered yourself with a cloud, so that prayer cannot pass through."

units.la: Et sarcasmos Brentianos.
units.tr: And the Brenzian sarcasms.

units.la: 8. Ex Computo Mathematico, Christum mole ac motu violento corporis sui sursum, forte nondum penetrasse Sphaeras Planetarum, & venisse in domum patris.
units.tr: 8. From a mathematical computation, that Christ, by the mass and violent motion of his body upward, perhaps had not yet penetrated the spheres of the planets, and had come into the house of the Father.

units.la: 9. Ibidem deambulare, spaciari, forte etiam decumbere.
units.tr: 9. That he walked about there, strolled, and perhaps even lay down.

units.la: ARTICVLVS IV.
units.tr: ARTICLE IV.

units.la: DE SESSIONE CHRISTI AD DEXTRAM DEI.
units.tr: ON THE SESSION OF CHRIST AT THE RIGHT HAND OF GOD.

units.la: I.
units.tr: I.

units.la: Sessio CHRISTI ad dextram Dei non est ipsa Adscensio ad coelum. Differunt enim.
units.tr: Christ's session at the right hand of God is not the same as his ascension into heaven. For they differ.

units.la: 1. Ordine temporis, vt prius & posterius. Prius enim adscendit ad coelum, quam sederet ad dextram Dei.
units.tr: 1. In order of time, as before and after. For he ascended into heaven before he sat at the right hand of God.

units.la: 2. Forma. Adscensus fuit motus localis sursum : Sessio est personæ adscendentis gloriosa conditio .
units.tr: 2. In form. The ascension was a local movement upward; the session is the glorious condition of the person who ascended.

units.la: 3. Finibus proximis. Adscensio facta est propter sessionem : Sessio propter ecclesiam .
units.tr: 3. In its nearer purposes. The ascension took place for the sake of the session; the session takes place for the sake of the Church.

units.la: 4. Duratione. Adscensio semel est facta, vt actus transiens; Sessio vt actus immanens: regnum & gloria Christi æternum durat .
units.tr: 4. In duration. The ascension happened once, as a transient act; the session is an abiding act: the kingdom and glory of Christ endure forever.

units.la: 5. Deniq; subiectis. Adscensio etiam sanctis conuenit: Sessio ad dextram Dei est gloria solius mediatoris exaltati .
units.tr: 5. Finally, in their subjects. The ascension also belongs to the saints; the session at the right hand of God is the glory of the exalted Mediator alone.

units.la: TESTIMONIA SCRIPTVRÆ.
units.tr: TESTIMONIES OF SCRIPTURE.

units.la: ] Marci 16, 19. Dominus igitur postquam locutus fuisset eis, sursum receptus est in cœlum, & sedit ad dextram Dei.
units.tr: Mark 16:19. So then the Lord, after he had spoken to them, was received up into heaven, and sat at the right hand of God.

units.la: ] Act. 1, 9. Adspicientibus discipulis elevatus est.
units.tr: Acts 1:9. He was lifted up while the disciples watched.

units.la: ] Hebr. 8, 1. Talem habemus Pontificem, qui consedit ad dextram throni maiestatis illius in cœlis.
units.tr: Heb. 8:1. We have such a High Priest, who has sat down at the right hand of the throne of the Majesty in the heavens.

units.la: ] Phil. 2, 9. Quapropter Deus ipsum in summam extulit sublimitatem, ac donauit ei nomen, quod est supra omne nomen: vt ad nomen Iesu omne genu se flectat.
units.tr: Phil. 2:9. Therefore God has exalted him to the highest place and has given him the name that is above every name, so that at the name of Jesus every knee should bow.

units.la: 1 Pet. 3, 22. Christus ad dextram Dei profectus est in cœlum. Hebr. 9, 24. Christus ingressus est in ipsum cœlum, vt compareat nunc faciei Dei pro nobis.
units.tr: 1 Pet. 3:22. Christ has gone into heaven, to the right hand of God. Heb. 9:24. Christ entered into heaven itself, to appear now before the face of God for us.

units.la: ] Eph. 4, 10. Christus adscendit longè supra omnes cœlos, vt impleret omnia. Et alios dedit Apostolos, &c.
units.tr: Eph. 4:10. Christ ascended far above all the heavens, that he might fill all things. And he gave some as apostles, etc.

units.la: ] Luc. 1. 33. Regni eius non erit finis. 1 Cor. 15, 25. Oportet eum regnare, vsquequo omnes inimicos subiecerit pedibus eius.
units.tr: Luke 1:33. Of his kingdom there will be no end. 1 Cor. 15:25. He must reign until he has put all his enemies under his feet.

units.la: ] 1 Thess. 4, 17. Rapiemur simul cum eis in nubes in occursum Domini in aerem: & ita semper cum Domino erimus. Hebr. 1, 13. Ad quem angelorum dixit unquam? Sede ad dextram meam.
units.tr: 1 Thess. 4:17. We shall be caught up together with them in the clouds, to meet the Lord in the air; and so we shall always be with the Lord. Heb. 1:13. To which of the angels did he ever say, Sit at my right hand?

units.la: II.
units.tr: II.

units.la: Nec est ipsa incarnatio: aut personalis vnio carnis cum λόγῳ: vt quidam vertiginosi contendunt.
units.tr: Nor is it the incarnation itself, or the personal union of the flesh with the Word [λόγος], as certain dizzy-headed men contend.

units.la: 1. Quia in symbolo ea discernitur, in quo non est ταυτο- λογία.
units.tr: 1. Because the creed distinguishes the two, and in it there is no tautology [ταυτολογία].

units.la: 2. Nusquam in scriptura humanitas dicitur sedere ad λόγῳ, sed ἀ λόγῳ assumta esse .
units.tr: 2. Nowhere in Scripture is the humanity said to sit at the Word [λόγῳ], but to have been assumed from the Word [ἀπὸ λόγου].

units.la: 3. Vnio facta est in vtero matris: sessio in cœlo .
units.tr: 3. The union took place in the mother's womb; the session is in heaven.

units.la: 4. Vnio in primo conceptionis articulo: sessio post adscensionem cœpit .
units.tr: 4. The union began at the first moment of conception; the session began after the ascension.

units.la: Vide etiam D. Parei. Apologet. Biblic. l. 3. c. 3.
units.tr: See also D. Pareus, Biblical Apologia, book 3, chapter 3.

units.la: 5. Unio est immutabilis simpliciter: Sessio mutabilis secun-dum quid, quantum ad externam regni formam attinet, quae, Apostolo dicte, tandem abolita morte plane [?] αἰχ[?]ῃ, nunc enim Christus in medio inimicorum (vt rosa inter spi-nas) per varia media regnat, tunc vero sine hostibus & sine mediis regnabit, quia Deus erit omnia in omnibus e.
units.tr: 5. The union is absolutely unchangeable; the session is changeable in a qualified sense, as far as concerns the external form of the kingdom, which, as the Apostle says, will at last be done away with, when death has been plainly [?] [?]. For now Christ reigns in the midst of his enemies (as a rose among thorns) by various means; but then he will reign without enemies and without means, because God will be all in all.

units.la: TESTIMONIA SCRIPTVRÆ.
units.tr: TESTIMONIES OF SCRIPTURE.

units.la: a] Heb.2,16. Non enim vtiq; angelos assumsit. Joh.1,14. Sermo caro factus est. b c] Luc.1, 31. Concipies in utero, & paries filium. Ephes. 1, 20. DEVS Christum collocauit ad dextram suam in coelis. d] 1 Corinth. 15. verf. 25. Oportet eum regnare vsquequo omnes inimicos subjecerit pedibus eius. Vltimus autem hostis aboleтur mors. e] Apoc.1 23. Esa.60,19. Non erit tibi amplius sol in lucem per diem, & splendor Lunæ non illuminabit te: sed erit tibi Iehoua in lucem sempiternam.
units.tr: a] Heb. 2:16. For surely he did not take hold of angels. John 1:14. The Word became flesh. b c] Luke 1:31. You will conceive in the womb and bear a son. Eph. 1:20. God set Christ at his right hand in the heavens. d] 1 Cor. 15:25. He must reign until he has put all his enemies under his feet. The last enemy to be abolished is death. e] Rev. 1:23. Isa. 60:19. The sun will no more be your light by day, and the brightness of the moon will not shine on you; but the LORD will be your everlasting light.

units.la: III.
units.tr: III.

units.la: Sed est, vt breuissimè dicamus, gloria consummata Mediatoris exaltati in suo sacerdotio & regno in coelis: phrasi à rebus humanis ad diuinas translata: quoniam Reges, quos maximè honorant, à dextris suis collocant. Neque enim dextra Dei, qui est spiritus, corporeum intelligitur membrum aut locus: neque Sessio ad dextram Patris situm Filij corporalem significat. Nisi enim, inquit Augustinus, spiritualiter hoc accipiatur, Pater Filio ad sinistram erit.
units.tr: But, to say it very briefly, it is the consummated glory of the exalted Mediator in his priesthood and kingdom in the heavens, a phrase transferred from human affairs to divine ones: because kings place at their right hand those whom they honor most. For the right hand of God, who is a spirit, is not understood as a bodily member or a place; nor does the session at the Father's right hand signify a bodily position of the Son. For, says Augustine, unless this is taken spiritually, the Father would be at the Son's left.

units.la: IV.
units.tr: IV.

units.la: Et quidem hæc gloria sic est Filij Mediatoris propria, vt neque Patris simul sit, neque Spiritus sancti: ac multo minus vllius creaturæ. Neque enim Patri aut Spiritui sancto, aut vllì angelorum dictum est: Sede à dextris meis, donec ponam inimicos tuos scabellum pedum tuorum. De solo autem Filio dicitur: Oportet eum regnare, donec &c. Unde consequens est, sedere ad dextram Dei haud idem esse, quod naturam Christi humanam omnipotentem, omniscium, omnipræsentem, denique æqualem Deo, & Deum esse: siue eam dignitatem ex vnione personali, siue ex ascensu in coelum, siue ex alia quacunque causa sortita dicatur.
units.tr: Indeed this glory is so proper to the Son as Mediator that it is not shared at the same time with the Father or the Holy Spirit, and much less with any creature. For it has not been said to the Father or the Holy Spirit, or to any of the angels: Sit at my right hand, until I make your enemies a footstool for your feet. But it is said of the Son alone: He must reign, until etc. Hence it follows that to sit at the right hand of God is not the same as the human nature of Christ being omnipotent, omniscient, omnipresent, and finally equal to God and God; whether that dignity is said to be obtained from the personal union, or from the ascent into heaven, or from any other cause whatever.

units.la: V.
units.tr: V.

units.la: Etsi verò ea gloria Mediatoris nobis hominibus in hac vita est ἀρρητος: tamen diligenter inter se collatis Apostoli tribus locis, quibus præcipuè eam describere voluit, vtcunque intelligimus, in his cum primis sitam esse:
units.tr: Although this glory of the Mediator is ineffable for us men in this life, nevertheless, when the three passages in which the Apostles especially wished to describe it are carefully compared with one another, we understand, however imperfectly, that it lies chiefly in these:

units.la: TESTIMONIA SCRIPTVRAE.
units.tr: TESTIMONIES OF SCRIPTURE.

units.la: DE SESSIONE CHRISTI AD DEXTRAM DEI.
units.tr: CONCERNING THE SESSION OF CHRIST AT THE RIGHT HAND OF GOD.

units.la: Deus Christum suscitauit ex mortuis, & collocauit ad dextram suam in coelis, longè supra omne imperium, ac potestatem, & potentiam & dominationem, & omne nomen, quod nominatur non solum in hoc saeculo, verum etiam in futuro: & omnia subjecit eius pedibus, eumque constituit caput super omnia ipsi Ecclesiae: quae est corpus ipsius, & complementum eius, qui omnia implet in omnibus.
units.tr: God raised Christ from the dead and seated him at his right hand in the heavens, far above every rule, authority, power and dominion, and every name that is named not only in this age but also in the age to come; and he put all things under his feet, and appointed him head over all things for the Church, which is his body and the fullness of him who fills all in all.

units.la: Deinde erit Filius, cum tradiderit regnum Deo ac Patri, cum aboleuerit omne imperium, & omnem potentiam & virtutem. Nam oportet eum regnare, vsquequo omnes inimicos subjecerit pedibus eius. Vltimus autem hostis aboletur mors.
units.tr: Then the Son will be subject, when he has handed over the kingdom to God and the Father, when he has abolished all rule and all authority and power. For he must reign until he has put all his enemies under his feet. The last enemy to be abolished is death.

units.la: Quapropter etiam Deus ipsum in summam extulit sublimitatem, & donauit ei nomen, quod est supra omne nomen: vt ad nomen Iesu omne genu se flectat coelestium ac terrestrium & subterraneorum: omnisque lingua profiteatur, Dominum esse Iesum Christum, ad gloriam Dei Patris.
units.tr: Therefore God also highly exalted him and gave him the name that is above every name, so that at the name of Jesus every knee should bow, of those in heaven, on earth and under the earth, and every tongue should confess that Jesus Christ is Lord, to the glory of God the Father.

units.la: VI.
units.tr: VI.

units.la: PRIMVM in summa perfectione ac dignitate personae Mediatoris etiam juxta naturam assumtam, donorum ineffabili excellentia, maiestate, ac felicitate ornati, & exaltati in summam sublimitatem, longè supra omne imperium, & potestatem, & potentiam, & dominium, &c. omnibus sub pedes eius subjectis, vt sit caput ecclesiae a, per quod Pater omnia in coelo & in terra gubernat b, salvis & inconfusis manentibus naturis, & naturarum proprietatibus in hac gloria: qua, vt ait Augustinus, carni immortalitatem dedit, naturam non abstulit c.
units.tr: FIRST, in the supreme perfection and dignity of the person of the Mediator, even according to the nature he assumed, adorned and exalted with gifts of ineffable excellence, majesty and felicity, raised to the highest sublimity, far above every rule, authority, power, dominion, etc., with all things made subject under his feet, so that he is head of the church, through whom the Father governs all things in heaven and on earth, the natures remaining unimpaired and unmingled, and the properties of the natures remaining in this glory; which, as Augustine says, gave the flesh immortality without taking away its nature.

units.la: TESTIMONIA SACRAE SCRIPTVRAE ET ANTIQVORVM DOCTORVM.
units.tr: THE TESTIMONIES OF HOLY SCRIPTURE AND OF THE ANCIENT DOCTORS.

units.la: a] Eph. 1, 20. 21. Deus Christum collocauit ad dextram suam in coelis, longè supra omne imperium, &c.
units.tr: a] Eph. 1, 20. 21. God placed Christ at his right hand in the heavens, far above every rule, &c.

units.la: b] Joh. 5. vers. 22. Nec enim Pater judicat quemquam, sed omne judicium dedit Filio.
units.tr: b] Joh. 5. vers. 22. For the Father judges no one, but has given all judgment to the Son.

units.la: Deus juste judicaturus est orbem terrarum, per eum virum, quem definiit.
units.tr: God is going to judge the world justly through that man whom he has appointed.

units.la: Augustinus epist. 57. ad Dardanum: Noli itaque dubitare ibi nunc esse hominem Christum Iesum, unde venturus est, memoriterque recole, & fideliter tene Christianam confessionem, quoniam resurrexit a mortuis, ascendit in coelum, sedet ad dextram Patris, nec aliunde, quam inde venturus est ad vivos mortuosque judicandos. Et sic venturus est, illa angelica voce testante, quemadmodum ire visus est in coelum, id est, in eadem carnis forma & substantia: cui profecto immortalitatem dedit, naturam non abstulit.
units.tr: Augustine, letter 57 to Dardanus: Do not doubt, therefore, that the man Christ Jesus is now there, from where he is to come, and recall it in memory, and faithfully hold the Christian confession, that he rose from the dead, ascended into heaven, sits at the right hand of the Father, and will come from there alone to judge the living and the dead. And he will come in just the way the angelic voice testified, as he was seen to go into heaven, that is, in the same form and substance of flesh: to that flesh he certainly gave immortality, but did not take away its nature.

units.la: VII.
units.tr: VII.

units.la: Secundo: In gloriosa administratione officij prophetici, sacerdotalis ac regij, Mediatoris declarantis sese, etiam in natura humana assumta, quod sit constitutus Dominus & Judex omnium, & regnantis efficacissimè in coelo & in terra ; colligendo sibi ex genere humano aeternam Ecclesiam, per Spiritum suum & verbum; interpellando pro ea , ac tuendo eam divina sua potentia in terris , donec ab aerumnis & hostibus universis liberatam glorificet in coelis.
units.tr: Secondly: In the glorious exercise of his prophetic, priestly and kingly office, the Mediator, who in his assumed human nature also declares that he has been appointed Lord and Judge of all, and reigns most effectively in heaven and on earth; gathering to himself from the human race an eternal Church, through his Spirit and Word; interceding for it, and protecting it by his divine power on earth, until he delivers it, freed from troubles and from all enemies, and glorifies it in heaven.

units.la: TESTIMONIA SCRIPTURAE.
units.tr: TESTIMONIES OF SCRIPTURE.

units.la: Act. 2, 36. Certò sciat ergo tota domus Israelis, quod Deus hunc fecerit Dominum & Christum: hunc ipsum, inquam, Iesum, quem vos crucifixistis.
units.tr: Acts 2:36. Let therefore all the house of Israel know assuredly that God has made this same Jesus, whom you crucified, both Lord and Christ.

units.la: Actor. 5, 31. Hunc Deus dextra sua exaltum, constituit Principem ac servatorem, ut det resipiscentiam Israeli & remissionem peccatorum.
units.tr: Acts 5:31. God has exalted him with his right hand to be Prince and Saviour, to give repentance to Israel and remission of sins.

units.la: Vide etiam paulo ante Act. 17, 31. Joh. 5, 22.
units.tr: See also a little before, Acts 17:31; John 5:22.

units.la: Psal. 110, 2. Dominare in medio inimicorum tuorum.
units.tr: Psal. 110, 2. Rule in the midst of your enemies.

units.la: 1 Cor. 15, 25. Oportet eum regnare, usquequo omnes inimicos sub pedibus eius.
units.tr: 1 Cor. 15, 25. He must reign until he has put all his enemies under his feet.

units.la: Eph. 4, 11. 12. Christus dedit alios apostolos, alios vero prophetas: alios autem evangelistas, alios autem pastores & doctores.
units.tr: Eph. 4, 11. 12. Christ gave some as apostles, some as prophets, some as evangelists, and some as pastors and teachers.

units.la: Rom. 1. vers. 17. Evangelium est potentia Dei ad salutem omni credenti.
units.tr: Rom. 1, vers. 17. The gospel is the power of God unto salvation for everyone who believes.

units.la: Marci 16, 21. Dominus cooperatus est, & sermonem confirmavit per signa subsequentia.
units.tr: Marci 16, 21. The Lord worked with them and confirmed the word by the signs that followed.

units.la: Rom. 8. vers. 34. Christus est ad dextram Dei, & interpellat pro nobis. Hebr. 9, 24. Christus ingressus est in cœlum ipsum, vt compareat nunc faciei Dei pro nobis.
units.tr: Rom. 8, vers. 34. Christ is at the right hand of God, and he intercedes for us. Hebr. 9, 24. Christ entered into heaven itself, now to appear before the face of God for us.

units.la: 1 Johan. 2, 1. Aduocatum apud Patrem habemus Iesum Christum justum.
units.tr: 1 John 2, 1. We have an advocate with the Father, Jesus Christ the righteous.

units.la: Matth. 16, 18. Porta inferorum non superabunt eam. Ioh. 10, 28. Ego ouibus meis do vitam aeternam, nec peribunt in aeternum: neq; rapiet eas quisquam è manu mea.
units.tr: Matth. 16, 18. The gates of hell shall not prevail against it. John 10, 28. I give my sheep eternal life, and they shall never perish; neither shall anyone snatch them out of my hand.

units.la: Joh. 17, 24. Pater, quos dedisti mihi, velim, vt vbi sum ego, & illi sint mecum, vt conspiciant gloriam meam.
units.tr: John 17, 24. Father, I desire that those whom you have given me be with me where I am, so that they may see my glory.

units.la: VIII.
units.tr: VIII.

units.la: DENIQVE in perfectione honoris & cultus a debiti Mediatori gloriosè regnanti etiam in natura humana, quod nimirum ab angelis, hominibus, & creaturis vniuersis caput & Dominus agnoscitur, adoratur & celebratur, sicut scriptum est: Et adorent eum omnes angeli Dei. Item: In nomine Iesu flectatur omne genu, cœlestium, terrestrium, & subterraneorum.
units.tr: Finally, in the perfection of the honour and worship owed to the Mediator, who reigns gloriously also in his human nature, he is acknowledged, adored and celebrated as head and Lord by angels, men and all creatures, as it is written: "And let all the angels of God worship him." Likewise: "At the name of Jesus every knee should bow, of things in heaven, things on earth, and things under the earth."

units.la: TESTIMONIA SCRIPTVRAE.
units.tr: TESTIMONIES OF SCRIPTURE.

units.la: Act. 9, 14. Hoc loco habet potestatem à principibus sacerdotum vinculi omnes, qui inuocant nomen tuum.
units.tr: Acts 9:14. Here he has authority from the chief priests to bind all who call upon your name.

units.la: 1 Corinth. 1. v. 2. Omnibus, qui inuocant nomen Domini nostri Iesu Christi quouis loco, Domini, inquam, tum ipsorum, tum nostri.
units.tr: 1 Cor. 1:2. To all who call upon the name of our Lord Jesus Christ in every place, their Lord, I say, as well as ours.

units.la: Apoc. 5, 9. Dignus es, qui accipias librum, & aperias eius sigilla: quoniam mactatus es, & redemisti nos per sanguinem tuum ex omni tribu, & lingua, & populo, & natione.
units.tr: Rev. 5:9. You are worthy to take the book and open its seals, for you were slain, and by your blood you redeemed us from every tribe, and tongue, and people, and nation.

units.la: IX.
units.tr: IX.

units.la: Falsa igitur & portentosa sunt haec & similia Vbiquitariorum dogmata.
units.tr: Therefore these and similar dogmas of the Ubiquitarians are false and monstrous.

units.la: 1. Quod humanitas Christi statim in conceptione, vbi verbum factum est caro, sederit ad dextram Dei Patris.
units.tr: 1. That the humanity of Christ sat at the right hand of God the Father immediately at his conception, when the Word was made flesh.

units.la: 2. Quod sedere ad dextram Dei nihil aliud sit, quàm Dei Filio, qui est dextra Patris, personaliter vniri.
units.tr: 2. That to sit at the right hand of God is nothing other than to be personally united to the Son of God, who is the right hand of the Father.

units.la: 3. Quod sit ascendere in cœlum.
units.tr: 3. That it means to ascend into heaven.

units.la: 4. Quod sit humanam naturam fieri & esse Deum.
units.tr: 4. That the human nature is made and is God.

units.la: 5. Quod sit, Christum humanitate sua cœlum & terram implere, & esse vbique.
units.tr: 5. That Christ fills heaven and earth by his humanity and is everywhere.

units.la: ARTICVLVS V, DE PRÆDESTINATIONE.
units.tr: ARTICLE V, ON PREDESTINATION.

units.la: I.
units.tr: I.

units.la: Negare in Deo esse æternam prædestinationem de genere humano, est ipsum Deum negare: & scripturam sacram mendacij arguere: Spoliatus siquidem Deus, vt verissime loquitur Lutherus a, virtute & sapientia eligendi, quid erit, nisi IDOLVM FORTVNÆ, cuius numine omnia temerè fiant? & tandem eò venietur, vt homines salui fiant & damnentur ignorante Deo, vt qui non DISCRIMINATA omnibus generali lenitate tolerante & indurante, tum misericordia corripiente & puniente, hominibus reliquerit, vtri velint salui fieri aut damnari, ipse interim forte ad conuiuium Æthiopum profectus, vt Homerus dicit. Et Augustinus ait lib. de bono perseuer. cap.18. Hoc scio, neminē contra istam prædestinationem, quam juxta scripturas sanctas defendimus, nisi errando disputare potuisse. Et cap.21. Nimia igitur contentionis est prædestinationi contradicere, vel de prædestinatione dubitare.
units.tr: To deny that there is an eternal predestination of the human race in God is to deny God himself and to charge Holy Scripture with falsehood. For God, stripped of the power and wisdom to choose, as Luther speaks most truly (a), what will he be but THE IDOL OF FORTUNE, by whose will everything happens at random? And at last it will come to this, that men are saved and damned while God is ignorant, since he, without distinguishing among all by a general forbearance and hardening, and by mercy calling and punishing, has left it to men to choose whether they wish to be saved or damned, while he himself perhaps has gone off to the banquet of the Ethiopians, as Homer says. And Augustine says in the book On the Gift of Perseverance, chapter 18: I know this, that no one could argue against that predestination, which we defend according to the holy Scriptures, except by error. And in chapter 21: Therefore it is excessive contentiousness to contradict predestination or to doubt concerning predestination.

units.la: a] de serv. arbitr. cap.143.
units.tr: a] On the Bondage of the Will, chap. 143.

units.la: II.
units.tr: II.

units.la: De prædestinatione autem loquendum & tacendum est cum scriptura sacra: quoniam, quæ Deus occulta esse voluit, non sunt scrutanda, quæ verò manifesta fecit, non sunt neganda: ne in illis illicitè curiosi, in istis damnabiliter ingrati, vt præclarè Ambrosius dixit b.
units.tr: Predestination, however, must be spoken of and kept silent about together with Holy Scripture, since what God has willed to be hidden is not to be searched out, and what he has made manifest is not to be denied, lest we be rashly curious about the former and damnably ungrateful for the latter, as Ambrose said well (b).

units.la: b[Lib.1. ad Monimum pag 8.
units.tr: b [Book 1, to Monimus, p. 8.

units.la: III.
units.tr: III.

units.la: Neque, vt hoc etiam cum Fulgentio moneamus, prædestinationis nomine aliqua voluntatis humanæ coactitia necessitas exprimitur, sed misericors & justa futuri operis diuini sempiterna dispositio prædicatur.
units.tr: Nor, that we may also warn with Fulgentius on this point, does the name of predestination express any compulsory necessity of the human will, but the merciful and just, eternal disposition of the future divine work is proclaimed.

units.la: IV.
