units.tr: IV.

units.la: Est enim PRÆDESTINATIO (vtà posteriori, hoc est, ab effectis Dei, ex scriptura & experientia irrefragabiliter notis, simplicissimè definiamus) æternum a consilium Dei, secundum quod ex perdita generis humani massa b, mero beneplacito c, quos vult, misericorditer fide in Christum, justitia & vita æterna donat, & gratuito per Christum seruat d: quos vult, ea fide, justitia & vita non donat e, sed in sua cæcitate, prauitate, atque exitio relinquens f, propter sua peccata æternis pœnis justissime addiaddicit ac damnatg: vt seruando credentes misericordiam & gratiam h, damnando impios iustitiam & potentiam suam in æternum declaret i.
units.tr: For PREDESTINATION (to define it most simply from the effects, that is, from what is irrefutably known from Scripture and experience) is the eternal a counsel of God, according to which, from the lost mass of the human race, by mere good pleasure b, c he mercifully grants faith in Christ, righteousness and eternal life to whom he wills, and freely saves them through Christ d; whom he wills, he does not grant that faith, righteousness and life e, but leaving them in their blindness, perversity and destruction f, condemns them and sentences them most justly to eternal punishments on account of their sins g, so that by saving believers he may declare his mercy and grace h, and by condemning the impious he may declare his justice and power forever i.

units.la: TESIMONIA SCRIPTVRAE.
units.tr: Testimonies of Scripture.

units.la: Act.15,18. Nota sunt Deo ab omni œuo opera sua. Eph.1, 4. Sicut elegit nos ante jacta mundi fundamenta. Act. 4,28. Vt facerent, quæcunque manus tua, & consilium tuum prius definierat, vt fierent. Rom. 9, 11. Vt propositum Dei, quod est secundum electionem, firmum maneret.
units.tr: Acts 15:18. Known to God are all his works from eternity. Eph. 1:4. As he chose us before the foundation of the world was laid. Acts 4:28. To do whatever your hand and your counsel had decided beforehand should come to pass. Rom. 9:11. That the purpose of God according to election might stand firm.

units.la: Rom. 9, 21. An non habet potestatem figulus in lutum, vt ex eadem massa faciat aliud quidem vas ad decus, aliud vero ad dedecus? Jerem. 18, 6. Numquid sicut figulus iste, non potero facere vobis, domus Israel? ait Iehoua. Ecce sicut est lutum in manu figuli, sic estis in manu mea, o Israel.
units.tr: Rom. 9:21. Has not the potter power over the clay, to make from the same lump one vessel for honour and another for dishonour? Jer. 18:6. Can I not do with you, house of Israel, as this potter does? says the LORD. Behold, as the clay is in the potter's hand, so are you in my hand, O Israel.

units.la: Matth. 1, 26. Etiam, Pater: quia ita placuit tibi. Rom. 9, 18. Cuius vult, miseretur: quem autem vult, indurat. Eph. 1. v. 5. 9. Qui prædestinauit nos, quos adoptaret in filios per Iesum Christum in se, pro beneuolo affectu voluntatis suæ. Patefacto nobis mysterio voluntatis suæ, secundum gratuitam suam benevolentiam, quam proposuerat in se.
units.tr: Matt. 11:26. Yes, Father, for so it pleased you. Rom. 9:18. He has mercy on whom he wills, and whom he wills he hardens. Eph. 1:5, 9. Who predestined us to be adopted as sons through Jesus Christ, according to the good pleasure of his will. Having made known to us the mystery of his will, according to his free goodwill, which he had purposed in himself.

units.la: Rom. 8, 29. 30. Quos præuouit, etiam prædestinauit, conformandos imagini Filij sui: vt is sit primogenitus inter multos fratres. Quos vero prædestinauit, eos etiam vocauit: & quos vocauit, eos etiam justificauit: quos autem justificauit, eos etiam glorificauit. Eph. 1, 4, 5. Sicut elegit nos ante jacta mundi fundamenta, vt simus sancti & inculpati coram eo cum charitate. Qui prædestinauit nos, quos adoptaret in filios per Iesum Christum in se, pro beneuolo affectu voluntatis suæ.
units.tr: Rom. 8:29, 30. Whom he foreknew, he also predestined to be conformed to the image of his Son, that he might be the firstborn among many brothers. And whom he predestined, these he also called; and whom he called, these he also justified; and whom he justified, these he also glorified. Eph. 1:4, 5. As he chose us before the foundation of the world, that we should be holy and blameless before him in love. Who predestined us to be adopted as sons through Jesus Christ, according to the good pleasure of his will.

units.la: Rom. 9, 18. Cuius vult, miseretur; quem autem vult, indurat. 2 Tim. 2, 25. 26. Seruum Domini oportet cum lenitate experiri, num aliquando daturus sit eis Deus respiscentiam ad agnitionem veritatis: & sanitate mentis recepta euasuri ex diaboli laqueo, captiui ab eo facti ad ipsius libitum.
units.tr: Rom. 9:18. He has mercy on whom he wills, and whom he wills he hardens. 2 Tim. 2:25, 26. The servant of the Lord must correct his opponents with gentleness, in case God may perhaps grant them repentance leading to the knowledge of the truth, and that they may come to their senses and escape from the snare of the devil, having been taken captive by him to do his will.

units.la: Rom. 9, 18. Cuius vult, miseretur, quem autem vult, indurat. Psal. 81, 13. Permisi igitur eos fortitudini cordis eorum, & ambulare in consilijs suis. Act. 14, 16. Quisque prateritis gentibus sinit omnes gentes suis ipsarum viis incedere.

units.tr: Deut. 27:26. Cursed is he who does not establish the words of this law by doing them.

units.la: Ezech. 18, 4. Anima quæ peccauerit, ipsa morietur.
units.tr: Ezek. 18:4. The soul that sins, it shall die.

units.la: Rom. 9, 23. Vt notas faceret diuitias gloriæ suæ erga vasa misericordiæ, quæ præparauit ad gloriam.
units.tr: Rom. 9:23. That he might make known the riches of his glory toward the vessels of mercy, which he has prepared for glory.

units.la: Ephes. 1, 6. Ad laudem gloriosæ suæ gratiæ, qua nos gratis sibi gratos effecit in illo dilecto.
units.tr: Eph. 1:6. To the praise of the glory of his grace, by which he has made us freely acceptable to himself in the Beloved.

units.la: Rom. 9, 22. Quid si verò volens ostendere iram, & notam facere potentiam suam, pertulit multa lenitate vasa irae coaptata ad interitum.
units.tr: Rom. 9:22. What if God, willing to show his wrath and make his power known, endured with much patience the vessels of wrath prepared for destruction?

units.la: Prouerb. 16, 4. Omnia operatus est Iehoua propter seipsum: etiam ipsum impium ad diem malum.
units.tr: Prov. 16:4. The LORD has made all things for himself, even the wicked for the day of evil.

units.la: V.
units.tr: V.

units.la: Quoniam verò nota sunt Deo omnia opera sua à seculo a, & nulla est apud Patrem luminum transmutatio, aut conuersionis obumbratio b: ideo dubitandum non est, quicquid Deus saluandis & damnandis hominibus nunc facit in tempore, id eum facere ab æterno decreuisse immutabiliter, & quidem eo modo facere, quo nunc facit, & Scriptura eum facere testatur. c.
units.tr: Since, however, all his works are known to God from the beginning of the world, and with the Father of lights there is no change, nor shadow of turning, therefore there is no doubt that whatever God now does in time in saving and condemning men, he has from eternity decided immutably to do, and indeed to do it in the very way in which he now does it, as Scripture testifies that he does.

units.la: TESTMONIA SCRIPTVRAE.
units.tr: TESTIMONIA SCRIPTVRAE.

units.la: a] Act. 15, 18. Nota sunt Deo ab omni ævo omnia opera sua.
units.tr: a] Acts 15:18. Known unto God from all eternity are all his works.

units.la: b] Jacob. 1, 17. Apud Patrem luminum nulla est transmutatio, aut conuersionis obumbratio.
units.tr: b] James 1:17. With the Father of lights there is no change, nor shadow of turning.

units.la: c] Esa. 14, 27. Iehoua exercituum decreuit; & quis irritabit?
units.tr: c] Isa. 14:27. The LORD of hosts hath purposed, and who shall disannul it?

units.la: VI.
units.tr: VI.

units.la: Aliter igitur etiam à priori non minus piè ex scriptura definimus prædestinationem, quod sit Dei æternum a, liberum b, justum c, immutabile d, & sanctum e consilium f, ac propositum g, quo ab æterno ante jacta mundi fundamenta h ex genere humano æqualiter corrupto ac perdito i (quippe quod mox post sanctam creationem impulsore diabolo esset lapsurum, & mortis æternæ obnoxium futurum k) ex mera Gloria & misericordia l, alios præuidit m, & elegit n, ac libro vitæ inscripsit o, atque adoptauit in seipso p, & ad vitam æternam destinauit q, per Christum Jesum seruandos r: quos ab initio ad finem usque mundi per verbum suum & Spiritum sanctum ad agnitionem Filij sui Jesu Christi efficaciter vocauit s, vera fide & conuersione cordis donauit, justificauit u, ac tandem etiam glorificabit x. Alios verò ex justissima sua voluntate non elegit, nec libro vitæ inscripsit y, sed tanquam impura vasa iræ propter peccata sua æterna morte punire decreuit aa: quorum etiam in tempore non miseretur tur {bb}: sed in excitate & prauitate sua deserendos reprobauit: vt in electis misericordiæ vasis diuitias bonitatis & gratiæ; in reprobatis iræ vasis potentiam iræ suæ demonstraret {dd}: atque ita misericors ac justus Judex mundi in omnem æternitatem agnoscatur & celebretur.
units.tr: Otherwise, then, no less piously, we define predestination from Scripture, from the same starting point, as God's eternal a, free b, just c, unchangeable d, and holy e counsel f and purpose g, by which, from all eternity and before the foundation of the world h, he foresaw m and chose n some out of the human race, which was equally corrupted and lost i (since it was to fall shortly after the holy creation, the devil being the instigator, and was to become liable to eternal death k), out of pure grace and mercy l; and he wrote them in the book of life o, adopted them in himself p, appointed them to eternal life q, to be saved through Christ Jesus r. Those whom he effectually called from the beginning to the end of the world, by his Word and Holy Spirit, to the knowledge of his Son Jesus Christ s, he endowed with true faith and conversion of heart, justified u, and at last will also glorify x. But others, out of his most just will, he did not choose, nor wrote in the book of life y; rather, as impure vessels of wrath, he decreed to punish them with eternal death for their sins aa. On these he does not have mercy even in time bb, but, in their blindness and wickedness, he reprobated them to be left behind, so that in the vessels of mercy he might show the riches of his goodness and grace, and in the vessels of wrath the power of his anger dd; and thus the merciful and just Judge of the world is to be acknowledged and celebrated throughout all eternity.

units.la: TESTIMONIA SCRIPTVRÆ, ET ipsius Spiritus sancti verba: quibus æternam Dei prædestinationem & electionem in VERBO suo manifestauit, nobisque credendam reliquit.
units.tr: TESTIMONIES OF SCRIPTURE, and the very words of the Holy Spirit, by which he has made known in his Word God's eternal predestination and election, and has left them for us to believe.

units.la: a] Psal. 33, 11. Consilium Iehouæ in saeculum stat: cogitationes cordis eius in generationem & generationem. b] Rom. 9. vers. 18. Deus cuius vult, miseretur: quem autem vult, indurat. Matth. 20, 15. Annon licet mihi, quod volo, facere in rebus meis? Esa 46, 10. Consilium meum stabit, & omnem voluntatem meam faciam. c] Dan. 9, 14. Iustus est Iehouah Deus noster in omnibus operibus suis, quæ fecit. d] Prou. 19, 21. Consilium Iehouæ permanet. Esa 14, 24. 25. Si non secundum quod cogitaui, sic fiet: & secundum quod decreui, consurget. Hoc est consilium, quod decretum est & me. Iehoua exercituum decreuit, & quis irritabit? Esa. 45, 7. Formans pacem, & creans malum. Esa. 46, 11. Formaui, etiam faciam illud. Ezech. 12, 25. Loquar verbum, & faciam illud. Malach. 3, 6. Ego Iehoua non mutor. Rom. 11, 29. Eorum Deum poenitere non potest. Hebr. 6, 17. Volens ostendere immutabilitatem consilij sui, fideiussit iurejurando. Iac. 1, 17. Apud Patrem luminum non est transmutatio. e] Esa. 6, 3. Sanctus, sanctus, sanctus Iehoua exercituum. Psal. 145, 17. Iustus Iehoua in omnibus viis suis, & sanctus in omnibus operibus suis. f] Eph. 1, 11. Omnia efficit ex consilio voluntatis suæ. Act. 4, 28. Vt facerent, quæcunque manus tua & consilium tuum prius definierunt, quæ fierent. g] Rom 8, 11. Vt propositum Dei, quod est secundum ipsius electionem, maneret. Ephes. 1, 11. In ipso adsciti sumus in sortem, cum essemus prædestinati secundum propositum eius, & qui omnia efficit ex consilio voluntatis suæ.
units.tr: a] Ps. 33:11. The counsel of the LORD standeth for ever, the thoughts of his heart to all generations. b] Rom. 9:18. He hath mercy on whom he will have mercy, and whom he will he hardeneth. Matt. 20:15. Is it not lawful for me to do what I will with my own? Isa. 46:10. My counsel shall stand, and I will do all my pleasure. c] Dan. 9:14. The LORD our God is righteous in all his works which he doeth. d] Prov. 19:21. The counsel of the LORD shall stand. Isa. 14:24, 25. As I have thought, so shall it come to pass; and as I have purposed, so shall it stand. This is the purpose that is purposed upon the whole earth. For the LORD of hosts hath purposed, and who shall disannul it? Isa. 45:7. I form the light, and create darkness; I make peace, and create evil. Isa. 46:11. I have spoken it, I will also bring it to pass. Ezek. 12:25. I will speak the word, and it shall be performed. Mal. 3:6. For I am the LORD, I change not. Rom. 11:29. For the gifts and calling of God are without repentance. Heb. 6:17. Wherein God, willing more abundantly to shew unto the heirs of promise the immutability of his counsel, confirmed it by an oath. James 1:17. With the Father of lights there is no variableness. e] Isa. 6:3. Holy, holy, holy is the LORD of hosts. Ps. 145:17. The LORD is righteous in all his ways, and holy in all his works. f] Eph. 1:11. Who worketh all things after the counsel of his own will. Acts 4:28. For to do whatsoever thy hand and thy counsel determined before to be done. g] Rom. 9:11. That the purpose of God according to election might stand. Eph. 1:11. In whom also we have obtained an inheritance, being predestinated according to the purpose of him who worketh all things after the counsel of his own will.

units.la: h] Ephes. 1. vers. 4. Sicut elegit nos in ipso ante jacta mundi fundamenta.
units.tr: h] Eph. 1:4. According as he hath chosen us in him before the foundation of the world.

units.la: i] Ephes. 2, 5. Cum per lapsus mortui essemus, una nos Deus vivificavit cum Christo.
units.tr: i] Eph. 2:5. Even when we were dead in sins, hath quickened us together with Christ.

units.tr: Rom. 9:21. Hath not the potter power over the clay, of the same lump to make one vessel unto honour, and another unto dishonour?

units.la: k] Genes. c. 1. v. 2. 3. & seqq.
units.tr: k] Gen. 1:2, 3 and following.

units.tr: l] Titus 3:5. Not by works of righteousness which we have done, but according to his mercy he saved us.

units.la: Rom. 9, 11. 18. Nondum enim nati pueris, cum nihil fecissent boni vel mali, ut propositum Dei, quod est secundum ipsius electionem, id est, non ex operibus, sed ex vocante, firmum maneret. Itaque, cuius vult, miseretur, quem vult, indurat.
units.tr: Rom. 9:11, 18. For the children being not yet born, neither having done any good or evil, that the purpose of God according to election might stand, not of works, but of him that calleth. Therefore hath he mercy on whom he will have mercy, and whom he will he hardeneth.

units.la: Deu. 7, 7. 8. Non quia plures essetis, pro omnibus populis amavit vos Iehova, & elegit vos: sed quia diligebat vos Iehova.
units.tr: Deut. 7:7, 8. The LORD did not set his love upon you, nor choose you, because ye were more in number than any people; but because the LORD loved you.

units.tr: m] Rom. 8:29. Whom he did foreknow, he also did predestinate to be conformed to the image of his Son, that he might be the firstborn among many brethren.

units.tr: n] Matt. 22:14. Many are called, but few are chosen.

units.la: Eph. 1, 4. Sicut elegit nos in ipso.
units.tr: Eph. 1:4. According as he hath chosen us in him.

units.tr: o] Phil. 4:3. Whose names are in the book of life.

units.tr: Dan. 12:1. And at that time thy people shall be delivered, every one that shall be found written in the book.

units.tr: Luke 10:20. Rejoice, because your names are written in heaven.

units.la: Apoc. 20, 12. Et alius liber apertus est: qui est liber vitae.

Rom.11,7. Electi assecuti sunt: reliqui verò obcaluerunt. z] Apoc.20,15. Qui non inuentus est in libro vitæ scriptus, coniectus est in stagnum ignis. Apoc.17, 8. Jerem.13. v.14. Neque vtar misericordia, nec miserebor, vt non destruam eos. cc] Psalm.81,13. Permisi igitur eos fortitudini cordis eorum, & ambulant in consiliis suis. Act.14,16. Deus praeteritis aetatibus sinit omnes gentes suis ipsorum viis incedere. Rom.1, 24.26.28. Quamobrem etiam tradidit eos Deus cupiditatibus cordium ipsorum, ad impuritatem, vt fœdarent corpora sua inter se, &c. dd] Rom.9,22.23. Deus judex est: hunc humiliat, & illum exaltat.
units.tr: Titus 1:1. According to the faith of God's elect. v] Rom. 8:30. Whom he called, them he also justified. x] Rom. 8:30. Whom he justified, them he also glorified. y] Matt. 22:14. Few are chosen. Rom. 11:7. The elect have obtained it, and the rest were blinded. z] Rev. 20:15. And whosoever was not found written in the book of life was cast into the lake of fire. Rev. 17:8. And in very deed for this cause have I raised thee up, for to shew in thee my power; and that my name might be declared throughout all the earth. Prov. 16:4. The LORD hath made all things for himself: yea, even the wicked for the day of evil. ee] Ps. 145:7. They shall abundantly utter the memory of thy great goodness, and shall sing of thy righteousness. Ps. 75:7. But God is the judge: he putteth down one, and setteth up another.

units.la: VII.
units.tr: VII.

units.la: Ex his dictis sacræ scripturæ manifestè liquet, Deum ipsum iam à iactis mundi fundamentis tale discrimen inter homines constituisse, vt dicat aliorum se misereri a, alios vero indurare b: alios illuminare, alios occæcare c: alios ad pœnitentiam vocare, alios non vocare: aliis dare fidem, aliis non dare d. Abel reception est à Deo, Cain reiectus e. Sem retinet benedictionem Dei, Cham est maledictus f. Abraham vocatur ex Vr Chaldæae: alii deseruntur. Isaac fit hæres: Ismael eiicitur h. Iacob diligitur: Esau odio habetur. Petrus post lapsum recipitur in gratiam i: Iudas relinquitur in desperatione. Ad summam: vsq; ad finem sæculi fiet id, quod prædixit Christus k: Tunc duo erunt in agro: vnus accipietur, & alter relinquetur; Duæ molentes in pistrino, vna accipietur, & altera relinquetur. Quis igitur dubitabit, Deum ab æterno ista sic decreuisse, quæ in tempore voluit fieri? Nam apud Deum Patrem luminum nulla est transmutatio. Iacob. 1.17. Vide supra Aphor. V.
units.tr: From these sayings of Holy Scripture it is plainly evident that God himself, already from the foundation of the world, made such a distinction among men that he says he has mercy on some a, but hardens others b; he enlightens some, blinds others c; he calls some to repentance and does not call others; to some he gives faith, to others he does not give it d. Abel was received by God, Cain rejected e. Shem retains God's blessing, Ham is cursed f. Abraham is called out of Ur of the Chaldees; others are forsaken. Isaac becomes the heir; Ishmael is cast out h. Jacob is loved; Esau is hated. Peter, after his fall, is restored to grace i; Judas is left in despair. In sum, until the end of the age what Christ foretold k will come to pass: "Then two will be in the field; one will be taken and the other left. Two women will be grinding at the mill; one will be taken and the other left." Who then will doubt that God decreed from eternity these things, which he willed to happen in time? For with the Father of lights there is no variation. James 1.17. See above, Aphorism V.

units.la: VIII.
units.tr: VIII.

units.la: Proinde non minus verum est, Prædestinationem esse, quam certum est, DEVM esse DEVM. Vide dictum Lutheri supra Aphorism. I.
units.tr: Therefore it is no less true that there is predestination than it is certain that God is God. See the saying of Luther above, Aphorism I.

units.la: IX.
units.tr: IX.

units.la: Causa, cur Deus ab æterno ex perdito genere humano alios ad vitam æternam per Christum saluandos prædestinarit in conscilio Dei alia nulla est, quam quæ in tempore eum permouit, vt electis iuxta patefactum suum verbum donaret fidem & vitam æternam: merâ scilicet εὐδοκία, & liberrima voluntas eos eligendi in Christo a: non autem præuisa eorum sanctitas, aut bona operationes b. Omnes enim pariter erant peccatores, & ad bona opera inepti c: nisi Deus ea ideo in illis operetur, quia eos ante prædestinarit & elegerit d.
units.tr: The cause why God from eternity predestined some out of the lost human race to be saved through Christ to eternal life is, in the counsel of God, no other than that which moved him in time to grant faith and eternal life to the elect according to his revealed word: namely, by pure good pleasure [εὐδοκία] and his most free will to choose them in Christ a; not, however, their foreseen holiness or good works b. For all were equally sinners and unfit for good works c, unless God works those very works in them because he has predestined and elected them beforehand d.

units.la: TESTIMONIA SCRIPTVRAE.
units.tr: THE TESTIMONIES OF SCRIPTURE.

units.la: Cuius vult, miseretur: & quem vult, indurat.
units.tr: "He has mercy on whom he wills, and he hardens whom he wills." (Rom. 9.18)

units.la: Ephes. 1.5. Qui prædestinauit nos, quos adoptaret in filios per Iesum Christum in sese, pro beneuolo affectu voluntatis suæ.
units.tr: Eph. 1.5. He predestined us to be adopted as his sons through Jesus Christ, into himself, according to the good pleasure of his will.

units.la: Matth. 11.26. Etiam, Pater: quoniam sic placuit tibi.
units.tr: Matt. 11.26. Yes, Father, for so it has pleased you.

units.la: In hoc est charitas, non quod nos dilexerimus Deum, sed quod ipse dilexerit nos.
units.tr: Herein is love: not that we loved God, but that he loved us.

units.la: Ioh. 15.16. Non vos me elegistis, sed ego elegi vos.
units.tr: John 15.16. You did not choose me, but I chose you.

units.la: Rom. 9.11. Non ex operibus, sed ex vocante.
units.tr: Rom. 9.11. Not by works, but by him who calls.

units.la: Tit. 3.5. Non ex operibus iustis, quæ fecerimus nos, sed ex sua misericordia seruauit nos.
units.tr: Titus 3.5. Not by works of righteousness that we have done, but according to his mercy he saved us.

units.la: Ephe. 1.4. Elegit nos in eo cum charitate. Deut.7, 7. Non quia plures essetis pra omnibus populis, amavit vos Iehova, & elegit vos: sed quia diligebat vos Iehova. Omnes natura eramus filij irae, sicut & caeteri. Matth.7,8. Arbor putris non potest ferre bonos fructus. Non quod idonei simus ex nobis ipsis, ad cogitandum quicquam, velut ex nobis ipsis: sed quod idonei sumus, id ex Deo est.
units.tr: Eph. 1.4. He chose us in him with love. Deut. 7.7. Jehovah did not set his love on you nor choose you because you were more in number than all the peoples, but because Jehovah loved you. By nature we were all children of wrath, like the rest. Matt. 7.18. A rotten tree cannot bear good fruit. Not that we are sufficient of ourselves to think anything as of ourselves, but our sufficiency is of God.

units.la: Videetiam Ephes.1,4. Rom.8,30.
units.tr: See also Eph. 1.4; Rom. 8.30.

units.la: X.
units.tr: X.

units.la: Causa, cur Deus non omnes elegerit, vel non omnes deserue rit, sed aliquos duntaxat, & cur nos potius, quàm illos, Iacobum, inquam, Petrum & Paulum potius, quàm Esauum, Iudam, & Simonem magum elegerit, rursum in aeterno Dei consilio alia nulla dari potest, quam quae in verbo patefacta est, quare scilicet non omnes in tempore vocarit, aut non vocarit, converterit, aut non converterit: nempe gratiosum & iustissimum beneplacitum voluntatis suae a: non autem praevisa hominum inaequalitas, dignitas vel indignitas: quasi Deus praeviderit hos in se fore pios, illos v. impios. Vidit enim Deus, omnes pariter esse corruptos: eoque ob dignitatem merito omnes debuisset reijcere b. Huius voluntatis ac beneplacitiD. Paulus ait fuisse declarationem misericordiae & irae Dei c. Quare vero sic, & non aliter Deo placuerit, abyssus est impserscrutabilis sapientiae Dei, adoranda cum Apostolo: O ALTITVDO! d. Occulta potest esse causa, injusta esse non potest, inquit Augustinus e.
units.tr: The reason why God chose some, and not all, or did not reject all but only some, and why he chose us rather than those others (I mean, why he chose James, Peter and Paul rather than Esau, Judas and Simon the magician), cannot be given from God's eternal counsel other than what is revealed in the Word. That is, the reason why he called, or did not call, converted, or did not convert, all in time, lies in the gracious and most just good pleasure of his will, and not in foreseen inequality among men, their worth or unworthiness, as though God had foreseen that these would be godly and those ungodly. For God saw that all alike were corrupt, and so by rights he ought to have rejected all on account of their unworthiness. Paul says that this will and good pleasure was a declaration of the mercy and wrath of God. But why it pleased God to act thus and not otherwise is an unsearchable abyss of the wisdom of God, to be adored with the Apostle: O THE DEPTH! The cause may be hidden, but it cannot be unjust, says Augustine.

units.la: TESTIMONIA SACRAE SCRIPTVRAE ET ANTIQVORVM DOCTORVM.
units.tr: Testimonies of Holy Scripture and of the ancient teachers.

units.la: Gloriam tibi tribuo, Pater, Domine coeli & terra, quod haec occultaueris a sapientibus & intelligentibus, & revelaueris infantibus. Etiam, Pater, quia ita placuit tibi.
units.tr: I give you thanks, Father, Lord of heaven and earth, that you have hidden these things from the wise and understanding and revealed them to infants. Yes, Father, for so it has pleased you.

units.la: Videetiam Ephes.1,5.6.
units.tr: See also Ephes. 1:5, 6.

units.la: Nondum natis pueris, cum nihil fecissent boni vel mali, ut propositum Dei, quod est secundum ipsius electionem, id est, non ex operibus, sed ex vocante, firmum maneret.
units.tr: Before the children were born, when they had done nothing good or evil, God's purpose, which stands according to his election (that is, not from works but from him who calls), might remain firm.

units.la: Quid si vero volens ostendere iram, & notam facere potentiam suam, pertulit multa lenitate vasa irae coaptata ad interitum, & ut notas faceret divitias gloriae suae erga vasa misericordiae, quae praeparauit ad gloriam?
units.tr: What if God, willing to show his wrath and make his power known, endured with great patience the vessels of wrath made ready for destruction, and did so in order to make known the riches of his glory toward the vessels of mercy, which he has prepared for glory?

units.la: Ibid. v.17. Ad hoc ipsum excitaui te, ut ostendam in te potentiam meam, & ut annunciet ur nomen meum in tota terra.
units.tr: Ibid. v. 17. For this very purpose I have raised you up, that I might show my power in you, and that my name might be proclaimed through all the earth.

units.la: Prou.16,4. Omnia operatus est Iehova propter seipsum: etiam ipsum impium ad diem malum.
units.tr: Prov. 16:4. Jehovah has made all things for himself, even the wicked for the day of evil.

units.la: XI.
units.tr: XI.

units.la: Causa autem, cur Deus hos non eligat, tamquam impura vasa, ad iram & poenam æternæ damnationis destinata a, rursum alia nulla est, quam cur & nunc & in æternum iuxta legem & Euangelium eos punit ac condemnat: ratione nimirum Dei, iustissima ira aduersus peccata b: ratione reproborum, peccata ipsorum, malitia & incredulitas c. Sicut enim Deus pro iustitia sua neminem punit, nisi propter peccata d: ita neminem ad poenam praedestinauit, nisi propter peccata.
units.tr: The reason why God does not choose these people, as impure vessels destined to wrath and to the punishment of eternal damnation a, is again no other than why he now and forever punishes and condemns them according to the law and the Gospel. On God's side, this is his most just wrath against sins b; on the side of the reprobate, it is their sins, their malice and unbelief c. For just as God, in keeping with his justice, punishes no one except on account of sins d, so he has predestined no one to punishment except on account of sins.

units.la: TESTIMONIA SCRIPTVRÆ.
units.tr: TESTIMONIES OF SCRIPTURE.

units.la: Vide etiam Rom. 9. 22. Matth. 25. 41. Iudæ vers. 4.
units.tr: See also Rom. 9. 22. Matth. 25. 41. Jude, vers. 4.

units.la: XII.
units.tr: XII.

units.la: Proinde in Prædestinatione Dei nihil fit iniuste, sed omnia ex mera gratia & iustitia. Nam ex gratia debitum condonat electis, à quibus iure posset exigere: idem ex iustitia exigit à reprobis, quibus non tenebatur illud remittere a. Imo vero etiam iustus foret Deus, si vtrûq; puniret. Quia vtrumq; in pari corruptione deprehendit. Non igitur illi, qui damnantur, prætendere possunt, se poenam non meruisse: neq; illi, qui iustificantur gloriari possunt, quasi gratiam meruerint e.
units.tr: Therefore nothing is done unjustly in the predestination of God, but all things proceed from pure grace and justice. For out of grace he remits to the elect the debt which he could rightfully demand from them; and out of justice he exacts it from the reprobate, whom he was not bound to release. Indeed, God would be just even if he punished both; for he finds both in the same corruption. Therefore neither those who are condemned can plead that they did not deserve punishment, nor can those who are justified boast as if they had merited grace.

units.la: TESTIMONIA SCRIPTVRAE ET ANTIQVORVM DOCTORVM.
units.tr: Testimonies of Scripture and of the ancient teachers.

units.la: c] Ambrosius libro 2. cap. 1. de vocatione gentium: Nec damnati justa querimonia: nec justificati verax est arrogantia: si vel ille dicat, non meruisse se poenam: vel iste asserat, meruisse se gratiam.
units.tr: c] Ambrose, book 2, chapter 1, On the Calling of the Gentiles: Neither is the condemned man's complaint just, nor is the justified man's boast truthful: if the one should say that he has not deserved punishment, or the other should assert that he has deserved grace.

units.la: XIII.
units.tr: XIII.

units.la: Ex praedestinatione Dei, inquit Lutherus, pendent omnia: nempe qui crediturí, qui non: qui à peccato liberandi, qui occæcandi: qui damnandi & justificandi sint. Nam in electis ad vitam operatur vocationem, poenitentiam, fidem, justitiam, consolationem & gloriam a: in praedestinatis ad damnationem non operatur, sed invenit peccata, incredulitatem, injustitiam, desperaturs, sed invenit peccata, incredulitatem, injustitiam, desperationem ac dedecus: in multis tamen operatur justissimam indurationem b: in omnibus vero aeternam desertionem, & rejectionem à facie Dei c.
units.tr: Luther says: "Everything depends on the predestination of God: namely, who will believe and who will not; who are to be freed from sin and who are to be blinded; who are to be condemned and who justified. For in the elect he works calling, repentance, faith, righteousness, comfort and glory a; in the predestined to damnation he does not work these, but finds sins, unbelief, injustice, despair and disgrace; yet in many he works a most just hardening b, and in all, eternal desertion and rejection from the face of God c."

units.la: TESTIMONIA SCRIPTVRAE.
units.tr: TESTIMONIES OF SCRIPTURE.

units.la: a] Rom. 8,29.30. Quos praenovit, etiam praedestinavit, confirmandos imagini Filii sui: ut is sit primogenitus inter multos fratres. Quos verò praedestinavit, eos etiam vocavit: & quos vocavit, eos etiam justificavit: quos autem justificavit, eos etiam glorificavit.
units.tr: a] Rom. 8,29.30. Those whom he foreknew, he also predestined to be conformed to the image of his Son, that he might be the firstborn among many brothers. Those whom he predestined, he also called; and those whom he called, he also justified; and those whom he justified, he also glorified.

units.la: Actor. 15, 48. Et crediderunt, quotquot ad vitam aeternam erant praedestinati.
units.tr: Acts 15, 48. And as many as were ordained to eternal life believed.

units.la: b] Rom. 9,18. Indurat, quos vult.
units.tr: b] Rom. 9,18. He hardens whom he will.

units.la: Rom. 11,7. 8. Electi assecuti sunt: reliqui vero obcaluerunt: sicut scriptum est: Dedit eis Deus spiritum soporis: oculos ut non videant, & aures ut non audiant.
units.tr: Rom. 11,7.8. The elect obtained it, but the rest were hardened, as it is written: God gave them a spirit of stupor, eyes that they should not see, and ears that they should not hear.

units.la: c] Jerem. 16, 5. Abstuli pacem meam à populo isto, dixit Iehova, misericordiam & miserationes.
units.tr: c] Jer. 16, 5. I have taken away my peace from this people, saith Jehovah, my mercy and my compassions.

units.la: Matth. 23,38. Ecce relinquitur vobis domus vestra deserta.
units.tr: Matt. 23,38. Behold, your house is left to you desolate.

units.la: Matth. 25, 41. Execrati abite à me in ignem aeternum, qui paratus est diabolo & angelis eius.
units.tr: Matt. 25, 41. Depart from me, you cursed, into the eternal fire prepared for the devil and his angels.

units.la: XIV.
units.tr: XIV.

units.la: Quoscunq; igitur Deus in Christo ad vitam praedestinavit, eos quoq; certò & immutabiliter vocat ad fidem, justificat, & glorificat a. Impossibile igitur est, electos perire, & ex libro vitæ posse deleri b. Horum si quisquam perit, inquit Augustinus, fallitur Deus: sed nemo eorum perit, quia non fallitur Deus. Horum si quisquam perit: quia nulla re vitio humano vincitur Deus: sed nemo eorum perit: quia nulla re vincitur Deus. Reliqui verò qui à Deo deseruntur, & sibimet ipsis relinquuntur, certò & immutabiliter pereunt. Arbor namque putris non potest ferre bonos fructus. Matth. 7,18.
units.tr: Therefore, those whom God predestined to life in Christ, these he also certainly and unchangeably calls to faith, justifies, and glorifies a. It is therefore impossible for the elect to perish or to be blotted out of the book of life. If any of these perished, says Augustine, God would be deceived; but none of them perishes, because God is not deceived. If any of these perished, it would be because God is overcome by some human fault; but none of them perishes, because God is overcome by nothing. The rest, however, who are forsaken by God and left to themselves, certainly and unchangeably perish. For a rotten tree cannot bear good fruit. Matt. 7:18.

units.la: a] De corr. & gratia, c. 7.
units.tr: a] On Correction and Grace, ch. 7.

units.la: TESTIMONIA SCRIPTVRAE.
units.tr: TESTIMONIES OF SCRIPTURE

units.la: a] Rom. 8. verf. 29. 30. Quos præcognouit, eos etiam vocauit, & justificauit. b] Matth. 24, 24. Si fieri posset, etiam electi seducerentur. Johan. 10, 28. Do omnibus meis vitam æternam: & nemo rapiet eas ex manu mea. Apoc. 3, 5. Qui vicerit, amicietur vestimentis albis: neq; unquam delebo nomen eius ex libro vitæ.
units.tr: a] Rom. 8:29-30. Whom he foreknew, these he also called, and justified. b] Matt. 24:24. If it were possible, even the elect would be led astray. John 10:28. I give my sheep eternal life, and no one shall snatch them out of my hand. Rev. 3:5. He who overcomes shall be clothed in white garments; and I will never blot his name out of the book of life.

units.la: XV.
units.tr: XV.

units.la: Hypocritis & hostibus minatur scriptura a, quod sint delendi ex libro viuentium, non quidē quasi in illo prius scripti fuerint, (additur enim: & cum justis non scribentur) sed quia externè gloriantur, aut pro iis habentur, qui in libro vitæ scripti sunt. Non sic Deus scribat in libro vitæ, & deleat illum. Si homo dixit: Quod scripsi, scripsi, de titulo, vbi scriptum erat: REX IVDÆORVM: DEVS quem quam scribit, & delet?
units.tr: Scripture threatens hypocrites and enemies a that they are to be blotted out of the book of the living; not, indeed, as though they had first been written in it (for it is added: and they shall not be written with the righteous), but because they boast outwardly, or are regarded as among those who are written in the book of life. God does not write someone in the book of life and then blot him out. If a man said, "What I have written, I have written," of the title where it was written, "THE KING OF THE JEWS," would God write and blot out?

units.la: TESEIMONIA SCRIPTVRAE.
units.tr: TESTIMONIES OF SCRIPTURE

units.la: a]Psalm. 69. verf. 29. Deleantur è libro viuentium, & cum justis non scribantur.
units.tr: a] Ps. 69:29. Let them be blotted out of the book of the living, and not be written with the righteous.

units.la: XVI.
units.tr: XVI.

units.la: Certum quoq; esse numerum electorum a: & pauciores esse electos, quam reprobos, testatur sacra scriptura b: neque prob dolor quotidiana experientia nos finit dubitare c.
units.tr: It is also certain that the number of the elect is fixed a, and that the elect are fewer than the reprobate, as holy Scripture testifies b; and, alas, daily experience does not allow us to doubt it c.

units.la: TESTIMONIA SCRIPTVRAE.
units.tr: TESTIMONIES OF SCRIPTURE

units.la: a]Joh. 13, 18. Ego scio, quos elegerim.
units.tr: a] John 13:18. I know whom I have chosen.

units.la: 2 Tim. 2, 19. Solidum fundamentum Dei stat, habens sigillum: Novit Dominus eos, qui sunt sui. b] Matth. 22, 14. Multi vocati, pauci electi. c] Matth. 7, 13. Lata est porta, & spaciosa via, quæ adducit in exitium: multiq; sunt, qui introeunt per eam.
units.tr: 2 Tim. 2:19. The solid foundation of God stands, having this seal: The Lord knows those who are his. b] Matt. 22:14. Many are called, but few chosen. c] Matt. 7:13. Wide is the gate and broad is the way that leads to destruction, and many are those who go in by it.

units.la: XVII.
units.tr: XVII.

units.la: Cæterum vt prædestinationem & electionem nostram scrutentur, non opus est in arcanum DEI consilium adscendere. Scrutatores namq; tales curiosi arcanorum Dei, qui à priore de electione judicant, haud dubiè, ait Lutherus, in confusionem conscientiæ, aut desperationē suā hac inepta curiositate ducent & præcipitabunt seipsos. Sed descendendum est ad effecta, ad vocationem nostram : vt exploremus, an simus in fide, nosqi probemus, an Christus in nobis habitet . Sunt enim hæc verè effecta, & signa electionis, & dona electorum propria: vt, efficax vocatio per Euangelium ad resipiscentiam , vera fides in Christum , noua obedientiae, pax cum Deo , testimonium Spiritus Dei in cordibus nostris de nostra adoptione . Hæc signa in nobis & aliis verè sentimus, certi sumus de nostra & aliorum electione. Ac de nostra quidem electione judicamus canone fidei, cuius est non falli: de aliorum vocatorum canone charitatis, cuius est falli: vt loquitur Lutherus .
units.tr: Moreover, in order to examine our predestination and election, there is no need to climb into the secret counsel of God. Such curious searchers into the hidden things of God, who judge of election from what comes before, will undoubtedly, says Luther, by this foolish curiosity lead and hurl themselves into confusion of conscience or into despair. But we must descend to the effects, to our calling, so that we may examine whether we are in the faith, and prove ourselves, whether Christ dwells in us. For these are truly the effects and signs of election, and the proper gifts of the elect: namely, effectual calling through the Gospel to repentance, true faith in Christ, new obedience, peace with God, and the testimony of the Spirit of God in our hearts concerning our adoption. When we truly perceive these signs in ourselves and in others, we are certain of our own election and of that of others. Indeed, we judge our own election by the rule of faith, whose office is not to be deceived; but we judge the election of other called persons by the rule of charity, whose office is to be deceived, as Luther puts it.

units.la: TESTIMONIA SCRIPTVRÆ.
units.tr: THE TESTIMONIES OF SCRIPTURE.

units.la: a] 1 Cor.1,26. Videtis enim vocationem vestram, fratres. b] 2 Cor.13,5. Vos ipsos tentate, an sitis in fide: vos ipsos probate: annon agnoscitis vosmet ipsos, videlicet Iesum Christum in vobis esse? nisi reiectanei estis. c] Rom.8,30 Quos prædestinauit, eos etiam vocauit. 1 Thess. 1. versf. 4. 5. Scimus fratres, à Deo electionem vestram. Quoniam Euangelium nostrum constitit apud vos non locutione duntaxat, sed etiam virtute, & in Spiritu sancto, & in multa persuasione. d] Tit.1,1. Apostolus secundum fidem electorum Dei. 2 Thess.3, 2. Fides non est omnium. Actor.13, 48. Et crediderant, quotquot prædestinati erant ad vitam æternam. e] Eph.1, 4. Elegit nos in ipso, vt essemus sancti & inculpati coram eo in charitate. 1 Petri 1. versf. 2. Electis ex præstitutione Dei Patris ad sanctificationem spiritus per obedientiam & aspersionem sanguinis Iesu Christi.
units.tr: a] 1 Cor.1,26. For you see your calling, brethren. b] 2 Cor.13,5. Test yourselves, whether you are in the faith; prove yourselves. Do you not recognise that Jesus Christ is in you? Unless indeed you are reprobates. c] Rom.8,30. Whom he predestined, those he also called. 1 Thess.1, vers. 4, 5. Brethren, we know that your election is from God. For our gospel came to you not in word only, but also in power, and in the Holy Spirit, and in much assurance. d] Tit.1,1. The apostle, according to the faith of God's elect. 2 Thess.3,2. Faith is not of all. Acts 13,48. And as many as were appointed to eternal life believed. e] Eph.1,4. He chose us in him, that we should be holy and blameless before him in love. 1 Pet.1, vers. 2. Elect according to the foreknowledge of God the Father, unto sanctification by the Spirit, unto obedience and the sprinkling of the blood of Jesus Christ.

units.la: 2 Pet.1, 10. Quapropter, fratres, potius studete vocationem vestram firmam efficere. f] Rom. 5, 1. Iustificati ex fide pacem habemus erga Deum per Dominum nostrum Iesum Christum. g] Rom.8,14,16. Quotquot Spiritu Dei aguntur, ii sunt filij Dei. Ipse Spiritus testatur vnà cum spiritu nostro, nos esse filios Dei. h] Lutherus de seruo arbitrio cap. 61. Sanctos eos dico, & habeo: Ecclesiam Dei eos voco & sentio, Canone charitatis, non Canone fidei: hoc est, charitas, quæ omnia optima de quoquis cogitat, nec est suspicax, omniaque credit ac præsumit de proximis bona, sanctum vocat quemlibet baptizatum, nec periculum est, si erret, quia charitatis est falli, cum sit exposita omnibus omnium visibus & abusibus, ministra generalis, bonorum, malorum, fidelium, infidelium, veracium, fallacium. Fides vero nullum vocat sanctum, nisi divino iudicio declaratum: quia fidei est, non falli. Ideo cum omnes debeamus haberi invicem sancti, iure charitatis, nullus tamen debet sanctus decerni, iure fidei, tamquam articulus sit fidei.
units.tr: 2 Pet.1,10. Therefore, brethren, be all the more eager to make your calling and election sure. f] Rom.5,1. Justified by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ. g] Rom.8,14,16. As many as are led by the Spirit of God, they are the sons of God. The Spirit himself bears witness with our spirit that we are the sons of God. h] Luther, On the Bondage of the Will, chap. 61. I call them saints and hold them to be such. I call them and feel them to be the Church of God by the canon of charity, not the canon of faith. That is, charity, which thinks the best of everyone, is not suspicious, believes and presumes all good things of its neighbours, calls every baptised person a saint, and there is no danger if it is mistaken, since it is characteristic of charity to be deceived; it is exposed to the sight and abuse of all, and is a general servant to good and bad, faithful and unfaithful, truthful and deceitful. Faith, however, calls no one a saint unless it has been declared so by the divine judgement, since it is characteristic of faith not to be deceived. Therefore, although we must all be held as saints toward one another by the right of charity, no one ought to be declared a saint by the right of faith, as if it were an article of faith.

units.la: XVIII.
units.tr: XVIII.

units.la: Hanc doctrinam de Prædestinatione Dei in Ecclesia retineri necessarium est, tum propter Dei gloriam, tum propter nostram consolationem. Primum ne gloriatio fidei nostræ, iustificationis, & æternæ salutis, nobis, aut libero nostro arbitrio, nostrisq; viribus, attribuatur, sed soli Deo cedat, & liberrimæ eius voluntati ac misericordiæ. Doctrina namque de hominis iustificatione, quæ fit per solam fidem, plane constare, intelligi, aut defendi nequit, nisi & doctrina de æterna Prædestinatione Dei, & electione, recte intelligatur, & sarta tecta in Ecclesiis Evangelicis conservetur. Quod nimirum non solum æterna felicitas & fidei iustificatio, sed ipsa quoque fides, merum Dei donum, & effectus Prædestinationis divinæ, in qua Deus nos, cum aliis meliores nec eramus, nec essemus futuri, aliis tamen præculit. Quod si enim fides aut ex parte, aut tota à nobis ipsis proficisci tur, statim iustificationem fidei absque operibus concidere necesse esset. Atque hæc schola est Christianæ humanitatis: ne quis adversus Deum glorietur. Deinde, ut certi simus, sicut fides & salus non est ex nobis, ita in nostris quoque viribus illam non esse: sed fundari in æterna atque immutabili Dei prædestinatione, neque non incertam, sed certam atque immutabilem esse: quicquid Diabolus contra tentet. Et sic quoque Lutherus scribit: Et hæc certè stabilis sententia & immota prædestinationis necessaria est. Tam imbecilles enim sumus, ut si in nostris manibus situm esset, paucissimi aut nulli salvarentur. Diabolus enim omnes vinceret. Nunc cum hæc stabilis & certissima Dei sententia munitus non possit, nec ab ulla creatura convelli, tum certe spes est nobis reliquæ, tandem vincendi peccati, quantumvis etiam nunc in carne sumus.
units.tr: It is necessary to retain this doctrine of the predestination of God in the Church, both for the glory of God and for our comfort. First, so that the glorying of our faith, of our justification, and of eternal salvation is not ascribed to us, or to our free will and our own strength, but yields to God alone and to his most free will and mercy. For the doctrine of man's justification, which takes place through faith alone, can plainly neither stand, be understood, nor be defended, unless the doctrine of God's eternal predestination and election is rightly understood and kept safe and sound in the evangelical churches. For it is not only eternal happiness and the justification of faith, but faith itself, that is the pure gift of God and the effect of divine predestination, in which God chose us beforehand over others, although we were not, and would not be, better than others. For if faith came from us, either in part or in whole, the justification of faith without works would at once collapse. And this is the school of Christian humility: that no one should glory before God. Second, so that we may be certain that, just as faith and salvation are not from us, so neither is it in our own strength; rather, it is grounded in the eternal and unchangeable predestination of God, and is not uncertain but certain and unchangeable, whatever the Devil may attempt against it. And so Luther also writes: "This firm and unmoved judgment of predestination is indeed necessary. For we are so feeble that, if it lay in our hands, very few or none would be saved; the Devil would conquer all. But now, since we are guarded by this firm and most certain judgment of God, which cannot be overturned by any creature, we certainly have the hope that we shall at last overcome sin, however much we are still in the flesh."

units.la: TESTIMONIA SCRIPTVRÆ.
units.tr: TESTIMONIES OF SCRIPTURE.

units.la: Eramus natura filij iræ: & per lapsus mortui.
units.tr: We were by nature children of wrath, and dead through our transgressions.

units.tr: 1 Cor. 4:7. For who makes you to differ from another? And what have you that you did not receive? Now if you did receive it, why do you boast, as if you had not received it?

units.la: {d} d
units.tr: {d} d

units.la: b]1 Cor.1,29. Vt ne glorietur vlla caro coram eo.
units.tr: b] 1 Cor. 1:29. So that no flesh may glory in his presence.

units.la: Vide etiam 1 Corinth. 4. verf. 7. & Rom. 3. verf. 19. Scimus autem, quaecunque lex dicit, iis qui in lege sunt, dicere: vt omne os obturetur: & obnoxius fiat totus mundus condemnationi Dei.
units.tr: See also 1 Cor. 4:7 and Rom. 3:19. Now we know that whatever the law says, it speaks to those who are under the law, so that every mouth may be stopped and the whole world may become accountable to God.

units.la: c]Ioh.10,28. Ego ouibus meis do vitam aeternam: neq; rapiet eas quisquam e manu mea.
units.tr: c] John 10:28. I give them eternal life, and no one shall snatch them out of my hand.

units.la: Matth.24,24. Non poterit fieri, vt electi seducantur.
units.tr: Matt. 24:24. It is impossible that the elect should be led astray.

units.la: Luc.22,32. Rogaui pro te, ne deficiat fides tua.
units.tr: Luke 22:32. I have prayed for you, that your faith may not fail.

units.la: 2 Tim.2,19. Solidum fundamentum Dei stat, habens sigillum hoc: Nouit Dominus eos, qui sunt sui.
units.tr: 2 Tim. 2:19. The firm foundation of God stands, bearing this seal: The Lord knows those who are his.

units.la: 1 Pet.1,5. Qui virtutis Dei praesidio custodimini per fidem ad salutem paratam patefieri tempore vltimo.
units.tr: 1 Pet. 1:5. You who are kept by the power of God through faith unto a salvation ready to be revealed in the last time.

units.la: XIX.
units.tr: XIX.

units.la: Reijcimus ergo, tanquam à fide, & consolatione Christiana alienas, Puccij, Huberi, & similium Pelagianas, ἀουσίας[?] & sese mutuo elidentes opiniones.
units.tr: We therefore reject, as alien from faith and Christian comfort, the Pelagian opinions of Puccius, Huber and their like, which [ἀουσίας[?]] collide with one another.

units.la: 1. Quod in Deo nullum sit electionis & reprobationis consilium.
units.tr: 1. That in God there is no counsel of election and reprobation.

units.la: 2. Quod electio sit generalis omnium.
units.tr: 2. That election is general, extending to all.

units.la: 3. Quod Paulus Ephes.1. verf.4. doceat generaliter, omnes in Christo esse electos ante jacta mundi fundamenta.
units.tr: 3. That Paul, Eph. 1:4, teaches generally that all are elected in Christ before the foundation of the world was laid.

units.la: 4. Quod omnes homines fuerint electi in Christo post lapsum Adami. Idem Hub. Thes.1001.
units.tr: 4. That all men were elected in Christ after the fall of Adam. The same Huber, Thes. 1001.

units.la: 5. Quod electi dicantur aliqui propter euentum, quia sint aliis meliores, vt aurum purum dicitur electum: & aer dicitur purus ob serenitatem.
units.tr: 5. That some are called elect on account of the outcome, because they are better than others, just as pure gold is called elect, and the air is called pure because of its clearness.

units.la: 6. Quod specialis electio nulla sit, quoad Deum: sed quoad homines, qui vniuersalem gratiam sibi applicant. Quod idem est, ac si dicas: Non Deus, sed nos homines electimus nosmetipsos.
units.tr: 6. That there is no special election on God's part, but only on men's part, who apply to themselves the universal grace. This is the same as if you were to say: not God, but we men elect ourselves.

units.la: 7. Quod multi electi pereant.
units.tr: 7. That many of the elect perish.

units.la: 8. Quod non sit certus electorum numerus apud Deum.
units.tr: 8. That the number of the elect is not certain with God.

units.la: 9. Quod doctrina praedestinationis pariat vel profanitatem, vel desperationem, proinde non sit docenda.
units.tr: 9. That the doctrine of predestination produces either profanity or despair, and therefore is not to be taught.

units.la: 10. Quod Deus statuatur injustus, crudelis tyrannus, [illegible, ~6 letters], inuidus, autor peccati & corruptionis hominis, si alios elegerit, alios non elegerit.
units.tr: 10. That God is made out to be unjust, a cruel tyrant, [illegible], envious, the author of sin and of human corruption, if he has chosen some and not chosen others.

units.la: 11. Quod fides nostra electionis nostrae sit causa, & non effectus: hoc est: quod Deus nos elegerit propter fidem nostram.
units.tr: 11. That our faith is the cause of our election and not its effect: that is, that God elected us on account of our faith.

units.la: ARTICVLVS VI.
units.tr: ARTICLE VI.

units.la: DE FIDE ET PRÆSTANTIA SANCTORVM.
units.tr: ON THE FAITH AND EXCELLENCE OF THE SAINTS.

units.la: I.
units.tr: I.

units.la: Credimus, fidem in Christo esse Dei donum , non genetale & commune omnibus : sed singulare effectum æternæ prædestinationis Dei : quod datur & omnibus & solis electis : non solum quod ad incrementa, sed etiam quod ad ipsum primum initium attinet : sicut vere est dictum ab Ambrosio: Deus initio- rum fidei, incrementiq; largitor est. Et Lutherus in Præfat. Epist. ad Rom. Ex æterna Dei prædestinatione proprie oritur, qui credere aut non credere debeat: ut hac ratione non in nostris sit manibus pietas nostra, sed in solius Dei potestate.
units.tr: We believe that faith in Christ is the gift of God, not a natural quality common to all, but the particular effect of God's eternal predestination. It is given both to all and only to the elect, and not only as to its growth but also as to its very first beginning, as Ambrose rightly said: God is the giver both of the beginnings and of the increase of faith. And Luther, in the preface to his Epistle to the Romans: From God's eternal predestination it arises properly who ought to believe or not to believe, so that our godliness is not in our own hands, but in the power of God alone.

units.la: TESTIMONIA SCRIPTVRAE.
units.tr: TESTIMONIES OF SCRIPTURE.

units.la: Johan. 6. vers. 29. Hoc est opus Dei, ut credatis in eum, quem misit ille.
units.tr: John 6:29. This is the work of God, that you believe in him whom he has sent.

units.la: Gal. 5. 22. Fructus Spiritus est fides.
units.tr: Gal. 5:22. The fruit of the Spirit is faith.

units.la: Eph. 2, 8. Gratia estis servati per fidem.
units.tr: Eph. 2:8. By grace you have been saved through faith.

units.la: Phil. 1, 29. Quia gratis datum est vobis in Christi negotio, non solum in eum credere, sed etiam pro eo pati.
units.tr: Phil. 1:29. For it has been freely given to you, in the cause of Christ, not only to believe in him but also to suffer for him.

units.la: 2 Thess. 3, 2. Fides non est omnium.
units.tr: 2 Thess. 3:2. Faith is not of all.

units.la: Actor. 13. vers. 48. Crediderunt quotquot erant ordinati ad vitam æternam.
units.tr: Acts 13:48. As many as were ordained to eternal life believed.

units.la: Tit. 1, 1. Secundum fidem electorum Dei.
units.tr: Titus 1:1. According to the faith of the elect of God.

units.la: Phil. 2, 13. Deus is est, qui efficit in vobis, & ut velitis, & ut efficiatis pro gratuita sua benevolentia.
units.tr: Phil. 2:13. It is God who works in you both to will and to work, for his good pleasure.

units.la: Philip. 1, 6. Qui cœpit in vobis opus bonum, perficiet usque ad diem Iesu Christi.
units.tr: Phil. 1:6. He who began a good work in you will complete it until the day of Jesus Christ.

units.la: II.
units.tr: II.

units.la: Perseverentia etiam, qua usque in finem perseveratur in fide Christi, & sine qua nemo servabitur, tale est Dei donum, quod certò datur omnibus electis. Matth. 24, 14.
units.tr: Perseverance also, by which one persists in faith in Christ to the end, and without which no one will be saved, is such a gift of God that it is certainly given to all the elect. Matt. 24:14.

units.la: III.
units.tr: III.

units.la: Hanc enim Deus promisit, dicens : Timorem meum dabo in cor eorum, ut à me non recedant, &c. Quod quid est aliud, inquit Augustinus , quam, talis ac tantus erit timor meus, quem dabo in cor eorum, ut mihi PERSEVERANTER adhæreant.
units.tr: For God has promised this, saying: I will put my fear in their heart, so that they do not depart from me, etc. What else is this, says Augustine, than: such and so great will be the fear of me that I will put in their heart, that they may cling to me PERSEVERINGLY.

units.la: Jeremiæ 32, 40.
De bono perseuer. cap. 2.
units.tr: On the Gift of Perseverance, chap. 2.

units.la: IV.
units.tr: IV.

units.la: Et sancti à Deo perseuerantiam in fide quotidie petunt indubitanter ergo eam à Deo accipiunt, juxta promissionem Christi Joh.16,23. Amen, amen dico vobis, quacunque petieritis à Patre meo in nomine meo, dabit vobis. Augustin.ibid. Cur perseuerantia poscitur à Deo, si non datur à Deo?
units.tr: And the saints daily ask God for perseverance in faith; therefore they undoubtedly receive it from God, according to the promise of Christ, John 16:23: Truly, truly I say to you, whatever you ask of my Father in my name, he will give you. Augustine, ibid.: Why is perseverance asked of God, if it is not given by God?

units.la: V.
units.tr: V.

units.la: Petunt verò & accipiunt à Deo non solum eam gratiam, vt in fine etiam vitæ fidem habeant, sed etiam vt eandem perpetuò retineant. Quæ in scholis appellatur perseuerantia finalis & totalis.
units.tr: Indeed they ask for and receive from God not only the grace that they may have faith even at the end of life, but also that they may keep it continually. This is called in the schools final and total perseverance.

units.la: VI.
units.tr: VI.

units.la: Tametsi enim non raro grauissimis lapsibus Deum offendant, Spiritum sanctum contristent, plurima eius dona excutiant & amittant, conscientiam polluant, fidem labefactent, & quandam in se est, frangant: vt exempla Dauidis & Petri ostendunt: nunquam tamen sic toto corde aduersus Deum ruunt, vt fiant hostes Dei, & gratia Dei penitus excidant, Spiritum sanctum prorsus excutiant, fidem omnino amittant: quoniam semen Dei in eis manet : tametsi efficax vis & sensus donorum Dei ad tempus sese non exerat, sed sub carnis infirmitate, velut ignis sub cineribus, aut Sol sub densis nubibus delitescat, donec Deus iterum exsuscitet. Quod vtique per veram poenitentiam eandem iterum exsuscitet. Quocirca totaliter nunquam fit ante finem vitæ, ne pereant. Quocirca totaliter nunquam excidunt Dei gratia: verum Deus ita irascitur illorum peccatis, vt tamen tanquam filios non prosequatur odio: ita eos castigans, vt tamen non planè à se reijciat . Scilicet vt pater filium delinquentem non protinus domo planè extrudit, multò minus paterna χειρὶ exuit, quamuis seuerè eum corripiat ac castiget.
units.tr: For although they not seldom offend God by most grievous falls, grieve the Holy Spirit, cast out and lose many of his gifts, pollute their conscience, weaken their faith, and in some measure break it, as the examples of David and Peter show, yet they never fall headlong against God with their whole heart so as to become enemies of God, utterly lose the grace of God, wholly cast out the Holy Spirit, or altogether lose faith, since the seed of God remains in them, even though the effective power and sense of God's gifts does not for a time show itself, but lies hidden under the weakness of the flesh, like fire under ashes or the sun behind thick clouds, until God again stirs them up. This he surely does through true repentance, which stirs them up again. Therefore they never wholly fall from the grace of God before the end of life, lest they perish. Rather, God is so angry at their sins that nevertheless, as sons, he does not pursue them with hatred; he chastises them so that he nevertheless does not utterly cast them off from himself. Just as a father does not at once drive a sinning son completely out of the house, much less strip him of the paternal hand [χειρί], although he rebukes and chastises him severely.

units.la: TESTIMONIA SCRIPTVRÆ.
units.tr: TESTIMONIES OF SCRIPTURE.

units.la: Johan.3.verf.9. Quisquis natus est ex Deo, peccato non dat operam: quoniam semen ipsius in eo manet: nec potest peccare, eo quod ex Deo natus est.
units.tr: John 3:9. Whoever is born of God does not practise sin, for his seed remains in him; nor can he sin, because he is born of God.

units.la: Psalm.37,24. Cum ceciderit, non prosternetur: quia Iehoua sustentat manum eius.
units.tr: Ps. 37:24. Though he fall, he shall not be cast down, for the LORD upholds his hand.

units.la: 2 Sam.7. verf.14.15. Ego ero illi in Patrem, & ipse erit mihi in filium: qui cum iniquè egerit, arguam eum virga hominum, & plagis filiorum hominum: Misericordia autem mea non recedet ab eo.
units.tr: 2 Sam. 7:14-15. I will be his Father, and he shall be my son. If he commits iniquity, I will chasten him with the rod of men and with the stripes of the children of men; but my mercy shall not depart from him.

units.la: VII.
units.tr: VII.

units.la: Hac consolatione se erigebat Dauid in lapsibus suis.
units.tr: With this consolation David raised himself up in his falls.

units.la: Psal.37,24. Iustus si ceciderit, non collidetur: quia Dominus supponit manus.
units.tr: Ps. 37:24. If the righteous fall, he shall not be cast down, for the Lord upholds him with his hand.

units.la: Psal.51,13. Ne proiicias me à facie tua: & Spiritum sanctum tuum ne auferas à me.
units.tr: Ps. 51:13. Cast me not away from your presence, and take not your Holy Spirit from me.

units.la: VIII.
units.tr: VIII.

units.la: Hoc ergo consolationis caput habent sancti in luctA conscientiæ, quod sciunt se credere, & per gratiam Dei porro credituros, & fidem suam nunquam penitus posse deficere, vt pereant: idque quia Euangelij voce docentur, eam immutabili electione Dei a, & efficacissimo merito atque intercessione Christi b sustentari, & virtute Dei custodiri c.
units.tr: Therefore the saints have this chief point of consolation in the anguish of conscience: they know that they believe, and that by the grace of God they will go on believing, and that their faith can never fail utterly so that they perish. This is because they are taught by the voice of the Gospel that it is sustained by the unchangeable election of God a, by the most effective merit and intercession of Christ b, and kept by the power of God c.

units.la: TESTIMONIA SCRIPTVRAE.
units.tr: TESTIMONIES OF SCRIPTURE.

units.la: a] Ephes.1. verf.4. Elegit nos in Christo ante jacta mundi fundamenta.
units.tr: a] Eph. 1, v. 4. He chose us in Christ before the foundation of the world.

units.la: Rom.8,39. Quos prædestinauit, eos etiam vocauit: & quos vocauit, eos etiam justificauit: quos autem justificauit, eos etiam glorificauit.
units.tr: Rom. 8:39. Whom he predestined, them he also called; and whom he called, them he also justified; and whom he justified, them he also glorified.

units.la: 2 Tim.2,19. Solidum fundamentum Dei stat, habens sigillum hoc: Nouit Dominus eos, qui sunt sui.
units.tr: 2 Tim. 2:19. Nevertheless the foundation of God standeth sure, having this seal: The Lord knoweth them that are his.

units.la: b] Rom.8,33. Quis intentabit crimen aduersus electos Dei? Deus est, qui justificat. Quis est qui condemnet? Christus est, qui mortuus est: imò verò, qui etiam excitatus est: qui etiam est ad dextram Dei, qui etiam interpellat pro nobis.
units.tr: b] Rom. 8:33. Who shall lay any thing to the charge of God's elect? It is God that justifieth. Who is he that condemneth? It is Christ that died, yea rather, that is risen again, who is even at the right hand of God, who also maketh intercession for us.

units.la: Joh.17,15. Rogo, vt serues eos à malo illo.
units.tr: John 17:15. I pray that thou shouldest keep them from the evil.

units.la: Lucæ 22. verf.31. Simon, Simon, Satanas appetiit vos, quos ventilaret, sicut triticum: sed ego rogaui pro te, ne deficiat fides tua.
units.tr: Luke 22:31-32. Simon, Simon, behold, Satan hath desired to have you, that he may sift you as wheat: but I have prayed for thee, that thy faith fail not.

units.la: c] 1 Petri 1,5. Qui virtutis DEI præsidio custodimini per fidem ad salutem.
units.tr: c] 1 Pet. 1:5. Who are kept by the power of God through faith unto salvation.

units.la: IX.
units.tr: IX.

units.la: Quibus accedunt & alia συνηγορίας huius expressa scripturæ sacræ firmamenta: quod impossibile est seducî electos a: Dei in Christo c: quod vocatio & dona Dei sunt ἀμεταμέλητα d: quod hæreditas ἄφθαρτος, ἀμίαντος, ἀμάραντος nobis in cœlo seruatur: quod virtute Dei per fidem custodimur ad salutem f: quod fidelis est Deus, qui non sinit nos tentari supra vires, sed præstat cum tentatione euasionem, vt possimus sufferre g.
units.tr: To these are added other express testimonies of Holy Scripture which support this: that it is impossible for the elect to be led astray by Christ's God [it is impossible for the elect to be deceived]; that the calling and gifts of God are irrevocable [ἀμεταμέλητα]; that the inheritance, incorruptible, undefiled and unfading [ἄφθαρτος, ἀμίαντος, ἀμάραντος], is kept for us in heaven; that we are kept by the power of God through faith unto salvation; and that God is faithful, who does not suffer us to be tempted beyond our strength, but with the temptation also provides a way of escape, so that we may be able to bear it.

units.la: TESTIMONIA SCRIPTVRAE.
units.tr: TESTIMONIES OF SCRIPTURE.

units.la: Matth.24,24. Impossibile est seduci electos.
units.tr: Matt. 24:24. It is impossible for the elect to be deceived.

units.la: Joh.10,28. Oues mea non peribunt in æternum: neque rapiet eas quisquam è manu mea.
units.tr: John 10:28. My sheep shall never perish; neither shall any man pluck them out of my hand.

units.la: Rom.8,39. Nulla creatura poterit nos separare à charitate Dei, quæ est in Christo Iesu Domino nostro.
units.tr: Rom. 8:39. No creature shall be able to separate us from the love of God, which is in Christ Jesus our Lord.

units.la: Rom.11,29. Dona illa, & vocatio Dei eiusmodi sunt, vt eorum ipsum pœnitere non posset.
units.tr: Rom. 11:29. The gifts and calling of God are such that he will never repent of them.

units.la: 1 Petri 1. verf.4.5. Christus nos regenuit ad hæreditatem, quæ nec perire potest, nec contaminari, nec marcescere, nobis in cœlis seruatam.
units.tr: 1 Pet. 1:4-5. Christ hath begotten us again to an inheritance which cannot perish, nor be defiled, nor fade away, reserved in heaven for us.

units.la: Ibid. Qui virtutis Dei præsidio custodimini per fidem ad salutem paratam patefieri tempore vltimo.
units.tr: Ibid. Who are kept by the power of God through faith unto salvation, ready to be revealed in the last time.

units.la: 1 Cor.10,13. Fidelis est Deus, qui non sinet vos tentari supra id, quod potestis, sed vna cum tentatione præstabit etiam exitum, vt possitis eam sufferre.
units.tr: 1 Cor. 10:13. God is faithful, who will not suffer you to be tempted above what you are able, but with the temptation will also make a way of escape, that you may be able to bear it.

units.la: X.
units.tr: X.

units.la: Qui verò de perseuerantia dubitant, vitam æternam non credunt: immò fidem & spem omnem eludunt: cum illa sit fiducia certa misericordiæ Dei præsentis & futuræ: hæc, exspectatio certa vitæ æternæ, non confundens. Rom.5,5. Spes non pudefacit: eo quod charitas Dei effusa est in cordibus nostris per Spiritum sanctum, qui datus est nobis. Fides verò est ὑπόστασις ἐλπιζομένων. Hebr.11,1. Dubitatio verò confundit. Jac.1,6.
units.tr: Those who doubt concerning perseverance do not believe in eternal life; indeed, they nullify all faith and hope, since hope is a sure confidence in the present and future mercy of God, and, not disappointing, a sure expectation of eternal life. Rom. 5:5. Hope does not make ashamed, because the love of God is shed abroad in our hearts by the Holy Spirit, who is given unto us. Faith, however, is the substance of things hoped for [ὑπόστασις ἐλπιζομένων]. Heb. 11:1. But doubt confounds. Jas. 1:6.

units.la: XI.
units.tr: XI.

units.la: Necesse hæc doctrina securitatis, nisi spiritualis . Nam cum certitudine perseuerantiæ in sanctis semper maneat propositum vitandi lapsus, vel ex lapsibus resipiscendi , Deo hæc omnia secundum æternam προθεσιν suam immutabiliter in eis operante, nec misericordiam suam ab eis penitus abstrahente, ne pereant .
units.tr: This doctrine of security is necessary, unless it is spiritual. For since the certainty of perseverance always remains in the saints, the purpose of avoiding falls, or of returning to repentance after falls, remains with them, God working all these things in them immutably according to his eternal purpose [πρόθεσιν], and not withdrawing his mercy from them entirely, lest they perish.

units.la: TESTIMONIA SCRIPTVRAE.
units.tr: TESTIMONIES OF SCRIPTURE.

units.la: Rom.8,38. Nam mihi persuasum est, neque mortem, neque vitam, neque angelos, neque principatus, neque potestates, neque præsentia, neque futura, neque vllam aliam creaturam posse nos separare à charitate Dei, quæ est in Christo Iesu Domino nostro.
units.tr: Rom. 8:38-39. For I am persuaded, that neither death, nor life, nor angels, nor principalities, nor powers, nor things present, nor things to come, nor any other creature, shall be able to separate us from the love of God, which is in Christ Jesus our Lord.

units.la: 1 Johan.5. verf.10. Qui credit in Filium Dei, habet testimonium in seipso.
units.tr: 1 John 5:10. He that believeth on the Son of God hath the witness in himself.

units.la: Noui, cui crediderim, & mihi persuasum est, eum posse depositum meum in illum diem seruare.
units.tr: I know whom I have believed, and I am persuaded that he is able to keep what I have committed to him until that day.

units.la: Quod perpetro, non agnosco. Non enim quod volo, hoc ago, sed quod odi, hoc facio. Quod si id facio, quod nolo, consentio legi, quod bona sit.
units.tr: What I do, I do not understand. For I do not do what I want, but what I hate, I do. But if I do what I do not want, I agree with the law that it is good.

units.la: In ipso in sortem adsciti sumus, cum essemus praedestinati secundum propositum eius, qui omnia efficit ex consilio voluntatis suae.
units.tr: In him we also have obtained an inheritance, being predestinated according to the purpose of him who worketh all things after the counsel of his own will.

units.la: In saeculum custodiam ei misericordiam meam, & pactum meum firmum erit ipsi.
units.tr: My mercy will I keep for him for evermore, and my covenant shall stand fast with him.

units.la: XII.
units.tr: XII.

units.la: Contrarias huic dulcissimae doctrinae opiniones Puccij, Huberi & similium in schola Pelagij natas repudiamus.
units.tr: We reject the opinions contrary to this most sweet doctrine, opinions of Puccius, Huber and their like, born in the school of Pelagius.

units.la: 1. Quod fides nunc in statu gratiae sit naturalis: sit donum Dei commune omnibus, sicut Sol bonis & malis Dei beneficio lucet.
units.tr: 1. That faith is now, in the state of grace, natural; that it is a gift of God common to all, just as the sun shines on the good and the bad by God's benefit.

units.la: 2. Quod fides sit a Deo, quoad incrementa, non quoad initium.
units.tr: 2. That faith is from God as to its increase, but not as to its beginning.

units.la: 3. Quod sit opus nostrum, ut credamus, hoc est, ut sinamus, eum nobis auxilium praestare.
units.tr: 3. That it is our work to believe, that is, to allow God to render us help.

units.la: 4. Quod de perseuerantia in finem sit dubitandum.
units.tr: 4. That one must doubt about perseverance to the end.

units.la: 5. Quod vana sit illa, quam ex apostolo Rom.11,29. jactamus, certitudo donorum Dei. Sic Hub. Thes.777.
units.tr: 5. That that certainty of God's gifts, which we boast of from the apostle, Rom. 11:29, is vain. Thus Huber, Thes. 777.

units.la: 6. Quod sancti, quoties mortaliter, ut loquuntur, peccant, penitus excidant gratia, penitus excutiant Spiritum sanctum, penitus deficiant a fide: atque ita multi electi damnentur & pereant.
units.tr: 6. That the saints, whenever they sin mortally, as they say, utterly fall away from grace, utterly cast out the Holy Spirit, utterly fail in faith; and so many of the elect are condemned and perish.

units.la: ARTICVLVS VII.
units.tr: ARTICLE VII.

units.la: DE MINISTERIO ECCLESIASTICO.
units.tr: ON THE ECCLESIASTICAL MINISTRY.

units.la: I.
units.tr: I.

units.la: De ministerio Ecclesiastico in novo Testamento credimus & docemus, quod sit officium publice docendi & gubernandi Ecclesiam voce Prophetarum & Apostolorum, ad perficiendam salutem electorum a Christo institutum .
units.tr: We believe and teach that the ecclesiastical ministry in the New Testament is the office of publicly teaching and governing the Church by the voice of the Prophets and Apostles, instituted by Christ to bring the salvation of the elect to completion.

units.la: TESEIMONIA SCRIPTVRAE.
units.tr: TESTIMONIES OF SCRIPTURE.

units.la: Ite, & docete omnes gentes, baptizantes eos in nomine Patris, Filij & Spiritus sancti. Marci 16, 16. Prædicate Euangelium omni creaturæ. Qui crediderit, & baptizatus fuerit, saluus erit. Qui verò non crediderit, damnabitur.
units.tr: "Go and teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit." Marci 16, 16. "Preach the gospel to every creature. He who believes and is baptized will be saved, but he who does not believe will be condemned."

units.la: Ephes. 2, 20. Superstructi estis super fundamentum Prophetarum & Apostolorum.
units.tr: Ephes. 2, 20. "You are built upon the foundation of the Prophets and Apostles."

units.la: Eph. 4, 11. Dedit alios quidem Apostolos: alios verò Prophetas: alios Euangelistas: alios autem pastores & doctores.
units.tr: Eph. 4, 11. "He gave some to be apostles, some prophets, some evangelists, and some ministers and teachers."

units.la: II.
units.tr: II.

units.la: IV. Quodque sit efficax Spiritus sancti organum, quo fidem & conuersionem in cordibus electorum accendit, operatur, & confirmat b.
units.tr: IV. And that it is the effective instrument of the Holy Spirit, by which He kindles faith and conversion in the hearts of the elect, works them, and confirms them.

units.la: TESTIMONIA SCRIPTVRÆ.
units.tr: TESTIMONIES OF SCRIPTURE.

units.la: b] Rom. 1. versi. 16. Euangelium est potentia Dei cuiuis credenti ad salutem.
units.tr: b] Rom. 1. vers. 16. The gospel is the power of God unto salvation to everyone who believes.

units.la: Rom. 1. versi. 17. Fides est ex auditu. Auditus autem per Verbum DEI.
units.tr: Rom. 1. vers. 17. Faith is by hearing, and hearing by the Word of God.

units.la: Act. 10, 44. Adhuc loquente Petro verba ista, illapsus est Spiritus sanctus in omnes, qui audiebant hunc sermonem.
units.tr: Acts 10:44. While Peter was still speaking these words, the Holy Spirit fell upon all who heard the discourse.

units.la: Actor. 16. versi. 14. Quædam mulier, nomine Lydia, quæ purpuram vendebat in urbe Thyatirorum, Deum colens, nos audiuit: cuius Dominus adaperuit cor, vt attenderet ea, quæ dicebantur à Paulo.
units.tr: Acts 16:14. A certain woman named Lydia, a seller of purple in the city of Thyatira, a worshipper of God, heard us; the Lord opened her heart to attend to the things that were spoken by Paul.

units.la: 2 Tim. 3, 16. 17. Tota scriptura diuinitus est inspirata, & vtilis ad doctrinam, ad redargutionē, ad correctionem, ad institutionem, quæ est in justitia: vt perfectus sit homo Dei, ad omne opus bonum perfecte instructus.
units.tr: 2 Tim. 3:16, 17. All Scripture is given by inspiration of God, and is profitable for doctrine, for reproof, for correction, for instruction in righteousness, that the man of God may be perfect, thoroughly furnished unto every good work.

units.la: III.
units.tr: III.

units.la: Vis tamen & efficacia interna, qua sanctificamur, non est ministrorum, nec verbis aut actionibus eorum inclusa vel alligata, sed est spiritus Dei a. Hominum vero est ministerium externum b, quo spiritus Dei ad mouendos animos & corda electorum vtitur, quando & quomodo ipsi visum est c: non quia non posset aliter, sed quia diuinæ sapientiæ placuit, per stultam prædicationem crucis saluos facere credentes d.
units.tr: The inward power and efficacy by which we are sanctified is not in the ministers, nor enclosed or bound up in their words or actions, but is the Spirit of God a. The outward ministry, however, belongs to men b, and by it the Spirit of God uses to move the minds and hearts of the elect, when and how it has seemed good to him c: not because he could not do otherwise, but because it pleased divine wisdom to save believers through the foolish preaching of the cross d.

units.la: TESTIMONIA SCRIPTVRAE.
units.tr: TESTIMONIES OF SCRIPTURE.

units.la: d] Esa. 43, 25. Ego, ego sum, qui deleo præuaricationes tuas. Johan. 3, 8. Ventus quò vult, spirat, & sonum eius audis, sed nescis, unde veniat, aut quò vadat: ita est, quisquis genitus est ex Spiritu sancto.
units.tr: d] Isa. 43:25. I, even I, am he who blots out your transgressions. John 3:8. The wind blows where it wills, and you hear its sound, but you do not know where it comes from or where it goes: so is everyone who is born of the Spirit.

units.la: 1 Cor. 12, 11. Omnia haec efficit unus ille & idem Spiritus, distribuens privatim illa singulis, sicut vult.
units.tr: 1 Cor. 12:11. All these things one and the same Spirit works, distributing to each one individually as he wills.

units.la: Matth. 3, 11. Ego quidem baptizo vos aqua, ad resipiscentiam: is verò, qui post me venit, validior me est: ipse vos baptizabit Spiritu sancto & igne.
units.tr: Matt. 3:11. I indeed baptize you with water unto repentance, but he who comes after me is mightier than I; he will baptize you with the Holy Spirit and with fire.

units.la: Johann. 1. vers. 23. 33. Ego sum vox clamantis in deserto: sed qui misit me, ut baptizarem aqua, hic est, qui baptizat Spiritu sancto.
units.tr: John 1:23, 33. I am the voice of one crying in the wilderness. But he who sent me to baptize with water, he is the one who baptizes with the Holy Spirit.

units.la: 1 Cor. 3, 5. 6. Quis igitur Paulus? quis Apollos, nisi ministri, per quos credidistis, & ut cuique Dominus dedit? Ego plantavi, Apollos rigavit: sed Deus dedit incrementum. Itaque neque qui planat, est aliquid, neque qui rigat: sed Deus, qui dat incrementum.
units.tr: 1 Cor. 3:5, 6. Who then is Paul, and who is Apollos, but ministers through whom you believed, and as the Lord gave to each? I planted, Apollos watered, but God gave the increase. So neither he who plants is anything, nor he who waters, but God, who gives the increase.

units.la: Joh. 3. vers. 8. Ventus quo vult spirat, & sonum eius audis, sed nescis, unde veniat, & quo vadat: ita est, quisquis genitus est ex Spiritu.
units.tr: John 3:8. The wind blows where it wills, and you hear its sound, but you do not know where it comes from or where it goes: so is everyone who is born of the Spirit.

units.la: 1 Cor. 12, 11. Sed omnia haec efficit unus ille, & idem Spiritus, distribuens privatim illa singulis, sicut vult.
units.tr: 1 Cor. 12:11. But all these things one and the same Spirit works, distributing to each one individually as he wills.

units.la: 1 Cor. 1, 21. Postquam in Dei sapientia mundus non cognovit Deum per istam sapientiam, placuit Deo per stultum praeconium servare credentes.
units.tr: 1 Cor. 1:21. Since in the wisdom of God the world through its wisdom did not know God, it pleased God through the foolishness of preaching to save those who believe.

units.la: IV.
units.tr: IV.

units.la: Haec vero partim impia sunt, partim nimis ψυχολογικά:
