units.tr: Some of these are impious, and others are far too psychological [ψυχολογικά]:

units.la: 1. Deum immediatè infundere fidem & conversionem.
units.tr: 1. That God immediately infuses faith and conversion.

units.la: 2. Ministerium esse literam mortuam: Exercitium solummodo externi hominis.
units.tr: 2. That the ministry is a dead letter, merely the exercise of the external man.

units.la: 3. Ex auditu verbi esse fidem non justificantem, sed historicam tantum.
units.tr: 3. That faith arising from the hearing of the Word is not justifying but only historical.

units.la: 4. Vim salutificam esse in voce & sub voce ministri; & Christum quidem internas: ministrum vero externas simul & internas partes habere.
units.tr: 4. That the saving power lies in the voice and under the voice of the minister; and that Christ indeed has only internal parts, but the minister has both external and internal parts.

units.la: ARTICVLVS VIII, DE SACRAMENTIS IN GENERE.
units.tr: ARTICLE VIII, CONCERNING THE SACRAMENTS IN GENERAL.

units.la: I.
units.tr: I.

units.la: Doctrinam generalem Sacramentorum, & utilem & summè quoque necessariam esse judicamus. Namabsq; ea vix intelligi potest, cur Baptismus & sacra Cœna Domini sint Sacramenta. Magnam verò vniuique Sacramento in specie accendit lucem, ad cauendos varios errores: ne vel in defectu pro frigidis habeantur cæremoniis: vel in excessu in idola transformentur. Quod necessario fit, nisi attendatur, quid sint Sacramenta: & cur à Deo instituta: quis eorum vsus & finis. Testantur enim historiae ecclesiasticae, Pontificem Romanum Missae Transsubstantiatione non ante potuisse stabilire, quam doctrinam de natura, efficacia, & vsu sacramentorum euertisset.
units.tr: We judge that the general doctrine of the Sacraments is both useful and most necessary. For without it one can hardly understand why Baptism and the Lord's Supper are sacraments. Yet a clear understanding of each sacrament in particular also sheds great light, so that we may guard against various errors: lest they be regarded as cold ceremonies through deficiency, or be turned into idols through excess. This necessarily happens unless attention is paid to what the sacraments are, why they were instituted by God, and what their use and purpose is. For the histories of the Church testify that the Roman Pontiff could not establish the transubstantiation of the Mass until he had overthrown the doctrine concerning the nature, efficacy and use of the sacraments.

units.la: II.
units.tr: II.

units.la: Sacramenta sunt signa foederis seu promissionis gratiae a à Deo ad fidem nostram confirmandam instituta .
units.tr: Sacraments are signs of the covenant, or of the promise of grace, instituted by God to confirm our faith.

units.la: TESTIMONIA SCRIPTVRÆ.
units.tr: TESTIMONIES OF SCRIPTURE.

units.la: Gen. 17, 11. Circumcidetis carnem praeputij vestri: erit q; signum pacti inter me & vos.
units.tr: Gen. 17, 11. You shall circumcise the flesh of your foreskin, and it shall be a sign of the covenant between me and you.

units.la: Rom. 4, 11. Et accepit signum circumcisionis sigillum justitiae fidei receptae in praeputio.
units.tr: Rom. 4, 11. And he received the sign of circumcision, a seal of the righteousness of faith which he had while in uncircumcision.

units.la: Apologia Confessionis Augustanae Tit. de Vsu Sacramentorum : Sacramenta non sunt tantum notae professionis inter homines, vt quidam fingunt, sed magis sunt signa & testimonia voluntatis DEI erga nos, per quae mouet DEVS corda ad credendum.
units.tr: Apology of the Augsburg Confession, title on the Use of the Sacraments: Sacraments are not merely marks of profession among men, as some feign, but rather are signs and testimonies of the will of God toward us, through which God moves hearts to believe.

units.la: III.
units.tr: III.

units.la: Constant Sacramenta Elemento & Verbo , seu externis signis, & promissione spiritualis gratiae: quae gratia in verbo & sacramentis omnibus vna est, nempe Christus, cum omnibus suis beneficiis . Vnus enim est Christus heri, hodie, & in saecula : & vna est communio sanctorum ab initio mundi, vsq; ad finem : quae est spiritualis vnio sanctorum cum Christo, & inter se, ad eandem charitatem, per Spiritum sanctum, in Christo, tanquam capite, & in nobis tanquam membris suis habitans : licet vna haec communio aliter in aliis sacramentis pro diuersitate signorum repraesentetur, & appelletur.
units.tr: Sacraments consist of an element and a word, that is, of external signs, and of the promise of spiritual grace; and this grace is one and the same in the Word and in all the sacraments, namely Christ, with all his benefits. For Christ is one, yesterday, today and forever; and there is one communion of the saints from the beginning of the world to its end, which is the spiritual union of the saints with Christ and with one another, in the same love, through the Holy Spirit dwelling in Christ as the head and in us as his members; although this one communion is represented and named differently in the different sacraments, according to the diversity of the signs.

units.la: TESTIMONIA SCRIPTVRAE, ET ALIORVM.
units.tr: TESTIMONIES OF SCRIPTURE AND OTHERS.

units.la: Apolog. Augustanae Conf. Tit. de vsu sacramenti & sacrificio: Sacramenta sunt signa voluntatis Dei erga nos, non tantum signa sunt hominum inter se. Et recte definiunt sacramentain nouo testamento esse signa gratiae. Et quia in sacramento duo sunt, signum & verbum, verbum in nouo Testamento est promissio remissionis peccatorum.
units.tr: Apology of the Augsburg Confession, title on the use of the sacrament and the sacrifice: Sacraments are signs of God's will toward us; they are not merely signs of human beings among themselves. And they rightly define sacraments in the New Testament as signs of grace. And since a sacrament has two parts, sign and word, the word in the New Testament is the promise of the forgiveness of sins.

units.la: Ibidem : Idem effectus est verbi & ritus, sicut praeclare dictum est ab Augustino: Sacramentum est verbum visibile: quia ritus oculis accipitur, & est quasi pictura verbi, idem significans, quod verbum. Quare idem est vtrinsque effectus.
units.tr: Ibidem: The effect of the word and of the rite is the same, as Augustine has aptly said: a sacrament is a visible word, because the rite is taken in by the eyes and is, as it were, a picture of the word, signifying the same thing as the word. Therefore the effect of both is the same.

units.la: Heb.13, 8. Iesus Christus heri & hodie idem est, & in secula. 1 Cor. 8, 6. Nobis vnus est Deus Pater ille, à quo omnia, & nos in ipso, & vnus Dominus Iesus Christus, per quem omnia, & nos per ipsum.
units.tr: Heb. 13, 8. Jesus Christ is the same yesterday and today, and forever. 1 Cor. 8, 6. For us there is one God the Father, from whom are all things, and we in him; and one Lord Jesus Christ, through whom are all things, and we through him.

units.la: 1 Corinth. 10. verf. 4. Omnes eandem escam spiritualem ederunt: & omnes eundem potum spiritualem biberunt. Bibebant enim ex sequente spirituali petra. Petra enim illa erat Christus. 1 Cor. 12, 13. Per vnum spiritum nos omnes in vnum corpus baptizati sumus: & Iudai, & Graci: & omnes potati sumus in vnum spiritum. Ephes. 4, 45. Elegit nos in ipso ante jacta mundi fundamenta: & praedestinauit nos, quos adoptaret in filios per Iesum Christum in sese.
units.tr: 1 Corinthians 10, verse 4. They all ate the same spiritual food, and they all drank the same spiritual drink; for they drank from the spiritual rock that followed them, and that rock was Christ. 1 Cor. 12, 13. By one Spirit we were all baptized into one body, whether Jews or Greeks, and we were all made to drink into one Spirit. Ephes. 4, 45. He chose us in him before the foundation of the world, and predestined us, whom he would adopt as sons through Jesus Christ to himself.

units.la: IV.
units.tr: IV.

units.la: Gratia haec spiritualis seu res significata cum signis percipitur in vero vsu sacramenti, qui est, cum vera fide & conuersione ad Deum percipitur sacramentum a. Sic enim Deus instituit sacramenta, vt symbola ad finem ordinata sumantur è manu ministri: promissio symbolis annexa, ipsaque gratia spiritualis promissa fide accipiatur à Deo b. Sicut & ipsa promissio non nisi fide percipi potest. Vnde iis, qui sine fide & conuersione sunt, sacramenta nihil prosunt.
units.tr: This spiritual grace, or the thing signified, is received together with the signs in the true use of the sacrament, which consists in receiving the sacrament with true faith and conversion to God a. For God instituted the sacraments so that the symbols, ordained for this end, are taken from the hand of the minister; the promise is annexed to the symbols, and the spiritual grace itself, promised, is received from God by faith b. Just as the promise itself can be grasped only by faith. Hence the sacraments profit nothing to those who are without faith and conversion.

units.la: TESTIMONIA SCRIPTVRÆ, ET ALIORVM.
units.tr: TESTIMONIES OF SCRIPTURE, AND OF OTHERS.

units.la: Joh.1, 26. 33. Ego baptizo aqua: sed in medio vestrum stat, quem vos non nostis. Hic est, qui baptizat Spiritu sancto. 1 Corinth. 3, 6. Ego plantaui, Apollo rigauit: sed Deus dedit benedictionem. Rom. 2, 25. Quod si transgressor legis fueris, circumcisio tua facta est praeputium. 1 Cor. 11, 20. Cum igitur conuenitis eodem loci, hoc non est Dominicam coenam edere. Apologia Augustanae Confess. Tit. de Vsu Sacrament. Ergo sicut promissio inutilis est, nisi fide accipiatur, ita inutilis est caremonia, nisi fides accedat, quae vere statuat hic offerri remissionem peccatorum.
units.tr: John 1:26, 33. "I baptize with water, but among you stands one whom you do not know. This is he who baptizes with the Holy Spirit." 1 Corinthians 3:6. "I planted, Apollos watered, but God gave the increase." Romans 2:25. "If you are a transgressor of the law, your circumcision has become uncircumcision." 1 Corinthians 11:20. "When therefore you come together in the same place, it is not to eat the Lord's Supper." Apology of the Augsburg Confession, title "On the Use of the Sacraments." Therefore, just as the promise is useless unless it is received by faith, so the ceremony is useless unless faith comes to it, which truly holds that the forgiveness of sins is offered here.

units.la: V.
units.tr: V.

units.la: Hic autem verus est vsus sacramentorum: quando signa sacramentalia vera fide & resipiscentia a percipiuntur: & ad eum diriguntur, ad quem à Deo sunt ordinata.
units.tr: This, however, is the true use of the sacraments: when the sacramental signs are received with true faith and repentance a, and are directed to that end for which they have been ordained by God.

units.la: TESTIMONIA SCRIPTVRÆ, ET ALIORVM.
units.tr: TESTIMONIES OF SCRIPTURE, AND OF OTHERS.

units.la: Marci 16,16. Qui crediderit & baptizatus fuerit, saluus erit. Rom.2,25. Circumcisio quidem prodest, si legem exequaris. Apologia Augustanæ Confess. de Sacramentis & eorum vsu: Itaque nos docemus, quod in vsu sacramentorum fides debeat accedere, quæ credat illis promissionibus, & accipiat res promissas, quæ ibi in sacramento offeruntur: Et est ratio plana & firmissima. Promissio est inutilis, nisi fide accipiatur.
units.tr: Mark 16:16. He who believes and is baptized will be saved. Rom. 2:25. Circumcision indeed profits, if you keep the law. Apology of the Augsburg Confession, on the sacraments and their use: Therefore we teach that in the use of the sacraments faith ought to be present, which believes those promises and receives the things promised, which are offered there in the sacrament. And the reasoning is plain and most firm: a promise is useless unless it is received by faith.

units.la: Item de vsu sacramenti, & sacrificio: Et talis vsus sacramenti, cum fides viuificat perterrefacta corda, cultus est novi Testamenti.
units.tr: Likewise, on the use of the sacrament and on sacrifice: And such use of the sacrament, when faith, terrified hearts having been revived, is the worship of the New Testament.

units.la: Idem: Illa autem fides, quæ agnoscit misericordiam. Et hic principalis est vsus sacramenti.
units.tr: The same: But that faith which acknowledges mercy. And this is the principal use of the sacrament.

units.la: VI.
units.tr: VI.

units.la: Propter sacramentalem significationem, obsignationem & exhibitionem rerum per signa fit, vt signa plerunq; rerum ipsarum nomina accipiant, quæ phrasis sacramentalis dicitur.
units.tr: Because of the sacramental signification, sealing and exhibition of things through signs, it comes about that the signs usually take the names of the things themselves; this is called the sacramental phrase.

units.la: TESTIMONIA SCRIPTVRAE, ET ALIORVM.
units.tr: Testimonies of Scripture and of others.

units.la: Genes.17,10. Hoc est pactum meum. Et verf.11. Eritque signum pacti inter me & vos. Exod.12,11. Est Pascha Domini. 1 Cor.11,24.25 Hoc est corpus meum. Ibid. Hic calix est nouum Testamentum in meo sanguine. Augstin. ad Bonifac.epist.23. Si sacramenta quandam similitudinem earum rerum, quarum sacramenta sunt, non haberent, omnino sacramenta non essent. Ex hac autem similitudine plerunq;, etiam ipsarum rerum nomina accipiunt.
units.tr: Genes.17,10. This is my covenant. And v.11: And it shall be a sign of the covenant between me and you. Exod.12,11. It is the Passover of the Lord. 1 Cor.11,24.25 This is my body. Ibid. This cup is the new covenant in my blood. Augustine, to Boniface, Epistle 23: If sacraments did not have a certain likeness to the things of which they are sacraments, they would not be sacraments at all. From this likeness they usually take the names of the things themselves as well.

units.la: Idem Tomo IV. in Leuit. Quæst. LVII. Solet autem res, quae significat, eius rei nomine, quam significat, nuncupari, sicut scriptum est: Septem spicae sunt septem anni.
units.tr: The same, Vol. IV, on Leviticus, Question 57: The thing that signifies is usually named by the name of the thing it signifies, as it is written: The seven ears are seven years.

units.la: VII.
units.tr: VII.

units.la: Reijcimus vero errores hos vere-Sacramentarios, partim Papistarum, partim Vbiquitariorum.
units.tr: We reject these errors of the truly sacramentarian kind, partly of the Papists and partly of the Ubiquitarians:

units.la: 1. Quod doctrina generali sacramentorum non sit opus.
units.tr: 1. That there is no need for a general doctrine of the sacraments.

units.la: 2. Quod sacramenta non plenè, sed tantum aliquatenus à causa efficiente & finali, seu effectibus possint definiri. vt docet Apologia Erfurtensis.
units.tr: 2. That sacraments cannot be fully defined, but only in some measure, from their efficient and final cause, or their effects, as the Erfurt Apology teaches.

units.la: 3. Quod non sint sigilla promissionis gratiae: nec confirment fidem: vt contendunt Jesuitae & Anabaptistae.
units.tr: 3. That they are not seals of the promise of grace, nor do they confirm faith, as the Jesuits and the Anabaptists contend.

units.la: 4. Quod gratiam justificantem in se tamquam vrcei aut vasa contineant. Quod sint instrumenta justificationis conse- rentia eam.
units.tr: 4. That they contain justifying grace in themselves as in pitchers or vessels, and that they are instruments of justification conferring it.

units.la: 5. Quod vi sua conferant gratiam justificantem omnibus sumentibus, ex opere operato, vt loquuntur.
units.tr: 5. That by their own power they confer justifying grace on all who receive them, ex opere operato, as they say.

units.la: 6. Quod non sit eadem gratia spiritualis & communio Christi in verbo & in sacramentis omnibus.
units.tr: 6. That the spiritual grace and communion of Christ are not the same in the Word and in all the sacraments.

units.la: 7. Quod vetera sacramenta fuerint nuda signa sine exhibitione rerum in vero vsu.
units.tr: 7. That the older sacraments were bare signs, without the exhibition of the things in actual use.

units.la: 8. Quod res spirituales significatæ non minus quàm symbola manibus ministrorum gestentur ac dispensentur.
units.tr: 8. That the spiritual things signified are not only carried and dispensed by the hands of ministers in the same way as the symbols.

units.la: 9. Quod res spirituales etiam sine fide ab impiis percipiantur.
units.tr: 9. That the spiritual things are received even by the impious, without faith.

units.la: 10. Quod nullæ sint phrases sacramentales & figuratæ, sed omnes sint propriæ in sacramentis.
units.tr: 10. That there are no sacramental and figurative phrases, but all are proper to the sacraments.

units.la: 11. Quod sint septem vel plura sacramenta, quàm duo à Christo instituta, Baptismus & Cœna Domini.
units.tr: 11. That there are seven or more sacraments, rather than the two instituted by Christ, Baptism and the Lord's Supper.

units.la: ARTICVLVS IX. DE BAPTISMO.
units.tr: ARTICLE IX. OF BAPTISM.

units.la: I.
units.tr: I.

units.la: Credimus, Baptismum esse lauacrum aquæ in verbo, quo Christus mundat Ecclesiam, regenerans eam ac renouans per Spiritum sanctum a, hoc est, esse sacramentum à Christo institutum, quo aqua baptizatis in nomine Dei Patris, & Filij, & Spiritus sancti, testificatur Deus b, se eos recipere in fœdus gratiæ propter Christum, & sanguine eius à Spiritu sancto mundare à peccatis, ac renouare.
units.tr: We believe that Baptism is a washing of water in the Word, by which Christ cleanses the Church, regenerating and renewing it through the Holy Spirit (a), that is, that it is a sacrament instituted by Christ, in which water applied to those baptized in the name of God the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit, testifies that God receives them into the covenant of grace for Christ's sake, and that by His blood and through the Holy Spirit He cleanses them from sins and renews them (b).

units.la: TESTIMONIA SCRIPTVRÆ.
units.tr: TESTIMONIES OF SCRIPTURE.

units.la: a Ephes. 5, 26. Sicut Christus dilexit Ecclesiam, & semetipsum exposuit pro ea: vt eam sanctificaret, postquam eam purgasset lauacro aquæ per verbum.
units.tr: (a) Eph. 5, 26. Even as Christ loved the Church and gave himself up for it, that he might sanctify it, having cleansed it by the washing of water through the Word.

units.la: Tit. 3, 5. Ex sua misericordia seruauit nos per lauacrum regenerationis, & renouationem Spiritus sancti.
units.tr: Tit. 3, 5. He saved us, not by works of righteousness which we have done, but according to his mercy, through the washing of regeneration and renewing of the Holy Spirit.

units.la: b Matt. 28, 19. Profecti, docete omnes gentes, baptizate eos, in nomen Patris, & Filij, & Spiritus sancti.
units.tr: (b) Matt. 28, 19. Go therefore and teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit.

units.la: Marci 16, 16. Qui crediderit, & baptizatus fuerit, saluabitur.
units.tr: Mark 16, 16. He who believes and is baptized will be saved.

units.la: 1 Cor. 6, 11. Abluti estis, sanctificati estis, justificati estis in nomine Domini Iesu.
units.tr: 1 Cor. 6, 11. You were washed, you were sanctified, you were justified in the name of the Lord Jesus.

units.la: 1 Corinth.12, 13. Per vnum Spiritum in vnum corpus baptizati sumus.
units.tr: 1 Cor. 12, 13. For by one Spirit we were all baptized into one body.

units.la: II.
units.tr: II.

units.la: Dicimus constare elemento & verbo : juxta vulgatum dictum a: Accedit Verbum ad Elementum, & fit Sacramentum, etiam ipsum tanquam visibile verbum : proinde & gemina ablutione b: externa aquæ, de qua sensus testantur : & interna sanguinis ac Spiritus sancti, de qua verbum concionatur. Externa significans fit à ministro, foris corpus tangens. Interna significata fit à Deo, intus animam abluens: Ego enim, inquit Baptista, baptizo aquâ : Christus vos baptizat Spiritu sancto c. Et Ambrosius: Aqua corpus abluitur, Spiritu anima delictA mundantur d.
units.tr: We say that it consists of an element and a word, according to the well-known saying of Augustine: The word comes to the element, and it becomes a sacrament, even as a visible word. Accordingly there is also a twofold washing (b): the external washing of water, of which the senses bear witness, and the internal washing of blood and of the Holy Spirit, which the word proclaims. The external washing, which signifies, is performed by the minister, touching the body from without. The internal washing, which is signified, is performed by God, cleansing the soul within. For I, said the Baptist, baptize with water; Christ baptizes you with the Holy Spirit (c). And Ambrose: The body is washed with water, and sins are cleansed from the soul by the Spirit (d).

units.la: TESTIMONIA SCRIPTVRAE, ET ALIORVM.
units.tr: TESTIMONIES OF SCRIPTURE, AND OF OTHERS.

units.la: a] Augustin. supra Joh. Tract. 80. & de cataclysm. cap. 3.
units.tr: a] Augustine, on John, Tractate 80, and On the Deluge (De cataclysmo), chapter 3.

units.la: b] 1 Petri 3. vers. 21. Baptismus nos quoque servat, non quo carnis sordes abiiciuntur, sed stipulatio bonæ conscientiæ apud Deum.
units.tr: b] 1 Peter 3:21. "Baptism also saves us, not by the putting away of the filth of the flesh, but by the answer of a good conscience toward God."

units.la: c] Joh. 1, 33. Hic est, qui vos baptizat Spiritu sancto. Ephes. 5, 26. Christus sanctificat suam Ecclesiam, postquam eam purgasset lavacro aquæ per verbum.
units.tr: c] John 1:33. "This is he who baptizes with the Holy Spirit." Ephesians 5:26. "Christ sanctifies his Church, having cleansed it by the washing of water through the word."

units.la: d] Ambrosius super Lucam lib. 2. cap. 3.
units.tr: d] Ambrose, on Luke, book 2, chapter 3.

units.la: III.
units.tr: III.

units.la: Nec ideo geminum Baptismi sacramentum facimus, cum ablutionem aquæ & Spiritus, seu externam & internam nominamus : sed unius Baptismi duas partes dicimus, ut quid homo minister, quid Deus conferat, distincte ostendamus : Sicut nec Paulus circumcisionis sacramentum in duo diuulsit, cum carnis & cordis circumcisionem distinxit a. Quam distinctionem qui tollunt, vel nihil, vel certè minus Deo quam ministris in Sacramentis relinquunt : Deo vix internas partes, ministris cum internis etiam externas vendicantes.
units.tr: Nor do we therefore make two sacraments of Baptism when we call the washing of water and of the Spirit, or the external and the internal, by two names. Rather, we say that there are two parts of the one Baptism, so that we may show clearly what the human minister does and what God bestows. In the same way Paul did not split the sacrament of circumcision into two when he distinguished the circumcision of the flesh from that of the heart. Those who do away with this distinction leave either nothing to God, or at least less to God than to the ministers in the sacraments: they assign to God scarcely the inner parts, while claiming for the ministers the outer parts along with the inner.

units.la: TESTIMONIA SCRIPTVRÆ.
units.tr: TESTIMONIES OF SCRIPTURE.

units.la: a] Rom. 2, 28. Non enim qui est in propatulo Iudaeus, Iudaeus est : nec ea, quæ est in propatulo circumcisio, id est, in carne, circumcisio est : sed qui in occulto Iudaeus est, & circumcisio cordis, id est, in Spiritu, non litera. IV. In
units.tr: a] Rom. 2:28-29. For he is not a Jew who is one outwardly, nor is that circumcision which is outward, in the flesh, circumcision; but he is a Jew who is one inwardly, and circumcision is of the heart, in the Spirit, not in the letter. IV. In

units.la: IV.
units.tr: IV.

units.la: 'In vsu baptismi legitimo interna per externam significatur, & verè exhibetur, atque obsignatur, iuxta promissionem; Qui crediderit, & baptizatus fuerit, saluus erit. Infideles verò & hy- pocritæ cũ tinguntur aqua: non baptizantur spiritu: quia Spi- ritus sanctus fugit hominem fictum, & non habitat in corpore subdito operis im-perf. peccatis, & ideo non fit filius Dei, vt certissimè dixit Chrysost.
units.tr: In the lawful use of baptism the inward is signified by the outward, and is truly exhibited and sealed, according to the promise: "Whoever believes and is baptized will be saved." But unbelievers and hypocrites, though they are washed with water, are not baptized with the Spirit, because "the Holy Spirit flees from a feigned man and does not dwell in a body subject to sins," and therefore such a person does not become a son of God, as Chrysostom most certainly said.

units.la: V.
units.tr: V.

units.la: Baptismus igitur abluit peccata, regenerat, saluos facit, &c. non vi latenter annexa vel impressa aquæ, nec ex opere operato: sed phrasi sacramentali, qua propter coniunctionem vtriusque ablutionis in vsu legitimo tribuitur externæ, quod est proprium internæ, vel per synecdochen, toti quod est partis.
units.tr: Baptism therefore washes away sins, regenerates, saves, and so on, not by a power latently annexed or impressed upon the water, nor by the work done (ex opere operato), but by sacramental phrase: because of the conjunction of the two washings, what is proper to the inward is in lawful use attributed to the outward, or, by synecdoche, the whole is attributed to the part.

units.la: VI.
units.tr: VI.

units.la: Cum baptismus circumcisioni successerit, vt sit initiatorium noui fœderis sacramentum: non debet iterari, etiam indignè, vel ante conuersionem acceptus: Quoniam conuersis semper manet ratus: sicut ipsa promissio Euangelii, & fœdus: agentibus veròpœnitentiam fit ratus & salutaris, atque vsus eius prius illegitimus tunc in legitimum eis conuertitur: in quam sen-tentiam Augustinus: Si, inquit, ille qui accipit, nunquam accepe-rit, nec sic rescissum est, sed agnitum, quod per se oberat, correcto proderit SACRAMENTVM.
units.tr: Since baptism has succeeded circumcision, so as to be the initiatory sacrament of the New Covenant, it ought not to be repeated, even if it was received unworthily or before conversion; for it always remains valid for those who are converted, just as the promise of the Gospel and the covenant itself do. For those who repent, it becomes valid and saving, and its previously unlawful use is then turned into a lawful one for them. To this effect Augustine says: "If he who receives it has never received it, it is not therefore annulled but recognized; what hindered in itself will profit once it is corrected" SACRAMENT.

units.la: TESTIMONIA SCRIPTVRÆ.
units.tr: TESTIMONIES OF SCRIPTURE.

units.la: Ierem. 3, 1. Tu fornicata es cum amatoribus multis, sed reuertere ad me, dixit Iehoua.
units.tr: Jer. 3:1. "You have played the harlot with many lovers; yet return to me, says the LORD."

units.la: Ezech. 16. 59. 60. Faciam tecum, sicut fecisti, qua contemsisti iu-ramentum, vt irritum faceres pactum. Recordabor tamen pa-ctii mei, quod pepigi tecum in diebus adolescentiæ tuæ, & con-firmabo tibi pactum sempiternum.
units.tr: Ezek. 16:59, 60. "I will deal with you as you have done, you who despised the oath by breaking the covenant. Nevertheless I will remember my covenant with you in the days of your youth, and I will establish with you an everlasting covenant."

units.la: VII.
units.tr: VII.

units.la: Conferri autem baptismus ab Ecclesia Christi, mandato de-bet omnibus adultis, fidem Christi & pœnitentiam profitenti-bus, atque etiam infantibus in Ecclesia natis, vel cum parenti-bus in eam transeuntibus: quoniam ad hos etiam promissio & fœdus pertinet b: Et hi Christo adducendi sunt. c. Idque fieri debet per ministros ordinarios, non per mulieres aut alias per-sonas ad ministerium Ecclesiasticum non vocatas d. cuius, ad-ministratio sacramentorum pars est e.
units.tr: Baptism ought to be conferred by the Church of Christ, by command, on all adults who profess faith in Christ and repentance, and also on infants born in the Church or who pass into it with their parents, since the promise and the covenant pertain to these as well (b). And these are to be brought to Christ (c). This ought to be done by the ordinary ministers, not by women or other persons not called to the ecclesiastical ministry (d), whose administration of the sacraments is a part (e).

units.la: b, c, d, e: marginal section letters as printed.
units.tr: b, c, d, e: marginal section letters as printed.

units.la: TESTIMONIA SCRIPTVRAE, ET ALIORVM.
units.tr: TESTIMONIES OF SCRIPTURE AND OF OTHERS.

units.la: Act.2,38. Resipiscite, & baptizetur unusquisque vestrum in nomen JESU CHRISTI in remissionem peccatorum: & accipietis donum Spiritus sancti. Vobis enim facta est promissio, & liberis vestris, & omnibus longè post futuris, quoscunque advocaverit Dominus Deus noster.
units.tr: Acts 2:38. "Repent, and let each of you be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ for the forgiveness of sins, and you will receive the gift of the Holy Spirit. For the promise is made to you and to your children, and to all who are far off, as many as the Lord our God shall call."

units.la: Mulier baptizare non præsumat. Appendix illa: nisi necessitate urgente, non est in Canone Concilij: sed addita à Pontifice Rom. Decret. Dist. 4. de Consecr. c. mulier. contra mentem & Concilij, & mandatum Christi, quod absque peccato violari nullo modo potest, nisi aliud speciale mandatum divinum accedat.
units.tr: "Let not a woman presume to baptize." The clause "unless in urgent necessity" is not in the canon of the Council; it was added by the Roman Pontiff (Decretum, Dist. 4, de Consecratione, c. Mulier), contrary to the mind of the Council and the command of Christ, which cannot be violated in any way without sin, unless some special divine command intervenes.

units.la: VIII.
units.tr: VIII.

units.la: Improbamus dogmata contraria.
units.tr: We reject the following contrary doctrines.

units.la: 1. Quod Baptismus non sit signum gratiæ: sed tantum tessera, Christianos discernens, & ad fidem, atque crucem obligans.
units.tr: 1. That Baptism is not a sign of grace, but only a token distinguishing Christians and binding them to the faith and the cross.

units.la: 2. Quod partes essentiales Baptismi non sint aqua, & verbum, sed aqua, & persona Spiritus sancti, in verbo inclusa.
units.tr: 2. That the essential parts of Baptism are not water and the word, but water and the person of the Holy Spirit included in the word.

units.la: 3. Quod aquæ Baptismi annexa, affixaque sit latens virtus, quæ Spiritus sancti gratiam baptizatis conferat.
units.tr: 3. That a hidden power is attached and joined to the water of Baptism, which confers the grace of the Holy Spirit on the baptized.

units.la: 4. Quod Spiritus sanctus ipsiusque effecta Baptismo sint alligata.
units.tr: 4. That the Holy Spirit and his effects are bound to Baptism.

units.la: 5. Quod Spiritus sancti & aquæ Baptismi æqualia sint effecta.
units.tr: 5. That the effects of the Holy Spirit and of the water of Baptism are equal.

units.la: 6. Quod hypocritæ & infideles baptizati, vt Judas, & Simon magus, &c. in Baptismo non minus quam fideles Spiritu sancto regenerentur.
units.tr: 6. That hypocrites and unbelievers baptized, such as Judas and Simon Magus, etc., are regenerated in Baptism by the Holy Spirit no less than believers.

units.la: 7. Quod Ministri non tantum aqua, sed & Spiritu sancto baptizent: atque ita in Baptismo plus præstent, quàm Christus ipse.
units.tr: 7. That ministers baptize not only with water but also with the Holy Spirit, and so accomplish more in Baptism than Christ himself.

units.la: 8. Quod infantes Ecclesiæ non sint baptizandi: baptizati sint rebaptizandi.
units.tr: 8. That the infants of the Church are not to be baptized, and that those who have been baptized are to be rebaptized.

units.la: 9. Quod Ecclesiæ infantes ante baptismum spiritualiter sint obsessi a diabolo : ac propterea certis verbis & crucibus exorcizandi.
units.tr: 9. That the infants of the Church before baptism are spiritually possessed by the devil, and therefore are to be exorcised with certain words and signs of the cross.

units.la: 10. Quod Ecclesiæ infantes ante baptismum non magis quam Turcarum ad fœdus Dei pertineant : immò quod infantes Christianorum & Turcarum nullum prorsus sit discrimen.
units.tr: 10. That the infants of the Church before baptism belong no more to the covenant of God than those of the Turks; indeed, that there is absolutely no difference between the infants of Christians and of Turks.

units.la: 11. Quod necessitate postulante obstetrices, & quiuis alij non vocati recte baptizent.
units.tr: 11. That midwives and any others not called may rightly baptize when necessity demands it.

units.la: ARTICVLVS X.
units.tr: ARTICLE X.

units.la: DE COENA DOMINI.
units.tr: ON THE LORD'S SUPPER.

units.la: I.
units.tr: I.

units.la: Credimus, sacram Cœnam esse communionem corporis & sanguinis Christi, quæ fit sumtione panis fracti & poculi benedicti in commemorationem mortis Domini, donec veniat b, hoc est, esse Sacramentum alterum noui Testamenti, à Christo institutum, quo nobis sumentibus panem ac vinum consecratum, cum fideli recordatione mortis eius, testificatur, se corpore suo pro nobis tradito, & sanguine suo pro nobis fuso nos pascere ac viuificare d, vt cum ipso & inter nos coalescamus in vnum corpus e, & fœdus in Baptismo cum Deo initum, nobis perpetuo ratum maneat f.
units.tr: We believe that the holy Supper is the communion of the body and blood of Christ, which takes place by the eating of the broken bread and the drinking of the blessed cup, in remembrance of the Lord's death until he comes b. That is, it is the second Sacrament of the New Testament, instituted by Christ, by which he testifies to us, when we eat the bread and drink the consecrated wine, along with faithful remembrance of his death, that he feeds and quickens us with his body given for us and his blood shed for us d, so that we may be joined with him and with one another into one body e, and that the covenant entered into with God in Baptism may remain ever ratified for us f.

units.la: TESTIMONIA SCRIPTVRÆ.
units.tr: TESTIMONIES OF SCRIPTURE.

units.la: 1 Cor. 10, 16. Poculum benedictionis, cui benedicimus, nonne est communio sanguinis Christi? Panis, quem frangimus, nonne est communio corporis Christi?
units.tr: 1 Cor. 10:16. The cup of blessing which we bless, is it not the communion of the blood of Christ? The bread which we break, is it not the communion of the body of Christ?

units.la: 1 Cor. 11. vers. 26. Quotiescunque ederitis panem hunc, & poculum hoc biberitis, mortem Domini annunciabitis, vsque quo venerit.
units.tr: 1 Cor. 11:26. As often as you eat this bread and drink this cup, you proclaim the Lord's death until he comes.

units.la: Matth. 26, 26. Marci 14, 22. Lucæ 22, 17. 1 Cor. 11, 21. Edentibus eis, cum accepisset panem, & benedixisset, fregit eum, deditque discipulis; & ait: Accipite, comedite: HOC EST CORPVS MEVM.
units.tr: Matt. 26:26. Mark 14:22. Luke 22:17. 1 Cor. 11:21. As they were eating, he took bread, and blessed it, and broke it, and gave it to the disciples; and said: Take, eat: THIS IS MY BODY.

units.la: Ioh. 6, 54. Qui edit carnem meam, & bibit sanguinem meum, habet vitam æternam: & ego suscitabo ipsum in vltimo illo die.
units.tr: John 6:54. He who eats my flesh and drinks my blood has eternal life: and I will raise him up at the last day.

units.la: Ioh. 6, 56. Qui edit meam carnem, & bibit sanguinem meum, in me manet, & ego in eo.
units.tr: John 6:56. He who eats my flesh and drinks my blood abides in me, and I in him.

units.la: 1 Cor. {f}1 Cor.10,17. Quoniam vnus panis est, vnum corpus nos illi multi sumus, nam omnes ex vno illo pane participamus.
units.tr: 1 Cor. 10:17. Since there is one bread, we who are many are one body, for we all partake of that one bread.

units.la: 1 Cor.12,13. Omnes potati sumus in vnum spiritum.
units.tr: 1 Cor. 12:13. We have all been made to drink into one Spirit.

units.la: {f}1 Cor.11. verf.25. Hoc poculum est nouum illud fœdus per meum sanguinem.
units.tr: 1 Cor. 11:25. This cup is the new covenant in my blood.

units.la: II.
units.tr: II.

units.la: Dicimus & hoc Sacramentum constare symbolis externis, & verbo promissionis gratiæ symbolis annexo{a}: proinde & gemina alimonia geminaque manducatione seu sumptione: externa panis & vini, quæ fit ore corporis, ex manu ministri, vt sensus testantur: & interna spirituali corporis & sanguinis CHRISTI, quæ fit fide, ex manu ipsius Domini; & per externam tum significatur, tum vere exhibetur & obsignatur in vsu legitimo Sacramenti: vt promissio symbolis annexa testificatur{b}.
units.tr: We say also that this Sacrament consists of external signs, and of the word of the promise of grace annexed to the signs; accordingly it is also a twofold nourishment and a twofold eating or receiving: the external, of the bread and wine, which takes place by the mouth of the body, from the hand of the minister, as the senses testify; and the internal, spiritual, of the body and blood of Christ, which takes place by faith, from the hand of the Lord himself. And through the external it is both signified and truly exhibited and sealed in the lawful use of the Sacrament, as the promise annexed to the signs bears witness.

units.la: TESTIMONIA SCRIPTVRÆ, ET ALIORVM.
units.tr: Testimonies of Scripture, and of Others.

units.la: {a} Apolog. Augustanæ Confess. Tit. de vsu sacramenti & sacrificio: Et quia in Sacramentis duo sunt, signum & verbum: Verbum in Nouo Testamento est promissio gratiæ, additæ signo. Promissio Noui Testamenti est promissio remissionis peccatorum, sicut textus hic dicit: HOC EST CORPVS MEVM, quod pro vobis datur: HIC EST CALIX Noui Testamenti cum sanguine meo qui pro multis effundetur in remissionem peccatorum. Verbum igitur offert remissionem peccatorum. Et caremonia est quasi pignus verbi seu sigilli, vt Paulus vocat, ostendens promissionem.
units.tr: {a} Apology of the Augsburg Confession, title on the use of the sacrament and the sacrifice: "And since there are two things in the sacraments, the sign and the word, the word in the New Testament is the promise of grace, added to the sign. The promise of the New Testament is the promise of the forgiveness of sins, as this text says: THIS IS MY BODY, WHICH IS GIVEN FOR YOU; THIS IS THE CUP of the New Testament in my blood, which is poured out for many for the forgiveness of sins. The word therefore offers the forgiveness of sins. And the ceremony is like a pledge or seal of the word, as Paul calls it, showing the promise."

units.la: {b} Matth. 26. &c.
units.tr: {b} Matt. 26, etc.

units.la: III.
units.tr: III.

units.la: Cum enim sacramenta omnia sint sigilla gratiæ in Euangelio promissæ{a}: haud est dubitandum, quin verba promissionis cœnæ: HOC EST CORPVS MEVM, QVOD PRO VOBIS TRADITVR; HIC EST SANGVIS MEVS, QVI PRO VOBIS EFFVNDITVR, &c. sint ipsissima illa promissio Euangelij apud Iohannem extans{b}. Panis, quem ego dabo, caro mea est, quem dabo pro mundi vita: Caro enim mea vere est cibus, & sanguis meus est vere potus: sacramentali vestita ritu, ac symbolica manducatione confirmata, maioris ἀντιφαλείας causa: Illam vero de spirituali pastu carnis & sanguinis Christi, qui fit fide, loqui palam est{c}.
units.tr: Since all the sacraments are seals of the grace promised in the Gospel, there is no doubt that the words of the Supper, THIS IS MY BODY, WHICH IS GIVEN FOR YOU; THIS IS MY BLOOD, WHICH IS POURED OUT FOR YOU, etc., are that very promise of the Gospel found in John: "The bread which I will give is my flesh, which I will give for the life of the world; for my flesh is truly food, and my blood is truly drink." This promise is clothed in the sacramental rite and confirmed by the symbolic eating, for the sake of greater assurance [ἀντιφαλείας]. But it is plain that the latter passage speaks of the spiritual eating of the flesh and blood of Christ, which takes place by faith.

units.la: TESTIMONIA SCRIPTVRAE, ET ALIORVM.
units.tr: TESTIMONIES OF SCRIPTURE, AND OF OTHERS.

units.la: Rom. 4. 11. Et accepit signum circumcisionis, sigillum justitiæ fidei receptæ in præputio.
units.tr: Rom. 4. 11. And he received the sign of circumcision, a seal of the righteousness of faith received while uncircumcised.

units.la: Apologia Augustanæ Confess. Tit. de Vsu Sacramenti & Sacrificio : Verbum in Nouo Testamento est promissio gratiæ: vt supra.
units.tr: Apology of the Augsburg Confession, title On the Use of the Sacrament and the Sacrifice: The word in the New Testament is a promise of grace: as above.

units.la: Io. 6, 51. Ego sum panis ille viuificus, qui è cœlo descendi: si quis ederit ex hoc pane, viuet in æternum. Panis autem, quem ego dabo, caro mea est, quam ego dabo pro mundi vita.
units.tr: Io. 6, 51. I am that living bread, which came down from heaven: if anyone eat of this bread, he shall live for ever. But the bread that I shall give is my flesh, which I shall give for the life of the world.

units.la: Ioh. 6, 35. Ego sum panis ille vitæ: qui venit ad me, nequaquam esuriet: & qui credit in me, non sitiet vnquam.
units.tr: Ioh. 6, 35. I am the bread of life: he who comes to me shall never hunger, and he who believes in me shall never thirst.

units.la: IV.
units.tr: IV.

units.la: Oralem manducationem carnis suæ Christus in Euangelio nusquam promisit: sed expressis argumentis rejecit: proinde cœnæ sacramento haudquaquam sanxit: & graviter sine dubio peccant, qui hodie Ecclesias turbant propter oralem manducationem, quam fatentur ad salutem nullis necessariam, multis vero perniciosam esse.
units.tr: Christ nowhere in the Gospel promised an oral eating of his flesh; rather, he rejected it by plain arguments. Accordingly, he did not sanction it at all in the sacrament of the Lord's Supper. And those who today disturb the Churches over oral eating, which they admit is necessary for salvation by no one but is in fact harmful to many, undoubtedly sin grievously.

units.la: TESTIMONIA SCRIPTVRÆ.
units.tr: TESTIMONIES OF SCRIPTURE.

units.la: Ioh. 6, 61. 62. 63. Sciens autem Iesus apud se, discipulos suos de hoc murmurare, dixit eis: Hoccine vos offendit? Quid si igitur spectaueritis Filium hominis ascendentem eò, vbi erat prius? Spiritus est id, quod viuificat: CARO NON PRODEST QVICQVAM. Verba, quæ ego loquor vobis, spiritus sunt, & vita.
units.tr: John 6:61, 62, 63. But Jesus, knowing within himself that his disciples murmured at this, said to them: Does this offend you? What if then you should see the Son of man ascending where he was before? It is the Spirit that quickens; THE FLESH PROFITETH NOTHING. The words that I speak to you are spirit, and life.

units.la: V.
units.tr: V.

units.la: Particula Hoc, ipsum panem fractum à Domino monstrari, & hunc panem esse verum Christi corpus credimus & docemus, non conuersione in corpus, nec coexistentia reali cum corpore, sed sacramentali ratione: quia corporis Christi est sacramentum, seu sacrum signum: sic interpretante mente Domini apostolo: cum poculum vocat NOVVM TESTAMENTVM: hoc est, Noui Testamenti Sacramentum, panem communionem corporis Christi: hoc est, Communionis eius sacramentum: & Augustinus, cum inquit: Non dubitauit Dominus dicere HOC EST CORPUS MEUM, cum daret signum sui corporis. Item Prospero, cum panem suo modo vocari corpus Christi: & actionem sacramentalem vocari passionem, mortem, crucifixionem Christi. NON REI VERITATE, SED SIGNIFICANTE MYSTERIO.
units.tr: We believe and teach that the particle This points to the bread itself, broken by the Lord, and that this bread is the true body of Christ. This is not by conversion into the body, nor by real coexistence with the body, but by a sacramental manner of speaking, because it is the sacrament, or sacred sign, of the body of Christ. The Apostle, with the mind of the Lord, interprets it in this way when he calls the cup THE NEW TESTAMENT, that is, the sacrament of the New Testament, and the bread the communion of the body of Christ, that is, the sacrament of his communion. So too Augustine, when he says: The Lord did not hesitate to say THIS IS MY BODY, when he gave the sign of his body. Likewise Prosper, who says that the bread is in its own way called the body of Christ, and that the sacramental action is called the passion, death, and crucifixion of Christ: NOT IN THE TRUTH OF THE THING, BUT IN A SIGNIFYING MYSTERY.

units.la: TESTIMONIA SCRIPTVRÆ, ET ALIORVM.
units.tr: TESTIMONIA SCRIPTVRÆ, ET ALIORVM.

units.la: 1 Corinth.11. vers.25. Hic calix est nouum fœdus per meum sanguinem.
units.tr: 1 Corinthians 11:25. This cup is the new covenant in my blood.

units.la: 1 Cor.10,16. Panis, quem frangimus, &c.
units.tr: 1 Corinthians 10:16. The bread which we break, etc.

units.la: Augustin. contra Adimant.cap.12.
units.tr: Augustine, against Adimantus, chapter 12.

units.la: Prosper in Decr. de Consecr. Dist. 2. cap. Hoc est.
units.tr: Prosper, in the Decretum on Consecration, distinction 2, chapter "Hoc est."

units.la: VI.
units.tr: VI.

units.la: Cumq; Christi corpus non in pane, aut specie panis: sed verbo promissionis fide manducandum exhibeatur: impij quidem symbola ad judicium manducant, quorum abusu in Christum ipsum peccant: sed fide destituti corpus eius non percipiunt: cuius tamen, apostolo teste, fiunt rei, non ipsum percipiendo, quod infidelitate proculcant, sed panem eius symbolum indigne manducando.
units.tr: Since the body of Christ is to be eaten not in the bread or the appearance of bread, but is offered to be eaten by faith through the word of promise, the impious indeed eat the symbols to their judgment, and by their abuse they sin against Christ himself; but, lacking faith, they do not receive his body. Yet, as the Apostle testifies, they become guilty of it, not by receiving it, which they trample underfoot through unbelief, but by eating his bread, the symbol, unworthily.

units.la: TESTIMONIA SCRIPTVRÆ.
units.tr: TESTIMONIES OF SCRIPTURE.

units.la: 1 Cor.11,27. Quisquis ederit panem hunc, vel biberit hoc poculum Domini indignè, reus tenetur corporis & sanguinis Domini. Item: Qui edit & bibit indignè, damnationem sibi ipsi edit & bibit, non discernens corpus Domini.
units.tr: 1 Cor.11,27. Whoever eats this bread or drinks this cup of the Lord unworthily is guilty of the body and blood of the Lord. Likewise: He who eats and drinks unworthily eats and drinks judgment on himself, not discerning the body of the Lord.

units.la: Hebr.10,29. Quantò acerbiore supplicio dignus censebitur, qui Filium Dei conculcarit, & sanguinem fœderis, per quem fuerat sanctificatus, profanum duxerit, & Spiritum gratiæ contumelia affecerit?
units.tr: Hebr.10,29. How much worse a punishment, do you think, will he be judged to deserve who has trampled underfoot the Son of God, counted profane the blood of the covenant by which he was sanctified, and insulted the Spirit of grace?

units.la: VII.
units.tr: VII.

units.la: Improbamus verò ἐπηρεάσματα istas:
units.tr: We reject these slanders [ἐπηρεάσματα]:

units.la: 1. Quod corpus Christi sit in pane, vel sub specie panis corporaliter præsens per συνουσίωσιν, vel per μεταποίησιν.
units.tr: 1. That the body of Christ is present bodily in the bread, or under the appearance of bread, by a union of substances [συνουσίωσιν] or by a change [μεταποίησιν].

units.la: 2. Quod Ministri gestent corpus CHRISTI in manibus proprie.
units.tr: 2. That the ministers actually carry the body of Christ in their hands.

units.la: 3. Quod ore manducent corpus Christi.
units.tr: 3. That they eat the body of Christ with the mouth.

units.la: 4. Quod Hoc demonstret indiuiduum vagum, vel substantiam indeterminatam.
units.tr: 4. That the word "this" points to a vague individual, or to an indeterminate substance.

units.la: 5. Quod Hoc demonstret simul panem & corpus Christi inuisibiliter in pane latens.
units.tr: 5. That the word "this" points at once to the bread and to the body of Christ, invisibly lying hidden in the bread.

units.la: 6. Quod impij manducent corpus Christi proprie.
units.tr: 6. That the wicked eat the body of Christ in the proper sense.

units.la: ARTICVLVS XI. DE MAGISTRATU CIVILI.
units.tr: ARTICLE XI. ON THE CIVIL MAGISTRATE.

units.la: APHORISMI
units.tr: APHORISMS

units.la: Ex Germanico in Latinum translati.
units.tr: Translated from German into Latin.

units.la: I.
units.tr: I.

units.la: DVPLEX in homine regimen statuitur. Vnum ad Animam, seu interiorem hominem pertinet, efficitque, vt HOMO verè agnoscat DEVM: eundem recté colat, ac tandem justitiam & vitam æternam consequatur. Alterum gubernat Corpus, & exteriorem hominem: vt civilem hanc vitam inter homines cum omni modestia & honestate transigat.
units.tr: Two kinds of government are established in a human being. The one pertains to the soul, or inner man, and brings it about that a man truly acknowledges God, worships him rightly, and at last attains righteousness and eternal life. The other governs the body and the outer man, so that he may conduct this civil life among other people with all modesty and honesty.

units.la: II.
units.tr: II.

units.la: Etsi verò sacra scriptura præcipuè agit de gubernatione Animæ, & pro hac dirigenda à Deo cum maximè est ordinata: tamen de externa quoque gubernatione corporis multa præclara & salutaria tradit præcepta. Ac pro hac quidem feliciter administranda ad conservationem generis humani Deus in verbo suo præcepit, vt inter homines alij civili vitæ gubernandæ præessent: alij verò subessent, ac parerent. Hi ex relatis appellantur MAGISTRATVS & SVBDITI.
units.tr: Although Holy Scripture deals chiefly with the governing of the soul, and was most of all ordained by God to direct it, nevertheless it also gives many excellent and salutary precepts concerning the external governance of the body. For the successful administration of this external governance, to preserve the human race, God commanded in his Word that some men should preside over civil life, while others should be subject to them and obey. These are called, in the terms of this relation, MAGISTRATES AND SUBJECTS.

units.la: III.
units.tr: III.

units.la: Magistratus civilis potestas humano generi non minus, immò adeo magis est necessaria, quam panis cottidianus, quam aqua, sol & aer: quippe sine quibus terrena hæc vita minimè consistere potest. Per hæc namque naturalia homo vitalè haurit spiritum, edit, bibit, vivit, ac movetur, sicut cætera omnia animantia, quibuscum hæc cum homine communia esse solent. Ne verò homines agant vitam planè beluinam, sed verè humanam: cum omni scilicet modestia & honestate coram Deo & hominibus: hoc est, vt omnis idololatria, blasphemia, & quiuis alij abusus nominis divini, itemque omnis generis turpitudines, & damna, quibus vel nos, vel proximi vita, fama ac possessiones lædi solent, caveantur; vera autem Dei agnitio, sincerus cultus, & timor, vt & omnis civilis honestas obtineat: neue publica pax & tranquillitas inter homines disturbetur: vnusquisque sua tutò possideat, honesti & necessarij contractus vigeant: ac denique in Republica omnia legitimè fiant, diligenter prouidere debet magistratus civilis, ea fini à Deo ordinatus. Quare merito ij, qui hanc Dei ordinationem inter homines tollunt aut euertunt, non inter homines, sed bruta censenda sunt.
units.tr: The power of the civil magistrate is no less necessary to the human race, indeed it is far more necessary, than daily bread, water, sun and air, since human life on earth cannot exist without these. For through these natural things a man draws the breath of life, eats, drinks, lives and moves, just as all other living creatures do, with which humans are usually held to have things in common. But so that men may lead not a merely beastly life, but a truly human one, that is, with all modesty and honesty before God and men, the civil magistrate, ordained by God for this end, ought diligently to provide that every idolatry, blasphemy and any other abuse of the divine name is prevented, as well as every kind of baseness and every harm by which our life, reputation or property are usually injured; that the true knowledge of God, sincere worship and fear of him, and all civil decency, may prevail; that public peace and tranquillity are not disturbed among men; that each may safely possess what is his; that honest and necessary contracts remain in force; and finally that all things in the commonwealth are done lawfully. Therefore those who destroy or overturn this ordinance of God among men are rightly judged not to be men but beasts.

units.la: IV.
units.tr: IV.

units.la: Absoluitur autem doctrina de magistratu ciuili tribus hisce capitibus:
units.tr: The doctrine of the civil magistrate is completed under three heads.

units.la: PRIMO; De authoritate Magistratus: An à Deo sit ordinatus; Deoq; placeat: de eiusdem officio, jure, ac potestate, in negotiis tam ecclesiasticis, quam politicis.
units.tr: FIRST; Concerning the authority of the Magistrate: whether he is ordained by God and pleasing to God; concerning his office, right, and power, both in ecclesiastical and in political affairs.

units.la: DEINDE; De legibus, quibus teneatur Magistratus Christianus.
units.tr: NEXT; Concerning the laws by which the Christian Magistrate is bound.

units.la: TERTIO; De officio subditorum: quid hi debeant suo magistratui: quousque obedientiam illi praestare teneantur.
units.tr: THIRDLY; Concerning the duty of subjects: what they owe to their magistrate, and how far they are bound to render obedience to him.

units.la: De singulis quid ex verbo Dei sit statuendum, sequentes Aphorismi docebunt.
units.tr: What is to be determined from the Word of God on each of these, the following aphorisms will teach.

units.la: V.
units.tr: V.

units.la: Magistratum esse à Deo ordinatum, docet expresse apostolus Paulus his verbis: Non est potestas, nisi à Deo: & quae sunt potestates, sunt à Deo ordinatae. Dei enim minister est tuo bono. Diuina hac authoritate munitus magistratus cogitet, sibi prudenter & attentè esse versandum in munere suo. Si enim ideo est à Deo, vt Dei sit minister, certè omni cura id agere debet, vt ad Dei ordinationem omnia fiant, non minus in Ecclesiasticis, quam politicis negotiis, neque sciens volens quicquam contra illam committat. Ex hoc fundamento ordinationis diuinae Moses, vt ille Dei, & pientissimus Rex Iosaphat, Judices ac Praefectos suos sic alloquuti sunt: Videte, quid vos facitis. Non enim homini judicatis, sed Iehouae: & erit vobiscum in negotiis judicio. Nunc igitur sit pavor Iehouae super vos: custodite, & facite: quoniam non est cum Iehova Deo nostro iniquitas, & acceptio personarum, & acceptio muneris.
units.tr: That the magistrate is ordained by God, the apostle Paul teaches expressly in these words: "There is no power but of God, and the powers that exist are ordained by God. For he is God's minister for your good" (Rom. 13). Armed with this divine authority, the magistrate should consider that he must conduct himself wisely and carefully in his office. For if he is from God so that he may be God's minister, he ought surely to take every care that all things are done according to God's ordinance, no less in ecclesiastical than in civil affairs, and that he knowingly and willingly commit nothing against it. On this foundation of divine ordinance, Moses, that man of God, and the most godly king Jehoshaphat addressed their judges and prefects in this way: "Take heed what you do; for you judge not for man, but for Jehovah, and he will be with you in the matter of judgment. Now therefore let the fear of Jehovah be upon you; take heed and do it, for with Jehovah our God there is no iniquity, nor respect of persons, nor taking of gifts" (2 Chron. 19).

units.la: Rursum; si magistratus est à Deo ordinatus, vt sit Dei minister, plane persuasum habere debet, Deo se inseruire: ad Dei honorem & cultum, ad hominum vero vtilitatem omnia se agere: modo ad praescriptum verbi diuini illud faciat.
units.tr: Again: if the magistrate is ordained by God so that he may be God's minister, he ought to be fully persuaded that he serves God, and that he does all things for the honour and worship of God, and for the benefit of men, provided that he does so according to the prescription of the divine Word.

units.la: VI.
units.tr: VI.

units.la: Deo igitur illud, quod ipsemet ordinauit, displicere nequit: adeo quidem, vt Magistratum etiam de suo nomine appellet <bl>אלהים</bl> Deos: quod judicium exerceat Dei loco. Exod. 22. v. 8. Si non inuentus fuerit fur, tunc applicabitur dominus domus ad Deos. Psal. 82,1. Deus in medio Deorum judicat. Quem Psalmum allegat Christus Joh. 10, 35. Si illos dixit Deos, ad quos sermo Dei factus est, Ego dixi, vos estis Dij. Scriptura iusuper testatur, multos viros sanctos officium magistratus exercuisse: vt in Regnis, Dauidem, Iosuam, Ezechiam; in Principatibus, Iosephum, Danielem: In Praefecturis, Moses, Iosuam, Gideonem.
units.tr: Therefore God cannot be displeased with that which he himself has ordained; so much so that he even calls magistrates by his own name, <bl>אלהים</bl> gods, because they exercise judgment in the place of God. Exod. 22. v. 8: "If the thief is not found, then the master of the house shall be brought before the gods." Ps. 82:1: "God stands in the midst of the gods, he judges." Christ cites this Psalm in John 10:35: "If he called them gods, to whom the word of God came, and the Scripture cannot be broken, do you say of me, whom the Father sanctified and sent into the world, 'You blaspheme,' because I said, I am the Son of God?" Scripture further testifies that many holy men exercised the office of magistrate: in kingdoms, David, Joshua, Hezekiah; in principalities, Joseph, Daniel; in prefectures, Moses, Joshua, Gideon.

units.la: VII.
units.tr: VII.

units.la: Facessant hoc loco Anabaptistarum, & aliorum fanaticorum hominum deliria, dicentium: In veteri quidem Testamento Magistratum populo Dei fuisse necessarium, ob populi Iudaici imperfectionem: In nouo vero Testamento scriptum esse: Reges gentium dominantur eis; & qui habent eas in potestate, BENEFICI vocantur: vos autem non sic. Item: In Christo nihil quicquam valet, nisi noua creatura. Item: Ego vero dico vobis, ne obsistite improbo.
units.tr: Let the ravings of the Anabaptists and other fanatics be set aside at this point. They say that in the Old Testament the magistracy was necessary for the people of God because of the imperfection of the Jewish people, but that in the New Testament it is written: The kings of the nations lord it over them, and those who have power over them are called benefactors; but you are not to be so. Likewise: In Christ nothing avails except a new creature. Likewise: But I say to you, do not resist the evil man.

units.la: VIII.
units.tr: VIII.

units.la: Nam primo: Si imperfectio populi Iudaici Magistratum necessario requirebat: certè multo magis nobis Christianis necessarius erit magistratus: quippe cum de nobis scriptum quoque sit: In multis offendimus omnes. Qui vero in multis offendunt, certè imperfecti sint oportet. Equidem non negamus, Christianos per Dei gratiam prae Iudaeis magnam nunc habere praerogatiuam, quoad clariorem agnitionem Dei, & gratiam nobis per Christum exhibitam. In ciuili vero vita nos non minus opus habemus ordinatione hac diuina magistratus, quàm populus Iudaicus.
units.tr: For first: if the imperfection of the Jewish people required the magistrate of necessity, then surely much more will the magistrate be necessary for us Christians, since it is written of us as well: In many things we all offend. Now those who offend in many things must surely be imperfect. Indeed we do not deny that Christians now have, through the grace of God, a great pre-eminence over the Jews, as regards the clearer knowledge of God and the grace offered to us through Christ. But in civil life we have no less need of this divine ordinance of the magistrate than did the Jewish people.

units.la: Praterea in nouo, non veteri Testamento, scriptum est ab apostolo Paulo: Dei est minister, tuo bono.
units.tr: Moreover, in the New Testament, not the Old, the apostle Paul has written: He is the minister of God for your good.

units.la: IX.
units.tr: IX.

units.la: In dicto Luc. 22, 25. Christus Reges huiusmodi non arcet ab Ecclesia; sed Apostolis & ministris Ecclesiae omnem prohibet mundanum luxum, omnem praeeminentiam, & dominatum ciuilem. Paulus vero Gal. 6, 15. non loquitur de externo Christianorum habitu: quorum aliqui erant circumcisi, vt fideles Iudaei: alij autem non circumcisi, vt Christiani ex gentibus. Cui dicto respondet illud Gal. 3, 28. Non est Iudaus, neq; Graecus: non est seruus, neq; liber: non est masculus, aut foemina. Quae verba si ad literam intelligant, certè & ipsi à Christo forent separandi: cum sint vel serui, vel liberi, vel mas, vel foemina. Sensus igitur Apostoli est: externum hominum discrimen nihil vel impedire, vel promouere salutem aeternam; solam vero creaturam nouam in Iesu Christo esse necessariam ad salutem.
units.tr: In the saying at Luke 22:25, Christ does not exclude such kings from the Church. He forbids the apostles and the ministers of the Church all worldly luxury, all pre-eminence, and civil domination. Paul, however, in Gal. 6:15, is not speaking of the external dress of Christians. Some of them were circumcised, such as the faithful Jews, and others were uncircumcised, such as Christians from the Gentiles. The verse Gal. 3:28 answers this saying: There is neither Jew nor Greek, there is neither bond nor free, there is neither male nor female. If these words are understood literally, then certainly Jews and Greeks, slaves and free, men and women would also have to be separated from Christ, since all of them are one or the other. The sense of the Apostle, therefore, is this: an external distinction among men neither hinders nor advances eternal salvation, and only the new creature in Jesus Christ is necessary for salvation.

units.la: X.
units.tr: X.

units.la: Denique dicto Matth. 5, 39. Christus non tollit pænas in improbos, sed priuatam vindictam. Secus enim nullus vel Christianus, vel pater & mater, vel Præceptores in Scholis, nullus denique Minister Ecclesiæ foret tolerandus: quorum omnium est suo loco malo & improbo resistere, & disciplinam tueri: absque quo horrenda sequeretur ἀναρχία, inueheretur licentia infinita, & tandem societatis humanæ, ipsiusque Ecclesiæ subuersio. Certè quidem Christus & Apostoli malo sæpissimè restiterunt. Neque vspiam in sacris literis legimus, eos, qui politicis officiis sunt defuncti, postquam ad fidem Christianam sunt conuersi, deseruisse suam prouinciam, vel, vt eam deserent, jussos fuisse. Sic regius ille Johan. 4. verf. 53. Credidit ipse, et domus eius tota. Sergius Paulus Propræfor Actor. 13, 12. Credidit. Et Commentariensis Actor. 16, 33. Baptizatus est ipse, et omnes domestici illius.
units.tr: Finally, by the saying at Matt. 5:39, Christ does not remove punishments from the wicked, but only private revenge. Otherwise no Christian, no father or mother, no teachers in schools, and finally no minister of the Church would be tolerated. It is the duty of all of these to resist evil and wicked people in their proper place and to uphold discipline. Without this there would follow a dreadful anarchy [ἀναρχία], unlimited licence would break in, and at last human society and the Church itself would be overthrown. Certainly Christ and the Apostles very often resisted evil. Nor do we read anywhere in Holy Scripture that those who had held civil offices, after they were converted to the Christian faith, abandoned their office, or were ordered to abandon it. So the royal official in John 4:53: He himself believed, and his whole house. Sergius Paulus, the proconsul, in Acts 13:12: He believed. And the chief jailer in Acts 16:33: He was baptized, he and all his household.

units.la: XI.
units.tr: XI.

units.la: De variis formis Reipublicæ, vtra optima sit, disputant Politici. In sacris literis mentio fit Cæsarum, Regum, Principum, Præfectorum, Præsidum, Prætorum, Consulum, Capitaneorum, Ducum: adeoque, vt verbo dicam, tam inferiorum, quam superiorum magistratuum: de quibus generalis hæc exstat sententia Pauli Apostoli: Non est potestas, nisi à Deo: vbi verò est potestas, à Deo est ordinata. Et D. Petri: Subiecti estote cuiusuis hutestas, ... mana ordinationi, propter Dominum, siue Regi, vt qui supereminet, siue præsidibus, vt qui per eum mittuntur. Irem: Deum timete, Regem honorate. Vbi notandum, quando ab Apostolo Petro magistratus ordinatio humana nominatur, minimè illud repugnare Paulo, qui ordinationem diuinam appellat. Magistratum namque solus Deus ordinauit. Formæ verò Reipublicæ, & eiusdem gradus distincti, vt in ea sint Cæsares, Reges, Principes, superiores, inferiores, dependent ab ordinatione hominum, & sanctiores ciuili: omnes tamen pariter à Deo gubernantur. Humana itaque ordinationi subditi esse cogimur, propter Dominum, inquit D.Petrus.
units.tr: Political writers dispute which of the various forms of commonwealth is the best. Holy Scripture mentions emperors, kings, princes, prefects, governors, praetors, consuls, captains, and dukes; in a word, magistrates of every rank, both lower and higher. Concerning them stands this general statement of the Apostle Paul: There is no power but of God; where there is power, it is ordained of God. And of St. Peter: Submit yourselves to every human ordinance for the Lord's sake, whether to the king as supreme, or to governors as sent by him. Again: Fear God, honour the king. Here it should be noted that when the Apostle Peter calls the magistracy a human ordinance, this does not contradict Paul, who calls it a divine ordinance. For God alone instituted the magistracy. But the forms of commonwealth, and the distinct grades within them, so that there are emperors, kings, princes, superiors and inferiors, depend on human ordinance, and are more or less civil. Yet all alike are governed by God. Therefore we are compelled to be subject to human ordinance for the Lord's sake, says St. Peter.

units.la: XII.
units.tr: XII.

units.la: De jure magistratus sic loquitur apostolus Paulus: Propter hoc etiam tributa soluitis: siquidem ministri Dei sunt, in hoc ipsum intendentes. Reddite igitur omnibus quod debetis: cui tributum debetur, tributum; cui vectigal, vectigal; cui timor, timorem; cui honorem, honorem. honorem. Item: Date Caesari, quod Caesaris est. Unde colligimus, jus magistratus in tribus esse positum.
units.tr: The Apostle Paul speaks as follows about the right of the magistrate: For this cause you also pay tribute, for they are ministers of God, attending continually to this very thing. Render therefore to all their dues: tribute to whom tribute is due, custom to whom custom, fear to whom fear, honour to whom honour. Likewise: Give to Caesar what is Caesar's. From this we gather that the right of the magistrate consists in three things.

units.la: Primo: ut agnoscatur tanquam minister Dei, cui honor, & reverentia ideo debetur, quia est loco Dei. Eo nomine, ut dictum, magistratus appellantur Dii.
units.tr: First, that he be acknowledged as a minister of God, to whom honour and reverence are therefore owed, because he stands in God's place. For this reason, as has been said, magistrates are called gods.

units.la: Secundo; ut propter authoritatem tanti muneris à subditis omni honore, reverentia & timore afficiatur, non minus atque parentes à liberis suis. Magistratus namque subditis parentum loco esse debet.
units.tr: Second, that because of the authority of so great an office he be regarded by his subjects with all honour, reverence and fear, no less than parents are by their children. For the magistrate ought to stand to his subjects in the place of parents.

units.la: Tertio; ut magistratui dependantur debita vectigalia, & tributa: è quibus & gravissimum sui muneris onus sustinere, & vitam suam pro dignitate conservare, atque ergo alios benignitatem suam exercere queat. Non minus tamen magistratus, quam ipsi subditi, ab omni luxu abesse debet, ut patet Jer. 22, 14. 15. & alibi passim in scriptura.
units.tr: Third, that the magistrate be paid the customary duties and taxes, from which he can both bear the very heavy burden of his office and maintain his life in a manner befitting his dignity, and so be able to exercise his kindness toward others. Nevertheless, the magistrate, no less than the subjects themselves, ought to be free from all luxury, as is clear from Jer. 22:14-15 and elsewhere throughout Scripture.

units.la: XIII.
units.tr: XIII.

units.la: Magistratum Deus summa instruxit potestate; ut aliis imperet, alios gubernet: etiam gladio, si opus, erga inobedientes vtatur, suamque authoritatem tueatur, atque defendat. Sic enim scriptum est: Deus regna hominum dat, cui voluerit. Item: Principes gentium dominantur, & magnates potestatem exercent in eas. Item; Gladium non gerit frustra.
units.tr: God has furnished the magistrate with supreme power, so that he may command others and govern them, and, if need be, use the sword against the disobedient, and maintain and defend his authority. For it is written: God gives the kingdoms of men to whomever he wills. Likewise: The princes of the nations lord it over them, and the great exercise authority over them. Likewise: He does not bear the sword in vain.

units.la: XIV.
units.tr: XIV.

units.la: Sed & aerumnabile prorsus, ac molestum illud onus magistratui ideo imposuit Deus, ut obedientiam legis divinae urgeat, promoueat, atque conserueat inter homines, praesertim Christianos. Nam primo honorem & cultum Dei ex praescripto primae tabulae tenetur sartum tectum tueri: pietatemque & verum Dei cultum ex voluntate Dei & verbi sui inter subditos propagare. Sic enim Deus praecipit Josuae: Non recedat liber legis iste ab ore tuo, ut custodias & facias secundum omne, quod scriptum est in eo. Et Paulus: Minister Dei, tuo bono. Summum vero bonum subditorum, est vera RELIGIO, & verus Dei cultus.
units.tr: But God has also laid upon the magistrate a truly burdensome and troublesome charge, so that he may press, advance and preserve obedience to the divine law among men, especially Christians. For first, he is bound to keep intact and protect the honour and worship of God, as prescribed in the first table of the law, and to propagate piety and the true worship of God among his subjects, according to the will of God and his Word. For thus God commands Joshua: "Let not this book of the law depart from your mouth, but meditate on it day and night, that you may observe and do according to all that is written in it." And Paul: "He is God's minister for your good." Now the highest good of the subjects is true RELIGION and the true worship of God.

units.la: XV.
units.tr: XV.

units.la: Deinde magistratus quoque officium est, jus & justitiam colere, honestatem, pacem ac concordiam conservare; bonos amare, malos vero terrere ac plectere: subditos suos & territoria adversus domesticos & externos hostes, etiam gladio & armis tueri, ac defendere, sicut scriptum est: Sic dicit Dominus: Facite judicium & justitiam, & liberate oppressum de manu opprimentis, & aduenam & pupillum, & viduam ne fraudetis, neque rapiatis, & sanguinem innocentis ne effundatis in loco isto. Item: Magistratus non sunt terrori bonis operibus, sed malis. Vis autem non terreri potestate? quod bonum est, facito. Quod si feceris, quod malum est, metue. Non enim frustra gladium gestat. Dei minister est, vltor ad iram ei, qui, quod malum est, fecerit.
units.tr: Second, it is also the duty of the magistrate to cultivate law and justice, and to maintain honesty, peace and concord; to love good men but to terrify and punish evil men; and to defend and protect his subjects and territories against domestic and foreign enemies, even with the sword and arms, as it is written: "Thus says the Lord: Do judgment and justice, and deliver the oppressed out of the hand of the oppressor; and do not wrong the stranger, the fatherless and the widow, nor rob them, nor shed innocent blood in this place." Likewise: "Rulers are not a terror to good works, but to evil. Do you wish not to be afraid of the power? Do what is good, and you will have praise from it. But if you do what is evil, fear; for he does not bear the sword in vain. He is God's minister, an avenger for wrath to him who does what is evil."

units.la: XVI.
units.tr: XVI.

units.la: Vtrumq; Magistratûs officiû impugnare solent tum Potificij in Papatu, tum Anabaptistæ, & fanatici alij.
units.tr: Both duties of the magistracy are commonly attacked, both by the Papists in the Papacy and by the Anabaptists and other fanatics.

units.la: XVII.
units.tr: XVII.

units.la: Pontificij in Papatu fatentur quidem, Magistratus non tantum curare ciuilia, & communem pacem promouere; sed & Dei cultum, prout à sacerdotibus in Papatu administratur, omni modo tueri, alias quascunque religiones, quas ipsi damnant, exterminare: sed non permittunt magistratui ciuili in religionem & cultum suum inquirere: verus ne ille sit, & sacris literis consentaneus, an falsus: piene viuant sacerdotes, & Ecclesiastici, an impie: Ecclesiis & Scholis recte prospectum sit, nec ne: an denique jurisdictionem Ecclesiasticam jure sibi vindicent: & id genus alia.
units.tr: The Papists in the Papacy indeed admit that the magistrate should not only look after civil matters and promote common peace, but also should in every way defend the worship of God as it is administered by the priests in the Papacy, and drive out all other religions which they condemn; but they do not permit the civil magistrate to inquire into their religion and worship: whether it is true and consonant with the holy writings or false; whether the priests and clergy live piously or impiously; whether provision is rightly made for the Churches and Schools or not; or finally whether they claim ecclesiastical jurisdiction for themselves by right; and other things of this kind.

units.la: XVIII.
units.tr: XVIII.

units.la: Hoc verò jus gubernandi Ecclesias & Scholas sacra Scriptura distincte magistratui ciuili attribuit, vt ei, quemadmodum tenetur diligenter procurare, vt bonum ciuile, hoc est, jus & justitia per Iurisperitos, & prudentiæ politicæ gnaros in foro & judiciis, juxta leges cuiusque prouinciæ legitimè administretur: ita non minor, imò longè maior eius cura esse debeat, vt jus diuinum, bonum illud animatum, hoc est, vera RELIGIO, & pietas per Theologos, viros sanctos, pios, doctos ac honestos, subditis suis in Ecclesiis & Scholis ad æternam eorum salutem proponatur juxta Legem & Testimonium: vt præcipit scriptura. Mandavit idipsum Deus Mosi & Iosuæ. Idem docent exempla laudatissimorum Regum, Davidis, Salomonis, Iosaphati, Hiskiæ, Iosiæ, & aliorum, qui cultum Dei studiose promouerunt, sacerdotes impios & ἀθέους graviter increparunt. Sic Paulus affatur Christianos Romanos: Minister est Dei tuo bono: vbi intelligit omne BONVM, tam ciuile & terrenum, quàm Ecclesiasticum seu spirituale. Secus namque magistratus homini Christiano non plus commodaret, quàm infideli. Ac sanè dolendum est, rectius in hoc capite sensisse olim Ethnicos, qui vnanimi consensu Regi suo demandarunt curam Religionis, & cultus Deorum; idque perpersuasi jure tam naturæ, quàm gentium. Nam magistratus politici proprium id munus esse statuerunt, subditos suos ciuiliter gubernare, hoc est, imbuere omni genere virtutum, inprimis autem fortitudine militari, & id genus aliis.
units.tr: But holy Scripture distinctly assigns this right of governing the Churches and Schools to the civil magistrate, so that, just as he is bound to take diligent care that the civil good, that is, law and justice, is administered lawfully by jurists and men skilled in political prudence in the forum and courts according to the laws of each province, so his care for the divine law, that living good, that is, the true RELIGION and piety, should be no less, indeed far greater, and should be set before his subjects in the Churches and Schools for their eternal salvation, by theologians who are holy, pious, learned and honourable men, according to the Law and the Testimony, as Scripture prescribes. God commanded the same to Moses and Joshua. The examples of the most praiseworthy kings, David, Solomon, Jehoshaphat, Hezekiah, Josiah and others, who zealously promoted the worship of God and severely rebuked impious and godless priests, teach the same. Thus Paul addresses the Christians at Rome: "He is God's minister for your good," where he understands all good, both civil and earthly, and ecclesiastical or spiritual. For otherwise the magistrate would be no more useful to a Christian man than to an unbeliever. And truly it is to be lamented that the heathen formerly thought more rightly on this point, who with one accord committed the care of religion and the worship of the gods to their king, being thoroughly persuaded of this by the right both of nature and of nations. For they determined that the proper duty of the political magistrate was to govern his subjects civilly, that is, to imbue them with every kind of virtue, especially military courage, and other things of this kind.

units.la: XIX.
units.tr: XIX.

units.la: Anabaptistæ & Fanatici facilè quoq; admittunt, & concedunt, magistratus esse officium, non tantum versari in foro, exercere judicia, sed & malum belli pacisq; tempore gladio plectere: negant vero Christianos id facere, aut faciendi habere potestatem: eo quod Christus discipulis suis dixerit: Nolite resistere improbo: neque gladium illis dederit, sed interdixerit, his verbis: Qui gladium sumserit, gladio peribit.
units.tr: The Anabaptists and Fanatics readily admit and concede that it is the office of the magistrate not only to sit in the courts and conduct judicial proceedings, but also to punish evildoers with the sword, in time of war as well as of peace. They deny, however, that Christians may do this or have the power to do it, because Christ said to his disciples, Do not resist an evil person, and did not give them the sword but forbade it, in these words: Whoever takes the sword will perish by the sword.

units.la: Dicunt idem, nouum Testamentum sanguinem non suadere, sed charitatem: & quicquid est huiusmodi affaniarum, ex Manichæorum schola: ut scilicet omnem magistratum ex Christianorum republica tollant.
units.tr: They also say that the New Testament does not urge bloodshed but love; and whatever nonsense of this kind there is comes from the school of the Manichaeans, namely, so that they may remove every magistrate from the commonwealth of Christians.

units.la: XX.
units.tr: XX.

units.la: Quibus opponi debet doctrina apostoli Pauli: Omnis potestas est à Deo: & est Dei minister. Num verò Deus aliquid ordinauit, quod vel non liceat, vel non possit præstari? Num Ethnicus rectius Deo seruiat, quam Christianus? Facessant itaq; homines illi cum suis deliriis, ac tolerentur sanè, quoad quidem non turbant ecclesias, aut magistratui debitum honorem & obsequium non denegant. Qua de re in Imperij Constitutionibus prouidè cautum est.
units.tr: To these people the teaching of the apostle Paul must be set against them: "All power is from God, and he is God's minister" (Rom. 13). Surely God has not ordained anything that is either unlawful or impossible to carry out? Does the heathen serve God more rightly than the Christian? Let those men depart with their follies. They may be tolerated, provided they do not disturb the churches or refuse the magistrate the honour and obedience that are owed to him. On this matter the imperial constitutions have wisely taken precautions.

units.la: De dicto Matth. 5, 39. supra Aphorism. X. egimus. Matth. 26. v. 52. Christus discipulis suis aliisque priuatis gladium ademit ideo, quia Apostolis, Episcopis, ministris, & aliis subditis, non debetur. Cæsari vero, cui Deus gladium antea dederat, eundem non ademit, sed demandauit; quia dixit: Date Cæsari, quod est Cæsaris. Et per Apostolum: Minister Dei est: nec gladium frustra gerit.
