units.la: XX. Traditiones inde suas vocat VERBVM DEI non scriptum, æquè certum, infallibile, canonicum, ad salutem necessarium, pari pietatis affectu & reuerentia cum verbo Dei scripto suscipiendum.
units.tr: XX. From this he calls his own traditions the WORD OF GOD unwritten, equally certain, infallible, canonical, necessary to salvation, and to be received with the same affection of piety and reverence as the written Word of God.

units.la: ASSERTIO.
units.tr: ASSERTION.

units.la: Vtramque hanc positionem, cum aduersarius silentio probet, assertione non indigent. Vtraque styli communis est in Papatu: nec
units.tr: Since the opponent accepts both of these propositions in silence, they need no proof. Both are a common manner of speech in the Papacy, and

units.la: Hæc dici potest, quam sint omnes hodie in Bibliorum, & scriptu- rarum, quas habent Christiani, imperfectione & defectibus ex- agirandis, contra in Traditionum suarum Diuinitate & necessi- tate exaggeranda, ingeniosi, diserti, acferuidi. Videatur pro omnibus Bellarmini Cardinalis liber IV. de verbo non-scripto, per totum. Atqui quam sit Deo contumeliosum, Verbum eius scriptum, quod hominem Dei ad omne opus bonum perfectum reddere, credentibusq; vitam æternam dare, ipsum de sese testatur, imperfe- ctionis næuo conspurcare, quantæ contra arrogantiæ & vanita- tis quantiq; periculi, Traditiones humanas, quibus Deus (quic- quid homines contra mentiantur) frustra colitur, non modo scri- pturis diuinis æquare, sed & supra eas efferre, arctioreque reli- gione colere: nostri in præsens non est instituti, pluribus expli- care: cum & per se omnes pij facilè intelligant, & à nostris sæ- pius fit demonstratum.
units.tr: One may say how all of them today, being eager and skilful and fervent, insist on exposing the imperfection and defects of the Bible and the Scriptures which Christians possess, but on the contrary, exaggerate the divinity and necessity of their own traditions. For all of them, see Cardinal Bellarmine's fourth book, On the Unwritten Word, throughout. But how insulting it is to God to stain his written Word, which itself testifies that it makes the man of God perfect for every good work, and gives eternal life to believers, with the blemish of imperfection; and how great the arrogance, vanity and danger it is to not only equate human traditions, by which God is worshipped in vain (whatever men may lie to the contrary), with the divine Scriptures, but also to raise them above them and cultivate them with a stricter religion. It is not my present purpose to explain this at length, since all the godly readily understand it of themselves, and our writers have often demonstrated it.

units.la: XXI. Scripturam blasphemat NASVM CEREVM, ambiguam, literam mortuam, atramento scriptam, quæ Ecclesiæ confirmatione INDIGVERIT: instar vaginæ recipientis quemuis gladium, chalybeum, plumbeum, ligneum, æneum. ASSERTIO.
units.tr: XXI. Scripture is blasphemed as a WAX NOSE, ambiguous, a dead letter written in ink, which has NOT DESERVED confirmation by the Church: like a sheath that takes in any sword, whether of steel, lead, wood or bronze. ASSERTION.

units.la: Blasphemias anathemate dignas tacitus agnoscit Iesuita. Vel- let tamen diluere mendacio, quasi injuria obijciantur Papatui. Sed nihil confictum, immò parum dictū est. Scripturam sacram pro NASO CEREO quasi flexiloquam, & ambiguam, vulgò in Pa- patu haberi: & quidem recte haberi, LINDANVS in Panoplia sua palam profitetur. Consulens enim, ne Papistæ cum hæreticis, Euangelicis scilicet, dehinc disputent ex scriptura sacra: Qua, inquit, ut vulgo videre est, ob facilem ipsius in varias sententiarum formas flexum rectè NASO fuit assimilata CEREO. En, RECTE fuit assimilata naso cereo. Excusat igitur, probat, defendit iste conui- tium, quod Iesuita vocat mendacium.
units.tr: The Jesuit silently admits that these blasphemies deserve anathema. Yet he would like to wash them away with a lie, as if the charge were unjustly brought against the Papacy. But nothing has been invented here; rather, too little has been said. That Holy Scripture is commonly regarded in the Papacy as a WAX NOSE, as if pliable and ambiguous, and indeed rightly so regarded, LINDANUS openly professes in his Panoply. For, advising that the Papists should not dispute with heretics, that is, the Evangelicals, from holy Scripture from now on, he says: "by which, as is commonly seen, because of its easy bending into various forms of meaning, it has been rightly compared to a wax nose." Behold, it was RIGHTLY compared to a wax nose. This man therefore excuses, approves and defends the insult which the Jesuit calls a lie.

units.la: COSTERVS Iesuita triarius triplicem scripturam sacram fingit: unam spiritualem, à spiritu inscriptam ingenio Ecclesiæ seu Pa- storibus alteram ab apostolis relictam Ecclesiæ, in chartaceis libris, & membranis, atramento scriptam: teriam in decretis Pontificum Conciliorum generalium fundatam. De scripturis chartaceis (sic loquens: Ha, inquit, priores illius INDIGVERVNT confirmatione: quod ista sint litera MORTVA, scripta atramento, in membrana, vel charcharta: quam si quis vel truncare velit, vel torquere, nihil sentit. Proinde est instar vaginæ, quæ quemlibet gladium admittit, non modo chalybeum, sed etiam plumbeum, ligneum, æneum. Itane igitur mentitur Pareus? an potius Iesuita frontem perdidit?
units.tr: COSTERUS the Jesuit, a stout champion, feigns a threefold Holy Scripture: one spiritual, inscribed by the Spirit on the mind of the Church or of the ministers; another left by the apostles to the Church, in paper books and parchment, written in ink; and a third founded on the decrees of the Popes and of the general councils. Speaking of the paper Scriptures, he says: "Ah, the former have NOT DESERVED confirmation, because they are a DEAD letter, written in ink on parchment or paper, which, if anyone wishes to cut or twist it, feels nothing. Therefore it is like a sheath, which admits any sword, not only of steel but also of lead, wood or bronze." Does Pareus then lie? Or rather has the Jesuit lost all shame?

units.la: Quin imò scabiosius scripturam sacram proscindunt. Linda Nus ille ex scriptura disputantes comparat Serram ligneam trahentibus, quibus fatigatis nullus sit elusionum finis.
units.tr: Indeed, they tear Scripture to pieces even more scurrilously. That same Lindanus compares those who dispute from Scripture to men pulling a wooden saw, after whose exhaustion there is no end to evasions.

units.la: Hosius libro De expresso Dei verbo per totum hæc tractat themata: Ex scripturis sacris disputare, est hæreticorum prius: non esse ex scripturis cum hæreticis congrediendum: Scripturas facere hæreticos: Expressum Dei verbum ab hæreticis (Euangelicis) contra omnium, hoc est, Ecclesiæ Pontificiæ sensum prolatum, esse expressum verbum diaboli, &c. Taceamus nefanda alia, quæ profectò nec Judæi legi Mosis, nec Mahumetani suo Alcorano impunè irrogarent: Romani Sibyllinis irrogata olim capitalius vindicassent. Pro talibus interim meritis, quibus illi Euangelicis nervos scilicet præcidisse visi sunt, unus trabeam Episcopalem, alter galerum Cardinalitium à Pontifice præmium tulit. O quid vobis scriptura vestra? ridenti isti. Sed ne glorieris in malitia tua: est potens misericordia Dei omni die, Psalm. 51. vers. 3.
units.tr: Hosius, in his book On the Expressed Word of God, treats these themes throughout: to dispute from the Scriptures is first of the heretics; one should not engage with heretics from the Scriptures; the Scriptures make heretics; the expressed Word of God, put forward by heretics (the Evangelicals) against the sense of everyone, that is, of the Papal Church, is the expressed word of the devil, and so on. Let me pass over the other unspeakable things, which surely neither the Jews would impose on the law of Moses, nor the Mahometans on their Alcoran, without punishment; the Romans would once have punished with greater severity those things imposed on the Sibylline books. For such merits, by which those men seem to have cut the sinews of the Evangelicals, one received an episcopal robe, another a cardinal's hat as a reward from the Pope. O what has your Scripture done for you, you who laugh? But do not boast in your malice: the mercy of God endures every day, Psalm 51:3.

units.la: At, inquit Iesuita, confictum est à Pareo, Wittakero, & similibus deformatis, in Papatu scripturas tantum valere, quantum fabulæ Æsopi, nisi accederet testimonium Ecclesiæ: Papam præferre Ecclesiam scriptura: in Papatu negari, verbum Dei rectè credendi & viuendi normam esse vel regulam.
units.tr: But, says the Jesuit, Pareus, Wittaker and similar deformed men have fabricated that in the Papacy Scriptures are worth as much as the fables of Aesop, unless the testimony of the Church were added; that the Pope puts the Church before Scripture; and that in the Papacy it is denied that the Word of God is rightly the rule of believing and living.

units.la: Respondeo, nihil horum in themate sæculari vobis obiectum. Quid igitur dissimulatis vere obiectis, de his insuper Papatum accusas? Tege, si sapis, hæc vlcera Babylonis tuæ.
units.tr: I reply: none of these things has been charged against you in this secular theme. Why then do you conceal the things truly charged, and accuse the Papacy of these additional ones? Cover up these ulcers of your Babylon, if you are wise.

units.la: Primum de fabulis Æsopi Brentius objecit Petro Asoto, Monacho Dominicano Anno 1556. Plane, inquit, de sacra scriptura idem se sentire haud obscurè significat, quod alius quispiam Asoticus scripsit, scripturam valere, quantum Fabulæ Æsopi, si destituatur authoritate Ecclesiæ.
units.tr: First, Brentius objected to Peter Soto, a Dominican monk, in the year 1556 concerning the fables of Aesop. Clearly, he says, he indicates with no little obscurity that his view of Holy Scripture is the same as that of some other Sotist who wrote that Scripture is worth as much as the fables of Aesop, if it is deprived of the authority of the Church.

units.la: Cui respondens Hosius Anno 1557. Et potuit tamen, inquit illud pio sensu dici, quem homo pius, qui charitatem habet, quæ non cogitat malum, ex iis verbis elicteret. Nam revera nisi nos Ecclesia doceret authoritas, hanc scripturam esse Canonicam, perexiguum apud nos pondus haberet.
units.tr: Hosius replied to him in the year 1557: "Yet it could be said in a godly sense, which a pious man who has charity, which thinks no evil, might draw from those words. For indeed, unless the authority of the Church taught us that this Scripture is canonical, it would have very little weight with us."

units.la: Dic sodes: quod Hosius tantus Ecclesiæ Papalis cardo pio sensu dici posse fatetur, tu Papatum sentire negabis? Dic, inter, tantum valere, quantum fabulæ Æsopi, quantum interest? Alterum vlcus miramur te tangere, quod praecipui vestri quasi scopulum in mari libenter refugiunt. Bellarminus sic tetigit, vt Conciliorum quidem decreta veritate, infallibilitate, & authoritate Canonica Euangeliis & scripturis sacris exaequet: Papam vero longè supra Conciliorum decreta euehat. Quomodo igitur Papa juxta Bellarminum non praefertur scripturae?
units.tr: Tell me, pray: when Hosius, so great a hinge of the Papal Church, admits that it can be said in a godly sense, will you deny that the Papacy holds it? Tell me, between being worth as much as the fables of Aesop and what difference is there? Next, we marvel that you touch on an ulcer which your chief men gladly flee, as if it were a reef in the sea. Bellarmine touched it in such a way that he indeed equates the decrees of the councils with the Gospels and the holy Scriptures in truth, infallibility and canonical authority, but he raises the Pope far above the decrees of the councils. How then, according to Bellarmine, is the Pope not preferred to Scripture?

units.la: Tertium etsi ignoramus, quis ita vt tu profers, vobis objiciat, tamen profecto verum est. Nam juxta eundem Cardinalem verbum Dei scriptum non est, nisi partialis recte credendi & viuendi Regula. Partialis verò regula est nulla regula, si regulae natura vrgeatur. Regula enim seu norma (Graece κανὼν[?]) est mensura infallibilis, additionem vel diminutionem nullam requirens vel admittens, ad hoc, vt sit regula: prout à Basilio & Varino regulam definiri, non ignorat Iesuita. Si igitur in Papatu verbum Dei scriptum tantum partialis est recte credendi & viuendi regula, additionem Traditionum non admittens tantum, sed omninò requirens, sequitur in Papatu negari, quod iste mentitur à Pareo confictum, verbum Dei scriptum esse recte credendi viundique regulam.
units.tr: Third, although we do not know who objects to you as you put it, yet it is certainly true. For according to the same Cardinal, the written Word of God is only a partial rule of believing and living. But a partial rule is no rule at all, if the nature of a rule is urged. For a rule or norm (in Greek kanōn [κανὼν]) is an infallible measure, requiring or admitting no addition or subtraction, in order to be a rule; as the Jesuit is not unaware is how Basil and Varinus define a rule. If therefore in the Papacy the written Word of God is only a partial rule of believing and living, not merely admitting additions of traditions but absolutely requiring them, it follows that in the Papacy it is denied what this man lies was fabricated by Pareus, that the written Word of God is the rule of believing and living.

units.la: XXII. Denique quod Irenaeus de haereticis antiquis scripsit, cum ex scripturis arguitur Papatus Rom. in accusationem conuertitur ipsarum scripturarum, quasi non recte habeant, neque sint ex authoritate: & quia variè sint dictae: & quia non possit ex his inueniri veritas, qui nesciunt Traditionem.
units.tr: XXII. Finally, what Irenaeus wrote about the ancient heretics: when the Roman Papacy is argued against from the Scriptures, the accusation is turned back against the Scriptures themselves, as if they were not rightly held, nor were of authority; and because they are variously interpreted; and because the truth cannot be found from them by those who do not know the tradition.

units.la: XXIII. Papatus igitur Rom. tot modis principium fidei, quae creditur, conuellendo & blasphemando, à fide defecit, fidem & salutem sibi & suis euertit.
units.tr: XXIII. Thus the Roman Papacy, by overturning and blaspheming in so many ways the principle of the faith which is believed, has fallen away from the faith and has undone both its own faith and salvation and that of its own people.

units.la: ASSERTIO.
units.tr: ASSERTION.

units.la: Si hodie Irenaeus antiquissimus ille scripturarum divinarum adversus haereticos assertor praesentes nostras videret controversias: quid, censes, aliud in Papatum Romanum diceret, quàm quod in sui temporis haereticos Traditionarios scripsit? eos cum ex scripturis arguuntur, congressum non ferre, sed in accusatione conuertit ipsarum scripturarum, eamque triplicem, quod non sint ex authoritate, quod sint varie dicta, obscura, flexiloqua: quod denique imperfecta, non omnem veritatem continentes: tandem vero in Traditione, quam scripturis perfectiorem ab Apostolis acceperint, pedem figere. A centum profecto jam annis omnes Papatus magistri hoc argumentum non alia tractarunt ratione, quam quæ olim fuit hæreticis propria. Quoties enim à nostris ex scripturis arguuntur, nonne congressionem illi dissuadent, SERRAM LIGNEAM nobiscum trahendam frustra non esse? nonne in accusationem conuertuntur ipsarum scripturarum: quod non sint ex authoritate, nisi quantum eius habent ab Ecclesia: quod sint obscurissimæ varieque dictæ: quod non possit ex illis inueniri omnis veritas, vtpote imperfectis? nonne tandem in traditionem exit omnis disceptatio? Videantur Bellarmini, Stapletoni, Lindani, Hosij, Valentiani, & aliorum de scriptura sacra disceptationes, atque discursus. Intelligit igitur Papatus, quibus Synagoga scholastica & Canonistica hac parte successerit: quodque principium fidei quæ creditur modis tam indignis conuellendo & blasphemando à fide defecerit, sibique & suis viam salutis inuiam reddiderit.
units.tr: If the most ancient defender of the divine Scriptures against heretics, Irenaeus, were to see our present controversies today, what do you think he would say about the Roman Papacy, other than what he wrote against the Traditionalist heretics of his own time? When those heretics were refuted from the Scriptures, they would not endure the contest but turned the accusation against the Scriptures themselves, and did so in three ways: that the Scriptures are not authoritative, that they are expressed in varied, obscure and ambiguous words, and finally that they are imperfect and do not contain the whole truth. At last they took their stand on a Tradition, which they said they had received from the Apostles as more perfect than the Scriptures. For a hundred years now, indeed, all the teachers of the Papacy have treated this argument in no other way than the one that was once peculiar to the heretics. Whenever they are refuted from the Scriptures by our side, do they not dissuade them from the contest, saying that it is pointless to drag a wooden saw along with us? Do they not turn the accusation against the Scriptures themselves: that they have authority only insofar as they have it from the Church; that they are most obscure and expressed in varied ways; that, being imperfect, they cannot yield the whole truth? Does not every dispute finally end in Tradition? Let the disputations and arguments of Bellarmine, Stapleton, Lindanus, Hosius, Valentianus and others on Holy Scripture be consulted. The Papacy therefore understands in what respects the scholastic and canonist Synagogue has succeeded them: and that by overthrowing and blaspheming in such unworthy ways the principle of the faith which is believed, it has fallen away from the faith and made the way of salvation impassable for itself and its own.

units.la: XXIV. Secvndo, fidem saluificam, quâ creditur ad justitiam, conuellere, & ex hominum cordibus euellere, est à fide deficere, fidem omnem salutemque sibi & aliis euertere.
units.tr: XXIV. Secondly, to overthrow the saving faith by which one believes unto righteousness, and to tear it out of men's hearts, is to fall from the faith and to overthrow all faith and salvation, both for oneself and for others.

units.la: XXV. Fides saluifica, qua creditur ad justitiam, est non solum notitia vel assensus eorum, quæ de Deo & Christo scripta sunt in verbo Dei, sed cumprimis fiducia promissionis Euangelij de remissione peccatorum propter Christi meritum.
units.tr: XXV. The saving faith by which one believes unto righteousness is not merely knowledge or assent to those things which are written about God and Christ in the Word of God, but above all trust in the promise of the Gospel concerning the forgiveness of sins for the sake of Christ's merit.

units.la: XXVI. Nec enim hæret in cerebro, sed radicatur in corde: quia corde creditur ad iustitiam, Rom.10,11.
units.tr: XXVI. For it does not cling in the brain but is rooted in the heart, because "with the heart one believes unto righteousness" (Rom. 10:10).

units.la: XXVII. Vnde Apostolus fidem definit substantiam eorum, quæ sperantur: quia obiecta sperata facit in mentibus & cordibus nostris quasi realiter præsentia existere.
units.tr: XXVII. Hence the Apostle defines faith as "the substance of things hoped for" (Heb. 11:1), because it makes the objects hoped for exist in our minds and hearts as if they were actually present.

units.la: XXVIII. Et elenchum eorum, quæ non apparent: quia de his conuincit mentes ad certum assensum, & corda ad certam fiduciam.
units.tr: XXVIII. And "the evidence of things not seen," because it convinces the minds to a sure assent and the hearts to a sure trust concerning these things.

units.la: XXIX. Inde & Augustinus de fide & symb. cap. 1. Profiteamur ore fidem, quam corde gestamus.
units.tr: XXIX. Hence also Augustine, in his book On Faith and the Creed, chapter 1: "Let us confess with the mouth the faith which we bear in the heart."

units.la: XXX. In solo cerebro hærens fides sine cordis fiducia, vel quæ per charitatem non est efficax, inanis,
units.tr: XXX. Faith that clings only to the brain, without trust of the heart, or that is not effective through love, is empty,

units.la: Rom.10.10. Hebr. 11, 1. anis, & mortua est, hypocritarum & dæmonum propria.
units.tr: (Rom. 10:10; Heb. 11:1) and dead, the peculiar property of hypocrites and demons.

units.la: XXXI. Sic enim credere, Deum esse Deum, & Christum esse Christum, non magis te jurat, quam credere, Venetias esse opulentissimam vrbem, in qua tamen tibi nulla sit domus.
units.tr: XXXI. For to believe in this way that God is God and that Christ is Christ profits you no more than to believe that Venice is a very wealthy city, though you have no house there.

units.la: XXXII. Hanc fidem saluificam, qua creditur ad justitiam, Papatus Rom. non vno modo, sed variè conuellit, atque ex cordibus hominum euellit.
units.tr: XXXII. The Papacy overthrows this saving faith, by which one believes unto righteousness, not in one way only but in various ways, and tears it out of the hearts of men.

units.la: XXXIII. Fidem saluificam vult esse non tam notitiam, quàm ignorantiam cum assensu implicito eorum, quæ credit Ecclesia.
units.tr: XXXIII. It wants saving faith to be not so much knowledge as ignorance joined with an implicit assent to what the Church believes.

units.la: ASSERTIO.
units.tr: ASSERTION.

units.la: Hæc Themata vniuersa, quibus fidei justificantis & saluificæ natura explicatur, Jesuita conuellere nec potuit, nec tentauit. Quædam verò mendaciis & calumniis eludere ita conatur, vt magis exasperet ulcera Papatus. PRIMO dicit: MENTITVR PAREVS, Apostolicæ definitioni contrarium esse, quod docet Papatus: Fidem Christianam notitiam esse. Sed mentitur Jesuita, Pareum hoc Papatui objcere.
units.tr: The Jesuit has been able neither to overthrow nor even to attempt to overthrow all these theses, by which the nature of justifying and saving faith is explained. Some of them, however, he tries to evade with lies and calumnies, so that he only irritates the sores of the Papacy the more. FIRST, he says: PAREUS LIES, that what the Papacy teaches is contrary to the Apostolic definition: that Christian faith is knowledge. But the Jesuit lies in charging this against Pareus to the Papacy.

units.la: Hucusque ASSERTIO Thematis secularis reperta est in liturariis Pareanis. Reliquæ enim chartæ in direptione Bibliothecæ, quæ ab impro-bis manibus Heidelbergæ facta est, perierunt.
units.tr: So far the Assertion of the Secular Thesis has been found among the papers of Pareus. The remaining papers perished in the plundering of the library which was carried out at Heidelberg by wicked hands.

units.la: SEQVVNTVR THEMATA CÆTERA.
units.tr: THE REMAINING THESES FOLLOW.

units.la: XXXIV. Fidem saluificam esse fiduciam misericordiæ Dei, pro hæresi damnat.
units.tr: XXXIV. He condemns as heresy the claim that saving faith is trust in the mercy of God.

units.la: XXXV. Fidem justificantem à dilectione, & ab omni virtute spirituali & morali separabilem esse contendit.
units.tr: XXXV. He contends that justifying faith is separable from love and from every spiritual and moral virtue.

units.la: XXXVI. Fidei certitudinem nullam concedit, nisi coniecturalem, qualis est opinionis.
units.tr: XXXVI. He grants no certainty of faith except a conjectural one, such as belongs to opinion.

units.la: XXXVII. De qua nemo certus esse apud se possit, nisi eam habeat, nisi opinabiliter.
units.tr: XXXVII. No one can be certain about it within himself unless he holds it only in an opinionative way.

units.la: XXXVIII. Multo minus certo confidere de gratia Dei, & remissione peccatorum, justificatione, & salute sua. XXXIX. Quia semper coniuncta sit cum anxietate, formidine deceptionis, dubitatione.
units.tr: XXXVIII. Much less can one trust with certainty in the grace of God, the remission of sins, one's justification and one's salvation. XXXIX. Because it is always joined with anxiety, fear of deception and doubt.

units.la: XL. Quæ profecto non est fides peccatoré erigens, sed opinio conscientiæ dubias crucians.
units.tr: XL. Which surely is not faith that raises up the sinner, but an opinion of the conscience that torments it with doubts.

units.la: XLI. Debuerunt enim locustæ abyssi cruciare homines mentes quinque.
units.tr: XLI. For the locusts of the abyss were to torment men for five months (Rev. 9:5).

units.la: XLII. Quin est hæsitatio, Deum mendacij arguens, blasphemans.
units.tr: XLII. Indeed, hesitation is a blasphemy that accuses God of lying.

units.la: XLIII. Papatus igitur fidem saluificam, qua creditur ad justitiam, tot modis conuellendo, à fide defecit, fidem omnem sibi & suis euertit.
units.tr: XLIII. Therefore the Papacy, by overthrowing in so many ways the saving faith by which one believes unto righteousness, has fallen from the faith and overthrown all faith for itself and its own.

units.la: XLIV. Tertio, euertere fundamentum salutis de justificatione fidei, per imputatam Christi justitiam & meritum, absque operibus, est à fide Euangelij deficere, salutem euertere.
units.tr: XLIV. Thirdly, to overthrow the foundation of salvation, which lies in the justification of faith through the imputed righteousness and merit of Christ, without works, is to fall from the faith of the Gospel and to overthrow salvation.

units.la: XLV. Dicit enim Apostolus: Constituimus igitur, fide hominem iustificari absque operibus legis.
units.tr: XLV. For the Apostle says: We conclude, therefore, that a man is justified by faith without the works of the law (Rom. 3:28).

units.la: XLVI. Et: Beatus, cui DEVS imputat iustitiam absque operibus.
units.tr: XLVI. And: Blessed is the man to whom God imputes righteousness without works (Rom. 4:6).

units.la: XLVII. Et: Iustificati fide pacem habemus apud Deum.
units.tr: XLVII. And: Being justified by faith, we have peace with God (Rom. 5:1).

units.la: XLVIII. Et: Per vnius (Christi) iustitiam (gratia redundat) in omnes homines, ad iustificationem vitæ.
units.tr: XLVIII. And: Through the righteousness of one (Christ) grace abounds unto all men, to the justification of life (Rom. 5:18).

units.la: XLIX. Et: Scientes, hominem non iustificari operibus legis, nisi per fidem Iesu Christi.
units.tr: XLIX. And: Knowing that a man is not justified by the works of the law, but by faith in Jesus Christ (Gal. 2:16).

units.la: L. Quotquot vero sub operibus legis sunt (seu operibus justificari volunt) sub exsecratione sunt.
units.tr: L. But as many as are under the works of the law (or wish to be justified by works) are under the curse (Gal. 3:10).

units.la: LI. Hoc fundamentum salutis non vno modo sed varie euertit Papatus Rom.
units.tr: LI. The Papacy overthrows this foundation of salvation not in one way only but in various ways.

units.la: LII. Negat contra Apostolum, hominem justificari fide absque operibus.
units.tr: LII. It denies, against the Apostle, that a man is justified by faith without works.

units.la: LIII. Credentibus, se imputatione justitiæ Christi justificari, absq; operibus, anathema dicit.
units.tr: LIII. It pronounces anathema on those who believe that they are justified without works by the imputation of the righteousness of Christ.

units.la: LIV. Docet, nos per fidem non justificari; sed ad justificationem disponi.
units.tr: LIV. It teaches that we are not justified through faith, but are disposed to justification.

units.la: LV. Docet, charitatem (quæ in sanctis fere est glaglacies, nedum perfectio) esse habitum perfectæ justitiæ.
units.tr: LV. It teaches that charity (which in the saints is scarcely a spark, let alone perfection) is the habit of perfect righteousness.

units.la: LVI. Docet, se perfectione virtutum seu bonorum operum justificari.
units.tr: LVI. It teaches that one is justified by the perfection of virtues or good works.

units.la: LVII. Quæ fides olim Philosophorum & Pharisæorum, hodie Turcarum & Judæorum est, mutato Christi nomine.
units.tr: LVII. This faith was once that of the philosophers and Pharisees, and today it is that of the Turks and Jews, with only the name of Christ changed.

units.la: LVIII. Docet, Christum nobis meritum esse vim metendi; nostrum esse, hac vi ex merito Christi fluente, mereri vitam æternam.
units.tr: LVIII. It teaches that Christ is merely a power of meriting for us, and that it is ours, by this power flowing from the merit of Christ, to merit eternal life.

units.la: LIX. Sic meritum Christi blasphemat, pro eo sua propria merita substituens.
units.tr: LIX. In this way it blasphemes the merit of Christ, substituting its own merits in its place.

units.la: LX. Sic homines, cum ex meritis suis superbia inflatos in cœlum tollit, in infernum præcipitat: quod cum Alcorano & Thalmud commune habet.
units.tr: LX. In this way, when it has lifted men puffed up with pride from their own merits into heaven, it hurls them down into hell; and this it has in common with the Koran and the Talmud.

units.la: LXI. Papatus Romanus igitur fundamentum salutis de justificatione peccatoris coram Deo tot modis convellendo, à fide Euangelij defecit, salutem sibi & suis euertit.
units.tr: LXI. The Papacy, therefore, by overthrowing in so many ways the foundation of salvation, which is the justification of the sinner before God, has fallen from the faith of the Gospel and overthrown salvation for itself and its own.

units.la: LXII. Quarto defendere dogmata falsa, impia, blasphema, scripturis sacris, & fundamento fidei repugnantia, est à fide deficere, salutem euertere.
units.tr: LXII. Fourthly, to defend false, impious and blasphemous doctrines that are opposed to the Holy Scriptures and to the foundation of the faith is to fall from the faith and overthrow salvation.

units.la: LXIII. Talia innumera (præter modo dicta) defendit Papa Rom. Exemplo sint hæc pauca:
units.tr: LXIII. The Pope of Rome defends countless such doctrines besides those just mentioned. Let these few serve as examples:

units.la: LXIV. Defendit corruptionem ex lapsu Adæ, seu peccatum originale, non consistere in aliqua prava qualitate, nec esse culpam, sed culpæ pœnam, & vitium, quale est curuitas in digito vel tibia: esse non contra, sed præter legem, contra scripturam: Omne figmentum cordis humani prauum ab iuuentute.
units.tr: LXIV. He defends the view that the corruption resulting from the fall of Adam, or original sin, does not consist in some depraved quality, nor is it guilt, but the punishment of guilt, and a defect, like a crookedness in a finger or shin; that it is not against the law but beside the law, and against Scripture: Every imagination of the thoughts of man's heart is evil from his youth (Gen. 8:21).

units.la: LXV. Et aliud, peccata quædam natura sua esse venialia, non pœna, sed venia digna, contra scripturam: Stipendium peccati mors.
units.tr: LXV. And another (claim): that certain sins are by their nature venial, deserving not punishment but pardon, against Scripture: The wages of sin is death (Rom. 6:23).

units.la: LXVI. Ex his aliud falsum: Liberum arbitrium hominis animalis non esse seruum peccati, contra scripturam: Cum essetis serui peccati.
units.tr: LXVI. From these comes another falsehood: that the free will of natural man is not a slave of sin, against Scripture: When you were the slaves of sin (Rom. 6:20).

units.la: LXVII. Et, posse ex se cooperari gratiæ primæ: contrà scripturam: Cum essetis mortui in peccatis: Prudentia carnis non potest subijci legi Dei.
units.tr: LXVII. And that it can of itself cooperate with first grace, against Scripture: When you were dead in sins (Eph. 2:1); The wisdom of the flesh cannot be subject to the law of God (Rom. 8:7).

units.la: LXVIII. Et, ex duobus verbi auditoribus vnum credere, quia voluit: alterum non credere, quia non voluit cooperari gratiæ, contra scripturam: Quid habes, quod non accepisti?
units.tr: LXVIII. And that of two hearers of the Word, one believes because he willed to, and the other does not believe because he did not will to cooperate with grace, contrary to Scripture: What have you that you did not receive?

units.la: LXIX. Et aliud falsum. Gratiam Dei, qua dicimur saluari, esse influxum generalem, indifferentem, qui hominis animalis arbitrio bene & male possit specificari.
units.tr: LXIX. And another falsehood: that the grace of God by which we are said to be saved is a general, indifferent influence, which can be specified for good or evil by the free choice of the natural man.

units.la: LXX. Vel esse influxum specialem quidem, sed suasorium, cuius efficacia sit in hominis arbitrio, contra scripturam: Deus dat velle & perficere. Nemo potest venire ad me, nisi Pater traxerit eum.
units.tr: LXX. Or that it is indeed a special influence, but merely persuasive, whose efficacy lies in the human will, contrary to Scripture: God gives to will and to work. No one can come to me unless the Father draw him.

units.la: LXXI. Rursum aliud falsum, impium, Deum, quos præ-destinauit ad gloriam, prædestinasse ex præuisis meritis, seu post & propter præuisa merita, contra scripturam: Antequam pueri quicquam boni, vel mali fecissent. Elegit nos ante iacta mundi fundamenta, vt essemus sancti & inculpati. Elegit nos secundum propositum voluntatis suæ in laudem gloriosæ gratiæ suæ.
units.tr: LXXI. Again another false and impious claim: that God predestined to glory those whom he foreknew on account of foreseen merits, or predestined them after and because of foreseen merits, contrary to Scripture: Before the children had done anything good or bad. He chose us before the foundation of the world, that we should be holy and blameless. He chose us according to the purpose of his will, to the praise of the glory of his grace.

units.la: LXXII. Quod Pelagianum somnium non prædestinatio, sed postdestinatio dicendum esset.
units.tr: LXXII. This Pelagian dream ought to be called not predestination but postdestination.

units.la: LXXIII. Rursus aliud falsum, impium, se posse legem Dei absolute implere, contra illud: In multis labimur omnes. Et: Quod legi erat impossibile.
units.tr: LXXIII. Again another false and impious claim: that a man can fulfil the law of God absolutely, contrary to: In many things we all stumble. And: What was impossible for the law.

units.la: LXXIV. Quin, se posse plus præstare, quàm ex lege debeant præstare, contra scripturam: Cum omnia fecerit is, dicite serui inutiles sumus, quod debuimus fecimus.
units.tr: LXXIV. Indeed, that a man can perform more than he is bound to perform by the law, contrary to Scripture: When you have done all that is commanded, say: we are unprofitable servants; we have done only what we ought to have done.

units.la: LXXV. Quin &, se posse absque omni peccato esse in hac vita, si velint, contra scripturam: Profecto non est iustus in terra, qui faciat bonum, & non peccet.
units.tr: LXXV. Indeed also, that one can be without any sin in this life, if he wishes, contrary to Scripture: Surely there is not a righteous man on earth who does good and does not sin.

units.la: LXXVI. Id olim Pelagiani iactantes, jubebantur ex precatione delere: Dimitte nobis peccata nostra: vel officiose mentiri, Deo illudere.
units.tr: LXXVI. The Pelagians, boasting of this, were ordered to strike it out of their prayer: Forgive us our sins; or else to lie dutifully and mock God.

units.la: LXXVII. Et aliud falsum, impium, se bonis operibus mereti vitam æternam ex condigno, contra scripturam: Donum Dei vita æterna.
units.tr: LXXVII. Another false and impious claim: that by good works one merits eternal life as of condign merit, contrary to Scripture: The gift of God is eternal life.

units.la: LXXVIII. Aliud quoque falsum, se in bonis operibus posse fiduciam collocare in judicio D E I, contra sacram Scripturam: Domine, si peccata observaueris, quis sustinebit?
units.tr: LXXVIII. Another false claim: that one can place confidence in good works at the judgment of God, contrary to holy Scripture: Lord, if you should mark iniquities, who shall stand?

units.la: LXXIX. Et aliud blasphemum, se meritis suis Deum facere sibi debitorem, adeo, ut nisi reddat vitam æternam, sit injustus, qui scilicet super injuriis conueniri possit, contra scripturas: Debitores sumus. Quis prior dedit ei, & retribuet illi? O homo, quis tu es, qui respondes Deo?
units.tr: LXXIX. And another blasphemous claim: that by his merits a man makes God his debtor, so that unless God gives him eternal life, God would be unjust, and could indeed be sued for injuries, contrary to the Scriptures: We are debtors. Who has first given to him, that it should be repaid to him? O man, who are you that answers back to God?

units.la: LXXX. Æquè blasphemum, non solum Christum esse Mediatorem, sed & sanctos à Papa canonizatos intercedere pro nobis vt mediatores in cœlis, contra scripturam: Vnus Mediator D E I & hominum, Homo Christus Iesus.
units.tr: LXXX. Equally blasphemous: not only that Christ is the Mediator, but also that saints canonized by the Pope intercede for us as mediators in heaven, contrary to Scripture: One Mediator between God and men, the man Christ Jesus.

units.la: LXXXI. Quale & hoc, decedentes in fide, vadere in ignem purgatorium, ad luenda peccata venialia, contra Euangelium: Beati, qui in Domino moriuntur à modo. Qui credit in me, habet vitam æternam, nec venit in iudicium, sed transit de morte in vitam.
units.tr: LXXXI. Similar to this is the claim that those who die in faith go into the purgatorial fire to pay for venial sins, contrary to the Gospel: Blessed are the dead who die in the Lord from now on. He who believes in me has eternal life, and does not come into judgment, but passes from death to life.

units.la: LXXXII. Et aliud falsum, hypocriticum, sacramenta divinitus instituta non esse signa gratiæ, fidem confirmantia, sed vasa gratiam continentia & conferentia ex opere operato, contra scripturam: Abraham accepit signum circumcisionis sigillum iustitiæ fidei.
units.tr: LXXXII. Another false and hypocritical claim: that the sacraments divinely instituted are not signs of grace confirming faith, but vessels containing and conferring grace ex opere operato, contrary to Scripture: Abraham received the sign of circumcision, a seal of the righteousness of faith.

units.la: LXXXIII. Nec non illud de septem sacramentis noui Testamenti, Euangelio & veteri Ecclesiæ ignotis.
units.tr: LXXXIII. Nor is that doctrine of seven sacraments of the New Testament, which was unknown to the Gospel and to the ancient Church.

units.la: LXXXIV. Illud quoque de cibis prohibitis, quod in nouo Testamento Apostolus diabolicum pronunciat.
units.tr: LXXXIV. Nor is that about forbidden foods, which the Apostle in the New Testament pronounces to be diabolical.

units.la: LXXXV. Tale & dogma, prohibens Episcopis matrimonium, contra scripturam: Episcopus sit vnius vxoris maritus.
units.tr: LXXXV. Likewise the dogma forbidding bishops to marry, contrary to Scripture: A bishop must be the husband of one wife.

units.la: LXXXVI. Et illud falsum atque blasphemum, Sacerdotes consecratione sua quinqueuerbia hostiam Missæ transubstantiare in verum corpus Christi, & quotidie id Deo Patri sanctificare atque destruere, pro peccatis viuentium in terra, & mortuorum in cœlo & purgatorio, contra scripturas: Christus amplius non moritur. Vna oblatione consummauit omnes.
units.tr: LXXXVI. And that false and blasphemous claim: that priests, by their consecration in five words, transubstantiate the host of the Mass into the true body of Christ, and daily offer and sacrifice it to God the Father for the sins of the living on earth and of the dead in heaven and purgatory, contrary to Scripture: Christ dies no more. By one offering he has made perfect all.

units.la: LXXXVII. Et quis falsa, impia, blasphema alia, de calice laicis sacrilegè surrepto, de contritionibus, confessionibus, satisfactionibus, indulgentiis, jubilæis, feriis, jejunijs, &c. enumeret?
units.tr: LXXXVII. And who could list the other false, impious and blasphemous claims: concerning the chalice sacrilegiously withheld from the laity, concerning contrition, confessions, satisfactions, indulgences, jubilees, holy days, fasts, and so on?

units.la: LXXXVIII. Papatus Rom. igitur tot falsa, impia, blasphema dogmata tuendo à fide defecit, fidem & salutem sibi & suis euertit.
units.tr: LXXXVIII. The Roman Papacy, therefore, by defending so many false, impious and blasphemous dogmas, has fallen away from the faith, and has overthrown faith and salvation for itself and for its followers.

units.la: LXXXIX. Quam apostasiā à fide diserte prædixit Spiritus, fore, vt posterem temporib. deficiant quidam à fide, attendentes spiritib. deceptoribus, & doctrinis dæmoniorum falsiloquidentes spiritib. deceptoribus, & doctrinis dæmoniorum falsiloquium, prohibentium nubere, & abstinere (iubentium) à cibis, quorum, prohibentium nubere, & abstinere (iubentium) à cibis, quos Deus creauit ad participandum cum gratiarum actione, &c.
units.tr: LXXXIX. This apostasy from the faith the Spirit expressly foretold, that in later times some would fall away from the faith, giving heed to deceiving spirits and doctrines of demons, speaking lies in hypocrisy, forbidding marriage, and commanding abstinence from foods which God created to be received with thanksgiving, etc.

units.la: XC. Quam & Apostolus prædixit, futuram ἀποστασίαν revelati hominis peccati, & filij perditionis, hoc est, Antichristi.
units.tr: XC. The Apostle also foretold the coming apostasy [ἀποστασίαν] of the revealed man of sin and son of perdition, that is, of Antichrist.

units.la: XCI. Hic est ingens ille terræ motus, quo Sol justitiæ Christus factus est niger vt saccus cilicinus: luna Ecclesia conuersa est in sanguinem; stellæ Episcopi cecidesunt de cœlo in terram: expansum scripturæ conuolutum abscessit: visione secunda Apocalypseos.
units.tr: XCI. This is that great earthquake by which the Sun of righteousness, Christ, became black as a sackcloth of hair; the moon, the Church, was turned into blood; the stars, the bishops, fell from heaven to earth; and the expanse of Scripture, rolled up like a scroll, departed. Second vision of the Apocalypse.

units.la: XCII. Hic ille pestilens fumus, quinta tuba clangente exputeo abyssi per stellam apostaticâ Antichristü aperto emergens, atrum illud Papalium decretaliū, & Theologiæ scholasticæ fascinum, quo sol justitiæ, Christus, & aer doctrinæ cœlestis obscuratus, innumeraq; locustaiū clericalium & monasticarum, vireta ecclesiæ depascentium, hominesq; cruciantium, infecta, orbi Christiano inuecta sunt. visione tertia Apocalypseos.
units.tr: XCII. This is that pestilent smoke which rose from the pit of the abyss when the fifth trumpet sounded, through the apostate star that had been opened to Antichrist: the dark spell of the Papal decretals and of scholastic theology, by which the Sun of righteousness, Christ, and the air of heavenly doctrine were obscured. Innumerable locusts of clerics and monks, devouring the green pastures of the Church and tormenting men, were brought in and infected the Christian world. Third vision of the Apocalypse.

units.la: XCIII. Hæc illa grandia & blasphema (sed nondum omnia) ad quæ bestia marina os suum aperuit: & illa loquela Draconica bestiæ terrenæ, duo agni cornua præferentis, visione quarta Apocalypseos.
units.tr: XCIII. These are those great and blasphemous things (but not yet all of them) at which the sea beast opened its mouth, and that dragon-like speech of the earthly beast which bore the two horns of a lamb. Fourth vision of the Apocalypse.

units.la: XCIV. Hæ tenebræ illæ, quibus, phiala quinta super thronum bestiæ effusa, regnum eius factum est tenebrosum, &c. visione quinta Apocalypseos.
units.tr: XCIV. These are those darknesses by which, when the fifth bowl was poured out on the throne of the beast, his kingdom became dark, etc. Fifth vision of the Apocalypse.

units.la: XCV. Habemus Papatus Romani apostasiam à fide, olim per angelum B. Johanni prænunciatum: seculo autem hactenus reuoluto, renascentis Euangelij luce retractam.
units.tr: XCV. We have the apostasy of the Roman Papacy from the faith, announced long ago to the blessed John by an angel; but now, the century having come round again, it has been brought back to light by the radiance of the renewed Gospel.

units.la: XCVI. Quæ CAVSA PRIMA vrgentissima fuit patribus nostris deserendi, nobis est fugiendi Papatus Rom. Sicque concluditur:
units.tr: XCVI. What was the most pressing first cause for our fathers in forsaking the Papacy is for us a cause for fleeing from the Roman Papacy. Thus the argument is concluded:

units.la: XCVII. Ecclesia apostatica à fide est deserenda, fugienda. Quæ enim communio luci & tenebris?
units.tr: XCVII. A Church that is apostate from the faith must be forsaken and fled from. For what communion has light with darkness?

units.la: XCVIII. Papatus Romanus est Ecclesia defectrix à fide, vt præcessit.
units.tr: XCVIII. The Roman Papacy is a Church that has defected from the faith, as has been shown above.

units.la: XCIX. Papatus Romanus igitur fuit deserendus, est fugiendus.
units.tr: XCIX. Therefore the Roman Papacy was to be forsaken, and is to be fled from.

units.la: II. Horribilis idololatria Papatus Romani.
units.tr: II. The horrible idolatry of the Roman Papacy.

units.la: C. Deus solus est religione colendus:
units.tr: C. God alone is to be worshipped with religion.

units.la: CI. Religio enim Lactantio est vinculum pietatis, quo DEO religati sumus, seu quo hominem DEVS sibi religat.
units.tr: CI. For Lactantius, religion is the bond of piety, by which we are bound to God, or by which God binds man to himself.

units.la: CII. Etiam CICERONI religio est, quæ superioris naturæ, quam Diuinam vocant, curam ceremoniamque affert.
units.tr: CII. Cicero too held that religion is what brings care and ceremony concerning that superior nature which they call divine.

units.la: CIII. A superstitione religio differt Lactantio, quod religio est veri cultus, superstitio falsi.
units.tr: CIII. For Lactantius, religion differs from superstition in that religion is the worship of what is true, superstition the worship of what is false.

units.la: CIV. Religio igitur creaturis, vel rebus præter Deum tributa, non est nisi falsa, quam sacræ literæ superstitionem & idololatriam vocant.
units.tr: CIV. Therefore religion paid to creatures, or to things other than God, is nothing but false religion, which the holy writings call superstition and idolatry.

units.la: CV. Est enim idololatria cultus numinis fictitius, vel superstitiosus.
units.tr: CV. For idolatry is the worship of a fictitious or superstitious deity.

units.la: CVI. Cuius duæ præcipuæ species. Vna, quando fictitium numen colitur, h. e. cum loco veri Dei, aut præter illum, alicui rei, siue existenti, siue fictæ, cultus religiosus Deo soli debitus, intus vel foris, tribuitur.
units.tr: CVI. It has two chief kinds. The first is when a fictitious deity is worshipped, that is, when religious worship due to God alone is given, inwardly or outwardly, to some thing, whether existing or imagined, in place of the true God or alongside him.

units.la: CVII. Hæc primo præcepto prohibetur: Non habebis Deos alienos coram me.
units.tr: CVII. This is forbidden in the first commandment: "You shall have no other gods before me."

units.la: CVIII. Talis erat idololatria Gentilium, religiose colentium Deos fictos, intus fiducia, foris ceremoniis & statuis.
units.tr: CVIII. Such was the idolatry of the Gentiles, who religiously worshipped fictitious gods, with inward trust and with outward ceremonies and statues.

units.la: CIX. Talis Apostolo auaritia, pecuniam intus fiducia colens pro Deo.
units.tr: CIX. Such, to the Apostle, is covetousness, which inwardly trusts in money and worships it as God.

units.la: CX. Altera idololatria est error in genere cultus, cùm vero Deo cultus, quem ipse vel non præcepit, vel prohibuit, hoc est, in statuis & ritibus humanitus excogitatis, præstari fingitur.
units.tr: CX. The second idolatry is an error in the kind of worship, when worship is pretended to be paid to the true God in a form that he either did not command or forbade, that is, in statues and rites devised by men.

units.la: CXI. Hæc secundo præcepto prohibetur: Non facies tibi sculptile, &c.
units.tr: CXI. This is forbidden in the second commandment: "You shall not make for yourself a graven image," etc.

units.la: CXII. Et declaratur in Deuteronomio: Ne inquiras de diis Gentium, dicendo: Quomodo colebant gentes illæ Deos suos, sic faciam & ego. Non facies sic Iehouæ Deo tuo: quia omnem abominationem Iehouæ, quam odit, fecerunt diis suis.
units.tr: CXII. And it is explained in Deuteronomy: "Do not inquire about the gods of the nations, saying, 'How did those nations worship their gods? I will do likewise.' You shall not do so to the LORD your God, for every abomination to the LORD, which he hates, they have done for their gods."

units.la: CXIII. Et proprie quidem ἰδωλολατρεία est, ratione cultus: redit vero ad ἀδωλολατρείαν, ratione obiecti.
units.tr: CXIII. Strictly speaking, idolatry [ἰδωλολατρεία] is so called with respect to the worship, but with respect to its object it refers back to [ἀδωλολατρείαν].

units.la: CXIV. Tribuere enim Deo peregrinum cultum, est affingere Deo aliam, quam quæ est, voluntatem, proinde est fingere alium Deum, & pro Deo colere idolum.
units.tr: CXIV. For to ascribe to God a foreign worship is to attribute to God a will other than the one he has, and so to invent another god and to worship an idol as God.

units.la: CXV. Talis idololatria est, cum Deus effigiatur, & in effigie coli fingitur.
units.tr: CXV. Such idolatry occurs when God is represented in an image and is pretended to be worshipped in that image.

units.la: CXVI. Talis etiam, cum Deus ad imagines, vel statuas creaturarum, cœlestium vel terrestrium, in honorem Dei vel sanctorum positarum, colitur, sive cultus in statuis vel sanctis terminari, sive ad DEVM transfertur fingatur.
units.tr: CXVI. Also such is the case when God is worshipped through images or statues of created things, heavenly or earthly, set up in honour of God or of the saints, whether the worship terminates in the statues or the saints, or is pretended to be transferred to God.

units.la: CXVII. Aduersus vtramque: Cauete, inquit Deus, Deut. 4. verf. 15. 16. animabus vestris, (non enim vidistis vllam imaginem die illo, quo locutus est vobis Iehoua in monte Horeb) ne forte corrumpatis animas vestras, & faciatis vobis sculptile, aut imaginem vllius simulacri, imaginem masculi, vel fœminæ, &c.
units.tr: CXVII. Against both, God says: "Take heed to your souls (for you saw no image on the day that the LORD spoke to you in Horeb), lest perhaps you corrupt yourselves and make for yourselves a graven image, the likeness of any figure, the image of male or female," etc. (Deut. 4:15–16).

units.la: CXVIII. In noua cumprimis Testamento, quando Deus vult coli in Spiritu & veritate, fuga idololatriæ & superstitionis cuiuscunque districtè præcipitur: Cauete vobis ab idolis. Fugite ab idolatria. Nemo vos seducat voluntario cultu, &c.
units.tr: CXVIII. Especially in the New Testament, where God wishes to be worshipped in spirit and truth, flight from idolatry and from every superstition is strictly enjoined: "Keep yourselves from idols." "Flee from idolatry." "Let no one deceive you by a voluntary worship," etc.

units.la: CXIX. Distrincte omnes idololatræ à regno DEI excluduntur: Ne errate: neque scortatores, neque idololatræ regnum DEI possidebunt. Foris scortatores, & idololatræ, & venefici.
units.tr: CXIX. All idolaters are expressly excluded from the kingdom of God: "Do not be deceived: neither fornicators, nor idolaters, shall inherit the kingdom of God." "Outside are the fornicators, and the idolaters, and the sorcerers."

units.la: CXX. Atqui Papatus Rom. à mille nunc annis, fœdis superstitionibus totus conflatus est, fœdaq; idololatria indies magis profanatur.
units.tr: CXX. Yet the Roman Papacy for a thousand years now has been wholly built up of foul superstitions, and its foul idolatry is daily more profaned.

units.la: CXXI. Superstitiones vanas, impias, quibus quotidie in Papatu magna religione, ad placandum Deum, ad promerendam peccatorum veniam, ad redimendas peccatorum & purgatorij, & inferni pœnas, vacatur, infinitas, quæstui sacerdotali excogitatas, quis enumeret? puta,
units.tr: CXXI. Who could enumerate the countless vain and impious superstitions, with which every day in the Papacy, with great religious zeal, men spend their time to appease God, to earn the forgiveness of sins, and to redeem the punishments of sins, of purgatory and of hell, devised for the profit of the priests? For example:

units.la: Orationes & vigilias pro defunctis: septimas & tricesimas anniuersarias; thesaurum & suffragia Ecclesiæ pro purgatorio; peregrinationes ad Diuorum statuas; ad loca sacra; ossa & reliquias sanctorum; fraternitates; religiones; dedicationes templorum & altarium; exorcismos; consecrationes imaginum & sepulchrorum; campanarum baptismos adhibitis patrimis; ciborum delectus; ieiunia quadrantalia, quadragesimalia; vestes religiosas & consecratas; horas canonicas; processiones religiosas; amburbalia, bacchanalia; consecrationes sacerdotum; unctiones infirmorum; chrismatis & baptisterij exorcizationes; tonsiones & rasuras; casulas; albas; vestes chorales; candelabra; cereos consecratos; lampades, ampullas, faces, famones, vexilla, thuribula; monstrantias; ciboria, campanellas, cymbala, crepitacula; aquas benedictas, harumque exorcizationes; sal consecratum, placentas benedictas, herbas exorcizatas ad fugandos daemonas; pulsationes contra tonitrua; imagunculas sanctorum pannis inuolutas; litanias sanctorum; confessiones; satisfactiones; rosarias; ramos palmarum consecratos; asinos palmis coronatos; oscula & adorationes crucis; crucem repositam in sepulchro; matutinas ad sepulchrum; solennes tumultus; strepitus ligneos nocturnos: ludicrum ascensum idoli pro CHRISTO super fornicem templi; deiectiones ignis & aquæ; circumgestationes hostiæ consecratæ; infinitas sanctorum ferias, sub pœna mortali imperatas; indulgentias; ablutiones pedum & altarium; imagines crucis cereas; agnos Dei; innumeras denique alias, superstitionis, magiæ, & idololatriæ plenas.
units.tr: prayers and vigils for the dead; the seventh-day and thirtieth-day anniversary masses; the treasury and suffrages of the Church for purgatory; pilgrimages to the statues of the saints, to holy places, to the bones and relics of the saints; fraternities; religious orders; dedications of temples and altars; exorcisms; consecrations of images and tombs; baptisms of bells, with godparents present; choices of foods; fasts of the quarter-days and of Lent; religious and consecrated vestments; the canonical hours; religious processions; the Ambarvalia and the Bacchanalia; consecrations of priests; anointings of the sick; exorcisms of the chrism and the baptismal font; tonsures and shavings; chasubles; albs; choir vestments; candelabra; consecrated wax candles; lamps, cruets, torches, flambeaux, banners, censers; monstrances; ciboria, little bells, cymbals, rattles; holy water and exorcisms of it; consecrated salt, blessed cakes, herbs exorcised to drive away demons; ringing against thunderstorms; little images of the saints wrapped in cloths; litanies of the saints; confessions; satisfactions; rosaries; consecrated palm branches; asses crowned with palms; kisses and adorations of the cross; the cross laid in the sepulchre; matins at the sepulchre; solemn tumults; wooden clappers at night; the ludicrous ascent of an idol, representing Christ, above the vault of the temple; the casting down of fire and water; processions carrying the consecrated host about; countless feast-days of the saints, enjoined under pain of mortal sin; indulgences; washings of feet and altars; wax images of the cross; the Lambs of God; and, in short, countless other things full of superstition, magic and idolatry.

units.la: CXXII. Quas quidè Episcopi ambitiosi, maxime Romani, vt placerent populo, ex Gentilismo, vtq; diuinam rem facere viderentur, ex Judaismo, Christianæ religioni inuexerunt: omnes verò Seruator noster Christus vno verbo elisit dicendo: Frustra me colunt doctrinis, mandatis hominum.
units.tr: CXXII. These the ambitious bishops, above all the Roman ones, introduced into the Christian religion, partly from Gentile practice, so that they might please the people and seem to be doing something divine, and partly from Judaism. Our Saviour Christ, however, shattered them all with one word, saying: "In vain do they worship me with the doctrines and commandments of men."

units.la: CXXIII. Horribiljor idololatria Papatus Romani est, quod sacrosanctæ Trinitati, Deo immenso & inconspicuo, in templis imagines & statuas fictas ponit, cereis, thymiamatis, geniculationibus, suspiriis, votis, pari cum Deo religione veneratur.
units.tr: CXXIII. The idolatry of the Roman Papacy is more horrible still, in that it sets up in its temples images and fictitious statues of the most holy Trinity, the immeasurable and invisible God, and venerates them with the same religious honour as God, with candles, incense, genuflections, sighs and vows.

units.la: CXXIV. Quod Christum Seruatorem gloriosè nunc in cœlo regnantem, rursus cruci affixum, ligneum vel saxeum, vniuersis templis, platearum angulis, viarum compitis suspendit, religiosè sub mortali, & capitis fidelium periculo, ingenti infidelium scandalo & ludibrio, venerandum.
units.tr: CXXIV. In that it hangs up, in all its temples, at the corners of streets and at the crossroads, a wooden or stone image of Christ our Saviour, now gloriously reigning in heaven, fixed again to the cross, and worships it religiously, under pain of mortal sin and risk to the heads of the faithful, to the great scandal and mockery of unbelievers.

units.la: CXXV. Quod lignum crucis, vt Christum ipsum, religiosè adoratum, venerandum.
units.tr: CXXV. In that it worships and venerates the wood of the cross religiously, as it does Christ himself.

units.la: CXXVI. Quod signum crucis in fronte, vel aere, vel super quascunque res digito expressum, contra vim dæmonum, ad sanctificationem suam sacrum & venerabile habet.
units.tr: CXXVI. In that it holds the sign of the cross, traced with the finger on the forehead, or in the air, or upon any objects, to be holy and venerable for its sanctifying power against the power of demons.

units.la: CXXVII. Quod Christum viuum, gloriosum, quotidie in Missa, sub specie hostiæ, realiter offert, sacrificat, destruit, hoc est, mactat, crucifigit: immaniore scelere, quam milites humilem semel cruci affixerunt.
units.tr: CXXVII. In that it daily offers, sacrifices, destroys, that is, slaughters and crucifies, the living and glorious Christ in the Mass, under the appearance of a host, with a greater crime than the soldiers who once fixed the lowly Christ to the cross.

units.la: CXXVIII. Quod hostiam panis in Missa eleuatam, exhibet adorandam pro Deo: spectatores, antequam comedant. edant, tundentes pectora proni adorant, dicentes: Tu es Deus, redemtor meus.
units.tr: CXXVIII. In that it exhibits the host of bread, raised up in the Mass, to be adored as God; the spectators, before they eat and drink, prostrate themselves, beating their breasts, and adore it, saying: "You are God, my redeemer."

units.la: CXXIX. Quod Missas priuatas in singulis templorum angulis facit pro viuis & mortuis.
units.tr: CXXIX. In that it makes private Masses in every corner of its temples, for the living and the dead.

units.la: CXXX. Quod Missas facit de corona spinea, de tribus clauis, de praeputio Christi, pro nauigantibus, pro equestri, aut pedestri itinere peregrinantibus, pro grauidis, pro parturientibus, pro sterilibus, pro febre quartana aut continua laborantibus.
units.tr: CXXX. In that it makes Masses concerning the crown of thorns, the three nails, the foreskin of Christ, for sailors, for travellers on horseback or on foot, for pregnant women, for women in labour, for barren women, for those suffering from quartan or continual fever.

units.la: CXXXI. Quod praeter innumeras, quas vocat, reliquias ementitas, consecrata Christi sandalia, pro peccatorum antidoto, religioso populo spectanda exhibet. quod ipse Papa Stephanus Rauennae.
units.tr: CXXXI. In that, besides the countless relics it calls forgeries, it exhibits the consecrated sandals of Christ for the devout people to gaze upon, as an antidote to sins; as Pope Stephen himself did at Ravenna.

units.la: CXXXII. Quod homines defunctos, quos ipse Sanctos vel Diuos fecit, religiose colit, adorat, inuocat, clamando: S. Petre, S. Hyacinthe, miserere mei: salua me: aperi mihi aditum coeli, da mihi sanitatem corporis, &c. Paganorum more, qui in Deorum vicem, honorabant, quos ex hominibus in coelum receptos putabant: Lactantius.
units.tr: CXXXII. In that it religiously worships, adores, invokes and cries out to men who have died, whom it has itself made saints or gods: "St Peter, St Hyacinth, have mercy on me; save me; open the way of heaven for me; give me health of body," etc. This is in the manner of the pagans, who honoured in place of gods those whom they thought had been received into heaven from among men (Lactantius).

units.la: CXXXIII. Quod iisdem defunctis consecrat templa, altaria, ferias, Missas & sacrificia: eosdemq; ciuitatibus, prouinciis Tutelares praeficit.
units.tr: CXXXIII. In that it consecrates temples, altars, feast-days, Masses and sacrifices to these same dead, and sets them over cities and provinces as their guardians.

units.la: CXXXIV. Quod eorundem imagines & statuas in templis, angiportis, compitis religiose colit, adorat, veneratur, pro animarum salute.
units.tr: CXXXIV. In that it worships, adores and venerates religiously, for the salvation of souls, their images and statues in temples, in alleys and at crossroads.

units.la: CXXXV. Quod MARIAE virgini statuas preciosiores, quam DEO vel CHRISTO, auro sericoque ornatas ponit, cereos, templa, ferias, sacrificos, Missas iisdem consecrat.
units.tr: CXXXV. In that it sets up for the Virgin Mary statues more precious than those of God or Christ, adorned with gold and silk, and consecrates to them candles, temples, feast-days, priests and Masses.

units.la: CXXXVI. Quod MARIAM virginem portam paradisi, matrem misericordiarum, vitam & dulcedinem suam, gratia thesaurariam, peccatorum refugium, scelerum expiatricem, hominum MEDIATRICEM, dies noctesque religiose inuocat, nihil Christo nisi verba relinquit.
units.tr: CXXXVI. In that it religiously invokes the Virgin Mary day and night as the gate of paradise, mother of mercies, our life and sweetness, treasurer of grace, refuge of sinners, expiator of crimes, MEDIATRIX of men, leaving Christ nothing but words.

units.la: CXXXVII. Quod MARIAM quotidie REGINAM COELI salutat, cultu olim apud paganos Isidi proprio: cui
units.tr: CXXXVII. Because they greet Mary every day as QUEEN OF HEAVEN, a title once proper to the worship of Isis among the pagans,

units.la: Apuleius Platonicus pro metamorphosi ex asino in hominē supplicans clamabat; Regina cœli, siue tu Ceres alma, &c.
units.tr: Apuleius the Platonist, when praying for release from his transformation from an ass into a man, cried out: Queen of heaven, whether you are kindly Ceres, etc.

units.la: CXXXVIII. Mariam Christo filio jure matris imperare postulans, vociferatur:
units.tr: CXXXVIII. Asking that Mary, by a mother's right, command her son Christ, they cry out:

units.la: O felix puerpera, Iure Matris IMPERA, Nostra pians scelera, REDEMTORI.
units.tr: O happy mother, by a mother's right COMMAND the REDEEMER, atoning for our sins.

units.la: CXXXIX. Quod Papatui nihil Deus, nihil Christus: sola Maria est & &, portus & aura salutis omnibus; in hymno:
units.tr: CXXXIX. That for the Papacy God is nothing and Christ nothing; Mary alone is all in all, the harbour and breath of salvation for everyone; in the hymn:

units.la: Tu spes certa miserorum, Medicamen infirmorum, Vera mater orphanorum, OMNIBUS ES OMNIA. Tu leuamen oppressorum,
units.tr: You, the sure hope of the wretched, the remedy of the sick, the true mother of orphans, ALL THINGS TO ALL MEN. You, the relief of the oppressed,

units.la: CXL. Quod Papatui Maria reuera est Deus, quip-pe in quam vniuersam Dei omnipotentis GLORIAM propriam Psalterio Mariæ dicato, horrendo sacrilegio transmouet, sic ei pro Deo supplicans, & scripturas diuinas adulterans:
units.tr: CXL. That for the Papacy Mary is truly God, since into her they transfer the whole GLORY of almighty God in a Psalter dedicated to Mary, with horrible sacrilege, begging her as God in this way and corrupting the divine Scriptures:

units.la: Domina in te speraui, non confundar in æternum. In Domina confido. Saluum me fac Mater. Cœli enarrant gloriam tuam, virgo Maria. Miserere mei Domina. Inclina Domina aurem tuam, exaudi me. Domina in nomine tuo saluum me fac. In manu tua Domina salus & vita consistunt. Ablue omnia peccata nostra: sana omnes infirmitates no-stras Domina. (MEVM. In manus tuas Domina COMMENDO SPIRITVM In nomine tuo Domina se flectit omne genu cœlestium, terrestrium & subterraneorum, &c.
units.tr: Lady, in you I have hoped; let me never be confounded. In the Lady I trust. Save me, Mother. The heavens declare your glory, Virgin Mary. Have mercy on me, Lady. Incline your ear, Lady, and hear me. Lady, save me in your name. In your hand, Lady, lie salvation and life. Wash away all our sins; heal all our infirmities, Lady. (... Into your hands, Lady, I COMMEND MY SPIRIT. In your name, Lady, every knee of the heavenly, the earthly and the subterranean bows, etc.

units.la: CXLI. Quod denique Papatus orbem Christianum altissimo superstitionum istarum cœno demersit: Reges que & incolas terræ, magnos & parvos, diuites & pauperes, liberos & seruos poculo fornicationum istarum inebriatos, quantum in se fuit, à Christo in æternæ salutis discrimen secum abduxit.
units.tr: CXLI. Finally, the Papacy has plunged the Christian world into the mire of these superstitions. As far as it was in its power, it has led kings and the inhabitants of the earth, great and small, rich and poor, free and slave, drunk with the cup of these fornications, away with itself from Christ and into the peril of eternal salvation.

units.la: CXLII. Hæc vrbs illa sancta, calcata à Gentibus, hoc est, Ecclesia vastata à Romanis gentilizantibus, sicut Jerosolyma calcata fuit à Romanis Gentibus: idq; mensēs xlii. quorum (si fas est diuinare) triginta quatuor ferme lapsi: octo vtinam Deus calcationi decurtet, propter electos: visione tertia apud Apocalypseos.
units.tr: CXLII. That holy city, trampled by the Gentiles, that is, the Church laid waste by the Romans who play the Gentile, just as Jerusalem was trampled by the Roman Gentiles; and this for forty-two months, of which (if it is right to conjecture) about thirty-four have now passed. Would that God would cut short the trampling of the remaining eight, for the sake of the elect: in the third vision of the Apocalypse.

units.la: CXLIII. Hæc illa spiritualis Sodoma, scortationum & Sodomitarum spiritualium & corporalium (quæ gaudent conjungi) fœdissima officina, de qua jam pridem Petrarcha: Stupra, raptus, incestus, adulteria, iam Pontificalis lasciuiæ ludi sunt. Visione eadem Apocalypseos.
units.tr: CXLIII. This is that spiritual Sodom, the most foul workshop of fornications and of spiritual and bodily Sodomites (who delight to be joined together), of which Petrarch long ago said: Rapes, abductions, incest, adulteries are now the games of papal wantonness. In the same vision of the Apocalypse.

units.la: CXLIV. Hæ illæ blasphemiæ, ad quas bestia maritima os suum aperuit aduersus Deum & nomen eius, cuius omnem GLORIAM in sua idola, quin, vt sequetur, in seipsam transmouet.
units.tr: CXLIV. These are those blasphemies, for which the sea beast opened its mouth against God and his name, transferring all his GLORY to its own idols, indeed, as will follow, to itself.

units.la: CXLV. Et aduersus tabernaculum eius, ecclesiam, quam pestilentis doctrinæ venenis inquinatam, signis mendacibus seduxit, idolomania horribili in exitium trusit.
units.tr: CXLV. And against his tabernacle, the Church, which it, polluted with the poisons of pestilent doctrine and seduced by lying signs, has thrust into ruin by horrible idolatry.

units.la: CXLVI. Et aduersus eos, qui in cœlo habitant: quibus iniuitiis, quæstus sui causa, diuinū honorem obtrusit, quosq; in Gentilium idolorum loca succedere coegit, variisque & sordidis fatigauit ministeriis, præficiens hunc porcis, illum equis, alium asinis, istum huic, alium isti oppido tuendo, opificio prosperando, morbo pellendo, calamitati arcendæ, &c. visione quarta Apocalypseos.
units.tr: CXLVI. And against those who dwell in heaven: by what iniquities, for the sake of gain, it has forced divine honour upon them, and compelled them to take the places of the Gentile idols, and wearied them with various and filthy duties, setting one over the pigs, another over the horses, another over the asses, this one to guard that town, another to prosper a trade, another to drive off disease, another to ward off calamity, etc. In the fourth vision of the Apocalypse.

units.la: CXLVII. Hæc illa imago bestiæ, basilicas, templa, sacella, compita imaginibus, simulacris, altaribus, lampadibus, vrceis lustralibus plena habens Papatus IMAGINARIUM REGNVM, quod qui non adorauerit, occiditur: visione eadem Apocalypseos.
units.tr: CXLVII. This is that image of the beast, the Papacy having its IMAGINARY KINGDOM, its basilicas, temples, chapels and crossroads full of images, statues, altars, lamps and vessels of lustral water: whoever does not adore it is put to death. In the same vision of the Apocalypse.

units.la: CXLVIII. Hæc denique Babylon illa magna, mater fornicationum & abominationum terræ, cum qua scortati sunt reges terræ, & cuius scortationis vino inebriati sunt incolæ terræ. visione eadem Apocalypseos.
units.tr: CXLVIII. Finally, this is that great Babylon, mother of fornications and abominations of the earth, with whom the kings of the earth have committed fornication, and with the wine of whose fornication the inhabitants of the earth have been made drunk. In the same vision of the Apocalypse.

units.la: CXLIX. Habemus Papatus Rom. horribilem idolomaniam, in quam cultum Dei conuertit, olim perangelum lum B. Iohanni prænunciatam: seculo autem hactenus reuoluto, renascentis Euangelij luce retectam.
units.tr: CXLIX. We have in the Roman Papacy the horrible idolatry into which it has turned the worship of God, long ago foretold to the blessed John by an angel, but now, the century having rolled round so far, uncovered by the light of the renewed Gospel.

units.la: CL. Quæ CAVSA ALTERA vrgentissima fuit patribus nostris deserendi, nobis & fugiendi Papatus Romani. Sicque concluditur:
units.tr: CL. This was the SECOND CAUSE, most urgent for our fathers to forsake, and for us to flee, the Roman Papacy. And so it is concluded:

units.la: CLI. Ecclesia idololatrica est deserenda, fugienda, quia scriptum: Fugite ab idololatria.
units.tr: CLI. An idolatrous church is to be forsaken and fled from, because it is written: Flee from idolatry.

units.la: CLII. Papatus Romanus est ecclesia idololatrica, vt præcessit. (fugiendus.
units.tr: CLII. The Roman Papacy is an idolatrous church, as has been shown before (and so is to be fled from).

units.la: CLIII. Papatus Rom. igitur fuit deserendus, est
units.tr: CLIII. Therefore the Roman Papacy was to be forsaken, and is.

units.la: III. Tyrannis Antichristiana Papatus Rom.
units.tr: III. The Antichristian tyranny of the Roman Papacy.

units.la: CLIV. Nimis ad fugiendum Papatum Rom. damnabilis apostasia, & horribilis idolomania sufficiebant.
units.tr: CLIV. The detestable apostasy and the horrible idolatry were enough to make the Roman Papacy to be fled from.

units.la: CLV. Quanto magis detestabilis, postquam Antichristiana Tyrannis accessit?
units.tr: CLV. How much more detestable is it since Antichristian tyranny has been added?

units.la: CLVI. Hæc tamen magis propria capitis: cum illæ vniuersum corpus inuaserint.
units.tr: CLVI. Yet these two are more proper to the head, since the tyranny has invaded the whole body.

units.la: CLVII. Duæ vero pestes priores tertiam peperierunt, vel necessario antecesserunt.
units.tr: CLVII. The two earlier plagues, however, gave birth to the third, or necessarily went before it.

units.la: CLVIII. Orbis enim Christianus nisi apostasia seductus, idolomania fascinatus, tyrannidis Antichristianæ capistrum jugumque nunquam recepisset.
units.tr: CLVIII. For the Christian world, unless it had been seduced by apostasy and bewitched by idolatry, would never have received the halter and yoke of Antichristian tyranny.

units.la: CLIX. Tyrannis est, Rempublicam jure vel injuria occupatam, contra jus vasq; premere, pessundare.
units.tr: CLIX. Tyranny is the oppressing and ruining of a commonwealth seized, whether rightly or wrongly, contrary to law and right.

units.la: CLX. Papa Rom. Ecclesiam remque Christianam non vna, sed gemina, spirituali & ciuili tyrannide innasit, oppressitque.
units.tr: CLX. The Roman Pope has assailed and oppressed the Church and the Christian commonwealth not with one tyranny but with a twofold one, spiritual and civil.

units.la: CLXI. Spirituali tyrannide inuasit, quando apostolicam ecclesiæ disciplinam per superbiam euertit.
units.tr: CLXI. He invaded with spiritual tyranny when through pride he overturned the apostolic discipline of the Church.

units.la: CLXII. Disciplina apostolica erat œconomica, vt sub vno patrefamilias seu capite, peregre in cælum profecto, Iesu Christo, plures œconomi, Apostoli, & post hos Episcopi, potestate pares, sua quique talenta, ad vtilitatem domus Dei viuentis suo quique loco dispensarent.
units.tr: CLXII. The apostolic discipline was economical: under one householder or head, Jesus Christ, gone abroad into heaven, there were several stewards, the Apostles and after them the bishops, equal in power, each dispensing his own talents, each in his own place, for the benefit of the house of the living God.

units.la: CLXIII. Ita enim de nobis reputet homo, inquit Apostolus, vt ministris Christi, & œconomis mysteriorum Dei.
units.tr: CLXIII. "For let a man so account of us," says the Apostle, "as of the ministers of Christ and stewards of the mysteries of God."

units.la: CLXIV. Et legitur quidem Dominus in cœlum asscendens Ecc esiæ præter Apostolos, Prophetas, Euangelistas, dedisse etiam Doctores & Pastores, seu Episcopos.
units.tr: CLXIV. And we read that the Lord, ascending into heaven, gave to the Church, besides Apostles, Prophets and Evangelists, also Teachers and Pastors, or Bishops.

units.la: CLXXV. Non legitur verò Ecclesiæ dedisse aliquem Principem sacerdotum vel Pontificem Maximum.
units.tr: CLXV. Yet we do not read that he gave the Church any chief priest or Supreme Pontiff.

units.la: CLXVI. Episcopatus vnus est, ait Cyprianus, cuius à singulis in solidum pars tenetur.
units.tr: CLXVI. "The episcopate is one," says Cyprian, "of which a part is held by each individual in solidum."

units.la: CLXVII. Neq; quisquam nostrum, ait idem, Episcopum se esse Episcoporum constituit, aut tyrannico terrore ad obsequendi necessitatem collegas suos adigit.
units.tr: CLXVII. "Nor does any of us," says the same, "set himself up as bishop of bishops, or drives his colleagues by tyrannical terror to the necessity of obeying."

units.la: CLXVIII. Crescentibus tandem Ecclesiis, crescen-teq; episcoporum ambitione, ordinis quidem ratione habita, propter imperij culmen, antiquæ Romæ Episco-po prima sedes tributa fuit.
units.tr: CLXVIII. As the Churches at last grew, and with them the ambition of bishops, the first seat was given to the bishop of old Rome, the order being observed because of the imperial greatness of the city.

units.la: CLXIX. Sed saluo canone, Augustini manu subscri-pto: Prima sedis Episcopus non appellatur Princeps Sacerdotum, vel summus Sacerdos, aut aliquid huiusmodi: sed tantum prima sedis Episcopus.
units.tr: CLXIX. But with the canon, subscribed by the hand of Augustine, still standing: "The bishop of the first see is not called Prince of Priests, or Chief Priest, or anything of the kind, but only bishop of the first see."

units.la: CLXX. Hic ordo, hæcque disciplina œconomica Ecclesiis Christianis post Christum natum annis sex-centis perdurauit.
units.tr: CLXX. This order and this economical discipline lasted in the Christian Churches for six hundred years after the birth of Christ.

units.la: CLXXI. Primus à SATANA dominandi libidine percitus, superbiæque œstro ad rumpenda disciplinæ apostolicæ repagula stimulatus, BONIFACIVS III. ingenti contentione tyrannidem ecclesiæ inuasit, à Phoca Imperatore Tyranno VNIVERSALIS pronunciatus: Gregorij prædecessoris sententia ANTICHRISTVS mun-do declaratus.
units.tr: CLXXI. The first, stirred up by SATAN with a lust for dominion, and goaded by the gadfly of pride to break the barriers of apostolic discipline, was BONIFACE III, who with great contention seized the tyranny of the Church, being pronounced UNIVERSAL by the tyrant Emperor Phocas; by the sentence of his predecessor Gregory he was declared ANTICHRIST to the world.

units.la: CLXXII. Ab hoc, ne obscura tyrannis esset, illud tyrannicum in sede Rom. vsurpari cœptum: SIC VOLV-MVS, SIC IVBEMVS.
units.tr: CLXXII. From this man on, lest the tyranny be unclear, that tyrannical formula began to be used in the Roman see: THUS WE WILL, THUS WE COMMAND.

units.la: CLXXIII. In cathedra vniuersalis pestilentiæ vix qui-dem annum expleuit: quia Tu viel strenge Herren regieren nichs nicht lang, hoc est, Nimis rigidi domini non diu regnant, juxta prouerbium.
units.tr: CLXXIII. He scarcely completed a year in the chair of universal pestilence, because "harsh lords do not rule for long" (the German proverb: Tu viel strenge Herren regieren nichs nicht lang), that is, according to the saying, overly rigid masters do not reign long.

units.la: CLXXIV. Inde verò typhus superbiæ VNIVERSALIS à Satana throno Romano semel afflatus, tyrannidem ecclesiasticam propagauit, & auxit in immensum.
units.tr: CLXXIV. Then the whirlwind of UNIVERSAL pride, breathed once upon the Roman throne by Satan, spread ecclesiastical tyranny and increased it immensely.

units.la: CLXXV. Inde Papa Rom. habet cœleste arbitrium.
units.tr: CLXXV. Hence the Roman Pope has heavenly judgment.

units.la: CLXXVI. Papa habet idem consistorium cum Deo: idem tribunal cum Christo.
units.tr: CLXXVI. The Pope has the same consistory as God, the same tribunal as Christ.

units.la: CLXXVII. Papa est quoddam numen, visibilem quendam Deum præ se ferens.
units.tr: CLXXVII. The Pope is a kind of divinity, bearing before himself a visible god.

units.la: CLXXVIII. Papa habet omnia iura in scrinio sui pectoris.
units.tr: CLXXVIII. The Pope has all laws in the coffer of his breast.

units.la: CLXXIX. Papa est Episcopus totius orbis, cui omnes episcopi & patriarchæ subesse debent de necessitate salutis.
units.tr: CLXXIX. The Pope is Bishop of the whole world, to whom all bishops and patriarchs must of necessity be subject for salvation.

units.la: CLXXX. Papa est omnium Princeps, Rex Regum, & caput omnium in Ecclesia militantium.
units.tr: CLXXX. The Pope is Prince of all, King of kings, and head of all in the militant Church.

units.la: CLXXXI. Papa omnes mortales habet subditos.
units.tr: CLXXXI. The Pope has all mortals as his subjects.

units.la: CLXXXII. Papa omnis creatura humana subest.
