units.tr: CLXXXII. Every human creature is subject to the Pope.

units.la: CLXXXIII. Papa est tradita omnis potestas in cælo & terra.
units.tr: CLXXXIII. All power in heaven and on earth has been handed over to the Pope.

units.la: CLXXXIV. Papa est super angelos iudex constitutus.
units.tr: CLXXXIV. The Pope has been appointed judge over the angels.

units.la: CLXXXV. A Papa ne ad Deum quidem appellari potest.
units.tr: CLXXXV. No appeal can be made from the Pope even to God.

units.la: CLXXXVI. Papa est supra omnia Concilia, solus ea convocandi, dirigendi, confirmandi, annihilandi habens potestatem.
units.tr: CLXXXVI. The Pope is above all councils, and alone has the power to convene, direct, confirm, and annul them.

units.la: CLXXXVII. Papa omnibus Episcopis iurisdictionem confers.
units.tr: CLXXXVII. The Pope confers jurisdiction on all bishops.

units.la: CLXXXVIII. Papa non potest se submittere conciliis.
units.tr: CLXXXVIII. The Pope cannot submit himself to councils.

units.la: CLXXXIX. Papa condit leges coactiuas in conscientiis.
units.tr: CLXXXIX. The Pope enacts coercive laws over consciences.

units.la: CXC. Papa omnes solus iudicat, à nemine iudicatur.
units.tr: CXC. The Pope alone judges all, and is judged by no one.

units.la: CXCI. Si Papa multa animarum millia præcipitet in gehennam, nemo dicet, Domine Papa, quare hoc facis?
units.tr: CXCI. If the Pope should hurl many thousands of souls into hell, no one will say, "Lord Pope, why do you do this?"

units.la: CXCII. Papa potest omnia facere, quæ Deus facit.
units.tr: CXCII. The Pope can do all that God does.

units.la: CXCIII. Papa nec Deus, nec angelus, nec homo, juxta versus: Papa stupor mundi, solus qui Maxime rerum NecDeus es, nec homo, quasi neuter es inter vtrunqi.
units.tr: CXCIII. The Pope is neither God, nor angel, nor man, according to the verse: "Pope, wonder of the world, who alone... you are neither God nor man, but as it were neutral between the two."

units.la: CXCIV. Immò Papa est Deus.
units.tr: CXCIV. Indeed, the Pope is God.

units.la: CXCV. Papa est causa causarum, Dominus dominantium.
units.tr: CXCV. The Pope is the cause of causes, the Lord of lords.

units.la: CXCVI. Papa est supremus Dei vicarius, & quicunq; contrarium dicit, mentitur.
units.tr: CXCVI. The Pope is the supreme vicar of God, and whoever says otherwise lies.

units.la: CXCVII. Papæ sententia est standum, etiamsi totus mundus contra sentiret.
units.tr: CXCVII. One must abide by the Pope's judgment, even if the whole world thought otherwise.

units.la: CXCVIII. Papæ nullus par, nisi Deus.
units.tr: CXCVIII. The Pope has no equal except God.

units.la: CXCIX. Papa est caput & sponsus vniuersalis Ecclesiæ.
units.tr: CXCIX. The Pope is the head and universal bridegroom of the Church.

units.la: CC. Hinc ferendum, & pia devotione tolerandum est iugum, quod à sancta sede imponitur, licet intolerabile videatur.
units.tr: CC. Hence the yoke imposed by the Holy See must be borne and endured with pious devotion, even if it seems intolerable.

units.la: CCI. Atqui qui Deum qui sponsum ecclesiæ se facit, non est hostis Dei, hostis & æmulus Christi, Antichristus?
units.tr: CCI. Yet is not he who makes himself the bridegroom of the Church the enemy of God, the enemy and rival of Christ, Antichrist?

units.la: CCII. Cæterum serpens nisi voraverit serpentem, non fit Draco, vt habet proverbium.
units.tr: CCII. For, as the proverb says, a serpent does not become a dragon unless it has swallowed another serpent.

units.la: CCIII. Sic Papa nisi devorato imperio Romano, nondum fuit plenus Antichristus.
units.tr: CCIII. So the Pope, unless he had devoured the Roman empire, was not yet fully Antichrist.

units.la: CCIV. Ad spiritualem igitur tyrannidem tandem & secularem rapuit.
units.tr: CCIV. Therefore he seized spiritual tyranny and, at last, secular tyranny as well.

units.la: CCV. In ficto patrimonio Petri vel Ecclesiæ Papa sit sane Princeps Italiæ secularis, vnus ex multis, præscri-ptione humana.
units.tr: CCV. Over the fictitious patrimony of Peter or of the Church, the Pope is indeed a secular prince of Italy, one among many, by human prescription.

units.la: CCVI. Papa Imperiali paludamento, coronaque Cæsarea redimitus, Spatham tenens manu, & clamans: Ego sum Cæsar: nonne Tyrannus Imperij, & Cæsaris hostis?
units.tr: CCVI. The Pope, wrapped in the imperial cloak and Caesar's crown, holding a sword in his hand and crying, I am Caesar! Is he not the tyrant of the empire and an enemy of Caesar?

units.la: CCVII. Neque casu hoc vnus fecit. Ambitio Pon-tificalis ab octingentis annis Imperium Romanum de-uorauit: Imperatores pedibus calcauit.
units.tr: CCVII. Nor did one man do this by chance. For eight hundred years papal ambition has devoured the Roman empire and trampled emperors underfoot.

units.la: CCVIII. Papæ debet Imperator præstare iuramentum fideli-tatis & obedientiæ.
units.tr: CCVIII. The emperor ought to swear an oath of fidelity and obedience to the Pope.

units.la: CCIX. Ex Papæ iudicio Imperator debet pendere, non Papæ ex Imperatoris: vt prius.
units.tr: CCIX. The emperor ought to depend on the Pope's judgment, and not the Pope on the emperor's, as formerly.

units.la: CCX. Papæ debet Imperator caput inclinare, ascendenti equum stratorem agere, frenum & stapedam tenere.
units.tr: CCX. The emperor ought to bow his head to the Pope, act as groom for him when he mounts his horse, and hold his bridle and stirrup.

units.la: CCXI. Papæ in conuiuio Imperator debet aquam ad lotionem manuum præbere.
units.tr: CCXI. At the Pope's banquet the emperor ought to bring water for washing the hands.

units.la: CCXII. Ad Papæ mensam Imperator debet primum fercu-lum portare.
units.tr: CCXII. At the Pope's table the emperor ought to carry in the first course.

units.la: CCXIII. Papa potest Imperatorem excommunicare, depone-re, vita priuare, tollere. CCXIV. Papa habet potestatem in omnes reges & principes, in omnia regna mundi, directam vel indirectam, & potest ea dare, cui vult.
units.tr: CCXIII. The Pope can excommunicate, depose, deprive of life, and remove the emperor. CCXIV. The Pope has power over all kings and princes, over all kingdoms of the world, direct or indirect, and can give them to whomever he wishes.

units.la: CCXV. Hinc Papa bicorpor, Pontificatu maximo gemino, quasi alter Numa Pompilius: vno Archiflaminis Gentilis: altero Imperatoris Rom. postquam Imperator profanum Pontificis Max. titulum deposuit: quod Gratianum primo fecisse quidam volunt.
units.tr: CCXV. Hence the Pope is two-bodied, holding a double supreme pontificate, like another Numa Pompilius: one as the pagan Archflamen, the other as the Roman emperor's, after the emperor laid aside the profane title of Pontifex Maximus; some hold that Gratian was the first to do this.

units.la: CCXVI. Hinc gemino armatus gladio, spirituali & sæculari: quia Bonifacius VIII. dixit: Ecce duo gladij hic.
units.tr: CCXVI. Hence he is armed with a double sword, spiritual and secular, because Boniface VIII said: Behold, here are two swords.

units.la: CCXVII. Neque vi tamen, quod mireris, sed arte, eaque triplici, tyrannidem tantam parasse legitur: Simonia, Dolo, Anathemate.
units.tr: CCXVII. Yet, which is surprising, he is recorded to have gained such tyranny not by force but by craft, and that a threefold craft: Simony, Trickery, Anathema.

units.la: CCXVIII. Simonis arte, ex sacris mercibus venalibus Patriarchatuum, Episcopatuum, Abbatiarum, Canonicatuum, præbendarum opimiorum, annatarum, palliorum, casuum matrimonialium & reseruatorum, dispensationum, absolutionum, indulgentiarum, ignis purgatorij, animarum humanarum, denique cœli & inferorum, vniuersi orbis clerum sibi vnicè obnoxium fecit: thesauros Ecclesiarum, Regum, & populorum Romam traduxit. Vnde argentum Papæ quid non valuit?
units.tr: CCXVIII. By the art of simony, he made the clergy of the whole world wholly bound to himself by selling sacred things: patriarchates, bishoprics, abbacies, canonries, rich prebends, annates, palliums, matrimonial and reserved cases, dispensations, absolutions, indulgences, the fire of purgatory, human souls, and finally heaven and hell. He drew the treasures of churches, kings and peoples to Rome. Hence, what has silver not been able to do for the Pope?

units.la: CCXIX. Dolo præcipuè tergemino, ceu totidem fascinis Christianum orbem ita sibi mancipauit: vt difcipis, factis, nutibus Papæ cœca obedientia non obtemperare, piaculum duceretur.
units.tr: CCXIX. Chiefly by a threefold trickery, as by so many charms, he so enslaved the Christian world to himself that to refuse blind obedience to the Pope's commands, deeds, or nods was considered a sin.

units.la: CCXX. Ementito primum Christi vicariatu, & S. Petri sede ac successione: tum prætensa Ecclesiæ Catholicæ Rom. cui omnes subesse de necessitate salutis oporteret, latua, ceu Gorgone obiecta, Reges & incolas terræ, malignos & paruos, diuites & pauperes, liberos & seruos, quasi in saxa conuersos, ad nutum habuit.
units.tr: CCXX. First by a feigned vicariate of Christ and the see and succession of St Peter; then by the pretended Roman Catholic Church, to which all must of necessity be subject for salvation, he held the kings and inhabitants of the earth, malicious and humble, rich and poor, free and slave, at his nod, as if they had been turned to stone by a Gorgon's head held up before them.

units.la: CCXXI. Addidit his prodigia & signa mendacia, nec raro hostias intoxicatas, quibus se numen ipso eventu probauit; ad apostoli oraculum: Cuius aduentus est ex effiex efficacia Satanæ cum omni potentia, & signis ac prodigiis men-dacibus, & cum omni fraude injustitiæ.
units.tr: CCXXI. To these he added lying prodigies and signs, and not infrequently poisoned hosts, by which he proved his divinity through the outcome itself, in line with the apostle's oracle: Whose coming is after the working of Satan, with all power and with lying signs and wonders, and with all deceit of unrighteousness.

units.la: CCXXII. ANATHEMATIS denique fulmine, si qui minus obsequentes viderentur, percussos, popula-tibus seditionibus facile repressit, subditis sacramenti fide solutis.
units.tr: CCXXII. Lastly, with the thunderbolt of anathema, he struck down those who seemed less obedient, and easily put down their rebellions by stirring up the people, releasing subjects from the bond of their oath of allegiance.

units.la: CCXXIII. Hac arte Gregorius II. Philippum & Leonem Impp. Orientis, eò quod Iconolatriam, verbo Dei damnatam, prohiberent, Exarchatu Italiæ excussit.
units.tr: CCXXIII. By this art Gregory II drove Philip and Leo, the emperors of the East, out of the exarchate of Italy, because they forbade image worship, which is condemned by the Word of God.

units.la: CCXXIV. Et paulo post Leo Papa Imperatoribus Orientis, eodem prætextu, tota Italia extubatis, ipse exuvias Romanas sibi vindicavit, Exarchatum totum invasit, neq; deinceps successoribus Impp. etiam Iconolatris restituit.
units.tr: CCXXIV. And a little later Pope Leo, on the same pretext, drove the emperors of the East out of all Italy, claimed the Roman spoils for himself, invaded the whole exarchate, and afterwards did not restore it to the emperors' successors, even though they too were image worshippers.

units.la: CCXXV. Hic igitur ille homo peccati, sedens in templo Dei quasi Deus, efferens se supra omne, quod dicitur Deus.
units.tr: CCXXV. This is that "man of sin, sitting in the temple of God" as if he were God, exalting himself above everything that is called God.

units.la: CCXXVI. Hæc illa gemina bestia, gemino ortu ex mari & terra quasi ἀμφίζωος, biformis, geminæ ad Christi æmulationem naturæ, tum ut sæcularis monarcha, tum ut ecclesiasticus seductor, figuratus Antichristus: visione quarta Apocalypseos.
units.tr: CCXXVI. This is that twofold beast, rising from both sea and land, two-girdled as it were, two-formed, with a double nature in imitation of Christ, both as a secular monarch and as an ecclesiastical seducer, foreshadowed as Antichrist: in the fourth vision of the Apocalypse.

units.la: CCXXVII. Hæc illa fornicatrix mulier, amicta purpu-ra & cocco, sanguine sanctorum & sanguine martyrum ebria, bestiam subiugem freno agens atque inequitans: visione quinta Apocalypseos.
units.tr: CCXXVII. This is that harlot woman, clothed in purple and scarlet, drunk with the blood of saints and martyrs, driving and riding the beast that is subdued with a bridle: in the fifth vision of the Apocalypse.

units.la: CCXXVIII. Hæc illa Babylon magna, superba, tyrannica, dicens in corde suo: Sedeo regina, & vidua non sum, nec luctum videbo: visione eadem.
units.tr: CCXXVIII. This is that great, proud, tyrannical Babylon, saying in her heart: I sit a queen, and am no widow, and shall see no sorrow: in the same vision.

units.la: CCXXIX. Habemus Pontificatus Rom. geminam tyrannidem: olim per angelum B. Johanni prænuncia-tam, seculo autem hactenus revoluto, renascentis Evan-gelij luce retectam.
units.tr: CCXXIX. We have the twofold tyranny of the Roman Pontificate, foretold long ago to John by an angel, and, now that a century has rolled by, uncovered by the light of the revived Gospel.

units.la: CCXXX. Quæ CAUSA TERTIA vrgentissima fuit patribus nostris deserendi, nobis est fugiendi Papatus Romani: sicque concluditur:
units.tr: CCXXX. The THIRD CAUSE, which was most pressing for our fathers to forsake, is for us the reason to flee from the Roman Papacy; and so it is concluded:

units.la: CCXXXI. Ecclesia Tyrannica, Babylon, est deserenda, fugienda, juxta vocem è cœlo dicentem: Exite ex ea populemi, ne participes sitis peccatorum eius, & ex plagis eius accipiatis.
units.tr: CCXXXI. The tyrannical Church, Babylon, is to be forsaken and fled from, according to the voice from heaven saying: Come out of her, my people, lest you share in her sins and receive of her plagues.

units.la: CCXXXII. Pontificatus cum Papatu Romano est ecclesia tyrannica, Babylon.
units.tr: CCXXXII. The Pontificate together with the Roman Papacy is the tyrannical Church, Babylon.

units.la: CCXXXIII. Pontificatus igitur cum Papatu Rom. fuit deserendus, est fugiendus.
units.tr: CCXXXIII. The Pontificate together with the Roman Papacy therefore had to be forsaken and must be fled from.

units.la: CCXXXIV. Quicunque verò formaliter, quod dicitur, Papista manet, hoc est, in hac apostasia & in hac idololatria, & sub hac tyrannide Pontificatus & Papatus sine poenitentia moritur, sine dubio in æternum peribit.
units.tr: CCXXXIV. Whoever, however, remains formally, as they say, a Papist, that is, in this apostasy and this idolatry, and under this tyranny of the Pontificate and Papacy dies without repentance, will undoubtedly perish forever.

units.la: CCXXXV. Quod dicentes, non damnamus, neque deserendas & fugiendas docemus personas, (super quo Deum testem invocamus) sed errores & excessus praedictos, verbo Dei damnatos.
units.tr: CCXXXV. In saying this we do not condemn, nor teach that persons are to be forsaken and fled from (on this point we call God to witness), but the aforesaid errors and excesses, condemned by the Word of God.

units.la: CCXXXVI. Quin imò, jubente sic charitate Christiana, pro omnibus sub Papatu sic constitutis, pro Regibus & incolis terræ, pro magnis & paruis, pro ipso Papa, & vniuerso eius clero, Deum toto pectore oramus, vt pro multitudine miserationum suarum oculos cordium eis aperiat, & conuertat conuertendos, seruet seruandos, signatos sigillo Dei in frontibus suis, per JESUM CHRI-STUM Dominum nostrum! Cui sit gloria, potestas, & honor in secula. Amen, Amen.
units.tr: CCXXXVI. Indeed, as Christian charity commands, we pray to God with our whole heart for all who are thus placed under the Papacy, for kings and inhabitants of the earth, for great and small, for the Pope himself and his whole clergy: that, according to the multitude of his mercies, he may open the eyes of their hearts, convert those who are to be converted, preserve those who are to be preserved, and seal them with the seal of God on their foreheads, through Jesus Christ our Lord! To whom be glory, power, and honour for ever and ever. Amen, Amen.

units.la: SYMBOLVM B. ATHANASII, De SS. Trinitate: & de Incarnatione Filj DEI Domini nostri Jesu Christi: Cum Notis D. DAVIDIS PAREI.
units.tr: THE CREED OF ST ATHANASIUS, On the Holy Trinity, and on the Incarnation of the Son of God our Lord Jesus Christ, with notes by D. David Pareus.

units.la: EIDEI CATHOLICAE DE TRINITATE
units.tr: THE CATHOLIC FAITH CONCERNING THE TRINITY

units.la: ARTICVLVS I.
units.tr: ARTICLE I.

units.la: QVICVNQVE 1. vult saluus esse, ante omnia opus est, vt teneat Catholicam fidem: quam nisi quisque integram inuiolatamque seruauerit, absque dubio in æternum peribit.
units.tr: Whoever wishes to be saved must above all hold the Catholic faith. Unless a person keeps this faith whole and inviolate, he will without doubt perish eternally.

units.la: Declaratio.
units.tr: Declaration.

units.la: Sic necessitas fidei catholicæ ad salutem passim in scriptura declaratur. Marci 16,16. Qui crediderit, & baptizatus fuerit, saluus erit: qui verò non crediderit, condemnabitur: vbi idem SS. Trinitatis primo requiri, ex Matt.28.19. patet. Heb.11. vers. 6. Absque fide impossibile est placere Deo: Ergo & impossibile saluari. 2 Thess.1,8. Dominus Iesus de cœlo veniens in flamma ignis vltionem infliget illis, qui Deum non nouerunt, neque auscultant Euangelio Domini nostri Iesu Christi. Qui verò Deum non nouerunt, nec Euangelio obediunt: fidem catholicam vbique non tenent. Salui igitur esse non possunt; sed absq; dubio in æternum peribunt.
units.tr: In this way the necessity of the Catholic faith for salvation is declared throughout Scripture. Mark 16:16: "He who believes and is baptized will be saved; but he who does not believe will be condemned." That the same faith in the Holy Trinity is required first is clear from Matt. 28:19. Heb. 11:6: "Without faith it is impossible to please God." Therefore it is also impossible to be saved. 2 Thess. 1:8: "The Lord Jesus, coming from heaven in flaming fire, will inflict vengeance on those who do not know God and do not obey the gospel of our Lord Jesus Christ." Those who do not know God, and do not obey the gospel, do not hold the Catholic faith anywhere. Therefore they cannot be saved, but without doubt will perish eternally.

units.la: ARTICVLVS II.
units.tr: ARTICLE II.

units.la: 2. Fides autem catholica hæc est, 3. vt vnum Deum in Trinitate, & Trinitatem in vnitate veneremur: 4. neque confundentes personas, 5. neq; essentiam separantes.
units.tr: 2. Now this is the Catholic faith: 3. that we worship one God in Trinity, and Trinity in unity; 4. neither confusing the persons, 5. nor separating the essence.

units.la: Declaratio.
units.tr: Declaration.

units.la: Fides catholica seu vniuersalis vocatur, non quæ ab vniuersis creditur, sed quæ vniuersis creditu necessaria faria est ad salutem. Sic enim Euphronius Presbyter in expositione huius symboli Athanas. Fides, inquit, Catholica, seu universalis dicitur: hoc est, recta; quam Ecclesia universa tenere debet. Ea duobus praecipuè capitibus symbolo B. Athanasij definitur: Fide sacrosanctae Trinitatis: & fide incarnationis atque mediationis Filij Dei.
units.tr: The faith is called catholic or universal, not because it is believed by all, but because it is necessary for salvation for all. For so Euphronius the elder, in his exposition of this creed of Athanasius, says: "The faith is called Catholic or universal, that is, right, which the whole Church ought to hold." This faith is defined in the creed of St Athanasius under two main heads: faith in the most holy Trinity, and faith in the incarnation and mediation of the Son of God.

units.la: 3. Ut unum Deum.] Hoc primum & summum illud mysterium, quo fides Christiana à Paganorum, Judaeorum, Mahumetanorum, haereticorumq; sectis discernitur. Absurdum quippe istis omnibus videtur, unum Deum in Trinitate, & Trinitatem in unitate venerari, hoc est, unum Deum essentia, Trinum personis, Patrem, Filium & Spiritum sanctum credere & adorare. Quasi verò rationi humanae, qua isti fidem metiuntur, minus absurdum sit, mundum ex nihilo, hominem ex gleba terrae, vel ut Alcoranus fingit, ex bulla aquae primò creatum, mortuosque vermibus absumptos potentia Dei resurrecturos credere, quae tamen ab illis creduntur. Atqui de Deo non secundum rationis captum, à quo natura Dei est remotissima, sed secundum parat factiones divinas ipsius verbo revelatas credendum est atque statuendum. Haec verò testantur, Deum verum & aeternum esse quidè non nisi unum numero & essentia: Deut.6,4. Audi Israel: Iehovah Deus noster, Iehovah unus est: nempe essentia: (nomen enim יהוה Hebraeis est ab esse, & essentiam proprie significat.) Esse verò etiam trinum hypostasibus Patrem, & Filium, & Spiritum sanctum. Christus enim (τῆς πίστεως ἀρχηγὸς καὶ τελειωτὴς, fidei dux & consummator) volens in novo Testamento omnes Gentes in unam fidem & cultum, unius veri Dei, novo Sacramento consecrari, jussit omnes baptizari in nomen Patris, & Filij, & Spiritus sancti, tanquam in nomen & fidem unius veri Dei, tribus hypostasibus sive personis subsistentem. Pater enim expresse vocatur ὑπόστασις seu persona divina, Heb.1,3. Qualis autem Pater, talis Filius, & talis Spiritus sanctus, Artic.IV. Neque baptizamur in nomen, nisi ὑποστάσεων divinarum. Filius igitur etiam ὑποστάσεως divina: tres ὑποστάσεις divinae: Spiritus quoque sanctus ὑποστάσεως divina; quae ὑποστάσεως divinae sunt unus & aeternus Deus. Clarius hoc mysterium expressit B. Johannes, inquiens: Tres sunt, qui testificantur in caelo: Pater, Sermo, & Spiritus sanctus: & hi tres unum sunt. Sermonem seu λόγον vocat Filium, appellatione sibi consueta. Tres autem testificantes in caelo intelligit vel tres Deos, vel tres hypostases divinas. Sed non tres Deos: Deus enim unus est. Tres igitur hypostases divinas. Et tres dicit unum esse, vel essentia, vel hypostasi. Sed non hypostasi: Sic enim tres non essent. Essentia igitur, eoq; voluntate & testimonij consensu tres vnum Deum esse docet.
units.tr: 3. "That we worship one God." This is the first and highest mystery, by which the Christian faith is distinguished from the sects of the pagans, Jews, Mohammedans and heretics. For to all of them it seems absurd to worship one God in Trinity and Trinity in unity, that is, to believe and adore one God in essence, three in persons, the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit. As if it were less absurd to human reason, by which they measure faith, to believe that the world was created out of nothing, that man was first created from a clod of earth, or, as the Koran invents, from a bubble of water, and that the dead, eaten by worms, will rise again by the power of God, which things they nevertheless do believe. But God is to be believed and held not according to the grasp of reason, from which the nature of God is most remote, but according to his divine works revealed in his own word. These testify that God is true and eternal, indeed only one in number and essence: Deut. 6:4, "Hear, Israel: Jehovah our God, Jehovah is one" [יהוה], that is, in essence (for the name יהוה among the Hebrews comes from to be and properly signifies essence). And that he is also three in hypostases: the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit. For Christ, the "leader and perfecter of faith" [τῆς πίστεως ἀρχηγὸς καὶ τελειωτὴς], wishing in the New Testament that all nations be consecrated by the new sacrament to one faith and worship of the one true God, commanded that "all be baptized in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit," as into the name and faith of the one true God, subsisting in three hypostases or persons. For the Father is expressly called a hypostasis or divine person, Heb. 1:3. But as the Father is, so the Son is, and so the Holy Spirit is (see Article IV). Nor are we baptized into a name except of divine hypostases. Therefore the Son is also a divine hypostasis; three divine hypostases; the Holy Spirit too is a divine hypostasis; and these divine hypostases are one and eternal God. The blessed John expressed this mystery more clearly, saying: "There are three who bear witness in heaven: the Father, the Word, and the Holy Spirit; and these three are one." He calls the Son Word or logos [λόγον], by a name customary for him. But by the three who bear witness in heaven he understands either three Gods or three divine hypostases. Not three Gods, for God is one. Therefore three divine hypostases. And he says that the three are one, either in essence or in hypostasis. Not in hypostasis, for so they would not be three. Therefore he teaches that the three are one God in essence, and so by will and agreement of testimony.

units.la: Mysterium hoc fidei sanctis Patribus in V. Testamento non fuisse omnino ignotum, varie doceri potest. Tam clarè verò omnibus illis non innotuisse, vt nunc, nihil vtiq; mirum: quandoquidem & huius & aliorum mysteriorum plena reuelatio, Filij Dei in carne manifestati, tanquam fidei consummatoris mysterio reseruata fuit: testante Johanne: Deum nemo vidit vnquam: Filius, qui est in sinu Patris, ipse enarrauit nobis.
units.tr: That this mystery of faith was by no means unknown to the holy Fathers in the Old Testament can be shown in various ways. Yet that it was not so clearly known to all of them as it is now is surely no wonder, since the full revelation both of this mystery and of the others, the Son of God having been manifested in the flesh, was reserved as the mystery of the consummator of faith; as John testifies: "No one has seen God at any time; the Son, who is in the bosom of the Father, he has declared him to us."

units.la: Quae verò ab hostibus SS. Trinitatis, ex ratione humana, vel scripturis malè depravatis contra disputari solent: in disputationis cursu explicanda venient.
units.tr: As to the objections which are commonly brought against the Holy Trinity by its enemies, from human reason or from wrongly distorted Scriptures, these will be explained in the course of the discussion.

units.la: 4. Neque confundentes.] Quod fecerunt Noetiani, Sabelliani, Patrispassiani dicti haeretici, vt vnum Deum, sic vnam tantum personam, modò Patris, modò Filij, modò Spiritus sancti nomine appellatam Deo tribuentes, nisi hoc rationis principio, hodie Mahumetanis, Iudaeus & haereticis communi: vnius naturae indiuiduae non posse nisi vnam esse hypostasin siue personam. Quod quidem de natura indiuidua finita, creata, verum est: de natura verò diuina, infinita, increata, falsum esse, reuelationes diuinae conuincunt.
units.tr: 4. "Neither confusing." This was done by the heretics called Noetians, Sabellians and Patripassians, who attributed to God one person only, now named by the name of the Father, now of the Son, now of the Holy Spirit, as one God; on the principle of reason which is common today to Mohammedans, Jews and heretics, that a single undivided nature can have only one hypostasis or person. This is indeed true of a finite, created, undivided nature; but that it is false of the divine, infinite and uncreated nature, the divine revelations prove.

units.la: 5. Neque essentiam separantes.] Quod fecerunt & faciunt Trinitheitae, cum personis diuinis essentiam Dei multiplicantes contra scripturas.
units.tr: 5. "Nor separating the essence." This was done, and is still done, by the Tritheists, who, contrary to the Scriptures, multiply the essence of God along with the divine persons.

units.la: ARTICVLVS III.
units.tr: Article III.

units.la: 6. Alia est enim Persona Patris, alia Filij, alia Spiritus sancti: 7. Sed Patris & Filij & Spiritus sancti vna est diuinitas, aequalis gloria, coaeterna maiestas.
units.tr: 6. For the Person of the Father is one, the Person of the Son another, and the Person of the Holy Spirit another. 7. But the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit have one divinity, equal glory and co-eternal majesty.

units.la: Declaratio.
units.tr: Declaration.

units.la: 6. Alia est enim.] Distinctio personarum, quod vna non sit alia: sed alius sit Pater, alius Filius, alius Spiritus sanctus, euidenter docetur in scripturis. Iohan.5. v.32. Est alius, qui testatur de me: & qui misit me Pater, ipse testatus est de me. Iohan.14. v.26. Paracletus autem ille Spiritus sanctus, quem mittit Pater in nomine meo. Iohan.14. vers.16. Ego rogabo Patrem, & alium Paracletum mittet vobis. Quomodo verò sint distinctae personae, sequitur Articulo VIII.
units.tr: 6. For the one is different.] The distinction of the persons, that one is not the other, but the Father is one, the Son another, and the Holy Spirit another, is plainly taught in Scripture. John 5:32: There is another who bears witness of me, and I know that the testimony which he bears of me is true. John 14:26: But that Paraclete, the Holy Spirit, whom the Father will send in my name. John 14:16: I will ask the Father, and he will send you another Paraclete. How the persons are distinct follows in Article VIII.

units.la: 7. Sed Patris & Filij.] Consubstantialitas & coaequalitas diuinarum personarum aduersus Arianos & Photinianos asseritur, juxta scripturas: Ioh.10,30. Ego & Pater vnum sumus: nempe diuinitatis essentia, eoq; & robore atq; potentia. Humanitatis enim naturâ Filius & Pater vnum non sunt. Joh.5.v.7. Et hi tres vnum sunt: nempe diuinitate, eoq; & voluntatis atque testimonij vnitate. In trium quoque non nomina, sed nomen tanquam vnius veri Dei baptizamur. Joh.5,18.& Joh.10,33. Intelligebant Judæi, quod Christus se faceret æqualem Deo. At non faciebat se æqualem Deo humanitatis natura: (sic enim vere blasphemum dixissent.) Ergo diuinitatis & diuinorum operum gloria. Joh.16,15. Omnia quæ habet Pater, mea sunt. Ergo & vna diuinitas & coæterna maiestas, quam habet Pater, est Filij: proinde & Spiritus sancti. Non sunt enim, nec fuerunt ab æterno Pater & Filius absque suo Spiritu. Trium igitur vna diuinitas, æqualis gloria, coæterna maiestas.
units.tr: 7. But of the Father and the Son.] The consubstantiality and co-equality of the divine persons is asserted against the Arians and Photinians, according to Scripture. John 10:30: I and the Father are one: namely in the essence of the divinity, and so also in strength and power. For in the nature of humanity the Son and the Father are not one. 1 John 5:7: And these three are one: namely in divinity, and so also in the unity of will and of testimony. We are baptized also not into the names but into the name of one true God. John 5:18 and John 10:33: the Jews understood that Christ made himself equal to God. But he did not make himself equal to God by the nature of his humanity (for in that case they would have spoken truly in calling it blasphemy). Therefore he is equal in the glory of the divinity and of the divine works. John 16:15: All that the Father has is mine. Therefore the one divinity and the co-eternal majesty which the Father has belongs also to the Son, and consequently to the Holy Spirit. For the Father and the Son are not, and have not been from eternity, without their Spirit. Therefore of the three there is one divinity, equal glory and co-eternal majesty.

units.la: ARTICVLVS IV.
units.tr: Article IV.

units.la: 8. Qualis Pater, talis Filius, talis Spiritus sanctus. Increatus Pater: increatus Filius: increatus Spiritus sanctus. Immensus Pater: immensus Filius: immensus Spiritus sanctus. Æternus Pater: æternus Filius: æternus Spiritus sanctus. 9. Et tamen non tres æterni, sed vnus æternus: sicut non tres increati: nec tres immensi: sed vnus increatus, & vnus immensus.
units.tr: 8. Such is the Father, such is the Son, such is the Holy Spirit. The Father uncreated, the Son uncreated, the Holy Spirit uncreated. The Father immense, the Son immense, the Holy Spirit immense. The Father eternal, the Son eternal, the Holy Spirit eternal. 9. And yet not three eternals, but one eternal: just as not three uncreated, nor three immense, but one uncreated and one immense.

units.la: Declaratio.
units.tr: Declaration.

units.la: 8. Qualis Pater.] Coæqualis & consubstantialis diuinarum personarum ex identitate essentialium attributorum Dei declaratur: quia vt Pater, ita Filius & Spiritus sanctus est increatus, immensus, æternus.
units.tr: 8. Such is the Father.] The equality and consubstantiality of the divine persons is declared from the identity of the essential attributes of God: because, as the Father is, so the Son and the Holy Spirit are uncreated, immense and eternal.

units.la: De Patre nemo ambigit.
units.tr: That the Father is so, no one doubts.

units.la: Filius pariter increatus: quia in principio creationis erat, & erat Deus, & omnia per ipsum facta sunt, & sine eo factum est nihil, quod factum est. Ioh.1,1,3. Heb.1,2.&c.
units.tr: The Son is likewise uncreated: because in the beginning of creation he was, and he was God, and all things were made through him, and without him nothing was made that has been made. John 1:1, 3; Heb. 1:2, etc.

units.la: Pariter immensus: quia vnà cum Patre mansionem facit, & habitat in cordibus omnium fidelium, Ioan.14.vers.23. Ephes.3,17. Estque nobiscum omnibus diebus, vsque ad consummationem seculi, Matth.28,20.
units.tr: Likewise immense: because he makes his abode together with the Father and dwells in the hearts of all the faithful, John 14:23; Eph. 3:17. And he is with us all days, even to the end of the age, Matt. 28:20.

units.la: Pariter æternus: quia antequam montes fundati essent, ante colles, erat genitus. Prou.8,25. Ioh.1,1. Ἐστιν ἀ καὶ ω [?], principium & finis, primus & nouissimus, Apoc.1,8. & 21,6. & 22,13.
units.tr: Likewise eternal: because before the mountains were founded, before the hills, he was begotten. Prov. 8:25; John 1:1. "I am the Alpha and the Omega [τὸ Ἄλφα καὶ τὸ Ὦ], the beginning and the end, the first and the last," Rev. 1:8; 21:6; 22:13.

units.la: Spiritus sanctus pariter increatus: quia in principio creationis quam creator ferebatur in superficie aquarum, Gen.1,2. ornauit cœlos, Iob.36,13. fecit & vivificat Iobum, Iob.33,4.&c. Pariter immensus: quia habitat in nobis, Rom.8,9.1Cor.3,16. 1Tim.1,14. Inde praeclarè Didymus: Ipse Spiritus sanctus si unus Did.lib.1.de ie creaturis esset, saltem circumscriptam haberet substantiam: sicut Spiritu S. universa, quae facta sunt, etsi non circumscribantur. Spiritus autem sanctus cum in pluribus sit, non habet substantiam circum- scriptam.
units.tr: The Holy Spirit is likewise uncreated: because at the beginning of creation he was carried over the surface of the waters, Gen. 1:2; he adorned the heavens, Job 26:13; he made Job and gives him life, Job 33:4, etc. Likewise immense: because he dwells in us, Rom. 8:9; 1 Cor. 3:16; 1 Tim. 1:14. Hence the excellent Didymus says: If the Holy Spirit himself were one of the creatures, he would at least have a circumscribed substance, just as all the things that were made, although they are not circumscribed. But since the Holy Spirit is in many, he does not have a circumscribed substance.

units.la: Pariter æternus: quia fuit in creatione rerum, Genes.1,2. & quia Deus nunquam fuit absque suo Spiritu sancto.
units.tr: Likewise eternal: because he was present at the creation of things, Gen. 1:2, and because God was never without his Holy Spirit.

units.la: 9. Et tamen non.] Sicut essentia divina non multiplicatur cum personis, quia una est tribus communis: sic recta fides vetat multiplicari essentialia attributa Dei cum personis: quia una eademque sunt tribus communia. Ut igitur fides Catholica cavet credere cum Tritheitis tres Deos, sed unum Deum in Trinitate veneratur: ita cavet dicere tres increatos, tres immensos, tres æternos, sed unum increatum, unum immensum, unum æternum in Trinitate profitetur.
units.tr: 9. And yet not.] Just as the divine essence is not multiplied with the persons, because it is one and common to the three, so sound faith forbids that the essential attributes of God be multiplied with the persons, because they are one and the same, common to the three. Therefore, as the Catholic faith takes care not to believe with the Tritheists in three Gods, but venerates one God in the Trinity, so it takes care not to say three uncreated, three immense, three eternal, but professes in the Trinity one uncreated, one immense and one eternal.

units.la: ARTICVLVS V.
units.tr: Article V.

units.la: 10. Similiter omnipotens Pater: omnipotens Filius: omnipotens Spiritus sanctus. 11. Et tamen non tres omnipotentes, sed unus omnipotens. Ita Deus Pater: Deus Filius: Deus Spiritus sanctus: & tamen non tres Dij, sed unus est Deus. Ita Dominus Pater: Dominus Filius: Dominus Spiritus sanctus: 12. Et tamen non tres Domini, sed unus Dominus.
units.tr: 10. Likewise the Father is almighty, the Son almighty, the Holy Spirit almighty. 11. And yet not three almighty, but one almighty. So God the Father, God the Son, God the Holy Spirit: and yet not three Gods, but one God. So the Lord the Father, the Lord the Son, the Lord the Holy Spirit: 12. And yet not three Lords, but one Lord.

units.la: Declaratio.
units.tr: Declaration.

units.la: 10. Similiter omnipotens.] Amplius declaratur coæqualitas & consubstantialitas divinarum personarum ex attributorum divinorum, ipsiusque Divinitatis unitate: quia ut Pater, ita Filius, & Spiritus sanctus omnipotens, Deus, & Dominus.
units.tr: 10. Likewise almighty.] The equality and consubstantiality of the divine persons is further declared from the divine attributes and from the unity of the Godhead itself: for the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit are each almighty, God and Lord.

units.la: De Patre nemo ambigit.
units.tr: No one disputes this of the Father.

units.la: Filius pariter omnipotens: quia omnia, quae habet Pater, sunt et-iam Filij: proinde & omnipotentia. Ioh.16,15. Et Deus omnipotens expressè vocatur Apoc.1,8. & 4,8.
units.tr: The Son is likewise almighty, since all things that the Father has are also the Son's, and therefore also omnipotence. John 16:15. And God is expressly called Almighty, Rev. 1:8 and 4:8.

units.la: Pariter igitur & Deus: &quidem Deus verus, 1Ioh.5,20.Deus benedictus in secula, Rom.9,5. ubi Dei nomen certè substantiam divinam, non substantiæ tantum attributum significat: contra duo impudentissima Socini effata, nusquam simplex Dei nomen Christo tributum substantiam significare: nusquam etiam in divinis literis inveniri scriptum, ubi Dei nomen locum subiecti tenens ad Christum necessariò sit referendum. Prius redarguitur pluripluribus scripturæ locis, præsertim illis: Rom. 9, 5. Ex quibus est Christus secundum carnem, qui est supra omnia Deus benedictus in secula. 1 Ioh. 5, 20. Sumus in vero illo, in Filio eius Iesu Christo. Hic est verus Deus & vita æterna. Posterius falsi convincitur tum aliis, tum his locis: Act. 20, 28. Deus ecclesiam proprio sanguine acquisivit. 1 Tim. 3, 16. Deus conspicuus factus est in carne.
units.tr: Likewise, then, he is God, indeed the true God, 1 John 5:20, God blessed for ever, Rom. 9:5, where the name of God certainly signifies the divine substance and not merely an attribute of the substance. Against this, the two most shameless assertions of the Socinians are that the simple name of God, when given to Christ, nowhere signifies substance, and that nowhere in the divine writings is it found written that the name of God, standing in the place of the subject, must necessarily be referred to Christ. The first is refuted by very many passages of Scripture, especially these: Rom. 9:5, "of whom, as concerning the flesh, Christ came, who is over all, God blessed for ever"; 1 John 5:20, "We are in him that is true, even in his Son Jesus Christ. This is the true God and eternal life." The second is shown to be false both by other passages and by these: Acts 20:28, "God purchased the church with his own blood"; 1 Tim. 3:16, "God was manifested in the flesh."

units.la: Pariter & Dominus. Luc. 2, 11. Vobis natus est hodie Seruator, qui est Christus Dominus, &c.
units.tr: Likewise also Lord. Luke 2:11, "For unto you is born this day in the city of David a Saviour, which is Christ the Lord," etc.

units.la: Spiritus sanctus pariter omnipotens: quia omnia charismata & energemata diuina efficit vnus ille & idem Spiritus, distribuens priuatim illa vnicuique, sicut vult, 1 Cor. 12, 11.
units.tr: The Holy Spirit is likewise almighty, since all these works are wrought by one and the same Spirit, dividing to every man severally as he will, 1 Cor. 12:11.

units.la: Pariter Deus & Iehoua olim locutus est per Prophetam Esaiam Act. 28, 25. & per os Dauidis, Act. 1, 25. in cuius nomen baptizamur, Matth. 28, 19. quique testatur cum Patre & Filio in cœlo, 1 Ioh. 5, 7. Cauillantur hæretici, non inueniri ad literam scriptū: Spiritus sanctus est Deus: effugio nimis friuolo. Vbi vero ad literam scriptum: Pater est Deus: Filius est Deus? Quis fideliū requirit tot literas scriptas, cum res sit scripta? Nonne aperte scriptum 1 Ioh. 5, 7. Spiritus sanctus testatur in cœlo. Et mox: Testimonium Dei maius est. Act. 5, 3. Mentitus es Spiritui sancto. Et mox: Mentitus es Deo. 1 Cor. 3, 16. Estis templum Dei, & Spiritus Dei habitat in vobis. Et mox c. 6, 19. Estis templum Spiritus sancti.
units.tr: Likewise God and Jehovah spoke by the prophet Isaiah, Acts 28:25, and by the mouth of David, Acts 1:16, in whose name we are baptized, Matt. 28:19, and who bears witness with the Father and the Son in heaven, 1 John 5:7. The heretics cavil that it is not found written word for word, "The Holy Spirit is God"; this is far too flimsy an escape. But where is it written word for word, "The Father is God; the Son is God"? Who among the faithful asks for so many words written, when the thing itself is written? Is it not plainly written in 1 John 5:7, "The Holy Spirit bears witness in heaven"? And soon after, "the witness of God is greater." Acts 5:3, "You have lied to the Holy Spirit"; and soon after, "You have lied to God." 1 Cor. 3:16, "You are the temple of God, and the Spirit of God dwells in you"; and soon after, 1 Cor. 6:19, "You are the temple of the Holy Spirit."

units.la: Pariter denique Dominus: quia pariter in Spiritus sancti, tanquam Domini nostri nomen, hoc est, cultum, seruitutem & obedientiam, atque in Patris & Filij nomen baptizamur. Matth. 28, 19. Et Apostoli Deum, qui per os Dauidis dixit: Quare fremuerunt gentes, hoc est, Spiritum sanctum sic inuocant: Domine, tu es Deus ille, qui fecisti cœlum & terram, mare & omnia, quæ in eis sunt. Actor. 4, 24.
units.tr: Finally, he is Lord likewise, since we are likewise baptized in the name of the Holy Spirit as of our Lord, that is, into worship, service and obedience, as well as in the name of the Father and the Son, Matt. 28:19. And the apostles, addressing God who by the mouth of David said, "Why do the heathen rage?", that is, they invoke the Holy Spirit in this way: "Lord, you are that God who made heaven and earth, the sea and all that is in them," Acts 4:24.

units.la: 11. Et tamen non. ] Vide num. 8.
units.tr: 11. And yet not.] See no. 8.

units.la: 12. Et tamen non tres.] Atqui vnus Dominus Iesus Christus 1 Cor. 8, 6. Ergo non Pater Dominus: nec Spiritus sanctus Dominus. Fides Catholica hoc ita conciliat, quod solus Dominus est Pater: Filius, & Spiritus sanctus, dominatu Deitatis, tribus personis communi: qui in rerum omnium creatione & gubernatione consistit: & à quo Apostolus 1 Cor. 8, 6. non Patrem, nec Spiritum sanctum, sed deos falsos & creaturas omnes excludit. Vnus vero & solus Dominus est Iesus Christus dominatu mediationis, non tribus personis communi, sed Christi proprio, qui in prophetico sacerdotali & regio Mediatoris officio consistit, & à quo Apostolus 1 Cor. 8, 6. non tam Patrem & Spiritum sanctum sequestrat, quam ficitios mediatores Paganorum, Iudæorum & Anitichristianorum excludit.
units.tr: 12. And yet not three.] But there is one Lord, Jesus Christ, 1 Cor. 8:6. Therefore the Father is not the Lord, nor is the Holy Spirit the Lord. The Catholic faith reconciles this by holding that the Father alone is Lord, and that the Son and the Holy Spirit share in the lordship of the Godhead, which is common to the three persons, and which consists in the creation and government of all things; and that by the words of 1 Cor. 8:6 the Apostle excludes from this not the Father and the Holy Spirit, but the false gods and all creatures. And there is one and only Lord, Jesus Christ, by the lordship of mediation, which is not common to the three persons but proper to Christ, and which consists in the prophetic, priestly and kingly office of the Mediator; and by the same words of 1 Cor. 8:6 the Apostle does not so much separate the Father and the Holy Spirit from him as exclude the fictitious mediators of the pagans, the Jews and the Antichristians.

units.la: ARTICVLVS VI.
units.tr: ARTICLE VI.

units.la: 13. Quia sicut sigillatim vnamquamque personam Deum &Dominum confiteri Christiana veritate compellimur: ita tres Deos, aut Dominos dicere, catholica religione prohibemur.
units.tr: 13. Since, just as we are compelled by Christian truth to confess each person severally as God and Lord, so by the Catholic religion we are forbidden to say that there are three Gods, or three Lords.

units.la: Declaratio.
units.tr: Declaration.

units.la: 13. Quia sicut.] Hic articulus reddit rationem antithescos articuli IV. & V. prius declaratam ex scripturis sacris: quibus solis &Christiana veritas, &catholica religio, tum quoad singularum personarum æqualitatem, tum quoad earundem ὁμοουσίαν, &in Trinitate consubstantialitatem fundatur. Christiana igitur veritas vnamquamq; personam Deum &Dominum nos confiteri compellit: quia scripturæ solui non possunt, ita asserentes, vt fuit num.9. Et catholica fides tres Deos, aut Dominos dicere prohibet: quia scripturæ solui nequeunt, vnum Deum &Dominum adstruentes: vt fuit num. 3. & 11.
units.tr: 13. Since just as.] This article gives the reason for the antithesis of Articles IV and V, previously declared from the holy Scriptures, on which alone both Christian truth and the Catholic religion are founded, both as to the equality of the individual persons and as to their homoousia [ὁμοουσίαν], that is, the consubstantiality in the Trinity. Christian truth therefore compels us to confess each person as God and Lord, because the Scriptures cannot be undone when they assert this, as was shown in no. 9. And the Catholic faith forbids us to say that there are three Gods, or three Lords, because the Scriptures cannot be undone when they establish one God and one Lord, as was shown in nos. 3 and 11.

units.la: ARTICVLVS VII.
units.tr: ARTICLE VII.

units.la: 14. Pater 15. à nullo est factus, 16. nec creatus, 17. nec genitus: 18. Filius à Patre solo est, 19. non factus, 20. nec creatus, 21. sed genitus. Spiritus sanctus, 22. à Patre & Filio 23. non factus, nec creatus, 24. nec genitus: 25. sed procedens. Vnus ergo Pater, non tres Patres: vnus Filius, non tres Filij: vnus Spiritus sanctus, non tres Spiritus sancti.
units.tr: 14. The Father 15. is made by no one, 16. nor created, 17. nor begotten. 18. The Son is from the Father alone, 19. not made, 20. nor created, 21. but begotten. The Holy Spirit 22. is from the Father and the Son, 23. not made, nor created, 24. nor begotten, 25. but proceeding. So there is one Father, not three Fathers; one Son, not three Sons; one Holy Spirit, not three Holy Spirits.

units.la: Declaratio.
units.tr: Declaration.

units.la: 14. Pater.] Hic articulus declarat tertium, de personarum distinctione: quæ in distincto existendi modo cuiusque personæ proprio consistit.
units.tr: 14. The Father.] This article sets out the third point, on the distinction of the persons, which consists in the distinct mode of existing that belongs to each person.

units.la: 15. A nullo.] Gr. ἀπ' ἀδίνος ποιουμένων. Græci patres dicunt ἀγέννητος, ortum vel originem nullam habens ab alio, quia à seipso est.
units.tr: 15. By no one.] Greek: ἀπ' ἀδίνος ποιουμένων [not made from anyone]. The Greek Fathers call him ἀγέννητος [unbegotten], having no origin or source from another, because he is from himself.

units.la: 16. Nec creatus.] Gr. ἀδί ἐκ ἐποιήθη, neq; ex aliquo factus, pro ἀδὲ κτίσεως neq; creatus: secus esset creatura alterius.
units.tr: 16. Nor created.] Greek: ἀδὲ ἐκ ἐποιήθη [nor made from anything], in place of ἀδὲ κτίσεως [nor created]: otherwise he would be the creature of another.

units.la: 17. Nec genitus.] Gr. ἀδὲ γεννηθείς, unde Græci Theologi Patrem vocant ἀγέννητον ingenitum: quia si esset genitus, esset filius, non pater. Atque hic est modus existendi, quo Pater à Filio & Spiritu sancto distinguitur, quod à nullo est, sed à se.
units.tr: 17. Nor begotten.] Greek: ἀδὲ γεννηθείς [nor begotten]. Hence the Greek theologians call the Father ἀγέννητον [unbegotten], because if he were begotten he would be a son, not a father. This is the mode of existing by which the Father is distinguished from the Son and the Holy Spirit: he is from no one, but from himself.

units.la: 18. Filius à Patre.] Non etiam à Spiritu sancto: quia vt sol habens Filium: sic à solo Patre est Filius. Ideo non est Filius Abrahæ & Dauidis & Mariæ, nisi secundum carnem.
units.tr: 18. The Son is from the Father.] Not also from the Holy Spirit: for just as the sun has the Son, so the Son is from the Father alone. Therefore he is the Son of Abraham, of David and of Mary only according to the flesh.

units.la: 19. Non factus. Quod factum ex muliere, dicit Apostolus Galat.4,4.secundum carnem est intelligendum, non secundum Diuinitatem.
units.tr: 19. Not made. What the Apostle says, that he was "made of a woman" (Gal. 4:4), must be understood according to the flesh, not according to the Godhead.

units.la: 20. Nec creatus. Vt Arius blasphemabat, Filium esse primo creatum, abutens loco apocrypho corrupto Syr.24,14. & depravans scripturas alias, quæ Christum vocant ἀρχὴ τῆς κτίσεως τοῦ Θεοῦ, principium creatura Dei, non vtique passiuum, sed actiuum. Coloss.1,5.18. Apoc.3,4..
units.tr: 20. Nor created. As Arius blasphemed, saying that the Son was first created, abusing the corrupt apocryphal passage at Sir. 24:14 and distorting other Scriptures which call Christ ἀρχὴ τῆς κτίσεως τοῦ Θεοῦ [the beginning of the creation of God], that is, "the beginning of the creature of God", not in the passive but in the active sense. Col. 1:5, 18; Rev. 3:14.

units.la: 21. Sed genitus. Græcè μονογενὴς ἐκ τοῦ πατρὸς γεννηθεὶς, seu γεννητὸς ἐκ τοῦ πατρὸς, genitus ex Patre: & quidem solus. Ideo est μονογενὴς παρὰ πατρὸς, unigenitus à Patre, Ioh.1,14. & sapientia genita, antequam montes fundati essent, Prou.8,25. hoc est, ab æterno. Hæc æterna Filii generatio à Patre est ineffabilis communicatio essentiæ diuinæ, qua sola secunda persona diuinitatis à sola prima, tanquam Filius ex Patre essentiam accipit eandem & integram, quam Pater habet. Atq; hic est modus existendi, quo Filius à Patre & Spiritu sancto distinguitur, quod solus est à Patre genitus.
units.tr: 21. But begotten. Greek: μονογενὴς ἐκ τοῦ πατρὸς γεννηθεὶς, or γεννητὸς ἐκ τοῦ πατρὸς [begotten of the Father], and indeed alone. Hence he is μονογενὴς παρὰ πατρὸς [the only-begotten from the Father], John 1:14, and "wisdom begotten before the mountains were settled" (Prov. 8:25), that is, from eternity. This eternal generation of the Son from the Father is an ineffable communication of the divine essence, by which the second person of the Godhead alone, from the first person alone, receives as Son from the Father the same and whole essence which the Father has. This is the mode of existing by which the Son is distinguished from the Father and the Holy Spirit: he alone is begotten of the Father.

units.la: 22. A Patre. Græcè ἀπὸ τοῦ πατρὸς, à Patre: vt Ioh.15,26. ὁ παρὰ τοῦ πατρὸς ἐκπορεύεται, qui à Patre procedit. Non vero dicit Athanasius: ἀπὸ τοῦ μόνου πατρὸς, à solo Patre: sicut dixerat de Filio: ἀπὸ τοῦ μόνου πατρὸς, quam exclusiuam cum posteriores Græci contra Ecclesiam Apostoli, & Athanasij tandem adderent, Latina Ecclesia ad explendum scripturæ sensum dixit: à Patre & Filio.
units.tr: 22. From the Father. Greek: ἀπὸ τοῦ πατρὸς [from the Father], as in John 15:26: ὁ παρὰ τοῦ πατρὸς ἐκπορεύεται [who proceeds from the Father]. But Athanasius does not say ἀπὸ τοῦ μόνου πατρὸς [from the Father alone], as he had said of the Son. The later Greeks, against the Church and the Apostle, and finally Athanasius, added this exclusive phrase; the Latin Church, to complete the sense of Scripture, said from the Father and the Son.

units.la: 23. Non factus. Contra Macedonianos, qui Spiritum sanctum creaturam, creatos motus, creata dona spiritualia fingebant.
units.tr: 23. Not made. Against the Macedonians, who imagined the Holy Spirit to be a creature, created motions and created spiritual gifts.

units.la: 24. Nec genitus. Quia sic Filius esset. Nam esse genitum est esse filium.
units.tr: 24. Nor begotten. Because then he would be the Son. For to be begotten is to be a son.

units.la: 25. Sed procedens. Græcè, ἐκπορευόμενον, seu ἐκπορευτὸν, seu ἐκπορεύεσθαι, vt dicitur Ioh.15,46. Est autem hæc processio seu emanatio ineffabilis communicatio essentiæ diuinæ, qua sola tertia persona Diuinitatis à Patre & Filio tanquam Spiritus, ab eo, cuius est spiritus, essentiam accepit eandem & integram, quam Pater & Filius habent. De modo huius processionis, vt & generationis, curiosè scisciitantibus illud Damasceni responderi debet. ... Illudq; Ambrosij: Licet scire, quod natus sit filius; non licet scire, quomodo natus sit, quomodo procedat. Atque hic modus est existendi, quod à Patre Filioque procedit. Est enim tam Filij, quàm Patris Spiritus, ab utroque mittitur, Ioh.15,26. Ab utroque igitur procedit.
units.tr: 25. But proceeding. Greek: ἐκπορευόμενον, or ἐκπορευτὸν, or ἐκπορεύεσθαι, as in John 15:26 [ἐκπορεύεται]. This procession or emanation is an ineffable communication of the divine essence, by which the third person of the Godhead alone, as Spirit, receives from the Father and the Son, from him whose Spirit he is, the same and whole essence which the Father and the Son have. Concerning the mode of this procession, as of the generation, the answer of Damascene should be given to those who inquire curiously: ... and the saying of Ambrose: We may know that the Son was born; we may not know how he was born, how he proceeds. This is the mode of existing by which he proceeds from the Father and the Son. For the Spirit is the Spirit of the Son as much as of the Father; he is sent by both (John 15:26). Therefore he proceeds from both.

units.la: Dam. lib.4. Orthod. fid. cap.10.
units.tr: Dam. lib. 4 Orthod. fid. cap. 10.

units.la: Articulus VIII.
units.tr: Article VIII.

units.la: Et in hac Trinitate 26. nihil prius aut posterius: 27. nihil maius aut minus: 28. sed totæ tres personæ coæternæ sibi sunt & coæquales: Ita, vt per omnia, sicut jam dictum est, & vnitas in Trinitate, & Trinitas in vnitate veneranda sit. 29. Qui vult ergo saluus esse, ita de Trinitate sentiat.
units.tr: And in this Trinity 26. there is nothing first or last, 27. nothing greater or less; 28. but all three persons are co-eternal and co-equal with one another. So that, as has already been said, both the unity in the Trinity and the Trinity in the unity are to be worshipped in every respect. 29. He therefore who wishes to be saved must thus think concerning the Trinity.

units.la: Declaratio.
units.tr: Declaration.

units.la: 26. Nihil prius.] Natura vel tempore: licet ordine existendi Pater sit prima, Filius secunda, Spiritus sanctus tertia persona.
units.tr: 26. Nothing first.] By nature or by time, although in the order of existing the Father is the first person, the Son the second, and the Holy Spirit the third.

units.la: 27. Nihil maius.] Quia Deus est expers quanti. Quod Filius Patrem maiorem se dixit Ioh. 14,28, non diuinitatis, sed humanitatis & mediationis respectu dixit. Secus non staret, quod dixit: Ego & Pater vnum sumus. Omnia quæ habet Pater, mea sunt.
units.tr: 27. Nothing greater.] Because God is without quantity. That the Son said the Father is greater than he (John 14:28), he said with respect to his humanity and mediation, not his divinity. Otherwise what he said could not stand: I and the Father are one; all that the Father has is mine (John 10:30; 16:15).

units.la: 28. Sed totæ.] Coæternitas igitur & coæqualitas, quin & coessentialitas Trinitatis in vnitate ἀλληλαγῶς omnimodè est veneranda.
units.tr: 28. But all.] Therefore the co-eternity and co-equality, and indeed the co-essentiality, of the Trinity in unity, mutually and in every way, are to be worshipped.

units.la: 28. Qui vult ergo.] Salutem igitur suam odit, qui SS. Trinitatem non credit. Quisquis enim negat Filium; is ne Patrem quidem habet: 1 Ioh. 2,23. Qui vero Spiritum Christi non habet, is non est eius. Rom. 8, 9. Nemo enim potest Iesum dicere Dominum, nisi per Spiritum sanctum, 1 Cor. 12,3.
units.tr: 28. He therefore who.] Therefore he who does not believe in the most holy Trinity hates his own salvation. For whoever denies the Son does not have the Father either (1 John 2:23). And whoever does not have the Spirit of Christ is not his (Rom. 8:9). For no one can say that Jesus is Lord except by the Holy Spirit (1 Cor. 12:3).

units.la: FIDES CATHOLICA DE INCARNATIONE FILII Dei, Domini nostri Jesv Christi, juxta Symbolum B. Athanasij breuiter declarata atque asserta.
units.tr: THE CATHOLIC FAITH CONCERNING THE INCARNATION OF THE SON OF GOD, OUR LORD JESUS CHRIST, briefly explained and asserted according to the Creed of Saint Athanasius.

units.la: Articulus I. Symboli IX.
units.tr: Article I. Of Creed IX.

units.la: Sed 1. necessarium est ad æternam salutem, vt quicunque vult saluus esse, 2. incarnationem quoque Domini nostri Iesu Christi 3. fideliter credat.
units.tr: But (1) it is necessary for eternal salvation that whoever wishes to be saved (2) also faithfully believe (3) the incarnation of our Lord Jesus Christ.

units.la: Declaratio.
units.tr: Declaration.

units.la: 1. Necessarium est.] Necessitas hæc passim traditur in scriptura. Ioh. 3,36. Qui credit in Filium, habet vitam æternam: Qui non credit Filio, non videbit vitam, sed ira Dei manet super eo. Ioh. 6,14. Hæc est vt est voluntas eius, qui misit me, vt omnis, qui videt Filium, & credit in eum, habeat vitam æternam. Johan.17. v.3. Hæc est vita æterna, vt cognoscant, te esse illum solum verum Deum, & quem misisti Iesum Christum. 1 Johan.4, 3. Quicunque spiritus non confitetur, Iesum Christum venisse in carnem, non est ex Deo. Actor.4,12. Non est in alio quoquam salus, nec est aliud nomen sub cœlo, quod datum sit inter homines, per quod oporteat nos seruari. Actor.10, 43. Huic testimonium dant omnes Prophetæ, remissionem peccatorum accepturum per nomen eius, quicunque crediderit in nomen eius. Fide igitur in Filium Dei incarnatum, omnes seruari oportet: & sine hac fide seruari nemo potest.
units.tr: (1) It is necessary. This necessity is taught throughout Scripture. John 3:36: "He who believes in the Son has eternal life; but he who does not believe the Son shall not see life, but the wrath of God remains on him." John 6:40: "This is the will of him who sent me, that everyone who sees the Son and believes in him should have eternal life." John 17:3: "This is eternal life, that they know you, the only true God, and Jesus Christ whom you have sent." 1 John 4:3: "Every spirit that does not confess that Jesus Christ has come in the flesh is not from God." Acts 4:12: "There is no salvation in anyone else, nor is there any other name under heaven given among men by which we must be saved." Acts 10:43: "To him all the prophets bear witness, that through his name everyone who believes in him receives forgiveness of sins." Therefore all must be saved by faith in the Son of God incarnate, and no one can be saved without this faith.

units.la: 2. Incarnationem quoq;.] Græcè ἐνσωμάτωσιν, inhumanationem, ἐνσωμάτωσιν incorporationem: de cuius causis, modo, & veritate Athanasius præclarū reliquit libellum cum titulo: Περὶ ἐνανθρωπήσεως τοῦ Θεοῦ λόγου. Græci alij fere vocant σάρκωσιν, ἐνσάρκωσιν, incarnationem, voce formata ex scripturæ dictis, quibus incarnatio Filij Dei præcipuè fundatur. Joh.1, 14. Verbum caro factum est, & habitauit in nobis. 1 Tim. 3,16. Deus conspicuus factus est in carne. Hebr.2,14. Quoniam pueri participes sunt carnis & sanguinis: ipse quoq; (Filius Dei) similiter particeps factus est eorundem. Et v.16. Non assumsit angelos, sed assumsit semen Abrahæ. 1 Joh.4.2. Quicunque Spiritus confitetur Iesum Christum venisse in carnem, ex Deo est. Huc pertinent verba angeli ad Mariam virginem, Lucæ 1,35. Spiritus sanctus superueniet in te, & virtus Altissimi inumbrabit te: propterea etiam, quod ex te nascetur sanctum, Filius Dei vocabitur. Et illud Apostoli Galat. 4. v. 4. Deus emisit Filium suum factum ex muliere. Ex quibus intelligitur hæc incarnatio esse admirabilis humanæ carnis seu naturæ, operatione Spiritus sancti, in utero virginis, à Filio Dei in vnitatem suæ hypostaseos facta assumtio.
units.tr: (2) Incarnation. In Greek it is ἐνσωμάτωσις [embodiment], that is, inhumanation or incorporation [ἐνσωμάτωσιν]. Athanasius left an outstanding little book on its causes, manner and truth, with the title "On the Incarnation of the Word of God" [Περὶ ἐνανθρωπήσεως τοῦ Θεοῦ λόγου]. Other Greeks mostly call it σάρκωσις [enfleshment], ἐνσάρκωσις [incarnation], a word formed from the sayings of Scripture on which the incarnation of the Son of God is chiefly founded. John 1:14: "The Word was made flesh and dwelt among us." 1 Tim. 3:16: "God was manifested in the flesh." Heb. 2:14: "Since the children share in flesh and blood, he himself likewise shared in the same"; and v. 16: "He did not take hold of angels, but he took hold of the seed of Abraham." 1 John 4:2: "Every spirit that confesses that Jesus Christ has come in the flesh is from God." To this belong the words of the angel to the virgin Mary, Luke 1:35: "The Holy Spirit will come upon you, and the power of the Most High will overshadow you; therefore also the holy one who is born of you will be called the Son of God." And that word of the Apostle, Gal. 4:4: "God sent forth his Son, made of a woman." From these it is understood that this incarnation is the wondrous assumption, by the operation of the Holy Spirit in the virgin's womb, of human flesh or nature into unity with the hypostasis of the Son of God.

units.la: 3. Fideliter credat.] Græcè βεβαίως, firmiter: Articulo vltimo πίστως τῆς χ. βεβαίως, fideliter, firmiterque: quorum prius spectat fidei huius synceritatem ab errore, negatione, & hæresi quacunque circa hoc mysterium defæcatam: posterius requirit certitudinem fiduciamque salutis in Filio Dei incarnato, dubitationi & coniecturali opinationi oppositam.
units.tr: (3) Faithfully. In Greek it is βεβαίως [firmly]; in the last article πίστως τῆς χ. βεβαίως [faithfully and firmly]. The former looks to the sincerity of this faith, purged of error, denial and any heresy concerning this mystery; the latter requires certainty and confidence of salvation in the incarnate Son of God, set over against doubt and conjectural opinion.

units.la: ARTICVLVS II. SYMBOLI X.
units.tr: ARTICLE II. OF CREED X.

units.la: Est ergo 4. fides recta, 5. vt credamus, & confiteamur, quod 6. Dominus noster Iesus Christus 7. Dei Filius sit 8. Deus & homo.
units.tr: Therefore (4) the right faith is (5) that we believe and confess that (6) our Lord Jesus Christ (7) is the Son of God, (8) God and man.

units.la: Declaratio.
units.tr: Declaration.

units.la: 4. Fides recta.] Fides recta de incarnatione Filij Dei duobus capitibus breuissimè exponitur. Prius est de ipso incarnationis mysterio, seu de persona Filij Dei incarnati. Posterius de eiusdem officio, seu de redemtionis nostræ mysterio, ab eodem in carne peracto & peragendo. Vtrumq; credere pariter necessariū est ad salutem, & quidem prius propter posterius: cuius fides nisi integra illi bataq; juxta declarationem euangelij retineatur, credere, Christum esse Deum & hominem (quod etiam dæmones credunt & contremiscunt) ad salutem nihil juuabit.
units.tr: (4) Right faith. The right faith concerning the incarnation of the Son of God is set out very briefly under two heads. The first concerns the mystery of the incarnation itself, or the person of the incarnate Son of God. The second concerns his office, or the mystery of our redemption, accomplished and to be accomplished by him in the flesh. It is equally necessary for salvation to believe both, and the first indeed on account of the second. Unless faith in the second is kept whole and unharmed according to the declaration of the gospel, the belief that Christ is God and man (which even the demons believe and tremble) will profit nothing for salvation.

units.la: 5. Vt credamus.] Credere & confiteri oportet: quia corde creditur ad justitiam: ore confessio fit ad salutem. Rom.10,10.
units.tr: (5) That we believe. We must both believe and confess, "for with the heart one believes unto righteousness, and with the mouth confession is made unto salvation." Rom. 10:10.

units.la: 6. Dominus noster.] Sic vocat eum angelus, ipso die natali Luc.2,11. Natus est vobis hodie Seruator, qui est Christus Dominus: & scriptura noui Testamenti innumeris locis, cumprimis apostolus 1 Cor.8,6. Nobis unus est Dominus Iesus Christus: ipseq; sic vult à nobis vocari Joh.13,13. Vocatis me Domine, & recte dicitis: sum enim. Hinc in symbolo credimus in Iesum Christum Dominum nostrum. Græcè τὸν κύριον ἡμῶν: quia voce κύριος LXX. vbique proprium Dei nomen יהוה expresserunt: quod inprimis est memorabile: quia præbet luculentum veræ Deitatis Iesu Christi Domini nostri argumentum. Si enim ὁ κύριος ἡμῶν est idem, quod Jehoua: certè ὁ κύριος ἡμῶν, Dominus noster est Deus יהוה. Est igitur Filius Dei Dominus noster gemino dominatu. Vno Deitatis sibi cum Patre & Spiritu sancto communi, qui est absolutum eius in res omnes imperium: altero mediationis sibi proprio, quo vt Mediator Dei & hominum solus est ad dextram Dei constitutus caput Ecclesiæ super omnia. Eph.1,22.
units.tr: (6) Our Lord. The angel calls him so on the very day of his birth: Luke 2:11, "There is born to you this day a Saviour, who is Christ the Lord." Scripture of the New Testament does so in countless places, especially the Apostle, 1 Cor. 8:6: "For us there is one Lord, Jesus Christ." He himself also wishes to be called so by us, John 13:13: "You call me Lord and Teacher, and you say rightly, for so I am." Hence in the Creed we believe "in Jesus Christ our Lord," in Greek τὸν κύριον ἡμῶν [our Lord], because the LXX everywhere rendered the proper name of God, the Hebrew [יהוה], by the word κύριος. This is especially worth remembering, because it provides a clear proof of the true deity of Jesus Christ our Lord. For if ὁ κύριος ἡμῶν [our Lord] is the same as Jehovah, then surely our Lord is the God [יהוה]. The Son of God is therefore our Lord with a twofold dominion: one of deity, common to him with the Father and the Holy Spirit, which is his absolute rule over all things; the other of mediation, proper to himself, by which, as the sole Mediator between God and men, he has been placed at the right hand of God as head of the Church over all things, Eph. 1:22.

units.la: 7. Dei Filius est.] Non filius gratia creationis, sicut angeli sunt filij Dei, Job.1,6. nec filius gratia adoptionis, quomodo prædestinati sunt adoptati in filios per Iesum Christum, Ephes.1. vers.5. Sed Filius Dei proprius, Rom.8,32. vnigenitus à Patre, Johan.1,14. ante res omnes conditas ab æterno genitus, Prov.8,23.25. cuius egressus ab initio, à diebus seculi, Mich.5,4. per quem omnia facta sunt, & sine quo factum est nihil, quod factum est, Joh.1,3.
units.tr: (7) The Son of God. Not the son by the grace of creation, as the angels are sons of God, Job 1:6; nor the son by the grace of adoption, in the way that the predestined were adopted as sons through Jesus Christ, Eph. 1:5. But the proper Son of God, Rom. 8:32, the only-begotten of the Father, John 1:14, begotten from eternity before all created things, Prov. 8:23, 25, whose going forth was from the beginning, from the days of eternity, Mic. 5:2, through whom all things were made, and without whom nothing was made that was made, John 1:3.

units.la: 8. Deus & homo.] Non Deus tantum, quia sic non esset verè Christus, hoc est, vnctus. Nam Deus tantum, vngens est, non vnctus. Nec homo tantum: quia sic non esset verè Iesus, hoc est, Seruator. Nam homo tantum, seruandus est, non seruans: sed Deus & homo, vnus idemq; Filius, duabus subsistens naturis, diuina & humana, in vnitate ὑποστάσεως.
units.tr: (8) God and man. Not God only, for so he would not truly be Christ, that is, anointed; for God alone anoints, he is not anointed. Nor man only, for so he would not truly be Jesus, that is, Saviour; for a man alone is to be saved, not to save. But God and man, one and the same Son, subsisting in two natures, divine and human, in the unity of the hypostasis.

units.la: Porro
units.tr: Furthermore

units.la: Porrò cur Filius Dei secunda S.S. Trinitatis persona potius, quam aliarum hypostaseon vna, Pater vel Spiritus sanctus, humanam sibi carnem vniuerit: etsi ratio humana stupescere, fides Christiana humiliter adorare, non scrutari mysterium debet: quædam tamen à Theologis explicari solent rationes non improbabiles: ita nimirum conueniens fuisse, vt qui Filius Dei erat à patre ante secula genitus, etiam Filius hominis esset, ex substantia matris in tempore natus.
units.tr: Furthermore, why the Son of God, rather than one of the other hypostases, the second person of the Most Holy Trinity, or the Father or the Holy Spirit, united human flesh to himself: although human reason ought to be astonished, Christian faith ought to adore humbly, and not to pry into the mystery, yet the theologians are accustomed to explain certain reasons that are not unlikely. It was fitting, of course, that he who was the Son of God, begotten of the Father before the ages, should also be the Son of man, born in time of the substance of his mother.

units.la: Primo, ne per incarnationem personarum diuinarum mutaretur denominatio, vel induceretur confusio: quodaccidisset, si aut Pater, aut Spiritus sanctus, aut simul omnes per dispensationem carnis Filii nomen sibi vendicassent.
units.tr: First, so that the denomination of the divine persons would not be changed or confusion introduced. This would have happened if the Father, or the Holy Spirit, or all together, through the dispensation of the Son's flesh, had claimed the name of Son for themselves.

units.la: Secundo, beneficium incarnationis ad hoc ordinatum fuit à Deo, atq; hominibus indultum, vt nos filij Dei heremus. Congruum autem fuit, vt filij Dei adoptiui efficeremur per eum, qui ipse est Filius Dei naturalis.
units.tr: Second, the benefit of the incarnation was ordained by God and granted to men, so that we might be made sons of God. It was fitting, then, that we should be made adoptive sons of God through him who is himself the natural Son of God.

units.la: Tertio, congruentissimum fuit, mediastinum inter creaturas locum sortitum, per mediam in S.S. Trinitate personam reparari, vt decenter medio medium responderet. Homo autem in meditullio est creaturarum collocatus, spiritualem supra se, & corporalem infra se creaturam constitutam sortitus. Par fuit igitur hominem per mediam Trinitatis personam reparari.
units.tr: Third, it was most fitting that the place of mediator among creatures should be assigned, and that man should be restored through the middle person of the Most Holy Trinity, so that the middle would fittingly answer to the middle. Man, moreover, has been placed in the midst of creatures, having above him a spiritual creature and beneath him a corporeal one. It was therefore proper that man be restored through the middle person of the Trinity.

units.la: Denique, nihil decentius, quam per eum reparari naturam lapsam, per quem fuit condita: quia omnia per ipsum facta sunt. Ioh. 1.3. Igitur per Filium Dei fuit reparandus, & pristinæ dignitati restituendus homo.
units.tr: Finally, nothing is more fitting than that the fallen nature be restored through him through whom it was created, because "all things were made through him," John 1:3. Therefore man was to be restored through the Son of God and returned to his former dignity.

units.la: ARTICVLVS III. SYMBOLI XI.
units.tr: Article III of the Creed, XI.

units.la: 9. Deus est, 10. ex substantia Patris 11. ante secula genitus: & homo, 12. ex substantia matris 13. in seculo natus. 14. Perfectus Deus, 15. perfectus homo; ex anima rationali & humana carne subsistens. 16. Æqualis Patri secundum diuinitatem: 17. minor Patre secundum humanitatem.
units.tr: 9. God is, 10. from the substance of the Father 11. begotten before the ages; and man, 12. from the substance of the mother 13. born in time. 14. Perfect God, 15. perfect man, subsisting of a rational soul and human flesh. 16. Equal to the Father according to the divinity, 17. less than the Father according to the humanity.

units.la: Declaratio.
units.tr: Declaration.

units.la: 9. Deus est. Filium Dei proprium & vnigenitum esse Deum, tam est euidens, quam filium hominis proprium & vnigenitum esse hominem: idque scriptura innumeris locis confirmat.
units.tr: 9. God is. That the Son of God is his own and only-begotten God is as evident as that the Son of man is his own and only-begotten man; and Scripture confirms this in countless places.

units.la: 10. Ex substantia Patris. Hoc etiam scriptura confirmat, quod Filium Dei genitum & vnigenitum ex Patre testatur. Gignere enim, cum naturæ intelligenti tribuitur, quid est proprie, nisi his ex substantia sua prolem educere, seu gignentem genito, Patrem Filio substantiam suam communicare?
units.tr: 10. From the substance of the Father. Scripture also confirms this, since it testifies that the Son of God is begotten and only-begotten of the Father. For to beget, when it is attributed to an intelligent nature, properly means nothing other than to bring forth offspring from one's own substance; that is, the begetter communicates his substance to the begotten, the Father to the Son.

units.la: 11. Ante secula genitus.
units.tr: 11. Begotten before the ages.

units.la: Prou.8, 22.23.25.30. Sapientia, quae est Filius Dei, se ante secula, & ante orbem conditum genitam, bis terue perspicue restatur: & apud sanos, nedum pios dubio vacare debet. Quomodo enim Pater ante secula fuit, si Filium ante secula non genuit? Modum genituræ ἀρρήτῳ, ineffabilem Ecclesia profitetur: Quomodo sanè (ait Rufinus in expos. symboli, quæ Cypriano vulgò adscribitur) Deus Pater genuerit Filium, nolo discutias: nec te curiosius inferas in profundi huius arcanum, ne forte, dum inaccessa lucis fulgorem pertinacius scrutaris, exiguum ipsum, qui mortalibus diuino munere concessus est, perdas aspectum. Diuina generationis mysterium scito omnibus, quæ in nobis sunt, tanto esse differentius & eminentius, quanto creator creaturis potentior, quanto artifex opere suo præstantior, &c. Filium cum audis, nolo cogitationem carnalis natiuitatis assumas, sed memento hæc de incorporea dici substantia naturæ simplici. Si enim vel in eo, quod cor generat verbum, vel mens sensum, vel lux ex se parit splendorem, nulla in tali generatione fragilitas cogitatur, quanto purius de horum omnium creatore censendum est? Hoc porro subsistendi modo sibi proprio filius Dei distinguitur in S. S. Trinitate à Patre & Spiritu sancto, quod solus est à Patre genitus ante secula: proinde & solus carnem humanam assumpsit, ex virgine natus in tempore.
units.tr: Prov. 8:22, 23, 25, 30. Wisdom, which is the Son of God, twice or thrice plainly declares that she was begotten before the ages and before the world was made; and this ought to be beyond doubt for sound people, let alone the pious. For how could the Father have existed before the ages if he had not begotten the Son before the ages? The Church professes the manner of the begetting to be [ἀρρήτῳ] ineffable. "How exactly (says Rufinus in his exposition of the creed, which is commonly ascribed to Cyprian) God the Father begat the Son, I do not wish you to examine. Do not pry more curiously into the secret of this depth, lest perhaps, while you too stubbornly search the blaze of inaccessible light, you lose the small glimpse of it that has been granted to mortals by divine gift. Know that the mystery of divine generation differs from all that is in us by as much as the Creator is mightier than creatures, and the craftsman more excellent than his work, etc. When you hear the word Son, I do not want you to conceive of a carnal birth, but remember that these things are said of an incorporeal substance of simple nature. For if in that which the heart generates a word, or the mind a thought, or the light by itself brings forth brightness, no frailty is conceived in such generation, how much more purely ought we to judge of the Creator of all these things?" Moreover, the Son of God is distinguished within the Holy Trinity from the Father and the Holy Spirit by this mode of subsisting that is proper to him: he alone is begotten of the Father before the ages; and therefore he alone assumed human flesh, being born of a virgin in time.

units.la: 12. Ex substantia matris.
units.tr: 12. Of the substance of the mother.

units.la: Luc.1, 35. Quod ex te hoc est, ex substantia & ex utero tuo, nascetur sanctum, Filius Dei vocabitur. Debuit enim Filius Dei esse Filius Dauidis, juxta promissionem 1 Par.22,10. Heb.1,5. Matt.1. v.1. ex semine Dauidis secundum carnem, Rom.1,3. Hinc vocatur fructus ventris Mariæ, Luc.1, 42. Fructus autem de arboris enascitur substantia. Quod contra Valentini dicitur furorem, asserentis: Christum à Patre missum, cœleste secum attulisse corpus, nihilque assumsisse de virgine Maria, sed per illam tanquam per riuum, aut per fistulam, sine vlla de illa assumta carne transisse. Augustin. de hæres.10.
units.tr: Luke 1:35. What is born of you, that is, from your substance and your womb, will be holy; he will be called the Son of God. For the Son of God had to be the Son of David, according to the promise of 1 Chron. 22:10; Heb. 1:5; Matt. 1:1: of the seed of David according to the flesh, Rom. 1:3. Hence he is called the fruit of Mary's womb, Luke 1:42. Now fruit grows out of the substance of the tree. This is said against the madness of Valentinus, who asserted that Christ, sent by the Father, brought a heavenly body with him, and took nothing from the Virgin Mary, but passed through her as through a channel or a pipe, without taking any flesh from her. Augustine, On Heresies, 10.

units.la: 13. In seculo.
units.tr: 13. In the age.

units.la: Pro in tempore, seu in plenitudine temporis, nempe præfiniti à Deo. Galat. 4. v.4. quod fuit imperij Augusti anno 42. orbis conditi anno vergente 3928. juxta computum optimum Beroaldi.
units.tr: Instead of "in time," or "in the fullness of time," namely the time fixed by God (Gal. 4:4). This was in the forty-second year of the reign of Augustus, in the year 3928 from the creation of the world, according to the best reckoning of Beroaldus.

units.la: 14. Perfectus Deus.
units.tr: 14. Perfect God.

units.la: Græcè θεὸς ὁ τέλειος, idem quod 1 Ioh.5,20. Θεὸς, verus Deus, qui non est nisi vnus & æternus ille natura Deus, אל שדי יהוה Deum sufficientiæ seu perfectionis se vocans, Genes. 17, 1. Non igitur est Deus æquiuoce dictus, propter donorum & officij excellentiam, vt angeli Psalm.97,7. vel vt homines Principes Psal.82,6. prout blasphemabat Samo-satenus, Photinus olim: hodie Seruetiani, Sociniani, Christum ex Maria initium sumsisse, necante eam fuisse, asseuerantes: Neque DEVS factitius vel creatus ante alia omnia ἐκ τῶν μὴ ὄντων, ex non entibus: vt furebat Arius.
