The Catechism attributes everything together to death, as Scripture also does, John 3: God gave his only-begotten Son (namely to death) that everyone who believes (namely in the Son delivered up and dead for him) should not perish, but have eternal life, etc. But you say: Q. 60 and 61 expressly divide the imputed righteousness into three parts, perfect satisfaction, righteousness and holiness, which it says are imputed to us; and Q. 36 says that the Mediator covers our sins, in which we were conceived, by his innocence and perfect holiness, so that they do not come into the sight of God.

units.la: Quod ad prius, aut est fatendum, ista pugnare cum superioribus: quod charitas & candor Christianus statuere vetat: aut neganda est partitio & commoda istorum inuenienda interpretatio & conciliatio. Salvis aliorum iudiciis dicam quid ego hic statuam, & quomodo Catechesin excusare soleam. Dico igitur: Catechesin hæc tria coniungere quidem, sed non, ut dicitur: Catechesin hæc tria coniungere quidem, sed non, ut debatur, expresse tanquam tria partiri: coniungit, inquam, tria illa non ut partiatur iustitiam imputatam in hæc tria, ut diversa, quasi imputata satisfactio nos faciat non iniustos, iustitia iustos, sanctitas sanctos; nam diversum prius docuerat: sed vel, quia authores Catecheseos phrasin hanc ex confessione D. Bezæ (cuius eam propriam esse constat) absque metu cavillatione retinuerunt, nullam interim ipsi partitionem observantes, aut intendentes: vel quia his quasi συνωνύμως totum cursum obedientiæ humiliationis usque ad mortem ἐμφαλωτίως notare voluerunt. Est enim humiliatio & mors Christi satisfactio: quia per eam iustitiæ divinæ est satisfactum pro nobis. Est & iustitia, quia est impletio legis per pœnam. Est denique sanctitas, quia est sanctum sacrificium, de quo dicitur: Pater ego me sanctifico pro eis: Et: Unica oblatione consecravit omnes qui iustificantur. Coniecturam certam inde facio, quod in prima editione ἅγιος, Gründlicher Bericht vom Abendmahl, Anno 1564. non eadem, sed similia tria sic fuerant coniuncta, pag. 21. Seines Verdienstes werden wir also theilhafftig, daß uns all sein Gehorsam, Gerechtigkeit und Heiligkeit also von Gott wird zugerechnet, &c. Sed postea motu scrupo partitionis, D. Ursinus libri author, consensu Collegarum, maxime D. Oleuiani, vitandæ ambiguitatis, & cauendæ controuersiæ causa, quatuor illis vocabulis, All/Gehorsamb/Gerechtigkeit/und Heiligkeit / in altera editione anno 66. sua manu dispunctis; hæc verba repositit: Daß uns sein Leiden und Sterben, damit er für alle unsere Sünde genug gethan, und uns das ewige Leben verdienet hat, also von Gott, &c. non sententiam mutans, sed ἀμφιβολίαν cauens & tollens. Autographum autoris sic lituratum & emendatum ipse habeo ad manus. Si idem in Catechesi tunc fuisset factum, minus nunc laboraremus. Scio rumores spargi, Ursinum ante obitum sententiam mutasse.
units.tr: As to the former point, either it must be admitted that these statements clash with the earlier ones, which charity and Christian candour forbid us to decide, or the division must be denied and a convenient interpretation and reconciliation of them found. Saving the judgements of others, I will say what I myself judge here, and how I am accustomed to excuse the Catechism. I say, then, that the Catechism indeed joins these three, but does not, as is claimed, expressly divide them into three parts. It joins them, I say, not so as to divide the imputed righteousness into these three as different things, as if imputed satisfaction makes us not unrighteous, righteousness makes us righteous, and holiness makes us holy; for it had taught otherwise before. Rather, either because the authors of the Catechism retained this phrase, taken from the confession of Dr Beza (whose it is known to be), without fear of cavil, while themselves observing or intending no division at all; or because they wished to denote by these, as synonyms [συνωνύμως], the whole course of obedience and humiliation unto death, emphatically [ἐμφατικῶς]. For the humiliation and death of Christ is satisfaction, because by it satisfaction has been made to divine justice on our behalf. It is also righteousness, because it is the fulfilment of the law through punishment. And finally it is holiness, because it is a holy sacrifice, of which it is said: Father, I sanctify myself for them; and: by one offering he has consecrated all who are justified. I make a sure conjecture from this, that in the first edition, published anonymously [ἀνωνύμως], Gründlicher Bericht vom Abendmahl, in the year 1564, the three were joined not in the same words but in similar ones, as on p. 21: "Thus we are made partakers of his merit, so that all his obedience, righteousness and holiness is imputed to us by God, etc." But afterwards, moved by the scruple of division, Dr Ursinus, the author of the book, with the consent of his colleagues, especially Dr Olevianus, for the sake of avoiding ambiguity and guarding against controversy, struck out in the second edition of 1566, in his own hand, those four words, all, obedience, righteousness and holiness, and put in their place these words: "That his suffering and death, by which he has done enough for all our sins and has merited eternal life for us, is thus imputed to us by God, etc." He was not changing his opinion, but guarding against and removing ambiguity. I have to hand the author's own copy, so crossed out and corrected. If the same had then been done in the Catechism, we would now have less trouble. I know that rumours are spread that Ursinus changed his opinion before his death.

units.la: An vero cum Ursino mutata fuisset veritas? Sed fides sit pene, authores. Ego tum aliis argumentis indubiis, tum hoc unicos ut diver-
units.tr: But was the truth really changed along with Ursinus? I would almost say the authors themselves should be trusted on this. By other clear arguments, and by this one above all, I am firmly led to hold the opposite view.

units.la: Ioh.17. ut diuersum statuam, firmiter inducor, quod in consideratione commonefactionis Chythrei, quam in morbo scripsit, absoluit, excudendam dedit, correxit, adeo ut pridie mortis, cum forte sphalma obrepsisset typographo, ipse non quieuerit, donec id à M. Pithophoeo (ex cuius ore haec scribo) correctum audiret, tandemque dixerit: Nun bin ich zu frieden/in hac, inquam, cygnea cantione D. Visini pagina 209. haec postrema eius confessio his verbis expresse legitur: CHRISTVS fidelibus suis donat iustitiam & vitam aeternam, propter sanguinem suum in cruce effusum.
units.tr: John 17. Ursinus wrote the reflection on Chythraeus's admonition while he was ill. He finished it, handed it to be printed, and corrected it, so that on the day before his death, when a slip had crept in past the printer, he would not rest until he heard from M. Pithopoeus (from whose mouth I write this) that it had been corrected. At last he said, "Now I am content," and in this, I say, his swan song, on page 209 of D. Visinus, that final confession is clearly read in these words: Christ gives his faithful people righteousness and eternal life, on account of his blood poured out on the cross.

units.la: Ad quaestionem XXXVI. quod attinet, liquet eam agere non de causa materiali, sed de efficiente, & sine qua non nostrae iustitiae. Innocentia igitur, & sanctitas Mediatoris peccatum nostrum originale fontem reliquorum tegere dicitur effectiue: quia effecit tanquam ὡς ἀκακίῳ [?], ut Mediator tegere & expiare posset, quoniam oportebat eum innocentem & perfecte sanctum nasci, ut posset pro nobis fieri victima. Hebr. 7. Tegere vero, ut meritum intelligi non potest: tum quia quaestio quinquagesima sexta Catechesis diuersum docet, tum quia repugnat illud Johannis: Sanguis Iesu Christi purgat nos ab omni peccato.
units.tr: As far as question 36 is concerned, it is clear that it treats not the material cause but the efficient cause, and the condition without which our righteousness cannot be. The innocence and holiness of the Mediator are therefore said to cover our original sin, the source of the rest, in an efficient sense: he has made it so, as though in innocence [ὡς ἀκακίῳ], that the Mediator could cover and expiate it, since he had to be born innocent and perfectly holy so that he could become a victim for us. Heb. 7. But covering cannot be understood as merit, both because question 56 of the Catechism teaches otherwise and because John's saying conflicts with it: The blood of Jesus Christ cleanses us from all sin.

units.la: Hac moderatione adhibita, quam passim in ipsis scripturis sacris conciliandis adhiberi oportet, omnia in Catechesi bene conuenient. Neque Agendae Palatinae diuersa est ratio vel sententia. Si authores ipsos superstites haberemus, nodos omnes haud dubie soluerent dexterius: quaquam sententiam illi suam minime obscuram nobis reliquerunt. Qui vero non soluere, sed secare hos nodos cogitant, pro libitu quiduis mutando aut eradendo; per me quidem licebit, suo illi fruantur sensu: certo tamen confirmo, nullam eos sui instituti causam satis gravem habituros, si ad legitimam cognitionem res veniat. Prudentis igitur Magistratus officium esse iudico, prouidere, ne quid temere à quoquam hic admittatur, quod cum justa offensione multorum fratrum, & perturbatione Ecclesiae coniunctum esse queat.
units.tr: If this moderation is applied, as it must be applied throughout when reconciling the sacred Scriptures themselves, everything in the Catechism agrees well. Nor is the reasoning or opinion in the Palatine Agenda different. If we still had the authors themselves, they would undoubtedly untie all these knots more skilfully, although they left us their view in no way obscure. But those who think of cutting these knots rather than untying them, changing or erasing whatever they please, may, so far as I am concerned, enjoy their own sense. Yet I firmly affirm that they will not find their undertaking has a sufficiently serious cause if the matter comes to a lawful examination. I therefore judge it the duty of a prudent magistrate to see to it that nothing here is rashly admitted by anyone which could be joined with the just offence of many brethren and the disturbance of the Church.

units.la: Haec habui, Generose Domine Comes, quae de hoc scrupulo (sic enim potius, quam controuersiam haberi velim) intelligendo & tollendo respondere nunc potui. Prolixitatem, qua moram vtcunque compensandam esse duxi, moleste ne feras, oro. Quod vero libere sententias contuli, & meam non dissimulaui, pro tua pietate in meliorem ut partem accipias, etiam atque etiam peto. Nihil in his est, quod non ferre possim, sciri à pluribus, aut quod clari velim: quandoquidem veritas lucem non fugit. Tuae tamen prudentiae committo omnia. Si quis quid alii-ter sentit, hoc quoque ei Deus reteget, vt promittit Apostolus, sectemur modo veritatem cum charitate. Phil.3, 15. Oportebat sane coagmentatos esse eadem mente & sententia & idem loqui omnes, juxta eiusdem Apostoli monitum: verum quando quaeso fuit, aut erit (nisi in illa perfectione, quam exspectamus) ea Ecclesiae felicitas, quin aliqua aliquando etiam summorum patrum etiam Apostolorum ὑπερδοξίας [?] nubecula serenitatem obduxerit? Nostrum tamen est ad sanctam ὁμοιώσιν [?] per omnia aspirare: nec dubito, quin hic quoque sarciri facile possit, si legitime conferantur & ponderentur sententiae. Nam ne id quoque dissimulem, multa in hac causa non videntur vacare λογο-μαχία [?], ex sententiis & rationibus partium non bene perceptis. Alij enim passiuam, alij actiuam obedientiam aliter accipiunt: quod non dubito, a tua etiam Generositate obseruari. Orandus Deus, vt nos sanet, & seruet. Interim beati, qui esuriunt, & sitiunt justitiam: quoniam saturabuntur. Omnibus Pater Domini nostri Jesu Christi nos omnes in vera sanctitate sanctificet. Te vero, Generose Domine, cum dilectissima coniuge, & liberis Illustribus gratia & Spiritu suo in hac veneranda aetate tua magis magisque vegeret: & Ecclesiae patronum cordatissimum, mihique Dominum clementissimum diu incolumem seruet.
units.tr: This, noble Lord Count, is what I have been able to answer now on this scruple (for so I would rather have it called than a controversy), in understanding and removing it. I beg you not to take it amiss that I have been long; I thought the length had to be made up for in some way. Moreover, I beg you again and again, in your piety, to receive in better part the fact that I have freely compared opinions and have not hidden my own. There is nothing in these matters that I could not bear to have known to many, nor that I would wish obscured, since truth does not shun the light. Nevertheless I commit all things to your prudence. If anyone thinks otherwise, God will also reveal this to him, as the Apostle promises, provided we pursue the truth in love. Phil. 3:15. Certainly, following the same Apostle's admonition, we ought to be joined together in the same mind and judgment and all speak the same thing. But when, I ask, has there been, or will there be (except in that perfection we look for), such happiness of the Church that some little cloud of excessive opinion [ὑπερδοξίας] has not at some time clouded the serenity even of the greatest Fathers and Apostles? Yet it is our duty to strive for holy likeness [ὁμοιώσιν] in all things, and I do not doubt that this too can easily be mended, if the opinions are properly compared and weighed. For, not to hide this either, much in this cause seems to lack no war of words [λογομαχία], arising from opinions and arguments of the parties not well understood. Some take passive obedience one way, others active obedience another way; and I do not doubt that your Nobility too will observe this. May God be prayed to heal and preserve us. Meanwhile blessed are those who hunger and thirst for righteousness, for they shall be satisfied. May the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ sanctify us all in true holiness. And may he keep you, noble Lord, together with your most beloved wife and noble children, invigorating you more and more with his grace and Spirit in this venerable age of yours; and may he long keep safe the most wise patron of the Church and my most merciful Lord.

units.la: Amen. Heidelbergae 3. Non.
units.tr: Amen. Heidelberg, the third day before the Nones.

units.la: Augusti 1598.
units.tr: August 1598.

units.la: FRAGMENTVM ORATIONIS De Quæstione AD QVOSNAM FRVCTVS PASSIONIS ET MORTIS CHRISTI proprie pertineant: & quomodo Christus pro omnibus dicatur esse mortuus. In inclyta Academia Heidelbergensi à JOSVA ZEVELIO Coloniensi, pridie Paschatis Anno 1590. recitatæ.
units.tr: THE FRAGMENT OF AN ORATION On the question TO WHOM THE FRUITS OF THE PASSION AND DEATH OF CHRIST properly pertain, and in what sense Christ is said to have died for all. Delivered at the famous Academy of Heidelberg by JOSUA ZEVELIUS of Cologne, on the day before Easter, in the year 1590.

units.la: AVTHORE D. DAVIDE PAREO.
units.tr: BY THE LATE DAVID PAREUS.

units.la: Satis multa verba fecisse mihi videor, Auditores, de historia, deque fructibus resurrectionis Domini. Restat, vt quod postremo loco instituimus, ad quosnam hi fructus pertineant, explicare pergamus.
units.tr: I seem, hearers, to have said enough about the history and the fruits of the Lord's resurrection. What remains is to go on to explain the last point we set out to treat: to whom these fruits properly belong.

units.la: Ad Scripturam itaque sanctam, tanquam ad Cynosuram cursum nostrum dirigentes, fructus hos tam pretiosos ad omnes & solos credentes pertinere, cum eadem scriptura sacra asserimus: incredulos vero & impios omnes, quoad tales manent, ab illis procul arcemus. Etenim omnes & soli credentes fructuum illorum, justificationis puta gratuitæ coram Deo, viuificationis à morte peccati & corporis denique immortalis vitæ & gloriæ dulcedinem sentiunt, omnes & soli percipiunt: quia omnes & soli hi vera fide eos sibi applicant. Hi enim sunt, qui sermonem Christi audiunt, bono & honesto corde suscipiunt, credunt, vitamque æternam habent, necin condemnationem veniunt. Hi sunt, qui fide justificantur, Deo reconciliantur, & pacem habent per Dominum nostrum JESVM CHRISTVM. Hi sunt, qui per Spiritum sanctum regenerati, in novam vitam cum Christo excitantur, quorum corda fide purificantur. Hi denique sunt, quos in Jesu dormientes, Deus tandem ex morte suscitatos, cum eo adducet, vitæ cœlestis gloria in æternum fruantur.
units.tr: Directing our course, then, as by the Cynosure, to Holy Scripture, we affirm from that same Holy Scripture that these fruits, so precious, belong to all and only believers, and we keep away from them all unbelievers and the impious, so long as they remain such. For all and only believers feel the sweetness of those fruits, namely justification freely before God, quickening from the death of sin, and finally the life and glory of an immortal body; all and only believers receive them, because all and only they apply them to themselves by true faith. For these are the ones who hear the word of Christ, receive it with a good and honest heart, believe, have eternal life, and do not come into condemnation. These are the ones who are justified by faith, reconciled to God, and have peace through our Lord Jesus Christ. These are the ones who are regenerated by the Holy Spirit and raised with Christ into new life, whose hearts are purified by faith. Finally, these are the ones whom God, when they sleep in Jesus, will at last raise from death and bring with him, that they may enjoy the glory of heavenly life for ever.

units.la: Impij vero & fide justificante destituti, quid de his tantis bonis participarent, qui Deo non placent, (sine fide enim Deo placere est impossibile) qui ad Christum non pertinent, qui non sunt hæredes, neque in re, neque ad rem (quod dicitur) jus vitæ
units.tr: But what share in these great goods would the impious have, and those destitute of justifying faith, who do not please God (for without faith it is impossible to please God), who do not belong to Christ, who are not heirs, either in fact or in right (as they say), and have no right whatever to life?

units.la: vllum habentes? Quomodo ad hos pertineret Christus, & beneficia Christi? Quin potius isti omnes voce Euangelij ab his thesauris procul arcentur, & æternæ maledictioni ac morti adjudicantur: Qui non credit, jam judicatus est: & ira Dei manet super eo. Et: Qui non habet Spiritum Christi, non est eius: quem admodum fallere nescit. Apostoli locum cumprimis huc facere arbitror. Si enim infideles ad Christum non pertinent, neque sunt Christi: a correlatis firmissime concluditur, vicissim Christum cum suis benefici̇s ad pios non pertinere: & sicut ipsi non sunt Christi, ita nec Christum ipsorum esse. Et quomodo, quaeso, ad eos pertinet Christus, quos ipse tandem in judicio extremo coram vniuerso mundo, à se, à beneficiis suis, à regno suo pronunciabit alienos? quos nunquam sibi cognitos fuisse testabitur, quos denique vt maledictos operarios iniquitatis, à se in gehennam ablegabit?
units.tr: How could Christ, and the benefits of Christ, belong to such people? Rather, all these are kept far from those treasures by the voice of the Gospel and are adjudged to eternal curse and death: He who does not believe is already judged, and the wrath of God remains on him. And: He who does not have the Spirit of Christ is not his, which the Apostle, who cannot deceive, says. I think the Apostle's words bear especially on this point. For if unbelievers do not belong to Christ and are not Christ's, then by the correlatives it is most firmly concluded, conversely, that Christ with his benefits does not belong to the pious; and just as they are not Christ's, so neither is Christ theirs. And how, I ask, does Christ belong to those whom he himself at last, in the final judgement, before the whole world, will pronounce strangers to himself, to his benefits and to his kingdom; whom he will testify never to have known; whom at last, as cursed workers of iniquity, he will send away from himself into gehenna?

units.la: At, inquies, Christus pro omnibus est mortuus. Pro omnibus ergo etiam resurrexit. Responsio duplex est. VNA; quoties Euangelium fructus operum & beneficiorum Christi ad omnes extendit: de vniuersitate in Christum credentium id esse accipiendum. Perpetua enim & constans Euangelij vox est: Qui crediderit, seruabitur: non veniet in judicium. Qui non crediderit, jam judicatus est: & ira Dei manet super eo. Arcet ergo Euangelium à Christi beneficiis omnes infideles, non modo diserta exclusione, sed & illa fidei ac poenitentiae conditione, sub qua expresse, vel tacite beneficia Christi Deus hominibus promittit, & quam in perseuerantibus in impietate nunquam inueniri palam est. Sic itaque Christus mortuus dicitur pro omnibus, nempe credentibus, & crediturus in ipsum: pro quibus etiam solis orauit, & in quibus solis fidem mortis suae assequitur. Ad infideles vero & reprobos, pro quibus CHRISTVS non orauit, quos pro suis nunquam agnouit, super quos ira Dei in aeternum manet, mortis Christi beneficia extendere, quid aliud est, quam contra ipsius met praeceptum, sanctum canibus dare, margaritas porcis proiicere? Haec scripturae & orthodoxorum patrum authoritate solide defendi possunt, & ad consolationem Christianorum faciunt.
units.tr: But you will say: Christ died for all. Therefore he also rose again for all. The answer is twofold. ONE: whenever the Gospel extends the fruits of Christ's works and benefits to all, this must be understood of all who believe in Christ. For the voice of the Gospel is constant and unchanging: He who believes will be saved; he will not come into judgement. He who does not believe is already judged, and the wrath of God remains on him. The Gospel therefore keeps all unbelievers away from the benefits of Christ, not only by an explicit exclusion but also by that condition of faith and repentance under which God promises the benefits of Christ to men, expressly or tacitly, and which is plainly never found in those who persist in impiety. Thus Christ is said to have died for all, namely for believers, and for those who will believe in him; for whom alone he prayed, and in whom alone the benefit of his death takes effect. But to extend the benefits of Christ's death to unbelievers and the reprobate, for whom Christ did not pray, whom he never acknowledged as his own, over whom the wrath of God remains for ever, what else is it than to act against his very own command: to give what is holy to dogs, and to cast pearls before swine? These things can be solidly defended by the authority of Scripture and of the orthodox Fathers, and they serve the comfort of Christians.

units.la: Est & alia in scholis recepta responsio, qua contentiosis gratificari possumus, Christum absolute pro omnibus mortuum esse, si λύτρῳ & meriti eius sufficientiam & amplitudinem spectes. Extra omnem enim est controversiam, tantum pondus habere mortem Filij Dei, vt sufficiat non vnius tantum mundi, sed millium peccatis expiandis: si modo hanc peccati medicinam omnes fide accipiant. Sed de efficacia & participatione ipsa fructuum proproprie est quæstio, cum quæritur : An Christus sit mortuus pro omnibus? Quoniam mori pro alio, proprie est, mori alterius vice & loco: ita vt is à morte liberetur, & in vita seruetur: sicut Dauid ciulans clamabat: Quis dabit mihi mori pro te? ô Absalon: pro: vti- nam ego mortuus essem tuo loco, vt tu viueres! Participationem vero hanc meriti Christi omnibus etiam non-credentibus & nunquam crediturus, communem esse, vel in euangelio promitti & dari, constanter negamus: neque eius respectu Christum pro omnibus, etiam non-credentibus, & reprobis, mortuum esse, recte dici, concedimus.
units.tr: There is also another answer, received in the schools, by which we may gratify the contentious: that Christ died absolutely for all, if you look to the sufficiency and the greatness of his price [λύτρῳ] and of his merit. For it is beyond all controversy that the death of the Son of God has such weight that it suffices to expiate the sins not of one world only but of thousands, provided that all receive this remedy for sin by faith. But the question concerning the efficacy and the very participation in the fruits is a different matter, when one asks: Did Christ die for all? For to die for another properly means to die in another's place and stead, so that he is freed from death and kept alive; as David, weeping, cried out: Who will give me to die for you, O Absalom! that is, would that I had died in your place, that you might live! But we firmly deny that this participation in the merit of Christ is common to all, including the unbelievers who will never believe, or that it is promised and given in the Gospel; and we concede that it cannot rightly be said, with respect to it, that Christ died for all, including unbelievers and the reprobate.

units.la: Hic vero quidam maleferiati infidelium patroni, ægrè ferentes, nos margaritas non æquo jure ouibus & porcis diuidere, clamant, nos abnegare sanguinem Iesu Christi: ac proferre Saracenicam, Mahumeticam, & plus quam paganam blasphemiam, qua religio Christiana funditus euertatur.
units.tr: But here certain malicious advocates of the unbelievers, taking it hard that we do not divide the pearls with equal right between sheep and swine, cry out that we deny the blood of Jesus Christ; and they bring forth a Saracen, Mahometan, and more than pagan blasphemy, by which the Christian religion is overthrown from its foundations.

units.la: Nobis verò, auditores, cum rabiosis istis logodædalis manus conserere, aut decertare, propositum non est. Sed primum super tam atroci calumnia protestamur, ad perpetuam Euangelij vocem & orthodoxæ Ecclesiæ consensum prouocantes: non abnegari sanguinem Iesu Christi, sed honorari, cum fusum eum esse dicimus, non pro iis, qui eum communem ducunt, & Christum pedibus conculcant: sed pro iis, qui eo per fidem justificantur, juxta Apostolum: Quem proposuit Deus placamentum PER FIDEM IN SANGVINE IPSIVS, ad declarandam justitiam suam per remissionem peccatorum præcedentium. Neque enim infidelium vox est: Qui lauit nos sanguine suo à peccatis nostris. Et illa: Sanguis Iesu Christi purgat nos ab omni peccato.
units.tr: But it is not our purpose, hearers, to join hands with these raging word-jugglers or to contend with them. Yet first, we protest against so atrocious a calumny, appealing to the constant voice of the Gospel and to the consensus of the orthodox Church: that the blood of Jesus Christ is not denied by us but honoured, when we say that it was shed not for those who count it common and trample Christ underfoot, but for those who are justified by it through faith, according to the Apostle: Whom God set forth as a propitiation THROUGH FAITH IN HIS BLOOD, to declare his righteousness through the remission of sins previously committed. For this is not the language of unbelievers: He who washed us from our sins in his own blood. And that: The blood of Jesus Christ cleanses us from all sin.

units.la: Hanc, inquam, non Saracenicam, Mahumeticam, & plusquam paganam blasphemiam esse; vt impudenter blasphemat calumnia: sed esse genuinam, veram, & salutarem ipsius Euangelij Iesu Christi doctrinam, ex Verbo Dei nouimus, atq; confidimus: id ipsum quouis tempore, coram tota Ecclesia demonstrare parati. Deinde, operæ pretium, atq; adeo necessarium esse ducimus, quanta fieri potest breuitate, lupis istis ouinam, qua tecti veniunt, detrahere, atque portentosum eorum dogma, calumniæ ψπελος, quod sub ea in Ecclesiam inuehere moliuntur, suis coloribus vobis depingere.
units.tr: That this, I say, is not a Saracen, Mahometan, or more than pagan blasphemy, as the calumny impudently blasphemes; but that it is the genuine, true, and saving doctrine of the Gospel of Jesus Christ itself, we know and are confident from the Word of God; and we are ready to demonstrate this at any time before the whole Church. Secondly, we judge it worth while, and indeed necessary, to strip, with all possible brevity, the sheep's clothing from those wolves who come in disguise, and to paint for you in their own colours the monstrous dogma which they are striving to bring into the Church under this stumbling block of calumny.

units.la: Contendunt, Christum pro omnibus mortuum esse. Quis negat? Hæc scripturæ locutio est. Addunt; pro omnibus & singulis mortuum esse. Ne hoc quidem simpliciter inficiamur, eo scilicet sensu, quem paulo ante indicauimus: licet scripturam sic loqui non inueniamus. Pergunt addere: pro omnibus & singulis pariter, electis & reprobis, pro Caino & Dauide, pro Juda
units.tr: They contend that Christ died for all. Who denies it? It is the language of Scripture. They add: for all and each. Not even this do we simply deny, in that sense which we indicated a little earlier, although we do not find Scripture speaking in this way. They go on to add: for all and each alike, elect and reprobate, for Cain and David, for Judas

units.la: & Petro, pro damnatis æque ac seruandis, absque fidei vel infidelitatis ratione, mortuum esse. Hoc durum est. Pergunt denique pro his omnibus & singulis, non modo quoad sufficientiam, sed & quoad efficaciam ἀντρᾳ mortuum esse. Quid hoc vero? Nempe Christum morte sua omnes absolutè, illos etiam, qui non saluantur, sed iam inde à Caino damnati sunt, & damnantur, & porrò damnabuntur, veraciterà morte liberasse, à peccatis purgasse, sanctificasse, Deo reconciliasse, inque sinum & gratiam eius restituisse. Hoc impium portentum: quo aliud non minus impium, & falsum concludunt: Impios, quotquot perierunt, pereunt, ac peribunt, non propter peccata sua, (quippe quæ sanguine CHRISTI expiata fuerint) sed propter solam incredulitatem periisse, perire, & perituros esse. Nihil nos hic fingere, fatebuntur ij, qui libellos eorum, & disputationes legerunt. Quam vero hæc sunt portentosa Christianis auribus?
units.tr: and Peter, for the damned no less than for those to be saved, without regard to faith or unbelief, that he died. This is harsh. Finally they go on to say that he died for all these and each, not only in respect of sufficiency but also in respect of efficacy. What, then, is this? Namely, that by his death Christ has truly freed from death, cleansed from sins, sanctified, reconciled to God, and restored to God's bosom and favour all absolutely, even those who are not saved but were condemned from Cain on, and are condemned, and will be condemned hereafter. This is an impious monstrosity; and from it they draw another no less impious and false conclusion: that the impious, however many have perished, are perishing, and will perish, have not perished, are not perishing, and will not perish on account of their sins (since these have been expiated by the blood of Christ), but solely on account of unbelief. Those who have read their little books and disputations will admit that I invent nothing here. But how monstrous these things sound to Christian ears!

units.la: Impios & impuros canes omnes, ante & post Christum mortuum, morte eius in sinum & gratiam Dei receptos esse, dicitane belli isti impiorum patroni.
units.tr: Do the patrons of this impious war say that all impious and unclean dogs, both before and after Christ's death, were received into the bosom and grace of God by his death?

units.la: Nos primò falsum & impium dogma esse dicimus: quia apertè repugnat scripturæ, quæ constanter clamat, impios, quoad manent absque fide & pœnitentia, non esse in sinu & gratia Dei, sed manere filios iræ & æternæ maledictionis: nec esse liberatos à peccato & morte, sed teneri captiuos laqueis diaboli, & efficaciter agitari, immò jam judicatos esse, & subira Dei manere.
units.tr: First, we say that this is a false and impious dogma, because it clearly contradicts Scripture, which constantly proclaims that the impious, so long as they remain without faith and repentance, are not in the bosom and grace of God, but remain sons of wrath and of eternal curse; nor are they freed from sin and death, but are held captive in the snares of the devil and driven about by him, and indeed have already been judged and remain under the wrath of God.

units.la: Deinde longè absurdissimum hoc esse portentum asserimus: quod multa principia Christianæ fidei, & seipsum elidit. Ponamus enim in medio thesin istam: Omnes homines, nullo excepto, fideles & infideles, ante & post Christum mortuum, sanguine Christi vere & indubitanter in gratiam & sinum Dei esse receptos. Quid quæso hinc sequitur? Certe Ilias absurditatum.
units.tr: Second, we assert that this monstrous notion is extremely absurd, and that it destroys itself and many principles of the Christian faith. For let us put this thesis in the middle: "All men, without exception, faithful and unfaithful, both before and after Christ's death, have truly and indubitably been received into grace and the bosom of God by the blood of Christ." What, I ask, follows from this? Certainly a whole heap of absurdities.

units.la: Primò: tolletur peccatum originis, nec vllus eius erit reatus: falsum erit, omnes homines nasci filios iræ: quia omnes nascentur in gratia & sinu Dei. At scriptura omnes filios iræ natura proclamat.
units.tr: First: the sin of origin will be removed, and there will be no guilt of it; it will be false that all men are born sons of wrath, since all will be born in the grace and bosom of God. But Scripture declares that all are by nature sons of wrath.

units.la: Secundò: Omnes Turcarum, Sarracenorum, Centaurorum, & Canibalum liberi, qui sunt extra fœdus, & ecclesiam Dei, nascentur gratia & sinu Dei. Erit ergo salus etiam extra fœdus Dei: extra ecclesiam Dei. O immanes Briareos! qui infantes Turcarum extra ecclesiam natos, in gratiam & sinum Dei collocare non dubitant, Christianorum contra infantes ante baptismum, ex Dei sinu in gehennam crudeliter præcipitant.
units.tr: Second: all the children of Turks, Saracens, Centaurs and cannibals, who are outside the covenant and the Church of God, will be born in the grace and bosom of God. There will therefore be salvation even outside the covenant of God, outside the Church of God. O monstrous Briareuses! who do not hesitate to place the infants of the Turks, born outside the Church, in the grace and bosom of God, while they cruelly hurl the infants of Christians, before baptism, out of God's bosom into hell.

units.la: Tertio igitur hoc portentum aliud ipsorum dogma de infantibus fidelium extra gratiam nascentibus, immò ante baptismum à diabolo obsessis, & damnatis manifestè elidit: Omnes enim nunc in sinum & gratiam Dei reponunt.
units.tr: Third, therefore, this monstrous notion clearly contradicts and refutes their other dogma, concerning the infants of believers who are born outside grace, and indeed before baptism are possessed by the devil and damned: for they now place all of them in the bosom and grace of God.

units.la: Quarto: Omnes impij, qui ante mortem Christi in gehennam inciderunt, morte Christi rursus fuerunt ex gehenna exemti: in sinum atque gratiam Dei restituti. Quomodo ergo rursus inde exciderunt, qui mortui recepti sunt, quando amplius peccare incredulitate non potuerunt? Ergo aut in sinu Dei impij manebunt, & sine fide seruabuntur: aut sine incredulitate inde rursus præcipitabuntur: quorum vtrumque insaniæ speciem habet.
units.tr: Fourth: all the impious who fell into hell before Christ's death were, by Christ's death, taken out of hell again and restored to the bosom and grace of God. How then do those fall out again from there, who were received back in death, since they can no longer sin by unbelief? Therefore either the impious will remain in the bosom of God and be preserved without faith, or without unbelief they will be cast down again from there; both of which have the appearance of madness.

units.la: Quinto: Incredulitas vel non erit peccatum: vel si sit, non omnia peccata fuerint morte Christi expiata: vel si sint omnia, ea saltem efficaciâ mortis Christi fortior fuerit. Hæc vero falsa & impia sunt omnia. Incredulitas enim & ipsa est peccatum & mater peccatorum reliquorum: & cum peccatis reliquis subinde etiam renatis adhærens: attamen sanguine Christi efficacissime expiata, atque remissa fidelibus.
units.tr: Fifth: either unbelief will not be a sin, or if it is, not all sins were expiated by Christ's death, or if all were, at least it was stronger than the efficacy of Christ's death. But these things are all false and impious. For unbelief is itself a sin and the mother of the other sins; and while it clings to the remaining sins, which also at times cling to the reborn, nevertheless it is most effectually expiated by the blood of Christ and remitted to believers.

units.la: Sexto: Impudens mendacium est, impios non propter peccata, sed propter solam incredulitatem damnari. Quid enim illud est 1 Corinth. 6. vers. 10. Fures, auari, ebriosi, &c. regnum DEI hereditate non consequentur? Et quod Christus in judicio dicturus est maledictis: Abite in gehennam, quia non cibastis me, &c. An non incredulitas in genere peccatorum primas tenet? Immo contra concludimus propter peccata damnari: quia propter incredulitatem damnantur. Vix enim vllum peccatum incredulitate est grauius. Nimis vero futiliter ludit apostata, excipiens, incredulitatem nunc non considerari, vt in se peccatum est, sed vt salutis media respuit. An non respuere salutis media, contemnere Deum vocantem, est grauissimum peccatum? Ideo ergo incredulitas peccatum est, quia salutem eiusque media respuit.
units.tr: Sixth: it is a shameless lie that the impious are condemned not for their sins, but for unbelief alone. For what of that passage in 1 Corinthians 6:10, "Thieves, covetous, drunkards, etc., shall not inherit the kingdom of God"? And what of Christ's words, when he will speak the curse at judgment: "Depart into hell, because you did not feed me, etc."? Does not unbelief hold the first place among the kinds of sin? Indeed we conclude the opposite: they are condemned for their sins, because they are condemned for unbelief. For there is hardly any sin graver than unbelief. The apostate plays too frivolously when he objects that unbelief is now not considered as sin in itself, but as it rejects the means of salvation. Is not rejecting the means of salvation, and despising God who calls, the gravest sin? Therefore unbelief is a sin precisely because it rejects salvation and its means.

units.la: Septimò: Portentosum hoc dogma tribuit impiis, quod stante doctrina Ecclesiæ de peccato originis, & de impiorum reatu, nullo vnquam momento illis insit, nec de illis verè prædicari possit. Sumamus enim Turcicum infantem, sumamus & barbarum adultum, qui mortem CHRISTI nunquam vel sano audiuerit: proinde nec incredulitate spreuerit. Dicant jam nobis isti disputatores, quo temporis momento istis, an dum essent embryones, an recens natis, an pueris, an adolescentibus, an viris, an decrepitis, denique viuis, an mortuis, tribuere velint, quod sint in sinu & gratia Dei, reconciliati Deo, justificati, sanctificati. Immò dicant, si recepti sunt, quomodo excidant, cumneque peccata, neque actualis incredulitas eos inde praecipitare queat. Hæc enim in tales non cadit. Illa vero morte Christi expiata fuerunt. Quicquid dixerint, audiemus, vel sine fide aliquos Deo placere: vel absq; incredulitate actuali aliquos è sinu Dei præcipitari: quæ & falsa & impia, seque mutuo clidentia portenta sunt.
units.tr: Seventh: this monstrous dogma attributes to the impious something which, given the doctrine of the Church concerning original sin and the guilt of the impious, is never present in them at any moment, and cannot truly be predicated of them. Let us take a Turkish infant, and let us take also a barbarian adult who has never heard the death of Christ, even in soundness, and therefore has not despised it by unbelief. Let these disputants now tell us at what moment of time they wish to ascribe to these persons that they are in the bosom and grace of God, reconciled to God, justified, sanctified: whether while they were embryos, or newly born, or boys, or youths, or men, or decrepit, finally whether living or dead. Indeed let them say, if they were received, how they fall out again, since neither sins nor actual unbelief can throw them down from there. For these do not befall such persons. Yet those sins were expiated by Christ's death. Whatever they say, we shall hear either that some please God without faith, or that some are cast out of God's bosom without actual unbelief: which are false and impious monsters, mutually destroying one another.

units.la: Denique, quid magis blasphemum dici possit, quam Deum in gratiam recepisse, & in sinu fouere omnes infideles, impios, Caynum, Saulem, Judam, Herodem, Caligulam, denique omnes omnino sceleratos & porcos? Quæ consolatio magis erit ludibrio similis, quam te esse Christi morte redemtum, in sinum & gratiam Dei restitutum, multa vero millia eorum, qui sic fuerunt restituti, nihilominus in æternum perire. Horret animus hæc monstra pluribus persequi. Dogma ergo tam falsum, impium, absurdum, blasphemum procul ab ecclesiæ limitibus arcendum atq; exterminandum esse quis amplius dubitet?
units.tr: Finally, what could be said to be more blasphemous than that God has received all unbelievers, the impious, Cain, Saul, Judas, Herod, Caligula, in short all utterly wicked and swinish men, into grace and cherishes them in his bosom? What consolation would be more like a mockery than to say that you have been redeemed by the death of Christ and restored to the bosom and grace of God, while in fact many thousands of those who have likewise been restored nevertheless perish for ever? My mind shudders at pursuing these monsters at greater length. Who then could doubt that such a false, impious, absurd, blasphemous dogma must be kept far from the boundaries of the Church and driven out?

units.la: Hic vero mihi videor audire vociferantes: promissiones Euangelij esse vniuersales, pertinere ad omnes. Nos vero primum quærimus, qualis hæc sit consecutio? Promissiones sunt vniversales. Ergo etiam reprobi, impuri canes & porci sunt in sinum & gratiam Dei restituti. Atqui potius contra: Promissiones Euangelij omnes annexam habent conditionem fidei & poenitentiæ. Ergo nihil illæ ad canes & porcos. Deinde quoties illi suum, omnes, omnes nobis occinunt: toties nos nostrum: credentes, credentes regimus. Sunt enim promissiones vniuersales, sed respectu agentium poenitentiam, & credentium Euangelio. Atque hic ad ipsam promissionum literam coram toto mundo provocamus. Venite ad me OMNES, inquit Christus? sed addit: qui laboratis & onerati estis, hoc est, sub peccatorum mole fatiscitis, quod fit iis, qui resipiscunt. Et alibi: Sic Deus dilexit mundum, ut Filium suum unigenitum daret, ut OMNIS, QVI CREDIT, non pereat, sed habeat vitam aeternam. Et Paulus: Iustitia Dei per fidem Iesu Christi in omnes & super omnes credentes. Et alibi: Conclusit scriptura omnia sub peccato, ut promissio ex fide Iesu Christi daretur credentibus. Et Christus: Qui credit in Filium, habet vitam aeternam. Et Petrus: Huic testimonium dant omnes prophetæ, remissionem peccatorum accepturum per nomen eius omnem qui credit in eum. Similis aliarum promissionum Euangelij omnium est ratio. Nam vel expressam, vel tacitam fidei & poenitentiæ conditionem annexam habent, nec possunt, nisi de vniversitate fidelium circa blasphemiam intelligi.
units.tr: Here indeed I seem to hear people shouting that the promises of the Gospel are universal and pertain to "all." But we first ask: what kind of inference is this? The promises are universal. Therefore even the reprobate, the impure dogs and swine, have been restored to the bosom and grace of God. And yet, on the contrary: all the promises of the Gospel have attached to them the condition of faith and repentance. Therefore they have nothing to do with dogs and swine. Next, as often as they sing to us their "all, all," so often we answer them with ours: "believers, believers." For the promises are universal, but with respect to those who repent and those who believe the Gospel. And here we appeal to the very letter of the promises before the whole world. "Come to me, all," says Christ? But he adds: "who labour and are burdened," that is, who faint under the weight of sins, which is the case with those who repent. And elsewhere: "God so loved the world that he gave his only-begotten Son, so that everyone who believes should not perish but have eternal life." And Paul: "The righteousness of God through faith in Jesus Christ unto all and upon all who believe." And elsewhere: "Scripture has concluded all things under sin, so that the promise by faith in Jesus Christ might be given to those who believe." And Christ: "He who believes in the Son has eternal life." And Peter: "To him all the prophets bear witness, that everyone who believes in him will receive remission of sins through his name." The reasoning is the same for all the other universal promises of the Gospel. For they have attached to them either an express or a tacit condition of faith and repentance, and they cannot be understood of the whole body of the faithful, except with blasphemy.

units.la: Exni-
units.tr: Exni-

units.la: Excipiunt: Sic statui promissiones particulares. Respondeat pro nobis Prosper de vocatio gentium. Habet, inquit, populus Dei plenitudinem suam: & quantumvis magna pars hominum saluantis gratiam aut negligat, aut repellat: in electis tamen & praescitis atque ab omnium generalitate discretis specialis quaedam censetur vniuersitas, vt de toto mundo totus mundus liberatus, & de omnibus hominibus omnes homines videantur redemti. Manet ergo promissiones euangelii vniuersales fidelibus: etsi ad canes & porcos nihil pertineant. Manet & maior syllogismi practici vniuersalis:
units.tr: They object: "Thus particular promises are established." Let Prosper answer for us, on the calling of the Gentiles: "The people of God has its fullness; and however great a part of mankind either neglects or rejects the grace of salvation, yet among the elect and the foreknown, and distinguished from the whole generality of all, a certain special totality is reckoned, so that of the whole world the whole world is seen to be set free, and of all men all men are seen to be redeemed." Therefore the universal promises of the Gospel remain for believers, although they pertain nothing to dogs and swine. The major premise of the universal practical syllogism also remains:

units.la: Promissiones ad omnes credentes pertinent.
units.tr: The promises pertain to all who believe.

units.la: Ego credo.
units.tr: I believe.

units.la: Ergo ad me pertinent.
units.tr: Therefore they pertain to me.

units.la: Item:
units.tr: Likewise:

units.la: Christus pro omnibus credentibus orauit, & mortuus est. Ego credo. Ergo pro me orauit, & mortuus est. Nimis vero frigidi sunt consolatores, qui sic docent efflictas conscientias argumentari:
units.tr: Christ prayed for all who believe, and died. I believe. Therefore he prayed for me, and died for me. Indeed, those comforters are far too cold who teach troubled consciences to reason in this way:

units.la: Christus pro omnibus hominibus est mortuus.
units.tr: Christ died for all men.

units.la: Ego sum homo.
units.tr: I am a man.

units.la: Ergo pro me etiam est mortuus. Quidni enim etiam Turca, canis & porcus, in volutabro manens, sic concludat? O egregios consolatores, & gratiae Dei praecones. Non hominem esse, sed fide Christo insitum esse, est Christianae consolationis nervus praeclarissimus.
units.tr: Therefore he also died for me. Why could not a Turk, a dog, or a pig wallowing in the mire reason in just this way? O splendid comforters and heralds of the grace of God! That one is not a man but is grafted into Christ by faith is the most distinguished sinew of Christian comfort.

units.la: Obiiciunt denique ex Apostolo: Omnes in Christo viuificari, quemadmodum omnes in Adamo moriuntur. Atqui, si absolute omnes in Christo viuificari dicant, scriptura & experientia eos refutabit. Hoc ergo dicit apostolus: Christum omnibus suis conferre vitam; sicut Adam omnibus suis contulit mortem. Et ille quidem per gratiam: quod maius est: hic per naturalem propagationem, quod facilius. Hunc Pauli sensum etiam sequentia verba liquido probant. Cum enim omnes in Christo viuificari dixisset: statim subiungit: Vnusquisque autem suo ordine. Primitiae Christus: postea qui sunt Christi: hoc est, credentes, qui ipsi a patre dati sunt, & pro quibus patrem ardentissime orauit. Nec dissimiliter Augustinus interpretatur, ideo dictum esse, omnes in Christo viuificari: non quia omnes, qui in Adamo moriuntur, membra sint Christi: sed quia, sicut nemo corpore animali nisi in Adam moritur: ita nemo corpore spirituali, nisi in Christo viuificatur.
units.tr: Finally, they object from the Apostle: As in Adam all die, so in Christ all are made alive. But if they say that all are absolutely made alive in Christ, Scripture and experience will refute them. The Apostle is therefore saying this: that Christ confers life on all his own, just as Adam conferred death on all his own. And the former indeed by grace, which is the greater; the latter by natural propagation, which is the easier. The following words also clearly confirm this sense of Paul. For after he had said that all are made alive in Christ, he immediately adds: But each in his own order: Christ the firstfruits; afterward those who are Christ's, that is, believers, who were themselves given to the Father and for whom he prayed most earnestly. Augustine interprets it in much the same way: it is said that all are made alive in Christ not because all who die in Adam are members of Christ, but because, just as no one dies in respect of the animal body except in Adam, so no one is made alive in respect of the spiritual body except in Christ.

units.la: Neque est, quod obstrepere pergant: hac ratione Adamum Christo fortiorem statui: si plures ille in exitium & mortis vaginem praecipitauerit, quam hic seruet, atque ex faucibus mortis eripiat. Nesciunt, quid obblaterent. Esto: omnes seruen- tur per Christum perditi ab Adamo. Atqui sic non superabun- dabit gratia, sed æqualis tantum erit peccato. Potentia vtriusque non numero eorum, qui moriuntur, vel viuificantur, sed modo, quo fit perditio vel viuificatio, nec non magnitudine beneficiorum amissorum & reparatorum æstimanda est. Laedere est facile, mederi difficile, iuxta prouerbium. Citius & facilius sexcentos homines perdas, quam vnum seruès: citius multos de ponte in profluentem præcipites, quam vnum ex submersionis periculo eripias. Sic multo facilius fuit, totum humanum genus perdere: quam vnicum hominem ex ruina restituere. Illud Saetan potuit, Adam potuit: hoc nemo nisi Christus potuit. Nocere, lædere, neci dare homines, bestiæ, & res aduersæ queunt. At salutem & vitam æternam reparare, in nullius creaturæ situm est facultate: sed solius Dei rerum omnium conditoris potentiæ est reseruatum. Fortiorigitur mors Christi Adami peccato fuisset, etiamsi vel vnicum hominem vitæ restituisset. Tum etiam certum est & indubitatum, bona illa quæ per Christum iam reparata sunt, tantum præcellere iis, quorum per Adamum feceramus iacturam, quantum terrenis & caducis rebus cælestes & æternæ præstant. Adam enim, teste Apostolo, est terrenus, Christus cœlestis: ille animalis, hic spiritualis. Ille ex terreno paradiso nos eiecit: hic in cælestem collocauit, æternaque felicitate donauit.
units.tr: Nor is there any reason for them to keep shouting that by this reasoning Adam is made stronger than Christ, if he has cast more people into ruin and the sheath of death than Christ saves and snatches from the jaws of death. They do not know what they are babbling. Grant it: all who have been lost through Adam are saved through Christ. Yet in that case grace would not abound, but would be merely equal to sin. The power of each is to be judged not by the number of those who die or are made alive, but by the manner in which destruction or making alive takes place, and by the greatness of the benefits lost and restored. To harm is easy, to heal difficult, as the proverb has it. You can destroy six hundred men more quickly and easily than you can save one; you can push many off a bridge into the river more quickly than you can snatch one from the danger of drowning. So it was far easier to destroy the whole human race than to restore a single man from the ruin. Satan could do the former, Adam could do it; the latter no one could do except Christ. Creatures, beasts, and adverse things can injure, harm, and kill men. But to restore salvation and eternal life lies within the ability of no creature; it has been reserved to the power of God alone, the Creator of all things. Therefore the death of Christ would be stronger than the sin of Adam, even if it had restored only one man to life. Moreover, it is certain and beyond doubt that the blessings now restored through Christ far surpass those we lost through Adam, just as heavenly and eternal things surpass earthly and perishable ones. For Adam, as the Apostle testifies, is earthly, Christ heavenly; the former is natural, the latter spiritual. The former cast us out of the earthly paradise; the latter has placed us in the heavenly one and endowed us with eternal happiness.

units.la: Hactenus, mortis & resurrectionis Christi fructus ad omnes & solos eos, qui fide Christo adhærent, & pœnitentiam agunt, pertinere, satis ostensum atque defensum esse, arbitramur.
units.tr: Thus far we judge it to have been sufficiently shown and defended that the fruits of the death and resurrection of Christ pertain to all and only those who cling to Christ by faith and repent.

units.la: ISAGOGE BREVISSIMA AD CONTROVERSIAM EVCHARISTICAM: Exponens quaestiones praecipuas non controversas & controversas inter evangelicos.
units.tr: A VERY BRIEF INTRODUCTION TO THE EUCHARISTIC CONTROVERSY: setting out the chief questions, both those not controverted and those controverted, among evangelicals.

units.la: D. DAVIDE PAREO AVTHORE. Quatuor [illegible, ~12 letters] generalia.
units.tr: By Dr. David Pareus, the author. Four [illegible, ~12 letters] general points.

units.la: I. Meminerint iuniores, discernendas esse quaestiones de caeremonia seu ritu Caenae: & quaestiones de doctrina, quae est promissio Euangelii ritui annexa.
units.tr: I. Let the younger men remember that the question about the ceremony or rite of the Supper must be distinguished from the question about doctrine, which is the promise of the Gospel attached to the rite.

units.la: II. Discant etiam discernere quaestiones tam de ritu, quam de doctrina, non controversas à controversis.
units.tr: II. Let them also learn to distinguish questions about rite and about doctrine that are not controverted from those that are controverted.

units.la: III. Sciant quaestiones controversas de ritu esse minus principales, & magna ex parte κατ' ἐπιείκειαν decidi posse ac debere, ex temporum, locorum & populorum circumstantiis: semper tamen ad aedificationem.
units.tr: III. Let them know that the controverted questions about rite are less principal, and for the most part can and should be settled according to equity [κατ' ἐπιείκειαν], according to the circumstances of times, places and peoples; yet always for edification.

units.la: IV. Sciant, quaestiones praecipuas de doctrina caenae non controversas esse tres: & controversas totidem: ad quas omnes aliae facile referri possunt. De utrisq; iuniores hic monebo breviss.
units.tr: IV. Let them know that there are three chief questions about the doctrine of the Supper that are not controverted, and as many that are controverted, to which all the others can easily be referred. I shall briefly point out both kinds to the younger men here.

units.la: Tres quaestiones non controversae de doctrina Caenae.
units.tr: Three questions about the doctrine of the Supper that are not controverted.

units.la: I. Quid sit Caena Domini.
units.tr: I. What the Lord's Supper is.

units.la: Consentiunt de hac omnes Evangelici, quod Caena Domini sit N.T. Sacramentum à Christo institutum, in quo sumto pane & vino, sumitur verum corpus & sanguis Christi, atque obsignatur fidelibus [illegible, ~8 letters] Christi & beneficiorum eius.
units.tr: All evangelicals agree on this: that the Lord's Supper is a sacrament of the New Testament instituted by Christ, in which, when bread and wine are taken, the true body and blood of Christ are taken, and are sealed to the faithful [illegible] of Christ and of his benefits.

units.la: II. Qui sint fines & usus Caenae à Christo institutae.
units.tr: II. What the ends and uses of the Supper instituted by Christ are.

units.la: Consentiunt hic quoq; omnes euangelici, quod sumtio haec confirmet fidem promissionis gratiae: tum quia hic est communis sacramentorum usus: tum quia Christus de hoc sacramento dixit: Hoc facite in mei recordationem. Et: Hoc poculum est novum foedus in meo sanguine. Proinde etiam consentiunt in hoc, S. Coe-nam esse commemorationem mortis Domini, donec veniat, iuxta Apostoli admonitionem.
units.tr: Here too all evangelicals agree that this partaking strengthens faith in the promise of grace, both because this is the common use of the sacraments and because Christ said of this sacrament: Do this in remembrance of me. And: This cup is the new covenant in my blood. Therefore they also agree that the Holy Supper is a commemoration of the death of the Lord, until he comes, according to the admonition of the Apostle.

units.la: III. Quid in caena Domini exhibeatur & percipiatur?
units.tr: III. What is exhibited and received in the Lord's Supper?

units.la: Consentiunt & hic Euangelici, panem & vinum ore & corpore, corpus & sanguinem Domini cum omnibus beneficiis, fideli corde percipi.
units.tr: Evangelicals agree here as well: the bread and wine are received with the mouth and body, and the body and blood of the Lord with all its benefits are received by a believing heart.

units.la: De his, inquam, consensus est inter Theologos euangelicos. Contentiosis vero matæologis, neque de his, neque de a-liis liis conuenit: quorum rixæ non debent esse mensura iudicii de ecclesiarum euangelicarum consensu, vel controversiis.
units.tr: I say, there is agreement on these points among evangelical theologians. But among contentious babblers there is agreement neither on these nor on other matters; and their quarrels should not be taken as the measure of judgment concerning the consensus of the evangelical churches, or of their controversies.

units.la: Quæstiones tres controuersæ sunt hæ:
units.tr: There are three controverted questions, these:

units.la: PRIMA QVÆSTIO.
units.tr: FIRST QUESTION.

units.la: Quid sit vnio signi & rei signatæ in Cæna Domini: num transsubstantiatio: an consubstantiatio: an vero relatio mystica.
units.tr: What is the union of the sign and the thing signified in the Lord's Supper: is it transubstantiation, or consubstantiation, or rather a mystical relation?

units.la: De his tribus propositionibus orthodoxe respondetur: duabus negantibus: vna affirmante.
units.tr: These three propositions are answered orthodoxly: two deny, one affirms.

units.la: Propositio I. Signa & res non viuuntur transsubstantiatione, hoc est, tali mutatione, qua substantia signorum convertatur in substantiam rerum, manentibus tantum accidentibus.
units.tr: Proposition I. The signs and the things are not united by transubstantiation, that is, by such a change in which the substance of the signs is converted into the substance of the things, with only the accidents remaining.

units.la: Ratio 1. Ex verbis Christi: Hoc est corpus meum. Non dixit, Hoc esto, aut fiat corpus meum.
units.tr: Reason 1. From the words of Christ: "This is my body." He did not say, "Let this be," or "Let it become my body."

units.la: Ratio 2. Panis nominatur in Scriptura panis in actione, ante & post actionem.
units.tr: Reason 2. In Scripture bread is called bread during the action, and before and after the action.

units.la: Ratio 3. Patres orthodoxi panem in Cœna retinent: & cum ὑπερβολικῶς de panis mutatione loquuntur, sacramentaliter intelligi volunt: vt Theodoretus Dial. 1 Voluit Christus sacramentis uentes non intentos esse in naturam eorum quæ cernuntur, sed per nominum permutationem credere ei, quæ ex gratia facta est mutationi. Hic mutationem sacramentalem intelligendam esse, Theodoretus ipse eodem dialogo docet, sic inquiens: Christi visibilia symbola corporis & sanguinis appellatione honorauit, non naturam mutans, sed naturæ gratiam adiiciens.
units.tr: Reason 3. The orthodox Fathers retain bread in the Supper, and when they speak of a change of the bread hyperbolically [ὑπερβολικῶς], they want it understood sacramentally. So Theodoret, Dialogue 1: Christ wished those who approach the sacraments not to fix their minds on the nature of the things that are seen, but to believe, through the change of names, in the change that has been made by grace. That the change here is to be understood as sacramental, Theodoret himself teaches in the same dialogue, saying: Christ honoured the visible symbols with the names of body and blood, not changing their nature, but adding grace to nature.

units.la: Propositio II. Signa & res signata non viuntur consubstantiatione, hoc est, reali duorum corporum in eodem loco sub iisdem accidentibus existentia, aut vnius in altero latentia: qualis est auena in sacco, pecunia in crumena: infantis in cunis: vini in cantharo, quæ sunt Consubstantiatorum similia.
units.tr: Proposition II. The signs and the thing signified are not united by consubstantiation, that is, by a real existence of two bodies in the same place under the same accidents, or by one lying hidden in the other: such as oats in a sack, money in a purse, an infant in a cradle, or wine in a cup, which are like the Consubstantiationists' view.

units.la: Ratio 1. Quia Christi verba: Hoc est corpus meum, sonant, non vbi sit corpus Christi: neque quid in, cum, sub pane sit: sed quid ipse panis sit, esseque debeat piis in hoc vsu, nempe corpus suum.
units.tr: Reason 1. Because the words of Christ, "This is my body," speak not of where the body of Christ is, nor of what is in, with, or under the bread, but of what the bread itself is and ought to be for the faithful in this use, namely, his body.

units.la: Ratio 2. Corpus Christi est verum organicum, finitum, & visibile corpus: post ascensionem non vt in terris vel vbiq; præsens: sed in cœlo existens & manens, vsq; ad reditum extremum: dicente Apostolo: Mortem Domini annunciate: DONEC VENIAT.
units.tr: Reason 2. The body of Christ is a true, organic, finite and visible body. After the ascension it is not present as it was on earth, nor everywhere, but exists and remains in heaven until the final return, the Apostle saying: "Proclaim the Lord's death until he comes."

units.la: Ratio 3. Orthodoxi patres corpus & sanguinem Christi in pane & vino esse docent, non in latibulis, sed vt in mysterio seu mystice. Chrysost. in opere imperfecto Matth. hom. 11. In vasis sanctificatis non verum Christi corpus, sed mysterium corporis Christi continetur.
units.tr: Reason 3. The orthodox Fathers teach that the body and blood of Christ are in the bread and wine not in hiding, but as in a mystery, or mystically. Chrysostom in the Opus imperfectum on Matthew, homily 11: "In the sanctified vessels is contained not the true body of Christ, but the mystery of the body of Christ."

units.la: PROPOSITIO III. Signa & res coharent in Sacramento cana vnione sacramentali.
units.tr: PROPOSITION III. The signs and the things cohere in the Sacrament of the Supper by a sacramental union.

units.la: Ea vero est, quæ toti sacramentorum generi communis est: alioqui non sacramentalis, sed cœnalis esset. In omnibus vero sacramentis aliis, vnio est relativa, hoc est, mystica rei signatæ per symbola externa significatio, obsignatio, præbitio & perceptio in vsu legitimo: qui non est sine fide & conuersione vtentium.
units.tr: This union is common to the whole kind of sacraments; otherwise it would not be sacramental but merely a supper. In all the other sacraments the union is relative, that is, a mystical signifying, sealing, offering and receiving of the thing signified through external symbols, in lawful use; and this use is not without faith and the conversion of those who use them.

units.la: Ratio 1. à genere. In omnibus sacramentis talis est vnio. Ergo etiam in cœna. Antecedens ex definitione & principali sacramentorum sine patet.
units.tr: Reason 1, from the genus. In all sacraments such a union exists; therefore also in the Supper. The antecedent is plain from the definition and principal nature of sacraments.

units.la: Ratio 2. Panis est corpus Christi aut rei veritate (vt loquitur Augustinus in sententia Prosperi:) aut significante mysterio. Non rei veritate seu essentialiter: quia non fit transsubstantiatio. Ergo significante mysterio.
units.tr: Reason 2. Bread is the body of Christ either in the truth of the thing (as Augustine says in the sentence of Prosper) or by a signifying mystery. Not in the truth of the thing, or essentially, because there is no transubstantiation. Therefore by a signifying mystery.

units.la: Ratio 3. Huc pertinent omnia argumenta, quibus sacramentalis locutio in verbis cœnæ probatur. Vnio enim sacramentalis phrases sacramentales parit.
units.tr: Reason 3. To this belong all the arguments by which sacramental speech is proved in the words of the Supper, for a sacramental union produces sacramental phrases.

units.la: Ratio 4. Testimonia patrum, quod panis sit signum, figura, sacramentum corporis Christi. Augustinus cont. Adim. cap. 12. Non dubitavit Dominus dicere, Hoc est corpus meum, cum daret signum sui corporis, &c.
units.tr: Reason 4. The testimonies of the Fathers that bread is the sign, figure and sacrament of the body of Christ. Augustine, Against Adimantus, ch. 12: The Lord did not hesitate to say, "This is my body," when he gave the sign of his body, etc.

units.la: Obiectio Papistarum pro transsubstantiatione ex verbis Cœnæ.
units.tr: Objection of the Papists for transubstantiation from the words of the Supper.

units.la: Hoc quod dabat Christus, & sacerdos consecrat, est corpus Christi. Ergo non est panis. Valet à disparatis. Hæc res est homo. Ergo non est bos. Respondeo. Negatur, quod fit argumentum à positione vnius speciei ad remotionem disparatæ eiusdem generis: quia est processus vitiosus à positione relationis sacramentalis, ad negationem subiecti seu fundamenti: qualis est, si dicam: Hic homo est pater. Ergo non est homo. Hic homo est Cæsar: Ergo non est homo. Sic illi: Hic panis est corpus Christi: Ergo non est panis. Est ergo fallacia accidentis non minus absurda, quam si a positione formæ ad negationem materiæ sic argumenteris: Hæc res est mensa. Ergo non est lignum. Licet enim corpus Christi non sit forma vel accidens panis: ipsa tamen relatio, quam panis, vi promissionis ad corpus Christi habet ac sustinet, forma est sacramenti. Sic non valet: Columba est spiritus sanctus. Ergo non est columba. Circumcisio est fœdus Dei: Ergo non est circumcisio. Poculum est nouum testamentum. Ergo non poculum.
units.tr: What Christ gives, and the priest consecrates, is the body of Christ; therefore it is not bread. The inference is from disparates, as: "This thing is a man; therefore it is not an ox." I answer. It is denied. The argument goes from the positing of one species to the removal of a disparate of the same genus; it is a faulty move from the positing of a sacramental relation to the denial of the subject or foundation. It is like saying: "This man is a father; therefore he is not a man." "This man is Caesar; therefore he is not a man." So too they say: "This bread is the body of Christ; therefore it is not bread." It is therefore a fallacy of accident, no less absurd than if you argued from the positing of a form to the denial of the matter: This thing is a table; therefore it is not wood. For although the body of Christ is not a form or accident of the bread, the relation itself, which the bread has and sustains by virtue of the promise to the body of Christ, is a form of the sacrament. Thus it does not follow: "The dove is the Holy Spirit; therefore it is not a dove." "Circumcision is the covenant of God; therefore it is not circumcision." "The cup is the new testament; therefore it is not a cup."

units.la: Ad testimonia patrum, quæ Papistæ de mutatione symbolorum obiiciunt, responsio communis est, ea de mutatione sacramentali, non de essentiali intelligenda esse, quod ex orthodoxo patrum consensu de hoc sacramento est manifestum.
units.tr: To the testimonies of the Fathers which the Papists object concerning the change of the symbols, the common answer is that they are to be understood of a sacramental change, not an essential one, as is clear from the orthodox agreement of the Fathers concerning this sacrament.

units.la: SECUNDA QVÆSTIO.
units.tr: SECUNDA QVÆSTIO.

units.la: Quomodo tum symbola, tum res cœlestes in cœna exhibeantur & percipiantur.
units.tr: How both the symbols and the heavenly things are exhibited and received in the Supper.

units.la: Hæc quæstio nobis controuersa est cum pontificiis simul & ubiquitariis, quia utrique volunt, res in signis, vel signorum speciebus latenter & miraculose præsentes manu ministrorum gestari, tractari, & in ora sumentium ingeri. Nos contra docemus, res cum symbolis exhiberi & percipi quidem coniunctim in legitimo cœnæ usu: sed dissimiliter: symbola manu ministrorum tractari: ore sumentium accipi. Res vero à summo pontifice Christo ipso præberi, ac fide à nobis percipi. Similiter vero tribus propositionibus explicari potest: duabus negantibus: una affirmante.
units.tr: This question is in dispute between us and the Papists, and also the Ubiquitarians, since both hold that the things, present hidden and miraculously within the signs or under the species of the signs, are carried and handled by the hands of the ministers and poured into the mouths of those who receive them. We, on the contrary, teach that the things are indeed exhibited and received together with the symbols in the lawful use of the Supper, but in different ways: the symbols are handled by the hands of the ministers and received by the mouths of the communicants, while the things themselves are offered by Christ, the highest bishop, and received by us through faith. This can be explained in three propositions: two negative and one affirmative.

units.la: PROPOSITIO I. Res signata, corpus & sanguis Domini, neque tractantur, neque exhibentur manu ministrorum in symbolis corporaliter percipienda.
units.tr: PROPOSITION I. The thing signified, the body and blood of the Lord, is neither handled nor exhibited by the hands of the ministers in the symbols, to be perceived bodily.

units.la: Ratio 1. à toto sacramentorum genere negative: In nullo sacramento ministri manu tractant & conferunt res spirituales significatas. Ergo nec in cœna.
units.tr: Reason 1, negatively from the whole genus of sacraments: In no sacrament do the ministers handle and confer the spiritual things signified. Therefore neither in the Supper.

units.la: Antecedens probatur tum inductione, quæ etiam aduersariorum & veriorum confessione patet: tum ex analogia sacramentorum & verbi. Marc. 1. Ego vox clamans. Johan. 1. Ego baptizo aqua: qui post me venit, baptizabit vos spiritu sancto & igni. 1. Cor. 3. 7. Neque qui init, neque qui plantat est aliquid, sed qui dat incrementum Deus. Ergo sic etiam in sacramentis, quæ sunt verbum visibile.
units.tr: The antecedent is proved both by induction, which is plain from the admission of our opponents and of the true teachers, and from the analogy of the sacraments and the Word. Mark 1: "I am the voice crying." John 1: "I baptize with water; but he who comes after me will baptize you with the Holy Spirit and with fire." 1 Cor. 3:7: "Neither he who plants nor he who waters is anything, but God who gives the increase." So also in the sacraments, which are the visible Word.

units.la: Ratio 2. Res signatæ non sunt in, cum, & sub symbolis præsentes: ut est ostensum q. 1. prop. 2. Non ergo manu ministri tractantur vel distribuuntur.
units.tr: Reason 2. The things signified are not present in, with, and under the symbols, as was shown in question 1, proposition 2. Therefore they are not handled or distributed by the hand of the minister.

units.la: Ratio 3. Res signatæ in cœna sunt spirituales, quæ in promissione gratiæ symbolis annexæ offeruntur fidelibus. Promissio autem gratiæ non tractatur manibus, &c.
units.tr: Reason 3. The things signified in the Supper are spiritual, and are offered to the faithful in the promise of grace annexed to the symbols. But the promise of grace is not handled by hands, etc.

units.la: Ratio 4. Testimonia patrum, ut: Chrysost. sermone de euch. in encæn. Ne putetis accedentes ad hæc mysteria, quod accipiatis divinum corpus ex homine: id est, ministro: & similia multa.
units.tr: Reason 4. The testimonies of the Fathers, such as Chrysostom in his sermon on the Eucharist in the Encaenia: "Do not think, when you approach these mysteries, that you receive the divine body from a man," that is, from the minister; and many similar passages.

units.la: PROPOSITIO II. Res signatæ corpus & sanguis Domini non percipiuntur cum, in, & sub pane & vino, oraliter seu ore corporeo.
units.tr: PROPOSITION II. The things signified, the body and blood of the Lord, are not received with, in, or under the bread and wine orally, that is, with the bodily mouth.

units.la: Ratio 1. Quia non sunt cum, in, sub symbolis corporaliter præsentes, ut est ostensum, quæst. 1 propos. 2.
units.tr: Reason 1. Because they are not bodily present with, in, or under the symbols, as was shown in question 1, proposition 2.

units.la: Ratio 2. Quia non ingrediuntur ventrem, qui destinatus est escis corporeis 1. Cor. 6. 13. Omne autem, quod ingreditur in os, in ventrem cedit. Matth. 15.
units.tr: Reason 2. Because they do not enter the belly, which is destined for bodily food: 1 Cor. 6:13. But whatever enters the mouth passes into the belly: Matt. 15.

units.la: Ratio 3. Quia promissio, qua res offeruntur, non capitur ore sed fide.
units.tr: Reason 3. Because the promise by which the things are offered is not grasped by the mouth but by faith.

units.la: PROPOSITIO III. Res signata corpus & sanguis Domini, percipiuntur fide, spiritualiter.
units.tr: PROPOSITION III. The things signified, the body and blood of the Lord, are received spiritually, by faith.

units.la: Ratio 1. à genere: quia in omnibus sacramentis res signatæ percipiuntur fide: qua sola vtiustificamur, ita omnia beneficia noui testamenti accipimus, per quam & Christus habitat in cordibus nostris. Eph. 3. 17.
units.tr: Reason 1, from the genus: because in all sacraments the things signified are received by faith, which alone justifies us, and by which we receive all the benefits of the New Testament, and through which Christ dwells in our hearts: Eph. 3:17.

units.la: Ratio 2. Quia promissio gratiæ non nisi fide percipitur, corporis vero & sanguinis Christi ɣʀαʀɩα est promissi gratiæ. Vide volum. 1. Vrsini pag. 103.
units.tr: Reason 2. Because the promise of grace is received only by faith, and the body and blood of Christ are the thing (the gift) of grace promised [χάρις]. See Ursinus's first volume, page 103.

units.la: Pro orali manducatione argutatio cuiusdam nobilis disputatoris.
units.tr: The subtle argument of a certain noble disputant in favour of oral manducation.

units.la: Cuicunque instrumento conuenit manducatio vnius rei in cœna Domini, eidem etiam alterius conueniat, oportet. Sed ori corporis manducatio vnius, hoc est, panis, in cœna conuenit. Ergo & alterius, hoc est, corporis Christi.
units.tr: Whatever instrument is suited to the eating of one thing in the Lord's Supper must also be suited to the eating of the other. But the eating of one thing, that is, the bread, by the mouth of the body, is suited in the Supper. Therefore the eating of the other, that is, of the body of Christ, is too.

units.la: Resp. Maior vera est de cibis physice copulatis, aut sese continentibus, vt est artocreas. At non ita copulantur panis & corpus Christi. De his igitur falsa est.
units.tr: Answer. The major is true of foods that are physically joined or that hold together, such as a meat pie (artocreas). But the bread and the body of Christ are not joined in this way. So the major is false in their case.

units.la: Probat ille maiorem. Quicunque panem & vinum, corpus & sanguinem Christi eidem manducationis vocabulo includit, is eodem etiam instrumento vtraque sumi affirmat. Sed Christus panem & vinum, corpus & sanguinem suum eidem manducationis vocabulo includit. Ergo Christus vtraque eodem etiam manducationis instrumento sumi affirmat.
units.tr: He proves the major thus: whoever includes bread and wine, and the body and blood of Christ, under one and the same word for eating, affirms that both are taken by the same instrument. But Christ includes bread and wine, and his body and blood, under the same word for eating. Therefore Christ affirms that both are taken by the same instrument of eating.

units.la: Resp. 1. Disputator non concludit maiorem negatam, quam debet concludere syllogismo vniuersali in Barbara. Ergo est inepta probatio.
units.tr: Answer 1. The disputant does not draw the denied major as he ought to draw it in a universal syllogism in Barbara. Therefore the proof is clumsy.

units.la: 2. Maior principium petit: & negatur. Falsitas patet ex Joh. 3. vbi Christus eodem natiuitatis vocabulo includit spiritum & carnem: nec tamen sequitur, eodem modo vel instrumento vtrumque nasci.
units.tr: 2. The major begs the question, and is denied. Its falsity is plain from John 3, where Christ includes the Spirit and the flesh under the same word for birth, and yet it does not follow that both are born in the same way or by the same instrument.

units.la: 3. Etiam minor est falsa. Verbum enim manducate, ad panem sacrum, non ad corpus refertur, nisi ex consequenti & analogia. Proprie enim ad id pertinet, quod Dominus manibus accepit & fregit: quod erat panis: non corpus eius. Ratio notatu digna hæc est, quia secundum papistas, & simplices consubstantiatores, corpus Christi ante pronunciata verba consecrationis, quæ vocant, nondum adest, sed in vltimo probationis instanti syllabarum; Hoc est enim corpus meum, adesse incipit. Secundum vbiquitarios vero, qui sunt quasi chymici consubstantiatores, adest quidem, vt in quouis pane, sed nondum est manducabile, nisi post consecrationem. Non ergo iussit Christus ore manducare in pane quod in pane nondum fuit, vel non dum manducabile fuit. Nos breuiter dicimus, verbo manducate tantum externi sacramenti seu panis manducationem oralem præcipi: verbo autem promissionis: Hoc est corpus meum quod pro vobis traditur, quæ promissio conuenit cum illa Joh.6.52. Panis quem ego dabo, est caro mea, quam dabo pro mundi vita, requiri spiritualiter manducantem corpus Christi traditum pro nobis, & bibentem Christi sanguinem pro nobis effusum in remissionem peccatorum.
units.tr: 3. The minor is also false. For the word eat refers to the sacred bread, and not to the body, except by consequence and analogy. For it properly applies to what the Lord took and broke with his hands, which was bread, and not his body. This point is worth noting: according to the Papists and the simple consubstantiators, the body of Christ is not yet present before the so-called words of consecration are pronounced, but begins to be present at the last instant of the pronouncing of the syllables, This is my body. According to the Ubiquitarians, who are like chemical consubstantiators, it is indeed present, as in any bread, but it is not yet eatable until after the consecration.
