Nor, however, are we drawn by the Father against our will (as is objected) any more than we are enlightened against our will.

units.la: VIII. Quia donum fidei & resipiscentiæ à spiritu Dei dari dicitur, non solum quod voluntati offertur resistibiliter, sed quod cordibus inditur siue infunditur irresistibiliter. Joh.6,65. Eph.2,8. Phil.1,19. 2 Tim.2,25. Rom.5,5. cauilli contrarii prorsus ἀλόγοι sunt.
units.tr: VIII. Because the gift of faith and repentance is said to be given by the Spirit of God, not only in the sense that it is offered to the will resistibly, but in that it is poured into hearts irresistibly (John 6.65; Eph. 2.8; Phil. 1.29; 2 Tim. 2.25; Rom. 5.5). The contrary cavils are utterly irrational [ἀλόγοι].

units.la: IX. Quia resistibilitas gratiæ, si debeat fieri conuersio, supponit bonam in voluntate non renata facultatem non resistendi. Hanc vero negat vniuersa scriptura. Hæc ratio annihil aduersus se concludat, denuo considerabunt Remonstrantes.
units.tr: IX. Because the resistibility of grace, if conversion is to take place, presupposes in the unregenerate will a good faculty of not resisting. But the whole of Scripture denies this. The Remonstrants will consider again whether this argument does not conclude against themselves.

units.la: X. Quia posita resistibilitate gratiæ, præcipuum opus nostræ saluti necessarium, ipsum nempe credere & resipiscere, in hominis arbitrio tanquam in proxima causa poneretur: discriminis quoque ratio, cur ex duobus non renatis audito Euangelio unus credat, alter non credat, ex homine esset, quod unus gratiæ non resistere, alter resistere voluit: Contra illud: Quis te discreuit? quid habes, quod non accepisti? Quod non modo respectu infidelium (ut fingitur) sed & respectu gratiæ dicitur. Si enim in duobus infidelibus gratia pariter resistibilis ponitur, utiq; non solum resistenti & non credenti, sed & gratiæ ac Deo respondere: Ego me discreui: quod mendacium à Remonstrantibus approbatur non sine blasphemia.
units.tr: X. Because, if resistibility of grace is granted, the chief work necessary for our salvation, namely to believe and repent, would be placed in the will of man as the proximate cause. And the reason for the difference, why of two unregenerate men who hear the Gospel one believes and the other does not, would lie in man, since the one chose not to resist grace and the other chose to resist. This is contrary to: Who makes you to differ? What do you have that you did not receive? This is said not only with respect to unbelievers (as is pretended) but also with respect to grace. For if grace is posited as equally resistible in two unbelievers, then surely each would be able to answer not only the one who resists and does not believe, but also grace and God: I made myself to differ. The Remonstrants approve this lie, and not without blasphemy.

units.la: XI. Addatur his ratio alia ex dicto Joh.15,5. Sine me nihil potestis facere. Si enim gratia conuertens est resistibilis: poterit is, qui non resistit gratiæ, Dominum refutare ac dicere: Ecce, sine te non resitit gratia. Nec poterit dicere: ex te non resistiti: quin cum ex hypothesi gratia eadem ponatur in resistente, dicere etiam debebit: Ille ex te resistit: quod est blasphemum.
units.tr: XI. Add to these another argument, from the saying in John 15:5, "Without me you can do nothing." If the converting grace is resistible, then the one who does not resist grace could rebut the Lord and say: "Behold, without you grace does not resist." Nor could he say: "It does not resist from you," since, on their hypothesis, the same grace is posited in the one who resists. He would then also have to say: "That one resists from you," which is blasphemous.

units.la: XII. Addatur & Augustini ratio. Qui habet humanorum cordium, quo placet, inclinandorum omnipotentissimam potestatem: & de ipsis hominum voluntatibus, quod vult facit: & magis habet in potestate voluntates hominum, quam ipsi suas: quinque interna atque occulta, mirabili ac ineffabili potestate operatur in cordibus hominum non solum novas revelationes, sed etiam BONAS VOLUNTATES: Et quidem hoc non facit, nisi per ipsorum hominum voluntates: Is gratia sua fidem & conuersionem in cordibus hominum, non RESISTIBILI operatione, sed prorsus IRRESISTIBILI, nec coactiua tamen operatur. Atqui Deus habet omnipotentissimam potestatem in voluntates hominum, &c. & in eadem operatur, prout dictum. Ergo, &c.
units.tr: XII. Add also the argument of Augustine. He who has the most almighty power to incline human hearts wherever he pleases, and who does what he wills with the very wills of men, and who has the wills of men in his power more than men have their own, works in the hearts of men, by a wonderful and ineffable power, not only new revelations but also good wills, and he does this only through the wills of men themselves. He works faith and conversion in the hearts of men by an operation that is not resistible but wholly irresistible, and yet he works it without compulsion. But God has the most almighty power over the wills of men, and he works in them as has been said. Therefore, and so on.

units.la: Maior habet euidentissimam veritatem, ex nexu causæ priæ cum suo effectu, ut negari nulla ratione possit.
units.tr: The major premise has the most evident truth, from the connection of the prior cause with its effect, so that it cannot be denied on any ground.

units.la: Assumtionem Augustinus docet exemplis duobus. Prius est ex 1 Sam.19,26. de Saule, cui cum Deus vellet dare regnum, Israelitarum hitarum vero voluntates possent se ei subdere vel resistere: Deus tetigit eorum corda, ut nec vellent, nec possent resistere: idq; fecit per ipsorum voluntates. Posterius ex 1 Paral. 11, & 12. de Dauide, quem cum Deus in regnum successu prosperiore constituere vellet: Spiritus Domini induit Abisai principem inter triginta, ut diceret: Tui sumus Dauid, & tecum futuri, fili Iesse. Nunquid, inquit Augustinus, ille posset aduersari voluntati Dei, & non potius eius facere voluntatem, qui in eius corde operatus est per spiritum suum quo induit est, ut hoc vellet, diceret & faceret? Ac per hos Dominus omnipotens, qui erat cum illo, adduxit istos, ut eum Regem constitue-rent. Nunquid corporalibus ullis vinculis alligauit? Intus egit, cordâ tenuit, cordâ mouit, eosque voluntatibus eorum, quas ipse in illis operatus est, traxit.
units.tr: Augustine teaches the minor premise by two examples. The first is from 1 Samuel 19:26, concerning Saul, to whom God wished to give the kingdom, while the wills of the Israelites could either submit to him or resist him. God touched their hearts so that they neither wished nor were able to resist, and he did this through their own wills. The second is from 1 Chronicles 11 and 12, concerning David, whom God wished to establish in the kingdom with more prosperous success. "The Spirit of the Lord clothed Amasai, chief of the thirty, so that he said: 'We are yours, David, and with you, son of Jesse.'" "Could he," says Augustine, "oppose the will of God, rather than doing the will of him who worked in his heart through his Spirit, with which he was clothed, so that he would will, say and do this? And so the Lord almighty, who was with him, brought those men to make him king. Did he bind them with any bodily chains? He acted within them; he held their hearts, he moved their hearts, and he drew them by those wills which he himself had worked in them."

units.la: Conclusionem denique praemittit his verbis: Deo volenti salvum facere, nullum hominum resistit arbitrium. Sic enim velle & nolle in volentis aut nolentis est potestate, ut divinam voluntatem non impediat, nec impediat potestatem. Ac ne quis excipiat, Deum resisten-tiam quidem, sed non resistibilitatem, auferre, dicit porro: Non est itaque dubitandum, voluntati Dei, qui in coelo & terra omnia, quacunque voluit, fecit, & qui etiam illa, quae futura sunt, fecit, humanas voluntates NON POSSE RESISTERE, quo minus faciat ipse, quod vult, quandoquidem etiam de ipsis hominum voluntatibus, quod vult, facit. Apertissimum est igitur, sanctum hunc Patrem non solum in hominis conversione atq; salute, sed in aliarum quoq; actionum arduarum, qualis est regum electio, directione, gratiae divinae operationem irresistibilem fortiter asserere, idque propter gloriam Dei: praetextus vero resistibilitatis & coactionis tanquam inanes elidere.
units.tr: Finally he prefaces the conclusion with these words: "When God wills to save, no human choice resists. For to will and not to will is in the power of the one who wills or does not will, in such a way that it does not hinder the divine will, nor does it hinder his power." And lest anyone except that God takes away resistance but not resistibility, he goes on to say: "Therefore there is no doubt that the human wills CANNOT RESIST the will of God, who has made all things in heaven and earth, whatever he willed, and who has also made those things which are going to be, so that he himself does what he wills, since he also does what he wills with the very wills of men." It is therefore most plain that this holy Father firmly asserts that the grace of God works an irresistible operation, not only in the conversion and salvation of man but also in the direction of other difficult actions, such as the choice of kings, and that he does this for the glory of God; and he dismisses the pretext of resistibility and compulsion as empty.

units.la: XIII. Denique, si gratia operans fidem & conversionem non est dicto modo irresistibilis, sed RESISTIBILIS, ut ab hominum voluntatibus impediri possit vel non, sequitur, inanes verborum fumos esse, quicquid tertio & quarto Articulo gratiae Dei ab istis magnifice tributitur, neque effectus illos, quos praedicant, gratiae Dei, nisi indifferenter & remote: voluntatibus vero hominum non resistentium specifice & proxime vendicandos esse: quod sic patet.
units.tr: XIII. Finally, if the grace that works faith and conversion is not irresistible in the way described, but is RESISTIBLE, so that it may or may not be hindered by the wills of men, it follows that whatever is magnificently attributed to the grace of God by these men in the third and fourth Articles is empty smoke of words; and that those effects which they proclaim belong to the grace of God only indifferently and remotely, while they must be claimed specifically and proximately for the wills of men who do not resist. This is shown as follows.

units.la: Effectus causae operantis resistibiliter, hoc est, ita ut eius productio vel inhibitio ab alia non resistente vel resistente causa pendeat: si producatur, indifferenter quidem & remote operanti, specifice vero & proxime non resistenti, sed admittenti: contra, si impediatur, specifice & proxime resistenti seu admittere nolenti, inhibitio eius debetur. v. g. Princeps subditis pluribus proponit bravium resistibiliter, ut qui voluetit rit certare, habeat, qui noluerit, non habeat bravium. Actio principis indifferenter se habet ad plures, volens certare specificabit eam bene: quia erit ei acceptio bravii: nolens certare specificabit male, quia erit ei carentia bravii. Quis non videat, tam hanc quam illam volenti certare, vel non, specifice & proxime Principi non nisi indifferenter & remote deberi? Addam aliud, quo gratiam resistibilem declarari ipse aliquando audivi. Pater catillum opsoniis plenum in media mensa assidentibus ex aequo proponit resistibiliter, ut volens capere habeat, nolens non habeat opsonia. Patris operatio indifferens est omnibus: volentes capere, specificant eam bene: nolentes male. Quis rursus non videat, opsonia capientibus specifice & proxime, patri nonnisi indifferenter & remote deberi? Talis est resistibilis operatio gratiae, quam isti docent.
units.tr: The effect of a cause that works resistibly, that is, in such a way that its production or inhibition depends on another cause that either resists or does not resist: if it is produced, it is due indifferently and remotely to the one who works, but specifically and proximately to the one who does not resist but admits it; on the other hand, if it is hindered, its inhibition is due specifically and proximately to the one who resists, or who is unwilling to admit it. For example, a prince offers a prize resistibly to several subjects, so that whoever is willing to compete will have it, and whoever is unwilling will not have the prize. The prince's action stands indifferently toward many; the one willing to compete specifies it well, because he will receive the prize; the one unwilling specifies it badly, because he will lack the prize. Who does not see that both this and that, for the one who is willing to compete or not, are due to the prince only indifferently and remotely, and not specifically and proximately? I will add another example, by which I once heard someone explain resistible grace. A father offers a dish full of delicacies equally to those sitting at the middle of the table, resistibly, so that whoever is willing to take will have the delicacies, and whoever is unwilling will not have them. The father's operation is indifferent to all: those willing to take specify it well, those unwilling badly. Again, who does not see that the delicacies are due to those who take them specifically and proximately, and to the father only indifferently and remotely? Such is the resistible operation of grace that these men teach.

units.la: Ea vero si sic est: illusoria vel falsa sint necesse est omnia gratiae effecta, quae commemorant: Illusorium vel falsum, quod homo fidem a seipso seu vi liberi arbitrii non habeat: Habebit enim a se specificationem operationis gratiae: quia nolendo resistere gratiae, discreuit se ab aliis: Quod non possit ex se aliquid boni cogitare, velle, facere: nam ex se bene specificare operationem resistibilem, indifferentem, bonum est: Quod Deus per Spiritum sanctum nos regignat & renovet; &c. Deus enim per Spiritum sanctum nonnisi resistibiliter, indifferenter ac remote, coque improprie, nos specifice, proxime & proprie nosmet regignemus & renovabimus: Quod haec gratia sit initium (de progressu & perfectione circa hanc gratiam non quaeritur) omnis boni: Initium enim bonae specificationis resistibilis & indifferentis operationis gratiae, bonum est, ex nostra non resistentia, &c.
units.tr: But if this is so, then it is necessary that all the effects of grace that they mention are illusory or false: it is illusory or false that man has faith from himself, or by the power of free will. For he would have from himself the specification of the operation of grace, because by unwillingly resisting grace he would have distinguished himself from others. And it is false that he cannot of himself think, will or do anything good; for to specify well from himself a resistible, indifferent operation is good. And it is false that God regenerates and renews us through the Holy Spirit, and so on. For God, through the Holy Spirit, only resistibly, indifferently and remotely, and therefore improperly, regenerates and renews us; we specifically, proximately and properly regenerate and renew ourselves. And it is false that this grace is the beginning (progress and perfection in regard to this grace are not at issue) of all good. For the beginning of a good specification of a resistible and indifferent operation of grace is good, from our non-resistance, and so on.

units.la: Quid porro? A Deo nonnisi resistibilis atque indifferens gratiae operatio petenda erit: nec nisi pro hac Deo gratiae debitae: nostrae voluntatis & virtutis erit, non resistentia, & specificatio bona gratiae. Hinc nonne Deus gloria sua spoliatur? homo reti suo habet quod sacrificet? ut infletur superbia in Deum, dicatque: Ego me discreui, hoc est, cum Satana in barathrum incerpiterat ferni praecipitetur. Si vero ex nobis resistibili gratiae non resistimus, oblatam accipimus, indifferentem specificamus, (quae cum clausula articuli quarti necessario cohaerent:) nonne stat liberi arbitrii idolum, iacet & evanescit peccatum originis, naturae corruptio, pravitas, de qua adque hominis animalis corruptio, queritur in scripturis Deus, queruntur Prophetae & Apostoli, queruntur ipsi sancti? ubi vero Catechesis, quod natura sinus propensi ad odium Dei & proximi, quod adeo corrupti, ut ad bene agendum prorsus non simus idonei? Nimirum hoc est, quod resistibilis gratia it profligatum.
units.tr: What then? Is a resistible and indifferent operation of grace the only thing to be asked of God, and is grace owed to God only for this? Will the non-resistance and good specification of grace be ours by our own will and virtue? Is God then robbed of his glory? Does man have what he may sacrifice from his own net? So that pride swells against God, and he says: "I have distinguished myself," that is, with Satan he is hurled into the abyss of hell. But if by ourselves we do not resist the resistible grace that is offered, and we accept it and specify it indifferently (which cohere necessarily with the clause of the fourth Article), does not the idol of free will stand upright, while the sin of origin, the corruption of nature, its perversity, and the corruption of the animal man, about which God complains in the Scriptures, about which the Prophets and Apostles complain, about which the saints themselves complain, lie prostrate and vanish away? Where then is the Catechism's teaching that the nature of man is so inclined to hatred of God and of neighbour, and so corrupted, that we are not at all fit to do good? Surely this is what resistible grace has overthrown.

units.la: Ex quibus omnibus manifestum est, Remonstrantes utroque articulo, praesertim clausula quarti, vel aequivocatione vocis gratia supra explicata abuti, operationem gratiae vocantis, suadentis, excitantis quam isti vocant adventitiam, praecedaneam) resistibilem asserendo, quam talem esse orthodoxi minime inficiantur, sicque inanibus rixis Ecclesias & rempublicam turbare: vel operationem gratiae operantis fidem & conversionem intelligendo, doctrinam gratiae cum Pelagio periculose depravare: vel denique contradictionis vinculo rursus se innodare, gratiae operanti soli fidem & regenerationem tribuentes: eandem vero resistibilem, hoc est, ab hominis voluntate indifferenter suspensam statuentes: Rursus, fidem merum Dei donum profitentes: eandem vero resistibiliter a voluntatis assensu suspendentes: quae nulla Sophistica conciliari possunt. Quando vero (ut supra) adversarius contradictoria inducere cogitur: victus esse cognoscitur.
units.tr: From all these things it is clear that the Remonstrants, in both articles and especially in the clause of the fourth, abuse the ambiguity of the word grace explained above: either by asserting that the operation of calling, persuading and stirring up grace, which they call adventitious and preceding, is resistible, which the orthodox by no means deny to be such, and so they disturb the Churches and the commonwealth with empty quarrels; or by understanding the operation of grace that works faith and conversion, and so dangerously corrupting the doctrine of grace together with Pelagius; or finally by binding themselves again in the knot of contradiction, ascribing faith and regeneration to grace alone that works, and yet declaring that same grace to be resistible, that is, suspended indifferently on the will of man; again professing faith to be the mere gift of God, and yet suspending that same faith resistibly on the assent of the will. These things cannot be reconciled by any sophistry. And when the adversary is forced to bring forward contradictory things, he is recognised as having been defeated.

units.la: Negant, gratiam (seu resistibilem seu non) ex absoluto Dei decreto descendere. Hoc enim cane peius & angue oderunt. Atqui satis est, testari hoc Apostolum, ubi vocationem, non externam tantum, sed propriissime internam illam iustificationis fidei effectricem; immediate cum praedestinatione; tanquam effectum cum causa prima connectit. Quicquid vero huius sit, nihil in rem illorum. Fac nullam esse in caelo praedestinationem: nullam electionem. Manet nihilominus firmissimum scripturae principium, ab Augustino locis allegatis assertum, Deum omnipotentem omnipotentissimam potestatem in hominum voluntates habere, ipsasque voluntates, sicut vult, vel malas relinquere & inclinare, vel bonas, hoc est, gratia sua non repugnabiles efficere: Cum quo principio illa, quae fingitur, gratiae resistibilitas, hoc est, ad fidem & conversionem efficiendam imbecillitas atque indifferentia: & voluntatum ad gratiae Deoque ipsi in homine operanti repellandum potentia, si stare posset; nec Deum in caelo omnipotentem fore, nec ullius vaquam hominis ad Deum conversionem & regenerationem futuram esse, tam est evidens, ut nulla in aeternum sophistica convelli possit. Atque haec de Articulo III. & IV. satis: de quibus, quam sint tolerabiles, liquet.
units.tr: They deny that grace (whether resistible or not) descends from God's absolute decree. For they hate this worse than a dog or a snake. Yet it is enough to show that the Apostle here links the calling, not only the external but most properly that inward calling which effects faith of justification, immediately with predestination, as effect with first cause. Whatever the case, it does nothing for their position. Suppose there is no predestination in heaven, no election. Still the most firm principle of Scripture remains, asserted by Augustine from the places cited: that God omnipotent has most omnipotent power over men's wills, and either leaves them evil and inclines them as he wills, or makes them good, that is, not resistant to his grace. With this principle, that invented resistibility of grace, that is, a weakness and indifference for producing faith and conversion, and a power of the wills to repel grace and God himself working in man, if it could stand, then God would not be omnipotent in heaven, and no man's conversion to God and regeneration would ever come about. It is so evident that no sophistry can overturn it for ever. And let this be enough on the third and fourth Articles: about them, how tolerable they are, is clear.

units.la: ARTICULUS QUINTUS.
units.tr: ARTICLE FIVE.

units.la: Qui Iesu Christo per veram fidem sunt insiti, ac proinde spiritus eius viuificantis participes, eos abunde habere facultatum, quibus contra Satanam, peccatum, mundum, & propriam suam carnem pugnent, & victoriam obtineant: verumtamen per gratiae Spiritus sancti subsidium: Iesum Christum vero, illis spiritu suo in omnibus tentationibus adesse, manum porrigere: & modo sint ad certamen prompti, & eius auxilium peregerint, neque officio suo desint, eos confirmare: atque id adeo quidem vt nulla satanae fraude, aut vi seducì, vel ab manibus Christi eripi possint, secundum illud Iohannis 10. nemo illos e manu mea eripiet. Sed an illi ipsi negligentia sua initium sui esse in Christo deserere non possint, & praesentem mundum iterum amplecti, a sancta doctrina ipsis semel tradita deficere, conscientiae naufragium facere, a gratia excidere: penitius ex sacra scriptura esset expendendum, antequam illud cum plena animi tranquillitate & plerophoria docere possent.
units.tr: Those who are grafted into Jesus Christ by true faith, and so partake of his life-giving Spirit, have enough powers to fight against Satan, sin, the world and their own flesh, and to win the victory, yet only through the help of the grace of the Holy Spirit. Jesus Christ, by his Spirit, is present to them in all temptations and stretches out his hand to them, and, provided they are ready for the contest, have sought his help and do not fail in their duty, he confirms them, so much so that they can by no deceit or force of Satan be led astray or snatched from the hands of Christ, according to John 10: "No one will snatch them out of my hand." But whether they themselves, by their negligence, can desert the beginning of their being in Christ, embrace the present world again, fall away from the sound doctrine once delivered to them, make shipwreck of their conscience, and fall from grace: this must be weighed more carefully from Holy Scripture before they can teach it with full tranquillity of mind and assurance.

units.la: EXAMEN.
units.tr: EXAMINATION.

units.la: Cum hoc Articulo doctrinam de perseuerantia sanctorum in fide se tradere in collatione profiteantur Remonstrantes, vermirari subeat haud immerito, cur vocem perseuerantiae vel verbum perseuerandi exprimere adeo caveant: ac multo magis, cum ne Deum quidem semel nominare audeant: Nisi quia adversariua clausula produnt, se & nomen & rem ab Ecclesia exterminatum ire; tam impii vero conatus auspicem Deum haudquaquam habere se, conscientia eis dictauit: adeo vt ne ferre quidem possint perseuerantiam donum Dei appellari: sed male sic dicere non erubescant. Atqui si verum fatendum est, proterviam cum inscitia sic nimis produnt. Negare enim, Dei donum recte dici, quod Deus ipse in scriptura fidelibus se daturum toties verbo suo promittit, quodque sancti a Deo sibi dari instanter flagitant, nonne protervum est? Nonne inscitia, negare perseuerantiam esse donum, & quidem infusum, nec cogitare, perseuerantiam nihil esse, nisi ipsam fidem perseuerantem in finem vsque? Ipsa vero fides nunquid non Dei donum infusum? non ne eam merum Dei donum fatentur ipsi?
units.tr: Since the Remonstrants profess in the conference that in this article they set out the doctrine of the perseverance of the saints in faith, it is not unreasonably a cause for wonder why they are so careful to avoid the word perseverance or the verb to persevere, and much more so since they dare not even name God once. Unless it is because their hostile clause betrays that they are going to banish both the name and the thing from the Church. Conscience has told them that such impious attempts have no God as their auspice, so that they cannot even bear to have perseverance called a gift of God, yet they are not ashamed to say so, and to say it wrongly. But if the truth must be confessed, they betray their insolence along with their ignorance. For is it not insolent to deny that what God himself so often promises in his word to give to the faithful is rightly called a gift of God, and what the saints earnestly beg God to give them? Is it not ignorance to deny that perseverance is a gift, and indeed an infused one, and not to think that perseverance is nothing other than faith itself persevering to the end? But faith itself, is it not an infused gift of God? Do they not themselves confess it to be a pure gift of God?

units.la: Atqui haudquaquam fugere eos potest, Augustinum donum perseuerantiae aduersus Pelagianorum reliquias peculiari assertionem libro, cui de bono perseuerantia titulum fecit. Eius argumentum tum non est aliud, quam hoc idsum: perseuerantiam in fide ad finem vsque, esse donum Dei, à Deo petendum, darique certo omnibus secundum propositum Dei vocatis atque prædestinatis. Hæc est sententia Augustini. Isti per totam collationem, vt apparet, ferre possunt perseuerantiam sanctorum: minime vero, vt ea ex prædestinatione, tanquam effectus ex causa defluere, eoque certa esse adstruatur: quandoquidem omnes quinque articulorum machinæ ad subuertendum diuinæ prædestinationis discretivæ consilium, contraque ad erigendum ἀυθεντίας idolum directæ sunt. Sed præsentis articuli verba ponderentur.
units.tr: Yet it cannot escape them that Augustine wrote a special treatise against the remnants of the Pelagians on the gift of perseverance, which he entitled On the Gift of Perseverance. Its argument is none other than this very thing: that perseverance in faith to the end is a gift of God, to be asked from God, and surely given to all those called and predestined according to God's purpose. This is Augustine's opinion. These men, as appears throughout the whole conference, can bear the perseverance of the saints; but by no means so that it is established as flowing from predestination as an effect from a cause, and therefore as certain. For all the machinery of the five articles is directed to overthrowing the discriminating counsel of divine predestination and, on the contrary, to erecting the idol of autonomy [αὐθεντίας]. But let the words of the present article be weighed.

units.la: Quintus quarto respondet. Vt enim quartus cum tertio in exollenda gratia liberalissimus, quæ erat largitus, extrema tandem clausula rursus abstulit: Ita iste facultatibus & securitati salutis fidelium membris tribus prioribus (quadrimembris enim videtur) liberaliter cavet.
units.tr: The fifth answers the fourth. For just as the fourth, while exalting grace along with the third, at the very end took back what it had so generously given, so this one generously provides for the faculties and the security of salvation of the faithful with the three preceding members (for it seems to have four members).

units.la: I. Quod abunde habeant facultatum ad satanam & peccatum debellandum per gratiæ subsidium.
units.tr: I. That they have enough powers to overcome Satan and sin through the help of grace.

units.la: II. Quod Iesus Christus in omnibus tentationibus eis adsit manumque porrigat.
units.tr: II. That Jesus Christ is present to them in all temptations and stretches out his hand.

units.la: III. Quod adeo eos confirmet, vt nulla Satanæ fraude vel vi seduci, vel è manibus Christi eripi possint. Tam luculentis priuilegiis perseuerantiæ nonne satis cautum?
units.tr: III. That he so confirms them that they cannot be seduced by any deceit or force of Satan, nor snatched from the hands of Christ. Is not sufficient care taken with such splendid privileges of perseverance?

units.la: Sed enim, vt prius, in cauda venenum Aduersatiua appendice, quæ dederant, in dubium revocant: in collatione palam auferunt: non tamen absque cothurnis: sed quibus eadem, quæ prius, incommoda incurrunt, vt vel æquiuocos sese turbatores prodant, vel contradictionibus irretiant: quæ sic patent.
units.tr: But indeed, as before, they poison the tail with an adversative appendix, and call into doubt what they had granted. In the conference they openly take it away, yet not without high-sounding airs. They incur the same disadvantages as before, so that they either reveal themselves as equivocating troublemakers or entangle themselves in contradictions. These are plain as follows.

units.la: In appendice dicunt: Sed an illi qui Iesu Christo vera fide sunt insiti, ac proinde spiritus eius viuificantis participes, non possint initium sui esse in Christo deserere, à fide deficere, à gratia excidere, penitius expendendum est ex scriptura, antequam id cum plerophoria docere possint: hoc est, se dubitare vtrum sit verum.
units.tr: In the appendix they say: But whether those who are grafted into Jesus Christ by true faith, and so partake of his life-giving Spirit, cannot desert the beginning of their being in Christ, fall from faith, fall from grace, must be weighed more carefully from Scripture before they can teach this with full assurance. That is, they doubt whether it is true.

units.la: Atqui si prius verum dixerunt, dubitare de hoc non possunt. Si enim illi vera fide Christo insiti abunde virium habent ad victoriam de Satana & carne, &c. & Christus in omnibus tentationibus illis adest, manumque porrigit: vt nulla Satanæ fraude vel vi Satanæ possint seduci, & ex manib.eius eripi: eos confirmat: quomodo quæso dubium esse potest, quin illi & facultatibus à Christo sibi datis, & eiusdem assistentia, cõfirmationeq; in omni, præsertim in defectionis tentatione adiuti ac freti, initium sui esse in Christo nunquam sint deserturi, nunquam à fide defecturi, nunquam à gratia destituendi. Reuocando igitur in dubium, quod prius asseruerunt, & quidem verissime, nonne locum ipsi con-fligunt?
units.tr: But if they spoke the truth before, they cannot doubt this. For if those grafted into Christ by true faith have enough strength for victory over Satan and the flesh, etc., and Christ is present to them in all temptations and stretches out his hand, so that they cannot be seduced by any deceit or force of Satan nor snatched from his hands; he confirms them, how, I ask, can it be doubtful that they, supported and relying both on the powers given them by Christ and on his assistance and confirmation in every temptation, especially in the temptation to fall away, will never desert the beginning of their being in Christ, never fall from faith, never be deprived of grace? By calling into doubt what they asserted before, and that most truly, do they not contradict themselves?

units.la: Excipient: Assertionem suam non esse Categoricam sed con-ditionatam, Christum fide vera sibi insitis spiritu suo adesse, manum porrigere, eosque confirmare, &c. si modo sint ad certa-men parati, & eius auxilium petant, neque officio suo desint, &c. Hanc vero conditionem à multis non poni seu praestari, non igitur sequi conflictum. Sed qualem quaeso Deum (quem tacite hinc excludunt) qualem Christum, qualem spiritum fingunt? Talem nimirum, qui vera fide Christo insitos facultatibus gra-tiæ resistibilis quidem instruat, ad certamen vero in tentatio-nibus paratos non reddat, sic stertere sinat, ut auxilium eius non petant, ut officio suo desint. Atqui promissiones atque asser-tiones divinæ longe diversum tradunt. Quantumuis enim con-ditio certaminis, precum & vigilantiæ, quam requirit, omnino sit necessaria ad perseverantiam: eam tamen non tam poni à fide-libus, (quod solum isti volunt) quam Spiritu Dei effici in fide-libus, docent haec & similia testimonia: Circumcidet Iehova Deus tuus cor tuum, & cor seminis tui, ut diligas Iehovam Deum tuum toto corde. Timorem meum dabo in corda eorum, ut non recedant à me, quod citans Augustinus pro bono perseverantiæ, explicat: Tantus erit timor meus, quem dabo in cor eorum, ut mihi perseveranter adhaereant. Spiritum meum dabo in medio vestri, efficiamque, ut in praeceptis meis ambuletis, & iudicia mea custodiatis, & faciatis illa. Hoc erit foedus meum cum istis, ait Iehova, Spiritus meus, qui est in te, & verba mea, quae posui in ore tuo, non recedent ab ore tuo. Effun-dam super domum Dauid & super habitatores Ierusalem Spiritum gratiæ, & precum, & respicient ad me, quem confixerunt, &c. Deus confirmabit vos usque in finem. Qui coepit in vobis opus bonum, idem perficiet usque ad diem Iesu Christi. Qui virtute Dei custodimur per fidem ad salutem, &c. Haec vel vanae sunt pollicitationes, quod ab-sit, vel falsa est assumtio, à multis vera fide Christo insitis con-ditionem non poni seu praestari.
units.tr: They will object: that their assertion is not categorical but conditional: that Christ is present with his Spirit to those grafted into him by true faith, stretches out his hand, and confirms them, etc., provided they are ready for the contest and seek his help, and do not fail in their duty, etc. But since this condition is not laid down or performed by many, no conflict follows. But what God, what Christ, what Spirit, I ask, do they imagine (whom they tacitly exclude here)? Surely one who equips those grafted into Christ by true faith with powers of grace that can indeed be resisted, but does not make them ready for the contest in temptations, and lets them slumber so that they do not seek his help and fail in their duty. But the divine promises and assertions teach something quite different. For however necessary the condition of contest, prayer and watchfulness, which it requires, may be for perseverance, yet these and similar testimonies teach that it is not so much laid down by the faithful (which is all these men want) as effected in the faithful by the Spirit of God: "The LORD your God will circumcise your heart and the heart of your seed, that you may love the LORD your God with all your heart." "I will put my fear in their hearts, that they may not depart from me," which Augustine, citing it for the gift of perseverance, explains: "My fear, which I will put in their heart, will be so great that they will cling to me perseveringly." "I will put my Spirit in the midst of you, and I will cause you to walk in my precepts, and keep my judgments, and do them. This is my covenant with them, says the LORD: my Spirit which is upon you, and my words which I have put in your mouth, shall not depart from your mouth. I will pour out upon the house of David and upon the inhabitants of Jerusalem the Spirit of grace and of supplications, and they shall look upon me whom they have pierced," etc. "God will confirm you to the end. He who began a good work in you will complete it until the day of Jesus Christ. Who by the power of God are kept through faith unto salvation," etc. Either these promises are empty, which is far from so, or the assumption is false, that the condition is not laid down or performed by many who are truly grafted into Christ by faith.

units.la: Neque contra faciunt cavilli, promissiones non esse absolutas, sed intelligendas cum conditione à fidelibus praestanda: stricte intellectas excludere etiam minima sanctorum peccata: conditionem praecipi, non promitti, &c. quae sunt inania effugia. Promissiones enim de ipsa conditione fidei, precum, perseverantiæ in fidelibus per Spiri-tum Dei efficienda diserte loquuntur. Nec sequitur, eius esse-ctionem non promitti, quia praecipitur & exigitur à fidelibus. Nam etiam praecipitur, ut timeant Deum, ut ambulent in prae-ceptis Dei, &c. & tamen promittit Deus: Dabo timorem meum, &c. efficiam ut ambulent in praeceptis meis. Praecipitur autem, non quod possint, sed quod debeant præstare, & vt agnita sua imbecillitate sciant, quid à Deo petere debeant. Ideo enim, dicit Augustinus, Deus iubet aliqua qua non possumus, vt noverimus, quid ab illo petere debeamus. Audientes igitur præceptum, petunt dari, quod præcipitur, dicentes cum Augustino: Da quod iubes, & iube quod vis: Quæ mea verba, inquit idem, Pelagius Romæ, cum à quodam fratre coepiscopo meo fuissent eo præsente commemorata, ferre non potuit, & contradicens aliquanto commotius, pene cum eo qui illa commemorabat, litigavit: Quod & orthodoxis cum istis hodie accidit. Nec tamen promissiones illæ Sanctorum lapsus & peccata magna vel parua excludunt, sed lapsos à ruina erigunt. Nam etiam ad labentes quandoque iustos promissiones diserte extenduntur: Iustus si ceciderit, non collidetur, quia Dominus supponit manum. Si dereliquerint filii eius legem meam, &c. visitabo virga prævaricationem eorum: misericordiam autem meam non auferam ab eo.
units.tr: Nor do the quibbles help against this, that the promises are not absolute but must be understood with the condition to be performed by the faithful; that, strictly understood, they exclude even the smallest sins of the saints; that the condition is commanded, not promised, etc. These are empty escapes. For the promises speak plainly of the very condition of faith, prayer and perseverance to be effected in the faithful through the Spirit of God. Nor does it follow that its effecting is not promised because it is commanded and required of the faithful. For it is also commanded that they fear God, that they walk in the precepts of God, etc., and yet God promises: "I will give my fear, etc. I will cause them to walk in my precepts." But it is commanded not because they are able, but because they ought to perform it, and so that, recognizing their weakness, they may know what they ought to ask of God. "For this reason," says Augustine, "God commands some things that we cannot do, so that we may know what we ought to ask of him." Hearing the precept, therefore, they ask that what is commanded be given, saying with Augustine: "Give what you command, and command what you will." "Quae mea verba," says the same Augustine, when a certain fellow bishop of mine had recalled these words of mine in Pelagius's presence at Rome, Pelagius could not bear it, and contradicting rather heatedly, nearly quarrelled with the one who recalled them. This also happens to the orthodox with these men today. Nor do those promises exclude the falls and sins of the saints, great or small, but raise the fallen from ruin. For the promises are expressly extended also to righteous men who sometimes stumble: "If the righteous falls, he will not be dashed down, because the Lord supports his hand. If his sons forsake my law, etc., I will visit their transgression with the rod, but I will not take away my mercy from him."

units.la: Si itaque articulus hic tribus prioribus membris est verus & certus, vt est verissimus & certissimus: non potest per conditionem insertam excusari ab hoc manifesto conflictu & contradictione aduersatiuæ appendicis: Omnes vera fide Christo insitos, ac proinde Spiritus eius viuificantis participes à Christo sic confirmari, vt nulla satanæ fraude vel vi possint seduci, vel è manibus eripi, est verum & certum: Et: Omnes vera fide Christo insitos, sic confirmari, vt non possint seduci, Christo eripi: non est verum & certum, sed dubium & incertum, penitius ex sacra scriptura expendendum: Qui conflictus iterum est malæ causæ & conscientiæ apertum argumentum: Neque vero conflictum eludunt sed nodum adstringunt, dicendo, se caput doctrinæ de perseuerantia sanctorum non trahere in dubium, sed petere tantum amplius instituí: Atqui tota collatione de perseuerantia sanctorum ita disputant, & instituí petunt, vt inter varias tergiuersationes idipsum, quod prioribus articuli membris vt verum & certum asseruerunt, reuera non dubium vel incertum, sed aperte falsum & impium esse contendant.
units.tr: If, then, this article is true and certain in its first three members, as it most certainly is, it cannot be excused by the condition inserted into it from this plain conflict and contradiction with the adversative appendix. That all who are grafted into Christ by true faith, and therefore partake of his quickening Spirit, are so confirmed by Christ that they cannot be seduced by any fraud or force of Satan or snatched from his hands, is true and certain. But the claim that all who are grafted into Christ by true faith are so confirmed that they cannot be seduced or snatched from Christ is not true and certain, but doubtful and uncertain, and must be weighed more carefully from holy Scripture. This conflict is again a clear sign of a bad cause and a bad conscience. Nor do they escape the conflict but tighten the knot when they say that they do not call into doubt the head of doctrine concerning the perseverance of the saints, but only seek that it be taught more fully. Yet throughout their whole discussion of the perseverance of the saints they argue, and ask to have it taught, in such a way that, amid various evasions, they contend that the very thing they affirmed in the earlier members of the article as true and certain is in fact not doubtful or uncertain but plainly false and impious.

units.la: Porro in eadem collatione passim, siue ad euitandum hunc conflictum, siue ad conflandam orthodoxis inuidiam, mutato sophistice Articuli subiecto, scribunt, orthodoxos docere: Qui semel crediderunt, eos nunquam posse labi, neque lapsuros, sed perseuerantia sibi habere, quicquid peccent, se nunquam posse fidem amittere, & gratia excidere, sed ineuitabiliter perseueraturos, & saluos futuros. Atque hoc solum dogma de perseuerantia, seu hunc perseue-rantiæ rantiæ modum tantum sese in dubium vocare seu improbare. Ad hoc igitur dogma expugnandum & refutandum, machinæ septem argumentorum, quibus sententiam orthodoxorum oppugnant, proprie directæ sunt.
units.tr: Moreover, throughout the same discussion, whether to avoid this conflict or to stir up hatred against the orthodox, they sophistically change the subject of the article and write that the orthodox teach this: that those who have once believed can never fall, nor will they fall, but whatever sins they commit, perseverance is theirs, and they can never lose faith and fall from grace, but will persevere inevitably and will be saved. And they claim that only this dogma of perseverance, or only this mode of perseverance, is called into doubt or disapproved by them. To overthrow and refute this dogma, therefore, the seven machines of arguments by which they attack the view of the orthodox are directly aimed.

units.la: I. Quia ex se veræ pietati & bonis operibus obsit: seu, quia eius prædicatio sit scandalosa, fides licentiosa,
units.tr: (1) Because it of itself harms true piety and good works; or, because its preaching is scandalous and its faith licentious.

units.la: II. Quia media hortationum, promissionum, minarum, &c. tollat.
units.tr: (2) Because it removes the means of exhortations, promises, threats, and so on.

units.la: III. Quia præmonitiones & commonefactiones Spiritus S. de fraudibus Satanæ cavendis inefficaces reddat.
units.tr: (3) Because it renders ineffective the warnings and admonitions of the Holy Spirit to beware of the frauds of Satan.

units.la: IV. Quia multos, qui crediderunt, à fide totaliter & finaliter defecisse, exempla testentur.
units.tr: (4) Because examples testify that many who believed have fallen away from faith totally and finally.

units.la: V. Quia multi fideles graviter lapsi legantur, ut opera carnis & turpia flagitia commiserint, cum quibus fides stare non possit.
units.tr: (5) Because we read that many faithful people fell grievously, committing the works of the flesh and shameful crimes, with which faith cannot stand.

units.la: VI. Quia eo posito omnes baptizati infantes, fidelibus parentibus nati, servarentur.
units.tr: (6) Because, on this view, all baptized infants born of faithful parents would be saved.

units.la: VII. Quia multi fideles flagitiis se eo usque contaminant, ut sint excommunicandi, & à ministris Ecclesiæ excommunicentur.
units.tr: (7) Because many faithful people defile themselves with such crimes that they must be excommunicated, and are excommunicated by the ministers of the Church.

units.la: Verum enimvero, si hoc solum & totum est, quod in dubium vocant & oppugnant: næ illi VEL inanes sese vitilitigatores, nedicam temerarios Ecclesiæ & Reip. perturbatores, rursus produnt, qui de dogmate lites tantas moverunt, quod non minus orthodoxi, quam ipsi, non modo ut dubium penitius expendendum è scripturis iudicant, sed ut palam falsum & scandalosum improbant, oppugnant, exque Ecclesiis eliminandum censent: VEL certe orthodoxos insigniter calumniantur, affingentes eis dogma, quod illi pro suo minime agnoscunt. Unde & septem illæ argumentorum machinæ non nisi falsum illud dogma feriunt, orthodoxorum sententiam nil prorsus lædunt, prout in collatione demonstratum habetur. Calumnia vero sic patent.
units.tr: But indeed, if this is the whole and only thing that they call into doubt and attack, then those men again reveal themselves either as idle wranglers over words, not to say rash disturbers of the Church and the commonwealth, who have stirred up such great quarrels over a dogma which the orthodox judge no less than they do should be examined more carefully from the Scriptures, but which they condemn, attack and judge should be removed from the churches as plainly false and scandalous; or else they grossly slander the orthodox, ascribing to them a dogma which those men by no means acknowledge as their own. Hence those seven machines of arguments strike only that false dogma and in no way harm the view of the orthodox, as has been shown in the discussion. The slanders are plain as follows.

units.la: Prima est in subiecto: Qui semel crediderunt. Neque enim de his omnibus affirmant orthodoxi perseverantiam: cum etiam hypocritæ & ἀπόστατοι, temporarii non perseverantes credere ὑποκριταὶ dicantur, sed de iis solis, qui per veram fidem Christo sunt insiti, & vivifici eius Spiritus participes.
units.tr: The first lies in the subject: those who have once believed. For the orthodox do not affirm perseverance of all of these, since even hypocrites and apostates, the temporary who do not persevere, are called believers (hypocrites [ὑποκριταί]); they affirm it only of those who by true faith are grafted into Christ and partake of his quickening Spirit.

units.la: Altera calumnia est in primo attributo: eos nunquam posse labi, nec lapsuros. Nam etiam vera fide Christo insitos & sanctos perseveraturos (cum homines maneant, à quibus nil humani alienum) per carnis imbecillitatem in magna & parua peccata non modo labi posse, sed saepe lapsos esse, scriptura sacra & experientia testantur, Orthodoxi sentiunt ac docent.
units.tr: The second slander lies in the first attribute: that they can never fall, nor will they fall. For the orthodox hold and teach that Holy Scripture and experience testify that those truly grafted into Christ by faith and holy persons who will persevere (since they remain human, and nothing human is alien to them) can not only fall into great and small sins through the weakness of the flesh, but often have fallen.

units.la: Tertia est in attributo altero: fideles, quicquid peccent, de perseverantia persuasos esse posse ac debere: hoc q; absurdam doctrinam de perseverantia sanctorum includere. Haec vero non minus aperta & stolida est sophistica accidentis, quam si dicant: quia homines sani currere & laborare & possunt & debent: etiam aegro sebre vel podagra currere & laborare posse ac debere. Atqui sicut morbidi affectus ex accidenti impediunt actiones vitales corporis: sic infirmitates carnis ex accidenti impediunt operationes spirituales fidei & spiritus.
units.tr: The third lies in the second attribute: that the faithful, whatever sins they commit, can and ought to be persuaded of perseverance; and that this includes the absurd doctrine of the perseverance of the saints. This sophistry about accidents is no less plain and foolish than if they were to say: since healthy men can and ought to run and labour, so also a sick man with fever or gout can and ought to run and labour. But just as diseased conditions accidentally hinder the vital actions of the body, so the infirmities of the flesh accidentally hinder the spiritual operations of faith and of the spirit.

units.la: Quarta calumnia est in attributo tertio, fideles nunquam posse finem amittere, vel gratia excidere. Hoc enim sonat istis absolutam impossibilitatem: Orthodoxi vero intelligunt limitatam: non posse hoc fieri, quantum ad gratiosas Dei promissiones, fidelem Spiritus sancti custodiam & immutabile Dei consilium de praedestinatis salvandis: idque ex ore Salvatoris: Matth. 24,24. Johan. 10,28. Quantum vero ad fraudes Satanae, & vires, immo infirmitates fidelium si sibi derelinquerentur, quovis momento posse & nimis posse eos a Satana & carne sua supplantari, excidere atque perire, palam fatentur.
units.tr: The fourth slander lies in the third attribute: that the faithful can never lose their faith or fall from grace. For to them this means absolute impossibility, but the orthodox understand it as limited: that this cannot happen, as far as God's gracious promises, the faithful custody of the Holy Spirit, and the immutable counsel of God concerning the salvation of the predestined are concerned, and this from the mouth of the Saviour (Matt. 24:24; John 10:28). But as far as the frauds of Satan and the powers, or rather the weaknesses, of the faithful are concerned, if they were left to themselves, the orthodox plainly confess that at any moment they can be, and all too easily can be, supplanted by Satan and by their own flesh, fall away and perish.

units.la: Quinta est in eodem attributo: Fidem amittere, gratia excidere: quod rursus isti intelligunt absolute, Orthodoxi vero dicunt limitate, quod non possint amittere fidem, excidere gratia, penitus seu totaliter: ita nimirum ut ex fidelibus fiant infideles & inimici Dei, sicut non renati peccantes: quod scriptura & experientia testante est falsum.
units.tr: The fifth lies in the same attribute: to lose faith and fall from grace. Those men again understand this absolutely, whereas the orthodox say in a limited sense that they cannot lose faith or fall from grace completely or totally, so that from the faithful they become unbelievers and enemies of God, as the unregenerate do when they sin. This, Scripture and experience testify, is false.

units.la: Sexta est in attributo quarto: sed inevitabiliter perseveraturos. Hoc enim istis est, qualescunque, etiam carnaliter securos, & vel invitos perseveraturos; quod est a candore & Orthodoxorum mente alienum.
units.tr: The sixth lies in the fourth attribute: but they will persevere inevitably. For to them this means that whatever sort of people they are, even carnally secure ones, they will persevere even against their will; and this is alien to the sincerity and the mind of the orthodox.

units.la: Sic vero cothurnis explicatis & calumniis remotis. Orthodoxorum doctrina de perseverantia sanctorum in fide, quod sit vera & salutaris, decem scripturae sacrae argumentis in collatione demonstratur.
units.tr: Thus, with these buskins laid aside and the slanders removed, the orthodox doctrine of the perseverance of the saints in faith, that it is true and salutary, is demonstrated in the discussion by ten arguments from Holy Scripture.

units.la: I. Quia Deus in verbo suo promisit fidelibus Christo insitis totalem & finale perseverantiam. Jer. 32,40. Psal. 125, 1. Joh. 10, 28. &c. Ergo & praestat: quia mentiri nequit. Hoc est primum Augustini argumentum pro bono perseverantiae.
units.tr: I. Because God has promised in his word to the faithful grafted into Christ a total and final perseverance (Jer. 32:40; Ps. 125:1; John 10:28, etc.). Therefore he also grants it, because he cannot lie. This is the first argument of Augustine for the good of perseverance.

units.la: II. Quia Apostoli testantur, Deum promissiones suas de custodia eorum in fide fideliter praestare & praestiturum, 1 Cor. 1,8. & 10,13. Phil. 1,6. 1 Thess. 5,23. &c.
units.tr: II. Because the Apostles testify that God faithfully fulfils and will fulfil his promises to keep them in faith (1 Cor. 1:8; 10:13; Phil. 1:6; 1 Thess. 5:23, etc.).

units.la: III. Quia ex doctrina Apostoli Rom. 8,30, perseveratio vocatocatorum secundum propositum est proprius effectus praedestinationis, adeo, ut etiam Bellarminus, gratiae indifferentis seu resistibilis summus patronus, diserte fateatur, perseverantiam esse praedestinationis maxime proprium effectum, adeo ut sine perseverantia praedestinatio impleri non possit.
units.tr: III. Because from the doctrine of the Apostle (Rom. 8:30), the perseverance of those called according to his purpose is the proper effect of predestination; so much so that even Bellarmine, the chief champion of indifferent or resistible grace, openly admits that perseverance is the most proper effect of predestination, so that predestination cannot be fulfilled without perseverance.

units.la: IV. Quia Christus pro perseverantia non solius Petri, sed omnium, qui per sermonem Apostolorum erant credituri in ipsum, oravit & orat. Pater autem Filium semper exaudit. Luc. 22.32. Joh.17,20. Joh.11,42. &c.
units.tr: IV. Because Christ prayed and prays for the perseverance not only of Peter but of all who were to believe in him through the word of the Apostles. The Father always hears the Son (Luke 22:32; John 17:20; John 11:42, etc.).

units.la: V. Quia vera fide Christo insiti indesinenter orant pro sua perseverantia: Quicquid vero ex fide orant, a Deo impetrant. Hoc erat secundum Augustini pro bono perseverantiae argumentum.
units.tr: V. Because those truly grafted into Christ by faith pray constantly for their perseverance; and whatever they pray for in faith, they obtain from God. This was Augustine's argument for the good of perseverance.

units.la: VI. Quia Christo per fidem vere insiti fideliter Dei virtute in fide ad finem usque perseverante custodiuntur. 1 Pet.1,5.
units.tr: VI. Because those truly grafted into Christ by faith are kept by God's power through faith, which perseveres to the end (1 Pet. 1:5).

units.la: VII. Quia vera fide Christo insiti, arrhabone Spiritus sancti in cordibus suis obsignantur de sua salute: proinde etiam de fide & perseverantia: 2 Cor.1,21. Eph.1,13. &c.
units.tr: VII. Because those truly grafted into Christ by faith are sealed in their hearts by the pledge of the Holy Spirit as to their salvation, and therefore also as to their faith and perseverance (2 Cor. 1:21; Eph. 1:13, etc.).

units.la: VIII. Quia vere fideles sunt velut arbor non arescens: vir prudens aedificans super petra: semen iactum in terram bonam, &c. iuxta scripturas.
units.tr: VIII. Because true believers are like a tree that does not wither, like the wise man building on the rock, like the seed sown in good ground, and so on, according to the Scriptures.

units.la: IX. Quia vere fideles discernuntur a temporariis defectoribus: eo quod illorum fides est radicata in cordibus: horum vero radicem non habet.
units.tr: IX. Because true believers are distinguished from temporary apostates, in that their faith is rooted in their hearts, whereas the others have no root.

units.la: X. Quia scriptura expresse confirmat, vere fideles nunquam penitus deficere vel defecturos. Rom. 6,2.8.9.10.11. 1 Joh.3,9. 1 Joh.5,4.
units.tr: X. Because Scripture expressly confirms that true believers never wholly fall away, nor will they fall away. Rom. 6:2, 8, 9, 10, 11; 1 John 3:9; 1 John 5:4.

units.la: Adversus haec, quae a Novatoribus in Col. a pag. 414. usque ad pag. 459 verbosissime disseruntur, universa redeunt ad unum punctum conditionis in fidelibus requisitae: quam exceptionem infirmam esse, & promissionibus ipsis elidi, prius ostensum est. Omnia vero ad unam hanc solidam invictamque demonstrationem, a positione causarum sufficientium ad positionem effectus revocantur hoc modo.
units.tr: All the objections that the innovators set out at great length in the Colloquy, from page 414 to page 459, come back to one point: the condition required of believers. It has already been shown that this exception is weak and is nullified by the promises themselves. All of these arguments are, however, reduced to one solid and unconquerable demonstration, which runs from the positing of sufficient causes to the positing of the effect, in this way.

units.la: Quibus Deus perseverantiam in fide certo dare promisit: & qui virtute Dei custodiuntur in fide usque in finem: & pro quo-rum perseverantia Christus oravit & orat: & qui ipsi indesinenter pro eadem orant: & quorum denique perseverantia in aeterna Dei praedestinatione fundata est: eorum perseverantia in fide ad finem usque, non est dubia, sed certa secundum scripturas. Omnes vera fide Christo insiti sunt tales, quibus Deus perseverantiam dare promisit. Jerem. 32,40. Psal. 125,1. &c. quique virtute Dei custodiuntur per fidem ad salutem. 1 Petr. 1. 5. & pro quorum perseverantia Christus orauit & orat. Joh.17,20. Rom. 8, 34. quique pro eadem quotidie Deum in precatione Dominica invocant: quorum denique perseverantia in aeterna Dei praedestinatione fundatur: Matth.24. vers.24. Rom.8,30. Ephes. 1,11.14. 1 Thess. 2,13.14. &c. Omnium igitur vera fide Christo insitorum perseverantia non est dubia, sed certa, secundum scripturas.
units.tr: Those to whom God has promised to give perseverance in faith with certainty, who are kept in faith by the power of God until the end, for whose perseverance Christ has prayed and prays, and who themselves pray unceasingly for the same, and whose perseverance is finally grounded in the eternal predestination of God: their perseverance in faith to the end is not doubtful but certain, according to the Scriptures. All who are engrafted into Christ by true faith are of this kind: God has promised them perseverance (Jer. 32:40; Ps. 125:1, etc.); they are kept by the power of God through faith unto salvation (1 Pet. 1:5); Christ has prayed and prays for their perseverance (John 17:20; Rom. 8:34); they call upon God daily for the same in the Lord's Prayer; and their perseverance is finally grounded in the eternal predestination of God (Matt. 24:24; Rom. 8:30; Eph. 1:11, 14; 1 Thess. 2:13, 14, etc.). Therefore the perseverance of all who are engrafted into Christ by true faith is not doubtful but certain, according to the Scriptures.

units.la: Non minus firmam demonstrationem praebet causa proxima procreans veram fidem, in renatis semper manens, ex duabus scripturae sententiis simul junctis, 1 Petri 1,23. Renati estis, non ex semine mortali, sed ex immortali per verbum Domini, quod manet in aeternum. Et 1 Johan.3,9. Qui ex Deo natus est, peccatum non facit: quoniam semen Dei manet in eo: nec potest peccare, quia ex Deo natus est. Hinc ita:
units.tr: The proximate cause that produces true faith, and that always remains in the reborn, provides no less firm a demonstration, when two sayings of Scripture are joined together: 1 Pet. 1:23, "You have been born again, not of mortal seed but of immortal, through the word of the Lord, which abides for ever"; and 1 John 3:9, "Whoever is born of God does not sin, for his seed remains in him; nor can he sin, because he is born of God." Thus:

units.la: Qui sunt renati ex semine immortali verbi Dei: & in quibus hoc semen immortale (non obstantibus eorum infirmitatibus) manet: in iis manet etiam, nec unquam deficit fides penitus, proinde & perseverantia: quae est ipsa fides non deficiens, sed manens & perseverans. Ratio huius est nexus individuus causae & effectus, quia semen immortale verbi Dei non manet (in quibus manet) nisi per fidem: Omnes vera fide Christo insiti sunt renati ex semine immortali verbi Dei, teste Petro apostolo, & in iis manet hoc semen immortale, (non obstantibus eorum infirmitatibus) teste Johanne apostolo: In omnibus igitur Christo vera fide insitis, manet, nec unquam penitus deficit fides, proinde & perseverantia, &c.
units.tr: Those who have been born again of the immortal seed of the Word of God, and in whom this immortal seed remains (notwithstanding their infirmities), in them faith also remains and never wholly fails, and therefore neither does perseverance, which is faith itself not failing but abiding and persevering. The reason for this is the inseparable bond of cause and effect: the immortal seed of the Word of God does not remain in those in whom it remains except through faith. All who are engrafted into Christ by true faith are born again of the immortal seed of the Word of God, as the apostle Peter testifies; and in them this immortal seed remains (notwithstanding their infirmities), as the apostle John testifies. Therefore in all who are engrafted into Christ by true faith, faith remains and never wholly fails, and so neither does perseverance, etc.

units.la: Quid multis? Si dubia est Sanctorum perseverantia: nec certo datur a Deo omnibus eam quotidie petentibus, toto corde orando: Sanctificetur nomen tuum: Adueniat regnum tuum: Fiat voluntas tua sicut in coelo & in terra: Ne inducas nos in tentationem: Sed libera nos a malo, &c. quibus petitionibus perseverantiam a Deo peti & impetrari, erudite & sancte docent Cyprianus & Augustinus: Inanis est, praeter alias, haec Dei promissio: Audite domus Iacob, qui portamini a me ab utero: usque ad senectam ego vobiscum sum, & usque ad canitiem ego portabo vos: ego feci: ego feram: ego quoq; portabo & eruam. Inanis erit cordatissima apostoli persuasio, fiducia & pollicitatio: Persuasum habeo hoc ipsum, fore, ut qui coepit in vobis opus bonum, perficiat usque in diem Iesu Christi: nam mihi persuasum est, neque vitam, neque mortem, &c. posse nos separare a dilectione Dei in Christo Iesu: Deus confirmabit vos usque ad finem inculpatos, in diem Domini nostri Iesu Christi. Inanis erit precatio & fiducia Sanctorum precantium cum Davide: Usque, in senium, & in canitiem Deus ne derelinquas me: Ostendisti mihi angustias multas & magnas. Reuersus viuificasti me. Inanis erit fides justificans, seu fiducia remissionis peccatorum in præsenti: quia qui dubitat de promissione Dei in futurum: mentitur se credere promissioni de præsenti: quia connexa est vna: Ego portaui vos: Ego portabo vos vsque in senium. Ego, Ego sum, qui deleo iniquitates tuas propter me: & peccatorum tuorum non recordabor amplius. Inanis denique fides vitæ æternæ & salutis: quia cui dubia est perseuerantia in fide, sine qua vita æterna non obtinetur, quomodo de vita æterna certo confidere potest? Qui enim incertus hæret de crastina, quomodo certus erit de æterna? Sic pro fide inducetur fallax opinatio: regnabit in conscientiis hæsitatio, dubitatio, formido, anxietas, fidem, fiduciam & consolationem Christianam omnem labefactans atq; euertens: Hos reuera fructus negatio perseuerantiæ progenerat. Atqui omnes sunt falsi, impij, blasphemi. Contra omnes igitur stat Sanctorum perseuerantia.
units.tr: Why say more? If the perseverance of the saints is doubtful, and it is not certainly granted by God to all who ask for it every day, praying with their whole heart: "Hallowed be your name; your kingdom come; your will be done on earth as it is in heaven; lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil," etc. By these petitions, Cyprian and Augustine teach learnedly and piously that perseverance is asked of God and obtained. Among other promises, this promise of God would be empty: "Hear, O house of Jacob, you who have been carried by me from the womb; even to old age I am with you, and to grey hairs I will carry you; I have made, I will bear, I will also carry and deliver." The most wise persuasion, confidence and assurance of the apostle would be empty too: "I am sure of this very thing, that he who began a good work in you will complete it until the day of Jesus Christ; for I am persuaded that neither life nor death, etc., can separate us from the love of God in Christ Jesus; God will confirm you blameless to the end, in the day of our Lord Jesus Christ." The prayer and confidence of the saints praying with David would be empty: "Do not forsake me, O God, even to old age and grey hairs. You have shown me many great troubles; you turned and gave me life." Faith that justifies, or the confidence of the forgiveness of sins in the present, would be empty as well, because whoever doubts the promise of God for the future pretends to believe the promise for the present, since the promises are linked as one: "I have carried you; I will carry you even to old age. I, I am he who blots out your iniquities for my own sake, and I will remember your sins no more." Finally, faith in eternal life and salvation would be empty, because how can one who doubts perseverance in faith, without which eternal life is not obtained, be certain of eternal life? For he who hangs in uncertainty about tomorrow, how will he be certain about eternity? Thus a false opinion would be introduced in place of faith; hesitation, doubt, dread and anxiety would reign in consciences, overthrowing and subverting all Christian faith, confidence and consolation. These are indeed the fruits that the denial of perseverance produces. But these are all false, impious and blasphemous. Therefore the perseverance of the saints stands against them all.

units.la: Nihil vero argumentis his officit cauillum de conditione promissionibus annexa, vt est ostensum.
units.tr: Nothing, however, is harmed by these arguments through the quibble about the condition attached to the promises, as has been shown.

units.la: Nihil etiam perseuerantiam Sanctorum lædit calumnia de prædicatione scandalosa, & fide licentiosa perseuerantiæ. Secus scandalose prædicassent eam Apostoli, licentiose credidissent Ecclesiæ: Ego, inquit Augustinus, nolo exaggerare meis verbis. Sed illis cogitandum potius relinquo, vt videant, quale sit illud, quod sibi persuaserunt, prædicationem perseuerantiæ audientibus plus desperationis quam exhortationis afferre. Hoc est enim dicere, tunc de sua salute hominem desperare, quando spem suam non in seipso, sed in Deo didicerit ponere, &c.
units.tr: Nor does the calumny about scandalous preaching and licentious faith harm the perseverance of the saints. Otherwise the apostles would have preached perseverance scandalously, and the Church would have believed it licentiously. "I," says Augustine, "do not wish to exaggerate in my words. But I leave it rather for them to consider, that they may see what it is they have persuaded themselves of: that preaching perseverance brings more despair than exhortation to those who hear it. For this is to say that a man must despair of his salvation when he has learned to place his hope not in himself but in God," etc.

units.la: Nihil paralogismus non causæ, de neglectu vel annullatione mediorum, & prænionitionum, &c. His ipsis enim Spiritus sanctus certitudinem perseuerantiæ in cordibus sanctorum operatur atque sustentat.
units.tr: Nor does the paralogism about neglect or annulment of means and warnings, etc., harm it, for by these very means the Holy Spirit works and sustains the certainty of perseverance in the hearts of the saints.

units.la: Nihil exempla hypocritarum vel apostatarum quartæ machinæ, de qualibus etiam quinque marginalia articuli loquuntur. Hi enim cum vere fidelibus nihil præter nomen fidei commune obtinent: de quibus proinde omnibus dicitur: Ex nobis egressi sunt, quia ex nobis non erant. Nam si fuissent ex nobis, mansissent utique nobiscum, verum vt manifestum fieret, quod ex nobis non essent, ideo egressi sunt. Videatur Augustinus de bono perseuer. cap. 8.
units.tr: Nor do the examples of hypocrites or apostates in the fourth machine harm it, of whom also the five marginal notes of this article speak. For these have nothing in common with true believers except the name of faith; therefore it is said of all of them: "They went out from us, because they were not of us; for if they had been of us, they would certainly have remained with us; but that it might be made plain that they were not of us, they went out." See Augustine, On the Gift of Perseverance, ch. 8.

units.la: Nihil Mosis, Aaronis, Dauidis, Salomonis, Petri, Judæ, & aliorum lapsus graues & atroces. Si quid enim contra facem rent, totalem saltem, minime finalem perseuerantiam labefactarent. Nam illos omnes, quos obijcere solent perseuerantiæ hostes, vel non fuisse vere fideles, sed hypocritas, vel finaliter resi-
units.tr: Nor do the grave and atrocious falls of Moses, Aaron, David, Solomon, Peter, Judas and others. For if they had sinned against the faith, they would have shaken at least their total perseverance, though not their final perseverance. For all those whom the enemies of perseverance are accustomed to cite, it can be shown either that they were not true believers but hypocrites, or that they finally repented.

units.la: De bono perseu. c.18.
units.tr: On the Gift of Perseverance, ch. 18.

units.la: Esa. 46,3. Esa. 43,25. Ioh. 2,19. resipuisse doceri potest. Sed neque totalis horum perseuerantia labefactari hinc potest, quin promissiones diuinæ simul labefactentur: quas prætensæ conditionis exceptione labefactari est impossibile.
units.tr: Isa. 46:3; Isa. 43:25; John 2:19. But their total perseverance cannot be shaken by this without the divine promises being shaken at the same time, and it is impossible for these to be shaken by the exception of a supposed condition.

units.la: Sunt autem (vt obiter hoc moneatur) lapsus sanctorum non mo- rosè hic exagitandi ab iis, qui in sanctorum censu haberi volunt, sed {χαιρῶς} ex caritatis regula deplorandi magis, quàm judican- di: consideratà tum Dei Patris, qui filios peccantes judicare habet, tum filiorum, qui Deo Patri peccant, ratione.
units.tr: Moreover (as is to be noted in passing) the falls of the saints are not to be harshly censured here by those who wish to be counted among the saints, but rather are to be lamented in the rule of charity, and not judged, with regard both to God the Father, who has to judge sinning children, and to the children, who sin against God the Father, [χαιρῶς] kindly.

units.la: Pari crimine quandoq; implicatur filius & seruus in domo: imò filius grauius quam seruus. Tamen pater terrenus seruum eijcit domo: filium non exhæredat, sed castigat ad emendationem. Peccatū igitur filij juuenili stultitia admissum, sicut odium filij in patrem non inuexit: ita gratiam Patris in filium non extinxit. Dauid proditorie occidit Vriam: Ioab Amasam: Petrus Christum ter perfide negauit: Judas semel prodidit. Sepone cuentum, grauius ille quam iste peccasse videtur. Christum tamen illum, non istum respexit. Adsint jam censores, & Petrum, pro cuius fide, ne deficeret, Christus orauit, ex metu negando, fidem penitus amisisse contendant.
units.tr: A son and a servant in a household can sometimes be implicated in the same crime, and indeed the son more gravely than the servant. Yet an earthly father casts the servant out of the house, but he does not disinherit the son; he chastises him for his correction. So the sin of a son, committed through youthful folly, has not stirred up hatred of the son toward the father, and in the same way it has not extinguished the father's grace toward the son. David treacherously killed Uriah; Joab killed Amasa; Peter denied Christ three times, faithlessly; Judas betrayed him once. Set aside the outcome: that one seems to have sinned more grievously than the other, yet Christ looked upon the former and not the latter. Let the critics now come forward, and let them contend that Peter, for whose faith Christ prayed that it might not fail, lost his faith altogether through his fear and denial.

units.la: Ad lapsus vero quod attinet, sicut morbis acutioribus vita hominis periclitatur, donec subueniat medicus: non mox tota extinguitur: ita lapsibus grauioribus Sanctorum concutitur fides & infirmatur: non mox penitus excutitur, emoriturque: quia medicus cœlestis gratia ineffabili semen immortale illud Dei (de quo fuit) in cordibus sustentat, supponitque manum justis, quando cadunt, ne collidantur. 1 Joh. 3, 9. Psalm. 37, 24. Hæc, nulla {ἐπιχείρησις} humana, nedum pietas Christiana, vlla specie expugnabit.
units.tr: As for the falls, just as a man's life is endangered by acute diseases until the physician comes to help, yet it is not at once wholly extinguished, so the faith of the saints is shaken and weakened by their graver falls, but it is not at once utterly cast out and does not die. The reason is that the heavenly physician, by his ineffable grace, sustains in their hearts that immortal seed of God (from which they were born), and he puts his hand under the righteous when they fall, lest they be dashed to pieces. 1 John 3:9; Psalm 37:24. No human stratagem, much less Christian piety, will overthrow this by any appearance.

units.la: Nihil denique duo postremi ineptissimi paralogismi perseuerantiam Sanctorum lædere possunt, si vel scholastice examinentur. Vterque enim, vt, quod debet, hoc est, contradictoriam perseuerantiæ: Aliquos vere & actualiter credentes atque regenitos, fidem & spiritum regenerationis amittere, directè conficiat: necesse habet, vel (ne præmissarum altera sit falsa) ex puris particularibus inepte concludere. Prior quidem hoc modo: Aliqui fidelium parentum liberi baptizati penitus amittunt fidem & Spiritum regenerationis: Ratio; quia alioqui omnes (nullo excepto) seruarentur: quod istis absurdum, nobis ex charitate maxime optandum videtur. Aliqui fidelium parentum liberi baptizati vere & actualiter credunt, & regenerantur. Igitur aliqui vere & actualiter credentes & regenerati penitus amittunt fidem & Spiritum regenerationis. Posterior vero hoc modo: Aliqui propter flagiflagitia excommunicati penitus amittunt fidem. Aliqui propter flagitia excommunicati sunt vere credentes & regenerati. Aliqui igitur vere credentes & regenerati penitus amittunt fidem. Vel cum hæ ineptiæ ineptæ sint (vt consequentiæ corrigantur) priorem Minorem vniuersalem falsam assumere: posterior Maiorem vniuersalem itidem falsam supponere: vt prior sic se habeat in Disamis: (aliter enim concludi nequit: nisi & Maiorem vniuersalem falsam malint) Aliqui fidelium parentum liberi baptizati penitus amittunt fidem & regenerationem. Omnes fidelium parentum liberi baptizati vere & actualiter credunt, & regenerantur. Igitur aliqui vere & actualiter credentes ac regeniti penitus amittunt fidem & regenerationem. Hic assumtionem vniuersalem (nisi sacramentaliter intelligatur: quomodo rursus vacillaret consequutio) esse falsam, nec ipsi Remonstrantes negabunt. Ex sententia enim Augustini, (quam Ecclesiæ orthodoxæ sequuntur) sicut in Isaac, qui octavo die circumcisus est, præcessit signaculum justitiæ fidei: & quoniam patris fidem imitatus est, secuta est in crescente ipsa justitia, cuius signaculum in infante præcesserat: ita & in baptizatis infantibus precedit regenerationis sacramentum: & si Christianam tenuerint pietatem, sequitur etiam conversio: cuius mysterium præcedit in corpore. Neque ad assumtionis vniuersalis falsæ probationem verba Catech. pag. 74 quicquam faciunt.
units.tr: Finally, the two last most absurd paralogisms cannot harm the perseverance of the saints, even if they are examined in the schools. For each of them, if it is to accomplish what it ought, that is, directly to establish the contradictory of perseverance, that some who truly and actually believe and are regenerate lose faith and the Spirit of regeneration, must either (lest one of the premises be false) conclude foolishly from purely particular premises. The first, indeed, runs in this way: Some children of believing parents, once baptized, wholly lose faith and the Spirit of regeneration. The reason: otherwise all of them (without exception) would be saved, which seems absurd to those men, but which we must most earnestly wish for out of charity. Some children of believing parents, once baptized, truly and actually believe and are regenerate. Therefore some who truly and actually believe and are regenerate wholly lose faith and the Spirit of regeneration. The latter runs in this way: Some who have been excommunicated on account of crimes wholly lose faith. Some who have been excommunicated on account of crimes are truly believers and regenerate. Therefore some who are truly believers and regenerate wholly lose faith. Or, since these absurdities are absurd, if the consequences are to be corrected, the first must assume as its minor premise a universal that is false, and the latter must likewise suppose as its major premise a universal that is false, so that the first stands thus in Disamis (for otherwise it cannot be concluded, unless they prefer a false universal major premise as well): Some children of believing parents, once baptized, wholly lose faith and regeneration. All children of believing parents, once baptized, truly and actually believe and are regenerate. Therefore some who truly and actually believe and are regenerate wholly lose faith and regeneration. Here the universal assumption is false (unless it is understood sacramentally; otherwise the consequence would again waver), and the Remonstrants themselves will not deny it. For according to the opinion of Augustine, which the orthodox churches follow, just as in Isaac, who was circumcised on the eighth day, the seal of the righteousness of faith went before, and because he imitated his father's faith, the righteousness itself followed as it grew, whose seal had gone before in the infant, so also in baptized infants the sacrament of regeneration goes before, and if they hold to the Christian piety, conversion follows as well, whose mystery goes before in the body. Nor do the words of the Catechism, page 74, contribute anything to proving the false universal assumption.

units.la: Posterior Maiore vniuersali in Datisi, vel minore conversa in Darij (aliter enim concludi nequit) sic erit: Omnes propter flagitia excommunicati veram fidem & Spiritum sanctum penitus amittunt. Aliqui propter flagitia excommunicati sunt vere fideles & regenerati. Aliqui igitur vere fideles & regenerati fidem & Spiritum sanctum penitus amittunt. Hic Maiorem vniuersalem esse falsam, ab Orthodoxis in collatione recte responsum est: ab alteris vero non refutatum. Possunt enim ex ecclesia & regno Christi excludi, qui nunquam vere in gratia steterunt, sed semper fuerunt hypocritæ, fide vera & Spiritu Dei destituti. Sic igitur veritatem orthodoxam de perseverantia sanctorum in fide à machinis istorum omni ex parte illæsam consistere, demonstratum est. Atque hæc quoque de Articulo quinto sufficiant.
units.tr: The latter, with the major universal in Datisi, or with the minor converted in Darii (for otherwise it cannot be concluded), will be this: All who have been excommunicated on account of crimes wholly lose true faith and the Holy Spirit. Some who have been excommunicated on account of crimes are truly faithful and regenerate. Therefore some who are truly faithful and regenerate wholly lose faith and the Holy Spirit. Here the major universal is false, and the Orthodox have rightly answered this in the collation; but the others have not refuted it. For those who never truly stood in grace, but have always been hypocrites, destitute of true faith and of the Spirit of God, can be excluded from the Church and the kingdom of Christ. Thus it has been demonstrated that the orthodox truth concerning the perseverance of the saints in faith stands entirely unharmed by the machinations of these men. And let these things also suffice concerning the fifth article.

units.la: OMISSA IN MISCELLANEIS.
units.tr: OMITTED ITEMS IN THE MISCELLANEOUS SECTION.

units.la: Articulo V. de Prædestinatione, Aphorismo VII. pag. 43. Omissa Testimonia Scriptura ita suis literis respondere debent. a] Rom. 9, 18. Cuius vult, miseretur. Ephes. 1, 5. Qui prædestinauit nos, quos adoptaret in filios per Iesum Christum in se pro benevolo affectu voluntatis suæ. Matth. 11, 26. Etiam Pater; quoniam sic placuit tibi. b] Rom. 9, 18. Quem vult, indurat. c] Psal. 81, 13. Permisi igitur eos fortitudini cordis eorum, & ambulaverunt in consiliis suis. Act. 14, 16. Quia, præteritis ætatibus suit omnes gentes suis ipsarum viis incedere. d] Actor. 13, 48. Et crediderunt, quotquot ordinati erant ad vitam æternam. Tit. 1, 1. Secundum fidem electorum Dei. e] Genes. cap. 4. f] Genes. capp. 9. & 10. g] Genes. 12. 1. h] Genes. 21, 10. i] Matth. cap. 27. k] Matth. 24, 40. l] Jacobi 1, 17. Actor. 15, 18.
units.tr: Article V, on Predestination, Aphorism VII, p. 43. The omitted testimonies of Scripture ought to answer to these letters as follows. a] Rom. 9:18. He has mercy on whom he will. Eph. 1:5. Who predestined us to adoption as children through Jesus Christ, according to the good pleasure of his will. Matt. 11:26. Even so, Father, for so it seemed good in your sight. b] Rom. 9:18. He hardens whom he will. c] Ps. 81:13. So I gave them over to the stubbornness of their hearts, and they walked in their own counsels. Acts 14:16. Who in past generations suffered all the nations to walk in their own ways. d] Acts 13:48. And as many as were ordained to eternal life believed. Titus 1:1. According to the faith of God's elect. e] Gen. cap. 4. f] Gen. capp. 9 and 10. g] Gen. 12:1. h] Gen. 21:10. i] Matt. cap. 27. k] Matt. 24:40. l] James 1:17. Acts 15:18.
